title: Holnicote Estate, National Trust
subtitle: Holnicote Estate makes up 12,000 acres of Exmoor National Park and is a contrasting landscape with everything from wild, rugged moorland and shingle beaches to ancient woodland and charming thatched villages.
bodyContent: Holnicote Estate, Exmoor, Somerset National Trust makes up 12,000 acres of Exmoor National Park and is a contrasting landscape with everything from wild, rugged moorland and shingle beaches to ancient woodland and charming thatched villages. A fantastic place for walking, horse riding and cycling, Holnicote has 150 miles of footpaths and bridleways to explore. Walk up to Dunkery Beacon, Somerset's highest point and a spectacular spot for stargazing, or take a more leisurely stroll and enjoy a picnic or BBQ at Bossington . Red deer, Exmoor ponies, bats and the rare heath fritillary butterfly along with an awesome array of lichens and mosses make Holnicote a unique and very special place to visit. Selworthy Green is an ideal place to begin with information on walks and other activities available from Selworthy shop. You can also pop into the nearby Periwinkle tearoom for a cream tea to set you up before exploring (seasonal opening).
tagline: Holnicote Estate makes up 12,000 acres of Exmoor National Park.

title: Cheddar Gorge
subtitle: Cheddar Gorge & Caves boasts extraordinary subterranean show caves, awe-inspiring cliffs and holds many fascinating secrets about our prehistoric ancestors.
bodyContent: Our Day Ticket gives access to six great attractions: Gough’s Cave: Prepare to be amazed by our stunning show cave featuring spectacular stalagmite and stalactite formations created over 500,000 years ago! See cheddar cheese maturing in the caves, view the site where Cheddar Man’s 10,000-year-old skeleton was discovered and learn about the extraordinary DNA discovery. A free audio guide is available in six languages, and there is also a special version for children. Cox’s Cave featuring Yeo’s Journey: The Power of Water. This spectacular immersive multimedia experience tells the captivating story of how our iconic caves were formed and evolved through the ‘Power of Water’. The story is brought to life using state-of-the-art animation, sound, lighting and colour. Beyond the View: Take a seat in front of our state of the art 270-degree screen. Discover historic tales, enjoy breathtaking aerial panoramic views, and learn about the special wildlife and plants that call the gorge home. Museum of Pre-History: Discover amazing artefacts unearthed in the Cheddar area that help tell the story of how people lived thousands of years ago. Jacob’s Ladder & The Lookout Tower: Venture up the 274 steps to the top of the gorge with rest stops along the route to admire the view. Marvel at the panoramic views and mosaic of landscapes across the Mendips and Somerset Levels. Cliff­ -Top Walk: Hike the 3-mile loop around the gorge. Look out for the wildlife and enjoy the stunning scenery. If you don’t have time to do the full circuit, you can go for a shorter walk up to the Pulpit Rock look out point, and head back down the ladder. Gough’s Café Sit back, relax, and take in the beauty of the gorge at Gough’s Cafe, close to the entrance of Gough's Cave. Enjoy a thirst-quenching chilled drink, warm yourself up with a hot beverage or choose from a selection of alcoholic drinks. Serving light lunches, delicious snacks, cream teas and delicious cake, to include vegetarian and vegan options. Enjoy the spectacular views from the comfort of our air-conditioned cafe or relax on the large patio where dogs are welcome. We even have a welcome bowl of water for our doggy friends. Our small play area for under 2-year-olds will keep the little ones entertained too! Accessibility Cheddar Gorge & Caves provides accessible toilets, free parking for blue badge holders and free admission for carers accompanied by a full paying visitor. The audio tour of Gough's cave is printed in braille. Assistance Dogs are permitted, and the museum is wheelchair accessible with lift. Those with severely restricted mobility or who are wheelchair dependent will find areas of Cheddar Gorge & Caves inaccessible. If you have any questions prior to your visit, please email Guest Services on info@cheddargorge.co.uk or call 01934 742343. Dog-Friendly Dogs are welcome in all attractions and water bowls are provided in the cave entrances, shop and café patio. Family and Children Cheddar Gorge & Cave is family friendly. We have baby changing facilities, buggy parking and are breast-feeding friendly. Gough’s café has a small play area for under two year olds, water refills and highchairs are available. Entry is free for children under the age of 5 years. Groups Cheddar Gorge & Caves has special group rates, coach parking and drop off points for group tours. We offer discounted exclusive group sessions for Rocksport adventure activities – adventure caving, rock climbing and freefall. Special Events We have a fantastic programme of events throughout the year to keep the whole family entertained, including the school holidays. Visit our What’s On page for more details. Thirst for adventure or a puzzle-solving mind? Rocksport: Imagine climbing the gorge rockface in the shadow of the 450ft cliffs, caving deep underground or taking part in our exhilarating Blackcat freefall in Gough’s Cave. Suitable for all abilities. Sessions available for adults and children aged 8 years and over. Escape Rooms : Up for a challenge? Our two Cheddar-themed rooms, Caved In and The Vault will test your brain power as you race against the clock to try to escape. Double the fun with our Ultimate Escape combo ticket at a discounted rate. Suitable for 12 years and over in groups of up to six people. Nature, wildlife, history, adventure - experience the wonder on an all-season day out in Somerset. For more information on how to plan your day at Cheddar Gorge & Caves and to book please visit www.cheddargorge.co.uk

title: Barrington Court, National Trust
subtitle: Barrington Court, located in the stunning south Somerset countryside, is a charming Tudor manor house complimented beautifully with Gertrude Jekyll-inspired gardens, apple orchards and a working kitchen garden.
bodyContent: Barrington Court Somerset National Trust - Discover the haunting echoes of the past at Barrington Court, a Tudor manor house free from collections and furniture. Explore using your imagination and your senses to discover a house full of memories, where light fills the rooms and you feel you can almost touch the past. The property was saved from ruin and restored by the Lyle family in 1920s, when the Court House resembled a barn rather than the proud manor house that it is. Close your eyes and you’ll almost be able to hear the sounds and see the sights of the glamorous parties held in the great hall during Barrington’s heyday. On the first floor listen out for the voices resonating from the past, of the young evacuees who called Barrington home during the Second World War. Stroll through the Gertrude Jekyll inspired gardens, which with their focus on plant varieties and colours are a delight for all the senses. Be spurred on in your own garden or allotment by the stone-walled kitchen garden that produces a variety of delicious fruit and vegetables. Don’t just take our word for it, why not stop off in the Strode House Restaurant to taste these home-grown delights. Barrington Court predominantly featured in BBC’s highly acclaimed recent production of Hilary Mantel’s Wolf Hall.
tagline: Barrington Court, located in the stunning south Somerset countryside.

title: Montacute House, National Trust
subtitle: Montacute House is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design
bodyContent: Montacute House, Somerset is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design. With its towering walls of glass, glow of ham stone and its surrounding gardens, it is a place of beauty and wonder. Sir Edward Phelips was the visionary force and money behind this masterpiece, which was completed in 1601. Built by skilled craftsman using local ham stone under the instruction of William Arnold, master mason, the house was a statement of wealth, ambition and showmanship. Come face to face with the past in the Long Gallery; measuring over 52 metres, it is the longest of its kind in England. The Gallery houses over 60 Tudor and Elizabethan portraits on loan from the National Portrait Gallery. Beautiful gardens surround Montacute, constantly changing, filling the house with scent in summer and providing an atmospheric backdrop for a winter walk. Whether you just want to let the children run and explore, or be inspired by the collections housed within the walls of Montacute, you will leave with lasting memories and a desire to soon return. You may even recognise some of the sights, as Montacute House featured in the BBC’s highly acclaimed production of Hilary Mantel’s Wolf Hall. Within 20 minutes’ drive you will find four fascinating smaller properties, each with a unique character, history and story to tell. Their combined age of 2,300 years spans from the medieval period to the early 19th century. Explore Stoke Priory, a fine collection of medieval farm buildings; Treasurer's House, with its great hall and unusual wall painting; Stembridge Tower Mill, the last remaining thatched windmill in England; and the Priest’s House, a medieval home of great character not to be missed. While you’re in the area, why not also visit Lytes Cary Manor and Tintinhull Garden (see the National Trust website for more details).
tagline: Montacute House in Somerset is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design

title: Dunster Castle
subtitle: Fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years, remodelled 100 years ago. Fine 17thC staircase and plaster ceilings. Terrace garden of rare shrubs.
bodyContent: Dunster Castle and Gardens are open daily from 10am-5pm. Last entry to the castle is 3.45pm and last entry to the gardens is 4pm. The Stables Shop, Watermill Tearoom, and parkland are open 10am-5pm and the car park is locked at 6pm. A fortress that became a family home for the Luttrells, who lived at Dunster for 600 years, the castle was extensively remodelled in the 1870s to create a Victorian country house. The castle boasts breath-taking views over Exmoor, Somerset, and the Bristol Channel as well as holding fine interior features such as a fine 17 th century carved staircase, ornate plaster ceilings, and rare leather wall hangings. Discover how Dunster Castle was used in its heyday and how the family hosted grand occasions from society balls to polo matches with the brilliant ‘Chapters’ guide as well as ‘Castle Explorers, available for children. You can then enjoy a leisurely stroll through beautiful terraced gardens with a collection of palms, sub-tropical plants, and the Dunster Lemon tree. Sited on the River Avill, Dunster Castle is also home to a working watermill that sits within the river gardens. Visit the mill to see the waterwheels in action and even purchase some of the freshly-milled flour. Refreshments are available in the newly-refurbished Watermill Tearoom and also outside the castle in the Tenants’ Hall Café. Please see our accessibility statement here. Facilities in addition to those listed below: Baby changing facilities Children's trails Courtesy vehicle Stair Climber Trampers available to book
tagline: Dramatically sited on a wooded hill and the fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years.

title: Komedia Bath
subtitle: Hosting over 400 events per year in a beautifully restored former Edwardian cinema, Komedia is a go-to destination for a great night out in the city of Bath. Take your pick from Saturday night stand-up, top gigs and tours, quirky cabaret shows, late night revelry and so much at the award-winning venue.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Komedia Bath was established in 2008 and community-owned since 2019, Komedia prides itself on offering something for everybody and operates two distinct performance spaces to do this. At the heart of it all is the Main Auditorium. With high ceilings, baroque grandeur and room for 600+ people, it’s a stunning setting for full-scale live performances and also functions as Bath’s only above-ground night club venue. The Main Auditorium is also home to the award-winning Komedia Comedy Club. The legendary Comedy Club features some of the best acts from the UK and international stand-up circuit every Saturday night. Each show features three world-class comedians and a top-notch compere. For the ultimate Saturday night out, add entry to The Big Disco after the comedy for just £2! Alongside this, Komedia is also very proud to run The Electric Bar – an intimate live performance space that was purpose-built to support grassroots-level music and rising comedy talent. The venue's Box Office is also situated within The Electric Bar, open Tuesday - Saturday from 10am - 5pm. Drop by to find out what’s on, take a quick tour of the venue or pick up a programme. Komedia is committed to being accessible to everyone and is continuously working to improve the experience of its disabled audiences, artists, and team members. For information on accessibility at Komedia, please visit: https://komediabath.co.uk/plan-your-visit/accessibility/
tagline: Hosting over 400 events per year in a beautifully restored former Edwardian cinema

title: Thatchers Cider
subtitle: For more than a hundred years, family-run Thatchers Cider has been quietly perfecting the magic that turns apples into cider.
bodyContent: For more than a hundred years, family-run Thatchers Cider has been quietly perfecting the magic that turns apples into cider. Here at Myrtle Farm in Sandford, each generation has passed on cider-making secrets, like encouraging bees to pollinate the apple blossom, or looking after the 150 year old oak vats where the cider matures. We lovingly craft a range of ciders but whichever you choose, they have all been made with the same care and attention, and with the same hands-on experience – we wouldn’t have it any other way. Nestled at the foot of the Mendip Hills , the Thatchers orchards are our pride and joy. With apples such as Dabinett, Somerset Redstreak and Porters Perfection, as well as some newer varieties such as Angela, Lizzie and Prince William, it’s here that the journey starts, inspired by the heritage and values of our company. Our flagship brand Thatchers Gold is a full flavoured, medium dry Somerset cider, with a wonderfully rich, golden colour. Thatchers Vintage is well balanced and mature, with a distinctive depth of character, while Thatchers Haze is a premium cloudy cider that has a crisp, sweet finish. We have recently introduced a new cider to our range, the gloriously pink Rosé, bursting with fruity apple flavours. Our other ciders include Thatchers Katy, Old Rascal and Green Goblin, together with our Stan’s Range of traditional ciders, such as Cheddar Valley, Trad. and Big Apple. Available on line and in our Cider Shop, Finally, holding down the fort at home, we have our award-winning Cider Barn range that’s exclusive to Myrtle Farm.that includes very special ciders such as Thatchers 458, Vilberie and Redstreak. You can buy all our ciders online at www.thatcherscider.co.uk Or visit our Cider Shop at Myrtle Farm. Here the shelves are packed with our ciders, alongside produce such as local cheeses and chutneys, and gifts including books and clothing. Our draught ciders are available straight from the barrel, so you can try before you buy. Why not book onto a tour of Myrtle Farm and see how we make our ciders. Visit www.thatcherscider.co.uk/visitus for more information. To book a tour of Myrtle Farm, please visit www.thatcherscider.co.uk

title: The Bell
subtitle: With roots dating back to 1640, The Bell at Broadway is the oldest pub in the area. Beautifully restored in 2018, this 17th-century inn blends historic charm with modern comfort. Enjoy delicious food, fine drinks, and relaxed stays in a timeless setting — celebrating tradition, warmth, and unforgettable hospitality.
bodyContent: With roots reaching back to 1640, The Bell at Broadway proudly holds its place as the oldest pub in the area — a true landmark of local heritage and community spirit. Steeped in history, this beautiful 17th-century inn has welcomed generations of travellers, villagers, and friends through its doors for centuries. Following an extensive renovation in 2018, The Bell has been lovingly restored to preserve the charm and craftsmanship of its past while introducing the warmth and comfort of modern design. Traditional beams, stonework, and characterful details sit effortlessly alongside stylish interiors, inviting open fires, and thoughtful touches that make every visit memorable. Whether you’re joining us for a hearty meal, a perfectly poured drink, or a peaceful overnight stay, The Bell offers a relaxed and welcoming atmosphere that celebrates the best of both old and new. Our menu showcases locally sourced ingredients and seasonal flavours, complemented by an excellent selection of ales, wines, and spirits — all served with genuine Somerset hospitality. From cosy corners for quiet conversations to lively gatherings with family and friends, The Bell at Broadway is a place to slow down, savour, and reconnect. Step inside, feel the history around you, and enjoy the comfort of a modern country inn that honours its past while embracing the present. Here’s to another three hundred years of good company, great food, and the enduring spirit of The Bell at Broadway.

title: May Half Term at The Bishop's Palace
subtitle: We’ve got plenty for families to enjoy this May Half Term at The Bishop's Palace, including our NEW Splash Play Zone!
bodyContent: Come and see our family of swans exploring the moat, relax on the South Lawn with a picnic, explore our gardens with our Half Term trail, and get creative with Art Adventurers. Here’s what’s on: 🦢 May Half Term Family Trail 📅 23 – 31 May 2026 | 9.30am – 5.30pm Explore our 14 acres of RHS partner gardens to find the swans hidden around the grounds and uncover fascinating facts about these special birds. ✂️ May Half Term Art Adventurers Crafting 📅 Thursday 28 May 2026 | 11am – 3pm Join us in the Palace’s atmospheric Undercroft for a special Art Adventurers crafting session this May Half Term. title: Shetland View - Collie Shepherd Huts
subtitle: Shetland View is a luxurious Somerset shepherd’s hut for two, offering spacious interiors, sweeping views of the Somerset Levels and refined finishes. Enjoy a private wood-fired hot tub with jacuzzi spa jets, peaceful surroundings, evening sunsets, stargazing nights and slow, relaxing mornings while exploring nature, scenic walks and nearby attractions.
bodyContent: Shetland View is a luxurious countryside hideaway created for couples who want to slow down, reconnect and savour uninterrupted time together. Overlooking the sweeping Somerset Levels, this beautifully designed shepherd’s hut offers complete tranquillity, soft light and a sense of space that instantly soothes the soul. Inside, warm textures and elegant simplicity set the tone for relaxation. The unique pull-down king-size bed invites long, lazy mornings, while underfloor heating and a glowing wood burner create a cosy, intimate atmosphere. The well-equipped kitchenette includes a combi oven, fridge with freezer compartment and everything needed for effortless self-catering, complemented by a thoughtful welcome breakfast pack. The modern ensuite features a heated towel rail, flushing toilet, fluffy bathrobes, slippers and soft towels, with an additional set provided for the hot tub. Step outside to your private garden, where a wood-fired hot tub with jacuzzi spa jets waits beneath open skies. As sunsets melt into starlight, couples can sink into the warm, bubbling water, share quiet conversations and enjoy moments that feel both indulgent and deeply peaceful. A fire pit and BBQ offer more ways to unwind, with complimentary logs provided throughout your stay. Surrounded by nature, the gentle presence of miniature Shetland ponies and set beside a working farm, Shetland View is a romantic retreat where time slows, connection deepens and every detail feels thoughtfully designed for couples seeking calm, luxury and unforgettable moments together
tagline: Collie Shepherd Hut is an exclusive countryside retreat in Somerset.

subtitle: Looking for a great-value family day out this summer?
bodyContent: Looking for a great-value family day out this summer? Wookey Hole has unveiled a magical line-up of adventures beneath the Mendip Hills, including its hugely popular new immersive cave projections. Wookey Hole is a surprising, whole day experience, where families can explore the legendary caves, home to the famous Witch of Wookey Hole, before discovering a packed programme of attractions above ground. From a 4D cinema, live circus shows (during weekends and Somerset School Holidays), adventure golf and soft play to a nostalgic vintage penny arcade, there’s plenty to keep children entertained throughout the day – all within one price. Using spectacular projection mapping, the natural rock formations come alive with tales of the Witch, ancient geology and daring explorers - creating a truly unforgettable, immersive adventure that families are already loving. To make visits even easier, visitors can enjoy up to 20% off tickets this summer (25 June and 2 September 2026).

title: Noah's Ark Zoo Farm - Marketing Operations Coordinator
subtitle: Contract: 12-Month Fixed Term Contract Hours: Full time (40 hours per week) Salary: £32,000 per annum
bodyContent: Help Deliver Marketing That Makes a Difference Are you an organised marketing professional who thrives on bringing campaigns to life? Do you enjoy juggling multiple projects, working with a wide range of people and ensuring everything runs smoothly behind the scenes? Noah's Ark Zoo Farm is looking for a Marketing Operations Coordinator to join our friendly Marketing team on a 12-month fixed-term contract. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in delivering our annual marketing programme, helping drive visitor numbers, support fundraising and promote our conservation mission. Every year we deliver a wide variety of campaigns including seasonal events, fundraising appeals and community initiatives. You'll be at the centre of making these campaigns happen, coordinating activity across the organisation and ensuring projects are delivered on time, on budget and to the highest standard. About the Role: Reporting to the Head of Sales & Marketing, you'll coordinate the delivery of our annual marketing plan, working closely with colleagues across the organisation, external agencies, media partners and suppliers. You'll help keep multiple campaigns on track, manage marketing administration and budgets, coordinate campaign assets and support reporting that helps us continually improve our marketing performance. This is a varied role that would suit someone who enjoys organisation just as much as creativity, and who loves seeing projects through from planning to delivery. What You'll Be Doing: You'll be responsible for: · Coordinating the delivery of marketing campaigns, promotions, fundraising initiatives and seasonal events. · Maintaining campaign schedules, timelines and marketing calendars. · Briefing internal teams to ensure campaigns launch successfully. · Working with media partners, agencies and suppliers to deliver campaigns across digital, print, outdoor and broadcast channels. · Monitoring marketing budgets, invoices and campaign expenditure. · Supporting paid digital advertising campaigns alongside our specialist agency. · Producing marketing reports and analysing campaign performance to maximise return on investment. · Supporting event marketing, market research and wider marketing projects. · Providing day-to-day administrative support to the Marketing and Sales teams. About You: We're looking for someone who is: · Highly organised with excellent attention to detail. · Comfortable managing multiple projects and competing deadlines. · A confident communicator who enjoys working with people across different teams. · You will have minimum of 2-3 years marketing experience. · Experienced in marketing, project coordination, communications and administration. · Confident working with spreadsheets, budgets and reporting data. · Proactive, solutions-focused and able to work independently when required. · Passionate about delivering high-quality work. An interest in conservation, wildlife, visitor attractions or charities would be an advantage, but isn't essential. Why Join Noah's Ark Zoo Farm? Noah's Ark Zoo Farm is more than just a visitor attraction. We're a conservation charity dedicated to connecting people with nature, inspiring future generations and protecting wildlife both here in the UK and around the world. Joining our team means becoming part of an organisation where your work genuinely makes a difference. Every marketing campaign you help deliver supports our mission to educate, conserve and inspire. Working Hours: This is a full-time position working 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday. The role also includes weekend and Bank Holiday cover on a staff rota where required, together with occasional evening work. Time off in lieu will be provided where applicable. Ready to Apply? If you're an organised marketing professional looking for a varied role where no two days are the same, we'd love to hear from you. Join us and help tell the stories that inspire people to visit, support conservation and connect with the natural world. Please send your CV and a covering letter via email to careers@noahsarkzoofarm.co.uk with a subject heading of ‘Marketing Operations Co-ordinator Application’ In your covering letter please describe your relevant experience and how you best match our ‘About you’ criteria. Please note that your application will not be considered without the covering letter. Closing date for applications: 2nd August 2026

title: Drawn-style monoprint workshop
subtitle: Come along and create your own drawn-style monoprint, with artist Jackie Curtis
bodyContent: Date: Tuesday 15th September Time: 10.00am-12.00pm or 1.00pm-3.00pm Cost: £10 suggested donation to support our work, booking is essential. Join artist Jackie Curtis to design and create a drawn-style monoprint. Be inspired by the varied scenery of Steart Marshes and the range of natural materials on offer to use in your work. Learn the process of printing through a demo with Jackie, before being guided to create your own piece. Coated card will be inked up with blue/black oil-based ink. You will then use a range of tools such as twigs, brushes and torn card to make a variety of marks in the ink. Larger areas of ink can be lifted off with cotton buds or gauze to leave lighter areas. Plant material found on site, such as grasses or reeds can be added to give extra depth. A print will then taken from the plate, using a small portable press (Xcut Xpress die cutter), with the possibility of a second fainter ghost print. No previous experience of printing is necessary to take part, this workshop is open to everybody. Please note – participants should be prepared to get inky! This is oil-based inks so wear clothes that can get messy. We advise wearing sturdy boots and dressing for the weather as we will also be working outdoors amongst nature. What to bring: A sketchbook and pens/pencils, if you don't have these we can provide them. Reading glasses if worn. Where to meet: In the main WWT car park at

title: Twilight Tobogganing at Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: ’Tis the season for Twilight Tobogganing! Mendip Activity Centre's most popular event
bodyContent: ’Tis the season for Twilight Tobogganing! Mendip Activity Centre's most popular event of the year returns from 6th November 2026 to 3rd January 2027. This magical one-hour adventure nestled in the Mendip Hills in Somerset - and perfect for families and friends looking to make winter memories together. Race down the slope on a Zibob toboggan, beneath a canopy of over 10,000 sparkling fairy lights, dancing lasers and holiday tunes, and earn your North Pole-approved Toboggan Licence. Then, follow the woodland trail to a hidden grotto. Gather around the campfire to toast marshmallows for s’mores, and enjoy delicious hot chocolate. Finish the evening with festive sparklers and a magical photo opportunity - with mince pies and mulled wine for the adults. Everything is included, with no hidden costs. Twilight Tobogganing a great adventure for everyone aged 4 and over - even teenagers and adults! Private group sessions for up to 8 people are available from £110. Individual spaces for ages 4-12 are from £22 per child. There's free parking onsite, and access to The Alpine Lounge cafe, toilets and changing rooms. Twilight Tobogganing has been running for over 10 years. Its popularity means peak dates always sell out fast, so early booking is strongly encouraged!

title: The Blackdown Hills - land of beauty
subtitle: Where steep lanes dip and twist between the rich fields - Vicky Banham visits the Blackdown Hills
bodyContent: An Englishman, an Irishman and a Scotsman (sounds like the start of an old joke) lived in the three cottages at the base of the Wellington Monument on the edge of the Blackdown Hills, or at least they should have done. According to my trusty source on all things Somerset, the late lamented Robin Bush, the original monument to mark the Duke’s victory at Waterloo was to have been a column topped by a cast-iron statue of the hero with cottages below, occupied by one retired army veteran from each of the three countries as well as 24 cannon from the battle. Alas, funds ran out before the project was completed but what we see today has its own claim to fame. It is the tallest three-sided obelisk in the world at 175 feet. It has been restored recently by its new owners the National Trust and has suitably ‘commanding’ views. One can see points on the Quantocks and Mendips, hills which along with the Blackdowns, hold the fertile Somerset lowlands in a warm embrace. Blackdown Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB) is one of the UK’s smallest, spanning just 15 miles in each direction, yet it is a place that holds many treasures and much fascination. Two thirds of it (and here I will have to whisper) is in Devon so, if you forgive me, I will concentrate on the parts in Somerset – well that is what it says on the magazine cover. The highest point, more than 1000 feet above sea level, is not where the monument stands but a little further east at Staple Hill, looked after by Forestry England. If you take the short all-ability trail from the car park you are rewarded with fantastic views as far as Exmoor on one side and across to Wales. Nearby Castle Neroche is one of my favourite walks with woodland tracks, stunning views and even the remains of an Iron Age Hill Fort. It is from here that the Devil is said to have thrown the large sandstone boulders found by the crossroads in the village of Staple Fitzpaine, its name being derived from the Old English stapol for pillar or post. The second part of the name comes from the Fitzpaine family who owned the manor in the 13 th century. The church, Norman in origin, has one of the splendid Perpendicular towers for which Somerset is famous complete with grotesque carvings known hereabouts as Hunky Punks. If all this makes you feel in need of a drink there is an excellent pub across the road, The Greyhound Inn. Refreshed, we can make our way into the depths of the Blackdowns where it is easy to become lost in one of the steep wooded slopes running down from the wide open, somewhat wild, plateau. Dotted among the verdant valleys are houses of local chert stone, cob and thatch and small fields enclosed by hedges that make up the delightful patchwork so characteristic of this AONB. It was a landscape that inspired several avant-garde painters of the Camden Town Group in the early 20 th century to capture it in the style of Cezanne, Gauguin and Van Gogh. In a recent exhibition, a number of contemporary artists recaptured the same sites around Clayhidon and Ringdown, illustrating graphically how relatively unchanged and unspoiled the Blackdowns are. That makes it all the easier to picture oneself among the pages of Patricia Wendorf’s evocative novel Larksleve, centred on the village of Buckland St Mary a couple of centuries ago. She writes of the Blackdowns in early summer and “how the blackthorn leaned together to make a shade, how the dog-rose climbed and starred the hedges, how the steep lanes dipped and twisted between the rich fields”. A short hop from the village is one of the area’s many nature reserves – Bishopswood Meadows - running down to the River Yarty which, along with the Otter and the Culm, makes up a trio of rivers rising in this lush corner. If it is wildlife you are after, you have come to the right place as the Blackdowns is home to a wide range of species including some real rarities such as dormice and white-clawed crayfish. Other nature hotspots are the tranquil Otterhead Lakes, a former Victorian Estate and the wonderful ancient Thurlbear Wood. One might think the archetypal English Countryside of the Blackdowns was always totally given over to quiet rural pursuits but it has a surprising industrial past. Its geology meant that it was important for iron-working, lime quarrying and mining whetstones that were used for sharpening tools. With these materials less in demand and the war-time intensive farming in the past, the emphasis now is on conserving this rich cultural and natural heritage for future generations.

title: New Woodland play area open at Tyntesfield
subtitle: The project forms part of the National Trust's ongoing investment in enabling children and families to spend more time outdoors and connect with nature.
bodyContent: Families visiting Tyntesfield, near Bristol, can now enjoy a new woodland play area, following a major refurbishment of the popular play trail in the Plantation woods. The improved play area has been designed and built by natural play specialists Earth Wrights. The project forms part of the National Trust's ongoing investment in enabling children and families to spend more time outdoors and connect with nature. The refreshed woodland play trail aims to encourage exploration of the wider estate through active and imaginative outdoor play. The play trail is arranged across three areas inspired by the woodland setting. The Treehouse Area features interconnected platforms linked by ropes, climbing routes and a double-width slide. A play tower with colourful windows and a space beneath for imaginative play creates opportunities for children to explore and create their own adventures. The Nest Area focuses on climbing and balancing, with log features, a climbing net and play structures designed to encourage confidence and physical activity. The Forest Explorers Area combines active play with quieter spaces, including raised decks, nets, woodland-inspired play features and areas for children to gather, explore and spend time outdoors. Edd Morgan, Facilities Manager at Tyntesfield, said: "The woodland play area is easily one of our most popular spots, so getting it back open with a fresh, updated design is a great result. This much-loved space now has a play offer that encourages adventure, imagination and exploration in nature. “Working with Earth Wrights has allowed us to create something that is rooted in the character of Tyntesfield while introducing some dynamic new features for kids to explore. It’s a durable, engaging space built for proper outdoor play, and we're looking forward to seeing families back out there using it" Built predominantly from natural materials, the new play structures have been designed to sit within the woodland landscape while providing opportunities for adventure, creativity and social play. Normal admission applies. For opening times and admission information please visit nationaltrust.org.uk/Tyntesfield .

title: Prezzo Clarks Village Review
subtitle: Located in the heart of Clarks Village, Prezzo offers far more than a convenient dining stop during a shopping trip.
bodyContent: Located in the heart of Clarks Village, Prezzo offers far more than a convenient dining stop during a shopping trip. Combining authentic Italian flavours with exceptional customer service, it's a restaurant that manages to create a memorable experience from the moment you walk through the door. On a busy evening visit, the restaurant was buzzing with joyful energy. Tables were filled with families, couples and groups of friends, creating a vibrant atmosphere without ever feeling rushed or overwhelming. Despite the restaurant being busy, the team remained attentive and professional throughout, ensuring guests felt relaxed and well looked after. A special mention must go to Lucy and the restaurant manager (Fabio), who helped make the experience particularly enjoyable. Their warm welcome, genuine enthusiasm and attention to detail stood out from the start. Service was friendly without being intrusive, and every member of staff seemed committed to ensuring guests enjoyed their visit. For the main course, I opted for the popular Marry Me Chicken Pasta, a dish that certainly lived up to its reputation. Rich, creamy and packed with flavour, the pasta delivered the kind of comforting Italian cooking that keeps diners coming back for more. The balance of ingredients was spot on, with every bite offering authentic flavours that felt both indulgent and satisfying. To finish, I chose the Affogato, a classic Italian dessert combining creamy vanilla ice cream with freshly poured espresso. Simple in concept but beautifully executed, it provided the perfect ending to the meal. The contrast between the hot coffee and cold ice cream created a delicious balance that was both refreshing and indulgent. One of the most impressive aspects of the experience was the quality of the food. Fresh ingredients and authentic Italian flavours were evident throughout, with dishes presented beautifully and prepared with care. It's clear that Prezzo takes pride in delivering consistency and quality across its menu. The restaurant also offers excellent value for money, particularly through its various deals and promotions. Given the quality of the food, generous portions and outstanding level of service, diners are likely to leave feeling they've received a great experience at a reasonable price. Whether you're looking for a romantic date night, celebrating a birthday with friends and family, or simply taking a break from a day of shopping at Clarks Village, Prezzo comfortably caters to all occasions. In a competitive dining market, it's often the little things that set a restaurant apart. At Prezzo Clarks Village, it's the combination of authentic Italian cuisine, outstanding hospitality and a welcoming atmosphere that makes the difference. From the excellent service provided by Meg, Lucy, Freya and Samuel & Fabio, to the flavour-packed dishes coming from the kitchen, every aspect of the visit exceeded expectations. It's a restaurant I would happily recommend and one that I look forward to visiting again. Clarks Village sunset shopping Clarks Village has transformed into the ultimate evening destination with extended opening hours for shopping and dining – plus free evening parking. Guests will now have more time to explore the Somerset shopping outlet, with brands opening an extra hour daily – and an extra two hours every Thursday – as well as vibrant late-night restaurants. To make evening visits even more seamless, free parking is also available at Clarks Village after 6pm. With a stunning outdoor setting including landscaped gardens and wide paved malls, Clarks Village is located in Street in the heart of Somerset and is home to more than 90 brands offering up to 60% off RRP, from designer names to high street favourites alongside delicious dining destinations. The new extended opening hours sees Clarks Village’s retail brands open from 9am-7pm on Monday to Saturdays, open an extra hour until 8pm on Thursdays. Sunday hours are from 10am-5pm. For evening dining, Clarks Village’s restaurants stay open until at least 9pm – opening as late as 10pm on weekdays and 11pm at weekends*. The extended opening hours comes as the outlet continues to grow and enhance its coveted line-up. Recent arrivals include iconic shoe brand Crocs and heritage homeware brand Christy, joining premium names such as Levi’s, Mint Velvet, Tommy Hilfiger, Sweaty Betty, Calvin Klein, Rituals and the largest Clarks shoe store in the world. Guests can also look forward to visiting the newly revamped Dune London shoe store and lifestyle brand Joules, which reopens later this month following a refurbishment. Offering indoor and alfresco dining, Clarks Village’s late-night restaurants include Wagamama, Bill’s, Pizza Express and the newly reimagined Prezzo Italian, as well as quick-service outlet Slim Chickens. title: Little Witches, Wizards and Monsters invited to meet the Witch of Wookey Hole and win a year of magical adventures this Halloween
subtitle: Running from 3 October to 1 November 2026, the attraction's Home of Halloween event transforms the famous caves and attractions into a spellbinding world of pumpkins, monsters, magic and family fun.
bodyContent: Families who visit Wookey Hole in Halloween costume this October could win a year-long membership as part of a magical daily prize draw. Children (and their grown-ups) are being encouraged to dust off their capes, polish their broomsticks and embrace their spooky side as Wookey Hole launches its biggest Halloween celebration yet, complete with a daily membership giveaway, immersive cave adventures and a chance to meet the legendary Witch of Wookey Hole herself. Running from 3 October to 1 November 2026 , the attraction's Home of Halloween event transforms the famous caves and attractions into a spellbinding world of pumpkins, monsters, magic and family fun. As part of this year’s spellbinding celebrations, every guest who arrives in fancy dress and snaps a photo with the Witch of Wookey Hole, they will be entered into a daily prize draw for the chance to win a year’s Wookey Hole Membership. The lucky winner will unlock unlimited adventures at Wookey Hole all year long, including access to the attraction’s magical new Winter Wonderland Christmas experience. The Halloween adventure begins deep underground, where visitors can journey through the famous Wookey Hole Caves and experience spectacular immersive projections that bring the legendary story of the Witch of Wookey Hole to life among the ancient rock formations. Above ground, families can follow a mysterious pumpkin trail hidden throughout the caves, solving clues and cracking the Witch's puzzle to claim a Halloween prize. Adding to the excitement is the all-new Monster's Ball Circus Extravaganza , where vampires, monsters and mischievous creatures take over the Wookey Hole Circus in a laugh-out-loud family show packed with acrobatics, stunts and Halloween surprises. Visitors can also enjoy Halloween-themed Monster Golf, a spooky 4D film, giant indoor soft play and dozens of additional attractions included within standard admission. Kelly Ballard, Head of Marketing at Wookey Hole, said: “ Halloween is a big favourite for our team and regular visitors to Wookey. We already have a legendary witch, ancient caves and a magical atmosphere, so October is one of the most exciting times of year to visit. This year, those who dress in their finest Halloween costumes and get their photo taken with the Witch are in with the chance to win a whole year of magical adventures at Wookey Hole. We love the atmosphere at Wookey when everyone dresses up and the children love it!” Halloween activities run every weekend from 3 October , before taking place daily throughout the school holidays from 24 October to 1 November . With cave adventures, pumpkin hunts, circus performances, family attractions and fancy-dress fun all included in the ticket price, Wookey Hole is once again set to become one of the South West's most magical Halloween destinations. Halloween at Wookey Hole 2026 Highlights: Meet the legendary Witch of Wookey Hole Daily fancy dress prize draw to win a year's membership Spectacular immersive cave projections Halloween pumpkin trail and puzzle challenge Monster's Ball Circus Extravaganza Halloween-themed Monster Golf Family-friendly 4D cinema experience Giant indoor soft play Full access to Wookey Hole's attractions and experiences Event Information When: 3 October to 1 November 2026 Daily Halloween activities: 24 October to 1 November Where: Wookey Hole, near Wells, Somerset For more information and tickets, visit https://ddec1-0-en-ctp.trendmicro.com:443/wis/clicktime/v1/query?url=www.wookey.co.uk%2fhalloween&umid=59ece326-e5d4-46db-bfdc-0d5022c0e799&rct=1788448735&auth=99011a216bb79adc5bac64261fe8280d56507cac-ecf2f564ec6eb9a26b79a7c90385d2b33caca782

title: Blorenge House
subtitle: Blorenge House offers delightful town centre accommodation in the heart of Somerset's county town: Taunton. Located within a short walk from the town centre, the residence is also close walk to Taunton railway station, and Somerset County Cricket Club.
bodyContent: Blorenge House offers a home away from home setting with luxury amenities, best-in-class accommodations, and an attention to detail which will ensure you enjoy a comfortable stay, whilst also getting great value for money. Here at Blorenge House, guest satisfaction is our utmost priority; so if you are looking for a long weekend getaway, or if you are looking for longer term accommodation or an extended stay, the self-catering two-bedroom apartments at Blorenge House are your best bet for finding the ideal setting for comfort and luxury during your time in Taunton. Our individually styled apartments are the perfect place to unwind and relax during your time in Taunton. The apartments include one Double Room with a superkingsize bed to ensure you enjoy a comfortable night's sleep, and one Twin Room with two 3ft single beds included. The Blorenge House apartments offer accommodation of style and distinction that will suit the needs of the discerning guest, so whether you are travelling for work, or you are heading to Taunton with the family, Blorenge House offers top quality accommodation at good value for money. The apartments at Blorenge House include a spacious, open plan area with a living room and fully equipped kitchen. A large bathroom with a bath and walk-in shower is also included. Operating on a 2 night minimum stay, your apartment includes everything to help you settle in seemlessly. Your apartment will ensure you feel home away from home, whether you are spending some quality time with your family, or if you are looking to unwind after a long day at work, the apartments at Blorenge House are a great space to call your own. Please note: Visit Taunton cannot accept any responsibility for matters arising between a customer and the accommodation provider. Visit Taunton does not accept liability for information on third party websites. This is not an exhaustive list.
tagline: Blorenge House offers delightful town centre accommodation in the heart of Somerset's county town.

title: The Paragon Townhouse
subtitle: The Paragon is a wondrously quirky Georgian Townhouse located in the bustling heart of historic Bath.
bodyContent: Arching over the ancient steps that lead from Roman Road down to Bath’s Artisan Quarter and Walcot Street, this listed building has been described as “like a Landmark Trust house but more beautiful.” Packed full of original features the house sleeps 8 in four double bedrooms and is spread over a total of 6 floors. Up to 2 extras sleep in comfortable day beds in the larger rooms. Awarded a special Gold by VisitBritain for 2018 / 19 and with the kitchen in the original vaults below street level you could not find a more original or characterful property for your special stay in Bath.
tagline: The Paragon is a wondrously quirky Georgian Townhouse

title: The Spa at Middlewick
subtitle: Nestled within our 16-acre converted farmstead, Middlewick Spa, Glastonbury may be the quirkiest Spa in Somerset.
bodyContent: Nestled at the back of our property within sight of the iconic Glastonbury Tor, Middlewick Spa is the perfect location to indulge in a treatment, use our pool and sauna, and treat yourself to delicious food and drink. Our Spa is a little different to others you might have visited. Our focus is your holistic wellbeing and the nourishment of your mind, body and soul. Experience an organic facial, rejuvenating massage or holistic beauty treatment. You can also book Spa packages – from a full Spa Day to a Swim, Sauna and Lunch. Begin your Middlewick moment in our Spa Lounge, where you can unwind with a complimentary herbal tea. Treatments take place in our quirky shepherd’s hut treatment rooms. All our airy spaces, from the Spa Lounge to the outdoor sauna, provide views of rolling hills and blue skies and are designed to connect you with nature. Hungry? Choose your breakfast, lunch or sweet treat and we’ll whip it up in our award-winning Café kitchen and deliver it to you in the Spa Lounge. We can also cater for special occasions – and our onsite Accommodation makes The Middlewick the perfect venue for Spa weekends and retreats.

title: Beeches Farmhouse Ensuite Rooms
subtitle: Farmyard accommodation in Bradford on Avon near Bath, has double / twin and family en-suite rooms and all, except one, in detached converted farm buildings.
bodyContent: Farmyard accommodation in Bradford on Avon near Bath, has double / twin and family en-suite rooms and all, except one, in detached converted farm buildings, each having their own front door key and own patio area, giving you the independence to come and go as you please. All rooms have full en-suite facilities including bath and/or shower and are decorated to a very high standard with exposed beams, stripped wooden floors and country pine furnishings. During busy periods there is usually a minimum stay of two nights at weekends unless ‘last minute’. These rooms can be used with our self catering cottages for additional bedrooms. We also offer self catering cottages “Beeches Farmhouse Cottages”. Find out more>>

title: Flow Bar Frome
subtitle: At the heart of Frome. A place to meet, mixing character, service and independent spirit. Occasional local food offerings and live music.
bodyContent: Flow Bar Frome is in a beautifully renovated Georgian building with contemporary styling, offering two floors of sophisticated bar space on a medieval bridge with views overlooking the river Frome near Bath. Enjoy a seasonal cocktail list using local garnishes and ingredients, local cider, gin and their own Flow Pale Ale, available to drink-in or takeaway. They also collaborate with independent local businesses, providing food offerings such as Tacos and Sharing Platters on certain days. See live and acoustic sets from local DJs and singer/songwriters, as well as specially curated events throughout the year, showcasing the best drinks, food and entertainment that Frome and Somerset have to offer.
tagline: At the heart of Frome. A place to meet, mixing character, service and independent spirit.

title: Photo Tours in Bath
subtitle: Photo Tours in Bath are led by photographer and historian Simon Mark who has lived in central Bath for 30 years.
bodyContent: The walking tours are designed to enable you to learn a little of Bath's fascinating history and also to capture some outstanding photos of Britain's most camera-friendly city. You don't need a very expensive camera to produce astonishing photographs and everyone - whether you use a phone camera or a Leica - is welcome. You will be shown great viewpoints and unique angles so that you will have fantastic photographs of your visit to Bath. Alternative options include Film & TV, Georgian Bath, Jane Austen, Twilight, and Bridgerton themed photo tours. Everything will be done at your pace and with a tour group size of your choosing. Find out more here: https://visitbath.co.uk/things-to-do/photo-tours-in-bath-p2143113

title: Invest Somerset
subtitle: What makes Somerset so special about relocating your business here?
bodyContent: Somerset is known for its natural beauty, a place to visit for recreation and inspiration, surrounded by history, landscape, agricultural heritage and market towns. Visitors from all parts of the U.K. and overseas benefit from its easy access and connectivity, the contrast between coast and countryside and year-round experiences from which to take memories home. Within this scene, are vibrant communities for living and business. Somerset is a place of creativity and innovation, a place of work ethic and collaboration and a place to energise our greatest asset, people. It is connections such as these that stimulate some visitors to consider relocating their own business here - taking advantage of all of these attributes, unlocking hidden benefits both professionally and personally. Invest Somerset is here to help you take such initial thoughts on a considered and durable progression, outlining support, opportunities and connections to change both your business and your life. Take a look at this short video with Jim Winchester of Electrified Automation in historic Bridgwater and learn why locating a business here brings such fulfilment - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GIaeIowg8mU Gavin Eddy of Forward Space explains why he chose Somerset to grow his dynamic company here - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U2F0QJvNsjE Make contact for an informal discussion by visiting www.investsomerset.co.uk and following on Linkedin - https://www.linkedin.com/company/invest-somerset/

title: Diamond Farm Holiday Park
subtitle: Diamond Farm Holiday Park in Brean, Somerset is on our family working farm.
bodyContent: Diamond Farm Holiday Park is situated on our 100-acre family working farm, ideally situated for the quiet family holiday, and it is only 3⁄4 mile from the 7 miles of sandy beach at Brean. On our site, you will find level and generous-sized pitches with car parking spaces alongside your caravan or tent. Countryside views are assured, and each pitch is within a short distance of the site facilities. All modern facilities including toilets, showers, electric hook-up, play area, shop, café, wifi and laundry. River fishing on site. Holiday cottages are also for hire.
tagline: Diamond Farm Holiday Park in Brean, Somerset is on our family working farm.

title: The Ilchester Arms Hotel
subtitle: Experience luxury at Somerset Hotel! Unwind in 15 lavish bedrooms, savour exquisite cuisine, and enjoy exclusive dining, vibrant lounge areas, and trendy bars. Relax, entertain, or unwind - we've got you covered for an unforgettable stay!
bodyContent: Located in the heart of Ilchester, Somerset, this family-run hotel boasts 15 en-suite bedrooms, including Superking/Twin, Family rooms with Toddler Bunk Beds, Ground Floor, and Double rooms. The property features a charming Lounge, Garden, two function rooms, Bar, and Restaurant, serving classic British cuisine using locally sourced ingredients for lunch and dinner. The hotel's character is enhanced by traditional windows, beams, and nautical ornaments, paying homage to Ilchester's Fleet Air Arms and Navy Base in nearby Yeovilton. Our extensive beverage selection includes an impressive wine collection from Liberty Wines, West Country ciders, and Coastal Real Ales, ensuring something for every palate. Book direct with us and enjoy a complimentary full English breakfast, featuring freshly squeezed orange juice, unlimited tea and coffee, and locally sourced ingredients, including premium bacon and sausages, as well as freshly baked bread from the nearby bakery on the A303.

title: Collie Shepherd Huts
subtitle: Collie Shepherd Hut is a peaceful countryside retreat in Somerset, offering a cosy and romantic escape for two. Enjoy a private wood-fired hot tub, stunning views across the Somerset Levels and thoughtful touches throughout. Perfect for relaxing breaks, stargazing nights and unwinding in comfort close to nature and local attractions.
bodyContent: Collie Shepherd Hut is an exclusive countryside retreat in Somerset, designed for couples seeking a luxurious and intimate escape. Set in a peaceful rural location with uninterrupted views across the Somerset Levels, it offers a restorative setting where guests can slow down, unwind and reconnect with nature. Beautifully styled throughout, the hut blends rustic charm with elevated comfort. The king-size bed sits within a cosy alcove, dressed in quality linens for a restful night’s sleep. A well-equipped kitchenette includes a microwave oven, double-ring gas hob, fridge with top freezer compartment and essentials for simple self-catering. Guests are welcomed with a complimentary breakfast pack, adding a thoughtful and indulgent start to their stay. The ensuite shower room with flushing toilet, along with fluffy bathrobes, slippers and towels — including an additional set for the hot tub — adds further comfort. Outside, your private wood-fired hot tub with jacuzzi spa jets awaits, perfectly positioned for slow evenings spent watching Somerset’s glowing sunsets fade into star-filled skies. Firewood and everything needed for your stay are provided, ensuring a seamless and relaxing experience from the moment you arrive. Ideal for romantic getaways, anniversaries and special occasions, Collie Shepherd Hut offers privacy, calm and complete escape from everyday life. Surrounded by Somerset’s natural beauty, the hut sits beside a working farm, offering an authentic and peaceful countryside setting where guests can enjoy scenic walks, explore charming nearby villages or simply relax in total seclusion. A refined rural retreat where luxury, romance and nature come together effortlessly.

title: Shetland View Shepherd Hut
subtitle: Shetland View is a luxurious Somerset shepherd’s hut for two, offering spacious interiors, sweeping views of the Somerset Levels and refined finishes. Enjoy a private wood-fired hot tub with jacuzzi spa jets, peaceful surroundings, evening sunsets, stargazing nights and slow, relaxing mornings while exploring nature, scenic walks and nearby attractions.
bodyContent: Shetland View is a luxurious countryside hideaway created for couples who want to slow down, reconnect and savour uninterrupted time together. Overlooking the sweeping Somerset Levels, this beautifully designed shepherd’s hut offers complete tranquillity, soft light and a sense of space that instantly soothes the soul. Inside, warm textures and elegant simplicity set the tone for relaxation. The unique pull-down king-size bed invites long, lazy mornings, while underfloor heating and a glowing wood burner create a cosy, intimate atmosphere. The well-equipped kitchenette includes a combi oven, fridge with freezer compartment and everything needed for effortless self-catering, complemented by a thoughtful welcome breakfast pack. The modern ensuite features a heated towel rail, flushing toilet, fluffy bathrobes, slippers and soft towels, with an additional set provided for the hot tub. Step outside to your private garden, where a wood-fired hot tub with jacuzzi spa jets waits beneath open skies. As sunsets melt into starlight, couples can sink into the warm, bubbling water, share quiet conversations and enjoy moments that feel both indulgent and deeply peaceful. A fire pit and BBQ offer more ways to unwind, with complimentary logs provided throughout your stay. Surrounded by nature, the gentle presence of miniature Shetland ponies and set beside a working farm, Shetland View is a romantic retreat where time slows, connection deepens and every detail feels thoughtfully designed for couples seeking calm, luxury and unforgettable moments together.

title: Meet Father Christmas at Dunster Castle
subtitle: Share your Christmas wishes with Father Christmas before he heads off on his trip around the world.
bodyContent: Step into the cosy castle where Father Christmas is getting ready for his trip around the world. Settle into the festive atmosphere, share Christmas wishes and receive a gift to take home with you. Your child's ticket includes meeting Father Christmas, and a present. Admission to Dunster Castle & Gardens is not included in this ticket. If you are not a National Trust member, you will need to purchase an admission ticket for each adult & child in Visitor Reception when you arrive-admission tickets cannot be booked in advance, and must be purchased on the day. National Trust members and Children under 5 go free. Please note that pricing for the Father Christmas Experience is £10 per child and time slots are exclusive to the booker. Up to 4 accompanying adults can attend per time slot. Please arrive at Visitor Reception 20 minutes before your slot. Allow 10 minutes to walk between Visitor Reception and Father Christmas' Grotto inside the castle.

title: Deep Time Walk at Steart Marshes
subtitle: Experience Steart Marshes from 250 million years ago, through to the present day and on to 1000 years into the future.
bodyContent: Date: Sunday 4th October Time: 10.00am-11.30am, 12.30pm-2.00pm, 3.00pm-4.30pm Cost: Free event, booking is essential. The Steart Marshes Deep Time Walk is a soundart walk across the Steart landscape led by Ralph Hoyte. We will start at Steart Marshes 250 million years ago, trundling through to the present and marching on at least 1000 years into the future. We will walk as a group, experiencing the soundart through a GPS-triggered autonomous speaker unit. At the conclusion you will be able to download the walk to your personal smartphone to enjoy again at leisure or to share with friends and family. Note: this is an authentically-based work of soundart inspired by Steart Marshes, not a natural-historical-geological guide. You do not need to bring any headphones etc. If you bring your smartphone you will be able to download the soundart to your smartphone on the spot (signal permitting); information on how to do this later at home will be provided. This workshop is suitable for all ages. Please note – we will be walking around the nature reserve, so dress accordingly, sturdy shoes are recommended. Where to meet: In the main WWT car park at Steart Marshes, Stert Drove, Bridgwater, Somerset, TA5 2PU. Book tickets here: https://www.wwt.org.uk/wetland-centres/steart-marshes/whats-on/events/deep-time-walk-at-steart-marshes
