title: Milk from the Moors
subtitle: The joys of buying fresh milk straight from the farm - by Richard Walsh
bodyContent: Many readers of this magazine will remember the days when every town and many villages had their own bakery, butchers and virtually all had their own milkman who delivered milk that had been produced by the local herd of dairy cows that very morning. In the course of time many of these aspects of life have disappeared - in the name of progress, or so we are told. However, the need to diversify and produce additional income streams in recent years has resulted in the return of locally sourced fresh milk - just the way it used to be. I refer of course to the milk vending machines that are appearing on the roadside in a number of places across the county - and doesn’t the fresh milk that is dispensed from them enhance the taste of your morning cereal or porridge and the custard that it makes is just so much better. I have to confess to being a long time convert to buying milk from these roadside vending machines and to that end I keep a couple of litre sized glass bottles in the car boot ready to be filled when I next pass a machine. Delicious milk shakes are also available for those who prefer flavoured milk and on many of the occasions that I have called in for a fill up there is a family selecting their favourite flavour of milk shake. The vending machine that I most frequently use is located at West Lyng alongside the A361 outside of Stagg Farm, where the herd of cows who produce the milk are sometimes to be seen causing a brief delay to the traffic, as they make their way from the fields to the milking parlour which is situated close by. The vending facility at Stagg Farm is just one of the various locations where Milk from the Moor is available and another that is very popular is located in Clarks Village at Street. Milk from the Moors is the brainchild of Fowlers Plot Farm at Chedzoy who back in early 2019 looked into ways of selling their milk direct to the public in order to try to cut out the middle man, increasing the amount they were paid for their product. Then when Coronavirus came along the reduction in demand from the hospitality sector meant that they had to throw some of their milk away, and it was this that led them investing in a milk vending machine to sell direct to the public. From this beginning Milk from the Moors has grown and there are several outlets around the area. So why is it that Milk from the Moors tastes so much better than what is bought from the supermarkets? It is not heavily processed and is gently pasteurised to kill any bacteria and non-homogenised so the cream rises to the top just like it should do, and always used to! Quite apart from the taste, the milk is fresh from the cows on a daily basis, there are zero food miles and coming from just one source is completely traceable. In addition, the milk is sold in reusable glass bottles so no recycling issues. In addition to Milk from the Moors there are a number of other dairy farmers who are selling their produce direct to the public from vending machines all across Somerset so why not find out where your nearest is and start to use it.

title: Ibiza comes to Somerset at the Grand Pier
subtitle: Legendary Bora Bora Music world tour takes over the Grand Pier this August.
bodyContent: This August, the true, unfiltered spirit of Ibiza is landing a quarter of a mile out to sea. The globally renowned Bora Bora Music World Tour is bringing an exclusive, open-air sunset terrace experience to Weston-super-Mare’s iconic Grand Pier on Saturday, 22nd August. For one night only, electronic music fans will experience a five-hour sun-downer session headlined by none other than Bora Bora founder and Ibiza pioneer, Gee Moore, performing an epic, extended three-hour set of timeless Ibiza classics. Born on the sun-drenched sands of Playa d’en Bossa, Bora Bora revolutionised daytime clubbing, becoming one of the most influential brands in dance music history. Synonymous with marathon sets, open-air freedom, and an electric connection between the DJ and the crowd, the legendary beach club culture is being reimagined for Somerset beneath open skies. As day turns to night, the event promises breathtaking golden-hour views over the Bristol Channel, paired with a world-class soundtrack spanning multiple stages: The Outdoor Terrace (Bora Bora Music): Ibiza Classics from 19:00 to Midnight, featuring Gee Moore (3-Hour Extended Set) with support from Nick Coles and Mr Christian. Stage Two (Boom Room): Upfront House and Tech Music from Heratiks, Afternoon Tea, Enygma, Hex, and Sugarshaker. The Official After-Party (CrashThe90s): The energy continues indoors from Midnight until 3:00 AM with pure 90s classics from Joe 'Freeze' Taylor, Danny Manning, and Scott Carey. Organiser Nick Coles of CrashThe90s says: "We are absolutely thrilled to bring this iconic Ibiza concept to Weston-super-Mare. Whether you lived through the original Ibiza terrace days or are discovering that Balearic magic for the very first time, this open-air setting on the Grand Pier is going to be something truly unforgettable." Tickets are strictly limited and available now for £20 (plus booking fee) via Skiddle. Event Summary: Event: Bora Bora Music presents Ibiza Classics Date: Saturday, 22nd August Time: 19:00 – 03:00 Venue: The Grand Pier, Marine Parade, Weston-super-Mare, BS23 1AL Tickets: £20 + BF available via Skiddle

title: Fun and Games exhibition brings local memories to life at The Bishop’s Palace
subtitle: For generations of local people, the Palace, gardens and moat have provided the backdrop to celebrations, events, family days out and memorable moments.
bodyContent: F rom moat boat races and community celebrations to family days out and treasured personal memories, a new exhibition at The Bishop’s Palace in Wells is celebrating the fun, laughter and shared experiences that have connected local people with the Palace over the years. Fun and Games at the Palace , running from 24 July to 13 September in the Conference Room at The Bishop’s Palace, brings together photographs, memorabilia and stories contributed by members of the local community. Rather than telling the story of the Palace solely through dates and historic events, the exhibition explores something much more personal: the memories made by the people who have spent time here. For generations of local people, the Palace, gardens and moat have provided the backdrop to celebrations, events, family days out and memorable moments. Fun and Games at the Palace brings some of those stories together and invites visitors to share their own. Community Engagement Manager Siobhan Goodwin said: “We know the Palace holds a special place in so many people’s hearts. This exhibition is all about celebrating those shared experiences; the laughter, the creativity and the sense of community that has always been part of this place. “What makes it particularly special is that local people have helped us tell the story. Their photographs, memorabilia and memories show that the Palace isn't simply somewhere people come to visit. It is somewhere people form connections with, return to and remember.” Visitors to the exhibition will also have the opportunity to contribute to the Palace’s growing collection of memories. During the exhibition, oral history volunteers will be recording people’s recollections, helping to capture personal stories that might otherwise be lost. Siobhan added: “We’d love people to come along, enjoy the exhibition and perhaps find themselves saying, ‘I remember that!’ We also want to hear the stories that aren't yet part of the exhibition. Those individual memories all help us build a richer picture of what the Palace has meant to the community over the years.” The exhibition has been made possible by a grant awarded by Museum Development South West , with thanks to support from Arts Council England . Fun and Games at the Palace runs from 24 July to 13 September 2026 in the Conference Room at The Bishop’s Palace , Wells. The exhibition is included with standard admission to The Bishop’s Palace.

title: Escape into autumn with National Trust events in Somerset
subtitle: There’s lots on offer this season, from toddler storytelling sessions to guided tours, and craft workshops to Heritage Open Days.
bodyContent: Across Somerset, National Trust places are full of warmth as the trees slowly turn to red, orange and gold. Enjoy crisp walks with family and friends and steaming mugs of hot chocolate. There’s lots on offer this season, from toddler storytelling sessions to guided tours, and craft workshops to Heritage Open Days. What’s more, every time you experience a National Trust day out, you help care for these special places for future generations. Here is what’s happening near you this autumn, please check property website for opening days and times: Barrington Court https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset/barrington-court Heritage Open Days 2026: Free entry to Barrington Court 14-18 September. 10am-5pm Enjoy free entry to Barrington Court's beautiful garden & historic orchards, farm buildings, avenues and the ground floor of Strode House, where you can imagine what it was like as the Lyle's 1920s family home. Price: Free event. Booking not required. Wild Creatures Hide & Seek Trail (October Half Term) 24 October-1 November. 10am-4pm Grab your wellies and explore the grounds to find fifteen wild creatures hiding around the estate. How many will you spot? Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Wild Woodwork: Drop-in wood crafting workshops (October Half Term) 26-30 October. 10am-4pm Grab some gloves, get hands on with tools and create your own piece of natural art to take home, made of timber gathered from the estate and inspired by some of the wild creatures who roam the Somerset countryside at and around Barrington Court. Price: Check website for event price (normal admission applies). Booking not required. Remarkable Rangers: Apple Harvest Days (October Half Term) 26-30 October. 11am-3pm After last year's bumper crop, the Ranger team are waiting to see what this year's harvest will be like. Dates may be subject to change, so visit the website for further information. Our orchards are home to well over 100 varieties of apples and once collected, they will go off to be turned into delicious cider. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Remarkable Rangers: Ranger Danger (October Half Term) 27 October. 11am-3pm Join the Ranger team for day of woodcraft in the Cricket Pitch woods. Learn how to make fire without matches and toast some yummy marshmallows. (Activity weather dependent and subject to change.) Price: £1 per child (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Coleridge Cottage https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset/coleridge-cottage Romantic Women Tour Every Wednesday, September-October. 12noon-1pm Join one of our volunteer tour guides and discover how the women in Samuel Taylor Coleridge’s life shaped his experiences and inspired his writing. Moving through the rooms of Coleridge Cottage, the tour brings hidden stories to light, including the resilience and resourcefulness of his wife Sara Fricker as well as his creative and intellectual friendship with Dorothy Wordsworth. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Nether Stowey Village Walk | Walks Programme Every Sunday of September. 1-2pm Meet at Coleridge Cottage and set off on this beginner walk around the charming village of Nether Stowey. From the home of Samuel Taylor Coleridge to St Mary's Church and a trip up to Castle Mount, this walk is the perfect introduction to Coleridge and the village that shaped his work. Price: Free event. Booking required. Stowey Surrounds | Walks Programme 10 September. 11am-2pm Connect with the landscape that inspired Coleridge's poetry and explore a landscape mix including close encounters with woodland and streams as well as open fields and vast panoramas with one our walk leaders. Price: Free event. Booking required. Wordsworth’s home to Coleridge Cottage| Walks Programme 30 September. 9.45am-2pm Join our walk leaders on a ramble between Kilve, Alfoxton and Nether Stowey. Take in the vast panoramic view, spot wildlife and connect with nature like Coleridge once did on his walk on the hills with his friends. Along the way, see where the Wordsworth’s lived during their time in the area and discover the path, they took on their way to Coleridge Cottage. Price: Free event. Booking required. Poetry Reading in the Garden Room 2 September-28 October (check websites for dates). 1-2pm Join Michael Bloom for a captivating reading of excerpts from some of Samuel Taylor Coleridge's best-loved poems, in the very cottage where many of them were first penned. Discover the stories, ideas and landscapes that inspired one of Britain's greatest Romantic poets as his words are brought to life in an intimate and atmospheric setting. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Somerset Arts Week: Exhibition by local artist Laura Daligan 23 September- 4 October. 11am-4pm As part of this year's Somerset Arts Week, local artist Laura Daligan will exhibit her work at Coleridge Cottage. Exploring the theme of 'Cultural Connections', this exhibition explores the artists' deep relationship with the Quantock Hills. Price: Free event. Booking not required. Dunster Castle https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset/dunster-castle-and-watermill Gilded Treasures Exhibition: 50 Years of the National Trust at Dunster Castle 1 September – 2 November. 10am-3.45pm Displayed throughout the castle, the exhibition highlights items featuring gilded decoration and golden detail. Alongside these objects, uncover the story of how Dunster Castle was generously gifted to the National Trust in 1976 by Lt. Col. Walter Luttrell, which included the estate and thirty acres of surrounding parkland. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Victorian Kitchen Tours (weekdays) Thursday & Fridays, September-October. Check website for timings. Where meals were made, stories were shared and servants kept the castle running. Head to the once state-of-the-art Victorian Kitchen with one of our knowledgeable tour guides and discover the heart of Victorian life at Dunster Castle. Price: £3pp (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Victorian Kitchen Tours (weekends) Every Saturday, September & October. 11am-12noon & 12noon-1pm Where meals were made, stories were shared and servants kept the castle running. Head to the once state-of-the-art Victorian Kitchen with one of our knowledgeable tour guides and discover the heart of Victorian life at Dunster Castle. Price: £3pp (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Behind-the-Ropes Tours (weekends) Every Saturday & Sunday, September – 1 November. Check website for timings. Embark on a new route, explore repurposed spaces and discover their history, all with the help of one of our brilliant volunteer guides. Venture into new areas from the butler's bedroom to the infamous 'creepy corridor', discover fascinating finds and gain an insight into the areas that allow us to do what we do. Price: £3pp (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Behind-the-Ropes Tours Every Monday, September-October. Check websites for times. Embark on a new route, explore repurposed spaces and discover their history, all with the help of one of our brilliant volunteer guides. Venture into new areas from the butler's bedroom to the infamous 'creepy corridor', discover fascinating finds and gain an insight into the areas that allow us to do what we do. Price: £3pp (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Attic Tours (Weekends) Every Sunday, September – 1 November. 1.30-2.30pm & 2.30-3.30pm Discover hidden spaces, explore tucked‑away rooms and corridors, and learn about the daily lives of the servants who once called these upstairs spaces home. Price: £3pp (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Exmoor Dark Skies: Stargazing Evening 21 October. 7-10pm Enjoy an evening of stargazing activities using telescopic equipment, laser guided star mapping, constellation story telling and much more. Wet weather options will include VR headsets and a mobile planetarium. Price: £25pp (normal admissions apply). Booking required. Hydrangea Masterclass at Dunster Castle 8 & 30 September. 10am-12noon Discover the diversity of hydrangeas and learn practical tips on cultivation, propagation and pruning groups. A relaxed session for anyone looking to get more from these garden favourites. Price: £35pp. Booking required. Dunster Castle Experience Days - A Day with the Head Gardener 23 September. 10.30am-3.30pm An exclusive chance to spend the day with Dunster Castle's Head Gardener, including a bespoke tour, and a two-course lunch. Price: £65pp. Booking required. Ghost Tours 2026 28 & 31 October. Check website for times. Step into the shadows and discover the darker side of Dunster Castle. Venture through the castle's most haunted spaces, hearing tales of ghostly sightings and mysterious happenings. Expect chills, thrills and a few scares along the way. Price: £25pp. Booking required. Fyne Court https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset/fyne-court Toddler Tuesdays Tuesdays through September & October (term time only). 10-11.30am Suitable for under 5s and their carers, the session is an opportunity to connect with nature through play, crafts, stories and gentle walks. The walks are pushchair friendly and designed with little feet in mind. Price: £2 per child. Booking required. Lytes Cary Manor https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset/lytes-cary-manor West wing open days 2 & 3 September 11am-4pm last entry 3.30pm The West Wing of Lytes Cary Manor will be open to visitors. Take the opportunity to walk around the well-preserved, extravagant house, with its dark wood-panelled walls, fine period furnishings and grand bedrooms. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Monthly Markets at Lytes Cary Manor 12 & 13 September, 10 & 11 October. 10am-4pm Held in the historic barns and courtyard areas. The Lytes Cary market showcases a variety of products that have been crafted by local artists. Price: Free event (normal admission applies to visit the house, garden & tea-room). Booking not required. Guided Group Walk Every Wednesday, September – 21 October. 11am-12.30pm Join walk leaders to explore the Lytes Cary Estate countryside and enjoy the natural landscape. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Heritage Open Days – Free Entry to Lytes Cary Manor 14-18 September. 10am-4.30pm Come and discover the historic manor house, enjoy a light lunch in the café courtyard, stroll around the formal garden or explore one of the wider estate walks. Price: Free event. Booking not required. Lytes Scary Halloween Trail 24 Oct -1 Nov. 10am-3.30pm Put your wellies on and come on a spooky adventure. Can you crack the riddle? Are you brave enough to take part? Price: £3.50 per trail (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Christmas Market at Lytes Cary Manor 14 & 15 November. 10am-3pm Join us for some festive cheer and find those unique Christmas gifts. Held in the historic barns and courtyard areas. The Lytes Cary market showcases a variety of products that have been crafted by local artists. Price: Free event (normal admission applies to visit the house, garden & tea-room). Booking not required. Montacute House Montacute House | Somerset | National Trust Heritage Open Days – Free Entry to Montacute House 14-18 September. 10am-5pm As part of Heritage Open Days, we invite you to explore Montacute House for free. See the ground floor of the house and enjoy a stroll through the gardens Price: Free event. Booking not required. Specialist Crafts Team demonstrations as part of Heritage Open Days 16 & 17 September. 10am-5pm The Specialist Craft team are showing off their skills. There is so much to see and learn of what goes on behind the scenes to protect and conserve our heritage. Price: Free event. Booking not required. Prior Park https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/bath-bristol/prior-park-landscape-garden Garden Yogis at Prior Park 12 September. 9.30-10.30 Start the weekend with an outdoors yoga class - mats next to the lake and iconic bridge in this beautiful National Trust garden. Price: £6pp. Booking not required. Jane Austen Festival: Take a turn around Prior Park 11-20 September. 10am-5pm Take a turn around the garden to discover a number of quotes from Jane Austen’s stories. Can you work out who said it? Frame your view and take your photograph through a large, ornate, Georgian-style frame, with the view of the Palladian bridge behind. 15% off entry for visitors arriving in Regency dress. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Jane Austen Festival: Regency feast 13 September. 5.30-7.45pm Enjoy an exquisite grazing feast on the Palladian bridge at Prior Park. Food will include options such as cured charcuterie, artisan cheeses and pickled figs. Take a turn around the lower garden, with exclusive evening access. Price: £45pp. Booking required. Jane Austen Festival: ‘To Sit in the Shade’ - an Austen painting workshop 16 & 17 September. 9-10.30am Explore watercolour techniques to create a beautiful floral border, then fill with your favourite Jane Austen quote. Price: £20pp. Booking required. Heritage Open Days at Prior Park 18 & 19 September. 10am-4pm Prior Park will be opening its gates for free on 18 and 19 September as part of Heritage Open Days. A chance to see Ralph Allen’s 18th century garden and its iconic Palladian bridge for free. Price: Free event. Booking not required. October half term at Prior Park 24 October-1 November. 10am-4pm Dotted around the garden this October half term at Prior Park will be a variety of spooky sights for children to discover. Can you spot them all? Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Tintinhull Garden https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset/tintinhull-garden Heritage Open Days – Free Entry to Tintinhull Garden 14-18 September. 11am-4pm Come and wander around the beautiful garden. Switch off and enjoy the tranquillity of the Pool Garden or enjoy a coffee in the courtyard tearoom. Price: Free event. Booking not required. Tyntesfield https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/bath-bristol/tyntesfield Tyntesfield Book Club 15 September, 13 October & 10 November. 10am-12noon The group meets in the Cow Barn Café for 2 hours with a break in the middle to get a drink. Two of our friendly Bookshop volunteers will be running the meetings. There is no criteria to joining other than an enthusiasm for reading; the willingness to try books that might differ from your usual choice and being ready to join in a discussion about them. There is no weekly charge, although a £10 donation once a year would be appreciated and will go towards the upkeep of Tyntesfield estate. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking required. A Conversation with Angela Tomaski 24 September. 2-3.15pm Tyntesfield estate is the inspiration and setting for the recently published and highly acclaimed novel The Infamous Gilberts by Angela Tomaski. It features in The Guardian’s list of best books for this summer’s reading and is described as ‘An irresistible old-fashioned comfort read...with romantic misadventures, dastardly characters, lost boys and lashings of atmosphere.’ Join Angela as she reads excerpts of her novel; shares insight into its creation and answers your questions. She is happy to sign your copy of the book. Price: £6pp (normal admissions apply). Booking required. Stoke-sub-Hamdon Priory https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset/stoke-sub-hamdon-priory Heritage Open Days Stoke-sub-Hamdon Priory opening day with talk 11 September. 10am-12.30pm Join a National Trust Archaeologist for a talk at 10am or 11.30am. The site will be open from 10am to 12.30pm. View the small complex of buildings, formerly the home of the priests serving the Chapel of St. Nicholas. Visit the newly restored dovecote. Please note - Stoke-Sub-Hamdon Priory is an unmanned site and entry (including NT members) must be booked in advance. Price: Free event. Booking required. Heritage Open Days - Stoke-sub-Hamdon Priory opening day 12-20 September. 10am-12noon View the small complex of buildings, formerly the home of the priests serving the Chapel of St. Nicholas. View the newly restored dovecote. Please note - Stoke-Sub-Hamdon Priory is an unmanned site and entry (including NT members) must be booked in advance. Price: Free event. Booking required. Brean Down https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset/brean-down Guided Coastal Walks 20 September. 10.30am-1pm Discover over 10,000 years of history at Brean Down on a free guided walk with our knowledgeable group walk volunteers. Price: Free event. Booking required.

title: Double-Gate Farm
subtitle: Georgian farmhouse B&B accommodation with self catering converted barns in a peaceful location in Somerset, near Glastonbury & Wells.
bodyContent: Welcome to Double-Gate Farm, our Georgian farmhouse situated on the banks of the River Sheppey. Our farm offers views of the Mendip Hills and the surrounding countryside. Whether you're looking for a romantic getaway, a family vacation, or a group retreat, we have a variety of accommodations to choose from. Our converted barn is perfect for couples, families, and groups, while our accessible Riverside rooms and facilities cater to everyone's requirements. Our seasonal Tea Room is open from March to December and offers a range of delicious breakfasts, light lunches, home-baked cakes, and our speciality, Afternoon Tea. How about renting our BBQ Hut for a fun and sociable evening of cooking with your loved ones? Our Games Room is the perfect place to unwind after a long day of exploring. With a full-size snooker table, table-tennis, and lots of board games and local information, you'll never run out of things to do. At Double-Gate Farm, we pride ourselves on providing a peaceful and relaxing environment that allows you to unwind and enjoy nature. You can fish from your patio, watch the wildlife, or simply sit back and read. We welcome everyone, including cycling groups, walkers, and countryside lovers. Our location is perfect for exploring Somerset's hidden gems. With easy access to Glastonbury, Wells, and Cheddar, you'll be able to experience all that this beautiful region has to offer. We're also dog-friendly, so you don't have to leave your furry friend behind. Two of our Riverside rooms are pet-friendly, so please call us to check availability when booking with your dog. Finally, our farm is next door to a renowned gastropub that serves food and local brews. It's just a short walk away, so you don't have to worry about transportation. Come and experience the beauty of Double-Gate Farm for yourself.
tagline: Georgian farmhouse B&B accommodation with self catering converted barns

title: Crowcombe Court
subtitle: Crowcombe Court is a licensed wedding venue able to host civil ceremonies and wedding receptions where you are offered an exclusive, bespoke day to remember.
bodyContent: Weddings http://www.crowcombecourt.co.uk/weddings/ Grade 1 Listed Crowcombe Court is West Somerset’s premier wedding and events venue. It offers couples the chance to celebrate in an exclusive and luxurious environment. Crowcombe Court is a licensed wedding venue able to host civil ceremonies and wedding receptions where you are offered an exclusive, bespoke day to remember. With inside and outside ceremony areas this really is an all season venue. The beautiful venue hosts plenty of accommodation for you and your guests, the house even has its own club in the vaulted undercroft. A newly refurbished ballroom is the perfect setting for your wedding breakfast and let’s not forget the getting ready room coming in 2020 for you and your wedding party to get ready before the big event. The excellence of the dining at Crowcombe Court has gained an enviable reputation. All catering requirements are delivered by our superb ‘in house’ Chefs where the couples and their guests can enjoy some of West Somerset's finest food beautifully prepared and served. The house is heated throughout and has ample free parking. Corporate Crowcombe Court offers an idyllic venue for corporate events such as seminars, presentations, team development through facilitated experiential learning, mindfulness and wellbeing in the workplace, product launches, press days and more. The wide range of magnificent rooms of varying sizes, including a vaulted undercroft and bar, can be combined to provide an event which includes reception, dining and lecture spaces. Multiple activities can be undertaken concurrently which can maximise the delivery of seminar, team development and training content. You are guaranteed exclusively and confidentiality, there is no public access. The house is heated throughout and has ample free parking. Shooting A magnificent Grade 1 listed mansion which offers hospitality to sporting guests with exclusivity and traditionality. Crowcombe Court may be booked by teams of guns and their companions, and can accommodate a maximum of 18 guests across 9 King size rooms. Ample car parking is available. Crowcombe Court may be booked by teams of guns and their companions, and can accommodate a maximum of 18 guests across 9 King size rooms. A typical stay will include dinner bed and breakfast either for the evening prior to shooting or the evening of the shoot. Dinner consists of three courses followed by local cheeses and wine selected from our standard wine list. (A fine wine list is available). Pre dinner drinks are included as is a decanter of malt whisky. The dinner menu must be chosen in advance. Post-shoot deep and remedial massage from "Bodyfix" available (prior booking required) Ample car parking is available. A drying room is available. Helicopter landing areas are available nearby.
tagline: Grade 1 Listed Crowcombe Court is West Somerset’s premier wedding and events venue.

title: 4 St George’s House
subtitle: Lovely new first floor apartment with private parking, 5 minutes level walk from the centre of Bath.
bodyContent: Newly built and opened in December 2014, St George’s House is a contemporary Bath stone building in a quiet location off a Georgian crescent, just 5 minutes level walk from the town centre and less than 10 minutes from Bath’s most famous crescent, The Royal Crescent. Our two bedroom apartment sleeps 4 in comfort. Soft leather and oak furniture, really comfortable beds, a sleek modern kitchen and two contemporary bathrooms, excellent modern heating and insulation all make for a relaxing and luxurious home for enjoying the pleasures of Bath. All of Bath’s famous sights and shops are within an easy walk – you won’t need your car while you are here and can leave it in our allocated private secure parking space. The same luxurious comfort as our other apartment, 3 Herschel Place.
tagline: Lovely new first floor apartment with private parking.

title: Church Farm Country Cottages
subtitle: Seven cottages tastefully converted from old cow byres with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams.
bodyContent: Seven cottages tastefully converted from old cow byres with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams. Three cottages sleep 2 persons and four cottages sleep 4 persons. Bath 5 miles. Bradford on Avon 2 miles. Ample parking. Working farm with sheep and horses in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Swim in our luxurious heated indoor pool (12m x 5m) whatever the weather! Games room with table tennis, pool table and table football. Village pub serving food 500m. Village shop 500m. Kennet and Avon Canal nearby for cycling, boating and walking. Locally produced welcome cream tea.
tagline: Seven cottages tastefully converted from old cow byres with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams.

title: Beeches Farmhouse Ensuite Rooms
subtitle: Farmyard accommodation in Bradford on Avon near Bath, has double / twin and family en-suite rooms and all, except one, in detached converted farm buildings.
bodyContent: Farmyard accommodation in Bradford on Avon near Bath, Somerset, with double / twin and family en-suite rooms and all, except one, in detached converted farm buildings. Most of their rooms are dog friendly, so your four-legged chum needn't miss out on a holiday! To the rear of the accommodation are grassy fields where your pet can run and play to their heart's content. Each room has their own front door key and own patio area, giving you the independence to come and go as you please. All rooms have full en-suite facilities including bath and/or shower and are decorated to a very high standard with exposed beams, stripped wooden floors and country pine furnishings. During busy periods there is usually a minimum stay of two nights at weekends unless ‘last minute’. They also offer self catering cottages “Beeches Farmhouse Cottages”, so their en suite rooms can be used with their self catering cottages for additional bedrooms - click here to find out more.

title: Koffmann & Mr. White's
subtitle: The first joint venture between culinary legends, Pierre Koffmann and Marco Pierre White is the brasserie-style eatery Koffmann & Mr. White's.
bodyContent: The first joint venture between culinary legends, Pierre Koffmann and Marco Pierre White is the brasserie-style eatery Koffmann & Mr. White's. The brasserie is located in central Bath just around from Bath Abbey, the Roman Baths and only five minutes walk from Bath Spa train station. Serving a mix of English and French classics for the discerning customer looking for good quality, the restaurant offers French dishes such as Snails à la Bourguignonne and Poulet noir Grand-mère alongside English favourites like Shepherd's Pie and Fish and Chips. Affordable food is served in a relaxed, stylish and unpretentious environment befitting the Georgian surroundings.
tagline: The first joint venture between culinary legends, Pierre Koffmann and Marco Pierre White.

title: Farrington Inn
subtitle: Discover real ales, log burning fires and great British pub food at The Farrington Inn.
bodyContent: Discover real ales, log burning fires and great British pub food at The Farrington Inn. Located in the small village of Farrington Gurney, just a short drive from Bristol, Bath , Wells and the Mendips . You will find the pub on the main A37 so it's a perfect meeting place or to somewhere to take a break when travelling. The Farrington Inn is popular with families and the large beer garden has a well maintained children's play area. For those rainy days colouring templates and the free wifi will keep the children happy. The Great British Deals menu is served from 10am - 9pm everyday and has several mains at 2 for £10 and 2 for £12. There is also a 2 course lunch menu at £7.99, served Monday to Saturday until 4pm. Our extremely popular all day breakfast is included in the 2 for £12 deal and comes with a hot drink and toast. The Farrington Inn is an excellent choice for those who want freshly cooked real food, exceptional value and a friendly atmosphere. Opening times: Monday - Sunday 10am - 11pm Food served all day 10am - 9pm
tagline: Discover real ales, log burning fires and great British pub food at The Farrington Inn.

bodyContent: The Moon and Sixpence is one of the most popular pubs in Clevedon. Situated in a prime seafront position looking out over the Bristol Channel and facing Clevedon's famous Victorian Pier. Spectacular sunsets can be witnessed from our pub balcony offering some of the best views in Clevedon or from our outside eating and drinking areas. The Moon & Sixpence is a welcoming, popular bar, restaurant and hotel offers a range of accommodation and entertainment as well as great pub food in comfortable surroundings. We specialise in traditional English and Mediterranean cuisine prepared by our chefs. See an example of the daily specials that we serve here.

title: Bath Abbey
subtitle: Living and Telling the Good News of Jesus with the City of Bath and its Visitors
bodyContent: A moment of stillness in the beating heart of a vibrant city. A space that’s alive with music and prayer, art and history. A place where awe-inspiring architecture lifts the eyes – and raises the spirit. Bath Abbey is many things to many people. Whether you come here to join a service or a tour , light a candle or listen to our choirs , what unites us all is a sense of wonder. There is so much to discover – please step inside…

title: Butlin’s, Minehead
subtitle: Join us for a Butlin’s day visit during the School holidays or during our Showtime breaks to enjoy a day of non-stop fun!
bodyContent: Nowhere else does fun and entertainment quite like Butlin’s. As the ‘nation’s host’, we pull out all the stops to make sure your day visit is packed with full on fun for the whole family to enjoy. In between watching a daytime show in the Skyline Pavilion, you can swim ‘til you’re wrinkly in our huge Splash Waterworld, go again and again with unlimited rides in the fairground and get stuck into endless activities (subject to availability). If you’ve still got energy to burn, you can make the most of the outdoor play areas and arcades or refuel in one of the bars or restaurants. Book in the Holiday Booking Shop at Minehead, before you leave and get up to 40% off selected breaks! title: Mercure Bridgwater Hotel
subtitle: A stylish 4-star hotel in the heart of Bridgwater, offering 119 contemporary bedrooms, exceptional service, and home to the renowned Marco Pierre White Steakhouse Bar & Grill. Perfect for business, leisure, or exploring Somerset.
bodyContent: Mercure Bridgwater is a modern 4-star hotel ideally located in Bridgwater town centre, just minutes from local attractions and with easy access to the M5. The hotel offers 119 beautifully designed bedrooms, combining comfort and style to ensure a relaxing stay for both business and leisure guests. Dining is a highlight, with the Marco Pierre White Steakhouse Bar & Grill serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner to the highest standards, alongside a stylish bar and lounge. For business travellers and events, the hotel offers versatile meeting and conference facilities equipped with the latest technology. The fitness suite is available for guests looking to stay active during their visit. Part of the Accor group, Mercure Bridgwater offers outstanding hospitality, a welcoming atmosphere, and access to exclusive loyalty benefits through ALL – Accor Live Limitless. The hotel is also a fantastic base for exploring Somerset, from the Quantock Hills and Exmoor National Park to the stunning coastline, historic towns, and world-famous attractions such as Cheddar Gorge and Glastonbury Tor. Whether you are visiting for work, a romantic getaway, or to discover all that Somerset has to offer, Mercure Bridgwater is the perfect choice.

bodyContent: This new food and drink trade show for Somerset will present you with an outstanding offering to help your business stay one step ahead, whether you’re looking for local craft producers, established brands, food service providers, equipment, or business services. title: New Immersive Cave Experience at Wookey Hole
subtitle: Wookey Hole offers one of the best May half term experiences in Somerset.
bodyContent: This May half term, Wookey Hole invites families to enjoy adventure, imagination and discovery all in one incredible location. Nestled beneath the Mendip Hills, it’s the perfect place for a fun‑filled day out or a memorable family staycation, with attractions for all ages, everything included in your ticket, and great‑value hotel packages for a stress‑free break. Step beneath the Mendip Hills and experience Wookey Hole like never before. Our new immersive cave projections bring legend, nature, and exploration together through light, atmosphere, and storytelling - enhancing the natural beauty of the caves without overpowering it. Guests journey through three extraordinary chambers, each transformed by subtle, cinematic projections that bring Wookey Hole's folklore and history to life in front of your very eyes. This atmospheric enhancement adds depth, wonder, and emotion to every visit - making the caves even more magical for both children and adults. Above ground, the adventure continues with a full day of family attractions included in every ticket. Enjoy live circus shows, a 4D cinema experience, Dinosaur Valley, adventure golf, traditional paper‑making demonstrations, giant soft play, the Zap Zone and so much more. Whether the sun is shining or the rain appears, there’s always something exciting to explore together. Wookey Hole offers one of the best May half term experiences in Somerset. From magical moments beneath the ground to laughter and thrills above it, it’s a place where families can reconnect and make lasting memories this half term.

title: Collie Shepherd Hut
subtitle: Collie Shepherd Hut is a peaceful countryside retreat in Somerset, offering a cosy and romantic escape for two. Enjoy a private wood-fired hot tub, stunning views across the Somerset Levels and thoughtful touches throughout. Perfect for relaxing breaks, stargazing nights and unwinding in comfort close to nature and local attractions.
bodyContent: Collie Shepherd Hut is an exclusive countryside retreat in Somerset, designed for couples seeking a luxurious and intimate escape. Set in a peaceful rural location with uninterrupted views across the Somerset Levels, it offers a restorative setting where guests can slow down, unwind and reconnect with nature. Beautifully styled throughout, the hut blends rustic charm with elevated comfort. The king-size bed sits within a cosy alcove, dressed in quality linens for a restful night’s sleep. A well-equipped kitchenette includes a microwave oven, double-ring gas hob, fridge with top freezer compartment and essentials for simple self-catering. Guests are welcomed with a complimentary breakfast pack, adding a thoughtful and indulgent start to their stay. The ensuite shower room with flushing toilet, along with fluffy bathrobes, slippers and towels — including an additional set for the hot tub — adds further comfort. Outside, your private wood-fired hot tub with jacuzzi spa jets awaits, perfectly positioned for slow evenings spent watching Somerset’s glowing sunsets fade into star-filled skies. Firewood and everything needed for your stay are provided, ensuring a seamless and relaxing experience from the moment you arrive.Ideal for romantic getaways, anniversaries and special occasions, Collie Shepherd Hut offers privacy, calm and complete escape from everyday life. Surrounded by Somerset’s natural beauty, the hut sits beside a working farm, offering an authentic and peaceful countryside setting where guests can enjoy scenic walks, explore charming nearby villages or simply relax in total seclusion. A refined rural retreat where luxury, romance and nature come together effortlessly.

title: Edinburgh Preview: Li Jin Hao + Emmeline Downie
subtitle: Li Jin Hao Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer Nominee and Chortle Best Newcomer winner Li Jin Hao is a comedy writer and performer.
bodyContent: Li Jin Hao Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer Nominee and Chortle Best Newcomer winner Li Jin Hao is a comedy writer and performer. Jin Hao was made in China and marinated in Singapore, loved and feared for his dry wit, gritty softness, and surreal energy, he quickly became a Chortle Student Finalist, BBC New Comedy Awards Finalist, and was accepted into the Pleasance Comedy Reserve 2023. His debut solo show “Swimming in a Submarine” had a sell-out run at Edinburgh Fringe 2024 and earned him a nomination for Best Newcomer at the Edinburgh Comedy Awards, with a London run at the Soho Theatre for three weeks, before taking the show to the Melbourne International Comedy Festival. His TV appearances include Silence is Golden (Dave), Comedy Central Live (Comedy Central), The Stand Up Sketch Show (ITV2), and ITVX Presents: Live Comedy From the Edinburgh Fringe. Emmeline Donnie Emmeline Downie is a comedian, writer and actor performing across the UK comedy circuit. She co-created and starred in Edinburgh hits, Manhunt and Manhunt 2: Big Mood, earning critical acclaim; "brilliantly performed, beautifully written" - ThreeWeeks ★★★★★ In 2025, Emmeline appeared in Brainsluts at Pleasance Dome, recognised by The Guardian for a "stand-out performance". Her writing credits include an Untitled BBC Studios Comedy Writers' Room and additional material for Ania Magliano's Forgive Me, Father and Leo Reich's Literally Who Cares?!!! (A24). "A knockout" - The Stage ★★★★
tagline: Li Jin Hao Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer Nominee and Chortle Best

title: Goblet Cell
subtitle: Established by Eve Lauder in 2021 who sadly lost her battle with Goblet Cell.
bodyContent: Established by Eve Lauder in 2021 who sadly lost her battle with Goblet Cell. The Goblet Cell Ball will return to The Grand Pier in Weston-super-Mare, this year to raise vital funds for Weston Hospicecare, who provided Eve and her family with invaluable support and care this year. The first Goblet Cell ball in 2021 raised over £7,000 for Cancer Research and in 2022 we succeeded this number to an incredible £13,170. The current total raised is an incredible £35,644.56 . This will be the 5th annual ball where we are on a mission to #bemoreeve and raise even more to the local charity Weston Hospice. Eve was only 47 years of age when she was diagnosed with stage 4 goblet cell cancer in 2020 . This is an exceedingly rare form of cancer, affecting only 1 in 2 million individuals, and unfortunately there is no cure. Being told this new is absolutely life changing, but rather than letting this hold her back, Eve spent her last moments raising over £50,000 for Cancer Research, £5,000 for the Eve Care Packages at Weston Hospital and £8,500 for Weston Hospicecare. Over 200 care packages have since been funded. We ask you to join us in raising more money for Weston Hospicecare and celebrating the life of Eve with her wonderful family. The 2026 event promises to be even bigger and better, and the evening will include a 3-course dinner, live entertainment, charity auction and raffle. Standard Tickets include: 3 Course Dinner Live

title: Halloween at Ferne
subtitle: Get ready for a frightfully fun Halloween celebration packed with activities for all ages! Join us for a day of spooky surprises, creative fun, and unforgettable entertainment.
bodyContent: 🎧 Silent Disco Dance the day away to your favourite tunes with our Halloween-themed Silent Disco. Pop on a pair of headphones and choose your soundtrack as you party. 👻 Fancy Dress Competition Show off your most terrifying, creative, or hilarious costume for a chance to win fantastic prizes. Whether you’re a wicked witch, fearless superhero, or creepy creature, everyone is welcome to take part. 🎨 Arts & Crafts Let your imagination run wild with Halloween-inspired arts and crafts. Create spooky decorations, design your own Halloween masterpieces, and enjoy hands-on fun for the whole family. ☕ Perdida Cafe Take a break from the Halloween excitement and enjoy a selection of delicious refreshments, sweet treats, and seasonal favourites available throughout the event at Perdida Cafe. 🕸️ Spooky Trail Follow our Haunted Trail and uncover eerie clues, mysterious surprises, and hidden Halloween characters along the way. Perfect for little explorers and brave adventurers alike! Don’t miss this fang-tastic Halloween event filled with music, costumes, creativity, and spooky fun. Gather your family and friends and join us for a Halloween celebration to remember! 🎃🕷️👻

title: Saltmarsh panorama drawing workshop
subtitle: Join Bath-based artist Jessica Palmer to explore Steart Marshes through watercolour, pen and pencil
bodyContent: Create a set of sketches in one long concertina book to form a Saltmarsh panorama. We will use watercolour wash and pen/pencil to capture impressions of a marsh-scape. Each section will be a snapshot view - making up a panorama of the saltmarsh on the day you visit – whatever the weather. This workshop is suitable for all. No drawing or painting experience necessary. All materials provided. This is fun for adults or for families working together in the sketchbook. Please note – we recommend wearing sturdy boots and dressing for the weather as we will also be working outdoors amongst nature. A bottle of water, suncream and sunhat are also advised. Where to meet: In the main WWT car park at Steart Marshes, Stert Drove, Bridgwater, Somerset, TA5 2PU.
tagline: Join Bath-based artist Jessica Palmer to explore Steart Marshes through watercolour, pen and pencil

title: Free Nature Walk with YHA Cheddar
subtitle: Be part of the YHA Festival of Walking!
bodyContent: Be part of the YHA Festival of Walking! Join a free 4-hour walk around the stunning Cheddar Gorge on Thursday 17th September. Starting at YHA Cheddar, this walk is hosted by YHA Cheddar in collaboration with Mendip Activity Centre - both Mendip Adventure destinations. It is led by Mendip Hills National Landscape nature recovery ranger, Nathan Orr. During the walk, you'll learn about nature recovery efforts in the Mendip Hills and how it’s helping improve biodiversity and sustainability. You'll also discover more about the area’s champion species, such as the Cheddar pink, the adder, the black oil beetle, skylark and small pearl-bordered fritillary. Free to join, with optional donations. Sign up today!
tagline: Be part of the YHA Festival of Walking!

title: Charles Dowding, Hero of the Land
subtitle: Rosie Inge learns about No Dig with Charles Dowding
bodyContent: It has taken me a very long time to write this article! Mainly because what I learned on Charles Dowding’s No-Dig Gardening course covered pages of my notebook but also because I spent an inordinate length of time watching his Youtube videos which each give an enormous amount of USEFUL information, and partly because I bought some of his books and haven’t been able to put them down! Principally No-Dig Children’s Gardening Book and Gardening Myths. Charles Dowding is a simple man. Simple = the opposite of complicated. His gardening philosophy is very simple – copy what Nature has always done and you’ll be fine. Watch how leaves die back on plants and trees and fall to the ground to create the nurturing soil of the future. He offers free and subscription videos on Youtube and he gives one day, two-day and online courses – all with his gentle, calm and exhaustive knowledge, gained over running his market garden near Castle Cary for 40 years and his No-Dig courses for the last ten years. He is also a worried man. “Food is getting more precious, more serious,” he says. “I’m concerned about food production in the future.” The message is to produce your own – it’s not difficult, and it is SO rewarding. I attended his one-day No-Dig (ND) course in mid April. Two students from Berlin and others from Gloucestershire, Sussex and central London made the pilgrimage to Homeacres, just outside Castle Cary. Pilgrimage is the right word: students are fanatic followers of his every word; one girl was upset that she wasn’t at home to sow the seeds he recommended for that particular day in his colourful and very useful Calendar. He reassured her that she could do the job the next day. Everything hinges on compost, whose corner I have personally been fighting for over 50 years since my father separated his kitchen bins into one for compost, one for paper to burn, one for glass recycling and the rest for the dustbin men. Making this friable, rich, essential material is almost as rewarding as growing the plants within it. “It is central to gardening, not just ND,” he enthuses. “It is very efficient in keeping carbon in the soil and can get rid of the gardener’s greatest enemies like couch grass, bindweed and ground elder within two years. Don’t give slugs anywhere to hide in your beds, add compost. Raised beds offer a hiding place around the edge for snails to lurk.” A pity, since I’ve just converted my veg patch to very raised beds to make weeding and harvesting easier! If you don’t produce enough raw material - vegetable peelings and other ‘green’ kitchen waste, or grass cuttings or have access to a pony’s rich production - collect coffee grounds from your local café, ask for grass mowings from the cemetery or sawdust from a joiner, put in broken up cardboard and shredded paper. Add fine wood chippings – or if the supplier gives you bigger pieces, run your lawn mower over the pile. Add everything – citrus, mildewed and blighted leaves. If it’s too moist, add paper; if too dry, add water. Use lots of cardboard (he has unending supplies from his publisher) and add woodchip on top. You only need to turn the compost heap once, after about six weeks, then leave it, covered, to dry out; once sieved, you will have perfect rich, friable, essential food for the earth. Nothing more is needed – certainly don’t add any chemicals or fertilisers. Spread the compost after the last autumn harvest and before Christmas; give it a light raking in the spring – and get sowing. Once the compost is spread on top, you can walk on it to firm it in. Dowding himself can only create two thirds of his own compost, so buys it in from the local recycling company. He’s wary of the quality – it might contain some chemicals from other people’s garden waste. He also has suppliers of spent mushroom compost but doesn’t add it to the heap if it is still hot – it won’t be ready. All the nourishment needed for a perfect growing medium is already there – compost doesn’t leach nutrients. “Don’t believe what you hear or read,” he says. “Don’t put stones in the bottom of pots; don’t plant out til the growth is quite strong, but you also don’t need to ‘harden’ the plants; don’t ‘rest’ or ‘fork’ the soil – you disturb the mycorrhizal roots. Digging can also make drainage worse, so only use a spade to dig up woody weeds – docks, couch grass, dandelions etc. There is no need to rotate plants – he has grown potatoes in the same bed for eight years and the harvest is still great. As mentioned above, his Gardening Myths and Misconceptions is reassuring as well as amusing. When sowing, put four seeds of onions, beetroots, turnips or carrots in one seed module tray (he has sourced robust plastic module trays which you can buy on the course, along with a sturdy dibber and any of his 11 books). Plant the root module in its place in the bed then later, twist the largest gently to harvest; the others will remain and continue to grow. There is no need to ‘pot’ on. Leave carrots, parsnips, spinach, parsley, fennel and onions to go to seed and potato plants in the ground – they will grow and produce their own seeds for the following years. To start from scratch in a field or weedy bed, you need to exclude light. If you are just using cardboard, add a two inch layer of compost on top and plant straight away; if you need to use black plastic, put the compost on top of the earth and plastic on top of that; make holes in the plastic and plant straight away. Spuds and spinach respond well to this method. Dowding permanently maintains a dig and No Dig bed next to each other to compare; every year, ND has stronger growth. He has always grown poppy seeds and rye for his homemade bread which was served at our lunch - utterly delicious, accompanied by six different dishes using vegetables grown on site. Unsurprisingly, he has published his No Dig Cookbook. Wise words fell from his heart all throughout the day. “It’s not what you know, it’s what you understand. “Leave the soil undisturbed and feed its life on the surface. “That’s gardening; you never stop learning and nothing is exactly the same year after year.“ Wise words indeed. www.charlesdowding.co.uk

title: Lost at the Ball - Georgian treasures unearthed beneath Bath Assembly Rooms
subtitle: Finds include a Georgian beauty pot, an initialled wig curler, clay tobacco pipes and embossed wine bottles.
bodyContent: · Archaeological excavations beneath Bath Assembly Rooms have uncovered Georgian and Victorian objects hidden for centuries. · Finds include a Georgian beauty pot, an initialled wig curler, clay tobacco pipes and embossed wine bottles, offering a glimpse into the lives and stories of Bath's fashionable visitors. · Animal bone remains reveal the foods served at the city's grand social gatherings, including turkey, goose and cod. · The discoveries were made as part of the National Trust's major restoration project, which will transform the Assembly Rooms and create a new immersive Georgian ball experience. · Many of the finds will be used in future displays, events and community activities, helping bring Bath's social history to life The National Trust is transforming Bath Assembly Rooms, restoring its Georgian splendour and creating a new immersive Georgian ball experience for visitors. As part of restoration work, archaeological investigations overseen by Wessex Archaeology have uncovered a fascinating collection of objects hidden beneath the building, which first opened in 1771. From beauty products and wig curlers to wine bottles and tobacco pipes, the discoveries offer an intimate glimpse into the lives of the fashionable visitors who flocked to Bath during the 18th and 19th centuries. Together, the finds reveal the human stories of beauty, status, dining and entertainment in one of Britain's most celebrated social venues. Beauty secrets of Georgian Bath Skincare may be booming today, but Georgians were equally preoccupied with achieving the perfect complexion. A remarkably well-preserved porcelain ointment pot (dating from 1730-1800) once held creams or salves made from oils, waxes and floral waters. Whether used to soften skin, protect against the elements or maintain the pale complexion that was the height of fashion, the pot is a reminder that getting ready for a night out was just as important 250 years ago as it is today. The Georgian equivalent of a hair curler Few modest-looking objects capture the glamour and extravagance of Georgian big‑hair days quite like wig curlers. Small clay cylinders dating from the 1750s were discovered, having once been used to create the elaborate curls and towering hairstyles that defined fashionable society. Wigs and hairpieces were an essential part of dressing for an evening at the Assembly Rooms, where appearance mattered and visitors came to see and be seen. One of the curlers is especially interesting because it bears the initials of the maker "WA" – a less common set of initials for those found in southern England. Was it dropped by a maid preparing guests for the evening? Lost by a servant rushing through last-minute preparations? Or forgotten by a fashionable visitor from the north of England eager not to miss the start of the ball? More than two centuries later, the mystery remains. A menu fit for Georgian high society Animal bone remains recovered during the work have revealed something of the menu enjoyed by visitors to Georgian Bath. Archaeologists identified sheep, goat, cattle, pig, goose, turkey and even cod among the remains. While many of these foods were common in 18th-century dining, turkey and goose were relatively expensive choices, hinting at the lavish suppers and special occasions hosted in the city's grandest social spaces. The finds even raise the possibility that some of these delicacies were enjoyed at prestigious events such as the annual ball held in honour of Queen Charlotte. The VIP wine cellar Wine flowed freely in the Assembly Rooms and one discovery offers a tantalising glimpse into the world of Bath's wealthy visitors. Found within the former cellar where alcohol was stored for guests, a fragment of wine bottle (dating from 1760-1860) is embossed with the name "DOLTON". The inscription suggests it may have belonged to a prosperous patron who had bottles marked so that wine merchants could refill and return them between visits. It's easy to imagine the bottle's owner arriving for the Bath season and finding their favourite wine waiting for them in one of the city's most fashionable venues. Smoke, drink and merriment Long before smoking was proven bad for health, it was a familiar part of social life for all classes in Georgian Bath, and the excavations uncovered dozens of clay tobacco pipe fragments linked to one of the city's most successful pipe-making families. More than 50 pipe fragments were identified as the works of pipe maker Robert Carpenter and his son, John Carpenter. The number of Carpenter pipes found highlights both the popularity of tobacco in Bath and the important role local craftsmen played in supplying the city's residents and visitors. The Carpenter family dominated the pipe-making market in Bath up to the early 1760s, operating workshops that served a growing and increasingly fashionable city. Although almost all the fragments found were brought in from elsewhere in the city to raise the ground level during construction of the building, they are typical of the pipes smoked in and around the Assembly Rooms. They are a vivid reminder of the sociable atmosphere that surrounded Bath's fashionable season, where conversation, gaming, dining and entertainment all played their part. Echoes of a grand Victorian celebration The Victorians who followed the Georgians also left their mark on the Assembly Rooms. Among the most striking discoveries were fragments of a decorative serving platter featuring Greek-inspired motifs, musical instruments and quivers of arrows. The design has been identified as Minton & Co's 'Trophy' pattern, first registered in 1867. Minton was one of Britain's most prestigious pottery manufacturers and this was far from everyday tableware. The elegant design hints at the scale and sophistication of Victorian banquets, receptions and celebrations held in the Assembly Rooms long after the Georgian era had passed. During the restoration, and when Bath Assembly Rooms reopens, a programme of workshops and events will be available that will give local communities the opportunity to get up close to these objects. These activities will invite people to explore the history of Bath Assembly Rooms and Georgian Bath to open up conversations about what life was like for ordinary people through history. Tatjana LeBoff, National Trust’s Project Curator for Bath Assembly Rooms, said: "These discoveries remind us that Bath Assembly Rooms was never just a beautiful building - it was a place filled with people. Behind every object is a human story: someone preparing for a glittering evening, sharing food and drink with friends, or perhaps accidentally leaving something behind more than two centuries ago. "As we restore the Assembly Rooms and create a new Georgian ball experience, these finds help us connect visitors not only with the history of the building, but with the lives of the generations who danced, dined and celebrated here. We're delighted that these remarkable discoveries will help bring the story of Bath Assembly Rooms to life for local communities and future visitors alike." Wessex Archaeology, which oversaw the excavation works is now supporting the transfer of the finds to the National Trust so they can be used in future displays, events and community activities. Marek Lewcun, from Wessex Archaeology, said: “It was a privilege to have found so many fascinating objects and through them to be able to help the National Trust present what life was like at the Assembly Rooms. A visit in Georgian times would have involved a lot of preparation, and hair curlers such as the ones we found would have played an important role in making sure their fashionable wigs were at their best. “Snuff taking and smoking were very popular in 18th century Bath, and many pipes bearing their makers’ marks were found during the excavations. Although smoking might have been frowned upon within the main building, the Coffee House and courtyard would have offered smokers a retreat from the hustle and bustle inside, very much like the smokers’ area that we find today.” Bath Assembly Rooms will reopen in 2027. For more information visit www.nationaltrust.org.uk/bath-assembly-rooms

title: Ferne Animal Sanctuary’s Charity Gala returns for 2026
subtitle: Ferne’s Charity Gala will return to The Shrubbery Hotel in Ilminster on Friday 16 October.
bodyContent: Following the success of last year’s event, Ferne Animal Sanctuary is inviting supporters, local businesses and members of the community to its 2026 Charity Gala. Ferne’s Charity Gala will return to The Shrubbery Hotel in Ilminster on Friday 16 October, 6.30pm-11.30pm bringing guests together for an evening of dining, entertainment and fundraising in support of the animals in the charity’s care. Ticket holders will enjoy a two-course meal, a welcome glass of Prosecco or orange juice, with music from DJ Baroness Boogie and Nelle Curtis, plus a silent auction and raffle featuring a range of prizes. Emma Purnell, Chief Executive Officer at Ferne Animal Sanctuary, says: “Following the success of last year’s gala, we’re delighted to be bringing the event back for 2026 and look forward to welcoming supporters, friends and local businesses for another memorable evening. “The gala is a wonderful opportunity to enjoy good food, music and company while helping the animals who rely on Ferne. We would particularly love to see businesses from across the region booking tables, whether they are bringing colleagues together, thanking their teams or entertaining clients. “As a non-government funded charity, events like this make an important contribution to our work. The money raised will help us continue to provide food, shelter, veterinary treatment and ongoing care for hundreds of animals.” The silent auction and raffle will feature prizes including: Champagne afternoon tea for two at The Ritz A selection of artwork An overnight stay at The Old George Broadwindsor A Boss handbag A Case of wine from Louma Country hotel Two Ferne limited edition Hoodie’s An Honor Pad 9 tablet A Galaxy smart watch Tickets cost £49 per person and include the welcome drink, two-course meal and evening’s entertainment. Tables seat 10 guests. The event is open to guests aged 18 and over. The dress code is evening wear, although black tie is not required. Ferne Animal Sanctuary is a non-government funded charity that has provided refuge and rehabilitation to animals for more than 85 years. Located in a National Landscapes area nestled in the Blackdown Hills near Chard, Somerset, Ferne Animal Sanctuary houses and cares for more than 300 animals on its 72-acre site. For more information or to book tickets, visit: www.ferneanimalsanctuary.org/product/fernes-charity-gala/

title: Annual fun dog show returns to Ferne Animal Sanctuary
subtitle: Ferne Animal Sanctuary celebrates the return of its annual dog show on Sunday 6th September . Set within the grounds of the Sanctuary’s 72-acre site near Chard, the event will bring together a day of dog friendly activities, entertainment and shopping.
bodyContent: The annual event, which is sponsored by Ye Olde Poppe Inn and Urban Paw Agency, will welcome visitors between 10am and 4pm. Tickets are priced at £10 per car, which includes access to the sanctuary, a car boot sale and a variety of stalls. Entries are open to dogs of all shapes, sizes and ages, with a wide range of popular categories returning, including: Best in Show sponsored by Blackdown Hills National Landscape Best Trick sponsored by Walpole Dunn Loveliest Little Dog sponsored by Hamstone Vets Loveliest Large Dog sponsored by WBW Solicitors Best Ferne Rescue sponsored by Coombefields Vets Best Rescue sponsored by Lentells Accountants Best Veteran (7 and over) sponsored by New Street Vets Prettiest Bitch sponsored by SMS PC & I-phone repair Most Handsome Dog sponsored by Debonair Dogz Waggiest Tail sponsored by Minster Veterinary Surgery Cutest Youngster sponsored by Alro Services Ltd Best Child Handler (awarded in each class) sponsored by Highfield Preserves Registration for each class is priced at £2 per entry and should be completed on arrival, with the first class commencing at 10:30 am and continuing throughout the day. Emma Purnell, Chief Executive Officer at Ferne Animal Sanctuary, says, “Our annual dog show is always a brilliant day in the Ferne calendar, bringing together our supporters, local community and their four-legged friends. This year, we’re excited to have even more for visitors to enjoy, from the dog show and family activities to the car boot sale and stalls. Most importantly, every ticket and entry helps us continue our work caring for and rehoming animals at the Sanctuary, so we hope to see lots of familiar and new faces joining us for a fun-filled day.” Additional dog themed activities and challenges will be available throughout the day including ‘Temptation Alley’ sponsored by paws4teaching, ‘Sit & Stay Challenge’ sponsored by Alro Services Lt and ‘Have A Go Agility sponsored by West Country Tea, all priced at £1 per entry. There will be wide variety of local stalls selling new and old items, including gifts, curiosities and treats for the whole family, with stallholders including: Rob Wheeler Art The Pamper Box Co Art Mad OAP Antlers Lodge Creations Ayesha Burnell Designs Dark Fairy Photography The Crafty Bumpkin Aidan Whitworth Art The Mouse and The Hedgehog Pick Pocket Foragers Elsie & Mabel Stapley’s Crafted With Love Jack and Josie Handmade WagWorthy Accessories The car boot sale will appear alongside the stalls, giving visitors the chance to hunt for a bargain, discover new, and pre-loved treasures, and give unwanted items a new lease of life while helping to raise vital funds for the Sanctuary. Visitors can enjoy treats from the on-site Perdida Café, while J&S Ices will be serving a delicious selection of ice cream. Founded in 1939, Ferne Animal Sanctuary is one of the UK’s oldest animal charities. Today, it cares for around 250 animals on its site, while successfully rehoming a further 200–250 each year. Since its beginnings, the Sanctuary has helped around 40,000 animals find safety, rehabilitation, and a second chance. For more information about Ferne Animal Sanctuary, please visit www.ferneanimalsanctuary.org

subtitle: Millfield Enterprises is a business that represents the prestigious name of Millfield and is responsible for maximising the use of the school’s extensive facilities during the evenings and school holiday periods. They offer holiday courses and facility hire at both the Street campus, Glastonbury campus and Kingweston campus
bodyContent: Millfield Enterprises is a business that represents the prestigious name of Millfield and is responsible for maximising the use of the school’s extensive facilities during the evenings and school holiday periods. They offer holiday courses and facility hire at both the Street campus, Glastonbury campus and Kingweston campus. Millfield Enterprises can cater for a wide range of bookings and events, and whether you want to simply hire a room or need them to organise your whole event or delegate package, they are able to offer support and guidance every step of the way. You can hire just one facility for an hour or multiple facilities for large events. Accommodation is available to hire as part of an event package. The facilities provide the perfect setting for conferences, sports tournaments/training, hospitality events and music concerts. Millfield are able to offer a wide range of catering options from packed lunches to fine dining with silver service and a number of beverage options including a cash bar. Facilities Across the Millfield campuses there are a wide range of facilities available. You can find an overview below, for a full list of the facilities available please visit millfieldenterprises.com/facilties Conferences: classrooms, meeting rooms, lecture theatres. Sports: athletics arena, 25m and 50m swimming pools, equestrian centre (indoor and outdoor facilities), sports halls, tennis centre, dojo, golf (putting and courses), gyms, astro pitches, grass pitches. The Arts: concert halls, theatre, music practice rooms, dance studios. Catering: dining hall, food van, pavilions, bar and coffee shop. Accommodation: boarding house accommodation with a mixture of single, single en-suite, two-bedded, three-bedded, four-bedded and six-bedded rooms dependent on house and campus. Each house has a common room, kitchen and garden/outdoor space.

title: Bloomfield House
subtitle: Bloomfield House, a Georgian detached Grade II listed building, has elegant and romantic rooms (four posters or half testers) fine art, antiques, splendid views all combined with environmental credentials and a friendly relaxed atmosphere.
bodyContent: The House Bloomfield House, a Georgian detached Grade II listed building, has elegant and romantic rooms (four posters or half testers) fine art, antiques, splendid views all combined with environmental credentials and a friendly relaxed atmosphere. The house is set well back from a quiet road. Well behaved children and pets are welcome, with dog friendly rooms. The Breakfast Their traditional full English breakfasts are freshly cooked to order and served from 7.30 am until 11 am. Ingredients are mostly organic, fair-traded and provided by local suppliers, including homemade preserves and artisan breads. Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options are always available. The Parking They have free off-street parking and an electric car charging point for their guests use. There is easy access to the city centre via a regular bus service which stops within a few feet of the entrance to the property. The walk into town is a downhill stroll of 20 mins, on the way back up – jump on the bus or grab a cab! . The Bedrooms All bedrooms have en-suite facilities and come with the usuals – TV, hospitality tray, toiletries, hair dryer. The guest bedrooms are situated on the second floor, there is no lift so they are not suitable for those with mobility issues. They are, of course, happy to help you up the stairs with your luggage. On the upside this does mean each room has far reaching views. Please note, for those with allergies , that this is a family home and there are both cats and dogs on the premises. The cats do not have access to the guest bedrooms (nor do their own dogs for that matter). DISCOUNTS Any mid-week stay (Sun-Thurs ) will attract a £10 discount. Please quote ‘Stay in Bath’ when booking (by phone) on 01225 420105. Any on-line booking – applicable discounts will be deducted upon check-out. (This sadly cannot be used in addition with other special offers.) They also offer discounts to those arriving in Bath by train or bus. Discounts do not apply to Bank Holidays or one night Saturday bookings which are, on occasions, available.

bodyContent: Maddy and Leigh welcome you to The Methuen Arms, an award winning Great British inn where hospitality meets fabulous food & drink at a relaxed pace. Set immediately beside the stately home and beautiful grounds of Corsham Court, and just eight miles from the enchanting city of Bath, Corsham is a hidden gem of charming Georgian buildings, cobbled streets, Almshouses, parkland and more, making this historic market town a must-see place to visit and stay.

title: Mendip Basecamp
subtitle: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure campsite in the Mendip Hills...
bodyContent: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure camp in the Mendip Hills National Landscape - just minutes from the M5 and Weston-super-Mare. Surrounded by ancient woodland you can pitch where you like, park right by your tent and enjoy evenings around the campfire. Well-behaved dogs are welcome! With no check-out time, you can leave whenever you are ready. Mendip Basecamp is camping how it should be: rural, laid-back and relaxed but with essential luxuries. Usually reserved for schools and private groups, in 2020, Mendip opened Basecamp up to families for the very first time- and hasn’t looked back since. Public bookings are available throughout the summer holidays and summer weekends. Bring your own tent or campervan, book bell tents, glamphouses or stay in Mendip Lodge (with free breakfast). Facilities include hot showers, clean flushing toilets, a camp shop, a country Lodge with a cider garden (and live music), an onsite activity centre, USB charging and WIFI. Free activities throughout the summer include live music, orienteering, circus skills, treasure hunts, free climbing tower and nature craft. The campsite is less than a 5-minute woodland walk from Mendip Activity Centre, home to over 20 different adventurous, outdoor activities including rock climbing, kayaking, archery, frisbee golf and air rifle. New for 2026, Mendip Basecamp is launching Mendip Mini Fests - six family-friendly festivals running throughout the summer holiday weekends. Great entertainment, headline bands, local talent competition, and more! Included at no extra cost, exclusively for campsite guests.
tagline: Mendip Basecamp was delighted to be awarded the Gold campsite at the 2023-2024

title: Withy Mills Farm
subtitle: Four sympathetically restored stone farm buildings, now providing beautifully appointed contemporary accommodation.
bodyContent: Withy Mills Farm has four romantic cottages in a secluded rural location with stunning views across the Mendip Hills. A twenty minute drive takes you to the city of Bath or Wells. It’s a great location for a family holiday or a romantic get away. Close to two popular wedding venues, Priston Mill and Radford Farm. Whippletree Cottage has two bedrooms and sleeps four people, while the other properties each have one bedroom and are designed for two people sharing. We can provide travel cots and high chairs etc for those travelling with a baby. All the cottages have the luxury of underfloor heating provided by our ground source heat pump. Wharfingers and The Engine House have whirlpool baths. Whippletree, Wharfingers and The Engine House also have a wood burning fire, ideal for cosy winter evenings. Please see our individual entries for each cottage or visit our website www.withymillsfarm.co.uk for further details. The four properties are Whippletree Cottage, The Engine House, Wharfingers Cottage and Barleycorn.

title: 2 Crescent Gardens
subtitle: 2 Crescent Gardens is a stylish guest house, which is close to the world famous Royal Crescent and within walking distance of all Bath’s main attractions.
bodyContent: 2 Crescent Gardens is a stylish guest house, which is close to the world famous Royal Crescent and within walking distance of all Bath’s main attractions. We reopened in June 2012 after a major refurbishment programme and we think you will be impressed by the results. Our individually-styled rooms are relaxing and comfortable and the perfect place to unwind. All our rooms are ensuite and we serve a delicious breakfast to start your day. Guests can reserve a parking space, in advance, for a small fee. We are also a short walk or taxi ride from Bath Spa train station
