title: Swan Hotel Wells
subtitle: The Swan combines the beauty of a historic building with all the advantages of a modern hotel. The hotel is a striking, idyllic 15th-century coaching inn set in the timeless city of Wells, opposite the famous Wells Cathedral. The city itself is full of culture and reminders of older times, a beautiful location to visit.
bodyContent: This hotel has a fantastic location in the city of Wells, being right in the centre with plenty of shops and places to visit. For 600 years they have had many guests enjoy this wonderful inn, with a few famous faces too. The Cathedral is directly opposite the hotel and you can admire its magnificence from our outside seating area, directly leading into the Cathedral gardens. For film buffs, this hotel also had various scenes filmed here for the well known Simon Pegg film ‘Hot Fuzz’ The bedrooms at The Swan are traditional, stylish and comfortable but still offer all the modern amenities you need to enjoy a relaxing stay in Wells. Some of our rooms have a stunning view of the famous Wells Cathedral, like our gorgeous suite with three separate luxurious rooms.

title: Flickers Tent - Tone Valley View Glamping
subtitle: Off-grid stargazing belle tent on an adult only site, with wood burning fire and stargazing roof you will feel really connected with nature. Private bathroom with shower and kitchenette. Outside there is your own wood burning hot tub and fire pit. The view is truly spectacular across the Tone Valley.
bodyContent: The tent is a lotus 5m Stargazer bell tent with Outbacker wood burners. It is truly beautiful, and they make the most of the spectacular views and stars at night. The tent is off grid, and we have a small solar system with batteries that provides power. It has a double bed. All linens and towels are provided. We even include extra blankets and an electric blanket. It is about 12 meters away from one of our other units but there are separated with a privacy fence. It has a fire pit and a wood burning hot tub. The hot tub will need to be lit and heated by you during your stay. In summer, it takes 1.5–2 hours to heat from cold (less if it’s already warm). We can pre-light it and bring it to temperature before your arrival for a £30 charge. A bin of wood is provided with every stay, and additional bags are available for £7 each. We can also offer packages for special occasions, contact us for details. In addition to this you get your own stable! The horses have moved out and a new bathroom and Kitchenette (Fridge with ice box, Sink, Twin hot plate, Toaster and Kettle) have been installed. The stable is insulated and have mains electric heating and electric hot water. The tent is a short walk from the stables, so we have a stone path connecting them.

title: Collie Shepherd Hut
subtitle: Collie Shepherd Hut is a peaceful countryside retreat in Somerset, offering a cosy and romantic escape for two. Enjoy a private wood-fired hot tub, stunning views across the Somerset Levels and thoughtful touches throughout. Perfect for relaxing breaks, stargazing nights and unwinding in comfort close to nature and local attractions.
bodyContent: Collie Shepherd Hut is an exclusive countryside retreat in Somerset, designed for couples seeking a luxurious and intimate escape. Set in a peaceful rural location with uninterrupted views across the Somerset Levels, it offers a restorative setting where guests can slow down, unwind and reconnect with nature. Beautifully styled throughout, the hut blends rustic charm with elevated comfort. The king-size bed sits within a cosy alcove, dressed in quality linens for a restful night’s sleep. A well-equipped kitchenette includes a microwave oven, double-ring gas hob, fridge with top freezer compartment and essentials for simple self-catering. Guests are welcomed with a complimentary breakfast pack, adding a thoughtful and indulgent start to their stay. The ensuite shower room with flushing toilet, along with fluffy bathrobes, slippers and towels — including an additional set for the hot tub — adds further comfort. Outside, your private wood-fired hot tub with jacuzzi spa jets awaits, perfectly positioned for slow evenings spent watching Somerset’s glowing sunsets fade into star-filled skies. Firewood and everything needed for your stay are provided, ensuring a seamless and relaxing experience from the moment you arrive.Ideal for romantic getaways, anniversaries and special occasions, Collie Shepherd Hut offers privacy, calm and complete escape from everyday life. Surrounded by Somerset’s natural beauty, the hut sits beside a working farm, offering an authentic and peaceful countryside setting where guests can enjoy scenic walks, explore charming nearby villages or simply relax in total seclusion. A refined rural retreat where luxury, romance and nature come together effortlessly.

title: Exhibition: Take a Walk in Our Shoes
subtitle: Take a Walk in Our Shoes is a vibrant exhibition showcasing the work of three local artists whose practices explore self‑expression, belonging and the stories we carry with us and would you know, two of them even draw shoes!
bodyContent: Take a Walk in Our Shoes is a vibrant exhibition showcasing the work of three local artists whose practices explore self‑expression, belonging and the stories we carry with us. Running throughout June. Exploring how art can be a tool for self‑expression, social development and how creativity can make space for every voice. Plus have a go yourself! Every Wednesday morning visitors are invited to drop into the education room for an art workshop run by one of the artists. Plus on12, 20 and 27 June join a creative, hands-on workshop where photography and collage come together and using a mix of printed images, personal photography, and found materials, you’ll create your own unique photographic map of a place that matters to you. Workshops and activities are free to Shoemakers Museum visitors and materials are provided.

title: Clay saltmarsh bubbles workshop
subtitle: Capture the marshes in clay, with this hands-on workshop with artist Margaret Micklewright
bodyContent: Can you reflect the nature of the saltmarsh in a clay bubble? Join artist Margaret to look closely at the vegetation, bird life and creatures that call Steart Marshes their home. Decorate a clay circle to capture what you see and hear. Press grasses and other vegetation into clay, draw bird footprints or insects, to make a composition that reflects your view of the saltmarsh. This workshop is open to all ages and is a drop-in session. All materials will be provided. Please note – we will be working outside on the nature reserve, so dress accordingly, sturdy shoes are recommended. Where to meet: Meet at the roundhouse, WWT Steart Marshes, Bridgwater, Somerset, TA5 2PU. (Ask a member of staff for directions).

title: The Art Bank -Where culture means business!
subtitle: Pauline Burr visits Art Bank in Shepton Mallet.
bodyContent: It was a damp and dreary Mendip morning in March when we arranged to visit Shepton Mallet to meet the team at the Art Bank. You know, one of those monochrome weather days, where you feel like the rain has just washed away the last dregs of any colour. We found the building, the old HSBC bank on the High Street; a formidable stone facade befitting its previous use. We let ourselves in - and we knew we weren’t in Kansas anymore! Wonderfully collaged life-size mannequins, artworks made from discarded children’s toys and a tree growing through the middle of the room, we entered a wonderland of creativity and imagination. The place was buzzing with activity and chatter. “Fridays are our busy day!” We were greeted warmly by Lucy, one of the Art Bank directors, and were shortly joined by co-directors Dimi and James. While one of the regulars tinkled on the ivories of an upright piano in the corner of the room, we slumped down on a slightly battered sofa, to hear about the Art Bank venture. The Art Bank is home to the Rubbish Art Project and the Art Bank Cafe and Bar; it welcomes people of all ages and walks of life and goes out of its way to celebrate diversity and inclusivity. It started through a chance meeting of two like minded souls at the Glastonbury Festival. After working in London for a number of years, Lucy Smith had returned to her native Somerset where, in 2005, she started working for the Glastonbury Festival, first in the press office and then as a co-ordinator of the festival’s green initiatives. She was involved in everything from helping with the introduction of compost toilets to running environmental campaigns aimed at festival goers, including programming and commissioning environmental messaging around the stages. Her commitment to consumer waste reduction and her firm belief in creativity as a catalyst for social cohesion prompted her to set up the Rubbish Art Project as a creative hub in Shepton Mallet. It was either a fortunate stroke of serendipity or the fabled magic of Glastonbury when Lucy met Dimitris Koutroumpasat the Festival and they came up with the idea of the Art Bank. Originally from Athens, but resident in the UK for more than 15 years and Somerset for 6, Dimitris is an artist with a passion for collage, photography and the power of nature. His friend and creative collaborator, James Barker, is the third member of the team. Following a career in international marketing and recruitment in the higher education sector, James became a full-time carer for his parents. Recognising the difficulties faced by people in similar situations, James secured grant funding to run a series of creative writing workshops for carers. He then followed this up with writing courses for people over 6o and disabled adults. For his own part James is about to finish his Phd in Creative Writing and has worked with Dimitris on a book and a performance piece highlighting some of the issues that carers experience. About five years ago the trio started the Art Bank, sharing their range of skills, knowledge and lived experiences with the communities in and around Shepton, aiming to operate a venue where people of all backgrounds, abilities and ages could come together to learn new skills, interact as a community, enjoy all aspects of the arts and have some fun! They now run a regular programme of arts activities and entertainment, and it’s a mark of their success to see how well it has developed as a integral part of the local cultural landscape. The cafe is open from 10am most days (closed Tuesdays and Sundays), serves a range of vegetarian and vegan food and local sourced produce. It’s licensed from midday and operates as a bar at the end of the week when there’s an entertaining and diverse programme of live music, theatre, comedy, spoken word and open mic events. During the day there’s a whole range of creative activities from watercolour painting and family signing sessions to knitting and crochet. All costs are kept low so there are no barriers to participation, anyone wanting to lead a workshop is offered space for free in the cafe and on Friday mornings the stage is given over to local artists and craftspeople as a commission-free marketplace for their work. The space is a melting pot for creative collaborations, there’s a clear “Art for All” approach, the programme appealing to as broad a range of people as possible and are always open to feedback and new ideas about different activities and events. With a strong belief that creativity is key to the health and well-being of a community, Art Bank works with local GP services, schools, local councils and a number of charities in delivering projects that support vulnerable people; on Mondays they run art and well-being sessions for adults with learning differences and people with dementia and memory loss enjoy “Love to Move” sessions on Tuesdays . Projects are not limited to the Art Bank itself, the group was successful in achieving funding from the National Lottery Platinum Jubilee Fund to involve the community in creating a giant living sculpture celebrating Community Spirit. The annual “Sheptopoly” event transforms the town centre into an interactive board game; now in its third year the event brings people together to learn about and celebrate some of the different cultures that make up the town’s population, with an interactive programme of music, performance, food and games. This year’s gathering included Romanian dances, Filipino games, painting for Ukraine, learning about the Greeks' contributions, deciphering the Korean alphabet, brushing up knowledge of Poland, playing "bella" bingo - Italian style and enjoying music from all around the world. With its history of wool, cloth and silk production and later brewing and England’s oldest prison, Shepton Mallet has always been recognised as a working town. Like many similar places, it has suffered neglect and, some would say, bad planning decisions. A development in the 1970s attempted to regenerate the town centre with new retail properties and a state of the art theatre complex. Like many asset based cultural regeneration projects it has struggled to really engage with the community and the theatre is currently empty and faces an uncertain future. In its favour, however, the town is now attracting quite a diverse population. Housing prices are relatively low for the area so people who can’t afford to live in nearby Wells or Bruton look to Shepton Mallet as an option. For cultural regeneration to work it needs to be embedded in the community. Lucy, Dimitris and James have a passion for people and the arts; they understand how culture and creativity can help to energise and galvanise a community and improve both the social and economic health of their town. With initiatives like the Art Bank Shepton can face a bright future! www.artbank.org.uk

title: Summer family fun at the Bishop's Palace
subtitle: Entertain the kids with space to run and play and a new splash play area. Plus see history come to life with displays and re-enactments on special event days.
bodyContent: Fancy a trip to a beautiful summer garden - but not with moaning kids in tow?! The Bishop's Palace can make that happen... Beautiful gardens are a lovely place to spend time over the summer - but can often lose their relaxing air when the kids are bored and just want to get the walk over with (we all know there's nothing like your own child's whinge to cut through a moment of calm). The Bishop's Palace has been deliberately sculpted to offer something a little different – and because of that, it manages to be a sanctuary for adults as well as fun for kids. The ancient site and RHS partner gardens provide a great backdrop for a family day out with lots to look at and discover. Ramparts, towers, poo-sticks bridges, ducks, swans and winding paths to explore plus a summer trail all about pollinators will keep kids entertained and busy while parents pause and enjoy the gardens. The recent addition of a new splash zone, plus the return of the ever-popular water wheel within the Dragon's Lair play area , provide stimulating entertainment that challenges both mind and body, especially on a hot sunny summer-holiday day. And if it's not so cheery outdoors (or even if it is!) the Palace itself is a captivating way to spend time. With audio guides especially for kids, dressing up, the cabinet of curiosities and a new 'table of games'. Kids will be happy to potter and play while adults take time to enjoy the beautiful surroundings and unwind. Plus, throughout the summer, special History Alive event days add extra excitement to your visit - and can't fail to entertain even the most determinedly grumpy child! On 1 st – 2 nd August and experience the sights, sounds and spirit of the 1940s with our Britain at War Day. With costumed performers, authentic activities and a welcoming family-friendly atmosphere. Or pop along on August bank holiday weekend ( 29 th - 31 st August ) and enjoy a medieval re-enactment including domestic crafts, camp skills and a bustling encampment experience. And on 12 th September it’s the turn of the Vikings! Including military drills and skimishes plus camp cooking and domestic living examples, this is one not to miss! All History Alive events are included as part of a normal admission ticket (and free to Annual Pass holders and Friends of the Palace) so you can enjoy the event as well as all the usual garden and Palace access. Gardens and Palace are open daily, 9.30am - 5.30pm. The Bishop’s Table cafe is open every day 9.30 - 5.30pm, last orders 5pm. Breakfast 9.30 - 11.30am, lunch 11.30am - 3pm. Please check our website for more details www.bishopspalace.org.uk

title: Centuries-old garden features have emerged beneath the lawns of The Bishop’s Palace and Gardens following the recent spell of hot, dry weather.
subtitle: The remarkable patterns, which are particularly clear when viewed from above, have been captured using drone photography.
bodyContent: The prolonged sunshine has revealed intriguing outlines in the grass in front of the ruined Great Hall, giving a glimpse of historic garden features thought to form part of the Palace’s 18th-century Dutch-style gardens. The remarkable patterns, which are particularly clear when viewed from above, have been captured using drone photography. They show lines believed to mark former gravel paths, with areas between them likely to have contained neatly clipped grass or box hedging. There are very few records of the gardens at this time, so these photographs are particularly interesting as they contribute to a lost historical record. An L-shaped feature visible on the South Lawn also appears to correspond with a water feature that we know once formed part of the garden. Although periods of dry weather have affected the Palace gardens before, the features have not previously been noticed with this level of clarity. Drone photography has provided a striking new perspective, making the patterns much easier to identify. Though not confirmed, the phenomenon is thought to be caused by differences in the ground beneath the grass. Remnants of old paths, walls and other structures can affect drainage, soil heat and restrict the depth of grass roots, causing the grass immediately above them to react differently during prolonged hot, dry conditions. James Cross, Head Gardener at The Bishop’s Palace and Gardens , said: “It’s fascinating to see these features appearing so clearly in the grass. We know that there was an 18th-century Dutch-style garden here, but have very few details more than that. Seeing these outlines emerge gives us a wonderful glimpse of how this part of the Palace grounds may once have looked. “The gardens have changed enormously over the centuries, so it’s quite extraordinary to think that traces of their earlier layouts are still sitting just beneath our feet. Sometimes it takes something as simple as a spell of very dry weather, and a view from above, to bring that history back into sight.” At the time these gardens were laid out, the walls of the immense medieval Great Hall were still standing, although its roof had already gone. Today, its dramatic ruins form one of the most recognisable features of The Bishop’s Palace. The discovery addsmore detail to the intriguing history of the Palace gardens, where there is evidence of gardening stretching back to even before Bishop Jocelin began work on the Palace in around 1206. The Bishop’s Palace and Gardens is home to 14 acres of RHS Partner Gardens in the heart of Wells, Somerset.

title: Taunton Visitor Centre
subtitle: For queries or assistance with finding things to do, booking travel and event tickets, general information and queries regarding the Visit Taunton website please contact the Taunton Visitor Centre as detailed below.
bodyContent: The Taunton Visitor Centre, based in the western wing of the landmark Market House, is the place to go to when you want to discover how to make the most of your time in Taunton. The Visitor Centre welcomes over 50,000 visitors and locals through its doors every year and the team is on hand to help you plan the perfect trip! The county town has plenty to offer from individual boutiques to historic architecture, modern dining to traditional tea rooms, and unspoilt views to the Blackdown Hills and Quantock Hills (both National Landscapes). Indeed Taunton offers a wide mix of activities, attractions and events and the Visitor Centre team are on hand to help you plan the perfect trip! Services offered: The Taunton Visitor Centre holds information on a wide and varied range of things to do within Taunton and the surrounding areas. The Visitor Centre Box Office offers tickets for most local and regional events taking place, including the hugely popular Taunton Flower Show. We are a box office for the Brewhouse Theatre and Tacchi-Morris Arts Centre in Taunton and the Playhouse Theatre in Weston-super-Mare. If you're looking for that special "experience" gift then give the gift of theatre with our Theatre Tokens Gift Cards. The Travel Centre acts as an agent for Bakers Dolphin, Berrys Coaches, Falcon & Megabus bus services, Holiday Extras and National Express. As well as the booking service we also offer friendly advice for local transport, parking and accommodation to help make your trip stress-free. We also offer multiple advertising and marketing opportunities to local businesses, events organisers, charities and more. Souvenirs and Publications: The Visitor Centre shop is bursting with products that will help you take home a taste of Taunton, including locally produced preserves, hand-crafted cards and a variety of colourful souvenirs. We also stock a large range of local maps, guides and books to help you truly discover Taunton and the surrounding areas.

title: Middlewick Holiday Cottages
subtitle: Self catering cottages in Glastonbury. Perfect short break in Somerset with indoor pool.
bodyContent: A secluded holiday resort just minutes from Glastonbury town centre, with stunning views of Glastonbury Tor and the Mendip Hills. Set on 16 peaceful acres, The Middlewick offers self-catering accommodation in 10 cottages converted from original 17th-century farm buildings, 3 log cabins and 3 glamping pods. Our properties range from 1 to 5 bedrooms, offering plenty of choice for couples, families, friends and groups looking for country getaway. Many are dog friendly. We have a Café , Farm Shop and Spa on site – all of which are open to day visitors as well as guests staying with us. Our site, including our indoor heated pool and steam room, is powered by renewable energy, and Spa treatments take place in our cosy Shepherd’s Huts. Surrounded by apple orchards, this is a real escape to the Somerset countryside – with plenty of space to roam in the beauty of nature. Visitors can walk to Glastonbury Tor easily in under 30 minutes. There’s so much to explore nearby, with Glastonbury Tor, Chalice Well and Gardens, Glastonbury Abbey and Clark’s Village on our doorstep. Glastonbury is a unique market town bustling with unusual shops and alternative events. The Avalon Marshes Nature Reserve, Cathedral City of Wells and Cheddar Gorge are within easy driving distance from The Middlewick. Somerset is known for its food, music and outstanding natural beauty – and this is the ideal base from which to explore the best of the county.

title: Burys Cottage
subtitle: Burys Cottage has a cosy and romantic feel to it. The location is at the end of a row of other cottages.
bodyContent: The open-plan kitchen and living room is perfect for quiet nights in, after a day out exploring the area. The kitchen is equipped with everything you should need to make some delicious meals. The bedroom has a 4-poster bed. It is made up with fresh, white linen ready for your arrival. They provide a hand towel and bath towel per person. There is plenty of storage and hanging space. There is an en-suite bathroom, with a shower-head over the bath. On the other side of the patio is the Indoor Heated Pool and Games Room, which is available for guests to use during their stay. Burys Cottage which sleeps 2 people is located on the edge of the village ‘Winsley’, 5 miles from Bath and 2 miles from Bradford on Avon. There are plenty of walks right from the doorstep, a Farm Shop, village shop and village pub all within 1 mile. The cottage is dog friendly, welcoming dogs for a small extra fee - check their website for more details.

title: The Pasta Laboratory
subtitle: A pasta making class with Federico Uliana at the Pasta Laboratory in Bath might just teach you more about Italian tradition and culture than a guided walk around the ancient Roman Baths.
bodyContent: Federico’s heritage charm and passion for food make him the perfect teacher for those of us looking try our hand at making fresh fantastically filled tortellini, unbelievably long linguini, and mind-blowingly curly macaroni. His cool and calm instructions knead all the stresses out of the art of pasta making and can make even the least culinarily skilled, of us, feel like a master chef. Though I reckon the red wine and arancini balls, on offer during his classes, also aid in creating this welcoming and serene learning environment. Despite the pressures put on by the pandemic, Pasta Uliana has thrived in its quiet spot, on Camden Road , and many students have graduated from Federico’s classes and gone on to severely impress guests at their next dinner parties Testimonies from his website include: "What a great way to spend an afternoon! Federico provided a great two-hour pasta making experience that was hugely enjoyable and resulted in enough pretty perfect pasta for a family meal that evening.” But it’s not just the family who can enjoy an afternoon with Federico. He offers a range of classes whether you’re planning a Hen Party, team building event, work Christmas-do, or a children’s party. Federico says, “It’s accessible for everyone, not just foodies.” Federico also has a background in event organisation and loves a party vibe, so you are in good hands no matter whether you are there to learn, connect or simply have fun. He can even crown a “Pasta Master” and “Pasta Corporate Master” or award a “Pass-Ta Bouquet” to the winning Hen at your event, adding a fun element of healthy competition to your party. “I love the classes! It’s something I have always wanted to do.” he says. “We do everything in two and half hours, or maybe three if it’s a Saturday and the wine is flowing, and I pride myself in making sure you walk out of here and you can make Pasta!”. So, if you are looking for a different and exciting way to get in touch with Bath’s Italian side, we suggest finding an afternoon, to join Federico, for a bespoke pasta-making class and become a master chef in a matter of hours. You can follow Federico’s business on social media here or you can book straight away from his website, here .

title: Willow Barn
subtitle: Comfortable luxury barn which has recently been converted to a high standard.
bodyContent: Willow Barn is a comfortable welcoming 4* barn which has been converted to a high standard and offering luxury self-catering rental accommodation. It is situated down a private drive in the grounds of a 17th Century Grade II listed Cotswold stone farmhouse, overlooking the Wiltshire countryside. The barn sleeps 4 and has an open plan kitchen, dining, living area with oak beams and a woodburning log fire. There is a large walled garden, tennis court and private parking. Perfectly situated for visiting the National Trust properties in this area including Lacock village and Abbey, Great Chalfield Manor, The Courts in Holt and Dyrham Park.The World Heritage city of Bath is 10 miles away. Willow Barn is an ideal base for shopping, walking, cycling, golf and equestrian activities. The holiday barn is adjacent to West Wilts Equestrian Centre. Local wedding venues include Wick Farm, Woolley Grange Hotel and the Tythe Barn in Bradford on Avon.

title: Abbey Rise
subtitle: Abbey Rise is a large Victorian terraced townhouse offering panoramic city views and guaranteed off road private parking throughout your stay. It is just an 8-minute stroll from the train and bus station and hub of the city.
bodyContent: Abbey Rise is a large Victorian terraced townhouse offering panoramic city views and guaranteed off road private parking throughout your stay. It is just an 8-minute stroll from the train and bus station and hub of the city. Bath is Katherine’s home town and after travelling around the world working in large prestigious hotels she was drawn back to this cosmopolitan and beautiful UNESCO city, where she decided to open up her own bed and breakfast. Living and working as part of the Royal Household at Buckingham Palace has left its mark and Katherine continues to maintain those standards in her own home, where guests are treated to crisply ironed sheets, fluffy towels and wonderfully comfortable beds whilst enjoying a homely and welcoming atmosphere. Katherine has been running Abbey Rise for a number of years now and frequently welcomes returning guests who will always find some new and interesting change or addition-though Katherine’s famous homemade brownies and cakes are always on the menu!
tagline: Abbey Rise is a large Victorian terraced townhouse offering panoramic city views

title: The Lordleaze Hotel
subtitle: Nestled in the Somerset countryside on the outskirts of Chard on the border of Dorset & Devon, our hotel offers the perfect sanctuary to unwind. Surrounded by heritage sites, traditional farm shops, and quaint rural villages. Explore the rolling green hills, a short drive to beaches at Lyme Regis and Charmouth,.
bodyContent: Our Family run hotel has 23 bedrooms all equipped with superfast Wi-Fi, Smart TV, tea and coffee and ensuite bathrooms. A scrumptious breakfast is included with all direct bookings and our kitchen serves up delicious lunches and evening meals in the bar and restaurant. The historic coastal town of Lyme Regis is just 20 minutes by car. We have a perfect mix of family, double or twin rooms. Or, if you want to treat yourself, check in to our four-poster suite. Rooms with disabled facilities are also available, just let us know and dogs are welcome with advance notice.

title: YHA Cheddar
subtitle: Nestled at the foot of the iconic Cheddar Gorge, YHA Cheddar offers the perfect base for exploring one of England’s most awe-inspiring natural landscapes.
bodyContent: Nestled at the foot of the iconic Cheddar Gorge, YHA Cheddar offers the perfect base for exploring one of England’s most awe-inspiring natural landscapes. With its warm, welcoming atmosphere and unbeatable location, this modernised Victorian hostel is ideal for schools, outdoor groups, and families seeking a group getaway. YHA Cheddar is currently available for Group Bookings (with catering and/or activities) and Exclusive Hire stays. Accommodation and Facilities YHA Cheddar is split across two charming buildings, offering a variety of room sizes to suit your group's needs. YHA Cheddar sleeps up to a total of 59 people. There is a capacity of up to 38 in the Main Building, and up to 21 in the Barton Building. Both buildings can be booked separately or together. With self-catering kitchens, social dining spaces, cosy lounges, and free Wi-Fi throughout, this hostel is designed for comfort and connection. Guests also benefit from secure cycle storage, free on-site parking, accessible rooms, and a peaceful garden space. An Incredible Location Set in the heart of Cheddar village and just minutes from the famous Cheddar Gorge and Caves, this hostel puts you right on the edge of adventure. The Mendip Hills and Somerset Levels offer spectacular walking and cycling routes, while Wookey Hole and the seaside town of Weston-super-Mare are just a short drive away. Part of the Mendip Adventure Family – and a YHA Partner Hostel YHA Cheddar is proudly part of the Mendip Adventure family—home to Mendip Activity Centre, SUP Bristol, Outdoor Instructor Training, and Mendip Basecamp. As a YHA Partner hostel, it shares the same mission of opening up access to nature, adventure, and lifelong learning. Groups staying here can enhance their experience with instructor-led outdoor activities like rock climbing, caving, kayaking, and hiking—all led by qualified, passionate instructors from the Mendip team. Book Your Stay Whether you're planning a school residential, a family celebration, or an outdoor club trip, YHA Cheddar offers the perfect combination of nature, adventure, and comfort—all in one unforgettable Somerset setting.

title: Mendip Basecamp
subtitle: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure campsite in the Mendip Hills...
bodyContent: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure camp in the Mendip Hills National Landscape - just minutes from the M5 and Weston-super-Mare. Surrounded by ancient woodland you can pitch where you like, park right by your tent and enjoy evenings around the campfire. Well-behaved dogs are welcome! With no check-out time, you can leave whenever you are ready. Mendip Basecamp is camping how it should be: rural, laid-back and relaxed but with essential luxuries. Usually reserved for schools and private groups, in 2020, Mendip opened Basecamp up to families for the very first time- and hasn’t looked back since. Public bookings are available throughout the summer holidays and summer weekends. Bring your own tent or campervan, book bell tents, glamphouses or stay in Mendip Lodge (with free breakfast). Facilities include hot showers, clean flushing toilets, a camp shop, a country Lodge with a cider garden (and live music), an onsite activity centre, USB charging and WIFI. Free activities throughout the summer include live music, orienteering, circus skills, treasure hunts, free climbing tower and nature craft. The campsite is less than a 5-minute woodland walk from Mendip Activity Centre, home to over 20 different adventurous, outdoor activities including rock climbing, kayaking, archery, frisbee golf and air rifle. New for 2026, Mendip Basecamp is launching Mendip Mini Fests - six family-friendly festivals running throughout the summer holiday weekends. Great entertainment, headline bands, local talent competition, and more! Included at no extra cost, exclusively for campsite guests.
tagline: Mendip Basecamp was delighted to be awarded the Gold campsite at the 2023-2024

title: Raffle's Lodge - Tone valley view glamping
subtitle: Raffles Lodge is a truly relaxing and beautiful stay awaits you. We are an adults only site.
bodyContent: Raffle’s lodge has full LED lights and sockets so you can charge phones. We are off grid so power is provided by our solar panels and batteries nearby. Therefore we can not run hairdryers or kettles in the unit.....however you do get a Stables with your booking. It has been converted in to your own bathroom and kitchen unit with full running hot water and mains electric. The hot tub will need to be lit and heated by you during your stay. In summer, it takes 1.5–2 hours to heat from cold (less if it’s already warm), and in winter, it takes 3–4 hours due to the cooler temperatures. We can pre-light it and bring it to temperature before your arrival for a £30 charge. A bin of wood is provided with every stay, and additional bags are available for £7 each. We can also offer packages for special occasions like birthdays and anniversary. Message for details. Your stable! The horses have moved out and a new bathroom (Shower, Toilet, Sink, Towel rad) and Kitchenette (Fridge with ice box, Sink, Twin hot plate, Toaster and Kettle) have been installed. Each is dedicated to a pod, so no sharing needed. They have been insulated and have mains electric heating and electric hot water. The lodge is a short walk from the stables, so we have a stone path connecting them and we give you a lantern. There is also a carpark area with parking for one car per tent.

title: World Cup 2026: England V Ghana

title: Nicko McBrain – An Evening In Conversation With
subtitle: Following the recent announcement of Hello Boys and Girls!
bodyContent: Following the recent announcement of Hello Boys and Girls!, Nicko McBrain’s thrilling, hilarious and deeply personal autobiography which will be published on 22nd October 2026, the much-loved drummer will now be taking to the road on a spoken word tour. Starting in Frankfurt on October 26th, Nicko McBrain will be visiting theatres across Germany, Netherlands, Scandinavia, Ireland and the UK, regaling audiences with colourful stories of a life well-lived. Featuring tales from behind the drum-stool of one of Britain’s biggest ever bands, alongside lessons learned from his eventful youth, his triumphant highs and deepest lows, this is a chance for fans to get up-close-and-personal with one of the most famous and admired men in rock history. Born in Hackney, East London in 1952, Michael “Nicko” McBrain always wanted to be a drummer, practising on his mother’s pots and pans until his father bought him his first drumkit when he was 11 years old. Playing initially in school bands, covering The Beatles and The Rolling Stones, by 14 he had become semi-professional, performing in wedding bands around London. Inspired by jazz as much as rock music, Nicko played with the likes of Streetwalkers, Pat Travers Band and Trust whilst honing his craft doing session work amongst the highly competitive mean streets and studios of London’s Soho. However, when he joined Iron Maiden in 1982 he quickly became one of the most recognisable and influential drummers in the world. Through his powerful and brilliant drumming style – full of flair and technique

title: Skerryvore
subtitle: For more than 20 years, Skerryvore have been captivating audiences
bodyContent: For more than 20 years, Skerryvore have been captivating audiences with their unique blend of traditional Scottish music and contemporary rock. Formed on the Isle of Tiree, the multi-award-winning eight-piece are renowned for their electrifying live performances and infectious energy that has seen them recognised as Scotland’s Live Act of the Year a record-breaking 4 times. This special appearance forms part of the band’s Beautiful Mistakes album tour. Produced by Jamie Squire, widely known as the “fifth member” of The 1975, Beautiful Mistakes captures the warmth, musicianship, and spirit that have made Skerryvore one of Scotland’s most celebrated live acts.

title: Summer of Play 2026: Knights' Quest
subtitle: Dunster Castle's gardens are transforming into a medieval playground this summer!
bodyContent: Young adventurers are invited to play their way around Dunster Castle’s knight‑themed activity zones and earn their title as a Knight of Dunster Castle. Come back week after week to enjoy a changing programme of hands‑on fun, from archery and forest school to sword‑fighting knights and more! Head to our 'Tournament Arena' on green court where you can hone your knightly skills in archery, hobby-horse jousting, wooden sword play, target games and more. Don't forget to capture a photo in the stocks! Step onto the dancefloor at 'Knight's Court'. Practice your jester skills and become a star of the court in this outdoor performance space. Finally, head over to 'Camp Dunster' to immerse yourself in the River Gardens natural play area. Become a knight of the 'oblong table' and design your very own coat-of-arms.

title: Latest phase of £25m redevelopment at Unity Beach unveiled by former Olympic swimmer Baroness Sharron Davies MBE
subtitle: The new lido has a capacity of just more than 400 and boasts two heated pools, one specially designed for children.
bodyContent: The latest phase of a £25m redevelopment of the Unity Beach family holiday park in Somerset was officially unveiled by former Olympic swimmer Baroness Sharron Davies MBE on Saturday. The resort’s new lido, water park and festival gardens came at a cost of £11m and mean Unity Beach now has a huge indoor and outdoor swimming complex with large family spaces. The new lido has a capacity of just more than 400 and boasts two heated pools, one specially designed for children. This is on top of Unity Beach’s 25m six-lane indoor pool, an indoor splash zone for Under-16s, two indoor water slides, and three more slides outside. Baroness Sharron, who won an Olympics silver medal in the 400m individual medley in 1980 as well as two Commonwealth Games gold medals, is an advocate for ensuring there are ample venues for swimming lessons and families to use the water to have fun and stay fit. At the opening she said: “At a time when we are seeing the amount of swimming facilities in the country dwindle – we’ve lost 500 since 2010 - to have Unity Holidays investing millions in pools and lidos across the country, and creating jobs for local people, is tremendous. “They are enabling children to gain water confidence and learn to swim, while giving families a stunning location to enjoy amazing spaces to play and relax. “Our seaside towns need this injection of funds, and I was honoured to officially open the lido and water park in Brean while also seeing first-hand how impressive what a modern, 21st-century family holiday park has to offer can be.” With more than 250 sun loungers, 15 cabanas and a giant TV screen, the new lido means families have the space and facilities to enjoy the outdoor pools but also relax. It is open only to caravan owners and holidaymakers until 1pm, after which local residents can pay a small entry fee if space permits. For refreshments, the lido has The Snack Shack, which serves food such as burgers, paninis, nachos, waffles and even whippy ice cream doughnut sandwiches. Drinks on offer include draught beers, cocktails, slush, hot drinks, iced coffees, coolers and soft drinks. For a real treat, a cabana can be booked at a cost of £65 for the day, allowing guests to enjoy their own private area complete with loungers and shade (should you wish!) plus a fridge that comes stocked with two Madri lagers, four Robinsons Fruit Shoots, four Pepsi Max, two mini proseccos and four bottles of water, plus four bags of crisps! Since purchasing the family resort in Brean, Unity Holidays have spent more than £25m on adding the Wonky Donkey pub/restaurant, creating a sports bar and arcade, opening their own Cider House and extending their fleet of caravans and lodges. “This has been a fantastic project to be part of and represents another major step forward for Unity Beach,” said Resort Director Jonny Green. “With our new indoor leisure facilities and outdoor heated lido now complete, we believe we’ve created one of the finest waterpark experiences in the south west – all within easy reach of both London and Birmingham. “Everything has been designed around families, giving children plenty to enjoy while creating spaces where parents and grandparents can relax and spend quality time together. “We’ve invested more than £25 million into the resort over the past 18 months, and we’re not stopping there. We have an exciting programme of further investment planned as we continue to develop Unity Beach into one of the UK’s leading family holiday destinations.” • A three-night break during August at Unity Beach in Somerset starts from £580 while four-night breaks are available from £749. Prices are based on up to six people sharing a Gold caravan and include full use of all water park facilities. Visit https://unityholidays.co.uk/our-parks/unity-beach/ for more information and to book.

title: Temperatures are soaring! Are your businesses & properties at risk of fire?
subtitle: Lloyd & Whyte Community Broking Taunton can provide advice and insurance solutions to cover your assets and financially protect you around fire damage.
bodyContent: With this summer seeing some of the hottest UK temperatures on record, 1 insurance for fire damage has never been more important. Devon & Somerset Fire & Rescue Service recently confirmed that their fire crews attended 813 fires this year, with the Fire & Rescue Service tackling 226 fires in the space of one week. 2 Only recently, fire services were called to tackle a large blaze near Taunton at around midnight on 16 th July, with 200 tonnes of burning wood and woodchip causing a large amount of smoke at a manufacturing business in Henlade. 3 With high temperatures, tinder dry ground, and strong winds, the likelihood of more fires remains high. Whether you are a business or farm, or are concerned about your residential home, Lloyd & Whyte Community Broking Taunton can provide advice and insurance solutions to cover your assets and financially protect you around fire damage. As this summer has shown, fire is a real risk. And while you may be aware of the risks and take all necessary precautions, your neighbours might not be as vigilant. A stray ember from a garden bonfire or a barbeque (disposable or installed), could ignite dry grass and vegetation, causing a fire which could rapidly spread to your property. What some people don’t know is that even if a fire was caused by a third party, you will usually need to cover the damage to your buildings and/or contents yourself. You can legally pursue your neighbour, for example, to cover the damage they have caused, but you will need to prove the fire was caused by their negligence (for example, faulty electrics they ignored or a lit cigarette). If it was a genuine accident on their part, it is unlikely you will receive any payments and will have to pay the repair costs yourself. Even if you can prove negligence, it may take months or possibly years to resolve. If you had your own insurance, you would claim under your policy and your insurer would pursue the neighbours' insurers on your behalf, if they believed there is a reasonable prospect of recovery; this is called subrogation. If you own a farm or farmland, a fire can be devastating to crops, livestock, farming equipment and farm buildings. A discarded cigarette can cause extensive damage, as shown in a recent fire at Newton Farm , just outside of Bath which was believed to have been caused by a lit cigarette. Fortunately, the fire was contained because the wheat had been harvested a few weeks earlier and sheep moved to a nearby field. If there had been straw bales in the field, that, combined with the power lines and transformer located in that same field, the consequences of the fire could have been extremely serious, with the blaze spreading to houses in close proximity. Without appropriate Farming and Agricultural Insurance in place, farms and farmland can suffer extensive damage and in some cases, total destruction. Some businesses face a higher risk of fire spreading due to the materials used in their operations or the construction of their premises. Others present a greater risk to life because of the number of people who may be on-site when a fire occurs. Motor trade businesses, restaurants, and hotels often have conditions that can make fires more difficult to control and increase the potential consequences of an incident. For example, just one cigarette or spark from machinery or equipment can start a blaze that causes extensive damage and business interruption. While you cannot control what neighbouring businesses, houses, or the public do to reduce the risk of fire, you can take a vital step towards protecting your business and/or home with the right insurance. Lloyd & Whyte Community Broking Taunton are specialists in providing cover for a wide range of properties and businesses. Their team will take time to assess any risks that could result in your assets being exposed to fire damage, and source and arrange the correct level of cover to financially protect you. title: Conferences at Wookey Hole Caves
subtitle: Wookey Hole is situated in the heart of the county and is home to one of the oldest Paper Mills in Britain. Combine these beautiful listed buildings with World famous caves and the recently established Wookey Hole Hotel and you; have yourself an experience you and your team will never forget
bodyContent: Wookey Hole is situated in the heart of the county and is home to one of the oldest Paper Mills in Britain. Combine these beautiful listed buildings with World famous caves and the recently established Wookey Hole Hotel and you; have yourself an experience you and your team will never forget. We are expert in creating and providing bespoke packages for businesses, colleagues and clients. From exclusive, private business meetings through to action-packed team-building away days and weekends, we have a vast array of offerings, each designed to amaze and impress whatever your occasion. Private Guided Tours of the caves can be tailored to your interests or, alternatively you can take the caves literally into your own hands and embark on Wild Wookey - the most innovative caving experience in the country! Our top level instructors will lead your group through a series of climbs, crawls and abseils, overcoming challenges and fears, with your staff’s personalities at the forefront of the adventure. You will be sure to exit the cave in style as you zip-line over the park! Equally as fun, the Pirate Adventure Golf is great for splitting into teams and seeing who can earn the most points! Complimentary ‘goody bags’ are included in your group’s private hire. Why not pair a round of Golf with private hire of the Vintage Penny Arcade? Home of the largest collection of machines anywhere in Britain ranging from Victorian times to the 1980’s; we guarantee endless waves of nostalgia and amusement. If you would prefer to sit back and observe your entertainment, we provide Private Circus Shows in our 400 seater Theatre. Our 400 seater Theatre is also ideal for showcases, conferences, presentations, award ceremonies and workshops. The space is split across two levels, able to accommodate smaller audiences in lower levels and larger audiences over other levels. Like the sound of the circus? You could even take this one step further and book a private Circus Workshop for you and your colleagues! Our World class trainers are one-of-kind and their talents, out-of-this-world. Just be prepared for some circus inspired activity back at the office! Paper-making demonstrations and workshops are also a particular highlight and can be the centre of, or factored in to your corporate event. Learn the ancient art of making the iconic Wookey paper with former employees of the country’s last Paper Mill or, watch the experts dazzle you with their ritual paper-making techniques. Accommodation at Wookey Hole couldn’t be any simpler. Take advantage of our 58 bedroom Hotel within the Wookey Hole Resort, each room including en-suite bathrooms, flat screen TV and those away-from-home essentials such as tea and coffee making facilities, free Wi-Fi, telephones and hairdryers. With 24 hour reception, you can enjoy the local nightlife without curfew. Or if you fancy a relaxing meal or drink onsite, you can visit the Hotel’s Bistro Restaurant and Bar. Onsite car, coach and bike parking is provided free, to all Wookey Hole Caves and Hotel visitors.

title: Taunton Park and Ride
subtitle: Taunton's Park and Ride operates from two sites: one on the east of the town and one on the west.
bodyContent: A bus service across Taunton that helps you beat the traffic.Catch it anywhere on route - you don't need to Park & Ride to use it! Taunton' s Park and Ride buses operate from two sites: Taunton Gateway (to the east of the town) and Silk Mills (to the west of the town). The buses run on a continual loop between the two sites, picking up and dropping off at several stops in the town centre and also at Musgrove Park Hospital. Taunton Gateway (TA3 5LU) has 850 parking spaces for cars and is perfectly situated for visitors and commuters driving to the town on the M5 motorway or approaching the town from the east. The travel time from Taunton Gateway into the town centre takes approximately 10 minutes, and approximately 19 minutes to the hospital. Silk Mills (TA1 5AA) has 760 parking spaces for cars and, located on the west of the town, is ideal for drivers coming from West Somerset and for people needing to access Musgrove Park Hospital. The travel time from Silk Mills into the town centre takes approximately 13 minutes, and approximately 7 minutes to the hospital. **2m vehicle height restriction** The buses run every 20 minutes Mondays to Saturdays
tagline: The easy way to get into Taunton

title: Boston Tea Party
subtitle: Boston Tea Party serves ethically sourced food and drink, including its award-winning brunch and breakfasts, homemade cakes, lunches and main meals alongside speciality coffees, loose-leaf teas, cold drinks and the odd tipple. We were the first café chain in the UK to remove single use cups for our takeaway drinks.
bodyContent: BTP loves breakfast! They believe there should always be time for breakfast, which is why they serve it all day. BTP's company purpose is to Make Things Better. That could be the food you eat, the team they hire, but most importantly the world around us; both the communities they serve and the planet we all share. They were the first café chain in UK to remove single use coffee cups to take away. And they even have their own national ‘Making Things Better’ Day, where each year on the first of June they commit to do one thing more for our planet. This year they removed the 192,000 plastic milk bottles they use each year. They are powered by green energy, free range meat and eggs, organic milk and direct trade coffee (to name a few). They have been named the most ethical café chain in the UK for 2019. They make their food in their café every day. Not some factory somewhere far away, they cook properly using raw ingredients, that need peeling, chopping, baking and seasoning. This matters to them, as they buy incredible ingredients that in turn, they make into delicious meals. They are there for you for breakfast, brunch, lunch, tea & cakes, celebrating with an afternoon tea or just popping in for a quick take away coffee. They are a dog friendly venue, in fact, they love them! They don’t take bookings but don’t worry, they have plenty of space and a lovely secret roof garden too! Facilities : Wifi, disabled access, easily accessible, disabled toilet
tagline: Boston Tea Party serves ethically sourced food and drink, including its award-winning brunches

bodyContent: At Church Farm Country Cottage you'll find seven cottages tastefully converted from old cow byres with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams. Three cottages sleep 2 persons and four cottages sleep 4 persons. Bath is 5 miles away and Bradford on Avon is 2 miles. The farm has ample parking and is dog friendly, it is a working farm with sheep and horses in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. bodyContent: Holiday Park Self Catering & Hotel in Somerset Our comfortable chalets accommodate from between 1 and 4 people, all being en-suite, double glazed and central heated throughout, freeview TV and the additional benefit of full catering facilities and a separate sitting room. title: Chapter 22 – the roots and records store in Bath
subtitle: Your eyes will arrive at Bath’s independent record and houseplant store, Chapter 22, long before you do, when they become transfixed on the stunning display of houseplants that come flowing out of its front door. The colourful cacti and beautiful button ferns brighten up the entirety of Broad Street and entice even the least curious of souls to poke their nose in.
bodyContent: Past the welcoming flora entrance, you will find the local owners, Dean Brown and Nicola Taylor, have a created a spectacle for the senses. Customers are not only treated to the sight of more luscious houseplants but also the crisp sounds of a classic LP playing in the background, and the aromatic smell of fresh coffee too. The unique store is only small but manages to artfully combine both of Dean and Nicolas’ life passions for music and floristry, all whist having room for people to sit down and enjoy a cup of coffee at the back. Dean has run the record label Chapter 22 Records since the 80’s and has helped develop bands like Balaam and the Angel, The Mission, Pop Will Eat Itself, Neds Atomic Dustbin and Dawn After Dark. Meanwhile, Nicola has been a florist for 30 years and her experience certainly shows by her ability to wonderfully arrange the rare and exotic houseplants around the shop. The two opened the store in September of this year after settling on the idea during the lockdown and say they have been overwhelmed with the city’s response. “We’ve only been open 9 weeks, but we’ve been really busy with local people and tourists.” Dean said, when we visited Chapter 22 at the beginning of November. “At a weekend, we have people here at 8.30pm grabbing a drink and listening to some music in the listening booths. It’s really become what we wanted it to be.” The store can be easily found on the left side of Broad Street, if you are walking up the hill, and it’s a great spot for getting someone a special gift, or to simply chill out. There’s full range of house plants on offer from Red Anthuriums to Big Band Zebra Cacti and Senecio ‘String of Pearls’ succulents. The variety of vinyl in Chapter 22 is equally as diverse with Ed Sheeran’s latest album ‘Equals’ being played next Abba’s Gold and the Sex Pistols’ Same Old Ten Inch Bollocks, all of which are available to purchase. Dean said his favourite thing about his shop was the amazing mix of people that come in but for us it had to be the awesome listening booths at the back, where you can set up for some work and listen to anything from Dean’s collection by yourself, using the booth’s personal record player and headphones. It’s a truly masterful use of space and has such a palpable connection to Dean and Nicolas’ wonderful personalities that you’d be foolish not to pop in on your next visit to Bath. You can check out Chapter 22’s website here and follow their social media here .

title: Yeabridge Farm Hideaway
subtitle: Set within the scenic Somerset countryside, 30 minutes from Glastonbury, 40 minutes from Lyme Regis and 20 minutes’ walk to the local country pub. Offering both romantic, family friendly glamping and exclusive use for group bookings, guests can enjoy a stay in a shepherd's hut, yurt, safari tent or bus.
bodyContent: Set down a secluded private track surrounded by fields of maize and grass; you will be able to relax in the tranquillity of the site. Hidden in a small, secret woodland copse, you can also soak in the beautiful views of the Somerset countryside. The site offers a selection of different glamping accommodations, suiting couples and families or groups looking for exclusive use. Each unit has its own private shower room in a shared block. Ideal for a romantic stay, the shepherd's huts, and bus sleep two and feature luxury furnishings, a double bed, linen and a wood burning stove. Each yurt sleeps five and offers one proper double bed for the adults and three single beds for the children, complete with thick, warm, duvets, pillows, and linen. The Loft sleeps four, kitted out with a double bed and two single futon beds. Outside all accommodation is a lovely area with two director's chairs to sit and enjoy a glass of wine. There is also a picnic table, your own BBQ and fire pit to toast marshmallows over. In the kitchen area, you get your own workstation complete with plates, cups, pots, pans etc, a camping stove, a fridge, a storage box, and a picnic table. There is also shared use of a double oven with gas hobs, plus a large communal fire pit. A short walk from the site you will find the farm lake which you are free to wander around or take a picnic to the lakeside.

title: Charlton House, Montigo Resorts Somerset
subtitle: Discover an oasis of calm at Montigo Resorts, Somerset. With luxurious, individually designed rooms, a spa inspired by Asian traditions, and farm-to-table dining, Charlton House offers an unparalleled rural escape. Experience relaxation, rejuvenation, and the best of Somerset’s local flavours.
bodyContent: Somersets, Montigo Resorts - Charlton House, Shepton Mallet - is nestled in the heart of Somerset’s picturesque countryside, Montigo Resorts, Somerset at Charlton House offers the perfect escape. This historic estate features 28 uniquely designed rooms, each with its own character and charm, combining contemporary comforts with the building’s rich heritage. Whether you’re seeking a cosy hideaway or a spacious suite for a longer stay, there’s a room to suit every taste. The resort’s spa is a serene sanctuary where Asian wellness meets the healing power of nature. Boasting state-of-the-art thermal facilities, hydrotherapy pools, and specialist therapies like Balinese and Thai massages, you’re assured a deeply relaxing experience. For dining, Montigo Resorts showcases the best of Somerset’s seasonal produce; from the colourful cocktails, seasoned meats, and fresh, locally sourced seafood, cooked to perfection, at Tiigo, our kitchen garden pop up promises an authentic pan-Asian experience in a laid-back setting, while the Charlton House restaurant offers a more refined affair and Bob’s Bistro ensures you can grab a bite in the bar or lounge at any time. Whether you’re here for a wellness retreat, a romantic weekend, or simply to unwind, Montigo Resorts, Somerset at Charlton House invites you to embrace the tranquillity of this little gem of a county.

title: Whitley Coach House
subtitle: Whitley Coach House is a truly luxurious self-contained 1804 Georgian built.
bodyContent: Recently modernised stone coach house providing self-catering accommodation for long, short or one night stays. Whitley Coach House is an ideal base from which to visit Bath, Lacock, Longleat, Bowood House, Stonehenge, National Trust properties and many other local attractions. Only 20 minutes from Bath and 5 Minutes from Lacock – 10-minute walk to a great Pub/Resturant and local shop/cafe, free fast Wi-Fi, 40″ smart TV with Netflix and free private parking. Private garden with teak furniture on wooden decking. With luxurious bedding including a handmade king size Lit Bateau bed with a Vi-Spring luxuriously comfortable handmade mattress. Immediate and live AVAILABILITY. Accepting: American Express plus most credit and debit cards. Whitley Coach House self-catering accommodation has a large bedroom with a super king-size (5ft 6ins x 6ft 6ins) Lit Bateau oak bed designed and handmade with a supremely comfortable Vi-Spring handmade pocket sprung mattress. The living room has high ceilings with exposed beams and includes two three-seater sofas one with a large double pull-out bed. In addition, there is a luxurious deep sprung folding bed for use in the bedroom or entrance hall. ONLINE BOOKING or do look at our Website: www.whitleycoachhouse.co.uk The Space Whitley Coach House is a detached former coach house to a Georgian house, renovated four years ago and just redecorated, providing spacious self-catering accommodation. Whitley Coach House has a large bedroom with an individually designed and handmade kingsize bateau bed designed and handmade in oak, with a supremely comfortable Vi-Spring pocket sprung mattress. The living room has high ceilings with exposed beams and a solid oak floor and includes two three-seater sofas one with a large super king size pull-out bed. The living room has views of the private garden, teak furniture and decked veranda. The kitchen table seats up to six people. This self-catering accommodation has fast broadband, a 40 inch smart TV with Freeview channels and the ability to watch other online services like Netflix. Guest Access The back has a private wooden decked terrace for use in dry weather and garden beyond. There is plenty of private parking. A barbeque can be provided if asked for at an extra charge. Whitley Coach House self-catering accommodation is not adapted for wheelchair users but has a step up into the property on entry. Once inside there are no steps, it is a converted coach house on one level. Interaction with Guests Your host will normally hand you the keys and discuss Whitley Coach House and the surrounding area with you on arrival. Unless you need help or are staying over a week, you will be left alone to enjoy your stay.

title: Bath Breaks Apartments
subtitle: Located within the heart of the World Heritage City of Bath you are just a short, level walking distance to all the attractions from the Roman Baths to the Royal Crescent.
bodyContent: As well as the wonderful history and stunning architecture there is a wealth of shops and restaurants. This is an ideal location if you want a romantic break, a family holiday, a relaxing spa or a cultural experience. These modern apartments are on the first floor and accessed by a single flight of stairs. They have private entrances with a bright, open plan lounge, kitchen and dinning areas with Wifi and TV. The bedrooms have clean fresh linen, towels and hairdryers. If you do not want to eat out at one of the many restaurants, the kitchens are fully equipped with microwave, oven and hob, dishwasher, fridge-freezer, toaster, kettle, dinner set and cutlery. Also included in the kitchen are tea towels, washing up liquid and bin bags. If you are arriving by car there is a car park located in Charlotte Street, approximately 250m away. Once you park your car and settle in to your apartment you may not need to use it again. Due to the central location of the apartments most of the attractions are within walking distance, but if you want to explore further afield the train and bus stations are close by and taxis are readily available. We hope your visit to Bath will be enhanced by your stay in these wonderful apartments.

title: Harry Brockway: Ways With Wood
subtitle: A new exhibition celebrating the life and work of Glastonbury based artist Harry Brockway.
bodyContent: ‘Ways with Wood’, is a major exhibition at Somerset Rural Life Museum celebrating the life and work of renowned Glastonbury-based artist Harry Brockway (1958–2024). Featuring an exceptional selection of his wood engravings, woodcuts and wooden sculpture, the exhibition offers a rich insight into the creativity, skill and craftsmanship that defined his distinguished artistic career. Harry Brockway was an exceptionally accomplished printmaker, sculptor, illustrator and stone carver. Alongside creating independent prints, he produced wood-engraved illustrations for a wide range of publishers – from major houses such as Penguin to specialist presses like The Folio Society. His work appears in celebrated editions of Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein and in texts by W. B. Yeats, Philip Pullman, Fyodor Dostoevsky, Samuel Taylor Coleridge and Mark Twain among others. Image credit: All rights reserved The Brockway Family, Harry Brockway, The Tor from Ten Acre Field, 2008. The museum is open Tuesday – Sunday, 10.00 am – 5.00 pm.
tagline: A new exhibition celebrating the life and work of Glastonbury based artist Harry Brockway.

title: Edinburgh Preview: Li Jin Hao + Emmeline Downie
subtitle: Li Jin Hao Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer Nominee and Chortle Best Newcomer winner Li Jin Hao is a comedy writer and performer.
bodyContent: Li Jin Hao Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer Nominee and Chortle Best Newcomer winner Li Jin Hao is a comedy writer and performer. Jin Hao was made in China and marinated in Singapore, loved and feared for his dry wit, gritty softness, and surreal energy, he quickly became a Chortle Student Finalist, BBC New Comedy Awards Finalist, and was accepted into the Pleasance Comedy Reserve 2023. His debut solo show “Swimming in a Submarine” had a sell-out run at Edinburgh Fringe 2024 and earned him a nomination for Best Newcomer at the Edinburgh Comedy Awards, with a London run at the Soho Theatre for three weeks, before taking the show to the Melbourne International Comedy Festival. His TV appearances include Silence is Golden (Dave), Comedy Central Live (Comedy Central), The Stand Up Sketch Show (ITV2), and ITVX Presents: Live Comedy From the Edinburgh Fringe. Emmeline Donnie Emmeline Downie is a comedian, writer and actor performing across the UK comedy circuit. She co-created and starred in Edinburgh hits, Manhunt and Manhunt 2: Big Mood, earning critical acclaim; "brilliantly performed, beautifully written" - ThreeWeeks ★★★★★ In 2025, Emmeline appeared in Brainsluts at Pleasance Dome, recognised by The Guardian for a "stand-out performance". Her writing credits include an Untitled BBC Studios Comedy Writers' Room and additional material for Ania Magliano's Forgive Me, Father and Leo Reich's Literally Who Cares?!!! (A24). "A knockout" - The Stage ★★★★
tagline: Li Jin Hao Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer Nominee and Chortle Best Newcomer winner

bodyContent: She’s back! Elvis Lesley is in the building...joined by the fabulous Audrey Heartburn. title: Primate State
subtitle: Primate State are a young three-piece rock band with bags of energy, strong musicianship and a natural chemistry on stage.
bodyContent: Ned (14 - guitar/vocals), Theo (15 - bass) and Tym (16 - drums/keys) came together through school, having previously played alongside each other in various musical settings, and have already picked up a Gold Award at the Young Musicians Awards. Their set spans everything from Arctic Monkeys, Jimi Hendrix and Red Hot Chili Peppers to Oasis, The Stone Roses, The Beatles and The Kinks. Ned brings accomplished guitar playing and a versatile lead vocal, Theo mixes rock bass with influences from funk, jazz and slap, while Tym drives the band on drums as well as being a highly skilled pianist and keyboard player. They’re not afraid to put their own spin on a song either, adding different arrangements, individual flourishes and the occasional bit of improvisation, while also being able to strip things back for acoustic sets. Still only a few gigs into their journey, they’re already writing their own material and developing quickly. Young, talented and clearly having a great time playing together, Primate State are a band worth keeping an eye on.
tagline: Primate State are a young three-piece rock band

title: Art with Abandon: Messy Play for Grown Ups at the Museum of Somerset
subtitle: This unique session offers a rare opportunity to explore creativity in a supportive, judgement-free environment.
bodyContent: Adults are invited to rediscover the joy of play at a new Somerset wellbeing event that tackles perfectionism through creativity. Led by experienced Art Psychotherapist Stacey Kiely, this unique session offers a rare opportunity to explore creativity in a supportive, judgement-free environment. No artistic ability is required. Just an hour to play, unwind and reconnect with yourself through colour, creativity and freedom. ‘Art with Abandon: Messy Play for Grown Ups’ takes place at The Museum of Somerset 2.00 pm – 3.00 pm on Saturday 15 August. Booking required, £15. The event is part of the Museum’s summer season of PLAY. Museumofsomerset.org.uk Image: Switch off your inner critic, get messy and rediscover the joy of creating at ‘Art with Abandon’. Photo: Jacob Lund.

title: South West Heritage Trust launches autumn programme of workshops, talks and tours
subtitle: The packed programme includes arts and crafts workshops, expert talks, behind-the-scenes tours and hands-on learning experiences at venues including Museums and Heritage Centres.
bodyContent: The South West Heritage Trust has unveiled its autumn programme of workshops, talks, tours and special events across Somerset and Devon, offering opportunities to explore creativity, local history and heritage. The packed programme includes arts and crafts workshops, expert talks, behind-the-scenes tours and hands-on learning experiences at venues including Museums and Heritage Centres. South West Heritage Trust Head of Museums and Engagement Estelle Gilbert said: "Our autumn programme offers something for everyone, whether you're interested in learning a new creative skill, discovering fascinating stories from the past, exploring our museums and archives, or meeting like-minded people. We're delighted to be welcoming visitors to a wide range of inspiring events that celebrate the rich heritage of Somerset and Devon." Art, craft, clay and woodworking workshops are taking place in Glastonbury and Bridgwater throughout the season. At Somerset Rural Life Museum, local artist Jackie Curtis is leading three workshops exploring different styles of printmaking. Visitors can also try drawing with charcoal with local artist Kate Lynch and create stained glass light catchers with Kate Doig from Firewolf Glass. At Avalon Archaeology there are prehistoric skills and woodworking workshops. At Somerset Brick and Tile Museum, adult clay workshops offer the chance to make a variety of seasonal creations, including gingerbread houses, ghosts, snowmen, Christmas wreaths and festive decorations. For those interested in history and archives, workshops at the Somerset Heritage Centre will provide an introduction to reading old handwriting, while the Devon Heritage Centre is hosting a session on caring for family and community archives. The Trust is also taking part in Heritage Open Days. The Somerset Heritage Centre will open its doors for a free drop-in event, giving visitors the opportunity to see original documents, hear talks about the lives of everyday people found within the archives and take a guided tour of the strongrooms. At Somerset Brick and Tile Museum, visitors can enjoy a free tour alongside a tile-making demonstration. As part of Somerset Art Weeks, exhibitions and talks will take place at Somerset Rural Life Museum. Working in partnership with Somerset Art Works, Cultural Connections will feature artist talks and displays of contemporary art exploring themes of migration and identity. Meanwhile, at The Museum of Somerset, the Victoria County History Society Annual Lecture will be delivered by author Chris Lewis, who will discuss Exon Domesday, the oldest but least well-known surviving manuscript from the Domesday survey of 1086. The Museum is also hosting The Royal Photographic Society International Photography Exhibition 167. For more information about South West Heritage Trust events and to book tickets, visit swheritage.org.uk .

subtitle: At the Hampton by Hilton Bristol Airport, you will find yourself just steps away from Bristol Airport with easy connections to the South West and many destinations across the world.
bodyContent: At the Hampton by Hilton Bristol Airport, you will find yourself just steps away from Bristol Airport with easy connections to the South West and many destinations across the world. Our 201 bedroom hotel is ideal for leisure and business travellers with our clean and fresh Hampton beds and free Wi-Fi in every room. Working is simple at the hotel with our modern Work Zone, equipped with computers, printer and plenty of work space, complimentary for all guests. Although if you're looking for a private space to work or hold a meeting, why not hire one of our fully equipped meeting rooms. Our meeting rooms have a partition wall to allow flexibility of having 2 separate meeting rooms or 1 larger meeting room, holding up to 18 people in a u shape layout. Breakfast is complimentary for all of our guests so that you start your morning in the right way, complete with freshly baked waffles. Continental breakfast is served from 4am, ready for those early morning travellers or you can tuck into a full English breakfast from 6am until 10am on weekdays or 11am on weekends. With hot food served 24 hours a day along with a snack shop to grab a quick bite, you'll never go hungry at our airport hotel. Making you happy makes us happy. So, if we can make your stay better, talk to any member of our team, and we'll make sure you're 100% happy. Guaranteed. Wherever your travels take you, count on Hampton to deliver value, consistency and thoughtful service. Make the most of your stays with Hilton hotels. title: Mill Meadow Eco Lodge
subtitle: Mill Meadow offers you a unique holiday experience in luxury eco wooden lodges and cottages with completely flexible arrival and departure days, an Electric Vehicle Charging Station free of charge, tranquil fishing lake, private hot tubs, warm welcomes for your dogs and a local pub.
bodyContent: Mill Meadow is a gated, private and secure destination nestled in green countryside at the foot of the Quantock Hills surrounded by a perfect natural landscape which provides a stunning backdrop to your stay close to Taunton in the heart of stunning Somerset. Everyone is welcome to our range of self catering options which can accommodate up to 74 guests, across 10 homes. As a family business we can offer helpful advice on places to visit and things to do during your stay. We communicate with our guests from the moment of booking and are available to answer any questions no matter how small. Relax in your hot tub, light the BBQ, enjoy fishing for free in our tranquil lake, sit, read or paint in our lakeside summerhouse, walk the beautiful local lanes and picturesque Quantock Hills, bring together family and friends for special celebrations, wedding accommodation, birthdays, hen weekends, honeymoons or simply a relaxing break amongst all that makes Somerset special. Indulge in holistic therapies, order vintage teas or a chef to cook for you. Open all year round, our super fast Wi-Fi makes your wooden lodge idea to "work from home" Our eco lodges are accessible for our less mobile guests and those with additional requirements and we love dogs too. Mill Meadow is conveniently situated close to Taunton mainline station and the M5 motorway. Bristol and Exeter International airports are within a one-hour drive. We offer a minimum of three night stays except in Goldcrest Lodge, which has a two night minimum stay So visit us soon and make your own 'Mill Meadow Memories' Accessibility: Ground floor accessible wet rooms and bedrooms in many lodges Access to local support services including equipment hire and hydro therapy pool Children & Infants: Children welcome Travel Cot & Highchair free of charge Pet Information: Dogs accepted in most lodges, other pets by arrangement Establishment Features: Countryside location Family run business Families welcome Groups welcome Free Superfast WiFi Eco Friendly Utilities included Leisure Facilities: Private Coarse Fishing on site Hot Tub available on most lodges Special provisions for cyclists Special provisions for walkers BBQ's Golf courses and other facilities nearby Parking & Tranport: Free parking Close to main rail/bus stations and road network Room & Unit Features: Dishwasher Washing machine Drying facilities DVD Player Free View TV Fridge/Freezer Linen and towels (not for hot tub) provided Ironing facilities Hair dryers Please note: Visit Taunton cannot accept any responsibility for matters arising between a customer and the accommodation provider.
