title: Greenacre Place Caravan Park
subtitle: We are Mark & Linda and we would like to extend a very warm welcome to our Touring Caravan Site & Holiday Cottage.
bodyContent: We took over Greenacre Place in 2006 and ran it as a fully grassed 10 pitch site , catering exclusively for adults. In 2019 we decided to completely re-configure & refurbish the site, to include hardstandings for each pitch, a dog walking area and fully refurbished facilities. These are all improvements that our guests have mentioned over the years and we are so proud and pleased with the results. We can now accommodate caravans and motorhomes, whatever the weather. The reviews from our guests have been very positive & complimentary. Our aim, as it always has been, is to make our guests feel valued, comfortable & happy with their stay. Our Touring Site and Holiday Cottage are positioned about a mile from Junction 22 of the M5 making them ideally located for exploring the Somerset coastline & countryside alike. The Cottage is warm & cosy with two bedrooms & two bathrooms. An enclosed patio to the rear gives our guests the chance to relax & enjoy the outdoors. There is also parking for two cars. We have been accredited with an AA three Pennants award for the Touring Site & an AA 4 Star rating for our Holiday Cottage. Burnham-on-sea is approximately five minutes’ drive away, with its miles of sandy beaches, cafes, bars & restaurants. We are also well located for visiting Weston-Super-Mare, Glastonbury, Cheddar, Taunton and Bristol. If you enjoy cycling or walking, Exmoor, The Quantocks and the Somerset levels are close by, where you can enjoy a wealth of walks, cycle tracks & bird sanctuaries. Just across the road from Greenacre Place is the Oaktree Arena, home to Championship The Somerset Rebels Speedway Team. Racing during the summer season is on Wednesday evening between 19:30 and 21:30.

title: Fudge Kitchen Bath
subtitle: Fudge Kitchen has been trading in Bath for over 30 years. In that time, they've made thousands of batches of hundreds of flavours of their devilishly different fudge.
bodyContent: Fudge Kitchen has been trading in Bath for over 30 years. In that time, they've made thousands of batches of hundreds of flavours of their devilishly different fudge. Every batch of their famous whipping cream fudge is hand-made by expert Fudge Makers, who lovingly produce, cut & decorate each piece in front of their customers, simultaneously entertaining both locals and visitors to the City. What’s more, they now offer Fudge Making Experiences – watch and learn from the experts, then get stuck in yourself! Fudge is a great ‘to me, from me’ gift, as well as something to treat friends and family with! They create bespoke wedding favours - contact weddings@fudgekitchen.co.uk for more information. They also produce a wide range of other fudge and sugar confectionery, including caramels and brittles, which wholesales across the UK and abroad to high end retailers, hoteliers and speciality food stores alike, from Selfridges to Claridge’s. Fun fact: Their Bath team recently worked with Bath Brewhouse to create a fudge beer!
tagline: Fudge Kitchen has been trading in Bath for over 30 years, making thousands of batches of fudge

title: The Spa at Middlewick
subtitle: Nestled within our 16-acre converted farmstead, Middlewick Spa, Glastonbury may be the quirkiest Spa in Somerset.
bodyContent: Nestled at the back of our property within sight of the iconic Glastonbury Tor, Middlewick Spa is the perfect location to indulge in a treatment, use our pool and sauna, and treat yourself to delicious food and drink. Our Spa is a little different to others you might have visited. Our focus is your holistic wellbeing and the nourishment of your mind, body and soul. Experience an organic facial, rejuvenating massage or holistic beauty treatment. You can also book Spa packages – from a full Spa Day to a Swim, Sauna and Lunch. Begin your Middlewick moment in our Spa Lounge, where you can unwind with a complimentary herbal tea. Treatments take place in our quirky shepherd’s hut treatment rooms. All our airy spaces, from the Spa Lounge to the outdoor sauna, provide views of rolling hills and blue skies and are designed to connect you with nature. Hungry? Choose your breakfast, lunch or sweet treat and we’ll whip it up in our award-winning Café kitchen and deliver it to you in the Spa Lounge. We can also cater for special occasions – and our onsite Accommodation makes The Middlewick the perfect venue for Spa weekends and retreats.

title: Grosvenor Villa B&B
subtitle: Grosvenor Villa is a grade two listed Georgian Villa, the house is a fine example of Georgian architecture and was built specifically to house the former high altar of Bath Abbey which now forms part of their impressive entrance hall.
bodyContent: Their bedrooms contain Super King sized beds and either have an en-suite shower room or a private bath room. The rooms have free Wi-Fi, bath robes, flat-screen TV and tea/coffee making facilities. Rooms are dog friendly also. Guests are welcome to relax in the garden and a continental breakfast is served in their Georgian dining room. Parking is available on Grosvenor Bridge Road and the road behind the property, Ringswell Gardens, neither of which has any parking restrictions, 24/7 free of charge. Grosvenor Villa is situated just 1.2 miles from Bath City Centre which can be reached from the bus stop outside the house or a by a gentle 20 minutes stroll along the canal tow path at the bottom of the road which brings you into Sydney Gardens at the end of Great Poultney Street. Their guests can be assured of a very friendly personal welcome, and the excellent reviews by their guests have placed Grosvenor Villa among the top rated B & B’s in Bath. Kitchen Continental breakfast included. Parking There is plenty of parking in Grosvenor Bridge Road and Ringswell Gardens where cars may be left 24/7 with no restrictions. Children They do not cater for Children Pets Pets are allowed free of charge with advance notice

title: World-First Attraction dedicated to Mary Shelley Opens 30 June 2021
subtitle: New Bath attraction, Mary Shelley’s House of Frankenstein, will officially open its doors to the public on 30 June 2021 – a monumental 205 years since Mary Shelley put pen to paper to write Frankenstein in Bath, during June 1816.
bodyContent: Attraction to feature an 8ft monster recreated as Mary imagined in her novel, and a horror experience in the dank and foreboding underbelly of the house Visit the website to book tickets now: houseoffrankenstein.com New Bath attraction, Mary Shelley’s House of Frankenstein, will officially open its doors to the public on 30 June 2021 – a monumental 205 years since Mary Shelley put pen to paper to write Frankenstein in Bath, during June 1816. This summer, visitors to Bath can uncover the true story behind the iconic monster and immerse themselves in the complex and often tragic past of its author, in the city where she wrote Frankenstein . In a world-first, horror fans, literary enthusiasts, and families with older children can come face-to-face with the monster as Mary imagined, as the attraction’s centrepiece will feature an 8ft monster recreated from the text of the first ever science-fiction novel. NEWLY ANNOUNCED: IMMERSIVE BASEMENT EXPERIENCE: Visitors can venture down into the dank foreboding basement, in a dark and disorientating walkthrough revealing the unhallowed practices of a deranged scientist. The attraction hopes it will be a major draw for visitors to the historical city of Bath on their UK staycations and summer holidays, and help support the city’s recovery after the coronavirus pandemic. Chris Harris, Co-Founder of the attraction, said : “Mary Shelley’s House of Frankenstein aims to deliver a unique and entertaining experience. Mary Shelley’s unconventional life was complex and chaotic, and every bit as grisly as her extraordinary novel. If you think you know Mary or her monster, think again! Our attraction offers an unnerving insight into this extraordinary and gifted young woman and reveals, for the very first time, the 8ft monster exactly as she imagined.” What’s inside Extending over four atmospheric floors bursting with unusual artefacts and vintage items, interactive multi-sensory environments, and assorted body parts, Mary Shelley’s House of Frankenstein is one attraction that visitors will not want to miss this summer. The attraction will contain ominous audio and visual effects, darkened environments, and some scenes of a disturbing nature. Franken-fans can book their tickets now to visit from 30 June 2021 at: www.houseoffrankenstein.com -ENDS- Ticket prices GROUP SAVING: Save up to 20% for group parties of 5, 6, 8 and 10 people online. Full pricing: - Bespoke ebooks & Free Ticket £15.50 - Adult (16 yrs+) £15.50 - Child (6-15yrs) £12.50 - Family of four £53.00 - Family of three £38.30 - Student £12.80 - Groups of 5 £68.00 - Groups of 6 £78.00 - Groups of 8 £100.00 - Groups of 10 £120.00 Location 37 Gay Street, Bath, Somerset BA1 2NT, UK Opening times 10am – 6pm, with last admission 5pm. Some opening times will vary throughout the year. COVID-19 Compliance In accordance with UK Government guidelines, social distancing and capacity management will be enforced throughout the attraction as well as COVID safety protocols in place throughout the building as directed. More Blog Posts Victoria Art Gallery in Bath reopens for 2021 with new exhibition Kurt Jackson: BiodiversityOnline 29 March– 30 June 2021 Gallery 18 May – 30 June 2021
tagline: New Bath attraction, Mary Shelley’s House of Frankenstein

title: Western Fuel
subtitle: Western Fuel is now one of the South West’s leading, independent fuel supply business. We have acquired an excellent reputation as competitive and reliable fuel distributors
bodyContent: Western Fuel was originally started in 1985 by our Managing Director Craig Lamont. He Started the business after a career in formula One, with a clear vision to set up an independent local oil distribution company, Western Counties Fuel Oils was born in Taunton. Craig has always been a hands-on MD and has done every job in the company, from answering customer calls, to routing the tankers and driving the tankers himself. In 1996 the company moved to larger premises in Bridgwater and was joined by shareholder and financial director Nick Smith. The company name was shortened to Western fuel Limited and has gone from strength to strength. The company started with 1 tanker and has steadily grown over the years to a fleet of 26 with over 50 staff in 2023. With our flagship depot in Bridgwater full with our ever growing number of tankers, we opened our Taunton depot in 2006.
tagline: Western Fuel is now one of the South West’s leading, independent fuel supply business.

title: Whippletree Cottage
subtitle: Sympathetically restored from a hay store to beautifully appointed contemporary accommodation.
bodyContent: This romantic cottage, only 20 minutes from Bath, has been restored from a barn to beautifully appointed contemporary accommodation. Whippletree Cottage has exposed oak beams and stone walls which hint at the original use of the building. Guests enjoy the pleasure of sleeping in a king sized bed with 100% cotton bed linen. The main bedroom in the old hay loft has stunning views across the Mendip Hills which are also enjoyed from its own garden. Twin 3ft beds in the second bedroom can be zipped together to make a super king sized bed. The cottage has free wifi, and provides a wonderful setting in which to relax and unwind with the luxury of underfloor heating throughout the property. Whippletree has a digital TV and bluetooth speaker. On a winter break, light the wood burner and settle down to a cosy romantic evening. Set in a rural location Withy Mills Farm provides a peaceful setting with ample off road parking. Enjoy easy access to tourist attractions and of course the cities of Bath, Wells and Bristol. Please visit our website for photographs and more details.

Vodka. Voting. Vengeance via SLIDO. Spirit of Comedy 2026 — may the funniest act win. Probably. SPIRIT OF COMEDY IS BACK… Dutch Barn Vodka is once again searching for the nation’s next comedy legend. Or, failing that, someone with a microphone, a few jokes and absolutely no fear of public humiliation. Last year, Valeria Vulpe took the crown. This year, it could be you. The winner gets £5,000. Everyone else gets character development, delivered live by an audience armed with Applause Paddles, a Laugh-o-Meter and SLIDO, an app that lets complete strangers rate your jokes in real time. title: American Ambassador opens Declaration of Independence Exhibition at the American Museum
subtitle: It is on display as part of the Museum’s series of special exhibitions and events marking the 250th anniversary of American independence from Britain.
bodyContent: Museum runs special £2.50 pricing for 250 years through weekday daytimes in July Exceptionally rare Declaration of Independence on display for the first time this year in England Special events, music and exhibitions during July and August The American Ambassador to the UK visited The American Museum & Gardens in Bath to open the exhibition of an extremely rare original printing of the Declaration of Independence, on display in England for the first time at the Museum. It is on display as part of the Museum’s series of special exhibitions and events marking the 250th anniversary of American independence from Britain. Warren A. Stephens, American Ambassador to the Court of St James, was greeted by children from Freshford Church School before touring the Museum’s outstanding collection of American decorative arts and design and formally opening the Declaration of Independence exhibition. The Ambassador’s visit comes before the Museum’s ‘Independence Day Weekend Celebrations’, taking place from 3–5 July, featuring live music and entertainment for all the family across the Museum and its rolling gardens, which include a recreation of George Washington’s Garden at Mount Vernon. Special events to mark 250 of Independence continue throughout July and August. Ambassador Stephens said: “The ties between our countries run deep, are visible across the United Kingdom, and speak to a living connection that goes far beyond bricks and mortar. It is why I’m honoured to open this exhibit celebrating the 250th anniversary of American independence. We know this exhibition will inspire visitors to reflect on the special relationship that has enriched our two countries for centuries, and that continues to do so today.” Lucy Littlewood, Director of The American Museum & Gardens, Bath, said: “ It is a pleasure to welcome Ambassador Stephens to the Museum during this significant 250th anniversary year. America 250 provides an opportunity to reflect on our shared histories and culture. The exhibitions and events we have created at the Museum and in our gardens enable people to discover the diverse and astonishing decorative arts of America, learn more about its history and have a once in a lifetime opportunity to see the Declaration of Independence – a document which changed the world.” America 250 Celebrations at the American Museum The American Museum & Gardens is bringing the story of American independence to life through a wide-ranging programme of exhibitions, performances and family events marking the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, with events taking place during July and August. To help as many people as possible experience the Museum during this landmark 250th anniversary year - including the rare opportunity to see the Declaration of Independence - weekday daytime admission throughout July has been reduced to just £2.50 per ticket. To help families make the most of the summer holidays, the Government has also reduced VAT on standard museum admission tickets from 20% to 5% between 25 June and 1 September 2026, making visits to museums more affordable throughout the school break.

title: 567 Glastonbury and Street Rail Link goes live!
subtitle: The new Glastonbury & Street to Castle Cary express bus service (route 567) commenced on Monday 3rd August
bodyContent: The new Glastonbury & Street to Castle Cary express bus service (route 567) commenced on Monday 3rd August - Click here for the timetable It runs 7 days a week, including late evening services on weekdays. The combination of the 567 and 667 will provide 29 journeys a day between Street and Castle Cary station including both directions. Fares are locked at the national £3 fare cap keeping all journeys affordable and making it a much cheaper alternative to driving to the station and parking. The bus will run fast from Street to Castle Cary station via Butleigh and Keinton Mandeville on the way. Daytime journeys will also extend to Castle Cary town centre after serving the station. The service will be operated by Somerset Council using 16 seater accessible minibuses. The service will run for a trial period of 6 months. Please spread the word and make the most of your new bus service. If not enough people use it, the service will be axed in 2027 so use it or lose it ! Exmoor 300 (formally Exmoor Coaster) has returned One of the most scenic bus trips in the country has returned for the Summer season running from now until the end of August. The open top bus runs between Minehead and Lynmouth and a separate closed top single decker bus between Lynmouth and Ilfracombe. The service is operated by Stagecoach and is subject to the £3 bus fare cap, an absolute bargain! Timetable here . Kids Go FREE this August Children aged 5–15 can travel for free on participating local buses all month long - no sign‑up, no hassle, just hop on and go! Although not required, teenagers are advised to carry proof of age if available to show the driver. Make the most of summer with easy, affordable days out. Whether it’s parks, beaches, museums or visiting friends, the bus is the simplest way to explore. A list of confirmed services here . £2 bus cap set to return in January 2027 The new Labour Prime Minster Andy Burnham has in his first week, announced a reduction of the bus fare cap from £3 to £2 starting in January 2027. More details to follow in a newsletter later in the year. Concessionary pass Across Somerset, a number of bus routes do allow concessionary pass use before 9:30, thanks to a quietly published list of early‑valid services. Somerset Bus Partnership encourages everyone with a concessionary pass to check whether their local route is included - it’s a simple change that can open up your morning options. Find the list here We recommend having a copy of this list to hand when boarding the bus in case your driver is unfamiliar with the easement and tries charging you. Wivey–Welly Bus User Group produces bus timetable Digital version of the timetable here The Wivey-Welly Bus User Group has produced a comprehensive timetable of the bus routes serving their local area including information on coaches and on-demand services. They hope this will fill the gap for those reliant on or who prefer printed timetables, which the bus companies no longer issue. The BUG is grateful for a grant from CAGS (Community Action Groups Somerset) towards the cost of this initial edition which they would like to produce each April to coincide with the annual service changes. They hope the timetable booklet will encourage people to use buses both for regular journeys and for longer trips, e.g. to Honiton, Seaton, Dulverton and Tiverton as well as to destinations such as Sheppy’s Cider and Rumwell Farm Shop, Coldharbour Mill, the Thelma Hulbert Gallery in Honiton and Tiverton Castle. Copies have been distributed via local libraries, town council offices, churches and shops in Wellington, Wiveliscombe, Milverton and Langford Budville and the BUG has sent a press release to the local press. Why bus it? Cheaper The cost of fuel, tyres, servicing our cars continues to rise. Bus travel remains capped at £3 a single trip until January when it becomes £2. Accessible Buses are for everyone and take us directly to the centre of our towns and right outside our hospitals and railway stations. Reduces traffic Each driver that chooses to bus it is one less car in the queue. So when you need to drive, you get to your destination faster. Environmentally friendly Buses slash emissions by moving more people with fewer vehicles helping to lower local air pollution. SLINKY The SLINKY is for everyone, want to go to a rural pub a couple of miles from the 54 bus route? Arrange for the SLINKY bus to pick you up at a stop on the 54 route and take you to a designated SLINKY stop near the pub. Want to nip to the next village along to see a friend? Book SLINKY . The service is continuing to expand with more buses and expanded areas. These areas can be booked on the app - Somerton, Taunton & Wellington and Sedgemoor Download the SLINKY Somerset App now These services are bookable by phone Mendip 01749 880482 South Somerset 08448 009646 West Somerset 01643 707090 You can register via phone or on the website . Management Team Update David Northey (pictured with the 567) has been elected as the new Chair of Somerset Bus Partnership. We thank Peter Travis and Tony Reece for their incredible efforts in starting this very special group and helping it grow to what it is today. They will continue as important members of Somerset Bus Partnership. Want to help out? We're always looking for volunteers to help out at either events mentioned above or ones that you'd like to organise. Have a soft spot for your local route and want to get involved in promoting it? How about showing off your social media skills? Is there a community event in your area where you would like to hold a bus stall? Get in touch . The long term future of all these services depends on us, our friends, families and colleagues taking advantage and promoting them whether that's a one off journey or making it part of our routine. FAQ Bus not turned up or arrived more than 20 minutes late? See Compensation after Disruption on our website for your options. Some operators may offer a travel vouchers. How do I track my bus? Bustimes.org - this covers all buses. Operators app or website Where do I get bus timetables? Special mention for TravelineSW . Type in your route number, click the relevant service. Select whether you want just the main stops and press 'PDF'. The website will generate your own personalised timetable which can be printed out. Timetables are also available on the operators website or via Bustimes.org Over the last few years we have persuaded some bus operators to continue to fund the printing of timetables however we are finding this more challenging. Local libraries will often print timetables for a small fee. We also fund a small number for distribution at our bus stalls. How do I plan my journey? www.google.com/maps (Covers all types of transport) somerset.thinktravel.info (Covers bus journeys) How much is a bus journey? All single bus journeys are capped at £3 until the end of the year. The cap will reduce to £2 in January 2027. Some operators offer discounted tickets for short journeys, area based tickets or group tickets. Consider these to save money.

title: 4 St Georges House
subtitle: A contemporary first floor self-catering apartment, luxuriously furnished and equipped, less than 10 minutes easy walk from the centre of Bath. Private, secure parking. Awarded 4 Star Gold by Visit England.
bodyContent: A contemporary first floor self-catering apartment, luxuriously furnished and equipped, less than 10 minutes easy walk from the centre of Bath. Private, secure parking. Awarded 4 Star Gold by Visit England. Open-Plan Living Area Two sets of French doors open onto small balconies. The leather sofa and two soft leather reclining armchairs with footstools are snooze-inducing! A great room for relaxing and socialising. Kitchen A sleek contemporary kitchen with granite worktops and fitted appliances. Master Bedroom and Bedroom Two Both peaceful bedrooms have been luxuriously furnished with really comfortable beds (either superking or separate twins, as you prefer) and oak furniture. Bathrooms En suite shower room Family Bathroom Outside Secure, private parking for 1 car at the apartment (included in your rental). Extra parking is available nearby in the council run long-stay car park (payable locally). Secure bike storage. The Neighbourhood Peaceful, calm and very convenient. You won't need your car when you are here, all of Bath's famous sights, shops, restaurants and bars are within an easy walk. Immediately around the corner is one of Bath's many Georgian crescents - Norfolk Crescent - with parkland and a pedestrian gate onto the footpath by the River Avon. Less than 10 minutes walk takes you to the famous Royal Crescent, past Royal Victoria Park. 5 minutes walk and you are in Queen's Square and the centre of town with its shops, cafés, restaurants and bars. 10 minutes walk to enjoy the waters at Thermae Bath Spa

title: Greenacre Place Touring Caravan Park
subtitle: We are Mark & Linda and we would like to extend a very warm welcome to our Touring Caravan Site & Holiday Cottage. We took over Greenacre Place in 2006 and ran it as a fully grassed 10 pitch site , catering exclusively for adults.
bodyContent: In 2019 we decided to completely re-configure & refurbish the site, to include hardstandings for each pitch, a dog walking area and fully refurbished facilities. These are all improvements that our guests have mentioned over the years and we are so proud and pleased with the results. We can now accommodate caravans and motorhomes, whatever the weather. The reviews from our guests have been very positive & complimentary. Our aim, as it always has been, is to make our guests feel valued, comfortable & happy with their stay. Our Touring Site and Holiday Cottage are positioned about a mile from Junction 22 of the M5 making them ideally located for exploring the Somerset coastline & countryside alike. The Cottage is warm & cosy with two bedrooms & two bathrooms. An enclosed patio to the rear gives our guests the chance to relax & enjoy the outdoors. There is also parking for two cars. We have been accredited with an AA three Pennants award for the Touring Site & an AA 4 Star rating for our Holiday Cottage. Burnham-on-sea is approximately five minutes’ drive away, with its miles of sandy beaches, cafes, bars & restaurants. We are also well located for visiting Weston-Super-Mare, Glastonbury, Cheddar, Taunton and Bristol. If you enjoy cycling or walking, Exmoor, The Quantocks and the Somerset levels are close by, where you can enjoy a wealth of walks, cycle tracks & bird sanctuaries. Just across the road from Greenacre Place is the Oaktree Arena, home to Championship The Somerset Rebels Speedway Team. Racing during the summer season is on Wednesday evening between 19:30 and 21:30.

bodyContent: Dunkery Beacon Hotel near Minehead offers luxury accommodation and provide the perfect place to escape the rigours of day-to-day life and relax and unwind in a truly tranquil, rural location where breath-taking scenery abounds. Dining & Drinks Relaxed, friendly and sophisticated award-winning dining with a seasonally changing menu and a focus on locally-sourced produce. Our extensive wine list is supplied by top London wine merchant Berry Bros. & Rudd and West Country merchant Christopher Piper Wines. title: The Pump Room Restaurant
subtitle: Built in 1795, the Pump Room is one of the most elegant and historical buildings in the country, and today after more than 300 years people still come together to celebrate in this unique venue.
bodyContent: The Pump Room in Bath, Somerset was built in 1795, and is one of the most elegant and historical buildings in the country, and today after more than 300 years people still come together to celebrate in this unique venue. The Pump Room Restaurant is open daily for morning coffee and afternoon tea. This magnificent venue is also available to hire exclusively during the evening, providing the perfect setting for an array of events from weddings and receptions to gala dinners and balls. Catering at The Pump Room Restaurant is provided by renowned caterer Searcys, which operates in some of the most iconic attractions, from the Gherkin in London to Blenheim Palace in Oxford. Searcys pride themselves on their quality food and brilliant flavours and use locally sourced ingredients wherever possible. It is the only restaurant in Bath to have live musical performances daily. In the early days the Pump Room trio were believed to be one of the first resident bands in the country to perform. When the trio are not performing guests can enjoy music from resident pianist Jools Scott. Today visitors still come to the Pump Room to ‘taste the water’ and the 43 minerals that flow from the Pump Room spa. The morning menu is served from 10.00 until 11.45, featuring famous Bath buns and cakes with tea or coffee. The afternoon tea menu is served from noon until 17.45, with savoury and sweet selections to enjoy. Pre-booking is required. Please visit www.searcys.co.uk/pump-room-tickets .
tagline: Built in 1795, the Pump Room is one of the most elegant and historical buildings in the country.

bodyContent: Hayleaze Cottage is the perfect base for a rural retreat. Rural features include a stable door on arrival, an open-plan living room and kitchen with exposed beams. The comfortable leather sofa is perfect for unwinding after a busy day of exploring. The bedroom has a comfortable double bed, wardrobe and enough room for a cot if you bring your baby or toddler with you (Cot can be provided – please state this when booking). Pets are very welcome, with the cottage being dog friendly. Located on the edge of the village of Winsley, 2 miles from Bradford on Avon. Bath is 5 miles away. There is a direct bus which goes to the centre every 30 mins. The Indoor Pool and Games Room is a big hit with other guests. It is like a big bath, at 32 degrees! All within a mile: Hartley Farm Shop/Kitchen , The Seven Stars pub and a village shop

title: Be Wilder Camp
subtitle: Nestled within the rolling hills of Somerset, located close to Frome and a stone’s throw from Bruton. Our camping & glamping site, sits peacefully on a hillside next to 100 acres of wild woodland. Beautiful rolling views framed by abundant and biodiverse hedgerows makes for an easy escape back into nature.
bodyContent: Be Wilder Camp provides a family friendly and truly immersive experience with a range of beautiful glamping accommodation under canvas. Imagine camping without the stress, in the comfort of your fully furnished tent. Outside you can sit under the stars, toasting marshmallows or cooking your dinner on fire whilst looking out across some magnificent Somerset views. Tailored activities, faciliFes and courses run throughout the summer and are designed to give you the chance to learn and connect with others and the environment, helping us on our path to rewild ourselves and the land around us. We’re also available for group glamping and camping trips, with discounts available for multiple unit bookings. Contact us to find out more. https://be-wilder.co.uk/contact/ As we are situated within the Redwood Rare Breeds Farm you and your family are welcome to take a tour around the farm and refreshments are available too. Besides all this, Be Wilder Camp is a perfect base camp for you to visit many local attractions such as the vibrant town of Frome, beautiful Bruton, with both Longleat and Cheddar Gorge just 30 minutes away. Our onsite facilites are there to make your stay as easy and as comfortable as possible. Please take a look and join us for 2022.

title: Tonic! Motivation
subtitle: Shane Dean and his refreshing TONIC! talks help people to live and work with enthusiasm, positivity and energy to thrive in life and work. With tips, examples and inspirational videos and stories, TONIC! seminars help your staff to smile, laugh and hope again. TONIC! are positivity and productivity-boosting, motivation, productivity and morale boosters for businesses and workers.
bodyContent: TONIC Founder Shane Dean has been speaking to audiences since 2003. He overcame mental health struggles, anxiety and fear to become relentlessly positive, life enthusiast and award-winning journalist. His fun, energetic unique TONIC talks explore latest science, historical and current inspirational examples, taking tips from dogs, monks and people such as Nelson Mandela. TONIC! is ideal for team-building days, work conferences or one-off inspirational sessions. Shane can speak for one hour, a morning or over one day. Andrew Scott, CEO of the Ascot Group, said: “I have worked with some of the best speakers in the world over the years, but I’ve never met anyone with more authenticity, passion and ability to really inspire people as Shane Dean. “He never fails to motivate our 100+ staff, including the management and leadership teams; and the content he delivers is ideal for businesses and corporate organisations looking to achieve growth and deliver a morale boost.”
tagline: Do your people need a happiness lift? In these anxiety, fear-ridden days, we all do!

title: Declaration of Independence on display
subtitle: See a rare original 1776 Declaration of Independence on display in England for the first time during the 250th anniversary year. Explore immersive displays, exhibitions, talks and events as part of America 250 at American Museum & Gardens..
bodyContent: This summer, American Museum & Gardens presents America 250 - a season of exhibitions, events and cultural experiences marking 250 years since the founding of the United States. At the heart of the programme is a rare original 1776 Dunlap printing of the Declaration of Independence, now on display in England for the first time during the 250th anniversary year. Only 26 Dunlap copies survive worldwide, and this is the only known example to have been intercepted by British forces during the American Revolution and later annotated by British government officials. Visitors can follow a specially curated trail through the Museum’s historic Manor House, where immersive interpretation and displays explore the people, ideas and objects that shaped the founding of the United States, culminating in the signing of the Declaration of Independence. Displayed alongside the Declaration is a specially commissioned film from the Museum of the American Revolution in Philadelphia, offering further insight into the document and its enduring significance.
tagline: This summer, American Museum & Gardens presents America 250

title: Gather & Make: Seasonal paper-cut workshop
subtitle: Create your own seasonal paper-cut artwork inspired by the landscapes of Steart Marshes with local paper artist Sam Pierpoint.
bodyContent: Date: Tuesday 8th September Time: 10.00am - 12.00pm or 1.00pm - 3.00pm Cost: £10 suggested donation to support our work, booking is essential. This relaxed, hands-on workshop begins with a gentle wander through the reserve, where we’ll observe and gather inspiration from the plants, seed heads, grasses and textures of the season. Back under shelter, you’ll transform what you’ve noticed into your own bold seasonal paper-cut poster to take home. With guidance on composition, shape and cutting techniques, you’ll be supported step by step, whether you’re completely new to paper-cutting or already love to craft. This is a welcoming, creative session for adults, friends and families who’d like to slow down, enjoy the process of making, and connect more deeply with the season we are in. Please note - we will be working outside on the nature reserve, so dress accordingly, sturdy shoes are recommended. All materials will be provided. Where to meet: In the main WWT car park at Steart Marshes, Stert Drove, Bridgwater, Somerset, TA5 2PU. Book tickets: https://www.wwt.org.uk/wetland-centres/steart-marshes/whats-on/events/gather-make-seasonal-paper-cut-workshop

title: Sophie Ellis-Bextor Leads Biggest Ever ‘Night at the Abbey’ Line-up
subtitle: Twenty acts across four stages at Glastonbury Abbey's flagship music fundraiser.
bodyContent: Sophie Ellis-Bextor, Inspiral Carpets, The Blow Monkeys and Orbital's Phil Hartnoll are set to perform against one of Britain's most spectacular historic backdrops after Glastonbury Abbey unveiled the full line-up for its biggest ever Night at the Abbey. More than 20 artists will perform across four stages on Saturday, 12th September as the historic Somerset landmark is transformed into an open-air celebration of live music, DJs, street food and light, raising vital funds for the conservation of the Abbey. Headlining the evening is Sophie Ellis-Bextor, whose recent career renaissance has introduced her music to a new global audience, joined by alternative rock pioneers Inspiral Carpets, sophisticated pop favourites The Blow Monkeys, acclaimed Scottish collective An Dannsa Dub, bluegrass innovators The Often Herd and blues powerhouse Ruzz Guitar's Blues Revue. Elsewhere within the Abbey grounds, electronic music takes centre stage as Phil Hartnoll of Orbital and Alexis Taylor of Hot Chip perform special DJ sets alongside D:Ream, Mr C ( The Shamen) Live, Feat David H Percussion, Shades of Rhythm and a host of respected DJs celebrating more than three decades of British dance music culture. Hidden beneath the trees, The Nook offers an intimate woodland dancefloor, while the spectacular medieval Lady Chapel once again becomes home to the much-loved Rave In The Nave, a silent disco staged within one of the most extraordinary historic buildings in Britain. While festivals regularly occupy parks and greenfield sites, few can claim a setting quite like Glastonbury Abbey. Founded in the seventh century and regarded as one of Britain's most important monastic sites, the Abbey has inspired centuries of mythology, archaeology and pilgrimage, with enduring links to King Arthur, Queen Guinevere and some of the country's earliest Christian history. Today, it continues to evolve as a living heritage destination, using carefully curated events to introduce new audiences to the site while helping generate vital income for its conservation and future. “Night at the Abbey allows visitors to experience this remarkable place after hours, surrounded by live music, light and atmosphere, while every ticket sold helps support the conservation of one of Britain's most important heritage sites,” said Helen Smith, Director of Glastonbury Abbey. “We're delighted to welcome such an amazing line-up of artists this year and to continue creating an event that feels completely unique to Glastonbury Abbey.” As daylight fades, the Abbey's soaring ruins will be illuminated, creating an unforgettable backdrop for performances that span disco, indie, electronica, blues, bluegrass and contemporary folk. Alongside the music, visitors can explore a world street food market, independent traders and bars showcasing Somerset drinks alongside local beers, ciders and cocktails. Night at the Abbey has grown steadily into one of Somerset's standout late summer events, attracting audiences from across the South West and beyond, while helping ensure one of Britain's greatest historic landmarks remains at the heart of modern cultural life. Tickets are on sale now, with early allocation already sold out and remaining Tier Two tickets available at www.glastonburyabbey.com

title: Pawsome Pooch is back at Clarks Village
subtitle: Clarks Village’s hugely popular dog-friendly weekend is back – and it’s bigger and better than ever.
bodyContent: Clarks Village’s hugely popular dog-friendly weekend is back – and it’s bigger and better than ever. The Pawsome Pooch event will be held at the Somerset shopping outlet on Saturday 12 th and Sunday 13 th September, with the hunt to find the region’s top dog to become its next CEO – Canine Executive Officer. As well as offering free professional photo shoots for pups, Clarks Village is hosting complimentary pet pampering, dog trick training, have-a-go agility sessions, and pick ‘n’ mix treats – all promising to get tails in a spin. Plus, for the first time, Pawsome Pooch will be introducing a ‘dog walk’ for freshly pampered pups to strut their stuff as well as the chance for single owners to find love. Pawfect Match will invite single owners to pick up a free red bow for their dog and let them sniff out a potential love match. The event will also welcome back three VIPs (Very Important Pups) to Clarks Village; current CEO Archie the golden miniature dachshund who won the Pawsome Pooch competition last year, former CEO Dudley the three-legged Hungarian Vizsla, along with Bailey the whippet - the original Pawsome Pooch winner. The trio will be invited onto the dogwalk to unveil newly-commissioned portraits to be installed in a new Hall of Fame for the outlet’s CEOs. All activities at the Pawsome Pooch event are free as Clarks Village celebrates its canine guests. Plus, one dog will be crowned the outlet’s next CEO and win a prize package worth up to £500 – including shopping vouchers, dog toys and treats, and vouchers for Bill’s restaurant, Prezzo Italian, Sweaty Betty, Raging Bull, Jack Wolfskin, and Hallmark. Mike Jones, Centre Director of Clarks Village, commented: “Due to popular demand, we’ve made Pawsome Pooch bigger and better than ever before with a full dog-takeover of Clarks Village for an entire weekend. Jam packed with free, tail-wagging activities, it’s our way of celebrating our canine companions and showcasing our dog-friendly facilities and ethos where every member of the family is welcome.” The full line-up at Clarks Village’s Pawsome Pooch, from 11am-4pm on Saturday 12 th and Sunday 13 th September: · CEO Competition: Professional pet photo shoots where you’ll be gifted a free digital image and automatically entered into the competition. The shortlist will be revealed on Clarks Village’s social channels after the event for a public vote to pick the ulti-mutt winner. Book a photo shoot by signing up to Clarks Village’s free member rewards scheme PLUS+ or visit one of our two additional roaming photographers at the event. · Pawfect Match: Looking for love? Pick up a free red bow for your dog and let them sniff out a match! · Tricks and agility: South West dog trainers Passion for Pets will host trick and hoopers agility sessions as well as showcasing demonstrations. · Pampered Pooch: Somerset grooming studio About the Dog will offer free spruce ups, including paw-dicures and face trims, with a spritz of dog fragrance. · Pet Paw-traits: Illustrator Alan Snow returns for quick-fire sketches of pooches – charitable donation encouraged to the Guide Dogs. · Dogwalk: A fashion-inspired dogwalk for pooches to strut their stuff in style, rewarded with treats from the pick ‘n’ mix station, hosted by the part-human, part-canine Pedigree Panel characters. · CEO Hall of Fame: Receive a pawshake from Clarks Village’s past and present CEOs as they unveil their paw-fficial portraits for the outlet’s new Hall of Fame. As the UK’s most dog-friendly shopping centre – as voted for at the DogFriendly Awards – Clarks Village is an outdoor outlet featuring wide, paved walkways, stunning landscaped gardens, and plenty of shady spots, making it ideal location to bring furry friends. With water bowls throughout, dogs receive a warm welcome across the outlet, within most brands, and at selected cafes and restaurants. For more details on Pawsome Pooch, and how to secure an exclusive pre-bookable photo shoot, visit the Clarks Village website: www.clarksvillage.co.uk And to help Clarks Village to retain its DogFriendly title, vote now in the 2026 awards: tinyurl.com/dogfriendlyCV

title: Ashton Cottages
subtitle: Two delightful self catering cottages situated close to Cheddar, Wedmore, Wells and Weston-Super-Mare. Cosy open planned living cottages. Cottage one Sleeps 2-4 and Cottage two Sleeps 2-5. A warm welcome awaits you and your family, come and enjoy a relaxing holiday and soak up the beautiful Somerset countryside as Ashton Cottages are a grand base to explore.
bodyContent: Ashton Cottages are two cosy holiday retreats designed with couples and families in mind. We are set just above the stunning Somerset Levels , looking out to the Mendip hills . Both cottages offer modern country open plan living, with two bedrooms each and private gardens with patio and BBQ’s. With their own off road parking for two cars and a wonderful field for picnicking in and family fun, the cottages make for a great base for exploring the beautiful Somerset countryside. On our doorstep is the Historic quaint village of Wedmore which dates back to King Alfred the great. The village boasts pretty tearooms and country shops. Also on our doorstep is the village of Cheddar with Cheddar Gorge offering it famous caves, many shops, pubs and tearooms too. In easy reach we have the City of Wells with its world famous cathedral and the Bishops Palace, Wookey Hole caves, Glastonbury Tor and the Abbey Ruins, Bath, Bristol, Burnham-on-Sea, Weston-Super-Mare and Longleat are all close by. Are you a cyclist or keen walker? Then this is the perfect spot for you! Easily accessible from the M5 Junction 22 just 20 minutes away
tagline: Two delightful self catering cottages situated close to popular towns and villages

title: Country View Holiday Park
subtitle: Country View Holiday Park, Sand Bay near Weston Super Mare, Somerset. Touring caravans, motor-homes and tents on a quiet, family orientated site in picturesque surroundings in Somerset.
bodyContent: A warm welcome awaits you at the Country View Holiday Park in Sand Bay next to Weston Super Mare . Come and re-explore the area, there are so many things to see and do for day trips or simply relax on site and enjoy our facilities. Sand Bay beach is only 200 yards. We can accommodate touring caravans, motor-homes and tents on a quiet, family orientated site in picturesque surroundings. The Park is licensed for 190 pitches available for holiday touring purposes and also seasonal pitches. Do call us to enquire regarding rates of seasonal pitches. We also offer a range of static holiday homes for sale, so you could have your own holiday home at Country View in Somerset. Country View boasts a Heated outdoor swimming pool , bar, play area, games room, country meadows and our huge 5 acre dog walk, all complimentary. Superb disabled facilities too, please call with any query.
tagline: Great Holiday Park just yards from the beautiful Sand Bay Beach

title: Apple View & Bramley Lodge
subtitle: Apple View is the west wing of TempleFarm which lies on the edge of the Somerset Levels in a little village called Chedzoy just outside Bridgwater.
bodyContent: Apple View - B&B Accommodation Apple View is the west wing of Temple Farm which lies on the edge of the Somerset Levels in a little village called Chedzoy just outside Bridgwater . Set on a working livestock farm between Orchards and lush pastures it is an ideal place to come and see real farm life and sample the special culinary treats created for you from our own home-grown produce regularly used in Breakfast . These include our own Free Range eggs, fruit, vegetables, lamb, beef, homemade bread and preserves and soon sausage bacon and pork. Rest in peaceful stylish rooms and sleep in the most comfortable bed ever between pure cotton sheets and warm woollen blankets all rooms are en-suite and one room has facilities for the disabled including an accessible bathroom. “Apple View B&B is Bed and Breakfast at it’s best” – central to all Somerset has to offer – Glastonbury , Street ( Clarks Village ), and the Bath & West showground to the east, Exmoor , Dunster and Minehead to the West, Cricket St Thomas and Taunton to the South and Chedda r, Wookey Hole , the Mendip s and Bath to the North. Bramley Lodge - Self catering Bramley Lodge is a Scandinavian Log cabin. It has 3 Bed rooms and 2 bathrooms (1 en-suite) for the purpose of self catering. This new self catering facility has facilities for the disabled guest and is a luxury country retreat with it's own private patio and BBQ and is set amongst a mixed fruit orchard on the edge of the Temple Farm site. Guests here will also be able to meet the farm animals if the wish.

title: Around and About Bath
subtitle: Around and About Bath is a revolutionary tour company based in Bath, that is transforming the concept of what a local tour or dining experience.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. Around and About Bath is a revolutionary tour company based in Bath , that is transforming the concept of what a local tour or dining experience. Their 'Curated Experiences' are carefully crafted journeys of discovery for up to eight curious, discerning travellers looking to go beyond the conventional and obvious, to experience and truly connect with the very best of local culture, history, landscapes, people, places, food and drink in an intimate and meaningful manner. Each tour collects from central Bath before heading into the local region, and includes all costs such as entrances, lunch and refreshments. Their guides are incredibly knowledgeable and engaging and go to extraordinary lengths to provide an unforgettable, personal and immersive experience that is totally unique. Around and About Bath also offer fully inclusive dining tours, half-day tours, specials and bespoke, private services. Discover authentic England and the Highlight of your visit. Guaranteed.
tagline: Around and About Bath is a revolutionary tour company based in Bath.

title: Horseshoe Cottage, Lime Kiln Farm
subtitle: Horseshoe is the largest of Lime Kiln Farm's three beautiful luxury self catering holiday cottages set in stunning Somerset countryside just 15 minutes drive from Bath.
bodyContent: Horseshoe is the largest of Lime Kiln Farm's three beautiful, luxury self catering holiday cottages set in stunning Somerset countryside just 15 minutes drive from Bath. The views are wonderful and there is a large private garden, perfect for family parties or BBQs. This converted stable building has two large ensuite bedrooms, sleeping up to 6 and is renovated to a very high standard, complete with all modern conveniences including free WIFI.The cottage is all on one level and suitable for wheelchair users. Lime Kiln Farm is pet and dog friendly so contact them when booking to discuss bringing your pets. With easy access to the Bath Park & Ride, Horseshoe Cottage is also perfectly located for exploring the many tourist attractions including local pubs and Lavender Farm, Cheddar Gorge, Wookey Hole Caves, Wells, Stourhead House & Gardens and the nearby Longleat Safari Park.

title: Pitchperfect Camping
subtitle: Tent and small campervan only on grass pitches. Electric hook ups available. Accept family groups.
bodyContent: Generous sized pitches. Clean facilities with free hot showers, washing up area with fridges/freezers. Central play area, petanque pitch, ping pong table, firepits available on all pitches. Small onsite shop. Onsite catering available including pizzas / pies / breakfasts. Nice local pubs. 5* Tripadvisor rating and Travellers’ Choice award winners since 2015.

title: The Beach Hotel Weston-super-Mare
subtitle: The Beach Hotel Weston boasts a variety of room types and spaces for you to relax within its spacious walls. Just a short walk along the promenade and you’ll find all the fun of the seaside, from Weston’s iconic Grand Pier to the Tropicana and beyond, there’s plenty to explore.
bodyContent: The newly revamped Beach Hotel is situated in the prime location for a seaside holiday to the infamous town of Weston-super-Mare. Overlooking the seafront and with views out and across the Bristol Channel to islands such as Steepholm and Flatholm, you can take in all of the scenic views from our hotel. With a variety of rooms to suit your needs, there is a space for everyone at the Beach Weston. From family rooms to 2 fully accessible bedrooms located on the ground floor, we can cater to your individual needs. Twinned with the award-winning Beach Hotel Minehead, we are a social enterprise run by YMCA Dulverton Group.
tagline: The Beach Hotel Weston boasts a variety of room types and spaces for you to relax

title: South Sands Hotel - Weston-super-Mare
subtitle: South Sands Hotel is an independent hotel nestled in the village of Kewstoke and located just across the road from the hidden gem that is Sand Bay.
bodyContent: South Sands Hotel offers a touch of luxury and serenity tucked away from the hustle and bustle of the main town of Weston-super-Mare. There are two restaurants in the hotel. Rock Salt, embraces a laid back dining experience serving fresh seafood and traditional dishes. The Bay, open for afternoon tea and dinner introduces a fresh, locally sourced menu where you can enjoy fresh fish caught along the South Coast or enjoy our local 35 day Himalayan salt-aged steaks. The Bay really does give you a reason to dress up and will often have live music to enjoy while you dine. As well as a fabulous choice of dining they also have the South Suite, an extensive space perfect for weddings, events and conferences. Find out more here https://www.south-sands.co.uk/

title: Walnut Tree Cottage
subtitle: Walnut Tree Cottage is a beautifully light & airy cottage. Extending over two floors with 3 bedrooms, quirky vaulted ceilings and two fully tiled bathrooms.
bodyContent: Walnut Tree Cottage is a beautifully light and airy cottage extending over two floors with 3 bedrooms and two full size bathrooms. The Cottage consists of a large lounge/kitchen/diner. It has a ground floor double bedroom with built in wardrobes and its own bathroom through a small lobby and then upstairs there is a substantial twin room a large single with vaulted ceilings and roof windows that look out over our fields, ancient Walnut Tree and chickens. There is also a further full size bathroom upstairs. We have taken care to finish this cottage to a high standard with engineered oak flooring, fully tiled bathrooms, large walk-in shower and co-ordinating fabrics and soft furnishings. It is a lovely place to stay. Outside of the cottage is a shared lawned paddock and an open air solar heated swimming pool. There is plenty of on-site parking available at the farm and our own little farmshop/butchery for all your breakfast needs! Next door to Walnut is its new “sister” property, Oak Tree Cottage.
tagline: Walnut Tree Cottage is a beautifully light & airy cottage

bodyContent: Get your spooky costumes ready for The Beachcomber's legendary Halloween party! Featuring live entertainment from Noughty Nineties, Ariana Grande Tribute and Chris Cullen’s children’s show. Free entry and everyone welcome. Visit www.beachcomberbrean.co.uk for more info.

Follow a flower-themed trail, take part in interactive challenges, make paper flower crowns and sunflowers, try your hand at ancient games, and meet the Roman goddess Flora as she prepares for her festival, Floralia. Activities will take place at different times. See website for further details.

bodyContent: Leave your pitchforks at the door and get in our swamp.. Ogrepalooza, is heading to Komedia Bath on Friday 4th December! Headlined by the UK's #1 Shrek tribute band, TheOgretones - an 8-piece live band featuring Shrek, Fiona and Donkey & Friends with legendary performances that will transport you straight to the heart of the swamp. Expect hits from Smash Mouth, Counting Crows, Ricky Martin, The Proclaimers, Bonnie Tyler, David Bowie, Led Zeppelin, Buzzcocks, and more! title: Sherlock Holmes and the Hound of the Baskervilles at The Bishop's Palace
subtitle: Join us for a summer evening of outdoor theatre in Somerset as The Pantaloons bring their riotous new adaptation of Sherlock Holmes and the Hound of the Baskervilles to the historic grounds of The Bishop’s Palace.
bodyContent: Set against the stunning backdrop of the Palace and 14 acres of RHS partner gardens, this open-air performance is a must-see event in Wells for summer 2026. The critically acclaimed The Pantaloons return with their signature high-energy style, blending live music, fast-paced comedy and audience interaction. Can detective duo Holmes and Watson uncover the truth behind the Baskerville family curse before it strikes again? Expect chaos, quick costume changes and plenty of laughter as this Victorian thriller is reimagined for modern audiences. Perfect for families, couples and theatre-lovers looking for unique things to do in Somerset this June. Bring a picnic blanket or camping chair, and relax on the South Lawn for a memorable open-air theatre experience. Whether you are visiting Wells for a short break, exploring Somerset on holiday, or looking for local events near you, this performance has something for everyone. This is a fundraising event for the Palace Trust.
tagline: Set against the stunning backdrop of the Palace and 14 acres of RHS partner gardens

title: From the Jam
subtitle: From the Jam was formed naturally in 2004 by Russell Hastings with 2/3 of the original line-up featuring Rick Buckler (The Jam) and Bruce Foxton (The Jam).
bodyContent: The band have toured extensively worldwide and, to this day, continue playing to adoring fans - including the original fans and, of course, younger ones being brought up on this music! Russell and the guys are known for not trying to be like Paul, Bruce and Rick, but magically they sound identical, with as much passion as the band produced in those five years from '77 through to '82. "I just go up and sing the songs how I remember them being sung and I am many thousands of shows in now, and I also had the good fortune of playing with Bruce and Rick for many years, and they became my dearest friends. So we ended up sharing the idiosyncrasies of the songs, which I guess gives its authenticity. Who knows? It just works, and people love singing those songs that mean so much to them!” - Russell Hastings Rick left the band in 2010 to pursue other projects, leaving both Bruce Foxton and Russell Hastings to form forces with Mark Brzezicki from Big Country on drum duties. It was around this time that the first ‘Foxton and Hastings’ album, Back In The Room, was born - recorded at Paul Weller’s Black Barn Studios and also featuring Paul Weller on three or four songs including the hit single ‘Number Six’ with Paul on piano duties. The band continued touring, filling larger and larger venues worldwide across Japan, America and Australia. In 2015 came the second album, Smash The Clock,
tagline: From the Jam was formed naturally in 2004 by Russell Hastings with 2/3 of the original line-up

title: Stone Age SOS at Cheddar Gorge and Caves
subtitle: SENDING OUT A STONE AGE SOS!
bodyContent: Discover the stinky, epic, dangerous world of our prehistoric ancestors - and the secrets of Stone Age survival at Cheddar Gorge and Caves this summer! Visitors will be transported through time and embark on an interactive and thrilling journey into the prehistoric world of our ancient ancestors this summer. Experience the excitement of the Stone Age in an action-packed day filled with live demonstrations, interactive fun, and unforgettable discoveries. Stay Alive’ • 1pm & 4pm - Ancient Remedies: ‘Healing plants and Stone Age secrets’ And keep a look out for Marmalade, our marvellous mammoth mascot; he’ll be doing meet and greets in front of Gough’s Café each day. title: The Three Waters audio event
subtitle: Join artists Simone Einfalt and Ralph Hoyte to experience interactive sounds and moving images, representing the environments at Steart Marshes.
bodyContent: Date: Sunday 20th September Time: 10.00am-11.00am, 12.00pm-1.00pm, 2.00pm-3.00pm. Cost: Free event, booking is essential. Simone Einfalt and Ralph Hoyte’s collaboration The Three Waters is an experiment in using interactive sound and moving image to respond to the liminal salt marsh environment of Steart Marshes. The Three Waters are Salt, Brackish and Fresh, with each Water becoming a character in its own right, representing the ever changing habitats. Visitors are invited to book in for one of the collective sound experiences mediated by linked autonomous speaker units on the marsh itself, and are also invited to visit the upcoming unique audio-visual gallery installations at East Quay and Bridgwater Art Centre between December 2026 - February 2027. Please note – we will be working outside on the nature reserve, so dress accordingly, sturdy shoes are recommended. All materials are provided for the event. Where to meet: Meet at the roundhouse, WWT Steart Marshes, Bridgwater, Somerset, TA5 2PU. (Ask a member of staff for directions). Book tickets here: https://www.wwt.org.uk/wetland-centres/steart-marshes/whats-on/events/the-three-waters-event-at-steart-marshes

title: Europe’s Only Willow Plantation for Elephants Reopens at Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm
subtitle: After a period of regeneration, Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm’s five African bull elephants are once again exploring their unique 5,000 square metre willow plantation.
bodyContent: After a period of regeneration, Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm’s five African bull elephants are once again exploring their unique 5,000 square metre willow plantation. Janu, the dominant male of the bachelor group, led the way as the plantation reopened, followed by other members of the herd. All five elephants will have the opportunity to explore the plantation as access is rotated, giving them the chance to investigate the regenerated vegetation at their own pace. Located within Elephant Eden in North Somerset, the plantation is the first of its kind in the UK and the only one in Europe, providing a large area of dense woodland within the elephants’ expansive habitat. The plantation was first opened to the elephants in 2022 following almost a decade of planning and growth. Since then, the bulls’ natural feeding and browsing behaviours have significantly shaped the landscape. The plantation is therefore periodically rested, allowing the vegetation to recover before the elephants return. Willow, aspen and poplar trees, alongside self-seeded trees, bushes and other elephant-friendly vegetation, have now had time to regenerate, creating a diverse and changing source of natural browse. African elephants can spend many hours of the day feeding, browsing and foraging. Their size and natural behaviours also have a significant impact on the landscape around them, making the plantation a constantly evolving part of their habitat. Tom Lindley, Elephant Section Leader at Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm, said: “The plantation has changed significantly since the elephants last had access to it, so it has been fascinating to watch them explore it again. With the current heatwave, it’s particularly great to see them enjoying the lush vegetation and making the most of the cool, green environment. African elephants are incredibly effective at shaping their environment. They browse, strip bark, break branches and feed their way through vegetation, so giving the plantation time to regenerate means that when they return, there is plenty of new growth for them to investigate. It will also be lovely to see our two newest bulls, Impi and Mchumba, exploring the plantation. They’ve been settling into the bachelor group really well since arriving in May, and having the opportunity to explore different areas of their habitat is an important part of becoming familiar with their new surroundings.

title: Victoria Art Gallery
subtitle: Opened in 1900, the Victoria Art Gallery boasts an outstanding collection of paintings, sculptures and decorative arts. The gallery is located in the centre of Bath, near the famous Pulteney Bridge. Entry to the permanent exhibitions is free.
bodyContent: Opened in 1900, the Victoria Art Gallery boasts an outstanding collection of paintings, sculptures and decorative arts. The gallery is located in the centre of Bath , near the famous Pulteney Bridge. Entry to the permanent exhibitions is free. You’ll see more than 1,500 artworks, including many by artists who have lived and worked in the Bath area, such as Thomas Gainsborough and Walter Sickert. The work on show spans the 15th century to the present day. In the 18th century Bath was an important centre for portrait painting, and in the 20th century it again became famous thanks to the innovative works being produced by artists at the renowned Bath Academy of Art at Corsham Court. Alongside the permanent collections, the Victoria Art Gallery also hosts an exciting programme of temporary exhibitions and events throughout the year. Please check the Victoria Art Gallery website for the latest information.
tagline: Opened in 1900, the Victoria Art Gallery boasts an outstanding collection.

title: Victorian Annexe
subtitle: The Victorian Annexe is a two bedroom, self contained holiday rental attached to a Georgian property.
bodyContent: The accommodation is a self-contained Annexe that was added to the main Georgian House in Victorian Times. The first and second floors cover a very generous 82m2. The open plan living area is on the ground floor, the 2 double bedrooms are on the first floor, and these are connected by a spiral staircase. There is a large hallway and second staircase to the bathroom and toilet. The open plan ground floor living area provides an extremely comfortable and functional space for 4 people. Entertainment is provided by a 40” HDTV and a fantastic inbuilt wood burner. A leather sofa and single armchair provide relaxing seating. For meal times there is a circular wooden table and 4 sturdy wooden chairs. There is a fully equipped kitchen with modern oven, induction hob, dishwasher, fridge-freezer, extractor fan, toaster and kettle. The downstairs lighting can be adjusted to match your mood and needs. For lots of light there are the downlighters, for the early evening there is the discrete yet functional kitchen lighting and for late evening there is the warm glow from the uplighters in the middle of the room. The space is also practical with plenty of coat hooks, boot rack, waste bin and under-sink recycling container. Upstairs there are 2 very comfortable Vi-Spring beds with crisp white cotton bedding. The first bed is superking size and the second is a double. Both rooms have a minimalist feel and are finished with floor-length silk curtains. The bathroom is comfortably large with the usual toilet, washbasin and large enamelled bath that houses a separate shower. For convenience the bathroom also contains a washer-dryer that can be set to wash and dry clothes overnight. Iron, ironing board and other standard equipment are contained in the ceiling high cupboard outside of the bathroom. The Annexe has walls that are 2 feet thick and is well insulated. As part of its refurbishment, underfloor heating was fitted downstairs and efficient radiators everywhere else. There are 2 separate and fully automatic heating circuits that ensure the 2 floors of the Annexe are warm and toasty when required but not oppressively so overnight. A third circuit ensures that the floor-ceiling towel warmer does its job and keeps the bathroom especially warm at peak times. Whilst this is a great space, the 2 staircases (without stairgates and with wide gaps between stanchions), relatively narrow access to the main entrance door would present particular challenges to those with mobility problems and potentially for families with small children. But please feel free to contact us to clarify any potential issues.
tagline: The Victorian Annexe is a two bedroom, self contained holiday rental

title: Apsley House
subtitle: Located about 30 minutes walk from the City Centre, the Apsley House in Bath was built as a country home by The Duke of Wellington.
bodyContent: Located about 30 minutes walk from the City Centre, the Apsley House in Bath was built as a country home by The Duke of Wellington, after his momentous victory against Napoleon in the Battle of Waterloo. The rumour is that it was built as a place where he could keep his mistress of that time, as he was estranged from his wife years earlier. The hotel has been refurbished in great style and every care has been taken to preserve the natural elegance of the house, but still provide modern comforts. The magnificently proportioned reception rooms offer both style and comfort, with many period features complimented by the house being furnished with fine antiques and original oil paintings. Owned by Nick and Claire Potts ‘Apsley House Hotel’ is one of Bath’s finest small hotels. Resident Managers, Kate and Miro, offer guests a very warm welcome and personal care with the atmosphere more in keeping to that of a Private House than that of a hotel. Reception is always available if you require information on how best to spend your time in and around the beautiful city of Bath. Our Reservations department is open from 10am – 9pm daily. The Hotel has 12 delightfully appointed en-suite rooms across three floors (no lift access). Some rooms feature air-conditioners. Free Wireless internet access is available throughout. A freshly cooked feast of a breakfast with daily specials, is served in our elegant dining room. A lovely south facing garden is ideal for the summer evening aperitif. Complimntary parking is also available.
tagline: Located about 30 minutes walk from the City Centre, the Apsley House in Bath

subtitle: Join artists Simone Einfalt and Ralph Hoyte to experience interactive sounds and moving images, representing the environments at Steart Marshes.
bodyContent: Date: Sunday 27th September Time: 10.00am-11.00am, 12.00pm-1.00pm, 2.00pm-3.00pm. Cost: Free event, booking is essential. Simone Einfalt and Ralph Hoyte’s collaboration The Three Waters is an experiment in using interactive sound and moving image to respond to the liminal salt marsh environment of Steart Marshes. The Three Waters are Salt, Brackish and Fresh, with each Water becoming a character in its own right, representing the ever changing habitats. Visitors are invited to book in for one of the collective sound experiences mediated by linked autonomous speaker units on the marsh itself, and are also invited to visit the upcoming unique audio-visual gallery installations at East Quay and Bridgwater Art Centre between December 2026 - February 2027. Please note – we will be working outside on the nature reserve, so dress accordingly, sturdy shoes are recommended. All materials are provided for the event. Where to meet: Meet at the roundhouse, WWT Steart Marshes, Bridgwater, Somerset, TA5 2PU. (Ask a member of staff for directions). Book tickets: https://www.wwt.org.uk/wetland-centres/steart-marshes/whats-on/events/three-waters-audio-event-at-steart-marshes

title: New Series of Inside Longleat Airs Next Week
subtitle: The series is back for an eight-episode run starting on Tuesday 21 July at 8pm on 5.
bodyContent: Inside Longleat returns for another series revealing what happens at the estate throughout the year. The series is back for an eight-episode run starting on Tuesday 21 July at 8pm on 5. Filming took place over a 10-month period to capture life on the estate and the people essential day-to-day operations, including Cheddar Gorge & Caves, Longleat’s sister attraction owned by the estate. Simon Askew, Chief Operating Officer, said “We’re incredibly excited to give viewers the chance to see behind the scenes once again and to celebrate the success of the programme so far. From a one-off episode in 2023, a three-part series in 2025 to eight episodes now is an incredible feat. “Viewers will see inside some of our events, as well as how much there truly is to Longleat beyond the animals and house.” The first episode focuses on the 60th anniversary of the Drive-Through Safari and how the much-loved attraction evolved into what guests see today. Throughout the series, viewers will see the transformation of The Farmhouse, one of the park’s luxury accommodation cottages, follow new Head Gardener Lucy, and discover the truth about previously unseen prehistoric bones at Cheddar Gorge. Viewers can Watch | Stream on 5 from 8pm on Tuesday 21 July.

title: Sunset shopping and late-night dining: Clarks Village extended opening hours and free evening parking
subtitle: Clarks Village has transformed into the ultimate evening destination with extended opening hours for shopping and dining – plus free evening parking.
bodyContent: Guests will now have more time to explore the Somerset shopping outlet, with brands opening an extra hour daily – and an extra two hours every Thursday – as well as vibrant late-night restaurants. To make evening visits even more seamless, free parking is also available at Clarks Village after 6pm. With a stunning outdoor setting including landscaped gardens and wide paved malls, Clarks Village is located in Street in the heart of Somerset and is home to more than 90 brands offering up to 60% off RRP, from designer names to high street favourites alongside delicious dining destinations. The new extended opening hours sees Clarks Village’s retail brands open from 9am-7pm on Monday to Saturdays, open an extra hour until 8pm on Thursdays. Sunday hours are from 10am-5pm. For evening dining, Clarks Village’s restaurants stay open until at least 9pm – opening as late as 10pm on weekdays and 11pm at weekends*. The extended opening hours comes as the outlet continues to grow and enhance its coveted line-up. Recent arrivals include iconic shoe brand Crocs and heritage homeware brand Christy, joining premium names such as Levi’s, Mint Velvet, Tommy Hilfiger, Sweaty Betty, Calvin Klein, Rituals and the largest Clarks shoe store in the world. Guests can also look forward to visiting the newly revamped Dune London shoe store and lifestyle brand Joules, which reopens later this month following a refurbishment. Offering indoor and alfresco dining, Clarks Village’s late-night restaurants include Wagamama, Bill’s, Pizza Express and the newly reimagined Prezzo Italian, as well as quick-service outlet Slim Chickens. Clarks Village is also family friendly with a fun adventure playground and monster-themed mindfulness trail. And as the UK’s most dog-friendly shopping centre, dogs receive a warm welcome throughout the outlet and most of its brands with its annual dog-celebratory Pawsome Pooch weekend set to be held on September 12th-13th. Mike Jones, Centre Director at Clarks Village, commented: “Clarks Village is an enormously popular daytime destination for both locals and guests visiting from further afield. By extending our hours and offering late-night dining combined with free evening parking, we’ve creating a ‘golden hour’ experience, giving our guests flexibility to make the most of everything the outlet has to offer at any time of the day and long into the evening.” For more details on opening hours, shopping and dining and what’s on at Clarks Village, including how to join its free members reward programme PLUS+, visit www.clarksvillage.co.uk * Restaurants opening times: Prezzo: 11.30am-10pm Sun-Thurs, 11.30am-11pm Fri-Sat. Wagamama: 11am-9pm daily. Bill’s: 9am-9pm Mon-Fri, 8am-9pm Sat, 9am-8pm Sun Pizza Express: 11.30am-9pm Mon-Weds, 11.30am-9.30pm Thurs & Sun, 11.30am-10pm Fri-Sat. Slim Chickens: 9.30am-9pm Mon-Thu, 9.30am-10pm Fri-Sat, 9.30am-8pm Sun.

title: Conference & Meeting Rooms at The Castle at Taunton
subtitle: The Castle Hotel offers a superb venue for your next conference, event or board meeting in Somerset. Located in Taunton town centre, we are just minutes from the M5 and a short walk from both the mainline train & coach stations. A perfect venue for regional meetings, The Castle is just half an hour from the outskirts of Exeter and 45 minutes from Bristol by car. Both cities have international airports.
bodyContent: The Castle Hotel offers a superb venue for your next conference, event or board meeting in Somerset. Located in Taunton town centre, we are just minutes from the M5 and a short walk from both the mainline train & coach stations. A perfect venue for regional meetings, The Castle is just half an hour from the outskirts of Exeter and 45 minutes from Bristol by car. Both cities have international airports. While many companies enjoy the Castle’s meeting facilities, corporate is not necessarily a word that you would associate with us. Each of our five private meeting rooms are individually decorated, imparting a distinct identity to your conference hire. From our Penthouse with its stunning views across Taunton and the Quantock Hills to the magnificent Music room with its high ceilings and large windows. Each room provides a space in which people can easily learn, think and be inspired. Our meeting rooms will be set up as you’ve requested, including equipment, and all refreshments will be delivered in a timely manner. Our Meeting Rooms: MUSIC ROOM The magnificient high ceilings, panelled walls and peaceful, secure setting make it an ideal venue for top level business meetings and conferences. The Music Room can accommodate up to 100 people theatre style. This is a perfect room for networking events & awards ceremonies. PENTHOUSE The Castle’s Penthouse is a versatile space, ideal for both board meetings & entertaining. Situated at the top of the hotel with panoramic views of the Blackdown & Quantock Hills, the Penthouse can seat up to 12 and has its own private roof garden. WISTERIA ROOM The Wisteria Room offers an intimate setting with outstanding views of the Castle’s legendary wisteria during the summer months. This room can accomodate up to 30 people or be opened into the adjoining Garden Room to create space for 80 people. GARDEN ROOM Our Garden room offers seating for up to 50 people on its own or it can also be joined with the Wisteria room to create seating for up to 80 people, all overlooking our beautiful Norman Gardens. SYNDICATE ROOM With seating for 8 in a professional boardroom atmosphere, the Syndicate Room is well suited to formal meetings.
tagline: The Castle Hotel offers a superb venue for your next conference, event or board meeting in Somerset.
