title: Somerset Yurts
subtitle: Somerset Yurts is situated on Hill Farm, an arable and dairy farm in the Quantock Hills. We are around 5 miles north of Taunton, the county town of Somerset.
bodyContent: You will find our site nestled over 3 beautiful, peaceful fields that boast stunning, uninterrupted views over Taunton Vale and the Blackdown Hills beyond. In such serene surroundings you’ll soon unwind and find yourself immersed in the countryside. Below you’ll find more information about the types of accomodation we have available for you. We have 4 traditional Mongolian yurts – Cherrygrove, Moonslade, Gotton Down and Furzeclose – and one UK made one – Meadow Yurt. The Mongolian yurts have a lovely cosy feeling to them, with multiple layers of fabric and felt to keep you warm and dry, and wonderful bright hand painted roof poles with tradition mongolian patterns. The Yurts are about 6m across and inside you’ll find: a double bed, double futon, table and chairs, a couple of smaller side units and the woodburner. Outside there is a BBQ and picnic table. There are plenty of Prakti charcoal stoves available to freely borrow if you fancy trying a charcoal hob…we cook with one at home a lot over the summer….and a couple of back up camping gas hobs if you need the control of gas. As with all our accomodation it’s a short walk to the facilities barn which provides a regular kitchen, hot power showers and proper flushing loos. Meadow Yurt is a slightly different design – it’s the same width approx 6m across and it has the same contents inside – double bed, futon, table / chairs side units and woodburner – but a slightly different layout and yurt design. It feels a little more open and spacious due to a different design of the roof poles and is made of a beautiful oiled cherry wood. Outside contents the same as the Mongolian Yurts – a picnic table and BBQ. There’s a map of the site and details about the dutch barn facilities below.
tagline: Somerset Yurts is situated on Hill Farm, an arable and dairy farm in the Quantock Hills

title: The Jane Austen Centre
subtitle: The Jane Austen Centre is in the heart of the Georgian city of Bath, between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths. Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The Jane Austen Centre is in the Georgian city of Bath , Somerset , between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths . Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family. Here you will find out more about Jane Austen, her time in Bath and how the city shaped her work. You can also dress up in Regency costume, taste Regency-recipe biscuits, sample perfumes from the era, try your hand at writing with a quill and ink, have your photo taken with their world famous waxwork, try their delightful ‘Tea With Mr Darcy’ in the Regency Tea Room, and browse their bespoke Giftshop.
tagline: The Jane Austen Centre is in the heart of the Georgian city of Bath.

title: Moncrate Cottage
subtitle: Superbly located cottage 2 miles from Bradford on Avon and 5 miles from Bath.
bodyContent: Superbly located cottage 2 miles from Bradford on Avon and 5 miles from Bath. The recently refurbished Moncrate Cottage gives the perfect home-from-home feel that everyone wants on holiday, plus the cottage is dog friendly if you want to include your pet on your holiday. Comfortable and cosy accommodation for a family getaway in wonderful rural surroundings. A well-equipped property with everything you should need. The Indoor heated pool and Games Room on site provides endless entertainment for the whole family.

title: The Plume of feathers
subtitle: Plume of Feathers is above all, a traditional English country pub. Serving the local community for over 200 years as a place to relax, enjoy company and exchange news and information.
bodyContent: A Traditional Country Pub Plume of Feathers is above all, a traditional English country pub. Serving the local community for over 200 years as a place to relax, enjoy company and exchange news and information. We have a hand picked selection of fine ales from the local Buttcombe brewery and always have one guest ale, and a traditional cider. A wide selection of wines are available by the glass or bottle, and our top shelf includes quality single malt whiskeys and other fine spirits. Families Welcome We welcome families and accompanied children. A stream runs past outside, and there is a shallow ford one hundred metres away. We have a beer garden at the rear of the pub . We have a variety of very traditional pub games including shove ha'penny, table skittles, darts and a pool table. Please think carefully before challenging the "Old Boys" to cribbage for 50p a corner. Board games and playing cards are available on request. The Food We use only fresh ingredients in all our meals. We use local produce and suppliers wherever possible for our meat, fish and vegetables. We have a dining room that seats twenty, and additional tables are available in our bar area. English weather permitting, food may also be served in our beer garden. Our chef shops on a daily basis, sourcing the freshest and best produce available, and only then deciding the best way to cook it. For this reason it is impossible to maintain an accurate menu of exactly what is on the blackboard today. title: Apple Tree Hotel
subtitle: The Apple Tree Hotel is a family owned and run Country Hotel surrounded by farmland and nestled at the foot of the Quantock Hills. The Apple Tree is a great choice if you are looking for a quality hotel in Somerset. Here, you'll receive a warm welcome, great food and excellent service making it one of the best places to stay in Somerset. We use local suppliers and produce wherever possible and collect our free range eggs from the farm in the next village.
bodyContent: Our homely country Bar offers a good selection of spirits, liqueurs, wines, draught and bottled beers to accompany your meal or just to relax and while away your evening. The library has a wide selection of books, choose one during your stay and nestle back into one of our comfy sofas. The hotel is located on the A39 between Bridgwater and Minehead, not far from the M5 and the closest hotel to Hinkley Point it is situated perfectly for exploring the many wonders and attractions in Somerset all year round. Ride on the West Somerset Railway, visit the Quantock Hills and Exmoor with their attractive villages, heathlands, hills and wooded coombes. There is ample free car parking and complimentary Hi-Speed Wi-Fi for all guests. If you are looking for a base near Bridgwater , Somerset which is ideally located for seeing the many places of interest and attractions, then the Apple Tree Hotel is for you. The nearby Quantock Hills which were designated as the first ever AONB (area of outstanding natural beauty) in England in 1956, have miles of the finest Walking, Mountain Biking and Riding tracks in the South West with amazing views over the Bristol Channel. Have a round of golf, horse ride or visit one of the nearby fishing lakes. The Somerset levels and Steart Marshes provide some great walking, bird watching and cycling tracks. Visit award winning Coleridges' Cottage in nearby Nether Stowey or the Walled Gardens of Cannington or take a trip on the West Somerset Steam Train. Slightly further afield is Exmoor , Medieval Dunster and Castle , Glastonbury Tor and Abbey , the Cathedral and town of Wells , Cheddar Gorge and Caves and Wookey Hole and Caves with lots to entertain the children and adults alike. If you have any spare time for shopping Clarks Village Outlet at Street is a must with over 90 designer and high street brands.
tagline: The Apple Tree Hotel is a family owned and run Country Hotel

title: Do Yoga
subtitle: Join us for SUP Yoga in the summer, regular Yoga classes, workshops and weekend retreats in Somerset and the South West
bodyContent: Do Yoga retreats are a wonderful way to relax and enjoy your Yoga practice in good company. Emma is a highly qualified and experienced teacher and you will be gently guided to make the most of your time away with Do Yoga. The beautiful settings for the retreats use nature as a backdrop for a weekend of true relaxation. Join us in inspiring surroundings, for healthy food, deep soulful Yoga flow and sparkling conversation. Drop in to any of the regular sessions that suits your schedule or join one of the weekend workshops to take a deeper dive and discover the healing potential of this ancient art.

title: Vellum Stone Cottage
subtitle: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway.
bodyContent: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway – indoor pool and games room on site, Kennet and Avon Canal Close by (3/4 of a mile), walking and cycling from your doorstep. Farm Shop and country pub(s) within walking distance. The cottage features a country feel with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams, with soft furnishings compliment. Enjoy admiring the sheep in the fields surrounding the farm.
tagline: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway.

title: At the Manor
subtitle: Manor Farm House self catering accommodation is spacious, comfortable and tastefully decorated and can accommodate large groups of 10-15 guests.
bodyContent: We are a 15 minute drive from the beautiful city of Bath and a perfect location for family celebrations, birthdays and anniversaries, wedding groups, girlie gatherings and business meetings. The country house has a calming, relaxing atmosphere. We also provide bed and breakfast accommodation. This gorgeous country Manor near Bath in the heart of Somerset was once a Grange and run by Monks from a nearby monastery in Tudor times. We are tucked away down a quiet country lane in the heart of the conservation village of Norton St Philip. The central village location allows our guests a leisurely stroll to the local pubs including the famous George Inn. Discover stunning countryside walks and a meander around the historic conservation village of Norton St Philip. There are many cycle routes in this area too including the renovated old train tunnel into Bath. We are also close to Bradford on Avon for canal walks, boating and cycling, Wells – the film Hot Fuzz was filmed here, Longleat Safari Park, Glastonbury – climb the ancient Tor, Stonehenge, Frome – the best market ever is held the first Sunday of each month and Salisbury.
tagline: Manor Farm House self catering accommodation is spacious, comfortable and tastefully decorated

title: Family Trail: Motte & Bailey Investigate the Viking Raid on Watchet Mint
subtitle: Come and see Dunster's rare double overshot watermill in action with a day of milling, demos, talks and more to celebrate National Mills Weeken
bodyContent: Detective duo, Motte & Bailey, have travelled back in time to the 10th Century. Vikings have raided the Royal Mint in the nearby harbour town of Watchet and stolen some Saxon silver coins. The Vikings have hidden the coins in the castle grounds for safe keeping until they board their longships at sea. Can you help Motte & Bailey recover the coins and return them to the Royal Mint? Follow the trail, crack the clues and take part in hands‑on activities as you learn all about the Vikings & Saxons! Complete the trail to claim your collectable Motte & Bailey Viking Badge. This event runs daily from Saturday 23rd May until Sunday 12th July. £3.50 per trail per person (includes prize).
tagline: Detective duo, Motte & Bailey, have travelled back in time to the 10th Century

title: Indoor Theatre: 'A Christmas Carol', one-man performance
bodyContent: ‘Marley was dead: to begin with.’ On a snowy Christmas Eve, Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by a series of ghosts determined to show him how his cruel actions have affected the lives of others. Will Scrooge repent and accept the error of his ways or continue down his dark path? This festive season, join Behind the Door Productions at Dunster Castle for a one-man performance of this Christmas classic. This highly immersive and atmospheric production of A Christmas Carol captures the joy, humour and darkness of this traditional piece. A true festive classic, told as Dickens did to friends and family at Christmas time, this one-man performance is not to be missed. This is a candlelit performance taking place in the Inner Hall and will begin at 7pm. title: Mediterranean Marvels
subtitle: Discover Dunster’s Mediterranean Marvels this June, with a vibrant trail of sub‑tropical planting and spectacular summer colour.
bodyContent: Experience a touch of the Mediterranean at Dunster Castle Gardens this June. Follow a self‑guided trail through our Mediterranean Marvels collection, where sun‑loving, sub‑tropical plants bring rich colour, texture and fragrance to the garden. Along the way, you’ll encounter rare and unusual species seldom seen in the UK, all thriving thanks to Dunster’s unique Mediterranean microclimate. A highlight of the trail is the striking lily displays, offering a truly memorable moment in the garden. For those looking to explore further, join our ‘Mediterranean Mile’ guided tour, running every Tuesday and Thursday in June at 1pm. Led by a member of our knowledgeable garden team, this 45‑minute tour showcases highlights of the collection, sharing expert insight into the plants, their care, and the special conditions that help them thrive. T ours are free, but booking is essential. Book tickets on our website here: https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset/dunster-castle-and-watermill/events/6b2243f0-41b3-480e-a8fb-fa36a5237b8a. Whether you choose to wander at your own pace or join a guided tour, discover a garden shaped by history, climate and a love of plants.
tagline: Discover Dunster’s Mediterranean Marvels

title: Trigger Happy 25th Anniversary tour
subtitle: It’s been twenty-five years since Trigger Happy TV burst onto our screens, transforming the hidden camera format with its surreal universe of characters and unforgettable pranks.
bodyContent: Now, to celebrate a quarter-century of chaos, Dom Joly is bringing his most iconic characters and sketches to the stage in the Trigger Happy TV – Live! 25th-anniversary tour. Fans will experience beloved moments from the show, including The Giant Snail, The Traffic Warden, The Morris Dancer, The Scout, A Gang of Squirrels, and THAT Big Mobile Phone. Dom will share behind-the-scenes stories and insights on how these unforgettable moments came to life. But the surprises don’t stop there – this is live theatre, and fans can expect the unexpected.
tagline: Now, to celebrate a quarter-century of chaos

title: Lily Lyons + Essy Sparrow
subtitle: An intimate afternoon performance from two rising singer-songwriters.
bodyContent: Lily Lyons: Growing up split between London and Somerset, Lily Lyons found solace in the car stereo on long drives between her parents. The tenderness of Simon and Garfunkel, Nick Drake and Joni Mitchell opened her to "a soft version of myself that wasn't as welcomed in my actual life" - happy songs with scathing lyrics, sad sounds with joyful messages. On gut feeling she enrolled at music college in Falmouth, where her first ever gig caught the attention of Island Records president Darcus Beese. After a spell at Sony's Black Butter Records, she fund her true home at Fiction. Debut album Reopen The World, produced with Joel Pott, embraces the multiplicities of self. Largely recorded live with minimal tinkering - "just the bare bones being enough" - and inspired by Lisa Marchiano's feminist text The Vital Spark, it's a love letter to inner strength: "Banging the doors down and saying, 'I'm coming in and I'm not hiding anymore'." Essy Sparrow: Essy Sparrow is a multi-disciplinary artist and songwriter creating gossip-filled nostalgic indie folk from her coastal studio in Cornwall. Her 2024 debut EP Still Upset About It Actually, produced by Jemima Coulter (Hailaker) sparked TikTok virality, with her track Artists Dreamers reaching over 2 million views. In 2025 she played Boardmasters with BBC Introducing, supported Tors and Semler, joined Lily Lyons in opening for The Staves and sold out her 200-cap London headline at St Mary with All Souls. title: General Levy
subtitle: One of the most in demand and distinctive MCs on the planet, Levy has been tearing up events for the last three decades, bringing an unparalleled energy to his sets.
bodyContent: Born Paul Levy in Central Middlesex Hospital NW10 London, England in 1971, Levy grew up in the vibrant Harlesden and Wembley area for most of his early years, surrounded by different West Indian, European, Asian and African influences. He grew up in a community heavily influenced by reggae music and black culture and from an early age, a certain militancy was instilled in him along with a love and respect for rebel music. He was also inspired by his big brother Winston Irie who had a vast record collection of music from ska to rock steady, calypso to soul, hip hop and reggae that gave Levy a steady diet of music through his adolescent years. Since then General Levy has gone on to work with various producers such as Sly & Robbie and Sting International, Shaggy, Steelie & Cleevie, Artful Dodger, Jetstar, Ajang, Joe Grind, Gussie P, Stingray, Heartical Records, to name but a few. Levy remains a Lionheart artist riding through the ups and downs of the music business and still maintaining focus, a love and joy for the business and people; and just like a fine wine getting even better with time and bringing the fire to any place he performs at!
tagline: One of the most in demand and distinctive MCs on the planet

title: Summer Holidays at The Bishop's Palace
subtitle: Looking for a family day out in Somerset this summer? From 23 July to 2 September, discover an unforgettable day at The Bishop's Palace in Wells.
bodyContent: Explore 14 acres of beautiful RHS partner gardens, uncover an 800-year-old medieval Palace, cool off in the Dragon's Lair Splash Play Zone, tackle our Family Trail, enjoy Nature Ninjas and Art Adventurers craft activities, outdoor theatre and interactive multimedia tours. With plenty to do indoors and out, it's the perfect family adventure whatever the weather. Summer Holiday Highlights 💦 Splash Play Zone 🐉 Dragon's Lair adventure play area 🔍 Family trails 🌿 Nature Ninjas and Art Adventurers craft activities 🏰 Explore the medieval Palace 🌳 14 acres of RHS partner gardens 📱 Interactive multimedia tours 🎲 Cabinet of Curiosity & Table of Games Special Events 23 Jul - 2 Sept - Pollinators Family Trail 23 Jul - Nature Ninjas in the Community Garden: Clay Bugs 24 Jul - Outdoor Theatre: The Big Bad Wolf (ticketed separately) 30 Jul - Nature Ninjas in the Community Garden: Nature Medallions 1 - 2 Aug - History Alive: Britain at War 6, 13 & 27 Aug - Art Adventurers Crafting in the Undercroft 7, 14, 21 & 28 Aug - Summer Late Openings 13 Aug - Outdoor Theatre: King Arthur & the Holy Fail (ticketed separately) 20 Aug - Nature Ninjas in the Community Garden: Potato Printing 29 - 31 Aug - History Alive: Bowlore Medieval All activities (except outdoor theatre) are included with standard admission, including Day Tickets, Annual Passes and Friends of the Palace. title: Mendip Adventure Named One of the UK's Top 50 SME Apprenticeship Employers
subtitle: Mendip Adventure has been recognised as one of the UK's Top 50 SME Apprenticeship Employers. This award highlights the company's long-standing commitment to developing the next generation of outdoor leaders and adventure professionals.
bodyContent: Mendip Adventure has been recognised as one of the UK's Top 50 SME Apprenticeship Employers. This award highlights the company's long-standing commitment to developing the next generation of outdoor leaders and adventure professionals. The national rankings celebrate employers that demonstrate excellence in apprenticeship delivery, achievement, and overall experience. It takes into account successful completions, commitment to apprenticeships (particularly for young people), and feedback directly from apprentices. Mendip Adventure is the only Travel & Tourism business in the top 50. It is also the only outdoor activity provider to receive the recognition. "This recognition means a huge amount to everyone at Mendip Adventure. Developing the next generation of outdoor instructors is a fundamental part of who we are," s ays Dave Sears, Apprenticeships Coordinator, "One piece of feedback that really stands out is that every apprentice who completed a review said they would recommend Mendip to a friend. That is something we're especially proud of" For more than 30 years, apprenticeships have been a core part of Mendip Adventure. Working with South Devon College, the company supports between five and eight apprentices each year. Many progress into permanent roles across the business. David Eddins, Mendip's owner and CEO, began his own career as a Mendip apprentice in the 1990s, before progressing to lead the business today. This clearly evidences the long-term impact of the company's apprenticeship programme. Mendip is now looking forward to continuing building on this success, and provide outstanding opportunities for future apprentices. ABOUT Mendip Adventure was founded in 1987 and has grown into one of the UK’s largest independently owned outdoor activity providers. From humble beginnings as a small outdoor pursuits company, it now employs over 90 full-time staff. Its flagship site, Mendip Activity Centre, is based on a 250-acre estate in the Mendip Hills in Somerset, and offers more than 20 adventurous activities. Mendip Adventure also operates Mendip Basecamp, an award-winning family campsite, SUP Bristol, YHA Cheddar, and the industry-leading Outdoor Instructor Training.

title: Pitch Perfect - 3 day comedy, music and acting weekend
subtitle: Stuff on the Stage is bringing three very different spectaculars to Taunton’s Cooper Associates County Ground, 11th-13th September.
bodyContent: Fancy a weekend of entertainment with a difference? Then put 11th–13th September in the diary, because Stuff on the Stage is bringing three very different spectaculars to Taunton’s Cooper Associates County Ground. And while the venue may be best known for sixes, wickets and Somerset cricket, for three days this September the pitch will become a stage for some very big names – and an unusually eclectic programme. Whether your idea of the perfect night out is laughing until your sides hurt, dancing to classic soul and disco or enjoying Shakespeare under the open sky, there is something here to tempt you. Friday – Laugh with John Bishop The weekend gets off to a hilarious start on Friday 11th September when one of Britain’s best-known comedians, John Bishop, takes centre stage. Bishop has come a long way since his early days performing on the comedy circuit. His observational humour and hugely engaging storytelling have made him a favourite with audiences across the country, while his television career has included everything from his own comedy shows to presenting and acting. For his Taunton appearance he is joined by Justin Moorhouse and Sally-Anne Hayward, making this a full evening of stand-up rather than simply a headline performance. Expect plenty of stories, observations and the sort of comedy that has made Bishop one of Britain's most successful touring performers. Gates open at 6pm with last entry at 7pm. Tickets are from £36, with hospitality packages also available. And there is a good reason not to hang around if John Bishop is on your must-see list: the organisers reported that more than half the tickets had already been sold by July. Saturday – Get your groove on! If Friday is about laughter, Saturday night is about getting your dancing shoes on. The Stuff on the Stage Groove Festival takes over the County Ground on Saturday 12 September, with a line-up that should appeal to anyone who likes their music soulful, funky and seriously danceable. At the top of the bill are Soul II Soul, the legendary British collective whose music helped provide the soundtrack to the late 1980s and early 1990s. With hits such as Back to Life (However Do You Want Me) and Keep On Movin' , Soul II Soul became one of Britain's most successful musical acts, blending soul, R&B, dance and club culture into a sound that remains instantly recognisable. They will be joined by another major name, The Brand New Heavies. The London group were at the forefront of the acid-jazz movement and subsequently enjoyed huge international success with their infectious mixture of funk, soul and jazz. Songs including You Are the Universe and Dream On Dreamer remain dance-floor favourites. And then there is Norman Jay MBE, one of the UK's most respected DJs and a hugely influential figure in British club culture. His career spans more than four decades, during which he has championed soul, funk, reggae, disco and dance music. Opening the festival is The Beatles Dub Club, the brainchild of Chris Arnold. Forget the Fab Four as you know them – this inventive project takes Beatles classics and gives them a completely different treatment through dub, reggae, ska, funk and drum and bass. Gates open at 5pm and tickets are from £43.50, with hospitality packages also available. Sunday – Shakespeare in the sunshine After two very different evenings, Stuff on the Stage concludes on Sunday 13th September with another change of direction. This time the stage belongs to William Shakespeare, as acclaimed outdoor theatre company Illyria presents As You Like It . And if the idea of Shakespeare on a cricket ground sounds slightly unconventional, that's precisely the point. Rather than being confined to a traditional theatre, audiences can enjoy one of Shakespeare's most popular comedies in the open air. As You Like It follows Rosalind as she escapes into the Forest of Arden, where disguises, romance, mistaken identities and an entertaining cast of characters create one of Shakespeare's most charming comedies. Illyria specialises in outdoor theatre and has developed a reputation for making classic plays accessible, energetic and entertaining for audiences of all ages. So this could be an ideal Sunday afternoon for families. Bring a picnic, settle down on the edge of the pitch and enjoy Shakespeare in a wonderfully relaxed setting. Gates open at 2.30pm with the performance beginning at 3.30pm. Tickets are £25 for adults and £15 for under-16s, with a family ticket for two adults and two children costing just £60. Stuff on the Stage, Cooper Associates County Ground, Taunton, 11th–13th September 2026. See https://cacgsomerset.co.uk

title: American Museum & Gardens
subtitle: The American Museum takes you on a journey through the history of America, from its early settlers to the twentieth century.
bodyContent: The American Museum on the outskirts of Bath, Somerset, takes you on a journey through the history of America, from its early settlers to the twentieth century. With its remarkable collection of folk and decorative arts, the Museum shows the diverse and complex nature of American traditions. The only museum of Americana outside the United States, it was founded to bring American history and cultures to the people of Britain and Europe. The permanent collection includes more than two hundred historic American quilts, exceptional pieces of Shaker furniture, Native American objects, and two hundred historical maps of the New World starting from the twelfth century and stretching through the Renaissance. The museum also has the most significant collection of American folk art in Europe. Visitors can also explore the extensive grounds, which include an arboretum of American trees. The New American Garden Designed by Washington DC-based landscape architecture firm OEHME, VAN SWEDEN, the New American Garden is its first European commission. With new landscaping, and planting the garden provides an exciting horticultural insight into the flora and fauna of the United States.

title: Edinburgh Preview: Larry Dean + Courtney Büchner
subtitle: Larry Dean: Three-time Edinburgh Comedy Award for Best Show nominee (2015, 2018, 2022),
bodyContent: Larry Dean: Three-time Edinburgh Comedy Award for Best Show nominee (2015, 2018, 2022), Larry Dean has firmly established himself as one of the UK’s leading stand-ups. Named by The Telegraph as one of the 50 Best Comedians of the 21st Century, his live performances have earned a string of ***** reviews, with The Herald calling him “a national treasure” and Rolling Stone praising him as “stitch-inducingly funny…an expert regaler of daft.” His TV credits include SNL UK, Live at the Apollo (as both host and guest), QI, Mock The Week, Michael McIntyre’s Big Show, Richard Osman’s House of Games, and The Royal Variety Performance 2024. He has fronted multiple series of the BBC New Comedy Awards, starred in Stand Up Sketch Show (ITV2), Comedy Central’s Roast Battle, and appeared on World’s Most Dangerous Roads (BBC Two). Larry’s reach extends far beyond the stage, with over 200 million views online and a combined social following of more than one million across TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube. Courtney Büchner: A show that will make you laugh, cringe and text your best friend immediately. Following her sold-out Edinburgh Fringe debut "I Wrote this Show Last Night" and her five-star follow-up "Big, If True", Courtney returns with a story about friendship. Or rather, the end of a friendship. "Uniquely charming" Edinburgh Fringe Review ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
tagline: Larry Dean: Three-time Edinburgh Comedy Award

title: Exhibition: Paths Taken
subtitle: A summer exhibition exploring a selection of shoes from the stored collection and the curious and fascinating journeys that brought them into the archive
bodyContent: Ever wondered about the journeys objects take before they end up in museums? This six-week exhibition explores four different paths that brought some remarkable shoes to the collections at Shoemakers Museum. With examples of historic shoes found by archaeologists, shoes collected as souvenirs, keepsakes and mementos of people we have loved and reminders of nostalgic times and even some examples of concealed shoes a tradition of burying shoes within the walls of buildings for safety and superstition. The exhibition runs daily 10-4pm from 1 August until 13 September 2026. Interested in finding out more? the curators behind the museum will be presenting an illustrated talk at the museum on 14 August. Please booking in advance for this talk.
tagline: A summer exhibition exploring a selection of shoes

title: Double Delight for Longleat With Arrival of Capybara Pups
subtitle: Bart and Mildred live alongside the Brazilian tapirs and the new trio of maned wolves, in African Village as part of the Drive-Through Safari.
bodyContent: Two new arrivals have been born at Longleat in a first for the park. The Wiltshire Estate’s pair of Capybara have successfully welcomed two pups, the first for the species at Longleat and announced to celebrate Capybara appreciation day, 10 July. Bart and Mildred live alongside the Brazilian tapirs and the new trio of maned wolves, in African Village as part of the Drive-Through Safari. Alexa Maultby, Hoofstock Keeper, said: “With Mildred having only arrived at the park last July, it is a fantastic achievement to have already welcomed two pups. “Mum and the pups are doing well, and are currently in a purpose-built nursery area, complete with private pool. Capybara pups are born precocial, meaning they are born with fur, open eyes and are able to move and swim within a few hours.” The gestation period for capybaras is between 120 – 150 days, approximately five months, with Mildred giving birth at 149 days. “The pups will suckle from mum for approximately 16 weeks, whilst also eating some grass from a week old. They weigh around 1kg at birth, and when fully grown typically reach 35 – 66kg. “As capybaras are a semi-aquatic species, we’re expecting mum and the pups to spend quite a bit of time in their private pool. While the pups won’t be the best swimmers to begin with, they will learn quickly and may even ride around on mum’s back while in the water initially.” Spending time in water acts as a deterrent for predators in the wild, and as such they have evolved to have partially webbed toes for swimming, long and brittle hair which dries quickly, and their small eyes, ears and noses are high on their heads so their faces can remain above water and keep alert. “We don’t yet know the sex of the pups as it is still early days, but we will find out at one of their health checks soon.” Currently, the herd of capybaras can be seen by keen eyed guests in their nursery area next to the giraffe house, adjacent to the African Village car park. Factfile Capybara - Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris IUCN Red List Status – Least Threatened Native to South America except Chile, residing in forest, savannah and wetlands. Capybaras are a semi-aquatic species and largest of the rodent taxonomy group. A typical litter can be between two – eight pups, averaging four. Capybaras are the largest species of rodent.

title: Launching this Summer: Kayak Hire on Bristol Harbour
subtitle: Local Paddlesports Company Unveils New Way To Explore Bristol.
bodyContent: This year, for the very first time, local paddlesports company, SUP Bristol, is launching sit-on-top Kayak Hire. It will give locals and visitors the freedom to discover the city's historic waterways at their own pace. Located at Baltic Wharf, a 30-minute walk from the city centre, the new experience offers a unique way to enjoy Bristol from the water. Perfect for catching up with friends after work, planning a family adventure, celebrating a birthday, or simply making the most of a sunny day. Participants can glide along the colourful harbourside, paddle up close to the SS Great Britain, and experience the city from a perspective few people ever see. Each two-hour hire includes a single or double sit-on-top kayak, paddles, buoyancy aids, one waterproof phone pouch for each group, and a full safety briefing before setting off to explore independently. With hot showers, changing facilities, and toilets available on-site, paddlers can turn their session into a full day-out. It's easy to freshen up before exploring Bristol's vibrant pubs and restaurants. SUP Bristol is perfectly placed to enjoy Bristol's cafés, pubs and restaurants just a short stroll away. The new Kayak Hire programme has been approved by Bristol City Council as a trial, and will operate on selected dates throughout August: 7th, 8th, 9th, 14th and 22nd August. The aim is for the trial to become a permanent addition to Bristol's watersports offering. Spaces are limited, so early booking is advised. Participants will have the opportunity to be among the very first to experience Bristol's waterside adventure, while helping shape the future of paddlesports in the heart of the city.

bodyContent: We are now offering the Coronavirus Guarantee to holidaymakers at the Hoburne here Your ideal retreat, nestled on the coast between the Quantocks and Exmoor . Right on the beach. Accessible by steam train. Next to a National Park. Sounds too good to be true, doesn't it? Waking up to the sea breeze and warm, West Country sun, you'll see why so many of our visitors return year after year. Hoburne Blue Anchor is the ideal holiday base, whether you¹re a couple looking for a quiet getaway, or a family seeking an adventure in the countryside. A new adventure every time you step outside. Kids have plenty to keep them busy. Between the pool activities, the nature trail, and watching the steam train chug alongside the park, you probably won¹t be able to tear them away from all the fun. We haven't forgotten about the adults either - why not sample a local cider or two at The Smugglers Inn down the road? If you visit in winter, the village's cosy cafés and pubs give you an easy excuse to while away the afternoon in comfort after a bracing walk. Of course, the park is so relaxing, you could spend your whole break here. There's miles of beach to explore on our doorstep. But if you can see it from your sun deck, why bother?

title: Big Domain
subtitle: Enjoy a getaway with all of your friends and family in Somerset with Big Domain, specialists in group accommodation across the UK and Europe.
bodyContent: Enjoy a getaway with all of your friends and family in Somerset with Big Domain, specialists in group accommodation across the UK and Europe. Sleeping 8 people and up, they have a selection of over 30 properties across Somerset’s gorgeous countryside and scenic coastline, perfect for multi-generational holidays, reunions with friends and special celebrations. Among the collection you’ll find a whole variety of wonderful places to stay, from traditional countryside cottages to cool and contemporary converted barns, each with a host of brilliant features there to help you make the most of your relaxing getaway. Log fires, bubbling hot tubs, swimming pools, tennis courts, cinema rooms and more can all be found at several of our properties, bound to entertain guests of all ages. Head to their website to see the full collection of large holiday cottages Big Domain has to offer across Somerset.

title: Conferences at Doubletree by Hilton, Cadbury House
subtitle: The peaceful yet accessible location of DoubleTree by Hilton, Cadbury House, is what makes it an ideal venue for business events and meetings.
bodyContent: Conferences at Cadbury House – The perfect experience awaits. From the moment you travel up the leafy drive and catch a glimpse of the historic manor house, combined with the modern features of the hotel, you know you have officially arrived at Cadbury House. With a warm cookie on arrival and a highly experienced team, we are dedicated to making your stay the best it can be. Your Experience This stunning hotel and conference venue is set in acres of woodland and boasts spectacular panoramic views overlooking the Bristol Channel and beyond into Wales. There is also two Marco Pierre White restaurants onsite, an award-winning health club and a renowned spa. Our Facilities We cater to a variety of occasions including conferences, events, product launches and team building. The former 18 th century manor house has 132 luxury bedrooms which saw half of them refurbished in the early part of 2018. With 11 meeting rooms that can cater from 2 to 400 delegates, and on-site parking for over 300 cars, the perfect experience awaits. Team Building With ample ground space, Cadbury house is perfectly equipped for team building events. Our conference and events team, in association with local event providers can provide win tasting and vineyard tours. Along with group activities such as archery and clay pigeon shooting. Location We are located on the B3133, four miles from the M5 motorway (junction 20 & 21) and just one mile from Yatton International Rail Station, with Bristol International Airport only five miles away. Our Hotel and conference venue is superbly located with easy access.
tagline: DoubleTree by Hilton, Cadbury House, is an ideal venue for business events and meetings.

title: Unique hideaways

bodyContent: Escape to the wild in comfort and luxury on your glamping adventure. Choose the perfect retreat for exploring the spellbinding county of Somerset. Watch the twinkle of the night sky from your hot tub, cosy up in front of the fire, go wild swimming, toast marshmallows over the firepit and watch the sun set over the horizon. With its peaceful countryside and fantastic walking locations, a glamping holiday in Somerset is an excellent way to discover the local area. Take your pick from our selection of charming shepherd’s huts with luxurious hot tubs, our quirky wagon or a Scandinavian style lodge. We even have a heavenly hideaway in the perfect position for exploring the enchanting town of Glastonbury, as well as plenty of dog-friendly options. Make your escape to nature the most magical experience with a stay at a Unique hideaway.
tagline: Discover a luxury glamping experience in Somerset with Unique hideaways!

title: The Roman Baths
subtitle: Famed for its hot springs, Bath houses the best preserved Roman Spa from the ancient world. Delve into the history of this magical monument and admire its architecture and engineering.
bodyContent: The Roman Baths, Bath, Somerset sits on the site of Britain’s only hot spring. Here the Romans built a magnificent temple and bathing complex, which still flows with natural hot water today. Come and explore the spectacular Roman Baths, at the heart of the World Heritage City of Bath , Somerset. Walk around the steaming Great Bath where people bathed nearly 2,000 years ago, see the ruins of the temple of Minerva where Roman worshippers gathered, and explore the fascinating museum where you can find out more about those who lived and worked here. The Beau Street Hoard, a collection of more than 17,000 Roman coins recently discovered in Beau Street, Bath is now on display in the museum. Costumed characters bring to life the stories of past inhabitants: you might meet a Roman lady called Flavia, slave girl Apulia, stonemasons Sulinus and Brucetus, or a travelling merchant named Peregrinus. Award-winning audioguides in twelve languages are included in the admission price. There is a special audioguide for children, narrated by Michael Rosen, and a “Bryson at the Baths” version featuring commentary from Bill Bryson. Enjoy lunch or afternoon tea with live music in the beautiful 18th-century Pump Room * National Art Pass holders receive a 10% discount off the entry fee.
tagline: Famed for its hot springs, Bath houses the best preserved Roman Spa from the ancient world.

title: Rickbarton Cottage
subtitle: Rickbarton Cottage is the ideal base for that countryside retreat that everyone thrives in.
bodyContent: Walks from your doorstep, fresh air, country Pubs and a Farm Shop. Yet, close proximity to Bath (5 miles) and Bradford on Avon (2 miles) means that you get the best of both worlds! Guests can make use of the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool during their stay, and feel free to bring your furry friend as the area is dog friendly. There is a Local Farm Shop village shop and a village pub within walking distance or a short drive. The Kennet and Avon Canal is also within walking distance, for any keen walkers or cyclists. The cottage itself has an open-plan kitchen/living room. It is equipped with everything you should need. The bedroom has a double bed, which has been made up with fresh white linen prior to your arrival. The en-suite bathroom has a bath with a shower above the bath. There is space for a cot if needed (please check in advance of stay)

title: The Manor Arms
subtitle: The Manor Arms, the only pub in the village, has always been a place of great attraction.
bodyContent: This lovely old village pub has withstood the ravages of modern design. The blue flagstone floors will still remain the same. Looking back over the years there are a few changes. The pub could be entered by a separate door from the outside to the top bar. To move from the best bar to the top bar from inside meant lifting up a section of the counter which was only allowed on special occasions. Behind the counter stood wooden barrels on a jib of beer and cider with their wooden taps which seemed to squeak at every turn. Draught beer could be bought at sixpence a pint, whisky sevenpence a nip and brandy bought at so much a noggin. Bottles of home brewed beer and Hunstman stout were taken straight out of the crates. The attractive sign bearing the Hoskyns Crest and family motto: "Finem Respice" which means "Look towards the end" hung on the outside wall until 1956. It was quite evident by then that all cattle lorries and furniture vans had been built much higher and the angle iron standing out carrying the sign was being continually bent back, and having to be repaired. Co-op vans and double decker sheep lorries became even broader and higher and seemed to look out and say "Get Back!". One fine morning it was discovered that the sign had received a real knock and was hanging precariously from its bracket by one chain. "This is enough!", said Colonel Macleod, the agent who had been appointed to follow Mr Raper in 1950. So the sign was taken down by George Toms and his merry men, John Diaper and Alec Eglon, all estate workers, and mounted on a wooden pillar in a much safer place on the edge of the village green, its present position. The beautiful sign in its ornamental iron frame is now crowned by the word "Food"! Most of the customers were locals who spent their evenings drinking while playing dominoes, shove halfpenny, table billiards and cards. Women hardly ever went inside the bar, but often fetched drink from the jug and bottle department. They never smoked. The pub closed sharp at 10 o'clock and quite often the village policeman was outside. The landlord, Mr Hallett was called "Buster". He drove a high spring trap and his pony, a very unpredictable sort, often refused to move off in the right direction. Harry Male, an old pensioner living across the road, often came to his assistance with a pat on its neck; to be led a few steps was all that was needed and away it trotted merrily. We have been unable to contact Mr Parkman's family to gain permission to use this snippet from what is an excellent book, and we are most grateful for the information provided. We will of course gladly post any credits due here if required. WE HAVE ONLY ONE DESIGNATED ROOM FOR THOSE OF YOU WHO WISH TO STAY WITH US AND BRING A DOG. PLEASE CONFIRM WHETHER THE ROOM IS AVAILABLE FOR YOUR STAY. THERE IS A CHARGE OF 5 POUNDS FOR THE DOGS ACCOMMODATION.
tagline: The Manor Arms, the only pub in the village, has always been a place of great attraction.

title: The George Hotel in Frome
subtitle: You’ll be spoiled for choice at our pub with hotel rooms in Frome. Not only is it within easy reach of Longleat, Stonehenge and Glastonbury, but you can also explore local jewels like Nunney Castle, the Walled Garden At Mells, Cooper Hall, Catherine Hill, Victoria Park and the artisan market at St Catherine’s.
bodyContent: The George Hotel enjoys a central location in the market town of Frome, surrounded by the stunning Somerset countryside. We’ve got 28 en suite bedrooms and a strong reputation for good home-cooked food (including a gluten-free menu). Our hotel room options include double, double superior and family rooms, along with singles and twins, plus a deluxe room with balcony and four-poster bed. The finer details... Check-in times: 3-10pm. Check-out times: By 11am. No late check-out facility. Accessibility : Please note, none of our rooms are on the ground floor and accessed by stairs, we do not have a lift. Breakfast options: We offer a complimentary continental breakfast and hot breakfast options. Due to Covid-19 restrictions we will not be offering our continental selection as a buffet but will ask for your orders. In-room hospitality : We provide a hospitality tray in each room (kettle, tea, coffee, biscuits), which is refreshed daily. We also provide towels, toiletries, ironing board and iron and a hairdryer. Pet-friendly rooms: We have 4 pet-friendly rooms; 1 Double, 1 Twin, and 2 Singles. Guests travelling with pets must check prior to booking if there is availability. Please do not arrive with unannounced pets as accommodation is not guaranteed. There is a surcharge of £10 per pet, per night. Car parking: Our car park is situated behind The George Hotel. Enter Cork Street at the side of the hotel, then turn right at Westway Cinema, down the ramp. Drive in-between the concrete pillars at the bottom, where you will find our underground parking spaces. The light will turn on as you enter. Please note that spaces are limited, and we are unable to reserve any. There is a 2 metre height restriction and a tight turn to enter the car park so please take care when entering and exiting. PLEASE NOTE – COVID-19: We have reduced the amount of soft furnishings, printed communications, hospitality tray items, laundry and toiletries in our rooms, to ensure minimal risk of exposure. If you require any top ups or additional items, we are happy to supply these upon request.
tagline: You’ll be spoiled for choice at our pub with hotel rooms in Frome

title: Avon View
subtitle: Avon View is an elegant Georgian guest house situated close to the seafront providing comfortable and relaxing accommodation for holiday and business visitors alike
bodyContent: Avon View is an elegant Georgian guest house situated close to the seafront providing comfortable and relaxing accommodation for holiday and business visitors alike. The principal bedrooms are individually decorated and enjoy glorious views over the Bristol Channel. Kate Ward, the resident owner, has lived in the house for more than 25 years and has been running the house as a bed and breakfast for more than 20. Her experience ensures guests enjoy a relaxed and comfortable stay concentrating on informal comfort with attentive but unobtrusive service. The seafront, open air pool, Lake Grounds and main High Street are all just a short walk away.
tagline: Avon View is an elegant Georgian guest house

title: Tyning Cottage
subtitle: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside.
bodyContent: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside on the edge of an area of outstanding natural beauty but only 5 miles from the world heritage city of Bath and 1 mile from the Saxon town of Bradford-on-Avon. Cumberwell Country Cottages are located on Great Cumberwell Farm, which has been in the James family since 1939 and was originally a dairy farm until 1992 when the herd was sold making way for a diversification into Cumberwell Park Golf Club, the farm itself has not changed a great deal and is still a working farm with over 300 acres of arable crop. The self-catering cottages available for your stay have been converted from an old tithe barn which has had many purposes in the past including stables, a grain store and cider production as the orchard at the front of the cottages was a cider apple orchard.
tagline: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages

title: Dylan Moran: Looking for Trouble
subtitle: Mick Perrin Worldwide presents Dylan Moran: Looking for Trouble.
bodyContent: Showtime. What are you going to do? Are you going to go to work? Or stay in bed, chasing oblivion. Guess what? We're fresh out of oblivion. The Economy will do fine without you - but how long will you survive without the usual giant horn of frozen caramel lattes and the five thousand other pieces of bullshit you have smushed together so you can point at it and croak ‘That’s my ..life?’ Now, now, all this drama and we’re not even out the door yet. Find out how it could all have been different. Find out how to reclaim your life by becoming a lethal kickboxing, chess champion. Pioneer new trends in global lovemaking, join tan elite band trillionaire poet/pastry chef/mountaineers. Just go LOOKING FOR TROUBLE. A brand new show from BAFTA and Perrier awarding winning comedian & star of Black Books, Dylan Moran. “Joyfully cynical” ★★★★★ Metro "Perfect for the times” ★★★★★ The i “Superb” ★★★★ The Guardian “Trumping Shakespeare, he reduces life to four ages: “Child, failure, old and dead”. Faced with one-liners as killing as that the world suddenly seems a better place.” ★★★★ Telegraph

title: The Preucil School String Orchestra at Wells Town Hall
subtitle: Visiting youth string orchestra from Iowa City (USA) presents a free evening concert featuring works from Bach, Mozart, Elgar, Dvořák and Scott Joplin.
bodyContent: The Preucil School String Orchestra from Iowa City, USA will perform a free concert at Wells Town Hall as part of the WOWFest 2026 Fringe. Comprised of talented young musicians aged 13–19, the orchestra is the flagship ensemble of the Preucil School of Music, a non-profit community music school with a strong international touring history across the USA, Europe and beyond. Under the direction of Carey Bostian, the ensemble is recognised for its high level of artistry and engaging performances. The programme features a varied selection of Baroque, Classical and contemporary works, showcasing music as a universal language and including music by Bach, Mozart, Elgar, Dvořák and Scott Joplin. This is a free concert and all are welcome. https://www.facebook.com/events/1733877351317401

bodyContent: Young adventurers are invited to play their way around Dunster Castle’s knight‑themed activity zones and earn their title as a Knight of Dunster Castle. title: Children go free at Shepton Mallet Prison this summer
subtitle: Families looking can visit Shepton Mallet Prison this summer with children receiving free entry as part of the attraction's Summer Family Offer.
bodyContent: Families looking for a different day out during the school holidays can visit Shepton Mallet Prison this summer with children receiving free entry as part of the attraction's Summer Family Offer: Kids Go Free & Eat Free. Available until 1 September 2026, the offer allows up to two children aged 5–15 to receive free Prison Entry with every paying adult. Children under five continue to receive free admission year-round. As an example, two paying adults visiting with three children aged 5–15 would save £36 on Prison Entry compared with purchasing standard admission tickets. Eligible children can also receive a free children's snack box in the on-site café, subject to offer terms and conditions.* For families looking for something beyond the usual summer attractions, Shepton Mallet Prison offers the chance to step inside more than 400 years of prison history together. The largely indoor attraction provides a weather-independent day out, with visitors free to discover the prison at their own pace before relaxing in the on-site café. Well-behaved dogs are also welcome. Guided Tours and Escape Rooms are available for those wishing to enhance their visit, subject to availability and additional charges. Charlie Lawson, Attraction Director at Shepton Mallet Prison, said: "Parents are always looking for something different to do during the summer holidays, and we know family days out can quickly become expensive. We wanted to make it easier for more families to experience Shepton Mallet Prison together, whether they're local to Somerset or visiting the area. It's somewhere children can explore, ask questions and discover stories they probably wouldn't come across anywhere else. We often hear from parents that it's one of the places their children keep talking about long after the visit, and that's exactly what we'd hope for from a family day out." The Summer Family Offer is available until 1 September 2026. Tickets can be booked online or purchased on arrival, subject to availability. Full terms and conditions are available at: https://www.sheptonmalletprison.com/events/family-days-out-somerset-summer-2026/

title: Wookey Hole Cave-Aged Cheddar Celebrates 20 Years with Champion Cheddar Award
subtitle: Milestone year for the West Country farmhouse cheddar matured 200 feet beneath Somerset.
bodyContent: Wookey Hole Cave-Aged Cheddar is celebrating 20 years since the first truckles were placed in the famous Somerset caves and has marked the anniversary by being named Champion Cheddar at the 2026 International Cheese & Dairy Awards. Made by Ford Farm Cheesemakers part of AJ and RG Barber, using milk from West Country herds, the traditional clothbound cheddar is matured 200 feet underground at Wookey Hole. The caves’ naturally cool temperature and high humidity help produce its distinctive earthy, nutty flavour and firm texture. A West Country Cheese with a Story in the Stone The idea of returning cheddar to the caves 20 years ago came from a collaboration between showman Gerry Cottle and cheesemaker and director Mike Pullin. Together they created the now-iconic name “Wookey Hole Cave-Aged Cheddar”, designed to firmly link the cheese to its dramatic Somerset home and encourage visitors to “come and see where the cheese is really matured”. “My family always talked about how, years ago on the Mendips, cheese was kept in caves before refrigeration,” explains Mike Pullin, Director, AJ and RG Barber. “Bringing cheddar back into the caves felt like reconnecting with that tradition – and we’ve spent the last 20 years proving just how special that environment is for flavour.” Award-Winning Flavour At the 2026 International Cheese & Dairy Awards, Wookey Hole Cave-Aged Cheddar was awarded Champion Cheddar among over 4,000 entries from across the UK and beyond. “There are thousands of cheeses on those judging tables, including all the big-name cheddars,” says Pullin. “To come out as Champion Cheddar this year shows just how exceptional the Wookey Hole cave-matured cheese really is.” Chris Goodchild, General Manager at Wookey Hole said, “Few cheeses can say they’re matured in one of Britain’s most famous caves. For the past 20 years, Wookey Hole has provided the perfect natural home for this remarkable cheddar, helping to create a flavour that is uniquely Somerset. We’re thrilled to celebrate this milestone and proud that the caves continue to play such an important role in producing an award-winning product produced in Somerset and enjoyed by cheese lovers across the UK and beyond.” This latest accolade echoes a landmark year in 2011, when the same cheese was the supreme winner across all cheese categories in Britain, helping to propel Wookey Hole Cave-Aged Cheddar into national prominence and onto the shelves of major retailers. Since then, it has continued to earn gold medals and critical acclaim. From Dorset and Somerset to Tables Across the UK and Beyond Approximately 300 to 400 tonnes of Wookey Hole Cave-Aged Cheddar are produced each year. The cheese is sold as a premium table cheese through major UK retailers including Tesco, M&S, Waitrose and Costco, as well as being stocked by independent delis, farm shops and regional markets. It is also used as a hero ingredient in speciality products such as Wookey Hole Cave-Aged crackers and is exported internationally, with Costco in the USA among its key overseas customers. Experience the Cheese Where It Matures Visitors to Wookey Hole can see the award-winning cheddar maturing deep within the caves as part of their visit, offering a rare chance to experience one of Britain's most unusual food production environments firsthand. For those looking to delve even deeper, Wookey Hole's new Wookey Uncovered premium experience culminates with a specially curated cave-aged cheddar and Somerset cider tasting. Visitors can also purchase Wookey Hole Cave-aged Cheddar in the Wookey Hole gift shop. For more information head to https://www.wookey.co.uk/cave-aged-cheddar-cheese Or https://www.fordfarm.com/cave-aged-cheddar/

bodyContent: Acacia Farm Campsite is a family run open large grassy area campsite set in the heart of Somerset close to Cheddar Gorge on the outskirts of a rural village of Rooksbridge. We offer a number of different options whether you are a caravan enthusiast or a dedicated sleep under the stars camper you will find a warm welcome and all the conveniences and facilities you require. From our beautiful rural location based at the foot of the Mendips we are perfectly positioned to explore many sights and sounds and experiences that Somerset has to offer whether on foot bicycle or motor vehicle. You will find we are close to all that Somerset has to offer. For those who prefer life under canvas we offer expanses of grass of which to pitch and bathroom and toilet facilities and a utility room with washing up facilities with hot water fridge and maps and reading books. Campfires and BBQ’s are allowed and give you the chance to admire our starlight skies free of light pollution. If you are looking for a touring pitch we have hard standings electric hook ups and an oversized pitch for RV vehicle touring caravans campervans and Motor Homes. As well as our camping and touring pitches we offer Acacia wood cabin with private facilities and all comforts of home. We also have a yurt which makes a glamping style alternative experience all of its own and is surprisingly spacious. Being a small holder we love animals and have a large 8 acre dog walking field to exercise and tire them out with great views. We are also very proud of our Green Tourism Silver award and our 3 star EnjoyEngland award status. You will find us just a short drive from the M5 Junction 22 rural enough to be lost in Somerset’s beauty but close enough to pop to the shops for tea. We look forward to meeting you and making the most of your holiday.
tagline: Acacia Farm Campsite is a family run open large grassy area campsite set in the heart of Somerset.

title: Bramley & The Cider Jug Cottages
subtitle: Charming barn conversion self catering accommodation in a quiet rural Somerset village near Wells. The Cider Jug sleeps 2/3, Bramley sleeps 4. National Nature reserves within easy reach. Close to coast, Wells and Cheddar. Warm welcome assured.
bodyContent: Two converted farm-buildings in the quiet village of Westhay near Wells . The Cider Jug has a twin bedded gallery bedroom and sofa bed in lounge while Bramley has two twin bedrooms plus sofa bed and private garden. Both have private car parking and access to a lockable shed for bicycles. Free wifi internet access in both cottages. Drying facilities and sheltered outdoor seating area. Sleeping 8 in total. Short breaks available please call to discuss. Visitors to Sage Farm cottages are offered an introductory tour of the immediate area with advice on where to see species of interest at different times of the year. The Owner, Martin Sage is a voluntary warden for Natural England, RSPB and Somerset Wildlife Trust.

title: TRE3DOM
subtitle: Our design and build philosophy centres around a connection to nature and is inspired by sacred geometry. We use modern construction techniques and locally sourced sustainable materials, to create handcrafted, low impact structures with a high attention to detail.
bodyContent: TRE3DOM Join Visit Somerset membership. John Turner CEO of Visit Somerset has said; " As the county moves to strive to become more upmarket and innovative as a destination TRE3DOM is the perfect match to support those aspirations. Their Tree Houses are stunning, innovative and a really significant quality offering that would lend itself to the cultural family and couples’ market. I am really excited to be able to introduce TRE3DOM to the membership, with the hope that there will be interest and early adoption of their incredible product offering" Owen Montgomery of TRE3DOM has said; "Really excited to be partnering with Visit Somerset, I grew up in Somerset and love being a tourist. I hope all tourists, returning and new, get a chance to experience our Treehouses and Pods; modular eco structures designed in the heart of Somerset" The Garden Pods and Treehouses are design led, modular structures, meaning they can be as big or small as the customer would like. Our current range comprises two distinct designs; the Hexagon and the Pentagon – or we can help you design and build a bespoke garden pod or treehouse . Garden Pods do not require planning permission (in most instances) and are hand-assembled onsite in under a month. These pods are adaptable, multi-purpose spaces and can be used as an office, extra room, studio, or games room for the kids. Treehouses are simply pods in the trees and offer a great solution for accommodation. Private landowners and farmers can start B&B rental businesses while hotels, resorts and glamping operations can offer a new experience to their customers. This a unique opportunity to diversify business lines, achieve yields of up to 50% and a payback of between two and three years. Our contemporary tree ‘holiday’ houses were designed with the entrepreneur in mind and can be modified dependent on your desired returns. We offer two and four berth units with some fun and functional add-ons, making each treehouse truly bespoke.

title: Bath Breaks Apartments
subtitle: Located within the heart of the World Heritage City of Bath you are just a short, level walking distance to all the attractions from the Roman Baths to the Royal Crescent.
bodyContent: As well as the wonderful history and stunning architecture there is a wealth of shops and restaurants. This is an ideal location if you want a romantic break, a family holiday, a relaxing spa or a cultural experience. These modern apartments are on the first floor and accessed by a single flight of stairs. They have private entrances with a bright, open plan lounge, kitchen and dinning areas with Wifi and TV. The bedrooms have clean fresh linen, towels and hairdryers. If you do not want to eat out at one of the many restaurants, the kitchens are fully equipped with microwave, oven and hob, dishwasher, fridge-freezer, toaster, kettle, dinner set and cutlery. Also included in the kitchen are tea towels, washing up liquid and bin bags. If you are arriving by car there is a car park located in Charlotte Street, approximately 250m away. Once you park your car and settle in to your apartment you may not need to use it again. Due to the central location of the apartments most of the attractions are within walking distance, but if you want to explore further afield the train and bus stations are close by and taxis are readily available. We hope your visit to Bath will be enhanced by your stay in these wonderful apartments.

title: Wentworth House Hotel
subtitle: Set in almost an acre of grounds, Wentworth House is just a 15-minute walk from Bath city centre.
bodyContent: It offers free parking , and a seasonal, heated pool located outdoors with views across the valley for the summer months. All rooms at Wentworth are traditionally furnished and neutrally decorated. Each room has a private bathroom, a TV, hairdryer and tea and coffee making facilities. A full English breakfast is served in the dining room which features a traditional bay window with views across the garden. Bath Spa Rail Station and the historic Roman Baths are just over 1.6 km from the guest house. The Theatre Royal Bath is less than a 10-minute drive away. We speak your language!

title: Stapeley Cottage
subtitle: Stapeley is a popular choice of cottage when looking for the family. The comfortable and well-equipped property has everything you should need for your time away.
bodyContent: Stapeley is a popular choice of cottage when looking for the family. The comfortable and well-equipped property has everything you should need for your time away. Families can enjoy the rural surroundings and experience life on our working sheep farm. Unwind in the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool and Games Room, and feel free to bring your dog as our farm is dog friendly - just let us know in advance!

title: The Hood Arms
subtitle: An historic 17th Century coaching inn situated in the village of Kilve on the edge of the Quantock Hills.
bodyContent: The Hood is a family run inn steeped in history, on the route of the Coleridge Way and close to the Jurassic coastline and beaches of Somerset. We are open for Lunch, Dinner & Sunday Roast. Children are always welcome & the bar/snug areas are dog friendly. We also have a large garden which is dog friendly and has a purpose built children's area. You can also enjoy a game of boules or table tennis. Sunday Lunch: We cherish a good family meal and Sunday Roasts are just that. Enjoy a selection of roast meats with all the trimmings. All our food is locally sourced, freshly cooked and lovingly prepared! *For allergy advice speak to a member of staff. We are Dog Friendly! We also have nine superior stylish and comfortable rooms to let with free wifi and high speed internet. Based on the edge of the beautiful Quantock Hills and Exmoor National Park, we are ideally placed for walkers. The South West Coast Path runs right past us on Kilve beach which is part of the spectaular Jurassic coast. Kilve is a perfect location for collecting ammonites and reptile remains. The beach is also ideal for rock pooling, set in tranquil surroundings and ideal for all the family to enjoy.
tagline: An historic 17th Century coaching inn situated in the village of Kilve

title: Breakfast with The Grinch
bodyContent: This Christmas, something wonderfully mischievous is happening… The Grinch is sneaking out of Whoville to join us for a very special festive breakfast – and you’re invited! Gather the family and step into a morning filled with giggles, festive magic, and a sprinkle of Grinchy mischief. Enjoy a hearty buffet breakfast with all your favourites, while the Grinch himself wanders the room, stopping by each table for fun, games, and unforgettable photo moments. Your Morning of Magic: Arrival & Seating: 9:00am – 9:30am Buffet Breakfast: 9:00am – 10:45am, with tea, coffee, and juice included Grinchy Shenanigans: 9:30am – 10:45am – meet the Grinch up close as he jokes, poses, and spreads festive cheer (in his own cheeky way!) Tickets Adults & Children: £20 per person Children under 2: £5 per child Tickets must be booked in advance

title: Pergolesi 's MAGNIFICAT & Monteverdi's BEATUS VIR
bodyContent: We are delighted to welcome back Tom Newall as leader for our Choral weekend. We had a very successful course working with him on Poulenc’s GLORIA in 2025. Tom has chosen two much older works for 2026, and we look forward to his interpretations. Tom studied at Durham University and the Royal Northern College of Music. He is a freelance conductor and Musical Director of Salford and Congleton Choral Societies. He works at the University of Warwick and conducts orchestras and opera in International venues, including Buxton International Festival and Teatru Manoel, Malta. Tom’s first appearance in Dunster last year was very well received by all the singers, and we look forward to working with him again in May 2026.

title: Elvana – Elvis Fronted Nirvana
subtitle: Elvana - The world's finest Elvis fronted tribute to Nirvana!
bodyContent: From somewhere deep in the bowels of Disgraceland, the King of Rock & Roll steps out of the afterlife, plugs in, and takes the mic for the band that changed the ’90s forever. Elvis fronts Nirvana. No compromise. Just pure, electrified chaos. Blending the swagger of rockabilly with the raw punch of grunge, Elvana rips through Nirvana’s catalogue while smashing it together with the finest moments of Elvis Presley’s legacy. Expect overdriven riffs, hip-shaking grooves, loud guitars, louder screams, and the kind of mash-ups that feel wrong until they feel absolutely perfect. It smells like cheeseburgers and teen spirit, daddy-o. Described as “Bafflingly Brilliant” by The Guardian, “Absolutely f**king epic” by NME, and “The only band worth getting excited about this year” by Vice, Elvana have built a reputation as one of the wildest live experiences on the planet. Even Billy Idol joked that if Elvis were still around, he’d probably be covering Nirvana anyway. Two icons. One stage. Zero rules. If you haven’t seen Elvana yet, you’re missing out. If you have, you already know… and you’re probably checking tour dates right now. Stupid and contagious. In the absolute best way. “Blowing my mind” ★ Rob Da Bank (Radio One/Bestival) “The World’s Number One tribute to Nirvana… Fronted By Elvis!” ★ Kerrang Magazine "I always thought if Elvis were alive he’d cover Nirvana’s Come As U R” ★ Billy Idol upon hearing Elvana "The World’s Greatest Elvis Presley/Nirvana tribute band” ★ Team Rock / Classic Rock “The King Lives!”

title: The University of Arkansas Children’s Choir at Wells Cathedral
subtitle: Visiting children's choir from Arkansas (USA) presents a lunchtime concert featuring traditional, spiritual and contemporary works including “This Little Light of Mine”, “Scarborough Fair”, “Lacrymosa” and “Let It Be”.
bodyContent: A vibrant lunchtime concert by The University of Arkansas Children’s Choir (USA) as part of their UK tour and the WOWFest 2026 Fringe. Come and enjoy a variety of popular, traditional and spiritual songs including 'This Little Light of Mine', 'Lacrymosa’, 'Scarborough Fair' and 'Let it Be'. The University of Arkansas Children’s Choir, founded in 1997, is a community outreach programme of the University of Arkansas Music Department. The ensemble provides young singers with training in performance, musicianship, and music theory within an inclusive and supportive environment. The choir's performances span a wide range of musical styles, languages, and traditions, combining strong musical standards with energy, warmth, and a commitment to creativity and inclusivity. Musical Directors: Shannon Wicker, Carla Summers and Rachel Cornett. This is a lunchtime concert and admission is included with Cathedral entry. https://www.facebook.com/events/941592248678080

subtitle: The Toy Fair has grown from 40 Stalls to over 300 and is now one of the biggest events of its type in the UK.
bodyContent: Catering for all collectors, you can walk around in the aisles looking for those elusive models that you have always been looking for, the list is endless: Dinky, Corgi, Comics, Minichamps, Hornby, Bassett Lowke, Meccano, Spot-On, Sci-Fi, Marklin, Matchbox, Scalextric, EFE, Lledo, Action man, Dolls, Teddies ..…. there are literally 1000’s of models and so much more, all to be found in the Showering Pavilion and on the Balcony. There is free parking for 3000 cars and the hall is only a short walk from the car park. You can also stop for refreshments in the newly refurbished Wessex Pavilion Restaurant serving breakfasts and lunches, tea and coffee. Early Birds from 08.30 – £10.00 each. General admission – £5 each Under 16s go free with a paying adult Dogs are welcome at this event, but please ensure they are kept on a lead at all times.

title: Brand New Cave Experience at Wookey Hole - up to 20% Off Tickets
subtitle: Looking for a great-value family day out this summer?
bodyContent: Looking for a great-value family day out this summer? Wookey Hole has unveiled a magical line-up of adventures beneath the Mendip Hills, including its hugely popular new immersive cave projections. Wookey Hole is a surprising, whole day experience, where families can explore the legendary caves, home to the famous Witch of Wookey Hole, before discovering a packed programme of attractions above ground. From a 4D cinema, live circus shows (during weekends and Somerset School Holidays), adventure golf and soft play to a nostalgic vintage penny arcade, there’s plenty to keep children entertained throughout the day – all within one price. A Magical Cave Experience Like Never Before Launched this May as part of a £250,000 investment, the all-new underground projection show transforms the caves into a living storybook. Using spectacular projection mapping, the natural rock formations come alive with tales of the Witch, ancient geology and daring explorers - creating a truly unforgettable, immersive adventure that families are already loving.
