title: Ferne Animal Sanctuary invites families to Summer Fun Day fundraiser
subtitle: The event will include a range of activities for all ages, from classic countryside fun to adventurous new experiences.
bodyContent: Sunday 19 July, 10am to 4pm | Ferne Animal Sanctuary, Somerset, TA20 3DH Ferne Animal Sanctuary, the Somerset based animal rehabilitation and rehoming charity, is inviting visitors to enjoy a family-friendly Summer Fun Day on Sunday 19 July, helping to raise vital funds for the animals in its care. Taking place from 10am to 4pm at the sanctuary’s 72-acre site near Chard, the event will include a range of activities for all ages, from classic countryside fun to adventurous new experiences. Visitors can take part in welly wanging, follow a QR code treasure hunt around the sanctuary, enter a raffle for the chance to win fantastic prizes, and try their luck at ‘name the bear’ to be in with a chance of taking home a cuddly new friend. The on-site Perdida Café will also be open throughout the day, serving lunches, drinks, cakes and snacks, offering visitors a place to relax between activities. Axe Nomads will also be joining Ferne Animal Sanctuary for the day, offering pre-bookable axe throwing sessions at 11am and 12pm. The coached sessions will include safety guidance, competitive games, professional targets and a variety of high-quality axes, giving visitors the chance to try something memorable in a safe and supported setting. Amy Lawrence, Corporate & Events Officer at Ferne Animal Sanctuary, says: “Our Summer Fun Day is a brilliant opportunity for families, friends and supporters to spend time together, enjoy the sanctuary and help raise funds for the animals who rely on our care. “Every ticket helps to support Ferne’s ongoing work. As a non-government funded charity, events like this make a real difference and we are so grateful to everyone who comes along, gets involved and supports the sanctuary.” Prebooked general admission tickets cost £6 for adults and £3.50 for children aged five to 15, with under-fives entering free, or full price on the day. Tickets include access to the sanctuary for the day. Axe throwing must be booked separately and is open to visitors aged 10 and over, with under-16s accompanied by an adult. To book Summer Fun Day and axe throwing tickets, please visit: www.ferneanimalsanctuary.org/product-category/workshops-courses-events Ferne Animal Sanctuary is a non-government funded charity that has provided refuge and rehabilitation to its animals for more than 85 years. Located in a National Landscapes area nestled in the Blackdown Hills near Chard, Somerset, Ferne Animal Sanctuary houses and cares for more than 300 animals on its 72-acre site.

title: Community Discovery Day Celebrates Extraordinary Roman Ring and Coin Hoard
subtitle: The event will be a celebration of the Roman treasure and offer visitors the opportunity to explore its history through creative activities, community displays and a curator’s talk.
bodyContent: Ilminster, Somerset – Thursday 20 August 2026 South West Heritage Trust and Ilminster Arts Centre are delighted to announce Ilminster Roman Ring Discovery Day , a free, family-friendly event celebrating the remarkable Ilminster Ring and coin hoard . Taking place on Thursday 20 August 2026 from 10.00 am to 3.00 pm at Ilminster Arts Centre, the event will be a celebration of the Roman treasure and offer visitors the opportunity to explore its history through creative activities, community displays and a curator’s talk. The acquisition of the ring and engagement programme has been made possible through funding from Arts Council England / V&A Purchase Grant Fund. The Discovery Day is further supported through the South West Heritage Trust’s Arts Council England NPO programme that takes museum collections into communities. Dating to around AD 297, the Ilminster Ring is an extraordinary Roman gold finger ring weighing 48 grams and set with a finely engraved gemstone depicting the goddess Victory driving a two-horse chariot. Buried alongside a small hoard of coins, the ring is exceptional for both its scale and craftsmanship, making it one of the most important Roman finds from South West England. Visitors to the Ilminster Ring Discovery Day will have the opportunity to view the Roman Ring alongside coins from the hoard, hear a talk by South West Heritage Trust Senior Curator Amal Khreisheh, and enjoy a display of artworks created by local primary school pupils. Drop-in activities throughout the day include making a screen print from a design inspired by the Roman Ring, decorating a wearable ring to take home, transforming a side-profile photograph into a digital Roman coin, and contributing to an interactive audiovisual installation by wearing and sharing the story behind a personal treasured ring. Amal Khreisheh, Senior Curator at South West Heritage Trust, said: “The Ilminster Ring is an extraordinary object that connects us directly to people living in Somerset more than 1,700 years ago. Its exceptional craftsmanship and remarkable preservation, alongside the Roman coin hoard with which it was discovered, make it a rare and significant find that sheds light on a pivotal moment in Somerset’s Roman history. We’re delighted to be able to share it with the community and to celebrate its story through a special day of activities that will inspire curiosity about Somerset’s rich heritage.” Julie Manley, Chair of Ilminster Arts Centre, said: "We're delighted to host this free Discovery Day for the community and hope that as many people as possible will visit to enjoy this extraordinary historic exhibit, on show in our wonderful gallery. The day will be packed with interactive events, exploration and storytelling, including a display from local schools. It'll be a great opportunity for the local community to come together and celebrate a fascinating and beautiful piece of history found on its doorstep." The Ilminster Ring and Hoard were acquired by the South West Heritage Trust on behalf of Somerset Council under the Treasure Act 1996 with generous support from the Arts Council England / V&A Purchase Grant Fund, Art Fund with a contribution from the Wolfson Foundation, and The Headley Trust, alongside vital contributions from the Friends of The Museum of Somerset, Ilminster Town Council, Taunton U3A and Ilminster Education Foundation. The Ilminster Ring Discovery Day is a free, drop-in day. For more information visit ilminsterartscentre.com and swheritage.org.uk

title: The Castle at Taunton
subtitle: The Castle at Taunton is one of the UK’s most historic & prestigious 4 Star Hotels, having been at the forefront of British cuisine for 40 years. We also operate Brazz, which since 1998 has provided the blueprint for British Brasseries across the country.
bodyContent: The Castle Hotel is a unique family-owned hotel set in a historic building in the heart of Taunton in Somerset. A simple ethos lies at the heart of the hotel – to offer the warmest of welcomes, give the utmost personal attention and exemplary service to each & every guest. The Castle Hotel is a one-off, not a link in a chain. The Castle’s reputation for fine food and wine, comfort, and attentive service has been built by three generations of the Chapman Family, with a passion for promoting the highest standards in every aspect of the hotel. Taunton lies at the heart of the region, making The Castle the ideal base from which to explore the history, magic and wonder of the West Country. Each of The Castle’s 44 bedrooms are individually decorated, offering its own personality and comfort away from home. Whether you’re looking for healthy or hearty, you’ll find it all at the award-winning restaurant, Brazz. Featuring a wide-ranging menu, you’ll find old favourites such as Brazz Fishcakes – which have been present since day one – as well as Quantock Lamb, Brixham Crab and much more. The Castle’s afternoon teas served in the art deco elegance of Castle Bow have become somewhat legendary. Freshly baked scones with west country clotted cream and strawberry jam, elegant finger sandwiches, pastries and cakes along with a fine selection of loose-leaf tea, make this a very special occasion… especially if you add a bottle of champagne. Some of these training options include: assistance with upskilling existing members of staff, pre-employment traineeships, apprenticeships, and we can assist you in the recruitment process. We are one of the top-performing Colleges in the country and offer award-winning teaching and support. Our progression routes are wide, starting at Entry Level and going through to Level 7 (Master’s Degree), meaning that your staff can become highly qualified using just one training provider. What puts Weston College ahead of other training providers is the quality and uniqueness of our provision, which is supported by dedicated and often award-winning facilities. We continuously invest in our courses, lecturers, assessors and teaching spaces, and consult with businesses to ensure that our provision is teaching the sector-relevant skills that will allow them to prosper through the creation of a highly motivated and skilled workforce. At the college we have a number of state of the art facilities which are available to hire. We have rooms that are suitable for smaller occasions and can also accommodate almost 1000 guests in our newly refurbished Winter Gardens Pavilion.

title: The Bird
subtitle: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to. A place to work and meet and by day and discover ever-changing bar experiences by night.
bodyContent: To be found just a few minutes’ stroll from Bath’s spectacular city-centre attractions, The Bird, Bath (previously The County Hotel) has re-branded to fit in with its distinctive new personality as part of the Kaleidoscope Collection. Owned by seasoned hoteliers, Ian and Christa Taylor, The Bird is a name that better reflects the vibrant transformation of the hotel, which has already seen refreshed public spaces, additional bedrooms, a new bar, relaxed restaurant and meeting spaces, as well as a much-loved pop-up beach bar for summer. Now with 27 en-suite bedrooms featuring every home comfort, many have far-reaching views across the cricket and rugby grounds to Bath Abbey, with the rolling hills of Bath and beyond. Breakfast is served in a lovely bright dining room, which overlooks Bath Abbey and opens into the conservatory, where morning coffee and afternoon tea can be enjoyed, while the Taylors have also created a wonderfully eclectic neighbourhood bar with relaxed food offering, designed as social hub for work or play. A space for freelancers to work, friends to meet for coffee or a relaxed dinner, there’s a bar for seasonal drinks and various seating areas centred around vast contemporary pieces of art. A separate meeting room also provides a creative space for workshops and get-togethers, private parties, celebrations and more. Visitors and locals alike won’t have to wait long for the next seasonal pop-up, a visually exciting Winter Wonderland for the festive season - arguably the coolest party space in town. Set in a fantastical venue full of surprises, woodland branches and spruces will be strewn with fairy lights, tables topped with flickering candelabra and chairs draped in Bavarian rugs to keep you cosy. Everyone is welcome to simply drop in to experience the magical vibe. The Bird is easily reached via all main approaches to Bath, and has plenty of parking for guests.

title: The Workshop
subtitle: A comfortable cabin for up to 4 people just a few minutes from Bath, set in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty with the Cotswold Way on its boundary.
bodyContent: The Workshop was once just that – a workshop where the owner, Jane and her staff made horse rugs until the business was sold about 10 years ago. Since then, it has been transformed into a stylish and comfortable house with startling views, comfy sofas and beds and a nifty kitchen with all necessary equipment to cook up a storm. Great walking perched close to the Cotswold Way, with a rural feel although Bath is just five miles away, the the park and ride a twenty minute walk or five minutes in the car. The entrance is through a porch for keeping the drafts out and leaving boots behind. This gives on to a large living room with sofas and dining table clustered around a Jotul wood burning stove. There is a spacious and fully equipped kitchen with dresser and pretty china on it, fridge, freezer, dishwasher and washing machine. For cooking, there is an induction hob and an electric oven together with a toaster and kettle and microwave. Eat outside in a ptretty courtyard or indoors at a handsome oak table by the fire Sleep in either of two large bedrooms unruffled by noise and separated from the living room by oak plank doors. The main bedroom is spacious with a comfortable king-sized bed, the second with a double bed. Both bedrooms amply furnished with provision for clothes and possessions The warm bathroom has a toilet, walk-in shower and washbasin and is furnished with large fluffy towels The cabin has oil-fired central heating and a wood burning stove and wood is provided for the first fire. The cabin has its own WiFi internet connection and Freeview TV. Outside, there is a balcony at the front of the cabin with views downhill across the fields towards the Welsh hills in the distance. At the side by the front door is a secluded patio area with table and chairs and a small barbeque for al fresco dining. The cabin has a dedicated parking place immediately next to it.
tagline: A comfortable cabin for up to 4 people just a few minutes from Bath

title: Colosseum
subtitle: Essential Progressive Jazz-Rock.
bodyContent: Colosseum came to fame in 1969 when the band led by legendary drummer Jon Hiseman released its debut album Those Who Are About To Die Salute You. Best selling studio albums followed, notably Valentyne Suite (1969) and The Daughter of Time is Truth (1970). Changes in personnel saw the arrival of the soulful Chris Farlowe, famed for his Sixties chart hit Out Of Time and Clem Clempson, the young blues guitar virtuoso and vocalist and bass player Mark Clarke. However the group broke up in 1971 and the musicians went their separate ways.

title: Midsummer Revels with GreenMatthews at Somerset Rural Life Museum
subtitle: Celebrate the summer days with musical duo GreenMatthews.
bodyContent: Step into a world of sunshine, song, and spirited tradition with Midsummer Revels. Blending English folksongs with original compositions and lively, toe-tapping dance tunes, this uplifting performance captures the essence of long summer days, blue skies, and rolling green fields. From tales of land and sea to stories of town and country, the music is brought vividly to life through a rich array of instruments, including English border bagpipes, mandocello, and shawm. All of it is delivered with GreenMatthews’ signature wit and warmth. Following the success of their acclaimed Midwinter Revels, this latest production offers a joyful seasonal counterpart, perfect for anyone looking to soak up the sounds and spirit of summer. Need to Know: • Booking required • The event takes place in a historic 14th-century Abbey Barn – please dress warmly if the weather is cool • A bar will be open during the interval (cash preferred) • This event is not suitable for children under 5 years old

title: Paddy Young: Will Sir Be Laughing Alone?
subtitle: The award-winning stand-up and star of Saturday Night Live UK heads out on tour with a brand new show.
bodyContent: You’re born alone, you die alone. That’s true enough. But what happened to that part in the middle? Big Year for Pad. SNL (UK, but still a big deal), a bunch of awards (hate bringing them up), and plenty of bit-parts to boot. But what’s it all about? I’ve fallen in love more times than you’ve had hot dinners and I’ve fumbled every single one of them. If you think I’ve learnt my lesson you couldn’t be wronger. I’m telling you, some of these baddies have got me winning staring competitions with the ceiling. But I don’t even think about that s*** anymore. Some of my ideas are so funny that they scare me, so GOD knows how you lot are gonna feel !! As seen on: Mitchell & Webb Are Not Helping, Everyone Else Burns, and his own stand-up special Hungry. Horny. Scared. “Young is surely on the road to stardom” ★★★★★ Rolling Stone “One of British comedy’s most intriguing new voices” ★★★★ The Independent “Bursting with energy and talent, and has the audience screaming with laughter until the end” ★★★★ Scotsman ”Wildly funny” ★★★★ Chortle ”A high-energy hour that’s bursting its buttons with jokes" ★★★★ Fest "Genuinely hilarious punchlines… Perfectly timed joke delivery” ★★★★ Wee Review “Quick on his feet, likeable and very funny” ★★★★ Beyond The Joke

title: The Slimline Shufflers + Desmond’s Dawn
subtitle: Join The Slimline Shufflers and Desmond’s Dawn for a soulful evening of blues music - part of our summer series of free, or pay-what-you-can, Electric Bar shows.
bodyContent: The Slimline Shufflers: Virtuosic piano playing, searing harmonica, and inspiration drawn from iconic Crescent City musicians such as Professor Longhair, James Booker, Allen Toussaint and Dr. John. The Slimline Shufflers are a dynamic New Orleans-style rhythm ‘n’ blues band hailing from Bristol, UK. They have toured the UK extensively with highlights including Suffolk’s Maverick Festival and Gloucester’s Cajun and Zydeco Festival. Stateside, they shared a bill with the Rebirth Brass Band at The Howlin’ Wolf, during the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival 2024, and performed with a few members of The Dirty Dozen Brass Band at Professor Longhair’s former house on Terpsichore St, where the official second line culminated as the street was renamed to Professor Longhair Lane. Following the release of their well-received debut album “Suspicious Blues”, The Slimline Shufflers released their first ever collection of original songs, “Turbo Island EP”, in May 2026. “The Slimline Shufflers focus on different sides of the blues…think early Georgie Fame, with blues harmonica and a really kicking rhythm section.” – Blues in Britain Desmond’s Dawn: Five-piece band playing original 'flunk' - a fusion of blues, rock, pop, folk, reggae, and punk coming together as tunes that will get you toes tapping and your hips wiggling. Two songwriters, two guitars, two lead vocalists in the name of Joe Munrow and Al Cosnett are joined by a few fellows, Paul Cannon on sax, Owen Davies on double bass and Alan Hudson on drums.
tagline: Join The Slimline Shufflers and Desmond’s Dawn for a soulful evening of blues music.

title: Summertime at Somerset Heritage Sites
subtitle: From interactive exhibitions and outdoor animal encounters to historical adventures and artistic exploration, there are opportunities for all ages.
bodyContent: Museums across Somerset are inviting visitors to make the most of the summer holidays with a vibrant programme of family-friendly activities. From interactive exhibitions and outdoor animal encounters to historical adventures and artistic exploration, there are opportunities for all ages to get involved, try something new and enjoy time together. With events taking place at the Museum of Somerset in Taunton, Somerset Rural Life Museum in Glastonbury, Somerset Brick and Tile Museum in Bridgwater, and Avalon Archaeology at the Avalon Marshes Centre, this summer promises a season of play, creativity and discovery across the county. South West Heritage Trust Museums’ Manager Susie Simmons said: “Across our museums, we’re offering a fantastic range of experiences—from hands-on creativity and imaginative exhibitions to outdoor adventures and living history.” The Museum of Somerset in Taunton This summer, visitors are invited to explore the joy of play at the Museum of Somerset, where a diverse range of playful experiences awaits. The family-friendly PLAY experience (25 July-10 Oct) encourages multi-generational discovery, offering opportunities to explore and rediscover much-loved toys and games. Families can share memories, spark their imagination, and enjoy moments of play together, with activities designed to delight visitors of all ages. The summer programme also features an Aardman Model Making Workshop , with sessions tailored for both families and adults-only. Adults can take part in further sessions designed exclusively for grownups at a special Art with Abandon messy-play session and a large-scale interactive gaming experience, Watch the Skies: Second Site . All workshops require pre-booking. The Museum of Somerset is open Tuesday to Saturday 10.00 am – 5.00 pm. Somerset Rural Life Museum in Glastonbury At Somerset Rural Life Museum families pay onceand can come back as many times as they like! All the daily summer holiday activities are included, alongside a new exhibition of printmaking by Glastonbury-artist Harry Brockway (1958 – 2024). There will be a menagerie of animals to meet including donkeys, shire horses and birds of prey, alongside arts and crafts and museum trails. Somerset Rural Life Museum is open Tuesday to Sunday 10.00 am – 5.00 pm. Somerset Brick and Tile Museum in Bridgwater At Somerset Brick and Tile Museum there are lots of chances for young creatives to ‘play with clay’. Potter Ella Phillips will offer two days of pot-throwing tuition, and local artist Jackie Curtis will run a family printing workshop. Other family days include a chance to sculpt a beehive ornament and a glass melt village. There’s also a special Bricktastic LEGO® day, family pottery painting day and a creative clay event for young adults (aged 10 – 16). Opening days vary – see website for details and booking. Avalon Archaeology at The Avalon Marshes Centre Avalon Archaeology is open every Saturday and Sunday during the school holidays. Visitors can immerse themselves in thousands of years of local history as they explore replica buildings including a Saxon Longhall and a Roman villa. Summer highlights include family tours, a Woodworking Workshop for Young People, and an atmospheric Arthurian Legends performance. There are also themed family‑fun days, and a visiting Roman Doctor who will share insights into Roman health care. Visitors can end the holidays with Hærfest honouring the ancient traditions. Avalon Archaeology is open 10.00 am – 4.00 pm every Saturday and Sunday during the school holidays (25 Jul – 30 Aug) with additional special event days. For more information about all the sites run by the South West Heritage Trust and summer events visit swheritage.org.uk

title: Camping at Wimbleball Lake - South West Lakes Trust
subtitle: Nestled in the hills of Exmoor National Park is Wimbleball Lake, offering an excellent outdoors holiday for glampers and campers alike.
bodyContent: Wimbleball Lake Campsite Bell tents, wooden pods, a cabin, grass, hard standing, electric and non-electric pitches Located in Exmoor National Park – designated Dark Skies Reserve Onsite activities include kayaking, canoeing, archery, cycling, sailing and much more Children’s play area, café and miles of off-road foot and cycle trails Whether you love pitching up a tent or prefer a night’s stay in comfort – nestled in the hills of Exmoor National Park is Wimbleball Lake, offering an excellent outdoors holiday for glampers and campers alike. Wimbleball Lake is an AA graded three star campsite, with three bell tents, two wooden pods, a new cabin and ample grass pitches. You can hire a fire pit, enjoy a barbeque (raised off the ground) and do a spot of stargazing with a rented telescope . Exmoor National Park is a designated International Dark Sky Reserve - Wimbleball is a designated Dark Sky Discovery Site and is the perfect place to stargaze and engage with nature and the outdoors in its greatest form. What can you do? There’s plenty of things to do at Wimbleball – spot birds from the hide, climb trees, build dens or take to the water and experience a canoe or paddle board adventure. If watersports isn’t your thing then try archery or highropes. Bring your bike or enjoy a walk, a network of off-road paths and trails follow the shorelines of the lake, meandering through woodlands and onto open moorland – keep an eye out for Exmoor’s iconic deer and ponies. There’s ample of open space to let your children play freely and get up close to nature – download and discover mini-beast below your feet, birds soaring over-head, identify trees and track foot prints.
tagline: Nestled in the hills of Exmoor National Park is Wimbleball Lake

title: Somerset Toiletry Company
subtitle: The Somerset Toiletry Company - Bath, Body, Home Fragrance, made with expertise and care
bodyContent: Established in 1999 as a small family company The Somerset Toiletry Company has flourished into an International business with toiletries sold in over 50 countries. We are renowned for bath, body and home fragrance products that vary from richly classical to wonderfully innovative. We sell our own brands as well as working with large retail groups to design, formulate and manufacture their own private label goods. With an extensive range of products from shower gels and hand washes to lotions, soaps, diffusers, candles, perfume, toiletry bags, accessories, cards and more we have a wealth of experience and expertise . We manufacture in any one of six countries meaning we are able to ensure different economical and philosophical requirements are catered for. Over the years we have won many design and business awards as well as The Queens Award for Enterprise. We love our Somerset roots and are thrilled to be part of Visit Somerset.
tagline: The Somerset Toiletry Company - Bath, Body, Home Fragrance, made with expertise.

title: The Corner House Hotel
subtitle: Hotel in the centre of Taunton near to Musgrove Park Hospital and the Castle.
bodyContent: Within walking distance of the centre of Somerset’s County town, this 45 bedroom hotel has been transformed to meet the demands of the modern day traveller. All the bedrooms have very recently been refurbished in a contemporary style. Not only are they tremendous value for money but we asked you what you wanted from a bedroom in the heart of this wonderful county town of Taunton; a good night’s sleep, a comfortable bed, a decent modern bathroom, an excellent television system and security - and that's what we offer! The recent addition of The Corner House Bar & Restaurant has been well received by hotel residents and locals alike. Ideal for business or pleasure, dining or for a drink. We also have meeting rooms and can facilitate your function or wedding. We are a pet friendly hotel too. Please note: Visit Taunton cannot accept any responsibility for matters arising between a customer and the accommodation provider. Visit Taunton does not accept liability for information on third party websites. This is not an exhaustive list.
tagline: Hotel in the centre of Taunton near to Musgrove Park Hospital and the Castle.

title: The Malthouse
subtitle: Fall in love with The Malthouse, a romantic Grade II listed building with modern levels of space and comfort, perfectly located for family holidays in Somerset. 7 bedrooms, 4 bathrooms, modern kitchen, with open fire, two large living areas, reliable wi-fi and idyllic views over the garden and private parking.
bodyContent: As soon as you walk through the heavy oak door into the original cart-way, you feel this warm friendly space, from the cart-way you will see the stylish handmade kitchen and dining room, complete with working stone fireplace. The huge pine dining table is just asking to host up to 14 people for an extended family meal or several breakfast sittings, cooked up in the well-equipped kitchen. A utility room in the basement has a washing machine, tumble drier and extra tall fridge plus a useful storage area for extra food. The two lounges are comfortable and thoughtfully furnished. One has an inglenook fireplace, very welcoming on those colder days, deep sofa, workspace and cosy lighting. The other is the garden room where you can enjoy far-reaching views of the idyllic countryside. Elegantly proportioned and plenty of room for family games, relaxation and 50inch smart TV. The 7 bedrooms are large and comfortable with crisp Egyptian cotton linen and fluffy towels. One king bedroom on the ground floor with its own bathroom, 1st and second floor a further 6 bedrooms and 3 bathrooms. Decorated with style and comfort in mind. There's a big open courtyard and large, long, well-managed garden. Guests enjoy alfresco dining and barbecues. A range of outdoor games including table tennis are provided for screen-free fun, well behaved dogs welcome. Private parking. On your doorstep Bath, Bristol, Longleat all easily reached, as well as many local walks and National Trust gardens.

title: By The Byre Holidays
subtitle: Beautiful self-catering accommodation nestled within the Somerset countryside close to the Wiltshire border. Charming accommodation comprising of both contemporary two bedroomed cottages and stylish three bedroomed lodges. Ideally situated for visiting Longleat, Bath, Bradford On Avon, Cheddar Gorge, Wookey Hole, Stonehenge, Wells, Glastonbury and much, much, more!
bodyContent: Situated on the edge of the charming village of Beckington, By The Byre Holidays offer seven stylish and comfortable properties for the perfect self-catered stay. Each of the four 2-bedroomed cottages (Sleeps 4 + Cot), are well-appointed, with a double and a twin bedroom, family bathroom, a modern, fully equipped kitchen and open plan lounge/diner. The three modern, single story, 3-bedroomed Lodges (Sleep 6 + Cot) have full height windows to make the most of the countryside views! Open plan lounge/kitchen/diner, family bathroom and 3 Bedrooms (Master with ensuite, 1 double/twin, 1 Twin). Each Lodge has a decked patio with uninterrupted views over the surrounding countryside. Set in four acres of grounds, there is plenty of open grass for barbeques and ball games. By The Byre is just a few minutes’ drive away from Longleat with good access to Bath, Bradford On Avon, Cheddar Gorge, Wookey Hole, Stonehenge, Wells, Glastonbury and much much more! The local market town of Frome has regular Independent markets and the award-winning White Row farm shop also has a restaurant/café, fish & chip shop and play park!

title: The Cornerhouse
subtitle: Hotel, Bar and Restaurant in Frome!
bodyContent: Located in the heart of Frome, The Cornerhouse offers a great range of local real ales & ciders, premium lagers, a carefully selected wine list, and premium spirits. We specialise in gin, being home to Frome's first and only Gin Society, as well as having over 40 gins on our shelves and a specific menu created for us by leaders in the premium mixer world - Fever Tree. We are very proud to be the only establishment in Frome serving the award winning Pieminister Pies. Meat, vegetarian, vegan and gluten free options are all available. The Cornerhouse showcases a variety of live music every weekend. Saturdays play host to local bands playing anything from classic rock to pop folk, while Sundays take a more chilled vibe with jazz being played on the first and third Sunday of every month. We have 11 en suite bedrooms, all rates with a hearty breakfast included. Our location is perfect for exploring the historical market town of Frome and a great base to visit surrounding areas such as Stourhead, Longleat and the City of Bath.

title: The Old Granary – Sleeps 12
subtitle: A stunning converted barn sleeping up to 12 people, set in a peaceful countryside location.
bodyContent: This detached barn is 3/4 of a mile from Church Farm along a country lane. It has its own landscaped garden and private driveway with plenty of parking. Use of the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool and Games Room 3/4 of a mile away at Church Farm is included, plus the barn is dog friendly. – Sleep up to 12 – 6 miles from Bath – Rural Retreat

title: Garden Theatre Festival
subtitle: The Garden Theatre Festival is back in Bath for its third triumphant year!
bodyContent: Opening Times 21 July 2023 - 5 Aug 2023 About Taking place in the magical gardens of the Holburne Museum, expect two weeks of superb performances from nationally renowned companies, in the beautiful, open-air thrust stage space, with something for all of the family to enjoy. Returning to the festival this year are fan-favourites The Three Inch Fools, Sarah Louise-Young and Bath’s very own Calf 2 Cow, and there will be exciting shows from Paulus - The Cabaret Geek, Heartbreak Productions, Tethered Wits Theatre Company, and Something Underground Theatre Company. The festival brings the best in outdoor entertainment from across the UK, including acts from the local area, right to the heart of Bath. Tickets go on sale from 5pm on Thursday 30 March, with a 10% discount applied on the ﬁrst 100 tickets for each show bought before Easter Monday, the 10 April. Programme: An Evening Without Kate Bush by Sarah Louise Young – Friday 21 July at 7:30pm Looking For Me Friend: The Music of Victoria Wood by Paulus, the Cabaret Geek – Saturday 22 July at 7pm David Walliams’s, Bad Dad by Heartbreak Productions - Sunday 23 July at 5pm The Great Gatsby by Tethered Wits Theatre Company - Tuesday 25 July at 7pm Doctor Dolittle by Tethered Wits Theatre Company - Wednesday 26 July at 7pm The Spirit of Woodstock by Something Underground Theatre Company - Thursday 27 July at 7pm As You Like It by The Three Inch Fools - Friday 28 and Sunday 30 July, both at 7pm Robin Hood by The Three Inch Fools - Saturday 29 and Monday 31 July, both at 7pm The Jabberwocky & Other Nonsense by Calf 2 Cow - Tuesday 1 to Saturday 5 August, all at 7pm Ticket Prices: Standard Tickets Standard Adult: £16.50 Standard Child (under 16): £12 Standard Family (2 adults + 2 children): £45 Premier Tickets Premier Tickets include a glass of prosecco or soft drink alternative, luxury nibbles and a branded tote bag. You will also gain access to the venue 30 minutes before the main doors. This gives you the opportunity to get your preferred spot in the garden. Premier Adult: £37 Premier Child: £25 (excludes prosecco, complimentary soft drink and snacks included) Premier Family (two adults two children): £85 A 10% discount will be applied to all tickets purchased before Easter Monday (10 April 2023). Visit www.gardentheatrefest.co.uk for further information.

title: The Town House in Bath
subtitle: A chic, luxury Georgian town house in the Centre of Bath. Beautifully designed and renovated with wonderful modern wet rooms and a double ended roll top bath.
bodyContent: Beautifully renovated, Georgian Town House in the centre of Bath. Chic, stylish and very central. Close to Milsom Street and the Assembly Rooms and offering luxury self catering accommodation. Perfect for families or for groups of friends sleeping up to 14 guests – please do see the floorplans to help you plan your stay. Karen and John have painstakingly rejunvenated this elegant property back to it’s original glory. Karen’s passion lies in restoring property using traditional methods to create the original atmosphere of former elegant times. The attention to detail makes staying at The Town House a particularly special experience. From the softness of the lime wash to the exquisite workmanship of the window shutters and original wooden floors make this property stand out and offers the opportunity for you to experience a truly unique stay in Bath. We can also offer The Post House , sleeping up to 12 guests and The Secret Escape , a chic apartment for 2 guests. The Town House is ideally situated just 10 minutes walk from the famous Thermae Bath Spa via the chic shopping area of Milsom Street. The must see Assembly Rooms, world famous Circus and Royal Crescent are all less than 400 metres away. Set in this central location of Bath, everything you would wish for from a City break is on your doorstep.
tagline: A chic, luxury Georgian town house in the Centre of Bath

bodyContent: At Bay Tree House we aim to provide our guests with a comfortable and relaxing stay. title: The Royal Bath & West Show 2026
subtitle: Join us this summer for a Great British family day out. The Show will feature a plethora of activities, demonstrations and entertainment; including interactive activities, fast pace excitement in the Main Ring and a much-enhanced food hall experience.
bodyContent: The Royal Bath & West Show returns to the Bath & West Showground this spring for three days of unforgettable family fun from 28th–30th May. Spread across 240 acres of picturesque Somerset countryside, this beloved annual tradition offers something for everyone - from toddlers to teens and adults alike. Kids will love the Discover the Future zone, where they can dive into free STEM (science, technology, engineering and maths) activities designed to spark curiosity and imagination. There’s also interactive farming fun at Lakeside Farm, where families can learn about animals, crops and where their food comes from. The Woodland & Countryside Arena is a hive of hands-on excitement, with chances to make wooden creations and explore countryside crafts. For animal lovers, the Show delivers close-up encounters and entertainment in the Main Ring, where the thrilling Shetland Pony Grand National takes centre stage - a fast-paced, joyful race featuring young jockeys and their lively ponies that’s sure to delight spectators of all ages. There are also heavy horse displays, Pony Club games and vintage vehicle parades to enjoy throughout the day. Families can relax and soak up the atmosphere on the Main Lawn with picnics or catch live music from vibrant local artists, including sets from energetic bands such as Jelly Roll Jazz Band. Music adds to the celebratory feel, with The Wurzels bringing their unmistakable West Country sound. Meanwhile, the Vintage Fairground adds old-fashioned thrills, and the Bath & West Railway offers a scenic ride for little adventurers. Food lovers

title: Rock n Ribs
subtitle: Rock N Ribs is a 3 day American themed family-friendly festival in Somerset, UK.
bodyContent: We’re excited to welcome the Rock n Ribs Festival to Bath & West Showground from 17th to 19th July 2026, a three-day celebration of American-inspired fun, food, music and entertainment in the heart of Somerset. Rock n Ribs is one of the UK’s most talked-about Americana festivals and brings together smokehouse BBQ, rock & country music, monster trucks, family-friendly activities and more across three unforgettable days. Expect live music from top bands, monster truck shows, tailgating and USA-style vehicles, wrestling, line dancing and BMX stunts, eating contests, plus plenty of food stalls serving legendary smoked ribs, brisket, burgers, hot dogs and more BBQ favourites. This year’s festival also features new experiences like Geezer’s Palace, a Las Vegas-style entertainment area with tribute acts, close-up magic, fun casino games, karaoke and drag queen bingo, and Billy Bob’s Woods, where campers can enjoy late-night campfire sessions deep into the night. Whether you’re into great food, live music, family fun, American vehicles or just good times with friends, Rock n Ribs promises something for everyone right here at Bath & West Showground. Monster Truck Shows • Country Music • American Rock • Tailgating • USA Vehicles • Wrestling • Line Dancing • Movie Cars • Smokehouse BBQ • Extreme BMX Shows • Mini Monster Truck Driving • Eating Contests • Fire Ladder Experience • Monster Truck Rides • High School Sports • Vehicle Parade • Wild West Horse Show • Wall Of Death and so much more! bodyContent: Informing and educating young consumers about where their food comes from and the hard work farmers do to make sure we eat the very best of British food. title: Dunster Castle Experience Days - A Day with the Head Gardener
subtitle: We are hosting an experience day, which offers the chance to spend the day with Dunster Castle's Head Gardener.
bodyContent: We are hosting an experience day, which offers the chance to spend the day with Dunster Castle's Head Gardener. Responsible for the maintenance of the 18 acres of garden at Dunster Castle, this is an opportunity not to be missed for all those gardening questions. You'll begin the day with refreshments and an introductory talk on Dunster Castle by James Cordingley, Head Gardener, who has been working in the horticultural industry for more than 18 years. You'll then embark on a tour of the gardens, including areas not usually open to the public. This is a great opportunity to go into depth on the castle's unusual subtropical environment and historic planting plans. Once the tour is over, you'll head down to the Watermill Tearoom for a delicious two-course lunch. James will accompany you and will be on hand to chat and answer questions. After lunch and questions, you'll have the opportunity to tour the nursery at Dunster Castle. See how the garden team grow and nurture the plants grown for the gardens and how they grow for the castle garden's unique microclimate. You'll then get hands on with compost and cuttings in a workshop with James where you'll learn techniques to take the best cuttings while maintaining the health of the parent plant. At the end of the day, finish your experience with a trip to the Stables Shop for souvenirs and local products before heading home.
tagline: We are hosting an experience day!

title: Cheddar Petruth Paddocks
subtitle: Cheddar Petruth Paddocks is a place where anyone can rock up and feel immediately at home. From the couple in their expensive new motor home to a bunch of young lads in a £29.99 tent from Aldi, from Mum, Dad and a couple of kids to a big group of family and friends – and everyone in between.
bodyContent: A live-and-let-live place where there are refreshingly few rules, kids can be kids, campfires are encouraged, music and bad singing are not a problem and people feel free to wander round making new friends. That’s what we mean by free range camping – and we love it. The world has become obsessed with health and safety, risk assessments, petty rules and irritating regulations. We think the whole point of camping, and spending time outside, is to get away from all that stuff. To leave bureaucracy and red tape behind. To wind the clock back to a time when you could just go out and enjoy yourself in a field without people trying to wrap everyone in cotton wool and present you with a long list of “dos” and “don’ts” (mainly “don’ts!”). That’s what Cheddar Petruth Paddocks is all about – creating a carefree space where kids can be kids, and you can be you, whether you are three or sixty three. We don’t have a bar you have to drink at, or a shop you have to buy your tinnies from - you can go to bed when you want, wander wherever you like, make friends or keep yourselves to yourselves. So long as you show a bit of common sense and respect for others you can do pretty much as you like. Life’s so complicated these days, and busy, that we just wanted to establish an environment where things are simple and slow. Where all kinds of different people can unwind and get to know each other. Most of the things you'll probably need while you're staying with us, you can get from Cheddar, which is just a short walk from the site. If that sounds like your kind of place you’re welcome to come and join us!

bodyContent: Make the most of those long summer days with our late-night opening throughout the holidays. title: The Stables
subtitle: Our beautiful detached three bedroomed former barn retains many original architectural features.
bodyContent: The holiday home comprises of two double bedrooms and a single bedroom (with an additional single pull out trundle bed) sleeping a maximum of six guests. Each bedroom has an ensuite shower, basin and WC. There is also a separate guest cloakroom on the first floor. On the ground floor there is a spacious living/dining room with a feature Victorian cast iron cooking range, perfect for self catering. The new spacious kitchen has solid granite worktops and hand painted units. This also leads to the shared garden and cider orchard. The holiday home was redecorated in subtle Farrow and Ball paint colours and re-carpeted throughout during the Spring of 2013. The Local Area The Stables is located beside the ancient Roman Fosse Way – the oldest Roman Road in the British Isles. It is walking distance from the village of Castle Combe and just 20 minutes drive from Bath. If you are looking to explore the great outdoors there are many local walking and cycle routes. Need more space? We have three self catering holiday homes in total. These sleep up to 16 guests with the option to up this to 22 guests using rooms from our bed and breakfast . We often provide accommodation for parties attending weddings in the local villages of Castle Combe, Grittleton and Euridge. The Dovecote sleeps up to 4 guests. The Garden House sleeps up to 6 guests. It is also pet friendly. We offer last minute dicounts so please contact us directly for the best deals.
tagline: Our beautiful detached three bedroomed former barn retains many original architectural features.

title: The Wurzels Annual Christmas Show
subtitle: The Wurzels announce a much anticipated return to Komedia Bath for Christmas 2026!
bodyContent: The Wurzels, also known as the "West Country's finest", are a legendary British band that have been entertaining audiences with their unique blend of rural folk, rock, and comedy for over five decades. Hailing from Somerset, England, this talented group has become synonymous with good old-fashioned fun and infectious foot-stomping music. Formed in 1966, The Wurzels were initially known as "Adge Cutler and the Wurzels", led by charismatic frontman Adge Cutler. Their music, often referred to as "scrumpy and western", is deeply rooted in the West Country culture and traditions, celebrating the joys and quirks of rural life. With their distinctive blend of accordion, banjo, drums, and guitar, The Wurzels have created a sound that is instantly recognizable and impossible to resist. And this time they`re starting early on a Sunday evening so plenty of time to visit the Christmas Market and still get home in good time! This band has paved the way over decades for Scrumpy n’ Western – a genre packed full of double entendre, mainstream parody, and a comical folk style. The perfect accompaniment to cider-drinking. Signed to label heavyweights Columbia and EMI, The Wurzels are world-famous and continue to play over 100 sell-out shows and festivals every year and Bath Komedia is always on their list. Their quintessentially West Country cover of Kaiser Chiefs’ ‘Ruby’ has been a massive show favourite of late, as well as their hip hop version of the ubiquitous hit ‘Combine Harvester’. title: Queer Romans on the edge(s) – talk by Dr Tatiana Ivleva
subtitle: In this talk, Dr Tatiana Ivleva from Newcastle University will examine Roman gravestones and memorials to explore relationships in the ancient world.
bodyContent: We may know about Emperor Hadrian and Antinous but what other queer lives can be uncovered? Did they exist only in Rome, or is there evidence of them in the far provinces of the Empire, such as Roman Britain or in places like Hadrian’s Wall? In this talk, Dr Tatiana Ivleva from Newcastle University will examine Roman gravestones and memorials to explore relationships in the ancient world. Some of these monuments suggest close bonds — including same sex partnerships — showing that queer lives were part of everyday life across the Roman world.
tagline: In this talk, Dr Tatiana Ivleva from Newcastle University will examine Roman gravestones

title: National Trust Invites Public to Discover Hidden Histories at Festival of Archaeology 2026
subtitle: The festival provides opportunities for participants of all ages and experience levels — whether a seasoned archaeology enthusiast or someone discovering the subject for the first time.
bodyContent: The National Trust is calling on history lovers, families and curious explorers to take part in the UK’s largest archaeological celebration, the Festival of Archaeology 2026, running from 18 July to 2 August 2026 across a wide range of historic locations here in the South West. Organised in partnership with the Council for British Archaeology, the annual festival offers a nationwide programme of engaging events designed to bring the past to life. From hands-on excavations and interactive dig boxes to expert-led talks and guided walks, visitors will have the chance to uncover the stories hidden beneath some of the UK’s most treasured landscapes and heritage sites. With activities taking place at numerous National Trust properties, the festival provides opportunities for participants of all ages and experience levels — whether a seasoned archaeology enthusiast or someone discovering the subject for the first time. Find an Event Near You Prior Park, nr Bath, Somerset: Festival of Archaeology at Prior Park 18 July-2 August. 10am-5pm Information will be on display about previous digs in the Pasture, as will old finds from previous projects, including the dams project. On selected dates, a volunteer will be available to answer questions and discuss findings. You will be able to view a timeline of the last 33 years, since the National Trust acquired Prior Park, outlining its restoration and changes over the years. Walk the site and find interpretation on different areas of importance, such as the Bath House. There are also two pre-bookable guided walks with the lead archaeologist from previous digs, available to book on the walks' event page (22 & 28 July). Barrington Court, Somerset: Festival of Archaeology 2026 18 July-2 August. 10am-4pm Heritage Explorer Challenge Pick up a free trail sheet at Visitor Reception and see if you can complete this self-led heritage explorer challenge! Discover 6 archaeological features around the estate which help to tell Barrington Court's story. Whilst you are exploring, pop into Strode House to find the timeline of Barrington Court. This tells the story of the property from the Romans to the present day. Sand Tray Excavation Have a go at excavating through sand to find artefacts hidden in the sand trays. What will you find? Archaeology Tours 18,22,26,28 July & 1 August. 11.30am-12.30pm Join a volunteer-led tour to explore the archaeology of Barrington Court and learn about how the estate has developed over time in the context of the surrounding landscape. Dunster Castle, Somerset: Ground Penetrating Radar Survey 20-21 July. 10am-4pm Visitors can watch archaeologists carry out a live ground‑penetrating radar survey in the Keep Garden, searching for evidence of the original Norman castle. A ‘finds’ table will also showcase artefacts uncovered during last year’s survey of Green Court. Medieval Tours 3-5 & 10-12 July. 1-2pm & 2-3pm 1000 years of history… but every story has a beginning. Trace Dunster Castle’s origins from Norman stronghold to Civil War battleground. Further details of all events are available on the National Trust website

title: Caravan and Campsites
subtitle: You'll find a range of caravan and campsites set in the beautiful countryside of Taunton Deane from where you can traverse miles and miles of walking and cycling routes, explore local villages and towns, and visit nearby coastlines.
bodyContent: Ashe Farm Camping & Caravan Site is a quiet informal family-run caravan and camping site on part of a working farm situated near Taunton between the Quantock and Blackdown Hills. Ball Hill Farm is a lovely, unspoilt and ancient cider farm overlooking West Sedgemoor which offers 'rough' camping to ensure the lightest footprint possible. Cadeside Caravan Site is a Caravan and Motorhome Club site. It has 16 touring pitches and is surrounded by some of the most beautiful landscapes in Somerset with the Quantocks and Brendon Hills to the north and the Blackdown Hills to the south. Cornish Farm Touring Park offers luxury camping in the heart of Somerset, and is situated close to Taunton Racecourse. Greenacres Touring Park is located near Wellington with views of the Blackdown Hills and the Quantock Hills, and is exclusively for adults. Holly Bush Park is set in the heart of the glorious Blackdown Hills and offers both seasonal and touring pitches all year round, and is just a few yards from a traditonal country pub! Nunnington Park Farm Campsite is a small, friendly campsite situated on a working beef, sheep and arable farm that nestles at the foot of the Brendon Hills (open from Good Friday to 31st October). Quantock Camping is a small, rustic, family-run campsite with large pitches. It is nestled on the edge of the Quantock Hills, the first designated Area of Outstanding Beauty, and is just a walk along a scenic footpath to the local pub! Tanpits Farm Campsite is a camping and caravanning site on a historic, family-run Cider Farm which has been in the idyllic and peaceful surroundings of the Somerset countryside for over 100 years. Waterrow Touring Park is a beautiful caravan park and campsite to the east of Exmoor which is exclusively for adults, catering for caravans, motorhomes, campervans and trailer tents. Please note: Visit Taunton cannot accept any responsibility for matters arising between a customer and the accommodation provider. Visit Taunton does not accept liability for information on third party websites. This is not an exhaustive list.
tagline: Located in some of the beautiful Taunton Deane countryside

title: Coach House Collection- Feather Down
subtitle: The Coach House Collection is spread across 70 acres, with a big, beautiful forest of 30 acres and 30 acres of grazing for between 30 and 100 sheep. The Brue and Alham Rivers meet close by the house.
bodyContent: The Coach House Collection single log cabin fits up to 6 people and is located in a very pretty field with views towards the hills and a couple of deer living in the surrounding area. There is a nearby waterfall children can play in. Kingfishers, dippers and otters have been spotted playing in the clear river water too. Why not try fly fishing for brown trout and cook up a wonderful meal? Rods can be borrowed if you don’t have your own, and a temporary license can be bought on the spot at the local post office. Facilities include: A Double bed Cupboard bunk bed Mezzanine bed Flushing toilet En-suite bathroom with warm shower and basin Sofa Wood-fired stove for heating and cooking Barbecue And more!
tagline: The Coach House Collection is spread across 70 acres, with a big, beautiful forest

title: The Old Vicarage Hotel and Restaurant, Bridgwater, Somerset
subtitle: This unique and quirky hotel is a 10 minute drive from the main line station at Bridgwater or 24 minutes from M5 Junction 24 - so is close to all connecting services and local amenities and supermarkets.
bodyContent: “Looking for somewhere really special to stay, look no further you have found it”, “I don’t think I have ever been made to feel so welcome”, are just some of our recent 5-star reviews. This historic hotel has been lovingly renovated with bedrooms individually designed for complete relaxation and comfort. If you want to be spoilt, relax and eat delicious food visit Candy, Peter and their friendly, professional team whose mission to give every guest (and their dogs) the warmest of welcomes and most memorable stay. The Old Vicarage is tucked away in peaceful surroundings overlooking St Mary’s Church, the only building in Bridgwater older than it, yet is only 10 minutes from the M5. The hotel is full of historic importance dating back to 1327; it is said that Isambard Kingdom Brunel designed the town bridge in the 17th century Oak Room and Judge Jeffery’s stayed, one of the bedrooms even has its own wig cabinet. Each of the 18 en-suite bedrooms are individually designed and kept spotlessly clean with the most comfortable beds and views over the gardens or church. The south facing gardens are glorious, perfect for weddings and enjoying in the sunshine. On cooler evenings there is a cosy bar and snug with comfy sofas for enjoying a drink or two in front of the fire, an oak panelled restaurant and a brand new undercover patio with a pizza oven. A short drive and you can be alone on the Quantock Hills walking in Coleridge’s footsteps, bird watching on the Somerset Levels or hunting for fossils on the Jurassic Coast at Kilve. For the more energetic kayaking, coasteering, mountain biking, pony trekking are all on hand or if shopping is your thing Bristol, Bath, Taunton, Glastonbury and Wells are not far away. Book today for your perfect holiday.
tagline: “Looking for somewhere really special to stay, look no further you have found it”

title: The Old Ship Aground
subtitle: The Old Ship Aground, built in 1911 and formally known as The Pier Hotel.
bodyContent: Is an historic listed Edwardian pub located on the harbour in Minehead. With some of the best views in Minehead across the harbour to the Quantocks and Wales, the location is idyllic. We fell in love with her and bought back in May 2013. Since then we sorted the old girl out and refitted almost everything from top to bottom. Now with 12 new bedrooms offering a variety of single, double, twin and super king sizes there is a room for everyone, with all the little extras you’d expect – flat screen tv’s, tea, coffee & biscuits, bathroom sets and free wifi etc. We offer great old fashioned hospitality, and doing a good job of it, is very important to us. You don’t have to just take our word for it, please check out our reviews, both on Google and Trip Adviser. Food is a very big part of what we do, and here at The Old Ship Aground we love to cook and are proud of our reputation. Our menu is very much ‘River Cottage’ style. If we cannot grow it or raise it on the farm, you can be sure it is locally sourced and the very best of quality. From home-smoked foods (we have our very own smoker) to our own baked soda bread you won’t go hungry. With a pedigree of over 100 years of hospitality you are assured of a truly classic English Inn experience, with all the trimmings!

title: Dirty Bath
subtitle: In this adult only* evening of entertainment, the Natural Theatre Company invite you to join them on a voyage through Bath’s murkier waters as they throw a light on the less virtuous aspects of the city’s history.
bodyContent: The Natural Theatre Company are bringing their laugh out loud show ‘Dirty Bath’ to the Roman Baths Clore Learning Centre this summer. Meet long-gone historical figures, hear tales of villainy and debauchery, and witness plenty of silliness in this riotous journey through time. It won’t be plain sailing, but it will be very, very funny. This is a Natural Theatre Company event, performed in the Roman Baths Clore Learning Centre. Find out more about this performance on the Natural Theatre Company website. *Please note - This performance contains adult humour and is not suitable for children. Tickets £18 per person (18+ only). Two performances each day at 6pm and 8pm. subtitle: Driving lessons for 10-17 year olds in Somerset!
bodyContent: The Bath & West Showground is one of Young Driver’s 70 nationwide venues. Young Driver is the UK’s biggest and best under 17 driving school with over 75% of the under 17 driving market. We have just delivered our 1,500,000th driving lesson! Taking lessons with Young Driver before you turn 17 at the Bath & West Showground reduces the number of on-road lessons you will need later on, increases the chance of passing your test and most importantly makes you a safer driver. (Young Driver pupils have 80% less accidents when they take to the real roads). However, the best bit is that lessons are great fun and boost confidence for all of our pupils. At the Bath & West Showground we create roundabouts, junctions, parking zones and manoeuvring areas. Our cars are stylish, easy to drive and better for the environment. We have automatic cars fitted with hand controls available on every one of our days at the Bath & West Showground, which enable us to cater for local youngsters with a wide range of additional needs, from wheelchair users to those with neurodivergence. All of our professional driving instructors are approved by the government and specially trained to work with under 17s Lessons at The Bath & West Showground for 9 – 17 year olds start at £46.99 For more information on dates and availability, please visit www.youngdriver.com or call us on 0333 5779010.

title: Exploring Fossils
subtitle: Two more of our popular Fossil Thursdays this Summer on 6th and 20th August when we will be joined by the Earth Science Centre for fossil handling sessions, local geology and activities that celebrate the ancient Somerset landscape.
bodyContent: Two more of our popular Fossil Thursdays this Summer on 6th and 20th August when we will be joined by the Earth Science Centre for fossil handling sessions, local geology and activities that celebrate the ancient Somerset landscape. 200m years ago sea dragons lived, hunted and swam through the ancient seas which once covered Somerset. Giant marine reptiles called Ichthyosaurs called this place home, and their fossils were uncovered in the famous Blue Lias rock layer that runs under the shoe factories in Street all the way to the Jurassic Coast. Alfred Gillett, a member of the Clarks family and an avid collector of fossils is responsible for the specimens on display at Shoemakers Museum. May be you have found your own discoveries and would like to learn more about them? Or if you are interested in discovering more about our remarkable landscape – pop in and meet the team from the Somerset Earth Science Centre. This is a free pop-up exhibition for Shoemakers Museum ticket holders.
tagline: An opportunity to handle fossil and geology finds with members of Somerset's Earth Sciences Centre.

title: Exhibition: Paths Taken
subtitle: A summer exhibition exploring a selection of shoes from the stored collection and the curious and fascinating journeys that brought them into the archive
bodyContent: Ever wondered about the journeys objects take before they end up in museums? This six-week exhibition explores four different paths that brought some remarkable shoes to the collections at Shoemakers Museum. With examples of historic shoes found by archaeologists, shoes collected as souvenirs, keepsakes and mementos of people we have loved and reminders of nostalgic times and even some examples of concealed shoes a tradition of burying shoes within the walls of buildings for safety and superstition. The exhibition runs daily 10-4pm from 1 August until 13 September 2026. Interested in finding out more? the curators behind the museum will be presenting an illustrated talk at the museum on 14 August. Please booking in advance for this talk.

title: VAT's the Problem
subtitle: Please sign the petition
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"592"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"You’ve hopefully seen UKHospitality’s “VAT’s the Problem” campaign which was launched last week – the ask is simple – reduce VAT on Hospitality to 10%.
 
VAT, or Value Added Tax, is a tax added to most things you buy in the UK. That includes your meal at a restaurant, a pint at a pub, a coffee from your local café, or a stay away in a hotel when you take a break in the UK.
 
The UK has a 20% rate of VAT, which is one of the highest rates for hospitality in Europe. It’s the second highest, in fact. Only Denmark is higher.

Most of our international competitors have a much lower rate. In Germany, it’s as low as 7%. France, Italy and Spain have a 10% rate.
 
Lowering the rate of VAT for hospitality is the single most important thing the Government could do to support our local pubs, restaurants, cafes, accommodation providers and many more.
 
It would be a huge boost to the great British public, too.
 
The most immediate benefit is to support our pubs, restaurants, cafes, accommodation providers, bars, nightclubs, festivals and many more – so many of which are vital to our Guests experience of visiting the area where your Business is located.
 
A lower rate of VAT will reduce the cost pressures facing the sector, and it will mean more venues are able to stay open, rather than close the doors for good.
 
Sign the petition HERE.

title: South West Heritage Trust partners with the British Museum for once-in-a-generation Bayeux Tapestry experience
subtitle: Coins from the internationally significant Chew Valley Hoard will feature in this once-in-a-generation show.
bodyContent: South West Heritage Trust is delighted to be working in partnership with the British Museum on its landmark experience The Bayeux Tapestry . The experience opens on 10 September 2026, with tickets going on sale this week (from 1 July.) Coins from the internationally significant Chew Valley Hoard will feature in this once-in-a-generation show, which will see the 70-metre Bayeux Tapestry return to England for the first time in nearly 1,000 years. The Chew Valley Hoard project is supported by major funding from The National Lottery Heritage Fund and Art Fund. The British Museum’s experience will place the Tapestry within the wider story of the Norman Conquest, bringing together objects from its own collection alongside carefully selected loans from UK and European partners. Among these is the Chew Valley Hoard, a remarkable collection of silver pennies of Harold II and William I, loaned from the South West Heritage Trust and Somerset Council museum collection. Buried in Somerset shortly after the Norman Conquest, the hoard is believed to have been hidden for safekeeping during unrest in the south-west, including the 1068 rebellion that saw Exeter “fight for its liberty” before being suppressed by William. South West Heritage Trust Head of Development and Partnerships Dylan Edgar said: “We are thrilled to be part of the British Museum’s historic show. The Chew Valley Hoard provides a powerful insight into the immediate impact of the Conquest and will help to tell the story of this turning point in English history.” Councillor Federica Smith-Roberts, Somerset Council’s Lead Member for Communities, said: “This is wonderful and exciting news. Somerset is being honoured by being part of the British Museum’s show, sitting alongside the iconic Bayeux Tapestry. I hope it will encourage more people to see the hoard in London and when it returns to the Museum of Somerset.” The South West Heritage Trust is further part of The British Museum National Programme working with partners across the UK to ensure audiences across the country can engage with the story of the Bayeux Tapestry. 2027 also marks the 1,000th anniversary of the birth of William the Conqueror with the Trust participating in the European Year of the Normans commemorations. The Chew Valley Hoard was acquired by the South West Heritage Trust for the Somerset Council museum collection under the Treasure Act 1996 thanks to major funding from The National Lottery Heritage Fund. The acquisition was further supported by Art Fund and smaller but vital amounts of funding from South West Heritage Trust, Somerset Archaeological and Natural History Society and the Friends of the Museum of Somerset. The Bayeux Tapestry Experience is open 10 September 2026 to 11 July 2027 and has been made possible by the generous support of Igor Tulchinsky.

title: Cider Barrel Cottage
subtitle: Self catering cottage sleeping 4 in idyllic rural location but near to Cheddar Gorge, Somerset.
bodyContent: Sleeps 4 in twin and double rooms. Nestling under the Mendip Hills , surrounded by fields, Honeyhurst Farm abuts a country lane in an idyllic location on the village fringe between Wells and Cheddar , pub/restaurant 1 mile. The peaceful cottage is within a delightful half-acre part walled ‘National Garden Scheme’ garden with four-acre traditional working cider-orchard and babbling brook edging the Somerset Levels. The spacious ground floor stone cottage was formerly a cider store in bygone times and offers modern facilities, power shower over bath, electric cooking. A small conservatory opens onto a sun-terrace, with patio furniture and barbecue.

title: Double-Gate Farm
subtitle: Georgian farmhouse B&B accommodation with self catering converted barns in a peaceful location in Somerset, near Glastonbury & Wells.
bodyContent: Welcome to Double-Gate Farm, our Georgian farmhouse situated on the banks of the River Sheppey. Our farm offers views of the Mendip Hills and the surrounding countryside. Whether you're looking for a romantic getaway, a family vacation, or a group retreat, we have a variety of accommodations to choose from. Our converted barn is perfect for couples, families, and groups, while our accessible Riverside rooms and facilities cater to everyone's requirements. Our seasonal Tea Room is open from March to December and offers a range of delicious breakfasts, light lunches, home-baked cakes, and our speciality, Afternoon Tea. How about renting our BBQ Hut for a fun and sociable evening of cooking with your loved ones? Our Games Room is the perfect place to unwind after a long day of exploring. With a full-size snooker table, table-tennis, and lots of board games and local information, you'll never run out of things to do. At Double-Gate Farm, we pride ourselves on providing a peaceful and relaxing environment that allows you to unwind and enjoy nature. You can fish from your patio, watch the wildlife, or simply sit back and read. We welcome everyone, including cycling groups, walkers, and countryside lovers. Our location is perfect for exploring Somerset's hidden gems. With easy access to Glastonbury, Wells, and Cheddar, you'll be able to experience all that this beautiful region has to offer. We're also dog-friendly, so you don't have to leave your furry friend behind. Two of our Riverside rooms are pet-friendly, so please call us to check availability when booking with your dog. Finally, our farm is next door to a renowned gastropub that serves food and local brews. It's just a short walk away, so you don't have to worry about transportation. Come and experience the beauty of Double-Gate Farm for yourself.
tagline: Georgian farmhouse B&B accommodation with self catering converted barns

title: Glamping
subtitle: From yurts and safari tents to shepherd's huts and bunkhouses, you'll find plenty of glamping, or luxury camping, options in the beautiful countryside of Taunton Deane.
bodyContent: Set on a small working hill farm which is in the heart of the Brendon Hills, on the edge of Exmoor National Park, Chitcombe Farm Camping Barns offers two converted stone barns as camping barns (or bunkhouses). Kittisford Barton offers 5 safari tents which can accomodate up to 6 people each, 2 two-person hot tubs, country walks, patchwork scenery and tranquility. Lavender Hill Holidays is a collection of luxury, eco holiday properties near Exmoor National Park which includes two treehouses and a large Brake Van railway carriage. Middle Stone Farm is a working organic farm is on the edge of Exmoor National Park with ​6 safari tents, a cabin and stable conversion cottage, featuring private hot tubs, firepits, hammocks, barbecues and wood burning stoves. If you don't want the hassle of bringing your own tent or caravan, Quantock Camping also offers a pod and a tradional shepherd's hut, all in the stunning surrounds of the Quantock Hills. Somerset Yurts offers luxury glamping holidays in yurts which are located across three fields of a working dairy farm with far-reaching views over Taunton Vale to the Blackdown Hills in the distance. Please note: Visit Taunton cannot accept any responsibility for matters arising between a customer and the accommodation provider. Visit Taunton does not accept liability for information on third party websites. This is not an exhaustive list.
tagline: Explore the glamping, or luxury camping, options on offer in Taunton Deane

subtitle: A charming, privately-owned and family run hotel with a warm and welcoming atmosphere in Somerset.
bodyContent: The hotel has been thoughtfully refurbished combining traditional elements with modern comforts; blending flagstone floors with period colours and cosy couches to create a relaxed ambience. The Northover has 21 ensuite bedrooms, all of which are cleaned to a high standard and in line with current government guidelines and legislation. Whether you’re looking for a relaxing few days to explore Somerset or for somewhere to stop for a night on your journey to Cornwall, we are always happy to welcome you to the hotel. After your restful night’s sleep, we will invite you to our restaurant to enjoy a delicious Full English breakfast. title: Toghill House Farm
subtitle: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds. Within a stone’s throw of the site of the battle of Lansdown and with the Cotswold Way and the old east to west Roman road running through the grounds, Toghill is steeped in history.
bodyContent: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds. Within a stone’s throw of the site of the battle of Lansdown and with the Cotswold Way and the old east to west Roman road running through the grounds, Toghill is steeped in history. Located on a working farm only 4 miles north of Bath, with spectacular views over the Welsh mountains, Mendips, Cotswolds and Historic Bath, Toghill House is dog friendly, welcoming well-behaved pets. They have 9 rooms, some of which are in the 17th century farmhouse and others in the pretty Cotswold stone converted barns and stables in a delightful courtyard setting.

title: Hayseed Dixie
bodyContent: Hayseed Dixie was formed in the summer of 2000 on the front porch of a cabin in the Appalachian Mountains of East Tennessee, when after drinking enough whiskey to float a battleship across the Sahara Desert, it became suddenly obvious to the boys that the "Lost Highway" of Hank Williams and the "Highway To Hell" of AC/DC were the same damned road. The rest of the world first got a taste of the boys on April 17, 2001 with the release of their first album, titled "A Hillbilly Tribute To AC/DC". The band has since gone on to record 13 further albums containing both original songs and reinterpretations of previously known works, albeit in their own inimitable style. Having sold over half a million albums worldwide and having played more than 1,000 live shows on every continent except Antarctica, Hayseed Dixie are acknowledged as the creators of the musical genre "Rockgrass."

Opening on Monday 4th May, this exciting new area will give all adventurers the chance to jump straight into outdoor fun in the heart of one of Somerset’s best-loved annual events.
bodyContent: Mendip Activity Centre is launching something brand new at this year’s North Somerset Show: the Mendip Adventure Zone. Opening on Monday 4th May, this exciting new area will give all adventurers the chance to jump straight into outdoor fun in the heart of one of Somerset’s best-loved annual events. The Adventure Zone will feature 10 exciting activities to enjoy throughout the day, including Rock Climbing, Archery, Air Rifle, and Axe Throwing. For those seeking more high-energy action, visitors can also take part in ArcheryActive, Nerf and Gel Fire Battles, and Frisbee Golf, ideal for families and groups. The North Somerset Show is well known for its packed programme, including: livestock and horse showing, blacksmith competitions, craft stalls, and much more. This year, Mendip’s brand-new Adventure Zone adds an extra reason for families to make a day of it. Gates will be opening at 8:30am, free parking is available, and tickets are on sale in advance. title: Harry Baker Presents: Something Borrowed Ft myndstate and Special Guest
subtitle: Harry Baker can’t get enough of Bath, and hopes Bath isn’t fed up of him yet. After bringing his sellout tour show to the Komedia earlier in the year he is back for a very special live edition of his beloved podcast, Something Borrowed!
bodyContent: Following on from last year’s triumphant live recording with Hollie McNish and Vanessa Kisuule, Harry is thrilled to be back with some of his favourite poets on one of his favourite stages in front of his favourite people (that’s you). Featuring live performance and lovely chat, it promises to be very special indeed. World Poetry Slam Champion Harry Baker is a poet, a maths graduate, and a new father. His work has connected with millions online, from being shared on TED.com to making people cry through their TikTok and Instagram feeds, but he thinks it is even better in person. His latest collection Tender came out in March 2026 and was an instant Sunday Times Bestseller, accompanied by a 60-date tour all over the UK and Ireland. He lives and writes and swims and runs and takes his baby to nice coffee shops in Margate. myndstate is a spoken word artist, poet, & performer whose work centres around sexuality, identity, and mental health. His words - full of emotion, vulnerability, and rhyme - have made him a national poetry slam winner, got him featured on the likes of BBC Radio London & Sky Sports, plus have amassed millions of views online. He is currently working on his latest EP, as well as planning a UK-wide tour for his debut book which is set to release in November 2026.

title: Harry Brockway: Ways With Wood
subtitle: A new exhibition celebrating the life and work of Glastonbury based artist Harry Brockway.
bodyContent: ‘Ways with Wood’, is a major exhibition at Somerset Rural Life Museum celebrating the life and work of renowned Glastonbury-based artist Harry Brockway (1958–2024). Featuring an exceptional selection of his wood engravings, woodcuts and wooden sculpture, the exhibition offers a rich insight into the creativity, skill and craftsmanship that defined his distinguished artistic career. Harry Brockway was an exceptionally accomplished printmaker, sculptor, illustrator and stone carver. Alongside creating independent prints, he produced wood-engraved illustrations for a wide range of publishers – from major houses such as Penguin to specialist presses like The Folio Society. His work appears in celebrated editions of Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein and in texts by W. B. Yeats, Philip Pullman, Fyodor Dostoevsky, Samuel Taylor Coleridge and Mark Twain among others. Image credit: All rights reserved The Brockway Family, Harry Brockway, The Tor from Ten Acre Field, 2008. The museum is open Tuesday – Sunday, 10.00 am – 5.00 pm.
tagline: A new exhibition celebrating the life and work of Glastonbury based artist Harry Brockway.
