title: Edinburgh Preview: Li Jin Hao + Emmeline Downie
subtitle: Li Jin Hao Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer Nominee and Chortle Best Newcomer winner Li Jin Hao is a comedy writer and performer.
bodyContent: Li Jin Hao Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer Nominee and Chortle Best Newcomer winner Li Jin Hao is a comedy writer and performer. Jin Hao was made in China and marinated in Singapore, loved and feared for his dry wit, gritty softness, and surreal energy, he quickly became a Chortle Student Finalist, BBC New Comedy Awards Finalist, and was accepted into the Pleasance Comedy Reserve 2023. His debut solo show “Swimming in a Submarine” had a sell-out run at Edinburgh Fringe 2024 and earned him a nomination for Best Newcomer at the Edinburgh Comedy Awards, with a London run at the Soho Theatre for three weeks, before taking the show to the Melbourne International Comedy Festival. His TV appearances include Silence is Golden (Dave), Comedy Central Live (Comedy Central), The Stand Up Sketch Show (ITV2), and ITVX Presents: Live Comedy From the Edinburgh Fringe. Emmeline Donnie Emmeline Downie is a comedian, writer and actor performing across the UK comedy circuit. She co-created and starred in Edinburgh hits, Manhunt and Manhunt 2: Big Mood, earning critical acclaim; "brilliantly performed, beautifully written" - ThreeWeeks ★★★★★ In 2025, Emmeline appeared in Brainsluts at Pleasance Dome, recognised by The Guardian for a "stand-out performance". Her writing credits include an Untitled BBC Studios Comedy Writers' Room and additional material for Ania Magliano's Forgive Me, Father and Leo Reich's Literally Who Cares?!!! (A24). "A knockout" - The Stage ★★★★
tagline: Li Jin Hao Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer Nominee and Chortle Best

title: Escape into autumn: Events in Somerset from September to mid-November
subtitle: Across Somerset, National Trust places are full of warmth as the trees slowly turn to red, orange and gold.
bodyContent: https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset Across Somerset, National Trust places are full of warmth as the trees slowly turn to red, orange and gold. Enjoy crisp walks with family and friends and steaming mugs of hot chocolate. There’s lots on offer this season, fromtoddler storytelling sessions to guided tours, and craft workshops to Heritage Open Days. What’s more, every time you experience a National Trust day out, you help care for these special places for future generations. Here is what’s happening near you this autumn, please check property website for opening days and times: Barrington Court https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset/barrington-court Storytelling Mondays (Autumn Term) September-October. 11am-1pm Monday morning storytelling sessions for little ones starting at 11am and 12noon. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Heritage Open Days 2026: Free entry to Barrington Court 14-18 September. 10am-5pm Enjoy free entry to Barrington Court's beautiful garden & historic orchards, farm buildings, avenues and the ground floor of Strode House, where you can imagine what it was like as the Lyle's 1920s family home. Price: Free event. Booking not required. Wild Creatures Hide & Seek Trail (October Half Term) 24 October-1 November. 10am-4pm Grab your wellies and explore the grounds to find fifteen wild creatures hiding around the estate. How many will you spot? Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Wild Woodwork: Drop-in wood crafting workshops (October Half Term) 26-30 October. 10am-4pm Grab some gloves, get hands on with tools and create your own piece of natural art to take home, made of timber gathered from the estate and inspired by some of the wild creatures who roam the Somerset countryside at and around Barrington Court. Price: Check website for event price (normal admission applies). Booking not required. Remarkable Rangers: Apple Harvest Days (October Half Term) 26-30 October. 11am-3pm After last year's bumper crop, the Ranger team are waiting to see what this year's harvest will be like. Watch this space for further information about the apple harvest later in the year. Our orchards are home to well over 100 varieties of apples and once collected, they will go off to be turned into delicious cider. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Remarkable Rangers: Ranger Danger (October Half Term) 27 October. 11am-3pm Join the Ranger team for day of woodcraft in the Cricket Pitch woods. Learn how to make fire without matches and toast some yummy marshmallows. Price: £1 per child (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Coleridge Cottage https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset/coleridge-cottage Romantic Women Tour Every Wednesday, September-October. 12noon-1pm Join one of our volunteer tour guides and discover how the women in Samuel Taylor Coleridge’s life shaped his experiences and inspired his writing. Moving through the rooms of Coleridge Cottage, the tour brings hidden stories to light, including the resilience and resourcefulness of his wife Sara Fricker as well as his creative and intellectual friendship with Dorothy Wordsworth. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Nether Stowey Village Walk | Walks Programme Every Sunday of September. 1-2pm Meet at Coleridge Cottage and set off on this beginner walk around the charming village of Nether Stowey. From the home of Samuel Taylor Coleridge to St Mary's Church and a trip up to Castle Mount, this walk is the perfect introduction to Coleridge and the village that shaped his work. Price: Free event. Booking required. Stowey Surrounds | Walks Programme 10 September. 11am-2pm Connect with the landscape that inspired Coleridge's poetry and explore a landscape mix including close encounters with woodland and streams as well as open fields and vast panoramas with one our walk leaders. Price: Free event. Booking required. Wordsworth’s home to Coleridge Cottage| Walks Programme 30 September. 9.45am-2pm Join our walk leaders on a ramble between Kilve, Alfoxton and Nether Stowey. Take in the vast panoramic view, spot wildlife and connect with nature like Coleridge once did on his walk on the hills with his friends. Along the way, see where the Wordsworth’s lived during their time in the area and discover the path, they took on their way to Coleridge Cottage. Price: Free event. Booking required. Dunster Castle https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/somerset/dunster-castle-and-watermill Gilded Treasures Exhibition: 50 Years of the National Trust at Dunster Castle 1 September – 2 November. 10am-3.45pm Displayed throughout the castle, the exhibition highlights items featuring gilded decoration and golden detail. Alongside these objects, uncover the story of how Dunster Castle was generously gifted to the National Trust in 1976 by Lt. Col. Walter Luttrell, which included the estate and thirty acres of surrounding parkland. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Victorian Kitchen Tours (weekdays) Thursday & Fridays, September-October. Check website for timings. Where meals were made, stories were shared and servants kept the castle running. Head to the once state-of-the-art Victorian Kitchen with one of our knowledgeable tour guides and discover the heart of Victorian life at Dunster Castle. Price: £3pp (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Victorian Kitchen Tours (weekends) Every Saturday, September & October. 11am-12noon & 12noon-1pm Where meals were made, stories were shared and servants kept the castle running. Head to the once state-of-the-art Victorian Kitchen with one of our knowledgeable tour guides and discover the heart of Victorian life at Dunster Castle. Price: £3pp (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Behind-the-Ropes Tours (weekends) Every Saturday & Sunday, September – 1 November. Check website for timings. Embark on a new route, explore repurposed spaces and discover their history, all with the help of one of our brilliant volunteer guides. Venture into new areas from the butler's bedroom to the infamous 'creepy corridor', discover fascinating finds and gain an insight into the areas that allow us to do what we do. Price: £3pp (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Attic Tours (Weekends) Every Sunday, September – 1 November. 1.30-2.30pm & 2.30-3.30pm Discover hidden spaces, explore tucked‑away rooms and corridors, and learn about the daily lives of the servants who once called these upstairs spaces home. Exmoor Dark Skies: Stargazing Evening 21 October. 7-10pm Enjoy an evening of stargazing activities using telescopic equipment, laser guided star mapping, constellation story telling and much more. Take the opportunity to walk around the well-preserved, extravagant house, with its dark wood-panelled walls, fine period furnishings and grand bedrooms. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Monthly Markets at Lytes Cary Manor 12 & 13 September, 10 & 11 October. 10am-4pm Held in the historic barns and courtyard areas. The Lytes Cary market showcases a variety of products that have been crafted by local artists. Price: Free event (normal admission applies to visit the house, garden & tea-room). Booking not required. Guided Group Walk Every Wednesday, September – 21 October. 11am-12.30pm Join walk leaders to explore the Lytes Cary Estate countryside and enjoy the natural landscape. Price: Free event (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Heritage Open Days – Free Entry to Lytes Cary Manor 14-18 September. 10am-4.30pm Come and discover the historic manor house, enjoy a light lunch in the café courtyard, stroll around the formal garden or explore one of the wider estate walks. Price: Free event. Booking not required. Lytes Scary Halloween Trail 24 Oct -1 Nov. 10am-3.30pm Put your wellies on and come on a spooky adventure. Can you crack the riddle? Are you brave enough to take part? Price: £3.50 per trail (normal admissions apply). Booking not required. Christmas Market at Lytes Cary Manor 14 & 15 November. 10am-3pm Join us for some festive cheer and find those unique Christmas gifts. Held in the historic barns and courtyard areas. The Lytes Cary market showcases a variety of products that have been crafted by local artists. Price: Free event. Booking not required. Prior Park https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/bath-bristol/prior-park-landscape-garden Garden Yogis at Prior Park 12 September. 9.30-10.30 Start the weekend with an outdoors yoga class - mats next to the lake and iconic bridge in this beautiful National Trust garden. Price: £6pp. Booking not required. Jane Austen Festival: Take a turn around Prior Park 11-20 September. 10am-5pm Take a turn around the garden to discover a number of quotes from Jane Austen’s stories. Can you work out who said it? subtitle: Diamond Farm Holiday Park in Brean, Somerset is on our family working farm.
bodyContent: Diamond Farm Holiday Park is situated on our 100-acre family working farm, ideally situated for the quiet family holiday, and it is only 3⁄4 mile from the 7 miles of sandy beach at Brean. On our site, you will find level and generous-sized pitches with car parking spaces alongside your caravan or tent. Countryside views are assured, and each pitch is within a short distance of the site facilities. All modern facilities including toilets, showers, electric hook-up, play area, shop, café, wifi and laundry. River fishing on site. Holiday cottages are also for hire.
tagline: Diamond Farm Holiday Park in Brean, Somerset is on our family working farm.

title: The Yarn Market Hotel
subtitle: Ideally located in the centre of the medieval village of Dunster. The hotel is two and half hours via the A39 from the M5 - but is ten minutes away from the West Somerset Railway England's longest heritage railway. With Minehead 20 minutes away there are all the major facilities you need.
bodyContent: The Yarn Market Hotel in Dunster is ideally located in the centre of Dunster, one of the most perfectly preserved medieval villages in England, and the gateway to Exmoor National Park. The magnificent Dunster Castle is at the end of the street and the West Somerset Railway runs close by. There are many themed breaks on offer throughout the year, and the area is perfect for those who enjoy outdoor activities or just a relaxing break. For walkers the hotel has excellent facilities including a boot and drying room, and maps are readily available combined with local knowledge to help you with your walks. Most of the bedrooms have either a view over the village or the surrounding countryside. Pets are most welcome at the hotel in the dog-friendly rooms. The restaurant opens daily for dinner, reservations are advisable.
tagline: Our Hotel is situated in the beautiful Village of Dunster, within the Exmoor National Park.

title: Circle Luxury Stays
subtitle: Your comfort is our highest priority. You are warmly invited to enjoy your stay in Bath, in one of the three luxury self-catering accommodation options.
bodyContent: Choose from a charming two-bedroom lodge house, or superb two or one bedroom self-catering apartments; perfect for a friends or family get-together to discover Bath and beyond. All of our holiday let properties are within 10 minutes’ walk of the centre of Bath, and are available for both short and extended stays. For total peace of mind, read more about our commitment to COVID secure accommodation here . If you’re looking for the ultimate luxury home for a special holiday, the Water Tower makes a wonderful base for those wanting to explore Devon’s Jurassic coastline.

title: Hunters Lodge Hotel
subtitle: Welcome to the Hunters Lodge Hotel.
bodyContent: 14 en-suite rooms all furnished to the highest standard, with large LCD TVs, free WIFI, tea / coffee making, iron and iron board and a host of complimentary items. Take a pick of doubles, family rooms or stay in the Meadow Vale suite, a luxurious four-poster room for an extra special evening. Oh, did we tell you that all our beds are King Size! Hairdryer Towel radiator Large, wall mounted LCD TV Tea and coffee making Ironing board and iron WIFI and wired inernet access Faxing

title: Vellum Stone Cottage
subtitle: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway.
bodyContent: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway – indoor pool and games room on site, Kennet and Avon Canal close by (3/4 of a mile), with walking and cycling options right on your doorstep. Farm Shop and country pub(s) within walking distance. The cottage features a country feel with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams, with matching soft furnishings. Enjoy admiring the sheep in the fields surrounding the farm, with the cottage being dog friendly.

title: Sunday Riffs and Roasts at the Bath Brew House
subtitle: Every Sunday, Roasts served 12pm-8pm Join us for a hearty roast, relax and enjoy our live music from 6pm!
bodyContent: Welcome to The Bath Brew House. Serving up the freshest beers in Bath since 2013. Whether you’re a beer fanatic, after some classic pub grub, or just looking to soak up some sun in a colourful beer garden – we’re the place to be!
tagline: Every Sunday, Roasts served 12pm-8pm

title: The Secret Escape
subtitle: A chic and cosy, quiet hideaway in Central Bath for 2. Ideal location for all restaurants and attractions.
bodyContent: Situated in the centre of the beautiful Georgian City of Bath but hidden away behind the bustling streets, this one bedroom, boutique flat offers a secret escape with added luxury. Newly renovated to a very high standard and offering a kitchen/sitting room, with breakfast bar, 32″ smart television and a small balcony with table and chairs for that all important morning coffee or sundowner! The bedroom is on the lower floor and has a king sized bed, dressing area, an ensuite shower room and a 22″ smart television. There is a door out to another exterior sitting area, with yet another table and chairs. There is one residents parking permit available, gold dust in the centre of the city! Our Secret Escape in Bath is perfect for city based holidays and short breaks.
tagline: A chic and cosy, quiet hideaway in Central Bath for 2.

title: Vox Lumiere Metropolis
bodyContent: Vox Lumiere shatters the boundaries between concert hall and cinema. Award-winning Vox Lumiere transforms Fritz Lang’s iconic 1927 silent masterpiece Metropolis into an explosive live experience with live band, thrilling original new music and powerhouse vocals. It's a rock concert, theatrical event, and cinematic journey rolled into one. 'Absolutely riveting!' The Los Angeles Times 'Vox Lumiere joins Cirque du Soleil and Stomp as a one-of-a-kind theatrical experience audiences crave!' Daily Breeze 'A multidimensional hi-decibel blast of visual and auditory splendor!' The Dallas Morning News 'Silent film with musicians, singers and dancers performing along with it. How friggin’ cool is that?' Phillylist.com

title: Party in the City
subtitle: You’re invited to join Bath’s biggest FREE party as the city centre bursts into life for one night only.
bodyContent: Join the fun and follow the Party in the City trail from park to pub, from church to museum, to hear the best from the local creative scene. Line up: The Sway Five piece from Liverpool taking elements of the Mersey sound and moulding it into their own, catchy melodies, pulsing choruses and introspective lyricism . The band have enjoyed slots across the UK including Glastonbury Festival, Ynot, Truck and more. Having sold out hometown shows in iconic venues such as the 02 Academy and Arts Club theatre recently their grassroots built following is looking to spread across the UK. Taynee Lord Among the clang of electric guitars, prepare yourself for high octane country twang as Taynee Lord gives you music for sunsets and highways. Nothing Rhymes with Orange A Bristol-based Indie Rock band tearing up the scene with raw, chaotic energy and fiery performances. Shrink Shrink are bottled and ready to explode. Frontman Will Coomes speaks his truths over a balance of chaos – silent conversation turned up loud. Bellyful A Neo-Trip-Hop duo originating from Bath/Bristol. Weaving dark Hip Hop beats between lush synths and hypnotic vocals, Bellyful is an atmospheric experience. Duo Fin Roach (producer, keys, guitar) and Lily Rainbow (vocalist, bassist) take the sound of 90s Bristol into a new era of modern unease.

title: Emma Doran – Emmaculate
subtitle: Smash hit Irish comedian, best-selling author, podcast host and viral online star Emma Doran hits the road once again taking her brand-new stand-up show Emmaculate across the UK and Ireland in 2025/26/27.
bodyContent: There's no such thing as a perfect family, but she wouldn't want one anyway... The many trials and tribulations of Emma’s blended family are laid bare, womanhood examined, and relationships put to the test in this witty, rambunctious show from one of Ireland’s most beloved stand-ups. Strap in for a night to remember, jam-packed with razor-sharp observations, riotous on-stage antics and conspiratorial gossipmongering. As seen and heard on No Worries If Not! (RTÉ 2), The Tommy Tiernan Show (RTÉ 1), LOL: Last One Laughing (Prime Video) hosted by Graham Norton, The Late Late Show (RTÉ), Celebrity Gogglebox (Virgin Media One), Modern Love (Prime Video) alongside Kit Harington, The Deirdre O’Kane Show (SKY), Bridget and Eamon (RTÉ), Callan Kicks (RTÉ), Republic Of Telly (RTÉ) and Irelands Fittest Family (RTÉ), while her podcast credits include: You’re Grounded with daughter Ella, And Another Thing! with Muireann O’ Connell and the four-part series Mischief Makers. Emma currently co-hosts the podcast Keep It Tight alongside fellow stand-up and LOL: Last One Laughing contestant Deirdre O’Kane. Emma is also author of best-selling book, Mad, Isn’t It? (published in 2024). “End-to-end laughs… you’d be mad to miss her” - Bruce Dessau, Evening Standard ★★★★ “Wickedly funny” - Brian Logan, The Guardian "Uproariously funny... a fiercely accomplished and fully formed talent" - Jay Richardson, The Reviews Hub ★★★★ “One of the funniest humans I’ve ever encountered” - Joanne McNally “A legend… one of the greats” - Brett Goldstein

title: Family Trail: Motte & Bailey Investigate the Viking Raid on Watchet Mint
subtitle: Come and see Dunster's rare double overshot watermill in action with a day of milling, demos, talks and more to celebrate National Mills Weeken
bodyContent: Detective duo, Motte & Bailey, have travelled back in time to the 10th Century. Vikings have raided the Royal Mint in the nearby harbour town of Watchet and stolen some Saxon silver coins. The Vikings have hidden the coins in the castle grounds for safe keeping until they board their longships at sea. Can you help Motte & Bailey recover the coins and return them to the Royal Mint? Follow the trail, crack the clues and take part in hands‑on activities as you learn all about the Vikings & Saxons! Complete the trail to claim your collectable Motte & Bailey Viking Badge. This event runs daily from Saturday 23rd May until Sunday 12th July. £3.50 per trail per person (includes prize).
tagline: Detective duo, Motte & Bailey, have travelled back in time to the 10th Century

title: Edinburgh Preview: Li Jin Hao + Emmeline Downie
subtitle: Li Jin Hao Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer Nominee and Chortle Best Newcomer winner Li Jin Hao is a comedy writer and performer.
bodyContent: Li Jin Hao Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer Nominee and Chortle Best Newcomer winner Li Jin Hao is a comedy writer and performer. Jin Hao was made in China and marinated in Singapore, loved and feared for his dry wit, gritty softness, and surreal energy, he quickly became a Chortle Student Finalist, BBC New Comedy Awards Finalist, and was accepted into the Pleasance Comedy Reserve 2023. His debut solo show “Swimming in a Submarine” had a sell-out run at Edinburgh Fringe 2024 and earned him a nomination for Best Newcomer at the Edinburgh Comedy Awards, with a London run at the Soho Theatre for three weeks, before taking the show to the Melbourne International Comedy Festival. His TV appearances include Silence is Golden (Dave), Comedy Central Live (Comedy Central), The Stand Up Sketch Show (ITV2), and ITVX Presents: Live Comedy From the Edinburgh Fringe. Emmeline Donnie Emmeline Downie is a comedian, writer and actor performing across the UK comedy circuit. She co-created and starred in Edinburgh hits, Manhunt and Manhunt 2: Big Mood, earning critical acclaim; "brilliantly performed, beautifully written" - ThreeWeeks ★★★★★ In 2025, Emmeline appeared in Brainsluts at Pleasance Dome, recognised by The Guardian for a "stand-out performance". Her writing credits include an Untitled BBC Studios Comedy Writers' Room and additional material for Ania Magliano's Forgive Me, Father and Leo Reich's Literally Who Cares?!!! (A24). "A knockout" - The Stage ★★★★
tagline: Li Jin Hao Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer Nominee and Chortle Best

title: Monochrome + Override + Slighted Hand
subtitle: Join Monochrome, Override, and Slighted Hand for an energetic evening of alternative music - part of our summer series of free, or pay-what-you-can, Electric Bar shows.
bodyContent: Monochrome: Since forming, Monochrome's force within the metal sphere of the Southwest has been unstoppable and irreplaceable. Brutality and beauty coexist in a distinct blend of crushing metal and ethereal layering, weaving a sound that is as heavy as it is haunting. Their debut EP, Haunted Faith and Hidden Trust, has introduced the world to their deep, dark sound, backed by a sold-out release show. The E.P. challenges listeners’ expectations and pushes the elements of the music to the absolute extreme, striking a unique balance between the past, present, and future of metal. 2025 was a triumphant year for Monochrome: they completed a national tour supporting Apathy UK, were picked up as newcomers at Bloodstock and Hammerdown Festival, and released their debut EP. 2026 will see Monochrome expand on their already distinct sound, delving further into the contrasting elements that make them special. Override: Override is a 3-piece heavy beat-down hardcore band from the Southwest, currently playing shows while working on an upcoming EP. Expect closed-fist mosh hardcore. FFO: Sanction, Long Goodbye, and Final Resting Place. Slighted Hand: Hailing from South Wales, Slighted Hand is an evil hardcore band.

title: Football Fun, Tennis and Racing Cars at Clarks Village Summer of Sport
subtitle: The Somerset shopping outlet will host football-themed games and live tennis screenings with prizes for guests to enjoy.
bodyContent: Clarks Village is bringing the excitement of a summer of sport into its gardens with three interactive zones celebrating the World Cup, Wimbledon and Formula 1. The Somerset shopping outlet will host football-themed games and live tennis screenings with prizes for guests to enjoy. To mark the World Cup, a giant inflatable football goal and touch wall from top sporting brand Pro Direct will take centre stage. Every weekend until the World Cup final, guests can test their skills by scoring a goal to earn their turn on a ‘Spin to Win’ wheel, with prizes including Pro Direct gift vouchers, footballs and in-store discounts. The football fun continues with ‘Subsoccer’ bench football stations – which pits two players against each other in a competitive seated football match – alongside a life-sized football selfie cut-out for the perfect photo opportunity to mark the occasion. The football goal and touch wall prize-winning activities will be hosted on Saturdays and Sundays until 19 th July, with additional activities available daily. Meanwhile, tennis enthusiasts can take a break to enjoy the highlights of Wimbledon, from Monday 29 th June to Sunday 12 th July, with a dedicated station featuring comfortable loungers with built-in mini televisions to screen live matches. Adding to the traditional courtside atmosphere, British homeware brand Christy will serve strawberries and cream outside its new store, as well as showcasing its official Wimbledon collection of Championship towels and elegant robes. Guests can also take part in a daily treasure hunt for the duration of the tournament, by finding one of 10 hidden tennis balls each day to win a free gift at the Christy store. Christy will also be serving branded ice creams from a gelato cart on Saturday 4 th and Saturday 11 th July, from 12pm-5pm. Finally, throughout August, Clarks Village will host Lightning Loop; a mini race-track experience located on the lawn of Shoemakers Museum. Children aged 4-10 will be able to ride mini, interactive F1 race cars around an inflatable racetrack, featuring a starting grid, finish line, chequered flag, winners podium and an oversized trophy for an all-important photo on finishing. The racetrack and cars will be branded bright orange in tribute to F1 racing driver Lando Norris who hails from Somerset. This is Clarks Village's second tribute to Norris, after officially renaming one of its pedestrianised avenues ‘Lando Lane’ when he became F1 World Champion. Lightning Loop tickets will be priced at £8, or £6 for PLUS+ members (Clarks Village’s free rewards programme). Mike Jones, Centre Director of Clarks Village, commented: “We’re looking forward to bringing the magic of the World Cup, Wimbledon and Formula 1 to life with these fun brand activations. Set within our beautiful, landscaped gardens, it’s the perfect spot to join in the fun of our football games or relax in our Wimbledon loungers to celebrate a summer of sport, as well as a visit to our infamous Lando Lane during the summer holidays for our brand-new racing car experience.” Clarks Village is located in Street, less than 25 minutes from the M5 and A303, with a stellar line-up of more than 90 brands from designer names and high street favourites offering up to 60% off RRP alongside late-night dining. For more details about what’s on at Clarks Village in addition to opening hours and how to join its free member rewards scheme PLUS+, visit https://www.clarksvillage.co.uk Footbal

title: Dimpsey Glamping
subtitle: Dimpsey offers 5* glamping in luxury two Blackdown Shepherd Huts based in Somerset. An idyllic space to get away from it all in style - a total retreat. We set out to create an inspiring stay place where you can see great places, eat great food and relax...
bodyContent: Hi, we’re Andrew and Emma, and together with our family, we live on a small farm estate on the Blackdown Hills in Somerset, which we’d love to share with you. Listed in the Domesday book, it’s an historic place, so that’s partly why we chose Shepherd Huts for our glamping business – as it combines heritage with luxury. You can expect a private getaway location with en-suite facilities and a full-sized double bed – plus a wood-fired hot tub, garden oven and firepit. We are perfectly located for walking on the Blackdown Hills and with Lyme Regis and the Jurassic Coast just 30 minutes drive away, you can hideaway or venture out – the choice is yours… Every now and again, you hear a word that rouses your curiosity because you haven’t heard it before – and Dimpsey as our brand name started from an occasion just like that. Cue a bit of google research and it turns out that it’s a West Country term for the half-light that comes at the end of the day, so twilight or dusk – we loved the word and so we had our brand name. What are the Dimpsey Shepherd’s Huts all about? We set out to create an inspiring, luxury stay place where you can see great places, eat great food, find cool stuff and chill out, so… We aim to provide a high-end stay experience in a field with all needs catered for and a concierge style recommendation service. When you stay with us at Dimpsey, the choice to stay in or go out and explore the area is yours – we’ll just help you see the very best that the South West has to offer. In keeping with the country name and the Shepherd’s Hut heritage – we source vintage and UK artisan made pieces – using natural materials like wool, leather, stone, and wood. We like to introduce people to the Somerset countryside and a little slice of farm life – closeness to nature is important. We search out handmade products and things you may not have come across before – things like magazines and books etc We create a space for you to just be, so we have no wi-fi, wood-fired cooking and hot-tub and a slow-boiling whistling kettle. So whether you’re escaping for a retreat, want to have some time as a couple or just need to relax – Dimpsey is the stay for you. We’re inspired by the Mandarin Oriental Mantra – “Luxury is achieved when service is intuitive and goes beyond obligation”. Facilities Woodfired hottub, en-suite bathrooms, woodfired outdoor kitchen
tagline: Dimpsey offers 5* glamping in luxury two Blackdown Shepherd Huts based in Somerset

title: John Fowler Holiday Parks
subtitle: Here at John Fowler Holiday Parks, we want to provide you with the very best family UK break that we can. Established for over 60 years!
bodyContent: Here at John Fowler Holiday Parks, we want to provide you with the very best family UK break that we can. Established for over 60 years, every year thousands of people trust us with their family holidays in the UK and every year we try to make that experience better than ever! We’ve invested millions of pounds to achieve that with new and upgraded lodges , caravans and chalets, new facillities and activities for you to enjoy plus an action packed entertainment programme. We've also added to our line up of themed weekends to bring you some unforgetable experiences. Plus we’ve held prices across many dates and parks so you’ve got more money left in your pocket for that extra little bit of holiday fun! With 11 amazing Holiday Parks in fantastic locations you’ll be amazed at how easy they are to reach. From Devon to Cornwall to Somerset, there’s loads to do and see. So why not book in a flash today and start painting those magical memories...... The choice is yours When you book your holiday or short break with John Fowler Holidays, you can rest assured you are getting a fantastic range of accommodation choices at the very best value price. From caravans to lodges, chalets, bungalows, cottages, houses and apartments. We also have lodges with hot tubs available at two of our sites for that special treat. So whatever you’re looking for, there’s sure to be something to suit you. We want to make your self catering holidays in the UK as relaxing as possible and that means feeling at home from the moment you step through the door. In our 60 plus years, we have learnt that there is nothing as ‘one size fits all’ which is why we have holiday homes that sleep from 2 to14. We grade our accommodation from top of the range platinum for extra luxury through to our value range so that our holidays are affordable for everyone. The grading is indicative of the age and recency of refurbishment of the unit. Sandy Glade Our Sandy Glade Holiday Park in Burnham-on-Sea in Somerset boasts plenty of open, green space for the kids to run free, a fantastic indoor pool with water jets and fountains and an adventure playground so they can let off steam while you relax. In the evenings take a trip to our clubhouse for fun and games and a great entertainment line up. A hop, skip and a jump across the road and its through the dunes onto a long expanse of golden beach where you can feel the sand between your toes and enjoy a 99 ice cream for that perfect UK seaside holiday experience. Just a short drive from the park are the bright lights of the fun fair at Brean Leisure Park, whizz yourself dizzy on the Waltzers, send your tummy tumbling on the Roller Coaster or bump and bash on the Dodgems. title: The Halfway House Inn
subtitle: The Halfway House Inn / Hotel Yeovil / Ilchester is a Pet Friendly Country Lodge with disabled Accommodation, A Fishing Lake Available for Guests to Fish Free. In the heart of the West Country.
bodyContent: A West Country Free House, The Halfway House Inn Country Lodge offers excellent bed and breakfast accommodation, that is pet friendly ( £7.50 Charge ) & includes a cooked to order breakfast. We are also ideal for Wedding Receptions, and Conference venue. We are very well situated for both business visitors and tourists in search of hotel accommodation in Somerset. Located just 1.5 miles from Yeovil, or Ilchester and Yeovilton and set among beautiful countryside surroundings. We offer guests a hotel bar, Dining room, & Menu with delicious fresh local produce and a beer garden with views over our fishing lake witch is free to fish to all guests. We have 19 comfortably furnished en suite rooms available including a beautiful Bridal Suite with a stunning four poster bed, a disabled friendly lodge and several family rooms, including 3 cottage style lodges with split level bedrooms. All rooms have TV, tea and coffee making facilities and free Wireless Internet. Well behaved pets are welcome by prior arrangement.

bodyContent: Welcome to The Bath Brew House. Serving up the freshest beers in Bath since 2013. Whether you’re a beer fanatic, after some classic pub grub, or just looking to soak up some sun in a colourful beer garden – we’re the place to be!

title: The Post House
subtitle: A beautifully restored Grade II Listed former village Bakery. The property has been restored with great sensitivity to be sure to retain the atmosphere of this 350 year old building.
bodyContent: Luxury self catering accommodation, situated on the Mendip Hills. 20 minutes from the City of Bath, this is the perfect location to explore this beautiful part of Somerset. Sleeping up to 13 guests in 5 bedrooms. Perfect for pampering weekends or for families. Please see the floorplans to help organise your visit. This beautifully restored, 400 year old, former village Post Office and Bakery is simply stunning. You won’t find another quite like it! All traditional methods have been used in the restoration and finished in light grey hues of lime wash to create a relaxed and stylish feel. Each living area opens up to another creating a feeling of space and tranquility. The original flag stone floor and large open fireplace in the sitting room offers a wonderful space to chill out and relax in front of Sky television! The stunning Dining Hall in the former bakery is a great place to organise a dinner party. In addition there is a Morning Room with open log fire and fully equipped Kitchen. The Mediterranean Courtyard is a perfect place to enjoy breakfast in the Summer or a sundowner. Please do see details of our other properties – The Town House , sleeping up to 12 guests and The Secret Escape for 2 guests.
tagline: A beautifully restored Grade II Listed former village Bakery

title: Bodhi House
subtitle: Situated just over a mile from the centre of Bath, Bodhi House provides spacious, stylish accommodation slightly removed from the hustle and bustle of the centre.
bodyContent: Situated just over a mile from the centre of Bath, Bodhi House provides spacious, stylish accommodation slightly removed from the hustle and bustle of the centre. With commanding views over the city, the light and modern accommodation offers high levels of comfort and features furnishings and materials of the highest quality. Organic, local produce is served whenever possible. Bodhi House offers off-street parking if required, and a garden with views of the City of Bath and beyond. title: The Wanted 2.0  - Glad You Came Tour
subtitle: Get ready for… The Wanted 2.0.
bodyContent: The next chapter in the history of one of Britain’s biggest ever pop bands, who are ready to take to the stage with their explosive energy and chart-topping anthems. Founding members Max George and Siva Kaneswaren now carry the torch as ‘The Wanted 2.0’, the definitive place to hear all the global smash hits by this powerhouse UK band. With over 20 million record sales worldwide, The Wanted notched up 10 UK Top Ten singles and 2 UK Number 1 singles. The band still boast almost 7 million monthly listeners on Spotify and have a huge worldwide following. The band’s catalogue contains pop masterpieces that defined an era, including the Number 1 Singles ‘All Time Low’ and ‘Glad You Came’, alongside fan-favourites like ‘Chasing The Sun’, ‘Walks Like Rihanna’, and the electrifying ‘Warzone’.

title: FREESOME
subtitle: Freesome – Celebrating the Timeless Rock of Free and Bad Company
bodyContent: Freesome is a passionate and powerful tribute to the legendary British rock bands Free and Bad Company. Delivering a dynamic two-hour set packed with classic hits and deeper cuts, the band captures the raw soul, bluesy swagger, and arena-sized energy that defined these iconic acts. Audiences can expect authentic, high-energy performances of anthems like All Right Now, Wishing Well, Feel Like Makin’ Love, Shooting Star, and many more, all played with the respect and fire these songs deserve. The members of Freesome are no strangers to the South West music scene. With years of live experience and a deep love for classic rock, Freesome brings a show that’s as faithful as it is fiery; a must-see for fans of 70s British blues-rock at its finest.
tagline: Freesome – Celebrating the Timeless Rock of Free and Bad Company

title: Hugh Cornwell
subtitle: An intimate evening of songs and stories, plus an open Q&A session.
bodyContent: As the lead singer and songwriter of The Stranglers during their golden period, Hugh Cornwell cast a spell by mixing fact, history, mythology and ideology within the lyrics of his songs. It was a heady mix that lead to the band's success around the world, with The Stranglers championed for balancing experimentation and commerciality in equal measure. Hugh was responsible for many of the band's most memorable songs across ten stellar albums, consolidating his stature as a unique songwriter and musician. His lyrics to Golden Brown are a songwriting masterclass. His solo career has produced ten albums of critically acclaimed songs, culminating in Moments of Madness, described as a "later-flowering classic" and "a modern-day masterpiece." Hugh last performed an acoustic solo show in the UK in 2017 and will be heading out across the country again this November 2026. Alongside dipping in both The Stranglers' catalogue and his own extensive body of work, he will also perform new songs from his next studio album, Succubus the follow up to Moments of Madness. These songs will be heard for the first time on his tour. There will also be an open Q&A segment during the show, giving the audience the chance to ask Hugh questions directly. "I'm not sure how much longer I can continue to perform, so this will be my final solo acoustic tour." Hugh Cornwell Take this opportunity to experience the legendary acoustic live performance of one of the UK's greatest living songwriters while you can. Just Hugh,

title: The Bishop's Palace Garden Fete
subtitle: Enjoy a classic English summer day out at The Bishop’s Palace in Wells, Somerset, as the popular Garden Fete returns to the beautiful surroundings of our 14 acres of RHS partner gardens.
bodyContent: Set against the backdrop of our 800-year-old medieval Palace, this family-friendly event brings together live music, a Craft and Produce Competition (in association with the WI), artisan stalls, traditional games and hands-on activities. With so much to see and do, it is the perfect summer event in Somerset for visitors of all ages. Here’s what to expect (full details on our website): - Craft & Produce Competition in partnership with Wells Tuesday WI (visit our website for more info) - Petting Farm with Puxton Park - Dog Show with Pawsability - Bushcraft - Big Bloomers Walkabout Show - Angie Mack Hula Hoop Show Artisan Stalls and local makers: Browse 50+ artisan stalls in the Palace and on the croquet lawn featuring local crafts, gifts and artisan produce, celebrating the best of Somerset’s independent businesses. Meet the Gardeners: You’ll have a chance to meet the Palace’s Gardening Team and find out more about how our stunning 14 acres of RHS partner gardens are created and maintained. Live music and entertainment: Relax and enjoy live performances from Saxkatz, a North Somerset saxophone quartet, playing a mixture of popular classics and jazz standards throughout the day. Food and Drink: Enjoy seasonal refreshments, including delicious options from the Bishop’s Table café and our visiting stallholders. Admission: - Friends of the Palace: FREE - Adult: £16 - Child (5-17): £8 - Family (2 x adults/2 x children): £42 family Buy Tickets Here: https://bit.ly/48qhBKB

title: Royal Clarence Hotel
subtitle: The No.1 Hotel in Burnham-on-Sea
bodyContent: The Royal Clarence Hotel in Burnham On Sea has been under new ownership since January 2020; we have already upgraded the WiFi, increased the size of the bath towels, added bath mats and extra hand towels, doubled the pillows to 2 per person in every room, replaced and fixed several showers, put the heating on longer, fixed the front door and several windows, and now we are starting to decorate the communal areas. During April, May and June 2020 we have taken the opportunity to decorate all the hallways. With its premier seafront location and great value rates, The Royal Clarence Hotel is the ideal place for your seaside break. The property is the only Hotel located on the seafront in Burnham-on-Sea and it's also just a few yards from the Town Centre and over 100 mostly independent shops, cafes, takeaways, restaurants, pubs and clubs. Within a very short walk there is a 3-screen cinema showing the latest releases, an indoor swimming pool and the Princess Theatre is nearby too. Guests can choose from a range of room options to suit most pockets. Even if the budget doesn't stretch to a sea view room, guests can relax in our enclosed glass-fronted veranda and enjoy the great views across Bridgwater Bay toward the North Devon and Welsh coastlines. Our sunsets are stunning. Whether you are staying for one night or one week, we will greet you with a friendly smile and a warm welcome.

bodyContent: Situated right in the heart of Bath, The Cork boasts two bars, two vaulted party pod booths, a conservatory and a very large alfresco terrace area. You won’t find a better pub in which to socialise, relax, watch live sport or have a full-on party! A full, varied range of wines, cocktails, hot beverages, real ales, cider, craft beers, plus an extensive list of whiskies, Bourbons and rums really makes The Cork one of the best pubs to visit in Bath. We are proud to have been accredited by Cask Marque, an award given to pubs serving great cask ale. Our Karaoke pod rooms come fully loaded with your own TV and karaoke system – perfect for a big night out or a big match. One pod is ideal for up to 8 people, the other up to 12. Please use the form below to book online.

bodyContent: Lil Wenker: BOYKING (WIP) ALL HAIL BOYKING! Eight-year-old Prince Wilfred (“Willy” for short) seeks power at all costs including but not limited to: death, destruction & dastardly deeds. Nowhere near in line for the throne, Prince Wilfred ruminates on a plan for total world domination while guzzling Mummy’s Milk. Bow down—this coronation’s a killer. Created by the award-winning performer-director duo Lil Wenker and Cecily Nash. Praise for past work (BANGTAIL): “Sheer, brilliant, well executed madness ... blows the roof off the venue with laughter level ten” Three Weeks ★★★★★ "A masterclass in clowning that made the crowd roar with laughter... title: Rhythm & Rhyme
subtitle: Join us for an evening where poetry and live jazz come together in conversation - part of our summer series of free, or pay-what-you-can, Electric Bar shows.
bodyContent: Rhythm + Rhyme brings together acclaimed poets, live musicians, and an open mic community for a night of storytelling, performance, improvisation, and connection. Throughout the evening, featured poets will share their work accompanied by a live jazz band, creating a unique atmosphere where spoken word and music intertwine. The evening will also include an open mic section, with sign-ups available on the night. Whether you're a seasoned performer or sharing your work for the first time, all are welcome. Manganaro - Host: Manganaro is a poet, performer, and event organiser. They’ve headlined events across the UK and their writing explores themes of identity, bilingual experience, and everyday nuances, drawing on the personal side of political. They were a 2025 Queer Bath Award recipient, the 2024 DIVA Magazine Poetry Competition winner, a two-time finalist for the 2026 Creative Bath Awards, and have supported artists such as Alice Oswald and Max Porter; performing in venues from Tobacco Factory Bristol to No. 1 Royal Crescent. Manganaro is passionate about uplifting the local grassroots creative community through events. Gray Taylor - Featured Poet: Gray Taylor is a Brighton-based spoken word artist with a penchant for punchlines. Originally from Derby, he has a musical background in hip hop, grime and R&B. He discovered his love of poetry after attending STATUS FLO at Brighton Dome, hosted by AFLO. the poet. Gray Taylor is a relatable storyteller, mixing serious subjects with elements of humour. title: Children’s Social Care jobs in Somerset
subtitle: #ThinkFamilyThinkSomerset
bodyContent: Are you a social worker who enjoyed your stay in Somerset? Would you like to come and work here? We are a progressive, improving and innovative authority. We offer nationally competitive salaries and if you are relocating or travelling some distance to work for us you could be eligible for up to £8k relocation allowance. Link to further benefits here Here’s what our social workers say about working for us Adults’ Social Care 'I successfully completed my placement [with SCC] in July 2017. My learning journey was focussed, organised, supported, enriching and on reflection, it was a whole lot of fun! Sadly, when I qualified there were no positions with SCC, so I ventured to a different local authority. I learnt a lot with my first employer, however, I felt limited. The scope for creativity was clearly part of SCCs culture, which I couldn’t help but crave. I returned to SCC as soon as a post became available and I can truly say that I have never looked forward to going to work before like I do now. Not just the team I work within, but the entire directorate are some of the most amazing, caring individuals I have ever had the pleasure of working with. SCC are so focussed on learning and development; the opportunities are endless! As well as the scope for creativity, I can confidently say that they are the best local authority I have had the privilege to represent.' Annabelle, Social Worker, Adults’ Safeguarding Team If you want to enjoy your role as much as Annabelle, follow this link to Adults Social Care Roles Children’s Social Care 'Somerset are a responsible and supportive as an employer, I have found that they are willing to invest time in growing their own social workers which is really encouraging. I did have an interview at a neighbouring authority and found the whole atmosphere at the interview with Somerset to be far more welcoming and friendly as well as being more professional.' George, Social Worker, Children Looked After, South Somerset 'I have been offered lots of support and the relocation allowance made the move easy. I feel like Somerset is the perfect environment to develop as a professional with access to a variety of learning opportunities, the training schedule is second to none.' Andy, Social Worker, Assessment, Bridgwater If you want to know more follow this link to Children’s Social Care roles 'In Somerset we are an inclusive authority, always striving to Improve Lives in our County. We are looking to recruit committed staff who want to help us provide a gold star service for the most vulnerable of our residents in both Adults’ and Children’s Services. We are working with Visit Somerset on some fun ways to engage and retain our current staff, as retention of our current staff is as important as recruiting new team members. We want our staff to feel valued by the organisation and the wider community and also relish all that Somerset has to offer.' Claire, Recruitment & Engagement Officer, HR and Social Care
tagline: #ThinkFamilyThinkSomerset

title: Cossington Park
subtitle: Cossington Park is a very special house set in 22 acres of beautifully maintained, peaceful gardens for the exclusive use of our guests.
bodyContent: Cossington Park is a very special house and cottage set in 22 acres of beautifully maintained, peaceful gardens – for between 6 and 22 guests. It is available to rent on a self-catering basis for families and friends for reunions and as a retreat Located in the pretty village of Cossington in Somerset,it is on the edge of the Polden Hills and the Somerset Levels . Within easy access are many of the West Country's beauty spots and attractions including: Cheddar Gorge and Caves ; Dunster Castle ; Exmoor , the Brendon Hills, the Mendips and the Quantocks ; the cities of Bath and Wells ; Glastonbury Priory and Tor ; Longleat ; and Wookey Hole Caves . You will find the atmosphere at Cossington Park informal and friendly, and yet very special. It is above all a place to relax and to be at peace, with good friends and family, and good books! title: Stay in Bath
subtitle: StayinBath.org is owned and run by BIGHA, the Bath Independent Guest House Association. We are a voluntary membership organisation made up of over 100 guesthouses, small hotels and self catering accommodation, all working together to offer overnight visitors to Bath the best possible experience.
bodyContent: Who are we? StayinBath.org is owned and run by BIGHA, the Bath Independent Guest House Association. We are a voluntary membership organisation made up of over 100 guesthouses, small hotels and self catering accommodation, all working together to offer overnight visitors to Bath the best possible experience. StayinBath.org offers you: A choice of independently owned B&Bs, small hotels or self-catering accommodation We have accommodation to suit every visitor to Bath, whether you: Are on holiday or on business Are on your own, with your family, travelling with a friend or in a group Want the bustle of the city centre or the tranquillity of the countryside Need somewhere which caters for mobility, visual or hearing problems Need somewhere with parking or with access to public transport links Want to bring your pets We can help you to discover: Bath’s rich history and architecture Bath’s wonderful independent restaurants offering a whole host of diverse cuisine Bath’s eclectic range of shops Bath’s amazing Festivals’ calendar Prestigious sporting events How are we run? BIGHA is run by an elected committee, all of whom are volunteers, working tirelessly to support and market Bath’s independent hotels, guest houses and self-catering accommodation. Why should you use StayinBath? All of our members live in Bath and North East Somerset. We have a wealth of local knowledge which you will be able to call upon to get the best out of Bath. In return, unlike when you book with another OTA ( Online Travel Agent) you are safe in the knowledge that you are contributing to the local economy of Bath so we can keep maintaining it for years to come as a great place to live, work – and visit Why should you trust us? We have been working together for over 20 years to ensure the highest standards are maintained by our members. All members have to adhere to the health and safety legislation as set by local and national government, including fire risk assessment, health & safety, food hygiene certificates ( where appropriate) and 3 rd party liability insurance. Many have attained external quality standards for their properties which are visible on line All properties are described with clear accurate information, a user-friendly booking procedure, terms and condition and access statement. Run by owners who are dedicated to providing quality accommodation. We also consider feedback from review and travel websites during this process.

title: Brooks Guesthouse Bath

bodyContent: Bathrooms are sleek and modern with Hansgrohe showers travertine tiles and Geneva Guild products. Breakfast is delicious & award winning. We are foodies at Brooks. title: Katie Gregson-Macleod + Special Guests
subtitle: Katie Gregson-MacLeod’s unique blend of deeply personal lyricism and folk-influenced sound have earned her a dedicated global audience.
bodyContent: Growing up in the Scottish Highlands, the 23 year old was immersed in music from an early age, singing alongside her pianist mother and losing herself in musicals with her parents - a love of which is rooted in her fascination with storytelling. Her infatuation with language and creative writing was instilled as a child, observing her father writing novels everyday before and after work, and that same thread runs through the folk music she came to discover in her late teens, alongside influences of Motown and Soul that came from inheriting her late grandfather’s record collection. Inspired by classic singer-songwriters like Joni Mitchell, Leonard Cohen, and Elliott Smith, Katie’s journey began busking in Inverness to playing local pub gigs in the city and self-releasing a low-fi EP ‘Games I Play’ aged 18. Fast forward to 2022 and a viral breakout on TikTok with single “complex”, which led to international recognition, a major label deal, an Ivor Novello nomination and a whirlwind of festival performances and headline tours. After parting ways with her major label home in early 2024, Katie embraced a new chapter of creative independence, signing with Matt Maltese’s Last Recordings on Earth and crafting a raw, intimate EP that reflects the balance between love and artistic uncertainty. Firmly rooted in her lifelong passion for storytelling, Katie’s work continues to explore themes of nostalgia, power dynamics, and self-reflection, all underscored by her signature poeticism and vulnerability.
tagline: Katie Gregson-MacLeod’s unique blend of deeply personal lyricism

title: The Anchor Inn
subtitle: Set in an 18th-century coaching inn, The Anchor Inn offers free Wi-Fi, home-cooked food and luxury rooms with scenic views.
bodyContent: The Anchor Inn is a rural riverside pub and inn with six letting bedrooms overlooking beautiful surroundings shaped by the river Exe. Exebridge is situated on the southern tip of Exmoor near the village of Dulverton. The lower bar at the front of the inn once entertained the celebrated English novelist R.D. Blackmore in the 19th century and features in his classic Lorna Doone. Overlooking the riverside garden is our upper bar and dining room; serving home made food which takes advantage of Somerset and Devonshire's excellent local produce. Meals are freshly prepared to order and cooked over charcoal to give extra flavour. We also welcome well-behaved dogs. We have six letting bedrooms available to cater for a variety of requirements, from families to individuals. All stays include a cooked Exmoor breakfast.

title: The Oak House
subtitle: A cabin in the woods for 2 (or 3) with Georgian Bath 10 minutes away, the Oak House is set in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty with the Cotswold Way running along our boundary.
bodyContent: As the name suggests, the Oak House is an oak framed cabin situated on the edge of a wood and surrounded by old oak trees. The fully equipped kitchen has an induction hob, oven, and dishwasher. There is a wood burning stove with wood provided for the first fire. The bedroom has a kingsize bed (the headboard is made from an oak branch which fell from one of our trees in a storm Next to this is a bathroom with full size power shower. The whole building is open to the roof except for the area above the bathroom which can be accessed by ladder and has a single mattress for an occasional extra guest. The Oak House is full of light from large windows overlooking the wood and stunning views to the west. The house is centrally heated with hot water on demand. There are games and books but no television (too many trees for reception) but that might be a good thing! There is a WiFi internet connection, linked to the main house. All linen and towels are provided as is everything you might need in the kitchen and bathroom. Outside, there is a covered open porch for boots and for sitting out a shower in comfy chairs. Attached to the house is an octagonal deck with table and chairs for al fresco meals or a glass of wine while you admire the views. . Just below is a barbecue and a fire pit (but you might have to saw up your own wood!). The Oak House was built with mostly reclaimed material by design although the plumbing and electrical equipment are new. The roof is clad in recycled Cornish slate, the floor is made from used but sanded scaffolding planks, the bathroom sink came from a school laboratory (suitably cleaned up!) and the shower is tiled in reject Burlington slate. The eclectic furniture is all carefully sourced with comfort and design in mind. We hope you like it.
tagline: A cabin in the woods for 2 (or 3) with Georgian Bath 10 minutes away

title: Vocal Works Presents “Gospel Rocks”
subtitle: Gospel Rocks is coming — and it’s louder, bolder, and more powerful than ever.
bodyContent: Join Vocal Works Gospel Choir for an electrifying night where gospel collides with iconic rock. This high-energy performance reimagines legendary songs by artists including the likes of Led Zeppelin, The Beatles, Pink Floyd, Jimi Hendrix, and Bon Jovi, transformed through rich gospel harmonies, driving rhythms, and unstoppable soul. With over 24 years of performance history under the direction of Tim King, Vocal Works Gospel Choir is a 60-strong powerhouse renowned for genre-defying collaborations and unforgettable live shows. The choir has shared stages with artists including Take That, The Heavy, and Reef, and has released its own acclaimed albums — including Choired Up — showcasing its signature blend of precision, passion, and raw vocal power. Expect soaring vocals, spine-tingling moments, and a wall of sound that lifts the spirit and shakes the room. This is music that bridges generations — classic rock anthems reborn with heart, fire, and faith. This isn’t just a concert. It’s gospel with an edge. It’s rock with a soul. This is an experience you don’t want to miss.

title: Ian Stone is Looking for the Wow
bodyContent: "Life can't just be the humdrum, the mundane and the routine before the inevitable slide of disease, decay and death. Why can't we sneak in a bit of awesome, a tad of amazing and maybe a smidge of wonderful?" A forest canopy opening onto a huge vista would be enchanting for some but Ian's ancestors wondered the desert for forty years, they've been outdoors enough. Others get their fix from the spiritual but Ian's been harbouring a grudge against God since his mother stopped him going to Arsenal after his Barmitzvah. Forty-nine years ago. 'God will be watching' she said. Well, at least he got to see the game. The point is, life could be so much better so Ian's on the lookout. Come and join him on the hunt. Ian Stone is a hugely experienced broadcaster, podcaster and writer and a brilliantly funny comedian. He performs at major comedy festivals and venues globally. His popular posts and reels on social media have quickly earned him a following of over 60k across BlueSky, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook, amassing millions of views. Aside from stand-up comedy, Ian co-hosted the award-winning Rock 'N' Roll Football show on Absolute Radio for five years with Ian Wright. He currently presents a very popular (50k downloads per episode), twice-weekly Arsenal podcast, Handbrake Off, for The Athletic. title: Court Farm Holiday Cottages
subtitle: Court Farm Holiday Cottages, Exford in the heart of Exmoor National Park are ideal for walkers, horse riders, cyclists, dogs and their owners and anyone who wants to enjoy the peace and tranquillity of the true English countryside.
bodyContent: Court Farm Holiday Cottages, Exford in the heart of Exmoor National Park are ideal for walkers, horse riders, cyclists, dogs and their owners and anyone who wants to enjoy the peace and tranquillity of the true English countryside. We have three charming, well-equipped cottages in a small hamlet close to the centre of Exford. Mountain Ash and Rowan cottages have two bedrooms and sleep up to four adults, Snowdrop cottage is a one-bedroom cottage sleeping two adults. All cottages are dog-friendly with their own gardens and miles of walking direct from the front door. Heating, electricity and bed-linen are included in the price. Our cottages are all non-smoking, have wood burning stoves as well as central heating and and have wifi. Positioned on a bridleway adjacent to the River Exe, our cottages are also ideal if you want to bring your horse as we can provide stabling and grazing by arrangement. You can ride or walk directly on to Exmoor at Room Hill where you may see England’s largest wild animal, the Red Deer and the endangered Exmoor Pony close by on Winsford Hill. Tarr Steps and Dunkery Beacon are also close by. The excellent food pubs and village shops in Exford are less than a 10 minute walk away while the beaches of North Devon are only a 40 minute drive. Whether you are seeking an active or relaxing break you can be assured of a warm welcome at Court Farm.
tagline: Court Farm Holiday Cottages, Exford in the heart of Exmoor National Park

title: Capturing Life: A Century of the New English Art Club
subtitle: Opening on 21 January at the Victoria Art Gallery in Bath, Capturing Life: A Century of the New English Art Club will showcase work by past and present members of the New English Art Club, an elected society of contemporary painters inspired by the visual world. The exhibition runs until 11 April 2023.
bodyContent: The New English Art Club was founded in 1886 by a group of rebellious young artists protesting against their repeated rejection by the Royal Academy. Their aim was to exhibit "really good modern painting". In 1937 the art historian and museum curator Mary Chamot described the Club as "unquestionably the most vital artistic movement in English painting of the last half century". The exhibition will feature more than 40 works by current Club members, all of which will be for sale. Also on show will be major paintings by former exhibitors including Gwen John, Winifred Nicholson, John Singer Sargent, Stanley Spencer, Walter Sickert, Augustus John, Dod Procter and Paul Nash. Kevin Guy, Leader of Bath & North East Somerset Council, said: “The Gallery has a long association with the New English Art Club, having hosted six exhibitions of members' work between 1907 and 1947. Key past members Lord Methuen and Walter Sickert lived locally, as does the Club’s current President, Peter Brown. We’re delighted that exhibition-goers will once again have a chance to see the best of the New English Art Club here in Bath.” Gwen John is represented by Bust of a girl with a bow before a pink background , on loan from the Arts Council Collection. In 1900, two years after completing her studies at the Slade School of Art, John exhibited her work for the very first time. The forum in which she chose to do so was the New English Art Club. She continued to exhibit with the Club until 1911. John Singer Sargent's At Torre Galli: Ladies in a Garden of 1910, on loan from the Royal Academy, exhibits all the Impressionist flair one would expect from a close friend of Claude Monet. After moving to London in 1885-86, Sargent quickly found a sympathetic exhibiting arena with the New English Art Club, with whom he shared an abiding love of modern French art. He served on the committee of the Club in 1887 and 1889 and, despite his American origins, he extended the association into the twentieth century. Sir Stanley Spencer was one of the most distinguished artists associated with the New English Art Club, having been elected a member in the 1920s. His important portrait of his second wife to be, the painter Patricia Preece, dates from 1933 and is on loan from Southampton Art Gallery. The artwork documents not only the two artists' fateful relationship, but also their joint connections with the New English Art Club. Walter Sickert was one of the most consistent New English Art Club exhibitors, showing over 130 paintings between 1888 and 1939. His portrait of Celia, Lady Brunel dates from about 1906 and typically defies any expectations of the sitter that her attractive features would be emphasized. Instead, he remained committed to subdued lighting and spontaneity. The sitter, who later lived in Bath's Royal Crescent, was the granddaughter of Isambard Kingdom Brunel. www.victoriagal.org.uk

title: The Home Cottage
subtitle: The Home Cottage is close to England’s smallest City of Wells, with trendy Frome, the picturesque village of Mells and the Mendip Hills all close by.
bodyContent: The Home Cottage is architect designed and newly built (completed in November 2016) and sleeps four in two bedrooms. The house is fully central heated. The cottage is very peaceful and sits at the end of a long track surrounded by farmland. The front of the house is south facing and the cottage is in an elevated position with wonderful views out over the surrounding fields and trees. There is a large garden of approximately 0.2 acres with flower borders and a large area of grass at the rear of the cottage which is suitable for ball games. In front of the cottage is a patio with teak table and chairs for guests to sit and enjoy the view. A sun parasol and barbecue are provided to allow guests to make the most of sunny summer days. The cottage has off-road parking for two cars on the gravel driveway. Inside the cottage has a well equipped fitted kitchen with a good range of appliances including a full-sized dish-washer. The kitchen also has a small dining area with two chairs and a bench. Next door is the sitting room which has a woodburner to allow you to cozy up on cold winter nights (or even chilly summer evenings) – a basket of logs is supplied and the fire is laid and ready to be lit. The cottage also has a good sized utility room complete with washing machine and lots of space for coats and wet walking boots. This room is also ideal for a well-behaved dog to stay. Upstairs the master bedroom has a double bed and windows to south and east – ideal for the morning sun. The second bedroom is small, but has room for two in bunk beds with full sized single mattresses. On arrival guests will find the cottage fully prepared with freshly ironed cotton bedding and fluffy white towels and face flannels. Milk, cookies, tea, coffee and sugar are provided along with fresh flowers from my garden. Other amenities include: • Wifi • TV and DVD player • Washing line, pegs and clothes airer • Hair dryer • Iron and ironing board • Travel cot and high chair (please request and I will bring it down to the cottage) • Children’s toys (please request and I will bring some down to the cottage)
tagline: The Home Cottage is close to England’s smallest City of Wells

title: Robyn Hitchcock
subtitle: Fair Endeavours warmly welcome English songwriting icon Robyn Hitchcock back to Bath for an acoustic, seated show!
bodyContent: With a career now spanning six decades, Robyn Hitchcock remains a truly one-of-a-kind artist – surrealist rock ‘n’ roller, iconic troubadour, guitarist, poet, painter, and performer. An unparalleled, deeply individualistic songwriter and stylist, Hitchcock has traversed many genres with humour, intelligence, and originality across over 30 albums and seemingly infinite live performances. From Soft Boys’ proto-psych-punk and The Egyptians’ Dadaist pop to solo masterpieces like 1984’s milestone I Often Dream of Trains and 1990’s Eye, Hitchcock has crafted a strikingly original oeuvre rife with sagacious observation, astringent wit, recurring marine life, mechanised rail services, cheese, Clint Eastwood, and innumerable finely drawn characters, real and imagined. Presented by Fair Endeavours.

title: Night Of Mystery – The Chinese Star Mystery
bodyContent: A previously undiscovered Sherlock Holmes mystery has been unearthed in a house clearance and is set to be auctioned at Christie’s of London. Sir Arthur Conan Doyle’s famous detective features in the story, and a record sum is expected when the manuscript goes under the hammer. The Chinese Star Mystery is being transported to London under high security, but when the guard in charge is murdered, there is only one woman in England who can hope to solve the crime. Miss Mapletree enters the world of antiquarian books as she investigates the case of The Chinese Star Mystery. A vintage Agatha Christie-inspired live-action whodunnit. Perfect Murder have been performing live-action murder mysteries for over twenty years, working throughout the UK and Europe. Their events are light-hearted and great fun with the classic Agatha Christie-style that guarantees you’ll will have a good time, whether you’re a seasoned sleuth or simply out for a good time! title: Edinburgh Preview: Spencer Jones + Phil Nichol
subtitle: Spencer Jones Hello my name is Spencer Jones and I am writing this blurb. I'm coming to Bath and I'm very excited. I am in the process of working out a new show.
bodyContent: Spencer Jones Hello my name is Spencer Jones and I am writing this blurb. I'm coming to Bath and I'm very excited. I am in the process of working out a new show. It's about dogs so if you like dogs you might like this. But I must impress upon you that if you hate dogs, or you are scared of them, you will still like this. There will be characters, some silly songs, some dog leads and some stories and stuff. By the time I come to Bath I think it's going to be a finished show so instead of it being a work in progress, this will be quite close to what I take up to Edinburgh festival, so fingers crossed it should be pretty flipping good. If you've never seen me before, then go online and read some reviews and have a look at it (me) if you have seen before. I'll see you again soon (Bath) x Phil Nichol: Aren’t We Lucky ‘Aren’t We Lucky’ is a dynamic, wonderfully heart-warming story exploring chance, love, magic, and loss. Through the deeply personal yet funny story of his friend Kevin Hearn’s battle with leukemia, and the extraordinary chain of events that followed, Phil reflects on regret, good fortune, and the simple, visceral act of appreciating what we have right here, right now. First brand new show in 7 years. Lou Reed. The Lottery. Ecstasy. Crisps. Prince Andrew. Sunshine. Punk. Terry Jones. Leukaemia. Butterflies. Chance. Dizzy Gillespie's Cheeks. Wasps.
tagline: Spencer Jones Hello my name is Spencer Jones

title: LCE Photo Show 2026
subtitle: LCE Photo Show featuring major photography and video brands comes to Haynes Motor Museum on 12 September 2026
bodyContent: London Camera Exchange (LCE) is bringing the LCE Photo Show 2026 to the legendary Haynes Motor Museum in Sparkford, Somerset on Saturday 12 September 2026. Following the success of the Exeter South West Photo Show in 2025, this year’s event offers photography enthusiasts, filmmakers, professional photographers and content creators a more extensive and immersive experience. Open from 9.30am to 4.30pm, the one-day event will feature top photography, video and optical brands showcasing the latest products alongside live demonstrations, seminars, networking opportunities and exclusive retail offers. Visitors will be able to: • Discover and test the latest cameras, lenses, accessories and video equipment • Learn from the experts at talks, seminars and practical masterclasses – many free to attend • Access the museum’s famous ‘Red Room’ featuring iconic red automobiles for unique photographic opportunities • View an exhibition of the winning images from the LCE Photographer of the Year 2026 competition • Network with fellow photography and filmmaking enthusiasts while enjoying refreshments The event will include a packed line-up of free-to-attend ticketed expert seminars and round-table discussion groups – plus practical demonstrations covering subjects such as lighting and portraiture, which can be purchased in advance. Tickets for selected sessions will be released in stages ahead of the show. Confirmed speakers and technical experts include Gavin Hoey and Amy Shore, with many more to be announced. Attendees will also have the opportunity to shop exclusive ‘show-only deals’, with all visitors able to redeem the cost of their entry ticket against qualifying purchases with LCE. title: Cannington Court
subtitle: As a unique Conference and Events venue nestled in the heart of Somerset, Cannington Court is a beautiful Grade 1 listed former 12th century Benedictine Nunnery. Artfully restored, with contemporary finishes, energy-efficient principles and advanced technology throughout, it offers the ideal venue for corporate events, meetings, training, team collaboration and more.
bodyContent: This historic building offers modern accommodation, contemporary dining and extensive meeting and event space, ideally located for those seeking a business event in relaxing surroundings. We are also the location for the interactive Hinkley Point Visitor Centre. Our 50 modern en-suite bedrooms, all come with complimentary toiletries and tea/coffee making facilities. We have accessible bedrooms, free Wi-Fi and relaxation areas to unwind in the evenings. We provide bistro and event dining options using seasonal local produce along with a full breakfast, lunch and dinner service. We have a bar area which provides you with somewhere to unwind in the evenings. From gala dinners in historic Clifford Hall, to Christmas parties and smaller private functions, our events team will be delighted to discuss & deliver an amazing experience for you. Cannington Court is a showcase for sustainability and an exemplar for Net Zero reducing running costs in the process. Onsite renewable energy and low-carbon heat solutions, Pod Point Charging Points, electric vehicle, courtesy shuttle service and a vehicle to grid (V2G) scheme are just some of the ways we are supporting this. HINKLEY POINT VISITOR CENTRE The centre highlights the importance of the energy mix and how Nuclear power plays an important part through a number of interactive displays. Visitors are encouraged to explore how electricity is created in a fun and immersive way and learn why there is an overwhelming need to produce low carbon energy.

This quiet family park provides pitches for owner occupied static caravans and seasonal touring caravans on a pleasant open site with distant views of the Mendip Hills and only five minutes’ walk from a safe sandy beach. Brean is a favourite place for holidays with everything you need within walking distance. There are plenty of attractions to visit in Somerset as well as wonderful food and wildlife. Static Park open end March to end October, Seasonal Park opens mid May to end September. The Pavilion area hosts 48 luxury pitches for 12' and 13' static caravans, we often have statics for sale please visit: Pavilion Brean Statics for sale. If you are looking for a seasonal pitch (mid May to end September) why not call us? Prices vary but an all inclusive package of grass pitch, electric and winter storage is £1,380
