title: Crealy Meadows
subtitle: Crealy Theme Park & Resort is the ultimate family holiday destination in Devon. Located within the stunning East Devon countryside just outside of Exeter, Crealy is easily accessible from junction 30 of the M5 making it the ideal base for exploring the county too.
bodyContent: Crealy Theme Park & Resort is the ultimate family holiday destination in Devon. Located within the stunning East Devon countryside just outside of Exeter, Crealy is easily accessible from junction 30 of the M5 making it the ideal base for exploring the county too. At Crealy, you’ll be spoilt for choice with the range of accommodation types that are available… all with a Theme Park with the most rides in Devon on your doorstep! Crealy Theme Park & Resort is the perfect destination for your family short break. Choose from a selection of luxurious hot tub lodges, which are cosy, comfortable, and ideal at all times of the year. Each one features an open-plan living area, integrated kitchen, and a private hot tub – perfect for short break throughout the year. Alternatively, you can enjoy the perfect combination of luxury and adventure in one of Crealy’s glamping tents. Discover the range of luxury safari cabins and medieval pavilions and conjure your very own magical adventure during your family holiday in Devon. What’s more, all lodge breaks and glamping holidays also include free theme park tickets to Crealy Theme Park! Make the most of your beautiful surroundings and become one with nature during camping holidays at Crealy. The generously sized pitches are perfect for tents, caravans, and motorhomes and offer magical breaks under the stars. When you stay at Crealy you will be able to take advantage of the wonderful facilities that are available there. The secure site is home to large family sized bathrooms and all the showers feature under floor heating and touch point units. You will find a convenience shop should you need to pick up some extra supplies as well as an on-site restaurant. For more information and to book your holiday at Crealy, visit: https://www.crealy.co.uk
tagline: Crealy Theme Park & Resort is the ultimate family holiday destination in Devon.

title: Rock Inn
subtitle: 3 Flavours already has a duo of thriving neighbourhood eateries in Barnet and Banbury and ‘3 Flavours Kitchen’ is the first to launch in the Southwest, with many more planned to roll-out in the near future. Chef Chanaka Fernando’s vision for 3 Flavours Kitchen is to provide an exceptional dining experience that combines culinary excellence with the charm of Waterrow, near Taunton.
bodyContent: Steaks are a standout feature on the menu with options such as the Rib-Eye Steak (250g) priced at £26.50, Sirloin Steak (250g) at £25.00, and Rump Steak (250g) at £21.00. Diners can enhance their steak experience with a variety of sauces, including peppercorn, mushroom, béarnaise, garlic butter, and chimichurri for an additional £2.00 each, or upgrade to a luxurious truffle red wine sauce for £3.00. Grill & Burger highlights include the Grilled Chicken Burger at £14.50 and the 3 Flavours Signature Beef Burger at £15.00, both served with caramelised onions, truffle mayo, rocket, ketchup, relish, and fries. Seafood lovers can indulge in the Miso Grilled Salmon at £23.50, served with a Japanese salad and sesame. Vegetarian options feature the Grilled Cauliflower Steak (v) at £15.50, paired with roasted pepper sauce, basil, and olive salsa, and the Grilled Vegetable Burger (V) at £11.00, featuring caramelised onion, mushroom, grilled courgettes, hash browns, rocket, and spicy mayo. Curries are a cornerstone of the new menu, offering a range of aromatic dishes served with steamed rice and crispy shallots. Notable dishes include the Monkfish & Tiger Prawn curry at £22.00, Aromatic Chicken Green Curry at £16.50, and the Ceylon Lamb at £17.50.
tagline: 3 Flavours Kitchen at The Rock Inn in Waterrow, near Taunton is the latest culinary concept

title: The Wild Escape at Victoria Art Gallery
subtitle: The Victoria Art Gallery is going wild in 2023! The Gallery is taking part in The Wild Escape, a nationwide project uniting hundreds of museums, schools and families to find nature in museums.
bodyContent: Led by national art charity Art Fund with support from Arts Council England, hundreds of museums, galleries and historic houses are coming together for the largest ever collaboration between UK museums. Taking place from January to July 2023, The Wild Escape invites children to find a favourite animal in their local museum and create an artwork imagining its ‘escape’ back to its natural habitat. The pictures and stories children create will be brought together by the Art Fund in a collective work of art that imagines a better future for the wildlife on our doorstep, launched online and in museums on Earth Day 2023 (Saturday 22 April). Kevin Guy, Leader of Bath & North East Somerset Council, said: “We’re delighted to be joining museums and galleries across the country in this exciting project. The Victoria Art Gallery is inviting local schools and families to get involved in a special programme of creative activities celebrating UK wildlife. I hope young visitors to the Gallery will enjoy exploring the collections and learning about our amazing wildlife and the importance of protecting it for the future.” Jenny Waldman, Director of Art Fund, said: “I’m thrilled that the Victoria Art Gallery is joining hundreds of organisations, from the Outer Hebrides to Folkestone, to connect thousands of children with the natural world through the UK’s truly great museums. Thanks to the invaluable support of Arts Council England, the Wild Escape will empower families and children across the UK to visit and discover our wonderful museums, whilst taking positive action to picture a better future for our wildlife.” The Gallery will be working closely with local primary schools to offer group visits, where children can be inspired by pictures of animals, create animal habitats using collage, and make sketchbooks to record their observations. There will be a themed trail around the Gallery, and special displays of sculpture, ceramics, paintings and drawings that celebrate nature, drawn from the Gallery’s collections. Over the February and Easter school holidays, there will be free drop-in sessions for families, where kids can make beautiful hanging butterflies, butterfly plant labels, and colourful fish and pond collages. There will also be family craft activities on Earth Day – look out for details on the Gallery website: www.victoriagal.org.uk/events . The Wild Escape is an opportunity to join the urgent conversation about the climate crisis and biodiversity loss and look for positive solutions, in partnership with leading environmental charities the RSPB and WWF and cultural organisations National Trust and English Heritage. The Wild Escape is inspired by Wild Isles , a landmark BBC series presented by Sir David Attenborough exploring the flora and fauna of the UK. www.thewildescape.org.uk #TheWildEscape

title: The Grove at Freshford
subtitle: The Grove at Freshford is a unique period property built in the 17th century, situated in the heart of the conservation village of Freshford, about 6 miles south east of Bath.
bodyContent: The Grove at Freshford provides self catering accommodation in a 5 bedroom exclusive, 17th century period property. Sleeping up to 10 people, the house is close to the pub, shop, cafe, church and rail station in this historic village of Freshford, only 6 miles south east of Bath. The house stands in over an acre of well-established garden with panoramic views over the rolling countryside and the River Avon. The secluded grounds and wrought iron gates ensure privacy for visiting guests in addition to providing a perfect, peaceful and tranquil setting for any occasion. In warmer months, there is an unheated outdoor swimming pool which is fully enclosed. The house is full of historical fascination and charm dating back to 1650. The ground floor contains 2 reception rooms furnished with classic pieces overlooking the gardens through French windows. There is also a separate TV lounge. Guests can choose to eat in the formal dinning room or more casually in the kitchen/breakfast room which is fully equipped with all modern appliances. Outside there is a delightful al fresco eating area. The house features art specially commissioned from a leading local artist. There are 5 individually styled bedrooms plus a travel cot and moses basket. We are also able to offer delicious catering from scrumptious afternoon tea, creative canapes, light suppers or even fully catered dinners.
tagline: The Grove at Freshford is a unique period property built in the 17th century

title: G2 Definitive Genesis at Komedia Bath
subtitle: G2 are currently celebrating their 25th anniversary year of playing classic 1970s Genesis.
bodyContent: G2 are currently celebrating their 25th anniversary year of playing classic 1970s Genesis. G2 pay tribute to a vintage period in Genesis’ long and colourful history, the four-man “Seconds Out” era, and earlier Gabriel years. With a repertoire extending from the 1970 Trespass album to 1980's Duke, G2 faithfully recreate some of the finest progressive rock ever written. Accolades posted online from recent shows include: “Best Performance by ANY Tribute Band (not just Genesis ones either) I have ever seen...” “Thanks to all the guys from G2 who were out of this world, I really cannot describe how terrifyingly good you guys are.” Hear classics such as Dance On A Volcano, Ripples, Los Endos, One For The Vine, and Afterglow, mixed up with the classics of the Gabriel years, Firth Of Fifth, Cinema Show, I Know What I Like and Suppers Ready. This is vintage Genesis, performed by G2 to a level Genesis themselves would be proud of! So take a little trip back and relive those wonderful moments of your Genesis musical history with G2.

title: BlueTone Festival
subtitle: 4 days of world class music right here in Somerset!
bodyContent: BlueTone Festival is a new celebration of jazz, blues, funk and soul, set in the heart of Somerset. Taking place in Taunton, BlueTone brings together outstanding live music, emerging UK talent and established artists for a weekend that’s all about groove, musicianship and connection. From smoky blues riffs and deep jazz cuts to funk-driven rhythms and soul voices that stop you in your tracks, BlueTone is curated for people who love real live music. We’re building a festival that feels welcoming, high-quality and delivered at a scale that prioritises audience experience and accessibility – a place where music fans, artists and the local community come together. Expect a carefully programmed lineup, great sound, space to discover new favourites, and an atmosphere that invites you to stay, explore and soak it all in. BlueTone is proudly rooted in the South West but looks far beyond it. Our ambition is to create a festival that draws music lovers from across the UK, while championing regional talent and independent culture. Whether you’re a lifelong jazz head, a blues devotee, or just someone who loves great live music in a beautiful setting, BlueTone is for you.

title: Highly popular & free exhibition train
subtitle: A free, interactive exhibition inside a train is heading to East Somerset Railway.
bodyContent: A free, interactive exhibition inside a train is heading to East Somerset Railway. Co-curated with the National Railway Museum and packed with hands-on exhibits and amazing stories, ‘Inspiration’ reveals how railways transformed the world. It includes a fascinating look at railway firsts, engineering challenges and a whistle-stop tour of interesting – and lesser-known – careers on the railway. This stop at Cranmore Railway Station near Shepton Mallet is one of the last on its historic tour – so don’t miss out! More than 80,000 have already visited Inspiration on its 60-stop, year-long tour of Britain and 9 in 10 would recommend it to a friend. Inspiration is part of Railway 200, the national campaign celebrating two centuries of the modern railway. Thousands of events across the UK and the world have celebrated a British innovation that revolutionised travel, supercharged economies and enabled mass tourism, sports leagues and the standardisation of time.

title: Focus Thirty + Intrusive
subtitle: Join Focus Thirty and Intrusive for an explosive evening of rock music - part of our summer series of free, or pay-what-you-can, Electric Bar shows.
bodyContent: Focus Thirty: Focus Thirty are a four-piece alternative rock band local to Bristol and Bath. Formed in late 2024, they wanted to create a blend of punchy riffs, melodic hooks and anthemic atmospheres inspired by 21st century alt rock bands such as Nothing But Thieves and Biffy Clyro. 2026 marks the start of their studio releases with their single ‘Dumb and Blind’ recorded in Bath, with many more to come. Intrusive: Originally hailing from South Wales and now tearing up stages across the South West, Intrusive are a sharp, fast, riff-driven rock band with a sound shaped by a wide mix of influences. Blending elements of rock, blues and funk with a heavier edge, they’ve crafted a signature style that’s unmistakably their own. With a focus on feel, energy and making every track stand apart, their passion comes through in every note.

title: The Big Conversation: could the Somerset Levels become our next National Park? 1st Oct in Glastonbury
subtitle: Join CPRE for a lively evening looking at the special qualities of the Somerset Levels and exploring what National Park status might mean for our landscapes, people and nature.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"583"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

The Big Conversation: could the Somerset Levels become our next National Park?

  Thu 1 Oct 2026 7:30 PM - 9:30 PM Glastonbury Town Hall, BA6 9EL 

CPRE , the Campaign to Protect Rural England, was at the forefront of the campaign to establish our UK National Parks, early in the 20th century. We’ve been fighting for better protection of our countryside for 100 years!

To mark CPRE’s centenary here in Somerset, we are thinking big. We want to start a conversation about our “big idea” of achieving National Park status for the Somerset Levels

Join us for a lively evening looking at the special qualities of the Somerset Levels and exploring what National Park status might mean for our landscapes, people and nature.  

CPRE Somerset President, Journalist and Broadcaster, Mariella Frostrup, will host the discussion and we have put together an inspiring panel of guests including CPRE, Somerset Wildlife Trust and Visit Somerset.   

Come with an open mind and plenty of questions!

The event is FREE OF CHARGE but  we invite you to give a donation to CPRE Somerset to cover our costs and help support our charity.

All are welcome  - pre-book your tickets now.

title: Thorney Lakes and Caravan Park
subtitle: A caravan and camping park with full facilities and coarse fishing available.
bodyContent: A caravan and camping park with full facilities and coarse fishing available. One mile form the historic village of Muchelney, our scenic park is perfect for touring the Somerset level and Moors , one of the most unchanged and distinctive landscape of lowland Britain. There are many interesting walks on the wetlands which are rich in flora, fauna and birdlife. Fishing lakes established in 1993, the setting attracts a host of wildlife and is regualry visited by otters, badgers, rabbits, deer and 70 species of birdlife including kingfishers. Just a short level walk from the caravan path the two miles of nature trails are a perfect for a short stroll or to enjoy a chat with the local fisher folk.
tagline: A caravan and camping park with full facilities and coarse fishing available.

title: Queensberry Hotel & Olive Tree Restaurant
subtitle: Bath hotels such as ours are few and far between; if you are looking for luxury and impeccable service housed in a Georgian townhouse, then you are absolutely in the right place.
bodyContent: We believe a room in a unique and slightly luscious hotel should be a little like a beautiful guest room in the house of stylish friends. But each room should look like it’s in a different house, belonging to different friends. No two the same, all of them gorgeous, but, thanks to the recent care we’ve lavished on them, they all offer the same level of experience. You’ll find the latest flat screen TVs and Bluetooth DAB radios, as well as luxury beds from Harrison Spinks affording our guests the best night’s rest. From Club and Classic Double rooms to the Four Poster suite, different guests come for different reasons with various budgets: our rooms offer something for all without sacrificing comfort and style. We’d advise you to make yourselves at home, but then why not take the chance to make yourselves feel a little more special than that?

title: Sh!t-faced Shakespeare: Romeo and Juliet
subtitle: The smash-hit, internationally acclaimed, award-winning, multi-sell-out phenomenon is back
bodyContent: Sh!t-faced Shakespeare: Romeo and Juliet The smash-hit, internationally acclaimed, award-winning, multi-sell-out phenomenon is back. Our cast will present an unconventional, no-holds-barred interpretation of 'Romeo and Juliet', with a tipsily tragic take on William Shakespeare's most iconic roll call of characters: from a rat-arsed Romeo to a juiced-up Juliet, a trollied Tybalt or a mashed-up Mercutios, along with enough booze to sterilise a brewery floor. This will be a tragedy like no other—the cup overfloweth. There is no love lost between the Capulet and Montague families, and everyone in Verona knows it. Surely the only hangover cure to centuries of family feuds is two forlorn teenagers from opposite households falling in love with each other? And a swig (or two) of the finest spirits to nudge them in the right direction, of course... What could possibly go wrong? Warning: Sh!t-faced Shakespeare® may feature foul language, nudity, disembowelled limbs and, occasionally, some Shakespeare.

title: East Cottage
subtitle: This gorgeous holiday cottage, which dates back to the 17th century, has an abundance of period features and traditional English country charm.
bodyContent: This gorgeous holiday cottage, which dates back to the 17th century, has an abundance of period features and traditional English country charm. This is tastefully combined with the provision of all the modern conveniences that you would expect to find in a 5 star cottage. The standard of the accommodation at East Cottage reflects our very high expectations of quality, cleanliness, attention to detail and service. Our charming holiday cottage is set in a beautiful rural location; lots of fresh air, farmland and farm animals with great walks and country pubs on the doorstep – always a good combination for keeping children, and parents (!) amused. The cottage itself has many lovely attributes. On the ground floor is the beamed living/dining-room with open inglenook fireplace, exposed stone walls and stone mullion windows, as well as TV, DVD and IPod dock; well-equipped kitchen with fridge, freezer, gas hob, electric oven and microwave; and utility room with washing-machine and dishwasher. A beautiful stone spiral staircase leads up to the first floor to the 2 large double bedrooms and bathroom with WC, washbasin, bath and separate shower cubicle. Again, beams, mullion windows and charming features in abundance! The cottage sleeps 4 (plus cot) in two bedrooms comprising 1 with king size double bed, and the other which can either be made up as a super king size double, or with 2 twin single beds. The cottage is therefore ideal for both families with children, or for couples trying to escape them! Children of all ages are welcome at East Cottage. A travel cot is provided, as well as stair-gates and high chair. We provide a baby-changing mat and baby bath, and there is also a toy box and a selection of games, jigsaws, books and DVDs. The cottage has gas central heating and free Wi-Fi. Towels are provided, as well as tea towels, toiletries, quality bed linen and an initial supply of logs for cosy nights in by the fire. We also provide basics such as tea, coffee, milk, sugar and cake! There are 2 parking spaces for the exclusive use of guests staying at East Cottage in the courtyard to the right of the cottage. Behind the courtyard, a small flight of steps leads to the private, secluded and gated garden. The well-established walled garden includes lawned areas, herbaceous borders and a south-facing patio, ideal for ‘al fresco’ dining. We also provide a barbeque and a supply of charcoal. The cottage is about 100 yards walking distance of the village shop, which sells local produce,and 300 yards to the wonderful village pub. The cottage is available for hire for a minimum of 2 nights. However in July & August it is let for whole weeks only, Saturday to Saturday. Please email or phone direct for tariff and seasonal offers. We look forward to welcoming you soon!
tagline: The standard of the accommodation at East Cottage reflects our very high expectations

title: Wambrook Farm - Feather Down
subtitle: Wambrook Farm can be found in the Blackdown Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, just 30 minutes from the beautiful beach at Lyme Regis.
bodyContent: The charming and breath taking land of Wambrook Farm can be found in the Blackdown Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, 30 minutes from the beach at Lyme Regis and is known by many of the locals as ‘the pearl of Dorset’. It is a susatinable mixed organic farm where you'll meet sheep and Aberdeen Angus cattle. The farmhouse, stables and buildings are all listed, built in the mid-seventeenth century. Echoes of the past are everywhere at Wambrook, such as a granary in the yard that looks like a chapel and an old counting house inside where long-ago farm workers received their pay. However, It has a solar farm and a biomass heating and hot water system fueled by sustainable wood grown on the farm. There are 2 types of lodges at Wambrook Farm, the Canvas lodge and the Canvas Frills Lodge with ensuite bathroom. See the website for the differences.
tagline: Wambrook Farm can be found in the Blackdown Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty

title: SQUIRRELS! ISN’T IT TIME FOR… HEY DUGGEE’S FIRST LIVE UK TOUR
subtitle: Hit children’s show HEY DUGGEE is to tour the UK for the first time ever in a vibrant and interactive stage show.
bodyContent: Duggee, The Squirrels and some of their friends will come together for HEY DUGGEE THE LIVE THEATRE SHOW in a brand new play packed with non-stop fun, laughs, singing, dancing and even more fun! The smash hit CBeebies series is brought to life through innovative puppetry and storytelling in this new live show which will tour across the UK from December through to summer 2023 including dates at Bath’s The Forum from Thursday April 20 to Saturday April 22 2023. Tickets are on sale NOW from www.ticketmaster.co.uk and direct from the venue. Since bursting onto TV screens in 2014, the BBC and Studio AKA creation has won no fewer than six BAFTAs and is an international Emmy award-winning hit. Hey Duggee was the most streamed children’s show on BBC iPlayer in 2021 and is popular among both children and parents; with fans both young and old, up and down the country now able to join the much-loved character on tour. HEY DUGGEE THE LIVE THEATRE SHOW is presented by award-winning theatre producer Kenny Wax and theatre and live entertainment promoters Cuffe and Taylor in association with Live Nation. Producer Kenny Wax said: “We are so thrilled to be working with Live Nation, Cuffe & Taylor, Studio AKA and BBC Studios to create a brand new stage show with lots of surprises touring the country with a sit down month in London over Christmas. I can't wait.” Ben Hatton, director of theatre touring for Cuffe and Taylor, added : “This is an incredibly exciting tour. Hey Duggee is quite simply a phenomenon and has taken the world of children’s entertainment by storm. “We are delighted to be working with Kenny and his team at Kenny Wax Family Entertainment, as well as all the extended Hey Duggee family at Studio AKA and BBC Studios. We look forward to Duggee and his friends filling theatres around the UK.” Mat Way, Global Director of Live Entertainment, Gaming and Interactive at BBC Studios, said: “Studio AKA’s Hey Duggee is such a fun and iconic show and we can’t wait to bring the humour and adventures to life for families all around the country. We’re delighted to be working with Kenny Wax and Cuffe and Taylor to introduce young people to the wonders of the theatre.” For more information go to www.heyduggeelive.com

title: Cavell House Bed and Breakfast B&B in Clevedon
bodyContent: Make yourself at home 3 minutes walk to the sea, 3 minutes walk to the Pier (best sea fishing in Somerset with fishing off the pier) 3 minutes walk to the shops, 1 minute to the Bank, 5 minutes walk to the pub/Chinese/Indian/English food/antiques/sea front cafes. 10 Min slow stroll along the sea front to the childrens leisure aea passing the sailing club, pub, amusements, fish and chips and ice cream on the way. Beautiful views across to Wales. Paddle steamer trips from the -pier, to Lundy, North Devon, Penarth and Gloucester. An ideal base for walkers and cyclists. Background to Cavell House Originally the Victorian home of Lord and Lady Belgrave, it later became a residential Girls School and Nurse Edith Cavell (the world war one heroine) spent some of her school days here. Prior to George and Daphne Hamnett becoming proprietors in 1996, Cavell House was a childrens home administered by the Assemblies of God Pentecostal Church. title: The Garden House
subtitle: This single storey, pet friendly property sleeps up to 4 adults and 2 children.
bodyContent: The Garden House living room has a working open fire which is the heart of the house during the winter months. Families particularly enjoy this feature at Christmas and New Year. The compact galley kitchen has solid granite worktops and oak cabinets. It provides a cosy space for preparing a delicious breakfast and provides all the equipment and utensils needed for you stay. Guests can also enjoy their meals in their very own private, glassed atrium. The conservatory dining room has wonderful views across the neighbouring fields and Shepherds Hut. There are two large double bedrooms – one of which has a stunning four poster bed plus extra foldaway beds for children. The family bathroom has a bath with overhead shower and the added luxury of underfloor heating. The Garden House accommodates a family of four adults and two children in total comfort. The Surrounding Area The Garden House is situated within the beautiful countryside of Castle Combe. There and many walks and bike rides around the local area. The city of Bath is also just 20 minutes drive away. We also accommodate larger parties within our other holiday homes – The Dovecote and The Stables We offer last minute discounts so please contact us for details!
tagline: This single storey, pet friendly property sleeps up to 4 adults and 2 children.

title: Humdinger Words for Whippersnappers & Guttersnipes
subtitle: A comedy-cabaret poetry party led by stage hypnotist-turned-primary school teacher, Ben Dali.
bodyContent: Framed as a school day with an unusually entertaining supply teacher, this is a fast-paced poetic journey through elements of the Key Stage2/3 curriculums. Using sharp wordplay, mind-blowing trivia, visual humour and all manner of crazy antics, 'Mr Dali' combines performance poetry, comedy and insights into his hypnotic past to celebrate language, curiosity and confidence. Set pieces include a rhyming balloon-modelling lesson, joyful exploration of English’s finest 'Humdinger Words', and genuine improvised rhyming mind-reading. Children can perform their own poems in the Show-and-Tell segment: so come prepared!

title: Agatha Christie's Towards Zero - Outdoor Theatre at Shoemakers Museum
subtitle: Street Theatre normally perform at Strode Theatre, as part of their 30th celebrations the company is performing an outdoor production as they did in 1996, this time in the grounds of the Shoemakers Museum with this Agatha Christie classic directed by Paul Townsend. bodyContent: Imagine, 1930’s England. When a house party gathers on the terrace of Gull’s Nest, the Devon clifftop home of Neville’s aunt, Lady Tressilian, British tennis player Neville Strange finds himself caught between his new wife Kay and ex wife Audrey. There is unfinished business between them and tensions are running high. Add to this a long-suffering lady’s companion, a cousin with a grudge, a mysterious stranger, and soon there will be murder. Can Inspector Leach solve the crime before another victim meets their death? A tense and absorbing thriller from the queen of crime Agatha Christie. Street Theatre normally perform at Strode Theatre, as part of their 30th celebrations the company is performing an outdoor production as they did in 1996, this time in the grounds of the Shoemakers Museum with this Agatha Christie classic directed by Paul Townsend. Bring a picnic and enjoy the show.

title: Brand New Cave Experience at Wookey Hole - up to 20% Off Tickets
subtitle: Looking for a great-value family day out this summer?
bodyContent: Looking for a great-value family day out this summer? Wookey Hole has unveiled a magical line-up of adventures beneath the Mendip Hills, including its hugely popular new immersive cave projections. Wookey Hole is a surprising, whole day experience, where families can explore the legendary caves, home to the famous Witch of Wookey Hole, before discovering a packed programme of attractions above ground. From a 4D cinema, live circus shows (during weekends and Somerset School Holidays), adventure golf and soft play to a nostalgic vintage penny arcade, there’s plenty to keep children entertained throughout the day – all within one price. A Magical Cave Experience Like Never Before Launched this May as part of a £250,000 investment, the all-new underground projection show transforms the caves into a living storybook. Using spectacular projection mapping, the natural rock formations come alive with tales of the Witch, ancient geology and daring explorers - creating a truly unforgettable, immersive adventure that families are already loving. To make visits even easier, visitors can enjoy up to 20% off tickets this summer (25 June and 2 September 2026).

title: David Harris-Heffer
subtitle: Visit Somerset reflects on the passing of David Harris-Heffer.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"581"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"The Visit Somerset team are shocked and devastated to hear of the passing of David Harris-Heffer. Our immediate thoughts are with his family and all that were close to him, both in his personal life and within his businesses.
 
David was an incredible positive energy around our work and he first approached Visit Somerset in connection with his company, Initiis, that operate a number of Vodafone shops in the county. David was extremely innovative and was continually looking at digital adoption in the visitor economy and how consumers could stay connected whilst travelling.
 
There are so many things that marked David out; astute, passionate, engaging, realistic, humorous – but above all he radiated a calm and generous spirit. A call with David always left you feeling enriched, as if a new catalyst had been lit underneath you to move forward with something.
 
His generosity wove through all his actions – the epitome of a modern management style. He was happy to invest with time and money to make things better for all.
 
David also operated outside of core business, wanting to make the world a better place. He instigated Net Zero Taunton and was so adept at softly nudging involvement and support. Last year he spent time connecting businesses in Bridgwater to align around raising the town’s profile. Earlier this year, he was piloting a Sustainable Tourism Framework, using Visit Somerset as a test, once again proving his ideals and vision.
 
David was known in many circles and we will all feel the sad effects of his passing.
 "},{"key":"NewsDate","value":"2026-04-08T00:00:00+01:00"},{"key":"NewsImage","value":"~/getmedia/6158c241-e0c8-4500-a4bf-7e434850dcc1/1583748215805.jpeg.aspx?width=200&height=200&ext=.jpeg"},{"key":"_kenticoNodeId","value":"52185"},{"key":"_kenticoClassName","value":"cms.news"}]

title: Warren Farm, Camping & Glamping
subtitle: Warren Farm, glamping, camping and yurts in Somerset wtith spectacular views across the Somerset levels.
bodyContent: CAMPING, GLAMPING & CABINS IN SOMERSET Warren Farm has been in the Small family since 1945. Cattle and sheep graze the limestone grasslands, enjoying some spectacular views across the Somerset levels . In fact, we believe Warren Farm to be one of the most beautifully located farms in the heart of Mendip Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB) because of its location, overlooking the world famous Cheddar Gorge , the highest inland cliffs in England. The animals graze on hundreds of acres of conservation land, some belonging to the National and Somerset Wildlife Trusts. Despite its inspiring size, some 1000 acres, there is much warmth in the details. We have had a lot of fun setting up the tents and wooden cabins, also in planning this unique farm holiday experience for you and we really hope you enjoy your stay with us. Details like the pigs, chickens and occasionally sheep in the animal paddocks close to the tents, and the children's play area close to the wood fired bread oven where tasty meals and treats can be cooked. At certain times there is the opportunity to take part in the pizza night (busy weekends or school holidays during April to October) just after a farm tour, everything is supplied, you just make up your pizza and James will cook it for you. You can eat well during your glamping adventure, with a selection of hampers bookable as extras. Furthermore, the farm larder is well-stocked with a range of local goodies and at times beef and lamb from the farm; you might want to indulge on some sweet marshmallows and hot chocolate at the campfire. Each tent has running water, flushing toilet, beds with duvets, sofas, crockery, cooking utensils, table and chairs and linen can be provided as an extra. The cabins have the same facilities as the tents, but also the extra touch of also having a heated shower within, adding that little touch of luxury to your stay. Lighting is by candles and oil lamps, no electric here! This is really getting away from the stresses of modern life and slipping back to an earlier time, to family time.
tagline: Warren Farm, glamping, camping and yurts in Somerset wtith spectacular views across Somerset.

title: White Hart Hotel
subtitle: An impressive Hamstone Grade II listed coaching inn dating from 1735. The White Hart Hotel is in the heart of the beautiful village of Martock, just off the A303, near Yeovil.
bodyContent: Whether for leisure or business, a friendly team will always offer you a warm welcome and will provide the highest of customer service to make sure your visit is pleasurable. The restaurant is renowned for its high quality and inventive cuisine. The chefs are creating modern and classic dishes daily, using the freshest of ingredients. The large bar has a cosy and relaxed atmosphere with Chesterfields around the fire place. The hotel is ideally situated as a base to explore the beauty of Somerset, Dorset and Devon, within a very short distance to several historical houses. A function room-skittle alley is also available in a separate building on site. The White Hart Hotel is an independent hotel, bar and restaurant owned by Peter and Isabelle Halkyard since 2003.

title: The Engine House
subtitle: Perfect for a romantic weekend away near the City of Bath, The Engine House has oodles of character with underfloor heating, a whirlpool bath and log fire.
bodyContent: Just 20 minutes from Bath, the Engine House, originally a stable, is now a romantic cottage for two. The bedroom, accessed by a cast iron spiral staircase, has an indulgent super king bed. Exposed beams and stone walls reveal much of its original character. Underfloor heating, free wi-fi, digital TV, bluetooth speaker, cotton bed linen and large white towels provide you with modern comforts. Snuggle up in front of the log burner on those long winter evenings. The engine House has stunning views along the Cam Valley that can also be enjoyed from its own garden. Downstairs the bathroom houses a whirlpool bath in which you can forget the stresses of normal life. Withy Mills Farm is approximately 1 mile from the vibrant village of Timsbury with shops, cafe and fish & chip shop. The farm is in a beautiful rural location with far reaching views across the Mendip Hills. It’s within easy access of tourist attractions as well as the cities of Bath and Wells.
tagline: Perfect for a romantic weekend away near the City of Bath

title: Chestnuts House
subtitle: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden and private off street parking.
bodyContent: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden and private off street parking. Set in the heart of the beautiful Georgian city of city. It is ideally situated off the main roads and adjacent to Henrietta park, but within a few minutes level stroll of the city centre with its many attractions, restaurants and excellent shopping centre. The House is built from natural Bath stone and has four beautifully decorated and furnished ensuite guest rooms, some with king size and wrought iron beds. Owners Toni and Dawn have created a splendid and delightful bed & breakfast with superb hospitality in a relaxing atmosphere, all the necessary ingredients for making your stay in Bath a truly memorable experience. Guests Chestnuts House has 5 individually themed ensuite rooms which can accommodate a total of 11 persons. Three Superior double bedded rooms, one family/twin room (max 3 persons) and one Classic double room Bedrooms The bedrooms have recently been refurbished to an exacting standard and have been tastefully decorated and beautifully furnished. All rooms have en suite bathrooms with bath and shower, hairdryers and large fluffy towels. The rooms have comfortable and relaxing beds with crisp cotton sheets, air con, remote flat screen colour television, radio, free wireless internet access and refreshment trays. Bathrooms All bedrooms are ensuite with large fluffy towels and White Company products. The superior & twin/family rooms are ensuite with bath & power shower. The Classic room is ensuite with walk in power shower. Kitchen Enjoy your inclusive breakfast in our light and airy dining room overlooking the garden. During the summer months breakfast can be served al fresco. Our breakfast includes both organic and local produce. As well as the traditional English breakfast, we offer smoked salmon with scrambled eggs and homemade blinis, poached buttered kippers (smoked haddock with poached eggs). There is also an extensive buffet table with fresh fruit salad, freshly baked pastries, cereals, yoghurts. We are happy to cater for special dietary requirements. Entertainment The Lounge has a large flat screen Television with both Sky & BT Sport Channels. Free internet wi-fi is available throughout Outside Chestnuts House is situated in a residential street with a small private walled garden for guests to enjoy and just 10 minutes walk to the centre. General Points Chestnuts House is situated in a residential street with private off street parking and just 10 minutes level walk to the city centre. Parking Chestnuts House has both private off street parking and parking permits available for Guests to use. This service is free of charge. Smoking Chestnuts is a non smoking establishment Children Family room can accommodate up to 3 guests. Children of all ages are welcome. Pets Unfortunately Chestnuts House does not accept pets
tagline: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden

title: Magique
subtitle: Magique Presents: Fire and Water - A Spellbinding Family Magic & Illusion Show at Wookey Hole
bodyContent: Magique Presents: Fire and Water - A Spellbinding Family Magic & Illusion Show at Wookey Hole Magique returns to Wookey Hole presenting their magic and illusion show "Fire and Water". Performing 9 times a year in the Wookey Hole Theatre, witness the ultimate showdown of fire and water - and prepare to be spellbound! A Magical Experience Like No Other Fire rages. Water rises. Two unstoppable forces collide in a battle of power, mystery, and illusion. title: Declaration of Independence on display
subtitle: See a rare original 1776 Declaration of Independence on display in England for the first time during the 250th anniversary year. Explore immersive displays, exhibitions, talks and events as part of America 250 at American Museum & Gardens..
bodyContent: This summer, American Museum & Gardens presents America 250 - a season of exhibitions, events and cultural experiences marking 250 years since the founding of the United States. At the heart of the programme is a rare original 1776 Dunlap printing of the Declaration of Independence, now on display in England for the first time during the 250th anniversary year. Only 26 Dunlap copies survive worldwide, and this is the only known example to have been intercepted by British forces during the American Revolution and later annotated by British government officials. Visitors can follow a specially curated trail through the Museum’s historic Manor House, where immersive interpretation and displays explore the people, ideas and objects that shaped the founding of the United States, culminating in the signing of the Declaration of Independence. Displayed alongside the Declaration is a specially commissioned film from the Museum of the American Revolution in Philadelphia, offering further insight into the document and its enduring significance.
tagline: This summer, American Museum & Gardens presents America 250

title: The Dovecote
subtitle: If Contemporary Loft Living is your style – then The Dovecote at Fosse Farmhouse is the perfect retreat! Our large open plan first floor space has a living/dining area, galley kitchen, double bed and two single beds.
bodyContent: The Dovecote offers an economic yet beautiful place to stay for up to four guests – two adults and two children enjoying a wonderful family holidays in The Cotswolds. Our large, first floor space has an open plan living/dining area, galley kitchen, double bed and two single beds. There is also a separate bathroom with a bath and overhead shower, basin and WC. The entrance hall has a built in wardrobe to store all your ‘Country Living’ essentials – Wellington boots, coats and umbrellas. The Dovecote garden area is located just beside the property. Here you can picnic and play and even barbeque, weather permitting! Family holidays can be great fun even in the rain. As well as the garden area, guests enjoy the charming Juliet Balcony that overlooks our vintage Shepherds’ Hut in the field behind. Children love staying here as we have a unique twinkling light feature in the ceiling. The Local Area All of our properties are situated just walking distance from the Cotswolds village of Castle Combe. They are also just a 20 minute drive from the city of Bath and Bristol. The lovely countryside where we are located offers some fabulous walking areas and places to cycle together with Horse riding Stables and Go Karting nearby. The Dovecote can be hired together with any of our other properties to offer space for up to 16 guests . This can be increased to up to 22 guests when using rooms from our BnB. Family reunions, wedding guests and even hen parties can all be catered for. The Garden House sleeps 4 adults and 2 children in two ensuite bedrooms. The Stables sleeps 6 guests in 3 ensuite bedrooms. All are also pet friendly. Please contact us for last minute discount rates!
tagline: Contemporary Loft Living The Dovecote at Fosse Farmhouse

title: The Claridge Lecture – Professor David Olusoga OBE
subtitle: The American Museum & Gardens welcomes back Professor David Olusoga OBE, for a special talk about the history of the Revolution and the impact on the Declaration of Independence.
bodyContent: 2026 marks the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, and the American Museum & Gardens is delighted to welcome back Professor David Olusoga OBE to deliver this year's Claridge Lecture. In this landmark anniversary year, he will deliver a custom lecture exploring the history of the Revolution on the anniversary of the Declaration. Taking place at the Guildhall in Bath City centre, this event forms part of the Museum’s year-long America 250 programme, commemorating the anniversary by exploring our shared UK–US history and celebrating American arts, artistry and culture. Please note that this event is taking place at the Guildhall, High Street, Bath, BA1 5AW.

title: Monochrome + Override + Slighted Hand
subtitle: Join Monochrome, Override, and Slighted Hand for an energetic evening of alternative music - part of our summer series of free, or pay-what-you-can, Electric Bar shows.
bodyContent: Monochrome: Since forming, Monochrome's force within the metal sphere of the Southwest has been unstoppable and irreplaceable. Brutality and beauty coexist in a distinct blend of crushing metal and ethereal layering, weaving a sound that is as heavy as it is haunting. Their debut EP, Haunted Faith and Hidden Trust, has introduced the world to their deep, dark sound, backed by a sold-out release show. The E.P. challenges listeners’ expectations and pushes the elements of the music to the absolute extreme, striking a unique balance between the past, present, and future of metal. 2025 was a triumphant year for Monochrome: they completed a national tour supporting Apathy UK, were picked up as newcomers at Bloodstock and Hammerdown Festival, and released their debut EP. 2026 will see Monochrome expand on their already distinct sound, delving further into the contrasting elements that make them special. Override: Override is a 3-piece heavy beat-down hardcore band from the Southwest, currently playing shows while working on an upcoming EP. Expect closed-fist mosh hardcore. FFO: Sanction, Long Goodbye, and Final Resting Place. Slighted Hand: Hailing from South Wales, Slighted Hand is an evil hardcore band.

title: Gorge View Cottage
subtitle: Gorge View Cottage is an award-winning sustainable four-star self-catering holiday cottage for two, nestling in the foothills of the Mendip Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.
bodyContent: Gorge View Cottage is an award-winning sustainable four-star self-catering holiday cottage for two, nestling in the foothills of the Mendip Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty . Originally an old gardeners cottage, it was recently fully renovated to exacting environmental standards whilst maintaining its natural charm, with attention paid to sustainability and comfort throughout. For anyone needing a gentle break from the pressures of life Gorge View Cottage has it all; a haven for walkers and nature lovers, with easy access to stunning walks around the Mendip hills and the famous gorge . The caves, shops, pubs, restaurants and cafés: all just a few minutes' walk away. The immediate village boasts a number of unique attractions: the UK’s largest gorge and highest inland cliffs. The caves including Britain’s most beautiful stalactite cavern. Here Britain’s oldest human skeleton was found: Cheddar Man, over 9,000 years old. And Cheddar is the home of the world famous cheese and you can still see it made in the last production facility in the gorge. The cottage provides an excellent base for exploring further afield with Somerset being an extraordinary county of variety and contrast: hills and levels , coast and moors, heritage and history , mythology and magic. Try Glastonbury , home of the famous festival and also the Tor , ancient Abbey and quirky shops. Or the small city of Wells with its beautiful Cathedral , lovely markets, and friendly cafes. Wookey Hole Caves , the Somerset levels and coast at Brean Down. All of this within 15 miles. For cities try Bristol, once England’s second city and now famous for its links with Brunel including the floating harbour, suspension Bridge and the SS Great Britain. Or the UNESCO heritage site that is Bath with glorious Georgian architecture, Roman Baths, abbey and narrow arcades of shops. But you don’t have to get out and about. The cottage itself is a perfect retreat: cool, light and airy in summer, with under-floor heating to keep the cottage snug when temperatures drop. And in the colder months the log-burning stove is perfect for cosy evenings. Outside you can idle on the patio catching the evening sun, or wander in to the large main house garden, run on organic and permaculture principles and an accredited Wildlife Garden. If you want to cycle but don’t have bikes then we’re happy to lend you a couple, ideal for wheeling off down the Strawberry Line.
tagline: Gorge View Cottage is an award-winning sustainable four-star self-catering holiday cottage

title: The Dairy Cottage
subtitle: A former milking parlour that has been tastefully renovated into a spacious family holiday cottage sleeping 5 + cot.
bodyContent: A former milking parlour that has been tastefully renovated into a spacious family holiday cottage sleeping 4 + cot. Graded with 4 stars The Dairy Cottage offers comfortable accommodation with the added benefit of being all over one level, lending itself to the less able and families with small children. Enter the property directly into a very large kitchen diner finished in light colours with fully fitted pine cupboards and wood flooring. A farmhouse table seating 6, sits central in the kitchen and all the mod cons expected have been provided including dishwasher, washing machine and stainless steel oven, hob and extractor. The lounge offers a comfortable area to relax and unwind with a glass door to rear of property. With wooden flooring, rugs and quality soft furnishings. A freeview television, DVD player and CD unit are provided for your entertainment. There are two bedrooms in the Dairy, a twin with en-suite and a double with its own bathroom. All finished in light colours and matching Sanderson fabrics and throws. Fitted wardrobes are provided with a range of pine bedroom furniture. The bathrooms are newly installed for 2015 and fully tiled with bath, shower, WC and sink. Outside, The Dairy has ramp access front and rear. It has its own little patio area as well as being just a few steps away from our paddock with play equipment, and open air solar heated swimming pool. There is plenty of on-site parking available and our own little farm shop/butchery for all your breakfast needs!
tagline: A former milking parlour that has been tastefully renovated into a spacious family holiday cottage

title: Cranleigh

bodyContent: Dating from 1897 Cranleigh was once a Victorian family home. Cranleigh can offer you a step back into Victorian style but with all the comforts of modern living. With 10 individually furnished en-suite rooms with many period features offering every comfort for your stay. Cranleigh is ideally located in a quiet residential area – away from the noise but just over 1.5 miles from the centre of Bath. With FREE PARKING and easy access to the city. Breakfast At Cranleigh breakfast is served in the comfort of your own room. You can choose delivery between 7:45 am to 9:30 am each morning. Since introduction, earlier this year customers have raved about our in-room breakfast hamper. Our ‘In Room’ hamper is a continental style breakfast including a selection of toasted bread, preserves, fresh fruit, juice, yoghurts, selection of Kellogg’s cereals, creamy porridge and choice of tea or coffee. When choosing to enjoy your breakfast in your room this will be delivered in a hamper to your room. Honesty Bar & Coffee Station We have a range of reasonably priced beers, wines, soft drinks, cakes and snacks available for you to purchase to enjoy in your room. title: Captain Fantastic and the Rocketman Band
subtitle: The unparalleled, authentic, see-it-to-believe-it Sir Elton John tribute experience returns to Komedia Bath, following a sold-out show.
bodyContent: Featuring brand-new production, Captain Fantastic and the Rocketman Band perform Elton’s greatest songs and most-loved hits, all centred around a real grand piano. World-class musicianship, timeless songs, and striking new costumes combine with modern staging to capture the spirit and spectacle of Elton at the height of his powers. With some of Elton’s most iconic costumes faithfully recreated, this is an authentic, uplifting show - and a night to remember.

title: Dunster Castle Experience Days - A Morning with the Head Gardener
subtitle: An exclusive chance to spend the morning with Dunster Castle's Head Gardener, including a bespoke tour, and afternoon tea at the Watermill Tearoom
bodyContent: Spend the morning with Dunster Castle's Head Gardener, James Cordingley. Responsible for the care and vision of Dunster’s 18 acres of historic and subtropical gardens, James brings more than 18 years of horticultural experience- this special event is your chance to explore the gardens with the person who knows them best. The morning begins with refreshments and an introductory talk, where James will share insights into the castle’s rich horticultural history, its unusual microclimate, and the challenges and joys of caring for such a diverse landscape. You’ll then set out on an exclusive guided tour, including access to areas of the garden not normally open to visitors. This is a rare opportunity to delve deeper into Dunster Castle’s remarkable plant collections, long-standing garden design principles, and the unique subtropical environment that shapes them. Once the tour is over, you'll head down to the Watermill Tearoom for a delicious Afternoon Tea. James will accompany you and will be on hand to chat and answer questions in a relaxed and friendly setting. Tickets are £45 per person, pre-booking is essential as places are limited. This event takes place 10:30am-1pm.
tagline: An exclusive chance to spend the morning with Dunster Castle's Head Gardener

title: Declaration of Independence on display
subtitle: See a rare original 1776 Declaration of Independence on display in England for the first time during the 250th anniversary year. Explore immersive displays, exhibitions, talks and events as part of America 250 at American Museum & Gardens..
bodyContent: This summer, American Museum & Gardens presents America 250 - a season of exhibitions, events and cultural experiences marking 250 years since the founding of the United States. At the heart of the programme is a rare original 1776 Dunlap printing of the Declaration of Independence, now on display in England for the first time during the 250th anniversary year. Only 26 Dunlap copies survive worldwide, and this is the only known example to have been intercepted by British forces during the American Revolution and later annotated by British government officials. Visitors can follow a specially curated trail through the Museum’s historic Manor House, where immersive interpretation and displays explore the people, ideas and objects that shaped the founding of the United States, culminating in the signing of the Declaration of Independence. Displayed alongside the Declaration is a specially commissioned film from the Museum of the American Revolution in Philadelphia, offering further insight into the document and its enduring significance.
tagline: This summer, American Museum & Gardens presents America 250

bodyContent: Discover the stinky, epic, dangerous world of our prehistoric ancestors - and the secrets of Stone Age survival at Cheddar Gorge and Caves this summer! Stay Alive’ • 1pm & 4pm - Ancient Remedies: ‘Healing plants and Stone Age secrets’ And keep a look out for Marmalade, our marvellous mammoth mascot; he’ll be doing meet and greets in front of Gough’s Café each day. title: Greyfield Farm Cottages
subtitle: Greyfield Farm Cottages is situated between the Cities of Bristol, Wells & Bath
bodyContent: Greyfield Farm Cottages is situated between the Cities of Bristol, Wells & Bath Self Catering Cottages and Serviced Holiday Breaks are available all year round in our five attractive on-site stone cottages, each one is unique, double glazed, centrally heated, fully equipped, comfortably furnished with TV/DVD/Xbox, log fire/burner and Free Wi-Fi Internet Access. Luxurious duvets and pillows along with quality linen and towels are provided in each cottage. Each cottage also has its own garden/patio area for having breakfast or enjoying that relaxing late afternoon drink. Our Site is located in a private, peaceful 3.5 acre setting close to Bath, Bristol & Wells and overlooking the Mendip Hills (an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty). It is an ideal location for visiting Somerset (heart of the West Country). Fed up with every high street being the same? – Our local market towns ( Frome , Glastonbury , Bradford-on-Avon) along with the Cities of Bath, Bristol & Wells have many small and independent shops, fairs & markets – explore their nooks and crannies and uncover those hidden treasures, locate that bargain. Whilst you are with us enjoy our Local Country Pubs, Cafes and Restaurants or bring home and try some of the fantastic fresh & local produce which you can find in the local shops, farm shops and markets. Walk on the Mendip Hills, enjoy our Local Ancient Woodland, explore the Somerset Levels or visit Capability Browns Stourhead. Have a fun day out visiting some of the attractions – The Pier at Weston-Super-Mare , Bristol Zoo, Noah’s Ark, Avon Valley Country Park, Wookey Hole , @Bristol, Bristol Aquarium and Longleat are all worth a visit. Afterwards you can kick back and make free use of Our Facilities, including our Hot Tub, Free Wi-Fi, Finish Sauna, Mini-Gym, Barbeque Hut, Boules Court and Information Hut with Book/DVD collection. Or pamper yourself at the world renowned Thermae Spa in Bath Self Catering Cottages and Fully Serviced Holiday Apartments with Fully Flexible Booking (No Change Over Days and Short Breaks are available All Year Round).

title: The Terrace Lodge Hotel
subtitle: Set within a beautifully refurbished 18th century building, The Terrace Lodge Hotel offers comfortable, modern accommodation in the heart of Yeovil.
bodyContent: The Terrace Lodge provides 30 non-smoking, en suite bedrooms, with both a bath and power shower, flat-screen digital TV with 33 free digital TV and radio channels, and free wireless internet access. City Lodge has a 24-hour reception for your convenience. The property is within 10 minutes' walk from all that the town has to offer, including restaurants and cafes, for breakfast, lunch and evening meals. Guests can benefit from a discounted gym day pass at Nuffield gym, located 1 minute walk from the hotel. Public parking is available at a surcharge and is opposite to the hotel. Situated in South Somerset, on the Somerset/Dorset border, Yeovil is on the A30 and A37 roads, providing easy access to a number of beautiful villages and English Heritage sites. It is also the ideal base for day trips to the Fleet Air Arm, Wookey Hole, Glastonbury Abbey, Sherborn Castle, and many more. We speak your language! Hotel Rooms: 30

title: The Dairy
subtitle: The Dairy is one of two beautifully converted barns which share an enclosed garden, is south facing with views along a small tranquil valley.
bodyContent: The Dairy | Park Farm Country Cottages near Chew Magna is one of two beautifully converted barns on a working farm with a private terrace and a shared enclosed garden with lovely interrupted views across open countryside and along a small valley. The Dairy, formally the milking parlour is light and airy with double sets of south facing French doors opening onto a large private terrace with quality wooden table, chairs and parasol. The cottage has been equipped to a high standard with slate flooring and toasty under floor heating, a dishwasher, washer/dryer, microwave etc. The bathroom has a powerful shower and a heated towel rail. WiFi, Flatscreen TV and DVD, Freeview. There are 2 steps within the cottage and 4 steps down to the front door. https://www.parkfarm-countrycottages.co.uk/luxury-holiday-cottages-bristol-the-barn

title: Fionn Regan
subtitle: The release of Fionn Regan's remarkable debut, The End of History, left music critics and the songwriting world stunned by extraordinary depth and prowess of his writing.
bodyContent: He has since toured the world, received numerous awards for his contribution to the arts and Irish literature, been nominated for a Mercury Prize, and released a further six albums. Fionn's unique poetic voice has earned him many fans among fellow creatives, with Oscar-winning actor Cillian Murphy featuring alongside Fionn in the music video for The Meetings of the Waters, and Bon Iver sampling Fionn's song Abacus in 0000 Million, featured on Grammy-nominated album 22, A Million. In 2024, Fionn released his seventh studio album, O Avalanche - a new venture into a brighter, sunnier, more dream-like setting, with music reflecting the Mediterranean island where the songs were written. It's our absolute pleasure to welcome such a gifted and visionary songwriter for his debut show in Bath.

subtitle: Wimbleball Lake is the perfect place to visit this summer! Enjoy an unforgettable family adventure, jam-packed with new experiences.
bodyContent: We have an action-packed activity programme suitable for all ages and abilities. Activities include paddleboarding, kayaking, canoeing, sailing, high ropes or eFoiling. Or go the whole hog and sign up for children's Multi-Activity Week to enjoy a whole range of different activities! We are also running a range of two-day RYA sailing courses for children and adults. Hire a variety of watersports equipment, launch your own kit or learn something new by taking part in a bespoke instructor-led session. Wimbleball is also a place where you can relax and observe the resident wildlife, somewhere to stretch your legs and embrace a moment of calm or a scenic retreat where you can enjoy a well-deserved café treat.

title: The Songs of Joni Mitchell feat. Jesca Hoop, Lail Arad, Richard Sears on piano + Special Guest Naima Bock
subtitle: Celebrating one of the greatest songwriters of all time, through the unique voices of the artists she continues to inspire.
bodyContent: Following a revered debut at the Roundhouse in 2024, two sold out tours and widespread critical acclaim, The Songs of Joni Mitchell returns for some very special shows and festivals in 2026. Jesca Hoop & Lail Arad, acclaimed singer-songwriters in their own right, will perform intimate interpretations of their favourite Joni Mitchell songs. They’ll be joined by special guest performers at every port, each bringing something new to Joni’s vast catalogue. Previous guests have included Kate Stables (This Is The Kit), Vashti Bunyan, Simon Armitage, Lisa Hannigan, Gail Ann Dorsey, Rachel Sermanni and Sam Amidon. Originally conceived and curated by Lail Arad to mark Joni Mitchell’s 80th birthday, the show was described as “a perfect celebration of Joni Mitchell” (Get In Her Ears), packed with “heartfelt and intricate performances”. Jesca Hoop, just a few months prior, presented Legend: The Joni Mitchell Story, the award-winning 6-part BBC Radio documentary and podcast about the life of Joni Mitchell, lending further gravitas to the event. Ahead of their last tour Jesca, Lail and Kate Stables released a companion EP on Small Matter Records: The Songs Of Joni Mitchell Vol. 1. These up close and personal recordings offer fresh interpretations of four treasured Joni songs and provide a lovely hint of what to expect on stage. “Such a stand-out show.” - Cerys Matthews “Their voices individually are just perfection. title: Brand New Cave Experience at Wookey Hole - up to 20% Off Tickets
subtitle: Looking for a great-value family day out this summer?
bodyContent: Looking for a great-value family day out this summer? Wookey Hole has unveiled a magical line-up of adventures beneath the Mendip Hills, including its hugely popular new immersive cave projections. Wookey Hole is a surprising, whole day experience, where families can explore the legendary caves, home to the famous Witch of Wookey Hole, before discovering a packed programme of attractions above ground. From a 4D cinema, live circus shows (during weekends and Somerset School Holidays), adventure golf and soft play to a nostalgic vintage penny arcade, there’s plenty to keep children entertained throughout the day – all within one price. A Magical Cave Experience Like Never Before Launched this May as part of a £250,000 investment, the all-new underground projection show transforms the caves into a living storybook. Using spectacular projection mapping, the natural rock formations come alive with tales of the Witch, ancient geology and daring explorers - creating a truly unforgettable, immersive adventure that families are already loving. To make visits even easier, visitors can enjoy up to 20% off tickets this summer (25 June and 2 September 2026).
tagline: Looking for a great-value family day out this summer?

title: Cheddar Visitor Information Centre open every day
subtitle: Cheddar Gorge Visitor Information Centre (VIC) is now open every day right through until end October, 10.30-3.30 during all weekends, school holidays and half terms, but mornings only on weekdays in term time.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"577"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"Cheddar Gorge Visitor Information Centre (VIC) is now open every day right through until end October, 10.30-3.30 during all weekends, school holidays and half terms, but mornings only on weekdays in term time.  The VIC has made a good start to the 2026 tourist season with visitor numbers holding up well, despite poor weather in February and early March, and the volunteers who run the facility are benefiting from improvements to the building carried out over the past few months.

As well as enjoying the facilities in the gorge many visitors come ready to tackle the circular three and a half mile clifftop walk, which gives magnificent views of the gorge itself and across the Somerset Levels.  The walk has been much improved by work on the path over the past year from the landowners National Trust and Longleat Estates.

The Lower Gorge too has had a welcome facelift with Longleat creating a new pedestrian paved area where Cox’s Mill once stood, opening up the view to Lion Rock and the cliffs.  In addition, Cheddar Parish Council has taken over the public toilets from Somerset Council and upgraded them significantly to provide excellent modern conveniences suitable for visitors and locals alike.

bodyContent: Set above Frome, the house is an eight-minute walk along the riverbank to the beautiful artisan centre. The split-level guest annexe has two south-facing double bedrooms and a sitting room with dining/work table, a bathroom and separate loo. Downstairs is a small kitchen. There is a single sofa bed in the sitting room for families whose children don’t wish to share the double bed in the second double bedroom. The garden wraps around the house and there is an area of the terrace/patio which is just for our annexe guests, complete with table and chairs. Dogs can roam the whole garden but it is not suitable for small children as the house is set into the hillside. The property is a short drive from some lovely walks and makes an ideal retreat both for a family trip or a romantic break. The annexe was the original 1940s house and has its own entrance, and we live in the extension that was added on seven years ago. Please note that your space is right next to ours, although there are double doors between the two parts of the house.

title: Peat & Diesel

title: Mike Rice – Cruel Little Man
subtitle: There's a cruelty to Mike Rice, a wickedness. In this show Mike talks about doing psychedelics with his brother, an entanglement with a Spanish Sausage Dog named Nino, and many other such rotten adventures.
bodyContent: 'A phenomenal wordsmith, and world class raconteur' - ★★★★½ Chortle 'Ireland has yet another legendary comedian' - Dan Nightingale About Mike: Irish farmer’s son and general Nasty Character Mike Rice is one of Ireland and the UK’s fastest rising comedy stars. Having started comedy in 2016 Mike has amassed a large online following from podcast and stand up clips, regularly getting millions of views on various platforms. Mike began stand up comedy in Chicago, where within two years he was working regularly at the most prestigious clubs in the city, including The Laugh Factory. He has since returned home because his mother made him, and has been quickly rising in the Irish and European scene, playing regularly in major clubs in Dublin and London, where he won the King Gong at the Comedy Store. Mike brought his first solo show The Best Boy in Ireland to the Edinburgh Fringe Festival 2018, in what was a sold-out run, and performed that same show to sold-out rooms at the Perth Fringe Festival in 2019. As well as co-hosting Mike & Vittorio’s Guide to Parenting with Vittorio Angelone, and Big Mike and The Chief with Rob Moriarty, Mike has appeared multiple times on smash hit podcast Have a Word, and released his first comedy special in October 2023.
tagline: 'A phenomenal wordsmith, and world class raconteur' -

title: The Circus Apartment
subtitle: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses.
bodyContent: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the secluded private garden to the rear. With the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minutes walk The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the secluded private garden to the rear. With the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minutes walk. This contemporary apartment, in a warm palate of chocolate, plum and biscuit throughout, has undergone several transformations in its lifetime yet has retained all its period charm. The large sitting and dining room with sash windows overlooking two aspects of The Circus has two French style velvet sofas by a decorative fireplace. There is a TV with Blue Ray DVD and a separate radio with I-pod docking. A dining table seats four and a French style dresser contains crockery, cutlery and a selection of novels, films and games. The neat fitted period kitchen has an electric hob and oven, a microwave, a large fridge/freezer, and a dishwasher.. A large mirrored lobby before the bedroom which has fitted wardrobes and shelving leads to the spacious and comfortable bedroom which has a 6′ bed, a fitted wardrobe, a dressing table with storage and a tallboy and a cupboard containing a washer/dryer machine. A radio/alarm with I-pod docking is provided. The contemporary bathroom has smart cappuccino coloured tiling and contains a double ended bath with shower over, a hand basin with lots of storage under and a WC. The apartment has gas central heating, hair dryer, iron, microwave, dishwasher, towels and toiletries. A Free car parking permit is available as is free internet access.

bodyContent: Concierge Presents An Evening With Jim Hamilton and Andy Goode from the Rugby Pod. Join us for a chaotic evening of laughter and razor-sharp humour with former rugby internationals Andy Goode and Jim Hamilton. Their hilarious and informative live show, The Rugby Pod the world’s most popular rugby podcast offers a unique behind-the-scenes insight into the modern game. Jim Hamilton played for top clubs including Leicester Tigers, Edinburgh Rugby, Gloucester Rugby, Montpellier, Saracens as well as 63 international caps for Scotland. His leadership abilities shone through when he captained Gloucester Rugby for the 2012–13 season, guiding the team through some intense matches. Andy Goode had an 18-year professional career playing over 400 games and scoring over 4,000 points for Leicester Tigers, Saracens, Worcester Warriors, Wasps and Newcastle Falcons, CA Brive in France’s Top 14 and for Super Rugby’s Sharks in South Africa. Goode also represented England 17 times between 2005 and 2009 scoring 107 points. He is the second highest scorer of all time in Premiership Rugby, having previously been the record holder, winning five Premiership titles and two European Cups all with Leicester. title: ZRI Cellar Sessions
subtitle: Classical and folk music intermingle, inspired by a 19th-century Viennese tavern where musicians from all scenes would meet after hours, and the boundaries between genres became blurry in tandem with the flow of beer and wine
bodyContent: Classical and folk music intermingle, inspired by a 19th-century Viennese tavern where musicians from all scenes would meet after hours, and the boundaries between genres became blurry in tandem with the flow of beer and wine . Prepare to dance, laugh, holler, and maybe even shed a tear with this mixed program which includes Bach to Donna Summer. ZRI's Cellar Sessions re-creates the atmosphere of the Red Hedgehog Tavern in Vienna from which the band takes its name. Schubert and Brahms were both fascinated by Hungarian ‘Gypsy-band’ music and it became as fashionable as the waltz in Vienna, with one of the tunes included here still part of the standard repertory in an arrangement by Brahms. ”Consummate virtuosity, magic and passion.” (Royal Albert Hall).
tagline: Classical and folk music intermingle, inspired by a 19th-century Viennese tavern

title: A Musical Journey Across America: Adrian Cox with New Orleans - Ragtime, Jazz and Blues
subtitle: As part of our year-long America 250 programme, marking 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, join us at our opening night with a celebration of 'The Crescent City’ New Orleans, the birthplace of Jazz.
bodyContent: As part of our year-long America 250 programme, marking 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, join us at our opening night with a celebration of 'The Crescent City’ New Orleans, the birthplace of Jazz. From South Rampart Street to Storyville via Basin Street and the Tango Belt. Soak up the infectious sounds and rhythms of Ragtime, Jazz and Blues, created in the musical genre melting pot by the giants such as Jelly Roll Morton, King Oliver, Louis Armstrong and Sidney Bechet. Clare Teal welcomes internationally acclaimed jazz clarinettist Adrian Cox, one of the leading exponents of the New Orleans clarinet who has a huge knowledge of the music and players of the era. His unrivalled feel and virtuosity for the music he plays has led to concerts with the biggest names in Jazz including Wynton Marsalis. “Exhilarating and always exciting, Adrian lights up any audience with his infectious brand of hot jazz – energetic, engaging and great fun” Clare Teal The performance will take place on the terrace lawn, don’t forget to bring a chair or a blanket to sit on, there are a limited amount of terrace seating tickets too. A bar and BBQ will be available so you can have supper and a truly relaxing evening in the stunning setting overlooking Limpley Stoke Valley.
tagline: As part of our year-long America 250 programme

title: Caitlin Moran: How To Be Hopeful
bodyContent: ‘No one’s inventing good, new futures any more,’ I say to my husband, Pete. ‘Everyone seems resigned to accepting that things will be dreadful. I can’t bear it. I need us to do something different.’ One morning, Caitlin Moran woke up - and realised that she had reached Peak Despair. And she’s not alone - in a world of worsening news, online fist-fights, and filthy rivers, it’s hard not to feel, well, terrible. Of course, in books, and movies, when the heroine faces such a crisis, she makes a seismic life-change: moving to a remote, ramshackle farmhouse; walking an ancient, 600-mile pathway; or reconnecting with her primal, joyful self by adopting a baby hawk, or hare. But Caitlin’s new book, How to be Hopeful, is not that kind of book. She tried - but it turns out remote Welsh farmhouses are really expensive. No one with a job can walk 600 miles. And it’s incredibly hard to get access to baby hawks in North London. Instead, Caitlin decided to go on … a domestic quest. To see if she could stay in the same house, in the same neighbourhood, and the same awful modern world - but try to make better days. She left 800,000 followers on social media; eschewed 24/7 rolling news for local newspapers; and sat on buses without headphones, to start listening to what people are really saying.
