title: Devonshire House
subtitle: Established in a building dating back to 1880 and once used as a Victorian Grocers shop.
bodyContent: ⭐ Book Direct for Reward Card Offers Established in a building dating back to 1880 and once used as a Victorian Grocers shop, Devonshire House has been fully renovated into the stylish Bed and Breakfast it is today. Within a twenty minute walk of the city, on a major bus route into the city and with plenty of free on street parking, Devonshire House offers a convenient base to explore the city and surrounds. Local owners Chris and Louise are on hand to give as much or as little advice as you want, to make your stay even more enjoyable. Each room is individually decorated, en suite, with tv and dvd player, beverage tray, fluffy white towels and plump feather duvets (do tell us before your stay if you need hypo allergenic). Two doubles, a twin and a triple bedded room, plus a holiday cottage which sleeps up to four are available. A lounge is for guest use, with squashy sofas, up to date magazines and the local paper, imbibe in a Harveys Bristol Cream sherry with our compliments and relax after your day or plan the next one with all the information and leaflets to hand. The choice to book a room only rate or breakfast included, is yours, breakfast is served in the light and airy breakfast room between 8 am and 9 am. A buffet is laid out, with juice, yoghurt, fresh fruit, cereals and a selection of breads and jams for you to help yourself and then either a traditional Full English breakfast or smoked salmon and scrambled eggs can be pre chosen, along with freshly brewed coffee or a pot of tea from the selection available.
tagline: Established in a building dating back to 1880 and once used as a Victorian Grocers shop.

title: Nick Cope Family Show
subtitle: Come and join Nick Cope for a delightful fun filled musical hour featuring all your favourite Nick Cope hits and more.
bodyContent: Nick has been writing and recording his beautiful and totally unique songs for children and their families for over 10 years, he performs with his guitar and stunning animations to sell-out crowds all over the country. His fanatical following of little and not so little fans has grown immeasurably over the last couple of years due to the phenomenal success of the CBeebies show ‘Nick Cope’s Popcast’. Nick has a magical way of reaching into people’s hearts, igniting children’s imagination in an organic, unpatronizing, educational and fun way. With his charming songs and humor Nick engages, entertains, and enthralls all generations. Nick’s live performances are legendary. If you haven’t heard his songs or seen his shows before, come along and find out what you’ve been missing.

title: Clare Teal Hits the Road
subtitle: As part of our year-long America 250 programme, join us on this special Independence Day performance marking 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, with a celebration of Tin Pan Alley and the Great American Songbook.
bodyContent: As part of our year-long America 250 programme, join us on this special Independence Day performance marking 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, with a celebration of Tin Pan Alley and the Great American Songbook. Get your kicks from Chicago to L.A. with The Clare Teal 5! Join their uplifting road trip across America stopping wherever the mood feels right - jazz, blues, swing, country, latin, rock 'n' roll, R&B, salsa, alongside hit songs by great writers made famous by trail blazing artists. Award winning jazz singer and broadcaster Clare Teal with special guest Tommy Blaize put their own spin on some of the greatest songs ever written sharing stories and anecdotes of the people who created and performed them. Tommy Blaize is used to entertaining millions of people on a weekly basis as lead singer of the BBC Strictly Come Dancing band, his powerful yet sensitive performances have helped create some of the most memorable TV moments of recent times. Singing live to a studio audience every week, Tommy is the man with the golden pipes whose unique, soulful sound is etched in the public consciousness. The performance will take place on the terrace lawn, don’t forget to bring a chair or a blanket to sit on, there are a limited amount of terrace seating tickets too. A bar and BBQ will be available so you can have supper and a truly relaxing evening in the stunning setting overlooking Limpley Stoke Valley.

title: Devin Townsend – Metamorphosis – Solo
subtitle: Forging a career over four decades in countless genres, Devin Townsend has reached cult status in the progressive-metal world for his polymathic talent and continual pushing of the envelope.
bodyContent: In 2025, after a career including iconic performances at Royal Albert Hall and multiple world tours, Townsend announced an indefinite hiatus from touring. Having then delivered the live debut in Groningen of ‘The Moth’, his most ambitious work to date, it was only natural to need a break. Townsend returned home to complete the studio album of ‘The Moth’ (out 29th May on InsideOut Music) and to rebuild himself in preparation for the next stage. According to Townsend: “The Moth feels like the culmination of all my musical experiences and my journey in life so far. And as ‘The Moth’ spreads its wings, I’m also aware of how much I’ve changed, and consequently how much remains to be expressed.” He continues: “The making of this album took me on quite a journey of self-exploration. This opportunity to get out there, tell my story with this renewed clarity, celebrate my entire anthology of music across a variety of projects (and the stories behind them) offers an opportunity to connect with the audience who made this all happen and do what I love in the process: Play music. I’ve been told ‘The Moth’ seems like my life’s work and I would agree, though it was a life that no longer exists. Moving into this new life is the path now, and these events offer an introduction to that.” This welcome change of heart should appeal to a legion of loyal fans worldwide, who now have the opportunity to watch Devin Townsend perform

title: The Billiard Room
subtitle: The Billiard Room is an historic, and quirky building set in the grounds of The Close, an 18th century house facing the duck pond, on the village green, in Biddestone.
bodyContent: The Billiard Room is an historic, and quirky building set in the grounds of The Close, an 18th century house facing the duck pond, on the village green, in Biddestone. It is ideally placed to visit the World Heritage City of Bath, and to explore the historic villages and countryside of Wiltshire & the Cotswolds.Originally a blanket factory, and subsequently the village school, it was converted into a billiard room by the owner of The Close in the early part of the twentieth century. It has recently undergone sympathetic restoration to create a unique living space, with a four-poster bed, living area and breakfast bar. The building is entered through a grand, old oak door, has a magnificent beamed vaulted roof, and a large stone fireplace with a wood burner. The property is equipped with a wardrobe & chest of drawers, a large leather sofa & TV, and a freestanding cooking range with electric oven & ceramic hob. A full range of crockery, glasses , cutlery & cooking utensils are provided. There is a separate utility area, providing a fridge & sink, together with a shower room & WC. Guests can wander through the orchard with several fruit trees, and the 2 acre paddock, home to the donkeys, Ossie and Bertie. This joins the village playing fields, and leads to attractive walks on adjoining farmland and woods. Residents have a parking area on the gravel drive of The Close. The wood store provides a free supply of logs, and access to a wheelie bin.
tagline: The Billiard Room is an historic, and quirky building set in the grounds of The Close

title: Dorian House
subtitle: A warm welcome awaits you at Dorian House, a stylish Victorian villa with stunning decor, eclectic Asian antiques and contemporary art collection.
bodyContent: A warm welcome awaits you at Dorian House, a stylish Victorian villa with stunning decor, eclectic Asian antiques and contemporary art collection. Set in a quiet, convienient location overlooking Bath towards the Royal Crescent, it is a 10-15 minute stroll into the centre and provides complimentary parking and well maintained Gardens. Rooms are gracious and all have views looking over Bath or our secluded hilly garden. Flatscreen TV's, WiFi, fluffy towels, high quality linen, bathrobes, high pressure showers, Nespresso Coffee machines and elegant French Damana herbal toiletries are standard in all rooms. Guests can also relax in our elegant sitting room, with local drinks from our honesty bar. In the morning look forward to a hearty, cooked to order breakfast in the Orangery situated in the Japanese-inspired garden. Begin with the extensive selection of locally sourced yoghurts, fresh fruit, Bath Cheeses, cereals, croissants, homemade preserves, fruit juices, freshly ground Bristol Coffee and a selection of Teas. Then our Full English breakfast, or a lighter option of Scottish Oak Smoked Salmon with free range Eggs. We hope to have the opportunity of welcoming you to our Villa soon.
tagline: A warm welcome awaits you at Dorian House, a stylish Victorian villa with stunning decor

title: Tom Jenkins + Supports
bodyContent: Tom Jenkins lives in the rolling hills of the South Wales valleys. A shepherd and hill farmer by trade, he has woven the post-industrial landscape and the stories of the working class communities into a tapestry of unique, traditionally crafted songs, originally inspired by his family of coal miners and farmers, with the stories of these hills and beyond being captured in his most anticipated album so far - 'When The Coal Dust Settled' set to be released in April 2025. His 2019 self-released debut, 'Misery In Comfort' written in the solitude of the New Zealand back country as a working shepherd and sheep shearer, was put out as nothing more than a passion project and a one off but instantly caught the attention of the music industry and his musical heroes, gaining him a personal invite to tour with American, Grammy and Oscar winning, singer-songwriter and Yellowstone star Ryan Bingham from the off, then followed by signing a record deal and landing big booking agency opportunities. This then led to a heavy live schedule, touring and opening for the likes of Bastille, country music mega star, Megan Moroney, Frank Turner, Cardinal Black and Skinny Lister to name a few and proving his unique, authentic mix of indie, country- folk could cut it with a mix of genres along with critical acclaim from the the music press, gaining him Huw Stephens' (BBC Radio Wales/ 6 Music) Artist and Album of the Week. bodyContent: Part of our year-long America 250 programme, celebrating 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, join us on our final evening celebrating American music. title: The Key of Life: celebrating the 50th anniversary of Stevie Wonder’s ‘Songs in the Key of Life’
bodyContent: Join music producer and singer Edward Bettella for an unforgettable performance of Stevie Wonder’s celebrated classic, ‘Songs in the Key of Life’. First released in September 1976, September 2026 represents a poignant 50th anniversary for the album, which broke musical boundaries and would influence countless artists from Elton John, Michael Jackson, to Pharell Williams and Kanye West. Featuring hits such as ‘Isn’t She Lovely’, ‘Sir Duke’ and ‘I Wish’, join Edward and his expanded big band with brass and string sections perform many of the tracks in their original arrangement, taking you on a musical journey through life and love. All profits from the night will be donated to the Orchestra of Everything Foundation, a local charity that provides free professional music tuition and instruments for around 250 children in primary schools across Bath.

bodyContent: For over 25 years holidaycottages.co.uk has offered a range of personally inspected holiday cottages and a friendly customer service, with a choice of more than 250 cottages in Somerset. Choose from a great selection of cottages in coastal, countryside and city locations, including family-friendly, romantic and dog-friendly cottages. Our cottages offer a home from home, and several are even packed with luxury touches to make your stay even more special, from log fires to hot tubs. title: Meryan House Hotel
subtitle: Located in the heart of the gorgeous Somerset countryside, the Meryan Hotel is a unique and very special place.
bodyContent: Our idyllic 15th century house is the perfect spot to stay, unwind, and escape from it all. Wake up in one of our luxury rooms, individually decorated and fitted with antique furniture. Take a leisurely stroll into Taunton, or through the surrounding countryside. Enjoy a glass of wine in our award-winning gardens. Dine in our restaurant, with its meals created from fresh, locally-sourced produce. Sound divine? Take a look at our rooms or our rates and book your break today. In our recent AA inspection we were praised for our “bedrooms with great individuality”, “diligent cleanliness” and “high standards through all areas of the establishment”. Our hotel gardens are regular winners of the Taunton in Bloom Best Hotel category too.

title: Ebborways Farm B&B
subtitle: Ebborways Farm is not just a bed and breakfast; it’s a camping site and one of the main camping sites for Priddy Folk Festival. We also hold rallies and are a wedding reception venue.
bodyContent: Ebborways Farm Bed and Breakfast is situated in a small village called Priddy, on top of the Mendip Hills near Wells in Somerset. We are in an area of outstanding natural beauty, and therefore it is a very popular area for walkers, cavers and horse riders alike. If you are looking for a romantic break or a holiday set in stunning scenery or if you wish to explore this beautiful county of Somerset, and all it has to offer, either by car, foot, bike or horse. At Ebborways Farm Bed and Breakfast we will do everything possible to ensure a memorable stay. The farm is perfectly positioned for sightseeing places such as Cheddar Gorge and Caves (5 miles), Wookey Hole Caves and Wookey Hole Paper Mill (2.7 Miles), Wells Cathedral (4 miles), Burrington Combe (5 miles), Bristol, Bath, Longleat and many other places of interest are also within easy reach. Annual attractions include Priddy Folk Fair in July, Priddy Funday & Craft Fair in September and also in November the Illuminated Carnival Season.

title: The Barn
subtitle: The Barn is one of two beautifully converted barns which share an enclosed garden, is south facing with views along a small tranquil valley.
bodyContent: The Barn | Park Farm Country Cottages near Chew Magna is one of two beautifully converted barns on a working farm with private terraces and a shared enclosed garden with lovely uninterrupted views across open countryside and along a small valley. The Barn is full of character, has an open gallery with exposed oak trusses, peg jointed purlins and has an airy yet homely feel. The south facing french doors open directly onto the private terrace with quality wooden table, chairs and parasol. The cottage has been equipped to a high standard with slate flooring, toasty underfloor heating, a dishwasher, washer/dryer, microwave, WiFi. There are 2 bathrooms and 2 bedrooms, a twin bedroom downstairs, a double bedroom upstairs with 1 additional guest bed on the gallery. Please note the the 5th bed on the gallery may not be suitable for very young children. https://www.parkfarm-countrycottages.co.uk/luxury-holiday-cottages-bristol-the-barn
tagline: The Barn is one of two beautifully converted barns which share an enclosed garden

title: Glenn Tilbrook
subtitle: Glenn Tilbrook - the voice of Squeeze with special guest Leon Tilbrook.
bodyContent: Glenn Tilbrook has more than earned his place at pop’s top table as one of our most cherished singers, guitarists and songwriters, not to mention an in-demand and endlessly endearing live performer. More than 40 years after first answering an ad placed by Chris Difford looking for like-minded souls to form the band that became the much-loved evergreen Squeeze, an ending remains nowhere in sight. Such is the continuing work ethic of a musician who has never been far from the action since Squeeze made their recording bow with the Packet of Three EP in 1977. Those humble three tracks led to a catalogue of enduring pop classics - Take Me I'm Yours, Cool for Cats, Up the Junction, Another Nail in My Heart, Tempted, Labelled With Love, Black Coffee in Bed, Hourglass (This could indeed go on for a while...) - as well as landmark albums including Argybargy, East Side Story, Some Fantastic Place and Cradle to the Grave. Following Squeeze's demise in 1998 (a state of affairs that proved happily temporary), Glenn embarked on a parallel solo career that produced The Incomplete Glenn Tilbrook (2001) and Transatlantic Ping-Pong (2004), albums that showcased an ever-maturing melodic and lyrical voice. In 2009 came the fizzing energy of Pandemonium Ensues, recorded with his touring band The Fluffers, while Happy Ending emerged as his most personal solo statement to date - an evocative set of songs about time, people and places, featuring contributions from his sons Leon and Wesley alongside long-time collaborators

title: Declaration of Independence on display
subtitle: See a rare original 1776 Declaration of Independence on display in England for the first time during the 250th anniversary year. Explore immersive displays, exhibitions, talks and events as part of America 250 at American Museum & Gardens..
bodyContent: This summer, American Museum & Gardens presents America 250 - a season of exhibitions, events and cultural experiences marking 250 years since the founding of the United States. At the heart of the programme is a rare original 1776 Dunlap printing of the Declaration of Independence, now on display in England for the first time during the 250th anniversary year. Only 26 Dunlap copies survive worldwide, and this is the only known example to have been intercepted by British forces during the American Revolution and later annotated by British government officials. Visitors can follow a specially curated trail through the Museum’s historic Manor House, where immersive interpretation and displays explore the people, ideas and objects that shaped the founding of the United States, culminating in the signing of the Declaration of Independence. Displayed alongside the Declaration is a specially commissioned film from the Museum of the American Revolution in Philadelphia, offering further insight into the document and its enduring significance.
tagline: This summer, American Museum & Gardens presents America 250

title: Holly Farm Cottages
subtitle: Somerset self catering barns converted to high standard with indoor pool, hot tub, games room and own gardens. Good pubs in easy reach.
bodyContent: Holly Farm Cottages have been converted from traditional Somerset Long Barns to a high standard. The original blue lias and exposed beams have been retained and modern comforts added. The cottages are fully equipped; each kitchen has a fridge-freezer, microwave, washing machine etc. access to a tumble dryer. The living rooms have been comfortably furnished and there is central heating throughout. Each cottage also has an enclosed garden and patio, parking and payphone. Linen and towels (except cot linen) are provided. There is an indoor, heated swimming pool and hot tub. Relax in the orchard or there is a games room for the more energetic, with a pool table and table tennis. Holly Farm is a working farm that has been in the Hembrow family for several generations. You are welcome to walk over the footpaths and see the farm. Stoke St Gregory, on the edge of West Sedgemoor, a well-known wetland and bird reserve, is also the heart of willow growing country. There are shops and good pubs serving food. We are 7 miles from Taunton .
tagline: Somerset self catering barns converted to high standard with indoor pool.

title: The Crown Hotel
subtitle: Situated at the heart of the Exmoor National Park Exford is one of it's prettiest villages.
bodyContent: Surrounded by stunning countryside and moorland where Exmoor ponies, red deer and birds of prey are a common sight. Our food has an excellent reputation both locally and nationally. You can choose to dine in our cosy country bar or extended lounge area, both serve real ales, fine wines, select gins and freshly prepared food. The Crown Hotel is dog friendly with lots of walks straight from our doorstep. Our roaring log fires, cosy rooms and friendly atmosphere make The Crown the ideal place to return after a day's touring, walking, riding, fishing or shooting on Exmoor.

title: The Apartment, Bath
subtitle: An exceptional two-bedroom luxury holiday home in central Bath, loved by guests for its perfect location, stylish decor, comfort, cleanliness and first class self-catering accommodation.
bodyContent: From Nespresso to Nintendo, The Apartment, Bath is an excellently-located two-bedroom apartment in central Bath. The first bedroom is a large, bright double bedroom with king size bed (or twin beds on request). The open fireplace and large sash windows are elegant original features and south-facing views take in the length of Ralph Allen Drive and Widcombe Hill. At the rear of the property, the second bedroom is a well-proportioned double bedroom, featuring a comfy double bed, original fireplace and built in wardrobe. The homely lounge is flooded with light from the large, original south-facing 16-pane sash window. The room hosts an extendable dining table and chairs, designer sofa (which can convert to a sofa bed) and a feature armchair. Brimming with technology, the lounge is equipped with satellite TV, blu-ray player, Nintendo Wii and wall-mounted 40” Samsung LCD TV. A well-equipped and cleverly designed galley kitchen features high-end integrated appliances to meet your every need, including a built-in double oven and sleek induction hob, full suite of cooking facilities and an integrated NEFF fridge with ice-box. A Nespresso machine and milk frother are provided for that much needed espresso or cappuccino to kick-start your day. And there is a washer dryer, so you can pack a little lighter! The newly renovated bathroom features a large walk-in rain shower with separate handheld spray. A chrome towel rail is complemented by a lit, motion-activated mirror cabinet featuring de-mist function and integrated razor/electric toothbrush socket. This gorgeous two-bedroom holiday home in central Bath is ranked in the ‘10 Best Holiday Homes in Bath’ by Booking.com and consistently rated positively by guests.
tagline: An exceptional two-bedroom luxury holiday home in central Bath

title: Eight
subtitle: Eight is a small and independent townhouse hotel with a restaurant in the heart of Bath.
bodyContent: Eight is a small and independent townhouse hotel with a restaurant in the heart of Bath. We have eight bedrooms that effortlessly marry past and present. Each one has its own history and charms, yet all share the latest in up-to-the-minute creature comforts. As a small, independent townhouse, we’re able to give each and every guest our undivided attention. Nothing is too much trouble. We serve eight dishes that change with the seasons. All of our plates are small so you can choose two, three or four each and savour the best ingredients available right now from coast, field and forest. Pair your selections with a glass or bottle from our extensive wine list or ask for a recommendation. Find out more here .
tagline: Eight is a small and independent townhouse hotel with a restaurant in the heart of Bath.

title: Bath Brunch Club: Mamma Mia! Bottomless Brunch at Komedia Bath

bodyContent: Mamma Mia, here we go… Get ready for the ultimate bottomless brunch experience at Bath Brunch Club! Hey there, dancing queens! title: Tango – the music and songs of Astor Piazzola
subtitle: A concert celebrating the music of Astor Piazzolla.
bodyContent: Using the tango as his starting point Piazzolla created a unique musical style – the Tango Nuevo. This concert includes some of the finest of his quintets by a superb combination of virtuoso musicians, led by brilliant accordionist Ryan Corbett. Nicholas Mulroy joins the band to sing music by Gardel, Vargas and Ramirez – as well as songs by Piazzolla including excerpts from his opera ‘Maria di Buenos Aires’. ‘Best of all, perhaps, is Nicholas Mulroy …singing milongas like one born to it. Exhilaratingly done, and a fine achievement.’ Gramophone Nicholas Mulroy Tenor Ryan Corbett Accordion Fergus McCreadie Piano Emma Baird Violin Tim Beattie Guitar
tagline: A concert celebrating the music of Astor Piazzolla.

title: Harry Brockway: Ways With Wood
subtitle: A new exhibition celebrating the life and work of Glastonbury based artist Harry Brockway.
bodyContent: ‘Ways with Wood’, is a major exhibition at Somerset Rural Life Museum celebrating the life and work of renowned Glastonbury-based artist Harry Brockway (1958–2024). Featuring an exceptional selection of his wood engravings, woodcuts and wooden sculpture, the exhibition offers a rich insight into the creativity, skill and craftsmanship that defined his distinguished artistic career. Harry Brockway was an exceptionally accomplished printmaker, sculptor, illustrator and stone carver. Alongside creating independent prints, he produced wood-engraved illustrations for a wide range of publishers – from major houses such as Penguin to specialist presses like The Folio Society. His work appears in celebrated editions of Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein and in texts by W. B. Yeats, Philip Pullman, Fyodor Dostoevsky, Samuel Taylor Coleridge and Mark Twain among others. Image credit: All rights reserved The Brockway Family, Harry Brockway, The Tor from Ten Acre Field, 2008. The museum is open Tuesday – Sunday, 10.00 am – 5.00 pm.
tagline: A new exhibition celebrating the life and work of Glastonbury based artist Harry Brockway.

subtitle: Self catering cottages in a queit setting near Brean. Berrow and weston super mare in Somerset. Short holiday breaks.
bodyContent: Very close to the Somerset coast but surrounded by the beautiful West Country countryside you will find Hope Farm's 4 luxury cottages. The beaches of Brean & Weston Super Mare are minutes drives away and there are a vast array of day trips to surrounding attractions, villages and countryside to keep everyone occupied. Each ground floor self catering cottage is on the edge of a beautiful lawned courtyard with open fields behind. Each has 2 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms and are easily accessible for those that have special requirements. Outside there are picnic tables and deckchairs for those lazy days and Summer evenings. Each cottage has off road, private and security lit parking spaces for 2 vehicles. Hope Farm has a wealth of facilities including a games room, outdoor children's play ground, laundry room and covered storage for bikes or trailers. And if you dont fancy driving there is a bus stop right at the gate to Weston Super Mare, Burnham on Sea , Taunton & Bristol. title: The Jazz Room: A Journey to the Heart of New Orleans
subtitle: Come on down to The Jazz Room in Bath!
bodyContent: With a mix of carefully chosen classics and spontaneous improvisation, this feel-good live music performance takes you on a journey to the roots of revolutionary New Orleans jazz. The Jazz Room is a journey back in time to the birthplace of this iconic genre. Set in a street-style bar that recreates 1920s New Orleans, this live jazz show promises a night of soul, passion, and rhythm. Enjoy a selection of the finest ‘hot jazz’ tunes - a unique blend of ragtime, brass, and blues - alongside moments of spontaneous improvisation, a hallmark of true jazz. Be part of jazz’s living legacy, where every note tells a story of freedom, creativity, and camaraderie.

Featuring an exceptional selection of his wood engravings, woodcuts and wooden sculpture, the exhibition offers a rich insight into the creativity, skill and craftsmanship that defined his distinguished artistic career. Harry Brockway was an exceptionally accomplished printmaker, sculptor, illustrator and stone carver. Alongside creating independent prints, he produced wood-engraved illustrations for a wide range of publishers – from major houses such as Penguin to specialist presses like The Folio Society. His work appears in celebrated editions of Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein and in texts by W. B. Yeats, Philip Pullman, Fyodor Dostoevsky, Samuel Taylor Coleridge and Mark Twain among others. Image credit: All rights reserved The Brockway Family, Harry Brockway, The Tor from Ten Acre Field, 2008. The museum is open Tuesday – Sunday, 10.00 am – 5.00 pm.
tagline: A new exhibition celebrating the life and work of Glastonbury based artist Harry Brockway.

title: Horizon at Tor View Cottage
subtitle: Horizon is a three bedroom detached barn, set in 3 acres available to let for self catering holidays.
bodyContent: Horizon is a three bedroom detached barn, set in 3 acres available to let for self catering holidays. It can accomodate 6 plus an infant. It has a ground floor double bedroom with en-suite bathroom, open plan kitchen and lounge area and family bathroom. Upstairs is a smaller room with two single beds (ideal for the Children) and a large double bedroom (this bed can be split into 2 singles on request) with an excellent view. It has its own private garden and patio area to the rear but also access to the enclosed 0.5 acre paddock.
tagline: Horizon is a three bedroom detached barn, set in 3 acres available to let for self catering holidays

title: Kingsway Hotel
subtitle: The Kingsway is an elegant purpose built hotel comprising of spacious bed rooms all with their own private en-suite facilities.
bodyContent: It is the wish of the owners to provide a home from home atmosphere and as such the facility is run as a guest house Bed and Breakfast only. Located on a corner plot The Kingsway is set within pleasant gardens and lawns within a similarly presented residential area. It is but a short stroll to the sea front and Minehead town centre. A high level of decoration and furnishings throughout create a high standard of accommodation that attracts repeat visits from many of our guests as well as comments on the high level of cleanliness. Minehead is an ancient port as well as a medieval town set at the edge of the exquisite Somerset Exmoor. Here visitors will observe the many attractions that exist within the town and close by surrounding areas within Somerset. Dunster castle is but a 5 minute drive. Porlock Lynton & Lynmouth is a relatively short distance away where views of the rockiest cliff formations within the UK can be viewed. Other similarly located villages within the Exmoor region as well as the differing array of tourist facilities ensure that Minehead remains popular throughout the autumn and winter periods. The town is ideally suited for all types of visitors more so since the high level of investment undertaken in the area. It provides an evironment for a relaxing stay or as a gateway to the many attractions available. Three types of room are available in the form of double twin and triple layouts. A large guest dining area is provided where a varied selection of food can be requested for breakfast. Afterwards guests can relax within the spacious private guest lounge. You will receive a warm welcome from the resident proprietors Diane and Joe Erfurt who will do everything they can to make your stay as comfortable and enjoyable as possible.

title: Fernhill Farm
subtitle: Here you can discover the ethos behind Fernhill, meet the team who manage this site, see a glimpse of its historical industrial scars, and find out about grazing livestock living alongside resident and seasonal wildlife.
bodyContent: Perched atop the Mendip Hills AONB on the B3134 between Burrington Coombe and Wells, we're 5 miles from Cheddar, 20 from Bath and Bristol, and 7 from Bristol Airport. This award-winning working livestock farm offers rustic venues, on-site accommodation, event extras and renewable energy — an Arcadian place to stay.
tagline: Here you can discover the ethos behind Fernhill

title: The Almshouse
subtitle: This charming, historic two-bedroom cottage nestles in a tranquil corner of Bath, but is only ten minutes’ stroll from the city centre, offering an ideal retreat for a romantic getaway or a base for exploring the glories of the West Country.
bodyContent: Beautifully refurbished in 2015, this 1843 almshouse nestles in a secret corner of the city, only 15 minutes from the M4 and a gentle walk downhill to the centre of Bath. There is plenty of parking, so you can leave the car and walk this historic town at your own pace. The main bedroom, with king-size bed, looks over gardens towards the church; the second bedroom can be made up as a single or twin-bedded room. The original features have been carefully preserved, but this charming house lives comfortably in the 21st century, including WiFi, flat-screen TV, and DAB radio. Guests can enjoy breakfast or an evening drink in the private courtyard, cook a delicious dinner in the Harvey Jones kitchen, or treat themselves in one of Bath’s many award-winning restaurants. Luxuriously furnished, this cosy cottage offers everything you need for a very special break, from champagne flutes to Egyptian cotton sheets and even a welcome basket on arrival! Bath has so much to offer, from the Roman Baths and gorgeous Georgian crescents, to the ultra-modern Thermae Bath Spa, quirky independent shops, museums and cultural festivals, that you may want to plan a longer stay to explore the glorious countryside: just let us know.
tagline: This charming, historic two-bedroom cottage nestles in a tranquil corner of Bath

title: Idle In Provence with Eric Idle
subtitle: We are absolutely thrilled to welcome comedian, actor, author and singer-songwriter, Eric Idle, back to Bath for his new memoir, Idle In Provence: A Brief History of Thyme.
bodyContent: Idle In Provence follows Eric's purchase of a ramshackle property in the south of France, just two years after the launch of Monty Python's Flying Circus. Both hilarious and tender, we follow Eric on a tale spanning fifty years, seeking his own slice of the simple life. Please note: Eric will not be doing a public signing at the event and copies of the book will not be signed. About the book: In 1971, two years after the launch of Monty Python’s Flying Circus made his comedy troupe global superstars - and made all their lives a little more complicated - Eric Idle decided to buy a ramshackle property in the south of France. In search of a simpler, quieter life, what followed was a story akin to A Year in Provence, but with more disaster, more heartbreak, more laughs - and much more spam. A tale spanning a fifty-year quest of home-building, friendship-making and bad-French-learning, Idle in Provence is a hilarious, tender and unforgettable memoir of Eric Idle's very own escape to the country. About the author: Eric Idle is a comedian, actor, author and singer-songwriter who found immediate fame on television with the sketch-comedy show Monty Python's Flying Circus. Following its success, the Pythons began making films that include Monty Python and the Holy Grail (1975), Monty Python's Life of Brian (1979) and The Meaning of Life (1983). Eric also wrote the award-winning musical Spamalot. He splits his time between Los Angeles and Provence.

title: Family Trail: Motte & Bailey Investigate the Viking Raid on Watchet Mint
subtitle: Come and see Dunster's rare double overshot watermill in action with a day of milling, demos, talks and more to celebrate National Mills Weeken
bodyContent: Detective duo, Motte & Bailey, have travelled back in time to the 10th Century. Vikings have raided the Royal Mint in the nearby harbour town of Watchet and stolen some Saxon silver coins. The Vikings have hidden the coins in the castle grounds for safe keeping until they board their longships at sea. Can you help Motte & Bailey recover the coins and return them to the Royal Mint? Follow the trail, crack the clues and take part in hands‑on activities as you learn all about the Vikings & Saxons! Complete the trail to claim your collectable Motte & Bailey Viking Badge. This event runs daily from Saturday 23rd May until Sunday 12th July. £3.50 per trail per person (includes prize).
tagline: Detective duo, Motte & Bailey, have travelled back in time to the 10th Century

title: The George Hotel - Crewkerne
subtitle: The George, situated in the heart of Crewkerne, has provided travellers with a warm welcome, comfortable bed and much needed refreshment for over 400 years.
bodyContent: It has been recently refurbished and we are proud to continue this tradition of hospitality, offering a range of well appointed rooms to meet the expectations of the modern traveller. Our Restaurant offers a extensive selection of classic British dishes and contemporary favourites whilst the Ale Bar has a wide range of local and craft ales. All of our tastefully decorated rooms are en-suite and offer flatscreen TVs, free Wi-fi, tea & coffee making facilities and many other modern amenities.

title: Glendower House
subtitle: Minehead, one of Somerset’s leading holiday resorts and the ‘Gateway to Exmoor’, is the ideal location from which to explore the National Park and surrounding area and Glendower House.
bodyContent: A family run, no smoking guesthouse, is the place to stay for quality Bed and Breakfast accommodation. Situated in an attractive tree lined road, this Edwardian terraced house is only a few minutes level walk from both Minehead town centre and the sea front with its wide sandy beach and promenade leading to the old harbour. Our accommodation is made up of three singles, five doubles, three twins, two of which are on the ground floor, giving level access to all areas, and for that special occasion a four poster. Those at the rear of the house overlook the garden and the hills on the edge of Exmoor. All rooms have been individually decorated and furnished to a high standard, are centrally heated and include the usual amenities, colour television, tea and coffee making facilities, radio/clock alarm and hair dryer. As you would expect from a guesthouse of this quality, all have their own en suite shower room, with luxury toiletries. Breakfast is served in our spacious dining room. We offer a varied selection of items, all freshly prepared, using wherever possible, local, organic and fairtrade products. These include fairtrade fruit juices, Exmoor organic sausage and bacon and marmalades and jams handcrafted in the Brendon Hills. Particular dietary requirements can be catered for, please let us know. A homely lounge provides the ideal place to relax, read a good book and meet other guests. We are not licensed, but you are welcome to bring your own drinks, which can be chilled if required and we will provide glasses. There is a large private car park at the rear of the house and a delightful garden in which to enjoy a sunny day. For the comfort and safety of all guests, a no smoking policy is adopted throughout.

title: Huxham Farmhouse
subtitle: Set in the picturesque hamlet of Huxham, with it's attractive green and surrounded by fields where sheep and cattle graze.
bodyContent: Huxham Farmhouse is an elegant Grade II listed Georgian Farmhouse. Situated just behind the main house, the Croft is our 2 bedroom self-contained annexe with it’s own front door which is available for self-catered stays. As the name implies the building was formerly a working farm house, most recently dairy, although earlier records show the surrounding land being popular for apple growing and the making of cider. In the early 1980's the dairy ceased, the outbuildings were converted to dwellings and the main farm house was sold as a private residence. Today Huxham Farmhouse is a comfortable family home which retains many original features and is furnished in a traditional manner with antique furnishings and open wood fires. The main house sits in grounds of about 7 acres, most of which are paddocks with about 1 acre of gardens, over which we enjoy glorious uninterrupted countryside views. So there’s plenty of outdoor space to relax in without us tripping over each other and guests are welcome to enjoy the garden, tennis court and hot tub, as well as the covered heated outdoor seating area. So whether you are here in Somerset for country pursuits, a wedding, a family gathering, sight-seeing, or a local event we very much look forward to welcoming you. You won’t want to leave. title: Tailpit Cottage
subtitle: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside
bodyContent: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside on the edge of an area of outstanding natural beauty but only 5 miles from the world heritage city of Bath and 1 mile from the Saxon town of Bradford-on-Avon. Cumberwell Country Cottages are located on Great Cumberwell Farm, which has been in the James family since 1939 and was originally a dairy farm until 1992 when the herd was sold making way for a diversification into Cumberwell Park Golf Club, the farm itself has not changed a great deal and is still a working farm with over 300 acres of arable crop. The self-catering cottages available for your stay have been converted from an old tithe barn which has had many purposes in the past including stables, a grain store and cider production as the orchard at the front of the cottages was a cider apple orchard.

title: Dion Smith
subtitle: Dion Smith is carving out a distinctive space with his brand of modern, guitar-driven rock.
bodyContent: Following the release of his acclaimed EP “Karma Comes Knocking,” Smith has been steadily building momentum, delivering music that blends powerful riffs with a sharp contemporary edge - layered with atmospheric synth textures that add depth and cinematic weight behind the guitars. Dion first built his reputation through striking guitar instrumentals, showcasing his technical ability and melodic instinct. Now, he’s stepping forward with a full band sound, bringing a bigger, more expansive live experience to the stage. With his latest EP, “City of Lost Souls,” this next chapter sees him pushing further into bold, vocal-led territory while retaining the raw energy that defines his playing. With UK festival appearances already lined up this year, Dion Smith continues to build momentum and expand his reach. This is modern rock with intent: guitar-driven at its core, elevated by subtle synth layers, and delivered with conviction. Dion will be performing songs from his debut EP “Karma Comes Knocking” plus showcasing new material from his latest EP “City Of Lost Souls”.
tagline: Dion Smith is carving out a distinctive space with his brand of modern, guitar-driven rock.

title: Goodrington Guest House
subtitle: We are a small bed and breakfast based in Weston super Mare, Somerset.
bodyContent: Excellently placed we are within walking distance of the beach and many local attractions. A short walk to the town centre, golf course, parks, train station and many transport routes. Goodrington is a large Victorian house with a warm and friendly atmosphere, occupying a quiet, pleasant residential position on the south side of the town. Only a short distance to the beach, around two hundred yards, you can walk to the beach in about 5 minutes. The town centre is about 1 mile from the house, a very nice stroll down the sea front, but for the not so fit there is a regular bus service which passes the end of Charlton Road. Just around the corner in Moorland Road there are a number of local shops including a Post Office, News Agent / Tobacconist and even a Fish Bar, so most things are available practically next door. At the end of Charlton Road is Weston’s seafront 18 hole golf course and Clarence Park bowling greens are just around the corner.

title: Pen Mill Hotel
subtitle: Please allow me to introduce ourselves. We are Jon & Sarah Palmer and have owned and personally run the Pen Mill Hotel since 2003.
bodyContent: We have taken the business from a drinking pub with live music to one of the areas most successful award winning, hotel based, food led pubs. Our success comes from shear hard work, determination and a love for our independent hotel. A hotel where Sarah and I first met in 1999. Business has not always been easy. We have suffered fire, recession and tremendous uncertainty in our sixteen years at the Pen Mill. However, we have bucked the trend of many businesses and recorded twelve continuous years of growth in a market that, many of the 'big boys' have stumbled and fallen by the wayside. Having survived and grown to record levels during these woeful times are facts that we are immensely proud of. Part of our success comes from working closely with our local, independent suppliers. Buying locally wherever we can. Be it food, drink or items for the hotel. We support local/British business wherever we can and hope that this is reciprocated. We only employ those who are enthusiastic, energetic and willing to learn. However, one thing we can't teach is personality and the ability to smile naturally in a job! Whether you've just been offered the job of your dreams or you team has lost in the cup final, you want to be met by a cheerful disposition and a smile! This is the Pen Mill way. Sarah takes charge at the 'back of house', the kitchen, the engine room of the business. She leads a brilliant team, tirelessly, whilst letting them flourish. Encouraging and building self belief, to be better today than you were yesterday. What type of food do we produce? Good quality, British pub fayre. Myself (Jon), I take care of the 'front of house'. I am generally found working on my computer at the end of the bar, drinking ....... tea! Honestly, it's tea! Overlooking a team of men, women, boys and girls that make me proud, every single day! (well, most days!). Customer service is one of the most important ingredients in our success. An ingredient that makes us the success we are today by making sure, you, our customer's return. We offer beautifully cooked, homemade food, from local ingredients with what the industry calls a 'perfect serve' drink. However, we're not a place for copious amounts of drinking. We want everybody to enjoy their visit to the Pen Mill. We don't want people leaving on their hands and knees. We want people to remember their visit. Add to this our beautifully presented hotel rooms with sumptuous beds and powerful showers and we offer the full package. I almost forgot, we're Taste of the West Gold winners for our food and Silver winners for our accommodation, going for gold in 2020!

title: Stable Cottage: 6 bed country cottage
subtitle: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.
bodyContent: It is located in the beautiful Georgian village of Freshford which lies at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys in the southern Cotswolds. There are some wonderful walks to local pubs following the riverside and canals. All just 15 minutes from Bath by car but the secret of this location is the 9 minute train journey to Bath from the village station, just a short stroll from the cottages. The cottage : Stable cottage is a newly renovated, limestone floored, 3 bedroom, two bathroom (one is en-suite) cottage. It has large windows to the front of the house filling the bedrooms and downstairs with light on a sunny day. It has an open plan living/dining area with free view TV/DVD and two large suedette couches and comfortable chairs. For dining there is a blond Oak dining table and chairs to seat 6 . The Stables can accommodate 6 people in three bedrooms (two king size and one double) . The kitchen is fully equipped with cookware,dishwasher and washing machine . The house also offers Iron/Ironing board, Hairdryers All bed linen and towels . There is a Welcome pack of tea, coffee, sugar, milk, bread, butter, eggs and bacon. Free WiFi. There are also books and board-games in the house for the use of guests. If you have any questions on Bath and the local area before or during your stay please let us know. We would be delighted to help. Neighbourhood overview : Freshford is a beautiful ancient village with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk from the cottage( The Inn at Freshford) that serves restaurant quality food and all the local beers and ciders.They have an excellent fully stocked( from wine to organic humus!)community shop that also has a good quality cafe that serves lunch. There is also a local doctors surgery. The village is nestled at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys . The Kennet and Avon canal is a 15 minute walk from the cottage. Getting around : You don’t need a car to stay in the cottage. The village station is a few minutes walk away. Trains hourly off peak and thrice hourly at peak times. Bath 9 mins, Bristol 22mins. London Padington to Bath Spa 1.5 hours Bath Spa to Freshford 9 minutes Bath Spa to Freshford “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/bath-spa-to-freshford ” Freshford to Bath Spa “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/freshford-to-bath-spa ” There is also a local bus service to all the adjacent villages and Bath. The cottage has two parking spaces suitable for one medium and one small car or a single large SUV.the surrounding towns you might want to visit. Other things to note If you are a runner or keep fit enthusiast the owner is a qualified Personal Trainer (Bath Uni) with much Marathon and half marathon experience. She specialises in Ladies training. Please let us know if you would like guided running or some Personal Fitness training.
tagline: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.

title: Harry Baker: Tender
subtitle: World Poetry Slam Champion Harry Baker brings his characteristic warmth, wit and wonder to new parenthood.
bodyContent: World Poetry Slam Champion Harry Baker brings his characteristic warmth, wit and wonder to new parenthood. From introducing his baby to a horse for the first time, to trying to work out if the GP really did drop them on purpose to test their reflexes, Tender contains poems from the first hundred days of new life and celebrates all of the euphoria, panic and vulnerability that come with it. Following on from the last two years’ 40-date sell out runs of Wonderful and Wonderful 2.0, he’ll even slip in some non-baby bangers too. Expect more laughter and tears than ever.

title: Harry Brockway: Ways With Wood
subtitle: A new exhibition celebrating the life and work of Glastonbury based artist Harry Brockway.
bodyContent: ‘Ways with Wood’, is a major exhibition at Somerset Rural Life Museum celebrating the life and work of renowned Glastonbury-based artist Harry Brockway (1958–2024). Featuring an exceptional selection of his wood engravings, woodcuts and wooden sculpture, the exhibition offers a rich insight into the creativity, skill and craftsmanship that defined his distinguished artistic career. Harry Brockway was an exceptionally accomplished printmaker, sculptor, illustrator and stone carver. Alongside creating independent prints, he produced wood-engraved illustrations for a wide range of publishers – from major houses such as Penguin to specialist presses like The Folio Society. His work appears in celebrated editions of Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein and in texts by W. B. Yeats, Philip Pullman, Fyodor Dostoevsky, Samuel Taylor Coleridge and Mark Twain among others. Image credit: All rights reserved The Brockway Family, Harry Brockway, The Tor from Ten Acre Field, 2008. The museum is open Tuesday – Sunday, 10.00 am – 5.00 pm.
tagline: A new exhibition celebrating the life and work of Glastonbury based artist Harry Brockway.

title: Lime Kiln Farm Cottages
subtitle: Lime Kiln Farm offers three beautiful luxury self catering holiday cottages set in stunning Somerset countryside near to Bath.
bodyContent: LUXURY SELF CATERING HOLIDAY COTTAGES IN BATH Lime Kiln Farm offers three beautiful luxury self catering holiday cottages set in stunning Somerset countryside near to Bath. Our cottages are built in the converted stable buildings of this former farm and have been renovated to a very high standard, complete with all modern conveniences including free WIFI access. The cottages are perfect for enjoying a self catering break in Bath, as we are located just 15 minutes from the city centre, close to the small village of Faulkland. All cottages have an open plan lounge and kitchen/ diner, plus 2 double bedrooms with ensuite. The cottages all benefit from a terrace with wonderful southerly views over the garden and stunning scenery beyond - perfect for sitting and enjoying a BBQ or glass of wine. Horseshoe Cottage has disabled access throughout, with super king size beds in both bedrooms. Linen and towels are provided. Only 9 miles from the centre of Bath and with easy access to the Bath Park & Ride (approx 8 miles), Lime Kiln Farm is perfectly located for exploring the many tourist attractions located in Wiltshire and Somerset. Nearby attractions include Cheddar Gorge , Wookey Hole Caves , the beautiful Cathedral in Wells , Stourhead House & Gardens and the nearby Longleat Safari Park , not forgetting the various attractions within the city of Bath itself such as the Roman Baths , Royal Crescent and recently opened Thermae Bath Spa . Faulkland village is only a half mile walk away across fields and offers a pub, a part-time post office, and the famous Somerset Lavendar Farm with shop and cafe - not to mention the village green complete with wooden stocks! The cottages are available for both short and long breaks. Lime Kiln Farm is pet friendly, so please enquire with us if you wish to bring a dog. Enjoy your Free Bath Reward Card when you stay!

title: Seventeen The Townhouse Bath
subtitle: Guests receive a very warm welcome to start their boutique break away in this beautiful 1810 Georgian townhouse.
bodyContent: Welcome to Seventeen The Town House a boutique Georgian Town House built circa 1810. Enter Number 17 through wrought iron gates off Camden road and follow the stone path through the front garden towards the steps to make your way through the main entrance door. You are welcomed by a long hallway with a traditional wood & tiled floor. There is plenty of space in the hall to hang your coat and store your shoes. An original spindle staircase leads guests to the first and lower ground floor. Walk through the hallway and you’ll find yourself in the living and dining area which seats seven guests around a large dining table. The living room is furnished with comfortable sofas, floor cushions and a footstool. There is a wall mounted wide flat screen TV with BT Vision, NETFLIX, BBC iplayer & ITV Hub, Sonos bar sound, DVD player & Roberts bluetooth CD/Radio. The sitting and dining rooms are inter-connecting and have exposed wooden floors, two original fireplaces and hand-crafted timber cupboards complete with a large choice of board games and puzzles for little ones. Walk out of the dining room turning left and you will find yourself in a cleverly arranged space for the study annex, a quiet place to read or plan your stay in Bath. There is a downstairs WC cloakroom to save you walking up or downstairs to the other bathrooms. The kitchen is close by and is a stunning room basking in natural light from the skylight ceiling. The kitchen has been equipped to a high standard with bespoke storage cupboards, a house keepers cupboard & drawer units with marble work surfaces, Belfast sink and space for all the usual kitchen appliances. To keep your toes warm on the stone floor there is under floor heating. The kitchen has a range of new features, a SMEG electric double oven with gas hob, Bosch dishwasher & microwave, Dualit kettle & toaster, Breville panini maker, Pizza stone, Kitchen Aid, Kenwood Blender, Ninja juicer, Nespresso Coffee machine, large selection of pots, pans, serving dishes, storage containers, cooking utensils, cutlery & glass ware. We provide Denby linen china for dining for seven guests – everything you need should be there if its not let us know! Leading off the kitchen is a laundry/utility room which houses a new fridge freezer, AEG washer dryer, Brabantia ironing board & iron, laundry basket and clothes airer. From the annex you can walk through the back door & take the stone steps up towards the garden where you will find the peace and quiet of the verandah. The verandah provides sheltered outdoor seating and dining for eight. Walk on up the steps through a wrought iron gate & you will find a peaceful garden with pretty shrubs, trees, lavender & landscaped lawn to lay your rug out and enjoy the views across Bath. At the end of lawn there is a beautiful summer house on raised timber decking. Take a seat in our wonderful wicker chairs, relax & soak up stunning views over the Bath valley. The summer house has comfortable wicker seating and is a peaceful place to read & enjoy the hills beyond. Moving back into the house on the first floor, there are two super king size bedrooms. They have period fireplaces and wardrobe style cupboards & shelving, one having an outlook to the front and one with a view over the rear garden. Bedroom One has a super king sized bed and bedroom two can be either a super king bed or two super singles. There is a further single bedroom facing to the front with a tallboy and side table for storage. The first floor bathroom has a lovely view from its sash window to the back garden & summerhouse. The bathroom has a roll top bath with a fixed rain shower and oval shower curtain over the bath. There is a small walk in airing cupboard for drying or storage of travel cases. Walking back down the staircase, the lower ground floor bedroom offers super king size or super single twin beds. There is a large sash window seat facing the front of the house & two wardrobe style cupboards with hanging & shelving space. Along the corridor on the lower ground floor is the rain shower room with a stone ceiling, under floor heating, heated towel rail, WC & sink. All the bedrooms have traditional sash windows and are furnished with pretty side tables & lamps, Sonos speakers, hairdryers, black out roman blinds, radiators, good sized beds, comfortable bedding and new mattresses. There are digital safes in the three kingsize bedrooms. Do note that the ceilings in this house will accommodate guests less than 6ft 3′. Outside the front landscaped garden is laid to gravel with a stone pathway leading to the front door. There is a large bin store. We are able to offer guests complimentary holiday house parking permit if they have a car. Alternatively Bath Spa train & bus station are a short taxi ride or 20 minute walk from the house. Taxis are easy to book and buses are frequent to and from the city centre from the nearby bus stop. We can also organise Private drivers for any size group from any UK international airports. We looking forward to welcoming you at Seventeen The Town House for a very special stay!
tagline: Guests receive a very warm welcome to start their boutique break away

title: Nick Cope Family Show
subtitle: Come and join Nick Cope for a delightful fun filled musical hour featuring all your favorite Nick Cope hits and more.
bodyContent: Come and join Nick Cope for a delightful fun filled musical hour featuring all your favorite Nick Cope hits and more. Nick has been writing and recording his beautiful and totally unique songs for children and their families for over 10 years, he performs with his guitar and stunning animations to sell-out crowds all over the country. His fanatical following of little and not so little fans has grown immeasurably over the last couple of years due to the phenomenal success of the CBeebies show ‘Nick Cope’s Popcast’. Nick has a magical way of reaching into people’s hearts, igniting children’s imagination in an organic, unpatronizing, educational and fun way. title: The Amazing Bubble Man
subtitle: Louis Pearl has been thrilling audiences around the world for over 30 years with the art, magic, science and fun of bubbles. He is a favorite at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival, where he has enjoyed 14 years of sell-out success.
bodyContent: Louis explores the breath-taking dynamics of bubbles, combining comedy and artistry with audience participation and enough spellbinding bubble tricks to keep everyone mesmerized. Most shows will also feature multi instrumentalist Jet Black Pearl accompanying Louis with bubbly music to double your pleasure. title: Hot 8 Brass Band
subtitle: The New Orleans-based Hot 8 Brass Band draw on the traditional jazz heritage of their hometown, alongside more modern styles, including elements of funk, hip hop, rap, and its local variation, “bounce.”
bodyContent: The collective earned a win in the 64th Annual Grammy Awards 2022 for their feature on Jon Batiste’s ‘Album of the Year', following the nomination of ‘The Life & Times Of…’ for ‘Best Regional Roots Album’ in 2013. Transcending genres and trends, Hot 8 have performed and collaborated with the likes of Jon Batiste, Blind Boys of Alabama, Basement Jaxx and Alice Russell, and provided live support for Mos Def, Lauryn Hill and Mary J Blige. Since forming they have established a decade-long affiliation with actor/BBC Radio 6 Music DJ Craig Charles, among other tastemakers, DJs and journalists worldwide. After a festive appearance Live at Maida Vale for Lauren Laverne (BBC Radio 6 Music), the Hot 8 Brass Band performed for Jools Holland's annual Hootenanny on BBC Two to welcome in 2019. Later that year, after taking to the stage at the BRIT awards in February, the Hot 8 Brass Band were invited on the European leg of George Ezra’s tour. With multiple sell-out shows at London’s Roundhouse and Brighton’s Dome, Hot 8 continue to share their acclaimed releases. Albums such as 'Vicennial...', 'On The Spot' and 'Take Cover', are brought to the stage, honouring their city’s musical traditions, while forging their own powerful legacy. Mixing an old-school street brass approach with funkier currents and hip hop vocals, Hot 8’s magnificent originals are juxtaposed with fresh versions of Snoop Dogg, Stevie Wonder, The Specials and of course their anthemic take on Marvin Gaye’s “Sexual Healing”. title: The Old Vicarage Hotel and Restaurant, Bridgwater, Somerset
subtitle: This unique and quirky hotel is a 10 minute drive from the main line station at Bridgwater or 24 minutes from M5 Junction 24 - so is close to all connecting services and local amenities and supermarkets.
bodyContent: “Looking for somewhere really special to stay, look no further you have found it”, “I don’t think I have ever been made to feel so welcome”, are just some of our recent 5-star reviews. This historic hotel has been lovingly renovated with bedrooms individually designed for complete relaxation and comfort. If you want to be spoilt, relax and eat delicious food visit Candy, Peter and their friendly, professional team whose mission to give every guest (and their dogs) the warmest of welcomes and most memorable stay. The Old Vicarage is tucked away in peaceful surroundings overlooking St Mary’s Church, the only building in Bridgwater older than it, yet is only 10 minutes from the M5. The hotel is full of historic importance dating back to 1327; it is said that Isambard Kingdom Brunel designed the town bridge in the 17th century Oak Room and Judge Jeffery’s stayed, one of the bedrooms even has its own wig cabinet. Each of the 18 en-suite bedrooms are individually designed and kept spotlessly clean with the most comfortable beds and views over the gardens or church. The south facing gardens are glorious, perfect for weddings and enjoying in the sunshine. On cooler evenings there is a cosy bar and snug with comfy sofas for enjoying a drink or two in front of the fire, an oak panelled restaurant and a brand new undercover patio with a pizza oven. A short drive and you can be alone on the Quantock Hills walking in Coleridge’s footsteps, bird watching on the Somerset Levels or hunting for fossils on the Jurassic Coast at Kilve. For the more energetic kayaking, coasteering, mountain biking, pony trekking are all on hand or if shopping is your thing Bristol, Bath, Taunton, Glastonbury and Wells are not far away. Book today for your perfect holiday.
tagline: “Looking for somewhere really special to stay, look no further you have found it”

title: Jazz Emu: The Pleasure Is All Yours
subtitle: Musical meteor Jazz Emu was born to please you.
bodyContent: Total and Utter Audience Satisfaction is his middle name - finally after a long and financially ruinous deed poll process. But he's feeling uneasy. A review described his last show as 'a bit much'. What? Was his seventeenth stage-dive too tastefully executed? Not this time. This time, he's living up to his middle namesake. Following a tour of the US, a triumphant Edinburgh Fringe run and sell-out runs in London, Jazz Emu is back on tour with a brand-new musical odyssey. Jazz Emu rose to prominence online - with his videos and songs receiving hundreds of millions of views and streams - before bringing his special brand of comedy mastery to the real world. He has since featured on 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown, won a host of awards, and been listed as the 26th Funniest Comedian of the 21st Century by The Telegraph. His latest show was among the Best Reviewed Shows at Edinburgh Fringe 2025 (British Comedy Guide) and was listed as one of The Guardian's Golden Shows to See at Edinburgh Fringe 2025.
tagline: Musical meteor Jazz Emu was born to please you.

title: Great Western Hotel - Taunton
subtitle: Relax or work in a beautifully renovated Victorian hotel, conveniently situated opposite Taunton rail station.
bodyContent: Stay with us All of our boutique rooms at the Great Western Hotel offer King sized beds, and simple quality bedrooms with free Wi-Fi. We are proud to say we are committed to going single use plastic free, and using amenities such as fresh milk and ground coffee in your room, so you wake up ready to get on with the day. The Station: Conference The 2 conference rooms at the Great Western Hotel are flexible spaces which can be tailored to suit your needs each seating up to 60 people theatre style, or 40 cabaret style. As well as the larger conference rooms, smaller breakout spaces can also be booked to provide additional space. Catering facilities can be provided at additional cost, with dietary requirements taken into account to provide healthy and nutritious buffets. The Lounge Relax in the comfort of the Lounge, whether you are business brunching, using it for a drop-in venue for ad-hoc meetings or just waiting for a train, the cafe dining area offers free high speed Wi-Fi and a varied menu, overseen by our award winning team from the Beach Hotel and complimented by locally sourced craft ales, ciders and gins.
tagline: Relax or work in a beautifully renovated Victorian hotel

title: Longleat Accommodation
subtitle: From the moment you arrive at Longleat for your stay, you will enjoy an unrivalled experience. During the day, explore the Safari Park and array of Main Square attractions, as well as leafy walks within our beautiful parkland. In the evening, make yourself at home in one of our stunning properties steeped in history, luxury and comfort.
bodyContent: Wake up as a resident of the Longleat Estate Welcome to our exclusive, rural escapes in the heart of the West Country. Nestled within Longleat Estate’s beautiful grounds and woodland, a stay in our luxury properties offers an unforgettable experience, each with a unique perspective of our astonishing kingdom. Surround yourself with acres of peace and quiet, enjoy woodland walks and cosy evenings, or delight in panoramic safari views and the sound of lions as your head hits the pillow. Your stay includes: Park entry for each day of your stay A continental breakfast each morning A decadent welcome hamper of delicious local food and drink A 24 hour concierge service The option for luxury enhancements, including Champagne afternoon tea delivered to your door Unrivalled ccess to the stunning surroundings of Longleat Estate. Visit Website
tagline: From the moment you arrive at Longleat for your stay, you will enjoy an unrivalled experience.

title: Rickbarton Cottage
subtitle: Rickbarton Cottage is the ideal base for that countryside retreat that everyone thrives from.
bodyContent: Walks from your doorstep, fresh air, country Pubs and a Farm Shop. Yet, close proximity to Bath (5 miles) and Bradford on Avon (2 miles) means that they get the best of both worlds! Guests can make use of the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool during their stay. Local Farm Shop village shop and village pub within walking distance or a short drive. The Kennet and Avon Canal is also within walking distance, for any keen walkers or cyclists. The cottage itself has an open-plan kitchen/living room. It is equipped with everything you should need. The bedroom has a double bed, which has been made up with fresh white linen prior to your arrival. The en-suite bathroom has a bath with a shower above the bath. There is space for a cot if needed (please check in advance of stay)
tagline: Rickbarton Cottage is the ideal base for that countryside retreat that everyone thrives from.

title: Ania Magliano: Peach Fuzz
subtitle: Fresh from starring in the latest series of Taskmaster, Ania Magliano (Live At The Apollo, Edinburgh Comedy Awards Best Show Nominee) brings a brand-new show full of jokes, confessions, and occasionally unhinged observations to venues nationwide
bodyContent: Fresh from starring in the latest series of Taskmaster, Ania Magliano (Live At The Apollo, Edinburgh Comedy Awards Best Show Nominee) brings a brand-new show full of jokes, confessions, and occasionally unhinged observations to venues nationwide. From the quirks of her own body to the legend that is Eve (yes, from Adam and), to her newly discovered boundaries, Peach Fuzz is Ania at her most relatable – and most funny. Ania has opened for Ed Gamble, Marc Maron and Catherine Cohen, and writes for Amelia Dimoldenberg’s Chicken Shop Date. Her choices on the Off Menu podcast are widely regarded as the worst of all time. 'A gift for observational comedy and weaving beautifully crafted routines' ★★★★★ The Telegraph 'Will have you crying with laughter' ★★★★ The Guardian
