title: The Glastonbury Town House
subtitle: Paula welcomes you to her comfortable 4 Star Edwardian Bed & Breakfast close to Glastonbury Town Centre, Glastonbury Tor, Chalice Well Gardens , Rural Life Museum and other local attractions.
bodyContent: We offer a quality bed and breakfast service in the heart of Glastonbury , from where exploring Glastonbury Abbey, Glastonbury Tor and the Glastonbury Thorn is a matter of a short stroll. The Bed and Breakfast offers group bookings. 2 twin rooms and a king room offer up to 6 people accommodation. Paula offers packed lunches, afternoon tea and evening meals at an extra cost for group bookings. Liaise with Paula direct to book group bookings. The Townhouse is only a few minutes’ walk from the hustle of Glastonbury‘s busy town centre full of unusual shops, churches, historic buildings and varied cafes and bars. The house has far reaching views of Glastonbury town and the Mendip Hills beyond. The Townhouse offer secure facilities for cyclists and is Proximity to Millfield school. The Glastonbury Townhouse is 1 miles from Street and the Clarkes Outlet Village and 3 miles from the various nature reserves on the Somerset levels. We are 28 miles South of Bristol and Bath, 20 miles from Bristol International airport and within easy reach of Stonehenge , Yeovilton Airbase and other historic places of interest. The Glastonbury Townhouse can be used as a base for exploring the Isles of Avalon, Somerset Peat Levels, Exmoor (Lorna Doone country), the North Somerset Coast and large parts of the county of Dorset . Our visitors tell us that our proximity to Bristol Airport , Bath , the bath and west showgound, Shepton Mallet, Frome, Wells, Street, Yeovil is a key part of their decision to make their stay with us in Glastonbury . Of course we also have guests who visit specifically for the Glastonbury Festival, Glastonbury Extravaganza and the famous Glastonbury Carnival, we are on the route, watch from the comfort of your room! We are also open for Christmas and New Year bookings.

title: The Golden Fleece
subtitle: Welcome to The Golden Fleece. Our luxury, en-suite rooms offer a peaceful place to stay and explore the Three Counties of Somerset, Dorset and Devon.
bodyContent: Our five luxury en-suite rooms are detached from the main building and set back from the main road. They offer independent access so you can come and go as you please with no need to pass through any communal areas or shared corridors. Dogs are welcome (with well behaved owners) for an extra £10 per dog per night.
tagline: Welcome to The Golden Fleece. Our luxury, en-suite rooms offer a peaceful place to stay

title: The Great House
subtitle: All five of our bedroom suites are large and filled with light flooding in from the large Georgian sash windows.
bodyContent: Each bedroom has been extensively refurbished over recent months, with great emphasis placed on the sympathetic restoration of the many original period features. Designer fabrics from GP & J Baker, Thibaut and Sanderson compliment historic paint colours by Farrow & Ball. We spoil all our guests with feather and down duvets and pillows, and the finest 100% Egyptian cotton bed linen, for an unbeatable sleeping experience. Pamper yourself with our luxurious Anyah complimentary toiletries which are both Green and Vegan – even the packaging carries the elusive EU Eco-label! Due to its Grade II Listed status, the installation of TV aerials would cause too much damage to the fabric of the house, so there are no televisions in our guest bedrooms. Please feel free to bring a tablet or laptop to stream programmes using our Wifi.

title: The Hatch Inn
subtitle: A warm and friendly welcome is exactly what you will receive when you stay with us.
bodyContent: Whether you wish to join us in the restaurant or just enjoy a peaceful escape to the beautiful countryside we will endeavour to make your stay at the Hatch Inn a pleasant and memorable one. Breakfast We offer a full English breakfast which we use award winning sausages from the local butcher or a continental style buffet.
tagline: A warm and friendly welcome is exactly what you will receive when you stay with us.

title: The Henry
subtitle: ‘The Henry’ is probably Bath’s most central Guest House. Just 100m from the railway and bus stations and 150m from the Abbey and Roman Baths.
bodyContent: ⭐ Book Direct for Reward Card Offers ‘The Henry’ is probably Bath’s most central Guest House. Just 100m from the railway and bus stations and 150m from the Abbey and Roman Baths, The Henry is perfectly located amongst the historic attractions of Bath. Located in a beautiful Georgian house we are less than a minute from Bath’s main shopping street. Whether your visit is as a tourist, for shopping or just for fun The Henry is the place to stay. We also have two self-contained apartments less than 100m away from the main house this can be rented as a self-catering or with breakfast served in the dining room at The Henry.
tagline: ‘The Henry’ is probably Bath’s most central Guest House.

title: The Hollies
subtitle: The Hollies was built in 1851 in a meadow beside the old Bath – Wells turnpike.
bodyContent: The Hollies was built in 1851 in a meadow beside the old Bath – Wells turnpike. This was also the Fosse Way, built by the Roman Legions some 2000 years ago. The house, with its late Georgian facade, was once the home of the curate of St. Lukes Church, which is next door. It is now a gracious guest house with three individually designed rooms overlooking the award-winning garden. Every room has its own bath or shower room and is complete with television, radio alarm clock, hairdryer, bath robes and tea and coffee tray. Our comfortable Library with over 2000 books is available for guests.
tagline: The Hollies was built in 1851 in a meadow beside the old Bath – Wells turnpike.

title: The Hood Arms
subtitle: An historic 17th Century coaching inn situated in the village of Kilve on the edge of the Quantock Hills.
bodyContent: The Hood is a family run inn steeped in history, on the route of the Coleridge Way and close to the Jurassic coastline and beaches of Somerset. We are open for Lunch, Dinner & Sunday Roast. Children are always welcome & the bar/snug areas are dog friendly. We also have a large garden which is dog friendly and has a purpose built children's area. You can also enjoy a game of boules or table tennis. Sunday Lunch: We cherish a good family meal and Sunday Roasts are just that. Enjoy a selection of roast meats with all the trimmings. All our food is locally sourced, freshly cooked and lovingly prepared! *For allergy advice speak to a member of staff. We are Dog Friendly! We also have nine superior stylish and comfortable rooms to let with free wifi and high speed internet. Based on the edge of the beautiful Quantock Hills and Exmoor National Park, we are ideally placed for walkers. The South West Coast Path runs right past us on Kilve beach which is part of the spectaular Jurassic coast. Kilve is a perfect location for collecting ammonites and reptile remains. The beach is also ideal for rock pooling, set in tranquil surroundings and ideal for all the family to enjoy.
tagline: An historic 17th Century coaching inn situated in the village of Kilve

title: The Kennard
subtitle: The Kennard gives you the chance to discover and enjoy a stay in a true Georgian Town House.
bodyContent: The Kennard gives you the chance to discover and enjoy a stay in a true Georgian Town House, now restored to a boutique guesthouse. Built as a lodging house in 1794, The Kennard, today, offers twelve recently refurbished and individually decorated bedrooms, furnished for your every comfort, over five floors with a fine selection of superior doubles, standard doubles, snug doubles, two singles with shared bathroom, a twin and a triple room. Our rooms offer either a view over our garden and the city, or look out onto the street. We also have a small sitting area and an honesty bar located on the landings. Quietly situated only 5 minutes from the Abbey, the Roman Baths, the Thermae Spa and the railway station and some of the best restaurants and shopping venues our beautiful city has to offer. We hope you will stay with us and enjoy the experience of staying in one of Bath’s original Georgian townhouses with service and accommodation that truly reflects this beautiful city’s social history and culture.
tagline: The Kennard gives you the chance to discover and enjoy a stay in a true Georgian Town House.

title: The Kings Arms
subtitle: The inn was completely refurbished in March 2013 and now offers 15 spacious and bright bedrooms for individuals, couples and families.
bodyContent: Each of our 15 rooms have been designed with your comfort in mind and benefit from: Colour television Tea and coffee making facilities En-suite toilet with bath and/or shower Complimentry toiletries. Hairdryers, irons and ironing boards are also available on request. All rooms are serviced daily and the inn also offers free off road parking to all guests subject to availablity. Breakfast is served daily and we offer the choice of either full traditional English or continental style breakfasts together with juice, tea and coffee. As we prepare all meals fresh on the premises, orders can be altered to suit your dietry requirements.
tagline: The inn was completely refurbished in March 2013 and now offers 15 spacious and bright bedrooms

title: The Loft Room
subtitle: We opened our new self catering venture in June 2018 and no longer offer B&B from the house. Mountlands Lodge is tucked away at the end of the Garden with your own enclosed space and side access. The perfect secret hideaway.

title: The Lynch Country House
subtitle: The Lynch bed and breakfast is a classic English country house set in beautiful, peaceful and secluded gardens.
bodyContent: A hidden gem that you wouldn't even know was there. A little haven of peace and quiet. A place to spend quality time away from the hustle and bustle of the wider world just beyond the trees. The Lynch Bed & Breakfast is the perfect base for exploring the Somerset levels. We are just 40 minutes from the fabulous Jurassic coast, beautiful countryside, grand houses and gardens, national treasures, great places to eat, drink and ...relax. Take a few minutes to look over our site, we are sure you will find what you are looking for.

title: The Manor Arms
subtitle: The Manor Arms, the only pub in the village, has always been a place of great attraction.
bodyContent: This lovely old village pub has withstood the ravages of modern design. The blue flagstone floors will still remain the same. Looking back over the years there are a few changes. The pub could be entered by a separate door from the outside to the top bar. To move from the best bar to the top bar from inside meant lifting up a section of the counter which was only allowed on special occasions. Behind the counter stood wooden barrels on a jib of beer and cider with their wooden taps which seemed to squeak at every turn. Draught beer could be bought at sixpence a pint, whisky sevenpence a nip and brandy bought at so much a noggin. Bottles of home brewed beer and Hunstman stout were taken straight out of the crates. The attractive sign bearing the Hoskyns Crest and family motto: "Finem Respice" which means "Look towards the end" hung on the outside wall until 1956. It was quite evident by then that all cattle lorries and furniture vans had been built much higher and the angle iron standing out carrying the sign was being continually bent back, and having to be repaired. Co-op vans and double decker sheep lorries became even broader and higher and seemed to look out and say "Get Back!". One fine morning it was discovered that the sign had received a real knock and was hanging precariously from its bracket by one chain. "This is enough!", said Colonel Macleod, the agent who had been appointed to follow Mr Raper in 1950. So the sign was taken down by George Toms and his merry men, John Diaper and Alec Eglon, all estate workers, and mounted on a wooden pillar in a much safer place on the edge of the village green, its present position. The beautiful sign in its ornamental iron frame is now crowned by the word "Food"! Most of the customers were locals who spent their evenings drinking while playing dominoes, shove halfpenny, table billiards and cards. Women hardly ever went inside the bar, but often fetched drink from the jug and bottle department. They never smoked. The pub closed sharp at 10 o'clock and quite often the village policeman was outside. The landlord, Mr Hallett was called "Buster". He drove a high spring trap and his pony, a very unpredictable sort, often refused to move off in the right direction. Harry Male, an old pensioner living across the road, often came to his assistance with a pat on its neck; to be led a few steps was all that was needed and away it trotted merrily. We have been unable to contact Mr Parkman's family to gain permission to use this snippet from what is an excellent book, and we are most grateful for the information provided. We will of course gladly post any credits due here if required. WE HAVE ONLY ONE DESIGNATED ROOM FOR THOSE OF YOU WHO WISH TO STAY WITH US AND BRING A DOG. PLEASE CONFIRM WHETHER THE ROOM IS AVAILABLE FOR YOUR STAY. THERE IS A CHARGE OF 5 POUNDS FOR THE DOGS ACCOMMODATION.
tagline: The Manor Arms, the only pub in the village, has always been a place of great attraction.

title: The Mendip Inn
subtitle: Our individually designed guest bedrooms are luxurious and elegant, welcoming and above all, comfortable.
bodyContent: All rooms are double en-suite, with tasteful, stylish décor and crisp, white linen. Facilities include complimentary toiletries, free Wi-Fi, Freeview TV, radio alarm clock and hair dryer. An iron and ironing board are available on request. All bathrooms have a power-assisted shower, hand wash basin and lavatory, towel warming rack and large mirror with bright lighting. Located centrally to the walks and tourist areas of Somerset, a stay at the Mendip Inn provides a comfortable stop-off en-route to your destination or a fantastic base from which to explore the delightful Somerset countryside.
tagline: Our individually designed guest bedrooms are luxurious and elegant

title: The Mill House
subtitle: Situated in Yeovil, Pen Mill Townhouse features accommodation with a flat-screen TV.
bodyContent: Guests can also relax in the garden or in the shared lounge area. Weymouth is 47 km from the homestay, while Taunton is 44 km from the property.

title: The Mount B&B Somerton
subtitle: A beautiful bed and breakfast in a Somerset village, close to Glastonbury, Yeovilton and the A303.
bodyContent: The Mount, Somerton is a grand but welcoming house set in an acre of garden, and yet only a three minute flat walk to three pubs and the charming Georgian town centre of Somerton. Our top floor suite is ideal for one to four people. Your own sitting room is a fabulous place to relax or work from, with a large work table looking out across the garden. One floor down, we have a lovely double room also with its own sitting room. All rooms enjoy total peace and quiet, with lots of sun and light, and lovely views. A hearty breakfast is included, and you also have your own microwave, fridge etc. ​ As well as pubs we also have a a popular antiques emporium and several good shops within a few minutes' flat walk. Our large 200-year old home is a beautiful, comfortable and peaceful place to stay, with lots of private off-street parking. We are proud of our 9.9 out of 10 rating on Booking.com, and excellent reviews on Trip Advisor. ​ The Mount is ideal for a well deserved rest, business trips, courses in Glastonbury, Compton Dundon, and Langport, a sight seeing holiday taking in Wells Cathedral, Barrington Court, Glastonbury Tor and many more, and it is also a wonderful place to stay if you are here for a family occasion such as a wedding. Please phone Trish or Henry on 01458 270 007 or 07975 879151 to book a room, or if you have any questions. We are always happy to oblige, if you have any special requests.

title: The Notley Arms Inn
subtitle: Re-built around 1870 The Notley Arms Inn, Exmoor National Park, Somerset has recently been refurbished back a traditional country inn.
bodyContent: With open fires and a beautiful beer garden bounded by a bubbling stream and a separate coach house with six en-suite bedrooms which have been awarded 'Four Star Gold' by the AA. COVID19 Update: Exmoor has been place in Tier 3. Consequently we are closed. We serve Somerset's finest Ales, Beers and Ciders as well as the best local produce for our meals, which are freshly prepared daily by our award winning team of chefs. Our prices includes a delicious fresh home cooked full Exmoor Somerset breakfast. Whilst in a stunningly beautiful part of Exmoor, we are conveniently located to Taunton (13 miles); Minehead (9 miles) and Dunster (7 miles). Other nearby points of interests are: Tarr Steps; Exmoor's most famous landmark is an ancient stone clapper bridge shaded by gnarled old trees. Its huge slabs are propped up on stone columns embedded in the River Barle. Local folklore aside (which declares it was used by the devil for sunbathing), it first pops into the historical record in the 1600s. Holnicote Estate; The 5060-hectare Holnicote Estate sweeps south east out of Porlock, taking in a string of impossibly pretty villages. Picturesque Bossington leads to charming Allerford , with its 15th-century packhorse bridge. The biggest, Selworthy , offers eye-catching Exmoor views, a cafe, shop, and cob-and-thatch cottages clustering around the village green. Cliff Railway; This extraordinary piece of Victorian engineering sees two cars linked by a steel cable descend or ascend the sloping cliff face according to the weight of water in the cars’ tanks. All burnished wood and polished brass, it’s been running since 1890 and makes for an unmissable ride. And finally we would like to recommend, the beautiful West Somerset Steam Railway; the longest Steam Heritage Railway in the UK connecting Minehead with Bishops Lydeard.

title: The Old Bookshop
subtitle: The Old Bookshop is a most elegant and charming period residence with pretty, well-maintained gardens occupying a wonderful village setting in Williton
bodyContent: he village is conveniently located at the foot of the famous Quantock Hills (AONB) close to the sea and Exmoor National Park and midway between Taunton and Minehead. Formerly a bookshop, the Old Bookshop is believed to date back to the 17th century. It has been tastefully renovated to offer you all the comforts needed to give you a stay to remember. It has delightful bedrooms with comfortable beds and either a private shower room or private bathroom. Both bedrooms are decorated in a homely style and have bathrobes, complimentary shower gel, shampoo and hot drink facilities. he guest living room has beams aplenty and a quirky brick floor with a good selection of books, games and maps There is a large flat screen television with Sky, Netflix and all the usual channels along with a selection of DVDs and CDs.

title: The Old Post Office – Central Frome
subtitle: Situated in Frome in the Somerset region, The Victorian Post House - Central Frome is a 5-star property boasting free WiFi.
bodyContent: You’re sure to put your stamp of approval on this former post office, ideally located just a few minutes’ walk from the heart of Frome. The property has the striking and quirky appeal of a boutique hotel, with lots of homely touches that make the Old Post House a welcoming home to return to after visiting the lions of Longleat, or indulging in retail therapy in the historic City of Bath. Families, couples and friends will be left with a wealth of lasting memories after a rewarding stay at the Victorian Post House. The Old Post Office’s corner-street position echoes its past as a community hub, and today it still feels like you’re in the prime location for a Frome adventure. Enter the house through the lovingly restored shop front and door, to find a welcoming open plan living area: comfortable sofas, a dining area and modern kitchen are all easily accessible to your family and friends. Light floods in through the wall of post house windows, and the space will quickly feel like home. Relax into the fluffy cushions with a good film on Netflix or CatchUp TV, while the little ones (or big kids!) amuse themselves with the board games, toys and books provided in house.

title: The Old Pound Inn
subtitle: The Old Pound Inn is a traditional village pub in Langport with a reputation for good honest food, drinks and rooms. We offer a family-friendly and dog-friendly service with regular events (quizzes, bingo, markets, live music nights) and special offers. Check out the website for the latest news.
bodyContent: The Old Pound Inn in Aller, Langport is a traditional village pub with a well-earned reputation for good honest food, drinks and rooms. We offer a family-friendly and dog-friendly service with regular events (quizzes, bingo, markets, live music nights) and special offers. Check out the website and/or follow us on Facebook for the latest news. Formerly known as the White Lion Public House, this 16th -century pub was re-christened the Old Pound Inn in 1980, named after the old village animal pound that occupied the site before it became a pub. The Old Pound Inn has a good selection of West Country beers that are pulled from the sprung stillage in our cellar. We have an open Dutch fire at the centre of the bar, a lounge area, a snug, and a 44-cover restaurant serving good honest food daily. We are of course a dog-friendly place - ask your server if they have any dog snacks available!
tagline: The Old Pound Inn is a traditional village pub in Langport

title: The Old Stables B&B
subtitle: Nestled in the hamlet of Chelynch, in the beautiful Somerset countryside, a warm and friendly welcome awaits you. The Old Stables is a lovingly restored 17th century, Grade II Listed barn of outstanding character.
bodyContent: Nestled in the hamlet of Chelynch, in the beautiful Somerset countryside, a warm and friendly welcome awaits you. The Old Stables is a lovingly restored 17th century, Grade II Listed barn of outstanding character. We are ideally located on the edge of the Mendip Hills (an area of Outstanding Natural Beauty) with easy access to the many delights that Somerset has to offer. Whether you want to revisit history in the UNESCO World Heritage City of Bath , hike in the magnificent Cheddar Gorge , attend one of the many events at The Royal Bath and West Showground or just enjoy a day walking in the beautiful surrounding countryside, Somerset has something for everyone! Our 3 en-suite rooms, The Garden Room, The Hayloft and The Granary, have been thoughtfully decorated and furnished with our guests in mind. Comfy beds with quality linens, locally made pine furniture, antique finds and all those luxurious little extras that you deserve. Home baked cakes or biscuits await you in your room. Fresh milk for your selection of teas and coffee can be found in the silent mini fridge together with bottled water. There’s adequate space in your fridge as well for any of the abundance of locally sourced goodies that you might pick up from one of the local Farmers’ markets that can be found all over the county. Our bountiful, traditional farmhouse breakfast, using locally sourced produce, whenever possible, is served in our very special 17th century beamed dining room. Take your time and enjoy – there’s no rush. We look forward to welcoming you to The Old Stables very soon.
tagline: Nestled in the hamlet of Chelynch, in the beautiful Somerset countryside.

title: The Olde House Dunster
subtitle: Welcome to The Olde House Dunster - a Family run Bed & Breakfast and Tea Shop in a 16th century Grade 2 Listed building at the heart of Dunster High Street.
bodyContent: George's Bed & Breakfast offers three high quality, value for money ensuite rooms in our 16th century Grade 2 listed building. Each has unique historic character. We welcome Walkers & Cyclists, but regrettably, not dogs.
tagline: Welcome to The Olde House Dunster - a Family run Bed & Breakfast and Tea Shop

title: The Place To Stay
subtitle: "Our Mission Is To Give Our Guests A Highly Comfortable, Relaxing and Unforgettable Stay, Making Them Want To Rush Back When They Leave!"
bodyContent: We are Joss and Sam Green-Armtyge, and as a mother and son team, in 2013 we took over ‘The Place To Stay’ at Knoll Hill Farm on the edge of the small Somerset village of Trudoxhill on the edge of the Mendip Hills. The ex-farm, its buildings and its adjoining acres were in a sorry state, but we felt the old early 20 th Century Farmhouse had loads of character and the adjacent barns had much potential. We developed a vision to provide really superior bed and breakfast accommodation based on what we would want ourselves - and with Trudoxhill being a 'stones throw' from Longleat and Longleat Safari Park, and being close to so many other lovely places such as Stourhead Gardens, Bath, Wells, Cheddar Gorge Caves and Wookey Hole, we felt The 'Place To Stay' would make a popular touring base. Two years later, an extensive refurbishment of the rooms in the old farmhouse and renovation and conversion of the old barns into smart and distinctive living accommodation, and ‘The Place To Be’ was moulded into a beautiful, boutique Guest House with 9 very stylish and individual rooms. Landscaping of the gardens followed and space was created for a collection of rare breed birds to be given a home and our lovely mare, Lucy and her companion pony, Rosie were treated to a new stable block with green pastures to graze in. Our friendly house dog, Dylan and pony Rosie are often available for children to spend time with.

title: The Rest and Be Thankful Inn
subtitle: Bed and Breakfast Accommodation in Exmoor National Park at The Rest and Be Thankful Inn and restaurant in the centre of Wheddon Cross, the highest village on Exmoor.
bodyContent: Our B and B is a perfect place to stay and a great base from which to explore the beautiful Exmoor National Park. The Inn was originally a staging post for travellers on their way between Dunster and Dulverton, and you will still find a warm welcome, good food and extremely comfortable accommodation awaiting you there today, almost 200 years later! Whether you are looking for a bed and breakfast for a relaxing break in beautiful surroundings on Exmoor, or a more active holiday, the Rest and Be Thankful Inn and Exmoor are sure to meet your every need. The fantastic Exmoor National Park is home to Snow Drop Valley. Tours and walks to Snow Drop Valley can be accessed from the bus leaving right from our door. The B&B also has enviable access to the West Somerset Railway less than 10 miles away. If you are looking for a walking, cycling, or fly-fishing break, we will do everything we can to provide you with the perfect holiday. There is a secure store at the Inn, where cycles and other equipment can be kept, and we also have a drying room for wet clothes and boots. Horse riding and hunting can be arranged with prior notice.

title: The Roseate Villa Bath
subtitle: The Roseate Villa Bath occupies a quiet corner of the city. A short walk from the heart of Bath, favoured for its heritage and cultural tourism, The Villa overlooks Henrietta Park, a 7 acre park opened to celebrate the Diamond Jubilee of Queen Victoria of 1897.
bodyContent: The Roseate Villa Bath occupies a quiet corner of the city. A short walk from the heart of Bath, favoured for its heritage and cultural tourism, the Villa overlooks Henrietta Park, a 7 acre park opened to celebrate the Diamond Jubilee of Queen Victoria of 1897. Henrietta Park is situated within walking distance of the city centre and is an oasis of tranquility with places to sit quietly or take a relaxing stroll around the circular walk amongst many fine trees and flora that include the Purple Sycamore, Golden Elms, Caucasion Mapel and a line of Baumannii Horse Chestnuts. The Villa encompasses two converted Victorian houses which have had a characterful legacy. Guests can always request information regarding informative excursions, or knowledge of the best activities whilst on a nonchalant weekend getaway. Take the tour of the Roman Baths and Regency Crescent or witness the views of Prior Park, Jane Austen Museum and the grandeur of Bath Abbey. You can always expect a warm welcome, immaculate hospitality, attention to detail and a genuine connection with every guest when you visit the Roseate Villa Bath. They are delighted to welcome dogs at The Roseate Villa Bath. Their team is always around to ensure that everyone can enjoy their stay with their dogs. Rooms The Villa houses 21 individual rooms with exclusive features. Every room has a bespoke Hypnos bed, goose down duvets and Egyptian cotton linen. Each attached bathroom is stocked with Penhaligon’s products and large fluffy bath sheets.The rooms are equipped with a flat-screen television and digital radio. The Villa hosts a private garden for guests to relax and enjoy an indulgent Afternoon Tea. Accolades The Roseate Villa Bath won the Customer service awards (Bath Business Awards) 2016 – 2017 & 2017 – 2018. Dine Breakfast: The Roseate Villa Bath features a dedicated breakfast chef who will tailor your breakfast preferences to your fancy. The Roseate Villa’s breakfast offering serves freshly baked bread straight from the oven, freshly squeezed orange juice, complimentary smoothies and Bucks Fizz with the food as well as a range of eggs, homemade jams and marmalades. Food offerings are locally procured and can be served in-room, breakfast-in-bed style. Afternoon Tea: Experience a truly exquisite Afternoon Tea, perfect for when you require light refreshment after a day of exploring Bath’s heritage and cultural spots. The Afternoon Tea symbolizes the quintessential English tea tradition with a few touches of modernity. Expect finger sandwiches, freshly baked scones with clotted cream and strawberry jam, delicate cakes, chocolate delice, pink lamingtons, macaroons and a host of tea choices, including a Champagne Afternoon Tea, perfect if you’d like to make the experience slightly more fulfilling and memorable.
tagline: The Roseate Villa Bath occupies a quiet corner of the city.

title: The Royal Oak
subtitle: The Royal Oak Inn offers 4* Accommodation in the heart of Exmoor with access directly onto the Moor.
bodyContent: All rooms were refurbished in May 2019 and have been refurbished further in November 2020 to provide additional luxury fixtures & features. Each of the eight rooms are individually designed with Sanderson Bed linens, soft crisp towels & comfortable beds for a relaxing night’s sleep. There are four different room types to choose from, the standard double with private facilities, deluxe doubles, superior double & superking/twin, the luxury king suite and luxury superking/twin rooms. Attention to Dog owners We love your four legged best friends and we have our own dogs here too. They are welcome throughout the building and can dine in the bars or restaurant with you. They even have their own menu. Dogs are welcome in Deluxe rooms only. They cannot be left in the rooms unattended and if we can ask that they are kept on a lead throughout the building. There are lots of wonderful walks straight from the door to exercise them. Please just ask a member of staff. There is a £9 per night per dog charge. If you require towels, bowls, waste bags etc, please just ask.
tagline: The Royal Oak Inn offers 4* Accommodation in the heart of Exmoor

title: The Royal Oak Luxborough
subtitle: The Royal Oak Inn Luxborough has been at the heart of the pretty village for over 600 years and still to this day retains some of the building's original features
bodyContent: Inside you’ll find the original flagstone and cobblestone flooring, coupled with rugged stone walls and open beams – giving the inn unrivalled character and charm. The Royal Oak Inn houses spacious guestrooms and a large yet intimate bar and dining area. It’s the perfect place to kick back by the fireplace and catch up with friends over a pint of real ale – or enjoy a freshly prepared meal featuring delicious local produce.

title: The School House
subtitle: Nicky and Jim welcome you to their historic Victorian school house where you can relax to plan your exploration of the Somerset countryside.
bodyContent: Built in1872, the school provided education for the children of Woolavington and the surrounding area. It was decommissioned as a school in 1984 and became a private dwelling. The house has been updated to include en suite showers or private bathrooms to each bedroom whilst still retaining the character of the property. The large double bedrooms are comfortably furnished with a separate television lounge/library available for visitors to relax in. Breakfast is served in the high ceilinged room once used as the infants classroom. The owners are onsite everyday. The village of Woolavington is located at the western end of the Polden Hills in Somerset above the Levels, six miles from the coast, and a short drive from the Quantock Hills in the west and the Mendip Hills to the east. It is a few minutes from the M5 (J23) motorway, the A39 and A303, with excellent links to the West Country. The towns of Bridgwater, Street and Glastonbury are approximately 10 minutes away, with Wells and Taunton about 20 minutes by car. Bristol and Bath are a 40 minute drive. A stay at The School House is perfect for: - enjoying the extensive wildlife and beauty of the area - walking, cycling and birdwatching on the Levels and surrounding hills - exploring the historic towns of Glastonbury, Wells and Bath - visiting Cheddar Gorge, Wookey Hole, Ebbor Gorge and the coast - visiting Quantock Hills and Mendip Hills, both AONB - shopping at Clarks Outlet Village, Kilver Court and Bristol - stopping off en-route to the West Country - transport enthusiasts with aviation, motor and railway museums close by - exploring the industrial heritage of the West Country - gardeners with many gardens and National Trust properties in the area - Glastonbury music festival - Bridgwater Carnival - business travellers - Millfield and Shapwick school

title: The Seymour Arms
subtitle: Set in a half-timbered building in the Mendip Hills, this casual pub with rooms is less than a mile from Blagdon Lake, 8 miles from caves at Cheddar Gorge, and 6 miles from Bristol Airport.
bodyContent: The 5 warm rooms feature hardwood floors and en suite bathrooms. They have Wi-Fi, flat-screens, and tea and coffeemakers. Some add lake views. The restaurant/bar serves British cuisine and a Sunday roast. Limited parking is available.

title: The Sheppey
subtitle: Our stunning, modern ensuite bedrooms in the heart of the Somerset Levels.
bodyContent: A stone’s throw from RSPB Ham Wall, West Hay Moor, Shapwick Heath, Avalon Marshes and only minutes from the historic and mystical town of Glastonbury and the City of Wells. Downstairs we offer brilliant modern European food, a constantly changing roster of beers and ales, and a bar covered in casks of local ciders that’ll knock your socks off. Reserved Parking Spaces for all Staying Guests as we know parking gets tight We’re also one of the best places to catch live music around – but that’s just our opinion.
tagline: Our stunning, modern ensuite bedrooms in the heart of the Somerset Levels.

title: The Swan
subtitle: We’re open all day for a quick drink, a snack or a delicious meal.
bodyContent: Come and sit in our bar beside a woodburner, watch the world go by at tables out front, dine in the restaurant or alfresco on the terrace – or just enjoy the peace of the garden. We have completely refurbished The Swan, sympathetically modernising the building and restoring much of the original eighteenth & nineteenth century architecture. Opening as a Beer House in the early 1700s, the property was subsequently enlarged to become ‘The Swan Hotel’ from the mid 1800s with rooms, stables and coaching yard. After many years in the hands of indifferent pub companies, The Swan is now firmly back in business! The Swan has seven individually designed and supremely comfortable en-suite guest bedrooms. For offers & rates click here. There are six bedrooms on the first floor comprising 3 Big rooms, 2 Medium rooms and 1 Small room. The upstairs 7th bedroom is a spacious, light filled Loft room.

title: The Tithe Barn
subtitle: We love welcoming guests to our beautiful home – and we’re really proud of the number who return again and again. And who recommend their friends. And become our friends!
bodyContent: We hope you’ll do the same, so we’ll do everything we can to make sure that your stay is exactly as you want it. So we don’t have lots of fixed rules. Some people need to catch a plane or get to a meeting, and want to be up and off quickly. Others want a relaxing break, so if you want to get up and have breakfast late, that’s fine too. You can arrive when you like, just let us know. We can also book local restaurants.

title: The Vobster
subtitle: We have four modern, individual bedrooms, popular with couples and families visiting the local area.
bodyContent: Also with business people who are looking for a unique and restful place to stay out of town. We serve a delicious breakfast of cereals, patisseries, cooked breakfast using local produce and free range eggs (sometimes by our own chickens) accompanied by juice, tea and coffee. Check In Time From 4.00. Check in outside these times is possible by prior arrangement. Check out Time By 10.30 am. Smoking All areas within the building are non-smoking. Pets We regret we do not allow pets in guest bedrooms. Closing Times We take accommodation seven days per week. Dinner Tuesday to Saturday 6.30-8.00pm
tagline: We have four modern, individual bedrooms, popular with couples

title: The Wheatsheaf Combe Hay
subtitle: The Wheatsheaf Combe Hay is a country pub in the time honoured tradition - a place to eat, drink and sleep.
bodyContent: Located in an ancient village in beautiful surroundings, we serve the very best seasonal food and finest beers and wines in a mellow and welcoming setting. Polite Dogs are very welcome at The Wheatsheaf Combe Hay, Margaux, Gloria, Lyla, Lucky & Poppy our Working Cocker Spaniels all live at The Wheatsheaf. the shop - Wheatsheaf Bath Open Friday - Sunday 10am til 4pm Introducing our brand new farm shop at The Wheatsheaf, the place to go for all your farm shop needs. fresh fruit and vegetables, fantastic quality meat & fish, freshly baked bread & store cupboard essentials. order online for click and collect or come and have a look. Friday: Takeaway coffee, cake, bacon & sausage baps Saturday & Sunday: Takeaway coffee, cake, deli sandwiches, homemade scotch eggs, sausage rolls, bacon baps and more...

title: The Wheelhouse
subtitle: The Wheelhouse forms part of Gawbridge Mill with the river Parrett flowing under the building, dating back to the 18th Century and reputably built with the Ham stones from the derelict Muchelney Abbey
bodyContent: The Wheelhouse forms part of Gawbridge Mill with the river Parrett flowing under the building, dating back to the 18th Century and reputably built with the Ham stones from the derelict Muchelney Abbey. Gawbridge Mill was fully working until the 1960's.Some of the old workings are still in place Water Wheel, gearing, grinding stones, winches & winding wheels. Now the much loved home of Lynda and Tony Holliss a very warm welcome awaits you at The Wheelhouse B&B with Tony's quirky sense of humour & Lynda's expertise in the kitchen. You can step into "the Good Life", we have our own chickens, pigs, large vegetable plot and stables and produce 50% of our own electricity. We also make all our own bread, cakes, jams & marmalades. Situated near Martock, The Wheelhouse B&B is a perfect base to fish the river (providing you have a licence), canoe on the Parrett, walk, horse trek, cycle or bird watch in the wonderful Somerset Levels all within 2 miles or just sit on the Sun terrace or garden with a good book. Excellent local pubs selling real ales, local ciders and wonderful homemade meals. We welcome well behaved dogs.

title: The White Guest House
subtitle: Steve and Anna Wynne welcome you to The White Guest House, a level 7 minutes’ walk from the centre of Bath.
bodyContent: Steve and Anna Wynne welcome you to The White Guest House, a level 7 minutes’ walk from the centre of Bath, Bath Spa train station, Bath coach station and the Kennet & Avon Canal. Bath Abbey,Thermae .Spa We take pride in our flower display and have been a Bath in Bloom winner.
tagline: Steve and Anna Wynne welcome you to The White Guest House

title: The White Hart Somerton
subtitle: Each of our 8 en-suite rooms is unique and designed to provide a cosy haven. The 3 rooms at the front overlook Market Place and the beautiful 13th Century Church of St Michael and All Angels.
bodyContent: We also have 2 smaller rooms in the centre of the building which, whilst not enjoying the same views, are furnished to the same high standard as the other rooms. The 3 rooms at the rear overlook either the courtyard or garden. Each room has a generous king or super king size bed, crisp Egyptian linen and eclectic furniture. Some rooms can be used as twins and we can also squeeze in children in an extra z bed or cot. All rooms have smart TVs and free WiFi. They also have fresh coffee and tea, deep pile towels and hand made Lovegrove luxury natural bath and body products. The rates indicated below are for Bed and Breakfast. Special Offer Advanced Purchase rates are available as well – these are non-refundable and payment is taken at the time of the booking. The rates will be visible if you click the Book a Room button.

title: The White Horse
subtitle: At the very heart of Exmoor, nestling by the bridge over the River Exe, you’ll find the Exmoor White Horse Inn.
bodyContent: Festooned in Virginia creeper, this traditional 16th century building with classic period features has been family owned and run for generations. Kick off your boots and unwind beside one of our log fires. Choose from over 200 Malt Whiskys along with our fine selection of local Real Ales, savour our delicious locally sourced produce and at the end of a fantastic evening, retire to a sumptuous room full of charm and character. It’s no more than you would expect from an idyllic Inn, which offers its guests a warm and welcoming atmosphere in a true Westcountry style – a favourite all year round.

title: The White House
subtitle: B&B near Wells, Somerset. A warm welcome awaits you at The White House in the small and delightful Hamlet of Dulcote, Somerset. Just outside the City of Wells, and a short walk from the Market Place and Cathedral, The White House is ideally placed to meet your every need.
bodyContent: A warm welcome awaits you at The White House in the small and delightful hamlet of Dulcote, Somerset. Just outside the City of Wells , and a short walk from the Market Place and Cathedral, The White House is ideally placed to meet your every need. Providing luxury Bed and Breakfast and self catering accommodation in a peaceful idyllic village setting with a choice of three self-contained private guest suites and guaranteed off road secure parking, The White House is a perfect base from which to explore this area of outstanding natural beauty. The Bishops Palace and Market Place in Wells are just a 20 minute walk away from The White House, reached by a paved pathway across Bishops Palace fields, offering stunning views of the Cathedral and Glastonbury Tor . And for guests who require a little more room we are now offering a beautiful holiday cottage in the Centre of Wells to complement our bed and breakfast offering. We bought The White House after falling in love with the area and this wonderful Grade II listed 17thCentury old coaching house. We have furnished it with love to provide both a wonderful home for their family and a luxurious get away for our guests. We pride ourselves on a warm friendly welcome, excellent food and luxurious accommodation with the relaxation and indulgence of our guests at the heart of all we do. We are able to offer a highly personalised service and if anything isn’t exactly to your liking, we do our utmost to deal with it then and there. The first record of The Whitehouse is in 1696, when John West an “inn-holder” of Wells leased the ale house beside the west mill. In this tiny community he served his beer from a room in this house, and this early-style pub was the social hub of the working community.” Between 1889 and 1914 the property is listed as a public house not an inn, proprietors Richard and Sarah Pointing. Folklore continues the story in that when Richard Pointing died, Sarah didn’t wish to continue to run The White Horse as a public house and so changed the “R” on the sign outside to a “U”, hence changing the name to “The White House” as it is know today…….
tagline: B&B near Wells, Somerset. A warm welcome awaits you at The White House

title: The White Post
subtitle: The family-run White Post offers a beautiful setting in Rimpton, outside Yeovil, with lovely views over the surrounding West Country.
bodyContent: The family-run White Post offers a beautiful setting in Rimpton, outside Yeovil, with lovely views over the surrounding West Country.

title: The Willows B&B
subtitle: A warm welcome awaits you at The Willows set just off the A303 at Wincanton on the borders of Somerset, Dorset and Wiltshire.
bodyContent: Staying at The Willows in Wincanton provides an ideal place for exploring this attractive corner of England. For the active, the countryside around Wincanton is perfect on foot,or bicycle. The Rooms are Tastefully and comfortably furnished to a high standard, En-Suite, Tea, coffee making facilities, Refrigerator, Fold away Table, Hair Dryer, Alarm Clock, TV, and free wi-fi, Ample off road parking, A Kitchenette with Microwave,Toaster, Hob Cutlery & Crockery is available for guest use,also an iron and ironing board. We aim to greet our guests on arrival but, if this is not possible a key will be left in a secure place for you to collect on arrival. Dogs are welcome by prior arrangement.

title: The Windsor
subtitle: The Windsor houses 15 beautiful traditionally styled en-suite bedrooms.
bodyContent: Each room enjoys the amenities listed below. For pricing on rooms ensure you call us on 01225 422 100 for our best rates. Should you need to cancel your reservation we require written confirmation (letter, fax or e-mail) by 2 p.m. three days prior to the date of arrival. Failure to do so will result in the full price of the stay being charged to your credit card. We operate a very strict cancellation policy, therefore we strongly recommend you take out travel insurance. Please note, all deposits are non-refundable and bookings are non-transferable.

title: The Windsor Townhouse
subtitle: Location, location, location. Just two minutes’ walk to the city centre, tourist attractions, shops and restaurants, The Windsor perfect choice for both leisure and business guests.
bodyContent: Location, location, location. Just two minutes’ walk to the city centre, tourist attractions, shops and restaurants, The Windsor perfect choice for both leisure and business guests. With 15 individually styled ensuite bedrooms with period features and stunning views over one of the finest boulevards in Europe to the front and the green space of the Recreation Ground to the rear. Room facilities include complimentary WIFI, flat screen televisions, air conditioning and hostess tray. Luxury soft fluffy towels, cosy dorma duvets, feather pillows and White Company toiletries complete the package and add to the guest experience. Acclaimed for our warm and friendly staff, we are always ready with a smile and happy to help with anything from restaurant suggestions to planning your onward journey. We pride ourselves in our customer service and along with our award winning breakfasts, our aim is to send you home with a desire to return.
tagline: Location, location, location. Just two minutes’ walk to the city centre

title: The Woodborough Inn
subtitle: Our cosy, en-suite guest bedrooms are ideal for visitors to the West Country, business people and families alike.
bodyContent: Perfectly suited for those looking to explore the Mendip hills which have so much to offer. Single, double and twin rooms are available. We also offer a large family room with a separate bunk room which can accommodate a family of four. All our rooms offer en-suite bathrooms, television, telephone, wi-fi connection, tea/coffee making facilities and a tasty breakfast to help kick start your day.
tagline: Our cosy, en-suite guest bedrooms are ideal for visitors to the West Country

title: Timbertop Suites
subtitle: Timbertop has been providing the perfect accommodation for holiday makers and business travellers for over 50 years.
bodyContent: The hotel quality rooms and self catering suites are complimented by a friendly, personal service and excellent location. This grand Edwardian building has undergone recent renovations to tastefully modernise the interior with a nod to the infamous Art Deco era...

title: Toghill House Farm
subtitle: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds. Within a stone’s throw of the site of the battle of Lansdown and with the Cotswold Way and the old east to west Roman road running through the grounds, Toghill is steeped in history.
bodyContent: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds. Within a stone’s throw of the site of the battle of Lansdown and with the Cotswold Way and the old east to west Roman road running through the grounds, Toghill is steeped in history. Located on a working farm only 4 miles north of Bath, with spectacular views over the Welsh mountains, Mendips, Cotswolds and Historic Bath. We have 9 rooms, some of which are in the 17th century farmhouse and others in the pretty Cotswold stone converted barns and stables in a delightful courtyard setting.
tagline: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds.

title: Toomer Farm
subtitle: Every room has its own tea and coffee making facility, television, iron with ironing board and hair dryer.
bodyContent: The Farmhouse has full central heating and a drawing room for the use of our guests. A full traditional English or Continental breakfast is served in the family dining room. Should you have any dietary requirements please mention this when booking your accommodation. There are two very good pubs nearby, and an Indian Restaurant all serving evening meals. The town of Sherborne is only a five minute drive away, where there is a selection of Restaurants for you to enjoy.

title: Tranmere House
subtitle: Your hosts Mark and Leisa welcome you to Tranmere House bed and breakfast guesthouse in Minehead, Somerset; the gateway to Exmoor National Park.
bodyContent: We take great pride in our hospitality and try to ensure every guest gets the most from their stay. Situated in a peaceful, tree-lined road within easy level walking distance of the beach, harbour and all amenities, Tranmere House offers excellent bed and breakfast accommodation. All rooms are equipped with Smart televisions to enable our guests to log into streaming services such as Netflix and provide access to BBC and ITV catch-up services.

title: Tudor Cottage
subtitle: If you are looking for somewhere special to stay while exploring Exmoor’s hills and coast, Tudor Cottage - once a 15th Century farmhouse - may well be the B&B for you.
bodyContent: Set in the peaceful National Trust village of Bossington, with its thatched cottages, flower-filled gardens, wooded coombes and a magnificent shingle beach just a ten minute level stroll away, Tudor Cottage is well-placed for exploring Exmoor National Park with its huge views, iconic ponies and red deer herds. Relaxed and friendly, but with little touches of luxury, many guests come back time and time again to this comfortable cottage to look at the views from the garden, enjoy a hearty breakfast and a home-cooked evening meal, and leave the world and its worries behind for a few days. We want you to have a wonderful time here and hope you will visit us soon.

title: Tudor Cottage B&B
subtitle: Beautiful B&B accommodation in Bossington near Minehead, Somerset.
bodyContent: Tudor cottage B&B is well situated in the pretty village of Bossington. Nestled in at the foot of Bossington Hill it is a lovely quiet tranquil retreat with views of Exmoor and just a short walk to Bossington Beach and Kitnors Tearoom. We provide evening meals on request and can serve drinks to accompany your meal. Weather permitting you can eat alfresco or sit in the garden until dark and marvel at the sight of our fantastic dark sky's experience. We are situated close to the South West Coast Path, and there are many planned walks around Exmoor and beyond. Do look at the website for more information and further photos of our enchanting location. Call direct for best rate and last minute offers.
tagline: Beautiful B&B accommodation in Bossington near Minehead, Somerset.

title: Turks Hall
subtitle: David and Caroline are delighted to welcome you to Turks Hall Bed & Breakfast in Bruton, Somerset.
bodyContent: Having run successful tea rooms in the South of France, they know how to make your stay enjoyable and comfortable. Turks Hall B&B is a Victorian family house with a lovely south facing courtyard, within walking distance of the centre of Bruton. Your double bedroom with en-suite bathroom, television, wifi etc is a comfortable, spacious room where you can either read David's large selection of books, listen to music or just chill. Turks Hall also offers a second twin bedded room with a beautifully appointed bathroom (sole use of the guests). A glass of sherry and home made cakes await you. ​ Come and enjoy our continental organic breakfasts with locally sourced products. A wide selection of organic Jing teas are also available for you to try. Bruton is a small medieval Somerset town just off the A303 near Wincanton with great transport links to Bristol, Bath and London. Parking is on road in front of the house. Bruton's attractions include St. Mary's church, Sexey's Hospital with its old almshouses and delightful gardens, ancient bartons, riverside walks and the 15th Dovecot. If you are a foodie, why not try out Matt's Kitchen, At The Chapel or Roth Bar & Grill and let us do the booking for you!

title: Villa Claudia
subtitle: If you’re looking for a family-friendly bed and breakfast in Bath, look no further than Villa Claudia.
bodyContent: While staying at Villa Claudia Hotel, visitors can check out Great Pulteney Street (0.3 mi) and Pulteney Bridge (0.5 mi), some of Bath's top attractions. Free wifi is offered to guests, and rooms at Villa Claudia offer a flat screen TV. Guests of Villa Claudia Hotel are also welcome to enjoy free breakfast, located on site. For travellers arriving by car, free parking is available. When you’re feeling hungry, be sure to check out Blue Quails Deli, Eveleigh's Cafe, and The Grocer on Locksbrook, which are some delis that are popular with locals and out-of-towners alike. Looking to explore? Then look no further than The Roman Baths (0.7 mi) and Bath Abbey (0.6 mi), which are some popular Bath attractions – all conveniently located within walking distance of the bed and breakfast. The staff at Villa Claudia looks forward to serving you during your upcoming visit.

title: Walton’s Guest House
subtitle: Walton’s Guest House, providing warm and friendly accommodation in central Bath for over 25 years.
bodyContent: Walton’s Guest House, an oasis in the centre of Bath catering for Business and Tourism. Centrally located in Bath, this Guest House offers great facilities and a short walk to the Royal Crescent, Bath City Centre & the Royal Bath Spa Complex. All rooms are luxury en- suite and our rates include a hearty full English breakfast cooked to order. A family business for over 40 years, we aim to make your stay enjoyable and trouble free and can offer helpful advice on what to do and see in the city and surrounding area including seasonal local events. Bath offers a wide variety of attractions throughout the year and Walton’s is within easy walking distance of the Music Festival venues, the Theatre Royal including The Egg and the Ustinov Studio, the Roman Baths and Thermae Spa complex, the Museum of Costume, Bath Rugby at the Recreation Ground, the Jane Austen Festival, the Christmas Markets in the Abbey Churchyard and all City Centre Shops. For those walking the Cotswold Way, Walton’s offers a convenient overnight stay on the western edge of the city centre. There is a bus stop outside the front door, should you wish to take a day trip to Bristol, during your stay There is free on-street parking between 6.00pm and 8.00am and a public car park immediately behind the hotel. I have a couple of Parking Permits, providing all day on- street parking. Call or email for group bookings and for seasonal and midweek offers. ​ Bedrooms: 7 Bathrooms: 7 Children: Most Welcome Pets: No Onsite Parking: No - On street parking permits available
tagline: Walton’s Guest House, providing warm and friendly accommodation

title: Warwick Arms
subtitle: The Warwick Arms, Clutton is based 12 miles from the center of Bristol.
bodyContent: Here at the Warwick Arms we strive for great customer service as well as quality food.

title: Waterhouse Guest House
subtitle: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath so once you have shopped till you are about to drop or taken the time to wonder along the local walking routes we have the perfect location set into the Midford Valley with country surroundings which ensures you will not be disturbed by the city noise or pace
bodyContent: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath so once you have shopped till you are about to drop or taken the time to wonder along the local walking routes we have the perfect location set into the Midford Valley with country surroundings which ensures you will not be disturbed by the city noise or pace. We have our own carpark, lift access, Bar, restaurant, conservatory, outside terrace and gardens place making Waterhouse a great place to work, rest, eat and play! We serve a selection of drinks which include local Beers, Ales, carefully selected wines and spirits to relax and unwind while taking in the stunning views across the Midford Valley. Our tranquil surroundings include the Midford Brook at the bottom of the property where we have fishing rights which people can use for a nominal fee, please enquire at reception should you like to make use of this exclusive facility. Across the Midford Valley there are stunning views and a selection of walks one of which is the two tunnels route which is one of the longest pedestrian tunnels in the UK. Other walks include the Kennet & Avon Canal. We are founded on Christian Values and aim to display the Love of Jesus to all who visit, please view the History of Waterhouse. Waterhouse is a 13 bedroom country house located in the idyllic and peaceful Midford valley 15 minutes south of Bath. Built around 1632, the house has been restored to provide bed and breakfast accommodation, meeting rooms and a venue for small events. All our bedrooms are located in the modern wing of the original house. We offer a choice of 8 double bedrooms, 1 twin room and 4 deluxe rooms, all en-suite.
tagline: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath

title: Waverley Bed & Breakfast
subtitle: We are ideally situated within the town.
bodyContent: The Waverley offers Bed & Breakfast. Only 3 minutes level walk to the beach, West Somerset Railway and easy access to Exmoor which is a must to be seen in all seasons. Minehead B and B The Waverley is a non-smoking, family run Hotel and the owners Ian & Michael take pride in their hospitality, ensuring that every guest gets the most from their holiday break, however long they should decide to stay.

title: Westbrook Barns
subtitle: Westbrook Barn, the Stone Barn and Old Westbrook Farmhouse are three lovely places to stay in Somerset and cater to a wide range of group sizes and events, being available individually or together.
bodyContent: The houses combine a couple of centuries of history with modern comforts and access to a wide range of local attractions. Each house has its own character, and can be completely private, or if hired as a group all houses can be made easily accessible to each other. For most of the year Judith Randel and Tony German live in Old Westbrook Farmhouse and so are nearby if you need anything when staying in Westbrook Barn or the Stone Barn. For a few weeks when Judith and Tony are away, Old Westbrook Farmhouse is available for very large families or groups. At the moment the Farmhouse is only available for stretches of 2 weeks or longer, if you are interested in staying in the Farmhouse please do get in touch directly.

title: Westbury Cross House
subtitle: Luxury boutique B&B between Wells & Cheddar in Somerset.
bodyContent: With 300 years of history, Westbury Cross House has been renovated and decorated to a high standard and modern style. Each guestroom has independent access, individual character, wifi, tv/dvd and bathroom. Guests may use the charming circular terrace encircled by an ancient fig tree. New! Our wonderful Barn - perfect for families with a king size four poster bed and a beautiful mezzanine with 2 single mattresses, an adventure in itself! Located in the heart of Somerset, the accommodation will appeal to those interested in walking, cycling, sightseeing, shopping and the many cultural and historical attractions of the region. Westbury-sub-Mendip has a pub serving meals and a village shop. Guests enjoy a warm welcome from Rachel and Robert who pride themselves in offering a home-from-home experience. Please see our website for a full look at our stylish boutique rooms. http://www.westburycrosshouse.com
tagline: Luxury boutique B&B between Wells & Cheddar in Somerset.

title: Wheelbrook Mill
subtitle: Wheelbrook mill is a converted watermill in the gorgeous Hamlet of Laverton, not 15 minutes from the Georgian City of Bath.
bodyContent: We have 4 Letting rooms, that offer avariety of occupancy from the Single Traveller, to rooms that sleep up to 4 person, or 2 rooms that sleep up to 6 persons ( 2 bathroom, 3 bedroom with 2 x double bedrooms and a twin bedded room) . We are a perfect location for exploring such wonderful places, including BATH, FROM, LONGLEAT, 25 MINUTES FROM STONEHENGE, AND 35 MINUTES FROM LACOCK...We are surrounded by Fantastic local pubs including a 14th Century Coaching Inn. We have a regular local Bus at the end of our lane tht goes into Bath & other local Town, and are in a good location for train stations too.(Freshford, Frome & Trowbridge ) We can arrange transport/taxi service in and out of BATH & surrounding areas. We are also situated near ORCHARLEIGH & WICKFARM & BABINGTON, so perfect location for those going to these local wedding Venues. We have previous won Awards of Excellence in other properties we have had, and now working to an Award of Excellence with Tripadvisor!! If you are planning a break away with friends, family, or a Girlie Weekend,Wheelbrook Mill is the perfect place - we can sleep up to 13 guests. We offer a Relaxed BB, with friendly, Knowledgeable hosts in a gorgeous location,steeped with history going back to the Domesday. Come and visit us and tell all your friends too!!

title: White Guest House
subtitle: Situated within a 7 minute walk to the city and all of Baths famous attractions with its stunning Roman and Georgian Architecture, Roman Baths, Bath Abbey, Royal Crescent, Thermae Spa .are all a must to see.
bodyContent: The city offers excellent shopping and restaurants along with a lot of independent and boutique shops .It’s a lovely walk into the city passing the Bath cricket grounds, crossing the river Avon and you are in the city. All our rooms are en-suite with hair dryers tv’s, complimentary drinks tray with various teas, coffee’s, hot chocolate and biscuits also Free WI-FI internet access.

bodyContent: The White Hart Hotel can be found in the heart of Wells , England’s smallest city. title: Whitfield Cottages
subtitle: Whitfield Cottages is an ideal base for exploring the West Country just outside the village of Kilmersdon, famous for the Jack and Jill nursery rhyme and just 15 minutes from The Bath & West Showground.
bodyContent: Recently reviewed as 5 star on Google, Whitfield Cottages is an ideal base for exploring the West Country just outside the village of Kilmersdon, famous for the Jack and Jill nursery rhyme and just 15 minutes from The Bath & West Showground. It is self contained with its own lounge with garden views and a kitchen with microwave, tea and coffee making facilities and a fridge stocked with fresh milk. Home cooked full english breakfast provided using only local produce where possible.​ Self catering is an option but please ring in advance. The annexe also features a twin bedded bedroom and ensuite with a walk in shower. Additionally, there is a hair dryer and fresh towels are provided for your stay and a Travel Cot and High Chair are available. The property offers ample safe off road parking and is also ideal for limited mobility access. Please do ring if you have any questions regarding accessibility. It is ideally situated within easy access of the Mendip Hills and the beautiful cities of Bath and Wells . A warm welcome awaits, homemade cake and tea on arrival, Viv looks forward to making your acquaintance.​ Special rates are available for stays of more than 2 nights, please ask for more details. We operate a non smoking policy.​
tagline: Whitfield Cottages is an ideal base for exploring the West Country

title: Withy Cottages
subtitle: Withy House sleeps 4/6/8 and has three bedrooms
bodyContent: one king, one king en-suite and one twin and a double sofa bed in the dining room. There is also a travel cot and high chair available (please bring your own linen for the cot). Withy House was built in 1898 in the style of a Victorian villa and retains many of the original features, including a painted logo on the wall of the family bathroom done by the painter and decorator in 1908 to advertise his work. The spacious accommodation has in addition to the three bedrooms a well equipped kitchen, lounge with open coal fire and separate dining room / second lounge . Situated just a short walk from the Rose and Crown public house and only a few minutes drive to a really great selection of restaurants and local pubs.

title: Woodleigh Bed and Breakfast
subtitle: Chris and Dee Mooney would like to welcome you to their family run 4 star bed and breakfast
bodyContent: Woodleigh Bed and Breakfast, Ilminster, offers high-quality en-suite accommodation in a beautifully refurbished 1895 Victorian house, retaining original charm and fireplaces. Enjoy spacious, light bedrooms and a guest-accessible garden. Ideally placed for Barrington Court, Montacute House, Forde Abbey, the Blackdown Hills, and the Jurassic Coast, just 18 miles away.
tagline: Chris and Dee Mooney would like to welcome you to their family run 4 star bed and breakfast

title: Worth House
subtitle: Located in the beautiful Somerset countryside, close to the medieval city of Wells, Worth House dates back 400 years.
bodyContent: Worth House, a 16th-century former farmhouse near Wells, offers stunning Mendip Hills and farmland views. Ideally placed for Wookey Hole Caves, Glastonbury and Cheddar Gorge, with country pubs nearby including The Pheasant. Enjoy the cosy living room, garden views, and warm hospitality from hosts Sarah and Nick.

title: Yallands Farmhouse
subtitle: Chris & Karen Ward look forward to welcoming you to Yallands Farmhouse
bodyContent: Yallands is a Grade II Listed 400-year-old farmhouse, a peaceful oasis with secluded garden, orchard and stone barn, 1½ miles from Taunton centre. Self-assessed 4-star, near M5 junctions 25/26, bus stop nearby. Handy for Taunton School, Somerset Heritage Centre, Nuffield Hospital. Parking and cycle storage available. No pets.
tagline: Chris & Karen Ward look forward to welcoming you to Yallands Farmhouse

title: Yew Tree House
subtitle: We look forward to welcoming guests to Yew Tree House. This area of Somerset is a great place to come away to, for a quiet break, a busy family holiday or a catch up with friends and family living or staying in the area.
bodyContent: Yew Tree House offers a warm welcome near the seven-mile Burnham-Berrow-Brean beach, the King Charles III coast path and Brean resort — ideal for quiet breaks, family holidays or exploring Somerset. Six comfortable rooms (three in the main house, three garden rooms) offer doubles, kings, twins and family options, each with WIFI, heating, TV and tea/coffee facilities. Enjoy private parking, bike storage and a relaxing garden. Award-winning breakfast, using local produce, is included daily. Walk to the beach or Brean, or reach nearby golf courses, cycle routes, Brean Splash pool and evening entertainment. Easily accessed via M5 Junction 22 or the Somerset Coaster bus.
tagline: Bed & Breakfast in Burnham on Sea, Somerset.

title: Coastal Strategy Meeting
subtitle: Tuesday 17th will see Visit Somerset coordinating the first Coastal Summit strategy meeting, in an effort to coordinate a more prosperous future for our coastal communities. Supported by the Hinkley Tourism Action Partnership, the meeting the brain child of Visit Somerset, Visit Weston, Weston Town Council and the Minehead BID will finally see, coordination and development of a joint marketing strategy
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"63"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"John Turner Visit Somerset CEO has said; " I am particularly looking forward to coordinating this with our public and private sector partners. Somerset's coastline boasts forty nine miles of glorious coastline, that in itself boasts a wealth of opportunity from wellbeing, sandy beaches, fossil hunting and many varieties of water sports, fishing and lot more." 

Here is the agenda:

 *   Introductions
 *   Back ground to the Hinkley Tourism Action Partnership and its support of the project.
 *   Define all of unique selling points to each coastal town represented and look at how we create a coastal town trail  - Talk through the creative marketing opportunity and how HTAP/ Visit Somerset will support - commission a creative opportunity to use to take to markets.
 *   Discuss with PR agency how we can attract journalists and tour operators once the USP’s have been defined.
 *   Understand what the varying target markets are visiting your coastal towns at present and what all of your aspirational customers are.
 *   Understand the routes to market; rail, bus, coach, car. How are we working with these transport networks and what can we do attract more visitors through the different modes of transport
 *   To talk through the MICE market and staycation markets and any opportunities to target those markets, such as twin town staycations.
 *   Environmental strategy & community engagement

 *   AOB
 *   Next Steps
 *   Further meeting arrangements

 *   Close 16:00

title: Somerset Tourism Environmental strategy
subtitle: Somerset Tourism Environmental strategy
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"24"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

Dear member, with the recent UN talks in Katowice and the news of rising CO2 levels, the Somerset Tourism Association is going to be taking immediate action, setting targets for the team to reduce its CO2 emissions by four tons a year, equivalent to a reduction of 10,000 miles of travel annually.

This will not only see environmental benefits, but also see STA productivity increase. (At present the Visit Somerset’s team spend a full working week, 40 hours, in their cars every month) We need to ensure our time is being spent supporting members and the work of the STA directly.  (Of course, if you want to meet with us in person, we will of course ensure that happens.)

 

What we want to do is proactively encourage our members, instead of visiting in person, to either SKYPE, FaceTime or Phone the office, using the car as a last resort. If you don’t know how to use any of the fore mentioned devices, then the Visit Somerset team will train you. We will be promoting these new environmental values as of now. 

 

If we also encourage our members to do the same, we will cross calculate the total mileage saved and put a CO2 value to that, which in a year’s time we can all rightly celebrate our achievements. 

 

We need to take action now and we believe this is the right and proper course of action for all our futures. 

 

Thank you 

 

Visit Somerset Team.

 

Calculate your own Carbon Footprint here.

title: Tourism sector deal update
subtitle: Tourism sector deal update
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"27"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

Welcoming the news that an official negotiation for a tourism sector deal has been confirmed by the UK Government, British Tourist Authority Chair Steve Ridgway CBE, former Chief Executive of Virgin Atlantic Airways, who is leading the UK tourism industry’s bid for a sector deal under the UK Government’s Industrial Strategy said:

“Tourism is an economic powerhouse, a growing industry with huge potential to scale-up productivity, so it is very welcome news that an official negotiation for a sector deal has today been confirmed by the UK Government.

“Securing this deal will be a game-changer for the industry, spelling a step-change in how we underpin the success of tourism for a generation, fixing issues from skills and productivity to extending the season year-round and building stronger tourism destinations up and down the country. And it will be a game-changer for the economy, with a sector deal growing the value of the industry and increasing employment in tourism." 

“One of the UK’s most valuable export industries, tourism needs no trade deals to attract overseas investment. It is also a fiercely competitive global industry and a sector deal moves tourism right up the UK Government’s agenda as a priority for future economic planning, ensuring we continue to compete as a world-class destination for all visitors.”

Mr Ridgway said the bid for a sector deal was a result of the tourism industry coming together with one voice during the last 18 months, getting behind the bid with its own ideas for the future and working in partnership.

"},{"key":"NewsDate","value":"2018-11-29T00:00:00+00:00"},{"key":"NewsImage","value":"~/getattachment/Business/Business-Support/Latest-News/Tourism-sector-deal-update/VisitEngland-Logo.jpg.aspx?lang=en-GB&width=250&height=188&ext=.jpg"},{"key":"_kenticoNodeId","value":"1422"},{"key":"_kenticoClassName","value":"cms.news"}]

title: Highlights from recent international marketing events
subtitle: Every year events are organised around the world bringing the UK tourism industry together with key players in international travel trade.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"28"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

Representatives from tourism industries build knowledge of Britain and what is on offer by delivering workshops and seminars across the overseas network.

Earlier in the year, the best of destination Britain was showcased at the annual Explore GB travel trade event in Newcastle. Now in its fourth year, more than 280 international travel buyers from 29 countries attended meeting with 330 tourism suppliers from across the UK. After the event, the buyers travelled around the country and experienced the tourism industries that Britain has to offer.

From  7th-11th March, over 50 UK partners joined the Visit Britain stand at ITB Berlin. ITB is the world’s largest travel trade exhibition, the five day trade show provided extensive networking opportunities and business meetings.

In October, Destination Britain North America saw 150 UK suppliers and North American buyers convene in Austin, Texas, to promote Britain’s tourism products at their annual event. The event aimed to build more Britain packages from USA and Canada, with networking being key at the event.

In November, over 90 UK travel trade representatives met with over 85 buyers from Asia at Destination Britain China and North East Asia. To mark the 10th anniversary, the workshop took places in Sanya, Hainan, which was where the first Destination Britain China event was held.

The sell-out event provided suppliers and buyers with a schedule of one-to-one meetings alongside industry seminars and networking opportunities. Over 5,000 business meetings took place during the event.

title: Weston College advances into flexible digital learning
subtitle: Weston College has been selected to pioneer an innovative approach to adult learning.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"29"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

Thanks to an award from the government’s Flexible Learning Fund, the College will launch a unique range of digital courses that enable adults to learn alongside other commitments.

The courses, which are designed for people who are unable to study full-time, will be launched in January 2019.

Learners can study the courses outside of regular working hours through a mixture of face-to-face and online training sessions.

The new courses include:

  • Investigating Enterprise Skills, Level 2 Award
  • An Introduction to Leadership and Management, Level 2 Award
  • Autism Awareness, Level 2 Award
  • Customer Service in a Health and Social Care Settings, Level 2 Certificate
  • Maintaining a Tenancy, Entry Level 3 Award
  • IT User Skills, Level 1 Certificate

These courses are free for adults that meet the eligibility criteria.

Anne Milton, Apprenticeship and Skills Minister, said: “These projects are an opportunity for people to get the skills they need to kick-start their working life.

“I’m really excited about these projects, which will help people learn the skills they need to grow and succeed in lots of different jobs.

“Whether working already or returning to work, it can be difficult for people to fit training around their busy lives. This funding aims to find out how providers and employers can work together to better meet the needs of adults of all ages, who want the opportunity to learn important new skills and change their lives.”

For more information, please visit www.weston.ac.uk/flexible-learning-fund
