title: Weston College at the forefront of T Level revolution
subtitle: Students at Weston College will be among the first in the country to study the new T Level qualification.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"30"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

The College is one of just 54 providers selected to launch the new technical equivalent to A Levels.

T Levels will be available in 15 industry-related subjects, known as ‘pathways’. Weston College will deliver the Digital (software applications design and development) programme from September 2020 – two years before the full roll-out.

Dr Paul Phillips CBE, Principal and Chief Executive of Weston College Group, said: “T Levels have been described as the biggest overhaul in post-school education for 70 years.

“For Weston College to be at the forefront of this revolution is an honour and an exciting challenge. We’ve built a national reputation for the quality of our sixth form and helping to launch this pioneering programme only enhances that standing.

“It also represents a tremendous opportunity for school leavers in Weston-super-Mare and beyond.

“T levels are shaped by employers and benefit from the unique insights of industry leaders. This means learners will be equipped with the skills and knowledge they need to get ahead in the modern jobs market.”

Delivered over a two-year period, T Levels provide an alternative to A Levels and are aimed at 16 to 19-year-olds who would rather study work-related courses than traditional academic subjects. They have been launched to counter the long-held assumption that only A Levels and a degree can lead to a fulfilling job. Though, T Level students will still be able to progress to university or higher-level technical qualifications.

T Levels have been created by expert panels of employers, are also designed to deliver the necessary skills required to strengthen and grow the UK economy. They will provide a mix of industry-specific technical knowledge and practical skills; relevant maths, English and digital skills; and a work placement of at least 45 days.

"},{"key":"NewsDate","value":"2018-11-07T00:00:00+00:00"},{"key":"NewsImage","value":"~/getattachment/Business/Business-Support/Latest-News/Weston-College-at-the-forefront-of-T-Level-revolut/WC_logo.png.aspx?lang=en-GB&width=117&height=120&ext=.png"},{"key":"_kenticoNodeId","value":"1425"},{"key":"_kenticoClassName","value":"cms.news"}]

title: Dr Paul Phillips CBE, scoops FE Leader of the Year
subtitle: Dr Paul Phillips CBE, Weston College has won the FE leader of the year at the annual Tes FE Awards 2019.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"35"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

In his 18 years at the helm of Weston College, Dr Paul Phillips has directed a dramatic turnaround in its fortunes. The judges commended Phillips for the proven impact of his leadership which has been sustained over time.

Turnover at the College has increased from £9 million when he joined in 2001 to more than £63 million in 2016-17 – making it one of the 10 biggest colleges in England.

He has personally championed social mobility for all, including raising standards across prison education in the South West.

Last year, the college was awarded a Queen’s Anniversary Prize for its inclusive practice for pupils with special educational needs or disabilities (SEND). The college was also the first to open a specialist autism residential training facility.

Under Phillips’ leadership, the College has had a major impact on the seaside town it serves, including restoring the 1920s Winter Gardens Pavilion and its ballroom for community use, while building a new Law and Professional Services Academy. In 2016, the University Centre Weston opened; a year later it was awarded a Teaching Excellence Framework (TEF) gold award.

Phillips has also committed to sharing best practice across the sector and has helped other colleges with everything from strategic planning to recovery plans and health and safety reviews. In 2017, he was made one of the first National Leaders in Further Education.

The judges said: “Dr Phillips gets results and has been truly transformative in the area.”

Winners attended a black-tie event at the Grosvenor House Hotel, London, hosted by the stand-up comedian, writer and presenter Dave Gorman. More than 700 attendees celebrated and showcased the most exciting ideas, the best practice and the most inspiring teaching and leadership to be found in the FE sector.

title: Weston College wins award for dedication to mental health and wellbeing
subtitle: A college-wide organisational transformation programme to enhance the mental health, wellbeing and welfare of its learners, its staff and its community has received national recognition by winning an Association of Colleges Beacon Award.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"36"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

 

Weston College picked up the award for developing sustainable community partnerships/peer networks to maximise engagement and minimise isolation, where staff and students have improved morale and wellbeing.

The judges were impressed by the colleges’ commitment to creating an ethos which puts mental health, wellbeing and welfare at the forefront of college investment -as an inclusive driver to achieve its mission of creating brighter futures for all its staff and students regardless of their starting point in life.

Now in its 24th year, the AoC Beacon Awards showcase best practice and innovation in colleges. It is designed to promote the interdependence of colleges, businesses and professional and voluntary organisations. The awards also highlight excellence and helps share best practice across the sector.

Dr Paul Phillips CBE, Principal and Chief Executive of Weston College, said; “This is a fantastic achievement for the College in such an important policy area, where we are delivering real impact for our students and staff. “

Judges also commented on the fantastic cross college holistic approach to mental health and well-being that was demonstrated by the College, which really set them apart from everyone else. 

David Hughes, Chief Executive of the Association of Colleges, said: “Each year the standard of entries is extremely high and this year is no exception. This makes choosing the winner so difficult, especially with so many worthy entrants.

“Colleges are inspirational places to learn because education and training is delivered by expert teaching staff in industry-standard facilities. Weston College should be proud of their award.”

For the first time, The AoC Beacon Awards and the TesFE Awards were presented alongside each other at the annual TES FE Awards ceremony in London on Friday 22 March 2019.

title: Business Sponsor Albert Goodman talks about 'Making Tax digital'
subtitle: You may have seen TV adverts talking about Making Tax Digital. This is HMRC’s drive to close the “Tax Gap” and to make the UK “the most digitally advanced tax authority in the world”. It will mean significant changes to how and when businesses deal with tax.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"38"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

Luckily, Albert Goodman is here to offer their support. According to their website, the first businesses to be affected by Making Tax Digital will be VAT registered businesses with turnover above the VAT threshold. These businesses will be required to maintain digital accounting records and use compliant software to file their VAT returns from the first VAT quarter starting on or after 1st April 2019.

 

The pilot is in full swing to test that the software (both the commercial products and HMRC’s systems) work properly under the full range of business types and VAT reporting arrangements. Businesses can continue to use spreadsheets to maintain their books and records although they will need to combine this with third-party software, using APIs to ensure a seamless flow of data between the business and HMRC.

 

Albert Goodman’s award-winning team can help you get started if you are not already keeping your accounts on compatible software or can do your bookkeeping for you. They can support you using Xero, QBO, Sage , FreeAgent or any other cloud package which suits your needs and can also help with the quarterly uploads, once these are needed, and will be able to prepare your year-end figures for you.

They have been actively involved in the consultation process throughout and are therefore well placed to guide you through the MTD requirements.

Click here to find out more.

bodyContent: Summer is on the horizon, and with it comes one of Taunton’s most exciting family-friendly events — Test Fest 2026 , returning to Taunton RFC on Saturday 20th June . Food, Stalls & Festival Goodness Of course, no festival is complete without great food — and Test Fest has you covered. Visitors can enjoy: 🍔 Delicious food stalls 🍹 A festival bar 🛍 Local traders and craft stalls ⛺ Camping options for those who want to make a weekend of it It’s an event designed for wandering, snacking, relaxing, dancing, and discovering something new around every corner. title: Blackdown Hills
subtitle: A National Landscape, a wide expanse of uplands offering constantly changing and surprising views; and a place where progress has apparently made but little impact: these are the Blackdown Hills
bodyContent: Rising steeply to a ridge from the valley of the Tone and declining gently down to the south coast, the Blackdown Hills are a unique landscape feature embracing a wealth of different habitats, from ancient oak woodlands to towering beech hedges, deeply-incised valleys to windswept downland where two wartime airfields created a temporary intrusion into the area’s tranquil character. Lanes, tracks and byways offer plenty of scope for walking, cycling and horse riding, and if you want to get really involved in the countryside there are courses for everything from traditional crafts to hedgerow skills. The Blackdown Hills offer an impressive scope of places to stay from country houses to cottages while the pubs and restaurants offer local food and drink of a rare quality and – thanks to the sheer diversity of landscape types – variety. For more information on the area, please contact our Visitor Centre in Taunton
tagline: A National Landscape, a wide expanse of uplands with stunning and surprising views.

title: Goodland Gardens
subtitle: Goodland Gardens boasts an three sections of parkland and has both hard-standing and grassed areas. It is the perfect location to take that much needed time out.
bodyContent: Edward Goodland was a member of a prominent Taunton family involved in the coal trade and in bringing coal to the town along the River Tone. He also played county cricket for Somerset. His family name is preserved in Goodland Gardens which is located in the heart of the town, close to the river.

title: West Somerset Railway
subtitle: West Somerset Railway, Somerset, is a heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton. It is the longest independent railway in Britain, (20 miles).
bodyContent: West Somerset Railway, Somerset is the longest Heritage line in the United Kingdom. Time Table can be seen HERE for 2024 The line is situated in Somerset, four miles outside the County town of Taunton , starting at Bishops Lydeard and finishing at Minehead . The line meanders through the Quantock Hills , an area of outstanding natural beauty and along the Bristol Channel Coast. We have 10 stations along the line each having something different to offer. There are various historic sites that may be of interest to visitors to the area, for example Crowcombe Heathfield station was the location for the filming of the Beatles’ “A Hard Days Night” and scenes from “The Land Girls” were also shot here. The historic town of Watchet dates back to Saxon times, and boasts narrow streets, local shops, museums and lots of places to eat and drink. Washford is a great place to alight, just a short walk from the station we have Cleeve Abbey and the Torre Cider Farm, which are both well worth a visit. Fancy something a little different then why not visit Dunster Castle which is nestled in the medieval village of Dunster ? Dunster also has a working Watermill , the Old Yarn Market building and the Dolls Museum or continue on to Minehead home of our final station. Minehead is situated at the foot of North Hill where the beach is literally right across the road, we have cafes, shops and plenty of arcades along the seafront, making this a go to location. The West Somerset Railway also have combined tickets on selected dates throughout the year. These include, Cream Tea and Cheese and cider specials and linked trips with Hestercombe Gardens and Dunster Castle. We organise Steam Galas in the Spring and Autumn, and we are host to a Diesel Gala too. In the latter part of the year we have our popular Christmas services, we have Santa services running out of Minehead and Bishops Lydeard from the end of November until Christmas Eve, we also have our Sherry and Mince pie specials for you to enjoy.
tagline: Heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton.

title: Somerset Heritage Centre
subtitle: The Somerset Heritage Centre provides state-of-the-art storage for the historic records of Somerset and access to them.
bodyContent: The Somerset Local Studies Library is located at the Heritage Centre. It holds published works relating to all aspects of Somerset life, including books, pamphlets, maps, journal articles and illustrations. The main collections of the Somerset Studies Library are on open access shelves in the searchroom at the Somerset Heritage Centre. The items which are held in the strongrooms may be ordered in advance or on the day. Remote enquiries can be submitted by telephone, letter or email, although longer enquiries should be directed to our Research Service The Museums Service’s reserve collection is also stored at the Somerset Heritage Centre. We cannot display all the objects we hold but they’re available for researchers and visitors to look at by appointment. Objects may also be used in temporary exhibitions or loaned to other institutions. The collection includes objects relating to Costume and Textiles, Fine and Decorative Art, Archaeology, Natural Sciences and Social History. We also care for the Somerset Military Museum Trust and North Somerset Council collections at this site.
tagline: Access to the Somerset Archives and Local Studies Library and the Historic Environment Record

title: Quantock Hills National Landscape
subtitle: Quantock Hills are situated between Taunton and Bridgwater stretching to the sea at the Bristol Channel. Though compact, measuring just twelve miles by four, they offer extensive views over much of Somerset and across to the Welsh coast.
bodyContent: THE QUANTOCKS The first place in Britain to be designated An Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty was the land on and around the Quantock Hills which inspired the great poets of the Romantic Movement, Coleridge and Wordsworth to pen some of their finest verses. The pair, accompanied by Wordsworth’s sister Dorothy, would wander the woods, rolling hills and coastal paths for hours and in many ways much of what they wondered at has not changed. Characterised by deep wooded valleys or "combes", open heath land and rich flora and fauna, the Quantocks are ideal for walking , cycling and horseriding . Such is their special quality, that this area was the first in the country to be designated an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty in 1956. Amongst the many picturesque villages are: Kingston St Mary, Bishops Lydeard , Holford,Crowcombe and Nether Stowey , one time home of Romantic poet Samuel Taylor Coleridge and starting point of the 51 mile Coleridge Way. Fyne Court , near Broomfield was once the home of Andrew Crosse, an early pioneer of electricity, is the main visitor centre for the Quantock Hills.

title: 18 The Circus
subtitle: City Centre - 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character.
bodyContent: 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character. The maisonette that occupies the top two floors of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the northern Lansdown slopes of stunning terraces of Georgian houses, and with the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minute’s walk. Access is via a communal hallway and carpeted staircase that leads to the maisonette’s front door on the second floor. Inside is a small hall, off which sits the spacious and airy sitting room that is tastefully and comfortably furnished and decorated and being south facing, is very light. On this floor is also a large fitted kitchen with dining table and chairs. A mezzanine room houses the washing machine and dryer for exclusive use of visitors to this home. The stairs on this floor lead to a well-lit landing, off which lie the bedrooms. The front bedroom is a very large room with a double bed and conveniently, a single bed for family use. This brightly furnished bedroom also has an en-suite shower room. The second bedroom has twin beds and is next door to a family sized bathroom with bath, shower-in-bath, basin, WC and airing cupboard. The property contains gas central heating, gas hob, gas double oven, fridge, dishwasher, washing machine and dryer, microwave, TV in lounge and master bedroom, video, stereo, towels and toiletries. Free Car Parking Permit available Free Unlimited fiber broadband Please note: the house is a listed 4 story Georgian townhouse and as such does not have an elevator. Find out more here.

subtitle: Large Parties - 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character.
bodyContent: 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character. The maisonette that occupies the top two floors of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the northern Lansdown slopes of stunning terraces of Georgian houses, and with the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minute’s walk. Access is via a communal hallway and carpeted staircase that leads to the maisonette’s front door on the second floor. Inside is a small hall, off which sits the spacious and airy sitting room that is tastefully and comfortably furnished and decorated and being south facing, is very light. On this floor is also a large fitted kitchen with dining table and chairs. A mezzanine room houses the washing machine and dryer for exclusive use of visitors to this home. The stairs on this floor lead to a well-lit landing, off which lie the bedrooms. The front bedroom is a very large room with a double bed and conveniently, a single bed for family use. This brightly furnished bedroom also has an en-suite shower room. The second bedroom has twin beds and is next door to a family sized bathroom with bath, shower-in-bath, basin, WC and airing cupboard. The property contains gas central heating, gas hob, gas double oven, fridge, dishwasher, washing machine and dryer, microwave, TV in lounge and master bedroom, video, stereo, towels and toiletries. Free Car Parking Permit available Free Unlimited fiber broadband Please note: the house is a listed 4 story Georgian townhouse and as such does not have an elevator. Find out more here.
tagline: Large Parties - 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character.

title: At the Manor
subtitle: Manor Farm House self catering accommodation is spacious, comfortable and tastefully decorated and can accommodate large groups of 10-15 guests.
bodyContent: We are a 15 minute drive from the beautiful city of Bath and a perfect location for family celebrations, birthdays and anniversaries, wedding groups, girlie gatherings and business meetings. The country house has a calming, relaxing atmosphere. We also provide bed and breakfast accommodation. This gorgeous country Manor near Bath in the heart of Somerset was once a Grange and run by Monks from a nearby monastery in Tudor times. We are tucked away down a quiet country lane in the heart of the conservation village of Norton St Philip. The central village location allows our guests a leisurely stroll to the local pubs including the famous George Inn. Discover stunning countryside walks and a meander around the historic conservation village of Norton St Philip. There are many cycle routes in this area too including the renovated old train tunnel into Bath. We are also close to Bradford on Avon for canal walks, boating and cycling, Wells – the film Hot Fuzz was filmed here, Longleat Safari Park, Glastonbury – climb the ancient Tor, Stonehenge, Frome – the best market ever is held the first Sunday of each month and Salisbury.
tagline: Manor Farm House self catering accommodation is spacious, comfortable and tastefully decorated

title: Bristol Airport
subtitle: Your holiday starts at the airport
bodyContent: Handling over 8.6 million passengers annually, Bristol Airport is the third largest regional airport in England and the main airport serving Somerset, situated just 7 miles from the edge of the county. With flights to over 125 direct destinations, the airport facilitates more than a million inbound visits to the South West each year, including over 200,000 to Somerset. Global connections to the region are also facilitated through multiple-daily flights between Bristol Airport and major European hubs, including Amsterdam, Brussels, Paris and Dublin. £225 million has been invested in passenger facilities at the Airport since 2010. Work has now begun on an updated Master Plan looking to the future to the mid-2040’s which will consider how best to meet growing demand for air travel to and from the South West and South Wales region. Retail & catering offers: https://www.bristolairport.co.uk/at-the-airport/shop-and-eat Holiday offers: https://www.bristolairport.co.uk/where-can-i-fly/offers Sign up to our Reward Emails: https://www.bristolairport.co.uk/rewards

title: First Bus in Somerset
subtitle: Sit back and enjoy Somerset and let us do the driving! You’ve arrived in Somerset and now it’s time to explore. What better way to get around than to forget about the stress of traffic and parking and get the bus. Catch the Mendip Xplorer Service 376 between Street and Bristol to see the famous Tor and Abbey at Glastonbury or to visit Wells Cathedral and The Bishop’s Palace and Gardens. Additionally, it's easy and convenient to get to Cheddar Gorge and the caves by bus, just change at Wells onto
bodyContent: Sit back and soak up the stunning coastal views from one of the Somerset’s Coaster open top Services. Hop off at Brean Leisure Park to enjoy the rides and attractions or have a more leisurely day on the beach at Weston-super-Mare building sand castles. A West of England Group day ticket allows unlimited travel on the two Somerset’s Coaster Services, plus any other First Bus in the area for up to 5 people for only £14. Why not take a trip to Bath? If a city escape is more your thing, we can get you there as well. We have a network of buses throughout Bath to get you anywhere you’d want to go, and not to worry if you’ve arrived by train because the bus station is just next door, you can’t miss it! With a Bath Day Ticket costing just £4.50, allowing unlimited travel on all our buses within the Bath Zone, there’s no excuse to miss out on all this beautiful city has to offer. For more ideas about great things to do in Bath, click here. Take the stress out of parking in Bath We also operate three Park & Ride services in Bath, helping you to get into the city centre from further afield, without worrying about the hassle of traffic and parking. The journey into the centre takes just 10 minutes and services operate at least every 12 minutes Monday to Saturday and at least every 15 minutes on Sundays.

title: West Somerset Railway
subtitle: West Somerset Railway, Somerset, is a heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton. It is the longest independent railway in Britain, (20 miles).
bodyContent: West Somerset Railway, Somerset is the longest Heritage line in the United Kingdom. Time Table can be seen HERE for 2024 The line is situated in Somerset, four miles outside the County town of Taunton , starting at Bishops Lydeard and finishing at Minehead . The line meanders through the Quantock Hills , an area of outstanding natural beauty and along the Bristol Channel Coast. We have 10 stations along the line each having something different to offer. There are various historic sites that may be of interest to visitors to the area, for example Crowcombe Heathfield station was the location for the filming of the Beatles’ “A Hard Days Night” and scenes from “The Land Girls” were also shot here. The historic town of Watchet dates back to Saxon times, and boasts narrow streets, local shops, museums and lots of places to eat and drink. Washford is a great place to alight, just a short walk from the station we have Cleeve Abbey and the Torre Cider Farm, which are both well worth a visit. Fancy something a little different then why not visit Dunster Castle which is nestled in the medieval village of Dunster ? Dunster also has a working Watermill , the Old Yarn Market building and the Dolls Museum or continue on to Minehead home of our final station. Minehead is situated at the foot of North Hill where the beach is literally right across the road, we have cafes, shops and plenty of arcades along the seafront, making this a go to location. The West Somerset Railway also have combined tickets on selected dates throughout the year. These include, Cream Tea and Cheese and cider specials and linked trips with Hestercombe Gardens and Dunster Castle. We organise Steam Galas in the Spring and Autumn, and we are host to a Diesel Gala too. In the latter part of the year we have our popular Christmas services, we have Santa services running out of Minehead and Bishops Lydeard from the end of November until Christmas Eve, we also have our Sherry and Mince pie specials for you to enjoy.
tagline: Heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton.

title: Haynes Motor Museum
subtitle: Haynes Motor Museum in Sparkford is a must-visit attraction, home to the UK’s largest collection of cars and motorbikes. Discover pioneering vehicles in The Dawn of Motoring, explore iconic red cars in the Red Room, and experience the thrill of legendary Williams Formula 1 racing cars up close.

title: Wookey Hole Caves & Attractions
subtitle: Wookey Hole Caves is a magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for all ages. It’s an experience millions of years in the making with plenty to do inside and out. Enjoy vintage penny arcades, museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, and of course the famous, beautiful caves.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Wookey Hole Caves and attractions lies In the heart of Somerset. A magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for the young and young at heart. When you visit Wookey Hole, you’ll enjoy an experience millions of years in the making. There is plenty to do inside and out, from vintage penny arcades to museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, to name but a few of the attractions. Not forgetting the breathtakingly beautiful caves, for which Wookey Hole is renowned. Your visit will take you through 8 chambers. Each with a unique beauty and story. You’ll also pass our cheese tunnel, home to the delicious Wookey Hole cheese. The cheese is not the only resident of the caves. Over the years, Wookey Hole has been home to giant hyenas, bears, Neanderthals, and many local people. It has even been a site of pagan and Roman worship. You’ll find Wookey Hole holds a surprise around every corner. You might even get to meet our most famous resident, the Witch of Wookey Hole. We have found she most likes to visit during school holidays! The world-famous Wookey Hole Circus School performs at Wookey Hole at weekends and in School Holidays. Every year over 250,000 people visit Wookey Hole and take-home cherished memories of a great day out. Whether it is your first time or your fiftieth, there is always something new to discover. We can’t wait to welcome you.
tagline: At Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions, Somerset, there’s always fun and adventure to be had.

title: The shop at Dunster Castle
subtitle: Explore the atmospheric 17th-century stables and visit the shop for high quality, original gifts and local products. Our shop is brimming with beautiful things, so you are sure to find something to tempt you, whether it's a treat for yourself or a gorgeous gift for a friend.
bodyContent: Explore the atmospheric 17th-century stables and visit the shop for high quality, original gifts and local products. Our shop is brimming with beautiful things, so you are sure to find something to tempt you, whether it's a treat for yourself or a gorgeous gift for a friend. A working watermill Bake the perfect loaf with some organic Dunster Watermill flour. Ground on site there's been a mill here since Domesday. If that doesn’t take your fancy how about some Dunster Watermill porridge or even a bag of muesli, made to our secret recipe. Harry's Cider Made in the heart of Somerset this premium quality cider is made on Harry's farm with 100% cider fruit. Different varieties are pressed, fermented and matured for several months before being blended to give a distinctive and refreshing taste. Find out more by visiting their website here. Handy history guide Get the most from your visit to Dunster Castle and Gardens with our new souvenir guidebook. With beautiful colour photographs, reconstruction drawings, historical images and a tour of the castle, it is a great momento of your day.

title: Somerset NHS Foundation Trust
subtitle: Somerset NHS Foundation Trust is the first NHS trust to provide community, mental health and acute hospital services. We work with health and social care partners in Somerset to ensure that we deliver outstanding services that meet the needs of our population.
bodyContent: Yeovil District Hospital is also recognised as one of the top performing Trusts in the UK for health and wellbeing of its employees where staff said they felt supported in their roles by their managers and would recommend us as an employer.We have also won the NHS Pastoral Care Quality Award for recruitment of staff. We are currently in the process of officially merging with Yeovil District Hospital to become one large trust covering the whole of Somerset which will give us the opportunity to support the health and care needs of the people of Somerset, and to provide consistent and accessible services across the county. We have ample development opportunities for our staff to engage in. We offer contract opportunities in fixed term, permanent, bank, secondments (internal secondments to other areas within the trust), rotational posts across the trust and much more! We have excellent on-site training facilities both via e-learning and face to face. Our benefits include: • Annual staff recognition awards • Relocation packages • Excellent annual leave entitlement – 27 days + bank holidays, raising to 29 after 5 years’ service and 33 after 10 years’ service • Fantastic support with staff wellbeing including access to a 24/7 counselling service for staff • Are you newly qualified? We cover the cost of your first year’s PIN registrations • Supportive preceptorship programme for all newly qualified staff • 1 to 1 supervision and appraisal processes in place as well as informal support from col leagues whenever needed • NHS pension scheme • NHS staff discount at various shops and restaurants

title: Strawberry Line Cycle Project
subtitle: Our Bike hire is based at Yatton Railway Station, a 15 minute journey by train from Weston-Super-Mare or Bristol Temple Meads. Cycle the beautiful Strawberry Line, nine miles of largely traffic free cycle path, stretching through North Somerset and into Somerset to Cheddar.
bodyContent: We're all about community. And we're all about getting people outdoors on the beautiful Strawberry Line. You can find Strawberry Line Cycle Hire in the car park by platform one of Yatton train station. From here, you can ride straight on to the Strawberry Line for nine-miles of traffic-free riding through the Somerset countryside. We think that cycling is for everyone and our range of traditional and adaptive bikes to rent reflects that, and so do our brilliant staff - we offer people with learning disabilities meaningful employment and training. We have a café on site We can also offer bike rentals for short break or holiday periods.

title: The King's Negroni
subtitle: Celebrate His Majesty's first Christmas on the throne with King’s Negroni A Negroni is a true classic cocktail, and provides countless opportunities for mixing and matching to your taste.
bodyContent: Our Perfect Pour pairs our Navy Strength Gin with Ginger Liquour and sweet Vermouth, to create a drink that’s not only delicious, but warms the cockles on a Winters night. 30ml Northmoor Navy Strength Gin 30ml The Kings Ginger 30ml Sweet Vermouth Ingredients This recipe doesn’t take a lot of science to get right, simply pour all ingredients into a glass with ice, and stir for 30 seconds. Strain the liquid into a fresh short/rock glass with fresh, cubed ice. Top of this nice and easy cocktail with a sprig of rosemary to garnish. https://www.exmoordistillery.co.uk/
tagline: Celebrate His Majesty's first Christmas on the throne with King’s Negroni

title: Thorney Lakes and Caravan Park
subtitle: A caravan and camping park with full facilities and coarse fishing available.
bodyContent: A caravan and camping park with full facilities and coarse fishing available. One mile form the historic village of Muchelney, our scenic park is perfect for touring the Somerset level and Moors , one of the most unchanged and distinctive landscape of lowland Britain. There are many interesting walks on the wetlands which are rich in flora, fauna and birdlife. Fishing lakes established in 1993, the setting attracts a host of wildlife and is regualry visited by otters, badgers, rabbits, deer and 70 species of birdlife including kingfishers. Just a short level walk from the caravan path the two miles of nature trails are a perfect for a short stroll or to enjoy a chat with the local fisher folk.
tagline: A caravan and camping park with full facilities and coarse fishing available.

title: Buses of Somerset
subtitle: Whether you fancy exploring or taking in the views of the county’s many charming villages and towns, you’ll find more with easier local travel. bodyContent: As well as our core network, we also have one of our Adventures By Bus tours operating in the area; the stunning open-top Exmoor Coaster which journeys through Exmoor National Park, from Doniford to Lynmouth. For more information about this route, and our other Adventures By Bus, including timetables and prices, please visit our Adventures By Bus website. From online tickets to timetables and route maps, we have a vast amount of resources to help you get around as easily as possible. We operate services running regularly throughout Somerset and the surrounding area, meaning there is always a bus ready to take you where you need to go. title: The Slow Farming Company
subtitle: The Slow Farming Company is a Somerset family farm spanning four generation
bodyContent: The Slow Farming Company is a Somerset family farm spanning four generations, led by Rob, a regenerative farming pioneer. They produce pasture-reared beef and free-range eggs, nutritious and low-cholesterol, sold alongside curated homewares via their new e-commerce site.
tagline: The concept of slow farming and slow food are, at their core.

title: Barrington Court, National Trust
subtitle: Barrington Court, located in the stunning south Somerset countryside, is a charming Tudor manor house complimented beautifully with Gertrude Jekyll-inspired gardens, apple orchards and a working kitchen garden.
bodyContent: Barrington Court Somerset National Trust - Discover the haunting echoes of the past at Barrington Court, a Tudor manor house free from collections and furniture. Explore using your imagination and your senses to discover a house full of memories, where light fills the rooms and you feel you can almost touch the past. The property was saved from ruin and restored by the Lyle family in 1920s, when the Court House resembled a barn rather than the proud manor house that it is. Close your eyes and you’ll almost be able to hear the sounds and see the sights of the glamorous parties held in the great hall during Barrington’s heyday. On the first floor listen out for the voices resonating from the past, of the young evacuees who called Barrington home during the Second World War. Stroll through the Gertrude Jekyll inspired gardens, which with their focus on plant varieties and colours are a delight for all the senses. Be spurred on in your own garden or allotment by the stone-walled kitchen garden that produces a variety of delicious fruit and vegetables. Don’t just take our word for it, why not stop off in the Strode House Restaurant to taste these home-grown delights. Barrington Court predominantly featured in BBC’s highly acclaimed recent production of Hilary Mantel’s Wolf Hall.
tagline: Barrington Court, located in the stunning south Somerset countryside.

title: Bushcraft and Survival Skills at Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Take the kids on a Somerset woodland adventure. This discovery experience is the perfect way to connect more with nature and have fun in the woods!
bodyContent: Take the kids on a Somerset woodland adventure. This discovery experience is the perfect way to connect more with nature and have fun in the woods! Could you survive in the wilderness? Experience a family friendly bushcraft and survival skills session in Mendip’s secluded ancient woodland. Your instructor will teach you some back to basics survival skills including fire lighting. Your efforts will be rewarded as you’ll get a chance to roast some marshmallows on the fire you built! 1.5 hour session bushcraft session Please note: This is a family friendly session, it is not aimed at or recommended for adult-only groups. Book Bushcraft and Survival Skills: https://mendip.me/book/survival_skills/

title: Caving with Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Mendip Activity Centre offer real Caving adventures right under Somerset’s Mendip Hills. It’s the perfect place to try something totally different. Explore underground tunnels, climb through hidden chambers, and experience the thrill of adventure beneath your feet.
bodyContent: Mendip Activity Centre offer real Caving adventures right under Somerset’s Mendip Hills. It’s the perfect place to try something totally different. Explore underground tunnels, climb through hidden chambers, and experience the thrill of adventure beneath your feet. Choose from Sandford Levy (great for beginners), Goatchurch Cavern (more adventurous) or Swildon’s Hole (previous experience recommended). Sessions are led by qualified instructors who’ll guide you safely at your pace. Discover the underground world of Somerset!

title: Target Sports at Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Target Sport activities for the whole family at Mendip Activity Centre.
bodyContent: Mendip Activity Centre offer Target Sports for public booking at their activity centre on the Mendip Hills. Perched in the heart of Somerset’s wild and beautiful countryside, this is your chance to channel your inner Robin Hood. Whether you're a beginner or a secret pro, these adventures are a blast. Activities available include Archery, Air Rifle and Axe Throwing whilst Nerf & Gel Battles and ArcheryActive are available as private group sessions. From calm precision to full-blown foam fun, there’s something for every level of energy and age group age 6+. All sessions are led by friendly, experienced instructors who’ll guide you safely and confidently every step of the way. Sessions run in all weathers thanks to undercover ranges, and you can book for individuals, families, birthday parties or just because you fancy something adventurous to do this week!
tagline: Targetsport activities for the whole family at Mendip Activity Centre.

title: Tobogganing at Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Blast down the floodlit toboggan slope on colorful Zibob toboggans! Tobogganing at Mendip Activity Centre is available for either individual spaces or exclusive hire of half or the whole slope! Keep an eye out for the extremely popular seasonal sessions at Easter, Halloween and Christmas!
bodyContent: Mendip Activity Centre offer Tobogganing sessions on their purpose-built slope in the Mendip Hills. It’s their most popular activity for a reason. Fast, fun and full of laughter, it’s a brilliant introduction to the thrills of the slope with no snow required and no experience needed. Tobogganing at Mendip is perfect for all ages, from adventurous kids to nostalgic grown-ups. Individual spaces are available for ages 4 to 12 whilst everyone can take part if you book it privately. And keep an eye out for their themed tobogganing sessions across the year, like Twilight Tobogganing, spooky Halloween specials and Easter adventures.

title: Watersports at Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Dive into Mendip Activity Centre’s watersport activities at their private watersports site.
bodyContent: Every summer, Mendip Activity Centre offer Watersports sessions at their site Hewish, just outside Weston-super-Mare. Whether you’re learning to paddle or racing your mates across the water, there’s no better place to get stuck in. Activities on offer include Kayaking, Canoeing, Paddleboarding and Raft Building. Sessions are open to all abilities and led by friendly, qualified instructors who’ll keep it fun, safe and confidence-boosting.

title: Frisbee Golf at Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: One of the UK’s only 18-hole frisbee golf (or disc golf) course is right here in Somerset!
bodyContent: Mendip Activity Centre have an 18-hole Frisbee Golf course set in the stunning Mendip Hills open to everyone year-round. It’s like traditional golf, but with frisbees, fresh air and far more fun. The course winds through open fields and ancient woodland, with incredible views and the occasional friendly sheep for company. Ideal for families and friends, it’s a low-pressure adventure that’s as chilled or competitive as you want it to be. Every player gets a scorecard and a disc. Book in advance or just turn up. Children can take part in the free Yeti Hunt along the way. It’s a magical extra that makes this a favourite for adventurous families exploring Somerset.

title: Muchelney Abbey
subtitle: Muchelney Abbey was once the second largest abbey in Somerset
bodyContent: Surrounded by picturesque farmland and countryside, Muchelney Abbey was once the second largest abbey in Somerset. Discover what life was like in the abbey, wander through peaceful grounds and explore its remarkably intact medieval buildings. Once a wealthy Benedictine house, Muchelney Abbey abruptly closed in 1538 during King Henry VIII’s famous dissolution of the monasteries. Yet there is still much to discover at this historic gem, set in an idyllic spot overlooking the Somerset Levels. Today you can still see the clearly laid out foundations of the abbey, parts of the richly decorated cloister walk and thatched monks’ lavatory – the only one of its kind in Britain. The 16th-century abbots’ house remains intact with its magnificent rooms, and site finds are on display illustrating monastic life. With plenty of rooms to explore, take a peaceful stroll into the past. On sunny days, children can let off steam and play in the grounds.

title: Brothers Drinks
subtitle: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family, who have been making cider in Somerset since 1658.
bodyContent: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family, who have been making cider in Somerset since 1658. We first started selling our Pear Cider at the Glastonbury Festival in 1995 near what was then called the Jazz World Stage. These days it is called The West Holts Stage. Over the years, festival goers kept asking us if it was possible to get our drink when the festival was over and so we decided to market it to pubs and supermarkets. Now you can get it all over the country and at many festivals. We are independent, British and are passionate about what we do. Our free-spirited essence is upheld by approaching things with a unique perspective. Here at Brothers, we take our values and commitment to sustainability very seriously, but it’s something we haven’t really shouted about until now. We have zero to landfill, all our waste is segregated to optimise the opportunity of being recycled or reused. A massive solar panel system is now installed here at the cider mill, where it will directly supply the presses with clean energy and lastly, all our left-over fruit pomace is turned into energy which helps to heat the local swimming pool!

title: Longleat
subtitle: Explore a world of adventure at Longleat. From a Drive Through Safari expedition, to discovering inside our iconic Elizabethan mansion, there’s plenty to entertain you.
bodyContent: Explore a world of adventure at Longleat. From a Drive Through Safari expedition, to discovering inside our iconic Elizabethan mansion, there’s plenty to entertain you. Travel the globe within this Wiltshire estate – stop off at African Village for a chance to see our new pack of African painted dogs, herd of Grants zebras and leap with lemurs. Say hi to our cheeky monkeys and bring your pack to meet our pack of wolves! Listen out for the Longleat lions’ roars as you explore. Continue your adventure on foot and walk with mischievous meerkats in Jungle Kingdom, feed rainbow lorikeets and watch our playful giant otters. Don’t forget to visit Koala Creek to see England’s only resident koalas, watch our sleepy sloths climb around or check in with our native red squirrels. Hop on board the Boat Safari and explore Half Mile Pond. Home to our family of noisy Californian sea lions, views of Gorilla Colony and Colobus monkeys will make quite a splash. Why not feed the sea lions to add to your unique day out? All aboard Longleat Railway! Enjoy a delightful ride around the lake and keep an eye on the action from our miniature railway. Or discover more about our history by adding a guided house tour to your itinerary. If your little cubs are looking to play, be sure to visit Little Explorer’s Garden and the Adventure Castle for plenty of room to let their imaginations run wild. Why not challenge yourself to our Hedge Maze and see if you can find your way through the winding passages? And no day is complete without a ride on Rockin’ Rhino! Book your tickets for a day out like no other or make your visit extra special with a VIP experience!
tagline: Longleat, nestled within 900 acres of ‘Capability’ Brown landscaped grounds.

title: Komedia Bath
subtitle: Hosting over 400 events per year in a beautifully restored former Edwardian cinema, Komedia is a go-to destination for a great night out in the city of Bath. Take your pick from Saturday night stand-up, top gigs and tours, quirky cabaret shows, late night revelry and so much at the award-winning venue.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Komedia Bath was established in 2008 and community-owned since 2019, Komedia prides itself on offering something for everybody and operates two distinct performance spaces to do this. At the heart of it all is the Main Auditorium. With high ceilings, baroque grandeur and room for 600+ people, it’s a stunning setting for full-scale live performances and also functions as Bath’s only above-ground night club venue. The Main Auditorium is also home to the award-winning Komedia Comedy Club. The legendary Comedy Club features some of the best acts from the UK and international stand-up circuit every Saturday night. Each show features three world-class comedians and a top-notch compere. For the ultimate Saturday night out, add entry to The Big Disco after the comedy for just £2! Alongside this, Komedia is also very proud to run The Electric Bar – an intimate live performance space that was purpose-built to support grassroots-level music and rising comedy talent. The venue's Box Office is also situated within The Electric Bar, open Tuesday - Saturday from 10am - 5pm. Drop by to find out what’s on, take a quick tour of the venue or pick up a programme. Komedia is committed to being accessible to everyone and is continuously working to improve the experience of its disabled audiences, artists, and team members. For information on accessibility at Komedia, please visit: https://komediabath.co.uk/plan-your-visit/accessibility/
tagline: Hosting over 400 events per year in a beautifully restored former Edwardian cinema

title: Clarks Village
subtitle: If you haven't experienced the magic of Clarks Village yet, you've been missing out! Nestled amidst the stunning Somerset countryside, our shopping centre offers a serene and breathtaking environment like no other.
bodyContent: Admire the majestic trees, some of which have stood for over a century, and enjoy our abundance of green spaces and landscaped gardens. Take a moment to relax amidst nature, savouring the horticulture, insects, and birds that inhabit our surroundings. We are also proud to be a dog-friendly outlet, where well-behaved four-legged companions are even allowed in most stores. At Clarks Village, we invite you to embark on a retail adventure and explore the remarkable experiences waiting to be discovered in our surrounding area. Come and discover the endless possibilities that await you! Time to shop! With over 75 stores and 90 renowned brands to explore, Clarks Village provides a shopping experience like no other. Enjoy up to 60% off the recommended retail prices every day, allowing you to shop to your heart's content. Take your time; there's no need to rush. As you peruse the stores, make sure to pause and treat yourself to a coffee, or perhaps a refreshing cup of tea—hot, iced, or even bubble tea. And when hunger strikes, indulge in a delightful assortment of snacks, including pasties, of course (because you are in the Westcountry!), cakes, waffles, sandwiches, and so much more. The options are endless. Accessible and Inclusive Clarks Village warmly welcomes all guests. With all stores located on ground level, easy access is provided for those with mobility challenges. Our Guest Services team is dedicated to supporting individuals with hidden disabilities, ensuring a comfortable experience for everyone. For more information, check out our accessibility information page .
tagline: If you haven't experienced the magic of Clarks Village yet, you've been missing out!

title: At the Manor
subtitle: Manor Farm House self catering accommodation is spacious, comfortable and tastefully decorated and can accommodate large groups of 10-15 guests.
bodyContent: We are a 15 minute drive from the beautiful city of Bath and a perfect location for family celebrations, birthdays and anniversaries, wedding groups, girlie gatherings and business meetings. The country house has a calming, relaxing atmosphere. We also provide bed and breakfast accommodation. This gorgeous country Manor near Bath in the heart of Somerset was once a Grange and run by Monks from a nearby monastery in Tudor times. We are tucked away down a quiet country lane in the heart of the conservation village of Norton St Philip. The central village location allows our guests a leisurely stroll to the local pubs including the famous George Inn. Discover stunning countryside walks and a meander around the historic conservation village of Norton St Philip. There are many cycle routes in this area too including the renovated old train tunnel into Bath. We are also close to Bradford on Avon for canal walks, boating and cycling, Wells – the film Hot Fuzz was filmed here, Longleat Safari Park, Glastonbury – climb the ancient Tor, Stonehenge, Frome – the best market ever is held the first Sunday of each month and Salisbury.
tagline: Manor Farm House self catering accommodation is spacious, comfortable and tastefully decorated

title: The Royal Hotel
subtitle: A great tradition providing hospitality for over 150 years, within walking distance of all of Bath’s leading attractions.
bodyContent: The Royal first opened as a hotel in 1846 and has been owned by the present owners since 1995. During this time there has been an ongoing programme of renovation and improvements to ensure that this lovely property, which was designed by Brunel, is well maintained and provides attractive facilities for our many guests.
tagline: A great tradition providing hospitality for over 150 years

title: Vellum Stone Cottage
subtitle: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway.
bodyContent: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway – indoor pool and games room on site, Kennet and Avon Canal Close by (3/4 of a mile), walking and cycling from your doorstep. Farm Shop and country pub(s) within walking distance. The cottage features a country feel with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams, with soft furnishings compliment. Enjoy admiring the sheep in the fields surrounding the farm.
tagline: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway.

title: Whitley Coach House
subtitle: Whitley Coach House is a truly luxurious self-contained 1804 Georgian built.
bodyContent: Recently modernised stone coach house providing self-catering accommodation for long, short or one night stays. Whitley Coach House is an ideal base from which to visit Bath, Lacock, Longleat, Bowood House, Stonehenge, National Trust properties and many other local attractions. Only 20 minutes from Bath and 5 Minutes from Lacock – 10-minute walk to a great Pub/Resturant and local shop/cafe, free fast Wi-Fi, 40″ smart TV with Netflix and free private parking. Private garden with teak furniture on wooden decking. With luxurious bedding including a handmade king size Lit Bateau bed with a Vi-Spring luxuriously comfortable handmade mattress. Immediate and live AVAILABILITY. Accepting: American Express plus most credit and debit cards. Whitley Coach House self-catering accommodation has a large bedroom with a super king-size (5ft 6ins x 6ft 6ins) Lit Bateau oak bed designed and handmade with a supremely comfortable Vi-Spring handmade pocket sprung mattress. The living room has high ceilings with exposed beams and includes two three-seater sofas one with a large double pull-out bed. In addition, there is a luxurious deep sprung folding bed for use in the bedroom or entrance hall. ONLINE BOOKING or do look at our Website: www.whitleycoachhouse.co.uk The Space Whitley Coach House is a detached former coach house to a Georgian house, renovated four years ago and just redecorated, providing spacious self-catering accommodation. Whitley Coach House has a large bedroom with an individually designed and handmade kingsize bateau bed designed and handmade in oak, with a supremely comfortable Vi-Spring pocket sprung mattress. The living room has high ceilings with exposed beams and a solid oak floor and includes two three-seater sofas one with a large super king size pull-out bed. The living room has views of the private garden, teak furniture and decked veranda. The kitchen table seats up to six people. This self-catering accommodation has fast broadband, a 40 inch smart TV with Freeview channels and the ability to watch other online services like Netflix. Guest Access The back has a private wooden decked terrace for use in dry weather and garden beyond. There is plenty of private parking. A barbeque can be provided if asked for at an extra charge. Whitley Coach House self-catering accommodation is not adapted for wheelchair users but has a step up into the property on entry. Once inside there are no steps, it is a converted coach house on one level. Interaction with Guests Your host will normally hand you the keys and discuss Whitley Coach House and the surrounding area with you on arrival. Unless you need help or are staying over a week, you will be left alone to enjoy your stay.
tagline: Whitley Coach House is a truly luxurious self-contained 1804 Georgian built.

title: The King Alfred Pilgrimage
subtitle: Follow in the footsteps of King Alfred in the heart of Somerset.
bodyContent: Image: Andy Lewington On the Twelfth Night, the 5th/6th January 878AD, the Viking Danish army led by Guthrum the Old launched a surprise attack on King Alfred’s winter court at Chippenham. Quickly overcoming the defenders, Alfred was forced to flee for his life with his family and a small retinue to the wetlands of Somerset. Anglo-Saxon England was reduced to an Iron Age marsh fort on the Isle of Athelney. Our journey in the footsteps of King Alfred begins at St Mary’s Church in North Petherton where, in 1693, the Alfred Jewel was found in a nearby field. Follow the route to Fordgate, an ancient crossing point of a now diverted river, the route crosses the Bridgwater & Taunton Canal allowing pedestrian access to the pilgrimage along the towpath from either of those towns. Take a moment to rest in the picnic area and learn about the local wetlands wildlife from information boards located there. Continue on the route toward Wisteria Farm and across fields to Moorland and the parish church of St Peter and St John, and on along drove roads to East Lyng, the gateway to Athelney. In 879AD, Alfred ordered that East Lyng be fortified and it became a burgh town. St Bartholomew’s Church boasts an Alfred window alongside the image of St Bartholomew, a Roman soldier who was martyred for refusing to denounce his faith The River Tone originally ran between East Lyng and the Isle of Athelney, with a timber walkway allowing access to the Iron Age marsh fort. As you walk up Cuts Road look to the left and the first, smaller hill is the site of Alfred’s defensive position from where he planned the defeat of Guthrum. Carrying on to Athelney Farm, take a moment to look at the information boards and follow the permissive footpath to the site of Athelney Abbey, founded by Alfred in 879AD. Return to the main footpath and continue with the river on your right. Burrow Mump , a strategic vantage point, will appear in front of you. Cross the road and continue along where the Rivers Tone and Parrett meet, past the King Alfred pub and St Michael’s church to just beyond the white building where steps will begin your ascent to the top. At the summit, look west to the Quantock Hills and North Petherton, south to Athelney and East Lyng, east to Aller Hill, north to Glastonbury Tor and Wedmore . Return to the King Alfred pub and rest a while whilst we reflect on the rest of the story. During the early months of 878AD, Alfred fought a guerrilla war against the Danes searching for him in the marshes of Somerset, sending riders on the perilous task to contact his Ealdermen with orders to raise the fyrds of Somerset, Wiltshire and East Hampshire. The army was to meet at Egbert’s Stone at Kingston Deverill, on the border of Somerset and Wiltshire, at the beginning of May 878AD. Alfred and a small force of warriors, using withy boats and hidden tracks, made their way to Aller church to pray for victory before heading to Langport and the ‘hard way’, an old Roman road running through Somerton and Bruton , then headed north to Egbert’s Stone where Alfred stood on King’s Hill and awaited the arrival of his army. The next day they moved north a few miles, rested overnight and readied themselves for the battle ahead. Sometime between 6th and 12th May 878AD, Alfred and the Anglo-Saxons clashed with Guthrum and the Danish army at Ethandun outside the walls of the fortress at Chippenham. Alfred’s soldiers, fighting on foot, confronted the Danes with a dense shield wall. The battle raged until Alfred, in the words of Asser, “overthrew the pagans with great slaughter, and smiting the fugitives, he pursued them as far as the fortress” His victory was decisive, forcing Guthrum to surrender and commit himself and thirty of his leading warriors to convert to Christianity. Continuing our journey, we walk beside the River Parrett , crossing to walk along the the River Sowy to Aller Drove, heading up to St Andrew’s Church at Aller. In early June 878AD, Guthrum, after his defeat at Ethandun, came to Aller church to be baptised along with 30 of his followers. Guthrum took the Christian name Æthelstan and was granted lands in East Anglia where he ruled as King until his death in 890AD. This act led to the creation of Danelaw and ultimately to a unified Christian England The Alfred window at Aller Church Depart the church through the gate at the rear, taking the left-hand footpath back to the River Parrett and into Langport . Image: James Thurtle Take some time to explore the artisan shops and cafes of this important Anglo-Saxon trading centre before heading up The Hill to St Mary’s Church. Follow the route to the Roman road to Somerton, but our route takes us via St John’s Church in Pitney where the Anglo-Saxon Pitney Brooch was discovered during renovations, perhaps from one of Alfred’s noblemen as they made their way to Egbert’s Stone. Continue into Somerton, the ancient capital of Wessex, where our journey ends at St Michael and All Angels’ Church for now whilst we plan the next stage to Egbert’s Stone and the Battle of Ethandun

title: Dogs Friends
subtitle: Dogs Friends is a rescue nestled in the heart of Somerset, driven by a profound passion for helping dogs in need.
bodyContent: Dogs Friends is more than just a rescue; it's a dedicated charity, officially established in 2009, driven by a singular mission: to find loving forever homes for dogs of all ages, sizes, and breeds. We proudly utilise our extensive fostering scheme as much as possible to allow our dogs to thrive in a warm, domestic setting, helping us truly understand their unique personalities and needs. When it comes to adoption, we always put the dog's needs first, crafting individual adoption profiles to ensure they find their perfect match. We also strive to be flexible with our adoption criteria, understanding that every family and every dog is different. So, if you're dreaming of adding a new furry companion to your family, considering the incredibly rewarding experience of fostering, or simply curious to learn more, visit our website today!

title: Bridgwater Here and Now
subtitle: Bridgwater Here and Now is a vibrant online hub and Facebook page celebrating Bridgwater’s culture, events, and local businesses. It showcases venues and activities, and helps residents and visitors explore, engage, and enjoy everything Bridgwater has to offer.
bodyContent: Bridgwater Here and Now is an online platform celebrating everything that makes Bridgwater special - right here, right now. The website is a one-stop hub for discovering local events, venues, shops, eateries, and community groups. Whether you're a resident or a visitor, it’s designed to help you explore, engage and enjoy all that Bridgwater has to offer. The website features a live events calendar, listings for places to stay, eat, and shop, and profiles of local businesses and venues. From the world-famous Bridgwater Carnival to intimate gigs, workshops, and seasonal fairs, the site showcases the town’s rich cultural life and rebellious spirit. Complementing the website is the Bridgwater Here and Now Facebook page, which keeps followers up to date with what is going on in and around Bridgwater. Whether you're planning a day out, promoting an event, or just curious about what’s going on, Bridgwater Here and Now is your go-to guide for everything local.

title: Bridgwater
subtitle: A rich legacy as a port and commercial centre is joined by Europe’s largest illuminated carnival, which lights up the streets every November.
bodyContent: Historic market town Bridgwater is home to the most illustrious of Somerset’s famous street carnivals A rich legacy as a port and commercial centre is joined by Europe’s largest illuminated carnival, which lights up the streets every November. What to do in Bridgwater A lively town with a rich history, Bridgwater Carnival best symbolises the town’s festive spirit. Residents near and far come together each November to witness the largest illuminated procession in Europe. To get in on the action, check the official Bridgwater Carnival Website for this year’s date, travel advice and accommodation information. Learn about the history of Bridgwater at the Blake Museum, where you’ll discover its past as a port and centre of commerce. The centre of Bridgwater is small enough to explore on foot, so head out to find examples of the fine architecture built during its commercial heydey - check out Cornhill, Castle Street and King Square for some key construction landmarks. Absorb some local culture at the Bridgwater Arts Centre - one of the first in the country - as well as Somerset Brick and Tile Museum, and the Bridgwater and Taunton Canal and Docks. Head to the town centre to find a combination of well-known and independent shops, plus lots of options for dining.

title: The Bell
subtitle: With roots dating back to 1640, The Bell at Broadway is the oldest pub in the area. Beautifully restored in 2018, this 17th-century inn blends historic charm with modern comfort. Enjoy delicious food, fine drinks, and relaxed stays in a timeless setting — celebrating tradition, warmth, and unforgettable hospitality.
bodyContent: With roots reaching back to 1640, The Bell at Broadway proudly holds its place as the oldest pub in the area — a true landmark of local heritage and community spirit. Steeped in history, this beautiful 17th-century inn has welcomed generations of travellers, villagers, and friends through its doors for centuries. Following an extensive renovation in 2018, The Bell has been lovingly restored to preserve the charm and craftsmanship of its past while introducing the warmth and comfort of modern design. Traditional beams, stonework, and characterful details sit effortlessly alongside stylish interiors, inviting open fires, and thoughtful touches that make every visit memorable. Whether you’re joining us for a hearty meal, a perfectly poured drink, or a peaceful overnight stay, The Bell offers a relaxed and welcoming atmosphere that celebrates the best of both old and new. Our menu showcases locally sourced ingredients and seasonal flavours, complemented by an excellent selection of ales, wines, and spirits — all served with genuine Somerset hospitality. From cosy corners for quiet conversations to lively gatherings with family and friends, The Bell at Broadway is a place to slow down, savour, and reconnect. Step inside, feel the history around you, and enjoy the comfort of a modern country inn that honours its past while embracing the present. Here’s to another three hundred years of good company, great food, and the enduring spirit of The Bell at Broadway.

title: Shoemakers Museum
subtitle: Discover the Quakers, the shoemakers and stories behind Clarks shoes in the place where it all began in Street, Somerset
bodyContent: Step inside a new family-friendly visitor attraction celebrating fashion, creativity and social change through 200-years of shoemaking. Find out how the Clarks shoe brand became a global story. A remarkable journey with exhibitions, film, interactives, tours, and regular events to explore enjoy. Meet the Shoemakers Four permanent exhibition galleries share the story of shoemaking in Street, from handmade shoes to factory life, fashions in advertising and shoe shopping. Discover life as a shoemaker, experience shoe shopping 1950s and 1980s style, and celebrate some of the nations’ favourite footwear. Plus meet fossil sea-dragons found under the Clarks factories! Galleries, gardens, café and interactive events An exhibition of 200 years of shoemaking alongside film footage that the factory floor to life. Explore your favourite shoes and experiences, from foot measurements to advertising. An exhibition of 200 years of shoemaking alongside film footage that brings the history of Clarks and the factory floor to life. Interactives include a 1980s shoe shop with 80s fashion to try on. Get creative in the education room and enjoy space to play. Accessibility Shoemakers Museum aims to be an accessible attraction. Facilities include accessible toilets, changing facility, lifts and accessible interactives. Please visit the website to view the access guide. Tickets Free carparking passes for Clarks Village Car Park II are available for museum ticket holders. Food and Drink Enjoy a taste of Somerset with the best of locally produced delicious hot and cold food and drink options available in café. Or bring a picnic to enjoy outside in the gardens and walled orchard. A great family day out Clarks Village, is right on our doorstep with outlet and high street shopping to indulge in after your visit. Shoemakers Museum in Street is a short distance away from historic Glastonbury, nature on the Somerset Levels, and artistic Somerton just down the road.
tagline: Discover the Quakers, the shoemakers and stories behind Clarks shoes

Explore your favourite shoes and experiences, from foot measurements to advertising. An exhibition of 200 years of shoemaking alongside film footage that brings the history of Clarks and the factory floor to life. Interactives include a 1980s shoe shop with 80s fashion to try on. Get creative in the education room and enjoy space to play. Accessibility Shoemakers Museum aims to be an accessible attraction. Facilities include accessible toilets, changing facility, lifts and accessible interactives. Please visit the website to view the access guide. Tickets Free carparking passes for Clarks Village Car Park II are available for museum ticket holders. Food and Drink Enjoy a taste of Somerset with the best of locally produced delicious hot and cold food and drink options available in café. Or bring a picnic to enjoy outside in the gardens and walled orchard. A great family day out Clarks Village, is right on our doorstep with outlet and high street shopping to indulge in after your visit. Shoemakers Museum in Street is a short distance away from historic Glastonbury, nature on the Somerset Levels, and artistic Somerton just down the road.
tagline: Discover the Quakers, the shoemakers and stories behind Clarks shoes

title: Extours – Haunted History
subtitle: Extours offers immersive ghost walks, haunted history tours and real paranormal investigations across Somerset and the South West.
bodyContent: Extours delivers unforgettable ghost walks, haunted history tours and hands-on paranormal investigations across Somerset and the wider South West. Founded by historian and paranormal investigator Bobbie, Extours was created to uncover the hidden stories, folklore and mysteries that are so often overlooked in the towns and landscapes around us. Each experience blends meticulously researched history with authentic investigative techniques, creating atmospheric, interactive events suitable for sceptics, believers and the simply curious. Discover the stories, legends and unexplained mysteries hidden in your local towns. Every experience is built on detailed research: historic documents, local accounts, folklore studies and years of real investigative practice. Rather than relying on theatrics or staged scares, Extours focuses on authenticity — offering genuine insights into the past while giving guests the chance to try real investigative equipment and techniques. Whether you're exploring medieval streets, atmospheric ruins or centuries-old legends, each tour is designed to be intriguing, engaging and accessible for everyone. Our hosts bring together backgrounds in history, performance, research and paranormal investigation, creating events that are welcoming, informative and surprisingly interactive. Guests frequently comment on how much history they learn, how atmospheric the locations are, and how fascinating it is to witness unexplained activity first-hand. With tours running throughout the year across Somerset — including Taunton, Dunster, Watchet, Wellington, Minehead, Glastonbury, Cheddar and more — Extours offers a fresh and meaningful way to engage with heritage, hauntings and local folklore. Whether you're a sceptic, a believer or simply curious, you’re invited to step into the mystery and discover what you will uncover.

title: Down Cemetery Road
subtitle: Locations: The West Somerset Railway/Bishops Lydeard Station, The Wessex Hotel in Street, Brean Down Release date: 2025
bodyContent: Images: West Somerset Railway, Apple TV, Screen Somerset. The hit Apple TV series Down Cemetery Road filmed across the Westcountry including key scenes shot in Somerset at Bishops Lydeard and in Street. The eight-part thriller based on based on Mick Herron’s novel stars Emma Thompson as private investigator Zoe Boehm and Ruth Wilson as art conservator Sarah Trafford, who become embroiled in a dark conspiracy following an explosion in Sarah’s Oxford home. West Somerset Railway’s Bishops Lydeard station features in episode six, doubling as the station in the fictitious Scottish town of Loch Forden. Zoe is amongst the passengers evacuated from the train and seen walking along the track to the station where she jumps into a taxi. The station also appears in episode eight, as a bus carrying Zoe crosses the bridge over the railway line, a view that will be familiar to anyone who has travelled on the 20-mile long heritage line which runs between Bishops Lydeard, near Taunton and Minehead on the coast. A crew of around 150 took over the station for two weeks in January 2025, giving the heritage station a modern makeover that included new signs and digital destination boards, before returning it to its picture postcard natural state. In the autumn of 2025 the production shot scenes on the Mendip Hills, a service station on the A37 and the Wessex Hotel in Street. The Wessex Hotel features as the hotel where Sarah lays low in episode three with scenes that took several days to shoot and required extensive set dressing of the foyer. Based at Bristol’s Bottleyard Studios, Down Cemetery Road also shot in the city’s St Nicholas Market and Baltic Wharf, as well as across the South West as far as Polperro and Holywell Bay in Cornwall. Useful Links: West Somerset Railway Exmoor National Park Visit Exmoor The Wessex Hotel
tagline: Locations: The West Somerset Railway/Bishops Lydeard Station, The Wessex Hotel in Street

title: Taunton Farmers' Market
subtitle: Taunton Farmers' Market, Taunton High Street, every Thursday from 9am until 3pm, year round.
bodyContent: The Vale is a genuine Farmer and Producers co-operative which has grown from strength to strength since its launch in 1999. We are fully certified by FARMA – the National Farmers’ Retail & Markets Association, so you can be confident you are really buying local produce. At our markets you can find just-picked seasonal fruit and vegetables, fresh fish, free-range and organic meat and eggs, a wide selection of regional cheeses, chutneys and preserves, hand-made bread and cakes and many more local specialities - things youcan’t always expect to find in supermarkets. You can also taste many of the goods on offer before you buy. In addition our stallholders are sincerely enthusiastic and knowledgeable about their produce and eager to share information about its growth and preparation. So come down and sample what good food really tastes like, in doing so you will also be supporting your local economy and helping the environment by reducing food-miles.
tagline: Taunton Farmers' Market, Taunton High Street, every Thursday from 9am until 2pm, year round.

title: The Spa at Middlewick
subtitle: Nestled within our 16-acre converted farmstead, Middlewick Spa, Glastonbury may be the quirkiest Spa in Somerset.
bodyContent: Nestled at the back of our property within sight of the iconic Glastonbury Tor, Middlewick Spa is the perfect location to indulge in a treatment, use our pool and sauna, and treat yourself to delicious food and drink. Our Spa is a little different to others you might have visited. Our focus is your holistic wellbeing and the nourishment of your mind, body and soul. Experience an organic facial, rejuvenating massage or holistic beauty treatment. You can also book Spa packages – from a full Spa Day to a Swim, Sauna and Lunch. Begin your Middlewick moment in our Spa Lounge, where you can unwind with a complimentary herbal tea. Treatments take place in our quirky shepherd’s hut treatment rooms. All our airy spaces, from the Spa Lounge to the outdoor sauna, provide views of rolling hills and blue skies and are designed to connect you with nature. Hungry? Choose your breakfast, lunch or sweet treat and we’ll whip it up in our award-winning Café kitchen and deliver it to you in the Spa Lounge. We can also cater for special occasions – and our onsite Accommodation makes The Middlewick the perfect venue for Spa weekends and retreats.

title: The Sheppey Inn
subtitle: The Sheppey Inn lies out on the beautiful wilds of the Somerset Levels, surrounded by peat moors, dairy farms and national wildlife reserves.
bodyContent: The pub pulls in people from miles around thanks to the brilliant, eclectic musicians it attracts, its fine selection of local ales and ciders (including all kinds of one-offs and speciality brews), and its fantastic food. Spending the afternoon out here in the countryside, lounging by the river, looking out for voles and kingfishers, isn’t the worst idea in the world, is it? There’s been a pub in Godney servicing the thirsty throats of Levels farmworkers for many centuries. The last owners ran it for 120 years, but on one day in 1976, they ran out of cider and lost the trust of the next two generations of locals. the pub has been renovated, revamped and restored, and now has about six casks of grown-ups’ apple juice on the bar to make sure that the such a thing never happens again. Check out the photos on the right for proof.
tagline: The Sheppey Inn lies out on the beautiful wilds of the Somerset Levels.
