title: SWALLOW Charity
subtitle: SWALLOW is a user-led charity supporting over 170 local people with learning disabilities. It provides supported housing, one-to-one outreach in the community, creative day activities, work skills training and paid employment opportunities – including two community cafes, plus a range of social and fitness activities.
bodyContent: SWALLOW is a user-led charity supporting over 170 local people with learning disabilities to live life to the full, in various locations across Bath & North East Somerset and Mendip. The charity provides a range of help and support to enable its members to live fulfilling and rewarding lives. Services include supported housing, one-to-one outreach in the community, creative day activities including craft and horticulture projects, work skills training and paid employment opportunities – particularly in two community cafes where members gain catering and front of house experience, plus a range of social and fitness activities. The two SWALLOW Community Cafes provide healthy, nutritious food at very reasonable prices, all freshly made and prepared. By visiting the cafes customers will be supporting the charity and its members whilst enjoying wonderful hospitality in a warm and welcoming environment.

title: Inflatable Theme Park – Taunton 2026
subtitle: The UK's Biggest Inflatable Theme Park returns to Moorfields, Taunton this July and August. Enjoy giant inflatables, all-day wristbands for just £10, food and refreshments, and fun for children aged 2–14. Free entry for accompanying adults. Open daily from 10am–5pm.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } The Inflatable Theme Park is one of the UK's leading giant inflatable specialists, operating some of the country's biggest and best inflatables and bouncy castles at major shows and events. With over 10 years of experience, we've earned a reputation for providing exciting, high-quality attractions that families return to year after year. Whether you're planning a full family day out or simply looking to keep the children entertained during the school holidays, there's something for everyone to enjoy. With giant inflatables, exciting activities, and plenty of space to play, children can bounce, climb, slide, and enjoy hours of active fun in a safe and welcoming environment. All-Day Wristbands – Just £10 For only £10, children receive an all-day wristband, allowing unlimited use of the inflatable attractions throughout the day. Please note: Bungee trampolines, zorbs, Wipeout, and ride-on cars are charged separately and are not included in the wristband price.
tagline: A giant inflatable theme park packed with bouncing, sliding and family fun.

title: Coates English Willow
subtitle: Discover an enormous range of willow baskets made by our team of skilled craftsmen and women using our own home-grown willow.
bodyContent: Discover authentic Somerset craftsmanship at Coates English Willow's unique Willow Basket shop, home to an enormous range of baskets handmade by skilled craftsmen and women using home-grown willow. From practical everyday designs to decorative treasures, find the perfect gift or souvenir while supporting this traditional industry. Can't find what you need? Our bespoke service creates tailor-made baskets, log baskets and willow hurdles to your exact specifications. Budding basket-makers will find willow, tools and books to get started, plus seasonal living willow kits for garden features. Explore the Basket Museum's rare willow artefacts dating from 1850, watch our film on willow cultivation and Coates Artists' Charcoal production, or enjoy a Willow Walk with three routes, including a popular Sculpture Trail for children with a free prize on completion. Shop online anytime, and prebook tours via our website.
tagline: Discover an enormous range of willow baskets made by our team of skilled craftsmen and women.

subtitle: This talk is part of the autumn programme of the Somerset Industrial Archaeology Society.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Ben Sumpter is a Research Consultant and co-owner of Cornwall Underground Adventures. He has ventured deep into archives and underground workings to research Cornwall's mining heritage, technology and practices, and how these eventually spread throughout the world. This fascinating talk explores Cornwall's rich mining history and the engineering innovations that helped shape mining industries both nationally and internationally. For details about how to take part in this online meeting, please visit: www.sias.me.uk
tagline: This talk is part of the autumn programme of the Somerset Industrial Archaeology Society.

title: Save the Date! Taunton Flower Show Returns This August
subtitle: Get ready for one of Somerset’s most beloved summer traditions!
bodyContent: Tickets now on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre Get ready for one of Somerset’s most beloved summer traditions! The Taunton Flower Show returns to Vivary Park on the first Friday and Saturday of August , bringing two full days of colour, creativity, and family fun. Widely known as the longest-running flower show in the UK – and the second oldest in the world – this iconic event has been delighting visitors since 1831 . Today, it attracts around 16,000 visitors across the weekend, all eager to enjoy the stunning displays, gardens, entertainment, and warm community spirit that the show is famous for. 🌿 What to Expect Whether you’re a gardening enthusiast, a family looking for a great day out, or simply love a vibrant summer event, the Taunton Flower Show has something for everyone: 🌼 Competition Marquee Marvel at the amazing talents of local growers, floral artists, and creative minds from across the community. 🌸 Floral Marquee & Designer Gardens Discover breathtaking displays and horticultural excellence from national exhibitors and designers. 🎶 Music & Arena Entertainment Enjoy live performances and a full programme of arena activities throughout both days. 🛍️ Local & National Traders Browse unique stalls offering plants, gifts, crafts, food, and much more. 👨‍👩‍👧 Family Fun With activities and entertainment for all ages, it’s the perfect outing for the whole family. Please note: Assistance dogs only are allowed into the showground. 🎟️ Buy Your Tickets Early and Save! Pre-show ticket prices are available until 6th August 2026 . Grab yours early to enjoy the best value. Pre-Show Prices Friday: Adult: £20.00 Child (Under 17): FREE with a paying adult (ticket still required) Saturday: Adult: £17.00 Child (Under 17): FREE with a paying adult (ticket still required) 🏷️ Where to Buy ✨ Tickets are now on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre! Pop in to secure your tickets and get ready for a fantastic day out at one of Taunton’s most historic and cherished events.

title: BlueTone Festival 2026 – Tickets On Sale Now at the Taunton Visitor Centre
subtitle: Get ready, Taunton—something spectacular is coming to Vivary Park this May, and we at the Taunton Visitor Centre are thrilled to be your local place to book tickets!
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Get ready, Taunton—something spectacular is coming to Vivary Park this May, and we at the Taunton Visitor Centre are thrilled to be your local place to book tickets! BlueTone Festival 2026 is set to bring four unforgettable days of jazz, blues, funk and soul to the heart of Taunton from Thursday 28th to Sunday 31st May 2026 . title: Quantock Hills
subtitle: The Quantock Hills are an area of wilderness and tranquillity. Panoramic views lead you through coast, heath and combe. Explore and you will find rocky Jurassic coastline, exposed heathland summits, deep wooded combes, undulating farmland and attractive villages all within this protected landscape.
bodyContent: One visit to the Quantock Hills is enough for anyone to realise why in 1956 they were created Britain’s first Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (now called National Landscape) – in terms of landscape quality a ranking just below that of national park. Consisting of hard red sandstone that was formerly quarried for road surfacing they run for 12 miles inland from the Bristol Channel coast at West Quantoxhead before dropping gently down to the Somerset Levels between Taunton and Bridgwater. Their majestic slopes provide a dramatic backdrop to much of the landscape around Taunton but it is the variety of scenery they offer that makes them quite so special, from the high windswept moorland plateau covered with heather and whortleberries – wild blueberries- to the deeply-incised wooded combes, or valleys, plunging down their sides. On a fine day their summit offers breathtaking views from Exmoor to the Malverns, the Brecon Beacons to the Dorset Downs. The Quantock Hills are home to a herd of wild red deer as well as an abundance of other wildlife and are now encircled by a walking trail. The Romantic poets loved the Quantocks. William Wordsworth and his sister, Dorothy, were frequent visitors while Samuel Taylor Coleridge’s cottage home in Nether Stowey is now owned by the National Trust and his residency here is celebrated in the 51-mile Coleridge Way which ends in Porlock, where he was staying when he wrote Kubla Khan in 1797 – the epic was never finished because Coleridge’s flow of verse was interrupted by the arrival of ‘a person from Porlock’. Other notable residents have included Andrew Crosse, an early pioneer of electricity and whose home at Fyne Court, near Broomfield, is now the main visitor centre for the hills.
tagline: The Quantock Hills are an area of wilderness and tranquillity.

title: Hudson Way Open Space
subtitle: Hudson Way is an increasingly popular family park in Taunton with a fun pirate-themed play area as well as a skate park.
bodyContent: The play area contains a large wooden pirate ship with climbing nets, slides, tunnels and bridges, along with trampolines, a zip wire, pod swings, cradle swings, spinning and rocking roundabouts and a large hamster wheel. This open space is in the Staplegrove area of Taunton.

title: The Museum of Somerset
subtitle: The Museum of Somerset is located in the 12th century great hall of Taunton Castle.
bodyContent: Set in the heart of Taunton, The Museum of Somerset lies within the 12th century Taunton Castle and tells the county’s fascinating story from prehistoric times to the present day, using real objects, interactive games, eye-catching film projections and the words and voices of Somerset people, past and present. From an under-floor Plesiosaur, to the largest collection of Roman coins ever discovered in Britain, in a single pot, and a chilling recreation of the infamous Bloody Assizes – The Museum of Somerset is a must-see visitor attraction. It contains objects from across many of the museum’s collections, including geology, archaeology, medieval and ethnography. The museum also houses the Somerset Military Museum. As well as the permanent galleries, the museum offers regularly changing exhibitions and activities such as family drop-in sessions and ‘talk and tea’ with curators or special guests. There is a programme of special events, including evening talks, music and outdoor theatre. The Somerset Military Museum is part of The Museum of Somerset and tells the story of the regiments of Somerset in war and peacetime. It features the history of the regiments of Somerset Light Infantry (Prince Albert’s),Somerset and Cornwall Light Infantry and the West Somerset Yeomanry amongst others. The Museum of Somerset is part of The South West Heritage Trust; a new independent charity committed to protecting and celebrating Somerset and Devon’s rich heritage. The Trust brings together services previously provided by Somerset and Devon County Councils, who remain our main funders. Services include the widely-praised Museum of Somerset, Somerset Rural Life Museum, and state-of-the-art facilities in Taunton and Exeter to care for the extraordinary archive collections of the two counties. We also provide essential advice about the historic environment and manage historic sites including the remarkable Cothelstone Hill in Somerset.
tagline: Discover 400 million years of history

title: Bath & West Showground
subtitle: The Bath & West Showground is a 240 acre venue in the heart of the West of England; home to The Royal Bath & West Show as well as a whole host of events of every description throughout the year!
bodyContent: Nestled in the heart of the West Country, the Bath & West Showground is a unique, versatile venue with a variety of inspiring indoor and outdoor event spaces. Although best known for the annual Royal Bath & West Show, one of the largest multi day agricultural shows in the country, the site has played host to a wide range of public events, exhibitions, conferences together with world class sports, recording artists and record-breaking music festivals. Today with a vision to develop more exciting events and bring back the nostalgia of yesteryear, the site is as busy as ever, hosting events for individuals, regional event management companies and large scale national corporates, promotors and agents. As the largest events and exhibition venue in the South West, the site plays a key part as a landmark in the region, offering a variety of unrivalled indoor pavilion space in varying sizes and configurations, plus ample outside space consisting of grassed areas, a viewing grandstand for 1,200 overlooking a three acre outdoor arena and in excess of three miles of roads and tracks. Spread across the spectacular site of 240 acres, and parking for up to 12,000 across a variety of car park configurations, the Showground features 6 sizeable indoor venues with numerous other meeting, conference & exhibition spaces with a new addition to the site in 2019, the Wessex Pavilion. A multifunctional venue able to cater for up to 850 diners spread over two separate self contained floors of 500 and 350 respectively. This fantastic new facility is now the largest dining venue in the region able to comfortably host corporate and private dinners, balls and award ceremonies. Whether accommodating a head count for just a few delegates or 150,000 visitors, the extremely adaptable environment, with its range of facilities and resources, can be tailored to suit any event. The Events Team are on hand every step of the way to ensure the success of your event however bespoke and whatever the requirements or size.

title: Exmoor National Park
subtitle: One of the most peaceful of all National Parks, Exmoor is renowned for its dramatic coastal views, heather moorland, ancient woodlands, steep combes and Exmoor Ponies. Exmoor National Park is a unique and special place.
bodyContent: The variety of coastal landscape in Somerset is truly remarkable, from rock pavements to sand dunes and from wooded cliffs to mudflats. There are geological and wildlife wonders for the scientifically minded, seaside resorts for those seeking entertainment, fishing and sailing for the sports fans, coasteering for the adventurous and long-distance trails for the energetic. This coast has something for everyone, even the four-legged members of the family as it has numerous dog-friendly beaches. It has all you’d expect from a sea-side: lighthouses, rock pools, fossils, ice cream parlours, piers and even a ship-wreck and then it has more in the form of the rare plants and birds that thrive in this environment. What adds to the fascination of this coast for many is that it has the second highest tidal range in the world which means that you can visit a resort one day when the water is lapping the shore and come back the next when you can hardly see the sea. First time visitors are always surprised at the undisturbed tranquillity of its heather-clad moorlands, not to mention its breath-taking coastline of plunging cliffs and sheltered bays. Exmoor National Park is rich in hidden haunts, deep valleys, ancient oak woodland, England's highest sea-cliffs, sparkling rivers and waterfalls. Its land and seascapes are dotted with medieval towns and villages , harbours and resorts full of character and timeless charm. Accounting for a quarter of the national park, there are 18,300 hectares of land lying between 305 metres and 509 metres. To best experience this landscape of big sky and even bigger views, take the B3223 across the moors, which also provides numerous places to stop, explore and take in the magnificence. Appropriately, this road starts in Dulverton, which houses the headquarters of Exmoor National Park. As you travel across the moors, chances are you’ll see the Exmoor ponies that make their home in the area. Stocky and hardy by nature, fossils of the breed dating back to 50,000 BC have been found in the region and Roman carvings show them being used as transport. The Domesday Book records their presence but by the late 1800s the breed had almost become extinct due to the vagaries of human intervention. They have now returned to the moors but are still classified as an endangered species.

title: Childrens Theatre Art Workshops supported by the 'Princess Theatre' - Burnham on Sea
subtitle: 3 online children’s workshops where you will explore ways to bring plays and ideas to life using scenery, lighting and… your imagination!
bodyContent: Mon 14th Dec 2020 - Mon 15th Mar 2021 For children and families 3 online children’s workshops where you will explore ways to bring plays and ideas to life using scenery, lighting and… your imagination! Episode 1: ABC Drawing Join our artist, Catherine for an introduction to the theatre arts. The ABC drawing workshop is designed to build your confidence and give you some simple techniques to draw your own imaginative design. Using letter forms as the basis for your drawing, Catherine will guide you in creating an exciting piece of work. You will need: a piece of paper and a drawing pencil. Episode 2: Setting the Scene The second in our series of online workshops. Moving on from the ABC Drawing sketch, Catherine will guide you in creating your own 3D model for the stage! You will need: a couple of pieces of paper, easy cut card (a cereal box will do), scissors, a glue stick and some sticky tape. Episode 3: Shadow Box Theatre Our final workshop explores theatre design using lighting. With Catherine, you will create a simple shadow box to help you tell your stories and even create a play. You will need: some tracing paper, ruler, a drawing pencil, easy cut card (a cereal box will do), craft glue and some sticky tape. Why not show us your work on our facebook page or email us on info@theprincesstheatre.co.uk we would love to see them.

title: 2 Crescent Gardens
subtitle: 2 Crescent Gardens is a stylish guest house, which is close to the world famous Royal Crescent and within walking distance of all Bath’s main attractions.
bodyContent: 2 Crescent Gardens is a stylish guest house, which is close to the world famous Royal Crescent and within walking distance of all Bath’s main attractions. We reopened in June 2012 after a major refurbishment programme and we think you will be impressed by the results. Our individually-styled rooms are relaxing and comfortable and the perfect place to unwind. All our rooms are ensuite and we serve a delicious breakfast to start your day. Guests can reserve a parking space, in advance, for a small fee. We are also a short walk or taxi ride from Bath Spa train station
tagline: 2 Crescent Gardens is a stylish guest house, which is close to the world famous Royal Crescent

title: 18 The Circus
subtitle: Self-Catering - 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character.
bodyContent: 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character. The maisonette that occupies the top two floors of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the northern Lansdown slopes of stunning terraces of Georgian houses, and with the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minute’s walk. Access is via a communal hallway and carpeted staircase that leads to the maisonette’s front door on the second floor. Inside is a small hall, off which sits the spacious and airy sitting room that is tastefully and comfortably furnished and decorated and being south facing, is very light. On this floor is also a large fitted kitchen with dining table and chairs. A mezzanine room houses the washing machine and dryer for exclusive use of visitors to this home. The stairs on this floor lead to a well-lit landing, off which lie the bedrooms. The front bedroom is a very large room with a double bed and conveniently, a single bed for family use. This brightly furnished bedroom also has an en-suite shower room. The second bedroom has twin beds and is next door to a family sized bathroom with bath, shower-in-bath, basin, WC and airing cupboard. The property contains gas central heating, gas hob, gas double oven, fridge, dishwasher, washing machine and dryer, microwave, TV in lounge and master bedroom, video, stereo, towels and toiletries. Free Car Parking Permit available Free Unlimited fiber broadband Please note: the house is a listed 4 story Georgian townhouse and as such does not have an elevator. Find out more here.
tagline: Self-Catering - 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character.

title: Great Western Railway
subtitle: Great Western Railway (GWR) links Somerset with London Paddington by mainline train services. We also offer direct and easy connections to London Heathrow Airport via the Reading – Heathrow ‘Rail-Air’ coach link or via Heathrow Express train services at Paddington.
bodyContent: GWR services call at the following principle towns and cities in the county: Bath, Bridgwater, Castle Cary, Taunton, Weston-super-Mare and Yeovil and link the county directly to Devon & Cornwall, Bristol & South Wales, the South Coast and the Cotswolds as well as the Capital. As a Great Western Railway ticket holder you can also take advantage of a wide range of value added offers with Somerset attractions. Visit www.daysoutguide.co.uk to see what’s available in Somerset. You can also save up to 10% on car and van hire with Europcar when you travel with GWR. Europcar services are available at Bath Spa and Taunton stations, among others on the network. Book your train tickets now at GWR.com
tagline: Great Western Railway (GWR) links Somerset with London Paddington by mainline train services.

title: The Somerset Donkey
subtitle: The Somerset Cider Brandy Company & Burrow Hill Cider have introduced a range of gorgeous cocktails using their products that you can e-create in your own homes.
bodyContent: Fill a tall glass with ice. Pour in 60ml Somerset Cider Brandy and top up with ginger ale. Add a dash of Angostura bitters and stir. Garnish with a twist of lemon. For more information and even more delicious cocktail recipes visit https://www.somersetciderbrandy.com/cocktails

title: Bath & West Showground
subtitle: Nestled in the heart of the West Country, the Bath & West Showground is the perfect place to entertain the whole family. Thirty Minutes from the city of Wells and 10 minutes from the main line train from London to Castle Carey. You are also 45 minutes from Frome and another train station and further strong amenities. The Show Ground doesn't have a hotel, however ample space for camping and parking of large amounts of resource applications.
bodyContent: Although best known for the annual Royal Bath & West Show, one of the largest multi-day agricultural shows in the country, the Bath & West Showground plays host to a wide range of public events, exhibitions, conferences together with world class sports, recording artists and record-breaking music festivals throughout the year. From crafting to camping, markets to music festivals or collectors’ fairs to comedy nights, there really is an experience to entertain everyone at the Bath & West Showground. The Showground has ample car parking, as well as an onsite bar & restaurant, allowing you to refuel on delicious coffee & cake, or enjoy a tasty locally sourced lunch, before you continue with the rest of your day. Visit our website to see What’s On at the Bath & West Showground. Are you already a regular visitor to the Showground? Or you live locally? Why not become a Member at the Bath & West. You’ll receive FREE entry to the Royal Bath & West Show, along with discount to other events held on the Bath & West Showground. Click HERE for more information. Please note: Bar & Restaurant opening times vary for each event. Please check before attending
tagline: The Bath & West Show Ground is the perfect place to entertain the whole family.

title: Somerset Craft Distillery Ltd
subtitle: Our award winning Spirit of Glastonbury ® hand crafted small batch dry gin is the very essence of Somerset. Distilled using water drawn from deep beneath the mystical Glastonbury Tor and containing nine botanicals including apples from Somersets traditional orchards, each bottle is wax sealed and handwritten with its own batch number. Conceived, developed, distilled and bottled in Somerset. Voted– Best Classic Gin in England at the World Gin Awards 2022.
bodyContent: Here at Somerset Craft Distillery we believe in quality. Our award winning gin is distilled in our own copper still named Guinevere . We use nine carefully chosen botanicals including juniper berries grown on English farms and apples from Somersets traditional orchards along with cinnamon, liquorice, orris. correander, angelica, almonds and lemon. Distilled using water drawn from deep beneath the 158m high Glastonbury Tor to an alcoholic strength of 42%. Tasting Notes: ‘On the nose - unmissable Juniper – but with Spirit of Glastonbury ® the distillers have turned up the volume – you know its gin before the first sip. The mouthfeel is very smooth and confident’ ( Hand Crafted Drinks Magazine); ‘ Rich sweet caramel and toffee on the nose. Some notes of vanilla. Dense and round and a little different while still retaining its classic character’ (World Gin Awards 2022). Tell us what you think? Navy Strength. Navy Strength gin is traditionally stronger and at 57% ABV our Navy Strength Spirit of Glastonbury ® certainly fits the bill. The higher ABV really allows those botanicals to shine through. Try it as a sipping gin – or with your favourite tonic. Silver Medal winner at the 2022 London Spirits Competition.
tagline: Our award winning Spirit of Glastonbury ® hand crafted

title: Taunton School
subtitle: Taunton School is a co-educational independent school serving pupils aged 13 to 18. The campus also includes Taunton School International and Taunton School International Middle School for overseas students; Taunton Preparatory School (aged 7 to 13); Taunton Pre-Prep School (aged 4 to 7); and Taunton Nursery (aged 0 to 4).
bodyContent: Set in a beautiful 56-acre site, Taunton School is a lively community, which aims to challenge, nurture and inspire young people to succeed in a global community. Taunton School consists of a caring Nursery and Pre-Preparatory School, inspiring Preparatory School and an innovative Senior School and International School. The campus includes a brand new £3.6 million Dining Hall, extensive sports fields, two swimming pools, specific music, art and D&T departments and a 19 th century Grade II listed Chapel. A new sixth form centre and library will be completed this year and plans are underway for a £20million state-of-the-art international school and enhanced sports facilities. The school offers a supportive boarding environment for children from 7 to 18 years. With close friends at hand, boarders have the opportunity to develop life skills within a relaxed but controlled atmosphere. As a non-selective school, Taunton School has achieved consistently excellent GCSE results and some of the most exceptional A-level and International Baccalaureate results in South West England. Approximately 96% of all sixth form leavers take up university or college places and approximately three or four students are accepted into Oxbridge each year. Taunton School is one of the only schools in the UK to offer four unique Sixth Form pathways: the popular IB Diploma, A-levels, Level 3 BTEC Diploma in Business and in Sport & Exercise Science, as well as Pre-foundation and Foundation courses in Business.

title: Wookey Hole Caves & Attractions
subtitle: Wookey Hole Caves is a magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for all ages. It’s an experience millions of years in the making with plenty to do inside and out. Enjoy vintage penny arcades, museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, and of course the famous, beautiful caves.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Wookey Hole Caves and attractions lies In the heart of Somerset. A magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for the young and young at heart. When you visit Wookey Hole, you’ll enjoy an experience millions of years in the making. There is plenty to do inside and out, from vintage penny arcades to museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, to name but a few of the attractions. Not forgetting the breathtakingly beautiful caves, for which Wookey Hole is renowned. Your visit will take you through 8 chambers. Each with a unique beauty and story. You’ll also pass our cheese tunnel, home to the delicious Wookey Hole cheese. The cheese is not the only resident of the caves. Over the years, Wookey Hole has been home to giant hyenas, bears, Neanderthals, and many local people. It has even been a site of pagan and Roman worship. You’ll find Wookey Hole holds a surprise around every corner. You might even get to meet our most famous resident, the Witch of Wookey Hole. We have found she most likes to visit during school holidays! The world-famous Wookey Hole Circus School performs at Wookey Hole at weekends and in School Holidays. Every year over 250,000 people visit Wookey Hole and take-home cherished memories of a great day out. Whether it is your first time or your fiftieth, there is always something new to discover. We can’t wait to welcome you.
tagline: At Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions, Somerset, there’s always fun and adventure to be had.

title: Weston Museum in Weston super Mare
subtitle: Weston Musuem in Weston super Mare has something for everyone. We want to open the museum to as many people as possible, so we’re constantly putting on events for all ages and interests. Head to the museum website to find out what is coming up soon.
bodyContent: “Once you know your history you understand more of who you are, you learn from the past and find ways to predict the future and even help create a better one.” Housed in a beautiful and distinctive historic building. We tell the story of the town and the surrounding area from prehistoric times to the present day. The museum is dedicated to being a social and educational hub for the people of Weston and its visitors. You can come to learn, relax or just have fun! The North Somerset Council museum collection contains around 50,000 individual objects. The newly refurbished museum also allows our guests to grab lunch at the cosy Clara’s Café, hire a space for a meeting or even a party in the courtyard. Museum’s do not have to be dull and dusty, in fact, Weston Museum encourages a hands-on approach to history. We also work closely with local schools and community groups to help support the Weston of today and grow the Weston of tomorrow. Our diverse volunteering programme also gives you the chance to get involved. Diversity is key! Our William Mable Gallery allows us, for the first time, to host exhibitions suitable for the world stage. We’ve already been able to display items from the Imperial War Museum and The British Museum. The content of this gallery changes throughout the year, so there is always something new at Weston Museum. Weston Museum is working towards being as accessible as possible. There is a lift for wheelchair users and those who cannot manage stairs to access the main upper floor galleries. Due to the nature of Clara’s Cottage being built in 1865, this part of the museum is unfortunately not completely accessible to wheelchair users due to narrow corridors and a staircase. Weston Museum’s free admission means that the museum is truly for everyone and is quickly becoming a popular destination among tourists as one of Weston's top attractions. Facilities Wheelchair Friendly, Café, Gift Shop, Baby Change Facilities, Accessible Lift, Parking Nearby, Disabled Toilet Available, Toilets Available
tagline: There is something for everyone here at Weston Museum.

title: SPICY SPANISH TOFFEE APPLE CHICKEN & RICE
subtitle: Spicy, sweet, smoky, and packed full of flavour. This recipe is perfect for the end of summer and the beauty of this one is the adaptability – the chicken can be finished on the BBQ, or it can be cooked in advance and served cold as a side dish, or served more like a one-pot wonder Paella when those evenings start to creep in. This homemade recipe is easy to make and best served with an ice-cold bottle of Brothers Toffee Apple cider.
bodyContent: METHOD • In a small bowl mix together all ingredients for the Spanish seasoning mix. • Place chicken thighs in a large bowl and drizzle with 2 tablespoons of oil. • Tip the seasonal mix onto the chicken and mix to coat well. • Add the remaining tablespoon of oil to a large skillet and bring to medium heat. • Cook chicken for 3 minutes on each side until browned. Transfer to a plate. (It won’t be cooked through at this point). • Add rice, chicken stock, the juice from 1/2 of the lemon, Toffee Apple cider and stir. • Return chicken to the pan on top of the rice. Cover and cook for 20-25 minutes until liquid is absorbed, rice is tender, and chicken is cooked through. • Garnish with lemon slices and freshly chopped parsley and serve immediately. Head over to the Brothers Cider Website for the ingredients, measurements and more! https://brotherscider.co.uk/blogs/recipes/spicy-spanish-toffee-apple-chicken-rice
tagline: Spicy, sweet, smoky, and packed full of flavour.

title: Fussels Fine Food
subtitle: Fussels Fine Food Company, family Somerset farmers since 2005
bodyContent: Produce quality cold-pressed extra virgin rapeseed oil—a fresh West Country alternative to olive oil, rich in Omega 3, vitamin E and monounsaturated fats. Tim & Andy oversee farming to bottling, plus mayonnaise, dressings, flavoured oils, vinaigrettes and gift boxes.
tagline: Producing oil from rapeseed has grown dramatically in popularity over the last few years

title: Bath Abbey
subtitle: Living and Telling the Good News of Jesus with the City of Bath and its Visitors
bodyContent: A moment of stillness in the beating heart of a vibrant city. A space that’s alive with music and prayer, art and history. A place where awe-inspiring architecture lifts the eyes – and raises the spirit. Bath Abbey is many things to many people. Whether you come here to join a service or a tour , light a candle or listen to our choirs , what unites us all is a sense of wonder. There is so much to discover – please step inside…

title: Ring the Syren Bells from Bishop's Palace Wells to Glastonbury Tor
subtitle: Welcome to your Syrens pilgrimage, a musical tour across ancient Somerset lands.
bodyContent: Follow this pebble-carrying pilgrimage along National Cycle Route 3, ringing eight Syren bells whose notes form a tune. Starting at Wells’ Bishop’s Palace moat, the route winds through Silver Street, East Somerset Way and quiet lanes, revealing glimpses of Wells Cathedral and Glastonbury Tor. Continue along tranquil Long Drove, flanked by swan-graced rhynes, before finishing near Old Wells Road—sharing paths with cyclists throughout this scenic Somerset walk.

title: The Slow Farming Company
subtitle: The Slow Farming Company is a Somerset family farm spanning four generation
bodyContent: The Slow Farming Company is a Somerset family farm spanning four generations, led by Rob, a regenerative farming pioneer. They produce pasture-reared beef and free-range eggs, nutritious and low-cholesterol, sold alongside curated homewares via their new e-commerce site.
tagline: The concept of slow farming and slow food are, at their core.

title: The Bath Cider House
subtitle: An iconic new late night bar with an array of classic keg ciders, farmhouse boxed ciders and our own weird and wonderful on site fermentations. Head over for quizzes, comedy nights, comedy nights and some excellent background beats followed by late night sets and monster pizzas.
bodyContent: BOOK BATH CIDER HOUSE Holding groups of up to 260 people, our unique venue provides the perfect location for events, parties and business meetings. Available for whole venue hire, we can make our space what you need it to be. Whether it's a gathering for 20 or 260. With cider tastings and tank tours of our still available, your event can be made into an interesting and distinctive experience. Make an enquiry to find out more. BOOK NOW HOW WE MAKE OUR CIDERS We collaborate with some expert scrumpers in Somerset who have plenty of room to hold tonnes of apples and to slowly age our cider for an 8-month period, allowing for the deeper complexities to develop. We then bring our cider to our in-house tanks where we blend and ferment different varieties with the best quality natural ingredients, from fruit purees to fresh juices. FIND OUT MORE
tagline: An iconic new late night bar with an array of classic keg ciders

title: World Horse Welfare Glenda Spooner Farm
subtitle: Glenda Spooner Farm is a rescue and rehabilitation centre, caring for up to 80 horses and ponies at once. Located in 220 acres of unspoilt countryside, there farm walks, behind-the-scenes tours, a coffee shop, outdoor playground and picnic area, second-hand tack shop and regular equine and canine events.
bodyContent: Glenda Spooner Farm, a rescue and rehabilitation centre, is home to around 80 horses and ponies at a time. You can meet some of the equines in our care in the undercover stableyard and take a stroll round the paddocks. The lake and hill walks are home to a diverse range of wildlife and provide stunning views of the surrounding countryside. There are guided farm tours every Wednesday if you want to see behind-the-scenes and learn more about our rehabilitation work. Relax in the coffee shop, which serves hot drinks, cakes and lunches and overlooks our fabulous indoor arena, which is busy with equine and canine activities. The indoor arena and conference room are available for hire and there is free public WiFi and ample parking available. During ths school holidays we run lots of activites and host other events throughout the year so its a good idea to follow our Facebook page, which also features stories about our horses and ponies and updates about the whole charity.

title: Snowsports at Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Experience Mendip Activity Centre's floodlit 165-meter snowsport slope nestled in ancient woodland, offering year-round thrills for all skill levels. Perfect for both beginners and experienced snowsport fanatics. Learn to ski or snowboard where legends like skier Dave Ryding and snowboarder Jenny Jones began.
bodyContent: Mendip Activity Centre offer Skiing and Snowboarding sessions on their 165-metre dry slope. It’s the only slope of its kind in Somerset and the perfect place to learn or practise, with views over the hills and the thrill of the mountains without leaving the West Country. Whether you're a total beginner or brushing up before a trip, their friendly instructors have you covered. Lessons run all year for children and adults. You can also book private lessons or ski or snowboard by yourself (as long as you are at the right recreational standard). Your adventure awaits!

title: Clifton Suspension Bridge Trust
subtitle: Clifton Suspension Bridge Visitor Centre tells the story of the 'ornament of Bristol' and the people who built, maintain and treasure it. Explore the turbulent history of the ‘first love’ of famous British engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel through an award winning exhibition packed with family activities and staffed by knowledgeable volunteers.
bodyContent: Visitor Centre Clifton Suspension Bridge Visitor Centre tells the story of the 'ornament of Bristol' and the people who built, maintain and treasure it. Explore the turbulent history of the ‘first love’ of famous British engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel through an award winning exhibition packed with family activities and staffed by knowledgeable volunteers. The Visitor Centre is open between Friday and Monday throughout the winter and may be found in Leigh Woods on the North Somerset side of the bridge, a short walk from Clifton Village where you’ll find bus stops, pay and display parking, boutique shopping, cafes and coffee shops. Under the current Covid-19 guidance, pre-booking of tickets is strongly recommended. ( www.cliftonbridge.org.uk/visitor-centre ) Bridge Once the far-fetched dream of local wine merchant William Vick, the bridge was the first solo project of the famous British engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel who came up with ambitious plans to build the highest and longest bridge in the world. Sadly, Brunel did not live to see his ‘first love’ completed. The bridge took 33 years to build and opened as a monument to his achievements after his death. The Bridge is open 24 hours a day 7 days a week, 365 days a year and can be crossed on foot or by bicycle free of charge, although vehicles must pay a £1 toll towards the maintenance and upkeep of this Grade I listed structure. Groups may book private tours at any time, with a coach drop-off point available on Observatory Road, BS8 4AW (there is a weight limit of 4 tons so coaches may not cross the bridge). A programme of events runs throughout the year for families and adult learners. The bridge spans the spectacular Avon Gorge and is illuminated each evening, lighting up half an hour before sunset. Photographers may like to visit the viewpoints on Sion Hill or at the Cumberland Basin.
tagline: The Bridge is open 24 hours a day 7 days a week, 365 days.

title: Somerset Art Works
subtitle: For those who love to discover new creative happenings on their doorstep, the Somerset Art Weeks Festival is the perfect opportunity to get out and explore the local art scene. Over 100 exhibitions and events, including family-friendly workshops, are taking place across Somerset from 21st September to the 6th October
bodyContent: Each year in Autumn, the much-loved Somerset Art Weeks event comes along to brighten our county. It has been run every year since 1994 by local charity Somerset Art Works, and has become a treasured part of the Somerset calendar. This year sees the return of the SAW Festival, where collaborative exhibitions and group shows spring up across the region, in this celebration of our county’s exciting creative voices. From the 21st September to the 6th October the instantly recognisable yellow road signs of Somerset Art Weeks will appear in every corner of the county, signalling people towards an exhibition or show to discover. The chosen theme this year is Landscape: Flux and Flow. Exhibiting artists will be responding to this theme in a number of different ways within their work. SAW has also provided vital opportunities and support to artists and makers to produce work on this theme during the Festival. This year’s SAW-sponsored projects include everything from immersive installations within the landscape to creative collaborations with a scientific laboratory. You can find out details of how to visit the event this year by going to the SAW website or downloading the official Somerset Art Weeks 2024 App, or pick up a guide from your local library, cultural organisation or tourist information centre for full information about all 100 venues. This year SAW is welcoming a new headline sponsor, Albert Goodman, whose contribution will allow the arts to reach more people, and help the organisation continue to thrive.

title: Farleigh Hungerford Castle
subtitle: Discover the hidden treasures and sinister past of Farleigh Hungerford Castle, near Bath.
bodyContent: Over the course of its 700-year history Farliehg Hungerford Castle has witnessed immense wealth, scandal, murder, imprisonment, debt and, finally, ruin. The remains of Farleigh Hungerford Castle stand in the beautiful valley of the river Frome. Started in the 14th century, the fortified mansion still has much for visitors to enjoy – providing a great day out for families, couples, and walkers enjoying the surrounding countryside. The castle was occupied for 300 years by the remarkable Hungerford family and today their intriguing, yet sometimes gruesome stories are told through graphic panels and a free audio tour. There are many hidden treasures – the chapel with rare medieval wall paintings and family tombs, extensive displays in the Priest’s house, and for those who are brave enough to enter the crypt, there’s the best collection of human-shaped lead coffins in Britain. "It's a perfect Sunday afternoon trip out for the family. It's a great place to sit and have a picnic on the grass, take in the atmosphere and the lovely views across the valley." Julie Smith, Visitor

title: Kilver Court and Gardens
subtitle: Kilver Court & Gardens in Somerset combines stunning historic architecture with luxury shopping outlets.
bodyContent: • For the curious. For the creative. For the cultivator. • Set behind a Victorian viaduct in Shepton Mallet, Kilver Court & Gardens is steeped in history and design. Known for its expansive gardens and rich heritage, it has recently undergone a transformation, unveiling its renewed charm. Originally established in the 19th century as part of a model factory, the gardens were later revitalized by Herbert Showering of Babycham and Chelsea Flower Show designer George Whitelegg. In the 1990s, Roger Saul, founder of Mulberry, transformed Kilver into the brand's headquarters, restoring the gardens and opening them to the public. Under the current stewardship of the Showering family, Kilver Court & Gardens has embraced a fresh identity, balancing its storied past with contemporary creativity. Alongside the gardens, it houses a curated selection of brands such as Mulberry, TOAST and Makers & Merchants, complemented by a café featuring seasonal dishes crafted from the site’s own organic garden produce. The venue hosts events and collaborations throughout the year. Discover Kilver Court & Gardens, where every visit promises moments of exploration and unexpected inspiration.

title: Waterhouse Guest House
subtitle: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath so once you have shopped till you are about to drop or taken the time to wonder along the local walking routes we have the perfect location set into the Midford Valley with country surroundings which ensures you will not be disturbed by the city noise or pace
bodyContent: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath so once you have shopped till you are about to drop or taken the time to wonder along the local walking routes we have the perfect location set into the Midford Valley with country surroundings which ensures you will not be disturbed by the city noise or pace. We have our own carpark, lift access, Bar, restaurant, conservatory, outside terrace and gardens place making Waterhouse a great place to work, rest, eat and play! We serve a selection of drinks which include local Beers, Ales, carefully selected wines and spirits to relax and unwind while taking in the stunning views across the Midford Valley. Our tranquil surroundings include the Midford Brook at the bottom of the property where we have fishing rights which people can use for a nominal fee, please enquire at reception should you like to make use of this exclusive facility. Across the Midford Valley there are stunning views and a selection of walks one of which is the two tunnels route which is one of the longest pedestrian tunnels in the UK. Other walks include the Kennet & Avon Canal. We are founded on Christian Values and aim to display the Love of Jesus to all who visit, please view the History of Waterhouse. Waterhouse is a 13 bedroom country house located in the idyllic and peaceful Midford valley 15 minutes south of Bath. Built around 1632, the house has been restored to provide bed and breakfast accommodation, meeting rooms and a venue for small events. All our bedrooms are located in the modern wing of the original house. We offer a choice of 8 double bedrooms, 1 twin room and 4 deluxe rooms, all en-suite.
tagline: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath

title: At the Manor
subtitle: Manor Farm House self catering accommodation is spacious, comfortable and tastefully decorated and can accommodate large groups of 10-15 guests.
bodyContent: We are a 15 minute drive from the beautiful city of Bath and a perfect location for family celebrations, birthdays and anniversaries, wedding groups, girlie gatherings and business meetings. The country house has a calming, relaxing atmosphere. We also provide bed and breakfast accommodation. This gorgeous country Manor near Bath in the heart of Somerset was once a Grange and run by Monks from a nearby monastery in Tudor times. We are tucked away down a quiet country lane in the heart of the conservation village of Norton St Philip. The central village location allows our guests a leisurely stroll to the local pubs including the famous George Inn. Discover stunning countryside walks and a meander around the historic conservation village of Norton St Philip. There are many cycle routes in this area too including the renovated old train tunnel into Bath. We are also close to Bradford on Avon for canal walks, boating and cycling, Wells – the film Hot Fuzz was filmed here, Longleat Safari Park, Glastonbury – climb the ancient Tor, Stonehenge, Frome – the best market ever is held the first Sunday of each month and Salisbury.
tagline: Manor Farm House self catering accommodation is spacious, comfortable and tastefully decorated

subtitle: Luxury 4 bedroom Georgian town house along a medieval cobbled street in the historic heart of Bath.
bodyContent: Located just a short stroll from Bath Abbey and the Roman Baths and a two to three minute walk from the Bath Spa railway station, Abbey Mews provides the perfect self-catering accommodation for your special stay in Bath. Newly available for exclusive use holiday rental after extensive renovations, Abbey Mews combines Georgian elegance with modern luxury. Ideal for families, friends and small groups, 6 Pierrepont Place sleeps from 8 to 10 persons and promises you privacy, exclusivity and independence during your stay in this World Heritage City.

title: The Bird
subtitle: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to. A place to work and meet and by day and discover ever-changing bar experiences by night.
bodyContent: To be found just a few minutes’ stroll from Bath’s spectacular city-centre attractions, The Bird in Bath (previously The County Hotel) has re-branded to fit in with its distinctive new personality as part of the Kaleidoscope Collection. Owned by seasoned hoteliers, Ian and Christa Taylor, The Bird is a name that better reflects the vibrant transformation of the hotel, which has already seen refreshed public spaces, additional bedrooms, a new bar, relaxed restaurant and meeting spaces, as well as a much-loved pop-up beach bar for summer. Now with 27 en-suite bedrooms featuring every home comfort, many have far-reaching views across the cricket and rugby grounds to Bath Abbey, with the rolling hills of Bath and beyond. Breakfast is served in a lovely bright dining room, which overlooks Bath Abbey and opens into the conservatory, where morning coffee and afternoon tea can be enjoyed, while the Taylors have also created a wonderfully eclectic neighbourhood bar with relaxed food offering, designed as social hub for work or play. A space for freelancers to work, friends to meet for coffee or a relaxed dinner, there’s a bar for seasonal drinks and various seating areas centred around vast contemporary pieces of art. A separate meeting room also provides a creative space for workshops and get-togethers, private parties, celebrations and more. Visitors and locals alike won’t have to wait long for the next seasonal pop-up, a visually exciting Winter Wonderland for the festive season, and arguably the coolest party space in town. Set in a fantastical venue full of surprises, woodland branches and spruces will be strewn with fairy lights, tables topped with flickering candelabra and chairs draped in Bavarian rugs to keep you cosy. Everyone is welcome to simply drop in to experience the magical vibe. The Bird is easily reached via all main approaches to Bath, and has plenty of parking for guests.
tagline: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to

The same luxurious comfort as our other apartment, 4 St George’s House .

title: Komedia Bath
subtitle: Hosting over 400 events per year in a beautifully restored former Edwardian cinema, Komedia is a go-to destination for a great night out in the city of Bath. Take your pick from Saturday night stand-up, top gigs and tours, quirky cabaret shows, late night revelry and so much at the award-winning venue.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Komedia Bath was established in 2008 and community-owned since 2019, Komedia prides itself on offering something for everybody and operates two distinct performance spaces to do this. At the heart of it all is the Main Auditorium. With high ceilings, baroque grandeur and room for 600+ people, it’s a stunning setting for full-scale live performances and also functions as Bath’s only above-ground night club venue. The Main Auditorium is also home to the award-winning Komedia Comedy Club. The legendary Comedy Club features some of the best acts from the UK and international stand-up circuit every Saturday night. Each show features three world-class comedians and a top-notch compere. For the ultimate Saturday night out, add entry to The Big Disco after the comedy for just £2! Alongside this, Komedia is also very proud to run The Electric Bar – an intimate live performance space that was purpose-built to support grassroots-level music and rising comedy talent. The venue's Box Office is also situated within The Electric Bar, open Tuesday - Saturday from 10am - 5pm. Drop by to find out what’s on, take a quick tour of the venue or pick up a programme. Komedia is committed to being accessible to everyone and is continuously working to improve the experience of its disabled audiences, artists, and team members. For information on accessibility at Komedia, please visit: https://komediabath.co.uk/plan-your-visit/accessibility/
tagline: Hosting over 400 events per year in a beautifully restored former Edwardian cinema

title: Somerset Chocolate
subtitle: Somerset Chocolate Co. is an award-winning artisan chocolatier founded in 2018 by Kellie Mewett.
bodyContent: Founded in 2018 by Kellie Mewett, Somerset Chocolate Co. began as a kitchen-based venture in Bridgwater, Somerset. The company specializes in handcrafted artisan chocolates, focusing on quality and traditional techniques. Now based in Stoke St Gregory, they continue to produce a range of delicious handmade chocolates.

title: Foot Trails
subtitle: • Foot Trails authentic walking holidays celebrate the beauty & culture of South West England, including Somerset, Bath & the Avon Valley. Our mission is to give our guests a sense of exploration and wellbeing that comes from time spent in nature, walking the landscape and staying in characterful rural villages.
bodyContent: Foot Trails curates a collection of authentic walking holidays that celebrate the beauty & culture of rural South West England (Somerset, Wiltshire, Dorset & the Cotswolds). Founded by Alison & David Howell in 2002, our mission is to give our guests a sense of exploration, discovery and wellbeing that comes from walking the English landscape and time spent in nature together with stays in characterful country inns and hotels. At Foot Trails, our dedicated team offers a personalised and tailored service, delivering trips of a lifetime that draw on our founders’ local knowledge and passion for creating unique experiences and showcasing rural South West England. We are committed to responsible travel, ensuring our countryside and environment remains sustainable now and for future generations. Walking is our passion, the thing we most wish to share with our guests. For us it is the perfect way to travel, slowing down and seeing the world at 2 miles an hour. It’s an indulgence, both relaxing and invigorating, it awakens the senses. Every Foot Trails walk is researched, walked, and written by the founders Alison & David Howell. Based on our local knowledge, we take our guests off the well-trodden national trails and on to the local footpaths. This gives our guests a unique experience, authentic to the area they are experiencing, where they can meet local people and enjoy the culture of rural England.

title: Ashridge Nurseries
subtitle: The best and cheapest way to transplant woody plants is bareroot in Winter, as long as you get them delivered by a nursery like Ashridge with a modern cold store (basically a fridge the size of a warehouse) so they arrive fresh as the day they were dug up. Outside the Winter bareroot planting season, Ashridge delivers a select range of the most popular woody plants in pots, as well as flower bulbs, dahlia tubers, and seedling plugs of summer annuals like sweet peas in their respective seasons.
bodyContent: The best and cheapest way to transplant woody plants is bareroot in Winter, so they have no soil on their roots, making them lightweight and easy to work with, especially in bulk. As long as your bareroot trees, hedging, or roses are delivered by a nursery like Ashridge with a modern cold store, which is basically a damp fridge the size of a warehouse, they will arrive fresh as the day they were dug up. Outside the Winter bareroot planting season, Ashridge delivers a select range of the most popular woody plants in pots, including a great range of lavender varieties, climbing plants, as well as flower bulbs, dahlia tubers, and seedling plugs of summer annuals like sweet peas in their respective seasons. In 2025, they earned the Feefo Platinum Trusted Service Award for the 3rd year in a row, and their customer service manager Dan received 4 marriage proposals. Because bareroot plants are only delivered in Winter, but most people are out in their gardens planning new wonders in Summer, it's common to order them months in advance of their planting date. Unlike most retail plant nurseries, Ashridge lets you book your plants online whenever it's convenient, and only charges you shortly before the delivery date.

title: Wookey Hole Caves & Attractions
subtitle: Wookey Hole Caves is a magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for all ages. It’s an experience millions of years in the making with plenty to do inside and out. Enjoy vintage penny arcades, museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, and of course the famous, beautiful caves.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Wookey Hole Caves and attractions lies In the heart of Somerset. A magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for the young and young at heart. When you visit Wookey Hole, you’ll enjoy an experience millions of years in the making. There is plenty to do inside and out, from vintage penny arcades to museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, to name but a few of the attractions. Not forgetting the breathtakingly beautiful caves, for which Wookey Hole is renowned. Your visit will take you through 8 chambers. Each with a unique beauty and story. You’ll also pass our cheese tunnel, home to the delicious Wookey Hole cheese. The cheese is not the only resident of the caves. Over the years, Wookey Hole has been home to giant hyenas, bears, Neanderthals, and many local people. It has even been a site of pagan and Roman worship. You’ll find Wookey Hole holds a surprise around every corner. You might even get to meet our most famous resident, the Witch of Wookey Hole. We have found she most likes to visit during school holidays! The world-famous Wookey Hole Circus School performs at Wookey Hole at weekends and in School Holidays. Every year over 250,000 people visit Wookey Hole and take-home cherished memories of a great day out. Whether it is your first time or your fiftieth, there is always something new to discover. We can’t wait to welcome you.
tagline: At Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions, Somerset, there’s always fun and adventure to be had.

title: The Paragon Townhouse
subtitle: The Paragon is a wondrously quirky Georgian Townhouse located in the bustling heart of historic Bath.
bodyContent: Arching over the ancient steps that lead from Roman Road down to Bath’s Artisan Quarter and Walcot Street, this listed building has been described as “like a Landmark Trust house but more beautiful.” Packed full of original features the house sleeps 8 in four double bedrooms and is spread over a total of 6 floors. Up to 2 extras sleep in comfortable day beds in the larger rooms. Awarded a special Gold by VisitBritain for 2018 / 19 and with the kitchen in the original vaults below street level you could not find a more original or characterful property for your special stay in Bath.
tagline: The Paragon is a wondrously quirky Georgian Townhouse

title: Frisbee Golf at Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: One of the UK’s only 18-hole frisbee golf (or disc golf) course is right here in Somerset!
bodyContent: Mendip Activity Centre have an 18-hole Frisbee Golf course set in the stunning Mendip Hills open to everyone year-round. It’s like traditional golf, but with frisbees, fresh air and far more fun. The course winds through open fields and ancient woodland, with incredible views and the occasional friendly sheep for company. Ideal for families and friends, it’s a low-pressure adventure that’s as chilled or competitive as you want it to be. Every player gets a scorecard and a disc. Book in advance or just turn up. Children can take part in the free Yeti Hunt along the way. It’s a magical extra that makes this a favourite for adventurous families exploring Somerset.

title: Marco Pierre White Steakhouse Bar & Grill Bridgwater
subtitle: Stylish, relaxed dining in the heart of Bridgwater. The Marco Pierre White Steakhouse Bar & Grill serves classic dishes with a modern twist, featuring the finest steaks, grills, and seasonal produce, all paired with an excellent wine and cocktail list.
bodyContent: Located within the Mercure Bridgwater Hotel, the Marco Pierre White Steakhouse Bar & Grill offers a dining experience that combines quality, style, and a warm welcome. Inspired by the renowned chef’s ethos of simple, classic cooking, the restaurant places an emphasis on seasonal produce, perfectly cooked steaks, and timeless favourites delivered to the highest standards. Every dish is created with care, showcasing the best ingredients and attention to detail that Marco Pierre White is famous for. The menu celebrates traditional British classics with subtle French influences, ensuring there is something for every palate. From signature steaks and grills cooked exactly to your preference, to hearty mains and lighter options, the variety makes it ideal for every occasion. Complementing the food is an impressive wine list, handpicked to pair beautifully with the menu, along with a wide choice of expertly mixed cocktails, premium spirits, and soft drinks. Guests can enjoy the restaurant throughout the day, whether for a relaxed lunch, indulgent Afternoon Tea, or an evening dinner with friends and family. The stylish setting, combined with a warm and welcoming atmosphere, makes it equally suited to business lunches, romantic dinners, or larger celebratory gatherings. Open to both hotel residents and non-residents, the restaurant has quickly become a favourite dining destination in Bridgwater. With exceptional food, attentive service, and a sophisticated yet comfortable environment, the Marco Pierre White Steakhouse Bar & Grill offers a truly memorable dining experience at the heart of Somerset.

title: Shoemakers Museum
subtitle: Discover the Quakers, the shoemakers and stories behind Clarks shoes in the place where it all began in Street, Somerset
bodyContent: Step inside a new family-friendly visitor attraction celebrating fashion, creativity and social change through 200-years of shoemaking. Find out how the Clarks shoe brand became a global story. A remarkable journey with exhibitions, film, interactives, tours, and regular events to explore enjoy. Meet the Shoemakers Four permanent exhibition galleries share the story of shoemaking in Street, from handmade shoes to factory life, fashions in advertising and shoe shopping. Discover life as a shoemaker, experience shoe shopping 1950s and 1980s style, and celebrate some of the nations’ favourite footwear. Plus meet fossil sea-dragons found under the Clarks factories! Galleries, gardens, café and interactive events An exhibition of 200 years of shoemaking alongside film footage that the factory floor to life. Explore your favourite shoes and experiences, from foot measurements to advertising. An exhibition of 200 years of shoemaking alongside film footage that brings the history of Clarks and the factory floor to life. Interactives include a 1980s shoe shop with 80s fashion to try on. Get creative in the education room and enjoy space to play. Accessibility Shoemakers Museum aims to be an accessible attraction. Facilities include accessible toilets, changing facility, lifts and accessible interactives. Please visit the website to view the access guide. Tickets Free carparking passes for Clarks Village Car Park II are available for museum ticket holders. Food and Drink Enjoy a taste of Somerset with the best of locally produced delicious hot and cold food and drink options available in café. Or bring a picnic to enjoy outside in the gardens and walled orchard. A great family day out Clarks Village, is right on our doorstep with outlet and high street shopping to indulge in after your visit. Shoemakers Museum in Street is a short distance away from historic Glastonbury, nature on the Somerset Levels, and artistic Somerton just down the road.
tagline: Discover the Quakers, the shoemakers and stories behind Clarks shoes

title: The Huntsmen: Winter War
subtitle: Locations: The Bishop’s Palace, Wells, and Wells Cathedral. Release date: April 2016.
bodyContent: Image Credits: Universal. Two historic landmarks in Wells were used to bring to life the fantastical world of The Huntsman: Winter’s War. Starring Charlize Theron as evil Queen Ravenna, Emily Blunt as her sister Freya and Chris Hemsworth as Eric the Huntsman, many of the opening scenes in the sequel/prequel to ‘Snow White and the Huntsman’ were shot in The Bishop’s Palace and Wells Cathedral . Filing in July 2015, it’s tale of betrayal and love set in a fantasy world of myths and monsters. The Palace’s atmospheric Undercroft was the setting for the dramatic chess scene between Ravenna and the king, and the scenes featuring the famous ‘mirror on the wall’ - look for the Undercrofts vaulted ceilings and distinctive windows. The Palace Green and Palace Gates can be seen as Freya rushes towards her secret marriage with the Duke of Blackwood, as can fake castle walls created next to the Bishop's Eye as part of the set. Steps and corridors within Wells Cathedral can be seen in the early chase scene, while the nave is the setting for the king’s funeral scene with the Cathedral’s unique scissored arches clearly visible. Useful Links: · Bishops Palace · Wells Cathedral · Visit Wells · IMDB listing The Huntsman: Winter's War (2016)
tagline: Locations: The Bishop’s Palace, Wells, and Wells Cathedral. Release date: April 2016.

title: The Roost in the Blackdowns
subtitle: The accommodation is in a peaceful small hamlet in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty without street lighting and with stunning views across the picturesque and hidden Culm Valley. There are country walks from your door, with pubs nearby. Dogs are welcome.
bodyContent: The Roost is a modern self-contained loft with large balcony window overlooking green fields and woods. The property has a single bedroom with comfortable king-size bed and a spacious living and dining area. There is a fully equipped kitchen with oven, hob, fridge and dishwasher. The bathroom has a walk-in deluge shower. Underneath, you have free parking, a private and secure garage to lock away your vehicle or bikes, a washing machine and a drier. We provide essentials such as Faith in Nature shampoo, conditioner and shower gel. There are coffee, teas, milk and cereals to start you off when you arrive. We care for our environment by providing comprehensive recycling facilities, eco-friendly consumables and we never use plastic wet wipes.

title: Monday Markets at Taunton’s Antique Centre & Craft Store
subtitle: Step into one of Taunton’s longest‑running traditions with the Monday Markets, a vibrant weekly event rooted in local history.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } 📅 Every Monday ⏰ 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM 📍 25–29 Silver Street, Taunton Step into one of Taunton’s longest‑running traditions with the Monday Markets , a vibrant weekly event rooted in local history. A Taunton Tradition Since 1978 The story began in 1978 when the original Taunton Antique Market opened its doors on Silver Street. Operating exclusively on Mondays, it quickly grew into a beloved local institution. With queues regularly stretching around the block and more than 100 dealers inside its quirky 15,000 sq ft building, the market became a national destination for antique lovers and treasure hunters. Revitalised for Today On 10 October 2022 , Antiques on High breathed new life into the iconic space, transforming 25 Silver Street into a traditional antique centre, while preserving the much‑loved Monday Market across 25–29 Silver Street —now complete with a cosy café for visitors. The centre and market have since welcomed special guests, including antique expert David Harper , who spent a day filming on-site. What to Expect Over 100 antique and craft dealers A mix of traditional antiques, vintage pieces, and handmade crafts A welcoming café to relax between treasure‑hunting A charming, historic atmosphere loved by locals and visitors alike ⏱ Seasonal Opening Times: Please call us to confirm the current opening times for both the shop and the Monday Market, as these vary throughout the year.
tagline: Step into one of Taunton’s longest‑running traditions with the Monday Markets.

title: Taunton Flower Show 2026
subtitle: Experience a festival atmosphere at the oldest flower show in the country, set in the heart of Taunton.
bodyContent: Taunton Flower Show is an annual two-day family show held on the first Friday and Saturday of August each year, attracting around 16,000 visitors over the two days. Established in 1831, Taunton Flower Show is the longest running Flower Show in the UK, and second oldest in the World. Set in the lovely surrounds of Vivary Park, the Show is a feast for all the family. Our fantastic competition marquee shows off the talents of our community and the floral marquee and designer gardens demonstrate national horticultural excellence. You will also find music, arena entertainment, local and national traders and fun for all the family. Save by purchasing your tickets in advance and enjoy a brilliant day out! Assistance dogs only allowed into the showground. Tickets on sale at Taunton Visitor Centre

title: Charlton House, Montigo Resorts Somerset
subtitle: Discover an oasis of calm at Montigo Resorts, Somerset. With luxurious, individually designed rooms, a spa inspired by Asian traditions, and farm-to-table dining, Charlton House offers an unparalleled rural escape. Experience relaxation, rejuvenation, and the best of Somerset’s local flavours.
bodyContent: Somersets, Montigo Resorts - Charlton House, Shepton Mallet - is nestled in the heart of Somerset’s picturesque countryside, Montigo Resorts, Somerset at Charlton House offers the perfect escape. This historic estate features 28 uniquely designed rooms, each with its own character and charm, combining contemporary comforts with the building’s rich heritage. Whether you’re seeking a cosy hideaway or a spacious suite for a longer stay, there’s a room to suit every taste. The resort’s spa is a serene sanctuary where Asian wellness meets the healing power of nature. Boasting state-of-the-art thermal facilities, hydrotherapy pools, and specialist therapies like Balinese and Thai massages, you’re assured a deeply relaxing experience. For dining, Montigo Resorts showcases the best of Somerset’s seasonal produce; from the colourful cocktails, seasoned meats, and fresh, locally sourced seafood, cooked to perfection, at Tiigo, our kitchen garden pop up promises an authentic pan-Asian experience in a laid-back setting, while the Charlton House restaurant offers a more refined affair and Bob’s Bistro ensures you can grab a bite in the bar or lounge at any time. Whether you’re here for a wellness retreat, a romantic weekend, or simply to unwind, Montigo Resorts, Somerset at Charlton House invites you to embrace the tranquillity of this little gem of a county.

title: Taunton Town FC Lion Trail 2026
subtitle: Join the Lion Trail around Taunton town centre this summer and discover 48 colourful lion displays inspired by football nations from around the world. Designed for families and children, the trail combines exploration, observation and the chance to win prizes.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Explore Taunton this summer with the Taunton Town FC Lion Trail, a free family-friendly trail featuring 48 colourful lion displays in shop windows across the town centre. Each lion represents a different football nation, challenging visitors to identify the countries and complete the trail sheet as they make their way around town. Completed entries must be submitted by 14 August 2026 for a chance to win prizes, including a Taunton Town FC 2026/27 home shirt. Pick up a trail sheet from the Taunton Visitor Centre and start your lion-hunting adventure around the town! Map can be found online at 80348_Taunton-Town-Football-Club-Ltd_Lion-Trail-Map-Leaflets-V2-Not-Printed-FOR-WEB.pdf
tagline: A free family trail featuring 48 colourful lions hidden around Taunton town centre.

title: The Mapping of Somerset – A Talk by Christine King
subtitle: This talk is part of the autumn programme of the Somerset Industrial Archaeology Society.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } The first printed map of Somerset was produced by Christopher Saxton and published between 1575 and 1579. Using many physical examples, Christine King explores how the development of cartography was driven forward by Saxton and other notable map-makers. The talk examines how maps evolved over time and how they reflected the physical and social changes taking place across Somerset and beyond. Tickets available on the door
tagline: This talk is part of the autumn programme of the Somerset Industrial Archaeology Society.

title: February Half Term in Taunton 2026
subtitle: Looking for fun ways to keep the kids entertained this half term?
bodyContent: Looking for fun ways to keep the kids entertained this half term? Taunton is packed with amazing family activities, adventures and events from 14–21 February 2026 ! 🎉 Download your FREE copy HERE or pick up a printed copy from the Taunton Visitor Centre. 🦣 Step back in time at the Museum of Somerset Follow the Woolly Mammoth Trail, handle real fossils and dive into prehistoric fun at Prehistoric Planet (17–19 Feb) . 🐞 Spring Bug Trail at the Cider Farm Little explorers can hunt for bugs in the orchards, enjoy Little Farmer sessions and tuck into treats at the House of Cider. 🎭 Family Theatre Fun From The Gruffalo’s Child to Mark Thompson’s Spectacular Science Show , there’s something magical for every age. 🎮 Unlimited Fun at Continue Arcades Retro gaming, pinball, air hockey and over 40 machines — pay once, play all day! ✨ Character Experiences & Soft Play Meet Stitch, blast off at Space Adventurers or craft, play and create at Matilda’s Marvellous Party . 🐄 Free day out at Doniford Farm Park Meet the animals, enjoy the Play Barn and explore the coastal views. 🌳 Outdoor Adventures Try the River Tone Story Trail, Month of Mud with the National Trust, Dunster Castle’s Trail of Tales, and Barrington Court’s activity book. 🎪 Plus more events coming up! Taunton Independent Market (1 March), Test Fest (20 June) and Taunton Flower Show (7–8 August). 👇 Pick your favourites and plan a half term to remember! Find full details at the Taunton Visitor Centre or over on our website. Here are some other great ideas of what you can do this school holidays... Find the Willow Cathedral and enjoy the River Tone Story Trail​ Explore Vivary Park Search for planets along the Bridgwater to Taunton Canal on the Somerset Space Walk Discover the rocky history of the Wellington Monument , the tallest three-sided obelisk in the world Find the pirate ship in Hudson Way Go on an animal spotting trip to the Quantocks Explore Coates English Willow Visitor Centre in Stoke St Gregory it offers a range of attractions.
