title: Wiveliscombe
subtitle: Wiveliscombe is situated at the foot of the Brendon Hills at the gateway to Exmoor.
bodyContent: This town is a thriving local centre which is surrounded by stunning countryside. ’Wivey’ is home to numerous shops and galleries, many still with their Victorian frontages whilst the pubs stock ales from the town’s two renowned breweries. Wiveliscombe is a former market and cloth-making town steeped in history. The 10 Parishes Festival held annually in September is a week long celebration of visual and performing arts that brings surrounding villages together to show their vibrant local talent to visitors. Wiveliscombe, just a 15-minute drive from Taunton, is a delightful town to visit with plenty of historic buildings to admire and some excellent independent shops. But whatever you do don’t leave without trying a pint….
tagline: Wiveliscombe is situated at the foot of the Brendon Hills at the gateway to Exmoor.

title: Club & Spa at DoubleTree by Hilton, Cadbury House
subtitle: Luxury spa hotel in North Somerset near Bristol with gourmet restaurant, DoubleTree by Hilton.
bodyContent: Set in the rolling North Somerset countryside, DoubleTree by Hilton, Cadbury House is one of the region's most popular destination spa hotels. Choose from a range of spa breaks and spa days, with numerous treatment rooms including a couple's suite for shared experiences. The treatment menu covers facials, massages, body wraps, hand and feet treatments, waxing and holistic therapies. Hotel guests also enjoy the 20m swimming pool, sauna, steam room, Jacuzzi and award-winning health club facilities, plus a Marco Pierre White restaurant serving brunch, lunch, dinner and afternoon tea. Recent improvements include an extended relaxation zone, outdoor sauna, hot tub and terrace. Facilities include ladies and men's saunas, an aromatherapy steam room, ladies-only steam room, gym, indoor pool and outdoor sun deck. On-site parking is available, and all major credit cards are accepted.

title: Roman Baths Shop
subtitle: The Roman Baths has two shops where you can buy interesting and exclusive gifts.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. One is at street level and can be visited independently of the Roman Baths ; the other is on the lower floor of the Roman Baths museum . Choose from a range of quality gifts, many with a Roman and Georgian flavour – including souvenirs, toiletries, jewellery, biscuits and chocolate, locally made crafts and much more. Don’t leave without buying a mini bottle of water from Bath’s hot spring, which was used for medicinal purposes by the Georgians! You can also purchase stylish guidebooks, postcards and prints. The Essential Roman Baths (£4.50) is the authorised guide to the site, illustrating why and how the complex was built and displaying many of its greatest treasures.

title: Greencombe Gardens
subtitle: A woodland garden and organic showpiece of international renown, Greencombe extends along a sheltered hillside below the tree-covered slopes of Exmoor and offers outstanding views over ancient fields onto Porlock Bay and the sea beyond
bodyContent: A woodland garden and organic showpiece of international renown, Greencombe extends along a sheltered hillside below the tree-covered slopes of Exmoor and offers outstanding views over ancient fields onto Porlock Bay and the sea beyond. Moss covered paths meander through an exceptional collection of ornamental plants that flourish beneath a magnificent canopy of oaks, hollies, conifers and sweet chestnuts. Camellias, magnolias, rhododendrons, azaleas, lilies and hydrangeas flower among rare ferns and the garden's four National Collections. Roses, clematis and other climbers wend their way upwards through an understory which includes a rich collection of maples. Greencombe is a postwar garden, laid out in 1946 on a north facing hill. For 50 years, Joan Loraine developed a collection of exceptional plants employing methods that she termed “intrinsic gardening”. Building on established organic methods and shunning chemical sprays, she produced all her own compost and spread copious amounts of leaf mould, resulting in fertile soil with a riot of birds and butterflies all around. While most of the plants have been carefully placed in their present positions, the garden gives the impression that it just occurred and that paths wander around plants that already existed. On display throughout the garden are four National Collections; Erythronium, small mountain-lilies; Vaccinium, 'whortleberries worldwide'; Gaultheria, 'whortleberries for bears'; and Polystichum, the 'thumbs-up' fern. Also of special interest, the garden is home to a champion English Holly tree (ilex aquifolium), the largest and oldest in the British Isles. Like all good plantsmen’s gardens, Greencombe is full of rare and wonderful plants and has much to interest and delight every visitor. Greencombe Garden Trust is a UK registered charity no 281878 dedicated to nature conservation and the improvement of horticulture.

title: Butcombe Brewery Ltd
subtitle: Stalwarts of the Somerset and Bristol brewery scene, Butcombe have been brewing consistently high-quality premium beers since 1978. Butcombe Brewing Co. love nothing more than hosting a bunch of beer enthusiasts at their brewery. Great for experts and beginners alike, we’ll happy share our passion and craft with you.
bodyContent: 40 years of brewing great beer. Simon Whitmore, Founder of Butcombe and former MD of Courage Western and prior to that with Guinness Worldwide, set up Butcombe Brewery in old farm buildings at his family home in Butcombe, 10 miles south of Bristol, in September 1978. He used his £24, 000 redundancy payment from Courage to convert the buildings, and buy most of the brewery equipment from Allied Breweries surplus plant department in Burton-on-Trent. Simon even picked up the plant and bought it back to Bristol in his famously unreliable second hand Bedford 35cwt truck …luckily he made it! The brewery has been extended twice since then. In the summer of 1982, increasing the brewery length to first 20 barrels and subsequently to 45 barrels, and again in the autumn of 1992 increasing the brew length to 85 barrels. The superb Boby 4 roller mill, which you can see in our shop today, milled for 27 years between 1978 and February 2005, a staggering 285, 000 barrels of beer or just over 82 million pints …no wonder it needed replacing! Simon and the team brewed one beer for the first 21 years – The iconic Butcombe Bitter, no wonder it’s called The Original! With Gold finally being added to the stable in 1999. Now owned by The Liberation Group, Butcombe have 7 beers in their classic range, including their newest launches Blackbeard Stout and Underfall Lager, as well as consistently launching seasonal beers and their own cider – Ashton Press. Butcombe beers (and cider) are available throughout Somerset in pubs, supermarkets and at the brewery shop. For a real taste experience of Butcombe, try visiting one of their own 19 managed or 23 tenanted pubs or the brewery shop on site in Wrington. There’s nothing we love more than hosting a bunch of beer enthusiasts at our brewery. Even if you don’t know much about beer and are keen to find out more, we’ll happily share passion and craft with you. We’ve got a great story to tell, and our vision for the future is just as exciting, so come have a look around and enjoy a pint with us. Get behind the scenes, see how we work our magic at the brewery and finally taste some of our finest brews with the people who lovingly made them. Facilities: Brewery Shop, Brewery Tours (First Tuesday of every month – pre-booking essential), 19 Managed pubs
tagline: There’s nothing we love more than hosting a bunch of beer enthusiasts at our brewery.

title: BIRDWATCHING (and listening!) in Somerset
bodyContent: Somerset is among the most rewarding places for birdwatching anywhere in Britain. There is such a wide range of habitats - from intertidal and wetland to woodland and moor. While the numbers of species in the country as a whole are declining, in Somerset they are increasing. As well as our resident populations, the county’s special landscape attracts visitors from overseas and this means that whatever time of year you choose, there is always something special to see. Add to this the fact that new species are nesting for the first time in centuries here or being re-introduced and you can see why the area is so important for birds and wildlife. In the winter, the internationally important Somerset Levels are a draw for migrant wading birds including wigeons, teals, shovelers and Bewick's swans. These months also see and hear the famous starling murmurations . (Ring the starling hotline 07866554142 for more details) On the coast, Bridgwater Bay is a major feeding and roosting site for waterfowl and waders such as Shelduck, dunlin, curlew, grey plover and avocet. Nearby, the newly created Steart Marshes area is the largest new wetland reserve in the country with flocks of waders and rare raptors. Year round on the Levels you can see bittern and marsh harriers which are scarce elsewhere. All you need for birdwatching is information on the best places to go (see links). You don’t have to buy expensive equipment or to walk for miles. Our local reserves are easily accessible and have hides so that you can see the wildlife but it can’t see you. Don’t be put off by thinking you have to have telescopes and long lenses – you can enjoy the company of birds just by keeping your eyes open or listening for their distinctive voices. Once you start, it can be hard to drag yourself away as you watch or hear them hunting, courting or just spuddling about. These are perfect places for children to learn to recognise the different shapes, sizes and sounds of the birds around them and perhaps begin a lifelong fascination for them. Follow these links for some of Somerset’s top nature reserves: http://www.rspb.org.uk/discoverandenjoynature/seenature/reserves/guide/g/greylake/index.aspx http://www.rspb.org.uk/discoverandenjoynature/seenature/reserves/guide/h/hamwall/index.aspx http://www.rspb.org.uk/discoverandenjoynature/seenature/reserves/guide/s/swellwood/index.aspx http://www.rspb.org.uk/discoverandenjoynature/seenature/reserves/guide/w/westsedgemoor/index.aspx http://www.somersetwildlife.org/reserves.html http://steart.wwt.org.uk/ http://www.avalonmarshes.org/ https://hawkandowltrust.org/

title: Somerset Farmers Market
subtitle: Established in 1999 as a not-for-profit organisation Somerset Farmers' Markets was set up to support and promote local farmers, food and drink producers and local towns. We aim to enhance town centres with vibrant markets providing customers with fresh, high-quality and traceable produce.
bodyContent: Somerset Farmers’ Markets were born as an initiative to ‘act locally’ to prevent climate change by focusing on sustainable development. By supporting small scale farms and food production by encouraging shoppers to buy local, food miles are kept low minimising the negative impact on the environment. From medieval town squares to bustling high streets, each market has its own character and boasts a unique line up from our membership of over 100 hundred producers. Visitors enjoy the experience of talking directly to producers about food and drink, picking up recipe suggestions and storage tips. We hold 8 markets across Somerset: Axbridge, First Saturday of the month, 9am - 1pm Burnham-on-Sea, Last Friday of the month, 9am - 1pm Crewkerne, Third Saturday of the month, 9am - 1pm Frome Cheese & Grain, Second Saturday of the month, 9am - 1pm SFM at Frome Independent, First Sunday of the month, 10am - 3pm Glastonbury, Fourth Saturday of the month, 9am - 2pm Keynsham, Second Saturday of the month, 9am - 1pm Midsomer Norton, First Saturday of the month, 9am - 1pm

title: Bridgwater & Taunton Canal
subtitle: The well-maintained towpath and interesting lock structures of the Bridgwater and Taunton Canal make for idyllic walking and peaceful boating.
bodyContent: The 14 mile Bridgwater and Taunton Canal opened in 1827, linking the River Tone and the River Parrett for commercial traffic between the two market towns. There is no navigable connection to the River Parrett today but the Canal is enjoyed by walkers, cyclists, nature enthusiasts, fishermen and boatmen alike. The majority of the Canal is rural and offers tranquility to all. The 'Somerset Space Walk' is located on the Canal and features two scale models of the Solar System centred around the sun at Maunsel Lock (also the site of a tea room). Follow the planets' trail to Maunsel Lock from the Brewhouse Theatre in Taunton or from Morrisons' supermarket in Bridgwater. The Somerset Boat Centre at North Newton offers canoes, kayaks, self-drive motor boats and a chartered narrowboat for exploring this stunning waterway.
tagline: A 14 mile canal with 7 locks

bodyContent: Somerset Community Foundation (SCF) has launched this year’s Surviving Winter campaign, which encourages people to donate some or all of their Winter Fuel Payment to help local people living in fuel poverty. Any online donations to the campaign made during the week-long Big Give Christmas Challenge - midday Tuesday 1 December to midday Tuesday 8 December - will be doubled ! SCF is also delighted to announce that Glastonbury Festival organiser and long-time Surviving Winter supporter Michael Eavis CBE has offered his support for another year. Surviving Winter began in 2010 right here in our office in Somerset . We were contacted by one of our donors who offered to give his Winter Fuel Payment to help local pensioners struggling with the cost of staying warm and healthy. He wanted his donation to pay for the everyday essentials that most of us take for granted, such as heating, warm clothing and food. From this simple idea Surviving Winter has spread across the country, raising millions nationally and over £800,000 in Somerset alone. The costs of running the Surviving Winter appeal are met entirely from Gift Aid contributions , so donors can be confident that their donation will reach those who need it the most. But for this reason we also ask you to please print the Gift Aid form if you are able to do so. For more details read more here

title: Bruton Museum
subtitle: Bruton Museum is nestled on the High Street, housed in the Dovecote Building just behind the Community Office. Founded in 1989, it tells the story of Bruton’s colourful history and is an essential destination whether you are a visitor to Bruton or live in the town.
bodyContent: We tell the story of Bruton’s past and present through the display of objects, from prehistoric to modern times. Amongst our vast range of artefacts, the exquisite wares of Bruton silversmith Gabriel Felling, the unique sculptures of WWII German refugee Ernst Blensdorf, and the writing desk commissioned by John Steinbeck when he lived here in 1959, are some of the highlights. Set in the heart of a rich agricultural landscape, Bruton emerged as a market town and important ecclesiastical centre, its priory evolving into the great abbey that once stood next to the beautiful church of St Mary. For centuries it was an important and prosperous mill town specialising in the production of woollen cloth and, later, silk. Among its many fascinating historic buildings are the splendid seventeenth-century almshouses that commemorate the town’s great benefactor, Sir Hugh Sexey. The internationally-renowned gallery and exhibition space Hauser and Wirth at Durslade Farm is within walking distance. The High Street now offers an array of independent shops and places to eat with plenty to do. Bruton is bursting with creative talent and to represent this the museum has created an ever-changing display “Casespace” to show contemporary art and collections. Check in and see “What’s on”. The Museum will be launching the first Bruton Festival of History and Heritage in the near future with a programme of exciting events at various locations. Plans are also in place for Museum members to participate in walks and visits during the Summer. We also run an annual programme of talks at the Museum in the Autumn. Please check our website for up to date information.
tagline: Bruton Museum is nestled on the High Street, housed in the Dovecote Building

title: Stroll along the Strawberry line to Sandford
subtitle: Rolling green fields, reedbeds, rhynes and orchards make the flat and accessible Strawberry Line an ideal route for families, dog walkers, cyclists and pedestrians.
bodyContent: How to get there Start at map ref: ST 425661 Car: Park at Yatton station or on-street nearby. Please park considerately if parking in residential roads. Bus: W1 Weston-Bristol service Carmel 88 connection to Clevedon Train: Trains stop regularly at Yatton Rolling green fields, reedbeds, rhynes and orchards make the flat and accessible Strawberry Line an ideal route for families, dog walkers, cyclists and pedestrians. The heritage trail follows the old railway route that ran from Yatton to Cheddar and Wells for 100 years until it closed in 1963. It takes its name from the strawberries that were grown on the Mendip Hills and transported by railway. Starting at Yatton station, pass under the metal arch which celebrates the diverse wildlife. As well as being a scenic route for walkers and cyclists, the Strawberry Line links different habitats, helping wildlife travel between them. You will soon see a special wildlife seat designed by children of Yatton junior school to celebrate Roman remains found nearby in 2000. Click HERE for full details and FREE PDF copy

title: Barleycorn
subtitle: Located in a picturesque rural setting, Barleycorn is a beautiful cottage for two people.
bodyContent: Sleep in a king sized bed with 100% cotton bedlinen and enjoy the luxury of underfloor heating throughout. Take a country walk from your cottage, visit the historic city of Bath or just enjoy the stunning views from the farm. Just twenty minutes drive from the City of Bath, Barleycorn is a beautifully converted old milking parlour suitable for two people sharing. Barleycorn is an excellent location for a romantic holiday within easy reach of Bath, Bristol or Wells. Withy MillsFarm is a set in a stunning rural setting and combines the peacefulness of the countryside with the closeness of three wonderful cities to explore. The open plan kitchen/living room has a fitted kitchen, oak dining table, settees and TV. It also has a large walk in shower room and in the bedroom a king sized bed with 100% cotton bed linen. You can also enjoy the luxury of underfloor heating throughout the cottage. Prices are inclusive of electricity, heating, Wi-Fi, cotton bed linen, large and small white towels. There is parking outside your door for up to two vehicles. Start your holiday with a home made cream tea on arrival, then plan the activities for your stay. There are numerous footpaths leading from the cottage. A useful guide book in Barleycorn suggests many of the best local walks. Withy Mills Farm is a working dairy farm, but the main business of the farm is carried out at another location. This means you will not be disturbed by any tractors early in the morning. Unfortunately we are unable to accept dogs at Withy Mills Farm.
tagline: Barleycorn is a beautiful cottage for two people.

bodyContent: Activate Fitness is an independent, community focused gym which offers a non-intimidating fitness environment in all areas, including the weights and cardio zones. Anytime Fitness (Taunton and Wellington) is the gym that fits your on-the-go lifestyle! Located in Taunton's town centre, in Somerset, the gym is open 24hrs - we never close! Blackbrook Leisure Centre & Spa has something for everyone: a quality and recently refurbished Fitness Gym as well as a recently extended fitness studio to hold a large variety of fitness classes for all ages and abilities. Cardio Cabin offers ladies' fitness, strength training and weight management in a non-intimidating environment. Enjoy access to world-class Technogym cardio equipment, a large free weights area with an Olympic lifting rack, group fitness classes (live and virtual!), dedicated functional training area with TRX and more at Snap Fitness 24/7 Somerset Adventures offers a fantastic range of exciting outdoor adventurous activities. With activities including kayaking, canoeing, raft building, archery, laser clay pigeon shooting, axe throwing, bushcraft, climbing, caving, abseiling and navigation training there is something for everyone. Somerset Bike Hire offers a full range of sizes and three levels of bike – Carbon Road, Aluminium Road and Hybrid which are ideal for less serious riders and those wishing to explore the canal towpath. It also runs group and 1-2-1 swimming lessons for juniors and adults. The Pilates Studio specialises in rehabilitation through Pilates and offers individualised programmes to clients using a range of specialist equipment. The Studio at Bank House is in the business of making people feel alive, energetic and confident through inspiring forms of exercise, including pilates. Vivary Golf & Adventure Centre is just 5 minutes walk from Taunton Town centre and consists of an adrenaline pumping High Ropes Course, Mini Golf Course for all the family and an 18 hole Golf Course for the more adventurous out there. Wellington Sports Centre holds a split level fitness gym, studio, Z3 (Junior Gym), indoor swimming pool and sports hall and is ideal for all ages. title: The Plume of feathers
subtitle: Plume of Feathers is above all, a traditional English country pub. Serving the local community for over 200 years as a place to relax, enjoy company and exchange news and information.
bodyContent: A Traditional Country Pub Plume of Feathers is above all, a traditional English country pub. Serving the local community for over 200 years as a place to relax, enjoy company and exchange news and information. We have a hand picked selection of fine ales from the local Buttcombe brewery and always have one guest ale, and a traditional cider. A wide selection of wines are available by the glass or bottle, and our top shelf includes quality single malt whiskeys and other fine spirits. Families Welcome We welcome families and accompanied children. A stream runs past outside, and there is a shallow ford one hundred metres away. We have a beer garden at the rear of the pub . We have a variety of very traditional pub games including shove ha'penny, table skittles, darts and a pool table. Please think carefully before challenging the "Old Boys" to cribbage for 50p a corner. Board games and playing cards are available on request. The Food We use only fresh ingredients in all our meals. We use local produce and suppliers wherever possible for our meat, fish and vegetables. We have a dining room that seats twenty, and additional tables are available in our bar area. bodyContent: Cultural fusion is in our DNA and we celebrate colour, diversity and historical influences from around the world in our tweed clothing collection that is lined in Dutch wax cotton batik. A Kashmiri pheran is the original inspiration for our tweed robe, the Battuta, while our fitted tweed women’s waistcoat incorporates elements of Prussian military styling and leather biker jackets; our tweed tunics nod to Mary Quant and the spirit of the 60’s and our trouser suits channel a seventies vibe in tweeds, velvets or corduroy.

title: Somerset Charcuterie
subtitle: Andy & James have been hobby charcutiers for several years. Andy grew up on a pig farm and James is a member of a small village cooperative of 6 families who raise livestock. Their daughters become best friends at the local school and it wasn’t long before they discovered that they shared passion for curing meats and making salami.
bodyContent: Over a pint of cider at a local lawn-mower race (this is Somerset!), the idea for a quality British Charcuterie business was conceived. Both of them have run their own food businesses for several years and could see an opportunity to develop a range of products that followed traditional Spanish, French and Italian methods but were adapted to the British market and capitalised on the rich food culture of the South West. Within 6 months the first products were ready to try on family and friends and, with some encouraging feedback, the first farmers markets were booked to test the product on the general public. The buzz around the stall at the first market was electric and the decision was made. Somerset Charcuterie was born. Now in their 8th year the team are going through up to two tonnes of pork a week along with local wild venison, local free range duck, grass fed beef and lamb. Everything is handmade now, and will remain that way in order to preserve the artisan texture, flavours and look. They moved into their new production unit on the farm a couple of years ago but are now already looking to expand in order to meet the growing demand. “We are committed to producing the best product with the best of Somerset ingredients wherever we can. We are now regularly in several markets across Somerset and Bristol, at festivals around the country, in pubs, restaurants and delis. It has been a fantastic success story so far and we are very lucky to have a loyal fan base to whom we are very grateful. We are looking forward to developing new and exciting products, meeting like-minded meat lovers and expanding our business further afield. If you are interested in stocking our product or would like to work with a great team in a fledgling artisan food business, please get in touch.” James & Andy Also customers can order on our website and collect from us, they will be notified by email once the order is ready. Avoiding delivery charges. If at all possible to add this too that would be much appreciated.
tagline: Everything is handmade now, and will remain that way in order to preserve the artisan texture

title: Coleridge Cottage, National Trust
subtitle: Historic home of the poet Samuel Taylor Coleridge in Somerset near Bridgwater As in the poets’ day, there is still wilderness, heathland and a rocky shoreline where you can lose yourself in thought. The mix of heath on the top is a characteristic of the Quantocks and includes heather, whortleberry, gorse, bracken and wavy-haired grass. There is woodland too, once prized as a source of timber for ship building and now by walkers for its tranquillity. The oaks here are Sessile with acorns that gro
bodyContent: Nestled in the quaint village of Nether Stowey, Somerset, Coleridge Cottage is the historic home of the poet Samuel Taylor Coleridge. It was here that Coleridge composed some of his most celebrated works, including "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner," "Frost at Midnight," and "This Lime Tree Bower, My Prison." The cottage was a gathering place for literary greats, with frequent visits from William Wordsworth- it was here that the seeds of the Romantic movement were sown. Coleridge's time at the cottage was marked by both creative brilliance and personal turmoil. His family life gradually disintegrated, exacerbated by a growing addiction to laudanum. Despite these struggles, the three extraordinary years he spent in Nether Stowey produced poems that continue to inspire across generations. Acquired by the National Trust in 1909 and restored in 2011, Coleridge Cottage offers plenty to engage visitors of all ages. Indulge in the Tearoom’s delightful offerings, from cakes to cream teas. The Poet’s Lunch, featuring a Cheese Scone, Cheddar Cheese, Onion Marmalade, and a hot drink, is truly a feast for the senses! Wander through the wildflower garden and find the Lime-Tree Bower—a perfect spot for quiet reflection or listening to audio posts that bring Coleridge’s verses to life. Try your hand at “Quill Writing,” or step back in time with our fancy dress box and “Dress like a Georgian.” Young visitors will enjoy the indoor “Mouse Trail,” a fun adventure discovering hidden mice throughout the cottage. Coleridge Cottage also hosts exclusive events, including poetry readings, guided nature walks, themed talks, and workshops. Stay updated by visiting our website for details. Please note the cottage is unsuitable for wheelchairs due to small rooms and narrow corridors.
tagline: Historic home of the poet Samuel Taylor Coleridge in Somerset near Bridgwater

title: Avalon Archaeology
subtitle: Discover Iron Age, Saxon, Roman and Viking Somerset through historic reconstructions.
bodyContent: Avalon Archaeology is open for general visits, guided tours, group visits and special events. Avalon Archaeology is a lovingly crafted reproduction of Somerset’s heritage in the heart of the Avalon Marshes. History is brought to life with richly decorated archaeological reconstructions filled with hand-crafted furniture and authentic art. On your visit you can explore: Saxon longhall based on the palace excavated at nearby Cheddar decorated with carved furniture, woodwork and murals Roman dining room from a typical Somerset villa with a magnificent mosaic floor and murals, and a hypocaust heating system Viking trading vessel with mast and rigging based on the Skuldelev 3 wreck Iron Age Roundhouse based on those in the Glastonbury Lake Village (under construction) The world’s oldest excavation hut and a cinema showing short films on local archaeology Avalon Archaeology is part of the South West Heritage Trust, an independent charity committed to protecting and celebrating Somerset and Devon’s rich heritage.

title: ⭐The Grand Pier - Weston Super Mare
subtitle: The Grand Pier is open every day, except Christmas Day, so come hail, rain or shine, you’ll always get a warm welcome. Whatever the weather is doing outside, it’s still fun, fun, fun on the inside.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The Grand Pier, Weston super Mare, Somerset is the ideal destination for non-stop indoor family theme park fun. This North Somerset pier, with its state-of-the-art Pavilion is a truly iconic destination for family days out, events, concerts, weddings, and corporate events. With rides, attractions and the latest arcade games a visit to the Pier is the perfect treat for kids of all ages. On weekends, bank holidays and North Somerset school holidays, Unlimited Ride Wristbands are available for both adults and children, explore here . Don't miss out on this fantastic deal for your fun-filled day! Come and discover everything the Grand Pier, Somerset has to offer, including: · The very latest amusements - including giant screen Space Invaders · Thrilling rides including: Sidewinder, Freefall and Robocoaster · An amazing two level 300 meter indoor Go-Kart track · Seaside favourites, including: dodgems, house of horrors and helter skelter · A three-level, dinosaur themed soft play area with dedicated adult seating · A choice of places to eat and drink - we even serve your favourite Costa coffee! With hundreds of amusements and games to play, a range of thrilling rides, and a choice of attractions for all ages everyone gets to have fun in the amazing Pavilion - it really is one big house of fun!!! When you’re ready for a bite to eat you’re spoilt for choice from traditional fish and chips to afternoon tea, and of course ice cream too! There’s even a pub for you to enjoy a relaxing drink as you take in the spectacular views. As a unique location our function rooms are always in demand, and we love creating the perfect setting for weddings and family celebrations. For businesses our dedicated events team is on hand for corporate events, ranging from team meetings and training sessions to large scale conferences.The fun continues into the night with a wide range of events from concerts to whodunnits. To make sure you don’t miss out visit and book your tickets online today.

title: Hot Fuzz
subtitle: Location: Various in and around Wells Release date: February 2007
bodyContent: Edgar Wright’s enduring cult comedy was filmed largely in the Director’s home city of Wells. Starring Simon Pegg (Nick Angel), Nick Frost (Danny Butterman) and a host of major British and international acting talent, it’s is a homage to 90s action films, set in the village of Sandford (there is a Sandford in North Somerset) but filmed in Wells featuring well-known locations and landmarks throughout England’s smallest city. These include the historic Market Place, the High Street, the Swan Hotel (exteriors), The Crown pub (exteriors, and home to a commemorative Hot Fuzz display) the City News newsagents (on the corner of High Street and Sadler Street), The Bishops Palace (site of the NWA meetings and other scenes), St Cuthbert’s Church (the site of the village fete), the Little Theatre (venue for the am dram production of Romeo and Juliette), and Wells Recreation Ground (involved in the swan chase). You won’t spot beautiful Wells Cathedral, which was digitally removed so as not to spoil the village look. You can join Hot Fuzz walking tours at various dates throughout the year. tagline: Location: Various in and around Wells Release date: February 2007

title: Find out how the Second World Wars Operation Star Fish confused the Luftwaffe
subtitle: Somerset Fascinating Facts - The highest hill in the Mendips, Black Down reaches 325 metres above the nearby Bristol Channel. The view from the top is astounding. As well as being the site for a well-known Second World War operation known as Starfish, there are also a number of ancient barrows (including one adjacent to the trig station).
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"238"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"




During the Second World War, Black Down, Mendips, Somerset was used as a bombing decoy site, part of a national programme to decoy German bombers away from towns and cities by using special effects to simulate Bristol at night. Bomb-proof bunkers housed generators and control switches enabling the RAF crew staffing the site to simulate an inadequately blacked-out city.

At first the site was fitted with decoy lighting. The lighting was concentrated in six clusters corresponding to six target sites in Bristol, including Canon’s Marsh and Temple Meads Station. In reality, the decoy was about 16 miles from Bristol, spread across Black Down between Tynings Farm and Burrington Combe.

Soon after, as the German bombing techniques changed, fires fuelled by creosote were used to simulate the incendiary bombs dropped to mark the target for further waves of bombers. These special fires were given the codename Starfish. Black Down was one of 12 Starfish sites around Bristol and one of 800 nationwide.

All that remains to be seen today are three bunkers, near the Tynings Farm entrance to Black Down.

At the south entrance lie the remains of a Z Battery, a Second World War anti-aircraft rocket launching site, which provided anti-aircraft gunfire, adding to the authenticity of the decoy town.


For more on Somerset's incredible history and heritage go to our interactive E Book.

title: Kilve
subtitle: Lying at the northern end of the Quantocks, Kilve is a picturesque village consisting of 3 settlements.
bodyContent: Things to do in Kilve, Somerset. Kilve lying at the northern end of the Quantocks , Kilve is a picturesque village consisting of 3 settlements. Here you will find the ruins of the old Chantry, founded in 1329 and once used for storing barrels of spirits smuggled in to Kilve Pill. The beach is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and a favourite haunt of geologists with its spectacular rock formations and fossils, including ammonites and reptile remains. The only parking for Kilve beach is at the Pay and Display Car Park.

subtitle: The historic village of Saltford is a large village (4,200 residents) situated alongside the A4, the River Avon, and the main-line railway with the Bristol to Bath cycle-path passing through. Saltford is surrounded by green belt land which preserves a rural setting for the village. Saltford is a perfect hub for activities in the Avon Valley and has a vibrant community with as many residents aged 17 years and under as over 65.
bodyContent: The historic village of Saltford is a large village (4,200 residents) situated alongside the A4, the River Avon, and the main-line railway with the Bristol to Bath cycle-path passing through. Saltford is surrounded by green belt land which preserves a rural setting for the village. Saltford is a perfect hub for activities in the Avon Valley and has a vibrant community with as many residents aged 17 years and under as over 65. There are many outdoor sport and recreation facilities in and around the village that benefit residents and visitors from neighbouring villages, towns and cities. These include tennis, cricket, football, walking, golf, cycling, horse riding, kayaking, rowing, and sailing. Saltford was the venue for the first Bath Regatta in 1849 and Saltford Rowing Centre now provides modern headquarters facilities for Avon Rowing Club and Canoe Avon. Bristol Avon Sailing Club is also based at Saltford. Saltford Golf Club hosted the prestigious English Ladies Open Tournament in 2011. Community involvement is centred on the Saltford Community Association and with its numerous affiliated organisations. There are pubs and restaurants, a primary school, a thriving Saltford Environment Group and Saltford has Fairtrade Village Status. Saltford is steeped in history with evidence that the Celts, Romans, Anglo-Saxons and Normans once lived and farmed here. Artefacts and historical features found in Saltford include possible evidence of roundhouses, a stone axe hammer, bronze axe heads, Roman coffins, many Roman and other ancient coins, the oldest being a Carthaginian Coin (300-264 BC), pottery fragments, an Anglo-Saxon burial ground, musket balls, and other miscellaneous glimpses of a long and interesting past. Saltford’s oldest dwelling is Saltford Manor House (c.1148) and is thought to be the oldest continuously occupied private house in England. Other important buildings include the Norman church of St Mary’s, with its late Anglo-Saxon period tower, that was attacked by Roundheads during the English Civil War and Saltford Brassmill, referred to in the Domesday Book entry for Saltford when it was a watermill. The mill was converted to working brass in the 18th Century and is now a Scheduled Ancient Monument frequently open to the public. Tunnel House was at one time purchased by Brunel in connection with the construction of the GWR line through Saltford and, next door, Saltford House was from 1856 to 1867 the home of Admiral Benedictus Marwood Kelly who had fought in the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic wars and served on the anti-slavery patrols off the west coast of Africa. Saltford also has a fascinating geological history with Lower Jurassic rocks seen across ploughed fields and in old quarries and it has been used in many of the older houses in the village. The rocks, mainly Blue Lias limestone, have abundant fossils and provide evidence that this region was once under a warm, shallow, sub-tropical sea, 180 million years ago. Some limestone exposures in Saltford are extremely important in our understanding of local and regional geology and have been protected as Regionally Important Geological Sites (RIGS) in recognition of this. A gravel deposit from the last ice age near Avon Farm has national protection as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). Saltford is a confident place where people enjoy living and working. The biennial Saltford Festival showcases all that is best about Saltford. For links to all Saltford organisations see Saltford Parish Council’s website . History walks around Saltford Saltford Environment Group has produced a series of history walks around Saltford following footpaths around the village. Although many boats can be seen along the river in Saltford, please note that moorings have been temporarily suspended at Mead Lane

title: Court Farm Country Park
subtitle: Somerset’s top award winning farm attraction, open all year.
bodyContent: Have a great family day out at Somerset’s top award winning farm attraction - all year round. Now into our 25th year as a family run farm attraction, all the animals and staff at Court Farm are looking forward to welcoming lots of children and their families for a fun packed summer of fun. With lots of new, baby animals mixed with a range of great play facilities that can tire out even the most energetic of kids (and adults), we hope that all our visitors, regardless of age, will have a day to remember. Don't forget that we have lots of things going on during the year so whenever you come, you may well see some new additions. From July come and get lost in our Maize Maze, it should be 8 ft tall by then!

title: Wellbeing
subtitle: With a number of spas and wellbeing centres situated within its beautiful landscape, Taunton Deane is a ideal destination for a relaxing break. The area boasts a large number of high-quality award-winning spas offering visitors a perfect place to unwind. From historic buildings to recent leisure complex’s, spa days in the Taunton area offer something for everybody.
bodyContent: Buff Urban Day Spa is an oasis of lavish urban chic, where relaxation, serenity and luxury are at the heart of your experience. Medineeds Health & Wellness Clinic in Taunton town centre has specialists who offer expert advice and treatment for all the small things that matter - with an equal focus on maintaining health and promoting wellbeing. The Spa Experience at Blackbrook Pavillion boasts a full wet thermal spa including hydro pool, sauna, steam room, monsoon shower, ice fountain and heat experience, plus the Spa offers access to 4 treatment rooms with a wide variety of massages and treatments available, nail bar, juice bar and relaxation room. The Cleve Spa at The Cleeve Hotel approach emphasises tailor-made natural treatments in a relaxed and informal spa environment which allows you to unwind and the make the day your own. The therapies at The Sangha House covering the pampering right through to the therapeutic. We offer massage, reflexology, facials, reiki, hypnotherapy, acupuncture, bowen therapy, evans alignment and traditional Chinese medicine.
tagline: Taunton Deane has a number of spas and wellbeing centres

title: Guddi & Gikki
subtitle: Guddi & Gikki is a restaurant serving home-style Indian food. This colourful family restaurant is run by Manveena, Chandeep and Diljot. With love and passion, they have fondly recreated the recipes their mothers cooked for them during their childhood. Today, they share their food and the joy of cooking authentic Indian recipes with very best English ingredients in a beautiful country town of Taunton. Their food is slow cooked, fresh and absolutely delicious.
bodyContent: Walias travelled five thousand miles away from home to get to the pretty country town of Taunton. Away from grandmother’s courtyard, and mother’s kitchen the pangs for the known comfort of a good curry led Manveena and Chandeep on a search for the great Indian meal. After trying out many restaurants, the two realized that Britain despite its great curry culture is still missing the touch of grandmother’s hand. They decided to recreate the tastes of their mother’s cooking in their own kitchen. When they found the perfect recipe, they figured it was too good to not be shared. Somerset Curry Club was formed in October 2011 as a pop-up restaurant with the intention of bringing together community over a steaming hot curry. The club was received with great gusto and warmth in over fifty villages. We unrolled the red carpets and worked up some ladle magic as people thronged to the local village halls for a date with us. We organized curry evenings that started with appetizers, proceeded with a buffet style main course meal and a delicious Indian dessert finally closing with loud applause, warm hugs and love. Repeated invitations from the villagers to “please come back again” followed. We knew our curry needed a home where families could join us every evening. However, nobody was willing to give us a chance. No one was betting on us. But we always had lovers of curry on our side. The venture eventually expanded into cookery courses with regular coverage in media and a distinct brand recognition in the community. For two years we ran a weekend stall in the Street. Encouraged by all the love we are now ready to give the best curry in Somerset a home. We have won people’s hearts by experimenting with food, offering fresh menus and healthy recipes, in the process gathering a deep understanding of people’s preferences and tastes. When we started, we promised people the best curry of their lives. We will continue to keep the promise. So, sit back, enjoy and soak in the experience that we bring to your table alongside the food because as we said earlier, we are only getting started.
tagline: Guddi & Gikki is a restaurant serving home-style Indian food.

title: Lytes Cary Manor, National Trust
subtitle: Intimate manor house with Arts and Crafts-style garden
bodyContent: Lytes Cary Manor is an intimate medieval manor house with a beautiful Arts and Crafts garden where you can imagine living. Originally the family home of Henry Lyte, where he translated the unique Niewe Herball book on herbal remedies, Lytes Cary was then lovingly restored in the 20th century by Sir Walter Jenner. The garden rooms contain a magical collection of topiary and herbaceous borders, while tranquil walks on the estate take you along the River Cary. To complete your visit, take a stroll among our community allotments and discover their creative and colourful designs. The garden that you see today at Lytes Cary Manor is very different to the garden that would have originally existed when the Lyte family were in residence. In the beginning The garden would have once been a very practical, working space. Henry Lyte, who lived in the house in the 1550s, was a keen herbalist and gardener. His son Thomas wrote that he grew apples, pears, plums, grapes, cherries, walnuts and peaches. Sadly, much of the original garden was lost after the Lytes family sold the estate in 1755. The following years saw a series of owners and tenants occupying the Manor, and the garden disappeared as the land was farmed right up to the house. Twentieth century changes When the Jenner family took up residence in 1907, Sir Walter and Lady Flora created a new garden. The design was Arts and Craft inspired and featured mostly rectangular ‘rooms’ separated by yew hedges and stone walls, each reflecting a different mood or purpose. After Sir Walter passed the house and estate to the National Trust, it was again let to tenants. In 1955, Jeremy Chittenden and his wife, Biddy, took the lease. Both worked tirelessly over the next 45 years to transform the gardens into those we now know.

title: Shakspeare Glass & Arts
subtitle: Visit Shakspeare Glass for one of a kind handblown glass pieces from master glassblower Will Shakspeare, and a gallery with unique pieces from a selection of other British makers. Enjoy a slice of cake and a coffee while you’re here, with the best views in Langport!
bodyContent: Overlooking the River Parrett, Shakspeare Glass & Arts is home to one of the finest master glassblowers in the country. Will Shakspeare creates individual pieces of handblown glass drawn from his influences of the Somerset countryside and coast. Browse the Gallery and shop for unique heirloom pieces and gifts, including works from other selected makers. A range of Will’s bespoke glass lighting, including chandeliers, pendant and wall lights are on display throughout the workshop and Gallery and are also available to order online . The coffee shop offers a variety of cakes and coffee and teas, and the perfect views across the river. It’s the ideal place to meet with friends and sit on the decking on a bright day, and during certain times, you can watch Will as he goes about his craft, blowing glass at the furnace. Will has been creating and making his own inimitable glassware for more than 30 and is one of the country’s most collected makers. He also offers occasional demonstration evenings and one-to-one glassblower workshops which are advertised through the website and on the Shakspeare Glass social media channels.
tagline: Visit Shakspeare Glass for one of a kind handblown glass pieces

title: Willow Farm Gourmet
subtitle: Open all year round from 9.30am to 2.30pm Thursday to Saturday (visit by appointment only), come and see our farm in action.
bodyContent: Come and Experience Willow Farm Open all year round from 9.30am to 2.30pm Thursday to Saturday (visit by appointment only), come and see our farm in action. If you are lucky, you may even get a chance to meet Bertie our award-winning pedigree Oxford Sandy and Black boar. We are a working farm, so our availability will depend on our core farm duties. To ensure you get the best from your visit, please make sure that you book 4 to 6 weeks in advance due to the popularity of these visits and our courses. Email: info@willowfarmgourmet.co.uk to enquire. Courses We are so proud of all of our hard work and we love to share what we do. Want to learn how we make our amazing local produce? We offer two fun courses: Tiny Welly Boot Cider-Making Cider making at its best! Come and see how proper Somerset cider is made. Learn about the intimate small batch craft cider making process including what happens to all of the waste products from the process. Arrive onsite at 9.30am and see the process from fruit to final bottled goods. Learn how we add modern twists to a Somerset favourite such as elderflower or white chocolate flavours. Also includes an opportunity to try some of our lovely ciders over lunch on the farm...what could be better! Available Thursdays and Saturdays from March to December. 9.30am to 1.30pm. £25.00 per person or £15.00 per person for farm tour, tasting and lunch only. Gift vouchers available and valid for up to 12 months. We also welcome block bookings for special occasions such as birthdays or hen parties and can accommodate up to 24 people for such events. Willow Farm Sausage-Making Want to see the secrets to our beloved Willow Farm sausages and faggots? Come and give them a go yourself. Have a laugh making our 100% pure meat bangers...none of that 'fluff' in these local sausages. Arrive onsite at 9.30am and immediately start having fun. We couldn't let you leave without trying some of your hard work so sample some of your own made sausage as part of this day out. Available weekdays from March through to December. 9.30am to 1.30pm. £45 per person including farm tour, cider tasting and lunch. Gift vouchers available and valid for up to 12 months. Stay with us Beautiful surroundings with good links to popular cities make Willow Farm a popular stop for many. We are a Caravan Club registered certified location and we also accept Britstops. Situated just off the A39, the farm has easy access to the cities of Bath , Bristol and Wells along with links to the Bristol Channel resorts of Weston-Super-Mare , Clevedon and Burnham on Sea. The site is located in a flat field with good access and sheltered by a mature hedge. Our 30-acre farm has a 1-acre paddock for Caravan Club pitches. The well-known Hunters Rest pub is further along Flatts Lane, with shops, a takeaway and another pub within 1 mile in the next village. Open all year. Arrivals: 11.00am to 6.00pm weekdays and 11.00am to 5.00pm weekends. Latest Departure: 10.00am. Facilities: 4 hard-standing and 2 grass pitches, electric hookup, fresh water and waste disposal. £10 per night per pitch, plus £5 per night for electricity. Booking in advance required. Book through the Caravan Club website: www.caravanclub.co.uk/certificated-locations/england/bath--north-east-somerset/bath/willow-farm-1 Britstops are also welcome via email: info@willowfarmgourmet.co.uk
tagline: Open all year round from 9.30am to 2.30pm Thursday to Saturday

title: The Billy Chip
subtitle: How it all began. The tragic death of Billy Abernethy-Hope in 2018, inspired his family to do something positive with all of their grief and saddness. Before Billy died, he came up with the idea of creating a system to support the homeless, avoiding the exchange of money and promoting kindness. The thought of giving cash to someone sleeping rough often deters people from helping, unsure if a donation will be used in a positive way.
bodyContent: The tragic death of Billy Abernethy-Hope in 2018, inspired his family to do something positive with all of their grief and saddness. Before Billy died, he came up with the idea of creating a system to support the homeless, avoiding the exchange of money and promoting kindness. The thought of giving cash to someone sleeping rough often deters people from helping, unsure if a donation will be used in a positive way. Good friends of Sakina, Jon and Sarah (Billy’s parents) and Meg, his sister have been working tirelessly to get the concept off the ground. The family organised Fest-a-Bill last year, in memory of Billy to celebrate his love of life, of which the awesome Professor Green made a welcome appearance. Almost 1,000 people attended the event raising £20,000, enough to launch the scheme. The response to the scheme has been incredible so far, with Bristol getting on board in a big way. It’s just the beginning of this incredible idea and we’re so glad to be a part of it. The story has been picked up by local and national press including the BBC and ITV. How it works You can buy a Billy Chip for £2 in participating cafes , to be given to someone on the streets. The chip can then be used to redeem a drink or something to eat in the participating venues. You can find all the cafes supporting the Billy chip on their website or by looking out for coffee shops displaying a Billy Chip window sticker. At the time of writing this blog, there are approximately 15 venues in Bristol and 1 in Bath. The intention is that Billy Chip becomes a national platform! Get Involved The following list gives you 10 ways you can show your support: Donate via our website when you shop with us (a £1 donation option is available in our checkout). Share this blog post on Social Media (using the buttons below) or leave a comment. Visit the Billy Chip website , find out more about their story and make a donation. Follow their progress on Instagram @thebillychip Like the team on Facebook TheBillyChip Follow their progress on Linked In Follow the journey on Twitter @thebillychip Like, share, comment, tag & tweet Billy Chip posts and drop the team an email – they’ll love to hear from you! Ask your local cafe if they’ve heard about the Billy Chip scheme and all tell your friends and family. Buy a chip in a participating venue and give one to someone in need. A random act of kindness spreads faith, hope, and charity, so please show your support and get involved today. We have various events in the pipeline, so please follow this amazing cause and see how wide it can spread.

title: Watchet Boat Museum
subtitle: Discover the fascinating history of the flatner the origins of which date back to before the Viking invasion. The story is celebrated through photographs, full size displays and local fishing paraphernalia. There is a collection of scale models on the upper deck, and activities for children to enjoy.
bodyContent: We are located opposite the West Somerset Railway station, adjacent to the Harbour Road car park, and accessed through Watchet Visitor Centre. The building was designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel and built in 1862 as a goods shed for the terminus of the Bristol and Exeter Railway. Its lofty roof creates an ideal space for displaying fully rigged boats. Interactive exhibits for children (and parents and grandparents!)) include dress-up and play in the play boat, a working ships wheel with engine room telegraph, and children’s trails and activity sheets. Learn how to catch salmon and fish for eels, see rope being made, learn how to tie knots and make an eye splice, and us old boys will teach Grandad to splice a mainbrace. Learn the lingo: What is a putcher? A grapple? How can you ride a mudhorse, and what is rayballing? The museum is run by volunteers from the Friends of the Flatner Association. It is our aim for you to have a good day and leave with new knowledge and experiences.
tagline: Discover the fascinating history of the flatner

title: The Sheppey Inn
subtitle: The Sheppey Inn lies out on the beautiful wilds of the Somerset Levels, surrounded by peat moors, dairy farms and national wildlife reserves.
bodyContent: The pub pulls in people from miles around thanks to the brilliant, eclectic musicians it attracts, its fine selection of local ales and ciders (including all kinds of one-offs and speciality brews), and its fantastic food. Spending the afternoon out here in the countryside, lounging by the river, looking out for voles and kingfishers, isn’t the worst idea in the world, is it? There’s been a pub in Godney servicing the thirsty throats of Levels farmworkers for many centuries. The last owners ran it for 120 years, but on one day in 1976, they ran out of cider and lost the trust of the next two generations of locals. the pub has been renovated, revamped and restored, and now has about six casks of grown-ups’ apple juice on the bar to make sure that the such a thing never happens again. Check out the photos on the right for proof.
tagline: The Sheppey Inn lies out on the beautiful wilds of the Somerset Levels.

title: The Barns at Quantock Lakes (Wedding Village)
subtitle: Quantock Lakes boasts stunning wedding accommodation that has been designed and brought to life by the family owners.
bodyContent: Bring your loved ones together from 4 pm on your wedding eve for pre-wedding celebrations and stay for 2 nights. There are three area’s of accommodation at Quantock Lakes; The Farmhouse, Quantock Barns and The Granary Barn. Our sleeping capacity with all three area’s is up to 62 guests. The Farmhouse is located next to the wedding venue and is always booked for 2 nights as part of your wedding package. With a sleeping capacity of up to 18 guests from your wedding eve. The Farmhouse boasts a bridal prep area, a bridal suite with a roll-top bath, hot tub, sauna and outside bar and barbeque. The Farmhouse is the most popular space for the Bride to get ready. Quantock Barns and the Granary Barn are optional extra accommodation and can be added at the booking stage. Quantock Barns is a courtyard of three barn conversions located just a short stroll from the venue with a sleeping capacity of up to 26 guests. Quantock Barns boasts a hot tub, games room, a bridal suite and picnic and barbecue area and is located a stone’s throw from the venue. The Granary Barn is a luxurious nine-bedroom barn conversion with a sleeping capacity of 18 guests. The Granary boasts an indoor heated pool, hot tub, open plan living space, nordic barbecue lodge, picnic and barbecue area, children’s play area and 2 master suites with roll-top baths. The Granary is the most popular space for the Groom to get ready.

title: Potter around Summer Walk Portbury Wharf...
subtitle: A former waste ground for dumping power station ash is now a tranquil nature reserve and thriving habitat for a wide variety of plants and animals.
bodyContent: How to get there Start at map ref: ST 486 761 Car: Park in a layby in Sheepway, just after the railway bridge. This holds about 7 cars. If full, there is another layby in Wharf Lane, just past Springfield Cottage. Bus: Services X2/X3 Portishead-Bristol stop next to the layby in Sheepway A former waste ground for dumping power station ash is now a tranquil nature reserve and thriving habitat for a wide variety of plants and animals. Portbury Wharf Nature Reserve lies between the eastern edge of Portishead and Portbury Dock and acts as a buffer between the town and Severn Estuary. For 50 years the site was a dumping ground for waste from Portishead’s now demolished power stations. The Village Quarter housing development now stands there with luxury apartments overlooking the water, and the nature reserve is a popular recreation spot. Many paths have been created to access the area, which includes two large pools, several ponds, rhynes, grazing marsh, hay meadows and hedgerows. Accessible, level paths go around the reserve and are suitable for bikes, wheelchairs and buggies. However, this Life walk follows the seasonal footpath which runs alongside grassy meadows. Enter the nature reserve from the Sheepway layby and follow the orange waymarker onto the paved path. Click HERE for full details and FREE PDF copy

title: Bodhi House
subtitle: Situated just over a mile from the centre of Bath, Bodhi House provides spacious, stylish accommodation slightly removed from the hustle and bustle of the centre.
bodyContent: Situated just over a mile from the centre of Bath, Bodhi House provides spacious, stylish accommodation slightly removed from the hustle and bustle of the centre. With commanding views over the city, the light and modern accommodation offers high levels of comfort and features furnishings and materials of the highest quality. Organic, local produce is served whenever possible. Bodhi House offers off-street parking if required, and a garden with views of the City of Bath and beyond. We offer a warm, informal welcome and will assist you with our helpful tips and information on how to make the very most of your stay in the glorious and historic City of Bath
tagline: Situated just over a mile from the centre of Bath, Bodhi House provides spacious, accommodation.

title: Beautiful loft room with views over Bath
subtitle: A bright and comfortable loft bedroom situated in a newly decorated and well equipped house just a fifteen minute walk away from the centre of Bath.
bodyContent: A bright and comfortable loft bedroom situated in a newly decorated and well equipped house just a fifteen minute walk away from the centre of Bath. This is one of four private rooms within the house. Situated in Oldfield Park and very close to Oldfield Park Train Station and local buses, this is a perfect base for exploring Bath. There is a free car park just fifty metres from the house which is a truly rare find in Bath! Four bedroom Victorian house retaining many period features. With an eclectic mix of individually furnished, quirky bedrooms and modern kitchen and bathroom. Stripped wooden floors in communal areas and 3 of the bedrooms with carpeted, snug attic room. Bright and airy and set over 3 floors. Easy off street parking. 200mb fibre optic broadband. Flat walk in to town (15 minutes walk/ 5 minutes taxi). 2 minutes walk to Oldfield Park Train Station (2 minutes to Bath Spa; 12 minutes to Bristol Temple Meads). The private double room benefits from use of a shared kitchen with breakfast bar. A comfortable living space in the centre of the house, with an extensive library of books for both the avid and casual reader. The property also boasts a garden at the rear; a great spot for relaxing during the summer months. I like to give guests their own space during their stay, however I am always available to offer recommendations and help, both before and during their stay. I am never far away or am in the house, and am always on hand should you need me. I usually arrange for a self check in but can always be on hand if a guest would like me to help them check in.
tagline: A bright and comfortable loft bedroom situated in a newly decorated and well equipped house

title: Beeches Farmhouse Ensuite Rooms
subtitle: Farmyard accommodation in Bradford on Avon near Bath, has double / twin and family en-suite rooms and all, except one, in detached converted farm buildings.
bodyContent: Farmyard accommodation in Bradford on Avon near Bath, has double / twin and family en-suite rooms and all, except one, in detached converted farm buildings, each having their own front door key and own patio area, giving you the independence to come and go as you please. All rooms have full en-suite facilities including bath and/or shower and are decorated to a very high standard with exposed beams, stripped wooden floors and country pine furnishings. During busy periods there is usually a minimum stay of two nights at weekends unless ‘last minute’. These rooms can be used with our self catering cottages for additional bedrooms. We also offer self catering cottages “Beeches Farmhouse Cottages”. Find out more>>
tagline: Farmyard accommodation in Bradford on Avon near Bath

title: Bath Townhouse 14
subtitle: Bath Townhouse is a beautiful Georgian townhouse situated in the centre of Bath.
bodyContent: Bath Townhouse is a beautiful Georgian townhouse situated in the centre of Bath. This townhouse is split in to two apartments; Bath Townhouse 14 and Bath Townhouse 8. They can be combined to sleep 23 or rented separately. This is a perfect location for groups of all kinds: mixed, female, male, families, wedding groups and corporate groups. The property has been lovingly restored and decorated to the highest standards in a modern vintage style which makes the most of the many original features, including the cornicing, Georgian fireplaces, original shutters , beautifully restored Georgian windows and original vault area. Both apartments are fully equipped for a self catering holiday break, with fully fitted kitchens, wide screen TVS, free WIFI and top quality bedding and towels. Bath Townhouse 14 has 6 spacious bedrooms, 4 beautifully presented wet rooms/bathrooms, an extensive lounge with modular, colourful seating, modern lighting, large kitchen with table and chairs for 14 people. Bars, restaurants, shops, and all Bath’s many interesting tourist sites are right outside the front door! The Roman Baths and Thermae Bath Spa are just a stones throw away. Bath Spa Train Station and Coach station are 5 minutes walk. Whether you are in Bath to watch Bath Rugby play at home at the famous Recreation Ground, visit your son or daughter at Bath University , have a little retail therapy in the great independent shops or enjoy the many festivals that take place in Bath then this is the perfect property for you and your group!
tagline: Bath Townhouse is a beautiful Georgian townhouse

title: Postscript
subtitle: Small but amazing independent stationery, arts and crafts, design and print shop in the heart of Frome. A small company with big appeal. An Aladdin's Cave of product, featuring brands like Lamy, Moleskine, Leuchtturm, Rhodia and many more.
bodyContent: Postscript was created in 2015 by Garry and Rachel who's team of creatives love design and all things art, craft and stationery. With an emphasis on sustainable and ethical product, Postscript verges on being a gift shop with plenty of diverse products to suit all ages, abilities and needs! Lacking creative ideas? Rachel's background in art and teaching makes her the perfect personal shopper - whether face to face, over the phone or via a Whatsapp video call! Bridie is Postscript's talented lead designer, and alongside Garry, who specialises in business and marketing, they offer design and print services for individuals, creatives and small and large businesses. From weddings to brand and packaging design, or business cards, or just simple quality printing, Postscript has something to offer everyone. Postscript has a high volume laser colour printer and a full colour wide format printer on site, and can print from A6 to A0 and beyond! They also outsource print commissions locally, where possible and always deliver the best value service in the business. "Postscript is not just our business, it is our way of life!" say Garry and Rachel. "We have a large and talented family, many of who have been and are still involved in the business. Our staff are our extended family and even Otis, our dog, is part of what we do!". Postscript have recently launched a website to offer most of their products and services to a larger audience.
tagline: Small but amazing independent stationery

title: Somerset Boat Centre
subtitle: A variety of ways to explore the beauty of Bridgwater & Taunton canal through our boat rental. Bar.
bodyContent: For boat and craft hire times please see our boat availability and booking section. Have you ever fancied messing about on the water? Ever felt that tingle of well-being and the sense of mindfulness being on or near water can bring? At Somerset Boat Centre we can offer you a variety of ways to get on or be near the water and have some fun. We offer canoes, kayaks, self-drive motor boats and a chartered narrowboat. In addition the centre itself is a fantastic destination for that special event with its unique location and brand new facilities. Somerset Boat Centre is a recognised RYA training centre for water related courses, alongside this we also offer other work based training programmes. We are a family business and have been on the water most our lives, the team here at ‘SBC’ are passionate about our inland waterways, in particular, the Bridgwater and Taunton Canal! Come along and meet the team, see the venue and boats and you’ll start to relax in minutes, as the old saying goes, time spent on the water is “The fastest way of slowing down” Check out What's On HERE Boats We have a range of boats available to hire to suit most needs and budgets. Please contact us to reserve the boat and date you want. Please pay attention to the terms and conditions of hire Skippered Narrow Boat Trips Available for morning, afternoon and evening cruises. A new trip narrow boat able to carry twelve passengers and two crew is available for private hire. Wheelchair Accessible Boat Trips Available to hire by the hour, minimum 1 hour maximum 3 hours. This is a specially adapted wheelchair accessible boat. We can carry up to 4 chair users and 4 carers, or a maximum of 10 passengers. (depending on size and weight of wheelchair) This comes with a skipper and those with upper mobility are able to have a go at driving with our unique helm position. Rowing Boats 4 seater rowing boats available to hire from 1 hour, very stable and dry boats ideal for those that want a little exercise! Day Boats Self drive day boats are available to hire on a daily basis and available all year. The Orkney dory’s can carry four people and are powered by new tohatsu 6hp engines. Full instruction is given before the hire starts. Please refer to hire agreement when booking. Canadian Canoes Pelican ram-x 3 seater canoes (or 2 adults 2 children) are available to book for an hour, half day or full day. Lifejackets and buoyancy aids will be provided. Kayaks We have single and twin seater Kayaks available to hire on a ‘turn up and paddle’ basis, however prior booking is advised. Paddle Boards We have stand up paddle boards available to hire, these are very stable and ideal for beginners, no need for wetsuits just wear comfortable clothing but bring some spare clothes just in case! Doggy Life Jackets & Dry Bag Ruck Sacks We have a some doggy life jackets and dry bag ruck sacks if available at the time of you booking.
tagline: A variety of ways to explore the beauty of Bridgwater & Taunton canal through our boat rental. Bar.

subtitle: A one-to-one, two-hour exclusive, behind the scenes experience with one of our dedicated elephant keepers. You can enjoy giving our elephants their breakfast and hiding treats in their enclosure, this is an experience you'll never forget!
bodyContent: Watch daily husbandry care being carried out by the keepers with protective contact training. This could include weighing, washing, skin and foot care. Exclusive experience for 2 hours with a keeper Entry to the zoo for participants Souvenir pack Please note: Elephant Eden at Noah’s Ark operates a Protected Contact Management System. Therefore, all activities are carried out from behind a protective barrier. There will be no physical contact and you will not be in the same enclosed area as the elephants at any time during this experience. You will need to have a good level of fitness to participate fully!

title: Montacute House, National Trust
subtitle: Montacute House is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design
bodyContent: Montacute House, Somerset is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design. With its towering walls of glass, glow of ham stone and its surrounding gardens, it is a place of beauty and wonder. Sir Edward Phelips was the visionary force and money behind this masterpiece, which was completed in 1601. Built by skilled craftsman using local ham stone under the instruction of William Arnold, master mason, the house was a statement of wealth, ambition and showmanship. Come face to face with the past in the Long Gallery; measuring over 52 metres, it is the longest of its kind in England. The Gallery houses over 60 Tudor and Elizabethan portraits on loan from the National Portrait Gallery. Beautiful gardens surround Montacute, constantly changing, filling the house with scent in summer and providing an atmospheric backdrop for a winter walk. Whether you just want to let the children run and explore, or be inspired by the collections housed within the walls of Montacute, you will leave with lasting memories and a desire to soon return. You may even recognise some of the sights, as Montacute House featured in the BBC’s highly acclaimed production of Hilary Mantel’s Wolf Hall. Within 20 minutes’ drive you will find four fascinating smaller properties, each with a unique character, history and story to tell. Their combined age of 2,300 years spans from the medieval period to the early 19th century. Explore Stoke Priory, a fine collection of medieval farm buildings; Treasurer's House, with its great hall and unusual wall painting; Stembridge Tower Mill, the last remaining thatched windmill in England; and the Priest’s House, a medieval home of great character not to be missed. While you’re in the area, why not also visit Lytes Cary Manor and Tintinhull Garden (see the National Trust website for more details).
tagline: Montacute House in Somerset is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design

title: Extours
subtitle: Step into a world where history comes alive and paranormal awaits! Extours is your gateway to extraordinary adventures through history with our thrilling ghost walks, immersive historical walking tours, and exhilarating paranormal investigations.
bodyContent: At Extours, we blend history and the supernatural to create unforgettable experiences, leaving you yearning more! For current availability just head over to the bookings section. Here you can select the date and time required from the available time slots and make your booking securely online. Information on our unique events can be found by navigating to that event using the buttons below. Shepton Mallet Ghost Walks Shepton Mallet is famous for having one of the most haunted prisons in the world. However, the prison is not the only place in this town where ghosts can be found! Join us for the Shepton Mallet Ghost Walk and hear intriguing stories from the towns past, learn about ghosts that are thought to haunt the area and get involved in some ghost hunting. Sedgemoor Batt lefield Ghost Walk Learn about the infamous Monmouth Rebellion at the very location where the Battle of Sedgemoor took place. Hundreds died on this battlefield so it is no surprise that this is a very active location. The Taunton Ghost Walk From Anglo-Saxon burial grounds to the infamous "Bloody Assizes" hundreds have been buried or executed at Taunton over the centuries. Join us and get involved with some ghost-hunting and learn fascinating stories from the history of the town. Watchet Ghost Walk The ancient harbour town of Watchet has a rich and fascinating history. If you would like to learn more and hear stories associated with the darker history of the town while getting involved with some ghost hunting then be sure to join us. Bridgwater Ghost Walk Join us for the historical walking tour of Bridgwater with a paranormal twist. The amazing history of this town often gets overlooked but there is so much to discover! You will also have the opportunity to get involved in some paranormal investigating for yourself. Dunster Ghost Walk After establishing ghost walks in a number of areas in Somerset I can safely say that Dunster is without a doubt the most haunted area that we cover! We will be back in October for the Dunster Ghost Walk. Be sure to join us and learn interesting stories relating to the towns past and people. You will also learn of many ghosts that are thought to haunt the area and have the opportunity to get involved with some paranormal investigating for yourself
tagline: At Extours, we blend history and the supernatural
