title: Wildwood Restaurants Taunton
subtitle: At Wildwood our aim is simple: A friendly team, serving great food, in a place where you can feel at home.
bodyContent: It all started in 2004 when we created a new Mediterranean pizza, pasta and grill concept. We collaborated with some exceptional chefs and operators to craft an eclectic menu, combining traditional European dishes with the best comfort food. We pride ourselves on quality – that’s both food and service – always. Our Taunton branch opened in 2015 and we made sure that the landmark Market House (built in 1772) kept many of its original features, creating a truly unique dining environment. Our well-balanced menu offers a wide grill selection and pizza and pasta dishes, as well as fresh salads, burgers, steaks, risottos and indulgent desserts. All produced using the best seasonal ingredients ensuring delicious food is served up every time. Little ones love our restaurants and the fun kids’ menu filled with age-appropriate activities and healthy food.

title: ChalkUp!
subtitle: Our bouldering wall, established in 2023, was designed to create a fantastic space for visitors to Somerset to explore bouldering. Be it a rainy day out with the kids, relaxing with a coffee while others do the hard climbing, or wanting to develop a newly-found skill in climbing, we have something for everyone.
bodyContent: Situated between Bridwater and Minehead by a rural village, with free parking, ChalkUp! is the ultimate way to spend a day when on holiday with kids without the need to go anywhere near a big city! We welcome anyone to this facility who is interested in giving it a go. This could be to try something new, to keep the kids occupied for the afternoon, for serious boulderers, or for outdoor climbers to be ready for a summer of climbing. No experience necessary; we provide climbing shoes; no need to book a time slot; you can choose to register online in advance or just turn up and register at the desk. No time limit to your climbing session so feel free to take breaks and enjoy a coffee and cake before getting back on the wall. If it’s a sunny day, why not take your coffee to our outdoor picnic area to enjoy the restful views during those must-have rest periods? Bouldering coaching is available on request, just ask our super-helpful staff. We also provide staffed kids’ parties with games and supervision all taken care of and a dedicated kids’ wall for younger children. There is a full fitness facility available free of charge for adult climbers to warm up and warm down. Don’t fancy climbing but want a great workout while on holiday…..we also provide top notch functional fitness classes and use of our wide ranging open gym facilities on a drop in basis. We hope to see you at the wall in the very near future!

title: The Ayrlington
subtitle: Built of golden Bath stone in 1874 by the architect J Elkinton Gill, the award-winning Ayrlington is a handsome listed Victorian house with exceptional views of the City and its medieval Abbey.
bodyContent: Built of golden Bath stone in 1874 by the architect J Elkinton Gill, the award-winning Ayrlington is a handsome listed Victorian house with exceptional views of the City and its medieval Abbey. Bath’s magnificent historic sites, speciality shops and excellent restaurants are all just a 5-10 minute level stroll away. The elegant and tranquil interior is a graceful blend of English and Asian antiques, artwork, fine fabrics and Egyptian cotton bedlinen – all 19 bedrooms have individual themes and are beautifully furnished, some with four-poster beds. We also offer a residents’ bar, secure private parking and is entirely non smoking. We do not accept children under 5 years of age. The Ayrlington was the proud recipient of a Silver-Gilt certificate at the 2014 Bath In Bloom awards.
tagline: Built of golden Bath stone in 1874 by the architect J Elkinton Gill

title: The Circus Apartment
subtitle: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses.
bodyContent: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the secluded private garden to the rear. With the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minutes walk The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the secluded private garden to the rear. With the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minutes walk. This contemporary apartment, in a warm palate of chocolate, plum and biscuit throughout, has undergone several transformations in its lifetime yet has retained all its period charm. The large sitting and dining room with sash windows overlooking two aspects of The Circus has two French style velvet sofas by a decorative fireplace. There is a TV with Blue Ray DVD and a separate radio with I-pod docking. A dining table seats four and a French style dresser contains crockery, cutlery and a selection of novels, films and games. The neat fitted period kitchen has an electric hob and oven, a microwave, a large fridge/freezer, and a dishwasher.. A large mirrored lobby before the bedroom which has fitted wardrobes and shelving leads to the spacious and comfortable bedroom which has a 6′ bed, a fitted wardrobe, a dressing table with storage and a tallboy and a cupboard containing a washer/dryer machine. A radio/alarm with I-pod docking is provided. The contemporary bathroom has smart cappuccino coloured tiling and contains a double ended bath with shower over, a hand basin with lots of storage under and a WC. The apartment has gas central heating, hair dryer, iron, microwave, dishwasher, towels and toiletries. A Free car parking permit is available as is free internet access.
tagline: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle

title: Old Stables: rural retreat, sleeps 6
subtitle: The Old Stables is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.
bodyContent: It is located in the beautiful Georgian village of Freshford which lies at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys in the southern Cotswolds. There are some wonderful walks to local pubs following the riverside and canals. All just 15 minutes from Bath by car but the secret of this location is the 9 minute train journey to Bath from the village station, just a short stroll from the cottages. A three bedroom cottage (two king and one twin-bed) with a fully equipped kitchen opening onto a dining room There is a separate living room with TV/DVD and two large leather couches . The living room has large patio doors that open up onto the courtyard area. The Old Stables can accommodate 6 people. This cottage has: Three bedrooms (two king size and one with twin beds) One family bathroom , a Living room with Freeview TV/DVD two large leather couches and a dining room with a table seating 6.The Kitchen is equipped with all the cookware you might need dishwasher along washing machine/dryer and Iron/Ironing board. Hairdryers , bed linen and towels are all provided in the bedrooms.We provide a “Welcome pack” of tea, coffee, sugar, milk, bread, butter, eggs and bacon. The cottage has Free WiFi. Neighbourhood overview: Freshford is a beautiful ancient village with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk from the cottage( The Inn at Freshford) that serves restaurant quality food and all the local beers and ciders.The village has an excellent fully stocked( from wine to organic humus!)community shop that also has a great cafe that serves lunch. There is also a local doctors surgery. The village is nestled at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys . The Kennet and Avon canal is a 15 minute walk from the cottage. Getting around: You don’t need a car to stay in the cottage. The village station is a few minutes walk away. Trains are hourly off peak and thrice hourly at peak times. Bath 9 mins, Bristol 22 mins. London Padington to Bath Spa 1.5 hours Bath Spa to Freshford 9 minutes Bath Spa to Freshford “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/bath-spa-to-freshford ” Freshford to Bath Spa “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/freshford-to-bath-spa ” There is also a local bus service to all the adjacent villages and Bath. The cottage has two parking spaces suitable for one medium and one small car or a single large SUV. Other things to note If you are a runner or keep fit enthusiast the owner is a qualified Personal Trainer (Bath Uni) with much Marathon and half marathon experience. She specialises in Ladies training. Please let us know if you would like guided running or some Personal Fitness training
tagline: The Old Stables is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.

title: Taunton Flower Show 2026
subtitle: Experience a festival atmosphere at the oldest flower show in the country, set in the heart of Taunton.
bodyContent: Taunton Flower Show is an annual two-day family show held on the first Friday and Saturday of August each year, attracting around 16,000 visitors over the two days. Established in 1831, Taunton Flower Show is the longest running Flower Show in the UK, and second oldest in the World. Set in the lovely surrounds of Vivary Park, the Show is a feast for all the family. Our fantastic competition marquee shows off the talents of our community and the floral marquee and designer gardens demonstrate national horticultural excellence. You will also find music, arena entertainment, local and national traders and fun for all the family. Save by purchasing your tickets in advance and enjoy a brilliant day out! Assistance dogs only allowed into the showground. Tickets on sale at Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: A vibrant festival surrounded by flowers

title: Legends talk of a winged Dragon
subtitle: Somerset's Fascinating Facts - Steeped in History and Mythology, the site of the long forsaken Cadbury Castle is an essential part of your visit to South Somerset.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"237"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

Cadbury Castle in Somerset, was a military stronghold for over 4000 years, the first earthen ramparts were raised in the Stone Age. During the Iron Age the fort was occupied by the Durotriges tribe (who gave their name to Dorset) and was where they made their stand against the invading Romans. They were ultimately defeated in AD 70, and the successful Roman aggressors went on to burn down the fort and surrounding village.

By AD 500 the fort was again standing tall, and was extended by Ethelred the Unready in

AD 1000, as a means of defence against the plundering Vikings. In the 16th century it was suggested that this site was indeed the stronghold of King Arthur during the 6th century and there is certainly plenty of archaeological evidence to suggest Cadbury Castle was an important fortification at that time.

Today, as you walk the earthen ramparts, the sigh of a cool northern wind eloquently speaks of the history this hill has seen and the many souls who once lived here. As you stand on the summit, alone except for the calling of crows or the rumble of distant thunder, it’s easy to become lost in the past, as Glastonbury Tor reaches out across the Somerset Levels before you and the Isle of Avalon sparkles.

‘LOCAL LEGEND TELLS OF A MIGHTY WINGED DRAGON THAT FLEW NIGHTLY OVER THE EXE VALLEY BETWEEN DOLEBURY HILL AND CADBURY CASTLE, GUARDING TWO HOARDS OF GOLD, WHILST LIGHTING THE NIGHT SKY WITH HIS FIERY BREATH.’

For more on Somerset's incredible history and heritage go to our interactive E Book.

title: Selworthy
subtitle: This delightful village of picturesque thatched cottages is part of the National Trust's huge Holnicote Estate, which takes in over 12,000 acres of Exmoor coast and countryside.
bodyContent: Things to do in Selworthy, Exmoor, Somerset - Selworthy is a delightful village of picturesque thatched cottages is part of the National Trust's huge Holnicote Estate , which takes in over 12,000 acres of Exmoor coast and countryside. The charm of Selworthy is the wonderfully preserved thatched cottages and the historic All Saints church. The church is perched on the side of the hill, and the view from the porch out over the Vale of Porlock to the moors beyond is quite superb. Highlights in the church include the 12th century font, painted nave ceiling, and 18th century gallery. A footpath from the village leads up to Selworthy Beacon, which offers excellent views in all directions.

title: Ferne Animal Sanctuary
subtitle: Ferne Animal Sanctuary is set within 72 acres of beautiful & protected countryside in the Blackdown Hills on the Devon/Somerset border. This charitable sanctuary takes in unwanted, abandoned and neglected animals and gives them a fantastic life either at the sanctuary or by finding them a special forever home.
bodyContent: Ferne Animal Sanctuary is set within 72 acres of beautiful & protected countryside in the Blackdown Hills on the Devon/Somerset border. This charitable sanctuary takes in unwanted, abandoned and neglected animals and gives them a fantastic life either at the sanctuary or by finding them a special forever home. Ferne Animal Sanctuary, located near Chard in Somerset, is a remarkable facility dedicated to the rehoming of dogs, cats, and horses. In addition to this, the sanctuary provides ongoing care and welfare for a wide variety of animals, including sheep, goats, cattle, pigs, geese, chickens, and an aviary housing birds from around the world. It is also home to smaller animals such as rabbits, guinea pigs, chinchillas and ferrets, ensuring they all receive the care and attention they need. Founded in 1939, at the onset of World War II, the charity was established to care for pets whose owners were going to war, or who had been displaced by the conflict. Over the years, it has forged strong connections with HM Armed Forces and the Royal Family. A typical visit to Ferne lasts between 90 to 150 minutes, during which visitors can enjoy observing the animals in their natural habitats. The experience includes a sensory garden designed to calm the senses with a variety of sounds, sights and smells. Visitors can explore the Willow Walk, which offers insights into animal care, as well as informative displays about our water voles, dragonflies, birds, and fungi. There's also a machinery wall showcasing equipment used throughout the years, along with a small play area for our younger visitors. Take the time to enjoy the stunning natural landscape of the Blackdown Hills from our viewing platform. Relax, gaze across the hills, and marvel at the beauty of nature at its finest. During the school holidays, Creative Corner offers a range of animal-themed activities and arts and crafts. We also host special events and workshops throughout the year, with full details available on our website. The Visitor Centre is open from 10 AM to 4 PM from Easter to October half term, though the shop and sanctuary are open every day, except Christmas Day, Boxing Day, and New Year's Day. Our well-stocked pet supplies and gift shop has everything you need for your animals, as well as delightful treats to tempt you. Dog friendly (dogs must be kept on leads) and accessible, Ferne has a good network of tarmac paths. However, due to the number of gates, we recommend that wheelchair users are accompanied. We have designated parking spaces for wheelchair users and visitors with special needs next to our Visitor Centre as well as in the main car park. All money raised goes to support our animal care and welfare. Unleash the Party Fun at Ferne Animal Sanctuary! title: The Bishop's Palace- Weddings
subtitle: Planning the wedding of the year in Somerset? Imagine starting your married life together in our breath-taking 800 year old medieval Palace.
bodyContent: Imagine starting your married life together in our breath-taking 800 year old medieval Palace. Walking over the drawbridge as - oh my goodness! - a “just married” couple, and joining your guests for a glass of bubbly, surrounded by 14 acres of stunning gardens. Picture your wedding breakfast, styled elegantly to compliment the history of the Undercroft, with your loved ones treated to the finest wedding breakfast ever tasted (their words, not ours). Stretch your legs in the Long Gallery for coffee & cake, before taking to the dancefloor and – let’s face it – showing off those champagne-infused dance moves. And most importantly, remember forever the sheer joy of those you love most as they shared your day in the most wonderful of surroundings. You don’t have to be royalty to celebrate your special day in a Palace - but we’ll treat you as if you were. Venue Hire Be a King and Queen for the day and exclusively hire the Palace and gardens - it’s just like having your own stately home! Princes and Princesses can hire the Palace buildings for the day and enjoy the attention they receive from our garden visitors. Or you can just enjoy evening parties, lunches or canapés and drinks and have photographs taken in the beautiful gardens - the choice is yours to create the wedding day you want. We have put together a choice of hire options so you can tailor your day to suit you and your guests. Have a look through our wedding brochure (download form below) to inspire you and then talk to us about your requirements. Our award-winning catering team will ensure that you and your guests have a beautifully catered wedding day, with a range of wonderful options to suit every budget. To download our sample wedding breakfast menu, click here . Planning Process Now for the fun part… The planning! Our dedicated wedding coordinator will work closely with you, advising about timings, décor, best use of space, and offering menu tastings. And who wants to be organising furniture arranging the day before their wedding? Not you. We’ll take care of setting up all the tables & chairs (according to your table plan) so you don’t have to. You’ll get to know us very well in the build up to your wedding, and we wouldn’t have it any other way. After all, you’ve entrusted us to deliver the biggest day of your lives so getting to know each other is essential. Extras Tempted by a whole weekend of wedding celebrations? Good news! We’re here 7 days a week, so if you like the idea of a pre-wedding dinner or BBQ in the gardens, photo sessions, or Sunday lunch the day after in The Bishop’s Table then you’re in the right place… To help you plan your day we’ve put together a list of wedding professionals who we think can add a little extra sparkle. All of them have worked with us before and have been hand picked by us because we love what they do. Drop us a line for more info about suppliers & accommodation. Book a viewing Sounding good? Time to arrange a visit to view the Palace and discuss your options? Contact our Wedding & Venue Manager, Bethany Hulme-Teague, on 01749 988111 ext. 209 or email weddings@bishopspalace.org.uk
tagline: Planning the wedding of the year in Somerset?

title: Chewton Mendip
subtitle: Chewton Mendip is a village and civil parish in the Mendip district of Somerset, England. It is situated 4 miles north of Wells, 16 miles south of Bristol on the Mendip Hills and is the source of the River Chew. The parish includes the hamlets of Bathway and Green Ore.
bodyContent: Image thanks to Paul Ashton Emery There were several lead mines and stone quarries in the parish. It is also the site of Attborough Swallet (also known as Red Quar Swallet), a cave which is unusual for a cave on the Mendip Hills in that it is not in limestone but instead in Dolomitic Conglomerateand Marl. The cave was first entered in 1992. There is a long barrow to the north of the village 100 ft (30 m) by 50 ft (15 m). Excavation in 1946 revealed six Bronze Age barrows below the crest of the Mendips. The shape of some of the existing fields suggest they are of medieval origin. The parish was part of the hundred of Chewton. On 12 June 1643 the village was the site of a skirmish in the English Civil War, between Royalist forces led by Robert Dormer, 1st Earl of Carnarvon and the parliamentary forces under William Waller including the cavalry unit of Sir Arthur Haselrig known as Haselrig's lobsters.

title: Montacute House, National Trust
subtitle: Montacute House is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design
bodyContent: Montacute House, Somerset is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design. With its towering walls of glass, glow of ham stone and its surrounding gardens, it is a place of beauty and wonder. Sir Edward Phelips was the visionary force and money behind this masterpiece, which was completed in 1601. Built by skilled craftsman using local ham stone under the instruction of William Arnold, master mason, the house was a statement of wealth, ambition and showmanship. Come face to face with the past in the Long Gallery; measuring over 52 metres, it is the longest of its kind in England. The Gallery houses over 60 Tudor and Elizabethan portraits on loan from the National Portrait Gallery. Beautiful gardens surround Montacute, constantly changing, filling the house with scent in summer and providing an atmospheric backdrop for a winter walk. Whether you just want to let the children run and explore, or be inspired by the collections housed within the walls of Montacute, you will leave with lasting memories and a desire to soon return. You may even recognise some of the sights, as Montacute House featured in the BBC’s highly acclaimed production of Hilary Mantel’s Wolf Hall. Within 20 minutes’ drive you will find four fascinating smaller properties, each with a unique character, history and story to tell. Their combined age of 2,300 years spans from the medieval period to the early 19th century. Explore Stoke Priory, a fine collection of medieval farm buildings; Treasurer's House, with its great hall and unusual wall painting; Stembridge Tower Mill, the last remaining thatched windmill in England; and the Priest’s House, a medieval home of great character not to be missed. While you’re in the area, why not also visit Lytes Cary Manor and Tintinhull Garden (see the National Trust website for more details).
tagline: Montacute House in Somerset is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design

title: Fyne Court
subtitle: Fyne Court is a hidden gem in the heart of the Quantock Hills. You can explore this wild garden and discover pieces of its history hiding in the undergrowth.
bodyContent: Fyne Court estate was the home of the Crosse family who lived here until the house was destroyed by fire in 1894. In our information room, you can learn more about Andrew Crosse, Fyne Court's most famous resident, known as 'The Thunder and Lightning Man' by the locals. There's plenty for the children to do including building a den, climbing a tree and hunting for bugs. Relax in our courtyard tea-room with a cream tea or a hot chocolate after a walk around one of the three waymarked trails. Dogs welcome on leads.
tagline: A nature reserve and visitor centre under the guardianship of the National Trust

title: Stay at Home for Somerset
subtitle: As the nation is now under further national restrictions encouraging people to stay home, Somerset County Council’s Public Health leaders are asking everyone in the county to pull together to keep coronavirus at bay and support the #StayHomeForSomerset campaign.
bodyContent: As the nation is now under further national restrictions encouraging people to stay home, Somerset County Council’s Public Health leaders are asking everyone in the county to pull together to keep coronavirus at bay and support the #StayHomeForSomerset campaign. Somerset has seen coronavirus cases rising at a steady rate. Although the local numbers seem comparatively low compared to other parts of the country, they have been, and continue to increase. Lockdown will be vital to flatten the curve – and bring the numbers back down – so all must play their part. The campaign wants to fire up the amazing community spirit shown in Somerset throughout the lockdown earlier this year – and recognise that “we are all in it together.” From now until December 2, the county council is asking people to take ‘selfie’, featuring the name of, or photo of, who they are staying home for. It could be to protect a vulnerable family member or friend or because you want to protect the NHS from extra pressure. The photos can then be uploaded to social media using the hashtag #StayHomeForSomerset. Find out how to get involved: https://somersetnewsroom.com/2020/11/06/stayhomeforsomerset/ South Somerset District Council Mendip District Council Sedgemoor District Council Somerset West and Taunton Avon and Somerset Police Somerset Activity & Sports Partnership - SASP Spark Somerset Community Council for Somerset Visit Somerset Somerset NHS Foundation Trust Somerset Community Foundation

title: Watchet Market House Museum
subtitle: Watchet Market House Museum houses a fine collection of local artefacts, fossils and marine paintings. The town’s rich maritime history features in many of the exhibits. With visitor numbers averaging 30,000 per season, this small Museum is a ‘not to miss’ attraction.
bodyContent: Located next to the harbour, where the Esplanade meets Market Street, Watchet Market House Museum occupies the ground floor of the town’s former Market House. We celebrated our 40th birthday in 2019. A special exhibition celebrates West Somerset’s Victorian industrial heritage when the West Somerset Mineral Railway carried iron ore from the Brendon Hills to Watchet for shipment to the steel making furnaces of South Wales. The Jurassic coast of West Somerset is highlighted with a splendid external window display describing it’s formation, with impressive fossils inside including an Ichthyosaur and a huge ammonite. A ‘Watchet Chronology’, is on display with a pictorial timeline by local artists telling the story of the town’s rich and varied past. These colourful displays will be of great interest to both young and old, as will the many photographs which will bring back many memories. Watchet’s rich maritime history is an important part of the museum and features in many of the exhibits on show with the ‘Yankee Jack’ statue and the ‘Ancient Mariner’ taking pride of place on the Esplanade.
tagline: Watchet Market House Museum houses a fine collection of local artefacts

title: The Red Lion Babcary
subtitle: Our award-winning, 17th century thatched pub and restaurant is set in the heart of this idyllic Somerset village, open every day of the year.
bodyContent: Oozing charm with traditional flagstone floors, exposed beams, open fires, cosy nooks and crannies and pretty garden. We offer everything from great local ales, inspiring à la carte menu, hearty Sunday lunch and outdoor wood-fired pizzas to individually planned weddings for up to 120 people. We are conveniently situated in a rural and peaceful location, just a few minutes north of Podimore roundabout on the A303 in Somerset, off the A37. Accessible down a winding country lane, you will stumble across us, past the village Church, open fields and a handful of stone cottages. We are very much a locals’ pub, welcoming familiar faces into our rural watering hole to sit, chat, eat and drink in these beautiful surroundings. Equally we love to see new faces who might be visiting this beautiful county – looking for their own ‘escape to the country’. The Red Lion is an ideal stopover point for lunch or an overnight stay on the way to Devon and Cornwall or back to London and the home counties.
tagline: Our award-winning, 17th century thatched pub and restaurant

title: Follow in the footsteps of poets
subtitle: Poets’ Walk is a little over a mile in length but the area includes a wealth of features, including limestone grassland, woodland, a rich diversity of wildlife, an Iron Age fort, Second World War shelter, and stunning views across the Bristol Channel. The site is managed by North Somerset Council with help from the Friends of Poets’ Walk volunteer group and, thanks to their hard work, some old footpaths have recently been opened up. Poets’ Walk is a tranquil route around Church Hill and Wain’s H
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: About 1.5 miles Difficulty: fairly easy – the route is short but there are lots of woody paths and steps. Wear suitable footwear. Duration: About an hour at a very leisurely pace Map: OS Explorer 153 Poets’ Walk is a little over a mile in length but the area includes a wealth of features, including limestone grassland, woodland, a rich diversity of wildlife, an Iron Age fort, Second World War shelter, and stunning views across the Bristol Channel. The site is managed by North Somerset Council with help from the Friends of Poets’ Walk volunteer group and, thanks to their hard work, some old footpaths have recently been opened up. Poets’ Walk is a tranquil route around Church Hill and Wain’s Hill. Its name is a reference to the English poets Samuel Taylor Coleridge and Alfred Tennyson, who visited Clevedon and were inspired by the time they spent there. Start this walk at Marine Lake, which underwent an £850,000 restoration last year. Click HERE for full details and FREE PDF copy

title: Beeches Farmhouse Self Catering Cottages
subtitle: The self catering cottages stand in the grounds of the idyllic 18th Beeches Farmhouse.
bodyContent: The self catering cottages stand in the grounds of the idyllic 18th Beeches Farmhouse, Bradford on Avon, near Bath having been tastefully converted from farm buildings and surrounded by open pasture with free range chickens, ducks, guinea fowl, English Setters and Shetland Ponies. Situated only a mile from the Saxon town of Bradford on Avon and seven miles from the World Heritage City of Bath. Each of the three, 2 bedroomed cottages has been imaginatively decorated with co-ordinated furnishings and rustic country furniture and those little extras not normally associated with a holiday cottage.

The recently refurbished Moncrate Cottage gives the perfect home-from-home feel that everyone wants on holiday. title: Bath Townhouse 8
subtitle: Bath Townhouse is a beautiful Georgian townhouse situated in the centre of Bath.
bodyContent: This townhouse is split in to two apartments; Bath Townhouse 14 and Bath Townhouse 8. They can be combined to sleep 23 or rented separately. This is a perfect location for groups of all kinds: mixed, female, male, families, wedding groups and corporate groups. The property has been lovingly restored and decorated to the highest standards in a modern vintage style which makes the most of the many original features, including the cornicing, Georgian fireplaces, original shutters , beautifully restored Georgian windows and original vault area. Both apartments are fully equipped for a self catering holiday break, with fully fitted kitchens, wide screen TVS, free WIFI and top quality bedding and towels. Bath Townhouse 8 has 3 spacious bedrooms, 3 beautifully presented wet rooms/bathrooms, a comfortable lounge with modular, colourful seating, modern lighting, fully fitted kitchen with table and chairs for 9 people. The lower ground floor has a additional entertainment area in the vaults, a great area if the ‘kids’ want their own space! Bars, restaurants, shops, and all Bath’s many interesting tourist sites are right outside the front door! The Roman Baths and Thermae Bath Spa are just a stones throw away. Bath Spa Train Station and Coach station are 5 minutes walk. Whether you are in Bath to watch Bath Rugby play at home at the famous Recreation Ground, visit your son or daughter at Bath University, have a little retail therapy in the great independent shops or enjoy the many festivals that take place in Bath then this is the perfect property for you and your group!
tagline: Bath Townhouse is a beautiful Georgian townhouse

bodyContent: Established in 1999 as a small family company The Somerset Toiletry Company has flourished into an International business with toiletries sold in over 50 countries. We are renowned for bath, body and home fragrance products that vary from richly classical to wonderfully innovative. We sell our own brands as well as working with large retail groups to design, formulate and manufacture their own private label goods. With an extensive range of products from shower gels and hand washes to lotions, soaps, diffusers, candles, perfume, toiletry bags, accessories, cards and more we have a wealth of experience and expertise . title: Clevedon Court, National Trust
subtitle: Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is a remarkable survival from the medieval period.
bodyContent: Clevedon Court in Clevedon, Somerset, National Trust property is an outstanding 14th-century manor house and 18th-century terraced garden Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is a remarkable survival from the medieval period. The house was purchased by Abraham Elton in 1709 and it is still the much-loved family home of his descendants today. Explore the striking display of Eltonware pottery and a fascinating collection of Nailsea glass.
tagline: Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is remarkable.

title: The Curzon Cinema Clevedon
subtitle: The Curzon cinema has been at the centre of life in Clevedon, North Somerset, since 1912.
bodyContent: The Curzon cinema has been at the centre of life in Clevedon, North Somerset, since 1912. One of the country’s oldest, continuously running cinemas: screening everything from blockbusters to classics and arthouse cinema, hosting live comedy and events in a beautiful heritage venue. Opening its doors in 1912, only 5 days after the Titanic disaster, the Curzon is one of the country’s oldest, continuously running cinemas. Enlarged in the 1920s, the neo-classical building houses a 320-seater auditorium, panelled in a rare example of pressed tin; a bar; a 1930s Christie pipe organ and a unique collection of cinema equipment. Alongside our varied film programme, we host live comedy, music and performance and are fully engaged with youth, arts and other community organisations, also running Front Room Cinema which takes the cinema experience out to residential homes. We are supported by a fantastic team of volunteers, who support our Front of House staff, help in the bar, give guided tours and help to maintain our lovely building. Click here you’re interested in finding out about volunteering at the Curzon.
tagline: The Curzon cinema has been at the centre of life in Clevedon, North Somerset, since 1912.

title: Fleet Air Arm Museum
subtitle: The all-weather attraction is the perfect place for all the family. With immersive experiences like the Search and Rescue Sea King Helicopter walk through and a walkthrough of the iconic Concorde 002.
bodyContent: This year make sure to set your sights on the Fleet Air Arm Museum in Ilchester and see where time flies. This must-see attraction has four large exhibition halls each containing dozens of incredible aircraft which tell the rich history of naval aviation. Grab your wingman and step inside the first British Concorde, experience the thrills of a working flight deck, and get up close to a wide range of rare and historical aircraft.
tagline: The all-weather attraction is the perfect place for all the family.

title: Pulteney Guest House Bed and Breakfast
subtitle: Pulteney House Bed and Breakfast is a large, elegant Victorian house set in its own picturesque west facing gardens, with fine views of Bath Abbey only 10 minutes’ level walk from the centre of Bath.
bodyContent: Pulteney House Bed and Breakfast is a large, elegant Victorian house set in its own picturesque west facing gardens, with fine views of Bath Abbey only 10 minutes’ level walk from the centre of Bath. The Bed and Breakfast has 16 rooms with en-suite facilities, and 1 with private facilities that are opposite the room. We offer a range of room types including family rooms, single rooms, double and twin rooms. A limited number are ground floor rooms. Pulteney House has been privately owned since 1979 and we provide a warm homely welcome to all guests. The large mature gardens are always kept in beautiful condition and guests are encouraged to utilise them where children can play in absolute safety. A comfortable family TV lounge is available for guests to use and relax in away from their room. Private onsite car park with CCTV for added security and peace of mind. Free Wi-Fi in all rooms and public areas. Free use of computer for those guests with no personal device. A large and varied Breakfast menu is available and we cater for a range of specific dietary requirements.
tagline: Pulteney House Bed and Breakfast is a large, elegant Victorian house

title: The Bird
subtitle: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to. A place to work and meet and by day and discover ever-changing bar experiences by night.
bodyContent: To be found just a few minutes’ stroll from Bath’s spectacular city-centre attractions, The Bird in Bath (previously The County Hotel) has re-branded to fit in with its distinctive new personality as part of the Kaleidoscope Collection. Owned by seasoned hoteliers, Ian and Christa Taylor, The Bird is a name that better reflects the vibrant transformation of the hotel, which has already seen refreshed public spaces, additional bedrooms, a new bar, relaxed restaurant and meeting spaces, as well as a much-loved pop-up beach bar for summer. Now with 27 en-suite bedrooms featuring every home comfort, many have far-reaching views across the cricket and rugby grounds to Bath Abbey, with the rolling hills of Bath and beyond. Breakfast is served in a lovely bright dining room, which overlooks Bath Abbey and opens into the conservatory, where morning coffee and afternoon tea can be enjoyed, while the Taylors have also created a wonderfully eclectic neighbourhood bar with relaxed food offering, designed as social hub for work or play. A space for freelancers to work, friends to meet for coffee or a relaxed dinner, there’s a bar for seasonal drinks and various seating areas centred around vast contemporary pieces of art. A separate meeting room also provides a creative space for workshops and get-togethers, private parties, celebrations and more. Visitors and locals alike won’t have to wait long for the next seasonal pop-up, a visually exciting Winter Wonderland for the festive season, and arguably the coolest party space in town. Set in a fantastical venue full of surprises, woodland branches and spruces will be strewn with fairy lights, tables topped with flickering candelabra and chairs draped in Bavarian rugs to keep you cosy. Everyone is welcome to simply drop in to experience the magical vibe. The Bird is easily reached via all main approaches to Bath, and has plenty of parking for guests.
tagline: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to

title: The Rising Sun Inn
subtitle: Book direct to get the best price at our hotel in Bath city centre.
bodyContent: Book direct to get the best price at our hotel in Bath city centre, a traditional English pub, dating from the 1700s. We’ve brought it bang up to date with a clean, fresh decor; subtle, modern lighting; and a warm, friendly atmosphere. We’re Just off the famous Pulteney bridge, right in the heart of historic Bath and we’re less than two minutes walk from the shops, restaurants, and attractions. title: The Apartment, Bath
subtitle: An exceptional two-bedroom luxury holiday home in central Bath, loved by guests for its perfect location, stylish decor, comfort, cleanliness and first class self-catering accommodation.
bodyContent: From Nespresso to Nintendo, The Apartment, Bath is an excellently-located two-bedroom apartment in central Bath. The first bedroom is a large, bright double bedroom with king size bed (or twin beds on request). The open fireplace and large sash windows are elegant original features and south-facing views take in the length of Ralph Allen Drive and Widcombe Hill. At the rear of the property, the second bedroom is a well-proportioned double bedroom, featuring a comfy double bed, original fireplace and built in wardrobe. The homely lounge is flooded with light from the large, original south-facing 16-pane sash window. The room hosts an extendable dining table and chairs, designer sofa (which can convert to a sofa bed) and a feature armchair. Brimming with technology, the lounge is equipped with satellite TV, blu-ray player, Nintendo Wii and wall-mounted 40” Samsung LCD TV. A well-equipped and cleverly designed galley kitchen features high-end integrated appliances to meet your every need, including a built-in double oven and sleek induction hob, full suite of cooking facilities and an integrated NEFF fridge with ice-box. A Nespresso machine and milk frother are provided for that much needed espresso or cappuccino to kick-start your day. And there is a washer dryer, so you can pack a little lighter! The newly renovated bathroom features a large walk-in rain shower with separate handheld spray. A chrome towel rail is complemented by a lit, motion-activated mirror cabinet featuring de-mist function and integrated razor/electric toothbrush socket. This gorgeous two-bedroom holiday home in central Bath is ranked in the ‘10 Best Holiday Homes in Bath’ by Booking.com and consistently rated positively by guests.
tagline: An exceptional two-bedroom luxury holiday home in central Bath

title: Devonshire House
subtitle: Established in a building dating back to 1880 and once used as a Victorian Grocers shop.
bodyContent: ⭐ Book Direct for Reward Card Offers Established in a building dating back to 1880 and once used as a Victorian Grocers shop, Devonshire House has been fully renovated into the stylish Bed and Breakfast it is today. Within a twenty minute walk of the city, on a major bus route into the city and with plenty of free on street parking, Devonshire House offers a convenient base to explore the city and surrounds. Local owners Chris and Louise are on hand to give as much or as little advice as you want, to make your stay even more enjoyable. Each room is individually decorated, en suite, with tv and dvd player, beverage tray, fluffy white towels and plump feather duvets (do tell us before your stay if you need hypo allergenic). Two doubles, a twin and a triple bedded room, plus a holiday cottage which sleeps up to four are available. A lounge is for guest use, with squashy sofas, up to date magazines and the local paper, imbibe in a Harveys Bristol Cream sherry with our compliments and relax after your day or plan the next one with all the information and leaflets to hand. The choice to book a room only rate or breakfast included, is yours, breakfast is served in the light and airy breakfast room between 8 am and 9 am. A buffet is laid out, with juice, yoghurt, fresh fruit, cereals and a selection of breads and jams for you to help yourself and then either a traditional Full English breakfast or smoked salmon and scrambled eggs can be pre chosen, along with freshly brewed coffee or a pot of tea from the selection available.
tagline: Established in a building dating back to 1880 and once used as a Victorian Grocers shop.

title: Oliver Randall - Writers in Whites
subtitle: As part of the Taunton Literary Festival's Autumn Festival of Talks, Oliver Randall explores the fascinating links between cricket and some of Britain's best-loved writers. Drawing on new research, he uncovers the influence the game had on literary culture from the late nineteenth century through to the 1960s.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Join writer, historian and cartoonist Oliver Randall as he discusses Writers in Whites, a study of the influential network of cricket-playing writers who helped shape English literary culture. From P.G. Wodehouse and J.M. Barrie to Arthur Conan Doyle, the book explores how cricket influenced some of Britain's most celebrated authors. Drawing on extensive new research, Randall reveals the connections between writers, their cricketing circles and the wider literary world, while examining the role the sport played in cultural life between the 1880s and the 1960s. Oliver Randall completed his doctoral thesis, Cricket, Literary Culture and Englishness, 1887–1968, in 2026 and has written for a range of publications, including the Times Literary Supplement. He has also worked as a historical researcher and cultural tour manager. This event offers readers, history enthusiasts and cricket fans the chance to discover an unexpected chapter in Britain's literary and sporting history. Tickets Available on the Website
tagline: Discover the surprising connection between cricket and Britain's literary greats.

title: Paulton
subtitle: Paulton is a large village with approximately 2,620 homes, located to the north of the Mendip Hills and is one of the largest in Bath & North East Somerset. Paulton is a former coal-mining village and the name Paulton is thought to have derived from the word ‘peall’ meaning village on the hillside.
bodyContent: Paulton is a large village with approximately 2,620 homes, located to the north of the Mendip Hills and is one of the largest in Bath & North East Somerset. Paulton is a former coal-mining village and the name Paulton is thought to have derived from the word ‘peall’ meaning village on the hillside. There are many groups and clubs active in the village, including sport, socialising, educational subjects and spiritual needs, providing many opportunities to get involved with the community. Paulton is very lucky to have three recreation areas, with all the parks and open spaces beautifully maintained and offering a variety of facilities: The Memorial Park is renowned in the local district for its play area and facilities, which include tennis and basketball courts for public use. These are checked and cleaned daily. Tennis rackets and balls are available to borrow from the parish council office thanks to the kind donation of the playing equipment from Camvale Tennis Club. The outdoor gym is free to be used at any time by anyone over the age of 14 years and can be found adjacent to the children’s play area. The children’s’ play equipment accommodates children from the very young to teenagers and it has been known that a few adults have been seen enjoying a swing! There is seating in the play area enabling adults to sit and watch their children or be ready to help them on the various pieces of equipment. Each summer the Memorial Park is the venue for Party in The Park, a free event for all, which features various stalls, attractions, food, drink, bands and displays, such as Karate. The Junior school puts on a fabulous dance display. The Miners’ Welfare Recreation Ground is home to local junior football teams who play at weekends during the season; Paulton Bowls Club have a very nice club house and green and the Scout and Guide movement have their headquarters in a multi-use building which enables them to hire it out to various other groups in the village. The Wallenge Open Space is another area with an assortment of children’s’ play equipment, although not as much as can be found in the Memorial Park. There are beautiful walks in and around the village and some are of historical interest, with Paulton Basin just north of the village being one. It had a dry dock for the barges that used to carry coal from the pits and was the terminus of the Somerset Coal Canal. In the same area you will find Paulton Engine, which was a foundry, now recently renovated into a family home and studio. Paulton was home to the now sadly closed Polestar/Purnell printing factory, along with Ashman’s boot factory where ‘Voidax’ safety footwear was manufactured and, in particular, motorcycle speedway boots. The village has some fantastic amenities, including a small Hospital with Maternity unit and Minor Accident department, a Doctor’s surgery, various Nurseries, Paulton Infant and Junior Schools, a Swimming Pool, Library, Café, Shops, Supermarket, Vet, Dentists, Restaurant, Takeaways, Pubs, Fire and Ambulance stations. The Parish Council has a website www.paultonparishcouncil.org.uk and a Facebook page, along with two noticeboards – one at the village hall and the other in Hill Court shopping precinct. These various forms of communication provide useful sources of information for our residents, including details of all council business. Each year, residents show their respect at a service at Double Hills to remember the pilots and soldiers who were killed when their glider crashed many years ago en route to Arnhem. A service of Remembrance also takes place at the War Memorial and is attended by many residents, some who are related to those killed in the two world wars. Christmas sees the Christmas Market & Lights Switch On which is organised by Paulton Parish Council and is an extremely popular event.

title: Taunton
subtitle: As befits a County Town, Taunton is steeped in history and has much to entertain our visitors, from the superb Somerset Museum in the remnants of the castle to the Cricket Ground and Racecourse. A centre for Arts and Culture, it has shops, cafes, restaurants, riverside walks and a weekly Farmers’ Market. Rooted between the majestic Quantock Hills, Somerset Levels and the woodland-cloaked Blackdowns, Taunton’s lively nature plays host to major sports centre Somerset County Cricket Club. It’s also
bodyContent: Things to do in Taunton Taunton’s ideal location and identity as county town of Somerset makes it perfect for exploring the wider area of Taunton Deane - everywhere from the cattle-grazed meadows of the Somerset Levels to the windswept heights of the Quantock Hills and striking Blackdowns . It also boasts an impressive cultural offering, ranging from museums and ancient monuments like the ancient Taunton Castle to contemporary centres like the Brewhouse Theatre & Arts Centre. Explore the Museum of Somerset , based at the 12th-century Taunton Castle, and follow Somerset’s history from prehistoric times to the present day. Stunning Perpendicular Gothic style architecture can be found soaring 163 feet above Taunton at the historic St Mary Magdalene Church, while Hestercombe Gardens are a paradise for nature lovers with fifty acres of enchanting gardens, stunning terraces, lakes and cascades. Taunton’s town centre is a mecca for shopping, with well-known high street brands and a brilliant selection of eateries and bars, as well as pubs serving locally-sourced food and drink. Take the Taunton Heritage Trail’s self-guided tour around the town’s historical sites to ensure you don’t miss a thing. Featured in the trail you’ll find Bath Place, a picturesque narrow street with 19th-century shop fronts now brimming with independent retailers and cafés. At the top of the high street proudly sits the Victorian-designed Vivary Park, home to the annual Taunton Flower Show, proudly described as the ‘The Chelsea of the West’. Taunton’s world-class sporting scene doesn’t disappoint. Catch a lively cricket match at The Cooper Associates County Ground or visit the Somerset Cricket Museum to explore the game’s fascinating history. Soak up a thrilling atmosphere at the Taunton Races or attend one of the racecourse’s brilliant events throughout the year, ranging from rural shows to concerts and circuses. For a quieter affair, the tranquility of Trull meadows and waterfall make them the perfect spot for a picnic or follow the towpath of the Bridgwater and Taunton Canal for a picturesque cycle ride. Taunton Visitor Centre Now based in the western wing of the landmark Market House, the Taunton Visitor Centre is the place to go to make the most of your time in Taunton. The county town has plenty to offer from individual boutiques to historic architecture, modern dining to traditional tea rooms and unspoilt views to the Blackdown Hills and Quantock Hills (both Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty). Taunton offers a wide mix of activities, attractions and events - we can’t wait to help you plan the perfect trip! Services offered: The Taunton Visitor Centre holds information on many wide and varied things to do within Taunton and the surrounding areas. Now a part of the bustling town centre mix, we welcome over 100,000 visitors and local residents through our doors each year. The Visitor Centre Box Office offers tickets for most local and regional events taking place, including the hugely popular Taunton Flower Show. We are a box office for the Brewhouse Theatre and Tacchi-Morris Arts Centre in Taunton and the Playhouse Theatre in Weston-super-Mare. If you're looking for that special "experience" gift then give the gift of theatre with our Theatre Tokens Gift Cards. The Travel Centre acts as an agent for Bakers Dolphin, Berry’s Coaches, Falcon bus service, Holiday Extras and National Express. As well as the booking service we offer friendly advice for local transport, parking and accommodation to make your trip stress-free. We also offer multiple advertising and marketing opportunities to local businesses, events organisers, charities and more. Souvenirs and Publications: The Visitor Centre shop is bursting with products that will help you take home a taste of Taunton, including locally produced biscuits and preserves, hand-crafted cards and a variety of colourful souvenirs. We also stock a large range of local maps, guides and books to help you truly discover Taunton and the surrounding areas.

title: Prior Park Landscape Garden, National Trust
subtitle: Beautiful and intimate 18th-century landscape garden.
bodyContent: Beautiful and intimate 18th-century landscape garden. One of only four Palladian bridges of this design in the world can be crossed at Prior Park, which was created in the 18th century by local entrepreneur Ralph Allen, with advice from 'Capability' Brown and the poet Alexander Pope. The garden is set in a sweeping valley where visitors can enjoy magnificent views of Bath. Restoration of the 'Wilderness' has reinstated the Serpentine Lake, Cascade and Cabinet. A five-minute walk leads to the Bath Skyline, a six-mile circular route encompassing beautiful woodlands and meadows, an Iron Age hill fort, Roman settlements, 18th-century follies and spectacular views. Current project to repair the historic dams is due to finish in 2022.
tagline: Beautiful and intimate 18th-century landscape garden.

title: Longleat
subtitle: Explore a world of adventure at Longleat. From a Drive Through Safari expedition, to discovering inside our iconic Elizabethan mansion, there’s plenty to entertain you.
bodyContent: Explore a world of adventure at Longleat. From a Drive Through Safari expedition, to discovering inside our iconic Elizabethan mansion, there’s plenty to entertain you. Travel the globe within this Wiltshire estate – stop off at African Village for a chance to see our new pack of African painted dogs, herd of Grants zebras and leap with lemurs. Say hi to our cheeky monkeys and bring your pack to meet our pack of wolves! Listen out for the Longleat lions’ roars as you explore. Continue your adventure on foot and walk with mischievous meerkats in Jungle Kingdom, feed rainbow lorikeets and watch our playful giant otters. Don’t forget to visit Koala Creek to see England’s only resident koalas, watch our sleepy sloths climb around or check in with our native red squirrels. Hop on board the Boat Safari and explore Half Mile Pond. Home to our family of noisy Californian sea lions, views of Gorilla Colony and Colobus monkeys will make quite a splash. Why not feed the sea lions to add to your unique day out? All aboard Longleat Railway! Enjoy a delightful ride around the lake and keep an eye on the action from our miniature railway. Or discover more about our history by adding a guided house tour to your itinerary. If your little cubs are looking to play, be sure to visit Little Explorer’s Garden and the Adventure Castle for plenty of room to let their imaginations run wild. Why not challenge yourself to our Hedge Maze and see if you can find your way through the winding passages? And no day is complete without a ride on Rockin’ Rhino! Book your tickets for a day out like no other or make your visit extra special with a VIP experience!
tagline: Longleat, nestled within 900 acres of ‘Capability’ Brown landscaped grounds.

title: Sports Clubs and Sporting Venues
subtitle: Taunton and the surrounding area has a great range of sporting venues and fixtures. It is the place to get your sporting fix!
bodyContent: The Cooper Associates County Ground in Taunton is the home of Somerset County Cricket Club who have played there since 1882. It plays host to a range of matches from T20 to International competitions. Situated within the wonderful grounds of Vivary Park, Taunton Bowling Club offers a warm welcome to all, regardless of age or ability. Taunton Racecourse is set in the heart of the Somerset countryside just a short distance from the centre of Taunton. Visitors enjoy national hunt racing featuring some of the biggest names in the sport. Photo courtesy of Bob Young Taunton Rugby Football Club is home to Taunton's National team, the Taunton Titans and is proud to champion every level of rugby. Taunton Tennis Club is based at Taunton Tennis Centre which is part of Blackbrook Leisure Centre and offers six floodlit outdoor courts and six indoor courts. Taunton Town Football Club (also known as The Peacocks) compete in the Southern League Premier Division South and play their home matches at their Wordsworth Drive ground which they moved into during the 1953 season.
tagline: Taunton and the surrounding area has a great range of sporting venues and fixtures.

title: Hestercombe House and Gardens
subtitle: Discover Somerset and lose yourself in fifty acres of lakes, temples, cascades, tranquil woodland walks, formal terraces, vivid colours and views that take your breath away…..
bodyContent: Discover Somerset and lose yourself in fifty acres of lakes, temples, cascades, tranquil woodland walks, formal terraces, vivid colours and views that take your breath away….. Hestercombe's famously restored gardens span three centuries of garden design and provide important examples of gardens in contrasting styles that continue to grow and develop. The restored 17th century watermill complex showcases historic uses of renewable energy alongside the original working mill machinery. The award-winning visitor facilities include the warm and welcoming Stables Restaurant with a bright, airy courtyard, gift shop and plant centre. Inside the historic Hestercombe House find Hestercombe Contemporary Art Gallery, gallery shop, second-hand bookshop and period rooms, providing lots more to see and do, whatever the weather.

title: The Bridge Bakery and Canteen
subtitle: Local organic products used as much as possible. Plastics used as little as possible. Theatre-style food production with happy smiley staff!
bodyContent: We’re a couple who live locally, love the town and the river, love the building that we’re in and have designed and created not just a bakery and canteen but also a communal hub where locals and visitors alike can enjoy a quick coffee or leisurely afternoon tea and cake or even an early supper. We work as a small team making quality foods using as much local and organic ingredients as possible. The cider is Perrys near Ilminster, the beer is Fine Tuned in Somerton, and we even have wines from Smith and Evans just up the road for which we helped to pick the grapes ourselves last year! We are a collection point for veg boxes from Plotgate and we have our own giant one every week. All our friends have helped with building the furniture, painting and decorating and turn it in to the lovely space it now is. We have added a new table outside overlooking the river and just need to build some more benches for them. Great food, including sourdough breads and pastries, prepared and produced in front of you with more than an eye on our ecological and environmental footprint. Local beers, ciders and even wines on sale. Facilities Bakery and canteen all on ground floor with tables inside and out. Help-yourself tap-water. Fully licensed. Vegetarian and vegan options. Wheelchair, child and dog friendly with disabled loo and baby-changing area.
tagline: Local organic products used as much as possible.

title: Westonzoyland Pumping Station Museum
subtitle: For a great family day out, visit us to discover one of the largest collections of working steam engines and pumps in England, at the home of Somerset’s first Steam Powered Pumping Station, established in 1830. Our friendly, knowledgeable volunteers will make your day with us a great success.
bodyContent: The use of steam power on the Somerset Levels, to control drainage of the low-lying moorlands, commenced at Westonzoyland in about 1830 when the first of eight pumping stations was built on the east bank of the River Parrett. The original pump was replaced in 1861 by the unique ‘Award Winning’ Easton Amos land drainage machine. This is preserved in working order in its original engine house and demonstrated on steam days, being capable of pumping 100 tons of flood water per minute, the equivalent of emptying 7 bath tubs a second. The original buildings are Grade II* listed. These, together with our modern exhibition hall, engine shed and pump room, house one of the largest growing collections of working stationary steam engines, pumps, winches and turbines in England. Steam is raised from a 1938 Marshall Portable Boiler, which has been fully restored. Many of our engines have been manufactured locally or have connections to Somerset’s industrial heritage. They have driven brickworks and breweries, powered hospitals, hauled milk tankers and pumped creosote, to name just a few of their uses. Ride behind an industrial locomotive on our 2’ narrow gauge railway, which is used for passengers and giving demonstrations. Enjoy light refreshments in our Café when we are in steam. Browse our Gift Shop, which stocks speciality books. Dogs Welcome on a lead, including in cafe
tagline: For a great family day out, visit us to discover one of the largest collections

title: The Mendip Inn
subtitle: The Mendip Inn is an exciting country pub and coaching rooms concept at the foot of the Mendip Hills, near Glastonbury, owned and run by hospitality entrepreneur, Matthew Lowe.
bodyContent: Styled by the talented team behind Jamie Oliver’s Fifteen restaurant, The Mendip Inn takes the concept of a great British Pub and adds an exciting, contemporary style of its own, to the food and design, without losing that sense of welcome you receive at the very best pubs. First class service is at the heart of all that we do. The Mendip Inn offers a fantastic, modern and fresh à la carte menu, seven days a week. We have a weekly specials menu, highlighting local, seasonal produce, cooked to express the flavours of the ingredients, with a twist on exceptional pub recipes. Wednesday is Steak Night, Friday is Fresh Fish Friday, with fresh market fish specials each week, and Sundays are, of course, for fabulous traditional roasts.
tagline: The Mendip Inn is an exciting country pub and coaching rooms

title: Beautiful views over Barrow Gurney
subtitle: Barrow Gurney is a pretty village close to Barrow tanks, three artificial reservoirs which supply drinking water for Bristol. Public footpaths near the tanks have recently been restored and stiles have been replaced with kissing gates so access to this area is now easier.
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: Just over 4 miles Difficulty: medium-difficult depending on fitness, as there is a long uphill section up Dundry Hill. Some parts can get quite muddy so wellies are recommended, especially in winter. Duration: 2-3 hours at a leisurely pace Map: OS Explorer 154 Barrow Gurney is a pretty village close to Barrow tanks, three artificial reservoirs which supply drinking water for Bristol. Public footpaths near the tanks have recently been restored and stiles have been replaced with kissing gates so access to this area is now easier. From Barrow Street, next to the Prince’s Motto pub, take the first right, a small lane which veers uphill. This joins Hobbs Lane. Follow the Sustrans route 334 sign through the gate onto the traffic-free section of Hobbs Lane. Follow it all the way to the end and you will come out on the A38. Turn left onto this and cross the road carefully. The public footpath starts on your righthand side, opposite Lakeside Spas. Go through the kissing gate into the field, and veer to the right-hand corner, between the hedgerows. Click HERE for full details and FREE PDF copy

title: Chestnuts House
subtitle: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden and private off street parking.
bodyContent: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden and private off street parking. Set in the heart of the beautiful Georgian city of city. It is ideally situated off the main roads and adjacent to Henrietta park, but within a few minutes level stroll of the city centre with its many attractions, restaurants and excellent shopping centre. The House is built from natural Bath stone and has four beautifully decorated and furnished ensuite guest rooms, some with king size and wrought iron beds. Owners Toni and Dawn have created a splendid and delightful bed & breakfast with superb hospitality in a relaxing atmosphere, all the necessary ingredients for making your stay in Bath a truly memorable experience. Guests Chestnuts House has 5 individually themed ensuite rooms which can accommodate a total of 11 persons. Three Superior double bedded rooms, one family/twin room (max 3 persons) and one Classic double room Bedrooms The bedrooms have recently been refurbished to an exacting standard and have been tastefully decorated and beautifully furnished. All rooms have en suite bathrooms with bath and shower, hairdryers and large fluffy towels. The rooms have comfortable and relaxing beds with crisp cotton sheets, air con, remote flat screen colour television, radio, free wireless internet access and refreshment trays. Bathrooms All bedrooms are ensuite with large fluffy towels and White Company products. The superior & twin/family rooms are ensuite with bath & power shower. The Classic room is ensuite with walk in power shower. Kitchen Enjoy your inclusive breakfast in our light and airy dining room overlooking the garden. During the summer months breakfast can be served al fresco. Our breakfast includes both organic and local produce. As well as the traditional English breakfast, we offer smoked salmon with scrambled eggs and homemade blinis, poached buttered kippers (smoked haddock with poached eggs). There is also an extensive buffet table with fresh fruit salad, freshly baked pastries, cereals, yoghurts. We are happy to cater for special dietary requirements. Entertainment The Lounge has a large flat screen Television with both Sky & BT Sport Channels. Free internet wi-fi is available throughout Outside Chestnuts House is situated in a residential street with a small private walled garden for guests to enjoy and just 10 minutes walk to the centre. General Points Chestnuts House is situated in a residential street with private off street parking and just 10 minutes level walk to the city centre. Parking Chestnuts House has both private off street parking and parking permits available for Guests to use. This service is free of charge. Smoking Chestnuts is a non smoking establishment Children Family room can accommodate up to 3 guests. Children of all ages are welcome. Pets Unfortunately Chestnuts House does not accept pets
tagline: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden

title: Bright private double bedroom

bodyContent: A quirky and comfortable double bedroom situated in a newly decorated and well equipped house just a fifteen minute walk away from the centre of Bath. This is one of four private rooms within the house. Situated in Oldfield park and very close to Oldfield Park Train Station and local buses, this is a perfect base for exploring Bath. bodyContent: Walks from your doorstep, fresh air, country Pubs and a Farm Shop. Yet, close proximity to Bath (5 miles) and Bradford on Avon (2 miles) means that they get the best of both worlds! Guests can make use of the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool during their stay. Local Farm Shop village shop and village pub within walking distance or a short drive. title: Pearled Spelt, Pancetta & Lemon Broth
subtitle: Sharpham Park introducing an Italian-inspired broth that's made with tender grains of pearled spelt simmered in a lemon and fennel-scented chicken broth with nuggets of pancetta and winter greens. Tip with parmesan and then snuggle down to dinner.
bodyContent: Serves 2-4, 55 Minutes Ingredients: 1 onion 1 carrot 1 fennel bulb 2 garlic cloves A handful of rosemary, leaves only 2 tbsp olive oil 100g cubed pancetta 100g Sharpham Park pearled spelt 1 tsp fennel seeds 750ml hot chicken broth or stock 1 bay leaf 1 lemon 100g greens (collard, kale, cabbage, chard) Parmesan, to serve For method and more information visit https://www.sharphampark.com/recipes/article/159-pearled-spelt-pancetta-lemon-broth
tagline: Sharpham Park introducing an Italian-inspired broth that's made with tender grains

title: Cheddar Gorge & Caves
subtitle: Cheddar Gorge & Caves boasts extraordinary subterranean show caves, awe-inspiring cliffs and holds many fascinating secrets about our prehistoric ancestors.
bodyContent: Our Day Ticket gives access to six great attractions: Gough’s Cave: Prepare to be amazed by our stunning show cave featuring spectacular stalagmite and stalactite formations created over 500,000 years ago! See cheddar cheese maturing in the caves, view the site where Cheddar Man’s 10,000-year-old skeleton was discovered and learn about the extraordinary DNA discovery. A free audio guide is available in six languages, and there is also a special version for children. Cox’s Cave featuring Yeo’s Journey: The Power of Water. This spectacular immersive multimedia experience tells the captivating story of how our iconic caves were formed and evolved through the ‘Power of Water’. The story is brought to life using state-of-the-art animation, sound, lighting and colour. Beyond the View: Take a seat in front of our state of the art 270-degree screen. Discover historic tales, enjoy breathtaking aerial panoramic views, and learn about the special wildlife and plants that call the gorge home. Museum of Pre-History: Discover amazing artefacts unearthed in the Cheddar area that help tell the story of how people lived thousands of years ago. Jacob’s Ladder & The Lookout Tower: Venture up the 274 steps to the top of the gorge with rest stops along the route to admire the view. Marvel at the panoramic views and mosaic of landscapes across the Mendips and Somerset Levels. Cliff­ -Top Walk: Hike the 3-mile loop around the gorge. Look out for the wildlife and enjoy the stunning scenery. If you don’t have time to do the full circuit, you can go for a shorter walk up to the Pulpit Rock look out point, and head back down the ladder. Gough’s Café Sit back, relax, and take in the beauty of the gorge at Gough’s Cafe, close to the entrance of Gough's Cave. Enjoy a thirst-quenching chilled drink, warm yourself up with a hot beverage or choose from a selection of alcoholic drinks. Serving light lunches, delicious snacks, cream teas and delicious cake, to include vegetarian and vegan options. Enjoy the spectacular views from the comfort of our air-conditioned cafe or relax on the large patio where dogs are welcome. We even have a welcome bowl of water for our doggy friends. Our small play area for under 2-year-olds will keep the little ones entertained too! Accessibility Cheddar Gorge & Caves provides accessible toilets, free parking for blue badge holders and free admission for carers accompanied by a full paying visitor. The audio tour of Gough's cave is printed in braille. Assistance Dogs are permitted, and the museum is wheelchair accessible with lift. Those with severely restricted mobility or who are wheelchair dependent will find areas of Cheddar Gorge & Caves inaccessible. If you have any questions prior to your visit, please email Guest Services on info@cheddargorge.co.uk or call 01934 742343. Dog-Friendly Dogs are welcome in all attractions and water bowls are provided in the cave entrances, shop and café patio. Family and Children Cheddar Gorge & Cave is family friendly. We have baby changing facilities, buggy parking and are breast-feeding friendly. Gough’s café has a small play area for under two year olds, water refills and highchairs are available. Entry is free for children under the age of 5 years. Groups Cheddar Gorge & Caves has special group rates, coach parking and drop off points for group tours. We offer discounted exclusive group sessions for Rocksport adventure activities – adventure caving, rock climbing and freefall. Special Events We have a fantastic programme of events throughout the year to keep the whole family entertained, including the school holidays. Visit our What’s On page for more details. Thirst for adventure or a puzzle-solving mind? Rocksport: Imagine climbing the gorge rockface in the shadow of the 450ft cliffs, caving deep underground or taking part in our exhilarating Blackcat freefall in Gough’s Cave. Suitable for all abilities. Sessions available for adults and children aged 8 years and over. Escape Rooms : Up for a challenge? Our two Cheddar-themed rooms, Caved In and The Vault will test your brain power as you race against the clock to try to escape. Double the fun with our Ultimate Escape combo ticket at a discounted rate. Suitable for 12 years and over in groups of up to six people. Nature, wildlife, history, adventure - experience the wonder on an all-season day out in Somerset. For more information on how to plan your day at Cheddar Gorge & Caves and to book please visit www.cheddargorge.co.uk
tagline: Explore Britain’s biggest gorge, from the stunning stalactite caverns to the dramatic cliffs.

title: Victoria Art Gallery
subtitle: Opened in 1900, the Victoria Art Gallery boasts an outstanding collection of paintings, sculptures and decorative arts. The gallery is located in the centre of Bath, near the famous Pulteney Bridge. Entry to the permanent exhibitions is free.
bodyContent: Opened in 1900, the Victoria Art Gallery boasts an outstanding collection of paintings, sculptures and decorative arts. The gallery is located in the centre of Bath , near the famous Pulteney Bridge. Entry to the permanent exhibitions is free. You’ll see more than 1,500 artworks, including many by artists who have lived and worked in the Bath area, such as Thomas Gainsborough and Walter Sickert. The work on show spans the 15th century to the present day. In the 18th century Bath was an important centre for portrait painting, and in the 20th century it again became famous thanks to the innovative works being produced by artists at the renowned Bath Academy of Art at Corsham Court. Alongside the permanent collections, the Victoria Art Gallery also hosts an exciting programme of temporary exhibitions and events throughout the year. Please check the Victoria Art Gallery website for the latest information.
tagline: Opened in 1900, the Victoria Art Gallery boasts an outstanding collection.

title: Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Mendip Activity Centre is the ultimate outdoor adventure playground in Somerset. They’ve been delivering adventurous outdoor activities for nearly 40 years, growing from humble beginnings to the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West!
bodyContent: It’s Time for Adventure with Mendip Activity Centre! Nestled in 250 acres of ancient woodland in the Mendip Hills National Landscape, Mendip Activity Centre is the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West. Just 20 minutes from Weston-super-Mare and Cheddar and open year-round, Mendip have been delivering Adventure, Learning and Training for individuals, families, schools, and groups since 1987. Activities available include: · Air Rifle · Tobogganing · Archery · Skiing · Snowboarding · Frisbee Golf · Kayaking · Nerf & Gel Battles · Caving · Paddle Boarding · Rock Climbing · Axe Throwing · ArcheryActive · Abseiling · Canoeing Come for the day or stay longer. In summer, pitch your tent at the award-winning Mendip Basecamp (link to https://mendipbasecamp.com/), a family adventure campsite awarded second at the Visit England Awards 2025. Pitch where you like, check out when it suits, camp fires encouraged, dogs welcome and endless adventure is on offer! Adventure for Everyone Mendip is more than just activities. It’s a place to switch off from screens, reconnect with nature, and each other. Whether you're learning something new, developing an existing skill or simply having fun outside, you’ll leave with muddy boots and big smiles. We believe in adventure for everyone. Many of our activities are adaptable for additional needs, and our friendly team will work with you to make it happen Refuel at the Alpine Lounge Overlooking the Ski Slope, the Alpine Lounge café serves pizzas, paninis, coffee and cake with stunning views- perfect for après-adventure refreshments

subtitle: An elegant Georgian House, dating back to 1735, built of classic honey coloured Bath stone.
bodyContent: An elegant Georgian House, dating back to 1735, built of classic honey coloured Bath stone. The dignified exterior conceals more than half an acre of magnificent walled gardens with splendid views out over the City of Bath. Small and privately owned, our aim is to offer the best personal service with attention to every detail. Bath Paradise House has 11 delightfully appointed rooms, all are individually styled to provide a mix of traditional elegance and modern comfort. Paradise House is a luxurious boutique B & B in Bath just 10 minutes walk from the town centre.
