title: Old Parsonage House
subtitle: Old Parsonage House is ideally situated in the heart of the pretty village of Beckington, just a short drive from the historic city of Bath.
bodyContent: Old Parsonage House is ideally situated in the heart of the pretty village of Beckington, just a short drive from the historic city of Bath. Privately owned and run by Tim and Jo guests are greeted with a warm welcome to Old Parsonage House which has been completely renovated assuring your stay will be relaxing and comfortable. With plenty of free private parking and excellent places to eat within a short walking distance Old Parsonage House is well situated for your visit to Bath, Longleat and the surrounding area.
tagline: Old Parsonage House is ideally situated in the heart of the pretty village of Beckington

title: Percy Place
subtitle: Period holiday apartment in Bath sleeping 7 people at walking distance from the city centre with free on street parking.
bodyContent: Percy Place is a holiday apartment in a Grade II listed Georgian house in the City of Bath. The house used to be the home of Rev. William Jay, one of the most eminent English Congregationalist preachers of Regency England who used to preach in the Argyle Chapel in Bath at the end of 1700s. We like to make our guests feel at home and highly valued. The original Georgian features of the building are enhanced by the stylish decor of the rooms such as antiques, trinkets and period furniture. At the same time, free wi-fi and a recently refurbished kitchen offer modern comfort. Both the town and the countryside are on our doorstep. We are just a few minutes walk from the city centre between the up and coming ‘Artisan Quarter’ bristling with local independent shops, and Larkhall village, a pretty quarter with a local butcher, a deli, a theatre and a few restaurants. We are also very close to the Kennet & Avon Canal at the back of Kensington Meadows. The view of the countryside and back garden from the back of the house is relaxing and inspiring.
tagline: Period holiday apartment in Bath sleeping 7 people at walking distance from the city centre

title: The Old Granary – Sleeps 12
subtitle: A stunning converted barn sleeping up to 12 people, set in a peaceful countryside location.
bodyContent: This detached barn is 3/4 of a mile from Church Farm along a country lane. It has its own landscaped garden and private driveway with plenty of parking. Use of the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool and Games Room 3/4 of a mile away at Church Farm – Sleep up to 12 – 6 miles from Bath – Rural Retreat
tagline: A stunning converted barn sleeping up to 12 people, set in a peaceful countryside location.

title: Bloomfield House
subtitle: Bloomfield House, a Georgian detached Grade II listed building, has elegant and romantic rooms (four posters or half testers) fine art, antiques, splendid views all combined with environmental credentials and a friendly relaxed atmosphere.
bodyContent: The House Bloomfield House, a Georgian detached Grade II listed building, has elegant and romantic rooms (four posters or half testers) fine art, antiques, splendid views all combined with environmental credentials and a friendly relaxed atmosphere. The house is set well back from a quiet road. Well behaved children and pets are welcome. The Breakfast Our traditional full English breakfasts are freshly cooked to order and served from 7.30 am until 11 am. Ingredients are mostly organic, fair-traded and provided by local suppliers, including homemade preserves and artisan breads. Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options are always available. The Parking We have free off-street parking and an electric car charging point for our guests use. There is easy access to the city centre via a regular bus service which stops within a few feet of the entrance to our property. The walk into town is a downhill stroll of 20 mins, on the way back up – jump on the bus or grab a cab! . The Bedrooms All bedrooms have en-suite facilities and come with the usuals – TV, hospitality tray, toiletries, hair dryer. The guest bedrooms are situated on the second floor, we have no lift so are not suitable for those with mobility issues. We are, of course, happy to help you up the stairs with your luggage. On the upside this does mean each room has far reaching views. Please note, for those with allergies , that this is a family home and we have both cats and dogs on the premises. The cats do not have access to the guest bedrooms (nor do our dogs for that matter). DISCOUNTS Any mid-week stay (Sun-Thurs ) will attract a £10 discount. Please quote ‘Stay in Bath’ when booking (by phone) on 01225 420105. Any on-line booking – applicable discounts will be deducted upon check-out. (This sadly cannot be used in addition with other special offers.) We also offer discounts to those arriving in Bath by train or bus. Discounts do not apply to Bank Holidays or one night Saturday bookings which are, on occasions, available.
tagline: Bloomfield House, a Georgian detached Grade II listed building

title: Horseshoe Cottage, Lime Kiln Farm
subtitle: Horseshoe is the largest of our three beautiful luxury self catering holiday cottages set in stunning Somerset countryside just 15 minutes drive from Bath.
bodyContent: Horseshoe is the largest of our three beautiful luxury self catering holiday cottages set in stunning Somerset countryside just 15 minutes drive from Bath. The views are wonderful and there is a large private garden, perfect for family parties or BBQs. This converted stable building has two large ensuite bedrooms, sleeping up to 6 and is renovated to a very high standard, complete with all modern conveniences including free WIFI . The cottage is all on one level and suitable for wheelchair users. With easy access to the Bath Park & Ride, we are also perfectly located for exploring the many tourist attractions including local pubs and Lavender Farm, Cheddar Gorge, Wookey Hole Caves, Wells, Stourhead House & Gardens and the nearby Longleat Safari Park.
tagline: Horseshoe is the largest of our three beautiful luxury self catering holiday cottages

title: Stapeley Cottage
subtitle: Stapeley is a popular choice of cottage when looking for the family. The comfortable and well-equipped property has everything you should need for your time away.
bodyContent: Stapeley is a popular choice of cottage when looking for the family. The comfortable and well-equipped property has everything you should need for your time away. Families can enjoy the rural surroundings and experience life on our working sheep farm. Unwind in the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool and Games Room.
tagline: Stapeley is a popular choice of cottage when looking for the family.

title: Burys Cottage
subtitle: Burys Cottage has a cosy and romantic feel to it being tucked away in the furthest corner of the row of cottages.
bodyContent: Burys Cottage has everything you should need for a romantic getaway. The cottage has a double bedroom with ensuite bathroom. It is ideally located between Bath (5 miles) and Bradford on Avon (2 miles). The popular ‘Longleat House and Safari Drive -Through’ is 12 miles (30% off gate price tickets available for our guests when purchased online – if booked at least one week in advance). Church Farm is a working sheep farm in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. There is a luxurious indoor heated indoor pool (12m x 5m) onsite, perfect for guests whatever the weather. Burys Cottage has its own individual patio area with table, chairs and sun parasol. Farm shop and country pub/s within walking distance. Kennet and Avon Canal nearby for boating, cycling and walking. The cottage features a country feel with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams with soft furnishings to compliment. Enjoy admiring the sheep in the fields surrounding the farm. Welcome cream tea on arrival. Free Wifi.
tagline: Burys Cottage has a cosy and romantic feel to it

title: The Bird
subtitle: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to. A place to work and meet and by day and discover ever-changing bar experiences by night.
bodyContent: To be found just a few minutes’ stroll from Bath’s spectacular city-centre attractions, The Bird in Bath (previously The County Hotel) has re-branded to fit in with its distinctive new personality as part of the Kaleidoscope Collection. Owned by seasoned hoteliers, Ian and Christa Taylor, The Bird is a name that better reflects the vibrant transformation of the hotel, which has already seen refreshed public spaces, additional bedrooms, a new bar, relaxed restaurant and meeting spaces, as well as a much-loved pop-up beach bar for summer. Now with 27 en-suite bedrooms featuring every home comfort, many have far-reaching views across the cricket and rugby grounds to Bath Abbey, with the rolling hills of Bath and beyond. Breakfast is served in a lovely bright dining room, which overlooks Bath Abbey and opens into the conservatory, where morning coffee and afternoon tea can be enjoyed, while the Taylors have also created a wonderfully eclectic neighbourhood bar with relaxed food offering, designed as social hub for work or play. A space for freelancers to work, friends to meet for coffee or a relaxed dinner, there’s a bar for seasonal drinks and various seating areas centred around vast contemporary pieces of art. A separate meeting room also provides a creative space for workshops and get-togethers, private parties, celebrations and more. Visitors and locals alike won’t have to wait long for the next seasonal pop-up, a visually exciting Winter Wonderland for the festive season, and arguably the coolest party space in town. Set in a fantastical venue full of surprises, woodland branches and spruces will be strewn with fairy lights, tables topped with flickering candelabra and chairs draped in Bavarian rugs to keep you cosy. Everyone is welcome to simply drop in to experience the magical vibe. The Bird is easily reached via all main approaches to Bath, and has plenty of parking for guests.
tagline: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to

title: Ben Kane - A Land Aflame
subtitle: Join bestselling historical novelist Ben Kane as he discusses A Land Aflame, the latest instalment in his epic series set during the Second Punic War. Exploring conflict, survival and power struggles across the Roman world, the event offers an opportunity to hear from one of the UK's most successful historical fiction authors.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Join Sunday Times bestselling author Ben Kane for an evening celebrating A Land Aflame, a gripping historical novel set in 211 BC during the ongoing conflict between Rome and Carthage. The story follows Hanno and Aurelia, shipwrecked and taken prisoner after fleeing Sicily, while Aurelia's brother Quintus is posted to Spain under the command of Scipio. Against a backdrop of endurance, siege warfare and major battles, the fate of the war hangs in the balance as Rome and Carthage continue their struggle for supremacy. Born in Kenya, Irish by blood and now living in Somerset, Ben Kane has travelled to more than 60 countries and all seven continents in pursuit of his passion for history. He has walked hundreds of miles in Roman military equipment, leads historical tours in Europe, and has written twenty novels, eleven of which have reached the Sunday Times Top Ten bestseller list. This event offers readers and history enthusiasts the chance to learn more about Kane's research, inspiration and latest work. Tickets Available on the Website
tagline: An evening with bestselling author Ben Kane discussing his latest historical epic.

title: History & Heritage
subtitle: Uncover Somerset's rich history and heritage, from ancient landmarks like Glastonbury Abbey to historic villages and iconic sites like Wells Cathedral. Discover centuries of stories that shaped this captivating county.

title: Williton
subtitle: Williton, in Somerset is a small town, home of West Somerset Council, situated on the junctions of the A39 and A358 roads from Minehead to Bridgwater and Taunton respectively.
bodyContent: It boasts a number of shops, 2 small supermarkets, several pubs and a library. Williton also is a station on the West Somerset railway , although the station is a little way out of the town. Nearby on the A39 road to crossroads at Washford Cross lies several large radio masts, one of the distinctive landmarks of West Somerset. Adjacent to this landmark is the tourist attraction of Tropiquaria, a small wildlife and aventure park.Also nearby is a Bakelite Museum.

title: WWT Steart Marshes
subtitle: A sprawling nature reserve in Somerset, managed by WWT, the charity for wetlands. Open all year round with free admission, visit for a walk or event and be inspired by the superpowers of wetlands.
bodyContent: Steart Marshes offers a peaceful and ever-changing landscape of saltmarsh, mudflats, and freshwater wetlands. The reserve is home to a rich variety of wildlife, including otters, dragonflies (designated a Dragonfly Hotspot by the British Dragonfly Society), hares, and thousands of migratory birds. The site is open all year round and free to access. A network of paths lead you round the reserve, much of which is accessible for wheelchairs and cyclists. Visitors can deepen their experience by joining the knowledgeable staff or volunteers for guided walks, pond-dipping and seasonal events. This is a fantastic way to explore the reserve, meet like-minded people, and discover the incredible role wetlands play in our world. Find out what upcoming events they have to offer on their website or contact them directly for a bespoke tour. Dogs are welcome at Steart Marshes but must be kept under close control at all times to protect wildlife. Please visit their website for more information. On Sundays there is usually catering on site with hot drinks and delicious treats in the car park from 11am until 3pm. Check @wwtsteartmarshes on Facebook for updates.
tagline: One of the UK’s largest wetland reserves, offering a vital habitat for wildlife.

title: The Chalice Well
subtitle: Historical well with legends in Glastonbury, Somerset.Chalice Well at the foot of Glastonbury Tor.
bodyContent: Chalice Well is one of Britain's most ancient wells, nestling in the Vale of Avalon between the famous Glastonbury Tor and Chalice Hill. Surrounded by beautiful gardens and orchards it is a living sanctuary in which the visitor can experience the quiet healing of this sacred place. Over three acres of peace. For over two thousand years this has been a place where people have gathered to drink the waters and find solace, peace and inspiration. At present we work with the theme of 'Many Paths, One Source' to welcome all people of goodwill to the gardens throughout the year. We also mark 'the wheel of the year' at regular intervals with events of celebration, silence and meditation, and conversation. This includes an evening programme of music, poetry and performance throughout the summer months in our candlelit gardens.
tagline: Historical well with legends in Glastonbury, Somerset.Chalice Well at the foot of Glastonbury Tor.

title: Somerset Lavender
subtitle: Buy gorgeous lavender products directly from the people who grow it in the stunning Somerset countryside.
bodyContent: Somerset Lavender in Somerset offers a shopping experience with a difference. Surrounded by the soothing presence of the lavender fields, you can browse our lavender product range in comfort and then relax with tea and cake in our on site café. We stock a wide range of gifts and lavender products made from the lavender grown on our farm. Products range from the lavender essential oil, distilled naturally on the farm using steam, to toiletries and soft furnishings. Our highly sought after honey made by the bees in the lavender field is certainly one to try but do hurry as stocks are limited due to the nature of this product. Lavender plants are also available for purchase. Somerset Lavender in Somerset will be open for six weeks from the 9 th November. A great opportunity to do some relaxed Christmas shopping. Wide range of unique gifts only available on the farm. Cafe will be open too, meet up with friends for a coffee and a chat. Hope to see you soon.

bodyContent: The Orangery Lawn at Hestercombe is just one perfect setting available for your dream wedding. title: Watchet
subtitle: Watchet, Somerset, maritime history colours every part of the town while the wild beauty of its coastline is untouched with ancient ammonite fossils lying on the shore, just waiting to be found.
bodyContent: Watchet port, in Somerset was highly valued by Alfred the Great, as he attempted to fend off the Vikings, and it even had its own mint, producing coins. Before that there was an Iron Age fort that has fragments still evident today. The port came into its own once again in the 19th century when iron ore from the nearby Brendon Hills was exported to Wales. In 2000, the harbour was converted into a modern Marina. Watched over on one side by the 150 year old lighthouse and on another by a statue of Coleridge’s Ancient Mariner, the quay makes for an interesting stroll with views across the Bristol Channel. Several boats offer fishing trips. There are plenty of other walks around Watchet, from day long rambles along parts of the Coleridge Way, The Mineral Line or the West Somerset Coastal Path, to shorter circular saunters in the surrounding countryside. For details on walks visit the Tourist Information Centre. The West Somerset Railway , brought here by Brunel, stops at the picturesque station in Watchet, next to the Marina and town centre. Passengers can spend time in one of the many bars and cafes or visit one of the Museums before resuming their journeys. The Market House Museum covers the fascinating history of a town where kings, queens, murderous knights, pirates, saints and even a famous singing sailor have their stories to tell. The Boat Museum houses an intriguing collection of local flat bottomed boats. The town is packed with independent shops full of antiques, vintage, craft and gifts. There are various art shops and galleries throughout the town as well as East Quay , a gallery and artist studios with restaurant and places to stay on the harbourside. Watchet is lucky enough to have not one but two beaches. To the east of the harbour you’ll find Helwell Bay, rich in fossils - ammonites, bi-valves and ‘Devil’s Toe Nails’. West Street beach has a wonderful old boating lake, extraordinary rock formations with quartz and alabaster running through them, as well as plenty of rock pools to explore. If you’re lucky, you might even spot the resident Peregrine Falcons along with Oyster Catchers and Egret.

title: Dovery Manor Museum
subtitle: Housed in a small, 15th Century Manor House, Dovery Manor Museum provides a unique insight into the history of the Exmoor village of Porlock and the nearby communities. Explore the beautiful Grade II* listed building, the delightful garden and the fascinating collection of artefacts, photographs, press cuttings and paintings.
bodyContent: Discover a fine example of a small, Grade II* listed, 15th Century Manor House in the delightful Exmoor village of Porlock. The building is partly made of Welsh stone, with handsome beamed ceilings, richly traceried windows and stone fireplaces. It was extensively restored in c1895 by Edmund Buckle for Sir Charles Chadwyck-Healey. Explore the inner hall with its wonderful fireplace featuring a fine ogee-headed lintel, and then climb the decorated, stone newel staircase to the upper floor. See local life and history portrayed through artefacts, costume, photographs, ceramics, tools, and domestic items. Examine our collection of Waistel Cooper’s work. Waistel (1921-2003) was a potter who worked at Culbone for 27 years and gained great respect for his concern with form and texture. Visit our annual summer exhibitions in the museum Solar, which focus on local events or visiting artists. Enjoy an evening’s entertainment when the history of the village is brought to life by the Museum Players, through performances of story, song and poetry. Dovery Manor Museum is keen to engage young people's interest in local history and can open for pre-booked school groups throughout the year. We are a learning destination for the Children's University. Rest awhile in the museum garden with its wide-ranging views across Porlock to the moors and the sea. It is evolving into a garden which reflects the early days of the Manor, through plants grown for medicinal and culinary use, and its evolution to modern times.
tagline: Housed in a small, 15th Century Manor House, Dovery Manor Museum

title: The Red Lion West Pennard
subtitle: Barrie brings over 15 years experience in the hospitality industry, including at some of Somerset’s best quality pubs and hotels, as well as popular venues in London.
bodyContent: Along with his hobby of interior design, Barrie has brought fresh ideas to the newly named The Lion, and hopes to keep developing the pub’s look into the future to attract both locals, and those from afar who want a traditional British stay in the heart of Somerset. Steeped in history, The Lion dates back about 500 years, and was built when King Charles I was on the British throne and even before the famous Gunpowder Plot of 1605. Originally constructed as a house, for centuries the quirky building has been welcoming visitors as a traditional British pub. With its low ceilings, exposed beams and homely inglenook fireplaces, it has all the charm of what you expect from a historic pub and restaurant. Listed as one of the Britain’s most important buildings, this is a slice of history set right in the heart of the Somerset countryside in a popular English village. The characterful and homely rooms offer a comfortable stay for those wanting to holiday or spend a night or two in this stunning part of the UK.
tagline: Barrie brings over 15 years experience in the hospitality industry

title: Seek out the animal sculptures
subtitle: Hidden within the woods near Wraxall are small stone sculptures waiting to be discovered by keen-eyed walkers.
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: About one mile Difficulty: Easy/medium. Steep steps on path from Jacklands Fishing Lake. Stony/uneven tracks through the woods, with some sharp uphill sections. Duration: Allow a leisurely 90 minutes Ty Sculpture Trail opened last year in Towerhouse Woods, between Nailsea and Wraxall, in memory of local resident Ty Partridge. Ty died suddenly at the age of 21 of leukaemia but as a child he loved exploring the paths, climbing trees and building dens in the woods. He would always ask for a treasure trail through the woods for his birthday party so the idea of creating a trail in his memory was born. All the woodland animal sculptures are dotted along the paths so you have to seek them out and become a ‘noticer’ of nature. The sculptures have all been carved by Piers Partridge and Phil Carter, the father of Ty’s best friend Sam. Life followed the route from Jacklands Fishing Lake. Follow the sign and cross the crystal-clear stream from the car park. Click HERE for full details and FREE PDF copy

title: Devonshire House

Within a twenty minute walk of the city, on a major bus route into the city and with plenty of free on street parking, Devonshire House offers a convenient base to explore the city and surrounds. A lounge is for guest use, with squashy sofas, up to date magazines and the local paper, imbibe in a Harveys Bristol Cream sherry with our compliments and relax after your day or plan the next one with all the information and leaflets to hand. subtitle: Rickbarton Cottage is the ideal base for that countryside retreat that everyone thrives from.
bodyContent: Walks from your doorstep, fresh air, country Pubs and a Farm Shop. Yet, close proximity to Bath (5 miles) and Bradford on Avon (2 miles) means that they get the best of both worlds! Guests can make use of the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool during their stay. Local Farm Shop village shop and village pub within walking distance or a short drive. title: Brooks’ View
subtitle: Brooks’ View is the epitome of the favoured cottage for those seeking a special place to stay.
bodyContent: Unashamedly a luxury romantic self-catering cottage 12 minutes from Bath city centre, the cottage is ideal for weekends away, mini moons, honey moons or just a few days’ escape in the delightful countryside. Many walks for walkers and splendid for cyclists being on Sustrans Two Tunnels Route 24. Sleeping 2 in the master bedroom, recently converted Brooks’ View not only has a luxury 1400 pocket sprung bed but also a decadent bathroom with a large walk in shower and a Victorian roll top claw bath. The cosy living room has a comfortable sofa and a snuggle sofabed for that extra guest. In the winter the traditional wood burning stove provides a lovely focal point and also extra heat. There is a small dining area with a traditional pine table and 4 chairs. The kitchen is fully equipped and has both a dishwasher and a clothes washer. On those halcyon days you can easily breakfast on the patio just outside the cottage. Built in the early 1800s, Brooks’ View is one of 4 artisan cottages built for the Somerset Coal Canal workers in the tiny hamlet of Tucking Mill, in the Midford Valley, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. An area of total peace and calm yet so close to the City. An ornithologist’s delight too..with the bird feeders attracting gold finches, coal finches, blue tits, herons and nuthatches to mention a few. Down by the brooks there is a summerhouse with a patio and a lovely stone barbecue. Ideal for enjoying that glass of cool crisp wine. Flyfishing can be arranged if you fancy a breakfast trout. AROUND AND ABOUT Lying in the historic hamlet of Tucking Mill there is plenty to interest our guests. The wildlife lovers will adore the birds and the geologists the delights of exploring the basis of the structure of the UK. this is the home of William Smith and many of his original surveys were done around this area. Bath is the most obvious attraction with the historic Abbey where Edgar the first King of England was crowned, the Roman Baths and the Thermae Spa together with the most wonderful Georgian architecture much loved by Jane Austen and her fans today. At only 20 minutes distance there is Longleat, the Saxon town of Bradford on Avon, the National Trust village of Lacock used in Jane Austen and Harry Potter films and 45 minutes drive takes you to . And there are many more…Cheddar Gorge, Wookey Hole, Bristol with the Science Museum and famous zoo. MEDIA FACILITIES There is free Wifi throughout the cottage and there is a small TV in the bedroom as well as a larger flat screen in the sitting room. An iPod Docking station is also provided. There is a selection of DVDs, a variety of books as well as some board games. PARKING Free private parking space for one car is provided and a second by arrangement REWARD CARD The benefits of the Reward Card with special discounts and extras like 3 hours for 2 in the Thermae Spa are available in this cottage. Full details in the cottage and on this website. ABOUT TUCKING MILL SELF CATERING Brooks’ View is one of the five 4 Star Luxury Gold properties in Tucking Mill Self Catering owned by Michael and Ann. There are two apartments in the city centre, The Old Smithy Loft and No 2 Hedgemead Court, and three cottages just 12 minutes drive away at Tucking Mill, Midford, a historic hamlet just outside the city boundaries in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. THOSE LOOKING AFTER YOU The property is managed by the Family Team..With Ann who has a background in hospitality and much travelling, Michael who built the barbecues and is in charge of the logs,birdfeeding and Head Housekeeper Nikki the team will do its utmost to ensure you enjoy your stay. You will also probably see Rob our invaluable man of all trades around… Short and long breaks available
tagline: Brooks’ View is the epitome of the favoured cottage for those seeking a special place to stay.

title: Haynes Motor Museum
subtitle: Haynes Motor Museum in Sparkford is a must-visit attraction, home to the UK’s largest collection of cars and motorbikes. Discover pioneering vehicles in The Dawn of Motoring, explore iconic red cars in the Red Room, and experience the thrill of legendary Williams Formula 1 racing cars up close.

title: Cheddar Gorge & Caves
subtitle: Cheddar Gorge & Caves boasts extraordinary subterranean show caves, awe-inspiring cliffs and holds many fascinating secrets about our prehistoric ancestors.
bodyContent: Our Day Ticket gives access to six great attractions: Gough’s Cave: Prepare to be amazed by our stunning show cave featuring spectacular stalagmite and stalactite formations created over 500,000 years ago! See cheddar cheese maturing in the caves, view the site where Cheddar Man’s 10,000-year-old skeleton was discovered and learn about the extraordinary DNA discovery. A free audio guide is available in six languages, and there is also a special version for children. Cox’s Cave featuring Yeo’s Journey: The Power of Water. This spectacular immersive multimedia experience tells the captivating story of how our iconic caves were formed and evolved through the ‘Power of Water’. The story is brought to life using state-of-the-art animation, sound, lighting and colour. Beyond the View: Take a seat in front of our state of the art 270-degree screen. Discover historic tales, enjoy breathtaking aerial panoramic views, and learn about the special wildlife and plants that call the gorge home. Museum of Pre-History: Discover amazing artefacts unearthed in the Cheddar area that help tell the story of how people lived thousands of years ago. Jacob’s Ladder & The Lookout Tower: Venture up the 274 steps to the top of the gorge with rest stops along the route to admire the view. Marvel at the panoramic views and mosaic of landscapes across the Mendips and Somerset Levels. Cliff­ -Top Walk: Hike the 3-mile loop around the gorge. Look out for the wildlife and enjoy the stunning scenery. If you don’t have time to do the full circuit, you can go for a shorter walk up to the Pulpit Rock look out point, and head back down the ladder. Gough’s Café Sit back, relax, and take in the beauty of the gorge at Gough’s Cafe, close to the entrance of Gough's Cave. Enjoy a thirst-quenching chilled drink, warm yourself up with a hot beverage or choose from a selection of alcoholic drinks. Serving light lunches, delicious snacks, cream teas and delicious cake, to include vegetarian and vegan options. Enjoy the spectacular views from the comfort of our air-conditioned cafe or relax on the large patio where dogs are welcome. We even have a welcome bowl of water for our doggy friends. Our small play area for under 2-year-olds will keep the little ones entertained too! Accessibility Cheddar Gorge & Caves provides accessible toilets, free parking for blue badge holders and free admission for carers accompanied by a full paying visitor. The audio tour of Gough's cave is printed in braille. Assistance Dogs are permitted, and the museum is wheelchair accessible with lift. Those with severely restricted mobility or who are wheelchair dependent will find areas of Cheddar Gorge & Caves inaccessible. If you have any questions prior to your visit, please email Guest Services on info@cheddargorge.co.uk or call 01934 742343. Dog-Friendly Dogs are welcome in all attractions and water bowls are provided in the cave entrances, shop and café patio. Family and Children Cheddar Gorge & Cave is family friendly. We have baby changing facilities, buggy parking and are breast-feeding friendly. Gough’s café has a small play area for under two year olds, water refills and highchairs are available. Entry is free for children under the age of 5 years. Groups Cheddar Gorge & Caves has special group rates, coach parking and drop off points for group tours. We offer discounted exclusive group sessions for Rocksport adventure activities – adventure caving, rock climbing and freefall. Special Events We have a fantastic programme of events throughout the year to keep the whole family entertained, including the school holidays. Visit our What’s On page for more details. Thirst for adventure or a puzzle-solving mind? Rocksport: Imagine climbing the gorge rockface in the shadow of the 450ft cliffs, caving deep underground or taking part in our exhilarating Blackcat freefall in Gough’s Cave. Suitable for all abilities. Sessions available for adults and children aged 8 years and over. Escape Rooms : Up for a challenge? Our two Cheddar-themed rooms, Caved In and The Vault will test your brain power as you race against the clock to try to escape. Double the fun with our Ultimate Escape combo ticket at a discounted rate. Suitable for 12 years and over in groups of up to six people. Nature, wildlife, history, adventure - experience the wonder on an all-season day out in Somerset. For more information on how to plan your day at Cheddar Gorge & Caves and to book please visit www.cheddargorge.co.uk
tagline: Explore Britain’s biggest gorge, from the stunning stalactite caverns to the dramatic cliffs.

title: Bistrot Pierre 1994
subtitle: Whether it’s a casual catch up over lunch, a special occasion or relaxed family meal, Bistrot Pierre offers the perfect environment in which to enjoy remarkable dishes, drinks and atmosphere.
bodyContent: Enjoy great value French bistrot cooking and seasonal menus featuring French bistrot classics such as steak-frites, boeuf bourguignon and tarte au citron alongside dishes from France’s many regions as well as vegetarian and vegan dishes. Open seven-days-a-week for lunch and dinner, along with breakfast at the weekend, there is something for everyone. Their NEW Menu Pierre offers three courses and a drink for just £22.95, whilst the extensive all-day menu offers a wide variety of dish options suitable for all tastes. You’ll find plenty of gluten-free dishes as well as a child-friendly menu on offer to help make your experience in the bistrot enjoyable for all. Located on Beach Road, their bistrot has incredible panoramic views across the bay, beach and Grand Pier. Their bistrot seats approximately 180 diners and has a large bar area downstairs, extensive outside terraced areas and a balcony, where their customers are able to enjoy the stunning views whilst they dine. With special events hosted each month (such as the Soiree Gastronomique on the 2nd and 4th Tues of the month) there’s always a reason to celebrate over a great meal and good company. This relaxed and friendly bistrot is the place to go for any occasion.
tagline: Whether it’s a casual catch up over lunch, a special occasion or relaxed family meal

title: Marlborough House
subtitle: Marlborough House is an enchanting Victorian Town House which has received 4 Stars and Gold Award for quality and service, and is operated by Peter Moore in a friendly and informal style.
bodyContent: Marlborough House is an enchanting Victorian Town House which has received 4 Stars and Gold Award for quality and service, and is operated by Peter Moore in a friendly and informal style. Marlborough House is in a great location. Conveniently located to all of Bath’s major attractions. The Royal Crescent, Circus, Assembly Rooms. Guild Hall, Abbey, Roman Baths, Thermae spas are all within a 2 – 15 minutes walk. Marlborough guest house, has 6 fully air conditioned, en-suite rooms, retaining many period features, and have been elegantly furnished to create a relaxing atmosphere. All rooms are different, some accommodate a family of 3 or 4. Have a minimum of a king size or superking size bed, one has an antique four poster bed. Our award wining breakfasts are served between 8.30-10 am, includes an abundant selection of freshly prepared fruit, cereals and yoghurts, followed by a choice of cooked to order vegetarian breakfasts. We have parking in our forecourt, and 3 special parking permits, please check availability of parking with us, prior to booking. Guests can check into Marlborough House any time between 11.30 am – 1.00 pm. or between 4.30 – 6.30 pm. Arriving outside of these times is by prior arrangement with the proprietor and before booking anywhere “on – line” Good discounts available for stays 3 of nights or more Sundays to Thursdays
tagline: Marlborough House is an enchanting Victorian Town House

title: Stable Cottage: 6 bed country cottage
subtitle: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.
bodyContent: It is located in the beautiful Georgian village of Freshford which lies at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys in the southern Cotswolds. There are some wonderful walks to local pubs following the riverside and canals. All just 15 minutes from Bath by car but the secret of this location is the 9 minute train journey to Bath from the village station, just a short stroll from the cottages. The cottage : Stable cottage is a newly renovated, limestone floored, 3 bedroom, two bathroom (one is en-suite) cottage. It has large windows to the front of the house filling the bedrooms and downstairs with light on a sunny day. It has an open plan living/dining area with free view TV/DVD and two large suedette couches and comfortable chairs. For dining there is a blond Oak dining table and chairs to seat 6 . The Stables can accommodate 6 people in three bedrooms (two king size and one double) . The kitchen is fully equipped with cookware,dishwasher and washing machine . The house also offers Iron/Ironing board, Hairdryers All bed linen and towels . There is a Welcome pack of tea, coffee, sugar, milk, bread, butter, eggs and bacon. Free WiFi. There are also books and board-games in the house for the use of guests. If you have any questions on Bath and the local area before or during your stay please let us know. We would be delighted to help. Neighbourhood overview : Freshford is a beautiful ancient village with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk from the cottage( The Inn at Freshford) that serves restaurant quality food and all the local beers and ciders.They have an excellent fully stocked( from wine to organic humus!)community shop that also has a good quality cafe that serves lunch. There is also a local doctors surgery. The village is nestled at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys . The Kennet and Avon canal is a 15 minute walk from the cottage. Getting around : You don’t need a car to stay in the cottage. The village station is a few minutes walk away. Trains hourly off peak and thrice hourly at peak times. Bath 9 mins, Bristol 22mins. London Padington to Bath Spa 1.5 hours Bath Spa to Freshford 9 minutes Bath Spa to Freshford “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/bath-spa-to-freshford ” Freshford to Bath Spa “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/freshford-to-bath-spa ” There is also a local bus service to all the adjacent villages and Bath. The cottage has two parking spaces suitable for one medium and one small car or a single large SUV.the surrounding towns you might want to visit. Other things to note If you are a runner or keep fit enthusiast the owner is a qualified Personal Trainer (Bath Uni) with much Marathon and half marathon experience. She specialises in Ladies training. Please let us know if you would like guided running or some Personal Fitness training.
tagline: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.

title: Chestnuts House
subtitle: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden and private off street parking.
bodyContent: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden and private off street parking. Set in the heart of the beautiful Georgian city of city. It is ideally situated off the main roads and adjacent to Henrietta park, but within a few minutes level stroll of the city centre with its many attractions, restaurants and excellent shopping centre. The House is built from natural Bath stone and has four beautifully decorated and furnished ensuite guest rooms, some with king size and wrought iron beds. Owners Toni and Dawn have created a splendid and delightful bed & breakfast with superb hospitality in a relaxing atmosphere, all the necessary ingredients for making your stay in Bath a truly memorable experience. Guests Chestnuts House has 5 individually themed ensuite rooms which can accommodate a total of 11 persons. Three Superior double bedded rooms, one family/twin room (max 3 persons) and one Classic double room Bedrooms The bedrooms have recently been refurbished to an exacting standard and have been tastefully decorated and beautifully furnished. All rooms have en suite bathrooms with bath and shower, hairdryers and large fluffy towels. The rooms have comfortable and relaxing beds with crisp cotton sheets, air con, remote flat screen colour television, radio, free wireless internet access and refreshment trays. Bathrooms All bedrooms are ensuite with large fluffy towels and White Company products. The superior & twin/family rooms are ensuite with bath & power shower. The Classic room is ensuite with walk in power shower. Kitchen Enjoy your inclusive breakfast in our light and airy dining room overlooking the garden. During the summer months breakfast can be served al fresco. Our breakfast includes both organic and local produce. As well as the traditional English breakfast, we offer smoked salmon with scrambled eggs and homemade blinis, poached buttered kippers (smoked haddock with poached eggs). There is also an extensive buffet table with fresh fruit salad, freshly baked pastries, cereals, yoghurts. We are happy to cater for special dietary requirements. Entertainment The Lounge has a large flat screen Television with both Sky & BT Sport Channels. subtitle: A gentle, guided poetry walk invites visitors to explore the gardens and capture their surroundings in words. Combining creativity with nature, it offers a relaxed and accessible introduction to writing haiku.

Along the way, participants take part in short and accessible writing exercises designed to spark ideas and build confidence. The focus is on simplicity, showing how just a few carefully chosen words can create a strong and meaningful poem. After the walk, the session continues indoors, where notes gathered outside are shaped into haiku poems. The workshop is open to all, with no previous experience required, making it suitable for anyone interested in trying something creative. Led by Somerset-based author and creative writing tutor Jo Middleton, the session is designed to be welcoming and accessible, offering a supportive introduction to poetry writing. title: Wellington
subtitle: Wellington, in Somerset is a friendly town set in the wide valley between the Brendon and Blackdown Hills, Wellington gave its name to the famous 'Iron Duke', victor of the Battle of Waterloo. The 175ft column built on the scarp edge of the Blackdowns was erected in his honour: at night it is an illuminated landmark for miles around.
bodyContent: The town's growth and prosperity date back to the 18th century when the Fox Family built their integrated woollen mill. Visit the Wellington museum to find out more about this historic town and unravel the Fox Family legacy. With a range of specialist shops, Wellington is ideal for browsing during the day whilst the 'Wellesley', the town's unique 1930s cinema offers entertainment in the evening. Wellington Park was restored in recent years thanks to a Heritage Lottery Grant. Wellington has also recently become a 'Food Town' and hosts various events and initiatives to celebrate the best in local food and drink. title: Westhay Moor National Nature Reserve
subtitle: Internationally famous as a haven for birdwatchers in particular, Somerset Wildlife Trust’s main site on the Peat Moors covers more than 100 hectares.
bodyContent: Internationally famous as a haven for birdwatchers in particular, Somerset Wildlife Trust’s main site on the Peat Moors covers more than 100 hectares. Restored peat diggings, three miles north-west of Glastonbury have been transformed into a network of open water, reed bed and the largest surviving fragment of lowland acid mire in the South-West. Designated as a National Nature Reserve, Westhay Moor was a pioneering project by Somerset Wildlife Trust, in the early 1980s. Since the site’s restoration it has become recognised as one of the top bird watching locations in Britain and often features in documentaries, including the BBC’s Springwatch and Autumnwatch series. Westhay's biggest attractions for birdwatchers arrive in autumn and stay through to January/ February -several million starlings fill the sky as they arrive to roost among the reeds each afternoon.
tagline: Internationally famous as a haven for birdwatchers in particular.

title: The Garden at Dunster Castle, National Trust
subtitle: The result of 100s of years of planning, building and restoration a walk around the gardens at Dunster Castle takes you around the world and though four different microclimates.
bodyContent: The result of 100s of years of planning, building and restoration a walk around the gardens at Dunster Castle takes you around the world and though four different microclimates. The South Terrace With far reaching views across the Bristol Channel and Deer Park the present day layout of the South Terrace stems from the Victorian period. In the 1820s, at the behest of George Luttrell, the architect Salvin demolished the existing Thornhill Chapel which had been built on the south facade in 1721. A new wing was constructed in its place and the resulting South Terrace was formed. To reflect its history, the flower beds are planted in the Victorian style with spring bulbs giving a spectacular floral display and in summer there is an abundance of brightly coloured bedding plants. The area has a Mediterranean feel due to its fortunate micro-climate and this enables tender plants to thrive including the row of Chusan Palms. This part of the garden also contains the Orangery, (now renamed the Camellia House) where you can pick up take away coffee and snacks, the Swan Pond which is home to goldfishes and newts and the Lemon House. The River Garden A native micro climate the River Garden is a wild, wooded area. Green throughout the year during spring it is full of colour as the magnolia trees bloom. During summer the giant rhubarb reaches its peak in growth getting so big they make an unusual umbrella when caught in the rain. Home to some rare species including the Handkerchief tree was grown from seeds smuggled back from Australia by Alys Luttrell in her purse in the 1920’s. Bridges cross the River Avil which runs through the garden and lead to walks on the wider estate. And at the end of the garden is the working watermill which produces over 6 tonnes of flour a year. The Yew bank There have been yews on this bank dating back to the eighteenth century when the original drive - The New Way - was commissioned in 1720 by Dorothy Luttrell. In those days, it was very fashionable to create areas of light and shade within a garden and yews were perfect in this respect for shade. However, over the years, the yews grew too large and they were coppiced in 2012 and are now kept within bounds. The Keep This area was originally the Upper Ward of the Norman Fortress of Dunster and, therefore, is the highest point in the Dunster landscape. In 1721, at the request of Dorothy Luttrell, the area was levelled and turned into a Bowling Green. To offer shelter and a dining area for the participants and the ladies, the Octagon Tower was constructed this now houses an exhibition exploring the history. Facilities in addition to those listed below: Baby changing facilities Children's Trails Courtesy Vehicle Stair Climber Trampers available to book
tagline: The result of 100s of years of planning, building and restoration a walk around the gardens.

title: Burnham, Berrow, Brean
subtitle: The character of the coast changes completely around the mouth of the Parrett with the rocky cliffs and shingle giving way to sand flats that run all the way to the promontory that is Brean Down. Sand naturally attracts holiday makers especially those keen to wield a bucket and spade which is one of the reasons for the popularity of the resorts and parks here. The three Bs - Burnham, Berrow and Brean - are famed for their miles of sand, ideal for walking, running, riding, angling, kite-flying an
bodyContent: As well attracting families looking for a fun-packed break, the beaches of Burnham, Berrow and Brean are also ideal for those wanting to get away from it all because there is room for all. There are dog walkers, wildlife watchers, horse riders, sand sailors, wind surfers and sand artists who all find what they’re seeking on these flat, open beaches with one of the world’s highest tidal ranges. Views across the Channel take in the islands of Steep Holm and Flat Holm and are particularly stunning at sunset. The tidal range and soft mud flats at low water do mean that visitors need to be cautious and avoid walking towards the sea at certain times. There is plenty of information about the dangers as well as beach wardens and rescue services. Burnham’s beaches have something for everyone with some focused on family and others appealing to those who want to watch boats or birds. Further along the strip is Berrow which has a section protected as a Site of Special Scientific Interest because of its rare sand dune habitat. Part of this area is managed by Sedgemoor District Council as a Local Nature Reserve. Vehicles are allowed to park on the sand and there are refreshments available in the summer. The beaches at Burnham and Berrow have been given Seaside Awards by Keep Britain Tidy. At the end of the strip is the headland Brean Down which offers fabulous 360 degree views over the sea on one side, across the Somerset Levels on the other and taking in some of the County’s best known features such as Glastonbury Tor and the Mendip Hills . A bonus some days is an elevated view of the work of sand artists who cannot resist the massive canvas.

Outdoor Splash is open from Whitsun to September and features several waterslides and an outdoor Splash Pool for the children with 3 waterslides, mega tipping bucket and water features. There is also a large sunbathing area so you can top up your tan when the sun shines. Do the children need to let off some steam? Don’t worry we have it covered! Brean Play also has extensive family friendly facilities including a large café and spectator area offering a range of healthy value for money meals and snacks, family changing rooms and free WIFI.

title: Tacchi-Morris Arts Centre
subtitle: The Tacchi-Morris Arts Centre is a multipurpose space that provides arts activities for the whole community and those visiting the area.
bodyContent: Completed in 2000 through a £1 million donation from the Tacchi-Morris Trust, together with a £2.1 million grant from National Lottery Funds, the Tacchi-Morris Arts Centre holds state-of-the-art facilities and aims to inspire all the community to get involved in the arts, be it coming to watch a show - or taking part yourself! As well as a busy programme of theatre, dance and music, the Tacchi-Morris Arts Centre runs a range of community classes open to all the family and hosts approximately eight visual art exhibitions annually in the foyer gallery space. We believe involvement in the arts is not only a great way to have fun and breed creativity but also a means for exploring what it means to be human. Our work as part of Heathfield Community School and The SPACE (as well as with other local secondary and primary schools and colleges) and with the wider community has shown us the value of the arts in developing skills and raising attainment, in challenging ideas and the world around us, in improving health and well-being and in building confidence and self-esteem. The Tacchi-Morris Arts Centre was developed through support from Kathleen Tacchi-Morris and continued support from the Tacchi-Morris Trust and Heathfield Community School. Core th the centre's existence is continuing the legacy of pacifism that echoed throughout Kathleen.
tagline: A multipurpose space that provides arts activities for the local community and beyond.

title: Vivary Golf Course
subtitle: Vivary Golf Course is situated on open parkland just a few minutes walk from Taunton town centre. It offers history, challenges and enjoyment.
bodyContent: This well-designed and well-maintained 80-year-old golf course is an 18-hole, 4620 yards, par 63 golf one. It proves challenging for players of all ages and abilities, with fabulous greens, and bunkers and water hazards aplenty. Just book a tee time, turn up and play.
tagline: A centrally-located golf course with far reaching views

title: Blake Museum
subtitle: Blake Museum is a 16th century house located in the heart of Bridgwater, a historic market town and port, first mentioned as Brugie in the Domesday Book of 1086.
bodyContent: The Museum was first opened to the public in 1926 and it is said that Robert Blake, the town's most famous citizen, was born in the house in 1598. We have fascinating collections for you to discover. Our displays tell the stories of the town of Bridgwater and the surrounding area - our communities, industries and occupations through time. The main exhibitions are displayed in six rooms over two floors, with a ground floor temporary exhibition room. Details of temporary exhibitions can be found on the home page.
tagline: Blake Museum is a 16th century house located in the heart of Bridgwater

title: Ring O Bells
subtitle: The Ring O Bells is a traditional country pub located in the pretty village of Compton Martin, North Somerset, which is listed in the Domesday Book.
bodyContent: The village sits in the heart of the Chew Valley, surrounded by undulating hills, churches and apple orchards which provides some of Somersets finest ciders. Situated at the foothills of the Mendips it is an area of outstanding natural beauty. Villagers Miles and Luca Leonard bought the Ring O’ Bells in 2012 with friends Matt and Fiona and transformed the pub back to it's original state. From the moment you walk in you'll feel immediately at home. With it's flagstone and wooden floors, inglenook fireplaces, old leather armchairs, upright piano, and vintage bar games, the Ring O Bells is the perfect place to simply come and have a drink or spend a whole weekend in the country.
tagline: The Ring O Bells is a traditional country pub located in the pretty village of Compton Martin

title: Wander through tranquil woodland
subtitle: A tranquil wilderness on the edge of North Somerset has been an important spot to local people for hundreds of years. Leigh Woods National Nature Reserve has ancient woodland and is home to many unusual plants and animals. Whether you want a peaceful walk to remote parts of the woods, or a short family stroll, there are numerous paths to follow.
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: about 1.5 miles Difficulty: easy – a level walk. Wellies or walking boots recommended in winter though. Duration: the circuit can be completed in about 45 mins. Map: OS Explorer 154 A tranquil wilderness on the edge of North Somerset has been an important spot to local people for hundreds of years. Leigh Woods National Nature Reserve has ancient woodland and is home to many unusual plants and animals. Whether you want a peaceful walk to remote parts of the woods, or a short family stroll, there are numerous paths to follow. Leigh Woods, which sits alongside Avon Gorge, has long been recognised for its rich, natural environment. It contains a hillfort, Stokeleigh Camp, which is thought to have been occupied from the third century BC, as well as limestone and celestine quarries which were worked in the 18th and 19th centuries. Part of the land was bought by George Wills, of Bristol’s Imperial Tobacco, after it was threatened with development. He donated it to the National Trust in 1909 to preserve it as a special place for the public. Other areas of the nature reserve have now been taken over by the Forestry Commission. title: Dorian House
subtitle: A warm welcome awaits you at Dorian House, a stylish Victorian villa with stunning decor, eclectic Asian antiques and contemporary art collection.
bodyContent: A warm welcome awaits you at Dorian House, a stylish Victorian villa with stunning decor, eclectic Asian antiques and contemporary art collection. Set in a quiet, convienient location overlooking Bath towards the Royal Crescent, it is a 10-15 minute stroll into the centre and provides complimentary parking and well maintained Gardens. Rooms are gracious and all have views looking over Bath or our secluded hilly garden. Flatscreen TV's, WiFi, fluffy towels, high quality linen, bathrobes, high pressure showers, Nespresso Coffee machines and elegant French Damana herbal toiletries are standard in all rooms. Guests can also relax in our elegant sitting room, with local drinks from our honesty bar. In the morning look forward to a hearty, cooked to order breakfast in the Orangery situated in the Japanese-inspired garden. Begin with the extensive selection of locally sourced yoghurts, fresh fruit, Bath Cheeses, cereals, croissants, homemade preserves, fruit juices, freshly ground Bristol Coffee and a selection of Teas. Then our Full English breakfast, or a lighter option of Scottish Oak Smoked Salmon with free range Eggs. We hope to have the opportunity of welcoming you to our Villa soon.
tagline: A warm welcome awaits you at Dorian House, a stylish Victorian villa with stunning decor

title: Circle Luxury Stays: Crescent apartment
subtitle: Choose from apartments in Bath city centre, or an exclusive newly built five-bed holiday home with indoor pool in Devon/Dorset coast.
bodyContent: Bath properties are in landmark locations such as the Royal Crescent and Camden Crescent, within walking distance to the High Street. All are modern in design and beautifully furnished, providing you with more privacy, space and comfort than a standard hotel. Whether you are coming to Bath for a family get-away, romantic break, get-togethers with friends, or business, the apartments are a great option for stay of any duration. You are assured of a warm welcome and memorable stay on every visit. ——————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————— Crescent Apartment is on the lower ground floor, comprises an open-plan sitting room / kitchen, a good sized master bedroom with super king bed, a single bedroom, bathroom and elegant French doors leading to the courtyard. The sitting room is furnished with two sofas (one is a double sofa bed), LCD TV and DVD. The master bedroom has a super king size deep-sprung divan bed, which can be converted into twin beds, wardrobe, console table and stool and flat-screen television. The second bedroom has a single bed. The modern kitchen is fully equipped with Neff hob, electric oven, microwave and integrated appliances: including a dishwasher, washer/dryer and fridge freezer.
tagline: Choose from apartments in Bath city centre, or an exclusive newly built five-bed holiday home

title: Bloomfield House
subtitle: Bloomfield House, a Georgian detached Grade II listed building, has elegant and romantic rooms (four posters or half testers) fine art, antiques, splendid views all combined with environmental credentials and a friendly relaxed atmosphere.
bodyContent: The House Bloomfield House, a Georgian detached Grade II listed building, has elegant and romantic rooms (four posters or half testers) fine art, antiques, splendid views all combined with environmental credentials and a friendly relaxed atmosphere. The house is set well back from a quiet road. Well behaved children and pets are welcome. The Breakfast Our traditional full English breakfasts are freshly cooked to order and served from 7.30 am until 11 am. Ingredients are mostly organic, fair-traded and provided by local suppliers, including homemade preserves and artisan breads. Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options are always available. The Parking We have free off-street parking and an electric car charging point for our guests use. There is easy access to the city centre via a regular bus service which stops within a few feet of the entrance to our property. The walk into town is a downhill stroll of 20 mins, on the way back up – jump on the bus or grab a cab! . The Bedrooms All bedrooms have en-suite facilities and come with the usuals – TV, hospitality tray, toiletries, hair dryer. The guest bedrooms are situated on the second floor, we have no lift so are not suitable for those with mobility issues. We are, of course, happy to help you up the stairs with your luggage. On the upside this does mean each room has far reaching views. Please note, for those with allergies , that this is a family home and we have both cats and dogs on the premises. The cats do not have access to the guest bedrooms (nor do our dogs for that matter). DISCOUNTS Any mid-week stay (Sun-Thurs ) will attract a £10 discount. Please quote ‘Stay in Bath’ when booking (by phone) on 01225 420105. Any on-line booking – applicable discounts will be deducted upon check-out. (This sadly cannot be used in addition with other special offers.) We also offer discounts to those arriving in Bath by train or bus. Discounts do not apply to Bank Holidays or one night Saturday bookings which are, on occasions, available.
tagline: Bloomfield House, a Georgian detached Grade II listed building

title: Church Farm Country Cottages
subtitle: Seven cottages tastefully converted from old cow byres with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams.
bodyContent: Seven cottages tastefully converted from old cow byres with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams. Three cottages sleep 2 persons and four cottages sleep 4 persons. Bath 5 miles. Bradford on Avon 2 miles. Ample parking. Working farm with sheep and horses in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Swim in our luxurious heated indoor pool (12m x 5m) whatever the weather! Games room with table tennis, pool table and table football. Village pub serving food 500m. Village shop 500m. Kennet and Avon Canal nearby for cycling, boating and walking. Locally produced welcome cream tea.
tagline: Seven cottages tastefully converted from old cow byres

title: Spacious Double Room in West Bath
subtitle: Spacious Double bedroom in Victorian terraced house to the west of the city of Bath.
bodyContent: Property has good transport links to city centre, as well as being close to all local amenities you should need for a pleasant stay with us. The house is situated to the west side of the beautiful city of Bath. Furnished with a mix of modern and vintage furniture, the property has all you need for a relaxing stay. There are good transport links to the town centre, with services stopping less than two minutes from us. There is also ample free street parking outside our door. The breakfast room/lounge has a very homely feel and contains books, games and suggestions on where to go in Bath. Guests also have use of our ultra fast fibre broadband. We’ve equipped the kitchen to make cooking easy with a host of ingredients and basic utensils. You’ll have your own private double bedroom with large comfortable double bed and ample storage space. You can also benefit from shared use of the modern and well equipped kitchen, comfortable living room and bathroom. I like to give guests their own space during their stay, however I am always available to offer recommendations and help, both before and during their stay. I am never far away or am in the house, and am always on hand should you need me. I usually arrange for a self check in but can always be on hand if a guest would like me to help them check in. We are a five minute walk from the high street where you’ll find a supermarket, takeaways and a few local shops. There are a number of good pubs and bars in the area all walking distance from us. Alternatively, its less than ten minutes into town by taxi and shouldn’t cost you more than £6-£7. The property is less than two minutes from the bus stop where you can catch regular services into the town centre. There is plenty of on street parking outside the house. We are about ten to fifteen minutes walk from Oldfield Park train station where you can access services to London and Bristol. Check-In: 3PM-9PM Not suitable for children (2-12 years) Not suitable for infants (under 2 years) Not suitable for pets No smoking No parties or events
tagline: Spacious Double bedroom in Victorian terraced house to the west of the city of Bath.

title: Burys Cottage
subtitle: Burys Cottage has a cosy and romantic feel to it being tucked away in the furthest corner of the row of cottages.
bodyContent: Burys Cottage has everything you should need for a romantic getaway. The cottage has a double bedroom with ensuite bathroom. It is ideally located between Bath (5 miles) and Bradford on Avon (2 miles). The popular ‘Longleat House and Safari Drive -Through’ is 12 miles (30% off gate price tickets available for our guests when purchased online – if booked at least one week in advance). Church Farm is a working sheep farm in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. There is a luxurious indoor heated indoor pool (12m x 5m) onsite, perfect for guests whatever the weather. Burys Cottage has its own individual patio area with table, chairs and sun parasol. Farm shop and country pub/s within walking distance. Kennet and Avon Canal nearby for boating, cycling and walking. The cottage features a country feel with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams with soft furnishings to compliment. Enjoy admiring the sheep in the fields surrounding the farm. Welcome cream tea on arrival. Free Wifi.
tagline: Burys Cottage has a cosy and romantic feel to it

title: Rhubarb Tray Bake
subtitle: A first-of-the-season fruit, rhubarb has a lovely sharp flavour. Sharpham grows it in the old-fashioned way, under terracotta cloches, which forces the stalks, making them slender, sweeter and more tender.
bodyContent: Makes 30 x 20cm / 12 x 8in traybake, Preparation Time: 15 mins, Cooking time: 50 mins Ingredients: 175g unsalted butter, softened, plus extra for greasing 6 sticks of rhubarb, chopped into 2.5cm chunks 270g golden caster sugar grated zest and juice of 1 orange 3 eggs 175g white spelt flour 75g Sharpham Park wholegrain spelt flour 75g ground almonds 2 tsp baking powder 1/4 tsp bicarbonate of soda 1 tsp ground cinnamon 1 tsp vanilla extract 1/4 tsp salt 150ml soured cream or Greek yoghurt For the method and more information visit https://www.sharphampark.com/recipes/article/189-rhubarb-tray-bake
tagline: A first-of-the-season fruit, rhubarb has a lovely sharp flavour.

title: Wells Cathedral
subtitle: Built between 1175 and 1490 Wells Cathedral in Somerset has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals”.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built between 1175 and 1490 Wells Cathedral has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals”. Set in the medieval heart of England’s smallest city, and an easy drive from Bristol, Bath and Cardiff, Wells is the earliest English Cathedral to be built in the Gothic style. The current building is a significant landmark in the South West of England, has an international reputation and is TripAdvisor ranked number one for things to do in Wells and in Somerset. Wells Cathedral has unique features that separate it from other English cathedrals including its iconic West Front and the beautiful ‘scissor arches’ supporting the central tower, as well as one of the largest collections of historic stained glass in the country. The Cathedral also boasts the famous Wells Clock (which is considered to be the second oldest clock mechanism in Great Britain), the fascinating octagonal Chapter House and one of only four chained libraries in the UK. Wells Cathedral welcomes thousands of visitors each year who join in with regular daily services and events or who come simply to enjoy the calm and hospitality of this wonderful and holy place. Stay, if you can, for Evensong with the Cathedral’s world renowned choir (term times); a peaceful and moving end to your day. Tours: Discover hidden spaces and chambers, explore the south transept roof space and marvel at the nave from a very different perspective via the Cathedral's popular and longer High Parts tours which can be pre-booked via the website at www.wellscathedral.org.uk/visit/tours . The Cathedral runs complimentary ground floor tours daily (Monday-Saturday) and tickets include access to an audio tour. Guided tours for group visits can also be pre-booked via the Visits team at visits@wellscathedral.org.uk Families When term breaks up the Cathedral offers creative workshops for children accompanied by their parents or guardians. We also provide free children explorer backpacks which are available free of charge on arrival and which help children to learn about the main highlights and history of the Cathedral. Group Visits: The group rate (+10) for pre booked self guided visits is £10 and £12 to include a highlights tour. Unreserved groups are charged the standard on the door price of £14. For more information, and to book, please email visits@wellscathedral.org.uk Vicars’ Close: Adjoining the Cathedral is Vicars’ Close, believed to be the only complete medieval street left in England. Vicars’ Close was designed to provide accommodation for the Vicars Choral, who sing the daily services, and this is still the case today. This centuries-old tradition is unique and a much valued part of the continuing life of Wells Cathedral. The medieval windows of the houses and the garden archways seem to have survived more or less intact until the early nineteenth century, and even now a few still exist. Make a Day of It A warm welcome awaits you at our Cathedral shop which stocks a wide range of unique mementoes and gifts. The Loft at Wells Cathedral café is also open daily for coffee, delicious home-made lunches and afternoon teas http://www.wellscathedral.org.uk
tagline: Wells Cathedral in Somerset has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals".

title: Revo Kitchen & Terrace
subtitle: Revo Kitchen & Terrace, is an enticing new restaurant located on Weston-super-Mare’s seafront in what was, until March 2019, the SeaQuarium. It’s hard to imagine anywhere that could offer better views whilst enjoying a meal, a snack or tea and cake in a relaxing environment. With views over the bay, the Grand Pier and over the water to Wales, it’s fast becoming the venue of choice.
bodyContent: And talking of the environment, Revo is highly conscious of its duty to care for our beautiful world. There are paper compostable straws for all drinks, all takeaway packaging is compostable and they aim to use local suppliers for all produce. Cakes and bakes are not bought in, the in-house bakery team come in as early as 3am some mornings to produce traditional and innovative baked goods, created freshly each day with locally sourced ingredients and high-quality produce. The homemade bread is a key ingredient in some of the brunch, lunch and dinner dishes. Weston-super-Mare is blessed with spectacular sunsets and with its panoramic windows, Revo is the perfect venue for a sundowner cocktail or mocktail, they even have fire-pits on the terrace which they’ll be pleased to light for you on request. You can get an idea of some of the delights on offer from their main menu here Revo Kitchen welcomes dogs on their leads, just remember that excessive barking is not so welcome, there’s a “3 barks and you’re out” policy. And if you’re feeling active, there’s an amazing indoor Glo Golf crazy golf course, try your skills in the darkened room with glowing golf holes and a bar in the middle! Normally open from 12 noon daily, it’s a great fun activity suitable for all age groups.
tagline: Revo Kitchen & Terrace, is an enticing new restaurant

title: Weddings at The Grand Pier
subtitle: Come and ‘tide’ the knot at the West Country’s favourite attraction! The Grand Pier is a truly unique, iconic and wonderfully British venue situated in the historical seaside town of Weston-super-Mare. The outstanding setting, located a quarter of a mile out to sea, boasts stunning sea views and provides the perfect back drop for you to say ‘I Do’. It’s almost guaranteed to be unlike anything you or your guests have ever experienced before!
bodyContent: Facilities and Capacity The Grand Pier offers a range of picture-perfect, licensed rooms for you to choose from for your special day, accommodating intimate gatherings to grand celebrations of 650 guests. Once married, newlyweds and their guests can capture vibrant photographs in our iconic amusement park, providing a unique backdrop for colourful and personality-filled images. Brides enjoy complimentary use of our elegant Bridal Suite, situated at the Pier's highest peak, ensuring comfort and relaxation while preparing for the big day. Our on-site chefs offer a variety of tasty canapes and a delicious wedding breakfast for you and your guests. Additionally, a buffet is available for those end-of-the-night cravings. Our wedding brochure includes a sample menu, but your designated wedding coordinator can customise this to suit your preferences. Whether it’s a full day affair or an evening celebration, we have just the space for your dream wedding: Regency Suite is a stunning, large and airy venue situated on the top floor of The Grand Pier that is complete with a private entrance and balcony, lift access and exclusive bar for up to 230 guests. The Tiffany Room is a romantic setting at the furthest point out to sea that is beautifully decorated in an elegant Edwardian style and boasts phenomenal panoramic views of the bay. This venue is licensed for civil wedding ceremonies and is perfect for your wedding breakfast and evening celebrations for up to 150 guests. The North Tower is the perfect top floor venue for an intimate number of guests. With private entrance and floor to ceiling views of the shoreline, this semi-circular room is suitable for a civil ceremony or small wedding breakfast for up to 24 guests. For those hosting larger weddings, The Great Hall effortlessly morphs from a bustling family attraction into a magnificent space solely dedicated to your grand celebration. Our Great Hall can host and extraordinary wedding breakfast for 650 guests. Our Promise We offer a range of packages that include everything you need to create a truly special day. However, we understand that every wedding is unique and are happy to discuss a totally bespoke package option to suit your individual requirements and budget. We look forward to discussing plans with you and help make your dream wedding become a reality. Telephone: 01934 646155 Email: weddings@grandpier.co.uk

title: Lorne House
subtitle: Lorne House is a large Victorian villa in the lovely Wiltshire village of Box, just six miles from the city of Bath.
bodyContent: Lorne House is a large Victorian villa in the lovely Wiltshire village of Box, just six miles from the city of Bath. We offer an elegant charm, gorgeous ensuite rooms and a very friendly, personal service. Lorne House provides an ideal base from which to explore Bath, the beautiful Wiltshire countryside and its many historic and beautiful local villages, including Lacock, Castle Combe, Bradford on Avon, Corsham and Avebury. The childhood home of Thomas the Tank Engine author, Reverend W.V.Awdry, Lorne House has been furnished to a very high standard; all our rooms are en-suite, with either wet-rooms or bathrooms, and come equipped with tea and coffee making facilities, hairdryer, flat screen television, iron and ironing board. There is free wifi throughout the house. Our breakfasts are hearty and substantial, with fruit, cereals, toast, traditional cooked English breakfast or continental options, served in our lovely light and spacious dining room. We source as many of our foodstuffs locally where possible and the marmalade is home-made. Guests have the choice of a comfy sitting room or a large outdoor verandah to relax and unwind.
tagline: Lorne House is a large Victorian villa in the lovely Wiltshire village of Box

title: Spacious Double Room in West Bath
subtitle: Spacious Double bedroom in Victorian terraced house to the west of the city of Bath.
bodyContent: Spacious Double bedroom in Victorian terraced house to the west of the city of Bath. Property has good transport links to city centre, as well as being close to all local amenities you should need for a pleasant stay with us. The house is situated to the west side of the beautiful city of Bath. Furnished with a mix of modern and vintage furniture, the property has all you need for a relaxing stay. There are good transport links to the town centre, with services stopping less than two minutes from us. There is also ample free street parking outside our door. The breakfast room/lounge has a very homely feel and contains books, games and suggestions on where to go in Bath. Guests also have use of our ultra fast fibre broadband. We’ve equipped the kitchen to make cooking easy with a host of ingredients and basic utensils. You’ll have your own private double bedroom with large comfortable double bed and ample storage space. You can also benefit from shared use of the modern and well equipped kitchen, comfortable living room and bathroom. I like to give guests their own space during their stay, however I am always available to offer recommendations and help, both before and during their stay. I am never far away or am in the house, and am always on hand should you need me. I usually arrange for a self check in but can always be on hand if a guest would like me to help them check in. We are a five minute walk from the high street where you’ll find a supermarket, takeaways and a few local shops. There are a number of good pubs and bars in the area all walking distance from us. Alternatively, its less than ten minutes into town by taxi and shouldn’t cost you more than £6-£7. The property is less than two minutes from the bus stop where you can catch regular services into the town centre. There is plenty of on street parking outside the house. We are about ten to fifteen minutes walk from Oldfield Park train station where you can access services to London and Bristol. Check-In: 3PM-9PM Not suitable for children (2-12 years) Not suitable for infants (under 2 years) Not suitable for pets No smoking No parties or events
tagline: Spacious Double bedroom in Victorian terraced house to the west of the city of Bath.

title: The Rising Sun Inn
subtitle: Book direct to get the best price at our hotel in Bath city centre.
bodyContent: Book direct to get the best price at our hotel in Bath city centre, a traditional English pub, dating from the 1700s. We’ve brought it bang up to date with a clean, fresh decor; subtle, modern lighting; and a warm, friendly atmosphere. We’re Just off the famous Pulteney bridge, right in the heart of historic Bath and we’re less than two minutes walk from the shops, restaurants, and attractions. Come and discover why customers love our dog friendly pub, excellent food, and bed & breakfast.
