title: The Henry
subtitle: ‘The Henry’ is probably Bath’s most central Guest House. Just 100m from the railway and bus stations and 150m from the Abbey and Roman Baths.
bodyContent: ⭐ Book Direct for Reward Card Offers ‘The Henry’ is probably Bath’s most central Guest House. Just 100m from the railway and bus stations and 150m from the Abbey and Roman Baths, The Henry is perfectly located amongst the historic attractions of Bath. Located in a beautiful Georgian house we are less than a minute from Bath’s main shopping street. Whether your visit is as a tourist, for shopping or just for fun The Henry is the place to stay. We also have two self-contained apartments less than 100m away from the main house this can be rented as a self-catering or with breakfast served in the dining room at The Henry.
tagline: ‘The Henry’ is probably Bath’s most central Guest House.

title: Komedia Bath
subtitle: Hosting over 400 events per year in a beautifully restored former Edwardian cinema, Komedia is a go-to destination for a great night out in the city of Bath. Take your pick from Saturday night stand-up, top gigs and tours, quirky cabaret shows, late night revelry and so much at the award-winning venue.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Komedia Bath was established in 2008 and community-owned since 2019, Komedia prides itself on offering something for everybody and operates two distinct performance spaces to do this. At the heart of it all is the Main Auditorium. With high ceilings, baroque grandeur and room for 600+ people, it’s a stunning setting for full-scale live performances and also functions as Bath’s only above-ground night club venue. The Main Auditorium is also home to the award-winning Komedia Comedy Club. The legendary Comedy Club features some of the best acts from the UK and international stand-up circuit every Saturday night. Each show features three world-class comedians and a top-notch compere. For the ultimate Saturday night out, add entry to The Big Disco after the comedy for just £2! Alongside this, Komedia is also very proud to run The Electric Bar – an intimate live performance space that was purpose-built to support grassroots-level music and rising comedy talent. The venue's Box Office is also situated within The Electric Bar, open Tuesday - Saturday from 10am - 5pm. Drop by to find out what’s on, take a quick tour of the venue or pick up a programme. Komedia is committed to being accessible to everyone and is continuously working to improve the experience of its disabled audiences, artists, and team members. For information on accessibility at Komedia, please visit: https://komediabath.co.uk/plan-your-visit/accessibility/
tagline: Hosting over 400 events per year in a beautifully restored former Edwardian cinema

title: Explore the Play Experience
subtitle: This summer, explore the joy of play at the Museum of Somerset, where you’ll discover a variety of playful experiences. This interactive exhibition invites you to get hands-on—create, explore, and rediscover familiar toys and games. Share memories, spark your imagination, and enjoy playful moments for all ages.
bodyContent: Explore Four Exciting Play Zones for All Ages Gaming In the Game zone, discover games from prehistory to Pokemon Mix it up with Nintendo and classic games of chess, draughts and noughts and crosses. See prehistoric tokens and early 20th century games from Ludo and Snakes and Ladders to Happy Families. Imagine Role play and see your childhood toys on display, in the Imaginative zone. Dress up, role play and strike a selfie in front of the costume wall. Where will you go and who will you see on your adventure? Reminisce about your favourite childhood toys – did you have a He-Man, Polly Pocket, Furby or Hornby train? Create Be inspired, make some noise and leave your mark in the Creative zone. Create a character out of magnets and leave your mark on the giant collective artwork. Play the Sound Game, and giggle at the unexpected noises made by toys! Explore Spark your next adventure in the Outdoor zone. Re-discover the simple pleasures of hula hoop and hopscotch. See old-fashioned scooters, wooden rackets, spinning tops and sticks from years gone by. Trails Everyday Enjoy boardgame-themed trails everyday in the summer holidays. Snakes and Ladders themed Museum trail (25 July – 8 August) Connect Four themed Museum trail (11 August – 2 September) ​25 July – 2 September, 10.00 am – 5.00 pm £2, drop in Play Events for Families Get hands-on, get creative and enjoy quality time together as a family. Family Aardman Model Making Workshops Drop in, Make & Play Craft a Game from the Past Workshop
tagline: Discover a variety of playful experiences.

title: Guided Tour of Taunton Minster
subtitle: If you’re looking to uncover the rich heritage of Taunton, the monthly guided tours at Taunton Minster are a must-add to your calendar.
bodyContent: Nestled in the heart of the town, this stunning building has stood for over a 700 years, and these tours offer a fascinating glimpse into its story. Come and explore the many interesting features of the building from its Saxon origins through to its role in modern-day Taunton. Visitors can admire beautiful architectural features, intricate stained glass, and hidden details that often go unnoticed during a casual visit. You’ll also hear stories from the past and present as the church seeks to serve the local community as a modern Minster. Whether you’re a history enthusiast, a local resident, or just visiting Somerset, the tours provide a welcoming and informative experience for all. It’s the perfect opportunity to slow down, explore, and connect with one of Taunton’s most treasured sites in a new way. Keep an eye on upcoming monthly dates every 2nd Saturday and treat yourself to a journey through time at Taunton Minster, you may discover something new with every visit. NOTE: Tours may be cancelled if there is an event - see website.
tagline: Discover the History of Taunton Minster: October's Monthly Guided Tour.

title: Wimbleball Lake
subtitle: It’s your outdoors – come and explore at Wimbleball Lake
bodyContent: Wimbleball Lake, nestled amongst the rolling hills of Exmoor , is a must-visit attraction during your stay in Somerset. Your little adventurers will love exploring and discovering all of the fun things to do at this majestic lake. Ditch the iPads, immerse yourself in nature and create lasting memories with the family. Den building, rolling down hills, spotting birds from a hide and, of course, enjoying a well-deserved ice cream from the Coffee Couture at Wimbleball are bound to be a huge hit. Activity Centre and Campsite Visit the Activity Centre and enjoy a family adventure like no other. Explore the lake by kayak Learn how to stand up paddleboard Spot wildlife from a canoe Hit the bullseye in a game of archery Face your fears and attempt the high ropes course Learn how to turn in a sail boat Relax and enjoy a spot of fishing Sleep under canvas or glamp in one of our pods, bell tents or cabin. Play Get your children learning and having fun on their next adventure by downloading South West Lakes’ 101 things to do this summer booklet and activity sheets . Identify trees, track prints, discover different leaves or go on a bug hunt. Visit the children’s play area or enjoy the plentiful open space for informal games. Walking and Cycling Embrace the outdoors and experience Wimbleball by bike or foot. The network of footpaths and cycle tracks suit visitors of all ages and abilities. Don’t forget to bring the dog! We want our four-legged friends to enjoy this special place. All we ask is for you to keep your dog on a lead and out of the water. Good Food Enjoy some delicious treats from our onsite cafe – Coffee Couture at Wimbleball. Treat the family to an ice cream or a cake and recharge with a coffee or a light lunch. Stargazing Exmoor National Park is designated an International Dark Sky Reserve - the very first in Europe! Wimbleball is a designated Dark Sky Discovery Site and is the perfect place to stargaze and engage with nature and the outdoors in its greatest form. Opening Times Wimbleball Lake is open all year round. The Activity Centre opening times vary throughout the season. Please visit www.swlakestrust.org.uk/activities for more information or call 01398 371460
tagline: It’s your outdoors – come and explore at Wimbleball Lake

title: The Stables Restaurant at Hestercombe Gardens
subtitle: Situated in the historic stables and cart house in Hestercombe’s Visitor Centre, The Stables Restaurant and Caffè + Gelato are the perfect place to indulge with some great home-made food.
bodyContent: The Stables Restaurant The Stables offers visitors an historic space to enjoy a delicious, home-made brunch, lunch or afternoon tea. It’s free to enter (no gardens admission required), whether you sit indoors within the warm and welcoming original stables, or outdoors in the stylish, light, glass-covered courtyard. Perfect for a celebratory lunch, a special catch up with friends or just a casual brunch. At The Stables, we pride ourselves on using high-quality ingredients, and whenever possible, we source locally, including fresh produce from on-site here at Hestercombe. This commitment to quality and locality is reflected in our unique menus, which are regularly updated to reflect the season. Reservations: call 01823 414197 between 10am - 5:00pm. Please note that during busy periods, The Stables Restaurant may not be able to answer your call immediately. Please leave a message with your name and contact details, and we will get back to you as soon as possible. Caffè + Gelato Our Caffè + Gelato is now open during the summer. Located in the former Gift Shop, Caffè + Gelato offers a varied assortment of sweet and savoury lunch options, hot and cold drinks and delicious, locally-made gelato by Baboo. It's also dog-friendly! Hestercombe is a fully cashless venue - only payments by debit or credit card, contactless, Apple Pay and Google Pay are accepted . ' Good to know Free to enter, no gardens admission required; The Stables is fully accessible; Dietary requirements can be catered for; Children's high chairs are available on request; The Stables is partially dog-friendly inside, and fully dog-friendly in the Courtyard. About Hestercombe Gardens Nestled at the foot of the Quantock Hills AONB, Hestercombe Gardens comprises of 50 acres of historic gardens, including the internationally-renowned Gertrude Jekyll and Sir Edwin Lutyens Formal Garden and Coplestone Warre Bampfylde’s magnificent Landscape Garden, complete with lakes, cascades, temples and incredible views. Located within the historic house alongside the Book Shop and Gift Shop, Hestercombe Gallery presents a regularly-changing programme of contemporary art, and is well worth a visit before or after dining at The Stables (gardens admission required).
tagline: Situated in the historic stables and cart house at Hestercombe Gardens

title: Weddings at Wookey Hole Resort
subtitle: Wookey Hole Caves are some of the most beautiful caves in the world and house some amazing rock formations and stunning clear pools. Carved by the River Axe over millions of years and with thousands of years of human history this makes a truly magical and atmospheric venue for wedding ceremonies.
bodyContent: Wookey Hole Caves are some of the most beautiful caves in the world and house some amazing rock formations and stunning clear pools. Carved by the River Axe over millions of years and with thousands of years of human history this makes a truly magical and atmospheric venue for wedding ceremonies. At Wookey Hole there are three chambers which are fully licensed for civil ceremonies, The Witch’s Kitchen, The Great Hall and The Witch’s Parlour. Each has its own qualities, such as the picturesque boat on the lake in Chamber 1, the vast height in the Great Hall which is where Chamber 2 gets its name, and the shallow dome of Chamber 3 which creates an intimate setting for small and large groups alike. The chosen chamber is lit with candles ready for the wedding ceremony and some of the chambers have coloured lights which can be changed to match the couples’ theme for their wedding. Only a handful of couples have chosen these beautiful caves for their ceremony and they remain one of the best kept secrets in Somerset and one of the few underground wedding venues in the world. A booking at Wookey Hole includes exclusive use of the caves and valley, reception room hire and discounted rooms in the hotel for guests. Some of the attractions are also available to hire as extras, such as the Victorian Penny Arcade or Pirate Golf to add a fun activity to the celebrations. The restaurant is a versatile space which can seat up to 200 people but is also suitable for much smaller parties, with ample space for music and dancing and also features an adjoining bar. Introducing Somerset’s newest Weddings and Functions space: The Water Wheel Suite; situated within the walls of the 17th Century, Grade II Listed Paper Mill at Wookey Hole, is a unique and elegant space able to lend itself beautifully to any occasion. Entitled the Water Wheel Suite, the name is derived from the stunning views offered through one of the many great windows of this room. Restored and revitalised, this room captures the true essence of Wookey Hole’s past. Inside, carved panels of exposed brickwork allude to this building’s rich heritage, offering a rustic look while contrasting with the most elegant interior. For weddings, this space can be beautifully illuminated and adorned to suit your individual desires.
tagline: Wookey Hole Caves are some of the most beautiful caves in the world and house some amazing rock form

title: Bossington Beach
subtitle: A picturesque hamlet in Selworthy Parish, on the National Trust's Holnicote Estate. Distinctve cottages with decorative chimney stacks and bread ovens bulging from the facades, line the single street. There are good walks along the Coast Path to Hurlestone Point and Porlock Marsh and superb views from Bossington Hill.
bodyContent: Pebbled beaches, secret coves, rocks and steep cliffs that is what Exmoor ’s 30 miles of coast are all about. At times you can get close to the water and at others you can look down on the sea from a swindling height or just sense the water beyond another green and inaccessible hill. Sometimes seagulls will sweep over your heads, telling stories of smugglers and rum, soldiers in hiding, and sailors lost at sea. Monuments in the landscape, made from stone or simple wood, standing sentinel against the force of the tide and the westerly wind, bear witness to the seagulls’ song of years gone by. It is so easy to lose yourself in this eternal landscape, where the tide is the second highest in the world. Thankfully the National Trust, Exmoor National Park and the South West Coast Path have combined their efforts to make sure that you won’t get lost while losing yourself. Many footpaths, all well signed, meander along the coast, providing access to many miles of stunning landscape. The South West Coast Path starts in Minehead , West Somerset’s nostalgic seaside resort where families, walkers, sunseekers and railway enthusiasts embark from the West Somerset Railway ’s steam trains for a first cone of locally made ice cream and a portion of fish and chips by the sea. Leaving Butlin’s resort to the east, a gentle stroll takes you to Minehead harbour, where - when the tide is in - modern day seafarers and fishermen are busy with their boats. Amongst them are wet-suited youngsters trying their balance on SUPs (stand up paddle boarding), while others, if the wind and the surf is right, fly across the sea windsurfing. Here the coast path leaves the sea level and heads up onto North Hill where Exmoor National Park begins. With a bit of luck, walkers will meet their first free roaming Exmoor Ponies before they head down again onto Bossington Beach which sweeps around Porlock Bay in a majestic swoosh all the way to Porlock Weir, another picturesque little harbour. In between and behind the pebbly ridge of the beach lies Porlock Marsh, a coastal wildlife area of national importance (designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest). On the shingle beach there are limekilns and pillboxes to be explored or simply used as a place to sit and stare. After Porlock Weir the coast is lined with cliffs, offering breathtaking viewpoints and steep descents. At Lynmouth awaits another little harbour which is linked by the Lynton and Lynmouth Cliff Railway, a cable car using the force of gravity, to its sister town on top of the cliff. In Lynmouth, West Lyn and East Lyn river join forces in a narrow gorge, causing death and distraction in the disaster of 1952, but now a safe place to watch the wild water tumbling over rocks towards the sea. Further west is the Valley of the Rocks, a place of unique rock formations and home to many feral goats as well as Exmoor Ponies. Here the Exmoor coast becomes even more rugged, but accessible enough for coasteering and abseiling. Those who don’t mind very narrow windy lanes should follow the road from the Valley of the Rocks to Hunters Inn, past Woody Bay. Leaving the car behind in the National Trust car park, it is worthwhile to go for a short walk down a narrow valley which finally opens out on a tiny pebbly beach, Heddon’s Mouth. It is a world away from the hustle and bustle of towns and cities. The Exmoor coast finally comes to an end at Combe Martin, the longest village in England. However, it is not far from there to Ilfracombe, an historic seaside town and fishing harbour, which has seen a return of fortunes in recent years. “Verity”, a controversial sculpture by Damien Hirst, has brought many tourists into the town which, since October 2016, is the proud home of a Michelin star restaurant, The Olive Room.

title: Dulverton
subtitle: Dulverton, Somerset is tucked away on the edge of Exmoor National Park, this tiny town boasts award-winning restaurants amongst the independent shops and historic houses that line the high street.
bodyContent: What to do in Dulverton, Exmoor, Somerset Dulverton in Exmoor, Somerset, is a jewel in the far west of Somerset, where streets are lined with cosy cottages and charming restaurants. It’s tucked into a spectacular and steeply-wooded valley where the River Barle meets the River Exe, and you’ll find many important bridges in the area - including the famous, prehistoric Tarr Steps, one of Exmoor’s highlights. Venture outside the village to explore the ancient Oldberry Castle site and the iron age hill forts of Mounsey Castle. Nature lovers will feel right at home in this national park, which is internationally recognised for its populations of deer, otters, bats and dormice. It’s been designated Europe’s first International Dark Skies Reserve, which means it offers stunning uninterrupted night sky views. The National Park Centre, which hosts exhibitions and a gallery about the area, makes for a great family day out, as does the Guildhall Heritage and Arts Centre. Here, you’ll see what life in Dulverton was like at the end of the 1800s thanks to the preserved Lamb Inn buildings.

title: Wookey Hole Cave Aged Cheddar
subtitle: Wookey Hole Cave Aged cheddar cheese, matured in the caves, a taste of Somerset.
bodyContent: Wookey Hole Cave Aged cheddar is a deliciously different traditional, PDO West Country Farmhouse Cheddar that has been the subject of countless awards for its unique flavour. And when you look at the process involved in the making of it before it reaches shop shelves, you'll understand why it has so often been crowned champion of cheddars since it was launched in 2006. Wookey Hole Cave Aged Cheddar starts life in the Dairy and is made using milk sourced from local grazing herds which graze the lush pastures of the Dorset Downs, no further than thirty miles from the Ashley Chase Estate where the dairy is located. The cheddars are made by hand to traditional cheddar recipes which date back many centuries by a team of highly skilled cheesemakers with over hundred years' experience between them. Once made and pressed into 27kg moulds, the truckles are bandaged in cheese cloth and transported to the Wookey Hole Caves where they are carried 200 feet underground by hand into a dedicated cave. The constant temperature and humidity of the caves provides the ideal conditions for maturing cheddars. The texture of Wookey Hole Cave Aged Cheddar is firm and the cheese is cream-coloured. The aroma is a complex mix of sweet, creamy, farmy and earthy. The flavours are big, robust and well rounded, with competing notes such as sweet and tangy as well as earthy and musty, reminiscent of the caves. Wookey Hole Cave Aged Cheddar carries the coveted PDO (protected designation of origin) badge. PDO regulations protect the names of traditional foods in order to define their authenticity and preserve their place of origin, traditional methods of production and essential ingredients. Wookey Hole Cave Aged Cheddar is the only PDO traditional West County Farmhouse Cheddars to be matured in caves. Wookey Hole Cave Aged Cheddar is widely available throughout the UK at supermarkets, delis and cheese shops. Look out also for Wookey Hole Cave Aged Goat's Cheese, a mild goat's cheese with a firm texture, similar to cheddar and a subtle clean goat flavour. If you cant get to us why not buy online? https://www.fordfarm.com/cave-aged-cheddar/
tagline: Wookey Hole Cave Aged cheddar cheese, matured in the caves, a taste of Somerset.

title: Tintinhull, National Trust
subtitle: A place of floral beauty, tranquillity and innovation - a gardener's garden paradise.
bodyContent: The garden, complete with working kitchen garden and orchard, lies in the charming village of Tintinhull, Somerset. Glittering pools, secluded lawns, colourful borders and clipped hedges provide the perfect spot to relax and unwind away from the hustle and bustle. The 17th century house is a National Trust holiday cottage sleeping up to eight people. Surrounded by the mellow colours of old brick and Ham stone, Tintinhull garden is the creation of two twentieth century gardeners: the first was an untrained amateur whose name is often still unrecognised, and the second is one of the UK’s most distinguished garden writers and designers. The garden was created around a 17 th century, Grade I listed house; garden and house are intertwined, with the house visible from every part of the garden and the garden layout planned with an eye to those looking out from house. The strong design of the garden was the work of Phyllis Reiss, who bought Tintinhull with her husband in 1933 and left it to the National Trust after her death in 1961. She was a shy woman, born into a disappearing world of leisured prosperity; influenced by gardens such as Hidcote and travels throughout France and Italy, she was part of a circle of gardeners that included the renowned Vita Sackville-West, then creating her own garden at Sissinghurst. Reiss took a ‘painterly’ approach to her garden, aiming for impact and emotional effect. She took ideas from famed garden designer Gertrude Jekyll, but simplified the herbaceous planting and planned imaginative and bold colour schemes. The garden is deceptively disciplined, with a strict formal framework offset with much looser floriferous planting; Reiss also included architectural plants for year-round interest. Twenty years after Reiss’s death, Penelope Hobhouse took on the tenancy at Tintinhull with her husband Professor Malins. It was while living at Tintinhull that Hobhouse developed her ideas on colour and became an internationally renowned garden designer and writer; many of her books reference her work at Tintinhull, where she used pots to dramatic effect and maintained Reiss’s experimental spirit. Reiss intended her ‘happy’ garden to be a place of peace and tranquillity, especially so after the creation of the Pool Garden in memory of her nephew, who was killed in the Second World War. After more than 50 years in National Trust ownership, Tintinhull is a garden with dramatic impact, but also a haven of quiet calm. If you need to call Tintinhull please ring 01458 224471, but be aware that the line connects to Lytes Cary Manor. title: Longleat
subtitle: Explore a world of adventure at Longleat. From a Drive Through Safari expedition, to discovering inside our iconic Elizabethan mansion, there’s plenty to entertain you.
bodyContent: Explore a world of adventure at Longleat. From a Drive Through Safari expedition, to discovering inside our iconic Elizabethan mansion, there’s plenty to entertain you. Travel the globe within this Wiltshire estate – stop off at African Village for a chance to see our new pack of African painted dogs, herd of Grants zebras and leap with lemurs. Say hi to our cheeky monkeys and bring your pack to meet our pack of wolves! Listen out for the Longleat lions’ roars as you explore. Continue your adventure on foot and walk with mischievous meerkats in Jungle Kingdom, feed rainbow lorikeets and watch our playful giant otters. Don’t forget to visit Koala Creek to see England’s only resident koalas, watch our sleepy sloths climb around or check in with our native red squirrels. Hop on board the Boat Safari and explore Half Mile Pond. Home to our family of noisy Californian sea lions, views of Gorilla Colony and Colobus monkeys will make quite a splash. Why not feed the sea lions to add to your unique day out? All aboard Longleat Railway! Enjoy a delightful ride around the lake and keep an eye on the action from our miniature railway. Or discover more about our history by adding a guided house tour to your itinerary. If your little cubs are looking to play, be sure to visit Little Explorer’s Garden and the Adventure Castle for plenty of room to let their imaginations run wild. Why not challenge yourself to our Hedge Maze and see if you can find your way through the winding passages? And no day is complete without a ride on Rockin’ Rhino! Book your tickets for a day out like no other or make your visit extra special with a VIP experience!
tagline: Longleat, nestled within 900 acres of ‘Capability’ Brown landscaped grounds.

title: East Somerset Railway
subtitle: The friendly steam railway welcomes you! Come to the lovely village of Cranmore, near Shepton Mallet, Somerset to meet our friendly staff and take a relaxing ride on our heritage steam trains.
bodyContent: The train journey is approximately 40 minutes over our 5 mile round trip. You are welcome to ride as many times as you like on your visit - subject to availability of seats. Due to Covid-19 restrictions and social distancing, pre booking is now essential to guarantee a place on the train of your choice. We are one of very few steam railways where you can visit our engine shed and workshop to see restoration in progress carried out by our skilled bunch of volunteers We have a newly refurbished museum, waiting room and ticket office. There is also the David Shepherd Discovery Centre on our restored second platform. Find out about the history of our railway and the life of the world famous wildlife artist whose vision for the railway made it what it is today. The signal box and miniature railway are also open on specific days – please see our website for details. We have a well stocked shop and the Whistlestop Café serves a great range of food and drink. You are also able to take afternoon tea on our Mendip Belle coach on certain days – pre-booking essential. We have a large, free car park with disabled spaces There is ramp access to the platform and wheelchair accessible seating on the train. We are working towards becoming dementia friendly across the whole site. We welcome dogs, which travel free. Our friendly staff and volunteers are always available to assist in any way.
tagline: The friendly steam railway welcomes you! Come to the lovely village of Cranmore

title: A winter wander around Weston-super-Mare
subtitle: Begin the walk at the Grade II-listed Weston-super-Mare train station – opened in 1884 on a new loop which replaced the 1841 branch line. Brunel’s Grade II-listed signal box is in the adjacent car park as a reminder of this previous trackway.
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: about 1.4 miles Difficulty: easy – a level walk on pavements. Wheelchair, pushchair and dog friendly Duration: about 90 minutes at a leisurely pace Begin the walk at the Grade II-listed Weston-super-Mare train station – opened in 1884 on a new loop which replaced the 1841 branch line. Brunel’s Grade II-listed signal box is in the adjacent car park as a reminder of this previous trackway. From the station, go over the zebra crossing onto Station Road, past a row of 1930s Art Deco houses on your left, and past local architect Hans Fowler Price’s French-style depository, now Nightingale’s storage facility. Behind the 20-metre Pennant and Ham stone tower of Victoria Methodist Church is the 190-year-old Whitecross Lodge, former home of Richard Parsley who built Weston’s first hotel. You then pass the 1934 former magistrates’ court, most recently used as a television drama location. At the roundabout look left towards Walliscote Primary School, built in 1897 by Hans Price as Weston’s first ‘board school’. Turn right past the Italianate Town Hall, opened in 1859, extended by Price in 1897, further extended in ‘Post Office Georgian’ in 1927, and the brick wing added in 1980. title: Cosy One Bedroom Apartment
subtitle: Bright and quirky one bedroom apartment in the heart of Bath.
bodyContent: Situated on the East side of Bath on the London Road, just a ten minute stroll from the centre of town. Walcot is Bath’s artisan quarter – home to The Bell (award winning, community owned pub) as well as many other bars, restaurants, antiques markets, small business’ and cafes. The property on Walcot Buildings is a top floor flat set in a converted grade II listed building. It has a bright double bedroom with comfortable bed and traditional wooden shutters. There is plenty of storage space with a built in cupboard and chest of drawers. South facing it gets the sunshine all day. The living room has a comfortable sofa, coffee table, books and games as well as a TV (with Netflix). A separate, self contained kitchen contains all the white goods and utensils you would need for an enjoyable stay. The bathroom has a bath and shower and all of the amenities you would expect. We love the flat and eclectic mix of neighbours and residents that live nearby. We’ve provided everything you’ll need to relax and feel at home. There is a large supermarket a couple of minutes walk away for all the supplies you’ll need to make your stay special. Also a 24 hour shop just 2 minutes away for those midnight snacks.

title: Stable Cottage: 6 bed country cottage
subtitle: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.
bodyContent: It is located in the beautiful Georgian village of Freshford which lies at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys in the southern Cotswolds. There are some wonderful walks to local pubs following the riverside and canals. All just 15 minutes from Bath by car but the secret of this location is the 9 minute train journey to Bath from the village station, just a short stroll from the cottages. The cottage : Stable cottage is a newly renovated, limestone floored, 3 bedroom, two bathroom (one is en-suite) cottage. It has large windows to the front of the house filling the bedrooms and downstairs with light on a sunny day. It has an open plan living/dining area with free view TV/DVD and two large suedette couches and comfortable chairs. For dining there is a blond Oak dining table and chairs to seat 6 . The Stables can accommodate 6 people in three bedrooms (two king size and one double) . The kitchen is fully equipped with cookware,dishwasher and washing machine . The house also offers Iron/Ironing board, Hairdryers All bed linen and towels . There is a Welcome pack of tea, coffee, sugar, milk, bread, butter, eggs and bacon. Free WiFi. There are also books and board-games in the house for the use of guests. If you have any questions on Bath and the local area before or during your stay please let us know. We would be delighted to help. Neighbourhood overview : Freshford is a beautiful ancient village with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk from the cottage( The Inn at Freshford) that serves restaurant quality food and all the local beers and ciders.They have an excellent fully stocked( from wine to organic humus!)community shop that also has a good quality cafe that serves lunch. There is also a local doctors surgery. The village is nestled at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys . The Kennet and Avon canal is a 15 minute walk from the cottage. Getting around : You don’t need a car to stay in the cottage. The village station is a few minutes walk away. Trains hourly off peak and thrice hourly at peak times. Bath 9 mins, Bristol 22mins. London Padington to Bath Spa 1.5 hours Bath Spa to Freshford 9 minutes Bath Spa to Freshford “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/bath-spa-to-freshford ” Freshford to Bath Spa “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/freshford-to-bath-spa ” There is also a local bus service to all the adjacent villages and Bath. The cottage has two parking spaces suitable for one medium and one small car or a single large SUV.the surrounding towns you might want to visit. Other things to note If you are a runner or keep fit enthusiast the owner is a qualified Personal Trainer (Bath Uni) with much Marathon and half marathon experience. She specialises in Ladies training. Please let us know if you would like guided running or some Personal Fitness training.
tagline: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.

title: ⭐Shepton Mallet Prison
subtitle: Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’; Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom...
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’, Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom. Shepton Mallet Prison is a recently decommissioned (2013) Georgian jail where visitors can walk in the footsteps of our social history and hear officers shine a light on what life was like for both the incarcerated and those who guarded them through the ages. Before its closure, it was a category C lifer prison holding 189 prisoners. Opened in 1646, it was expanded in 1790, with further building work undertaken in the 1820s and 1830s, including the installation of a treadwheel for those sentenced to hard labour. In 1930, the inmate numbers fell and the prison was closed. During the Second World War, the prison was reopened and used as a military prison. It was initially used by the British Army and later by American forces, who constructed a new execution block for condemned prisoners. It was also used for the storage of important historical documents, including the Domesday Book. It returned to civilian use in 1966. Shepton Mallet prison is also known for its tales of paranormal activity. One of the most popular stories is that of the White Lady. She is frequently seen or sensed in various locations, especially A Wing. Staff and prisoners would often complain of an icy wind moving through the wing, the sweet smell of perfume and shadowy figures. She supposedly dates from the late 1700s, when she spent some time in the prison. During a lovers' tiff which escalated, she murdered her betrothed. Once found guilty and sentenced to death, she was housed in Shepton Mallet Prison. On the evening before her execution, she asked for her wedding dress to be brought to the prison, which they allowed. She wore it to bed that night, but in the morning the officers found that she had died during the night. No cause of death was ever found, so we are left to presume that she died of a broken heart. Perhaps this is why she still haunts the prison? In the early 1950s, the Kray Twins were also held here after deserting the British Army. Today, the prison is open as a tourist attraction offering Guided Tours, Self-Guided Tours, Escape Rooms, Night Behind Bars and Ghost Hunting Behind Bars. This is an immersive experience without gizmos or gimmicks – the jail is very much as it was when the last prisoners left in 2013. In 2025, Shepton Mallet Prison received the prestigious Trip Advisor Travellers’ Choice, for the 7th time running, placing it among the top 10% of attractions worldwide.

title: Wookey Hole Caves & Attractions
subtitle: Wookey Hole Caves is a magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for all ages. It’s an experience millions of years in the making with plenty to do inside and out. Enjoy vintage penny arcades, museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, and of course the famous, beautiful caves.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Wookey Hole Caves and attractions lies In the heart of Somerset. A magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for the young and young at heart. When you visit Wookey Hole, you’ll enjoy an experience millions of years in the making. There is plenty to do inside and out, from vintage penny arcades to museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, to name but a few of the attractions. Not forgetting the breathtakingly beautiful caves, for which Wookey Hole is renowned. Your visit will take you through 8 chambers. Each with a unique beauty and story. You’ll also pass our cheese tunnel, home to the delicious Wookey Hole cheese. The cheese is not the only resident of the caves. Over the years, Wookey Hole has been home to giant hyenas, bears, Neanderthals, and many local people. It has even been a site of pagan and Roman worship. You’ll find Wookey Hole holds a surprise around every corner. You might even get to meet our most famous resident, the Witch of Wookey Hole. We have found she most likes to visit during school holidays! The world-famous Wookey Hole Circus School performs at Wookey Hole at weekends and in School Holidays. Every year over 250,000 people visit Wookey Hole and take-home cherished memories of a great day out. Whether it is your first time or your fiftieth, there is always something new to discover. We can’t wait to welcome you.
tagline: At Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions, Somerset, there’s always fun and adventure to be had.

We have found she most likes to visit during school holidays! The world-famous Wookey Hole Circus School performs at Wookey Hole at weekends and in School Holidays. Every year over 250,000 people visit Wookey Hole and take-home cherished memories of a great day out. Whether it is your first time or your fiftieth, there is always something new to discover. We can’t wait to welcome you.
tagline: At Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions, Somerset, there’s always fun and adventure to be had.

title: Queen of Cups Restaurant and Freehouse
subtitle: Queen of Cups is a restaurant and free house based in Glastonbury that focuses on local and seasonal food and drink combined with Mediterranean flavours. The talented kitchen team is helmed by Chef Proprietor Ayesha Kalaji. We stock local wines, ales and spirits and offer unique takes on cocktails and mocktails. Queen of Cups caters for omnivores, vegetarians, vegans and special diets alike.
bodyContent: Queen of Cups is open for lunch and dinner year round. The menu changes seasonally and all desserts are made in-house. The space features a lovely back garden as well as a suntrap pavement terrace for after-work drinks. We have been named the #1 restaurant in Glastonbury on TripAdvisor, as well as #3 in Somerset. As we occupy what was the famous Hawthorns Hotel, we have kept on their weekly music nights such as Sunday Blues Jam and Tuesday Open Mic (please refer to Facebook or our website for event updates). Not forgetting our incredibly well stocked bar, we are a proud member of CAMRA: the Campaign for Real Ale. Queen of Cups also offers a private dining room that seats up to 12 people, curated by Kim Von Coels of Heart of the Tribe. In the private dining room we offer our popular Queen's Feast sharing menu, as well as create custom menus.
tagline: Queen of Cups is a restaurant and free house based in Glastonbury

title: Leighton Townhouse
subtitle: Spoil yourselves at Leighton Townhouse. We are just a 10 minute walk from the city centre.
bodyContent: Spoil yourselves at Leighton Townhouse. We are just a 10 minute walk from the city centre, in a peaceful 140-year old Victorian villa, set in lovely gardens, with great views away from the hustle and bustle of the city centre and offering complimentary on-site car parking. We have recently refurbished and refreshed all our bedrooms and guest areas to provide 10 individually designed and beautifully decorated guest rooms, all of which have air conditioning, as well as beautiful bathrooms with underfloor heating, power showers and many with spa baths.
tagline: Spoil yourselves at Leighton Townhouse. We are just a 10 minute walk from the city centre.

title: The Bird
subtitle: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to. A place to work and meet and by day and discover ever-changing bar experiences by night.
bodyContent: To be found just a few minutes’ stroll from Bath’s spectacular city-centre attractions, The Bird, Bath (previously The County Hotel) has re-branded to fit in with its distinctive new personality as part of the Kaleidoscope Collection. Owned by seasoned hoteliers, Ian and Christa Taylor, The Bird is a name that better reflects the vibrant transformation of the hotel, which has already seen refreshed public spaces, additional bedrooms, a new bar, relaxed restaurant and meeting spaces, as well as a much-loved pop-up beach bar for summer. Now with 27 en-suite bedrooms featuring every home comfort, many have far-reaching views across the cricket and rugby grounds to Bath Abbey, with the rolling hills of Bath and beyond. Breakfast is served in a lovely bright dining room, which overlooks Bath Abbey and opens into the conservatory, where morning coffee and afternoon tea can be enjoyed, while the Taylors have also created a wonderfully eclectic neighbourhood bar with a relaxed food offering, designed as social hub for work or play. A space for freelancers to work, friends to meet for coffee or a relaxed dinner, there’s a bar for seasonal drinks and various seating areas centred around vast contemporary pieces of art. A separate meeting room also provides a creative space for workshops and get-togethers, private parties, celebrations and more. Visitors and locals alike won’t have to wait long for the next seasonal pop-up, a visually exciting Winter Wonderland for the festive season, and arguably the coolest party space in town. Set in a fantastical venue full of surprises, woodland branches and spruces will be strewn with fairy lights, tables topped with flickering candelabra and chairs draped in Bavarian rugs to keep you cosy. Everyone is welcome to simply drop in to experience the magical vibe. The Bird is easily reached via all main approaches to Bath, and has plenty of parking for guests.
tagline: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to

title: Spacious Double Room in West Bath
subtitle: Spacious Double bedroom in Victorian terraced house to the west of the city of Bath.
bodyContent: Property has good transport links to city centre, as well as being close to all local amenities you should need for a pleasant stay with us. The house is situated to the west side of the beautiful city of Bath. Furnished with a mix of modern and vintage furniture, the property has all you need for a relaxing stay. There are good transport links to the town centre, with services stopping less than two minutes from us. There is also ample free street parking outside our door. The breakfast room/lounge has a very homely feel and contains books, games and suggestions on where to go in Bath. Guests also have use of our ultra fast fibre broadband. We’ve equipped the kitchen to make cooking easy with a host of ingredients and basic utensils. You’ll have your own private double bedroom with large comfortable double bed and ample storage space. You can also benefit from shared use of the modern and well equipped kitchen, comfortable living room and bathroom. I like to give guests their own space during their stay, however I am always available to offer recommendations and help, both before and during their stay. I am never far away or am in the house, and am always on hand should you need me. I usually arrange for a self check in but can always be on hand if a guest would like me to help them check in. We are a five minute walk from the high street where you’ll find a supermarket, takeaways and a few local shops. There are a number of good pubs and bars in the area all walking distance from us. Alternatively, its less than ten minutes into town by taxi and shouldn’t cost you more than £6-£7. The property is less than two minutes from the bus stop where you can catch regular services into the town centre. There is plenty of on street parking outside the house. We are about ten to fifteen minutes walk from Oldfield Park train station where you can access services to London and Bristol. Check-In: 3PM-9PM Not suitable for children (2-12 years) Not suitable for infants (under 2 years) Not suitable for pets No smoking No parties or events
tagline: Spacious Double bedroom in Victorian terraced house to the west of the city of Bath.

title: Toghill House Farm
subtitle: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds. Within a stone’s throw of the site of the battle of Lansdown and with the Cotswold Way and the old east to west Roman road running through the grounds, Toghill is steeped in history.
bodyContent: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds. Within a stone’s throw of the site of the battle of Lansdown and with the Cotswold Way and the old east to west Roman road running through the grounds, Toghill is steeped in history. Located on a working farm only 4 miles north of Bath, with spectacular views over the Welsh mountains, Mendips, Cotswolds and Historic Bath. We have 9 rooms, some of which are in the 17th century farmhouse and others in the pretty Cotswold stone converted barns and stables in a delightful courtyard setting.
tagline: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds.

title: Continue Arcades
subtitle: A “Free Play” gaming lounge that has zero restrictions upon entry. Pay once for unlimited play.
bodyContent: A “Free Play” gaming lounge that has zero restrictions upon entry. Pay once for unlimited play. Where gaming dreams come to life! As Somerset's go-to arcade destination, offering a diverse selection of games and a vibrant gaming community. Whether you're a seasoned gamer or just looking for a fun day out, Continue Arcades has something for everyone., offering a route back in time, high street escapism and endless fun. Step through our doors and embark on a journey through gaming history and innovation. With over 70 arcade machines spanning decades of gaming evolution, Continue Arcades is not just a place to play but a time machine that transports you back to the golden era of gaming. From retro classics like Pac-Man and Space Invaders to modern favorites such as Dance Dance Revolution and racing simulators, every corner of our arcade is designed to evoke nostalgia and excitement.
tagline: Where dreams come to life!

title: Children's Orchard Trail
subtitle: Explore Sheppy's orchards on a family-friendly Story Trail designed for children aged 3–8. Discover woodland animals, enjoy the countryside and take part in a range of seasonal activities during the summer holidays.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Enjoy a summer adventure at Sheppy's Cider Farm with the Children's Orchard Trail. Designed for children aged 3–8, the trail takes families through the orchards to discover woodland animals and follow their holiday adventures while enjoying the sights and sounds of nature. Alongside the trail, visitors can meet the farm animals, explore the children's play areas, visit the duck pond and enjoy the café and farm shop. Families can also take part in the Wildlife Photography Competition and the Big Butterfly Count, helping to record the wildlife living in the orchards. Walking routes can become muddy, so suitable footwear is recommended. All children must be accompanied by a parent or guardian at all times.
tagline: A family-friendly orchard trail with woodland adventures and summer wildlife activities.

title: Guided Tour of Taunton Minster
subtitle: Our September Monthly Guided Tour coincides with the Heritage Open Days, making it a wonderful opportunity to explore the Minster as part of this special national celebration.
bodyContent: Nestled in the heart of the town, this stunning building has stood for over a 700 years, and these tours offer a fascinating glimpse into its story. Come and explore the many interesting features of the building from its Saxon origins through to its role in modern-day Taunton. Visitors can admire beautiful architectural features, intricate stained glass, and hidden details that often go unnoticed during a casual visit. You’ll also hear stories from the past and present as the church seeks to serve the local community as a modern Minster. Whether you’re a history enthusiast, a local resident, or just visiting Somerset, the tours provide a welcoming and informative experience for all. It’s the perfect opportunity to slow down, explore, and connect with one of Taunton’s most treasured sites in a new way. Keep an eye on upcoming monthly dates every 2nd Saturday and treat yourself to a journey through time at Taunton Minster, you may discover something new with every visit. NOTE: Tours may be cancelled if there is an event - see website.
tagline: The monthly guided tours at Taunton Minster are a must-add to your calendar.

title: The Kennet and Avon Cannel runs 140 KM
subtitle: Fascinating Somerset facts The Kennet and Avon Cannel runs 140 KM through Bath, Somerset Linking the Bristol Channel and London. Completed in 1810, this canal was the culmination of 80 years’ work as the River Kennet and River Avon were joined by the canal.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"197"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

THE KENNET AND AVON CANAL RUNS 140 KM through Bath, Somerset - Linking the Bristol Channel and London. Completed in 1810, this canal was the culmination of 80 years’ work as the River Kennet and River Avon were joined by the canal.

Despite the best of intentions, the canal never really flourished as an industrial waterway after the Great Western Railway route was opened between the two cities, and traffic on the canal declined dramatically. The canal soon fell into disrepair and it wasn’t until 1963 that the British Waterways commenced restoration work alongside a newly formed trust. The canal is now part of the National Cycle Network, with the entire Somerset section of the path suitable for either an afternoon stroll or a more strenuous cycle ride.

 





For a pleasant walk and introduction to the magnificent architecture adjacent to the canal, a good starting point is Sydney Gardens, situated next to the Holburne Museum. The walk towards Bathampton takes in splendid views of the canal boats now cruising with relaxed holidaymakers, and an ideal midpoint stop (before returning) is the George Inn, which sits beside the canal. If you decide to walk towards the centre of Bath, you’ll discover elegant cast-iron bridges sweeping over the canal and the architectural beauty of Cleveland House, one of the canal’s most famous features.

For more on Somerset's incredible history and heritage go to our interactive E Book.

title: Frome
subtitle: The picturesque town of Frome is the perfect destination for a day trip or short break. Explore medieval streets lined with independent stores, experience award-winning markets, soak up the thriving arts scene, indulge in local culinary delights and venture into the beautiful surrounding countryside.
bodyContent: Frome’s welcoming charm is instant, so it’s no surprise that the town’s been named one of the best places to live in Britain by The Sunday Times, one of Time Out’s best weekend breaks from London and ‘the most Stylish town in the UK’. Perfectly placed at the eastern end of the Mendip Hills, Frome enjoys excellent rail and local transport links making it the ideal base from which to explore North East Somerset. Once one of the largest towns in Somerset, Frome boasts a rich industrial heritage founded in the wool and cloth industry and later diversifying into metal-working and printing. Although these industries have since declined, their legacy lives on with Frome laying claim to over 350 listed buildings – more than any other town in Somerset. For those interested in exploring this historical side to the town, the Frome Museum is a hive of information and Frome’s popular guided walks offer a unique insight into the colourful history of the town. In recent years Frome has become synonymous with the word “Independent”. Local retailers have reclaimed the streets of Frome providing a unique shopping experience. The cornerstone of this vibrant scene is St Catherine’s artisan quarter where you’ll find everything from gifts and vintage clothing to bespoke jewellery and modern arts and crafts studios. Heading down the hill to the Market Place and Cheap Street you’ll find local produce, music and book stores and interior design retailers. Refuel at one of Frome’s many eateries – choose from friendly cafés, traditional pubs, stylish restaurants and lively bars. The Frome market scene is thriving with weekly markets on Wednesday and Saturday. On the first weekend of each month the town hosts Frome Vegan Market, followed by the award-winning Frome Farmer’s Market on each second Saturday. On the first Sunday of the month you’ll find the award-winning Frome Independent - fast becoming one of the UK’s most popular destination markets. Frome’s also spoilt for choice when it comes to the arts and entertainment. The Cheese and Grain, rooted in the centre of Frome is one of Somerset’s key music venues and has played host to some of the finest acts in the world, while the Merlin and Memorial theatres welcome touring shows, comedy and local productions. The Frome Festival, Carnival and Agricultural & Cheese Show are annual events not to be missed. Explore outside Frome to see rolling Somerset countryside at its finest. Walks include the 50-mile Mendip way, starting in Frome and ending by the sea at Weston-super-Mare. For cycling enthusiasts, the Collier’s Way takes you on a picturesque ride towards Bath making use of disused railway tracks and quiet country lanes. For urban adventures, Frome’s eBike hire scheme means you can discover the town with an electrically-assisted cycle, making traversing hills a breeze. Discover Frome Information Point: Located at Black Swan Arts, the information point is manned by volunteers and specifically focusses on the arts, events and trails. Welcoming residents and visitors alike, the information point is part of a plan to better inform people of the amazing array of events and experiences that the town has to offer. Enquiries can also be directed to Frome Town Hall.

title: Somerset Cider Brandy Company & Burrow Hill Cider
subtitle: At Burrow Hill we make traditional ciders as well as Somerset Cider Brandy. Visit the farm and see the UK’s first commercial cider distillery, explore the orchards and wander amongst 170 year old vats.
bodyContent: Somerset Cider resides at Burrow Hill where they make traditional ciders as well as Somerset Cider Brandy. Visit the farm and see the UK’s first commercial cider distillery, explore the orchards and wander amongst 170 year old vats. Or just come and sample our award winning ciders, Somerset Cider Brandy and liqueurs. Guided tours can also be booked in advance. Open all year. Monday - Saturday 9.00 - 5.00 Cider House - In the ciderhouse there is cider and Somerset Cider Brandy to sample amongst the oak vats, barrels and presses - all the paraphernalia associated with 150 years of cider making. Burrow Hill - Visitors are also encouraged to walk to the top of our hill and admire the incredible views of the Somerset Levels. On a good day you can see Glastonbury Tor in the distance. The Orchard - The starting point of both our cider and Somerset Cider Brandy is apples from our orchards. Visitors can follow our orchard trail where different apple varieties and other interesting features are explained. The walk takes about 30 minutes and you may need wellies. Distillery - Visitors are welcome to view the copper stills, protected by armour-plated glass and 68 locks and seals (by order of HM Customs & Excise) in the distillery. You can also buy our products online at https://www.somersetciderbrandy.com/

title: The Garden Coffee House
subtitle: Come and visit our fabulous new coffee house! Delicious breakfasts, cream teas and homemade cakes – sharing boards, summer salads and light lunches – a la carte evening dining, sundowner cocktails and GinSpiration drinks menu. Not to mention the locally roasted specialty Brazier coffees and Somerset Miles teas! We offer a stylish and relaxing atmosphere set within the grounds of The Cleve, a historic country house and spa. We boast ample parking and a beautiful garden to soak up the stunning Som
bodyContent: The Garden Coffee House at The Cleve is the latest addition to our family-owned and run country house hotel and spa. In celebration of our 40 th year of owning The Cleve, we have introduced a fabulous new element for our guests and a new passion to our adventures – coffee! We sourced the most wonderful locally roasted speciality coffee at Brazier’s Coffee Roasters and we have adopted the much loved Miles Somerset Teas. These form the basis for our coffee house, with an emphasis on locally produced ingredients and on quality foods and drinks. We are particularly passionate about Brazier’s coffees because of the very personal link that they have to our beautiful house – Brazier coffee is roasted in an old mill formerly owned and run by the Fox family, who designed and built The Cleve. When you visit, ask our staff about the history of The Cleve and take a look at the various photographs of the Victorian mills that line our walls of the Garden Coffee House. The Garden Coffee House is open to all from breakfast through to after dinner drinks. Visit us for delicious food at breakfast, lunch or dinner, or for a catch up over good quality coffee and homemade cake. Or if after-work drinks are more your thing, share a Tapas board with friends or colleagues over a Sundowner cocktail or two. Dogs more than welcome!
tagline: A stylish licensed coffee house, with specialty Brazier coffees

title: Museum of Somerset
subtitle: The Museum of Somerset tells the county's story from prehistoric times to the present day using real objects combined with evocative films, sounds and images, and the voices and words of Somerset people past and present.
bodyContent: ENTRY TO THE MUSEUM IS FREE! Visit Taunton Castle Housed in Taunton ’s historic castle, the Museum of Somerset tells the county's fascinating story from prehistoric times to the present day. Within the 12th century castle walls you’ll find contemporary gallery spaces and great family visitor facilities, all situated within the vibrant town centre. Discover 400 million years of history With an amazing nine themed galleries, each with its own distinctive character, there’s something for everyone to discover. Our ‘must see’ exhibits include a 200 million year old Plesiosaur fossil (a type of marine reptile); the impressive Low Ham Roman mosaic; a stunning Bronze Age Gold Torc; the Giant’s Shoes worn by 7ft4 Joseph Sewell; and the Banwell Bear skull of an 80,000 year old Ice Age hunter-killer. The museum also houses The Somerset Military Museum. What's On? There's always something going on for families with activities and family fun days throughout the year. February & October half term Drop in for family fun activities throughout the school holidays Easter Complete our Egg-cellent Easter Trail and take part in themed activities Summer Fun Whatever the weather you'll find something for everyone at our family friendly summer exhibition and events Halloween Explore the Museum on the spookiest night of the year - dress up if you dare! Christmas Visit Santa in his grotto every Saturday in December Entry to the museum is free but donations are welcome. There may be a charge for some activities, events or exhibitions. Café and shop The Courtyard Café offers a selection of home-made Somerset treats, from soups, sandwiches and salads, to pastries and home-made cakes. You can also visit the museum shop which stocks a range of reasonably-priced toys, cards, books and gifts including the ‘Made in Somerset’ range of local food and drink. The Museum of Somerset is part of the South West Heritage Trust, an independent charity committed to protecting and celebrating Somerset and Devon’s rich heritage.
tagline: The Museum of Somerset tells the county's story from prehistoric times to the present day.

title: The County Ground
subtitle: The striking and historic County Ground in Taunton is the home of Somerset County Cricket Club.
bodyContent: The Cooper Associates County Ground in Taunton is the home of Somerset County Cricket Club who have played there since 1882. It is overlooked by the towers of three churches and is renowned for its quintessentially English character and history. The pitch is surrounded by a number of stands and pavillions such as the Somerset Stand, the Old Pavillion and the Marcus Trescothick stand. It currently has a capacity of 8,500 but can be increased to 12,500 for internationals. The County Ground hosted International World Cup games in 1983, 1999, 2017 and 2019. It has also played host to sell-out concerts from artists including Elton John and Rod Stewart. The Somerset Cricket Museum is located at The County Ground and houses displays that mainly concentrate on the history of Somerset County cricket. Also on site are the SCCC Shop , the official merchandise store of Somerset County Cricket Club, and The Stragglers Coffee House which offers high quality breakfasts, lunches and drinks.
tagline: The home of Somerset County Cricket Club

title: Mattancherry
subtitle: Warm, welcoming and full of life and colour our restaurant captures the essence of Mattancherry. Step inside a little piece of India and experience the exotic aromas and flavours of Keralan cuisine in an atmosphere that captures the hospitality and generosity of Mattancherry’s unique community.
bodyContent: Mattancherry - a remarkable, diverse and vibrant waterside area of Kochi inspires us to create a restaurant that celebrates its unique culinary social history. Explorers,traders and adventurers have been drawn here for more than a 1000 years from all corners of india and the world. All leaving their influence on a region already rich in the finest spices and exotic ingredients. Our restaurant brings you the taste of southern india's world class cuisine, along with the best of india, a mix of flavours, ingredients, textures and tastes that can only be Mattancherry in three square miles
tagline: India in three square miles

title: Lock and Code Escape Rooms
subtitle: Amazing escape rooms on the outskirts of Taunton, which are suitable for all ages either couples, families, friends, stag and hen parties or corporate events. Come and challenge your puzzle solving abilities, use your teamwork and see if you can escape. With 3 escape rooms in Taunton, we are the number one for fun and games in Taunton on Tripadvisor.
bodyContent: One team, one room, one mission. Can you escape in just 60 minutes? Real-life room escape games are a type of physical adventure game in which people are in a room with other participants and have to use elements of the room to solve a series of puzzles, find clues, and escape the room within a set time limit. Think of it as a mix between The Da Vinci code and a treasure hunt. Here at Lock and Code we intend to deliver an unforgettable experience, with story driven and atmospheric rooms. Our rooms are suitable for couples, groups of adults, families and older children. You need a minimum of 2 people to play and a maximum of 6 for each room. Don't worry, if you're playing as a couple or smaller group, you still get the room to yourself. We wont add in other players like some other escape rooms! More people or a corporate event? We can arrange for you to have more than one room. Why not read our 5 star reviews on Tripadvisor or on our Facebook page?
tagline: Escape rooms on the outskirts Taunton, which are suitable for all ages

title: Delving into Nailsea’s industrial heritage
subtitle: Start at the15th century Holy Trinity Church, in Church Lane. It has a tower typical to the area but the pinnacles weren’t added until 1904.
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: about 2.5 miles Difficulty: easy - a level, urban walk with a short detour through a couple of fields. Suitable footwear recommended. Duration: about 2 hours Refreshments: The Coffee Lounge at Holy Trinity Church is open 9am-1pm every Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Start at the15th century Holy Trinity Church, in Church Lane. It has a tower typical to the area but the pinnacles weren’t added until 1904. There are six bells, one from the former Bristol Gaol. Opposite is the medieval Tithe Barn, now used as an events space. By 1791 it contained two school rooms, one belonging to local writer and philanthropist Hannah More. You’ll also pass Glebe Cottage, built for the schoolmaster and mistress. Continue up Church Lane, past the church hall. The lane bears left, past a row of cottages. In the middle is Nile Cottage, with a plaque showing the year 1798 to commemorate Nelson’s victory over Napoleon’s fleet at the Battle of the Nile. In 1844 it was a private school.

bodyContent: Bradford on Avon self catering cottage accommodation -Seven luxurious and spacious self catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside on the edge of an area of outstanding natural beauty but only 5 miles from the world heritage city of Bath and 1 mile from the Saxon town of Bradford on Avon. The self catering cottages available for your stay have been converted from an old Tythe Barn which has had many purposes in the past including stables, cider production as the orchard at the front of the cottages was a cider apple orchard. Cumberwell Country Cottages near Bradford On Avon and Bath offer many features which will make your stay that extra bit more comfortable and have flexibility to accommodate our guests at various times of the week. You can sample country life, town life and city life all from your stay at Cumberwell Country Cottages. If you’re looking for a quiet retreat in the countryside yet within easy reach of Bath, Bradford on Avon, Longleat and numerous other attarctions then Cumberwell Country Cottages could be perfect for you. Cumberwell Country Cottages has 7 luxury 1 or 2 bedroom self catering cottages accommodating up to 4 people. 7 self catering cottages sleeping from 2 to 4 people Quiet and peaceful rural location Close to Bath and Bradford On Avon All cottages have underfloor downstairs heating All linen and towels provided for your stay Free Laundry Facilities Available All bedrooms ensuite 20″ Flat Screen LCD Televisions in all bedrooms LCD Televisions in all living areas with Freeview, DVD & Hi-Fi Fully equipped kitchens including Microwave, Sandwich Toaster and George Foreman Grills Each Cottage has its own Patio with Garden Furniture BBQ’s available on request Open all year round 36 hole championship golf course and 9 hole par3 golf course on site Flexible arrival and departure days 2 night weekend breaks available Parking – Ample parking near to the cottages Free Wifi No Smoking in all cottages

title: Camden Lodge
subtitle: A detached Georgian Lodge house in the heart of Bath of individual charm and character.
bodyContent: City centre location, 5 min. walk to the shops and restaurants. Ideal for access to all that the historic sites the city has to offer. Built around 1780, this bath stone house sits on Camden Crescent, second most famous street in Bath. This unique Lodge house is Grade II listed and situated in a beautiful part of the City Centre. A short walk away from the landmark locations of the Royal Crescent, the Circus and the High Street where you will find an abundant selection of restaurants, bars, and the shoppers’ paradise of Milsom Street. The character and location of this unique Lodge is ideal for a city break. Situated in one of Bath’s most sought after locations, the Lodge has 2 bedrooms (1 double and 1 single), 1 bathroom and an open-plan kitchen. The sitting room is furnished with two sofas (one is a double sofa bed), LCD TV & DVD, and SONOS integrated sound system.
tagline: A detached Georgian Lodge house in the heart of Bath of individual charm and character.

title: Revo Kitchen & Terrace

bodyContent: Revo Kitchen and Terrace, Weston super Mare - As a lot of our local customers know, our venue used to be the SeaQuarium, which closed in March of 2019. We began building Revo Kitchen in January 2021 and set to work on creating our vision of a relaxed atmosphere for people to enjoy live music, great coffee and impressive food. We are constantly looking to innovate our offerings based on the latest trends and ‘food frenzies’ that explode onto the scene. Our take on brunch is a careful combination of classic and unique dishes, all with a Revo twist. Our lunch & dinner menus are centered around our sourdough pizzas and freshly made burgers. In addition, we have a specials menu which varies depending on the fresh produce that is available. However, it does include some staples such fish and chips, along with our Revo chicken and waffles. We aim to cater to a wide range of dietary requirements, offering a variety of dairy free gluten free and vegan dishes on our menu.

subtitle: Haynes Motor Museum in Sparkford is a must-visit attraction, home to the UK’s largest collection of cars and motorbikes. Discover pioneering vehicles in The Dawn of Motoring, explore iconic red cars in the Red Room, and experience the thrill of legendary Williams Formula 1 racing cars up close.

title: Cheddar Gorge & Caves
subtitle: Cheddar Gorge & Caves boasts extraordinary subterranean show caves, awe-inspiring cliffs and holds many fascinating secrets about our prehistoric ancestors.
bodyContent: Our Day Ticket gives access to six great attractions: Gough’s Cave: Prepare to be amazed by our stunning show cave featuring spectacular stalagmite and stalactite formations created over 500,000 years ago! See cheddar cheese maturing in the caves, view the site where Cheddar Man’s 10,000-year-old skeleton was discovered and learn about the extraordinary DNA discovery. A free audio guide is available in six languages, and there is also a special version for children. Cox’s Cave featuring Yeo’s Journey: The Power of Water. This spectacular immersive multimedia experience tells the captivating story of how our iconic caves were formed and evolved through the ‘Power of Water’. The story is brought to life using state-of-the-art animation, sound, lighting and colour. Beyond the View: Take a seat in front of our state of the art 270-degree screen. Discover historic tales, enjoy breathtaking aerial panoramic views, and learn about the special wildlife and plants that call the gorge home. Museum of Pre-History: Discover amazing artefacts unearthed in the Cheddar area that help tell the story of how people lived thousands of years ago. Jacob’s Ladder & The Lookout Tower: Venture up the 274 steps to the top of the gorge with rest stops along the route to admire the view. title: Lytes Cary Manor, National Trust
subtitle: Intimate manor house with Arts and Crafts-style garden
bodyContent: Lytes Cary Manor is an intimate medieval manor house with a beautiful Arts and Crafts garden where you can imagine living. Originally the family home of Henry Lyte, where he translated the unique Niewe Herball book on herbal remedies, Lytes Cary was then lovingly restored in the 20th century by Sir Walter Jenner. The garden rooms contain a magical collection of topiary and herbaceous borders, while tranquil walks on the estate take you along the River Cary. To complete your visit, take a stroll among our community allotments and discover their creative and colourful designs. The garden that you see today at Lytes Cary Manor is very different to the garden that would have originally existed when the Lyte family were in residence. In the beginning The garden would have once been a very practical, working space. Henry Lyte, who lived in the house in the 1550s, was a keen herbalist and gardener. His son Thomas wrote that he grew apples, pears, plums, grapes, cherries, walnuts and peaches. Sadly, much of the original garden was lost after the Lytes family sold the estate in 1755. The following years saw a series of owners and tenants occupying the Manor, and the garden disappeared as the land was farmed right up to the house. Twentieth century changes When the Jenner family took up residence in 1907, Sir Walter and Lady Flora created a new garden. The design was Arts and Craft inspired and featured mostly rectangular ‘rooms’ separated by yew hedges and stone walls, each reflecting a different mood or purpose. After Sir Walter passed the house and estate to the National Trust, it was again let to tenants. In 1955, Jeremy Chittenden and his wife, Biddy, took the lease. Both worked tirelessly over the next 45 years to transform the gardens into those we now know.
