title: Hill House
subtitle: Escape the busy routines of life and Relax at Hill House with a bit of “home from home ”me time”.
bodyContent: Welcome To Guest Accommodation Hill House Bath Escape the busy routines of life and Relax at Hill House with a bit of “home from home ”me time”. Whether it’s history and heritage , the amazing array of independent shops restaurants, its art and culture or just the scenery and friendly social vibe, the central location of Hill House (yet only 15 minutes from country walks) makes it an ideal location to Explore Bath and the South West. If you need any further information Harry, Douglas and the team are always there to assist. All you have to do is ask. Hill House is a four storey Georgian Town House, built in 1762, which, being situated in the heart of historic Bath between the 3 Crescents – The Royal Crescent, Lansdown Crescent and Camden Crescent- is a great base to Experience all that Bath has to offer. Refurbished in 2011 its six individually decorated en suite rooms retain much of their original charm and character with all the amenities expected by a traveller in the 21st century including original artwork throughout.
tagline: Escape the busy routines of life and Relax at Hill House

title: Hedgemead Court apartment designed for luxury relaxation
subtitle: Our newly renovated contemporary apartment at No 2 Hedgemead Court is designed for luxury relaxation.
bodyContent: This is a spacious two bedroom apartment which has been awarded 4 Star Gold for special welcome. It is within easy reach of Bath, the M4 and Bristol Airport with free off road parking. This is a tranquil apartment with views down to the middle of the city from the sitting room and is adjacent to Hedgemead Park, one of the original pleasure gardens in Bath. There is a also lovely little balcony to sit and enjoy the view over Bath. Hedgemead Court ACCOMMODATION This beautiful luxury self catering apartment sleeps up to 4 in 2 bedrooms, made up either as 6 ft 3 super kings or singles. Together with Egyptian cotton linen and 1200 pocket sprung mattresses this ensures a restful night’s sleep. No 2 Hedgemead Court has luxury finishes throughout: with a large modern fully equipped kitchen and living dining area, realistic wall hung fire and 46 flat screen television and flat screen TVs in the bedrooms, comfy Schreiber sofa and snuggle chairs all combine to make the perfect end to a busy day in Bath. A calm drink on the balcony looking down into the city just tops it all. The bathroom has a large walk in drench shower and a luxurious Victorian claw bath. MEDIA FACILITIES Media facilities include free high speed Wifi throughout, iPod docking station, Smart flat screen TV with Netflix in the sitting room and flatscreen televisions in each bedroom. Books and DVDs are also available in the apartment together with a few board games. REWARD CARD If you book with us you can enjoy all the benefits of the bath Reward Card…giving discounts across a wide variety of city restaurants and attractions such as 3 hour spa session at the Thermae Spa for the price of 2 (Mon-Frid only), 10% off the Roman Baths and 10% off No 1 Royal Crescent. ABOUT TUCKING MILL SELF CATERING This is another of the five properties owned by Tucking Mill Self Catering. Do look at our other city property, The Old Smithy Loft or our 3 country cottages at Tucking Mill just 12 mins drive from the city centre in rural bliss, Tucking Mill View, Brooks’ View and Fishermen’s Retreat. THOSE LOOKING AFTER YOU The apartment is owned and managed by the Family Team; with Ann who has a background in hospitality and much travelling, Michael and Nikki Head Housekeeper the team does their utmost to ensure you enjoy your stay.. You will also likely come across Rob our invaluable man of all trades..
tagline: Our newly renovated contemporary apartment at No 2 Hedgemead Court

title: Rickbarton Cottage
subtitle: Rickbarton Cottage is the ideal base for that countryside retreat that everyone thrives from.
bodyContent: Walks from your doorstep, fresh air, country Pubs and a Farm Shop. Yet, close proximity to Bath (5 miles) and Bradford on Avon (2 miles) means that they get the best of both worlds! Guests can make use of the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool during their stay. Local Farm Shop village shop and village pub within walking distance or a short drive. The Kennet and Avon Canal is also within walking distance, for any keen walkers or cyclists. The cottage itself has an open-plan kitchen/living room. It is equipped with everything you should need. The bedroom has a double bed, which has been made up with fresh white linen prior to your arrival. The en-suite bathroom has a bath with a shower above the bath. There is space for a cot if needed (please check in advance of stay)
tagline: Rickbarton Cottage is the ideal base for that countryside retreat that everyone thrives from.

title: Cranleigh
subtitle: Dating from 1897 Cranleigh was once a Victorian family home. Cranleigh can offer you a step back into Victorian style but with all the comforts of modern living.
bodyContent: Dating from 1897 Cranleigh was once a Victorian family home. Cranleigh can offer you a step back into Victorian style but with all the comforts of modern living. With 10 individually furnished en-suite rooms with many period features offering every comfort for your stay. Cranleigh is ideally located in a quiet residential area – away from the noise but just over 1.5 miles from the centre of Bath. With FREE PARKING and easy access to the city. Breakfast At Cranleigh breakfast is served in the comfort of your own room. You can choose delivery between 7:45 am to 9:30 am each morning. Since introduction, earlier this year customers have raved about our in-room breakfast hamper. Our ‘In Room’ hamper is a continental style breakfast including a selection of toasted bread, preserves, fresh fruit, juice, yoghurts, selection of Kellogg’s cereals, creamy porridge and choice of tea or coffee. When choosing to enjoy your breakfast in your room this will be delivered in a hamper to your room. Honesty Bar & Coffee Station We have a range of reasonably priced beers, wines, soft drinks, cakes and snacks available for you to purchase to enjoy in your room. You can also help yourself to complimentary freshly ground coffee.
tagline: Dating from 1897 Cranleigh was once a Victorian family home.

title: The Paragon Townhouse
subtitle: The Paragon is a wondrously quirky Georgian Townhouse located in the bustling heart of historic Bath.
bodyContent: Arching over the ancient steps that lead from Roman Road down to Bath’s Artisan Quarter and Walcot Street, this listed building has been described as “like a Landmark Trust house but more beautiful.” Packed full of original features the house sleeps 8 in four double bedrooms and is spread over a total of 6 floors. Up to 2 extras sleep in comfortable day beds in the larger rooms. Awarded a special Gold by VisitBritain for 2018 / 19 and with the kitchen in the original vaults below street level you could not find a more original or characterful property for your special stay in Bath.
tagline: The Paragon is a wondrously quirky Georgian Townhouse

title: Chestnuts House
subtitle: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden and private off street parking.
bodyContent: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden and private off street parking. Set in the heart of the beautiful Georgian city of city. It is ideally situated off the main roads and adjacent to Henrietta park, but within a few minutes level stroll of the city centre with its many attractions, restaurants and excellent shopping centre. The House is built from natural Bath stone and has four beautifully decorated and furnished ensuite guest rooms, some with king size and wrought iron beds. Owners Toni and Dawn have created a splendid and delightful bed & breakfast with superb hospitality in a relaxing atmosphere, all the necessary ingredients for making your stay in Bath a truly memorable experience. Guests Chestnuts House has 5 individually themed ensuite rooms which can accommodate a total of 11 persons. Three Superior double bedded rooms, one family/twin room (max 3 persons) and one Classic double room Bedrooms The bedrooms have recently been refurbished to an exacting standard and have been tastefully decorated and beautifully furnished. All rooms have en suite bathrooms with bath and shower, hairdryers and large fluffy towels. The rooms have comfortable and relaxing beds with crisp cotton sheets, air con, remote flat screen colour television, radio, free wireless internet access and refreshment trays. Bathrooms All bedrooms are ensuite with large fluffy towels and White Company products. The superior & twin/family rooms are ensuite with bath & power shower. The Classic room is ensuite with walk in power shower. Kitchen Enjoy your inclusive breakfast in our light and airy dining room overlooking the garden. During the summer months breakfast can be served al fresco. Our breakfast includes both organic and local produce. As well as the traditional English breakfast, we offer smoked salmon with scrambled eggs and homemade blinis, poached buttered kippers (smoked haddock with poached eggs). There is also an extensive buffet table with fresh fruit salad, freshly baked pastries, cereals, yoghurts. We are happy to cater for special dietary requirements. Entertainment The Lounge has a large flat screen Television with both Sky & BT Sport Channels. Free internet wi-fi is available throughout Outside Chestnuts House is situated in a residential street with a small private walled garden for guests to enjoy and just 10 minutes walk to the centre. General Points Chestnuts House is situated in a residential street with private off street parking and just 10 minutes level walk to the city centre. Parking Chestnuts House has both private off street parking and parking permits available for Guests to use. This service is free of charge. Smoking Chestnuts is a non smoking establishment Children Family room can accommodate up to 3 guests. Children of all ages are welcome. Pets Unfortunately Chestnuts House does not accept pets
tagline: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden

title: Guided Tour of Taunton Minster
subtitle: If you’re looking to uncover the rich heritage of Taunton, the monthly guided tours at Taunton Minster are a must-add to your calendar.
bodyContent: Nestled in the heart of the town, this stunning building has stood for over a 700 years, and these tours offer a fascinating glimpse into its story. Come and explore the many interesting features of the building from its Saxon origins through to its role in modern-day Taunton. Visitors can admire beautiful architectural features, intricate stained glass, and hidden details that often go unnoticed during a casual visit. You’ll also hear stories from the past and present as the church seeks to serve the local community as a modern Minster. Whether you’re a history enthusiast, a local resident, or just visiting Somerset, the tours provide a welcoming and informative experience for all. It’s the perfect opportunity to slow down, explore, and connect with one of Taunton’s most treasured sites in a new way. Keep an eye on upcoming monthly dates every 2nd Saturday and treat yourself to a journey through time at Taunton Minster, you may discover something new with every visit. NOTE: Tours may be cancelled if there is an event - see website.
tagline: Discover the History of Taunton Minster: August's Monthly Guided Tour.

Sally Lunn's Historic Eating House & Museum. BATH, Somerset, UK situated in one of the oldest buildings in Bath Somerset - read the story of the famous BathBun

Sally Lunn’s in Bath, Somerset was the home of legendary Huguenot baker Sally Lunn, who created the first Bath bun. An authentic regional speciality now known over the world, the bun is large, very light and like a brioche in texture and served
with both delightfully sweet
and savoury toppings.






The actual recipe is a closely guarded secret, known only by the baker in the house and passed from generation to generation. The area the café occupies dates back to Roman times and there is evidence of food being made here at that time.

When Sally Lunn (real name Solange Luyon, which was difficult for the English to pronounce) arrived in 1680, after escaping persecution in France, there was still a café on the site.

Today you can visit the Sally Lunn House, enjoy the rambling staircases (mind your head) and cosy rooms spread over three floors, eat this truly delightful bun and visit the museum on the lower ground floor.


For more on Somerset's incredible history and heritage go to our interactive E Book.

title: Shepton Mallet
subtitle: The maker of big business including fashion house Mulberry and cider maker Brothers, today Shepton offers luxury outlet shopping, internationally-recognised country shows and one of the oldest prisons in the UK, now open to the public.
bodyContent: What to do in Shepton Mallet Set in undulating hills between Wells and Frome , Shepton Mallet dates back to Roman times: it was an important stop on the Fosse Way, a Roman road that traversed the south west. Since then, it’s played host to factories for world-famous brands, premium outlet shops, a redeveloping high street and the UK’s oldest prison . For many years the town was the centre of production for a number of leading UK brands, all locally founded, including fashion house Mulberry, cider makers Thatchers and Brothers , and sparkling wine Babysham. What’s more, Dairy giants Wyke Farms and confectionary marque James Chocolates are based in villages just down the road. The former Mulberry factory is now a swish outlet village , selling premium brands at discounted prices. Wander around the beautifully-updated site and stop for lunch in the courtyard restaurant, then while away the hours in the walled gardens under the Charlton Viaduct next door. Kept secret from the public for many years and finally opened to all in 2008, the gardens are home to exotic trees and flowers, waterfalls, streams and dovecotes. Shepton Mallet prison is Britain’s oldest, and it’s now a Grade-II listed site that’s reopened as a unique family attraction. Walk the halls and discover how incarcerated life has evolved over the 400 years since the prison’s first dungeon-like iteration. Outside in the town centre, walk the narrow streets to see the high prison walls, and stop at one of the ancient pubs loved by locals and visitors alike. In keeping with the agricultural spirit of Somerset, the Shepton Mallet area plays host to the Royal Bath and West Show each year. Spread over the 240-acre showground site are exhibits, stalls, stores and shows that represent the best of British agriculture, entertainment, food and drink. For a relaxed escape, spend the weekend at Shepton Mallet’s own Charlton House Hotel and Spa. Set amid stunning landscaped grounds, this perfectly-renovated former stately home includes a Bannatyne Health Club and restaurant crafting dishes inspired by - and using - locally-sourced produce. Shepton Mallet is a small market town in the Mendip district of Somerset. The town lies on the route of the Fosse Way, the principal Roman road into the South West of England. There are 218 listed buildings in the town including the market cross that dates back to the 1500’s and a 10th century church. There are a number of fine houses in the older parts of the town around Lower Lane and Leg Square as well as the outlying suburbs such as Bowlish and Charlton. The newest addition to the town is the Rock Flock, the stone sheep on the Cannard’s Grave roundabout. Shepton Mallet retains a strong character as a small market town and place to live. title: American Museum & Gardens
subtitle: The American Museum takes you on a journey through the history of America, from its early settlers to the twentieth century.
bodyContent: The American Museum on the outskirts of Bath, Somerset, takes you on a journey through the history of America, from its early settlers to the twentieth century. With its remarkable collection of folk and decorative arts, the Museum shows the diverse and complex nature of American traditions. The only museum of Americana outside the United States, it was founded to bring American history and cultures to the people of Britain and Europe. The permanent collection includes more than two hundred historic American quilts, exceptional pieces of Shaker furniture, Native American objects, and two hundred historical maps of the New World starting from the twelfth century and stretching through the Renaissance. The museum also has the most significant collection of American folk art in Europe. Visitors can also explore the extensive grounds, which include an arboretum of American trees. The New American Garden Designed by Washington DC-based landscape architecture firm OEHME, VAN SWEDEN, the New American Garden is its first European commission. With new landscaping, and planting the garden provides an exciting horticultural insight into the flora and fauna of the United States.
tagline: The American Museum takes you on a journey through the history of America.

title: Sharpham Park
subtitle: Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels near Glastonbury.
bodyContent: Our organic farm and mill Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels near Glastonbury . It’s the home of Mulberry founder Roger Saul who moved from the world of fashion to food in 2004 when he launched the Sharpham Park brand from his organic farm. At Sharpham Park we grow organic spelt and stone grind it in the traditional way to preserve the delicious, nutty taste of the ancient grain. Today, we turned the milled spelt into flour, cereals and grains however history records show spelt has been grown for approximately 4,000 years in the area since the Bronze and Iron ages. The farm is also sustainably managed – the spelt fields have 4 metre margins and the hedgerows are cut every other year meaning wildlife such as wild deer, hare, bees and dormice are allowed to shelter and forage for food all year round. The ancient grain Spelt is an ancient grain which as has gained popularity in recent times because it’s an excellent source of dietary fibre and contains protein as well as some vitamins and minerals. It’s both easy to digest and leaves you feeling fuller for longer as well as being a good source of slow release energy; so much so the Roman Army called it their “marching grain”. Within working with Bowel Cancer UK Eating a high fibre diet is important in the fight against Bowel Cancer and we have teamed up with Bowel Cancer UK to spread this message. More than 40 top chefs have donated spelt recipes to the campaign and you can find these Great British Spelt Recipes on our website. Sharpham Pantry restaurant at Kilver Court Designer Village You can enjoy a range of spelt dishes in the Sharpham Pantry restaurant including our spelt flat breads and spelt bread and butter pudding. You can find the full range of our delicious spelt products in the Great House at Kilver Court Designer Village in Shepton Mallet. Come and browse our selection of cereals including flakes, muesli and porridge as well as our grains and four different types of flour made to meet all of your baking needs.
tagline: Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels.

title: The Watermill Tearoom, Dunster Castle
subtitle: Whether you want a sit down lunch, a take away cup of coffee to sip as you wander the grounds or have brought your own picnic there's plenty of options at Dunster Castle.
bodyContent: The Watermill tea-room is opposite the working watermill in peaceful surroundings alongside the River Avill and at the entrance to the River Gardens. Morning coffees, light lunches and traditional, afternoon teas are available daily from the tea-room which is approximately a 10 minute walk from the carpark. The tea-garden makes for beautiful and relaxing surroundings in which to enjoy a refreshing cup of tea or to indulge with a slice of hand- made chocolate cake or a scone. The adjacent watermill is fully operational; you can see milling every first Wednesday of each month up to October and the organic flour produced is sold in the mill shop. Four legged friends are able to sit in the tea-garden but we ask that they don’t go into the tea-room. The Camellia House Why not take tea with a relative of the tea-plant – the Camellia? Hot and cold drinks along with light refreshments and locally made ice cream are available to take out from the Camellia House. These include delicious hand- made flap jacks and slices of cake. There are a small number of tables within the cosy Camellia House from which to admire the Camellia plants themselves or choose a bench outside on the sheltered, Mediterranean inspired South Terrace and take in the views. On clear days the views extend all along the Somerset coast as well as toward the distant, rolling Quantock Hills. The Camellia House formed part of Anthony Salvin’s remodelling of Dunster Castle during the early 1870s for the Luttrell family. A true plantsman’s garden would not be complete without a Camellia house. Picnics A picnic area with picnic benches are available near to the main car park, with views over the surrounding parkland, up to the Castle and out to the Bristol Channel. Alternatively feel free to picnic anywhere in the Castle grounds.
tagline: Whether you want a sit down lunch, a take away cup of coffee to sip as you wander the grounds

title: Vivary Golf & Adventure Centre
subtitle: We have lots of different activities available for all abilities and all age types including crazy golf and high ropes.
bodyContent: Vivary Golf & Adventure Centre is located within easy reach of Taunton town centre and offers a whole host of activities for the whole family to enjoy. Whether you want a go on the low ropes, the high ropes, the climbing wall, power fan descender, totem pole, mini golf, or full-sized golf, we've got you covered. There's even a cafe where you can recharge after a hectic - but above all fun - day out! The 18-hole golf course is challenging for players of all ages and abilities, with fabulous greens, plenty of bunkers and water hazards aplenty. Just book a tee time, turn up and play. We can even help provide all the kit you need. If the full-sized version isn't quite your game, then why not give our 18-hole crazy golf course a go? It's fantastic fun for all the family, and a brilliant way to get started in the game. The high ropes centre offers a fantastic range of activities for everyone to enjoy. There are lower, less intense ropes to start off with, but you can then graduate onto the climbing wall, the high ropes, the totem pole and the power fan descender too, alongside a number of other activities.
tagline: Fun for all the family

title: The Old Ship Aground
subtitle: After selling up our restaurant in Bath whilst working at our Farm at Wheddon Cross, we were looking to expand our farmhouse restaurant as we had most definitely outgrown our cozy front room dining experience.
bodyContent: Back in 2013, after looking hard for 2 years, we came across The Old Ship Aground – a boarded up and run down building, which was perfect for our needs, apart from the fact that she needed a stack of cash spent on her. From the first time we saw her she just oozed Old Englishness – a quintessential pub, pure and simple. She was originally built in 1911 as The Pier Hotel, a rather grand Edwardian hotel with stabling (which is now the Courtyard Bar) to accommodate guests from the great paddle steamers which then docked at the Old Pier. And what a perfect setting, right on the harbour. So we set about trying to buy her and succeeded on May the 9th 2013. We remained closed for a further 3 months whilst we started putting things back in order. There was an awful lot to get done – lots of cold sweats for sure – with new kitchens, bathrooms, plumbing and re-wiring, a compete refit. Finally we were ready(ish) and opened for the beginning of September. Right from the start we wanted to provide good old fashioned hospitality with great honest local ingredients. Put simply a pub that we would want to go to. Our food is very much ‘River Cottage’ in style, taking inspiration from our farming experiences. From our own baked soda breads, home smoked fish and farm raised meats you can rest assured of the very best of quality because if we can’t grow it or make it, it is locally sourced. We hope that you enjoy your visit…
tagline: After selling up our restaurant in Bath whilst working at our Farm at Wheddon Cross

title: Seven Streams
subtitle: Begin at the community centre in Keedwell Hill. Take the path that leads across the children’s play area to Keeds Lane.
bodyContent: How to get there Start at map ref: ST 537704 By car: Park at Long Ashton Community Centre, in Keedwell Hill, or considerately on the road. This walk was devised by Tony Hibbitt, who sadly passed away last year. Tony was a keen walker and wrote many footpath walks, which can be downloaded from www.longashtonparishcouncil.gov.uk (under ‘local information’ tab) Enjoy far-reaching views across North Somerset and a meander along picturesque streams during this circular walk near Long Ashton Begin at the community centre in Keedwell Hill. Take the path that leads across the children’s play area to Keeds Lane. Turn right here and go up the lane before turning left into Peel Park. The field was originally part of Long Ashton Research Station and named after Andrée Peel, an important member of the French Resistance during the Second World War. Follow the winding path through the park until you reach the far side. Turn left into King Crofts, a modern housing development, and follow it down, then bearing left to reach Weston Road. Turn right onto the main road before taking the next right, up Warren Lane.

title: Grosvenor Villa B&B
subtitle: Grosvenor Villa is a grade two listed Georgian Villa, the house is a fine example of Georgian architecture and was built specifically to house the former high altar of Bath Abbey which now forms part of our impressive entrance hall.
bodyContent: Receive access when you book directly! Our bedrooms contain Super King sized beds and either have an en-suite shower room or a private bath room. The rooms have free Wi-Fi, bath robes, flat-screen TV and tea/coffee making facilities. Guests are welcome to relax in our garden and a continental breakfast is served in our Georgian dining room. Parking is available on Grosvenor Bridge Road and the road behind us, Ringswell Gardens, neither has any parking restrictions 24/7 free of charge. We are situated just 1.2 miles from Bath City Centre which can be reached from the bus stop outside the house or a by a gentle 20 minutes stroll along the canal tow path at the bottom of the road which brings you into Sydney Gardens at the end of Great Poultney Street. Our guests can be assured of a very friendly personal welcome, and the excellent reviews by our guests have placed us among the top rated B & B’s in Bath. Kitchen Continental breakfast included. Parking There is plenty of parking in Grosvenor Bridge Road and the road behind us Ringswell Gardens where cars may be left 24/7 with no restrictions. Children We do not cater for Children Pets Pets are allowed free of charge with advance notice

title: Dream Stays Bath
subtitle: With a bright, welcoming feel and bags of well thought out features, Dream Stays’ range of Bath apartments are perfect for any city break.
bodyContent: Fresh and spacious, each location blends practical know how with little luxuries and quirky extras. Whether you are looking for a romantic bolthole for two, a family friendly haven or accommodation for a whole group of guests, Dream Stays have just the place. Each of its Bath lets is inviting and well-considered. They know what its like to arrive late or need a plan B on a rainy night; hence they provide everything from well-equipped cooking and dining areas, to plush sofas and home entertainment for cosy evenings in. Everything you need and a bit of what you fancy, with perfect city centre locations and friendly assistance on hand.
tagline: With a bright, welcoming feel and bags of well thought out features

title: Circle Luxury Stays: Crescent apartment
subtitle: Choose from apartments in Bath city centre, or an exclusive newly built five-bed holiday home with indoor pool in Devon/Dorset coast.
bodyContent: Bath properties are in landmark locations such as the Royal Crescent and Camden Crescent, within walking distance to the High Street. All are modern in design and beautifully furnished, providing you with more privacy, space and comfort than a standard hotel. Whether you are coming to Bath for a family get-away, romantic break, get-togethers with friends, or business, the apartments are a great option for stay of any duration. You are assured of a warm welcome and memorable stay on every visit. ——————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————— Crescent Apartment is on the lower ground floor, comprises an open-plan sitting room / kitchen, a good sized master bedroom with super king bed, a single bedroom, bathroom and elegant French doors leading to the courtyard. The sitting room is furnished with two sofas (one is a double sofa bed), LCD TV and DVD. The master bedroom has a super king size deep-sprung divan bed, which can be converted into twin beds, wardrobe, console table and stool and flat-screen television. The second bedroom has a single bed. The modern kitchen is fully equipped with Neff hob, electric oven, microwave and integrated appliances: including a dishwasher, washer/dryer and fridge freezer.
tagline: Choose from apartments in Bath city centre

title: The Annexe Yew Tree Cottage
subtitle: Situated in a country lane near the village of Wick with lovely view over the countryside.
bodyContent: Situated in a country lane near the village of Wick with lovely view over the countryside, the Annexe at Yew Tree Cottage will provide you with everything, you need for a lovely break. This one bedroom accommodation has been fully renovated in 2014 and awarded 4 star gold by Visit England. It sits in a beautiful garden visited by a variety of wildlife. There is so much to see, all with easy reach of the Annexe. Only 7 miles from the historic city of Bath and Bristol, it is ideally situated to visit both towns. On the edge of the Cotswold and Witshire and within reach of lovely scenery, historic sites it will be perfect for a romantic holiday or visiting family or friends.
tagline: Situated in a country lane near the village of Wick with lovely view over the countryside.

title: Coachmans Cottage
subtitle: Enjoy peace and quiet in a Beautiful Wiltshire Village. Close to the Wiltshire/Somerset Border. BA14 6HH
bodyContent: If you are looking for peace and quiet, but want to be part of a village community then Coachmans Cottage is THE COTTAGE for you. An immaculate, stand alone, all ground floor, 1 bedroom cottage, managed by the owner who lives next door. Set in the heart of the beautiful conservation village of Steeple Ashton in Wiltshire. Stunning 365 days of the year. Classic, Immaculate. Individual. Comfortable. Perfect to unwind and enjoy life at a slower pace. Yet only a car or train journey into the centre of Bath. Sorry No Children, Infants, Babies or pets. Immediately feel at home the spacious 18′ sitting/dining room, furnished with Georgian style mahogany and comfortable sofas, With Freeview T.V., WiFi. The wonderfully comfortable 16′ Master Bedroom has a Super King Size Bed with 1800 pocket sprung mattress. Bring your own bedding, bed linen, etc.. Also there is a spacious office/study/dressing room. The kitchen is separate and although SMALL is well equipped with a dishwasher, washer/drier, fridge with icebox, oven and hob. The sparkling bathroom has a full size bath with power shower over, loo and basin. Bring your own towels etc.. All of the ground floor accommodation is accessed from the hall. The cottage has full central heating, constant hot water, and is double glazed. Please phone me, Penny, on +44(0)1380 870764 for information on the cottage and area and just for the simple reassurance of speaking to a real person. You can see much more at https://www.coachmans-cottage.com Steeple Ashton village never fails to charms guests, as one once commented “like Midsomer without the murders”. There is a walkable pub that serves good food, and a walkable award winning community shop. The fine architecture, and magnificent St Mary’s Church cannot help but impress. Only 12 miles from Bath. If you do not feel like driving into the city then hop onto the train at one of the local train stations in Trowbridge, Westbury Melksham or Bradford on Avon.
tagline: Enjoy peace and quiet in a Beautiful Wiltshire Village

title: The History Hut
subtitle: A re-imagined WW2 nissen hut celebrating the history of Somerset, in a rural setting with panoramic views.
bodyContent: The nissen hut, one of 5 which made a base camp during WW2. With many original features, but some modern comforts, it offers somewhere a bit different to read about the importance of Somerset in England's history. Suitable for all ages, and with disabled facilities. The nissen hut was used by The Gloucester Regiment, and some American soldiers manning a searchlight during WW2. Sketches by Stanley Lewis, an artist, who was based there, show day to day army life. It still has the original galvanised shell, and ribs, but some of the inside has wooden cladding to create a more welcoming atmosphere, and enable wall displays. Reference, picture and story books about all aspects of Somerset fill the bookcases. A children's section has the popular 'Horrible History' books, as well as books about the war, dinosaurs, nature, and science. Tea, coffee and biscuits are available, more light refreshments can be provided, and visitors are welcome to stay as long as they want to. A toilet block has disabled facilities. For cold weather there is a log burner. During warmer days there are tables and chairs outside, to enjoy the peaceful rural surroundings and amazing views to the High Ham windmill, across to Glastonbury Tor. The History Hut has hosted Arts Week, Historic England,a photographic competition/exhibition, Carol Service, meetings, school visits, and family gatherings. Groups and Clubs can book privately. Admission is free, but donations are welcomed and go to The Royal British Legion, and help for Heroes. All works have been done without funding or grants so far, but it is hoped to get a foundation charity status in future to provide extra resources.

title: Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Mendip Activity Centre is the ultimate outdoor adventure playground in Somerset. They’ve been delivering adventurous outdoor activities for nearly 40 years, growing from humble beginnings to the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West!
bodyContent: It’s Time for Adventure with Mendip Activity Centre! Nestled in 250 acres of ancient woodland in the Mendip Hills National Landscape, Mendip Activity Centre is the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West. Just 20 minutes from Weston-super-Mare and Cheddar and open year-round, Mendip have been delivering Adventure, Learning and Training for individuals, families, schools, and groups since 1987. Activities available include: · Air Rifle · Tobogganing · Archery · Skiing · Snowboarding · Frisbee Golf · Kayaking · Nerf & Gel Battles · Caving · Paddle Boarding · Rock Climbing · Axe Throwing · ArcheryActive · Abseiling · Canoeing Come for the day or stay longer. In summer, pitch your tent at the award-winning Mendip Basecamp (link to https://mendipbasecamp.com/), a family adventure campsite awarded second at the Visit England Awards 2025. Pitch where you like, check out when it suits, camp fires encouraged, dogs welcome and endless adventure is on offer! Adventure for Everyone Mendip is more than just activities. It’s a place to switch off from screens, reconnect with nature, and each other. Whether you're learning something new, developing an existing skill or simply having fun outside, you’ll leave with muddy boots and big smiles. We believe in adventure for everyone. Many of our activities are adaptable for additional needs, and our friendly team will work with you to make it happen Refuel at the Alpine Lounge Overlooking the Ski Slope, the Alpine Lounge café serves pizzas, paninis, coffee and cake with stunning views- perfect for après-adventure refreshments

title: Henrietta House
subtitle: Henrietta House is an elegant, double fronted Georgian townhouse located in a quiet central area of Bath.
bodyContent: Henrietta House is an elegant, double fronted Georgian townhouse located in a quiet central area of Bath. It was completely renovated in 2011 to provide boutique Bed and Breakfast accommodation. Privately owned, we provide guests with an excellent personal service. title: The Witch of Wookey
subtitle: Fascinating Somerset Facts The Witch of Wookey in Somerset
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"198"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

THE WITCH OF WOOKEY in Somerset
At Wookey Hole in Wookey, Somerset, legend has it that during the Dark Ages an old woman who kept a dog and some goats lived alone in the caves. Everything that went wrong in the village was blamed
on her, and local people believed she was a witch, casting spells and causing misfortune.
Eventually, they sought the assistance of the Abbot at nearby Glastonbury Abbey, who sent a monk, Father Bernard, to exorcise the witch’s spirit. Entering the cave armed only with a Bible and a candle, in the faint light Father Bernard saw the witch stooping over her cooking pot. He tried to talk to her, but, screaming curses and casting spells, the witch fled deeper into the cave, down a narrow passageway called Hell’s Ladder.
The brave monk followed and they met again in the shadowy depths of an inner cavern. Quickly, Father Bernard scooped up a handful of water from the river, blessed it and threw it over the witch. She turned instantly to stone and her frozen figure remains in the cavern — known as The Witch’s Kitchen — to this day.

For more on Wookey Hole please see here

For more on Somerset's incredible history and heritage go to our interactive E Book.

title: Brothers Cider
subtitle: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family, who have been making cider in Somerset since 1658.
bodyContent: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family, who have been making cider in Somerset since 1658. We first started selling our Pear Cider at the Glastonbury Festival in 1995 near what was then called the Jazz World Stage. These days it is called The West Holts Stage. Over the years, festival goers kept asking us if it was possible to get our drink when the festival was over and so we decided to market it to pubs and supermarkets. Now you can get it all over the country and at many festivals. We are independent, British and are passionate about what we do. Our free-spirited essence is upheld by approaching things with a unique perspective. Here at Brothers, we take our values and commitment to sustainability very seriously, but it’s something we haven’t really shouted about until now. We have zero to landfill, all our waste is segregated to optimise the opportunity of being recycled or reused. A massive solar panel system is now installed here at the cider mill, where it will directly supply the presses with clean energy and lastly, all our left-over fruit pomace is turned into energy which helps to heat the local swimming pool!
tagline: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family.

title: Street
subtitle: The factory site of Clarks Shoes - a legacy Somerset brand - is now the UK’s first purpose-built factory outlet centre. After grabbing a bargain, head into Street centre to find eateries offering everything from pub classics to Italian, Indian and Thai.
bodyContent: What to do in Street Long the home of Clarks Shoes, one of the world’s most iconic footwear brands, the village of Street feels more like a town thanks to its size and wealth of shopping and dining options. In fact, Street’s list of credentials is longer than most places of its kind: other jewels in its crown include the prestigious Millfield school and the dinosaur skeletons unearthed in a nearby quarry. Located on a Roman road - hence the name Street, derived from the Latin word for road, strata - Street’s signature Clarks Village shopping centre draws millions of shoppers from far and wide looking for premium brands and bargain prices. The outlet village was the first purpose-built of its kind in the UK and hosts brands offering everything from fashion and footwear to beauty, homeware and children’s toys. Clarks Village is conveniently located right in the heart of Street, so it’s just a few steps from the village’s high street. Like the outlet village, Street’s centre is packed with shops from the national staple to the independent. At the far eastern end of the high street you’ll find Greenbank Pool, an outdoor swimming location that’s famous amongst locals and a family must-visit during the summer. After a hard day of shopping or swimming, head to one of the many eateries Street has to offer: options include Italian, Indian, Thai and Chinese alongside traditional British pub favourites and American-style fast food. If you still have an appetite for more local adventure, take to the Somerset Levels - with access points around Street in almost every direction - for endless walks, cycle rides and opportunities to explore more quintessentially Somerset scenes.

title: Nando's
subtitle: Home to the legendary flame-grilled PERi-PERi chicken. Afro-Portuguese inspired. South African born.
bodyContent: PERi-PERi is the heart and soul of Nando’s. Its story is our story. For centuries the people of Southeast Africa have used PERi-PERi to bring fire to their food. It is in Mozambique’s rich soil and blistering sunshine that the African Bird’s Eye Chilli grows into its fiery best. When Portuguese explorers arrived there, they were enchanted by its flavour. They added a squeeze of lemon and a kick of garlic and turned PERi-PERi into a very well-travelled spice. Which is how, many years later it ended up in Rosettenville, Johannesburg. One afternoon in 1987, two friends went for lunch at a humble Portuguese eatery. As their meal drew to a close, they knew they’d tasted something that had to be shared. PERi-PERi was about to make one more journey – from Rosettenville to the world.
tagline: The legendary flame-grilled PERi-PERi chicken

title: Country walk around Claverham
subtitle: Claverham, between Yatton and Cleeve, was originally a farming hamlet within the North Somerset levels. It was probably named after the clover fields which surround the village.
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: 2.7 miles Difficulty: a flat route, following quiet country lanes. It is accessible for wheelchairs and buggies. There is no pavement along some of the lanes but roads were quiet when Life did the walk. Duration: about 1 hour Map: OS 154 Explorer Claverham, between Yatton and Cleeve, was originally a farming hamlet within the North Somerset levels. It was probably named after the clover fields which surround the village. This walk takes a leisurely stroll along the village lanes. Start at the corner of High Street and Claverham Road. The building on this corner was originally the village post office and more recently a restaurant. Go along the High Street, passing Chestnut Drive on your left and Melanie’s hairdressers and Pizza2Go on your right. Continue along this road as it turns a sharp right corner. It becomes a lane and the pavement runs out so be careful of vehicles. Click HERE for full details and FREE PDF copy

title: Georgian House
subtitle: This gorgeous, light & peaceful 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom loft apartment is located in a Grade 1 listed Georgian building on a wide, pedestrianised street.
bodyContent: One king size bedroom One twin bedroom with an additional single bed on request Two bathrooms, one ensuite shower room plus family bathroom with over bath shower Excellent central location Lift access Gorgeous views of river, cricket ground & Bathwick Hill This gorgeous, light & peaceful 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom loft apartment is located in a Grade 1 listed Georgian building on a wide, pedestrianised street. Duke Street is an ideal location for all your city needs with all the sights of Bath within easy reach. Bath Abbey, the Roman Baths & Bath’s many delightful shops are a short stroll from the apartment & Bath Rugby’s ground is a mere 2 minutes walk along the river towards Pulteney Bridge. In addition, there are many fabulous restaurants on your doorstep. When you return for the day you’ll be able to put up your feet & gaze at the glorious view of Bathwick Hill & the distant Sham Castle to relax & rejuvenate before the next day. To help with that home to home feeling there is free Wifi, a Nespresso coffee machine, dishwasher, microwave, washing machine, tumble dryer & the comfiest beds we could find. A highchair, cot or extra child’s bed can be also provided on request. In addition a widescreen TV & DVD player with DVDs of some of the many films shot in Bath over the years are waiting for you. If you fancy some exercise, Bath Leisure Centre with a pool, gym & exercise classes is a hop and a skip over North Parade Bridge. Whilst for those fresh air fiends, the canal can be easily accessed for walks/runs/cycle to Bathampton (3 miles) & beyond. Bikes can be hired locally or you can bring your own & keep them in Georgian House’s basement bike store (please bring your own lock). The canal is also a lovely way to walk to the Holburne Museum. Georgian House is an amalgamation of three Georgian townhouses & has retained its grand feature staircase and useful lift from its hotel past. A 5 minute level walk from Bath Spa Train & Bus Station, public transport is the best way to visit Bath. If however you need to bring your car, the apartment has a parking permit allowing free parking is central zone spaces. For busy times, there is also a long stay car park 2 minutes walk away.

title: Montacute House, National Trust
subtitle: Montacute House is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design
bodyContent: Montacute House, Somerset is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design. With its towering walls of glass, glow of ham stone and its surrounding gardens, it is a place of beauty and wonder. Sir Edward Phelips was the visionary force and money behind this masterpiece, which was completed in 1601. Built by skilled craftsman using local ham stone under the instruction of William Arnold, master mason, the house was a statement of wealth, ambition and showmanship. Come face to face with the past in the Long Gallery; measuring over 52 metres, it is the longest of its kind in England. The Gallery houses over 60 Tudor and Elizabethan portraits on loan from the National Portrait Gallery. Beautiful gardens surround Montacute, constantly changing, filling the house with scent in summer and providing an atmospheric backdrop for a winter walk. Whether you just want to let the children run and explore, or be inspired by the collections housed within the walls of Montacute, you will leave with lasting memories and a desire to soon return. You may even recognise some of the sights, as Montacute House featured in the BBC’s highly acclaimed production of Hilary Mantel’s Wolf Hall. Within 20 minutes’ drive you will find four fascinating smaller properties, each with a unique character, history and story to tell. Their combined age of 2,300 years spans from the medieval period to the early 19th century. Explore Stoke Priory, a fine collection of medieval farm buildings; Treasurer's House, with its great hall and unusual wall painting; Stembridge Tower Mill, the last remaining thatched windmill in England; and the Priest’s House, a medieval home of great character not to be missed. While you’re in the area, why not also visit Lytes Cary Manor and Tintinhull Garden (see the National Trust website for more details).
tagline: Montacute House in Somerset is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design

title: Stable Cottage: 6 bed country cottage
subtitle: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.
bodyContent: It is located in the beautiful Georgian village of Freshford which lies at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys in the southern Cotswolds. There are some wonderful walks to local pubs following the riverside and canals. All just 15 minutes from Bath by car but the secret of this location is the 9 minute train journey to Bath from the village station, just a short stroll from the cottages. The cottage : Stable cottage is a newly renovated, limestone floored, 3 bedroom, two bathroom (one is en-suite) cottage. It has large windows to the front of the house filling the bedrooms and downstairs with light on a sunny day. It has an open plan living/dining area with free view TV/DVD and two large suedette couches and comfortable chairs. For dining there is a blond Oak dining table and chairs to seat 6 . The Stables can accommodate 6 people in three bedrooms (two king size and one double) . The kitchen is fully equipped with cookware,dishwasher and washing machine . The house also offers Iron/Ironing board, Hairdryers All bed linen and towels . There is a Welcome pack of tea, coffee, sugar, milk, bread, butter, eggs and bacon. Free WiFi. There are also books and board-games in the house for the use of guests. If you have any questions on Bath and the local area before or during your stay please let us know. We would be delighted to help. Neighbourhood overview : Freshford is a beautiful ancient village with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk from the cottage( The Inn at Freshford) that serves restaurant quality food and all the local beers and ciders.They have an excellent fully stocked( from wine to organic humus!)community shop that also has a good quality cafe that serves lunch. There is also a local doctors surgery. The village is nestled at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys . The Kennet and Avon canal is a 15 minute walk from the cottage. Getting around : You don’t need a car to stay in the cottage. The village station is a few minutes walk away. Trains hourly off peak and thrice hourly at peak times. Bath 9 mins, Bristol 22mins. London Padington to Bath Spa 1.5 hours Bath Spa to Freshford 9 minutes Bath Spa to Freshford “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/bath-spa-to-freshford ” Freshford to Bath Spa “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/freshford-to-bath-spa ” There is also a local bus service to all the adjacent villages and Bath. The cottage has two parking spaces suitable for one medium and one small car or a single large SUV.the surrounding towns you might want to visit. Other things to note If you are a runner or keep fit enthusiast the owner is a qualified Personal Trainer (Bath Uni) with much Marathon and half marathon experience. She specialises in Ladies training. Please let us know if you would like guided running or some Personal Fitness training.
tagline: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.

title: Percy Place
subtitle: Period holiday apartment in Bath sleeping 7 people at walking distance from the city centre with free on street parking.
bodyContent: Percy Place is a holiday apartment in a Grade II listed Georgian house in the City of Bath. The house used to be the home of Rev. William Jay, one of the most eminent English Congregationalist preachers of Regency England who used to preach in the Argyle Chapel in Bath at the end of 1700s. We like to make our guests feel at home and highly valued. The original Georgian features of the building are enhanced by the stylish decor of the rooms such as antiques, trinkets and period furniture. At the same time, free wi-fi and a recently refurbished kitchen offer modern comfort. Both the town and the countryside are on our doorstep. We are just a few minutes walk from the city centre between the up and coming ‘Artisan Quarter’ bristling with local independent shops, and Larkhall village, a pretty quarter with a local butcher, a deli, a theatre and a few restaurants. We are also very close to the Kennet & Avon Canal at the back of Kensington Meadows. The view of the countryside and back garden from the back of the house is relaxing and inspiring.

title: Fishermen’s Retreat
subtitle: A veritable rural retreat, Fishermen’s Retreat is an award winning haven of calm where you can totally escape from the bustle of Bath and relax in the beautiful Midford Valley beside the Midford Brook.
bodyContent: One of a rank of 4 cottages built for the Somerset Coal Canal workers in the late 1800s and renovated today to 4 Star standard and has now been awarded a Gold Star for exceptional accommodation and welcome. Sleeping facilities are on the first floor with a king size luxury 1400 pocket sprung bed in the master bedroom with crisp Egyptian cotton linen and a small overnight guest room. There is also a sofabed in the sitting room. With the original fireplace and wood burning stove the sitting room is very welcoming and comfortable. There is also a pine dining table for 4 in the window alcove so you can watch the birds feeding as you eat. This is more like a home than a holiday cottage. Just outside the front door there is a small private patio with table and chairs where you can pop out for a quick cup of coffee and admire the roses. Fishermen’s Retreat has a south facing mature garden leading down to the Midford brook where there is a stone built barbecue on the brookside patio. There is nothing more enjoyable than relaxing with a glass of wine while your cook is at work! Wildlife abounds here with a variety of birds..kingfishers, warblers, heron, cormorants all frequent visitors, preying on the local trout. AROUND AND ABOUT The Brook is a fishery stocked by the Avon Anglers and day tickets can be purchased for fly fishing. Need to be organised in advance. Alternatively, you can enjoy the many walks and cycle rides around: Sustrans 24 is just above the cottage and you are not be more than 300 yards along the road from the famous Two Tunnel Cycle way into Bath. The Kennet and Avon Canal path also provides excellent cycling opportunities and you can cycle one way i to Bath and the other to Bradford on Avon and Devizes. Wild swimming is available at Warleigh Weir and Farleigh Hungerford, 2-4 miles away Maps are supplied in all cottages. MEDIA FACILITIES There is free Wifi throughout the cottage and a flat screen TV in the sitting room. An iPod Docking station is also provided. There is a selection of DVDs, a variety of books as well as some board games. PARKING Free private parking space for one car is provided and a second by arrangement ABOUT TUCKING MILL SELF CATERING Fishermen’s Retreat is one of the five 4 Star Luxury Gold properties in Tucking Mill Self Catering owned by Michael and Ann. There are two apartments in the city centre, The Old Smithy Loft and No 2 Hedgemead Court, and two other cottages Brooks’ View and Tucking Mill View just 12 minutes drive away at Tucking Mill, Midford, a historic hamlet just outside the city boundaries in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. REWARD CARD All our guests benefit from the Reward Card and you can enjoy exclusive discounts for many of the city’s restaurants and cafes. One special deal is the 3 hour session for the price of 2 at the Thermae Spa – Mon-Fri. THOSE LOOKING AFTER YOU The property is managed by the Family Team..With Ann who has a background in hospitality and much travelling, Michael who built the barbecues and is in charge of logs, bird feeding and Head housekeeper Nikki the team will do its utmost to ensure you enjoy your stay. You will also likely meet our invaluable man of all trades, Rob Short or long breaks available.
tagline: A veritable rural retreat, Fishermen’s Retreat is an award winning haven of calm

title: Fascinating Somerset facts the incredible story of Shepton Mallet Prison
subtitle: Shepton Mallet Prison was built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’; Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom up until its closure at the end of March 2013. The land was purchased from Reverend Edward Barnards for a cost of £160.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"202"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

Only if the walls could speak!

Shepton Mallet prison in Shepton Mallet, Somerset was built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’; Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom up until its closure at the end of March 2013. The land was purchased from Reverend Edward Barnards for a cost of £160. 

The House of correction would hold men women and children together.  Debtors, thieves, ‘misfits’, vagrants and people with mental health disorders were sentenced to long periods of time in Shepton Prison.  There are very few records of the conditions inside, many people could not read and write and it was not considered necessary to keep a record of ‘matters of such distaste’. Conditions and favours by jailors resulted in promiscuous behaviour, lax discipline and drunken behaviour. To say that conditions were awful is possibly a large understatement. Primitive sanitation led to regular outbreaks of gaol fever, ulcers, jaundice, asthma, itch and venereal diseases.  The only real medical aid was the local surgeon (doctor) being called in to pronounce a death.  Following any deaths within the house of correction bodies were taken to an unconsecrated burial ground just outside the prison, the door in the wall on Frithfield lane still exists as do 9 unmarked graves within the grounds. It was common practice with British executions to bury prisoners in this way, sad though it is now it was just the norm back then.

title: Aerosaurus Balloons
subtitle: Aerosaurus Balloons in Somerset are the largest provider of Champagne Balloon Flights in the South West. 1000s of passengers each year enjoy drifting peacefully over the beautiful landscapes, towns and villages of the West country.
bodyContent: Experience with Aerosaurus Balloons in Somerset a hot air balloon ride with a family run company over the stunning countryside of Somerset. Flights take place at both dusk & dawn, weather permitting, and short notice spaces are sometimes available. Choose from one of our handpicked launch sites across the South West, each one offering a unique perspective on the fabulous landmarks that can be seen from the balloon – all toasted with Champagne on landing! From Somerset, we fly from Prockters Farm Shop in Taunton. We also fly from Bristol, Bath , South Wales, Dorset, Wiltshire, Devon & Cornwall, so wherever you are – there is a flight for you! Please see link for flight locations HERE Treat yourself or a loved one to one of our Champagne Balloon Rides and experience a flight like no other! Prices start from £145 for a 12-month voucher which can be instantly emailed to you or posted first class. Flights take place between April and October. What to Expect From A Balloon Flight A hot air balloon flight is a wonderful; experience for all ages, balloon flights are very smooth and calming so you don’t have to be an adrenaline lover to enjoy a flight with us! The whole experience lasts around 3 – 4 hours with the option to be as involved as much or as little as you wish in the whole process. When we meet you, you will receive a thorough safety briefing from our highly experienced Pilots, before being taken to the specially selected launch site based on the conditions that day. Once at the launch site you can participate in setting up the balloon, before drifting gently off for around an hour. During the flight, our very knowledgeable Pilot will be on hand to answer any questions and to point out any local landmarks. Upon landing you can help to pack away the balloon before being served chilled Champagne and presented with your personalised flight certificate signed by your Pilot and then we will take you back to the original meeting location. Aerosaurus and Bailey Balloons will be operating flights at next year’s Bristol Balloon Fiesta 11 th – 14 th of August 2022, the fiesta is an amazing spectacle and we cannot wait for this exciting event! To have a chance to be a part of this iconic balloon fiesta, please contact Aerosaurus Balloons. Flights start from £200 per person in a shared balloon with other passengers, you can also book a 2-person exclusive for £900.
tagline: Aerosaurus Balloons are the largest provider of Champagne Balloon Flights in the South West.

title: Chelwood
subtitle: Four parishioners of Chelwood went to and returned safely from World War I, therefore Chelwood has been designated a "Thankful Village". I believe there are only 8 such villages in Somerset.
bodyContent: Four parishioners of Chelwood went to and returned safely from World War I, therefore Chelwood has been designated a "Thankful Village". I believe there are only 8 such villages in Somerset. The church may be of interest to some visitors. St Leonard is an Anglican parish church built in the 14th century and has been designated as a Grade II listed building. The church is dedicated to St Leonard, who was born in 559. The foundations of the church and certain features are probably Norman but the main structure is 14th Century, the tower being rebuilt in 1722. The tower houses a bell dating from 1773. The Norman font was made from a block of Dundry limestone around 1125 and the ironwork can still be seen which locked the cover, lest witches stole the holy water. The detailing on the corbels on the ends of the south arcade is 14th Century-vines leaves over a female head to the east, fig leaves to the west. The south windows contain many fragments of 16th Century Flemish glass.

title: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm
subtitle: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is a conservation charity and the largest zoo in Somerset with over 100 species of animals. The multi award winning Zoo is open 7 days a week and aims to make Noah's Ark a place of joy, wonder, adventure and refreshment that supports the well-being of all visitors, staff and volunteers. Through education and fun, they aim to inspire and motivate this generation and the next to consider sustainable lifestyles and care for our planet.
bodyContent: Amazing Animals The home of the big Zoo animals! Visit Noah’s Ark and come face to face with a cheeky mob of meerkats, be awed by African elephants and dazzled by the zebra herd! Experience the majestic beauty and see the skies come alive during the daily birds of prey displays! The Wings of Wonder display showcases the owls, hawks, falcons and eagles in an unforgettably mesmerizing spectacle. Indoor and Outdoor Adventures Play and adventure never stops with our 10 play areas across the 100-acre site. Enjoy the huge indoor play barns including under 5’s soft play and a giant rainbow slide. The Zoo also has accessible play equipment including nest swings and a wheelchair accessible roundabout. Fancy an a-maze-ing adventure? Navigate through Britain’s longest hedge maze. The British wildlife themed maze has 3.4km of paths and wooden nest tower at the center. Keep the whole family smiling and active all day, whatever the weather! Accessibility Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is proud to be an accessible attraction. Facilities include multiple accessible toilets, Changing Places facility, accessible play equipment, hearing loops and more. Please visit the website before your visit for up-to-date information and to view the Access guide. Prices Buy online and save! Noah’s Ark recommends that all tickets, including those for free essential carers and under 2’s are purchased online prior to your arrival. Prices are seasonal, please check the website for up-to-date ticket prices. Food and Drink With a range of delicious hot and cold food and drink options available in our Food Barn and convenient snack kiosks across the Zoo, there is something for everyone! Alternatively, visitors are very welcome to bring their own lunch and enjoy it in one of our many picnic spots. Mini Experiences Noah’s Ark offers incredible up-close mini experiences with Meerkats, Capybara, Andean Bears and Giant Tortoise. You will enjoy 20 minutes behind the scenes with the keeper, learn some interesting facts and get involved with their feeding and enrichment programme. Pre-book your experience online to ensure availability. Minimum age and terms and conditions apply. Animal Experiences Find out what it’s like to be a keeper for the day with our one-to-one keeper experiences before the zoo opens. Experiences include: African Elephants, Junior Keeper Experience, and Giraffe and Rhino experience.
tagline: You’ll be amazed at the variety of nature you’ll see with over 100 species of animals

title: Sherborne Castle & Gardens
subtitle: Sherborne Castle and Gardens Discover the historic Digby stately home built by Sir Walter Raleigh in 1594 and its great stories. See magnificent state rooms; Raleigh’s kitchen, relics from the Civil War and a museum in the castle’s cellars. Explore acres of impressive lakeside gardens and pleasure grounds in a stunning setting.
bodyContent: Sherborne Castle & Gardens, on the Somerset - Dorset border will allow you to Walk in the footsteps of SIR WALTER RALEIGH in the home he built more than 400 years ago Buy tickets in advance on-line at www.sherbornecastle.com to receive a 10% saving on admission • Children under 16 GO FREE (up to 4 children per full paying adult admission) Built by Sir Walter Raleigh in 1594 and the stately home of the Digby family since 1617; a fascinating visit to the historic SHERBORNE CASTLE awaits you: • Take a leisurely stroll around 42 acres of our beautiful ENGLISH LANDSCAPE GARDENS. Experience the peace and tranquillity; marvel at the spectacular views • An award winning Tea Room situated in a Gothic Dairy offers a welcoming atmosphere for morning coffees, a range of traditional light lunches and delicious afternoon teas. After, why not browse our Gift Shop to see an unusual variety of souvenirs, gifts and Sherborne Castle wine • Discover magnificent staterooms displaying nationally important collections of Art, Furniture & Porcelain, a Tudor kitchen and the Family Museum in the Castle's cellars • Uncover the Great Stories of Sherborne Castle telling the stories of key moments in history at the Castle • Discover walks round the 50-acre lake to Garden features such as Raleigh's Seat, The Cascade and a new Fossil House • Enjoy colour throughout the season in the Gardens from spectacular carpet arrays of spring bulbs, glorious herbaceous borders and the breathtaking colours of autumn reflected in the lake • In the Family Museum you can see Raleigh’s Kitchen, fascinating family artefacts and Fossil & Archive displays. Our Sir Walter Raleigh display covers the great man's time here at the Castle and our ‘Capability’ Brown display drawn from the archives shows his impact and legacy on the Gardens. Combined with the Castle, the historic market town of Sherborne and its wonderful Abbey are close by for a memorable day out.

title: Potter around Pill
subtitle: Pill means tidal inlet, small harbour or creek. The original name of the village was Crockerne Pill, meaning ‘pottery wharf’ after the large-scale pottery (crockery) industry which thrived here in the middle ages.
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: about 1¾ miles Difficulty: easy, with a short climb to the top of Watchhouse Hill Duration: about an hour at a leisurely pace Refreshments and toilets: shops in the precinct, and you can use the toilet in the Community Resource Centre if you ask Map: OS 154 Explorer Pill sits on the southern banks of the River Avon and has a long history, from its pottery-making days to the pilots guiding ships up the water. Meander along the riverbank and then up onto Watchhouse Hill for glorious views all around during this short walk. Pill means tidal inlet, small harbour or creek. The original name of the village was Crockerne Pill, meaning ‘pottery wharf’ after the large-scale pottery (crockery) industry which thrived here in the middle ages. Pill has been a maritime community since the 13th century and was home to pilots, the men who guided boats safely up the Avon Gorge to Bristol. The pilots were in competition with each other to intercept incoming ships, which led to the design of a new boat – the Pill Pilot Cutter – now regarded as one of the finest wooden boats ever built. However, in 1918 the pilots decided to stop competing and share out the work. From the shopping precinct, walk down the steps to the grassy area leading under the railway bridge and towards the creek. At the creek there is a monument to commemorate the Methodist preachers who sailed from Pill to America in the 1770s. Click HERE for full details and FREE PDF copy

title: Immersive Events at Shepton Mallet Prison
subtitle: Established in 2015, Immersive Events or ‘IME’ is an award winning, interactive, immersive events company based in Shepton Mallet Prison.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. Shepton Mallet Prison, Somerset specialise in designing and running events nationwide from Scream Parks & Scare Mazes to Escape Rooms, overnight stays to prison breaks, from corporate training to Hens and Stags. IME has proudly been nominated for a SCAR 2016 – Best Zombie Survival Event for Lockdown and became winner of SCAR 2017 Experience for Lockdown I, Lockdown II and Lockdown Origins. Annual, monthly and weekly a huge variety of events are held at Shepton Mallet Prison. Every year over the Halloween period IME host the sold-out event ‘The Street’. This scare maze is to be endured for a gruelling 25 minutes and is one of a kind. The scare maze is riddled with twists and turns, jump scares and horrors. Due to popular demand, ‘The Street’ at Shepton Mallet Prison, Somerset's Ultimate Scare Maze is re-opening for Christmas; with the addition of Santa's GROTto! Tickets are just £10 and are now on sale. The event will be held on the 21st and 22nd December. Let’s hope you have been good this year! Escape Rooms are held every Saturday at 11:00am, the maximum group size is 18 people and pre-booking is recommended. title: Georgian House
subtitle: This gorgeous, light & peaceful 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom loft apartment is located in a Grade 1 listed Georgian building on a wide, pedestrianised street.
bodyContent: One king size bedroom One twin bedroom with an additional single bed on request Two bathrooms, one ensuite shower room plus family bathroom with over bath shower Excellent central location Lift access Gorgeous views of river, cricket ground & Bathwick Hill This gorgeous, light & peaceful 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom loft apartment is located in a Grade 1 listed Georgian building on a wide, pedestrianised street. Duke Street is an ideal location for all your city needs with all the sights of Bath within easy reach. Bath Abbey, the Roman Baths & Bath’s many delightful shops are a short stroll from the apartment & Bath Rugby’s ground is a mere 2 minutes walk along the river towards Pulteney Bridge. In addition, there are many fabulous restaurants on your doorstep. When you return for the day you’ll be able to put up your feet & gaze at the glorious view of Bathwick Hill & the distant Sham Castle to relax & rejuvenate before the next day. To help with that home to home feeling there is free Wifi, a Nespresso coffee machine, dishwasher, microwave, washing machine, tumble dryer & the comfiest beds we could find. A highchair, cot or extra child’s bed can be also provided on request. In addition a widescreen TV & DVD player with DVDs of some of the many films shot in Bath over the years are waiting for you. If you fancy some exercise, Bath Leisure Centre with a pool, gym & exercise classes is a hop and a skip over North Parade Bridge. Whilst for those fresh air fiends, the canal can be easily accessed for walks/runs/cycle to Bathampton (3 miles) & beyond. Bikes can be hired locally or you can bring your own & keep them in Georgian House’s basement bike store (please bring your own lock). The canal is also a lovely way to walk to the Holburne Museum. Georgian House is an amalgamation of three Georgian townhouses & has retained its grand feature staircase and useful lift from its hotel past. A 5 minute level walk from Bath Spa Train & Bus Station, public transport is the best way to visit Bath. If however you need to bring your car, the apartment has a parking permit allowing free parking is central zone spaces. For busy times, there is also a long stay car park 2 minutes walk away.
tagline: This gorgeous, light & peaceful 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom loft apartment

title: Rickbarton Cottage
subtitle: Rickbarton Cottage is the ideal base for that countryside retreat that everyone thrives from.
bodyContent: Walks from your doorstep, fresh air, country Pubs and a Farm Shop. Yet, close proximity to Bath (5 miles) and Bradford on Avon (2 miles) means that they get the best of both worlds! Guests can make use of the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool during their stay. Local Farm Shop village shop and village pub within walking distance or a short drive. The Kennet and Avon Canal is also within walking distance, for any keen walkers or cyclists. The cottage itself has an open-plan kitchen/living room. It is equipped with everything you should need. The bedroom has a double bed, which has been made up with fresh white linen prior to your arrival. The en-suite bathroom has a bath with a shower above the bath. There is space for a cot if needed (please check in advance of stay)

title: 18 The Circus
subtitle: Large Parties - 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character.
bodyContent: 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character. The maisonette that occupies the top two floors of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the northern Lansdown slopes of stunning terraces of Georgian houses, and with the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minute’s walk. Access is via a communal hallway and carpeted staircase that leads to the maisonette’s front door on the second floor. Inside is a small hall, off which sits the spacious and airy sitting room that is tastefully and comfortably furnished and decorated and being south facing, is very light. On this floor is also a large fitted kitchen with dining table and chairs. A mezzanine room houses the washing machine and dryer for exclusive use of visitors to this home. The stairs on this floor lead to a well-lit landing, off which lie the bedrooms. The front bedroom is a very large room with a double bed and conveniently, a single bed for family use. This brightly furnished bedroom also has an en-suite shower room. The second bedroom has twin beds and is next door to a family sized bathroom with bath, shower-in-bath, basin, WC and airing cupboard. The property contains gas central heating, gas hob, gas double oven, fridge, dishwasher, washing machine and dryer, microwave, TV in lounge and master bedroom, video, stereo, towels and toiletries. Free Car Parking Permit available Free Unlimited fiber broadband Please note: the house is a listed 4 story Georgian townhouse and as such does not have an elevator. Find out more here.
tagline: Large Parties - 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character.

title: Old Stables: rural retreat, sleeps 6
subtitle: The Old Stables is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.
bodyContent: It is located in the beautiful Georgian village of Freshford which lies at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys in the southern Cotswolds. There are some wonderful walks to local pubs following the riverside and canals. All just 15 minutes from Bath by car but the secret of this location is the 9 minute train journey to Bath from the village station, just a short stroll from the cottages. A three bedroom cottage (two king and one twin-bed) with a fully equipped kitchen opening onto a dining room There is a separate living room with TV/DVD and two large leather couches . The living room has large patio doors that open up onto the courtyard area. The Old Stables can accommodate 6 people. This cottage has: Three bedrooms (two king size and one with twin beds) One family bathroom , a Living room with Freeview TV/DVD two large leather couches and a dining room with a table seating 6.The Kitchen is equipped with all the cookware you might need dishwasher along washing machine/dryer and Iron/Ironing board. Hairdryers , bed linen and towels are all provided in the bedrooms.We provide a “Welcome pack” of tea, coffee, sugar, milk, bread, butter, eggs and bacon. The cottage has Free WiFi. Neighbourhood overview: Freshford is a beautiful ancient village with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk from the cottage( The Inn at Freshford) that serves restaurant quality food and all the local beers and ciders.The village has an excellent fully stocked( from wine to organic humus!)community shop that also has a great cafe that serves lunch. There is also a local doctors surgery. The village is nestled at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys . The Kennet and Avon canal is a 15 minute walk from the cottage. Getting around: You don’t need a car to stay in the cottage. The village station is a few minutes walk away. Trains are hourly off peak and thrice hourly at peak times. Bath 9 mins, Bristol 22 mins. London Padington to Bath Spa 1.5 hours Bath Spa to Freshford 9 minutes Bath Spa to Freshford “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/bath-spa-to-freshford ” Freshford to Bath Spa “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/freshford-to-bath-spa ” There is also a local bus service to all the adjacent villages and Bath. The cottage has two parking spaces suitable for one medium and one small car or a single large SUV. Other things to note If you are a runner or keep fit enthusiast the owner is a qualified Personal Trainer (Bath Uni) with much Marathon and half marathon experience. She specialises in Ladies training. Please let us know if you would like guided running or some Personal Fitness training
tagline: The Old Stables is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.

bodyContent: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds. Within a stone’s throw of the site of the battle of Lansdown and with the Cotswold Way and the old east to west Roman road running through the grounds, Toghill is steeped in history. Located on a working farm only 4 miles north of Bath, with spectacular views over the Welsh mountains, Mendips, Cotswolds and Historic Bath. We have 9 rooms, some of which are in the 17th century farmhouse and others in the pretty Cotswold stone converted barns and stables in a delightful courtyard setting.
