title: A Life in Art: Roger Fry
subtitle: As part of the Bloomsbury Group, Roger Fry (1866-1934) helped spark new ideas in art, design and culture — inspiring a fresh, modern way of looking at the world. See vibrant portraits, landscapes, and interiors, including rarely seen works from private collections alongside important national pieces.
bodyContent: J This exhibition is the first major show in more than 25 years to highlight Roger Fry (1866-1934) as a painter, revealing works by one of Britain’s most influential art figures. It comes to The Museum of Somerset courtesy of Charleston , the Sussex-home synonymous with the influential Bloomsbury Group. Alongside Vanessa Bell and Duncan Grant, Fry was a key member of the Bloomsbury Group – a group of artists, writers and thinkers that helped shape new ideas in art, literature and design in the 20th century. Changing the Course of British Art Best known for his work as an art critic, writer, and curator, Fry was instrumental in bringing post-impressionism to England. His 1910 and 1912 exhibitions at the Grafton Galleries in London, featuring Cézanne, Matisse, Van Gogh, were revolutionary. They introduced a shocked British public to this bold new movement, helping to ignite the modernist era in Britain and forever changing the course of British art. Still life with Coffee Pot (recto), 1915, oil on canvas, The Courtauld. Photo © The Courtauld. Discover 1. See rare and remarkable artworks, including pieces never before displayed publicly, shown alongside nationally significant works 2. Explore more than 40 stunning artworks, from landscapes and portraits to interiors that showcase Fry’s modern style and bold use of colour 3. Discover the Somerset story behind a nationally important artist 4. View works by Helen Coombe, Fry’s wife and an accomplished artist whose work is seldom seen Still Life: Flowers, 1912, oil on canvas, Tate. Photo © Tate. Enjoy 1. Experience the wellbeing benefits of art, with the exhibition offering space for reflection, calm and connection 2. Enjoy great art in Somerset, celebrating modern British art at its best 3. Come along to expert talks and tours to learn more about modernism and the Bloomsbury Group 4. Explore your own creativity at workshops for adults and families
tagline: See vibrant portraits, landscapes, and interiors and more

title: A Climb up little Solsbury Hill
subtitle: Fascinating Somerset facts - Did you know there is a Hill just outside Bath, Somerset that is linked to Saxon Battles and the Iron Age and also featured in a very famous music artist song in the mid 70's.
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"196"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"



Did you know there is a Hill just outside Bath, Somerset that is linked to Saxon Battles and the Iron Age and also featured in a very famous music artist song in the mid 70's. 

More commonly known as Solsbury Hill, its a good introduction to Bath in Somerset and encompasses an Iron Age history lesson along with stunning views — and a slice of English musical history. Situated a few miles from Bath at Batheaston, an Iron Age hill fort occupied this 191-metre hill between 300 BC and
100 BC.

After this period, it appears some of the huts were burnt down and the site was abandoned, never to be occupied again. The fort was possibly forsaken during the Battle of Badon, fought between the Britons and the Saxons.

The hill also has a link to modern music culture. The song ‘Solsbury Hill’ (1977), by English musician Peter Gabriel, records a spiritual experience by the artist on top of the hill after his departure from the rock band Genesis.

A track completely circles the hill and on a overcast day when the wind howls across the tops, the sound speaks of the souls who lived here over 2000 years ago, along with a sense of loss, inspiring a modern-day hit single.


For more on Somerset's incredible history and heritage go to our interactive E Book.

title: Dunster Working Watermill, National Trust
subtitle: On site of a mill mentioned in the Domesday Survey of c1086. The present mill dates from 18thC and was restored to working order.
bodyContent: Dunster Working Mill, Somerset, National Trust is a fully restored watermill A restored 18th-century watermill built on the site of a mill mentioned in the Domesday Survey of 1086. The mill is set in peaceful surroundings alongside the River Avill and at the entrance to the Dunster Castle River gardens. The watermill is fully operational. You can often see original milling here and even buy the flour produced.
tagline: A restored 18th-century watermill built on the site of a mill mentioned in the Domesday Survey.

title: The Natterjack Inn
subtitle: Adrian and Kate welcome you to The Natterjack Inn. We hope our site will inspire you to pay us a visit.
bodyContent: Whether it's Accommodation, a family or celebratory meal, working lunch or just a drink to unwind, we aim to make your visit a pleasurable one. The Natterjack is a truly traditional pub, offering a wide choice of locally sourced, home-cooked food, real ales and fine wines. Its warm and friendly atmosphere lends itself to all occasions. Why not visit us and introduce your dog to the delights of The Natterjack Inn. We are proud of The Natterjacks history as a Pub and Inn that served the community of Evercreech Junction and beyond. We continue in the tradition of a community Pub, welcoming all and offering good food in comfortable and friendly surroundings. We source from local suppliers so that we can offer fresh, local and seasonal produce and also keep our environmental footprints to a minimum. Award winning butcher Paul Loader supplies our beef, pork, lamb and poultry and it all comes from local farms. In fact as you drive towards the pub from Shepton Mallet you can see the free range pigs grazing in a field on the left. When we say local we mean it!!
tagline: Adrian and Kate welcome you to The Natterjack Inn

title: The Friendly Spirit
subtitle: Looking for a place to stay in Bridgwater? Then look no further than Friendly Spirit Inn, a quaint inn that brings the best of Bridgwater to your doorstep.
bodyContent: You can take advantage of some of the amenities offered by Friendly Spirit Inn, including room service and a sun terrace. In addition, guests can enjoy a lounge during their visit. As an added convenience, there is free parking available to guests. Close to Bridgwater Docks Canalside (2.7 mi), a popular Bridgwater landmark, Friendly Spirit Inn is a great destination for tourists. While you’re here, be sure to check out some of the Mediterranean restaurants, including Green Olive Meze Restaurant & Bar and Roma restaurant, all of which are a short distance from Friendly Spirit Inn. Best of all, Friendly Spirit Inn makes it easy to experience some great Bridgwater attractions like Burrow Mump, which is a popular ancient ruins. We’re sure you’ll enjoy your stay at Friendly Spirit Inn as you experience everything Bridgwater has to offer.
tagline: Looking for a place to stay in Bridgwater? Then look no further than Friendly Spirit Inn

title: Beautiful views from Bleadon Hill
subtitle: Walk along rocky paths and enjoy far-reaching views of the Somerset Levels and coast during this short climb around Bleadon Hill and Canada Coombe. Bleadon Hill is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and part of the Mendip Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: about 2 miles. Difficulty: easy to medium, with one fairly steep climb. The walk is along a compact gravel surface then a rocky, uneven lane. There are some loose stones, ruts and mud, so wear suitable footwear. Duration: about 1.5 hours at a leisurely pace. Map: OS 153 Explorer Walk along rocky paths and enjoy far-reaching views of the Somerset Levels and coast during this short climb around Bleadon Hill and Canada Coombe. Bleadon Hill is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and part of the Mendip Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. It features grassland, scrub and woodland, and is home to a variety of plants. Enjoy far-reaching views of the Somerset Levels and coast during this short walk. From the layby on Roman Road, continue east. At the bend, where the road becomes Canada Coombe, continue ahead on the footpath. This is a compact gravel path and bridleway and you’ll catch glimpses of Weston-super-Mare in the distance between the trees. At the end of the path you’ll come to a t-junction. This is signposted as a bridleway, the Butcombe Mendip Pub Trail, and the West Mendip Way. Click HERE for full details and FREE PDF copy

title: Hill House
subtitle: Escape the busy routines of life and Relax at Hill House with a bit of “home from home ”me time”.
bodyContent: Welcome To Guest Accommodation Hill House Bath Escape the busy routines of life and Relax at Hill House with a bit of “home from home ”me time”. Whether it’s history and heritage , the amazing array of independent shops restaurants, its art and culture or just the scenery and friendly social vibe, the central location of Hill House (yet only 15 minutes from country walks) makes it an ideal location to Explore Bath and the South West. If you need any further information Harry, Douglas and the team are always there to assist. All you have to do is ask. Hill House is a four storey Georgian Town House, built in 1762, which, being situated in the heart of historic Bath between the 3 Crescents – The Royal Crescent, Lansdown Crescent and Camden Crescent- is a great base to Experience all that Bath has to offer. Refurbished in 2011 its six individually decorated en suite rooms retain much of their original charm and character with all the amenities expected by a traveller in the 21st century including original artwork throughout.
tagline: Escape the busy routines of life and Relax at Hill House

title: Tucking Mill View, luxury self-catering cottage
subtitle: Tucking Mill View is a luxury self-catering cottage with outstanding views over the Midford/Tucking Mill valley, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty all on one level.
bodyContent: A real home from home, this self-catering cottage is ideal for those holidaymakers who wish to combine the country with the city… Newly renovated and maintained to the highest standard Tucking Mill View has been awarded the coveted 4 Star Gold Award for Exceptional Accommodation and Welcome by Visit England. TUCKING MILL VIEW ACCOMMODATION The single storey luxury self-catering cottage is 66 metres square…with a large open plan sitting room, with a 3 seater sofa and a snuggle sofa (which can double as a single sofa bed) and a modern fully equipped kitchen with washing machine and full size dishwasher. The calmly appointed bedroom in cream and turquoise has a luxury 1400 sprung king sized bed, with top quality Egyptian cotton bed linen. The only noise likely to waken you are the owls in the tree tops. For those balmy evenings, the private patio overlooking the valley is an ideal spot ..with a stone built barbecue and table and chairs you can enjoy every meal without being disturbed. Being so close to Bath, Tucking Mill View is the perfect balance for relaxing and unwinding as well as exploring the beauties of the Bath and wandering in the Somerset and Wiltshire countryside. As well as the gold Award for exceptional welcome, Visit England have also awarded the cottage the Cyclists’ and Walkers’ Welcome Awards and the cottage is an ideal centre for waling and cycling, particularly with he newly opened Two Tunnel Route into Bath..Sustrans 24 which passes by the cottage. AROUND AND ABOUT This secluded hamlet takes its name from the process of ‘tucking’ ,a process for cleansing wool, was undertaken. Being halfway between the historic villages of Midford and Monkton Combe, Tucking Mill benefits from access to two independent gastro pubs both within a 15 minute walk along the lanes, serving delicious home cooked food at evening and lunch times. The famous community pub, the Packhorse in South Stoke is a lovely 30 minute walk up the valley. MEDIA FACILITIES Facilities include free wifi , iPod docking station, flatscreen TV and DVD in the living room. Being so close to Bath, Tucking Mill View is the perfect balance for relaxing and unwinding as well as exploring the beauties of the Bath and wandering in the Somerset and Wiltshire countryside. PARKING Free private parking space for 2 cars is provided immediately outside the entrance to the cottage. REWARD CARD The benefits of the Reward Card with special discounts and extras like 3 hours for 2 in the Thermal span and 10% off entrance to the Roman Baths are available to all guests. Just look at the Reward website for more details. ABOUT TUCKING MILL SELFCATERING Tucking Mill view is one of the five 4 Star Luxury Gold properties int he Tucking Mill Self Catering portfolio owned by Michael and Ann. There are tow apartness in the city centre – the Old smithy Loft and No 2 Hedgemead court and a further two cottages in the vicinity of Tucking Mill, Midford….Brooks’ View and Fishermen’s Retreat, in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. THOSE LOOKING AFTER YOU The property is managed by the Family Team ..with Ann who has a background in hospitality and done much travelling, Michael who built the barbecues and cares of the birds and the gardens and Head Housekeepr Nikki, the team will do its utmost to ensure you enjoy your stays. You will also likely meet Rob our invaluable man of all trades. We all hope you enjoy your stay.
tagline: Tucking Mill View is a luxury self-catering cottage

title: Crescent Apartment
subtitle: New luxury self catering/ serviced apartment in Bath. City centre location, 5 minutes walk to the Circus and world famous Royal Crescent.
bodyContent: Enjoying an excellent city centre location, Bath Circle is a newly built Georgian town house, offering luxurious serviced accommodation 5 minutes walk from Royal Crescent and The Circus, making it ideal to explore the city and beyond. The apartments are available for short and medium term lets. All are furnished to the highest standard and every detail has been carefully considered. Crescent Apartment (2 bed apartment, plus sofabed, sleeps up to 5) is on the lower ground floor and the Circus Apartment (1 bed apartment, plus sofabed, sleeps up to 4) is on the first floor of a Georgian townhouse. The apartments are built to the highest standard with quality and comfort in mind. The Crescent apartment comprises an open-plan sitting room/ kitchen, master bedroom, single bedroom, bathroom and elegant French doors leading to the courtyard. The sitting room is furnished with two sofas (one is a sofa bed), LCD TV & DVD, Hi-Fi with a dock for your iPhone or iPad and a dining table suitable for six people. The master bedroom has a super king size deep-sprung divan bed, which can be converted into twin beds, fitted wardrobe, console table and stool and flat-screen television. The bedding is fine percale cotton linen with a luxurious mattress topper and completed with a feather-light goose down duvet and pillows. The second bedroom has a single deep-sprung divan bed with similar bedding to the master bedroom. The quality modern kitchen has been carefully planned and fitted; fully equipped with Neff induction hob, electric oven and integrated appliances: including a microwave, dishwasher, washer/dryer, fridge and separate freezer. The contemporary bathroom is fitted with Villeroy and Boch sanitary ware consisting of a bath, shower, wall-hung toilet, sink, and includes Duck Island toiletries and luxury bath sheets. On your arrival you will find some of life essentials in a complimentary welcome basket.
tagline: New luxury self catering/ serviced apartment in Bath

title: Marston Park
subtitle: Offering an exhilarating Pandora’s box of unique cultural experiences in jaw-droppingly picturesque surroundings, Marston Park has a lively programme of creative workshops, wellbeing sessions and musical performances, as well as a late night lakeside bar and food truck serving delicious hyper seasonal food.
bodyContent: Marston Park is located near charming, historic Frome, and is just 40 minutes from Somerset’s popular gems, Bath and Glastonbury, and two hours from London. Its selection of beautiful canvas studios line one side of the lake and come furnished with a desk, guitar, easel and artists’ materials. Across the water wood-fired eats and al fresco banquets are available to all. The lakeside bar is open every day until 11pm. Food trucks serve a rotating menu with a melting pot of local flavours and globally-influenced cooking, from Latin, Greek and Northern-Thai street food to a wood-loaded pizza oven, spinning rustic sourdough pizzas. The Futuro House at Marston Park is the first of many on-site collaborations with artists, architects, designers and ingenious folk from the world over. Marston Park aims to bring together like-minded people to share ideas and good times in a beautiful and peaceful environment. Marston Park has a year round holistic programme of workshops and classes plus exciting event collaborations such as its Ibiza-themed luxury weekends , curated by the world-famous rock ’n’ roll hotel, Pikes Ibiza and plenty of seasonal fun including All Hallow’s Eve and Guy Fawkes Night.

title: Prior Park Landscape Garden, National Trust
subtitle: Beautiful and intimate 18th-century landscape garden.
bodyContent: Beautiful and intimate 18th-century landscape garden. One of only four Palladian bridges of this design in the world can be crossed at Prior Park, which was created in the 18th century by local entrepreneur Ralph Allen, with advice from 'Capability' Brown and the poet Alexander Pope. The garden is set in a sweeping valley where visitors can enjoy magnificent views of Bath. Restoration of the 'Wilderness' has reinstated the Serpentine Lake, Cascade and Cabinet. A five-minute walk leads to the Bath Skyline, a six-mile circular route encompassing beautiful woodlands and meadows, an Iron Age hill fort, Roman settlements, 18th-century follies and spectacular views. Current project to repair the historic dams is due to finish in 2022.
tagline: Beautiful and intimate 18th-century landscape garden.

title: At the Manor
subtitle: Manor Farm House self catering accommodation is spacious, comfortable and tastefully decorated and can accommodate large groups of 10-15 guests.
bodyContent: We are a 15 minute drive from the beautiful city of Bath and a perfect location for family celebrations, birthdays and anniversaries, wedding groups, girlie gatherings and business meetings. The country house has a calming, relaxing atmosphere. We also provide bed and breakfast accommodation. This gorgeous country Manor near Bath in the heart of Somerset was once a Grange and run by Monks from a nearby monastery in Tudor times. We are tucked away down a quiet country lane in the heart of the conservation village of Norton St Philip. The central village location allows our guests a leisurely stroll to the local pubs including the famous George Inn. Discover stunning countryside walks and a meander around the historic conservation village of Norton St Philip. There are many cycle routes in this area too including the renovated old train tunnel into Bath. We are also close to Bradford on Avon for canal walks, boating and cycling, Wells – the film Hot Fuzz was filmed here, Longleat Safari Park, Glastonbury – climb the ancient Tor, Stonehenge, Frome – the best market ever is held the first Sunday of each month and Salisbury.
tagline: Manor Farm House self catering accommodation is spacious, comfortable and tastefully decorated

title: Moncrate Cottage
subtitle: Superbly located cottage 2 miles from Bradford on Avon and 5 miles from Bath.
bodyContent: Superbly located cottage 2 miles from Bradford on Avon and 5 miles from Bath. title: Eight
subtitle: Eight is a small and independent townhouse hotel with a restaurant in the heart of Bath.
bodyContent: Eight is a small and independent townhouse hotel with a restaurant in the heart of Bath. We have eight bedrooms that effortlessly marry past and present. Each one has its own history and charms, yet all share the latest in up-to-the-minute creature comforts. As a small, independent townhouse, we’re able to give each and every guest our undivided attention. Nothing is too much trouble. We serve eight dishes that change with the seasons. All of our plates are small so you can choose two, three or four each and savour the best ingredients available right now from coast, field and forest. Pair your selections with a glass or bottle from our extensive wine list or ask for a recommendation. Find out more here .

title: More Somerset Fascinating Facts about possibly the oldest Prison in the UK - Shepton Mallet Prison.
subtitle: The Shepton Mallet Prison, Shepton Mallet, Somerset has a long history of death sentences being carried out under methods including HDQ, hanged and by firing squad. The Hanging room which still exists, though has been used as office space for many years. Following the Monmouth Rebellion of 1642-1685 at least 12 Shepton men were HDQ for having sympathised with the rebels, their bowels were burned and their heads placed on poles around the town.

title: Immersive Events at Shepton Mallet Prison
subtitle: Established in 2015, Immersive Events or ‘IME’ is an award winning, interactive, immersive events company based in Shepton Mallet Prison.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. Shepton Mallet Prison, Somerset specialise in designing and running events nationwide from Scream Parks & Scare Mazes to Escape Rooms, overnight stays to prison breaks, from corporate training to Hens and Stags. IME has proudly been nominated for a SCAR 2016 – Best Zombie Survival Event for Lockdown and became winner of SCAR 2017 Experience for Lockdown I, Lockdown II and Lockdown Origins. Annual, monthly and weekly a huge variety of events are held at Shepton Mallet Prison. Every year over the Halloween period IME host the sold-out event ‘The Street’. This scare maze is to be endured for a gruelling 25 minutes and is one of a kind. The scare maze is riddled with twists and turns, jump scares and horrors. Due to popular demand, ‘The Street’ at Shepton Mallet Prison, Somerset's Ultimate Scare Maze is re-opening for Christmas; with the addition of Santa's GROTto! Tickets are just £10 and are now on sale. The event will be held on the 21st and 22nd December. Let’s hope you have been good this year! Escape Rooms are held every Saturday at 11:00am, the maximum group size is 18 people and pre-booking is recommended. To escape from a cell in Shepton Mallet you have to complete a sequence of riddles, puzzles and a series of mind-challenging games. Think you can escape from your prison cell? Tickets are just £20pp. New for 2019, IME’s Prison Break event is a much larger scale of an escape room and is heavily interactive. Yourself ‘The Criminal’, is processed by ‘officers’ in reception, giving you the immersed feeling that a convict would have experienced before being led to your cell. To escape not only the cell but escape the prison itself, you will have to answer riddles, solve puzzles and out think the officers. Battle archery is a private pre-book event that requires a minimum of 8 people and costs £25pp for two hours. With bows and foam-tipped safety arrows, this exciting action-packed game offers mission based archery experience. Bespoke packages are also available for this event with the option to add on a cell escape at £35pp (1 hour for each activity). Shepton Mallet Prison, offers a specific type of backdrop and scenery which can’t be accessed in many places. This provides a great opportunity for a truly unique experience for your event or party. Our packages for private parties, stags, hens & birthdays can be custom built to suit your needs. From cocktail making to scare experiences we are sure to put together a package that works for you. We have developed our team building and corporate training days to suit every business, big or small. Team building days aim to motivate your team, increase productivity, collaboration and communication and develop a business with forward thinking employees. Our Team Building days focus on fun and collaborative activities for employees to create and share team memories. We can mix and match any of the activities to create a team building session that is right for you, alternatively you can contact us and we will happily look at customising a package for you.
tagline: Shepton Mallet Prison, Somerset offers specific type of backdrop which can’t be accessed generally

title: Barrington Court, National Trust
subtitle: Barrington Court, located in the stunning south Somerset countryside, is a charming Tudor manor house complimented beautifully with Gertrude Jekyll-inspired gardens, apple orchards and a working kitchen garden.
bodyContent: Barrington Court Somerset National Trust - Discover the haunting echoes of the past at Barrington Court, a Tudor manor house free from collections and furniture. Explore using your imagination and your senses to discover a house full of memories, where light fills the rooms and you feel you can almost touch the past. The property was saved from ruin and restored by the Lyle family in 1920s, when the Court House resembled a barn rather than the proud manor house that it is. Close your eyes and you’ll almost be able to hear the sounds and see the sights of the glamorous parties held in the great hall during Barrington’s heyday. On the first floor listen out for the voices resonating from the past, of the young evacuees who called Barrington home during the Second World War. Stroll through the Gertrude Jekyll inspired gardens, which with their focus on plant varieties and colours are a delight for all the senses. Be spurred on in your own garden or allotment by the stone-walled kitchen garden that produces a variety of delicious fruit and vegetables. Don’t just take our word for it, why not stop off in the Strode House Restaurant to taste these home-grown delights. Barrington Court predominantly featured in BBC’s highly acclaimed recent production of Hilary Mantel’s Wolf Hall.
tagline: Barrington Court, located in the stunning south Somerset countryside.

title: Thatchers Cider
subtitle: For more than a hundred years, family-run Thatchers Cider has been quietly perfecting the magic that turns apples into cider.
bodyContent: For more than a hundred years, family-run Thatchers Cider has been quietly perfecting the magic that turns apples into cider. Here at Myrtle Farm in Sandford, each generation has passed on cider-making secrets, like encouraging bees to pollinate the apple blossom, or looking after the 150 year old oak vats where the cider matures. We lovingly craft a range of ciders but whichever you choose, they have all been made with the same care and attention, and with the same hands-on experience – we wouldn’t have it any other way. Nestled at the foot of the Mendip Hills , the Thatchers orchards are our pride and joy. With apples such as Dabinett, Somerset Redstreak and Porters Perfection, as well as some newer varieties such as Angela, Lizzie and Prince William, it’s here that the journey starts, inspired by the heritage and values of our company. Our flagship brand Thatchers Gold is a full flavoured, medium dry Somerset cider, with a wonderfully rich, golden colour. Thatchers Vintage is well balanced and mature, with a distinctive depth of character, while Thatchers Haze is a premium cloudy cider that has a crisp, sweet finish. We have recently introduced a new cider to our range, the gloriously pink Rosé, bursting with fruity apple flavours. Our other ciders include Thatchers Katy, Old Rascal and Green Goblin, together with our Stan’s Range of traditional ciders, such as Cheddar Valley, Trad. and Big Apple. Available on line and in our Cider Shop, Finally, holding down the fort at home, we have our award-winning Cider Barn range that’s exclusive to Myrtle Farm.that includes very special ciders such as Thatchers 458, Vilberie and Redstreak. You can buy all our ciders online at www.thatcherscider.co.uk Or visit our Cider Shop at Myrtle Farm. Here the shelves are packed with our ciders, alongside produce such as local cheeses and chutneys, and gifts including books and clothing. Our draught ciders are available straight from the barrel, so you can try before you buy. Why not book onto a tour of Myrtle Farm and see how we make our ciders. Visit www.thatcherscider.co.uk/visitus for more information. To book a tour of Myrtle Farm, please visit www.thatcherscider.co.uk
tagline: For more than a hundred years, family-run Thatchers Cider has been quietly perfecting cider.

title: Sheppy's House of Cider
subtitle: Sheppy's Cider, Somerset is one of the longest established cider companies in the UK.
bodyContent: With a history spanning six generations, and over 200 years, Sheppy's Cider is one of the longest established cider companies in the UK. The Sheppy family business remains independent and produces traditional ciders with apple juice from cider apples grown in orchards on their own Three Bridges Farm or locally. Traditional standard and more modern bush orchards over 70 acres play host to visitors, while producing a harvest which creates ciders of renowned quality for the local and wider British market. Natural fermentation takes place in giant oak vats as well as modern steel tanks, and the unavoidable smell of cider enhances the visitor experience. Old Conky cider celebrates both Sheppy’s bicentenary, history and location near the famous Somerset town of Wellington, with the great Iron Duke’s famous victory at the battle of Waterloo just over 200 years ago. He was sometimes known affectionately as “Old Conky” because of his conspicuous nose. This cider is medium-sweet and slightly sparkling and will also be available in 20 litre bag-in-box format and in 50 litre kegs for the pub trade. A traditional farming business is run alongside cider production, and a magnificent herd of Old English Longhorn cattle can be seen in the Summer months grazing around the farm and orchards. These produce meat for sale in the farm shop and for our Cider House Tea Room and Restaurant. All public buildings offer disabled access. We have a children’s playground and there are picnic tables outside for visitors to enjoy in the Summer. A museum collection of old agricultural and cider-making tools, gathered over the years from local farms, is of interest to our many visitors. A video of the cider-making year at Sheppy’s takes the visitor from Winter pruning through the seasons to the apple harvest and pressing time. Our shop contains our complete range of ciders and home-bred Old English Longhorn beef as well as a wide selection of locally produced food and drink. Visitors are encouraged to enjoy a taste of cider or apple juice before buying. Sheppy’s range of ciders includes a selection of single varieties, organic cider, vintage cider and Somerset’s famous Scrumpy. Our Cider House Tea Room and Restaurant (Closed from April 4th for major redevelopment) offers delicious home-made seasonal meals as well as cakes and light refreshments, all made from our own and locally sourced ingredients, as well as our ciders, of course. We can cater for all dietary requirements. The room is also available for evening or weekend bookings at times when the restaurant is closed to the public. We offer two types of visit: Fully guided tours during the Summer (May to end of October) can be booked in advance (minimum notice 14 days) for parties of any size. The tour includes a walk to the orchards, a visit to the press room and a vat house, a tour of the museum followed by a fully guided cider tasting. A meal can be provided for the group and menu choices are available. Guided tours take approximately two hours. Unguided visits are more casual. We like to know if a group is coming, but visits can take place at any time during opening hours. For a very modest fee, visitors can see the museum and enjoy a cider tasting in the shop. Visitors are always encouraged to enjoy a walk in the beautiful orchards, and perhaps end their visit with a treat and a cup of tea from the tea room. Apple pressing takes place in October and November when the harvest comes in, and this is an excellent time to visit. It is a busy time on the farm and visitors can see apples being delivered to the holding bays followed by pressing itself. At this time the farm is filled with the scent of apples and the yeasty smell of early fermentation taking place in the dark vat houses.
tagline: Sheppy's Cider, Somerset is one of the longest established cider companies.

title: The Manor Arms
subtitle: The Manor Arms, the only pub in the village, has always been a place of great attraction.
bodyContent: This lovely old village pub has withstood the ravages of modern design. The blue flagstone floors will still remain the same. Looking back over the years there are a few changes. The pub could be entered by a separate door from the outside to the top bar. To move from the best bar to the top bar from inside meant lifting up a section of the counter which was only allowed on special occasions. Behind the counter stood wooden barrels on a jib of beer and cider with their wooden taps which seemed to squeak at every turn. Draught beer could be bought at sixpence a pint, whisky sevenpence a nip and brandy bought at so much a noggin. Bottles of home brewed beer and Hunstman stout were taken straight out of the crates. The attractive sign bearing the Hoskyns Crest and family motto: "Finem Respice" which means "Look towards the end" hung on the outside wall until 1956. It was quite evident by then that all cattle lorries and furniture vans had been built much higher and the angle iron standing out carrying the sign was being continually bent back, and having to be repaired. Co-op vans and double decker sheep lorries became even broader and higher and seemed to look out and say "Get Back!". One fine morning it was discovered that the sign had received a real knock and was hanging precariously from its bracket by one chain.
tagline: The Manor Arms, the only pub in the village, has always been a place of great attraction.

title: The Duke Of York
subtitle: The Duke of York was Paul and Hayley's local long before it was their pub!
bodyContent: When they took it over in 2002 they had a firm idea of what they were looking to create - a pub with a traditional feel that would be welcoming to both their local neighbours and visitors to the area. Set in the beautiful Somerset village of Shepton Beauchamp, the Duke of York is a 17th Century Free House, that offers visitors a fantastic menu prepared by one of the area's leading chefs. On offer is a good selection of real ales, local Somerset ciders and an excellent range of wines, plus the Duke of York has been consistently featured in the Good Beer Guide for many years.
tagline: The Duke of York was Paul and Hayley's local long before it was their pub!

title: Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Mendip Activity Centre is the ultimate outdoor adventure playground in Somerset. They’ve been delivering adventurous outdoor activities for nearly 40 years, growing from humble beginnings to the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West!
bodyContent: It’s Time for Adventure with Mendip Activity Centre! Nestled in 250 acres of ancient woodland in the Mendip Hills National Landscape, Mendip Activity Centre is the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West. Just 20 minutes from Weston-super-Mare and Cheddar and open year-round, Mendip have been delivering Adventure, Learning and Training for individuals, families, schools, and groups since 1987. Activities available include: · Air Rifle · Tobogganing · Archery · Skiing · Snowboarding · Frisbee Golf · Kayaking · Nerf & Gel Battles · Caving · Paddle Boarding · Rock Climbing · Axe Throwing · ArcheryActive · Abseiling · Canoeing Come for the day or stay longer. In summer, pitch your tent at the award-winning Mendip Basecamp (link to https://mendipbasecamp.com/), a family adventure campsite awarded second at the Visit England Awards 2025. Pitch where you like, check out when it suits, camp fires encouraged, dogs welcome and endless adventure is on offer! Adventure for Everyone Mendip is more than just activities. It’s a place to switch off from screens, reconnect with nature, and each other. Whether you're learning something new, developing an existing skill or simply having fun outside, you’ll leave with muddy boots and big smiles. We believe in adventure for everyone. Many of our activities are adaptable for additional needs, and our friendly team will work with you to make it happen Refuel at the Alpine Lounge Overlooking the Ski Slope, the Alpine Lounge café serves pizzas, paninis, coffee and cake with stunning views- perfect for après-adventure refreshments

title: Blow away the cobwebs at Battery Point
subtitle: Battery Point is the blustery headland in Portishead at the northern end of the Esplanade
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: about 2.3 miles Difficulty: medium – some rocky, uneven, uphill paths in Eastwood. A couple of sets of steps, going both up and down. Wear suitable footwear Duration: about 1.5 hours at a leisurely pace Map: OS 154 Explorer Battery Point is the blustery headland in Portishead at the northern end of the Esplanade. Last year, the historic site was one of 100 areas across the country to be named a Centenary Field, giving it protection in perpetuity as a site of remembrance. The Centenary Fields programme, run by the Fields in Trust charity, protects valuable green space as a living remembrance to those who fought and lost their lives in World War 1. title: Leighton Townhouse

bodyContent: Spoil yourselves at Leighton Townhouse. We are just a 10 minute walk from the city centre, in a peaceful 140-year old Victorian villa, set in lovely gardens, with great views away from the hustle and bustle of the city centre and offering complimentary on-site car parking. title: Georgian House
subtitle: This gorgeous, light & peaceful 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom loft apartment is located in a Grade 1 listed Georgian building on a wide, pedestrianised street.
bodyContent: One king size bedroom One twin bedroom with an additional single bed on request Two bathrooms, one ensuite shower room plus family bathroom with over bath shower Excellent central location Lift access Gorgeous views of river, cricket ground & Bathwick Hill This gorgeous, light & peaceful 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom loft apartment is located in a Grade 1 listed Georgian building on a wide, pedestrianised street. Duke Street is an ideal location for all your city needs with all the sights of Bath within easy reach. Bath Abbey, the Roman Baths & Bath’s many delightful shops are a short stroll from the apartment & Bath Rugby’s ground is a mere 2 minutes walk along the river towards Pulteney Bridge. In addition, there are many fabulous restaurants on your doorstep. When you return for the day you’ll be able to put up your feet & gaze at the glorious view of Bathwick Hill & the distant Sham Castle to relax & rejuvenate before the next day. To help with that home to home feeling there is free Wifi, a Nespresso coffee machine, dishwasher, microwave, washing machine, tumble dryer & the comfiest beds we could find. A highchair, cot or extra child’s bed can be also provided on request. In addition a widescreen TV & DVD player with DVDs of some of the many films shot in Bath over the years are waiting for you. If you fancy some exercise, Bath Leisure Centre with a pool, gym & exercise classes is a hop and a skip over North Parade Bridge. Whilst for those fresh air fiends, the canal can be easily accessed for walks/runs/cycle to Bathampton (3 miles) & beyond. Bikes can be hired locally or you can bring your own & keep them in Georgian House’s basement bike store (please bring your own lock). The canal is also a lovely way to walk to the Holburne Museum. Georgian House is an amalgamation of three Georgian townhouses & has retained its grand feature staircase and useful lift from its hotel past. A 5 minute level walk from Bath Spa Train & Bus Station, public transport is the best way to visit Bath. If however you need to bring your car, the apartment has a parking permit allowing free parking is central zone spaces. For busy times, there is also a long stay car park 2 minutes walk away.
tagline: This gorgeous, light & peaceful 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom loft apartment

title: Cumberwell Country Cottages Benzes Mead Cottage
subtitle: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages.
bodyContent: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside on the edge of an area of outstanding natural beauty but only 5 miles from the world heritage city of Bath and 1 mile from the Saxon town of Bradford-on-Avon. Cumberwell Country Cottages are located on Great Cumberwell Farm, which has been in the James family since 1939 and was originally a dairy farm until 1992 when the herd was sold making way for a diversification into Cumberwell Park Golf Club, the farm itself has not changed a great deal and is still a working farm with over 300 acres of arable crop. The self-catering cottages available for your stay have been converted from an old tithe barn which has had many purposes in the past including stables, a grain store and cider production as the orchard at the front of the cottages was a cider apple orchard. Cumberwell is believed to have links with the Doomsday book when Cumberwell Manor used to exist at the top of the Farmhouse Garden, until it burnt down – Rumoured to have been by a cigarette left alight by the drunken butler!! The Farm where the cottages are located has been in the James family since 1939. Originally and for 55 years it was a dairy farm until 1992 when the dairy cows were sold making way for a diversification into Cumberwell Park Golf Club. The original Great Cumberwell Farm and its buildings have not changed a great deal over the years and in fact we still farm over 300 acres of arable each year, crops including Wheat, Barley and Oilseed Rape. The Cottages you can stay in have been converted from an old tythe barn, which has been restored with its original character in mind. Each cottage has taken its name from an original field on the farm, many of which have now been taken over by the golf course. The original tythe barn had many uses over the years.
tagline: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages

title: Waterhouse Guest House
subtitle: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath so once you have shopped till you are about to drop or taken the time to wonder along the local walking routes we have the perfect location set into the Midford Valley with country surroundings which ensures you will not be disturbed by the city noise or pace
bodyContent: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath so once you have shopped till you are about to drop or taken the time to wonder along the local walking routes we have the perfect location set into the Midford Valley with country surroundings which ensures you will not be disturbed by the city noise or pace. We have our own carpark, lift access, Bar, restaurant, conservatory, outside terrace and gardens place making Waterhouse a great place to work, rest, eat and play! We serve a selection of drinks which include local Beers, Ales, carefully selected wines and spirits to relax and unwind while taking in the stunning views across the Midford Valley. Our tranquil surroundings include the Midford Brook at the bottom of the property where we have fishing rights which people can use for a nominal fee, please enquire at reception should you like to make use of this exclusive facility. Across the Midford Valley there are stunning views and a selection of walks one of which is the two tunnels route which is one of the longest pedestrian tunnels in the UK. Other walks include the Kennet & Avon Canal. We are founded on Christian Values and aim to display the Love of Jesus to all who visit, please view the History of Waterhouse. Waterhouse is a 13 bedroom country house located in the idyllic and peaceful Midford valley 15 minutes south of Bath. Built around 1632, the house has been restored to provide bed and breakfast accommodation, meeting rooms and a venue for small events. All our bedrooms are located in the modern wing of the original house. We offer a choice of 8 double bedrooms, 1 twin room and 4 deluxe rooms, all en-suite.
tagline: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath

title: Layers of Time: The Gardens of Hestercombe
subtitle: Layers of Time: The Gardens of Hestercombe exhibition at Hestercombe
bodyContent: Hestercombe is more than a garden — it is a landscape shaped by visionaries, caretakers and changing ideas across four centuries. This exhibition explores that story, from its early formal beginnings to the sweeping eighteenth-century landscape, the artistry of the Edwardian terraces, and the remarkable restoration that has brought them back to life. Through images and interpretation, discover how each generation has left its mark on this Somerset estate — creating a place where history, design and nature exist in layers, still unfolding today.

title: For a spectacular view of Bath
subtitle: Somerset's Fascinating Facts For a spectacular view of Bath National Trust in Bath - Prior Park and Bath Skyline
customFields:
[{"key":"NewsID","value":"195"},{"key":"NewsBody","value":"

FOR A SPECTACULAR VIEW OF BATH National Trust in Bath - Prior Park and Bath Skyline 

A visit to Prior Park, Bath Somerset is essential. Situated in a sweeping valley, the park features an architectural masterpiece, one of only four Palladian bridges in the world.

A park first appeared on the site around 1100, when deer were released. In the 18th century Bath entrepreneur Ralph Allen extended and added to the park (with advice from two experts, poet Alexander Pope and landscape architect Lancelot ‘Capability’ Brown).

Their influence can be felt in this garden, particularly when standing beside the Palladian bridge on a cool autumnal morning, when mist fills the Avon valley below.

The walk up the hill towards the large Prior Park Estate building (not open to the public) provides a sweeping view of Bath and its Georgian splendour. Over 55,000 trees were planted on the slopes of the valley and the woodland walks provide glimpses of both the serpentine lake and gardens.

A small tearoom nestled in the woods provides the perfect place for a pick- me-up cup of tea after your walk.

More on Prior Park in Bath, Somerset  here 

For more on Somerset's incredible history and heritage go to our interactive E Book.

bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The Holburne, also known as the filming location for ‘Lady Danbury’s house’ in Bridgerton, is one of the UK’s best loved independent museums. As well as housing a wonderful and eclectic collection, it presents world-class exhibitions of historical and contemporary art and a dynamic programme of creative activities and events for all ages. Located at the end of the majestic Great Pulteney Street, and with a fantastic café, museum shop and gardens, it’s a must-see for any visit to Bath.

title: Stretch your legs around Sandford
subtitle: Sandford is part of the Mendip Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and after a wander through woodland and a steep climb, you’re rewarded with wonderful views across this rolling countryside.
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: about 3 miles Difficulty: medium to hard: narrow, rocky paths, a few wooden stiles, a steep climb. Paths can get muddy so wear suitable footwear Duration: about 1.5 hours at a leisurely pace Map: OS 141 Explorer Sandford is part of the Mendip Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and after a wander through woodland and a steep climb, you’re rewarded with wonderful views across this rolling countryside. Start on Hill Road in Sandford and head up The Batch. Follow the paved path around The Old Bakery. Continue around this house and follow the yellow waymarker to the right, veering uphill towards Batch House. The footpath goes uphill alongside Batch House, becoming a narrow, muddy track. Go through the metal gate and turn left, following the yellow waymarker. For more info and FREE PDF click HERE

title: Lorne House
subtitle: Lorne House is a large Victorian villa in the lovely Wiltshire village of Box, just six miles from the city of Bath.
bodyContent: Lorne House is a large Victorian villa in the lovely Wiltshire village of Box, just six miles from the city of Bath. We offer an elegant charm, gorgeous ensuite rooms and a very friendly, personal service. Lorne House provides an ideal base from which to explore Bath, the beautiful Wiltshire countryside and its many historic and beautiful local villages, including Lacock, Castle Combe, Bradford on Avon, Corsham and Avebury. The childhood home of Thomas the Tank Engine author, Reverend W.V.Awdry, Lorne House has been furnished to a very high standard; all our rooms are en-suite, with either wet-rooms or bathrooms, and come equipped with tea and coffee making facilities, hairdryer, flat screen television, iron and ironing board. There is free wifi throughout the house. Our breakfasts are hearty and substantial, with fruit, cereals, toast, traditional cooked English breakfast or continental options, served in our lovely light and spacious dining room. We source as many of our foodstuffs locally where possible and the marmalade is home-made. Guests have the choice of a comfy sitting room or a large outdoor verandah to relax and unwind.
tagline: Lorne House is a large Victorian villa in the lovely Wiltshire village of Box

title: Hedgemead Court apartment designed for luxury relaxation
subtitle: Our newly renovated contemporary apartment at No 2 Hedgemead Court is designed for luxury relaxation.
bodyContent: This is a spacious two bedroom apartment which has been awarded 4 Star Gold for special welcome. It is within easy reach of Bath, the M4 and Bristol Airport with free off road parking. This is a tranquil apartment with views down to the middle of the city from the sitting room and is adjacent to Hedgemead Park, one of the original pleasure gardens in Bath. There is a also lovely little balcony to sit and enjoy the view over Bath. Hedgemead Court ACCOMMODATION This beautiful luxury self catering apartment sleeps up to 4 in 2 bedrooms, made up either as 6 ft 3 super kings or singles. Together with Egyptian cotton linen and 1200 pocket sprung mattresses this ensures a restful night’s sleep. No 2 Hedgemead Court has luxury finishes throughout: with a large modern fully equipped kitchen and living dining area, realistic wall hung fire and 46 flat screen television and flat screen TVs in the bedrooms, comfy Schreiber sofa and snuggle chairs all combine to make the perfect end to a busy day in Bath. A calm drink on the balcony looking down into the city just tops it all. The bathroom has a large walk in drench shower and a luxurious Victorian claw bath. MEDIA FACILITIES Media facilities include free high speed Wifi throughout, iPod docking station, Smart flat screen TV with Netflix in the sitting room and flatscreen televisions in each bedroom. Books and DVDs are also available in the apartment together with a few board games. REWARD CARD If you book with us you can enjoy all the benefits of the bath Reward Card…giving discounts across a wide variety of city restaurants and attractions such as 3 hour spa session at the Thermae Spa for the price of 2 (Mon-Frid only), 10% off the Roman Baths and 10% off No 1 Royal Crescent. ABOUT TUCKING MILL SELF CATERING This is another of the five properties owned by Tucking Mill Self Catering. Do look at our other city property, The Old Smithy Loft or our 3 country cottages at Tucking Mill just 12 mins drive from the city centre in rural bliss, Tucking Mill View, Brooks’ View and Fishermen’s Retreat. THOSE LOOKING AFTER YOU The apartment is owned and managed by the Family Team; with Ann who has a background in hospitality and much travelling, Michael and Nikki Head Housekeeper the team does their utmost to ensure you enjoy your stay.. You will also likely come across Rob our invaluable man of all trades..

title: Whitley Coach House
subtitle: Whitley Coach House is a truly luxurious self-contained 1804 Georgian built.
bodyContent: Recently modernised stone coach house providing self-catering accommodation for long, short or one night stays. Whitley Coach House is an ideal base from which to visit Bath, Lacock, Longleat, Bowood House, Stonehenge, National Trust properties and many other local attractions. Only 20 minutes from Bath and 5 Minutes from Lacock – 10-minute walk to a great Pub/Resturant and local shop/cafe, free fast Wi-Fi, 40″ smart TV with Netflix and free private parking. Private garden with teak furniture on wooden decking. With luxurious bedding including a handmade king size Lit Bateau bed with a Vi-Spring luxuriously comfortable handmade mattress. Immediate and live AVAILABILITY. Accepting: American Express plus most credit and debit cards. Whitley Coach House self-catering accommodation has a large bedroom with a super king-size (5ft 6ins x 6ft 6ins) Lit Bateau oak bed designed and handmade with a supremely comfortable Vi-Spring handmade pocket sprung mattress. The living room has high ceilings with exposed beams and includes two three-seater sofas one with a large double pull-out bed. In addition, there is a luxurious deep sprung folding bed for use in the bedroom or entrance hall. ONLINE BOOKING or do look at our Website: www.whitleycoachhouse.co.uk The Space Whitley Coach House is a detached former coach house to a Georgian house, renovated four years ago and just redecorated, providing spacious self-catering accommodation. Whitley Coach House has a large bedroom with an individually designed and handmade kingsize bateau bed designed and handmade in oak, with a supremely comfortable Vi-Spring pocket sprung mattress. The living room has high ceilings with exposed beams and a solid oak floor and includes two three-seater sofas one with a large super king size pull-out bed. The living room has views of the private garden, teak furniture and decked veranda. The kitchen table seats up to six people. This self-catering accommodation has fast broadband, a 40 inch smart TV with Freeview channels and the ability to watch other online services like Netflix. Guest Access The back has a private wooden decked terrace for use in dry weather and garden beyond. There is plenty of private parking. A barbeque can be provided if asked for at an extra charge. Whitley Coach House self-catering accommodation is not adapted for wheelchair users but has a step up into the property on entry. Once inside there are no steps, it is a converted coach house on one level. Interaction with Guests Your host will normally hand you the keys and discuss Whitley Coach House and the surrounding area with you on arrival. Unless you need help or are staying over a week, you will be left alone to enjoy your stay.

title: Dash Corner Cottage
subtitle: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside.
bodyContent: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside on the edge of an area of outstanding natural beauty but only 5 miles from the world heritage city of Bath and 1 mile from the Saxon town of Bradford-on-Avon. Cumberwell Country Cottages are located on Great Cumberwell Farm, which has been in the James family since 1939 and was originally a dairy farm until 1992 when the herd was sold making way for a diversification into Cumberwell Park Golf Club, the farm itself has not changed a great deal and is still a working farm with over 300 acres of arable crop. The self-catering cottages available for your stay have been converted from an old tithe barn which has had many purposes in the past including stables, a grain store and cider production as the orchard at the front of the cottages was a cider apple orchard.

title: ⭐Shepton Mallet Prison
subtitle: Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’; Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom...
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’, Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom. Shepton Mallet Prison is a recently decommissioned (2013) Georgian jail where visitors can walk in the footsteps of our social history and hear officers shine a light on what life was like for both the incarcerated and those who guarded them through the ages. Before its closure, it was a category C lifer prison holding 189 prisoners. Opened in 1646, it was expanded in 1790, with further building work undertaken in the 1820s and 1830s, including the installation of a treadwheel for those sentenced to hard labour. In 1930, the inmate numbers fell and the prison was closed. During the Second World War, the prison was reopened and used as a military prison. It was initially used by the British Army and later by American forces, who constructed a new execution block for condemned prisoners. It was also used for the storage of important historical documents, including the Domesday Book. It returned to civilian use in 1966. Shepton Mallet prison is also known for its tales of paranormal activity. One of the most popular stories is that of the White Lady. She is frequently seen or sensed in various locations, especially A Wing. Staff and prisoners would often complain of an icy wind moving through the wing, the sweet smell of perfume and shadowy figures. She supposedly dates from the late 1700s, when she spent some time in the prison. During a lovers' tiff which escalated, she murdered her betrothed. Once found guilty and sentenced to death, she was housed in Shepton Mallet Prison. On the evening before her execution, she asked for her wedding dress to be brought to the prison, which they allowed. She wore it to bed that night, but in the morning the officers found that she had died during the night. No cause of death was ever found, so we are left to presume that she died of a broken heart. Perhaps this is why she still haunts the prison? In the early 1950s, the Kray Twins were also held here after deserting the British Army. Today, the prison is open as a tourist attraction offering Guided Tours, Self-Guided Tours, Escape Rooms, Night Behind Bars and Ghost Hunting Behind Bars. This is an immersive experience without gizmos or gimmicks – the jail is very much as it was when the last prisoners left in 2013. In 2025, Shepton Mallet Prison received the prestigious Trip Advisor Travellers’ Choice, for the 7th time running, placing it among the top 10% of attractions worldwide.

title: Old Stables: rural retreat, sleeps 6
subtitle: The Old Stables is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.
bodyContent: It is located in the beautiful Georgian village of Freshford which lies at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys in the southern Cotswolds. There are some wonderful walks to local pubs following the riverside and canals. All just 15 minutes from Bath by car but the secret of this location is the 9 minute train journey to Bath from the village station, just a short stroll from the cottages. A three bedroom cottage (two king and one twin-bed) with a fully equipped kitchen opening onto a dining room There is a separate living room with TV/DVD and two large leather couches . The living room has large patio doors that open up onto the courtyard area. The Old Stables can accommodate 6 people. This cottage has: Three bedrooms (two king size and one with twin beds) One family bathroom , a Living room with Freeview TV/DVD two large leather couches and a dining room with a table seating 6.The Kitchen is equipped with all the cookware you might need dishwasher along washing machine/dryer and Iron/Ironing board. Hairdryers , bed linen and towels are all provided in the bedrooms.We provide a “Welcome pack” of tea, coffee, sugar, milk, bread, butter, eggs and bacon. The cottage has Free WiFi. Neighbourhood overview: Freshford is a beautiful ancient village with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk from the cottage( The Inn at Freshford) that serves restaurant quality food and all the local beers and ciders.The village has an excellent fully stocked( from wine to organic humus!)community shop that also has a great cafe that serves lunch. There is also a local doctors surgery. The village is nestled at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys . The Kennet and Avon canal is a 15 minute walk from the cottage. Getting around: You don’t need a car to stay in the cottage. The village station is a few minutes walk away. Trains are hourly off peak and thrice hourly at peak times. Bath 9 mins, Bristol 22 mins. London Padington to Bath Spa 1.5 hours Bath Spa to Freshford 9 minutes Bath Spa to Freshford “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/bath-spa-to-freshford ” Freshford to Bath Spa “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/freshford-to-bath-spa ” There is also a local bus service to all the adjacent villages and Bath. The cottage has two parking spaces suitable for one medium and one small car or a single large SUV. Other things to note If you are a runner or keep fit enthusiast the owner is a qualified Personal Trainer (Bath Uni) with much Marathon and half marathon experience. She specialises in Ladies training. Please let us know if you would like guided running or some Personal Fitness training
tagline: The Old Stables is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.

title: Arcadian Visions: The art of Coplestone Warre Bampfylde
subtitle: Arcadian Visions: The art of Coplestone Warre Bampfylde exhibition at Hestercombe
bodyContent: Discover the world of Coplestone Warre Bampfylde — artist, traveller and garden designer. Born at Hestercombe in 1720, Bampfylde found lifelong inspiration in the landscapes around him. His paintings range from grand, classical scenes to lively views of Britain’s coasts and countryside, capturing both real places and imagined worlds. This exhibition brings together his remarkable work, inviting visitors of all ages to explore the beauty of landscape through eighteenth-century eyes.

title: The world heritage city of Bath is one of the most popular tourist destinations in England
subtitle: Somerset's Fascinating Facts - The world heritage city of Bath is one of the most popular tourist destinations in England The City of Bath in Somerset has been hosting visitors since around AD 60, when the Romans started building a temple complex and discovered healing hot waters emanating from a nearby spring. The town was named Aquae Sulis, in honour of the Roman goddess Minerva and the Celtic goddess Sulis, an early attempt at reconciliation between the old and new gods.

title: Somerset Coalfield Life at Radstock Museum
subtitle: Our award-winning museum transports you back to the Victorian industrial age; a time when Somerset had 75 coal mines covering an area 240 square miles.
bodyContent: Our award-winning museum transports you back to the Victorian industrial age; a time when Somerset had 75 coal mines covering an area of 240 square miles. The mines brought with them canals, tramways and railways and our villages and towns grew to accommodate the miners and their families plus all the people needed to support the collieries and the transportation of coal to places such as Bath and London. Explore our reconstructed coalmine and through the candlelit darkness you will see for yourself how dangerous and difficult it was for men and boys as young as five years old working in Somerset’s famously narrow coal seams, sometimes just two feet high. Hear the sounds of their picks and shovels; see the carting boy crawling through the tunnel dragging his put of coal. Why is he wearing only trousers and no boots? See how the miner’s wife managed daily life in our miner’s cottage, with as many as fourteen children to raise, and only a tin bath in front of the coal range for her husband and sons to wash in after a day down the mine. Go into her laundry room and outside privy, where a bucket under a wooden shelf with a hole in it provided the only toilet for several families to share! Where was the bucket emptied? Visit our old Co-op shop and learn how the co-operative society was set up by the people of Radstock to provide them with affordable food. Gaze upon our array of old packaging - can you see any recognisable brands still with us today? In our blacksmith’s shop the forge glows red hot; the blacksmith would heat his metal to make tools for the local farmers, repair the miners’ picks and shovels, shoe horses and repair colliery machinery. Walk through the Victorian schoolroom; compare it with today’s classrooms. Imagine having only a slate to write on or worse, being caned! Why did Victorian girls wear aprons to school? Get a birds eye view of central Radstock in the days of steam; our model shows where the Somerset and Dorset and Great Western Railways converged and where coal was loaded into wagons and taken by steam locomotives far and wide. See our collection of railway exhibits. Enjoy our fossil collection, visiting exhibitions, and our book and gift shop. Then relax in our cafe selling hot and cold drinks, delicious cakes and snacks.
tagline: Our award-winning museum transports you back to the Victorian industrial age.

title: Godminster Cheese
subtitle: Here at Godminster, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe. Our shop is open seven days a week and we have cheese available to sample every day.
bodyContent: Here at Godminster, Somerset, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe. Our shop is open seven days a week and we have cheese available to sample every day. There is free parking outside, so come and taste for yourself why Godminster has so many loyal friends around the world. We also offer fruit-infused vodka spirits, and over 18s are welcome to try those too. If you’re looking for a lovely foodie gift or a delicious souvenir of your trip to Somerset, come and take your pick from our range. Godminster’s Vintage Organic Cheddar is a deliciously soft and creamy cheddar matured for up to 12 months, at which point we select the best cheese to be made into one of our award-winning truckles. This sumptuous cheese is encased in the iconic burgundy wax to emphasise its pedigree and truly special status. The cheese is full bodied with a long, nutty, savoury bite. We also offer an Oak-Smoked Vintage Organic Cheddar, which sees the same top quality cheddar smoked over sustainably sourced oak chippings. The cheddar has a rich depth of flavour and the smokiness is evenly balanced with the acidity of the cheddar. Godminster Farm is set on the outskirts of the town of Bruton, Somerset, whose historic pedigree is recorded in the Doomsday Book of 1086. The Farm was registered as organic in 1999 and now boasts orchards with cider apples, peaches, nectarines and grapes, whilst keenly observing Soil Association and Government regulations relating to animal husbandry and the environmentally varied approach to business. The farm boasts a herb garden that enhances the natural remedies used to treat cows on the farm, 15 ponds supporting bio-diversity, and reeds which filter ground water. 25,000 broadleaf trees have been planted at the Farm since owner Richard Hollingbery took over, fostering diverse habitats and encouraging increases in the wildlife population. The cows at Godminster Farm, Somerset enjoy a simple and wholesome life. Richard sees them as the foundations for a truly holistic approach to his business, with the Farm’s milk turned into Godminster Vintage Organic Cheddar. Our mantra is "Nature repays those who treat her kindly," and that ethos runs across the business. Can’t make it to Bruton this time? Visit our website www.godminster.com let’s be friends on social media – we’re on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and Pinterest.
tagline: Here at Godminster, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe.

title: Cheddar Gorge, National Trust
subtitle: Discover the heights of Somerset's famous Cheddar Gorge
bodyContent: Cheddar Gorge is one of England's most iconic and spectacular landscapes. We are really proud to own the north side of this spectacular gorge and we hope that you will enjoy exploring it in a way that suits you. At almost 400 feet deep and three miles long, this is England’s largest gorge, and with its weathered crags and pinnacles, one of our most spectacular natural sights. The gorge would have begun forming about one million years ago during the last Ice Age when water from melting glaciers formed a river, which over time started to carve into the limestone rock creating the steep cliffs you see today. The Cheddar Yeo River gradually made its way underground, creating the famous Cheddar Caves. Please be aware that the National Trust do not own the caves at Cheddar Gorge or any of the car parking.

bodyContent: originally a working farm run by Jane's family since the late 1800's, into a delightful restaurant. Together with Jane's sister Sue, we can genuinely say that we provide a restaurant with rooms that is family run with a relaxed ambience and a service personal but not intrusive. Jane creates her dishes using local suppliers and produce as much as possible and all the food is freshly prepared on the premises, even the bread rolls - made by Crispin. Vegetarians are also catered for with something more exciting than Lasagne! Please look at our restaurant menus to see what is currently on offer.

title: Stunning views from Sand Point
subtitle: Sand Point is an extension of the Mendip Hills and walkers trekking across the peninsular will be rewarded with wonderful views across the Bristol Channel.
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: about 4 miles Difficulty: medium to hard: narrow, rugged paths, a couple of wooden stiles. Wear suitable footwear Duration: allow 2-2.5 hours at a leisurely pace Map: OS 153 Explorer Sand Point is an extension of the Mendip Hills and walkers trekking across the peninsular will be rewarded with wonderful views across the Bristol Channel. Head onto the beach from the Sand Road car park. The sand dunes are man-made sea defences, installed in 1983/4 after a major storm in 1981. More than 600,000 tonnes of sand was dredged up from the Severn Estuary to raise the beach by about three metres. Fencing was also installed to help stabilise the dunes and encourage vegetation. Head north on the beach, towards Sand Point. The sand becomes grassy and it can get a bit muddy so you might want to step up onto firmer ground, next to the trees. You will come to a wall, the remains of concrete forts which were used as a line of defence during World War 2 by local troops and the Home Guard. Walk alongside the wall and at the end there are a couple of steps leading to a path and the National Trust car park. For more info and a PDF please click HERE

title: Marlborough House
subtitle: Marlborough House is an enchanting Victorian Town House which has received 4 Stars and Gold Award for quality and service, and is operated by Peter Moore in a friendly and informal style.
bodyContent: Marlborough House is an enchanting Victorian Town House which has received 4 Stars and Gold Award for quality and service, and is operated by Peter Moore in a friendly and informal style. Marlborough House is in a great location. Conveniently located to all of Bath’s major attractions. The Royal Crescent, Circus, Assembly Rooms. Guild Hall, Abbey, Roman Baths, Thermae spas are all within a 2 – 15 minutes walk. Marlborough guest house, has 6 fully air conditioned, en-suite rooms, retaining many period features, and have been elegantly furnished to create a relaxing atmosphere. All rooms are different, some accommodate a family of 3 or 4. Have a minimum of a king size or superking size bed, one has an antique four poster bed. Our award wining breakfasts are served between 8.30-10 am, includes an abundant selection of freshly prepared fruit, cereals and yoghurts, followed by a choice of cooked to order vegetarian breakfasts. We have parking in our forecourt, and 3 special parking permits, please check availability of parking with us, prior to booking. Guests can check into Marlborough House any time between 11.30 am – 1.00 pm. or between 4.30 – 6.30 pm. Arriving outside of these times is by prior arrangement with the proprietor and before booking anywhere “on – line” Good discounts available for stays 3 of nights or more Sundays to Thursdays
tagline: Marlborough House is an enchanting Victorian Town House

title: Horseshoe Cottage, Lime Kiln Farm
subtitle: Horseshoe is the largest of our three beautiful luxury self catering holiday cottages set in stunning Somerset countryside just 15 minutes drive from Bath.
bodyContent: Horseshoe is the largest of our three beautiful luxury self catering holiday cottages set in stunning Somerset countryside just 15 minutes drive from Bath. The views are wonderful and there is a large private garden, perfect for family parties or BBQs. This converted stable building has two large ensuite bedrooms, sleeping up to 6 and is renovated to a very high standard, complete with all modern conveniences including free WIFI . The cottage is all on one level and suitable for wheelchair users. With easy access to the Bath Park & Ride, we are also perfectly located for exploring the many tourist attractions including local pubs and Lavender Farm, Cheddar Gorge, Wookey Hole Caves, Wells, Stourhead House & Gardens and the nearby Longleat Safari Park.

title: Fig Cottage
subtitle: Fig Cottage is immersed in idyllic countryside and bordered by National Trust gardens, yet just 20 minutes from the magical city of Bath and a five-minute walk from great pubs and cafes.
bodyContent: Fig Cottage is a light, airy cottage, tucked away in the pretty village of Holt. It is nestled in the grounds of a Grade II listed house, bordering The Courts National Trust gardens and open meadows. The modern kitchen is fully equipped with a Nespresso coffee machine, kettle, oven, hob and microwave. There’s also a fridge freezer, dishwasher and washing machine. However, if you’d like someone else to do the hard work for you, stroll round the corner to one of our fantastic village pubs and cafes. Holt has award winning cuisine, delicious brunches, scrumptious cakes and an excellent cup of tea or coffee. Fig Cottage has a spacious living area, with a comfy sofa, easy chair and double doors leading onto a private decked area. For dining and relaxation, there is also a pretty courtyard garden. Relax on the comfortable sofa or armchair indoors, watch the flat screen TV, listen to the stereo system or get stuck into a novel. There is fast WIFI, plus access to Netflix and other on demand TV. The pretty, vintage style bedroom has a superbly comfortable King size bed, made by luxury bed makers Loaf. Sink into crisp white bed linen and a feather duvet at night. At Fig Cottage , we are more than happy to provide a cot for any infant visitors, plus there is a sofa bed in the living area, which can accommodate two children or one adult (two adults if you’re prepared to be a little cosy). There is a large, walk in rainfall shower in the bathroom and fluffy white cotton towels. There are a wealth of activities in the local area. The world famous city of Bath is just a 20 minute drive away and Bradford-on-Avon is just five minutes by car. There you’ll find a wealth of independent shops, beautiful houses and churches, and miles of canal towpath to explore by bike, boat or foot. The Courts Gardens and Great Chalfield Manor (where Poldark was filmed) are both within walking distance, and Lacock Abbey, Dyrham Park, Iford Manor, Stourhead Gardens, Avebury Manor, Longleat and Bowood are all within easy reach. Bristol, with its aquarium, bustling waterfront and great shopping makes for a great day out too.
tagline: Fig Cottage is immersed in idyllic countryside
