title: Bushcraft and Survival Skills at Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Take the kids on a Somerset woodland adventure. This discovery experience is the perfect way to connect more with nature and have fun in the woods!
bodyContent: Take the kids on a Somerset woodland adventure. This discovery experience is the perfect way to connect more with nature and have fun in the woods! Could you survive in the wilderness? Experience a family friendly bushcraft and survival skills session in Mendip’s secluded ancient woodland. Your instructor will teach you some back to basics survival skills including fire lighting. Your efforts will be rewarded as you’ll get a chance to roast some marshmallows on the fire you built! 1.5 hour session bushcraft session Please note: This is a family friendly session, it is not aimed at or recommended for adult-only groups. Book Bushcraft and Survival Skills: https://mendip.me/book/survival_skills/

title: Dorian House
subtitle: A warm welcome awaits you at Dorian House, a stylish Victorian villa with stunning decor, eclectic Asian antiques and contemporary art collection.
bodyContent: A warm welcome awaits you at Dorian House, a stylish Victorian villa with stunning decor, eclectic Asian antiques and contemporary art collection. Set in a quiet, convienient location overlooking Bath towards the Royal Crescent, it is a 10-15 minute stroll into the centre and provides complimentary parking and well maintained Gardens. Rooms are gracious and all have views looking over Bath or our secluded hilly garden. Flatscreen TV's, WiFi, fluffy towels, high quality linen, bathrobes, high pressure showers, Nespresso Coffee machines and elegant French Damana herbal toiletries are standard in all rooms. Guests can also relax in our elegant sitting room, with local drinks from our honesty bar. In the morning look forward to a hearty, cooked to order breakfast in the Orangery situated in the Japanese-inspired garden. Begin with the extensive selection of locally sourced yoghurts, fresh fruit, Bath Cheeses, cereals, croissants, homemade preserves, fruit juices, freshly ground Bristol Coffee and a selection of Teas. Then our Full English breakfast, or a lighter option of Scottish Oak Smoked Salmon with free range Eggs. We hope to have the opportunity of welcoming you to our Villa soon.
tagline: A warm welcome awaits you at Dorian House, a stylish Victorian villa with stunning decor

title: Circle Luxury Stays: Crescent apartment
subtitle: Choose from apartments in Bath city centre, or an exclusive newly built five-bed holiday home with indoor pool in Devon/Dorset coast.
bodyContent: Bath properties are in landmark locations such as the Royal Crescent and Camden Crescent, within walking distance to the High Street. All are modern in design and beautifully furnished, providing you with more privacy, space and comfort than a standard hotel. Whether you are coming to Bath for a family get-away, romantic break, get-togethers with friends, or business, the apartments are a great option for stay of any duration. You are assured of a warm welcome and memorable stay on every visit. ——————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————— Crescent Apartment is on the lower ground floor, comprises an open-plan sitting room / kitchen, a good sized master bedroom with super king bed, a single bedroom, bathroom and elegant French doors leading to the courtyard. The sitting room is furnished with two sofas (one is a double sofa bed), LCD TV and DVD. The master bedroom has a super king size deep-sprung divan bed, which can be converted into twin beds, wardrobe, console table and stool and flat-screen television. The second bedroom has a single bed. The modern kitchen is fully equipped with Neff hob, electric oven, microwave and integrated appliances: including a dishwasher, washer/dryer and fridge freezer.
tagline: Choose from apartments in Bath city centre

title: Shoemakers Museum
subtitle: Discover the Quakers, the shoemakers and stories behind Clarks shoes in the place where it all began in Street, Somerset
bodyContent: Step inside a new family-friendly visitor attraction celebrating fashion, creativity and social change through 200-years of shoemaking. Find out how the Clarks shoe brand became a global story. A remarkable journey with exhibitions, film, interactives, tours, and regular events to explore enjoy. Meet the Shoemakers Four permanent exhibition galleries share the story of shoemaking in Street, from handmade shoes to factory life, fashions in advertising and shoe shopping. Discover life as a shoemaker, experience shoe shopping 1950s and 1980s style, and celebrate some of the nations’ favourite footwear. Plus meet fossil sea-dragons found under the Clarks factories! Galleries, gardens, café and interactive events An exhibition of 200 years of shoemaking alongside film footage that the factory floor to life. Explore your favourite shoes and experiences, from foot measurements to advertising. An exhibition of 200 years of shoemaking alongside film footage that brings the history of Clarks and the factory floor to life. Interactives include a 1980s shoe shop with 80s fashion to try on. Get creative in the education room and enjoy space to play. Accessibility Shoemakers Museum aims to be an accessible attraction. Facilities include accessible toilets, changing facility, lifts and accessible interactives. Please visit the website to view the access guide. Tickets Free carparking passes for Clarks Village Car Park II are available for museum ticket holders. Food and Drink Enjoy a taste of Somerset with the best of locally produced delicious hot and cold food and drink options available in café. Or bring a picnic to enjoy outside in the gardens and walled orchard. A great family day out Clarks Village, is right on our doorstep with outlet and high street shopping to indulge in after your visit. Shoemakers Museum in Street is a short distance away from historic Glastonbury, nature on the Somerset Levels, and artistic Somerton just down the road.
tagline: Discover the Quakers, the shoemakers and stories behind Clarks shoes

title: The Friends of the Museum of Somerset (FOTMOS)
subtitle: The Friends of the Museum of Somerset bring together people who are passionate about Somerset's past and future. The primary purpose of the Friends is to support the Museum.
bodyContent: Monthly talk programme upto July 2026 Tuesday January 20 th On-line 19:30 Jonathan Holt Somerset Follies Tuesday February 17 th On-line 19:30 AGM followed by Sean Pringle Kosikowsky Hadrian’s Wall Tuesday March 17 th On-line 19:30 Amy Downes The Snailman of Pontefract Tuesday April 21 st Museum 19:30 Richard Cooper-Knight Commonwealth War Graves in Somerset Tuesday May 19 t h Museum 19:30 Mike Motum The History of the Somerset Light Infantry Tuesday June 16 th Museum 19:30 Brian Wright Humpty Dumpty Sat on a Wall: Nursery Rhymes – a hidden history Tuesday 21st July Museum 19.30 John Young Thomas Young (1793-1829) All talks start at 19:30 and are held in the Great Hall of the Museum of Somerset during the Summer and on-line via ‘Zoom’ when the country is on Greenwich Mean Time during the Winter. Our aims are to: • further the education of the public by promotion, support, assistance and improvement of the Museum through the activities of a group of Friends • encourage, promote and assist the formation and development of a group of Friends of the Museum • further the charitable purposes of the Museum and encourage the development of the facilities which it affords • engage in, support and co-ordinate research, publishing, education, advertising and other charitable work • make the individual skills of its members available to the Museum and assist the staff with voluntary help The Friends help the Museum in a number of ways, including helping with their collections, supporting and co-ordinating research, raising funds for special projects and improving access to the collections.
tagline: The programme of monthly talks 2026.

title: Clevedon Court, National Trust
subtitle: Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is a remarkable survival from the medieval period.
bodyContent: Clevedon Court in Clevedon, Somerset, National Trust property is an outstanding 14th-century manor house and 18th-century terraced garden Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is a remarkable survival from the medieval period. The house was purchased by Abraham Elton in 1709 and it is still the much-loved family home of his descendants today. Explore the striking display of Eltonware pottery and a fascinating collection of Nailsea glass.
tagline: Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is remarkable.

title: Somerset Rural Life Museum
subtitle: Visitors to Somerset Rural Life Museum can explore rural life from the 1800s onwards and discover more about the county’s heritage including its landscape, food and farming, working life and rural crafts.
bodyContent: Visitors to Somerset Rural Life Museum can explore rural life from the 1800s onwards and discover more about the county’s heritage including its landscape, food and farming, working life and rural crafts. The museum tells the story of Somerset’s rich rural and social history. Visitors can enjoy the five Farmhouse Galleries which explore the themes of ‘Creating’, ‘Learning’, ‘Believing’, ‘Celebrating’ and ‘Remembering.’ In the large Farmyard Gallery the major themes are ‘Working Village’ and ‘Working the Land’. The magnificent 14th-century Abbey Barn remains the centrepiece of the site, providing a unique and remarkable setting for exhibitions and events. Outside spaces, including the Farmyard and the Orchard, contain sculpture and family trails that interpret the history of the site and its buildings. The Grain Store Café is open all year round at this family-friendly destination, offering high-quality locally-sourced food and drink. A programme of seasonal events take place throughout the year.
tagline: Visitors to Somerset Rural Life Museum can explore rural life from the 1800s onwards.

title: A Woodland Wonder
subtitle: Walk information Distance: about 5.2 miles Difficulty: medium to hard: narrow, rugged paths, a couple of wooden stiles. Wear suitable footwear. Ticks are present in this woodland so wear long sleeves, trousers and boots. Duration: allow 2.5 hours at a leisurely pace Map: OS 154 Explorer
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: about 5.2 miles Difficulty: medium to hard: narrow, rugged paths, a couple of wooden stiles. Wear suitable footwear. Ticks are present in this woodland so wear long sleeves, trousers and boots. Duration: allow 2.5 hours at a leisurely pace Map: OS 154 Explorer Take a wander around the tranquil woodland of Goblin Combe and spot rare ferns and beautiful butterflies in the shady undergrowth. From the parking area, turn right into Plunder Street and go past the old school building. Follow the footpath sign down the driveway towards Walnut Tree Farm. Go through the gate marked The Congresbury Estate and ‘Footpath to Wrington only’. Keep on this stone track, into Cleeve Wood. Goblin Combe is a limestone gorge. About 200 million years ago it was dry desert but torrential rainstorms and flash floods created waterfalls which wore away the rock. Millions of years later, this process was repeated when snow melted following the Ice Age. Read more and download the PDF HERE

title: Hedgemead Court apartment designed for luxury relaxation
subtitle: Our newly renovated contemporary apartment at No 2 Hedgemead Court is designed for luxury relaxation.
bodyContent: This is a spacious two bedroom apartment which has been awarded 4 Star Gold for special welcome. It is within easy reach of Bath, the M4 and Bristol Airport with free off road parking. This is a tranquil apartment with views down to the middle of the city from the sitting room and is adjacent to Hedgemead Park, one of the original pleasure gardens in Bath. There is a also lovely little balcony to sit and enjoy the view over Bath. Hedgemead Court ACCOMMODATION This beautiful luxury self catering apartment sleeps up to 4 in 2 bedrooms, made up either as 6 ft 3 super kings or singles. Together with Egyptian cotton linen and 1200 pocket sprung mattresses this ensures a restful night’s sleep. No 2 Hedgemead Court has luxury finishes throughout: with a large modern fully equipped kitchen and living dining area, realistic wall hung fire and 46 flat screen television and flat screen TVs in the bedrooms, comfy Schreiber sofa and snuggle chairs all combine to make the perfect end to a busy day in Bath. A calm drink on the balcony looking down into the city just tops it all. The bathroom has a large walk in drench shower and a luxurious Victorian claw bath. MEDIA FACILITIES Media facilities include free high speed Wifi throughout, iPod docking station, Smart flat screen TV with Netflix in the sitting room and flatscreen televisions in each bedroom. Books and DVDs are also available in the apartment together with a few board games. REWARD CARD If you book with us you can enjoy all the benefits of the bath Reward Card…giving discounts across a wide variety of city restaurants and attractions such as 3 hour spa session at the Thermae Spa for the price of 2 (Mon-Frid only), 10% off the Roman Baths and 10% off No 1 Royal Crescent. ABOUT TUCKING MILL SELF CATERING This is another of the five properties owned by Tucking Mill Self Catering. Do look at our other city property, The Old Smithy Loft or our 3 country cottages at Tucking Mill just 12 mins drive from the city centre in rural bliss, Tucking Mill View, Brooks’ View and Fishermen’s Retreat. THOSE LOOKING AFTER YOU The apartment is owned and managed by the Family Team; with Ann who has a background in hospitality and much travelling, Michael and Nikki Head Housekeeper the team does their utmost to ensure you enjoy your stay.. You will also likely come across Rob our invaluable man of all trades..

title: Fishermen’s Retreat
subtitle: A veritable rural retreat, Fishermen’s Retreat is an award winning haven of calm where you can totally escape from the bustle of Bath and relax in the beautiful Midford Valley beside the Midford Brook.
bodyContent: One of a rank of 4 cottages built for the Somerset Coal Canal workers in the late 1800s and renovated today to 4 Star standard and has now been awarded a Gold Star for exceptional accommodation and welcome. Sleeping facilities are on the first floor with a king size luxury 1400 pocket sprung bed in the master bedroom with crisp Egyptian cotton linen and a small overnight guest room. There is also a sofabed in the sitting room. With the original fireplace and wood burning stove the sitting room is very welcoming and comfortable. There is also a pine dining table for 4 in the window alcove so you can watch the birds feeding as you eat. This is more like a home than a holiday cottage. Just outside the front door there is a small private patio with table and chairs where you can pop out for a quick cup of coffee and admire the roses. Fishermen’s Retreat has a south facing mature garden leading down to the Midford brook where there is a stone built barbecue on the brookside patio. There is nothing more enjoyable than relaxing with a glass of wine while your cook is at work! Wildlife abounds here with a variety of birds..kingfishers, warblers, heron, cormorants all frequent visitors, preying on the local trout. AROUND AND ABOUT The Brook is a fishery stocked by the Avon Anglers and day tickets can be purchased for fly fishing. Need to be organised in advance. Alternatively, you can enjoy the many walks and cycle rides around: Sustrans 24 is just above the cottage and you are not be more than 300 yards along the road from the famous Two Tunnel Cycle way into Bath. The Kennet and Avon Canal path also provides excellent cycling opportunities and you can cycle one way i to Bath and the other to Bradford on Avon and Devizes. Wild swimming is available at Warleigh Weir and Farleigh Hungerford, 2-4 miles away Maps are supplied in all cottages. MEDIA FACILITIES There is free Wifi throughout the cottage and a flat screen TV in the sitting room. An iPod Docking station is also provided. There is a selection of DVDs, a variety of books as well as some board games. PARKING Free private parking space for one car is provided and a second by arrangement ABOUT TUCKING MILL SELF CATERING Fishermen’s Retreat is one of the five 4 Star Luxury Gold properties in Tucking Mill Self Catering owned by Michael and Ann. There are two apartments in the city centre, The Old Smithy Loft and No 2 Hedgemead Court, and two other cottages Brooks’ View and Tucking Mill View just 12 minutes drive away at Tucking Mill, Midford, a historic hamlet just outside the city boundaries in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. REWARD CARD All our guests benefit from the Reward Card and you can enjoy exclusive discounts for many of the city’s restaurants and cafes. One special deal is the 3 hour session for the price of 2 at the Thermae Spa – Mon-Fri. THOSE LOOKING AFTER YOU The property is managed by the Family Team..With Ann who has a background in hospitality and much travelling, Michael who built the barbecues and is in charge of logs, bird feeding and Head housekeeper Nikki the team will do its utmost to ensure you enjoy your stay. You will also likely meet our invaluable man of all trades, Rob Short or long breaks available.
tagline: A veritable rural retreat, Fishermen’s Retreat is an award winning haven of calm

title: The Bishop's Palace
subtitle: The Bishop’s Palace and Gardens in Wells has been home to the Bishops of Bath and Wells for over 800 years and this stunning medieval palace is now open for all to enjoy. It’s a great family day out in Somerset with a full programme of year-round events, free guided walks, open-air music and theatre, garden workshops and more and a slice of cake with afternoon tea at the ever-popular Bishop’s Table café is always welcome!
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Visit Highlights: There are 14 acres of outstanding RHS Partner gardens to explore (including the beautiful well pools from which the city takes its name), Dragon’s Lair play area, guided tours, children’s trails and workshops and a café with the best views in Wells! Multi media tours of the Palace building are also included with admission with the choice of an adult version or one tailored for a more family audience including quizzes, treasure hunts and talking Bishops from years gone by! Visitors are guided around the Palace buildings through five narrative themes using stories, music, imagery, quizzes and talking Bishops bringing stories of their tenure and legacy at the Palace to life in an interactive and engaging way. A year-round programme of themed family events is also included with admission including a Civil War Weekend; Archery, Vikings and more! Other events are ticketed separately including summer outdoor theatre; the Palace’s Garden Fair and History Live. The Bishop’s Palace dates from the early-thirteenth century when Bishop Jocelin Trotman received a crown licence to build a residence and deer park on land to the south of the Cathedral of St Andrew. Although home to the Bishop and other families, visitors can walk in the footsteps of past bishops through a number of rooms within the Palace. Visitors are also welcome to look around the Bishop’s private Chapel and explore the ruined Great Hall. The moat has been home to mute swans since the 1800s. The tradition of swans on the moat at The Bishop’s Palace in Wells is thought to go back to the 1850’s when it is likely that a Bishop’s daughter first taught the swans to ring a bell at the Gatehouse for food. We now have two swan bells – one just beneath the window on the left of the Gatehouse, the other to the right – both with a rope hanging down for the swans to pull. The Palace Gardens are open daily from 10am until 4pm in winter and 9.30am - 5.30pm in summer although there may be restricted access due to events and activities taking place (check the website for details). There are toilets on site. Guided tours are also included with Admission – check available times at the Ticket Office on arrival. Families: There’s so much for families to do at The Bishop’s Palace, whatever the weather. Little ones love to explore the gardens, trying to spot the swans and their cygnets; there are waterfalls and springs to see, trees to climb and places to hide. Children also love to explore the magical discovery area that is the Dragon’s Lair in a far corner of the Gardens! And throughout the school holidays, there are always plenty of events to keep families busy including crafting, outdoor gardening, family trails, storytelling and more. Refreshments: The Bishop’s Table café is open daily serving delicious, locally-sourced homemade food and some of the best coffee and cake you'll find in Wells. It’s the perfect place to meet friends for breakfast, lunch and afternoon teas or Sunday Lunches are now being served! Accessibility: From the main entrance of the Palace to the Palace building, around the gardens and to the café's dining area, there is level access. We have one lift to all floors of the Palace building. The outer gardens are accessible via a bridge which is 810mm wide. There are fully accessible toilets with level access within the Stableyard area and the Palace building. There are three spaces available on site for accessible parking, however, it is necessary to book these at least 48 hours before arrival via info@bishopspalace.org.uk or call 01749 988111.
tagline: The Bishop's Palace and Gardens, Wells, Somerset is a great family day out in Somerset.

title: **DO NOT DELETE** Taunton Literary Festival 2025
subtitle: An autumn festival of talks, brought to Taunton by Brendon Books.
bodyContent: Zoe Langley-Wathen - 630 Miles Braver: Midlifing on the South West Coast Path As a passionate storyteller, Zoe’s mission is to encourage others, and particularly midlife women, to ‘HeadRightOut’ of their comfort zone in the outdoors. It all began after a life-changing, seven-weeks solo walk along the UK’s longest national trail, the South West Coast Path. Zoe set about sharing her experiences of wild camping solo and wading estuaries at forty. She knows first-hand the dread of trying something new, but the benefits are worth it. Brendon Books, Taunton Wednesday 1st October 7pm - 8.30pm Catherine Hanley - Nemesis: Medieval England's Greatest Enemy The extraordinary tale of Philip Augustus, one of medieval Europe’s greatest monarchs, and the part he played in the downfall of four Plantagenet kings of England. Philip Augustus would rise to dominate the political landscape of medieval Europe, pitting his sharp mind against the formidable Plantagenet dynasty. This captivating narrative by acclaimed medieval historian Catherine Hanley traces Philip’s relentless struggle against Henry II of England and his ambitious sons. Brendon Books, Taunton Friday 3rd October 7pm - 8.30pm Andrew Miller - The Land in Winter December 1962, the West Country. In the darkness of an old asylum, a young man unscrews the lid from a bottle of sleeping pills. In the nearby village, two couples begin their day. Local doctor, Eric Parry, mulling secrets, sets out on his rounds, while his pregnant wife sleeps on in the warmth of their cottage. Across the field, in a farmhouse impossible to heat, funny, troubled Rita is also asleep, her head full of images of a past life her husband prefers to ignore. He's been up for hours, tending to the needs of the small dairy farm he bought, a place where he hoped to create a new version of himself, a project that's already faltering. Brendon Books, Taunton Wednesday 8th October 7pm - 8.30pm Robin Ince - Normally Weird and Weirdly Normal: My Adventures in Neurodiversity A powerful, personal exploration of anxiety, ADHD and neurodiversity, Normally Weird and Weirdly Normal reminds us all – no matter how weird we feel – that it’s okay to be a little different. We all are. Brendon Books, Taunton Thursday 9th October 7pm - 8.30pm Nicola Wilson - Recommended! : The influencers who changed how we read Before Reese Witherspoon and Zoella's Book Clubs, there was Oprah Winfrey and Richard and Judy. And before them, there was Hugh Walpole and the Book Society. This is the story of Britain's first celebrity book club and the judges who changed how we read. Brendon Books, Taunton Friday 10th October 6.30pm - 8pm Sam Leith - The Haunted Wood : A History of Childhood Reading Can you remember the first time you fell in love with a book?The stories we read as children matter. The best ones are indelible in our memories; reaching far beyond our childhoods, they are a window into our deepest hopes, joys and anxieties. They reveal our past – collective and individual, remembered and imagined – and invite us to dream up different futures. In a pioneering history of the children’s literary canon, The Haunted Wood reveals the magic of childhood reading, from the ancient tales of Aesop, through the Victorian and Edwardian golden age to new classics. Excavating the complex lives of our most beloved writers, Sam Leith offers a humane portrait of a genre and celebrates the power of books to inspire and console entire generations. Brendon Books, Taunton Wednesday 15th October 6.30pm - 8pm Kate Lord Brown - The Golden Hour From Cairo 1939 on the eve of the war and then thirty years later to 1970s Beirut on the eve of yet another conflict, The Golden Hour is an epic dual timeline story which interweaves glory-seeking desert archaeologists, priceless treasures, Nefertiti’s tomb and the decadent cabarets of WW2 Cairo with restless expat lives in bohemian Beirut. Brendon Books, Taunton Thursday 16th October 6.30pm - 8pm **Nigel Planer - Young Once:A Life Less Heavy The hilarious and heart-warming memoir of actor and comedian Nigel Planer. Most famous for playing Neil the hippy in The Young Ones and a pillar of the 80’s alternative comedy (the Comic Strip Presents and Bad News) and inspired by a recent sold-out tour where the audiences lapped up his witty and self-depreciating stories, Nigel Planer wants to take us back through the roles, the friendships and the rivalries, the triumphs and comic disasters that have taken him to where he is now. Nigel will be bringing his memoir to life and taking questions from the audience. He will also be reading from his poetry collection, Making Other Plans. A book signing will follow the event. Tacchi Morris Arts Centre, School Road, Monkton Heathfield, Taunton. Friday 19th October 7pm - 8.30pm Paula Byrne - Six Weeks By the Sea. The Summer Jane Austen Fell in Love Summer 1801. Sidmouth, England. The Austen Family descends upon a fashionable Georgian seaside resort in Devonshire for a six-week holiday. Jane's brother, Frank, is on leave from the Royal Navy, and dearly wishes to unite his sister with his friend Captain Peter Parker. But another holidaymaker, a handsome stranger, catches sight of Jane and is determined to make her acquaintance. This rival to Captain Parker is Samuel Rose: a lawyer, literary man and abolitionist. Brendon Books, Taunton Saturday 18th October 7pm - 8.30pm Mike Berners-Lee - A Climate of Truth : Why We Need It and How To Get It We have all the technology we need to live better than ever before, and yet humanity is still accelerating into a climate and ecological emergency. To understand why - and to give ourselves a chance of doing better - we have to look at the challenge from new angles. A Climate of Truth does this by standing further back from the problem to gain perspective, by digging deeper under the surface to see the root causes, by joining up every element of the challenges we face, and by learning from our failures so far. The need for radically higher standards of honesty - especially in our politics, media, and business - emerges as the single most critical point of leverage for those seeking change. This urgent and practical book points to what all of us can do to maximise ourimpact and be part of the evolution that humanity so urgently needs to avoid the polycrisis. Temple Methodist Church, Taunton Sunday 19th October 12.30pm - 2pm Rob Hopkins - How to Fall in Love With the Future:Time Traveller’s Guide to Changing the World There are an infinite number of possible futures that lie ahead of us—like threads stretching out into the distance. Rob Hopkins, cofounder of the international Transition Network movement, invites us to travel to future worlds we would actually want to live in. In 2020, when the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted every aspect of daily life, climate activist and Transition Network cofounder Rob Hopkins responded the way a lot of people did: by starting a podcast. Temple Methodist Church, Taunton Wednesday 22nd October 6.30pm - 8pm Adam Nicolson - Bird School : A Beginner in the Wood Step into the hide for a glorious new encounter with the British wild Close to Adam Nicolson’s home in Sussex, there is a forgotten field overrun by bracken and thicketed by brambles. It is the haunt of deer and many birds – nightingales, the occasional cuckoo, ravens, robins, owls and in summer the sweet-singing warblers that come north from Africa to breed in English woods. This gorgeous book charts his attempt to encounter birds, to engage with a marvellous layer of life he had previously almost ignored. Taunton School, Taunton Thursday 23rd October 2.30pm - 4pm Tim Gregory - Going Nuclear : How the Atom Will Save the World In this visionary book, Dr Tim Gregory urges us to rethink the path to net zero. He argues that the solution to climate change lies not simply in replacing fossil fuels with renewables, but in fully embracing another energy source that emits zero carbon dioxide: nuclear power. Brendon Books, Taunton Thursday 23rd October 7pm - 8.30pm Nicola Chester - Two Women’s Journeys Through Time, Land and Community From the Wainwright Nature Prize Highly Commended author Nicola Chester, a rural narrative between two women in two different eras who both wanted to become farmers. Was it easier for women to become farmers in the 1940s than it is now?Moving between Nicola’s own attempts to work outdoors and Miss White’s desire to farm a generation earlier, Nicola explores the parallels between their lives – and the differences. Miss White buys a derelict farm and begins to renovate and modernize it. As ghost (barn) owls flit between these two worlds, Nicola draws connections with farming and rural life in both times, from the role of women in rural communities in the modern day to Miss White’s experience in the 1940s. Brendon Books, Taunton Friday 24th October 7pm - 8.30pm Countess Carnarvon - A Year at Highclere Join Lady Carnarvon as she exclusively reveals into the daily rhythms, seasonal changes and timeless traditions of one of Britain’s most iconic stately homes. Built in a bygone era, Highclere Castle and its surrounding five-thousand-acre estate is a place where history breathes through its walls and verdant landscapes. From the grandeur of Victorian architecture to the whispers of Anglo-Saxon roots, every stone and tree has a story to tell throughout its sweeping grounds. Castle Hotel, Taunton Wednesday 29th October 6.30pm - 8pm Fiona Williams - House of Broken Bricks Every marriage has its seasons, Richard and Tess’s is in a deep winter. As day breaks over the Somerset Levels, Tess watches the chamomile clouds part. This morning, two sunrises graze the frosted floodplains: one rises low over a stretch of willows, while the other shines brightly from beneath the water. The light paints the house a startling crimson: a painful beauty that Tess, Richard and their son Max - riddled with grief - find easy to ignore. But none of them can ignore Sonny, who desperately wants things to go back to the way they were before. As the seasons change, and the cracks in the bricks let in more light, might this broken family find a way to start to heal? Brendon Books, Taunton Thursday 30th October 7pm - 8.30pm Saul David - Tunisgrad : Victory in Africa From the Sunday Times bestselling author of Sky Warriors and SBS comes an epic history about the North African campaign during the Second World War. On 8 November 1942, British and American troops invaded French North Africa as part of Operation Torch, the largest amphibious operation of the war to date. The Germans responded by flooding troops into Tunisia and the stage was set for one of the most decisive clashes of the war. Brendon Books, Taunton Tuesday 4th November 6.30pm - 8pm Michael Benton - Extinctions : How Life Survives, Adapts and Evolves Palaeontology shows us that many billions of species that once existed are now extinct, and their natural extinctions enabled new species to inherit the Earth. We identify mass extinctions during which 50–95% of species were killed off, and yet life always recovered. In fact, some of the great diversifications in the history of life were triggered by the opportunities afforded by mass extinctions. So, extinction in the context of modern life, especially the needless slaughter of species by human action or carelessness, is inexcusable. Who does not mourn the loss of the Polynesian tree snail or the dodo? Palaeontologists of course work on longer time scales and can see how extinction events have released the potential of new groups to show their evolutionary mettle. This is one of the wonders of exploring the geological record but should not allow us to think we can hasten the extinction of any modern species. Brendon Books, Taunton Thursday 6th November 7pm - 8.30pm Andrew Ziminski - Church Going : A Stonemason’s Guide to the Churches of the British Isles Churches are many things to us - they are places of worship, vibrant community hubs and oases of calm reflection. To know a church is to hold a key to the past that unlocks an understanding of our shared history. Andrew Ziminski has spent decades as a stonemason and church conservator, acting as an informal guide to curious visitors. Church Going is his handbook to the medieval churches of the British Isles, in which he reveals their fascinating histories, features and furnishings, from flying buttresses to rood screens, lichgates to chancels. Beautifully written and richly illustrated, it is a celebration of British architectural history. Taunton Library, Taunton Friday 7th November 2.30pm - 4pm Christian Wolmar - Fire and Steam : How the Railways Transformed Britain A new and updated edition of the classic history of the British railway, published to coincide with the 200th anniversary of train travel in 2025. The opening of the pioneering Stockton and Darlington railway, the world's first passenger line, in 1825 marked the beginning of the railways' vital role in changing the face of Britain. Fire and Steam celebrates the vision and determination of the ambitious Victorian pioneers who developed this revolutionary transport system and the navvies who cut through the land to enable a country-wide network to emerge. Brendon Books, Taunton Friday 7th November 7pm - 8.30pm Richard Whitehead-Victory in Australia:The Remarkable Story of England's Greatest Ashes Triumph Winning the Ashes in England is one thing, winning them in Australia, quite another. England's triumph in the 1954-55 Ashes series marks a watershed moment in the history of English cricket. Under the leadership of Len Hutton, the country's first professional captain, one of the greatest group of players ever to represent England won an Ashes series in Australia for the first time in more than 20 years. It is a feat that has been repeated only four times in more than 70 years since. Hutton's men had to overcome the additional obstacle of being thrashed in the first Test - only one other England team has recovered from such a monumental setback to win a series in Australia. Brendon Books, Taunton Saturday 8th November 7pm - 8.30pm Susannah Fisher - Sink or Swim : How the world needs to adapt to a changing climate The world needs to adapt to climate change – but how? What are the key problems and hard choices that lie ahead for the global community? This book reveals all. Heatwaves, wildfires, hurricanes and flooding caused by climate change are already impacting people and nature. Adaptation until now has been incremental with governments and institutions tinkering around the edges of current systems. Brendon Books, Taunton Wednesday 12th November 6.30pm - 8pm Elizabeth Delo - Writing Workshop: Show Don’t Tell “Don’t tell me the moon is shining; show me the glint of light on broken glass.” This famous quote by Anton Chekhov is often used in creative writing teaching to demonstrate the use of descriptive language to convey meaning, rather than directly stating it. ‘Show, Don’t Tell’ is one of the first rules of writing. In this workshop we will practise ways to apply it to your prose, so that your reader becomes immersed in your story, and not only believes it, but feels it. This workshop is suitable for beginner writers. Brendon Books, Taunton Thursday13th November 7pm - 8.30pm Brian Clegg - The Multiverse : When One Universe Isn't Enough The universe was supposed to be all there was - the whole of existence. For centuries the size of the universe and whether or not it is finite, fascinated scientists and philosophers. Brendon Books, Taunton Friday 14th November 7pm - 8.30pm The Fire River Poets - Slava Ukraini! Fire River Poets present an evening that bears witness to the richness, heritage and vitality of Ukrainian Poetry. Since the Russian invasion of February 2022 there has been a renaissance of poetry in Ukraine. A population under daily bombardment has turned to creative expression, especially the craft of the spoken word, to process their suffering, to stiffen the courage of resistance and to gain solace from shared humanity in a world turned upside down. Brendon Books, Taunton Wednesday 19th November 6.30pm - 8pm Nigel Phillips - The Nature of the Quantocks, A Landscape of Heath, Mire & Wooded Combes Nigel Phillips is here to talk about the nature of the Quantocks, an intimate mixture of hilltop heathland, oak woodland set in deep combes, and many fast-flowing streams, combine to create the Quantock Hills National Landscape. This detailed and informative book covers the well-known flowering plants and ferns, birdlife and mammals of these magnificent hills. It also explores lesser-known wildlife, with chapters on mosses and liverworts, fungi and lichens, and invertebrates. Brendon Books, Taunton Thursday 20th November 7pm - 8pm Mr Lyward’s Answer - Michael Burn: From Square Pegs to well-rounded adolescents Described at the time as “one of the most important educational experiments of the century,” Finchden Manor was a therapeutic community from 1939 to 1974 where visionary George Lyward OBE healed troubled adolescents. Please join us at Brendon Books for the relaunch of Michael Burn’s timeless true story, “Mr. Lyward’s Answer”, first published by Hamish Hamilton in 1956. Brendon Books, Taunton Friday 21st November 7pm - 8.30pm Graham Fawcett - Auden in Europe On my twentieth birthday in 1966, a friend in Cambridge gave me W H Auden’s new collection, About The House , poems from the early years of Auden’s summers from 1958 to 1972 in Kirchstetten, a village not far from Vienna. This book of his would give me my first real sense of being personally involved by Auden as a poet. I found myself riding on what he saw and felt and thought, much of it as a direct result of his village experience, a small rural community near a legendary cultural centre in a country not his own, and where another language was spoken, and it felt like a blueprint for what I would do seven years later. Brendon Books, Taunton Wednesday 26th November 6.30pm - 8.30pm Lionel Ward - Somerset Odyssey: Elliot Todd Mystery 3 Following his earlier adventures in Rome, Elliot Todd finds himself in possession of an early edition of The Lyrical Ballads by Wordswoth and Coleridge, the seminal work of literature often identified as the origin of the Romantic Movement. He decides to donate the book to The Coleridge Society in Somerset by way of a walk along the Coleridge Way. It is a revelatory experience but things take an unexpected and menacing turn both for himself and his mother - who just happens to be in the area researching her dissertation in religious cults as a mature student. Brendon Books, Taunton Thursday 27th November 7pm - 9pm **An Evening of Music with Amy Jeffs, Gwen Burns & Natalie Brice Amy and Natalie will perform some ballads based on Amy and Gwen’s book Old Songs: Stories of Love and Death from Traditional Ballads. Old Songs fuses short stories, histories, lyrics and illustrations in an enthralling reimagining of traditional folk ballads. Sunday Times Bestselling historian Amy Jeffs and Illustrator Gwen Burns combine forces to create a rich compendium, singing of travel, mystery, magic and the essential urges of humanity. Featuring iterations of fairy tales and sinister descendants of Greek myths and bible stories, as well as a cast of lesser-known characters with names like Tam Lim, Child Wynd and Maisery, Old Songs threads a tapestry of Britain’s landscape, history and cultures. Tacchi Morris Arts Centre, School Road, Monkton Heathfield, Taunton Saturday 29th November 7pm - 8.30pm

title: Caving with Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Mendip Activity Centre offer real Caving adventures right under Somerset’s Mendip Hills. It’s the perfect place to try something totally different. Explore underground tunnels, climb through hidden chambers, and experience the thrill of adventure beneath your feet.
bodyContent: Mendip Activity Centre offer real Caving adventures right under Somerset’s Mendip Hills. It’s the perfect place to try something totally different. Explore underground tunnels, climb through hidden chambers, and experience the thrill of adventure beneath your feet. Choose from Sandford Levy (great for beginners), Goatchurch Cavern (more adventurous) or Swildon’s Hole (previous experience recommended). Sessions are led by qualified instructors who’ll guide you safely at your pace. Discover the underground world of Somerset!

title: Devonshire House
subtitle: Established in a building dating back to 1880 and once used as a Victorian Grocers shop.
bodyContent: ⭐ Book Direct for Reward Card Offers Established in a building dating back to 1880 and once used as a Victorian Grocers shop, Devonshire House has been fully renovated into the stylish Bed and Breakfast it is today. Within a twenty minute walk of the city, on a major bus route into the city and with plenty of free on street parking, Devonshire House offers a convenient base to explore the city and surrounds. Local owners Chris and Louise are on hand to give as much or as little advice as you want, to make your stay even more enjoyable. Each room is individually decorated, en suite, with tv and dvd player, beverage tray, fluffy white towels and plump feather duvets (do tell us before your stay if you need hypo allergenic). Two doubles, a twin and a triple bedded room, plus a holiday cottage which sleeps up to four are available. A lounge is for guest use, with squashy sofas, up to date magazines and the local paper, imbibe in a Harveys Bristol Cream sherry with our compliments and relax after your day or plan the next one with all the information and leaflets to hand. The choice to book a room only rate or breakfast included, is yours, breakfast is served in the light and airy breakfast room between 8 am and 9 am. A buffet is laid out, with juice, yoghurt, fresh fruit, cereals and a selection of breads and jams for you to help yourself and then either a traditional Full English breakfast or smoked salmon and scrambled eggs can be pre chosen, along with freshly brewed coffee or a pot of tea from the selection available.
tagline: Established in a building dating back to 1880 and once used as a Victorian Grocers shop.

bodyContent: Horseshoe is the largest of our three beautiful luxury self catering holiday cottages set in stunning Somerset countryside just 15 minutes drive from Bath. The views are wonderful and there is a large private garden, perfect for family parties or BBQs. This converted stable building has two large ensuite bedrooms, sleeping up to 6 and is renovated to a very high standard, complete with all modern conveniences including free WIFI . The cottage is all on one level and suitable for wheelchair users. With easy access to the Bath Park & Ride, we are also perfectly located for exploring the many tourist attractions including local pubs and Lavender Farm, Cheddar Gorge, Wookey Hole Caves, Wells, Stourhead House & Gardens and the nearby Longleat Safari Park.

title: Willow Farm Gourmet
subtitle: Open all year round from 9.30am to 2.30pm Thursday to Saturday (visit by appointment only), come and see our farm in action.
bodyContent: Come and Experience Willow Farm Open all year round from 9.30am to 2.30pm Thursday to Saturday (visit by appointment only), come and see our farm in action. If you are lucky, you may even get a chance to meet Bertie our award-winning pedigree Oxford Sandy and Black boar. We are a working farm, so our availability will depend on our core farm duties. To ensure you get the best from your visit, please make sure that you book 4 to 6 weeks in advance due to the popularity of these visits and our courses. Email: info@willowfarmgourmet.co.uk to enquire. Courses We are so proud of all of our hard work and we love to share what we do. Want to learn how we make our amazing local produce? We offer two fun courses: Tiny Welly Boot Cider-Making Cider making at its best! Come and see how proper Somerset cider is made. Learn about the intimate small batch craft cider making process including what happens to all of the waste products from the process. Arrive onsite at 9.30am and see the process from fruit to final bottled goods. Learn how we add modern twists to a Somerset favourite such as elderflower or white chocolate flavours. Also includes an opportunity to try some of our lovely ciders over lunch on the farm...what could be better! Available Thursdays and Saturdays from March to December. 9.30am to 1.30pm. £25.00 per person or £15.00 per person for farm tour, tasting and lunch only. Gift vouchers available and valid for up to 12 months. We also welcome block bookings for special occasions such as birthdays or hen parties and can accommodate up to 24 people for such events. Willow Farm Sausage-Making Want to see the secrets to our beloved Willow Farm sausages and faggots? Come and give them a go yourself. Have a laugh making our 100% pure meat bangers...none of that 'fluff' in these local sausages. Arrive onsite at 9.30am and immediately start having fun. We couldn't let you leave without trying some of your hard work so sample some of your own made sausage as part of this day out. Available weekdays from March through to December. 9.30am to 1.30pm. £45 per person including farm tour, cider tasting and lunch. Gift vouchers available and valid for up to 12 months. Stay with us Beautiful surroundings with good links to popular cities make Willow Farm a popular stop for many. We are a Caravan Club registered certified location and we also accept Britstops. Situated just off the A39, the farm has easy access to the cities of Bath , Bristol and Wells along with links to the Bristol Channel resorts of Weston-Super-Mare , Clevedon and Burnham on Sea. The site is located in a flat field with good access and sheltered by a mature hedge. Our 30-acre farm has a 1-acre paddock for Caravan Club pitches. The well-known Hunters Rest pub is further along Flatts Lane, with shops, a takeaway and another pub within 1 mile in the next village. Open all year. Arrivals: 11.00am to 6.00pm weekdays and 11.00am to 5.00pm weekends. Latest Departure: 10.00am. Facilities: 4 hard-standing and 2 grass pitches, electric hookup, fresh water and waste disposal. £10 per night per pitch, plus £5 per night for electricity. Booking in advance required. Book through the Caravan Club website: www.caravanclub.co.uk/certificated-locations/england/bath--north-east-somerset/bath/willow-farm-1 Britstops are also welcome via email: info@willowfarmgourmet.co.uk

title: Clifton Suspension Bridge Trust
subtitle: Clifton Suspension Bridge Visitor Centre tells the story of the 'ornament of Bristol' and the people who built, maintain and treasure it. Explore the turbulent history of the ‘first love’ of famous British engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel through an award winning exhibition packed with family activities and staffed by knowledgeable volunteers.
bodyContent: Visitor Centre Clifton Suspension Bridge Visitor Centre tells the story of the 'ornament of Bristol' and the people who built, maintain and treasure it. Explore the turbulent history of the ‘first love’ of famous British engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel through an award winning exhibition packed with family activities and staffed by knowledgeable volunteers. The Visitor Centre is open between Friday and Monday throughout the winter and may be found in Leigh Woods on the North Somerset side of the bridge, a short walk from Clifton Village where you’ll find bus stops, pay and display parking, boutique shopping, cafes and coffee shops. Under the current Covid-19 guidance, pre-booking of tickets is strongly recommended. ( www.cliftonbridge.org.uk/visitor-centre ) Bridge Once the far-fetched dream of local wine merchant William Vick, the bridge was the first solo project of the famous British engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel who came up with ambitious plans to build the highest and longest bridge in the world. Sadly, Brunel did not live to see his ‘first love’ completed. The bridge took 33 years to build and opened as a monument to his achievements after his death. The Bridge is open 24 hours a day 7 days a week, 365 days a year and can be crossed on foot or by bicycle free of charge, although vehicles must pay a £1 toll towards the maintenance and upkeep of this Grade I listed structure. Groups may book private tours at any time, with a coach drop-off point available on Observatory Road, BS8 4AW (there is a weight limit of 4 tons so coaches may not cross the bridge). A programme of events runs throughout the year for families and adult learners. The bridge spans the spectacular Avon Gorge and is illuminated each evening, lighting up half an hour before sunset. Photographers may like to visit the viewpoints on Sion Hill or at the Cumberland Basin.
tagline: The Bridge is open 24 hours a day 7 days a week, 365 days.

title: The Jane Austen Centre
subtitle: The Jane Austen Centre is in the heart of the Georgian city of Bath, between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths. Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The Jane Austen Centre is in the Georgian city of Bath , Somerset , between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths . Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family. Here you will find out more about Jane Austen, her time in Bath and how the city shaped her work. You can also dress up in Regency costume, taste Regency-recipe biscuits, sample perfumes from the era, try your hand at writing with a quill and ink, have your photo taken with their world famous waxwork, try their delightful ‘Tea With Mr Darcy’ in the Regency Tea Room, and browse their bespoke Giftshop.

title: Garden Apartment
subtitle: The Garden Apartment is a luxury 2 bedroom Georgian Grade II apartment in the heart of Bath.
bodyContent: This apartment has recently been refurbished to a very high standard and offers spacious accommodation arranged over 2 floors covering a very spacious 90m2 each. The Garden Apartment is an absolute gem providing luxury accommodation within a Grade II listed Georgian Terrace in the heart of Bath. Have a peaceful and relaxing stay right in the centre of Bath and enjoy all that the city has to offer within easy walking distance. With close proximity to the train station, shops, restaurants, cafes and local attractions this is the perfect place to stay and make your base. The accommodation is in a Grade II Listed Georgian building situated on a very quiet street less than a 3 minutes walk from Bath Spa station and Bath city centre shops, restaurants and cafes. The property also has access to a garage. The apartment has just been refurbished to a very high standard and offers spacious accommodation for up to 4 guests arranged over 2 floors covering a very spacious 90m2. The property offers two generous sized bedrooms, both have Kingsize beds with Vi Spring mattresses. Crisp white linen and fluffy towels are provided. Both bedrooms have a luxury but minimalist feel and are finished with linen roman blinds. There is also a private garden with seating to enjoy the early and evening sun and wonderful views out across the city. The lounge has period features and is equipped with a large HDTV and makes a great space for relaxing. The connecting kitchen/dining area has gorgeous views over the garden, Bath city centre and surrounding hills. The kitchen is a fully equipped with modern oven, induction hob, dishwasher, fridge-freezer, extractor fan, toaster and kettle. A waste and recycling bins are provided. The modern bathroom is fitted with a bath and over shower and has under floor heating. There are efficient radiators in all rooms so the apartment is always warm and cozy. There is an additional cloakroom and WC. An iron and ironing board, and travel cot are provided. The Garden Apartment really is the perfect place to come to for your self catering break in Bath. title: Marston Park
subtitle: Offering an exhilarating Pandora’s box of unique cultural experiences in jaw-droppingly picturesque surroundings, Marston Park has a lively programme of creative workshops, wellbeing sessions and musical performances, as well as a late night lakeside bar and food truck serving delicious hyper seasonal food.
bodyContent: Marston Park is located near charming, historic Frome, and is just 40 minutes from Somerset’s popular gems, Bath and Glastonbury, and two hours from London. Its selection of beautiful canvas studios line one side of the lake and come furnished with a desk, guitar, easel and artists’ materials. Across the water wood-fired eats and al fresco banquets are available to all. The lakeside bar is open every day until 11pm. Food trucks serve a rotating menu with a melting pot of local flavours and globally-influenced cooking, from Latin, Greek and Northern-Thai street food to a wood-loaded pizza oven, spinning rustic sourdough pizzas. The Futuro House at Marston Park is the first of many on-site collaborations with artists, architects, designers and ingenious folk from the world over. Marston Park aims to bring together like-minded people to share ideas and good times in a beautiful and peaceful environment. Marston Park has a year round holistic programme of workshops and classes plus exciting event collaborations such as its Ibiza-themed luxury weekends , curated by the world-famous rock ’n’ roll hotel, Pikes Ibiza and plenty of seasonal fun including All Hallow’s Eve and Guy Fawkes Night.

title: The Curzon Cinema Clevedon
subtitle: The Curzon cinema has been at the centre of life in Clevedon, North Somerset, since 1912.
bodyContent: The Curzon cinema has been at the centre of life in Clevedon, North Somerset, since 1912. One of the country’s oldest, continuously running cinemas: screening everything from blockbusters to classics and arthouse cinema, hosting live comedy and events in a beautiful heritage venue. Opening its doors in 1912, only 5 days after the Titanic disaster, the Curzon is one of the country’s oldest, continuously running cinemas. Enlarged in the 1920s, the neo-classical building houses a 320-seater auditorium, panelled in a rare example of pressed tin; a bar; a 1930s Christie pipe organ and a unique collection of cinema equipment. Alongside our varied film programme, we host live comedy, music and performance and are fully engaged with youth, arts and other community organisations, also running Front Room Cinema which takes the cinema experience out to residential homes. We are supported by a fantastic team of volunteers, who support our Front of House staff, help in the bar, give guided tours and help to maintain our lovely building. Click here you’re interested in finding out about volunteering at the Curzon.
tagline: The Curzon cinema has been at the centre of life in Clevedon, North Somerset, since 1912.

title: Ferne Animal Sanctuary
subtitle: Ferne Animal Sanctuary is set within 72 acres of beautiful & protected countryside in the Blackdown Hills on the Devon/Somerset border. This charitable sanctuary takes in unwanted, abandoned and neglected animals and gives them a fantastic life either at the sanctuary or by finding them a special forever home.
bodyContent: Ferne Animal Sanctuary is set within 72 acres of beautiful & protected countryside in the Blackdown Hills on the Devon/Somerset border. This charitable sanctuary takes in unwanted, abandoned and neglected animals and gives them a fantastic life either at the sanctuary or by finding them a special forever home. Ferne Animal Sanctuary, located near Chard in Somerset, is a remarkable facility dedicated to the rehoming of dogs, cats, and horses. In addition to this, the sanctuary provides ongoing care and welfare for a wide variety of animals, including sheep, goats, cattle, pigs, geese, chickens, and an aviary housing birds from around the world. It is also home to smaller animals such as rabbits, guinea pigs, chinchillas and ferrets, ensuring they all receive the care and attention they need. Founded in 1939, at the onset of World War II, the charity was established to care for pets whose owners were going to war, or who had been displaced by the conflict. Over the years, it has forged strong connections with HM Armed Forces and the Royal Family. A typical visit to Ferne lasts between 90 to 150 minutes, during which visitors can enjoy observing the animals in their natural habitats. The experience includes a sensory garden designed to calm the senses with a variety of sounds, sights and smells. Visitors can explore the Willow Walk, which offers insights into animal care, as well as informative displays about our water voles, dragonflies, birds, and fungi. There's also a machinery wall showcasing equipment used throughout the years, along with a small play area for our younger visitors. Take the time to enjoy the stunning natural landscape of the Blackdown Hills from our viewing platform. Relax, gaze across the hills, and marvel at the beauty of nature at its finest. During the school holidays, Creative Corner offers a range of animal-themed activities and arts and crafts. We also host special events and workshops throughout the year, with full details available on our website. The Visitor Centre is open from 10 AM to 4 PM from Easter to October half term, though the shop and sanctuary are open every day, except Christmas Day, Boxing Day, and New Year's Day. Our well-stocked pet supplies and gift shop has everything you need for your animals, as well as delightful treats to tempt you. Dog friendly (dogs must be kept on leads) and accessible, Ferne has a good network of tarmac paths. However, due to the number of gates, we recommend that wheelchair users are accompanied. We have designated parking spaces for wheelchair users and visitors with special needs next to our Visitor Centre as well as in the main car park. All money raised goes to support our animal care and welfare. Unleash the Party Fun at Ferne Animal Sanctuary! tagline: Ferne Animal Sanctuary is set within 72 acres of beautiful & protected countryside.

If you need any further information Harry, Douglas and the team are always there to assist. All you have to do is ask. Hill House is a four storey Georgian Town House, built in 1762, which, being situated in the heart of historic Bath between the 3 Crescents – The Royal Crescent, Lansdown Crescent and Camden Crescent- is a great base to Experience all that Bath has to offer. Refurbished in 2011 its six individually decorated en suite rooms retain much of their original charm and character with all the amenities expected by a traveller in the 21st century including original artwork throughout.

title: Coleridge Cottage, National Trust
subtitle: Historic home of the poet Samuel Taylor Coleridge in Somerset near Bridgwater As in the poets’ day, there is still wilderness, heathland and a rocky shoreline where you can lose yourself in thought. The mix of heath on the top is a characteristic of the Quantocks and includes heather, whortleberry, gorse, bracken and wavy-haired grass. There is woodland too, once prized as a source of timber for ship building and now by walkers for its tranquillity. The oaks here are Sessile with acorns that gro
bodyContent: Nestled in the quaint village of Nether Stowey, Somerset, Coleridge Cottage is the historic home of the poet Samuel Taylor Coleridge. It was here that Coleridge composed some of his most celebrated works, including "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner," "Frost at Midnight," and "This Lime Tree Bower, My Prison." The cottage was a gathering place for literary greats, with frequent visits from William Wordsworth- it was here that the seeds of the Romantic movement were sown. Coleridge's time at the cottage was marked by both creative brilliance and personal turmoil. His family life gradually disintegrated, exacerbated by a growing addiction to laudanum. Despite these struggles, the three extraordinary years he spent in Nether Stowey produced poems that continue to inspire across generations. Acquired by the National Trust in 1909 and restored in 2011, Coleridge Cottage offers plenty to engage visitors of all ages. Indulge in the Tearoom’s delightful offerings, from cakes to cream teas. The Poet’s Lunch, featuring a Cheese Scone, Cheddar Cheese, Onion Marmalade, and a hot drink, is truly a feast for the senses! Wander through the wildflower garden and find the Lime-Tree Bower—a perfect spot for quiet reflection or listening to audio posts that bring Coleridge’s verses to life. Try your hand at “Quill Writing,” or step back in time with our fancy dress box and “Dress like a Georgian.” Young visitors will enjoy the indoor “Mouse Trail,” a fun adventure discovering hidden mice throughout the cottage. Coleridge Cottage also hosts exclusive events, including poetry readings, guided nature walks, themed talks, and workshops. Stay updated by visiting our website for details. Please note the cottage is unsuitable for wheelchairs due to small rooms and narrow corridors.
tagline: Historic home of the poet Samuel Taylor Coleridge in Somerset near Bridgwater

title: Weston Museum
subtitle: There is something for everyone here at Weston Museum. We want to open the museum to as many people as possible, so we’re constantly putting on events for all ages and interests. Head to the museum website to find out what is coming up soon.
bodyContent: “Once you know your history you understand more of who you are, you learn from the past and find ways to predict the future and even help create a better one.” Housed in a beautiful and distinctive historic building. We tell the story of the town and the surrounding area from prehistoric times to the present day. The museum is dedicated to being a social and educational hub for the people of Weston and its visitors. You can come to learn, relax or just have fun! The North Somerset Council museum collection contains around 50,000 individual objects. The newly refurbished museum also allows our guests to grab lunch at the cosy Clara’s Café, hire a space for a meeting or even a party in the courtyard. Museum’s do not have to be dull and dusty, in fact, Weston Museum encourages a hands-on approach to history. We also work closely with local schools and community groups to help support the Weston of today and grow the Weston of tomorrow. Our diverse volunteering programme also gives you the chance to get involved. Diversity is key! Our William Mable Gallery allows us, for the first time, to host exhibitions suitable for the world stage. We’ve already been able to display items from the Imperial War Museum and The British Museum. The content of this gallery changes throughout the year, so there is always something new at Weston Museum. Weston Museum is working towards being as accessible as possible. There is a lift for wheelchair users and those who cannot manage stairs to access the main upper floor galleries. Due to the nature of Clara’s Cottage being built in 1865, this part of the museum is unfortunately not completely accessible to wheelchair users due to narrow corridors and a staircase. Weston Museum’s free admission means that the museum is truly for everyone and is quickly becoming a popular destination among tourists as one of Weston's top attractions. Facilities Wheelchair Friendly, Café, Gift Shop, Baby Change Facilities, Accessible Lift, Parking Nearby, Disabled Toilet Available, Toilets Available
tagline: There is something for everyone here at Weston Museum.

title: Haymaker Inn
subtitle: Carrie and Jason and their boys took over the Haymaker in August 2016 and it is now a free house specialising in homemade “pub” food, and plenty of it.
bodyContent: We serve traditional food and all our desserts are homemade, why not try one of our chef’s cheesecakes while you are with us, a crumble and custard or maybe bread and butter pudding? While staying at the Haymaker you can enjoy the traditional charm of Somerset life, you may hear the sound of skittle balls rolling down the alley attached to the pub, or enjoy the story of our resident Ghost “Busty Victoria”. Savour a pint of Otter ale with your meal or take a stroll around our countryside. The pub is set in the tiny village of Wadeford on the edge of the beautiful Blackdown Hills in Somerset. It is close to Chard and the A303 trunk road that runs from Basingstoke in Hampshire to Honiton in Devon. The Blackdown Hills have been designated an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, reaching 1035 above sea level at the highest point. You can explore this area whilst using the Haymaker Inn as your base. Overlooking the wooded valley of the River Isle, the Inn has undergone extensive refurbishment recently and the five letting bedrooms are now proving very popular with both holiday makers and businessmen looking for somewhere peaceful to stay. There are a huge number of attractions in the area, including Chard museum, Chard reservoir nature reserve, Perry’s traditional cider, Forde Abbey, a former monastic house with one of the top gardens in England. Forde abbey is a privately owned farmer cistern monastery in Dorset, less than 7 miles away from us, the house and gardens are run as a tourist attraction while the 1,600 estate is farmed.
tagline: Carrie and Jason and their boys took over the Haymaker in August 2016

bodyContent: Our bright and airy restaurants are great venues for every occasion. Our chefs have assembled the perfect combination of classics and modern signatures, providing the most tempting array of choices. We offer a great selection of pizza and pasta, grills and seasonal specials. All produced by using simple ingredients and serving up deliciously fresh food, every time. Grab a light bite and cocktails with colleagues, have lunch with your little ones, or celebrate a special event. With our attention to detail, warm hospitality and high quality, good value food we will guarantee you will always have a great time.

title: ⭐The Grand Pier - Weston Super Mare
subtitle: The Grand Pier is open every day, except Christmas Day, so come hail, rain or shine, you’ll always get a warm welcome. Whatever the weather is doing outside, it’s still fun, fun, fun on the inside.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The Grand Pier, Weston super Mare, Somerset is the ideal destination for non-stop indoor family theme park fun. This North Somerset pier, with its state-of-the-art Pavilion is a truly iconic destination for family days out, events, concerts, weddings, and corporate events. With rides, attractions and the latest arcade games a visit to the Pier is the perfect treat for kids of all ages. On weekends, bank holidays and North Somerset school holidays, Unlimited Ride Wristbands are available for both adults and children, explore here . Don't miss out on this fantastic deal for your fun-filled day! Come and discover everything the Grand Pier, Somerset has to offer, including: · The very latest amusements - including giant screen Space Invaders · Thrilling rides including: Sidewinder, Freefall and Robocoaster · An amazing two level 300 meter indoor Go-Kart track · Seaside favourites, including: dodgems, house of horrors and helter skelter · A three-level, dinosaur themed soft play area with dedicated adult seating · A choice of places to eat and drink - we even serve your favourite Costa coffee! With hundreds of amusements and games to play, a range of thrilling rides, and a choice of attractions for all ages everyone gets to have fun in the amazing Pavilion - it really is one big house of fun!!! When you’re ready for a bite to eat you’re spoilt for choice from traditional fish and chips to afternoon tea, and of course ice cream too! There’s even a pub for you to enjoy a relaxing drink as you take in the spectacular views. As a unique location our function rooms are always in demand, and we love creating the perfect setting for weddings and family celebrations. For businesses our dedicated events team is on hand for corporate events, ranging from team meetings and training sessions to large scale conferences.The fun continues into the night with a wide range of events from concerts to whodunnits. To make sure you don’t miss out visit and book your tickets online today.
tagline: The Grand Pier, is the ideal destination for non-stop indoor family theme park fun.

title: Cranleigh
subtitle: Dating from 1897 Cranleigh was once a Victorian family home. Cranleigh can offer you a step back into Victorian style but with all the comforts of modern living.
bodyContent: Dating from 1897 Cranleigh was once a Victorian family home. Cranleigh can offer you a step back into Victorian style but with all the comforts of modern living. With 10 individually furnished en-suite rooms with many period features offering every comfort for your stay. Cranleigh is ideally located in a quiet residential area – away from the noise but just over 1.5 miles from the centre of Bath. With FREE PARKING and easy access to the city. Breakfast At Cranleigh breakfast is served in the comfort of your own room. You can choose delivery between 7:45 am to 9:30 am each morning. Since introduction, earlier this year customers have raved about our in-room breakfast hamper. Our ‘In Room’ hamper is a continental style breakfast including a selection of toasted bread, preserves, fresh fruit, juice, yoghurts, selection of Kellogg’s cereals, creamy porridge and choice of tea or coffee. When choosing to enjoy your breakfast in your room this will be delivered in a hamper to your room. Honesty Bar & Coffee Station We have a range of reasonably priced beers, wines, soft drinks, cakes and snacks available for you to purchase to enjoy in your room. You can also help yourself to complimentary freshly ground coffee.
tagline: Dating from 1897 Cranleigh was once a Victorian family home.

title: Bloomfield House
subtitle: Bloomfield House, a Georgian detached Grade II listed building, has elegant and romantic rooms (four posters or half testers) fine art, antiques, splendid views all combined with environmental credentials and a friendly relaxed atmosphere.
bodyContent: The House Bloomfield House, a Georgian detached Grade II listed building, has elegant and romantic rooms (four posters or half testers) fine art, antiques, splendid views all combined with environmental credentials and a friendly relaxed atmosphere. The house is set well back from a quiet road. Well behaved children and pets are welcome. The Breakfast Our traditional full English breakfasts are freshly cooked to order and served from 7.30 am until 11 am. Ingredients are mostly organic, fair-traded and provided by local suppliers, including homemade preserves and artisan breads. Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options are always available. The Parking We have free off-street parking and an electric car charging point for our guests use. There is easy access to the city centre via a regular bus service which stops within a few feet of the entrance to our property. The walk into town is a downhill stroll of 20 mins, on the way back up – jump on the bus or grab a cab! . The Bedrooms All bedrooms have en-suite facilities and come with the usuals – TV, hospitality tray, toiletries, hair dryer. The guest bedrooms are situated on the second floor, we have no lift so are not suitable for those with mobility issues. We are, of course, happy to help you up the stairs with your luggage. On the upside this does mean each room has far reaching views. Please note, for those with allergies , that this is a family home and we have both cats and dogs on the premises. The cats do not have access to the guest bedrooms (nor do our dogs for that matter). DISCOUNTS Any mid-week stay (Sun-Thurs ) will attract a £10 discount. Please quote ‘Stay in Bath’ when booking (by phone) on 01225 420105. Any on-line booking – applicable discounts will be deducted upon check-out. (This sadly cannot be used in addition with other special offers.) We also offer discounts to those arriving in Bath by train or bus. Discounts do not apply to Bank Holidays or one night Saturday bookings which are, on occasions, available.
tagline: Bloomfield House, a Georgian detached Grade II listed building

title: Dunster Castle
subtitle: Fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years, remodelled 100 years ago. Fine 17thC staircase and plaster ceilings. Terrace garden of rare shrubs.
bodyContent: During the winter months, the castle, watermill, and grounds are open at weekends and closed during the week. The Watermill Tearoom, Stables Shop and Parkland are open daily from 10am until 4pm. The car park is also open daily from 10am until 5pm. From 5 April 2025, the whole site is open daily. A fortress that became a family home for the Luttrells, who lived at Dunster for 600 years, the castle was extensively remodelled in the 1870s to create a Victorian country house. The castle boasts breath-taking views over Exmoor, Somerset, and the Bristol Channel as well as holding fine interior features such as a fine 17 th century carved staircase, ornate plaster ceilings, and rare leather wall hangings. Discover how Dunster Castle was used in its heyday and how the family hosted grand occasions from society balls to polo matches with the brilliant ‘Chapters’ guide as well as ‘Castle Explorers, available for children. You can then enjoy a leisurely stroll through beautiful terraced gardens with a collection of palms, sub-tropical plants, and the Dunster Lemon tree. Sited on the River Avill, Dunster Castle is also home to a working watermill that sits within the river gardens. Visit the mill to see the waterwheels in action and even purchase some of the freshly-milled flour. Refreshments are available in the newly-refurbished Watermill Tearoom and also outside the castle in the Tenants’ Hall Café. Accessibility Overview here. Facilities in addition to those listed below: Baby changing facilities Children's trails Courtesy vehicle Stair Climber Trampers available to book

title: The shop at Dunster Castle
subtitle: Explore the atmospheric 17th-century stables and visit the shop for high quality, original gifts and local products. Our shop is brimming with beautiful things, so you are sure to find something to tempt you, whether it's a treat for yourself or a gorgeous gift for a friend.
bodyContent: Explore the atmospheric 17th-century stables and visit the shop for high quality, original gifts and local products. Our shop is brimming with beautiful things, so you are sure to find something to tempt you, whether it's a treat for yourself or a gorgeous gift for a friend. A working watermill Bake the perfect loaf with some organic Dunster Watermill flour. Ground on site there's been a mill here since Domesday. If that doesn’t take your fancy how about some Dunster Watermill porridge or even a bag of muesli, made to our secret recipe. Harry's Cider Made in the heart of Somerset this premium quality cider is made on Harry's farm with 100% cider fruit. Different varieties are pressed, fermented and matured for several months before being blended to give a distinctive and refreshing taste. Find out more by visiting their website here. Handy history guide Get the most from your visit to Dunster Castle and Gardens with our new souvenir guidebook. With beautiful colour photographs, reconstruction drawings, historical images and a tour of the castle, it is a great momento of your day.

title: The Apple Tree Inn
subtitle: The Apple Tree Inn is a large roadside pub dating back to 1674 which has retained many original features whilst adding a farm shop within the front bar area.
bodyContent: Most of the food offerings are locally sourced with meat being provided by the pubs owner from his own livestock. There is a back room with a dining area and a snug which is used by the locals. The Glastonbury festival site is close to the pub and opening hours are affected during the festival. Bus services pass the door Mon to Sat (not public holidays) every 2 hours on Shepton Mallet, Glastonbury & Street route. The last bus to Street is 16.25 and the last to Shepton Mallet is 18.10. HISTORY At least five medieval houses still survive in part, probably the earliest Old Farmhouse, East Street, which has true crucks similar to those in Bridge Farm, Baltonsborough, which date from the mid 14th century. (fn. 50) Significant alterations and additions were made to several houses in the later 16th and the earlier 17th centuries including upper floors in Higher Southtown Farm, remodelling at Pennard Farm (datestone 1640), and a new wing at Manor Farmhouse, Coxbridge. The Cottage, Higher Southtown, is a timber framed building of the early 17th century. At least four surviving houses date from the mid or late 17th century including Sticklinch Manor and the Apple Tree inn. (fn. 51) The house of a yeoman at Newtown in 1678 comprised porch, hall, parlour, two butteries, and kitchen on the ground floor and five chambers over including a cheese chamber. (fn. 52) There was significant rebuilding of farm houses in the early 19th century.
tagline: The Apple Tree Inn is a large roadside pub dating back to 1674
