title: The Hatch Inn
subtitle: We're a family run pub that have always had a passion for hospitality throughout our careers, as a family we've always dreamt of bringing a pub to life.
bodyContent: The Hatch Inn is that pub, we poured our hearts and souls into a refurbishment back in October 2015 and now with a pub full of rustic charm our dream has become reality. We now strive to serve quality food whilst creating an atmosphere that will have you coming back for more. That's enough about us... what about the pub... The Hatch Inn is an 18th century coaching Inn set in the picturesque Somerset countryside at Hatch Beauchamp just 10 minutes from Taunton. The M5 is just 5 minutes away providing easy links to Cornwall, Devon, Dorset and Beyond. Guests can enjoy a cosy and relaxed evening by real log fires in the lounge or enjoy a drink with our locals at the village bar and in the warmer months relax on our spacious patio. We have regular live entertainment, from folk music to acoustic...... Whether you just want to kick back and relax or be more adventurous there's always something to get up to. We are on a numbered British cycle route (33), there are stables locally for horse riding enthusiasts and plenty of walking trails too. Night life is only a cab ride away if dancing is what you need. We have lots of local ciders to sample and always welcome group bookings.
tagline: We're a family run pub that have always had a passion for hospitality

title: Zizzi
subtitle: Located on Magdalene Square, opposite St Mary's church you'll find Zizzi Taunton! Our restaurant is an old Tudor school house which still retains all of its original features with high vaulted ceilings and arched windows. It's an incredibly beautiful restaurant, which you'll definitely have to come & see for yourself! Taking on a modern rustic design, our Taunton restaurant features an open pizza oven, our signature Zizzi logs, comfy seating & an illustrated mural inspired by the local area.
bodyContent: Our Italian restaurant serves tasty, authentic dishes from pizza, pasta and risotto to salads and indulgent desserts – all in a uniquely designed restaurant. Our Italian menu also includes Vegan and Vegetarian options. We are open Monday – Sunday for lunch and dinner. Dine al fresco with an outdoor dining area for sunny weather at our Taunton restaurant. Plus tweet what you eat with free WiFi available here (if you're in to that).
tagline: Italian food in an incredibly beautiful restaurant..

title: Valley of Rocks
subtitle: Nothing prepares you for the Valley of Rocks. It’s like a giant prehistoric landscape, straight out of One Million Years BC (sorry, we can’t promise Raquel Welch)
bodyContent: Instead of dinosaurs, feral goats seem to egg each other on to take ever‐more crazy routes around the crags, caves and crevices, but by some miracle they manage to hang on. It looks glacial, but in fact during the Ice Age the ice sheet missed it, leaving it a waterless valley, long since silted up to become the U shape it is now. It really is an incredible sight, and well worth either a bracing walk from Lynton along the South West Coastal Path, or a shorter visit by parking at the site’s car park. This is a flat tarmacked route, so if you have someone in your party in a wheelchair or with mobility issues, this is a good outing to consider. The Walk 2 miles Directions: From Minehead take the A39 to Lynton and follow the signs through the town to the Valley of Rocks. At the Valley of Rocks itself, there are 60 spaces with two hours free parking. There are lots of parking options in Lynton and Lynmouth, so check online before you leave: https://www.visitlyntonandlynmouth.com/how‐to‐ get‐here Sat Nav: EX35 6HJ One option is to park in Lynmouth, get the funicular Cliff Railway up to Lynton and then walk the flat one mile from the end of North Walk, part of the South West coast path to the Valley of Rocks. It’s a stunning clifftop location with jaw‐dropping views. Alternatively, drive to the Valley of Rocks car park and wander around the area. If you choose to drive, you’ll find a flat tarmac road running through the Valley which makes it quite accessible. Once here, we strongly advise against climbing the rocks as it is extremely dangerous, and only the goats know how to hang on! Download walk leaflet here For more information on Exmoor walks and to view the full series for The Little Book of Walks, contact E Info@exmoorcharactercottages.co.uk W www.exmoorcharactercottages.co.uk T 07817 698366

title: Pulteney Guest House Bed and Breakfast
subtitle: Pulteney House Bed and Breakfast is a large, elegant Victorian house set in its own picturesque west facing gardens, with fine views of Bath Abbey only 10 minutes’ level walk from the centre of Bath.
bodyContent: Pulteney House Bed and Breakfast is a large, elegant Victorian house set in its own picturesque west facing gardens, with fine views of Bath Abbey only 10 minutes’ level walk from the centre of Bath. The Bed and Breakfast has 16 rooms with en-suite facilities, and 1 with private facilities that are opposite the room. We offer a range of room types including family rooms, single rooms, double and twin rooms. A limited number are ground floor rooms. Pulteney House has been privately owned since 1979 and we provide a warm homely welcome to all guests. The large mature gardens are always kept in beautiful condition and guests are encouraged to utilise them where children can play in absolute safety. A comfortable family TV lounge is available for guests to use and relax in away from their room. Private onsite car park with CCTV for added security and peace of mind. Free Wi-Fi in all rooms and public areas. Free use of computer for those guests with no personal device. A large and varied Breakfast menu is available and we cater for a range of specific dietary requirements.
tagline: Pulteney House Bed and Breakfast is a large, elegant Victorian house

title: The Jane Austen Centre
subtitle: The Jane Austen Centre is in the heart of the Georgian city of Bath, between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths. Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The Jane Austen Centre is in the Georgian city of Bath , Somerset , between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths . Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family. Here you will find out more about Jane Austen, her time in Bath and how the city shaped her work. You can also dress up in Regency costume, taste Regency-recipe biscuits, sample perfumes from the era, try your hand at writing with a quill and ink, have your photo taken with their world famous waxwork, try their delightful ‘Tea With Mr Darcy’ in the Regency Tea Room, and browse their bespoke Giftshop.
tagline: The Jane Austen Centre is in the heart of the Georgian city of Bath.

title: Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Mendip Activity Centre is the ultimate outdoor adventure playground in Somerset. They’ve been delivering adventurous outdoor activities for nearly 40 years, growing from humble beginnings to the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West!
bodyContent: It’s Time for Adventure with Mendip Activity Centre! Nestled in 250 acres of ancient woodland in the Mendip Hills National Landscape, Mendip Activity Centre is the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West. Just 20 minutes from Weston-super-Mare and Cheddar and open year-round, Mendip have been delivering Adventure, Learning and Training for individuals, families, schools, and groups since 1987. Activities available include: · Air Rifle · Tobogganing · Archery · Skiing · Snowboarding · Frisbee Golf · Kayaking · Nerf & Gel Battles · Caving · Paddle Boarding · Rock Climbing · Axe Throwing · ArcheryActive · Abseiling · Canoeing Come for the day or stay longer. In summer, pitch your tent at the award-winning Mendip Basecamp (link to https://mendipbasecamp.com/), a family adventure campsite awarded second at the Visit England Awards 2025. Pitch where you like, check out when it suits, camp fires encouraged, dogs welcome and endless adventure is on offer! Adventure for Everyone Mendip is more than just activities. It’s a place to switch off from screens, reconnect with nature, and each other. Whether you're learning something new, developing an existing skill or simply having fun outside, you’ll leave with muddy boots and big smiles. We believe in adventure for everyone. Many of our activities are adaptable for additional needs, and our friendly team will work with you to make it happen Refuel at the Alpine Lounge Overlooking the Ski Slope, the Alpine Lounge café serves pizzas, paninis, coffee and cake with stunning views- perfect for après-adventure refreshments

title: Chestnuts House
subtitle: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden and private off street parking.
bodyContent: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden and private off street parking. Set in the heart of the beautiful Georgian city of city. It is ideally situated off the main roads and adjacent to Henrietta park, but within a few minutes level stroll of the city centre with its many attractions, restaurants and excellent shopping centre. The House is built from natural Bath stone and has four beautifully decorated and furnished ensuite guest rooms, some with king size and wrought iron beds. Owners Toni and Dawn have created a splendid and delightful bed & breakfast with superb hospitality in a relaxing atmosphere, all the necessary ingredients for making your stay in Bath a truly memorable experience. Guests Chestnuts House has 5 individually themed ensuite rooms which can accommodate a total of 11 persons. Three Superior double bedded rooms, one family/twin room (max 3 persons) and one Classic double room Bedrooms The bedrooms have recently been refurbished to an exacting standard and have been tastefully decorated and beautifully furnished. All rooms have en suite bathrooms with bath and shower, hairdryers and large fluffy towels. The rooms have comfortable and relaxing beds with crisp cotton sheets, air con, remote flat screen colour television, radio, free wireless internet access and refreshment trays. Bathrooms All bedrooms are ensuite with large fluffy towels and White Company products. The superior & twin/family rooms are ensuite with bath & power shower. The Classic room is ensuite with walk in power shower. Kitchen Enjoy your inclusive breakfast in our light and airy dining room overlooking the garden. During the summer months breakfast can be served al fresco. Our breakfast includes both organic and local produce. As well as the traditional English breakfast, we offer smoked salmon with scrambled eggs and homemade blinis, poached buttered kippers (smoked haddock with poached eggs). There is also an extensive buffet table with fresh fruit salad, freshly baked pastries, cereals, yoghurts. We are happy to cater for special dietary requirements. Entertainment The Lounge has a large flat screen Television with both Sky & BT Sport Channels. Free internet wi-fi is available throughout Outside Chestnuts House is situated in a residential street with a small private walled garden for guests to enjoy and just 10 minutes walk to the centre. General Points Chestnuts House is situated in a residential street with private off street parking and just 10 minutes level walk to the city centre. Parking Chestnuts House has both private off street parking and parking permits available for Guests to use. This service is free of charge. Smoking Chestnuts is a non smoking establishment Children Family room can accommodate up to 3 guests. Children of all ages are welcome. Pets Unfortunately Chestnuts House does not accept pets
tagline: Chestnuts House is a fine Edwardian detached house with an enclosed garden

title: Horseshoe Cottage, Lime Kiln Farm

bodyContent: Horseshoe is the largest of our three beautiful luxury self catering holiday cottages set in stunning Somerset countryside just 15 minutes drive from Bath. The views are wonderful and there is a large private garden, perfect for family parties or BBQs. title: Old Parsonage House
subtitle: Old Parsonage House is ideally situated in the heart of the pretty village of Beckington, just a short drive from the historic city of Bath.
bodyContent: Old Parsonage House is ideally situated in the heart of the pretty village of Beckington, just a short drive from the historic city of Bath. Privately owned and run by Tim and Jo guests are greeted with a warm welcome to Old Parsonage House which has been completely renovated assuring your stay will be relaxing and comfortable. With plenty of free private parking and excellent places to eat within a short walking distance Old Parsonage House is well situated for your visit to Bath, Longleat and the surrounding area.

title: Farleigh Hungerford Castle
subtitle: In a beautiful valley of the river Frome, on the border between Wiltshire and Somerset and only nine miles from Bath, stands the remains of Farleigh Hungerford Castle.
bodyContent: In a beautiful valley of the river Frome , on the border between Wiltshire and Somerset and only nine miles from Bath , stands the remains of Farleigh Hungerford Castle. Started in the 14th century, it still has much for visitors to enjoy and provides a great day out for families with children, couples and even walkers enjoying the beautiful surrounding countryside. This fortified mansion was occupied for 300 years by the remarkable Hungerford family and today their intriguing, yet sometimes gruesome stories are told through graphic interpretation panels and a free audio tour. There are many hidden treasures - the chapel with rare medieval wall paintings and family tombs; extensive displays in the Priest’s house; and for those who are brave enough to enter the crypt, there’s the best collection of human-shaped lead coffins in Britain. Don't Miss: A glimpse of the rare medieval wall paintings in the chapel and the strange portrait coffins in the crypt Our free audio tour which tells the sinister stories of Farleigh's past residents The exhibition of objects found on-site in the Priest's House The collection of carved and painted tombs and wall paintings in the chapel
tagline: In a beautiful valley of the river Frome, on the border between Wiltshire and Somerset.

title: Mambo
subtitle: In the middle of Taunton, this unique and historic lounge and eatery suits all ages and tastes, with extensive outdoor cover and plenty of outdoor heating. We are fully COVID compliant, with state of the art Track and Trace systems, as well as new delicious menus, themed nights and exceptional service from our wonderful tea.
bodyContent: When in Taunton, why not try the most unique bar & eatery in town! A multi level, indoor and outdoor venue hosting super cosy chill out & VIP areas that can be pre booked for you and your social bubble of 6. Our focus is ensuring customers have the chance to meet in secure environment and still enjoy the pleasures of a day out for lunch, or a night out for drinks and since. Any permutation of numbers can be safely arranged, thanks to our moveable & retractable plastic screens. Our spaces are versatile and individual, and our menu has a choice of food for you and the whole family. We pride ourself on customer satisfaction, service, and our exceptional selection of premium spirits, non alcoholic drinks and coffees. Keen on trying out our menu? You’ve got plenty to look forward to, including our delicious tasty teaser dude food tapas, some juicy, home-pressed burgers and homemade, stone baked pizzas, unique to Mambo. Main courses include a variety of fabulous fish dishes, a few of our favourite steaks, and a whole lot more dude food for you to indulge in. There is a children's' menu available, as well as delightful desserts and milkshakes for everyone to enjoy. In addition, we offer some wonderful drinks and food packages, available to view on our party package menu on our website. Totally weather proof, our retractable roof and heaters can warm everyone up when it's chilly or cold outside, or if there are clear skies and stars, you can enjoy that too with our wide variety of outdoor space. Pre book now for our Autumn and Winter theme nights, and pre Christmas festivities! If you have a Birthday, Anniversary, Wedding or a special occasion, we can discuss packages to suit your individual needs. We call it " Mambo Love”. It's ALL about you!
tagline: In the middle of Taunton, this unique and historic lounge and eatery

title: The Princess Theatre and Arts Centre, Burnham on Sea
subtitle: The Princess Theatre and Arts Centre, is the main venue for arts and entertainment in Burnham on Sea and Highbridge welcoming more than 7000 audience members last year.
bodyContent: The Princess Theatre and Arts Centre, is the main venue for arts and entertainment in Burnham on Sea and Highbridge welcoming more than 7000 audience members last year. Our Mission is to enrich, educate and entertain our community by providing superior theatre and arts experiences. Our regular programme of events, shows and talks; produced by professional and community companies is ever expanding, attracting a diverse audience from across the county and beyond. Take a look at our What’s On . Our strong links across the community means the arts centre offers a great deal of activities to cater for all tastes including: crafts, visual arts, youth theatres and wellbeing groups. Take a look at our Activities Page. The Gallery space in the Cafe plays host to artists both professional and amateur alike and we are very proud of the work that is presented on our walls. 2021 will see our Theatre and studio space beautifully refurbished and with further capital development plans in the pipeline everyone at the Princess is excited.

title: Little Manor Stay and Walk
subtitle: A beautifully renovated Somerset farmhouse near the Mendip Hills, Bristol and Weston-Super-Mare offering luxury B&B and short guided walking breaks from June to October.
bodyContent: Little Manor is a beautiful Somerset farmhouse that’s been renovated to include three delightful, en-suite rooms for B&B guests, each with their own unique character. The Garden Room, the Japanese Room and the Arcadian Room each evoke a different vibe but are all finished to the highest standard of comfort and luxury with smart TVs, home-baked goods, hospitality trays, free WiFi, hair dryers and big fluffy towels. Breakfast is served as a buffet in the dining room and guests can relax in the sitting room with board games or television if they wish. There is free parking onsite. The house is set in a large garden with views to the south of the Mendip Hills. From here guests can explore the Georgian cities of Bristol and Bath, visit the famous Cheddar Gorge and caves, have a round of golf at the nearby Mendip Spring Golf Course, go horse riding, cycle the Strawberry Line, spend a day on the beach at Weston-Super-Mare or just relax in the garden. Walkers and bird watchers will love the Mendip Hills AONB and the internationally significant habitat of the Somerset Levels and Moors. Located in the hamlet of West Hewish, just over a mile from J21 of the M5, two miles from a main line railway station and seven miles from Bristol International Airport, Little Manor is very easy to get to and has easy access to Cardiff and Taunton for slightly longer jaunts. Of interest to walkers new to Somerset, I can offer guided walking breaks of two or three days taking in walks to suit various abilities in the beautiful Mendip and Quantock Hills. For further details of this please contact me.

title: The Ayrlington
subtitle: Built of golden Bath stone in 1874 by the architect J Elkinton Gill, the award-winning Ayrlington is a handsome listed Victorian house with exceptional views of the City and its medieval Abbey.
bodyContent: Built of golden Bath stone in 1874 by the architect J Elkinton Gill, the award-winning Ayrlington is a handsome listed Victorian house with exceptional views of the City and its medieval Abbey. Bath’s magnificent historic sites, speciality shops and excellent restaurants are all just a 5-10 minute level stroll away. The elegant and tranquil interior is a graceful blend of English and Asian antiques, artwork, fine fabrics and Egyptian cotton bedlinen – all 19 bedrooms have individual themes and are beautifully furnished, some with four-poster beds. We also offer a residents’ bar, secure private parking and is entirely non smoking. We do not accept children under 5 years of age. The Ayrlington was the proud recipient of a Silver-Gilt certificate at the 2014 Bath In Bloom awards.
tagline: Built of golden Bath stone in 1874 by the architect J Elkinton Gill

title: Old Stables: rural retreat, sleeps 6
subtitle: The Old Stables is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.
bodyContent: It is located in the beautiful Georgian village of Freshford which lies at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys in the southern Cotswolds. There are some wonderful walks to local pubs following the riverside and canals. All just 15 minutes from Bath by car but the secret of this location is the 9 minute train journey to Bath from the village station, just a short stroll from the cottages. A three bedroom cottage (two king and one twin-bed) with a fully equipped kitchen opening onto a dining room There is a separate living room with TV/DVD and two large leather couches . The living room has large patio doors that open up onto the courtyard area. The Old Stables can accommodate 6 people. This cottage has: Three bedrooms (two king size and one with twin beds) One family bathroom , a Living room with Freeview TV/DVD two large leather couches and a dining room with a table seating 6.The Kitchen is equipped with all the cookware you might need dishwasher along washing machine/dryer and Iron/Ironing board. Hairdryers , bed linen and towels are all provided in the bedrooms.We provide a “Welcome pack” of tea, coffee, sugar, milk, bread, butter, eggs and bacon. The cottage has Free WiFi. Neighbourhood overview: Freshford is a beautiful ancient village with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk from the cottage( The Inn at Freshford) that serves restaurant quality food and all the local beers and ciders.The village has an excellent fully stocked( from wine to organic humus!)community shop that also has a great cafe that serves lunch. There is also a local doctors surgery. The village is nestled at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys . The Kennet and Avon canal is a 15 minute walk from the cottage. Getting around: You don’t need a car to stay in the cottage. The village station is a few minutes walk away. Trains are hourly off peak and thrice hourly at peak times. Bath 9 mins, Bristol 22 mins. London Padington to Bath Spa 1.5 hours Bath Spa to Freshford 9 minutes Bath Spa to Freshford “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/bath-spa-to-freshford ” Freshford to Bath Spa “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/freshford-to-bath-spa ” There is also a local bus service to all the adjacent villages and Bath. The cottage has two parking spaces suitable for one medium and one small car or a single large SUV. Other things to note If you are a runner or keep fit enthusiast the owner is a qualified Personal Trainer (Bath Uni) with much Marathon and half marathon experience. She specialises in Ladies training. Please let us know if you would like guided running or some Personal Fitness training
tagline: The Old Stables is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.

title: Pulled Chicken Burger, and Hazy Ketchup
subtitle: "Thatchers Haze – rich but not too sweet – will easily carry strong aromatics and a little chilli heat. Its strength lies in its drinkability, its casual appley sweetness on the palate comes with a tang of freshness." - Tim Maddams
bodyContent: Serves 6 – 8 Ingredients: Fot the marinade: ½ bottle Thatchers Somerset Haze cider 1 dsrtsp smoked paprika 1 hot chilli, finely chopped 2 tbsp honey 1 tsp coriander seeds 1 tsp cumin seeds 1 tsp nigella seeds ½ star anise Fot the Chicken: 1 large free range organic chicken Salt Pepper 2 bulbs of garlic For the method and more information visit https://www.thatcherscider.co.uk/recipes/pulled-chicken-burger-and-hazy-ketchup/

title: Cheddar Gorge & Caves
subtitle: Cheddar Gorge & Caves boasts extraordinary subterranean show caves, awe-inspiring cliffs and holds many fascinating secrets about our prehistoric ancestors.
bodyContent: Our Day Ticket gives access to six great attractions: Gough’s Cave: Prepare to be amazed by our stunning show cave featuring spectacular stalagmite and stalactite formations created over 500,000 years ago! See cheddar cheese maturing in the caves, view the site where Cheddar Man’s 10,000-year-old skeleton was discovered and learn about the extraordinary DNA discovery. A free audio guide is available in six languages, and there is also a special version for children. Cox’s Cave featuring Yeo’s Journey: The Power of Water. This spectacular immersive multimedia experience tells the captivating story of how our iconic caves were formed and evolved through the ‘Power of Water’. The story is brought to life using state-of-the-art animation, sound, lighting and colour. Beyond the View: Take a seat in front of our state of the art 270-degree screen. Discover historic tales, enjoy breathtaking aerial panoramic views, and learn about the special wildlife and plants that call the gorge home. Museum of Pre-History: Discover amazing artefacts unearthed in the Cheddar area that help tell the story of how people lived thousands of years ago. Jacob’s Ladder & The Lookout Tower: Venture up the 274 steps to the top of the gorge with rest stops along the route to admire the view. Marvel at the panoramic views and mosaic of landscapes across the Mendips and Somerset Levels. Cliff­ -Top Walk: Hike the 3-mile loop around the gorge. Look out for the wildlife and enjoy the stunning scenery. If you don’t have time to do the full circuit, you can go for a shorter walk up to the Pulpit Rock look out point, and head back down the ladder. Gough’s Café Sit back, relax, and take in the beauty of the gorge at Gough’s Cafe, close to the entrance of Gough's Cave. Enjoy a thirst-quenching chilled drink, warm yourself up with a hot beverage or choose from a selection of alcoholic drinks. Serving light lunches, delicious snacks, cream teas and delicious cake, to include vegetarian and vegan options. Enjoy the spectacular views from the comfort of our air-conditioned cafe or relax on the large patio where dogs are welcome. We even have a welcome bowl of water for our doggy friends. Our small play area for under 2-year-olds will keep the little ones entertained too! Accessibility Cheddar Gorge & Caves provides accessible toilets, free parking for blue badge holders and free admission for carers accompanied by a full paying visitor. The audio tour of Gough's cave is printed in braille. Assistance Dogs are permitted, and the museum is wheelchair accessible with lift. Those with severely restricted mobility or who are wheelchair dependent will find areas of Cheddar Gorge & Caves inaccessible. If you have any questions prior to your visit, please email Guest Services on info@cheddargorge.co.uk or call 01934 742343. Dog-Friendly Dogs are welcome in all attractions and water bowls are provided in the cave entrances, shop and café patio. Family and Children Cheddar Gorge & Cave is family friendly. We have baby changing facilities, buggy parking and are breast-feeding friendly. Gough’s café has a small play area for under two year olds, water refills and highchairs are available. Entry is free for children under the age of 5 years. Groups Cheddar Gorge & Caves has special group rates, coach parking and drop off points for group tours. We offer discounted exclusive group sessions for Rocksport adventure activities – adventure caving, rock climbing and freefall. Special Events We have a fantastic programme of events throughout the year to keep the whole family entertained, including the school holidays. Visit our What’s On page for more details. Thirst for adventure or a puzzle-solving mind? Rocksport: Imagine climbing the gorge rockface in the shadow of the 450ft cliffs, caving deep underground or taking part in our exhilarating Blackcat freefall in Gough’s Cave. Suitable for all abilities. Sessions available for adults and children aged 8 years and over. Escape Rooms : Up for a challenge? Our two Cheddar-themed rooms, Caved In and The Vault will test your brain power as you race against the clock to try to escape. Double the fun with our Ultimate Escape combo ticket at a discounted rate. Suitable for 12 years and over in groups of up to six people. Nature, wildlife, history, adventure - experience the wonder on an all-season day out in Somerset. For more information on how to plan your day at Cheddar Gorge & Caves and to book please visit www.cheddargorge.co.uk
tagline: Explore Britain’s biggest gorge, from the stunning stalactite caverns to the dramatic cliffs.

title: Beautiful loft room with views over Bath
subtitle: A bright and comfortable loft bedroom situated in a newly decorated and well equipped house just a fifteen minute walk away from the centre of Bath.
bodyContent: A bright and comfortable loft bedroom situated in a newly decorated and well equipped house just a fifteen minute walk away from the centre of Bath. This is one of four private rooms within the house. Situated in Oldfield Park and very close to Oldfield Park Train Station and local buses, this is a perfect base for exploring Bath. There is a free car park just fifty metres from the house which is a truly rare find in Bath! Four bedroom Victorian house retaining many period features. With an eclectic mix of individually furnished, quirky bedrooms and modern kitchen and bathroom. Stripped wooden floors in communal areas and 3 of the bedrooms with carpeted, snug attic room. Bright and airy and set over 3 floors. Easy off street parking. 200mb fibre optic broadband. Flat walk in to town (15 minutes walk/ 5 minutes taxi). 2 minutes walk to Oldfield Park Train Station (2 minutes to Bath Spa; 12 minutes to Bristol Temple Meads). bodyContent: Marlborough House is an enchanting Victorian Town House which has received 4 Stars and Gold Award for quality and service, and is operated by Peter Moore in a friendly and informal style. title: Fyne Court, National Trust
subtitle: Fyne Court is a hidden gem in the heart of the Quantock Hills. Explore a wild garden, reclaimed by nature after once being part of a family estate.
bodyContent: Fyne Court in Somerset National Trust is a hidden gem in the heart of the Quantock Hills. Explore a wild garden, reclaimed by nature after once being part of a family estate. The estate was the home of the Crosse family who lived here until the house was destroyed by fire in 1894. Scientist and poet Andrew Crosse, the ‘Thunder and Lightning Man’ and Fyne Court’s most famous resident, became a recluse after his controversial experiments were made public. Step into the Snug to find out more about Fyne Court’s history. There’s plenty for families to enjoy including den building, climbing on fallen trees, splashing in streams and picnicking on the Courtyard lawn. In summer, see a haze of wildflowers and hear the buzz of bees in the walled garden. The Courtyard Café is open seven days a week all year round and serves hot & cold drinks, light lunches and homemade cakes. Fyne Court is open daily from dawn until dusk (opening times may vary due to weather conditions). There is no charge for entry and parking is free for National Trust members or £5 for non-members. Tramper mobility scooter available – call or email in advance to book. Level access to Courtyard and Café. Accessible route around the garden. Natural play areas for children. To find out more, visit: www.nationaltrust.org.uk/fyne-court or call 01823 451587. For those that wish to stay a little longer, Fyne Court cottage sits above the grounds and sleeps 6. To find out more, visit: https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/holidays/fyne-court-cottage-somerset

title: The Lorna Doone Walk
subtitle: When you’re travelling around Exmoor, you’ll come across mentions of Lorna Doone.
bodyContent: 'Photo: Julia Amies-Green’ When you’re travelling around Exmoor, you’ll come across mentions of Lorna Doone, the heroine of the 1869 eponymous historical romance by RD Blackmore. The dramatic story races through a love affair, violent gangs, murder and revenge and a wedding. The area of Exmoor in the book quickly became known as Lorna Doone Country, and at its heart is 'Doone Valley' also known as Badgworthy Valley. It's a magical, mystical place and it makes for a lovely walk. It’s also considered one of the most romantic places on Exmoor, and we certainly agree with that! The area offers several walking options, the longer to Lorna Doone Valley and a shorter version stopping off at Oare Church. The Walk 6 miles 3 hours Download the walk and print here

title: Percy Place
subtitle: Period holiday apartment in Bath sleeping 7 people at walking distance from the city centre with free on street parking.
bodyContent: Percy Place is a holiday apartment in a Grade II listed Georgian house in the City of Bath. The house used to be the home of Rev. William Jay, one of the most eminent English Congregationalist preachers of Regency England who used to preach in the Argyle Chapel in Bath at the end of 1700s. We like to make our guests feel at home and highly valued. The original Georgian features of the building are enhanced by the stylish decor of the rooms such as antiques, trinkets and period furniture. At the same time, free wi-fi and a recently refurbished kitchen offer modern comfort. Both the town and the countryside are on our doorstep. We are just a few minutes walk from the city centre between the up and coming ‘Artisan Quarter’ bristling with local independent shops, and Larkhall village, a pretty quarter with a local butcher, a deli, a theatre and a few restaurants. We are also very close to the Kennet & Avon Canal at the back of Kensington Meadows. The view of the countryside and back garden from the back of the house is relaxing and inspiring.
tagline: Period holiday apartment in Bath sleeping 7 people at walking distance from the city

Families often use this option when attending weddings in the nearby villages of Castle Combe, Grittleton and Euridge.

title: Wookey Hole Caves & Attractions
subtitle: Wookey Hole Caves is a magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for all ages. It’s an experience millions of years in the making with plenty to do inside and out. Enjoy vintage penny arcades, museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, and of course the famous, beautiful caves.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Wookey Hole Caves and attractions lies In the heart of Somerset. A magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for the young and young at heart. When you visit Wookey Hole, you’ll enjoy an experience millions of years in the making. There is plenty to do inside and out, from vintage penny arcades to museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, to name but a few of the attractions. Not forgetting the breathtakingly beautiful caves, for which Wookey Hole is renowned. Your visit will take you through 8 chambers. Each with a unique beauty and story. You’ll also pass our cheese tunnel, home to the delicious Wookey Hole cheese. The cheese is not the only resident of the caves. Over the years, Wookey Hole has been home to giant hyenas, bears, Neanderthals, and many local people. It has even been a site of pagan and Roman worship. You’ll find Wookey Hole holds a surprise around every corner. You might even get to meet our most famous resident, the Witch of Wookey Hole. We have found she most likes to visit during school holidays! The world-famous Wookey Hole Circus School performs at Wookey Hole at weekends and in School Holidays. Every year over 250,000 people visit Wookey Hole and take-home cherished memories of a great day out. Whether it is your first time or your fiftieth, there is always something new to discover. We can’t wait to welcome you.
tagline: At Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions, Somerset, there’s always fun and adventure to be had.

title: Wells Cathedral
subtitle: Built between 1175 and 1490 Wells Cathedral in Somerset has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals”.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built between 1175 and 1490 Wells Cathedral has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals”. Set in the medieval heart of England’s smallest city, and an easy drive from Bristol, Bath and Cardiff, Wells is the earliest English Cathedral to be built in the Gothic style. The current building is a significant landmark in the South West of England, has an international reputation and is TripAdvisor ranked number one for things to do in Wells and in Somerset. Wells Cathedral has unique features that separate it from other English cathedrals including its iconic West Front and the beautiful ‘scissor arches’ supporting the central tower, as well as one of the largest collections of historic stained glass in the country. The Cathedral also boasts the famous Wells Clock (which is considered to be the second oldest clock mechanism in Great Britain), the fascinating octagonal Chapter House and one of only four chained libraries in the UK. Wells Cathedral welcomes thousands of visitors each year who join in with regular daily services and events or who come simply to enjoy the calm and hospitality of this wonderful and holy place. Stay, if you can, for Evensong with the Cathedral’s world renowned choir (term times); a peaceful and moving end to your day. Tours: Discover hidden spaces and chambers, explore the south transept roof space and marvel at the nave from a very different perspective via the Cathedral's popular and longer High Parts tours which can be pre-booked via the website at www.wellscathedral.org.uk/visit/tours . The Cathedral runs complimentary ground floor tours daily (Monday-Saturday) and tickets include access to an audio tour. Guided tours for group visits can also be pre-booked via the Visits team at visits@wellscathedral.org.uk Families When term breaks up the Cathedral offers creative workshops for children accompanied by their parents or guardians. We also provide free children explorer backpacks which are available free of charge on arrival and which help children to learn about the main highlights and history of the Cathedral. Group Visits: The group rate (+10) for pre booked self guided visits is £10 and £12 to include a highlights tour. Unreserved groups are charged the standard on the door price of £14. For more information, and to book, please email visits@wellscathedral.org.uk Vicars’ Close: Adjoining the Cathedral is Vicars’ Close, believed to be the only complete medieval street left in England. Vicars’ Close was designed to provide accommodation for the Vicars Choral, who sing the daily services, and this is still the case today. This centuries-old tradition is unique and a much valued part of the continuing life of Wells Cathedral. The medieval windows of the houses and the garden archways seem to have survived more or less intact until the early nineteenth century, and even now a few still exist. Make a Day of It A warm welcome awaits you at our Cathedral shop which stocks a wide range of unique mementoes and gifts. The Loft at Wells Cathedral café is also open daily for coffee, delicious home-made lunches and afternoon teas http://www.wellscathedral.org.uk
tagline: Wells Cathedral in Somerset has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals".

title: Bodhi House
subtitle: Situated just over a mile from the centre of Bath, Bodhi House provides spacious, stylish accommodation slightly removed from the hustle and bustle of the centre.
bodyContent: Situated just over a mile from the centre of Bath, Bodhi House provides spacious, stylish accommodation slightly removed from the hustle and bustle of the centre. With commanding views over the city, the light and modern accommodation offers high levels of comfort and features furnishings and materials of the highest quality. Organic, local produce is served whenever possible. Bodhi House offers off-street parking if required, and a garden with views of the City of Bath and beyond. We offer a warm, informal welcome and will assist you with our helpful tips and information on how to make the very most of your stay in the glorious and historic City of Bath

title: Harington’s Hotel
subtitle: Harington’s City Hotel is privately owned and operated boutique hotel, set in the heart of the city centre (two minute walk from the Thermae Spa) with ample off-site parking. Each room and bathroom are totally unique.
bodyContent: Harington’s City Hotel is a privately owned and operated boutique hotel, set in the heart of the city centre (two minute walk from the Thermae Spa) with ample off-site parking. Each room and bathroom are totally unique. Haringtons offers a small coffee lounge (perfect for an afternoon cream tea). A dapper new edition to Harington’s City Hotel is the luvvly bubbly hot tub. Imagine how super it would be to have the warm bubbles soothe your aching muscles after a busy day shopping, sightseeing, or even at the office…it’s all possible at Harington’s.

title: Percy Place
subtitle: Period holiday apartment in Bath sleeping 7 people at walking distance from the city centre with free on street parking.
bodyContent: Percy Place is a holiday apartment in a Grade II listed Georgian house in the City of Bath. The house used to be the home of Rev. William Jay, one of the most eminent English Congregationalist preachers of Regency England who used to preach in the Argyle Chapel in Bath at the end of 1700s. We like to make our guests feel at home and highly valued. The original Georgian features of the building are enhanced by the stylish decor of the rooms such as antiques, trinkets and period furniture. At the same time, free wi-fi and a recently refurbished kitchen offer modern comfort. Both the town and the countryside are on our doorstep. We are just a few minutes walk from the city centre between the up and coming ‘Artisan Quarter’ bristling with local independent shops, and Larkhall village, a pretty quarter with a local butcher, a deli, a theatre and a few restaurants. We are also very close to the Kennet & Avon Canal at the back of Kensington Meadows. The view of the countryside and back garden from the back of the house is relaxing and inspiring.
tagline: Period holiday apartment in Bath sleeping 7 people at walking distance from the city centre

title: Glastonbury Abbey
subtitle: Glastonbury Abbey, Glastonbury, Somerset is connected with legend to a degree that is unparalleled by any other abbey in England. Since Medieval times it has held legendary status as the earliest Christian foundation in Britain linked to Joseph of Arimathea and the burial place of King Arthur.
bodyContent: Glastonbury Abbey, Glastonbury, Somerset is an internationally renowned site attracting visitors from around the world for its history, heritage, myths and legends as well as for its spiritual enrichment and there has been a church on the site for at least 1500 years with evidence of even earlier occupation. Glastonbury was the richest monastery in England at the end of the Saxon period and was second only to Westminster at the close of the middle ages. Its Abbot lived in considerable splendour and wielded tremendous power with the main surviving example of this power and wealth to be found in the Abbot’s Kitchen, one of only three surviving medieval examples in the world. It’s history is intertwined with English traditions; one of its Abbots – St Dunstan, wrote the Coronation words last used for the coronation of our present Queen Elizabeth II and William Blake’s popular “Jerusalem” is said to be written about the story that a young Jesus, accompanied by Joseph of Arimathea, visited Glastonbury . The Holy Thorn which grows at Glastonbury Abbey has become part of the legend of Joseph of Arimathea. According to the story when Joseph arrived in Britain he landed on the island of Avalon and climbed up Wearyall Hill, exhausted he thrust his staff into the ground and rested. By morning his staff had taken root and it grew into the miraculous thorn tree which flowers every Easter and Christmas. In 1191 the monks told the world they had found the bodies of King Arthur and his Queen found on the south side of the Lady Chapel. On 19th April 1278 their remains were removed in the presence of King Edward 1 and Queen Eleanor to a black marble tomb within the abbey itself. The tomb survived until the dissolution of the abbey in 1539. In 1536, during the 27 th year of the reign of Henry VIII, there were over 800 monasteries, nunneries and friaries in Britain. By 1541 there were none and the last abbot of Glastonbury , Richard Whiting was hung, drawn and quartered on Glastonbury Tor ; a brutal end for a pious man. Today it is a tranquil setting in which visitors can discover the stories behind Glastonbury Abbey with tours from costumed Living History presenters in the grounds; these tours are free but should be booked in advance for groups. A packed events calendar brings theatre, concerts, exhibitions and workshops to the abbey grounds every year and the abbey’s spectacular Night at the Abbey which last year won a national award. School and university groups can enjoy tailor-made itineraries and there are specific activities for families too. An accredited museum showcases items from the abbey’s history and gives more information about the chronology of events, archaeological finds and gives an insight into monastic life. There are 36 acres of parkland to explore with a dedicated wildlife area as well as new plans to recreate a Medieval Kitchen Garden. Groups are welcomed with a pre-booked meet and greet service available too and a special rate; driver and tour guide go free. A full access statement is on the abbey’s website – www.glastonburyabbey.com – along with maps in 14 different languages. Find us on Facebook /GlastonburyAbbeySomerset, follow us on Twitter @Glastonburyabbe or give us a call on 01458 832267. We look forward to meeting you
tagline: Glastonbury Abbey is connected with legend to a degree that is unparalleled by any other abbey

title: West Somerset Railway
subtitle: West Somerset Railway, Somerset, is a heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton. It is the longest independent railway in Britain, (20 miles).
bodyContent: West Somerset Railway, Somerset is the longest Heritage line in the United Kingdom. Time Table can be seen HERE for 2024 The line is situated in Somerset, four miles outside the County town of Taunton , starting at Bishops Lydeard and finishing at Minehead . The line meanders through the Quantock Hills , an area of outstanding natural beauty and along the Bristol Channel Coast. We have 10 stations along the line each having something different to offer. There are various historic sites that may be of interest to visitors to the area, for example Crowcombe Heathfield station was the location for the filming of the Beatles’ “A Hard Days Night” and scenes from “The Land Girls” were also shot here. The historic town of Watchet dates back to Saxon times, and boasts narrow streets, local shops, museums and lots of places to eat and drink. Washford is a great place to alight, just a short walk from the station we have Cleeve Abbey and the Torre Cider Farm, which are both well worth a visit. Fancy something a little different then why not visit Dunster Castle which is nestled in the medieval village of Dunster ? Dunster also has a working Watermill , the Old Yarn Market building and the Dolls Museum or continue on to Minehead home of our final station. Minehead is situated at the foot of North Hill where the beach is literally right across the road, we have cafes, shops and plenty of arcades along the seafront, making this a go to location. The West Somerset Railway also have combined tickets on selected dates throughout the year. These include, Cream Tea and Cheese and cider specials and linked trips with Hestercombe Gardens and Dunster Castle. We organise Steam Galas in the Spring and Autumn, and we are host to a Diesel Gala too. In the latter part of the year we have our popular Christmas services, we have Santa services running out of Minehead and Bishops Lydeard from the end of November until Christmas Eve, we also have our Sherry and Mince pie specials for you to enjoy.
tagline: Heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton.

subtitle: At the King Alfred you will find wonderful freshly prepared pub food, a fine selection of wines and ales and a warm welcome from your hosts.

King Alfred was one of England’s most famous and respected Kings who had close links to this area of Somerset. You can be guaranteed a warm welcome from Paul and the team and we hope you will come and visit us soon!

title: The Hollies
subtitle: The Hollies was built in 1851 in a meadow beside the old Bath – Wells turnpike.
bodyContent: The Hollies was built in 1851 in a meadow beside the old Bath – Wells turnpike. This was also the Fosse Way, built by the Roman Legions some 2000 years ago. The house, with its late Georgian facade, was once the home of the curate of St. Lukes Church, which is next door. It is now a gracious guest house with three individually designed rooms overlooking the award-winning garden. Every room has its own bath or shower room and is complete with television, radio alarm clock, hairdryer, bath robes and tea and coffee tray. Our comfortable Library with over 2000 books is available for guests.
tagline: The Hollies was built in 1851 in a meadow beside the old Bath – Wells turnpike.

title: Grove Cottage
subtitle: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside.
bodyContent: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside on the edge of an area of outstanding natural beauty but only 5 miles from the world heritage city of Bath and 1 mile from the Saxon town of Bradford-on-Avon. Cumberwell Country Cottages are located on Great Cumberwell Farm, which has been in the James family since 1939 and was originally a dairy farm until 1992 when the herd was sold making way for a diversification into Cumberwell Park Golf Club, the farm itself has not changed a great deal and is still a working farm with over 300 acres of arable crop. The self-catering cottages available for your stay have been converted from an old tithe barn which has had many purposes in the past including stables, a grain store and cider production as the orchard at the front of the cottages was a cider apple orchard.
tagline: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages

title: Mendip Basecamp
subtitle: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure campsite in the Mendip Hills...
bodyContent: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure camp in the Mendip Hills National Landscape - just minutes from the M5 and Weston-super-Mare. Surrounded by ancient woodland you can pitch where you like, park right by your tent and enjoy evenings around the campfire. Well-behaved dogs are welcome! With no check-out time, you can leave whenever you are ready. Mendip Basecamp is camping how it should be: rural, laid-back and relaxed but with essential luxuries. Usually reserved for schools and private groups, in 2020, Mendip opened Basecamp up to families for the very first time- and hasn’t looked back since. Public bookings are available throughout the summer holidays and summer weekends. Bring your own tent or campervan, book bell tents, glamphouses or stay in Mendip Lodge (with free breakfast). Facilities include hot showers, clean flushing toilets, a camp shop, a country Lodge with a cider garden (and live music), an onsite activity centre, USB charging and WIFI. Free activities throughout the summer include live music, orienteering, circus skills, treasure hunts, free climbing tower and nature craft. The campsite is less than a 5-minute woodland walk from Mendip Activity Centre, home to over 20 different adventurous, outdoor activities including rock climbing, kayaking, archery, frisbee golf and air rifle. New for 2026, Mendip Basecamp is launching Mendip Mini Fests - six family-friendly festivals running throughout the summer holiday weekends. Great entertainment, headline bands, local talent competition, and more! Included at no extra cost, exclusively for campsite guests.
tagline: Mendip Basecamp was delighted to be awarded the Gold campsite at the 2023-2024

subtitle: With a bright, welcoming feel and bags of well thought out features, Dream Stays’ range of Bath apartments are perfect for any city break.

Whether you are looking for a romantic bolthole for two, a family friendly haven or accommodation for a whole group of guests, Dream Stays have just the place. Each of its Bath lets is inviting and well-considered. title: Pulteney Guest House Bed and Breakfast
subtitle: Pulteney House Bed and Breakfast is a large, elegant Victorian house set in its own picturesque west facing gardens, with fine views of Bath Abbey only 10 minutes’ level walk from the centre of Bath.
bodyContent: Pulteney House Bed and Breakfast is a large, elegant Victorian house set in its own picturesque west facing gardens, with fine views of Bath Abbey only 10 minutes’ level walk from the centre of Bath. The Bed and Breakfast has 16 rooms with en-suite facilities, and 1 with private facilities that are opposite the room. We offer a range of room types including family rooms, single rooms, double and twin rooms. A limited number are ground floor rooms. Pulteney House has been privately owned since 1979 and we provide a warm homely welcome to all guests. The large mature gardens are always kept in beautiful condition and guests are encouraged to utilise them where children can play in absolute safety. A comfortable family TV lounge is available for guests to use and relax in away from their room. Private onsite car park with CCTV for added security and peace of mind. Free Wi-Fi in all rooms and public areas. Free use of computer for those guests with no personal device. A large and varied Breakfast menu is available and we cater for a range of specific dietary requirements.

title: Glastonbury Tor, National Trust
subtitle: Glastonbury Tor is a well-loved Somerset landmark associated with myths and legends, but it is also a place where children can run about and have fun. Fields at the foot of the Tor are good for games or you could play at the top in the ruined tower.
bodyContent: Prominent hill overlooking the Isle of Avalon, Glastonbury and Somerset. This iconic and evocative landmark offers magnificent views of the Somerset Levels , Dorset, Wiltshire and Wales. Steeped in history and legend, excavations at the top of the Tor have revealed the plans of two superimposed churches of St Michael, of which only a 15th-century tower remains. Glastonbury Tor also has a grisly past. Abbot Richard Whiting was executed here in 1549 on the orders of Thomas Cromwell, the first Earl of Essex. Glastonbury Tor is known as being one of the most spiritual sites in the country. Its pagan beliefs are still very much celebrated. It’s a beautiful place to walk, unwind and relax.
tagline: Glastonbury Tor is a well-loved Somerset landmark associated with myths and legends.

title: Westons, Golden Jubilee Restaurant
subtitle: Our award winning Golden Jubilee Restaurant in Weston Super Mare, Somerset epitomises the elegant Regency style for which Weston was formally renowned. Open to both residents and non-residents this proves to be a very popular eatery to all.
bodyContent: Our award winning Golden Jubilee Restaurant epitomises the elegant Regency style for which Weston was formally renowned. Open to both residents and non-residents this proves to be a very popular eatery to all. Breakfast We are proud to be presented with the Enjoy England’s Breakfast Award, which we have achieved year after year. Only about 8% of guest accommodation have received this award, recognizing hotels and B&Bs that offer a quality and varied choice of breakfast and high level of service and hospitality. We offer breakfast fit for a king, with our continental buffet-style banquet, followed by either a traditional cooked to order Full English Breakfast, steak and eggs, omelettes or choose from our lighter options such as filled bagels and fish dishes. With unlimited tea and coffee readily available this will most definitely be the best start to your day. Lunch & Dinner In these captivating surroundings you can enjoy dishes carefully selected for our appealing À la Carte menu which has been designed by our Head Chef to tempt and excite all tastes. With our menu changing with the season you are guaranteed that our kitchen only use the best local ingredients allowing our dishes to be full of flavour and goodness! Our cuisine is classic British with a twist of French infusion, offering a variety of fresh fish & meat dishes, steaks and grills along with vegetarian and vegan options. Our famous Carvery is available on Tuesdays, Thursdays and of course Sundays offering a choice of freshly cooked joints of meat accompanied by a selection of garden vegetables, Roasted Potatoes and all the trimmings. Afternoon Tea Appetites are indulged with an afternoon tea for two or four, which pleases palates with a selection of sandwiches and a pot of tea for each person. The sweet edge is provided in the form of homemade scones with dollops of clotted cream and jam, plus a slice of traditional English Victoria Sponge. Guests also have the option to include a glass of Prosecco for a fizzy twist.
tagline: Open to both residents and non-residents this proves to be a very popular eatery to all.

title: Wimbleball Lake
subtitle: It’s your outdoors – come and explore at Wimbleball Lake
bodyContent: Wimbleball Lake, nestled amongst the rolling hills of Exmoor , is a must-visit attraction during your stay in Somerset. Your little adventurers will love exploring and discovering all of the fun things to do at this majestic lake. Ditch the iPads, immerse yourself in nature and create lasting memories with the family. Den building, rolling down hills, spotting birds from a hide and, of course, enjoying a well-deserved ice cream from the Coffee Couture at Wimbleball are bound to be a huge hit. Activity Centre and Campsite Visit the Activity Centre and enjoy a family adventure like no other. Explore the lake by kayak Learn how to stand up paddleboard Spot wildlife from a canoe Hit the bullseye in a game of archery Face your fears and attempt the high ropes course Learn how to turn in a sail boat Relax and enjoy a spot of fishing Sleep under canvas or glamp in one of our pods, bell tents or cabin. Play Get your children learning and having fun on their next adventure by downloading South West Lakes’ 101 things to do this summer booklet and activity sheets . Identify trees, track prints, discover different leaves or go on a bug hunt. Visit the children’s play area or enjoy the plentiful open space for informal games. Walking and Cycling Embrace the outdoors and experience Wimbleball by bike or foot. The network of footpaths and cycle tracks suit visitors of all ages and abilities. Don’t forget to bring the dog! We want our four-legged friends to enjoy this special place. All we ask is for you to keep your dog on a lead and out of the water. Good Food Enjoy some delicious treats from our onsite cafe – Coffee Couture at Wimbleball. Treat the family to an ice cream or a cake and recharge with a coffee or a light lunch. Stargazing Exmoor National Park is designated an International Dark Sky Reserve - the very first in Europe! Wimbleball is a designated Dark Sky Discovery Site and is the perfect place to stargaze and engage with nature and the outdoors in its greatest form. Opening Times Wimbleball Lake is open all year round. The Activity Centre opening times vary throughout the season. Please visit www.swlakestrust.org.uk/activities for more information or call 01398 371460
tagline: It’s your outdoors – come and explore at Wimbleball Lake

title: The Butchers Arms
subtitle: Situated in the quiet village of Carhampton, The Butchers Arms is a Grade II listed building on the edge of Exmoor National Park
bodyContent: Situated in the quiet village of Carhampton, The Butchers Arms is a Grade II listed building on the edge of Exmoor National Park. It features an on-site restaurant and bar with open fireplaces, and free on-site parking. A TV and tea/coffee making facilities are provided in each room at The Butchers Arms, as well as an en suite bathroom. A full English breakfast is served each morning in the dining room, and packed lunches can be provided on request. Slow-cooked roast pork, beef and turkey are available each Sunday as part of the carvery, and accompanied by the chef’s free homemade soup of the day. Lunch and evening courses are also on offer. Blue Anchor’s seafront can be reached in a 10-minute drive, and the Quantock Hills are less than 10 miles away. Mountain biking, hiking and horse riding can be enjoyed within Exmoor National Park.
tagline: Situated in the quiet village of Carhampton, the Butchers Arms is a Grade II listed building

title: Five of the most romantic, circular walks in and around Bath
subtitle: With Love under lockdown, we will all be looking for creative ways to make up for the loss of Valentine’s day 2021. Away from extravagant amazon parcels or misjudged Love-Honey gifts, there is a much simpler way to recompense for missing this year’s romantic season. Look no further than the number of wonderful walks around Bath.
bodyContent: Article by Robbie Pecchia 5 Most romantic, circular walks in and around Bath With Love under lockdown, we will all be looking for creative ways to make up for the loss of Valentine’s day 2021. Away from extravagant amazon parcels or misjudged Love-Honey gifts, there is a much simpler way to recompense for missing this year’s romantic season. Look no further than the number of wonderful walks around Bath. We have consolidated the 5 most romantic and circular walks in and around Bath, for you, and have named them after the romantic movies we recommend watching on your return. These scenic stretches will bring you closer to nature, the city’s rich history and, hopefully, to one another. The walks, truly, are as timeless as the city on which they sit upon. So, in more precedented times be sure to include some these romantic rambles in your next visit to Bath. 1. The Shape of (Bath) Water Fortunately, the only amphibious creatures you’ll meet on this walk along the canal and river of Bath will be the ducks, but that doesn’t mean this stroll hasn’t got all the romance of Guillermo del Toro’s freaky and heart wrenching film. Weaving the waterways on this trip you’ll be treated to a serene and leisurely walk that gives you all the beauty of Bath without the need of hiking any hill or jostling with any crowds. There’s a chance to be still with the water and stunning stone in this tasteful 2-mile circuit which offers great views. www.plotaroute.com/route/1391018 Recommended places to stay nearby: The Kennard , Roseate House , Chestnuts House Recommended movie to watch afterwards: The Shape of Water (2017) 2. Once upon a time in Freshford… …There was a beautiful long walk with a big castle, grand manor and a selection of cosy pubs. On this fairy trail just outside of Bath, we once again find ourselves looking to where river meets canal but this time with a rural, Game of Thrones and Downtown Abbey theme. Starting and finishing at the comfortable Inn at Freshford, this walk takes you over fields and onto a gothic church, historic castle and an impressive Manor house where you can enjoy an afternoon tea. As a couple you’ll be spoilt for fantasies on this truly stunning country walk. www.plotaroute.com/route/1389626 Recommended places to stay nearby: Homewood Park, Waterhouse Recommended movie to watch afterwards: Once upon a time in Hollywood (2019) 3. Locks, Ducts and Two Smoking Tunnels This long loop is as action packed as Guy Ritchie’s 1998 classic, but you’ll be happy to know it isn’t as climatic. The 13-mile amble is fantastically flat, making it accessible to walkers of any level and it has a bit of everything for you and your partner in crime. After a small stint through the town and along the riverside, you will be given the unique experience of stepping through Bath’s remarkable restored railway tunnels. The tunnels have an amazing story, that you can read on the route, and the walls inside have a palpable connection with city’s history. Then it’s over and under great viaducts before travelling back to your starting point via the meandering canal track. If you have time on your next visit, we highly recommend walking this route and rewarding yourself with a hearty lunch at one of the fine pubs on the way. www.plotaroute.com/route/1390617 Recommended places to stay nearby: No. 15 Great Pulteney , The Windsor Town House , Dukes Recommended movie to watch afterwards: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels 4. Walk the (Sky) Line There is no walk quite like the National Trust’s Bath Skyline walk. The views are simply unmatched. If Johnny Cash had walked this route, I am sure he would have written a ballad on its beauty. Past the castle, over the fields and through the woodlands; you’ll constantly be in awe of the range of vision over the city, you have, on this walk. So, we recommend you take your best camera, your best walking boots and explore all of Bath on this one incredible loop around it. www.plotaroute.com/route/1391086 Recommended places to stay nearby: The Ayrlington , The Bird , Pulteney Guest House B&B Recommended movie to watch afterwards: Walk the Line (2005) 5. Four Crescents and a Circus This walk starts off as more of a climb but don’t be perturbed by this; it is an outstandingly rewarding ascension. If Hugh Grant is up for the challenge of attending that many weddings, you can survive this. Not only do you get a chance to gorge on the stunning Georgian architecture as you wind your way up, but you are also gifted some of the best views over Bath when you turn around. The Hedgemead park and smaller crescents act as a perfect starter to the second half of the show. On your way down, you can choose to indulge yourselves on the exotic flora and fauna of the Royal Victoria Botanical Gardens. Or you can opt to head straight to the two architectural gems of Bath; finishing the circuit on high as you admire John Wood and John Wood Juniors’ greatest works of the Royal Crescent and Circus. www.plotaroute.com/route/1391142 Recommended places to stay nearby: Brocks Guest House, The Queensbury Hotel, Hill House Recommended movie to watch afterwards: Four Weddings and A Funeral (1994)

title: The Kennard
subtitle: The Kennard gives you the chance to discover and enjoy a stay in a true Georgian Town House.
bodyContent: The Kennard gives you the chance to discover and enjoy a stay in a true Georgian Town House, now restored to a boutique guesthouse. Built as a lodging house in 1794, The Kennard, today, offers twelve recently refurbished and individually decorated bedrooms, furnished for your every comfort, over five floors with a fine selection of superior doubles, standard doubles, snug doubles, two singles with shared bathroom, a twin and a triple room. Our rooms offer either a view over our garden and the city, or look out onto the street. We also have a small sitting area and an honesty bar located on the landings. Quietly situated only 5 minutes from the Abbey, the Roman Baths, the Thermae Spa and the railway station and some of the best restaurants and shopping venues our beautiful city has to offer. We hope you will stay with us and enjoy the experience of staying in one of Bath’s original Georgian townhouses with service and accommodation that truly reflects this beautiful city’s social history and culture.
tagline: The Kennard gives you the chance to discover and enjoy a stay in a true Georgian Town House.

title: The Apartment, Bath
subtitle: An exceptional two-bedroom luxury holiday home in central Bath, loved by guests for its perfect location, stylish decor, comfort, cleanliness and first class self-catering accommodation.
bodyContent: From Nespresso to Nintendo, The Apartment, Bath is an excellently-located two-bedroom apartment in central Bath. The first bedroom is a large, bright double bedroom with king size bed (or twin beds on request). The open fireplace and large sash windows are elegant original features and south-facing views take in the length of Ralph Allen Drive and Widcombe Hill. At the rear of the property, the second bedroom is a well-proportioned double bedroom, featuring a comfy double bed, original fireplace and built in wardrobe. The homely lounge is flooded with light from the large, original south-facing 16-pane sash window. The room hosts an extendable dining table and chairs, designer sofa (which can convert to a sofa bed) and a feature armchair. Brimming with technology, the lounge is equipped with satellite TV, blu-ray player, Nintendo Wii and wall-mounted 40” Samsung LCD TV. A well-equipped and cleverly designed galley kitchen features high-end integrated appliances to meet your every need, including a built-in double oven and sleek induction hob, full suite of cooking facilities and an integrated NEFF fridge with ice-box. A Nespresso machine and milk frother are provided for that much needed espresso or cappuccino to kick-start your day. And there is a washer dryer, so you can pack a little lighter! The newly renovated bathroom features a large walk-in rain shower with separate handheld spray. A chrome towel rail is complemented by a lit, motion-activated mirror cabinet featuring de-mist function and integrated razor/electric toothbrush socket. This gorgeous two-bedroom holiday home in central Bath is ranked in the ‘10 Best Holiday Homes in Bath’ by Booking.com and consistently rated positively by guests.

title: Blagdon Lake
subtitle: Are there many anglers in the world who haven’t heard of Blagdon? The name stirs emotions for thousands of anglers as the home of still water trout fly fishing with catch records going back as far as the early 1900's.
bodyContent: The lake is relatively shallow, with an average depth of 14 feet and only 38 feet at its deepest point near the dam (west end of the lake). Travel along its narrow length to the east and you come to the shallowest area of the lake at Top End where the River Yeo enters. In between there are many superb fishing areas with proven track records of producing the goods – Bell’s Bush, Peg’s Point, Rainbow Point, Ash Trees, Rugmoor and Green Lawn, are all areas that successful anglers will quickly become accustomed to. All methods work on the lake but many locals and experts stick to small flies and nymphs fished slowly on or near the surface. Early season and in the dying days of the year lures and sinking lines can be effective, but it is the patterns that imitate the naturals which command most attention. Sitting at the foot of the Mendip Hills in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB), Blagdon Lake covers 440 acres and is classified as a SSSI by Natural England for its’ wildflower meadows and bird populations. The long, narrow shape makes it ideal for both boat and bank fishing. There are deep basins and long banks to drift over, plenty of points and promontories for access to deeper areas as well as shallow, sheltered bays of quieter water. Most of the seven-mile perimeter has easy bank access but to explore the more remote areas a boat is the answer. On the south shore of the Lake below Blagdon village is the Fishing Lodge. This beautiful, timber framed building epitomizes the old world charm of Blagdon Lake. There is an office and small tackle shop on site selling all the essential flies and accessories. The Lodge is manned during the mornings by friendly, knowledgeable staff who are there to help you enjoy your day by giving up to the minute information on how the water is fishing. Enjoy a complimentary cup of tea or coffee before fishing or during a leisurely lunch. We have a fleet of 20 boats for hire at Blagdon. Advance booking is essential as each boat is individually locked and when Blagdon Lodge is unstaffed anglers must report to Woodford Lodge, Chew Valley Lake, in order to sign in. title: Georgian House

Bath Abbey, the Roman Baths & Bath’s many delightful shops are a short stroll from the apartment & Bath Rugby’s ground is a mere 2 minutes walk along the river towards Pulteney Bridge. In addition, there are many fabulous restaurants on your doorstep. When you return for the day you’ll be able to put up your feet & gaze at the glorious view of Bathwick Hill & the distant Sham Castle to relax & rejuvenate before the next day. To help with that home to home feeling there is free Wifi, a Nespresso coffee machine, dishwasher, microwave, washing machine, tumble dryer & the comfiest beds we could find. A highchair, cot or extra child’s bed can be also provided on request. In addition a widescreen TV & DVD player with DVDs of some of the many films shot in Bath over the years are waiting for you. If you fancy some exercise, Bath Leisure Centre with a pool, gym & exercise classes is a hop and a skip over North Parade Bridge. Whilst for those fresh air fiends, the canal can be easily accessed for walks/runs/cycle to Bathampton (3 miles) & beyond. Bikes can be hired locally or you can bring your own & keep them in Georgian House’s basement bike store (please bring your own lock). The canal is also a lovely way to walk to the Holburne Museum. Georgian House is an amalgamation of three Georgian townhouses & has retained its grand feature staircase and useful lift from its hotel past. A 5 minute level walk from Bath Spa Train & Bus Station, public transport is the best way to visit Bath. If however you need to bring your car, the apartment has a parking permit allowing free parking is central zone spaces. For busy times, there is also a long stay car park 2 minutes walk away.
tagline: This gorgeous, light & peaceful 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom loft apartment

title: Cumberwell Country Cottages
subtitle: Bradford on Avon self catering cottage accommodation
bodyContent: Bradford on Avon self catering cottage accommodation -Seven luxurious and spacious self catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside on the edge of an area of outstanding natural beauty but only 5 miles from the world heritage city of Bath and 1 mile from the Saxon town of Bradford on Avon. The self catering cottages available for your stay have been converted from an old Tythe Barn which has had many purposes in the past including stables, cider production as the orchard at the front of the cottages was a cider apple orchard. Cumberwell Country Cottages near Bradford On Avon and Bath offer many features which will make your stay that extra bit more comfortable and have flexibility to accommodate our guests at various times of the week. You can sample country life, town life and city life all from your stay at Cumberwell Country Cottages. If you’re looking for a quiet retreat in the countryside yet within easy reach of Bath, Bradford on Avon, Longleat and numerous other attarctions then Cumberwell Country Cottages could be perfect for you. Cumberwell Country Cottages has 7 luxury 1 or 2 bedroom self catering cottages accommodating up to 4 people. 7 self catering cottages sleeping from 2 to 4 people Quiet and peaceful rural location Close to Bath and Bradford On Avon All cottages have underfloor downstairs heating All linen and towels provided for your stay Free Laundry Facilities Available All bedrooms ensuite 20″ Flat Screen LCD Televisions in all bedrooms LCD Televisions in all living areas with Freeview, DVD & Hi-Fi Fully equipped kitchens including Microwave, Sandwich Toaster and George Foreman Grills Each Cottage has its own Patio with Garden Furniture BBQ’s available on request Open all year round 36 hole championship golf course and 9 hole par3 golf course on site Flexible arrival and departure days 2 night weekend breaks available Parking – Ample parking near to the cottages Free Wifi No Smoking in all cottages

A large and varied Breakfast menu is available and we cater for a range of specific dietary requirements.

title: Holnicote Estate, National Trust
subtitle: Holnicote Estate makes up 12,000 acres of Exmoor National Park and is a contrasting landscape with everything from wild, rugged moorland and shingle beaches to ancient woodland and charming thatched villages.
bodyContent: Holnicote Estate, Exmoor, Somerset National Trust makes up 12,000 acres of Exmoor National Park and is a contrasting landscape with everything from wild, rugged moorland and shingle beaches to ancient woodland and charming thatched villages. A fantastic place for walking, horse riding and cycling, Holnicote has 150 miles of footpaths and bridleways to explore. Walk up to Dunkery Beacon, Somerset's highest point and a spectacular spot for stargazing, or take a more leisurely stroll and enjoy a picnic or BBQ at Bossington . Red deer, Exmoor ponies, bats and the rare heath fritillary butterfly along with an awesome array of lichens and mosses make Holnicote a unique and very special place to visit. Selworthy Green is an ideal place to begin with information on walks and other activities available from Selworthy shop. You can also pop into the nearby Periwinkle tearoom for a cream tea to set you up before exploring (seasonal opening).
tagline: Holnicote Estate makes up 12,000 acres of Exmoor National Park.
