title: Wookey Hole Caves & Attractions
subtitle: Wookey Hole Caves is a magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for all ages. It’s an experience millions of years in the making with plenty to do inside and out. Enjoy vintage penny arcades, museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, and of course the famous, beautiful caves.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Wookey Hole Caves and attractions lies In the heart of Somerset. A magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for the young and young at heart. When you visit Wookey Hole, you’ll enjoy an experience millions of years in the making. There is plenty to do inside and out, from vintage penny arcades to museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, to name but a few of the attractions. Not forgetting the breathtakingly beautiful caves, for which Wookey Hole is renowned. Your visit will take you through 8 chambers. Each with a unique beauty and story. You’ll also pass our cheese tunnel, home to the delicious Wookey Hole cheese. The cheese is not the only resident of the caves. Over the years, Wookey Hole has been home to giant hyenas, bears, Neanderthals, and many local people. It has even been a site of pagan and Roman worship. You’ll find Wookey Hole holds a surprise around every corner. You might even get to meet our most famous resident, the Witch of Wookey Hole. We have found she most likes to visit during school holidays! The world-famous Wookey Hole Circus School performs at Wookey Hole at weekends and in School Holidays. Every year over 250,000 people visit Wookey Hole and take-home cherished memories of a great day out. Whether it is your first time or your fiftieth, there is always something new to discover. We can’t wait to welcome you.
tagline: At Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions, Somerset, there’s always fun and adventure to be had.

See live and acoustic sets from local DJs and singer/songwriters, as well as specially curated events throughout the year, showcasing the best drinks, food and entertainment that Frome and Somerset have to offer.

subtitle: This is the perfect place for a warning beacon ‘in order to alarm the country in times of civil discord or foreign invasion’.
bodyContent: With it’s high vantage point, you’ll enjoy splendid far-reaching views from the beacon. And a perfect spot for an ancient warning beacon. On a clear day it could be seen from 15 counties. Today, lucky walkers might spot red deer or Exmoor ponies. title: The Roseate Villa Bath
subtitle: The Roseate Villa Bath occupies a quiet corner of the city. A short walk from the heart of Bath, favoured for its heritage and cultural tourism, The Villa overlooks Henrietta Park, a 7 acre park opened to celebrate the Diamond Jubilee of Queen Victoria of 1897.
bodyContent: The Roseate Villa Bath occupies a quiet corner of the city. A short walk from the heart of Bath, favoured for its heritage and cultural tourism, the Villa overlooks Henrietta Park, a 7 acre park opened to celebrate the Diamond Jubilee of Queen Victoria of 1897. Henrietta Park is situated within walking distance of the city centre and is an oasis of tranquility with places to sit quietly or take a relaxing stroll around the circular walk amongst many fine trees and flora that include the Purple Sycamore, Golden Elms, Caucasion Mapel and a line of Baumannii Horse Chestnuts. The Villa encompasses two converted Victorian houses which have had a characterful legacy. Guests can always request information regarding informative excursions, or knowledge of the best activities whilst on a nonchalant weekend getaway. Take the tour of the Roman Baths and Regency Crescent or witness the views of Prior Park, Jane Austen Museum and the grandeur of Bath Abbey. You can always expect a warm welcome, immaculate hospitality, attention to detail and a genuine connection with every guest when you visit the Roseate Villa Bath. They are delighted to welcome dogs at The Roseate Villa Bath. Their team is always around to ensure that everyone can enjoy their stay with their dogs. Rooms The Villa houses 21 individual rooms with exclusive features. Every room has a bespoke Hypnos bed, goose down duvets and Egyptian cotton linen. Each attached bathroom is stocked with Penhaligon’s products and large fluffy bath sheets.The rooms are equipped with a flat-screen television and digital radio. The Villa hosts a private garden for guests to relax and enjoy an indulgent Afternoon Tea. Accolades The Roseate Villa Bath won the Customer service awards (Bath Business Awards) 2016 – 2017 & 2017 – 2018. Dine Breakfast: The Roseate Villa Bath features a dedicated breakfast chef who will tailor your breakfast preferences to your fancy. The Roseate Villa’s breakfast offering serves freshly baked bread straight from the oven, freshly squeezed orange juice, complimentary smoothies and Bucks Fizz with the food as well as a range of eggs, homemade jams and marmalades. Food offerings are locally procured and can be served in-room, breakfast-in-bed style. Afternoon Tea: Experience a truly exquisite Afternoon Tea, perfect for when you require light refreshment after a day of exploring Bath’s heritage and cultural spots. The Afternoon Tea symbolizes the quintessential English tea tradition with a few touches of modernity. Expect finger sandwiches, freshly baked scones with clotted cream and strawberry jam, delicate cakes, chocolate delice, pink lamingtons, macaroons and a host of tea choices, including a Champagne Afternoon Tea, perfect if you’d like to make the experience slightly more fulfilling and memorable.
tagline: The Roseate Villa Bath occupies a quiet corner of the city.

title: Rickbarton Cottage
subtitle: Rickbarton Cottage is the ideal base for that countryside retreat that everyone thrives from.
bodyContent: Walks from your doorstep, fresh air, country Pubs and a Farm Shop. Yet, close proximity to Bath (5 miles) and Bradford on Avon (2 miles) means that they get the best of both worlds! Guests can make use of the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool during their stay. Local Farm Shop village shop and village pub within walking distance or a short drive. The Kennet and Avon Canal is also within walking distance, for any keen walkers or cyclists. The cottage itself has an open-plan kitchen/living room. It is equipped with everything you should need. The bedroom has a double bed, which has been made up with fresh white linen prior to your arrival. The en-suite bathroom has a bath with a shower above the bath. There is space for a cot if needed (please check in advance of stay)
tagline: Rickbarton Cottage is the ideal base for that countryside retreat that everyone thrives from.

title: The Bird
subtitle: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to. A place to work and meet and by day and discover ever-changing bar experiences by night.
bodyContent: To be found just a few minutes’ stroll from Bath’s spectacular city-centre attractions, The Bird in Bath (previously The County Hotel) has re-branded to fit in with its distinctive new personality as part of the Kaleidoscope Collection. Owned by seasoned hoteliers, Ian and Christa Taylor, The Bird is a name that better reflects the vibrant transformation of the hotel, which has already seen refreshed public spaces, additional bedrooms, a new bar, relaxed restaurant and meeting spaces, as well as a much-loved pop-up beach bar for summer. Now with 27 en-suite bedrooms featuring every home comfort, many have far-reaching views across the cricket and rugby grounds to Bath Abbey, with the rolling hills of Bath and beyond. Breakfast is served in a lovely bright dining room, which overlooks Bath Abbey and opens into the conservatory, where morning coffee and afternoon tea can be enjoyed, while the Taylors have also created a wonderfully eclectic neighbourhood bar with relaxed food offering, designed as social hub for work or play. A space for freelancers to work, friends to meet for coffee or a relaxed dinner, there’s a bar for seasonal drinks and various seating areas centred around vast contemporary pieces of art. A separate meeting room also provides a creative space for workshops and get-togethers, private parties, celebrations and more. Visitors and locals alike won’t have to wait long for the next seasonal pop-up, a visually exciting Winter Wonderland for the festive season, and arguably the coolest party space in town. Set in a fantastical venue full of surprises, woodland branches and spruces will be strewn with fairy lights, tables topped with flickering candelabra and chairs draped in Bavarian rugs to keep you cosy. Everyone is welcome to simply drop in to experience the magical vibe. The Bird is easily reached via all main approaches to Bath, and has plenty of parking for guests.
tagline: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to

title: Hope Place
subtitle: Just a stone’s throw from the Royal Crescent, Hope Place is a luxurious one bed elevated apartment within a Grade II listed development delivering panoramic views of the city of Bath and the Avon Valley.
bodyContent: Situated in the prestigious residential suburb of Lansdown, just a stones throw from The Royal Crescent, nestled in the treasured Bath Conservation Area, Hope Place is a top of the range, modern and stylish residence. Whether you are looking for a weekend break, a self-catered home from home, a holiday or accommodation whilst on business, Hope Place provides a luxurious stay in the heart of the beautiful city of Bath. Throughout the apartment you will find decadent and exquisite touches to ensure your stay is one of pure indulgence. The open plan living room and dining area consists of stylish, contemporary furniture and decoration offering a comfortable and relaxing place to unwind. The kitchen is fully equipped with all you need to enjoy a premium break, including a Nespresso machine and Denby and Le Creuset crockery. The table is perfectly situated to allow you to enjoy breathtaking views over Bath and six acres of private parkland as you dine. For your entertainment there is a Sonos music bluetooth device together with a 43 inch smart television that has Netflix and Amazon video. The bedroom offers a peaceful and tranquil space to rest. The deluxe flower feature wall induces a sense of calm as you sink into the sumptuous Simba mattress, duvet and pillows and White Company bed linen. The room is opulently decorated and furnished with top of the range lighting, a Hollywood style mirror and a 43 inch smart television with Netflix and Amazon video. Discover the spectacular and captivating views across the city from this serene accommodation. On entering the bathroom you will find a range of luxurious Bramleys toiletries to indulge in. Take a long radiant soak in the bath or enjoy a fully immersive and energising shower under the extravagant rainfall shower head. Dry off with plush Christy towels and relax in the White Company Hydrocotton dressing gowns that are provided for your ultimate comfort.
tagline: Just a stone’s throw from the Royal Crescent, Hope Place is a luxurious one bed elevated apartment

title: Cider and Apple Pie
subtitle: Thatchers have teamed up with Kate Hackworthy to bring you some traditional 1920’s recipes, that pair perfectly with the Stan’s range. A delicious dessert, perfect for all the family to enjoy.
bodyContent: Indredients: For the Pastry: 350g plain flour 2 tbsp caster sugar Pinch of salt 175g cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes 1 egg yolk 1-2 tbsp very cold water Milk (to glaze) For the filling: 1kg eating apples, peeled, cored and chopped into chunks 50g caster sugar, plus extra for sprinkling 3 tbsp caster sugar 2 tbsp dry cider ½ tsp ground cinnamon For the method and more information visit https://www.thatcherscider.co.uk/recipes/cider-and-apple-pie/

title: Bay Tree House
subtitle: At Bay Tree House we aim to provide our guests with a comfortable and relaxing stay.
bodyContent: At Bay Tree House we aim to provide our guests with a comfortable and relaxing stay. Being on the doorstep of this beautiful City we are just 5 minutes walk from the Thermae Bath Spa, The Roman Baths, The Royal Crescent and The Circus, as well as the vast selection of shops! Our rooms are stylish and homely along with a friendly and professional service, with all the personal touches of a small family run business. Our modern Bed & Breakfast also offers parking and a central location.

title: Cosy One Bedroom Apartment
subtitle: Bright and quirky one bedroom apartment in the heart of Bath.
bodyContent: Situated on the East side of Bath on the London Road, just a ten minute stroll from the centre of town. Walcot is Bath’s artisan quarter – home to The Bell (award winning, community owned pub) as well as many other bars, restaurants, antiques markets, small business’ and cafes. The property on Walcot Buildings is a top floor flat set in a converted grade II listed building. It has a bright double bedroom with comfortable bed and traditional wooden shutters. There is plenty of storage space with a built in cupboard and chest of drawers. South facing it gets the sunshine all day. The living room has a comfortable sofa, coffee table, books and games as well as a TV (with Netflix). A separate, self contained kitchen contains all the white goods and utensils you would need for an enjoyable stay. The bathroom has a bath and shower and all of the amenities you would expect. We love the flat and eclectic mix of neighbours and residents that live nearby. We’ve provided everything you’ll need to relax and feel at home. There is a large supermarket a couple of minutes walk away for all the supplies you’ll need to make your stay special. Also a 24 hour shop just 2 minutes away for those midnight snacks.
tagline: Bright and quirky one bedroom apartment in the heart of Bath.

title: Montacute House, National Trust
subtitle: Montacute House is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design
bodyContent: Montacute House, Somerset is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design. With its towering walls of glass, glow of ham stone and its surrounding gardens, it is a place of beauty and wonder. Sir Edward Phelips was the visionary force and money behind this masterpiece, which was completed in 1601. Built by skilled craftsman using local ham stone under the instruction of William Arnold, master mason, the house was a statement of wealth, ambition and showmanship. Come face to face with the past in the Long Gallery; measuring over 52 metres, it is the longest of its kind in England. The Gallery houses over 60 Tudor and Elizabethan portraits on loan from the National Portrait Gallery. Beautiful gardens surround Montacute, constantly changing, filling the house with scent in summer and providing an atmospheric backdrop for a winter walk. Whether you just want to let the children run and explore, or be inspired by the collections housed within the walls of Montacute, you will leave with lasting memories and a desire to soon return. You may even recognise some of the sights, as Montacute House featured in the BBC’s highly acclaimed production of Hilary Mantel’s Wolf Hall. Within 20 minutes’ drive you will find four fascinating smaller properties, each with a unique character, history and story to tell. Their combined age of 2,300 years spans from the medieval period to the early 19th century. Explore Stoke Priory, a fine collection of medieval farm buildings; Treasurer's House, with its great hall and unusual wall painting; Stembridge Tower Mill, the last remaining thatched windmill in England; and the Priest’s House, a medieval home of great character not to be missed. While you’re in the area, why not also visit Lytes Cary Manor and Tintinhull Garden (see the National Trust website for more details).
tagline: Montacute House in Somerset is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design

title: Yeovil Railway Centre
subtitle: Originally formed in 1994 to preserve the original turntable, the Centre has grown to offer Steam and Diesel days, special events, Shop and Café, and welcomes the occasional main line steam engine. Please check days we open and what’s happening.
bodyContent: The Southern Railway turntable installed in 1947 has been overhauled and visitors can watch the spectacle of large steam engines being turned and serviced. A Peckett steam engine ‘Pectin’ is currently operational and provides the power for public rides on the demonstration line of around 1/3 rd mile. Visitors ride in a historic brake van or in a coach. During these events, both Miniature and Model Railways are normally available together with light refreshments and the Shop. Demonstration of the turntable is often given. There are several Industrial diesels on site, one of which is used on our Diesel Days. Special events (including Model Railways, Tractors, Halloween and Characters) operate on a regular basis and of course our ever-popular Santa Specials are run in December – pre-booking essential to avoid disappointment. We offer pre-booked Driver Experience -see website. Our Shop has ‘Thomas’ and other children’s gifts for sale as well as a large selection of books (new and second hand) and lots of other railway related items. The Shop opens every Sunday (except Christmas and New Year) from 10am to 12 noon and longer during most events. A historic 1864 built Transfer Shed acts as home to our Visitor Centre and Café, Museum area and Signalling exhibiton. Can be hired for meetings etc. The Charity is run by a friendly group of volunteers who endeavour to make our visitors as welcome as possible. Please remember to check our website of Facebook for when we are open and what’s happening!
tagline: Yeovil Railway Centre was formed in 1994 to preserve the original Southern Railway turntable.

title: Ring O'Bells
subtitle: Free house local pub in Somerset between Street & Glastonbury.
bodyContent: The Ring O’Bells is an 18th Century “free house” pub in the Somerset village of Ashcott near Street and Glastonbury, which for the last 29 years has been run by a family partnership. A unique pub with unique food, all prepared by us in our own kitchens. Local meat from a local butcher. Somerset produce at its best. Daily Specials blackboard including freshly made desserts. Home-made fudge with your coffee to finish! We are a genuine Free House and it is our policy to feature beers from small independent breweries, many from the West Country but occasionally also more “exotic” visitors! The range of beers varies constantly but our list of forthcoming beers features usually at least one beer from one of the local micro breweries. CAMRA Good Beer Guide 2016 CAMRA Good Pub Food Guide 2016, (star-rated, and entered in this guide for the nineteenth consecutive year). AA Pubs and Inns Guide 2016 The Good Pub Guide 2016
tagline: Free house local pub in Somerset between Street & Glastonbury.

Marco’s restaurant has his personality stamped all over it and the menu comprises everything you’d expect from a traditional steakhouse. Whether you are hosting a small business meeting to a multi-day conference, DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House does not disappoint as a destination location for business needs.

title: Castles & Coast Way
subtitle: Circular walk from Nether Stowey Castle to Stogursey Castle and the England Coast Path
bodyContent: The walk links The Coleridge Way in Nether Stowey and the England Coast Path and can be completed as a day walk or in sections which lend themselves to easier circular walks. The route is well signposted and waymarked with the Castles and Coast Way logo. On the route from Nether Stowey to Stogursey, as you walk by rivers, ditches, lakes or ponds, you might spot a kingfisher - a neon flash of this bird as it darts by is a sight to remember. Barbastelle bats are also known in the area. The route mostly follows public rights of way and crosses a wide variety of terrain and farmland. Please remain on the public footpaths at all times and do not deviate onto private land. There is no access to any of the woodlands in the vicinity of the walk. For more information click here .

bodyContent: Steve and Anna Wynne welcome you to The White Guest House, a level 7 minutes’ walk from the centre of Bath, Bath Spa train station, Bath coach station and the Kennet & Avon Canal. Bath Abbey,Thermae .Spa We take pride in our flower display and have been a Bath in Bloom winner.

title: Spacious Double Room in West Bath
subtitle: Spacious Double bedroom in Victorian terraced house to the west of the city of Bath.
bodyContent: Property has good transport links to city centre, as well as being close to all local amenities you should need for a pleasant stay with us. The house is situated to the west side of the beautiful city of Bath. Furnished with a mix of modern and vintage furniture, the property has all you need for a relaxing stay. There are good transport links to the town centre, with services stopping less than two minutes from us. There is also ample free street parking outside our door. The breakfast room/lounge has a very homely feel and contains books, games and suggestions on where to go in Bath. Guests also have use of our ultra fast fibre broadband. We’ve equipped the kitchen to make cooking easy with a host of ingredients and basic utensils. You’ll have your own private double bedroom with large comfortable double bed and ample storage space. You can also benefit from shared use of the modern and well equipped kitchen, comfortable living room and bathroom. I like to give guests their own space during their stay, however I am always available to offer recommendations and help, both before and during their stay. I am never far away or am in the house, and am always on hand should you need me. I usually arrange for a self check in but can always be on hand if a guest would like me to help them check in. We are a five minute walk from the high street where you’ll find a supermarket, takeaways and a few local shops. There are a number of good pubs and bars in the area all walking distance from us. Alternatively, its less than ten minutes into town by taxi and shouldn’t cost you more than £6-£7. The property is less than two minutes from the bus stop where you can catch regular services into the town centre. There is plenty of on street parking outside the house. We are about ten to fifteen minutes walk from Oldfield Park train station where you can access services to London and Bristol. Check-In: 3PM-9PM Not suitable for children (2-12 years) Not suitable for infants (under 2 years) Not suitable for pets No smoking No parties or events
tagline: Spacious Double bedroom in Victorian terraced house to the west of the city of Bath.

title: The Circus Apartment
subtitle: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses.
bodyContent: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the secluded private garden to the rear. With the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minutes walk The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the secluded private garden to the rear. With the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minutes walk. This contemporary apartment, in a warm palate of chocolate, plum and biscuit throughout, has undergone several transformations in its lifetime yet has retained all its period charm. The large sitting and dining room with sash windows overlooking two aspects of The Circus has two French style velvet sofas by a decorative fireplace. There is a TV with Blue Ray DVD and a separate radio with I-pod docking. A dining table seats four and a French style dresser contains crockery, cutlery and a selection of novels, films and games. The neat fitted period kitchen has an electric hob and oven, a microwave, a large fridge/freezer, and a dishwasher.. A large mirrored lobby before the bedroom which has fitted wardrobes and shelving leads to the spacious and comfortable bedroom which has a 6′ bed, a fitted wardrobe, a dressing table with storage and a tallboy and a cupboard containing a washer/dryer machine. A radio/alarm with I-pod docking is provided. The contemporary bathroom has smart cappuccino coloured tiling and contains a double ended bath with shower over, a hand basin with lots of storage under and a WC. The apartment has gas central heating, hair dryer, iron, microwave, dishwasher, towels and toiletries. A Free car parking permit is available as is free internet access.
tagline: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle

title: Stable Cottage: 6 bed country cottage
subtitle: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.
bodyContent: It is located in the beautiful Georgian village of Freshford which lies at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys in the southern Cotswolds. There are some wonderful walks to local pubs following the riverside and canals. All just 15 minutes from Bath by car but the secret of this location is the 9 minute train journey to Bath from the village station, just a short stroll from the cottages. The cottage : Stable cottage is a newly renovated, limestone floored, 3 bedroom, two bathroom (one is en-suite) cottage. It has large windows to the front of the house filling the bedrooms and downstairs with light on a sunny day. It has an open plan living/dining area with free view TV/DVD and two large suedette couches and comfortable chairs. For dining there is a blond Oak dining table and chairs to seat 6 . The Stables can accommodate 6 people in three bedrooms (two king size and one double) . The kitchen is fully equipped with cookware,dishwasher and washing machine . The house also offers Iron/Ironing board, Hairdryers All bed linen and towels . There is a Welcome pack of tea, coffee, sugar, milk, bread, butter, eggs and bacon. Free WiFi. There are also books and board-games in the house for the use of guests. If you have any questions on Bath and the local area before or during your stay please let us know. We would be delighted to help. Neighbourhood overview : Freshford is a beautiful ancient village with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk from the cottage( The Inn at Freshford) that serves restaurant quality food and all the local beers and ciders.They have an excellent fully stocked( from wine to organic humus!)community shop that also has a good quality cafe that serves lunch. There is also a local doctors surgery. The village is nestled at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys . The Kennet and Avon canal is a 15 minute walk from the cottage. Getting around : You don’t need a car to stay in the cottage. The village station is a few minutes walk away. Trains hourly off peak and thrice hourly at peak times. Bath 9 mins, Bristol 22mins. London Padington to Bath Spa 1.5 hours Bath Spa to Freshford 9 minutes Bath Spa to Freshford “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/bath-spa-to-freshford ” Freshford to Bath Spa “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/freshford-to-bath-spa ” There is also a local bus service to all the adjacent villages and Bath. The cottage has two parking spaces suitable for one medium and one small car or a single large SUV.the surrounding towns you might want to visit. Other things to note If you are a runner or keep fit enthusiast the owner is a qualified Personal Trainer (Bath Uni) with much Marathon and half marathon experience. She specialises in Ladies training. Please let us know if you would like guided running or some Personal Fitness training.
tagline: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.

All are modern in design and beautifully furnished, providing you with more privacy, space and comfort than a standard hotel. Whether you are coming to Bath for a family get-away, romantic break, get-togethers with friends, or business, the apartments are a great option for stay of any duration. You are assured of a warm welcome and memorable stay on every visit. ——————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————— Crescent Apartment is on the lower ground floor, comprises an open-plan sitting room / kitchen, a good sized master bedroom with super king bed, a single bedroom, bathroom and elegant French doors leading to the courtyard. The sitting room is furnished with two sofas (one is a double sofa bed), LCD TV and DVD. The master bedroom has a super king size deep-sprung divan bed, which can be converted into twin beds, wardrobe, console table and stool and flat-screen television. The second bedroom has a single bed. The modern kitchen is fully equipped with Neff hob, electric oven, microwave and integrated appliances: including a dishwasher, washer/dryer and fridge freezer.

title: Nunney Castle
subtitle: A small 14thC century moated castle, distinctively French in style.
bodyContent: The striking and picturesque moated castle of Nunney was built in the 1370's by Sir John de la Mere, a local knight who was beginning to enjoy royal favour. Extensively modernised in the late 16th century, the castle was held for the King during the Civil War, but quickly fell to Parliamentarian canon in 1645:not until Christmas Day 1910, however di the gun-damaged portion of the wall finally collapse.
tagline: A small 14thC century moated castle, distinctively French in style.

title: The Railway Inn
subtitle: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you. Treat yourself to a delicious meal in our restaurant, have a bar snack in our cosy bar, or simply enjoy a pint of Thatchers Somerset Cider.
bodyContent: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you. Treat yourself to a delicious meal in our restaurant, have a bar snack in our cosy bar, or simply enjoy a pint of Thatchers Somerset Cider . The food we proudly serve features regional and seasonal ingredients from local producers, with a strong emphasis on great quality, great taste and sensible prices. Our drinks menu is carefully chosen, with of course the full range of ciders from Thatchers; beers, wines and soft drinks. Our team of enthusiastic front of house staff love to share their knowledge and appetite for products with guests, and are proud to go that extra mile in making visits a memorable one. The Railway Inn has been at the hub of Sandford village for over 140 years. As a reminder of its long tradition, the original signals from the old Sandford railway line take pride of place outside, together with two authentic oak vats. The Railway Inn Cider House and Kitchen is decorated with artefacts and pictures reflecting the cidermaking heritage of Thatchers. Keen to represent local craftsmanship at its best, the bar and restaurant has been given extra special interest with hand carvings in English oak describing the story of the cidermaking year. A short walk along the road and you’ll come to the Thatchers Cider Shop . Here the shelves are packed with our ciders, alongside produce such as local cheeses and chutneys, and gifts including books and clothing. Our draught ciders are available straight from the barrel so you can try before you buy. Please call the Railway Inn on 01934 611518, or book online at www.therailwayinn.com
tagline: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you.

title: The Lodge at Bucklegrove
subtitle: Bucklegrove offers a family friendly base, with indoor swimming pool, The Lodge – Bar, Grill & Restaurant and a range of pitches from camping and tourers to luxury lodges with hot tubs.
bodyContent: Receive access when you book directly! Bucklegrove Holiday Park Bucklegrove offers a family friendly base, with indoor swimming pool, The Lodge – Bar, Grill & Restaurant and a range of pitches from camping and tourers to luxury lodges with hot tubs. ‘The Lodge’ is an ideal place to relax and unwind, serving local produce including ales and scrumpy. There is a covered outside area with snugly throws for chilly nights and a sun terrace for warm days with a view of the children’s play park. Flame-grilled steaks and burgers, homemade classics and a Sunday roast to take your breath away, children are also well catered for with our Little Campers menu. Take-away option available. ‘The Lodge’ also offers live entertainment and kids arts and crafts sessions during the holiday season. Bucklegrove boasts some of the best views in Somerset , looking across to the levels and moors with the backdrop of the Mendip Hills behind. A truly captivating spot where you can relax and enjoy the surroundings.
tagline: Bucklegrove Holiday Park Bucklegrove offers a family friendly base

title: Burnham-on-Sea Circular
subtitle: Burnham-on-Sea sits at the mouth of the River Parrett and the end of the second longest strip of sand in Europe.
bodyContent: Burnham-on-Sea sits at the mouth of the River Parrett and the end of the second longest strip of sand in Europe. It is a town of surprises from its independent shops to its short pier and three lighthouses. There is an information centre on the Esplanade and a choice of places for refreshment. Suitable for all walkers. For more information click here .

title: The Windsor Townhouse
subtitle: Location, location, location. Just two minutes’ walk to the city centre, tourist attractions, shops and restaurants, The Windsor perfect choice for both leisure and business guests.
bodyContent: Location, location, location. Just two minutes’ walk to the city centre, tourist attractions, shops and restaurants, The Windsor perfect choice for both leisure and business guests. With 15 individually styled ensuite bedrooms with period features and stunning views over one of the finest boulevards in Europe to the front and the green space of the Recreation Ground to the rear. Room facilities include complimentary WIFI, flat screen televisions, air conditioning and hostess tray. Luxury soft fluffy towels, cosy dorma duvets, feather pillows and White Company toiletries complete the package and add to the guest experience. Acclaimed for our warm and friendly staff, we are always ready with a smile and happy to help with anything from restaurant suggestions to planning your onward journey. We pride ourselves in our customer service and along with our award winning breakfasts, our aim is to send you home with a desire to return.
tagline: Location, location, location. Just two minutes’ walk to the city centre

title: Spacious Double Room in West Bath
subtitle: Spacious Double bedroom in Victorian terraced house to the west of the city of Bath.
bodyContent: Spacious Double bedroom in Victorian terraced house to the west of the city of Bath. Property has good transport links to city centre, as well as being close to all local amenities you should need for a pleasant stay with us. The house is situated to the west side of the beautiful city of Bath. Furnished with a mix of modern and vintage furniture, the property has all you need for a relaxing stay. There are good transport links to the town centre, with services stopping less than two minutes from us. There is also ample free street parking outside our door. The breakfast room/lounge has a very homely feel and contains books, games and suggestions on where to go in Bath. Guests also have use of our ultra fast fibre broadband. We’ve equipped the kitchen to make cooking easy with a host of ingredients and basic utensils. You’ll have your own private double bedroom with large comfortable double bed and ample storage space. You can also benefit from shared use of the modern and well equipped kitchen, comfortable living room and bathroom. I like to give guests their own space during their stay, however I am always available to offer recommendations and help, both before and during their stay. I am never far away or am in the house, and am always on hand should you need me. I usually arrange for a self check in but can always be on hand if a guest would like me to help them check in. We are a five minute walk from the high street where you’ll find a supermarket, takeaways and a few local shops. There are a number of good pubs and bars in the area all walking distance from us. Alternatively, its less than ten minutes into town by taxi and shouldn’t cost you more than £6-£7. The property is less than two minutes from the bus stop where you can catch regular services into the town centre. There is plenty of on street parking outside the house. We are about ten to fifteen minutes walk from Oldfield Park train station where you can access services to London and Bristol. Check-In: 3PM-9PM Not suitable for children (2-12 years) Not suitable for infants (under 2 years) Not suitable for pets No smoking No parties or events
tagline: Spacious Double bedroom in Victorian terraced house to the west of the city of Bath.

title: Stapeley Cottage
subtitle: Stapeley is a popular choice of cottage when looking for the family. The comfortable and well-equipped property has everything you should need for your time away.
bodyContent: Stapeley is a popular choice of cottage when looking for the family. The comfortable and well-equipped property has everything you should need for your time away. Families can enjoy the rural surroundings and experience life on our working sheep farm. Unwind in the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool and Games Room.

title: Lady Margaret’s
subtitle: This stunning Georgian Townhouse is located in the most beautiful area of old Bath.
bodyContent: This stunning Georgian Townhouse is located in the most beautiful area of old Bath – betwixt the Royal Crescent and the King’s Circus along the uber chic Margaret’s Buildings. Ideal for a get together of friends and family, Lady Margaret’s has received the highest possible reviews including a 5*s from VisitEngland. Sleeps 12.
tagline: This stunning Georgian Townhouse is located in the most beautiful area of old Bath.

title: Apsley House
subtitle: Located about 30 minutes walk from the City Centre, the Apsley House in Bath was built as a country home by The Duke of Wellington.
bodyContent: Located about 30 minutes walk from the City Centre, the Apsley House in Bath was built as a country home by The Duke of Wellington, after his momentous victory against Napoleon in the Battle of Waterloo. The rumour is that it was built as a place where he could keep his mistress of that time, as he was estranged from his wife years earlier. The hotel has been refurbished in great style and every care has been taken to preserve the natural elegance of the house, but still provide modern comforts. The magnificently proportioned reception rooms offer both style and comfort, with many period features complimented by the house being furnished with fine antiques and original oil paintings. Owned by Nick and Claire Potts ‘Apsley House Hotel’ is one of Bath’s finest small hotels. Resident Managers, Kate and Miro, offer guests a very warm welcome and personal care with the atmosphere more in keeping to that of a Private House than that of a hotel. Reception is always available if you require information on how best to spend your time in and around the beautiful city of Bath. Our Reservations department is open from 10am – 9pm daily. The Hotel has 12 delightfully appointed en-suite rooms across three floors (no lift access). Some rooms feature air-conditioners. Free Wireless internet access is available throughout. A freshly cooked feast of a breakfast with daily specials, is served in our elegant dining room. A lovely south facing garden is ideal for the summer evening aperitif. Complimntary parking is also available.
tagline: Located about 30 minutes walk from the City Centre, the Apsley House in Bath

title: Apple Tree Guest House
subtitle: Ling welcomes you to her Victorian period home in the centre of Bath
bodyContent: A World Heritage City with Roman roots, a medieval abbey and stunning Georgian architecture. Bath is located in the Cotswolds, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The Apple Tree is a 5 minute stroll to the city centre and a 10 minute level walk from the train station. We offer complimentary off-site permit parking in front of the house in a quiet residential location. All rooms are individually themed with an elegant blend of English and Asian artwork where East meets West, fresh cotton bedlinen and modern facilities.
tagline: Ling welcomes you to her Victorian period home in the centre of Bath

title: Circle Luxury Stays: Crescent apartment
subtitle: Choose from apartments in Bath city centre, or an exclusive newly built five-bed holiday home with indoor pool in Devon/Dorset coast.
bodyContent: Bath properties are in landmark locations such as the Royal Crescent and Camden Crescent, within walking distance to the High Street. All are modern in design and beautifully furnished, providing you with more privacy, space and comfort than a standard hotel. Whether you are coming to Bath for a family get-away, romantic break, get-togethers with friends, or business, the apartments are a great option for stay of any duration. You are assured of a warm welcome and memorable stay on every visit. ——————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————— Crescent Apartment is on the lower ground floor, comprises an open-plan sitting room / kitchen, a good sized master bedroom with super king bed, a single bedroom, bathroom and elegant French doors leading to the courtyard. The sitting room is furnished with two sofas (one is a double sofa bed), LCD TV and DVD. The master bedroom has a super king size deep-sprung divan bed, which can be converted into twin beds, wardrobe, console table and stool and flat-screen television. The second bedroom has a single bed. The modern kitchen is fully equipped with Neff hob, electric oven, microwave and integrated appliances: including a dishwasher, washer/dryer and fridge freezer.
tagline: Choose from apartments in Bath city centre

title: The Henry
subtitle: ‘The Henry’ is probably Bath’s most central Guest House. Just 100m from the railway and bus stations and 150m from the Abbey and Roman Baths.
bodyContent: ⭐ Book Direct for Reward Card Offers ‘The Henry’ is probably Bath’s most central Guest House. Just 100m from the railway and bus stations and 150m from the Abbey and Roman Baths, The Henry is perfectly located amongst the historic attractions of Bath. Located in a beautiful Georgian house we are less than a minute from Bath’s main shopping street. Whether your visit is as a tourist, for shopping or just for fun The Henry is the place to stay. We also have two self-contained apartments less than 100m away from the main house this can be rented as a self-catering or with breakfast served in the dining room at The Henry.
tagline: ‘The Henry’ is probably Bath’s most central Guest House.

title: Priest's House, National Trust
subtitle: Late medieval house with large Gothic hall windows, originally residence of priests serving the parish church opposite.
bodyContent: The Priest's House, Somerset National Trust This medieval hall-house was built in 1308 for the parish priest of the church opposite, and has been little altered since the early 17th century. Interesting features include the Gothic doorway, magnificent double-height tracery windows and a massive 15th-century stone fireplace.
tagline: Late medieval house with large Gothic hall windows.

bodyContent: Situated within the Bristol Hippodrome Piano Bar, Hanover Street Bistro is a stylish dining establishment serving a delicious menu. title: Farrington Inn
subtitle: Discover real ales, log burning fires and great British pub food at The Farrington Inn.
bodyContent: Discover real ales, log burning fires and great British pub food at The Farrington Inn. Located in the small village of Farrington Gurney, just a short drive from Bristol, Bath , Wells and the Mendips . You will find the pub on the main A37 so it's a perfect meeting place or to just take a break when travelling. The Farrington Inn is popular with families and the large beer garden has a well maintained children's play area. For those rainy days colouring templates and the free wifi will keep the children happy. The Great British Deals menu is served from 10am - 9pm everyday and has several mains at 2 for £10 and 2 for £12. There is also a 2 course lunch menu at £7.99, served Monday to Saturday until 4pm. Our extremely popular all day breakfast is included in the 2 for £12 deal and comes with a hot drink and toast. The Farrington Inn is an excellent choice for those who want freshly cooked real food, exceptional value and a friendly atmosphere. -Opening times Monday - Sunday 10am - 11pm Food served all day 10am - 9pm.

title: Berrow Beach Circular
subtitle: This walk is tidal - please check tide times before setting off. Suitable for all walkers.
bodyContent: Berrow is part of one of Europe’s longest strips of sand and there are dunes which growing rarer. They occur when sand, dried out at low tide, is blown inland and forms mounds that become anchored by grass growing on them. This walk is tidal - please check tide times before setting off. Suitable for all walkers. Click here for more information.

title: Toghill House Farm
subtitle: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds. Within a stone’s throw of the site of the battle of Lansdown and with the Cotswold Way and the old east to west Roman road running through the grounds, Toghill is steeped in history.
bodyContent: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds. Within a stone’s throw of the site of the battle of Lansdown and with the Cotswold Way and the old east to west Roman road running through the grounds, Toghill is steeped in history. Located on a working farm only 4 miles north of Bath, with spectacular views over the Welsh mountains, Mendips, Cotswolds and Historic Bath. We have 9 rooms, some of which are in the 17th century farmhouse and others in the pretty Cotswold stone converted barns and stables in a delightful courtyard setting.
tagline: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds.

title: Stable Cottage: 6 bed country cottage
subtitle: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.
bodyContent: It is located in the beautiful Georgian village of Freshford which lies at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys in the southern Cotswolds. There are some wonderful walks to local pubs following the riverside and canals. All just 15 minutes from Bath by car but the secret of this location is the 9 minute train journey to Bath from the village station, just a short stroll from the cottages. The cottage : Stable cottage is a newly renovated, limestone floored, 3 bedroom, two bathroom (one is en-suite) cottage. It has large windows to the front of the house filling the bedrooms and downstairs with light on a sunny day. It has an open plan living/dining area with free view TV/DVD and two large suedette couches and comfortable chairs. For dining there is a blond Oak dining table and chairs to seat 6 . The Stables can accommodate 6 people in three bedrooms (two king size and one double) . The kitchen is fully equipped with cookware,dishwasher and washing machine . The house also offers Iron/Ironing board, Hairdryers All bed linen and towels . There is a Welcome pack of tea, coffee, sugar, milk, bread, butter, eggs and bacon. Free WiFi. There are also books and board-games in the house for the use of guests. If you have any questions on Bath and the local area before or during your stay please let us know. We would be delighted to help. Neighbourhood overview : Freshford is a beautiful ancient village with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk from the cottage( The Inn at Freshford) that serves restaurant quality food and all the local beers and ciders.They have an excellent fully stocked( from wine to organic humus!)community shop that also has a good quality cafe that serves lunch. There is also a local doctors surgery. The village is nestled at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys . The Kennet and Avon canal is a 15 minute walk from the cottage. Getting around : You don’t need a car to stay in the cottage. The village station is a few minutes walk away. Trains hourly off peak and thrice hourly at peak times. Bath 9 mins, Bristol 22mins. London Padington to Bath Spa 1.5 hours Bath Spa to Freshford 9 minutes Bath Spa to Freshford “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/bath-spa-to-freshford ” Freshford to Bath Spa “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/freshford-to-bath-spa ” There is also a local bus service to all the adjacent villages and Bath. The cottage has two parking spaces suitable for one medium and one small car or a single large SUV.the surrounding towns you might want to visit. Other things to note If you are a runner or keep fit enthusiast the owner is a qualified Personal Trainer (Bath Uni) with much Marathon and half marathon experience. She specialises in Ladies training. Please let us know if you would like guided running or some Personal Fitness training.
tagline: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.

title: Lime Kiln Cottage
subtitle: Lime Kiln Cottage is a great cottage for all the family. Tastefully decorated giving it a country, yet contemporary feel.
bodyContent: Lime Kiln Cottage is a great cottage for all the family. Tastefully decorated giving it a country, yet contemporary feel. Enjoy use of the indoor heated swimming pool and games room onsite. Welcomed by a local produced cream tea on arrival. This property has received a Mobility Level 2 award making it a suitable option for the elderly or those with restricted mobility.
tagline: Lime Kiln Cottage is a great cottage for all the family.

title: Albany Guest House
subtitle: The Albany is a small and friendly guest house just off the centre or Bath. We offer a welcoming atmosphere.
bodyContent: The Albany is a small and friendly guest house just off the centre or Bath. We offer a welcoming atmosphere, with many of our guests returning time and time again to enjoy the personal service we offer. We accommodate special requirements, whether it’s a particular dietary requirement or an allergy. Please just let us know so we can make your stay as comfortable as possible. The Albany offers a great base to allow you to explore the many attractions of Bath. We also offer free parking.
tagline: The Albany is a small and friendly guest house just off the centre or Bath.

title: Church Farm Country Cottages
subtitle: Seven cottages tastefully converted from old cow byres with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams.
bodyContent: Seven cottages tastefully converted from old cow byres with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams. Three cottages sleep 2 persons and four cottages sleep 4 persons. Bath 5 miles. Bradford on Avon 2 miles. Ample parking. Working farm with sheep and horses in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Swim in our luxurious heated indoor pool (12m x 5m) whatever the weather! Games room with table tennis, pool table and table football. Village pub serving food 500m. Village shop 500m. Kennet and Avon Canal nearby for cycling, boating and walking. Locally produced welcome cream tea.
tagline: Seven cottages tastefully converted from old cow byres

title: The Apartment, Bath
subtitle: An exceptional two-bedroom luxury holiday home in central Bath, loved by guests for its perfect location, stylish decor, comfort, cleanliness and first class self-catering accommodation.
bodyContent: From Nespresso to Nintendo, The Apartment, Bath is an excellently-located two-bedroom apartment in central Bath. The first bedroom is a large, bright double bedroom with king size bed (or twin beds on request). The open fireplace and large sash windows are elegant original features and south-facing views take in the length of Ralph Allen Drive and Widcombe Hill. At the rear of the property, the second bedroom is a well-proportioned double bedroom, featuring a comfy double bed, original fireplace and built in wardrobe. The homely lounge is flooded with light from the large, original south-facing 16-pane sash window. The room hosts an extendable dining table and chairs, designer sofa (which can convert to a sofa bed) and a feature armchair. Brimming with technology, the lounge is equipped with satellite TV, blu-ray player, Nintendo Wii and wall-mounted 40” Samsung LCD TV. A well-equipped and cleverly designed galley kitchen features high-end integrated appliances to meet your every need, including a built-in double oven and sleek induction hob, full suite of cooking facilities and an integrated NEFF fridge with ice-box. A Nespresso machine and milk frother are provided for that much needed espresso or cappuccino to kick-start your day. And there is a washer dryer, so you can pack a little lighter! The newly renovated bathroom features a large walk-in rain shower with separate handheld spray. A chrome towel rail is complemented by a lit, motion-activated mirror cabinet featuring de-mist function and integrated razor/electric toothbrush socket. This gorgeous two-bedroom holiday home in central Bath is ranked in the ‘10 Best Holiday Homes in Bath’ by Booking.com and consistently rated positively by guests.
tagline: An exceptional two-bedroom luxury holiday home in central Bath

title: The Hollies
subtitle: The Hollies was built in 1851 in a meadow beside the old Bath – Wells turnpike.
bodyContent: The Hollies was built in 1851 in a meadow beside the old Bath – Wells turnpike. This was also the Fosse Way, built by the Roman Legions some 2000 years ago. The house, with its late Georgian facade, was once the home of the curate of St. Lukes Church, which is next door. It is now a gracious guest house with three individually designed rooms overlooking the award-winning garden. Every room has its own bath or shower room and is complete with television, radio alarm clock, hairdryer, bath robes and tea and coffee tray. Our comfortable Library with over 2000 books is available for guests.
tagline: The Hollies was built in 1851 in a meadow beside the old Bath – Wells turnpike.

title: The Bishop's Palace
subtitle: The Bishop’s Palace and Gardens in Wells has been home to the Bishops of Bath and Wells for over 800 years and this stunning medieval palace is now open for all to enjoy. It’s a great family day out in Somerset with a full programme of year-round events, free guided walks, open-air music and theatre, garden workshops and more and a slice of cake with afternoon tea at the ever-popular Bishop’s Table café is always welcome!
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Visit Highlights: There are 14 acres of outstanding RHS Partner gardens to explore (including the beautiful well pools from which the city takes its name), Dragon’s Lair play area, guided tours, children’s trails and workshops and a café with the best views in Wells! Multi media tours of the Palace building are also included with admission with the choice of an adult version or one tailored for a more family audience including quizzes, treasure hunts and talking Bishops from years gone by! Visitors are guided around the Palace buildings through five narrative themes using stories, music, imagery, quizzes and talking Bishops bringing stories of their tenure and legacy at the Palace to life in an interactive and engaging way. A year-round programme of themed family events is also included with admission including a Civil War Weekend; Archery, Vikings and more! Other events are ticketed separately including summer outdoor theatre; the Palace’s Garden Fair and History Live. The Bishop’s Palace dates from the early-thirteenth century when Bishop Jocelin Trotman received a crown licence to build a residence and deer park on land to the south of the Cathedral of St Andrew. Although home to the Bishop and other families, visitors can walk in the footsteps of past bishops through a number of rooms within the Palace. Visitors are also welcome to look around the Bishop’s private Chapel and explore the ruined Great Hall. The moat has been home to mute swans since the 1800s. The tradition of swans on the moat at The Bishop’s Palace in Wells is thought to go back to the 1850’s when it is likely that a Bishop’s daughter first taught the swans to ring a bell at the Gatehouse for food. We now have two swan bells – one just beneath the window on the left of the Gatehouse, the other to the right – both with a rope hanging down for the swans to pull. The Palace Gardens are open daily from 10am until 4pm in winter and 9.30am - 5.30pm in summer although there may be restricted access due to events and activities taking place (check the website for details). There are toilets on site. Guided tours are also included with Admission – check available times at the Ticket Office on arrival. Families: There’s so much for families to do at The Bishop’s Palace, whatever the weather. Little ones love to explore the gardens, trying to spot the swans and their cygnets; there are waterfalls and springs to see, trees to climb and places to hide. Children also love to explore the magical discovery area that is the Dragon’s Lair in a far corner of the Gardens! And throughout the school holidays, there are always plenty of events to keep families busy including crafting, outdoor gardening, family trails, storytelling and more. Refreshments: The Bishop’s Table café is open daily serving delicious, locally-sourced homemade food and some of the best coffee and cake you'll find in Wells. It’s the perfect place to meet friends for breakfast, lunch and afternoon teas or Sunday Lunches are now being served! Accessibility: From the main entrance of the Palace to the Palace building, around the gardens and to the café's dining area, there is level access. We have one lift to all floors of the Palace building. The outer gardens are accessible via a bridge which is 810mm wide. There are fully accessible toilets with level access within the Stableyard area and the Palace building. There are three spaces available on site for accessible parking, however, it is necessary to book these at least 48 hours before arrival via info@bishopspalace.org.uk or call 01749 988111.
tagline: The Bishop's Palace and Gardens, Wells, Somerset is a great family day out in Somerset.

title: Koffmann & Mr. White's
subtitle: The first joint venture between culinary legends, Pierre Koffmann and Marco Pierre White is the brasserie-style eatery Koffmann & Mr. White's.
bodyContent: The first joint venture between culinary legends, Pierre Koffmann and Marco Pierre White is the brasserie-style eatery Koffmann & Mr. White's. The brasserie is located in central Bath just around from Bath Abbey, the Roman Baths and only five minutes walk from Bath Spa train station. Serving a mix of English and French classics for the discerning customer looking for good quality, the restaurant offers French dishes such as Snails à la Bourguignonne and Poulet noir Grand-mère alongside English favourites like Shepherd's Pie and Fish and Chips. Affordable food is served in a relaxed, stylish and unpretentious environment befitting the Georgian surroundings.
tagline: The first joint venture between culinary legends, Pierre Koffmann and Marco Pierre White.

title: Walton’s Guest House
subtitle: Walton’s Guest House, providing warm and friendly accommodation in central Bath for over 25 years.
bodyContent: Walton’s Guest House, an oasis in the centre of Bath catering for Business and Tourism. Centrally located in Bath, this Guest House offers great facilities and a short walk to the Royal Crescent, Bath City Centre & the Royal Bath Spa Complex. All rooms are luxury en- suite and our rates include a hearty full English breakfast cooked to order. A family business for over 40 years, we aim to make your stay enjoyable and trouble free and can offer helpful advice on what to do and see in the city and surrounding area including seasonal local events. Bath offers a wide variety of attractions throughout the year and Walton’s is within easy walking distance of the Music Festival venues, the Theatre Royal including The Egg and the Ustinov Studio, the Roman Baths and Thermae Spa complex, the Museum of Costume, Bath Rugby at the Recreation Ground, the Jane Austen Festival, the Christmas Markets in the Abbey Churchyard and all City Centre Shops. For those walking the Cotswold Way, Walton’s offers a convenient overnight stay on the western edge of the city centre. There is a bus stop outside the front door, should you wish to take a day trip to Bristol, during your stay There is free on-street parking between 6.00pm and 8.00am and a public car park immediately behind the hotel. I have a couple of Parking Permits, providing all day on- street parking. Call or email for group bookings and for seasonal and midweek offers. ​ Bedrooms: 7 Bathrooms: 7 Children: Most Welcome Pets: No Onsite Parking: No - On street parking permits available
tagline: Walton’s Guest House, providing warm and friendly accommodation

title: The Bird
subtitle: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to. A place to work and meet and by day and discover ever-changing bar experiences by night.
bodyContent: To be found just a few minutes’ stroll from Bath’s spectacular city-centre attractions, The Bird, Bath (previously The County Hotel) has re-branded to fit in with its distinctive new personality as part of the Kaleidoscope Collection. Owned by seasoned hoteliers, Ian and Christa Taylor, The Bird is a name that better reflects the vibrant transformation of the hotel, which has already seen refreshed public spaces, additional bedrooms, a new bar, relaxed restaurant and meeting spaces, as well as a much-loved pop-up beach bar for summer. Now with 27 en-suite bedrooms featuring every home comfort, many have far-reaching views across the cricket and rugby grounds to Bath Abbey, with the rolling hills of Bath and beyond. Breakfast is served in a lovely bright dining room, which overlooks Bath Abbey and opens into the conservatory, where morning coffee and afternoon tea can be enjoyed, while the Taylors have also created a wonderfully eclectic neighbourhood bar with a relaxed food offering, designed as social hub for work or play. A space for freelancers to work, friends to meet for coffee or a relaxed dinner, there’s a bar for seasonal drinks and various seating areas centred around vast contemporary pieces of art. A separate meeting room also provides a creative space for workshops and get-togethers, private parties, celebrations and more. Visitors and locals alike won’t have to wait long for the next seasonal pop-up, a visually exciting Winter Wonderland for the festive season, and arguably the coolest party space in town. Set in a fantastical venue full of surprises, woodland branches and spruces will be strewn with fairy lights, tables topped with flickering candelabra and chairs draped in Bavarian rugs to keep you cosy. Everyone is welcome to simply drop in to experience the magical vibe. The Bird is easily reached via all main approaches to Bath, and has plenty of parking for guests.
tagline: A unique neighbourhood hotel where visitors to Bath migrate to

title: Little Paradise
subtitle: Little Paradise is an attractive detached 2 bedroom cottage accommodating four persons.
bodyContent: Little Paradise is a spacious and fully equipped holiday cottage set in peaceful rural surroundings close to Bath, Bristol & Wells. Because the cottage is double glazed, has full oil fired central heating and a log fireplace it is cosy and ideal for winter breaks. The cottage has two bedrooms (One Super-King and One Twin Single) and accommodates four persons. The cottage is Mobility 1 Graded. It has 3 steps with hand rail for access. It is on ground floor level and has no internal steps or stairs. Old Dairy has a private enclosed garden with furniture and a rotary washing line. The cottage has adjacent safe parking. Free use of all our facilities – Boules Court, Hot Tub, Sauna, Mini Gym, Barbecue Hut and Wi-Fi. Booking Little Paradise Fully flexible short breaks are available all year round. Visit our website for a live availability calendar and to download full details. Email or Phone us if you have any questions. A warm welcome awaits you at Greyfield Farm Cottages.
tagline: Little Paradise is an attractive detached 2 bedroom cottage accommodating four persons.

title: Abbey Rise
subtitle: Abbey Rise is a large Victorian terraced townhouse offering panoramic city views and guaranteed off road private parking throughout your stay. It is just an 8-minute stroll from the train and bus station and hub of the city.
bodyContent: Abbey Rise is a large Victorian terraced townhouse offering panoramic city views and guaranteed off road private parking throughout your stay. It is just an 8-minute stroll from the train and bus station and hub of the city. Bath is Katherine’s home town and after travelling around the world working in large prestigious hotels she was drawn back to this cosmopolitan and beautiful UNESCO city, where she decided to open up her own bed and breakfast. Living and working as part of the Royal Household at Buckingham Palace has left its mark and Katherine continues to maintain those standards in her own home, where guests are treated to crisply ironed sheets, fluffy towels and wonderfully comfortable beds whilst enjoying a homely and welcoming atmosphere. Katherine has been running Abbey Rise for a number of years now and frequently welcomes returning guests who will always find some new and interesting change or addition-though Katherine’s famous homemade brownies and cakes are always on the menu!
tagline: Abbey Rise is a large Victorian terraced townhouse offering panoramic city views

title: The Kennard
subtitle: The Kennard gives you the chance to discover and enjoy a stay in a true Georgian Town House.
bodyContent: The Kennard gives you the chance to discover and enjoy a stay in a true Georgian Town House, now restored to a boutique guesthouse. Built as a lodging house in 1794, The Kennard, today, offers twelve recently refurbished and individually decorated bedrooms, furnished for your every comfort, over five floors with a fine selection of superior doubles, standard doubles, snug doubles, two singles with shared bathroom, a twin and a triple room. Our rooms offer either a view over our garden and the city, or look out onto the street. We also have a small sitting area and an honesty bar located on the landings. Quietly situated only 5 minutes from the Abbey, the Roman Baths, the Thermae Spa and the railway station and some of the best restaurants and shopping venues our beautiful city has to offer. We hope you will stay with us and enjoy the experience of staying in one of Bath’s original Georgian townhouses with service and accommodation that truly reflects this beautiful city’s social history and culture.
tagline: The Kennard gives you the chance to discover and enjoy a stay in a true Georgian Town House.

subtitle: A favourite watering hole in the Bristol pub scene, The Bell is located at the bottom of Stokes Croft in central Bristol. This pub is full of character like its local area, with a graffiti mural along the outside wall, and some DJ decks in the corner for Friday and Saturday nights.
bodyContent: A favourite watering hole in the Bristol pub scene, The Bell is located at the bottom of Stokes Croft in central Bristol. This pub is full of character like its local area, with a graffiti mural along the outside wall, and some DJ decks in the corner for Friday and Saturday nights. The Bell serves up a great, honest Butcombe pint and the garden out the back becomes a great sun trap during the summer months. On Sunday the Bell’s traditional Sunday roast is a firm favourite with the locals. A range of local art now adorns the walls, and the toilet graffiti art has to be seen to be believed!

title: Waterhouse Guest House
subtitle: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath so once you have shopped till you are about to drop or taken the time to wonder along the local walking routes we have the perfect location set into the Midford Valley with country surroundings which ensures you will not be disturbed by the city noise or pace
bodyContent: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath so once you have shopped till you are about to drop or taken the time to wonder along the local walking routes we have the perfect location set into the Midford Valley with country surroundings which ensures you will not be disturbed by the city noise or pace. We have our own carpark, lift access, Bar, restaurant, conservatory, outside terrace and gardens place making Waterhouse a great place to work, rest, eat and play! We serve a selection of drinks which include local Beers, Ales, carefully selected wines and spirits to relax and unwind while taking in the stunning views across the Midford Valley. Our tranquil surroundings include the Midford Brook at the bottom of the property where we have fishing rights which people can use for a nominal fee, please enquire at reception should you like to make use of this exclusive facility. Across the Midford Valley there are stunning views and a selection of walks one of which is the two tunnels route which is one of the longest pedestrian tunnels in the UK. Other walks include the Kennet & Avon Canal. We are founded on Christian Values and aim to display the Love of Jesus to all who visit, please view the History of Waterhouse. Waterhouse is a 13 bedroom country house located in the idyllic and peaceful Midford valley 15 minutes south of Bath. Built around 1632, the house has been restored to provide bed and breakfast accommodation, meeting rooms and a venue for small events. All our bedrooms are located in the modern wing of the original house. We offer a choice of 8 double bedrooms, 1 twin room and 4 deluxe rooms, all en-suite.
tagline: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath

title: The Old Smithy Loft
subtitle: Our luxury 4 Star Gold self-catering apartment was once the workplace (smithy) of local blacksmiths.
bodyContent: Just two minutes walk from the Kennet and Avon Canal (good spot for cycle rental) which runs through Bath city centre and 10 minutes from Bath Abbey. THE OLD SMITHY LOFT This elegant first floor apartment is decorated in duck egg blue and cream throughout and is particularly relaxing as the Old Smithy is down a cul de sac, away from the hustle and bustle of Bath.Situated just off Bathwick Hill, your stroll in to town in Jane Austen’s footsteps takes you along iconic Pulteney Street, past Laura Square, along Pulteney Bridge, the only bridge with shops on in the UK and admire the weir. You will find yourself just beside the Abbey and the Guild Hall. Of course, you don’t need to go even that far to enjoy the historic features of Bath..the Holburne Museum, home of many Gainsboroughs and a lovely cafe and Sydney Gardens one of the Uk’s original pleasure Gardens are within 10 minutes walk. Newly converted, the large open plan fully equipped kitchen, dining and sitting area with ample room for 4 is ideal for relaxing after a day in Bath. The apartment sleeps up to 4 in 2 bedrooms with the option of kingsize double and single beds and a flat screen TV in each. All our beds gave luxury 1200 pocket sprung mattress and Egyptian cotton bed linen to ensure you have a very comfortable sleep. The bathroom has a full sized bath and a drench shower. PARKING This is free and immediately outside the door and is 3 metres (the standard car park size) wide. The neighbouring property has no rights over the car park area. MEDIA The Old Smithy Loft, 4 Star Gold luxury self catering also benefits from free Wifi, iPod docking staton, flat screen TV, games and books apart from the TVs in both bedrooms and in the sitting room. REWARD CARD In the apartment you will find full details of the Reward Card which entitles you to discounts at many restaurants, shops and attractions such as 3 hours for 2 at the Thermae Spa. THOSE LOOKING AFTER YOU Owned and managed by the Family Team…with a background in hospitality and having travelled all over, Ann, Nikki and Michael will all do their best to use their experience to make your stay enjoyable.
tagline: Our luxury 4 Star Gold self-catering apartment

title: Meadow Cottage
subtitle: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside.
bodyContent: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside on the edge of an area of outstanding natural beauty but only 5 miles from the world heritage city of Bath and 1 mile from the Saxon town of Bradford-on-Avon. Cumberwell Country Cottages are located on Great Cumberwell Farm, which has been in the James family since 1939 and was originally a dairy farm until 1992 when the herd was sold making way for a diversification into Cumberwell Park Golf Club, the farm itself has not changed a great deal and is still a working farm with over 300 acres of arable crop. bodyContent: 2 Crescent Gardens is a stylish guest house, which is close to the world famous Royal Crescent and within walking distance of all Bath’s main attractions. We reopened in June 2012 after a major refurbishment programme and we think you will be impressed by the results. bodyContent: The open-plan kitchen and living room is perfect for quiet nights in, after a day out exploring the area. The kitchen is equipped with everything you should need to make some delicious meals. The bedroom has a 4-poster bed. It is made up with fresh, white linen ready for your arrival. We provide a hand towel and bath towel per person. There is plenty of storage and hanging space. There is an en-suite bathroom, with a shower-head over the bath. On the other side of the patio is the Indoor Heated Pool and Games Room, which is available for our guests to use during their stay. Burys Cottage is locate on the edge of the village ‘Winsley’, 5 miles from Bath and 2 miles from Bradford on Avon. There are plenty of walks right from the doorstep, a Farm Shop, village shop and village pub all within 1 mile.

title: Bright private double bedroom

bodyContent: A quirky and comfortable double bedroom situated in a newly decorated and well equipped house just a fifteen minute walk away from the centre of Bath. This is one of four private rooms within the house. Situated in Oldfield park and very close to Oldfield Park Train Station and local buses, this is a perfect base for exploring Bath. There is a free car park just fifty meters from the house which is a truly rare find in Bath! The private double room benefits from use of a shared kitchen with breakfast bar. bodyContent: The Bower Inn is a beautiful 18th century building surrounded by a picturesque cottage garden on the outskirts of Bridgwater.
