title: The Pillars Restaurant & Lounge Bar
subtitle: Experience and enjoy the sophisticated atmosphere that Street's newest venue now offers. Set over two floors with a secluded alfresco terrace, the ground floor bar offers an extensive range of wines, Champagnes, beers, as well its own brand of home brewed craft ale. Pillars has been sympathetically refurbished to acknowledge its entertainment history throughout the decades.
bodyContent: Welcome to The Pillars Restaurant and Lounge Bar - an exciting new venue in the heart of Street We're quickly earning a reputation for one of the best venues in town. Set over two floors with a secluded alfresco terrace, our ground floor bar offers an extensive range of wines, Champagnes, beers, ales and ciders as well as our own brand of home brewed craft ale. Experience and enjoy the sophisticated atmosphere that Street's newest venue now offers. The Pillars has been sympathetically refurbished to acknowledge its entertainment history throughout the decades. History of The Site The beginning The building was built in 1920 for two local businessmen, Mr Voaks, a local butcher and Mr Hecks, the forerunner of the local Hecks cider farm. The doors first opened on 15th January, 1921 as "The Playhouse Theatre." The Playhouse had four changing rooms, a 20ft deep stage and a 26ft wide proscenium. The original proscenium arch can still be seen today above what is now the piano deck. The arched ceiling is an original pressed tin design. The transition The Playhouse Theatre gave way to the Playhouse Cinema as technology evolved and the big curtains gave way to the big screen. The age of the cinema The building retained the name "The Playhouse" for 25 years until July 1946, when it was renamed "Maximes Cinema". For over 40 years, the building enjoyed life as a cinema with a variety of owners including Cornell Cinemas until the mid 50's and then Myles Byrne Cinemas. Maximes had one screen and 561 seats. Many local Somerset people will recall watching their first film on the big screen and many we are sure will recall magical and memorable romantic interludes within the many rows! The end of the big screen Maximes cinema played its last film on 15th September 1989. The start of the nightclub After the cinema closed, the seats were removed to create large open spaces. The screen was taken down to create more depth to the building and the next phase of the building's life was born into Maximes Nightclub. Maximes traded as a night club for many years. In 2001, the club embarked on a major refurbishment and was re-born as "Envy". Most residents of Somerset refer to the building now as the 'Envy building'. Envy enjoyed being a popular destination for thousands of party-goers hosting many themed nights and live music presentations. In June 2015, the owner Adam Fynn, announced he was to relocate and set about plans to sell the building and applied for planning permission to develop the site into residential properties. The end of the night club era On 11th December 2016, the then operators of Envy announced that the club would close at the end of the year and on 31st December 2016, Envy Nighclub opened and closed its doors for the very last time. The building sat dormant, empty and cold for nearly four months before going to auction on 27th April 2017. The building failed to sell at auction and the doors at Envy remained closed. A new beginning The building was finally purchased by us in June 2017. The new owner vowed to preserve the historic building and return it to back to its former glory as an entertainment venue for the mid Somerset arena. Throughout the remainder of 2017 and into the first half of 2018, plans were made and relevant planning permissions granted to commence the transformation of the building into the Loft. Throughout the re-development of the site, we have been sympathetic to the buildings unique history as an entertainment venue. We have combined all its past into the future, with food, drink, entertainment and music, all under one roof! We are very proud of the achievements and of the building. We do hope that you enjoy your experience here and look forward to welcoming you back to Pillars again soon. The Management Facilities include: Facilities : Unrivalled Grill Menu Al fresco dining area Regular Live Music & Entertainment Our own craft ales and beers Over 45 wines from around the world Available for private hire Wedding Receptions Unrivalled Cocktail & Gin Bar Market Fresh Daily Food Christmas Parties Christenings Large Dance Floor
tagline: The Pillars Restaurant and Lounge Bar is an exciting venue in the heart of Street.

bodyContent: Arching over the ancient steps that lead from Roman Road down to Bath’s Artisan Quarter and Walcot Street, this listed building has been described as “like a Landmark Trust house but more beautiful.” Packed full of original features the house sleeps 8 in four double bedrooms and is spread over a total of 6 floors. Up to 2 extras sleep in comfortable day beds in the larger rooms. Awarded a special Gold by VisitBritain for 2018 / 19 and with the kitchen in the original vaults below street level you could not find a more original or characterful property for your special stay in Bath.

subtitle: Come and stay in our elegant Georgian home built by John Wood the younger in 1765. Ideally situated in our unique location between the World heritage Royal Crescent and The Circus.
bodyContent: Come and stay in our elegant Georgian home built by John Wood the younger in 1765. Ideally situated in our unique location between the World heritage Royal Crescent and The Circus. We are just a gentle walk from the centre of this beautiful Heritage City. All rooms have Freeview Television, Hair Dryers, Radio Alarm Clocks and Refreshment Tray. A free car parking permit is available as is complementary Wi-Fi in all rooms. Brocks Guest House has been awarded Four Stars in connection with AA Quality Standards. title: Beeches Farmhouse Self Catering Cottages
subtitle: The self catering cottages stand in the grounds of the idyllic 18th Beeches Farmhouse.
bodyContent: The self catering cottages stand in the grounds of the idyllic 18th Beeches Farmhouse, Bradford on Avon, near Bath having been tastefully converted from farm buildings and surrounded by open pasture with free range chickens, ducks, guinea fowl, English Setters and Shetland Ponies. Situated only a mile from the Saxon town of Bradford on Avon and seven miles from the World Heritage City of Bath. Each of the three, 2 bedroomed cottages has been imaginatively decorated with co-ordinated furnishings and rustic country furniture and those little extras not normally associated with a holiday cottage.
tagline: The self catering cottages stand in the grounds of the idyllic 18th Beeches Farmhouse.

title: The Hollies
subtitle: The Hollies was built in 1851 in a meadow beside the old Bath – Wells turnpike.
bodyContent: The Hollies was built in 1851 in a meadow beside the old Bath – Wells turnpike. This was also the Fosse Way, built by the Roman Legions some 2000 years ago. The house, with its late Georgian facade, was once the home of the curate of St. Lukes Church, which is next door. It is now a gracious guest house with three individually designed rooms overlooking the award-winning garden. Every room has its own bath or shower room and is complete with television, radio alarm clock, hairdryer, bath robes and tea and coffee tray. Our comfortable Library with over 2000 books is available for guests.
tagline: The Hollies was built in 1851 in a meadow beside the old Bath – Wells turnpike.

title: Southwest Tailored Tours (Bath)
subtitle: Why not get the most out of your visit to Bath and the South West with a professional guide. Every tour is individually tailored to suite your interests, fit in with your schedule and specific requirements.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. Why not get the most out of your visit to Bath and Somerset with a professional guide. Every tour is individually tailored to suite your interests, fit in with your schedule and specific requirements. Visit the Cathedrals and churches of the South West to learn about saints and sinners, bishops, builders and bodies, as well as admiring the fabric of these beautiful buildings. Tour the great landscape gardens of the region and learn about their creators. See the influence of the Arts and Craft movement in gardens, houses, churches in the area. Walking tours are an excellent way to get to know a city. Every town has its stories and a guided tour will fill the streets with life.
tagline: Why not get the most out of your visit to Bath and the South West with a professional guide.

title: The Bowl Inn
subtitle: This traditional inn is a little gem tucked away in the village of Almondsbury, taking its name from the shape of the land surrounding the Severn estuary, which can be seen from the inn.
bodyContent: This traditional inn is a little gem tucked away in the village of Almondsbury, taking its name from the shape of the land surrounding the Severn estuary, which can be seen from the inn. You'll find plenty of thick stone walls, rustic beams and cosy fires ready to roar in the winter and sunny patios for the warmer months, as well as 12 en-suite rooms for you to enjoy. Whether you're after a thirst quenching pint, a meal or even somewhere to lay your head for the night, The Bowl Inn is perfectly placed for you.
tagline: This traditional inn is a little gem tucked away in the village of Almondsbury

title: Lasseter's
subtitle: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion. It serves locally sourced dishes created by a team of professional chefs.
bodyContent: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion. It serves locally sourced dishes created by a team of professional chefs. The restaurant focuses on bringing high-quality dining and great-value food to Weston, and is quickly gaining a reputation for excellent food, atmosphere and welcoming service. The restaurant boasts stunning views of Weston-super-Mare’s bay, as well as exciting menus that are based around fresh ingredients. It serves lunch and dinner from Wednesday to Saturday – including special set lunch menus and early-bird pre-theatre offers – and a carvery on Sundays from noon. Lasseter’s also serves an extensive range of cocktails, spirits and wines, with over 100 drinks to choose from. The wine list has been hand-selected by the restaurant manager, with a variety of different types and styles for all tastes. There is something for everyone at Lasseter’s. You can relax in the bar or on the terrace – with a snack if, you fancy – or enjoy a meal in our glorious restaurant overlooking the seafront.
tagline: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion.

title: The Apartment, Bath
subtitle: An exceptional two-bedroom luxury holiday home in central Bath, loved by guests for its perfect location, stylish decor, comfort, cleanliness and first class self-catering accommodation.
bodyContent: From Nespresso to Nintendo, The Apartment, Bath is an excellently-located two-bedroom apartment in central Bath. The first bedroom is a large, bright double bedroom with king size bed (or twin beds on request). The open fireplace and large sash windows are elegant original features and south-facing views take in the length of Ralph Allen Drive and Widcombe Hill. At the rear of the property, the second bedroom is a well-proportioned double bedroom, featuring a comfy double bed, original fireplace and built in wardrobe. The homely lounge is flooded with light from the large, original south-facing 16-pane sash window. The room hosts an extendable dining table and chairs, designer sofa (which can convert to a sofa bed) and a feature armchair. Brimming with technology, the lounge is equipped with satellite TV, blu-ray player, Nintendo Wii and wall-mounted 40” Samsung LCD TV. A well-equipped and cleverly designed galley kitchen features high-end integrated appliances to meet your every need, including a built-in double oven and sleek induction hob, full suite of cooking facilities and an integrated NEFF fridge with ice-box. A Nespresso machine and milk frother are provided for that much needed espresso or cappuccino to kick-start your day. And there is a washer dryer, so you can pack a little lighter! The newly renovated bathroom features a large walk-in rain shower with separate handheld spray. A chrome towel rail is complemented by a lit, motion-activated mirror cabinet featuring de-mist function and integrated razor/electric toothbrush socket. This gorgeous two-bedroom holiday home in central Bath is ranked in the ‘10 Best Holiday Homes in Bath’ by Booking.com and consistently rated positively by guests.

bodyContent: A bright and comfortable loft bedroom situated in a newly decorated and well equipped house just a fifteen minute walk away from the centre of Bath. A comfortable living space in the centre of the house, with an extensive library of books for both the avid and casual reader. I like to give guests their own space during their stay, however I am always available to offer recommendations and help, both before and during their stay. title: The Circus Apartment
subtitle: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses.
bodyContent: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the secluded private garden to the rear. With the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minutes walk The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the secluded private garden to the rear. With the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minutes walk. This contemporary apartment, in a warm palate of chocolate, plum and biscuit throughout, has undergone several transformations in its lifetime yet has retained all its period charm. The large sitting and dining room with sash windows overlooking two aspects of The Circus has two French style velvet sofas by a decorative fireplace. There is a TV with Blue Ray DVD and a separate radio with I-pod docking. A dining table seats four and a French style dresser contains crockery, cutlery and a selection of novels, films and games. The neat fitted period kitchen has an electric hob and oven, a microwave, a large fridge/freezer, and a dishwasher.. A large mirrored lobby before the bedroom which has fitted wardrobes and shelving leads to the spacious and comfortable bedroom which has a 6′ bed, a fitted wardrobe, a dressing table with storage and a tallboy and a cupboard containing a washer/dryer machine. A radio/alarm with I-pod docking is provided. The contemporary bathroom has smart cappuccino coloured tiling and contains a double ended bath with shower over, a hand basin with lots of storage under and a WC. The apartment has gas central heating, hair dryer, iron, microwave, dishwasher, towels and toiletries. A Free car parking permit is available as is free internet access.
tagline: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle

bodyContent: Arching over the ancient steps that lead from Roman Road down to Bath’s Artisan Quarter and Walcot Street, this listed building has been described as “like a Landmark Trust house but more beautiful.” Packed full of original features the house sleeps 8 in four double bedrooms and is spread over a total of 6 floors. title: Midford Mill
subtitle: A Grade II Listed Mill House situated in a country location on the southern outskirts of Bath.
bodyContent: The ground floor living area provides an extremely comfortable and functional space for 10 people. Entertainment is provided by two 50″ HDTVs, with a fantastic woodburner to the main reception room. Comfortable sofas and armchairs provide relaxing seating. For meal times there is a large wooden table in the dining room together with a cosy ‘lookout’ seating area that overlooks the mill weir. There is a fully equipped kitchen with AGA, additional induction hob, dishwasher, fridge-freezer, microwave, toaster, coffee machine and kettle. The space is also practical with plenty of coat hooks and a boot rack, waste bin and recycling containers in the utility area. Upstairs there are very comfortable Vi-Spring beds with crisp white cotton bedding and fluffy towels are provided. There are 4 very large bedrooms that all have beautiful views over the river and countryside beyond. On the first floor there is a a family bathroom, and two bedrooms: one bedroom has a Kingsize bed and the second bedroom has a king and single bed. On the second floor there is the master bedroom with Superking bed and the second bedroom has a double and single bed. The rooms are connected by a very large landing where a small sofa and light have been placed, which is great space for those looking for a quiet place to chill out. All rooms have a minimalist feel and are finished with hand-made linen roman blinds. Bathroom, Shower-room and facilities: The mid-floor bathroom is very large with the usual toilet, washbasin and large free-standing teardrop bath. Downstairs there is a modern wet-room with large shower area. For convenience a washing machine, separate tumble dryer, iron, ironing board, travel cot and hairdryer are provided. Externally: There is a fantastic (120 m2) patio in-between the mill-house and the river and over 3/4 acre of gardens that include river fishing rights, an island and a large lawn. For more information or to enquire about your preferred dates, please contact us today . Please use code MB19-10OFF at the Availability Page to gain a 10% discount.
tagline: A Grade II Listed Mill House situated in a country location on the southern outskirts of Bath.

title: 18 The Circus
subtitle: City Centre - 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character.
bodyContent: 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character. The maisonette that occupies the top two floors of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the northern Lansdown slopes of stunning terraces of Georgian houses, and with the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minute’s walk. Access is via a communal hallway and carpeted staircase that leads to the maisonette’s front door on the second floor. Inside is a small hall, off which sits the spacious and airy sitting room that is tastefully and comfortably furnished and decorated and being south facing, is very light. On this floor is also a large fitted kitchen with dining table and chairs. A mezzanine room houses the washing machine and dryer for exclusive use of visitors to this home. The stairs on this floor lead to a well-lit landing, off which lie the bedrooms. The front bedroom is a very large room with a double bed and conveniently, a single bed for family use. This brightly furnished bedroom also has an en-suite shower room. The second bedroom has twin beds and is next door to a family sized bathroom with bath, shower-in-bath, basin, WC and airing cupboard. The property contains gas central heating, gas hob, gas double oven, fridge, dishwasher, washing machine and dryer, microwave, TV in lounge and master bedroom, video, stereo, towels and toiletries. Free Car Parking Permit available Free Unlimited fiber broadband Please note: the house is a listed 4 story Georgian townhouse and as such does not have an elevator. Find out more here.
tagline: City Centre - 18 The Circus is a self-catering property with character.

title: Walk Minehead to Brean
subtitle: Explore some of Somerset’s superb coast with a walk along part or all of the new 58-mile route that is the latest addition to the National Coast Path.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. From glorious beaches to amazing wildlife, historical delights to geological marvels, the Somerset stretch of the England Coast Path offers walkers of all levels - from holidaymakers and families to serious walking enthusiasts - the chance to explore, relax and enjoy some of Britain's most unusual and beautiful coastal scenery. Starting from the genteel Victorian resort of Minehead and walking east towards the natural promontory of Brean Down, you will pass a medieval village , alabaster rocks, an ancient harbour, a stunning waterfall , limestone pavements, saltmarshes, sand dunes and a lighthouse on legs. For more info click here
tagline: Explore some of Somerset’s superb coast with a walk along part or all of the new 58-mile route.

title: Dunster Circular
subtitle: This walk takes you from the shingle beach at Dunster up to the magnificent medieval village with its yarn market and topped off with a castle.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. This walk takes you from the shingle beach at Dunster up to the magnificent medieval village with its yarn market and topped off with a castle. Originally “Dunn’s Torre”, a craggy fortification overlooking the Bristol Channel, the settlement was given by William the Conqueror gave to the powerful de Mohun family to build a castle to protect the coast. In 1375 the feudal barony was purchased by the Luttrell family who owned the Castle until 1976 when it was gifted to the National Trust. Having explored the streets and shops, the walk takes you past the heritage railway station back to the beach along the riverside. Click here for more information
tagline: This walk takes you from the shingle beach at Dunster up to the magnificent medieval village.

subtitle: The Pelly, as it's fondly referred to by locals, is set in the centre of Chew Magna in the beautiful Somerset countryside.
bodyContent: The Pelly, as it's fondly referred to by locals, is set in the centre of Chew Magna in the beautiful Somerset countryside. This well-loved pub boasts a top notch food offering which will keep you enticed through every course. With a fabulous wine list and even better selection of Butcombe beers on the bar, there's something to tickle even the most refined taste buds. Come rain or shine, you can choose from cosy log fires or their stunning sun trap to while away your hours with friends and loved ones. The Barn: As well as hosting regular events in their function room, their private space is available for meetings, parties, baby showers, intimate wedding receptions and more. Contact them directly to check availability for your event or special day. As part of the Butcombe Estate of pubs and Inns, The Pelican Inn prides itself on serving quality cask ales and locally sourced food, in a unique setting.
tagline: The Pelly, as it's fondly referred to by locals, is set in the centre of Chew Magna

title: The Old Smithy Loft
subtitle: Our luxury 4 Star Gold self-catering apartment was once the workplace (smithy) of local blacksmiths.
bodyContent: Just two minutes walk from the Kennet and Avon Canal (good spot for cycle rental) which runs through Bath city centre and 10 minutes from Bath Abbey. THE OLD SMITHY LOFT This elegant first floor apartment is decorated in duck egg blue and cream throughout and is particularly relaxing as the Old Smithy is down a cul de sac, away from the hustle and bustle of Bath.Situated just off Bathwick Hill, your stroll in to town in Jane Austen’s footsteps takes you along iconic Pulteney Street, past Laura Square, along Pulteney Bridge, the only bridge with shops on in the UK and admire the weir. You will find yourself just beside the Abbey and the Guild Hall. Of course, you don’t need to go even that far to enjoy the historic features of Bath..the Holburne Museum, home of many Gainsboroughs and a lovely cafe and Sydney Gardens one of the Uk’s original pleasure Gardens are within 10 minutes walk. Newly converted, the large open plan fully equipped kitchen, dining and sitting area with ample room for 4 is ideal for relaxing after a day in Bath. The apartment sleeps up to 4 in 2 bedrooms with the option of kingsize double and single beds and a flat screen TV in each. All our beds gave luxury 1200 pocket sprung mattress and Egyptian cotton bed linen to ensure you have a very comfortable sleep. The bathroom has a full sized bath and a drench shower. PARKING This is free and immediately outside the door and is 3 metres (the standard car park size) wide. The neighbouring property has no rights over the car park area. MEDIA The Old Smithy Loft, 4 Star Gold luxury self catering also benefits from free Wifi, iPod docking staton, flat screen TV, games and books apart from the TVs in both bedrooms and in the sitting room. REWARD CARD In the apartment you will find full details of the Reward Card which entitles you to discounts at many restaurants, shops and attractions such as 3 hours for 2 at the Thermae Spa. THOSE LOOKING AFTER YOU Owned and managed by the Family Team…with a background in hospitality and having travelled all over, Ann, Nikki and Michael will all do their best to use their experience to make your stay enjoyable.
tagline: Our luxury 4 Star Gold self-catering apartment was once the workplace

title: Number 14 York Street
subtitle: Number 14 York Street is a fashionable former city centre merchants house, now owned by an artist.
bodyContent: Number 14 York Street is a fashionable city centre former merchants house, now owned by an artist. It is superbly situated in the very heart of historic Bath! Bath’s most significant tourist attractions – the Roman Baths, the Bath Abbey, the Thermae Spa – are all within 200m.The train and bus stations are 4/5 minutes walk. Car parking is available. Please see our website www.yorkstreetbath.co.uk The house has been renovated to the highest standards and stylishly combines period detail with contemporary fittings. The luxurious 4* accommodation is arranged over 3 floors. You will find plenty of space to sleep 4 adults in two bedroom suites (one with king bed and adjoining luxury bathroom -the other with twin beds and adjoining luxury monsoon shower room) . Each room has a flat screen TV/DVD . As you would expect there is an ultra-modern kitchen with dishwasher, freezer and washing machine. You will find a comfortable living/dining room. Internet (wifi) access is provided. Original art works hang in every room. If you are looking for an eclectic mix of a grade 2 listed dwelling combined with every modern facility right in the centre of Bath then this is the place for you!
tagline: Number 14 York Street is a fashionable former city centre merchants house

title: The White Guest House
subtitle: Steve and Anna Wynne welcome you to The White Guest House, a level 7 minutes’ walk from the centre of Bath.
bodyContent: Steve and Anna Wynne welcome you to The White Guest House, a level 7 minutes’ walk from the centre of Bath, Bath Spa train station, Bath coach station and the Kennet & Avon Canal. Bath Abbey,Thermae .Spa We take pride in our flower display and have been a Bath in Bloom winner.
tagline: Steve and Anna Wynne welcome you to The White Guest House

title: Walton’s Guest House
subtitle: Walton’s Guest House, providing warm and friendly accommodation in central Bath for over 25 years.
bodyContent: Walton’s Guest House, an oasis in the centre of Bath catering for Business and Tourism. Centrally located in Bath, this Guest House offers great facilities and a short walk to the Royal Crescent, Bath City Centre & the Royal Bath Spa Complex. All rooms are luxury en- suite and our rates include a hearty full English breakfast cooked to order. A family business for over 40 years, we aim to make your stay enjoyable and trouble free and can offer helpful advice on what to do and see in the city and surrounding area including seasonal local events. Bath offers a wide variety of attractions throughout the year and Walton’s is within easy walking distance of the Music Festival venues, the Theatre Royal including The Egg and the Ustinov Studio, the Roman Baths and Thermae Spa complex, the Museum of Costume, Bath Rugby at the Recreation Ground, the Jane Austen Festival, the Christmas Markets in the Abbey Churchyard and all City Centre Shops. For those walking the Cotswold Way, Walton’s offers a convenient overnight stay on the western edge of the city centre. There is a bus stop outside the front door, should you wish to take a day trip to Bristol, during your stay There is free on-street parking between 6.00pm and 8.00am and a public car park immediately behind the hotel. I have a couple of Parking Permits, providing all day on- street parking. Call or email for group bookings and for seasonal and midweek offers. ​ Bedrooms: 7 Bathrooms: 7 Children: Most Welcome Pets: No Onsite Parking: No - On street parking permits available
tagline: Walton’s Guest House, providing warm and friendly accommodation

title: Kilve Circular
subtitle: This circular walk will take you on a journey around the picturesque village of Kilve and its lovely beach, where the ancient limestone has been carved over millions of years into glorious geometric patterns.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. Youngsters will be able to play in the rock pools and look out for ammonites and other fossils which litter this part of the Jurassic coast. Historians and geologists have been studying Kilve for generations and it is mentioned in the Domesday Book in 1086 as Clive (probably meaning cliff), after the amazing cliffs that dominate the area. For more info click here
tagline: This circular walk will take you on a journey around the picturesque village of Kilve.

title: The Ostrich
subtitle: Perched on the edge of the historic Bristol harbourside, The Ostrich sits proudly with its large pub garden and stunning interior to match.
bodyContent: Perched on the edge of the historic Bristol harbourside, The Ostrich sits proudly with its large pub garden and stunning interior to match. Enjoy traditional British pub classics from its dining menu, or Americana style street food from the iconic Airstream parked out front. Pair award-winning beers perfectly with small plates or explore the extensive rum menu, a nod to its roots as a dock-side inn where sailors, merchants and dock-workers once drank.
tagline: Perched on the edge of the historic Bristol harbourside

title: The Paragon Townhouse
subtitle: The Paragon is a wondrously quirky Georgian Townhouse located in the bustling heart of historic Bath.
bodyContent: Arching over the ancient steps that lead from Roman Road down to Bath’s Artisan Quarter and Walcot Street, this listed building has been described as “like a Landmark Trust house but more beautiful.” Packed full of original features the house sleeps 8 in four double bedrooms and is spread over a total of 6 floors. Up to 2 extras sleep in comfortable day beds in the larger rooms. Awarded a special Gold by VisitBritain for 2018 / 19 and with the kitchen in the original vaults below street level you could not find a more original or characterful property for your special stay in Bath.
tagline: The Paragon is a wondrously quirky Georgian Townhouse

title: Oak Tree Cottage
subtitle: Oak Tree Cottage has been created over Winter 2015/2016 and is now a lovely light two bedroomed, two bathroomed holiday home.
bodyContent: It has a ground floor twin bedroom and bathroom, a lounge/diner with separate kitchen and a second floor with huge double bedroom and en-suite bathroom. It also has the benefit of an extra “snug” style TV room – perfect for children to watch TV and play games. A vaulted ceiling theme runs through Oak Tree’s 1st floor bedroom and it has lovely roof windows with views. Outside of the cottage is a shared lawned paddock and an open air solar heated swimming pool. There is plenty of on-site parking available at the farm and our own little farm shop/butchery for all your breakfast needs! Next door to Oak Tree is its “sister” property, Walnut Tree.
tagline: Oak Tree Cottage has been created over Winter 2015/2016 and is now a lovely two bedroom cottage

title: The Windsor Townhouse
subtitle: Location, location, location. Just two minutes’ walk to the city centre, tourist attractions, shops and restaurants, The Windsor perfect choice for both leisure and business guests.
bodyContent: Location, location, location. Just two minutes’ walk to the city centre, tourist attractions, shops and restaurants, The Windsor perfect choice for both leisure and business guests. With 15 individually styled ensuite bedrooms with period features and stunning views over one of the finest boulevards in Europe to the front and the green space of the Recreation Ground to the rear. Room facilities include complimentary WIFI, flat screen televisions, air conditioning and hostess tray. Luxury soft fluffy towels, cosy dorma duvets, feather pillows and White Company toiletries complete the package and add to the guest experience. Acclaimed for our warm and friendly staff, we are always ready with a smile and happy to help with anything from restaurant suggestions to planning your onward journey. We pride ourselves in our customer service and along with our award winning breakfasts, our aim is to send you home with a desire to return.
tagline: Location, location, location. Just two minutes’ walk to the city centre

title: Brean Down Circular
subtitle: Brean Down is a promontory of the Mendips Hills extending 1.5 miles out into the Bristol Channel at the eastern end of Bridgwater Bay with views over to the two small islands of Steep Holm and Flat Holm.
bodyContent: The walk takes you around the Down where people have lived, worked and fought since the Bronze Age. Archaeological highlights include the remains on an ancient Roman-Celtic temple and a Victorian fort. Brean Down is also rich in wildlife and is a Site of Special Scientific Interest for both its geological significance and the presence of nationally rare plants including the white rock-rose. For more Info click here
tagline: Brean Down is a promontory of the Mendips Hills.

title: The Methuen Arms
subtitle: Maddy and Leigh welcome you to The Methuen Arms, an award winning Great British inn where hospitality meets fabulous food & drink at a relaxed pace.
bodyContent: Maddy and Leigh welcome you to The Methuen Arms, an award winning Great British inn where hospitality meets fabulous food & drink at a relaxed pace. Set immediately beside the stately home and beautiful grounds of Corsham Court, and just eight miles from the enchanting city of Bath, Corsham is a hidden gem of charming Georgian buildings, cobbled streets, Almshouses, parkland and more, making this historic market town a must-see place to visit and stay.
tagline: Maddy and Leigh welcome you to The Methuen Arms

title: Tucking Mill View, luxury self-catering cottage
subtitle: Tucking Mill View is a luxury self-catering cottage with outstanding views over the Midford/Tucking Mill valley, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty all on one level.
bodyContent: A real home from home, this self-catering cottage is ideal for those holidaymakers who wish to combine the country with the city… Newly renovated and maintained to the highest standard Tucking Mill View has been awarded the coveted 4 Star Gold Award for Exceptional Accommodation and Welcome by Visit England. TUCKING MILL VIEW ACCOMMODATION The single storey luxury self-catering cottage is 66 metres square…with a large open plan sitting room, with a 3 seater sofa and a snuggle sofa (which can double as a single sofa bed) and a modern fully equipped kitchen with washing machine and full size dishwasher. The calmly appointed bedroom in cream and turquoise has a luxury 1400 sprung king sized bed, with top quality Egyptian cotton bed linen. The only noise likely to waken you are the owls in the tree tops. For those balmy evenings, the private patio overlooking the valley is an ideal spot ..with a stone built barbecue and table and chairs you can enjoy every meal without being disturbed. Being so close to Bath, Tucking Mill View is the perfect balance for relaxing and unwinding as well as exploring the beauties of the Bath and wandering in the Somerset and Wiltshire countryside. As well as the gold Award for exceptional welcome, Visit England have also awarded the cottage the Cyclists’ and Walkers’ Welcome Awards and the cottage is an ideal centre for waling and cycling, particularly with he newly opened Two Tunnel Route into Bath..Sustrans 24 which passes by the cottage. AROUND AND ABOUT This secluded hamlet takes its name from the process of ‘tucking’ ,a process for cleansing wool, was undertaken. Being halfway between the historic villages of Midford and Monkton Combe, Tucking Mill benefits from access to two independent gastro pubs both within a 15 minute walk along the lanes, serving delicious home cooked food at evening and lunch times. The famous community pub, the Packhorse in South Stoke is a lovely 30 minute walk up the valley. MEDIA FACILITIES Facilities include free wifi , iPod docking station, flatscreen TV and DVD in the living room. Being so close to Bath, Tucking Mill View is the perfect balance for relaxing and unwinding as well as exploring the beauties of the Bath and wandering in the Somerset and Wiltshire countryside. PARKING Free private parking space for 2 cars is provided immediately outside the entrance to the cottage. REWARD CARD The benefits of the Reward Card with special discounts and extras like 3 hours for 2 in the Thermal span and 10% off entrance to the Roman Baths are available to all guests. Just look at the Reward website for more details. ABOUT TUCKING MILL SELFCATERING Tucking Mill view is one of the five 4 Star Luxury Gold properties int he Tucking Mill Self Catering portfolio owned by Michael and Ann. There are tow apartness in the city centre – the Old smithy Loft and No 2 Hedgemead court and a further two cottages in the vicinity of Tucking Mill, Midford….Brooks’ View and Fishermen’s Retreat, in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. THOSE LOOKING AFTER YOU The property is managed by the Family Team ..with Ann who has a background in hospitality and done much travelling, Michael who built the barbecues and cares of the birds and the gardens and Head Housekeepr Nikki, the team will do its utmost to ensure you enjoy your stays. You will also likely meet Rob our invaluable man of all trades. We all hope you enjoy your stay.
tagline: Tucking Mill View is a luxury self-catering cottage with outstanding views

title: Three Abbey Green
subtitle: A Grade II listed city centre Georgian building, parts of which date back to 1689, Three Abbey Green (including the Jane Austen Wing next door) is a Four Star Gold Award bed and breakfast.
bodyContent: A Grade II listed city centre Georgian building, parts of which date back to 1689, Three Abbey Green (including the Jane Austen Wing next door) is a Four Star Gold Award bed and breakfast, hidden away in a quiet cobbled square in the heart of central Bath. A stone’s throw from Bath Abbey and the Roman Baths, everything you could wish to see is on your doorstep. We think Three Abbey Green is one of the most beautiful buildings in Bath, a city overflowing with Georgian grandeur and astonishing architecture. We never cease to be excited about running our family business in Abbey Green. It is rare to find such a beautiful, almost pedestrian-only square in the heart of a city. It should be remembered, however, that we are in the centre of a vibrant city and pedestrians are not always as quiet as we might like them to be! The main house has seven rooms (including two large suites ideal for families or groups) and the associated Jane Austen Wing in Four Abbey Green, adjacent to the main house, has three rooms, each with its own character and unique charm. Three Abbey Green is a family business started in 2002 by Derek and Sue. From the beginning, the ethos of the business has always been to provide the highest standard of accommodation combined with excellent customer service, reflecting our own expectations. Nici took over the reins in 2010 with her husband Alan. They also have a child, Finlay, and a dog called Bear, but they still aim to balance provision of excellent service with a normal, busy family life. It is a point of pride for us to maintain our high standards without compromising the personal touch that brings guests back to stay with us again and again.
tagline: A Grade II listed city centre Georgian building, parts of which date back to 1689

title: Old Dairy
subtitle: The Old Dairy is a spacious and tastefully furnished fully equipped cottage set in quiet, peaceful surroundings.
bodyContent: The Old Dairy is a spacious and tastefully furnished fully equipped holiday cottage set in peaceful rural surroundings close to Bath, Bristol & Wells. Because the cottage is double glazed, has full oil fired central heating and a log fireplace it is cosy and ideal for winter breaks. The cottage is on ground floor level and has no internal steps or stairs. It has a private patio area with garden furniture and a rotary washing line. The cottage has adjacent safe parking. Free use of all our facilities – Boules Court, Hot Tub, Sauna, Mini Gym, Barbecue Hut and Wi-Fi. Booking Old Dairy Fully flexible short breaks are available all year round. Visit our website for a live availability calendar and to download full details. Email or Phone us if you have any questions. A warm welcome awaits you at Greyfield Farm Cottages.
tagline: The Old Dairy is a spacious and tastefully furnished fully equipped cottage

title: Apple Tree Guest House
subtitle: Ling welcomes you to her Victorian period home in the centre of Bath
bodyContent: A World Heritage City with Roman roots, a medieval abbey and stunning Georgian architecture. Bath is located in the Cotswolds, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The Apple Tree is a 5 minute stroll to the city centre and a 10 minute level walk from the train station. We offer complimentary off-site permit parking in front of the house in a quiet residential location. All rooms are individually themed with an elegant blend of English and Asian artwork where East meets West, fresh cotton bedlinen and modern facilities.
tagline: Ling welcomes you to her Victorian period home in the centre of Bath

title: St Audries Bay
subtitle: The circular walk centred on St Audries Beach is ideal for families as it has plenty to stir the imagination with interesting rock patterns – natural and man-made – an incredible waterfall, fossils and sea creatures.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. Look out for the Blue Lias pavements and Devonian red sandstone. It is important to be aware of the tide times when planning a visit. For more info click here
tagline: The circular walk centred on St Audries Beach is ideal for families.

title: The Lime Kiln
subtitle: The Lime Kiln is a traditional 17th century freehouse situated in the village of Knole in Somerset.
bodyContent: The Lime Kiln is a traditional 17th century freehouse situated in the village of Knole in Somerset. You can expect a wealth of home cooked food and real ales in a pub full of character and charm. The Lime Kiln has been fully restored to its original glory with settles, antique furniture and old pictures of local village scenes and includes a large dining room and an impressive inglenook fireplace.
tagline: The Lime Kiln is a traditional 17th century freehouse situated in the village of Knole in Somerset.

title: Vellum Stone Cottage
subtitle: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway.
bodyContent: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway – indoor pool and games room on site, Kennet and Avon Canal Close by (3/4 of a mile), walking and cycling from your doorstep. Farm Shop and country pub(s) within walking distance. The cottage features a country feel with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams, with soft furnishings compliment. Enjoy admiring the sheep in the fields surrounding the farm.
tagline: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway.

title: Toghill House Farm
subtitle: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds. Within a stone’s throw of the site of the battle of Lansdown and with the Cotswold Way and the old east to west Roman road running through the grounds, Toghill is steeped in history.
bodyContent: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds. Within a stone’s throw of the site of the battle of Lansdown and with the Cotswold Way and the old east to west Roman road running through the grounds, Toghill is steeped in history. Located on a working farm only 4 miles north of Bath, with spectacular views over the Welsh mountains, Mendips, Cotswolds and Historic Bath. We have 9 rooms, some of which are in the 17th century farmhouse and others in the pretty Cotswold stone converted barns and stables in a delightful courtyard setting.
tagline: Toghill House stands on the very edge of the Cotswolds.

title: Watchet, Washford along the Old Mineral Line
subtitle: The Watchet to Washford walk along the Old Mineral Line is ideal for keen walkers and families. There is loads to see and do in beautiful Watchet.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. The Watchet to Washford walk along the Old Mineral Line is ideal for keen walkers and families. This is a moderate to difficult walk in places, with steps, steep climbs and some uneven surfaces, although it is stile free. There is loads to see and do in beautiful Watchet, including taking a trip from the town’s picturesque station on the West Somerset Railway. Museums include the fascinating Market House Museum with its tales of kings, queens, murderous knights and pirates and the Boat Museum which houses an intriguing collection of local flat bottomed boats. The town is also packed with independent shops and art galleries including Contains Art, a gallery and studios in converted shipping containers on the quayside. For more information click here .
tagline: This is a moderate to difficult walk in places.

title: The Lamb Inn
subtitle: Located in the beautiful Cheddar Valley market town of Axbridge.
bodyContent: Located in the beautiful Cheddar Valley market town of Axbridge, the Lamb is a great, traditional English pub. Dating back to 1480, the Lamb has all the features you’d expect from a pub just shy of 600 years old – low beams, open fireplaces and country bric-a-brac on its walls. The Lamb serves up traditional pub food, delicious cask ale and is the perfect place to stop by after a country walk nearby. The Lamb is the focal point of the town, situated in the heart of the square, and opposite the famous King John’s Hunting Lodge.
tagline: Located in the beautiful Cheddar Valley market town of Axbridge.

title: Whitley Coach House
subtitle: Whitley Coach House is a truly luxurious self-contained 1804 Georgian built.
bodyContent: Recently modernised stone coach house providing self-catering accommodation for long, short or one night stays. Whitley Coach House is an ideal base from which to visit Bath, Lacock, Longleat, Bowood House, Stonehenge, National Trust properties and many other local attractions. Only 20 minutes from Bath and 5 Minutes from Lacock – 10-minute walk to a great Pub/Resturant and local shop/cafe, free fast Wi-Fi, 40″ smart TV with Netflix and free private parking. Private garden with teak furniture on wooden decking. With luxurious bedding including a handmade king size Lit Bateau bed with a Vi-Spring luxuriously comfortable handmade mattress. Immediate and live AVAILABILITY. Accepting: American Express plus most credit and debit cards. Whitley Coach House self-catering accommodation has a large bedroom with a super king-size (5ft 6ins x 6ft 6ins) Lit Bateau oak bed designed and handmade with a supremely comfortable Vi-Spring handmade pocket sprung mattress. The living room has high ceilings with exposed beams and includes two three-seater sofas one with a large double pull-out bed. In addition, there is a luxurious deep sprung folding bed for use in the bedroom or entrance hall. ONLINE BOOKING or do look at our Website: www.whitleycoachhouse.co.uk The Space Whitley Coach House is a detached former coach house to a Georgian house, renovated four years ago and just redecorated, providing spacious self-catering accommodation. Whitley Coach House has a large bedroom with an individually designed and handmade kingsize bateau bed designed and handmade in oak, with a supremely comfortable Vi-Spring pocket sprung mattress. The living room has high ceilings with exposed beams and a solid oak floor and includes two three-seater sofas one with a large super king size pull-out bed. title: Old Stables
subtitle: The Old Stables is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.
bodyContent: It is located in the beautiful Georgian village of Freshford which lies at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys in the southern Cotswolds. There are some wonderful walks to local pubs following the riverside and canals. All just 15 minutes from Bath by car but the secret of this location is the 9 minute train journey to Bath from the village station, just a short stroll from the cottages. A three bedroom cottage (two king and one twin-bed)with a fully equipped kitchen opening onto a dining room There is a separate living room with TV/DVD and two large leather couches . The living room has large patio doors that open up onto the courtyard area. The Old Stables can accommodate 6 people. This cottage has: Three bedrooms (two king size and one with twin beds) One family bathroom Living room with Freeview TV/DVD two large leather couches Dining table with 6 chairs Kitchen equipped with all cookware,dishwasher and washing machine Iron/Ironing board. Hairdryers , bed linen and towels are all provided in the bedrooms.Welcome pack of tea, coffee, sugar, milk, bread, butter, eggs and bacon. Free WiFi. Neighbourhood overview Freshford is a beautiful ancient village with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk from the cottage( The Inn at Freshford) that serves restaurant quality food and all the local beers and ciders.They have an excellent fully stocked( from wine to organic humus!)community shop that also has a good quality cafe that serves lunch. There is also a local doctors surgery. The village is nestled at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys . The Kennet and Avon canal is a 15 minute walk from the cottage. Getting around You don’t need a car to stay in the cottage. The village station is a few minutes walk away. Trains are hourly off peak and thrice hourly at peak times. Bath 9 mins, Bristol 22 mins. London Padington to Bath Spa 1.5 hours Bath Spa to Freshford 9 minutes Bath Spa to Freshford “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/bath-spa-to-freshford ” Freshford to Bath Spa “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/freshford-to-bath-spa ” There is also a local bus service to all the adjacent villages and Bath. The cottage has two parking spaces suitable for one medium and one small car or a single large SUV. Other things to note If you are a runner or keep fit enthusiast the owner is a qualified Personal Trainer (Bath Uni) with much Marathon and half marathon experience. She specialises in Ladies training. Please let us know if you would like guided running or some Personal Fitness training
tagline: The Old Stables is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.

title: Cottage Inn
subtitle: The Cottage Inn boasts one of the best pub locations in Bristol on the historic harbour at Baltic Wharf.
bodyContent: The Cottage Inn boasts one of the best pub locations in Bristol on the historic harbour at Baltic Wharf. In the summer, the Cottage buzzes with people wanting to enjoy their time in the sun by the river eating delicious food and drinking great beer. In the winter months the pub becomes a home away from home with warm fireplaces and comfort food. We offer full table service throughout the year and always do that little bit extra to make sure our guests leave happy. The original building dates back to 1868 and was used by merchants for storing Baltic timber for the growing number of businesses in the Dock in that period. When the Docks closed in 1975 the building went into decline and then became the home for the Harbour Master's Office. In 1983 it was refurbished and became ''The Cottage''. A perfect spot for watching the boats float up and down the harbour, paddle-boarding and the occasional hot air balloon drift by.
tagline: The Cottage Inn boasts one of the best pub locations in Bristol

title: Percy Place
subtitle: Period holiday apartment in Bath sleeping 6 people at walking distance from the city centre with free on street parking.
bodyContent: Percy Place is a holiday apartment in a Grade II listed Georgian house in the City of Bath. The house used to be the home of Rev. William Jay, one of the most eminent English Congregationalist preachers of Regency England who used to preach in the Argyle Chapel in Bath at the end of 1700s. We like to make our guests feel at home and highly valued. The original Georgian features of the building are enhanced by the stylish decor of the rooms such as antiques, trinkets and period furniture. At the same time, free wi-fi and a recently refurbished kitchen offer modern comfort. Both the town and the countryside are on our doorstep. We are just a few minutes walk from the city centre between the up and coming ‘Artisan Quarter’ bristling with local independent shops, and Larkhall village, a pretty quarter with a local butcher, a deli, a theatre and a few restaurants. We are also very close to the Kennet & Avon Canal at the back of Kensington Meadows. The view of the countryside and back garden from the back of the house is relaxing and inspiring.
tagline: Period holiday apartment in Bath sleeping 6 people at walking distance from the city centre

title: Bridgwater Docks & Town Circular
subtitle: The walk around historic Bridgwater fittingly starts and finishes at the Docks because thanks to its position on the tidal river Parrett.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. The walk around historic Bridgwater fittingly starts and finishes at the Docks because thanks to its position on the tidal river Parrett, the town has always been a hive of industry. Its colourful past is reflected in its many notable buildings. The earliest evidence of settlement here was the discovery of thousands of worked flints indicating a ‘factory’ site from around 6800 BC. Today it is a fascinating town to visit with plenty to see, including museums reflecting its manufacturing and military heritage. For more information click here

title: Pigwig Country Cottage
subtitle: Pigwig Cottage is a cosy, detached, single storey, spacious two bedroom self catering cottage at sleeping up to 4 or 5 with an additional bed.
bodyContent: Pigwig Cottage is a lovely detached, single storey, spacious two bedroom self catering cottage at Bradford on Avon, near Bath sleeping up to 4 or 5 with an additional bed. Each bedroom can be a double or twin ensuring very flexible accommodation for families or friends. It is situated in a semi-rural location just outside Bradford-on-Avon in a small group with two other cottages and B&B rooms in converted farm buildings. The B&B rooms can be used as additional ensuite rooms if you need more bedrooms. Being single storey it is popular with less mobile guests and those with young children. The cottage overlooks agricultural fields to the rear and a grass lawn to the front. This charming cottage features a fully equipped kitchen, log burning stove, exposed wooden beams, electric heating, wi-fi internet access, Freeview television with DVD player, washer/dryer aswell as a BBQ and patio. Bed linens are provided. There is also a games room, children play area and games field. Our pets and other free ranging animals include two Shetland ponies, two over friendly English Setters, two black cats and various hens and ducks. Although currently not dog friendly we have Cow Byre 1 or 2 which are. Bath is a pleasant short train journey taking you right to the town centre meaning you dont have to navigate the tricky one way system and then find a car park! The George at Woolley is a 10 minute walk firstly across a grassed field so bring your wellies if it is wet. There are lots of other good restaurants and pubs in Bradford on Avon and the surrounding area. Bradford on Avon is a 20 minute walk into town. Lastly we offer 30% off day tickets for nearby Longleat and 25% for Cheddar Gorge and Caves We hope you will choose us for your stay near Bath. *Late Availability Discounts’

bodyContent: Located 3 miles from the World Heritage City of Bath so once you have shopped till you are about to drop or taken the time to wonder along the local walking routes we have the perfect location set into the Midford Valley with country surroundings which ensures you will not be disturbed by the city noise or pace. We have our own carpark, lift access, Bar, restaurant, conservatory, outside terrace and gardens place making Waterhouse a great place to work, rest, eat and play! We serve a selection of drinks which include local Beers, Ales, carefully selected wines and spirits to relax and unwind while taking in the stunning views across the Midford Valley. Our tranquil surroundings include the Midford Brook at the bottom of the property where we have fishing rights which people can use for a nominal fee, please enquire at reception should you like to make use of this exclusive facility. Across the Midford Valley there are stunning views and a selection of walks one of which is the two tunnels route which is one of the longest pedestrian tunnels in the UK. Waterhouse is a 13 bedroom country house located in the idyllic and peaceful Midford valley 15 minutes south of Bath. Built around 1632, the house has been restored to provide bed and breakfast accommodation, meeting rooms and a venue for small events. title: Wells Cathedral High Parts Tours
subtitle: Climb the spiral staircase to walk in the footsteps of Wells Cathedral masons with new behind-the-scenes tours of Wells Cathedral’s High Parts; one of the most memorable things to do in Wells!
bodyContent: Climb the spiral staircase to walk in the footsteps of Wells Cathedral masons with new behind-the-scenes tours of Wells Cathedral’s High Parts; one of the most memorable things to do in Wells ! - Discover hidden spaces, galleries and chambers, including behind the Wells clock - See one of only two surviving tracing floors in the country where masons drew templates on the floor - Walk along the singing gallery and learn about trumpet holes! - Explore the south transept roof space - And marvel at the nave from a very different perspective! (Note that the tour route does not take in the top of the tower). High Parts Tours take place regularly throughout the week; bookings can be made via the Cathedral's website up to 24 hours prior to the tour taking place. Want to make a last minute booking? Call us on 01749 672773 or ask at the Welcome desk on the day of your visit. The tour length is 1.5 hours. Tour and tea packages are also available. Who can book: The maximum number in any upper levels tour is 12 and no children under the age of 10 years are permitted on the tour. Children between the ages of 10 and 16 years must be accompanied by one adult for every two children, unless they are part of an organised youth group when at least two adults must be in attendance. Any visitors with a fear of heights or confined spaces and/in poor health should consider carefully their suitability for the tour. There are up to 250 steps, uneven floors, low ceilings and the narrowest point is just 60cm (2ft.) wide. The tour route does not include access to the top of the tower. Other Terms and Conditions of Booking do apply (see website for details). Where to meet your Guide: At the Donation Desk in the entrance of the Cathedral 15 minutes before your Tour begins. You will unfortunately not be able to join the Tour if you miss the start time. If you purchase a Tour and tea package, your Guide will indicate where to take your refreshments at the end of the Tour. www.wellscathedral.org.uk/visit/tours
tagline: Climb the spiral staircase to walk in the footsteps of Wells Cathedral masons.

title: Seventeen The Townhouse Bath
subtitle: Guests receive a very warm welcome to start their boutique break away in this beautiful 1810 Georgian townhouse.
bodyContent: Welcome to Seventeen The Town House a boutique Georgian Town House built circa 1810. Enter Number 17 through wrought iron gates off Camden road and follow the stone path through the front garden towards the steps to make your way through the main entrance door. You are welcomed by a long hallway with a traditional wood & tiled floor. There is plenty of space in the hall to hang your coat and store your shoes. An original spindle staircase leads guests to the first and lower ground floor. Walk through the hallway and you’ll find yourself in the living and dining area which seats seven guests around a large dining table. The living room is furnished with comfortable sofas, floor cushions and a footstool. There is a wall mounted wide flat screen TV with BT Vision, NETFLIX, BBC iplayer & ITV Hub, Sonos bar sound, DVD player & Roberts bluetooth CD/Radio. The sitting and dining rooms are inter-connecting and have exposed wooden floors, two original fireplaces and hand-crafted timber cupboards complete with a large choice of board games and puzzles for little ones. Walk out of the dining room turning left and you will find yourself in a cleverly arranged space for the study annex, a quiet place to read or plan your stay in Bath. There is a downstairs WC cloakroom to save you walking up or downstairs to the other bathrooms. The kitchen is close by and is a stunning room basking in natural light from the skylight ceiling. The kitchen has been equipped to a high standard with bespoke storage cupboards, a house keepers cupboard & drawer units with marble work surfaces, Belfast sink and space for all the usual kitchen appliances. To keep your toes warm on the stone floor there is under floor heating. The kitchen has a range of new features, a SMEG electric double oven with gas hob, Bosch dishwasher & microwave, Dualit kettle & toaster, Breville panini maker, Pizza stone, Kitchen Aid, Kenwood Blender, Ninja juicer, Nespresso Coffee machine, large selection of pots, pans, serving dishes, storage containers, cooking utensils, cutlery & glass ware. We provide Denby linen china for dining for seven guests – everything you need should be there if its not let us know! Leading off the kitchen is a laundry/utility room which houses a new fridge freezer, AEG washer dryer, Brabantia ironing board & iron, laundry basket and clothes airer. From the annex you can walk through the back door & take the stone steps up towards the garden where you will find the peace and quiet of the verandah. The verandah provides sheltered outdoor seating and dining for eight. Walk on up the steps through a wrought iron gate & you will find a peaceful garden with pretty shrubs, trees, lavender & landscaped lawn to lay your rug out and enjoy the views across Bath. At the end of lawn there is a beautiful summer house on raised timber decking. Take a seat in our wonderful wicker chairs, relax & soak up stunning views over the Bath valley. The summer house has comfortable wicker seating and is a peaceful place to read & enjoy the hills beyond. Moving back into the house on the first floor, there are two super king size bedrooms. They have period fireplaces and wardrobe style cupboards & shelving, one having an outlook to the front and one with a view over the rear garden. Bedroom One has a super king sized bed and bedroom two can be either a super king bed or two super singles. There is a further single bedroom facing to the front with a tallboy and side table for storage. The first floor bathroom has a lovely view from its sash window to the back garden & summerhouse. The bathroom has a roll top bath with a fixed rain shower and oval shower curtain over the bath. There is a small walk in airing cupboard for drying or storage of travel cases. Walking back down the staircase, the lower ground floor bedroom offers super king size or super single twin beds. There is a large sash window seat facing the front of the house & two wardrobe style cupboards with hanging & shelving space. Along the corridor on the lower ground floor is the rain shower room with a stone ceiling, under floor heating, heated towel rail, WC & sink. All the bedrooms have traditional sash windows and are furnished with pretty side tables & lamps, Sonos speakers, hairdryers, black out roman blinds, radiators, good sized beds, comfortable bedding and new mattresses. There are digital safes in the three kingsize bedrooms. Do note that the ceilings in this house will accommodate guests less than 6ft 3′. Outside the front landscaped garden is laid to gravel with a stone pathway leading to the front door. There is a large bin store. We are able to offer guests complimentary holiday house parking permit if they have a car. Alternatively Bath Spa train & bus station are a short taxi ride or 20 minute walk from the house. Taxis are easy to book and buses are frequent to and from the city centre from the nearby bus stop. We can also organise Private drivers for any size group from any UK international airports. We looking forward to welcoming you at Seventeen The Town House for a very special stay!
tagline: Guests receive a very warm welcome to start their boutique break away

title: Stable Cottage: 6 bed country cottage
subtitle: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.
bodyContent: It is located in the beautiful Georgian village of Freshford which lies at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys in the southern Cotswolds. There are some wonderful walks to local pubs following the riverside and canals. All just 15 minutes from Bath by car but the secret of this location is the 9 minute train journey to Bath from the village station, just a short stroll from the cottages. The cottage : Stable cottage is a newly renovated, limestone floored, 3 bedroom, two bathroom (one is en-suite) cottage. It has large windows to the front of the house filling the bedrooms and downstairs with light on a sunny day. It has an open plan living/dining area with free view TV/DVD and two large suedette couches and comfortable chairs. For dining there is a blond Oak dining table and chairs to seat 6 . The Stables can accommodate 6 people in three bedrooms (two king size and one double) . The kitchen is fully equipped with cookware,dishwasher and washing machine . The house also offers Iron/Ironing board, Hairdryers All bed linen and towels . There is a Welcome pack of tea, coffee, sugar, milk, bread, butter, eggs and bacon. Free WiFi. There are also books and board-games in the house for the use of guests. If you have any questions on Bath and the local area before or during your stay please let us know. We would be delighted to help. Neighbourhood overview : Freshford is a beautiful ancient village with a wonderful pub just a few minutes walk from the cottage( The Inn at Freshford) that serves restaurant quality food and all the local beers and ciders.They have an excellent fully stocked( from wine to organic humus!)community shop that also has a good quality cafe that serves lunch. There is also a local doctors surgery. The village is nestled at the junction of the Frome and Avon valleys . The Kennet and Avon canal is a 15 minute walk from the cottage. Getting around : You don’t need a car to stay in the cottage. The village station is a few minutes walk away. Trains hourly off peak and thrice hourly at peak times. Bath 9 mins, Bristol 22mins. London Padington to Bath Spa 1.5 hours Bath Spa to Freshford 9 minutes Bath Spa to Freshford “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/bath-spa-to-freshford ” Freshford to Bath Spa “ https://www.thetrainline.com/train-times/freshford-to-bath-spa ” There is also a local bus service to all the adjacent villages and Bath. The cottage has two parking spaces suitable for one medium and one small car or a single large SUV.the surrounding towns you might want to visit. Other things to note If you are a runner or keep fit enthusiast the owner is a qualified Personal Trainer (Bath Uni) with much Marathon and half marathon experience. She specialises in Ladies training. Please let us know if you would like guided running or some Personal Fitness training.
tagline: Stable cottage is created from a stone built-stable block dating from the 1840’s.

title: Stapeley Cottage
subtitle: Stapeley is a popular choice of cottage when looking for the family. The comfortable and well-equipped property has everything you should need for your time away.
bodyContent: Stapeley is a popular choice of cottage when looking for the family. The comfortable and well-equipped property has everything you should need for your time away. Families can enjoy the rural surroundings and experience life on our working sheep farm. Unwind in the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool and Games Room.
tagline: Stapeley is a popular choice of cottage when looking for the family.

title: Tailpit Cottage
subtitle: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside
bodyContent: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside on the edge of an area of outstanding natural beauty but only 5 miles from the world heritage city of Bath and 1 mile from the Saxon town of Bradford-on-Avon. Cumberwell Country Cottages are located on Great Cumberwell Farm, which has been in the James family since 1939 and was originally a dairy farm until 1992 when the herd was sold making way for a diversification into Cumberwell Park Golf Club, the farm itself has not changed a great deal and is still a working farm with over 300 acres of arable crop. The self-catering cottages available for your stay have been converted from an old tithe barn which has had many purposes in the past including stables, a grain store and cider production as the orchard at the front of the cottages was a cider apple orchard.
tagline: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages

title: The Almshouse
subtitle: This charming, historic two-bedroom cottage nestles in a tranquil corner of Bath, but is only ten minutes’ stroll from the city centre, offering an ideal retreat for a romantic getaway or a base for exploring the glories of the West Country.
bodyContent: Beautifully refurbished in 2015, this 1843 almshouse nestles in a secret corner of the city, only 15 minutes from the M4 and a gentle walk downhill to the centre of Bath. There is plenty of parking, so you can leave the car and walk this historic town at your own pace. The main bedroom, with king-size bed, looks over gardens towards the church; the second bedroom can be made up as a single or twin-bedded room. The original features have been carefully preserved, but this charming house lives comfortably in the 21st century, including WiFi, flat-screen TV, and DAB radio. Guests can enjoy breakfast or an evening drink in the private courtyard, cook a delicious dinner in the Harvey Jones kitchen, or treat themselves in one of Bath’s many award-winning restaurants. Luxuriously furnished, this cosy cottage offers everything you need for a very special break, from champagne flutes to Egyptian cotton sheets and even a welcome basket on arrival! Bath has so much to offer, from the Roman Baths and gorgeous Georgian crescents, to the ultra-modern Thermae Bath Spa, quirky independent shops, museums and cultural festivals, that you may want to plan a longer stay to explore the glorious countryside: just let us know.
tagline: This charming, historic two-bedroom cottage nestles in a tranquil corner of Bath

title: The Annexe Yew Tree Cottage
subtitle: Situated in a country lane near the village of Wick with lovely view over the countryside.
bodyContent: Situated in a country lane near the village of Wick with lovely view over the countryside, the Annexe at Yew Tree Cottage will provide you with everything, you need for a lovely break. This one bedroom accommodation has been fully renovated in 2014 and awarded 4 star gold by Visit England. It sits in a beautiful garden visited by a variety of wildlife. There is so much to see, all with easy reach of the Annexe. Only 7 miles from the historic city of Bath and Bristol, it is ideally situated to visit both towns. On the edge of the Cotswold and Witshire and within reach of lovely scenery, historic sites it will be perfect for a romantic holiday or visiting family or friends.
tagline: Situated in a country lane near the village of Wick with lovely view over the countryside.
