title: The Apartment, Bath
subtitle: An exceptional two-bedroom luxury holiday home in central Bath, loved by guests for its perfect location, stylish decor, comfort, cleanliness and first class self-catering accommodation.
bodyContent: From Nespresso to Nintendo, The Apartment, Bath is an excellently-located two-bedroom apartment in central Bath. The first bedroom is a large, bright double bedroom with king size bed (or twin beds on request). The open fireplace and large sash windows are elegant original features and south-facing views take in the length of Ralph Allen Drive and Widcombe Hill. At the rear of the property, the second bedroom is a well-proportioned double bedroom, featuring a comfy double bed, original fireplace and built in wardrobe. The homely lounge is flooded with light from the large, original south-facing 16-pane sash window. The room hosts an extendable dining table and chairs, designer sofa (which can convert to a sofa bed) and a feature armchair. Brimming with technology, the lounge is equipped with satellite TV, blu-ray player, Nintendo Wii and wall-mounted 40” Samsung LCD TV. A well-equipped and cleverly designed galley kitchen features high-end integrated appliances to meet your every need, including a built-in double oven and sleek induction hob, full suite of cooking facilities and an integrated NEFF fridge with ice-box. A Nespresso machine and milk frother are provided for that much needed espresso or cappuccino to kick-start your day. And there is a washer dryer, so you can pack a little lighter! The newly renovated bathroom features a large walk-in rain shower with separate handheld spray. A chrome towel rail is complemented by a lit, motion-activated mirror cabinet featuring de-mist function and integrated razor/electric toothbrush socket. This gorgeous two-bedroom holiday home in central Bath is ranked in the ‘10 Best Holiday Homes in Bath’ by Booking.com and consistently rated positively by guests.
tagline: An exceptional two-bedroom luxury holiday home in central Bath

title: The Barn
subtitle: The Barn is one of two beautifully converted barns which share an enclosed garden, is south facing with views along a small tranquil valley.
bodyContent: The Barn | Park Farm Country Cottages near Chew Magna is one of two beautifully converted barns on a working farm with private terraces and a shared enclosed garden with lovely uninterrupted views across open countryside and along a small valley. The Barn is full of character, has an open gallery with exposed oak trusses, peg jointed purlins and has an airy yet homely feel. The south facing french doors open directly onto the private terrace with quality wooden table, chairs and parasol. The cottage has been equipped to a high standard with slate flooring, toasty underfloor heating, a dishwasher, washer/dryer, microwave, WiFi. There are 2 bathrooms and 2 bedrooms, a twin bedroom downstairs, a double bedroom upstairs with 1 additional guest bed on the gallery. Please note the the 5th bed on the gallery may not be suitable for very young children. https://www.parkfarm-countrycottages.co.uk/luxury-holiday-cottages-bristol-the-barn
tagline: The Barn is one of two beautifully converted barns which share an enclosed garden

title: The Billiard Room
subtitle: The Billiard Room is an historic, and quirky building set in the grounds of The Close, an 18th century house facing the duck pond, on the village green, in Biddestone.
bodyContent: The Billiard Room is an historic, and quirky building set in the grounds of The Close, an 18th century house facing the duck pond, on the village green, in Biddestone. It is ideally placed to visit the World Heritage City of Bath, and to explore the historic villages and countryside of Wiltshire & the Cotswolds.Originally a blanket factory, and subsequently the village school, it was converted into a billiard room by the owner of The Close in the early part of the twentieth century. It has recently undergone sympathetic restoration to create a unique living space, with a four-poster bed, living area and breakfast bar. The building is entered through a grand, old oak door, has a magnificent beamed vaulted roof, and a large stone fireplace with a wood burner. The property is equipped with a wardrobe & chest of drawers, a large leather sofa & TV, and a freestanding cooking range with electric oven & ceramic hob. A full range of crockery, glasses , cutlery & cooking utensils are provided. There is a separate utility area, providing a fridge & sink, together with a shower room & WC. Guests can wander through the orchard with several fruit trees, and the 2 acre paddock, home to the donkeys, Ossie and Bertie. This joins the village playing fields, and leads to attractive walks on adjoining farmland and woods. Residents have a parking area on the gravel drive of The Close. The wood store provides a free supply of logs, and access to a wheelie bin.
tagline: The Billiard Room is an historic, and quirky building set in the grounds of The Close

title: The Cart Shed
subtitle: Beautiful cottage just 2 Miles from Bath city centre & surrounded by countryside with river, canal, cafés and restaurants nearby. Sleeps 2 people
bodyContent: The welcoming Cart Shed at New Leaf Farm is just 2 miles to Bath City Centre. This 4-Star cottage has 1 bedroom and sleeps up to 2 people – ideal for couples visiting Bath Local attractions include the Kennett & Avon canal, walks, pubs and cruises into Bath along the river Avon.
tagline: Beautiful cottage just 2 Miles from Bath city centre

title: The Circus Apartment
subtitle: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses.
bodyContent: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the secluded private garden to the rear. With the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minutes walk The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle of Grade I Georgian houses. With views over the rest of The Circus, the mature trees in the middle, and the secluded private garden to the rear. With the Royal Crescent, Queens Square, Assembly Rooms and the town centre within a few minutes walk. This contemporary apartment, in a warm palate of chocolate, plum and biscuit throughout, has undergone several transformations in its lifetime yet has retained all its period charm. The large sitting and dining room with sash windows overlooking two aspects of The Circus has two French style velvet sofas by a decorative fireplace. There is a TV with Blue Ray DVD and a separate radio with I-pod docking. A dining table seats four and a French style dresser contains crockery, cutlery and a selection of novels, films and games. The neat fitted period kitchen has an electric hob and oven, a microwave, a large fridge/freezer, and a dishwasher.. A large mirrored lobby before the bedroom which has fitted wardrobes and shelving leads to the spacious and comfortable bedroom which has a 6′ bed, a fitted wardrobe, a dressing table with storage and a tallboy and a cupboard containing a washer/dryer machine. A radio/alarm with I-pod docking is provided. The contemporary bathroom has smart cappuccino coloured tiling and contains a double ended bath with shower over, a hand basin with lots of storage under and a WC. The apartment has gas central heating, hair dryer, iron, microwave, dishwasher, towels and toiletries. A Free car parking permit is available as is free internet access.
tagline: The apartment is on the ground floor of one of this architecturally impressive circle

title: The Cow Byre
subtitle: Pretty cottage just 2 Miles from Bath city centre & surrounded by countryside with river, canal, cafés and restaurants nearby. Sleeps 4 people.
bodyContent: The Cow Byre at New Leaf Farm is just 2 miles to Bath City Centre. This 4-Star cottage has 2 bedrooms and sleeps up to 4 people with Bath a short walk or boat ride away. Local attractions include the Kennet & Avon canal, walks, pubs and cruises into Bath along the river Avon.
tagline: Pretty cottage just 2 Miles from Bath city centre

title: The Dairy
subtitle: The Dairy is one of two beautifully converted barns which share an enclosed garden, is south facing with views along a small tranquil valley.
bodyContent: The Dairy | Park Farm Country Cottages near Chew Magna is one of two beautifully converted barns on a working farm with a private terrace and a shared enclosed garden with lovely interrupted views across open countryside and along a small valley. The Dairy, formally the milking parlour is light and airy with double sets of south facing French doors opening onto a large private terrace with quality wooden table, chairs and parasol. The cottage has been equipped to a high standard with slate flooring and toasty under floor heating, a dishwasher, washer/dryer, microwave etc. The bathroom has a powerful shower and a heated towel rail. WiFi, Flatscreen TV and DVD, Freeview. There are 2 steps within the cottage and 4 steps down to the front door. https://www.parkfarm-countrycottages.co.uk/luxury-holiday-cottages-bristol-the-barn
tagline: The Dairy is one of two beautifully converted barns which share an enclosed garden

title: The Dairy Cottage
subtitle: A former milking parlour that has been tastefully renovated into a spacious family holiday cottage sleeping 5 + cot.
bodyContent: A former milking parlour that has been tastefully renovated into a spacious family holiday cottage sleeping 4 + cot. Graded with 4 stars The Dairy Cottage offers comfortable accommodation with the added benefit of being all over one level, lending itself to the less able and families with small children. Enter the property directly into a very large kitchen diner finished in light colours with fully fitted pine cupboards and wood flooring. A farmhouse table seating 6, sits central in the kitchen and all the mod cons expected have been provided including dishwasher, washing machine and stainless steel oven, hob and extractor. The lounge offers a comfortable area to relax and unwind with a glass door to rear of property. With wooden flooring, rugs and quality soft furnishings. A freeview television, DVD player and CD unit are provided for your entertainment. There are two bedrooms in the Dairy, a twin with en-suite and a double with its own bathroom. All finished in light colours and matching Sanderson fabrics and throws. Fitted wardrobes are provided with a range of pine bedroom furniture. The bathrooms are newly installed for 2015 and fully tiled with bath, shower, WC and sink. Outside, The Dairy has ramp access front and rear. It has its own little patio area as well as being just a few steps away from our paddock with play equipment, and open air solar heated swimming pool. There is plenty of on-site parking available and our own little farm shop/butchery for all your breakfast needs!
tagline: A former milking parlour that has been tastefully renovated into a spacious family holiday cottage

title: The Dovecote
subtitle: If Contemporary Loft Living is your style – then The Dovecote at Fosse Farmhouse is the perfect retreat! Our large open plan first floor space has a living/dining area, galley kitchen, double bed and two single beds.
bodyContent: The Dovecote offers an economic yet beautiful place to stay for up to four guests – two adults and two children enjoying a wonderful family holidays in The Cotswolds. Our large, first floor space has an open plan living/dining area, galley kitchen, double bed and two single beds. There is also a separate bathroom with a bath and overhead shower, basin and WC. The entrance hall has a built in wardrobe to store all your ‘Country Living’ essentials – Wellington boots, coats and umbrellas. The Dovecote garden area is located just beside the property. Here you can picnic and play and even barbeque, weather permitting! Family holidays can be great fun even in the rain. As well as the garden area, guests enjoy the charming Juliet Balcony that overlooks our vintage Shepherds’ Hut in the field behind. Children love staying here as we have a unique twinkling light feature in the ceiling. The Local Area All of our properties are situated just walking distance from the Cotswolds village of Castle Combe. They are also just a 20 minute drive from the city of Bath and Bristol. The lovely countryside where we are located offers some fabulous walking areas and places to cycle together with Horse riding Stables and Go Karting nearby. The Dovecote can be hired together with any of our other properties to offer space for up to 16 guests . This can be increased to up to 22 guests when using rooms from our BnB. Family reunions, wedding guests and even hen parties can all be catered for. The Garden House sleeps 4 adults and 2 children in two ensuite bedrooms. The Stables sleeps 6 guests in 3 ensuite bedrooms. All are also pet friendly. Please contact us for last minute discount rates!
tagline: Contemporary Loft Living The Dovecote at Fosse Farmhouse

title: The Engine House
subtitle: Perfect for a romantic weekend away near the City of Bath, The Engine House has oodles of character with underfloor heating, a whirlpool bath and log fire.
bodyContent: Just 20 minutes from Bath, the Engine House, originally a stable, is now a romantic cottage for two. The bedroom, accessed by a cast iron spiral staircase, has an indulgent super king bed. Exposed beams and stone walls reveal much of its original character. Underfloor heating, free wi-fi, digital TV, bluetooth speaker, cotton bed linen and large white towels provide you with modern comforts. Snuggle up in front of the log burner on those long winter evenings. The engine House has stunning views along the Cam Valley that can also be enjoyed from its own garden. Downstairs the bathroom houses a whirlpool bath in which you can forget the stresses of normal life. Withy Mills Farm is approximately 1 mile from the vibrant village of Timsbury with shops, cafe and fish & chip shop. The farm is in a beautiful rural location with far reaching views across the Mendip Hills. It’s within easy access of tourist attractions as well as the cities of Bath and Wells.
tagline: Perfect for a romantic weekend away near the City of Bath

title: The Garden House
subtitle: This single storey, pet friendly property sleeps up to 4 adults and 2 children.
bodyContent: The Garden House living room has a working open fire which is the heart of the house during the winter months. Families particularly enjoy this feature at Christmas and New Year. The compact galley kitchen has solid granite worktops and oak cabinets. It provides a cosy space for preparing a delicious breakfast and provides all the equipment and utensils needed for you stay. Guests can also enjoy their meals in their very own private, glassed atrium. The conservatory dining room has wonderful views across the neighbouring fields and Shepherds Hut. There are two large double bedrooms – one of which has a stunning four poster bed plus extra foldaway beds for children. The family bathroom has a bath with overhead shower and the added luxury of underfloor heating. The Garden House accommodates a family of four adults and two children in total comfort. The Surrounding Area The Garden House is situated within the beautiful countryside of Castle Combe. There and many walks and bike rides around the local area. The city of Bath is also just 20 minutes drive away. We also accommodate larger parties within our other holiday homes – The Dovecote and The Stables We offer last minute discounts so please contact us for details!
tagline: This single storey, pet friendly property sleeps up to 4 adults and 2 children.

title: The Green Leaf Apartment
subtitle: This beautifully decorated two bedroom self-catering apartment is situated in the heart of Bath and is ideal for families or smaller groups.
bodyContent: Fitted to a very high standard with everything you will need to enjoy a comfortable stay. This Gold Award winning apartment also includes free parking and free wifi. Experience Bath Excellence… Experience The Green Leaf Apartment…
tagline: This beautifully decorated two bedroom self-catering apartment is situated in the heart of Bath

title: The Grove at Freshford
subtitle: The Grove at Freshford is a unique period property built in the 17th century, situated in the heart of the conservation village of Freshford, about 6 miles south east of Bath.
bodyContent: The Grove at Freshford provides self catering accommodation in a 5 bedroom exclusive, 17th century period property. Sleeping up to 10 people, the house is close to the pub, shop, cafe, church and rail station in this historic village of Freshford, only 6 miles south east of Bath. The house stands in over an acre of well-established garden with panoramic views over the rolling countryside and the River Avon. The secluded grounds and wrought iron gates ensure privacy for visiting guests in addition to providing a perfect, peaceful and tranquil setting for any occasion. In warmer months, there is an unheated outdoor swimming pool which is fully enclosed. The house is full of historical fascination and charm dating back to 1650. The ground floor contains 2 reception rooms furnished with classic pieces overlooking the gardens through French windows. There is also a separate TV lounge. Guests can choose to eat in the formal dinning room or more casually in the kitchen/breakfast room which is fully equipped with all modern appliances. Outside there is a delightful al fresco eating area. The house features art specially commissioned from a leading local artist. There are 5 individually styled bedrooms plus a travel cot and moses basket. We are also able to offer delicious catering from scrumptious afternoon tea, creative canapes, light suppers or even fully catered dinners.
tagline: The Grove at Freshford is a unique period property built in the 17th century

title: The Hay Barn
subtitle: Beautiful cottage just 2 Miles from Bath city centre & surrounded by countryside with river, canal, cafés and restaurants nearby.
bodyContent: The Hay Barn at New Leaf Farm is just 2 miles to Bath City Centre. This 4-Star cottage has 5 bedrooms and sleeps up to 10 people – ideal for large groups visiting Bath Local attractions include the Kennet & Avon canal, walks, pubs and cruises into Bath along the river Avon.
tagline: Beautiful cottage just 2 Miles from Bath city centre

title: The Home Cottage
subtitle: The Home Cottage is close to England’s smallest City of Wells, with trendy Frome, the picturesque village of Mells and the Mendip Hills all close by.
bodyContent: The Home Cottage is architect designed and newly built (completed in November 2016) and sleeps four in two bedrooms. The house is fully central heated. The cottage is very peaceful and sits at the end of a long track surrounded by farmland. The front of the house is south facing and the cottage is in an elevated position with wonderful views out over the surrounding fields and trees. There is a large garden of approximately 0.2 acres with flower borders and a large area of grass at the rear of the cottage which is suitable for ball games. In front of the cottage is a patio with teak table and chairs for guests to sit and enjoy the view. A sun parasol and barbecue are provided to allow guests to make the most of sunny summer days. The cottage has off-road parking for two cars on the gravel driveway. Inside the cottage has a well equipped fitted kitchen with a good range of appliances including a full-sized dish-washer. The kitchen also has a small dining area with two chairs and a bench. Next door is the sitting room which has a woodburner to allow you to cozy up on cold winter nights (or even chilly summer evenings) – a basket of logs is supplied and the fire is laid and ready to be lit. The cottage also has a good sized utility room complete with washing machine and lots of space for coats and wet walking boots. This room is also ideal for a well-behaved dog to stay. Upstairs the master bedroom has a double bed and windows to south and east – ideal for the morning sun. The second bedroom is small, but has room for two in bunk beds with full sized single mattresses. On arrival guests will find the cottage fully prepared with freshly ironed cotton bedding and fluffy white towels and face flannels. Milk, cookies, tea, coffee and sugar are provided along with fresh flowers from my garden. Other amenities include: • Wifi • TV and DVD player • Washing line, pegs and clothes airer • Hair dryer • Iron and ironing board • Travel cot and high chair (please request and I will bring it down to the cottage) • Children’s toys (please request and I will bring some down to the cottage)
tagline: The Home Cottage is close to England’s smallest City of Wells

title: The Oak House
subtitle: A cabin in the woods for 2 (or 3) with Georgian Bath 10 minutes away, the Oak House is set in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty with the Cotswold Way running along our boundary.
bodyContent: As the name suggests, the Oak House is an oak framed cabin situated on the edge of a wood and surrounded by old oak trees. The fully equipped kitchen has an induction hob, oven, and dishwasher. There is a wood burning stove with wood provided for the first fire. The bedroom has a kingsize bed (the headboard is made from an oak branch which fell from one of our trees in a storm Next to this is a bathroom with full size power shower. The whole building is open to the roof except for the area above the bathroom which can be accessed by ladder and has a single mattress for an occasional extra guest. The Oak House is full of light from large windows overlooking the wood and stunning views to the west. The house is centrally heated with hot water on demand. There are games and books but no television (too many trees for reception) but that might be a good thing! There is a WiFi internet connection, linked to the main house. All linen and towels are provided as is everything you might need in the kitchen and bathroom. Outside, there is a covered open porch for boots and for sitting out a shower in comfy chairs. Attached to the house is an octagonal deck with table and chairs for al fresco meals or a glass of wine while you admire the views. . Just below is a barbecue and a fire pit (but you might have to saw up your own wood!). The Oak House was built with mostly reclaimed material by design although the plumbing and electrical equipment are new. The roof is clad in recycled Cornish slate, the floor is made from used but sanded scaffolding planks, the bathroom sink came from a school laboratory (suitably cleaned up!) and the shower is tiled in reject Burlington slate. The eclectic furniture is all carefully sourced with comfort and design in mind. We hope you like it.
tagline: A cabin in the woods for 2 (or 3) with Georgian Bath 10 minutes away

title: The Old Crescent Bakery
subtitle: Next to the Royal Crescent, The Old Crescent Bakery is a listed Georgian townhouse that retains all its historical charm as an old Georgian Bakery/Deli, but with boutique style furnishings that give it a contemporary feel.
bodyContent: The Old Crescent Bakery has a relaxing lounge, a warm period kitchen and a large dining table. The four spacious bedrooms of this converted Georgian shop provide lots of space and comfort for guests. There are a number of period features still present in the house such as a large bread oven fireplace and an old Georgian safe (now lovingly restored into a one-of-a-kind botanicals gin bar for your use during your stay!) You can enjoy complimentary Cowshed bathing products when you sink into the freestanding bath or use the large walk-in showers, allowing you to relax to the fullest. We also provide local, tea and coffee for you to enjoy. This property is also dog friendly, so bring your four-legged friend along to enjoy the city of Bath as well. 2 night min stay at weekends (Fri-Sun) and a min 10 guest rate at weekends & Christmas (if less than 10 staying, the 10 person price will still apply).
tagline: Next to the Royal Crescent, The Old Crescent Bakery is a listed Georgian townhouse

title: The Old Granary – Sleeps 12
subtitle: A stunning converted barn sleeping up to 12 people, set in a peaceful countryside location.
bodyContent: This detached barn is 3/4 of a mile from Church Farm along a country lane. It has its own landscaped garden and private driveway with plenty of parking. Use of the Indoor Heated Swimming Pool and Games Room 3/4 of a mile away at Church Farm – Sleep up to 12 – 6 miles from Bath – Rural Retreat
tagline: A stunning converted barn sleeping up to 12 people, set in a peaceful countryside location.

title: The Post House
subtitle: A beautifully restored Grade II Listed former village Bakery. The property has been restored with great sensitivity to be sure to retain the atmosphere of this 350 year old building.
bodyContent: Luxury self catering accommodation, situated on the Mendip Hills. 20 minutes from the City of Bath, this is the perfect location to explore this beautiful part of Somerset. Sleeping up to 13 guests in 5 bedrooms. Perfect for pampering weekends or for families. Please see the floorplans to help organise your visit. This beautifully restored, 400 year old, former village Post Office and Bakery is simply stunning. You won’t find another quite like it! All traditional methods have been used in the restoration and finished in light grey hues of lime wash to create a relaxed and stylish feel. Each living area opens up to another creating a feeling of space and tranquility. The original flag stone floor and large open fireplace in the sitting room offers a wonderful space to chill out and relax in front of Sky television! The stunning Dining Hall in the former bakery is a great place to organise a dinner party. In addition there is a Morning Room with open log fire and fully equipped Kitchen. The Mediterranean Courtyard is a perfect place to enjoy breakfast in the Summer or a sundowner. Please do see details of our other properties – The Town House , sleeping up to 12 guests and The Secret Escape for 2 guests.
tagline: A beautifully restored Grade II Listed former village Bakery

title: The Secret Escape
subtitle: A chic and cosy, quiet hideaway in Central Bath for 2. Ideal location for all restaurants and attractions.
bodyContent: Situated in the centre of the beautiful Georgian City of Bath but hidden away behind the bustling streets, this one bedroom, boutique flat offers a secret escape with added luxury. Newly renovated to a very high standard and offering a kitchen/sitting room, with breakfast bar, 32″ smart television and a small balcony with table and chairs for that all important morning coffee or sundowner! The bedroom is on the lower floor and has a king sized bed, dressing area, an ensuite shower room and a 22″ smart television. There is a door out to another exterior sitting area, with yet another table and chairs. There is one residents parking permit available, gold dust in the centre of the city! Our Secret Escape in Bath is perfect for city based holidays and short breaks.
tagline: A chic and cosy, quiet hideaway in Central Bath for 2.

title: The Seed Shed
subtitle: Pretty cottage just 2 Miles from Bath city centre & surrounded by countryside with river, canal, cafés and restaurants nearby.
bodyContent: The cosy Seed Shed cottage at New Leaf Farm is just 2 miles to Bath City Centre. This 4-Star cottage has 1 bedroom and sleeps up to 2 people – ideal for couples visiting Bath Local attractions include the Kennet & Avon canal, walks, pubs and cruises into Bath along the river Avon.
tagline: Pretty cottage just 2 Miles from Bath city centre & surrounded by countryside

title: The Sheep Shed
subtitle: Beautiful cottage just 2 Miles from Bath city centre & surrounded by countryside with river, canal, cafés and restaurants nearby. Sleeps 6 people.
bodyContent: The Sheep Shed at New Leaf Farm is just 2 miles to Bath City Centre. This 4-Star cottage has 3 bedrooms and sleeps up to 6 people – ideal for friends and family visiting Bath. Local attractions include the Kennet & Avon canal, walks, pubs and cruises into Bath along the river Avon.
tagline: Beautiful cottage just 2 Miles from Bath city centre & surrounded by countryside with river

title: The Stables
subtitle: Our beautiful detached three bedroomed former barn retains many original architectural features.
bodyContent: The holiday home comprises of two double bedrooms and a single bedroom (with an additional single pull out trundle bed) sleeping a maximum of six guests. Each bedroom has an ensuite shower, basin and WC. There is also a separate guest cloakroom on the first floor. On the ground floor there is a spacious living/dining room with a feature Victorian cast iron cooking range, perfect for self catering. The new spacious kitchen has solid granite worktops and hand painted units. This also leads to the shared garden and cider orchard. The holiday home was redecorated in subtle Farrow and Ball paint colours and re-carpeted throughout during the Spring of 2013. The Local Area The Stables is located beside the ancient Roman Fosse Way – the oldest Roman Road in the British Isles. It is walking distance from the village of Castle Combe and just 20 minutes drive from Bath. If you are looking to explore the great outdoors there are many local walking and cycle routes. Need more space? We have three self catering holiday homes in total. These sleep up to 16 guests with the option to up this to 22 guests using rooms from our bed and breakfast . We often provide accommodation for parties attending weddings in the local villages of Castle Combe, Grittleton and Euridge. The Dovecote sleeps up to 4 guests. The Garden House sleeps up to 6 guests. It is also pet friendly. We offer last minute dicounts so please contact us directly for the best deals.
tagline: Our beautiful detached three bedroomed former barn retains many original architectural features.

title: The Town House in Bath
subtitle: A chic, luxury Georgian town house in the Centre of Bath. Beautifully designed and renovated with wonderful modern wet rooms and a double ended roll top bath.
bodyContent: Beautifully renovated, Georgian Town House in the centre of Bath. Chic, stylish and very central. Close to Milsom Street and the Assembly Rooms and offering luxury self catering accommodation. Perfect for families or for groups of friends sleeping up to 14 guests – please do see the floorplans to help you plan your stay. Karen and John have painstakingly rejunvenated this elegant property back to it’s original glory. Karen’s passion lies in restoring property using traditional methods to create the original atmosphere of former elegant times. The attention to detail makes staying at The Town House a particularly special experience. From the softness of the lime wash to the exquisite workmanship of the window shutters and original wooden floors make this property stand out and offers the opportunity for you to experience a truly unique stay in Bath. We can also offer The Post House , sleeping up to 12 guests and The Secret Escape , a chic apartment for 2 guests. The Town House is ideally situated just 10 minutes walk from the famous Thermae Bath Spa via the chic shopping area of Milsom Street. The must see Assembly Rooms, world famous Circus and Royal Crescent are all less than 400 metres away. Set in this central location of Bath, everything you would wish for from a City break is on your doorstep.
tagline: A chic, luxury Georgian town house in the Centre of Bath

title: The Workshop
subtitle: A comfortable cabin for up to 4 people just a few minutes from Bath, set in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty with the Cotswold Way on its boundary.
bodyContent: The Workshop was once just that – a workshop where the owner, Jane and her staff made horse rugs until the business was sold about 10 years ago. Since then, it has been transformed into a stylish and comfortable house with startling views, comfy sofas and beds and a nifty kitchen with all necessary equipment to cook up a storm. Great walking perched close to the Cotswold Way, with a rural feel although Bath is just five miles away, the the park and ride a twenty minute walk or five minutes in the car. The entrance is through a porch for keeping the drafts out and leaving boots behind. This gives on to a large living room with sofas and dining table clustered around a Jotul wood burning stove. There is a spacious and fully equipped kitchen with dresser and pretty china on it, fridge, freezer, dishwasher and washing machine. For cooking, there is an induction hob and an electric oven together with a toaster and kettle and microwave. Eat outside in a ptretty courtyard or indoors at a handsome oak table by the fire Sleep in either of two large bedrooms unruffled by noise and separated from the living room by oak plank doors. The main bedroom is spacious with a comfortable king-sized bed, the second with a double bed. Both bedrooms amply furnished with provision for clothes and possessions The warm bathroom has a toilet, walk-in shower and washbasin and is furnished with large fluffy towels The cabin has oil-fired central heating and a wood burning stove and wood is provided for the first fire. The cabin has its own WiFi internet connection and Freeview TV. Outside, there is a balcony at the front of the cabin with views downhill across the fields towards the Welsh hills in the distance. At the side by the front door is a secluded patio area with table and chairs and a small barbeque for al fresco dining. The cabin has a dedicated parking place immediately next to it.
tagline: A comfortable cabin for up to 4 people just a few minutes from Bath

title: Tyning Cottage
subtitle: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside.
bodyContent: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages offers 7 award winning unique, luxurious and spacious self-catering cottages set in the beautiful Wiltshire Countryside on the edge of an area of outstanding natural beauty but only 5 miles from the world heritage city of Bath and 1 mile from the Saxon town of Bradford-on-Avon. Cumberwell Country Cottages are located on Great Cumberwell Farm, which has been in the James family since 1939 and was originally a dairy farm until 1992 when the herd was sold making way for a diversification into Cumberwell Park Golf Club, the farm itself has not changed a great deal and is still a working farm with over 300 acres of arable crop. The self-catering cottages available for your stay have been converted from an old tithe barn which has had many purposes in the past including stables, a grain store and cider production as the orchard at the front of the cottages was a cider apple orchard.
tagline: Set in a peaceful, rural location, Cumberwell Country Cottages

title: Valley View
subtitle: This lovely cottage accommodates three/four persons. It has beautiful views across to the Mendip Hills and is tastefully furnished and fully equipped.
bodyContent: Valley View is a Holiday Cottage with beautiful views across to the Mendip Hills. It is tastefully furnished, fully equipped and located in peaceful rural surroundings close to Bath, Bristol & Wells. Because the cottage is double glazed, has full oil fired central heating and a log fireplace it is cosy and ideal for winter breaks. Valley View has a private patio area with garden furniture and a rotary washing line. The sun room / dining room has lovely views over the valley to the Mendip Hills. There is ample, safe parking adjacent to the cottage. Pets are accepted by prior arrangement only. The cottage has adjacent safe parking. Free use of all our onsite facilities – Boules Court, Hot Tub, Sauna, Mini Gym, Barbecue Hut and Wi-Fi. Booking Valley View Fully flexible short breaks are available all year round. Visit our website for a live availability calendar and to download full details. Email or Phone us if you have any questions. A warm welcome awaits you at Greyfield Farm Cottages.
tagline: This lovely cottage accommodates three/four persons. It has beautiful views

title: Vellum Stone Cottage
subtitle: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway.
bodyContent: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway – indoor pool and games room on site, Kennet and Avon Canal Close by (3/4 of a mile), walking and cycling from your doorstep. Farm Shop and country pub(s) within walking distance. The cottage features a country feel with vaulted ceilings and exposed beams, with soft furnishings compliment. Enjoy admiring the sheep in the fields surrounding the farm.
tagline: Vellum Stone Cottage has everything you should need for the ideal family getaway.

title: Victorian Annexe
subtitle: The Victorian Annexe is a two bedroom, self contained holiday rental attached to a Georgian property.
bodyContent: The accommodation is a self-contained Annexe that was added to the main Georgian House in Victorian Times. The first and second floors cover a very generous 82m2. The open plan living area is on the ground floor, the 2 double bedrooms are on the first floor, and these are connected by a spiral staircase. There is a large hallway and second staircase to the bathroom and toilet. The open plan ground floor living area provides an extremely comfortable and functional space for 4 people. Entertainment is provided by a 40” HDTV and a fantastic inbuilt wood burner. A leather sofa and single armchair provide relaxing seating. For meal times there is a circular wooden table and 4 sturdy wooden chairs. There is a fully equipped kitchen with modern oven, induction hob, dishwasher, fridge-freezer, extractor fan, toaster and kettle. The downstairs lighting can be adjusted to match your mood and needs. For lots of light there are the downlighters, for the early evening there is the discrete yet functional kitchen lighting and for late evening there is the warm glow from the uplighters in the middle of the room. The space is also practical with plenty of coat hooks, boot rack, waste bin and under-sink recycling container. Upstairs there are 2 very comfortable Vi-Spring beds with crisp white cotton bedding. The first bed is superking size and the second is a double. Both rooms have a minimalist feel and are finished with floor-length silk curtains. The bathroom is comfortably large with the usual toilet, washbasin and large enamelled bath that houses a separate shower. For convenience the bathroom also contains a washer-dryer that can be set to wash and dry clothes overnight. Iron, ironing board and other standard equipment are contained in the ceiling high cupboard outside of the bathroom. The Annexe has walls that are 2 feet thick and is well insulated. As part of its refurbishment, underfloor heating was fitted downstairs and efficient radiators everywhere else. There are 2 separate and fully automatic heating circuits that ensure the 2 floors of the Annexe are warm and toasty when required but not oppressively so overnight. A third circuit ensures that the floor-ceiling towel warmer does its job and keeps the bathroom especially warm at peak times. Whilst this is a great space, the 2 staircases (without stairgates and with wide gaps between stanchions), relatively narrow access to the main entrance door would present particular challenges to those with mobility problems and potentially for families with small children. But please feel free to contact us to clarify any potential issues.
tagline: The Victorian Annexe is a two bedroom, self contained holiday rental

title: Walnut Tree Cottage
subtitle: Walnut Tree Cottage is a beautifully light & airy cottage. Extending over two floors with 3 bedrooms, quirky vaulted ceilings and two fully tiled bathrooms.
bodyContent: Walnut Tree Cottage is a beautifully light and airy cottage extending over two floors with 3 bedrooms and two full size bathrooms. The Cottage consists of a large lounge/kitchen/diner. It has a ground floor double bedroom with built in wardrobes and its own bathroom through a small lobby and then upstairs there is a substantial twin room a large single with vaulted ceilings and roof windows that look out over our fields, ancient Walnut Tree and chickens. There is also a further full size bathroom upstairs. We have taken care to finish this cottage to a high standard with engineered oak flooring, fully tiled bathrooms, large walk-in shower and co-ordinating fabrics and soft furnishings. It is a lovely place to stay. Outside of the cottage is a shared lawned paddock and an open air solar heated swimming pool. There is plenty of on-site parking available at the farm and our own little farmshop/butchery for all your breakfast needs! Next door to Walnut is its new “sister” property, Oak Tree Cottage.
tagline: Walnut Tree Cottage is a beautifully light & airy cottage

title: Wharfingers Cottage
subtitle: Wharfingers Cottage is a beautifully appointed cottage for two.
bodyContent: This romantic cottage has the luxury of underfloor heating throughout as well as a wood burner to keep you cosy on those frosty winter nights. Relax and unwind in the whilpool bath big enough for two! Just 20 minutes from Bath, Wharfingers Cottage, is a romantic cottage for two. All the rooms are on the ground level. Enjoy the luxury of underfloor heating throughout with a wood burner to keep you cosy on those frosty winter evenings. Wharfingers Cottage has stunning views along the Cam Valley to be enjoyed from its own garden. It is equipped with modern kitchen appliances, digital TV and free wif-fi. Laze in the corner whirlpool bath, large enough for two, where you can relax from the stresses of normal life. Sleep in the king sized double bed on 100% cotton bed linen. Withy Mills Farm is set in a tranquil rural location with ample off road parking. Enjoy the peace and quiet of the countryside while having easy access to tourist attractions and the cities of Bath or Wells. Please take a look at our website for photographs of the cottage and more information.

title: Whippletree Cottage
subtitle: Sympathetically restored from a hay store to beautifully appointed contemporary accommodation.
bodyContent: This romantic cottage, only 20 minutes from Bath, has been restored from a barn to beautifully appointed contemporary accommodation. Whippletree Cottage has exposed oak beams and stone walls which hint at the original use of the building. Guests enjoy the pleasure of sleeping in a king sized bed with 100% cotton bed linen. The main bedroom in the old hay loft has stunning views across the Mendip Hills which are also enjoyed from its own garden. Twin 3ft beds in the second bedroom can be zipped together to make a super king sized bed. The cottage has free wifi, and provides a wonderful setting in which to relax and unwind with the luxury of underfloor heating throughout the property. Whippletree has a digital TV and bluetooth speaker. On a winter break, light the wood burner and settle down to a cosy romantic evening. Set in a rural location Withy Mills Farm provides a peaceful setting with ample off road parking. Enjoy easy access to tourist attractions and of course the cities of Bath, Wells and Bristol. Please visit our website for photographs and more details.

title: Whitley Coach House
subtitle: Whitley Coach House is a truly luxurious self-contained 1804 Georgian built.
bodyContent: Recently modernised stone coach house providing self-catering accommodation for long, short or one night stays. Whitley Coach House is an ideal base from which to visit Bath, Lacock, Longleat, Bowood House, Stonehenge, National Trust properties and many other local attractions. Only 20 minutes from Bath and 5 Minutes from Lacock – 10-minute walk to a great Pub/Resturant and local shop/cafe, free fast Wi-Fi, 40″ smart TV with Netflix and free private parking. Private garden with teak furniture on wooden decking. With luxurious bedding including a handmade king size Lit Bateau bed with a Vi-Spring luxuriously comfortable handmade mattress. Immediate and live AVAILABILITY. Accepting: American Express plus most credit and debit cards. Whitley Coach House self-catering accommodation has a large bedroom with a super king-size (5ft 6ins x 6ft 6ins) Lit Bateau oak bed designed and handmade with a supremely comfortable Vi-Spring handmade pocket sprung mattress. The living room has high ceilings with exposed beams and includes two three-seater sofas one with a large double pull-out bed. In addition, there is a luxurious deep sprung folding bed for use in the bedroom or entrance hall. ONLINE BOOKING or do look at our Website: www.whitleycoachhouse.co.uk The Space Whitley Coach House is a detached former coach house to a Georgian house, renovated four years ago and just redecorated, providing spacious self-catering accommodation. Whitley Coach House has a large bedroom with an individually designed and handmade kingsize bateau bed designed and handmade in oak, with a supremely comfortable Vi-Spring pocket sprung mattress. The living room has high ceilings with exposed beams and a solid oak floor and includes two three-seater sofas one with a large super king size pull-out bed. The living room has views of the private garden, teak furniture and decked veranda. The kitchen table seats up to six people. This self-catering accommodation has fast broadband, a 40 inch smart TV with Freeview channels and the ability to watch other online services like Netflix. Guest Access The back has a private wooden decked terrace for use in dry weather and garden beyond. There is plenty of private parking. A barbeque can be provided if asked for at an extra charge. Whitley Coach House self-catering accommodation is not adapted for wheelchair users but has a step up into the property on entry. Once inside there are no steps, it is a converted coach house on one level. Interaction with Guests Your host will normally hand you the keys and discuss Whitley Coach House and the surrounding area with you on arrival. Unless you need help or are staying over a week, you will be left alone to enjoy your stay.

title: Willow Barn
subtitle: Comfortable luxury barn which has recently been converted to a high standard.
bodyContent: Willow Barn is a comfortable welcoming 4* barn which has been converted to a high standard and offering luxury self-catering rental accommodation. It is situated down a private drive in the grounds of a 17th Century Grade II listed Cotswold stone farmhouse, overlooking the Wiltshire countryside. The barn sleeps 4 and has an open plan kitchen, dining, living area with oak beams and a woodburning log fire. There is a large walled garden, tennis court and private parking. Perfectly situated for visiting the National Trust properties in this area including Lacock village and Abbey, Great Chalfield Manor, The Courts in Holt and Dyrham Park.The World Heritage city of Bath is 10 miles away. Willow Barn is an ideal base for shopping, walking, cycling, golf and equestrian activities. The holiday barn is adjacent to West Wilts Equestrian Centre. Local wedding venues include Wick Farm, Woolley Grange Hotel and the Tythe Barn in Bradford on Avon.

title: Withy Mills Farm
subtitle: Four sympathetically restored stone farm buildings, now providing beautifully appointed contemporary accommodation.
bodyContent: Withy Mills Farm has four romantic cottages in a secluded rural location with stunning views across the Mendip Hills. A twenty minute drive takes you to the city of Bath or Wells. It’s a great location for a family holiday or a romantic get away. Close to two popular wedding venues, Priston Mill and Radford Farm. Whippletree Cottage has two bedrooms and sleeps four people, while the other properties each have one bedroom and are designed for two people sharing. We can provide travel cots and high chairs etc for those travelling with a baby. All the cottages have the luxury of underfloor heating provided by our ground source heat pump. Wharfingers and The Engine House have whirlpool baths. Whippletree, Wharfingers and The Engine House also have a wood burning fire, ideal for cosy winter evenings. Please see our individual entries for each cottage or visit our website www.withymillsfarm.co.uk for further details. The four properties are Whippletree Cottage, The Engine House, Wharfingers Cottage and Barleycorn.

title: Walking in famous historical footsteps with a little Train Travel to support!
subtitle: Take the Train and Bus to the home to UNESCO World Heritage Georgian City of Bath and the smallest medieval city in the UK, Wells, with origins going back 2000 years to Roman times. Then the spiritual town of Glastonbury with legends of Christ, Joseph of Arimathea and the resting place of King Arthur & Guinevere. Whilst being known for the foundations of European Christianity.

title: Family weekend in North Somerset
subtitle: Excitement, Adventure, Memories. These are the take-aways from a great family weekend that gives renewed energy for the week ahead.

title: Three Day Family Fun in and around Minehead
subtitle: Minehead has been a famous family destination for decades, reflecting a rural community on the fringes of Exmoor in West Somerset with a long sandy beach framed by a picturesque harbour and the iconic North Hill behind. Where better then to start your Minehead family fun with a Day Pass to Butlins resort, found at the end of the promenade and brimming with fun! There are rides, the Splash Waterworld, play areas, activities and the entertainment in Skyline pavilion plus so much more.

title: Paranormal Trail
subtitle: Walk through some of Somerset's most haunted locations and explore the ghostly going on that really cannot be explained.

title: The Wolf Hall Intinerary
subtitle: Visit some of the locations of the recent BBC Wolf Hall adaption now playing on the BBC

title: Famous Somerset
subtitle: Somerset, England, is a treasure trove of stunning landscapes, historic landmarks, and charming villages that have long caught the attention of filmmakers and television producers. For those interested in film tourism, this picturesque county offers an ideal opportunity to explore iconic locations that have graced the screen while immersing yourself in the unique charm of the region.

title: Bristol Airport
subtitle: Your holiday starts at the airport
bodyContent: Handling over 8.6 million passengers annually, Bristol Airport is the third largest regional airport in England and the main airport serving Somerset, situated just 7 miles from the edge of the county. With flights to over 125 direct destinations, the airport facilitates more than a million inbound visits to the South West each year, including over 200,000 to Somerset. Global connections to the region are also facilitated through multiple-daily flights between Bristol Airport and major European hubs, including Amsterdam, Brussels, Paris and Dublin. £225 million has been invested in passenger facilities at the Airport since 2010. Work has now begun on an updated Master Plan looking to the future to the mid-2040’s which will consider how best to meet growing demand for air travel to and from the South West and South Wales region. Retail & catering offers: https://www.bristolairport.co.uk/at-the-airport/shop-and-eat Holiday offers: https://www.bristolairport.co.uk/where-can-i-fly/offers Sign up to our Reward Emails: https://www.bristolairport.co.uk/rewards

title: Izzi Stockton
subtitle: With over 18 years experience as a Bridal Dressmaker, Izzi understands how to help you achieve the perfect look for your big day.
bodyContent: Bridal Gowns Izzi Stockton Bridal in Taunton stocks a great range of beautiful bridal dresses from top UK Designers, Veromia’s Sonsie collecton, Callista Bride and Tiffany’s Jessica Grace Bridal, with prices starting from £300! We have bridal gowns from sizes 10-30 and specialise in gowns for Plus Size Brides. All dresses are altered and fitted in house so that they fit you perfectly, and we can be store your gown until you are ready to collect up to the day before your wedding. With a wide range of Bridesmaids dresses, Junior Bridesmaids and Flower Girls available, you can be sure to find the right dresses for your wedding. Appointments are recommended but not always necessary. Prom Promise Izzi keeps a record of every Prom dress sold ensuring that no two identical dresses go to the same Prom. title: Somerset Farmers Market
subtitle: Established in 1999 as a not-for-profit organisation Somerset Farmers' Markets was set up to support and promote local farmers, food and drink producers and local towns. We aim to enhance town centres with vibrant markets providing customers with fresh, high-quality and traceable produce.
bodyContent: Somerset Farmers’ Markets were born as an initiative to ‘act locally’ to prevent climate change by focusing on sustainable development. By supporting small scale farms and food production by encouraging shoppers to buy local, food miles are kept low minimising the negative impact on the environment. From medieval town squares to bustling high streets, each market has its own character and boasts a unique line up from our membership of over 100 hundred producers. Visitors enjoy the experience of talking directly to producers about food and drink, picking up recipe suggestions and storage tips. We hold 8 markets across Somerset: Axbridge, First Saturday of the month, 9am - 1pm Burnham-on-Sea, Last Friday of the month, 9am - 1pm Crewkerne, Third Saturday of the month, 9am - 1pm Frome Cheese & Grain, Second Saturday of the month, 9am - 1pm SFM at Frome Independent, First Sunday of the month, 10am - 3pm Glastonbury, Fourth Saturday of the month, 9am - 2pm Keynsham, Second Saturday of the month, 9am - 1pm Midsomer Norton, First Saturday of the month, 9am - 1pm

title: Blakehay Theatre Re-Opening
subtitle: The Blakehay Theatre, in Weston-super-Mare, is delighted to announce that they are re-opening in January 2022.
bodyContent: Having closed in March 2020 due to the pandemic, and after receiving a Culture Recovery Fund Grant in October 2020, the theatre staff were able to create Blakehay@Home, and stage ‘Comedy at the Quarry’ in June 2021. However, the majority of this fund was to make alterations to the theatre and in May 2021, the contractors moved into the theatre. During 2021 the contractors have been busy installing a new ventilation system and altering the backstage dressing rooms. At the same time the theatre has undergone a complete electrical re-wire making the theatre future-proof and helping with the theatre’s carbon footprint. Work on the theatre is now in the last stages of completion and will re-open to the public in January 2022 with the first performance performed by Weston Operatic Society juniors, OPPITTS, with their aptly named show ‘Opening Up’ with songs from all your favourite shows from stage and screen on Saturday 29 th and Sunday 30 th January, tickets on sale now. The studios will be re-opening in week commencing Monday 10 th January with the return of our Community Classes, including a few new classes for 2022. Check out the theatre website for more information. “We are so happy to be opening the theatre bringing live performances back. It has been a tough couple of years, not just for us but for the whole industry. The pandemic has impacted heavily on theatre and we hope that 2022 will be our busiest year yet. We have an amazing variety of shows and we are confident that there is something for everyone. We can’t wait to welcome people back into this beautiful building, there really is nothing like sitting in a theatre and watching live performance.” – Sally Heath, Theatre Manager. As an important venue in the heart of Weston-super-Mare the Blakehay Theatre will be welcoming back local groups to perform on the stage as well as professional productions that were postponed from 2020. “The small but beautiful Blakehay Theatre is the town’s own theatre, owned by the people of our town through the town council. It is wonderful to see it reopening after nearly 2 years and a refurbishment and I’m definitely going to take the opportunity to see a show in early 2022.” Malcolm Nicholson, Town Clerk The Blakehay Theatre is an approved venue to be able to use the industry-wide ‘See it Safely’ mark, so you can feel confident and safe knowing that our venue is COVID-secure and will be following the latest government guidance. If you would like to see the work that has been done at the theatre, there will be an open day on Saturday 22 nd January 2022 from 10am to 4pm . Everyone is welcome to pop in and have a look around the theatre as well as buy tickets to our upcoming shows and events. For further information and to book your tickets, please visit the theatre’s website www.blakehaytheatre.co.uk
tagline: The Blakehay Theatre, in Weston-super-Mare, is delighted to announce that they are re-opening

title: Ask Italian
subtitle: FROM OUR KITCHEN TO YOUR HOME
bodyContent: The ASK Italian chain of restaurants produces a good range of Italian dishes including pizza, pasta and salads. The informal dining experience appeals to all age groups from lunches to evening meal. We chose just about the most beautiful building we could find for our ASK Italian restaurant in Wells: the Market Hall on Market Place. Of course it can’t compare to the sheer majesty of Wells Cathedral, or the moated Bishop’s Palace, both a few minutes’ stroll from our doors, but the historic architecture of Wells is one of the main reasons the city is such a lovely place to live and so popular with holidaymakers. We bring a little continental culture ourselves, overlooking the river with a view of Bishops castle, we boast a menu crammed with dishes flavoured with ingredients straight from Italy, and a friendly, relaxing atmosphere. Outside the city there are more natural and manmade wonders to explore. We recommend the Mendip Hills and Somerset Levels, Cheddar Gorge and Wookey Hole Caves in particular, but a stop at Wells Visitor Information Service in Wells Museum will allow you to plan a perfect itinerary. It’s just a five-minute walk from our restaurant.

title: Red Sky at Myrtle Farm
subtitle: Stunning views of Glastonbury Tor and the Somerset Levels await you at this gorgeous campsite, perched on the south side of the Mendip Hills. Myrtle Farm is the perfect base for exploring the surrounding countryside and woodland, local tourist attractions and the historic city of Wells, just two miles away.
bodyContent: Your bell tent will be furnished with real beds and mattresses, duvets, pillows and much more for a cosy night’s sleep. You’ll be right by the caves, tunnels and museum at Wookey Hole and just a short drive from the stunning Cheddar and Ebbor Gorges; climbing at Burrington Combe; fishing at local reservoirs; and loads of leafy lanes and trails.

title: Mistral
subtitle: As a spirited, independent teenager, our founder Tracey followed her love of the fashion industry to London.
bodyContent: She earned her stripes in the heartland of the great British highstreet, gaining experience on the buying team of a major retailer, before leaving the capital to start a family. In the mid-90s, still passionate about casual wear, Tracey joined forces with her father John, forming a formidable father-daughter team that combined their business skill and creative flair. As a result, the first Mistral shop opened in Malmesbury. Our Talented Team The Mistral brand has come a long way since we started out with just five staff (including John and Tracey)! Over time, and as a result of our team’s hard work and passion, Mistral has grown. Today you’ll find our stores on high streets across the UK, and a booming wholesale business run across the UK and Europe. We’re going from strength to strength online too – pulling out all the stops to ensure that our lovely customers can get their Mistral fashion fix wherever or whenever they please. John retired in March 2020, but has left the business in excellent hands. The future is looking as bright as Mistral's signature prints. When it comes to our distinctive style, we have our talented in-house creatives to thank. Inspired by the ever-changing landscapes around us, as well as destinations further afield, all of our beautiful print designs start life in our head office. Each one is crafted by our fabulous designers, who can be found cutting lino and happily painting on a daily basis. Our Company Statement We are a community of like-minded, empowered, creative and lively individuals who are brought together by fashion. Our uniquely crafted, quirky DNA and colourful in-house designs inspires confidence, pride and fun by making fashion a feeling to all. Bright and Beautiful At Mistral, our designs are guided by you, our lovely customers. You are totally central to the heart of the clothing we produce, and we will always listen to your loves, wishes, wants and feedback. We have always been passionate about the bright, bold prints that you tell us you love so much, and we’re committed to creating garments which bring a smile to your faces, and help you feel like the glorious individuals that you are. Our culture reflects our fun, family ethos. We care deeply about our staff, and in turn they care for each other and our customers. We try to reflect this commitment to a supportive, kind environment in our social responsibility. We are constantly reviewing and striving to do the very best we can for our customers, our community and the wider environment.

title: The Sheppey Inn
subtitle: The Sheppey Inn lies out on the beautiful wilds of the Somerset Levels, surrounded by peat moors, dairy farms and national wildlife reserves.
bodyContent: The pub pulls in people from miles around thanks to the brilliant, eclectic musicians it attracts, its fine selection of local ales and ciders (including all kinds of one-offs and speciality brews), and its fantastic food. Spending the afternoon out here in the countryside, lounging by the river, looking out for voles and kingfishers, isn’t the worst idea in the world, is it? There’s been a pub in Godney servicing the thirsty throats of Levels farmworkers for many centuries. The last owners ran it for 120 years, but on one day in 1976, they ran out of cider and lost the trust of the next two generations of locals. the pub has been renovated, revamped and restored, and now has about six casks of grown-ups’ apple juice on the bar to make sure that the such a thing never happens again. Check out the photos on the right for proof.
tagline: The Sheppey Inn lies out on the beautiful wilds of the Somerset Levels.

title: The Glastonbury Town House
subtitle: Paula welcomes you to her comfortable 4 Star Edwardian Bed & Breakfast close to Glastonbury Town Centre, Glastonbury Tor, Chalice Well Gardens , Rural Life Museum and other local attractions.
bodyContent: We offer a quality bed and breakfast service in the heart of Glastonbury , from where exploring Glastonbury Abbey, Glastonbury Tor and the Glastonbury Thorn is a matter of a short stroll. The Bed and Breakfast offers group bookings. 2 twin rooms and a king room offer up to 6 people accommodation. Paula offers packed lunches, afternoon tea and evening meals at an extra cost for group bookings. Liaise with Paula direct to book group bookings. The Townhouse is only a few minutes’ walk from the hustle of Glastonbury‘s busy town centre full of unusual shops, churches, historic buildings and varied cafes and bars. The house has far reaching views of Glastonbury town and the Mendip Hills beyond. The Townhouse offer secure facilities for cyclists and is Proximity to Millfield school. The Glastonbury Townhouse is 1 miles from Street and the Clarkes Outlet Village and 3 miles from the various nature reserves on the Somerset levels. We are 28 miles South of Bristol and Bath, 20 miles from Bristol International airport and within easy reach of Stonehenge , Yeovilton Airbase and other historic places of interest. The Glastonbury Townhouse can be used as a base for exploring the Isles of Avalon, Somerset Peat Levels, Exmoor (Lorna Doone country), the North Somerset Coast and large parts of the county of Dorset . Our visitors tell us that our proximity to Bristol Airport , Bath , the bath and west showgound, Shepton Mallet, Frome, Wells, Street, Yeovil is a key part of their decision to make their stay with us in Glastonbury . Of course we also have guests who visit specifically for the Glastonbury Festival, Glastonbury Extravaganza and the famous Glastonbury Carnival, we are on the route, watch from the comfort of your room! We are also open for Christmas and New Year bookings.

title: The Pillars Restaurant & Lounge Bar
subtitle: Experience and enjoy the sophisticated atmosphere that Street's newest venue now offers. Set over two floors with a secluded alfresco terrace, the ground floor bar offers an extensive range of wines, Champagnes, beers, as well its own brand of home brewed craft ale. Pillars has been sympathetically refurbished to acknowledge its entertainment history throughout the decades.
bodyContent: Welcome to The Pillars Restaurant and Lounge Bar - an exciting new venue in the heart of Street We're quickly earning a reputation for one of the best venues in town. Set over two floors with a secluded alfresco terrace, our ground floor bar offers an extensive range of wines, Champagnes, beers, ales and ciders as well as our own brand of home brewed craft ale. Experience and enjoy the sophisticated atmosphere that Street's newest venue now offers. The Pillars has been sympathetically refurbished to acknowledge its entertainment history throughout the decades. History of The Site The beginning The building was built in 1920 for two local businessmen, Mr Voaks, a local butcher and Mr Hecks, the forerunner of the local Hecks cider farm. The doors first opened on 15th January, 1921 as "The Playhouse Theatre." The Playhouse had four changing rooms, a 20ft deep stage and a 26ft wide proscenium. The original proscenium arch can still be seen today above what is now the piano deck. The arched ceiling is an original pressed tin design. The transition The Playhouse Theatre gave way to the Playhouse Cinema as technology evolved and the big curtains gave way to the big screen. The age of the cinema The building retained the name "The Playhouse" for 25 years until July 1946, when it was renamed "Maximes Cinema". For over 40 years, the building enjoyed life as a cinema with a variety of owners including Cornell Cinemas until the mid 50's and then Myles Byrne Cinemas. Maximes had one screen and 561 seats. Many local Somerset people will recall watching their first film on the big screen and many we are sure will recall magical and memorable romantic interludes within the many rows! The end of the big screen Maximes cinema played its last film on 15th September 1989. The start of the nightclub After the cinema closed, the seats were removed to create large open spaces. The screen was taken down to create more depth to the building and the next phase of the building's life was born into Maximes Nightclub. Maximes traded as a night club for many years. In 2001, the club embarked on a major refurbishment and was re-born as "Envy". Most residents of Somerset refer to the building now as the 'Envy building'. Envy enjoyed being a popular destination for thousands of party-goers hosting many themed nights and live music presentations. In June 2015, the owner Adam Fynn, announced he was to relocate and set about plans to sell the building and applied for planning permission to develop the site into residential properties. The end of the night club era On 11th December 2016, the then operators of Envy announced that the club would close at the end of the year and on 31st December 2016, Envy Nighclub opened and closed its doors for the very last time. The building sat dormant, empty and cold for nearly four months before going to auction on 27th April 2017. The building failed to sell at auction and the doors at Envy remained closed. A new beginning The building was finally purchased by us in June 2017. The new owner vowed to preserve the historic building and return it to back to its former glory as an entertainment venue for the mid Somerset arena. Throughout the remainder of 2017 and into the first half of 2018, plans were made and relevant planning permissions granted to commence the transformation of the building into the Loft. Throughout the re-development of the site, we have been sympathetic to the buildings unique history as an entertainment venue. We have combined all its past into the future, with food, drink, entertainment and music, all under one roof! We are very proud of the achievements and of the building. We do hope that you enjoy your experience here and look forward to welcoming you back to Pillars again soon. The Management Facilities include: Facilities : Unrivalled Grill Menu Al fresco dining area Regular Live Music & Entertainment Our own craft ales and beers Over 45 wines from around the world Available for private hire Wedding Receptions Unrivalled Cocktail & Gin Bar Market Fresh Daily Food Christmas Parties Christenings Large Dance Floor
tagline: The Pillars Restaurant and Lounge Bar is an exciting venue in the heart of Street.

title: Nether Stowey
subtitle: The village of Nether Stowey is an ideal base for exploring the Quantock Hills – England’s first Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty – as its famous former resident Samuel Taylor Coleridge discovered more than 200 years ago.
bodyContent: The poet, who completed most of his best work while living in Nether Stowey , was on a walking tour of Somerset when he met Thomas Poole, another important resident whose legacy is everywhere in the village and who became a lifelong friend. For a while, William Wordsworth rented a mansion nearby and the two poets walked miles together across the hills and along the route to Lynmouth now known as Coleridge Way. As if the National Trust owned Coleridge Cottage were not enough, Nether Stowey is packed with other gems including a ruined Norman castle, a Victorian town clock and lock up, cobbled pavement, a stream running down the side of the street and a clutch of ancient cottages. Today Nether Stowey is divided in two by the A39 but it does mean there is less traffic in the centre. Across the road from the main village is the imposing Stowey Court with a stone gazebo built into its outer wall and St Mary’s Church with its substantial memorial to Thomas Poole. Stowey Estate belonged to Lord Audley in 1343 but fell into ruin for several hundred years before being completed. A hoard of silverware was found nearby thought to date from the Civil War. Also on this side of the village is Cricketer Farm Shop and cafe.

title: Greenbank Pool
subtitle: Greenbank Pool is an outdoor heated family friendly swimming pool in the heart of Street, Somerset. It is within easy walking distance of both the High Street and Clarks Village.
bodyContent: Greenbank Pool opened in 1937 and is in an art deco style. There are two pools. The smaller one is the children’s pool with a slide for under 8s in the shallow end. There is also a larger pool which is deeper and suitable for competent swimmers. The pools are ringed by low walls containing the paved poolside area. Beyond the low walls is grass which provides a lot of space for picnicking. There is also a wet play area on the site with fountains and jets which is terrific fun for children and the young at heart. The pool also has a small shop on site. In the main building are changing rooms and showers; including a larger sized accessible changing room which is bookable when the pool is open. There are accessible features in the showers and toilets. At the rear of the site is level access for wheelchair users. There is one disabled parking space outside the pool.

title: Blakehay Theatre Re-Opening
subtitle: The Blakehay Theatre, in Weston-super-Mare, is delighted to announce that they are re-opening in January 2022.
bodyContent: Having closed in March 2020 due to the pandemic, and after receiving a Culture Recovery Fund Grant in October 2020, the theatre staff were able to create Blakehay@Home, and stage ‘Comedy at the Quarry’ in June 2021. However, the majority of this fund was to make alterations to the theatre and in May 2021, the contractors moved into the theatre. During 2021 the contractors have been busy installing a new ventilation system and altering the backstage dressing rooms. At the same time the theatre has undergone a complete electrical re-wire making the theatre future-proof and helping with the theatre’s carbon footprint. Work on the theatre is now in the last stages of completion and will re-open to the public in January 2022 with the first performance performed by Weston Operatic Society juniors, OPPITTS, with their aptly named show ‘Opening Up’ with songs from all your favourite shows from stage and screen on Saturday 29 th and Sunday 30 th January, tickets on sale now. The studios will be re-opening in week commencing Monday 10 th January with the return of our Community Classes, including a few new classes for 2022. Check out the theatre website for more information. “We are so happy to be opening the theatre bringing live performances back. It has been a tough couple of years, not just for us but for the whole industry. The pandemic has impacted heavily on theatre and we hope that 2022 will be our busiest year yet. We have an amazing variety of shows and we are confident that there is something for everyone. We can’t wait to welcome people back into this beautiful building, there really is nothing like sitting in a theatre and watching live performance.” – Sally Heath, Theatre Manager. As an important venue in the heart of Weston-super-Mare the Blakehay Theatre will be welcoming back local groups to perform on the stage as well as professional productions that were postponed from 2020. “The small but beautiful Blakehay Theatre is the town’s own theatre, owned by the people of our town through the town council. It is wonderful to see it reopening after nearly 2 years and a refurbishment and I’m definitely going to take the opportunity to see a show in early 2022.” Malcolm Nicholson, Town Clerk The Blakehay Theatre is an approved venue to be able to use the industry-wide ‘See it Safely’ mark, so you can feel confident and safe knowing that our venue is COVID-secure and will be following the latest government guidance. If you would like to see the work that has been done at the theatre, there will be an open day on Saturday 22 nd January 2022 from 10am to 4pm . Everyone is welcome to pop in and have a look around the theatre as well as buy tickets to our upcoming shows and events. For further information and to book your tickets, please visit the theatre’s website www.blakehaytheatre.co.uk
tagline: The Blakehay Theatre, in Weston-super-Mare, is delighted to announce that they are re-opening

title: The Old Vicarage Hotel and Restaurant, Bridgwater, Somerset
subtitle: This unique and quirky hotel is a 10 minute drive from the main line station at Bridgwater or 24 minutes from M5 Junction 24 - so is close to all connecting services and local amenities and supermarkets.
bodyContent: “Looking for somewhere really special to stay, look no further you have found it”, “I don’t think I have ever been made to feel so welcome”, are just some of our recent 5-star reviews. This historic hotel has been lovingly renovated with bedrooms individually designed for complete relaxation and comfort. If you want to be spoilt, relax and eat delicious food visit Candy, Peter and their friendly, professional team whose mission to give every guest (and their dogs) the warmest of welcomes and most memorable stay. The Old Vicarage is tucked away in peaceful surroundings overlooking St Mary’s Church, the only building in Bridgwater older than it, yet is only 10 minutes from the M5. The hotel is full of historic importance dating back to 1327; it is said that Isambard Kingdom Brunel designed the town bridge in the 17th century Oak Room and Judge Jeffery’s stayed, one of the bedrooms even has its own wig cabinet. Each of the 18 en-suite bedrooms are individually designed and kept spotlessly clean with the most comfortable beds and views over the gardens or church. The south facing gardens are glorious, perfect for weddings and enjoying in the sunshine. On cooler evenings there is a cosy bar and snug with comfy sofas for enjoying a drink or two in front of the fire, an oak panelled restaurant and a brand new undercover patio with a pizza oven. A short drive and you can be alone on the Quantock Hills walking in Coleridge’s footsteps, bird watching on the Somerset Levels or hunting for fossils on the Jurassic Coast at Kilve. For the more energetic kayaking, coasteering, mountain biking, pony trekking are all on hand or if shopping is your thing Bristol, Bath, Taunton, Glastonbury and Wells are not far away. Book today for your perfect holiday.
tagline: “Looking for somewhere really special to stay, look no further you have found it”
