title: Spine-chilling ghost tours to bring spooky tales to life at Dunster Castle
subtitle: The National Trust team at Dunster Castle is once again offering visitors the chance to uncover the creepy tales, unused corridors and dark corners of the castle with two nights of candlelit, late night guided tours.
bodyContent: The tours will be held on the 30 and 31 October with the first tour at 6.20pm and the last at 10.20pm. Tickets available at www.nationaltrust.org.uk/dunster-castle . Many of the historic houses that the National Trust look after have their fair share of dark and grisly tales and the hilltop at Dunster, home to a castle for more than 1,000 years, is no exception with many reports of ghostly sightings and sensations. Among the castle’s grimmest of tales, is the story of the oubliette that adjoins the old gateway. Many medieval castles would have had a means of holding their prisoners in an underground cell beneath a gatehouse, and this dark, damp space is reputed to be a pit dungeon where prisoners would have been lowered in through a trap door, forgotten about and left to die. Sir Walter Luttrell told the story of a skeleton being found here in the 19th century, creating the legend of an excavation which unearthed a 7-foot-tall skeleton manacled to the wall by his wrists and ankles. Dogs seem particularly troubled by this sinister site and sometimes refuse to climb the steps near to where the body was found. David Moore, House and Collections Manager at Dunster Castle, agreed that working at the castle can sometimes be eerie: ‘When we are closing up the castle at night, especially at this time of year, it is difficult not to see strange shadows in windows and hear footsteps or keys rattling.’ Each ghost tour will be led by an expert storyteller who will relay a wealth of haunted tales from the castle’s long and fascinating history including recent reports of men’s voices and loud marching footsteps in areas of the castle known to be empty. Jill Schofield, Senior Programming and Partnerships Officer at Dunster Castle added “We can’t wait to welcome you to this year’s Ghost Tours at the castle. They’ve always been such a popular event here, though definitely not for the faint-hearted, it’ll be such a pleasure to welcome visitors again for two nights of jumps and chills!” Dunster Castle’s ghost tours will take place on Monday 30 October and Tuesday 31 October and last approximately 50 minutes. Tickets are £25 per person and must be booked in advance at https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/dunster-castle or by calling 0344 249 1895.
tagline: Spine-chilling ghost tours to bring spooky tales to life at Dunster Castle

bodyContent: Many of the historic houses that the National Trust look after, have their fair share of dark and grisly tales and Dunster Castle is no exception with many reports of ghostly sightings and sensations. Each ghost tour will be led by an guide who will relay a wealth of haunted tales from the castle’s long and fascinating history including recent reports of men’s voices and loud marching footsteps in areas of the castle known to be empty. Get ready to be scared, who knows what you may find in the dark? Please note Please meet at the Ticket Office at least 10 minutes before the tour is due to depart. Tours will leave on time. Please wear sensible, flat shoes and come well wrapped up. There is a steep hill leading up to the castle. Changes of levels, steep and uneven steps and confined spaces within the tour route, as well as low lighting levels. The tours are recommended for ages 13 and over. Takeaway refreshments available: hot and cold drinks, bacon and sausage baps, bakes, cakes, crisps. Food and drink are not permitted on the tours. Please be considerate of your tour guide and other visitors at all times. You will not be admitted or will be asked to leave if your behaviour is inappropriate i.e. under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Tickets are non-refundable.

title: The Yarn Market Hotel
subtitle: Ideally located in the centre of the medieval village of Dunster. The hotel is two and half hours via the A39 from the M5 - but is ten minutes away from the West Somerset Railway England's longest heritage railway. With Minehead 20 minutes away there are all the major facilities you need.
bodyContent: The Yarn Market Hotel in Dunster is ideally located in the centre of Dunster, one of the most perfectly preserved medieval villages in England, and the gateway to Exmoor National Park. The magnificent Dunster Castle is at the end of the street and the West Somerset Railway runs close by. There are many themed breaks on offer throughout the year, and the area is perfect for those who enjoy outdoor activities or just a relaxing break. For walkers the hotel has excellent facilities including a boot and drying room, and maps are readily available combined with local knowledge to help you with your walks. Most of the bedrooms have either a view over the village or the surrounding countryside. Pets are most welcome at the hotel in the dog-friendly rooms. The restaurant opens daily for dinner, reservations are advisable.
tagline: Our Hotel is situated in the beautiful Village of Dunster, within the Exmoor National Park.

title: Charlton House, Montigo Resorts Somerset
subtitle: Discover an oasis of calm at Montigo Resorts, Somerset. With luxurious, individually designed rooms, a spa inspired by Asian traditions, and farm-to-table dining, Charlton House offers an unparalleled rural escape. Experience relaxation, rejuvenation, and the best of Somerset’s local flavours.
bodyContent: Somersets, Montigo Resorts - Charlton House, Shepton Mallet - is nestled in the heart of Somerset’s picturesque countryside, Montigo Resorts, Somerset at Charlton House offers the perfect escape. This historic estate features 28 uniquely designed rooms, each with its own character and charm, combining contemporary comforts with the building’s rich heritage. Whether you’re seeking a cosy hideaway or a spacious suite for a longer stay, there’s a room to suit every taste. The resort’s spa is a serene sanctuary where Asian wellness meets the healing power of nature. Boasting state-of-the-art thermal facilities, hydrotherapy pools, and specialist therapies like Balinese and Thai massages, you’re assured a deeply relaxing experience. For dining, Montigo Resorts showcases the best of Somerset’s seasonal produce; from the colourful cocktails, seasoned meats, and fresh, locally sourced seafood, cooked to perfection, at Tiigo, our kitchen garden pop up promises an authentic pan-Asian experience in a laid-back setting, while the Charlton House restaurant offers a more refined affair and Bob’s Bistro ensures you can grab a bite in the bar or lounge at any time. Whether you’re here for a wellness retreat, a romantic weekend, or simply to unwind, Montigo Resorts, Somerset at Charlton House invites you to embrace the tranquillity of this little gem of a county.
tagline: Discover an oasis of calm at Montigo Resorts, Somerset. With luxurious, individually designed rooms

title: Whatever The Weather

bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Ever feel overwhelmed, very sad, full of joy or a little bit angry? Led by two performers, children will journey through storm clouds, jump in puddles and bask in the sunshine, discovering how different feelings can be expressed and understood. title: Anyone for Tennis?
subtitle: A hilarious behind-the-scenes look at the world of professional tennis, Anyone for Tennis? sees former Wimbledon line judge and comedian Pauline Eyre sharing stories, secrets and laughs from two decades on the court.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } After 20 years as a Wimbledon line judge, comedian Pauline Eyre is ready to spill the Pimms on life behind the scenes at professional tennis tournaments. From the royal box to the locker room, Anyone for Tennis? serves up an entertaining mix of gossip, anecdotes and personal experiences from one of the sport's most iconic championships. Expect smashing stories, ace anecdotes and a heartfelt love letter to the game, delivered with warmth, wit and impeccable comic timing. The show explores everything from the traditions of Wimbledon to the decision to phase out line judges, all while providing plenty of laughs along the way. Fresh from a sold-out run at the Edinburgh Fringe 2025, Pauline's show has earned praise from audiences and critics alike for its blend of insider knowledge and engaging comedy. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: Wimbledon stories, tennis secrets and comedy from former line judge Pauline Eyre.

title: A two day break in Wellington
subtitle: Wellington is an atmospheric and historic place to spend a night and give yourself time to explore this traditional town and surrounding area.
bodyContent: Day One – Market Town Living Upon arrival enjoy a late breakfast or brunch at Café Licious , A House of Cake or BrewTwo at the Cleeve before exploring Wellington's independent shopping streets. Browse boutiques , gift shops, delicatessens and Wellington's popular and characterful independent stores along Fore Street and South Street. Late morning visit to Wellington Museum to understand how this small market town developed from wool production into the thriving community it is today. Lunch at one of the town's independent restaurants, for example Ruxstons . Spend the afternoon following a self-guided heritage walk , discovering: Wellington's churches historic buildings former banking heritage Duke of Wellington connections public art. Explore Wellington Park and the Basins. Finish with drinks and dinner at The Green Dragon . Overnight at the Green Dragon or The Blue Mantle Guesthouse Day Two – Blackdown Hills Adventure After breakfast, drive ten minutes to Wellington Monument . Standing proudly on the Blackdown Hills, the 175-foot monument celebrates Arthur Wellesley, the Duke of Wellington, and offers one of the area's most recognisable landmarks. Spend the morning walking one of the many footpaths through the Blackdown Hills National Landscape, enjoying spectacular views across Somerset and Devon. Return via local villages, and stopping at farm shops and nurseries including Sheppy’s Cider Farm, Willowbrook Garden Centre. Also check Brazier Coffee Roasters at Tonedale Mill and the Fox Brothers fine flannel and cloth shop.

title: Family weekend in North Somerset via Train from London!
subtitle: Excitement, Adventure, Memories. These are the take-aways from a great family weekend that gives renewed energy for the week ahead. Get the train to Nailsea in North Somerset and find many hidden gems to really make a family day out truly special!

title: Coastal walks, Street Art and other amazing discoveries around Weston-super-Mare
subtitle: Fresh air and discoveries without the hassle of driving and parking? Then this is the two day experience for you. We start in Weston-super-Mare at the town’s newly refurbished museum just back from the seafront in Burlington Street. With free entry, this is the ideal base from which to learn about the town and surrounding area that will give great context for your two day discovery. With 50,000 objects there is no shortage of diversity!

title: Weekend break for couples in Minehead

title: The Strawberry Line - Winscombe to Axbridge Hill
subtitle: On leaving Winscombe towards the Mendips, cutting and embankment alternate. Hills to both sides turn into a deep wooded cutting before the line passes under Shute Shelve Hill through an original 165-metre, lit railway tunnel. Inside, you can clearly see the change in geology from soft brick-faced soft marl to hard limestone.

title: Astaires
subtitle: Astaires Outfitters and Tailors. We provide ready made clothing, made to measure clothing and formal hire.
bodyContent: We provide ready made clothing, made to measure clothing and formal hire. Ready Made Clothing- At Astaires we pride ourselves on the diverse range of ready to wear clothing and accessories that we hold. Formal Hire - Your wedding day is one of the most important days of your life and your wedding suit is a major part of that. If you look your best, you will feel your best. Here at Astaires in Taunton we can offer an extensive range of mens and boys wedding suits to hire, from classic top hat and tails to contemporary designs that set you apart, all supplied by Cameron Ross. We can offer many waistcoat colours and designs that are exclusive to us in Taunton, with coordinating neckwear. Made to Measure - Here at Astaires in partnership with Bernhardt fashion we are bringing Made To Measure Tailoring into the 21st Century with computer guided pattern making and garment cutting. We can offer many of the features usually only found on a bespoke garment, such as padded lapels, working cuffs and canvas interlinings, in addition to suits, jackets, trousers, waistcoats and shirts at a modest cost.

title: Somerset Cider Brandy Company & Burrow Hill Cider
subtitle: At Burrow Hill we make traditional ciders as well as Somerset Cider Brandy. Visit the farm and see the UK’s first commercial cider distillery, explore the orchards and wander amongst 170 year old vats.
bodyContent: Somerset Cider resides at Burrow Hill where they make traditional ciders as well as Somerset Cider Brandy. Visit the farm and see the UK’s first commercial cider distillery, explore the orchards and wander amongst 170 year old vats. Or just come and sample our award winning ciders, Somerset Cider Brandy and liqueurs. Guided tours can also be booked in advance. Open all year. Monday - Saturday 9.00 - 5.00 Cider House - In the ciderhouse there is cider and Somerset Cider Brandy to sample amongst the oak vats, barrels and presses - all the paraphernalia associated with 150 years of cider making. Burrow Hill - Visitors are also encouraged to walk to the top of our hill and admire the incredible views of the Somerset Levels. On a good day you can see Glastonbury Tor in the distance. The Orchard - The starting point of both our cider and Somerset Cider Brandy is apples from our orchards. Visitors can follow our orchard trail where different apple varieties and other interesting features are explained. The walk takes about 30 minutes and you may need wellies. Distillery - Visitors are welcome to view the copper stills, protected by armour-plated glass and 68 locks and seals (by order of HM Customs & Excise) in the distillery. You can also buy our products online at https://www.somersetciderbrandy.com/

title: Holly Farm Cottages
subtitle: Somerset self catering barns converted to high standard with indoor pool, hot tub, games room and own gardens. Good pubs in easy reach.
bodyContent: Holly Farm Cottages have been converted from traditional Somerset Long Barns to a high standard. The original blue lias and exposed beams have been retained and modern comforts added. The cottages are fully equipped; each kitchen has a fridge-freezer, microwave, washing machine etc. access to a tumble dryer. The living rooms have been comfortably furnished and there is central heating throughout. Each cottage also has an enclosed garden and patio, parking and payphone. Linen and towels (except cot linen) are provided. There is an indoor, heated swimming pool and hot tub. Relax in the orchard or there is a games room for the more energetic, with a pool table and table tennis. Holly Farm is a working farm that has been in the Hembrow family for several generations. You are welcome to walk over the footpaths and see the farm. Stoke St Gregory, on the edge of West Sedgemoor, a well-known wetland and bird reserve, is also the heart of willow growing country. There are shops and good pubs serving food. We are 7 miles from Taunton .
tagline: Somerset self catering barns converted to high standard with indoor pool.

title: Ham Hill
subtitle: Ham Hill country park offers wonderful views of the South Somerset Moors, Exmoor and the Mendip Hills.
bodyContent: Ham Hill country park offers wonderful views of the South Somerset Moors, Exmoor and the Mendip Hills . The 164-hectare country park centres on the huge hill fort that flourished here during the Iron Age. Evidence has been uncovered that this fort was one of the largest in the southwest and the centre of trade in the region for many years. In later times the hill stone (known as Hamstone) was quarried extensively, particularly during the Victorian era. The Houses of Parliament in London are fronted with Hamstone. The park offers a number of walks allowing many splendid views, with The Prince of Wales Hotel, which sits perched on the top of the hill, the perfect place for a lunch break.

title: Watkin TOYS
subtitle: The Watkin family first established Watkin Toys in 1940
bodyContent: The Watkin family first established Watkin Toys in 1940 having moved to the area after the war. The shop still remains a family business today but under the ownership of the Slocombe family. The shop is well known In Taunton and remains a much loved destination for many families. We stock a wide range of Branded Toys, Games, Models, Soft toys, Beanies etc. Each day we receive new stock from our suppliers, so it’s always worth asking if you cannot find what you are looking for in the shop. You never know we may well have it in stock. We are all way amazed to see where the products we sell end up. Over the years we have received a number of Photographs showing our Watkin Toys bags at their final destinations. Take a look at the pictures we have been Sent. You are never too old to Visit a Toy Shop so why not pay US A VISIT !!!

bodyContent: The on-site Marco Pierre White Steakhouse Bar & Grill is one of the finest eateries in the area with an elegant dining room, bar and newly-added Garden Room conservatory which boasts panoramic views and a fully retractable roof for al fresco dining. Marco’s restaurant has his personality stamped all over it and the menu comprises everything you’d expect from a traditional steakhouse. The hotel offers 132 luxury bedrooms including suites, on-site parking and excellent transport access meaning guests can enjoy the facilities for both business and pleasure. Please note from May 1 st , 2022 overnight parking will be chargeable at £5.00 per vehicle. Corporate customers are also well catered for with 12 meeting rooms, multiple breakout areas, and a dedicated conference team on hand. Whether you are hosting a small business meeting to a multi-day conference, DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House does not disappoint as a destination location for business needs.

title: Cavell House Bed and Breakfast B&B in Clevedon
bodyContent: Make yourself at home 3 minutes walk to the sea, 3 minutes walk to the Pier (best sea fishing in Somerset with fishing off the pier) 3 minutes walk to the shops, 1 minute to the Bank, 5 minutes walk to the pub/Chinese/Indian/English food/antiques/sea front cafes. 10 Min slow stroll along the sea front to the childrens leisure aea passing the sailing club, pub, amusements, fish and chips and ice cream on the way. Beautiful views across to Wales. Paddle steamer trips from the -pier, to Lundy, North Devon, Penarth and Gloucester. An ideal base for walkers and cyclists. Background to Cavell House Originally the Victorian home of Lord and Lady Belgrave, it later became a residential Girls School and Nurse Edith Cavell (the world war one heroine) spent some of her school days here. Prior to George and Daphne Hamnett becoming proprietors in 1996, Cavell House was a childrens home administered by the Assemblies of God Pentecostal Church. Breakfast served in room Box Selection of Cereal, milk, Orange Juice, fruit Muffin, Selection of Nuts, Complemented with Croissant, Fresh Coffee, Tea decafe or caffeinated and fresh fruit. - special requests taken Please let reception know what time you would like breakfast, as a guide between 8am and 10am

title: Wookey Hole Hotel
subtitle: Wookey Hole Hotel is 20 minutes from the oldest medieval city in the UK Wells and sixty minutes from the City of Bath so well positioned for all local locations.
bodyContent: Come and stay at the Wookey Hole Hotel for great value family breaks all year round. Ideally placed in the heart of Somerset, the Wookey Hole Hotel can boast comfortable accommodation in picturesque surroundings. Receive access when you book directly! The Wookey Hole Hotel, located on the southern edge of the rolling Mendip Hills , lies in the Sleepy village of Wookey Hole, with easy access to the historic city of Wells and its stunning Cathedral. The Mendip Hills have been recognised as an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and offer stunning landscapes of sweeping slopes and limestone gorges, with endless walking trails and sightseeing spots. Traverse the Mendips and the hills fall away to the breath-taking lakes of the Chew Valley, just a short drive from Wookey Hole. Also close by are Cheddar Gorge and the ancient town of Glastonbury , with Bath, Bristol and the beaches of Burnham-on-Sea and Weston-Super-Mare slightly further afield. The Hotel includes free and secure car and coach parking, modern bedrooms with free wifi plus a stylish Bar and Bistro. The perfect place for a family break or special occasion - we look forward to welcoming you! And of course, discounted tickets to Wookey Hole Caves and attractions!
tagline: Come and stay at The West Country’s newest hotel. Great value family breaks all year round.

title: The Laundry
subtitle: Here at The Laundry we believe that style comes simply and can be fun!
bodyContent: Elegant collections with a little twist and gorgeous fabrics make dressing exciting again. We enjoy finding new labels and brands that work well alongside our established labels allowing our customers to mix and match traditional with unique. The Laundry opened its doors in 2008 in Wells, a beautiful city in the heart of Somerset. Theodora fell in love with the city having relocated herself and her family from London in 2004. Whilst in London Theo enjoyed a successful career as a buyer for Pringle of Scotland and Hermes, Paris. It was whilst working for these labels that her understanding of buying simple but fabulous collections came about. Looking after her customers has always been of paramount importance to Theo and a part of life that she extremely enjoys. Many customers have become good friends and will pop into the shop for a chat as well as to see what is new and exciting! We look forward to welcoming you at The Laundry.

title: Cedars Hall, Wells
subtitle: Welcome to Cedars Hall Cedars Hall is a state-of-the-art performance venue providing a varied programme of top quality entertainment all year round. It is situated in the beautiful grounds of Wells Cathedral School in the heart of the City of Wells.
bodyContent: The hall hosts a number of professional (and amateur) productions throughout the year which include classical, jazz, folk and rock and pop and cabaret concerts, drama, talks and films. The main recital hall, Eavis Hall, has the capacity for audiences up to 350 and is a flexible and modern performance space. In addition to events in Eavis Hall, it serves as a hub for its significant community outreach, which provides music education (including workshops, concerts and masterclasses) for thousands of primary school children, elderly and disability groups in the South West each year. Cedars Hall is also available to hire for concerts and events - please enquire at boxoffice@cedarshallwells.co.uk Tickets for all events can be booked online or via our box office on 01749 834483 For more information visit: https://cedarshallwells.co.uk/

title: The Apple Tree Inn
subtitle: The Apple Tree Inn is a large roadside pub dating back to 1674 which has retained many original features whilst adding a farm shop within the front bar area.
bodyContent: Most of the food offerings are locally sourced with meat being provided by the pubs owner from his own livestock. There is a back room with a dining area and a snug which is used by the locals. The Glastonbury festival site is close to the pub and opening hours are affected during the festival. Bus services pass the door Mon to Sat (not public holidays) every 2 hours on Shepton Mallet, Glastonbury & Street route. The last bus to Street is 16.25 and the last to Shepton Mallet is 18.10. HISTORY At least five medieval houses still survive in part, probably the earliest Old Farmhouse, East Street, which has true crucks similar to those in Bridge Farm, Baltonsborough, which date from the mid 14th century. (fn. 50) Significant alterations and additions were made to several houses in the later 16th and the earlier 17th centuries including upper floors in Higher Southtown Farm, remodelling at Pennard Farm (datestone 1640), and a new wing at Manor Farmhouse, Coxbridge. The Cottage, Higher Southtown, is a timber framed building of the early 17th century. At least four surviving houses date from the mid or late 17th century including Sticklinch Manor and the Apple Tree inn. (fn. 51) The house of a yeoman at Newtown in 1678 comprised porch, hall, parlour, two butteries, and kitchen on the ground floor and five chambers over including a cheese chamber. (fn. 52) There was significant rebuilding of farm houses in the early 19th century.
tagline: The Apple Tree Inn is a large roadside pub dating back to 1674

title: Glastonbury Tor, National Trust
subtitle: Glastonbury Tor is a well-loved Somerset landmark associated with myths and legends, but it is also a place where children can run about and have fun. Fields at the foot of the Tor are good for games or you could play at the top in the ruined tower.
bodyContent: Prominent hill overlooking the Isle of Avalon, Glastonbury and Somerset. This iconic and evocative landmark offers magnificent views of the Somerset Levels , Dorset, Wiltshire and Wales. Steeped in history and legend, excavations at the top of the Tor have revealed the plans of two superimposed churches of St Michael, of which only a 15th-century tower remains. Glastonbury Tor also has a grisly past. Abbot Richard Whiting was executed here in 1549 on the orders of Thomas Cromwell, the first Earl of Essex. Glastonbury Tor is known as being one of the most spiritual sites in the country. Its pagan beliefs are still very much celebrated. It’s a beautiful place to walk, unwind and relax.
tagline: Glastonbury Tor is a well-loved Somerset landmark associated with myths and legends.

title: Ubley
subtitle: Ubley Parish sits in the Yeo valley at the west end of the Chew Valley. It is bordered to the north and south with ridges of hills, most significantly the Mendips to the south. It sits within the Mendip Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB) and close to Blagdon Lake.
bodyContent: Ubley Parish sits in the Yeo valley at the west end of the Chew Valley. It is bordered to the north and south with ridges of hills, most significantly the Mendips to the south. It sits within the Mendip Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB) and close to Blagdon Lake. Ubley is an attractive village set mostly on the valley floor but rises up on the lower slopes of the Mendip Hills to the south. The surrounding valley landscape is of farmland with small and medium sized fields largely for grazing. Fields are separated by well-kept hedgerows with intermittent mature trees. The whole area is rich in wildlife and is rural and unspoilt in character. There are magnificent views from the slopes of the Mendips across the Parish and as far as South Wales to the west and the hills above Bath to the east. There is quite a lot of greenery throughout the village. There are many mature trees, mostly in gardens and the Churchyard in and around the Conservation Area. The roads are lined by a mixture of hedgerows and walls, the latter of which are of local stone. The slopes of the Mendip scarp are densely wooded with an area known as Ubley Wood. The centre of the village is at The Cross, outside the 13th century St Bartholomew’s Church. This is a conservation area, with charming houses and gardens and a view up to the Mendip Hills. There is also a Primary School and a large village hall with a grass amenity area. The village hall hosts some large events such as the ever-popular beer festival in September which are open to all. The site of the Old Sawmill now hosts an artisan cheese-maker. Ubley has many way-marked paths leading either up to the Mendip Hills or down to the edges of Blagdon and Chew Valley Lakes. From the Mendip Hills above Ubley both lakes can be seen, and on a clear day the view is spread from Cardiff to the hills above Bath. There is an Airbnb property in the village, which has recently been developed from an old Methodist Church. Neighbouring villages have accommodation and public houses and are a good base for fisherman who use both lakes to catch trout. Further information can be found at: · Chew Valley Lake · Fly fishing on the lakes

title: The Strode Theatre
subtitle: Strode Theatre is a part of Strode College in Street, near Glastonbury, in Somerset. It is equipped as both theatre and cinema, incorporating two venues. The main Theatre has 343 seats and a proscenium arch stage. The Studio has 64 seats in a retractable unit and is used for film screenings and for classes and rehearsals.
bodyContent: Strode Theatre is a part of Strode College in Street, near Glastonbury, in Somerset. It is equipped as both theatre and cinema, incorporating two venues. The main Theatre has 343 seats and a proscenium arch stage. The Studio has 64 seats in a retractable unit and is used for film screenings and for classes and rehearsals. We promote a mixed programme of live professional and amateur events on stage (‘Live on Stage’), mainstream and arthouse films as well as live and recorded transmissions of opera, ballet and theatre (‘Live on Screen’). The foyer is home to changing exhibitions of work by local and regional artists. Opened in 1963, funded by the Clarks Foundation, Strode Theatre has been an essential part of the community for more than five decades. We are pleased to offer a warm and welcoming environment for all our visitors, performers and artists. At the heart of the community, we provide spaces for meeting, rehearsing, performing and exhibiting. Opening an hour before a performance our bar gives a friendly place to meet beforehand and a relaxed atmosphere to chat afterwards.

subtitle: On site of a mill mentioned in the Domesday Survey of c1086. The present mill dates from 18thC and was restored to working order.
bodyContent: Dunster Working Mill, Somerset, National Trust is a fully restored watermill A restored 18th-century watermill built on the site of a mill mentioned in the Domesday Survey of 1086. The mill is set in peaceful surroundings alongside the River Avill and at the entrance to the Dunster Castle River gardens. The watermill is fully operational. You can often see original milling here and even buy the flour produced.
tagline: A restored 18th-century watermill built on the site of a mill mentioned in the Domesday Survey.

title: Bath Theatrical Costume Hire
subtitle: Bath Theatrical Costume Hire, a family business established in 1969 moved from our quirky little shop in Bath to our warehouse in Frome in 2001, housing more than 30,000 costumes. We work with hundreds of companies, casts, actors, and partygoers to ensure they have the best costumes for their event.
bodyContent: Bath Theatrical Costume Hire, from its small beginnings above a hairdresser on the London Road in Bath, is now based in Frome and houses over 30,000 costumes. “When we moved from our overcrowded premises on London Road, we thought we would never fill our new home, even with our two friendly ghosts in tow. Now that too, is crammed with fabulous stuff, some of which is already put together as costumes but much of which is waiting for our touch of magic to bring the characters to life”, said Dinah Auton, the second generation to run the business. Bath Theatrical is like no other business and for those who know it, they are delighted that it is so different. It is perhaps its quirkiness which has helped it ride the economic and professional changes which have flavoured the past 50 years. Through all this Bath Theatrical has managed to add its magic to many a party goer, wedding guest and stage costumes. We service professional and amateurs’ groups, schools, corporate promotions, alternative weddings, events, and a wide array of private hire for parties. Talk to our staff about how we can make your event, production or celebratory occasion that extra special.
tagline: Bath Theatrical Costume Hire, a family business established in 1969

title: Hope Farm Cottages
subtitle: Self catering cottages in a queit setting near Brean. Berrow and weston super mare in Somerset. Short holiday breaks.
bodyContent: Very close to the Somerset coast but surrounded by the beautiful West Country countryside you will find Hope Farm's 4 luxury cottages. The beaches of Brean & Weston Super Mare are minutes drives away and there are a vast array of day trips to surrounding attractions, villages and countryside to keep everyone occupied. Each ground floor self catering cottage is on the edge of a beautiful lawned courtyard with open fields behind. Each has 2 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms and are easily accessible for those that have special requirements. Outside there are picnic tables and deckchairs for those lazy days and Summer evenings. Each cottage has off road, private and security lit parking spaces for 2 vehicles. Hope Farm has a wealth of facilities including a games room, outdoor children's play ground, laundry room and covered storage for bikes or trailers. And if you dont fancy driving there is a bus stop right at the gate to Weston Super Mare, Burnham on Sea , Taunton & Bristol. We can accommodate most requests so do call us to discuss to make your break perfect.
tagline: Self catering cottages in a queit setting near Brean. Berrow and weston super mare in Somerset.

title: Extours
subtitle: Step into a world where history comes alive and paranormal awaits! Extours is your gateway to extraordinary adventures through history with our thrilling ghost walks, immersive historical walking tours, and exhilarating paranormal investigations.
bodyContent: At Extours, we blend history and the supernatural to create unforgettable experiences, leaving you yearning more! For current availability just head over to the bookings section. Here you can select the date and time required from the available time slots and make your booking securely online. Information on our unique events can be found by navigating to that event using the buttons below. Shepton Mallet Ghost Walks Shepton Mallet is famous for having one of the most haunted prisons in the world. However, the prison is not the only place in this town where ghosts can be found! Join us for the Shepton Mallet Ghost Walk and hear intriguing stories from the towns past, learn about ghosts that are thought to haunt the area and get involved in some ghost hunting. Sedgemoor Batt lefield Ghost Walk Learn about the infamous Monmouth Rebellion at the very location where the Battle of Sedgemoor took place. Hundreds died on this battlefield so it is no surprise that this is a very active location. The Taunton Ghost Walk From Anglo-Saxon burial grounds to the infamous "Bloody Assizes" hundreds have been buried or executed at Taunton over the centuries. Join us and get involved with some ghost-hunting and learn fascinating stories from the history of the town. Watchet Ghost Walk The ancient harbour town of Watchet has a rich and fascinating history. If you would like to learn more and hear stories associated with the darker history of the town while getting involved with some ghost hunting then be sure to join us. Bridgwater Ghost Walk Join us for the historical walking tour of Bridgwater with a paranormal twist. The amazing history of this town often gets overlooked but there is so much to discover! You will also have the opportunity to get involved in some paranormal investigating for yourself. Dunster Ghost Walk After establishing ghost walks in a number of areas in Somerset I can safely say that Dunster is without a doubt the most haunted area that we cover! We will be back in October for the Dunster Ghost Walk. Be sure to join us and learn interesting stories relating to the towns past and people. You will also learn of many ghosts that are thought to haunt the area and have the opportunity to get involved with some paranormal investigating for yourself
tagline: At Extours, we blend history and the supernatural

title: Lilstock Circular
subtitle: Amazing rock formations are revealed at low-tide on this walk from the charming and historic estate of Lilstock which offers glimpses of rare flora and fauna and remarkable geology
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. Amazing rock formations are revealed at low-tide on this walk from the charming and historic estate of Lilstock which offers glimpses of rare flora and fauna and remarkable geology. The harbour at Lilstock and its stone pier no longer exist but there are reminders everywhere of the once thriving port which sold everything from luxury goods to Welsh coal, used to fire the large lime kilns along the cliff. For more information click here
tagline: Amazing rock formations are revealed at low-tide on this walk from the charming and historic estate

title: Webbington Farm Holiday Cottages
subtitle: Self catering accommodation in Somerset nestled below Crooks Peak (SSSI & AONB) on the edge of the Somerset Mendips Hills. Thirty minutes from the M5 Junction 22 and 40 minutes from Bristol Airport.
bodyContent: Self catering accommodation in Somerset nestled below Crooks Peak (SSSI & AONB) on the edge of the Somerset Mendips Hills and amidst Somerset's famous cider making and Cheddar strawberry growing area, the cottages are commutable to most of Somerset's amazing attractions between Cheddar & Weston-super-Mare. Stay on a working beef farm in luxury! We offer beautiful bespoke holidays for families, couples and groups, so please call us at anytime for your personally tailored holiday. You may want the hot tub, party barn, catering, tranquility, the farmhouse, one cottage or all four. Its up to you so do call. Nestled below Crooks Peak (SSSI & AONB) on the edge of the Somerset Mendips Hills and amidst Somerset's famous cider making and Cheddar strawberry growing area, the cottages are commutable to most of Somerset's amazing attractions. The 4 fantastic oak beamed cottages comprise: KITTY accommodates 4 adults & 1 baby in 2 bedrooms (1 double bed & 2 singles) with family bathroom and open plan lounge/kitchen/diner downstairs with patio to the front of the cottage. GOLIGHTLY accommodates 7 adults & 1 baby in 3 bedrooms - 1 triple (double & single), 1 twin & 1 bunk bed room, with family bathroom and open plan lounge/diner & separate kitchen downstairs with patio to the front of the cottage. TIARKS accommodates 7 adults & 1 baby in 2 bedrooms (1 double, 1 triple & 1 double sofa bed in the lounge). This cottage has the benefit of being on one level and is therefore suitable for the elderly/less mobile & has its own private patio to the rear of this cottage and private luxury hot tub room! The hot tub room is available to guests who book Tiarks individually OR as part of a larger booking. POPPY accommodates 7 adults & 1 baby in 3 bedrooms one double ensuite, one triple (double & single) and one twin with family bathroom, and large open plan lounge/kitchen/diner downstairs with patio to the front of the cottage. Each cottage has full central heating throughout. The kitchens are fully equipped with a dishwasher, washer/dryer, fridge/freezer, electric oven/hob and microwave. The lounges/dining areas have leather suites, wide screen Smart TV and Wifi. The bathroom has a "P" bath/shower, shaver point, toilet, hand basin and heated towel rail. Directly outside the properties is a large patio area equipped with individual outdoor furniture. The large, communal and enclosed gardens and children's activity play area are located across the courtyard. Car parking also available. Self Catering Rates: All inclusive of all power, bed linen and towels (not swimming or hot tub), along with Spa day pass (indoor pool, sauna, steam room, tennis courts and gym) and a Somerset goodies welcome pack. THE RUSTIC PARTY BARN - available for hire with self catering accommodation for larger groups comprising bar, seating for 30, wood burner, sound system and room to party the night away. If you don't fancy having to organise the catering we can help! FARMHOUSE accommodation is located opposite the holiday lets which is rented out on a room only basis & accommodates 5 adults & one baby in a triple shower ensuite and an interconnecting twin bedroom. Note: if both rooms are booked the modern family bathroom opposite is also included. As a family farm there is opportunity to see the animals and experience at close hand 'life on the farm'. We are very keen on the environment and have planted 10,000 trees into a woodland, replanted an apple orchard and are involved in a number of schemes promoting good environmental practice, including a reed bed. We also have our own river frontage on the River Axe for private fishing! ***PLEASE CONTACT 07900 273722 TO BOOK FRIDAY TO MONDAY STAYS*** ***USE THE BOOK DIRECT BUTTON TO BOOK MONDAY TO THURSDAY STAYS*** Or call direct to have a chat and book direct. Bespoke 2/3 night Short Breaks & Farmhouse accommodation - on request.
tagline: Self catering accommodation in Somerset nestled below Crooks Peak

title: BrewTwo
subtitle: BrewTwo: Where Somerset Soul Meets Artisanal Flare Nestled in the heart of The Cleve in Wellington, BrewTwo isn't just a café—it’s a destination. Founded by the visionary duo Shopna Nicholls and Josh Baker, this cozy-yet-vibrant bistro captures the essence of Somerset living, blending rustic charm with a sophisticated culinary edge.
bodyContent: BrewTwo: Your Charming Community Hub in Wellington Indulge Your Senses, Support Local, and Give Back BrewTwo has brought a burst of charm to The Cleve in Wellington. As co-founders, Shopna and Josh have poured our hearts into creating a truly special spot where you can kick back, relax, and soak in breathtaking views of the Somerset countryside. Step into BrewTwo and be enchanted by our homely decor, designed to make you feel instantly at ease. But it’s not just about the ambiance – prepare your taste buds for a treat! From freshly brewed coffee that will awaken your senses to a delectable array of afternoon teas and an irresistible selection of cakes, every craving is catered for. A Culinary Delight Awaits Looking for something more substantial? Dive into our mouthwatering brunch, lunch, and evening meals, or unwind with a fantastic choice of alcoholic drinks. We pride ourselves on using local suppliers, ensuring the freshest ingredients while contributing to the vitality of the West Country’s economy. At BrewTwo, we are deeply committed to our community and its wellbeing. That’s why we proudly support local businesses. And our commitment extends to our furry friends too! We are proud to support the St Giles Animal Rescue Centre charity, helping to give animals in need a second chance. Your Perfect Event Destination and Entertainment Hub Beyond a fantastic dining experience, BrewTwo is your go-to for memorable gatherings. We offer a private room, perfect for everything from intimate family celebrations to productive meetings, conferences, and launch parties. If you’re dreaming of hosting an unforgettable event, the entire venue is available for private hire – the possibilities are endless! But the excitement doesn’t stop there. Throughout the year, we host special music and dinner events, promising unforgettable evenings filled with great food and fantastic entertainment. Keep an eye on our schedule for upcoming dates!

title: Olive and Rosy
subtitle: Olive and Rosy tucked away down on North Street is home to a collection of carefully curated food and fashion inspired by the tastes, slower pace and aesthetics of Italy. Stefano and Rachael have been bringing a little of the Italian experience to Wellington since December 2016.
bodyContent: Often described as a ‘hidden gem’, many visitors are surprised by how much there is to discover behind those small windows. With two floors to explore, you are encouraged to slow down, take your time, have a browse through their recipe and style books or try some samples of fresh produce before you buy should you wish. Downstairs the little Italian store offers you authentic food and wines - a small but mighty collection of delicious produce, from Stefano's best loved staples to new and exclusive finds. Everything is chosen with attention to its taste, quality and product story. The deli has become particularly popular for its range of olive oils, pastries, speciality cheeses and accompaniments plus sharing platters made to order. Olive and Rosy are regulars at Wellington’s markets and outdoor events, when fresh focaccia and pizza is also available. If you are planning a weekend visit to the park, why not call in on the way and pick up some picnic treats? The clothing boutique upstairs replicates the same careful consideration of story and quality, with a collection of garments ranging through sustainable, natural, upcycled or pre-loved boutique brands. Think loved linens, restored cashmere, vintage inspired prints and that classic Italian flair! Olive and Rosy also sell your pre-owned clothing for you and help to otherwise rehome no-longer-worn pieces through hosting regular Clothes Swap events within the town.

title: Adam Kay & Guests!
subtitle: Adam Kay brings a special extended headline comedy appearance to the stage, sharing stories from life on and off the wards. Joined by guest comedians, the evening promises a mix of humour, storytelling and live entertainment.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Adam Kay returns to the stage for a special extended headline performance. Best known for his bestselling book This Is Going to Hurt, which sold millions of copies and was later adapted into a multi-BAFTA-winning BBC series, Kay has become one of the UK's most popular comedy storytellers. His show Undoctored continues the story beyond This Is Going to Hurt, drawing on experiences from life both inside and outside the medical profession. Combining humour with personal anecdotes, the performance has been enjoyed by audiences across a record-breaking Edinburgh Fringe run, a sell-out West End season and a national tour. Known from appearances on programmes including The Russell Howard Hour, Lorraine, 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown and The Jonathan Ross Show, Adam Kay brings his distinctive style of storytelling and comedy to this live event. He will be joined by two guest comedians, with names to be announced. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: A special comedy night with bestselling author, comedian and former doctor Adam Kay.

Offering fun for all ages, the circus combines traditional family entertainment with a range of live acts and spectacular performances. Visitors can experience the atmosphere of a classic travelling circus while enjoying a show lasting approximately 1 hour and 45 minutes. With a variety of seating options available and special family ticket offers, Circus Wonderland provides an entertaining day out during the school holiday period.

title: Southern Sinfonia: Inside the Orchestra
subtitle: Step inside the world of a live orchestra with this welcoming and interactive experience from Southern Sinfonia. Designed especially for families, first-time concertgoers and curious listeners, the event offers the chance to sit close to the musicians and discover how an orchestra works.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } What does it feel like to sit inside an orchestra, close enough to see the bows move, feel the rhythm and hear the music surround you? Inside the Orchestra is a relaxed and welcoming event from Southern Sinfonia, the South West's professional chamber orchestra. Across a series of short sessions, audiences can experience a live string orchestra at close quarters, with a limited number of seats available on stage amongst the musicians. Additional seating will also be available in the auditorium. Rather than a formal classical concert, this event is designed for first-timers, families and anyone who would like classical music to feel accessible and engaging. The conductor will introduce the instruments and share the stories behind the music, while musicians demonstrate how melody, rhythm, texture and accompaniment combine to create an orchestral performance. Featuring familiar and instantly enjoyable music selections, each session offers a friendly atmosphere with the lights up and an informal approach. The event is SEND-friendly, carers are welcome and information will be provided in advance to help visitors feel comfortable attending. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: An interactive orchestral experience for families, newcomers and curious music lovers.

title: The Story of Swing
subtitle: From the Rat Pack to Robbie Williams, The Story of Swing celebrates the timeless music of swing and big band jazz in an evening packed with classic hits, outstanding musicianship and unforgettable performances.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Presented by award-winning vocalist and world-class trumpet player Gareth John, and featuring the acclaimed SOS Big Band, The Story of Swing takes audiences on a musical journey through the golden age of swing and its continuing influence on modern music. The show features beloved songs made famous by Bobby Darin, Frank Sinatra, Dean Martin and Sammy Davis Jr, alongside favourites from contemporary stars including Michael Bublé, Robbie Williams, Matt Goss, Paul Anka and Harry Connick Jr. Renowned for his exceptional showmanship and natural rapport with audiences, Gareth John brings passion and energy to every performance. Throughout his career he has shared the stage with artists including The Beautiful South and The Specials, earning a reputation as one of the UK's leading swing performers. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre

title: Spend a Day in Wellington
subtitle: Have a look at our ideas for spending a day in Wellington with your family.
bodyContent: A Perfect Day in Wellington for families The theme for your day: History, parks, great food and discovering hidden gems. Breakfast to start the day Begin your day at BrewTwo , a modern independent café on Mantle Street serving excellent coffee, pastries and hearty breakfasts. Parents can enjoy locally roasted coffee while younger visitors choose from pancakes, toast or pastries. Discover Wellington's fascinating story Walk a couple of minutes into Fore Street and visit Wellington Museum . Although compact, it's packed with stories that children enjoy, from the Duke of Wellington and the Battle of Waterloo to Wellington's woollen mills, the famous Wellesley Cinema and even the last private bank in England to print its own banknotes. The recently refurbished museum makes an excellent introduction to the town. Explore the High Street colourful independent shopfronts hidden alleyways interesting architectural details public access buildings such as St John’s Church A highlight is the Brickhaus creative café and shop – This is a unique space for everyone – adults young and old, as well as children! Whether you’re a lifelong LEGO® fan or just discovering the joy of building, you can unwind in the cosy and inviting atmosphere while creating amazing sets. Lunch Choose from one of Wellington's independent cafés such as Cafe Licious or enjoy a relaxed family lunch at The Green Dragon . Spend the afternoon at Wellington Park . The beautifully maintained Victorian park offers: children's play area wide lawns ornamental planting tennis courts plenty of room for games and picnics. Parents can relax while children burn off some energy. Alternatively visit Flip Out Somerset , indoor trampoline and adventure park and complete your day there. Another highlight for activities is pottery and wooden duck painting! The Duck and Brush is situated on the High Street and offers up to 2.5 hours to pick a piece, grab a brush and start painting! Finish with an ice cream before browsing Wellington's independent gift shops , bookshops and food retailers for local produce to take home.

subtitle: Train Travel to Weston can see sudden fresh air and discoveries without the hassle of driving and parking? Then this is the two day experience for you. With 50,000 objects there is no shortage of diversity!

title: Activity weekend in North Somerset
subtitle: You’ve arrived in North Somerset, brimming with adrenaline that needs burning off!If it’s mountain biking that you are after, then a good place to start is at Ashton Gate Estate where you can hire bikes at Pedal Progression. The great thing is that they give tuition, so if this is a new thing for you, it gives the chance to get safe and build confidence before setting out to enjoy the challenging scenery. Advanced skills coaching allows further personal development.

title: The Strawberry Line Yatton to Winscombe   -

title: Somerset Cider Brandy Company & Burrow Hill Cider
subtitle: At Burrow Hill we make traditional ciders as well as Somerset Cider Brandy. Visit the farm and see the UK’s first commercial cider distillery, explore the orchards and wander amongst 170 year old vats.
bodyContent: Somerset Cider resides at Burrow Hill where they make traditional ciders as well as Somerset Cider Brandy. Visit the farm and see the UK’s first commercial cider distillery, explore the orchards and wander amongst 170 year old vats. Or just come and sample our award winning ciders, Somerset Cider Brandy and liqueurs. Guided tours can also be booked in advance. Open all year. Monday - Saturday 9.00 - 5.00 Cider House - In the ciderhouse there is cider and Somerset Cider Brandy to sample amongst the oak vats, barrels and presses - all the paraphernalia associated with 150 years of cider making. Burrow Hill - Visitors are also encouraged to walk to the top of our hill and admire the incredible views of the Somerset Levels. On a good day you can see Glastonbury Tor in the distance. The Orchard - The starting point of both our cider and Somerset Cider Brandy is apples from our orchards. Visitors can follow our orchard trail where different apple varieties and other interesting features are explained. The walk takes about 30 minutes and you may need wellies. Distillery - Visitors are welcome to view the copper stills, protected by armour-plated glass and 68 locks and seals (by order of HM Customs & Excise) in the distillery. You can also buy our products online at https://www.somersetciderbrandy.com/

title: Thorney Lakes and Caravan Park
subtitle: A caravan and camping park with full facilities and coarse fishing available.
bodyContent: A caravan and camping park with full facilities and coarse fishing available. One mile form the historic village of Muchelney, our scenic park is perfect for touring the Somerset level and Moors , one of the most unchanged and distinctive landscape of lowland Britain. There are many interesting walks on the wetlands which are rich in flora, fauna and birdlife. Fishing lakes established in 1993, the setting attracts a host of wildlife and is regualry visited by otters, badgers, rabbits, deer and 70 species of birdlife including kingfishers. Just a short level walk from the caravan path the two miles of nature trails are a perfect for a short stroll or to enjoy a chat with the local fisher folk.
tagline: A caravan and camping park with full facilities and coarse fishing available.

title: Woodborough Inn
subtitle: A warm welcome, great food & drink and a cracking pub atmosphere is what makes The Woodborough Inn so special
bodyContent: Sat in the heart of the village of Winscombe and surrounded by the beautiful Mendip hills, The Woodborough Inn is the perfect place to relax and explore the local area which includes the beautiful Cheddar Gorge, the cathedral city of Wells and Glastonbury Tor. The Mendips providing a great space to enjoy the great outdoors. Whether a gentle walk or some extreme mountain biking; The Mendips has it all. Our guest accommodation consists of 7 cosy en-suite rooms, ideal for visitors to the West Country, business people and families alike, and come at competitive rates. Open daily from 11am, lunch from 12-2.00pm and our dinner service runs from 5.30pm. Sunday food hours are 12-3 and 5.30-7.30pm. Our chefs serve up some fabulous food. Hearty pub classics, an exciting range of specials, plus pizza and lighter dishes; all food cooked fresh using locally sourced ingredients. Our Sunday roasts are also not to be missed! Local real ales are always on tap along with crisp lagers, craft beers and local ciders. We have a wonderful wine list and our popular new “Gin List” heads up our selection of premium spirits. We also offer a great range of soft drinks, coffee, tea and cake! This is a popular spot for walkers and naturally, well-behaved dogs are welcome.
tagline: A warm welcome, great food & drink and a cracking pub atmosphere

title: Forever England
subtitle: Forever England Ltd was founded in 1997 when James and Katie opened their first shop in the sea-side town of Sidmouth in Devon.
bodyContent: Their attempt to provide a range of individual home accessories, giftware and bedding locally proved successful with the local community from the off. Utilising their previous experience in retail and the antiques trade, it was not long before shops in Sherborne and Lymington also opened. In 2009, a new shop opened in Salisbury. Katie started to design and develop her own products for the company based on customer feedback and her work with antiques. Since 2005, the company has been in a position to offer a diverse choice of quilted bedspreads, exclusively available to Forever England’s loyal and fast-growing customer base. In conjunction to four beautiful stores, we exhibit at many shows around the country throughout the year. Our annual show calendar often features the same shows with similar dates. We are always so pleased to see familiar faces looking to find us as well as welcoming new ones! BEHIND THE NAME The name Forever England was taken from R. Brooke’s (1914) war sonnet, The Soldier. Written before the horrors of the Great War, Brooke’s highly patriotic, idealistic and traditional values are shared in his belief that to die in war, was to die a hero. THE SOLDIER (Rupert Brooke) If I should die, think only this of me: That there's some corner of a foreign field That is forever England. There shall be In that rich earth a richer dust concealed; A dust whom England bore, shaped, made aware, Gave, once, her flowers to love, her ways to roam; A body of England's, breathing English air, Washed by the rivers, blest by suns of home. And think, this heart, all evil shed away, A pulse in the eternal mind, no less Gives somewhere back the thoughts by England given; Her sights and sounds; dreams happy as her day; And laughter, learnt of friends; and gentleness, In hearts at peace, under an English heaven.

title: Wookey Hole Caves & Attractions
subtitle: Wookey Hole Caves is a magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for all ages. It’s an experience millions of years in the making with plenty to do inside and out. Enjoy vintage penny arcades, museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, and of course the famous, beautiful caves.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Wookey Hole Caves and attractions lies In the heart of Somerset. A magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for the young and young at heart. When you visit Wookey Hole, you’ll enjoy an experience millions of years in the making. There is plenty to do inside and out, from vintage penny arcades to museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, to name but a few of the attractions. Not forgetting the breathtakingly beautiful caves, for which Wookey Hole is renowned. Your visit will take you through 8 chambers. Each with a unique beauty and story. You’ll also pass our cheese tunnel, home to the delicious Wookey Hole cheese. The cheese is not the only resident of the caves. Over the years, Wookey Hole has been home to giant hyenas, bears, Neanderthals, and many local people. It has even been a site of pagan and Roman worship. You’ll find Wookey Hole holds a surprise around every corner. You might even get to meet our most famous resident, the Witch of Wookey Hole. We have found she most likes to visit during school holidays! The world-famous Wookey Hole Circus School performs at Wookey Hole at weekends and in School Holidays. Every year over 250,000 people visit Wookey Hole and take-home cherished memories of a great day out. Whether it is your first time or your fiftieth, there is always something new to discover. We can’t wait to welcome you.
tagline: At Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions, Somerset, there’s always fun and adventure to be had.

title: West Harptree
subtitle: West Harptree is a small village in the Chew Valley, North Somerset.
bodyContent: West Harptree is a small village in the Chew Valley, North Somerset . It is approximately 10 miles south of Bristol and 10 miles from Bath . It has a population of 380. The parish of West Harptree lies on the north side of the Mendip Hills and consists of the main village and the hamlets of Ridge, North Widcombe and parts of South Widcombe. The name 'Harptree' was listed in the Domesday Book of 1086 as 'Herpatreu'. At this time, West Harptree comprised of two manors (later they were called Gournay and Tilly) and to this day, two very fine manor houses remain on the same sites; Gournay Court and Tilly Manor. In the centre of the village is the very pretty twelfth century church of St Mary. The area to the north of the parish was flooded in 1956 to create Chew Valley Lake which is the second largest reservoir in the Mendip area. The picturesque lake is a haven for bird watchers, sailors and fishermen. The village boasts a memorial hall, a thriving shop, post office, doctors surgery, dentist, beauty salon and two public houses.

title: Blenheim Gardens
subtitle: Minehead premier gardens just off the town centre and a few minutes’ walk from the sea front and the harbour
bodyContent: Blenheim Gardens (maintained and run by Somerset West and Taunton council) is ideally situated in the centre of Minehead and covers nearly 2.5 hectares of parkland. Created in the 1920's it is now a mature, attractive and sheltered haven, popular with residents and visitors. The park provides spring and summer bedding displays, a wide range of trees, shrubs and perennials which thrive in the mild seaside climate. The flower beds and shrub areas are framed by lawns. The park boasts a bandstand for summer weekend concerts/brass bands. There is an 18-hole putting green but currently there is no formal play provision for children. The Gardens contain female, male and disabled toilets maintained and run by Minehead Town Council. There are several access points into the Gardens (from North Road, Blenheim Road and via a footpath from The Avenue) and a public car park with 62 spaces on the eastern boundary accessible from North Road.

title: The Garden at Dunster Castle, National Trust
subtitle: The result of 100s of years of planning, building and restoration a walk around the gardens at Dunster Castle takes you around the world and though four different microclimates.
bodyContent: The result of 100s of years of planning, building and restoration a walk around the gardens at Dunster Castle takes you around the world and though four different microclimates. The South Terrace With far reaching views across the Bristol Channel and Deer Park the present day layout of the South Terrace stems from the Victorian period. In the 1820s, at the behest of George Luttrell, the architect Salvin demolished the existing Thornhill Chapel which had been built on the south facade in 1721. A new wing was constructed in its place and the resulting South Terrace was formed. To reflect its history, the flower beds are planted in the Victorian style with spring bulbs giving a spectacular floral display and in summer there is an abundance of brightly coloured bedding plants. The area has a Mediterranean feel due to its fortunate micro-climate and this enables tender plants to thrive including the row of Chusan Palms. This part of the garden also contains the Orangery, (now renamed the Camellia House) where you can pick up take away coffee and snacks, the Swan Pond which is home to goldfishes and newts and the Lemon House. The River Garden A native micro climate the River Garden is a wild, wooded area. Green throughout the year during spring it is full of colour as the magnolia trees bloom. During summer the giant rhubarb reaches its peak in growth getting so big they make an unusual umbrella when caught in the rain. Home to some rare species including the Handkerchief tree was grown from seeds smuggled back from Australia by Alys Luttrell in her purse in the 1920’s. Bridges cross the River Avil which runs through the garden and lead to walks on the wider estate. And at the end of the garden is the working watermill which produces over 6 tonnes of flour a year. The Yew bank There have been yews on this bank dating back to the eighteenth century when the original drive - The New Way - was commissioned in 1720 by Dorothy Luttrell. In those days, it was very fashionable to create areas of light and shade within a garden and yews were perfect in this respect for shade. However, over the years, the yews grew too large and they were coppiced in 2012 and are now kept within bounds. The Keep This area was originally the Upper Ward of the Norman Fortress of Dunster and, therefore, is the highest point in the Dunster landscape. In 1721, at the request of Dorothy Luttrell, the area was levelled and turned into a Bowling Green. To offer shelter and a dining area for the participants and the ladies, the Octagon Tower was constructed this now houses an exhibition exploring the history. Facilities in addition to those listed below: Baby changing facilities Children's Trails Courtesy Vehicle Stair Climber Trampers available to book
tagline: The result of 100s of years of planning, building and restoration a walk around the gardens.

title: Woodborough Inn
subtitle: A warm welcome, great food & drink and a cracking pub atmosphere is what makes The Woodborough Inn so special
bodyContent: Sat in the heart of the village of Winscombe and surrounded by the beautiful Mendip hills, The Woodborough Inn is the perfect place to relax and explore the local area which includes the beautiful Cheddar Gorge, the cathedral city of Wells and Glastonbury Tor. The Mendips providing a great space to enjoy the great outdoors. Whether a gentle walk or some extreme mountain biking; The Mendips has it all. Our guest accommodation consists of 7 cosy en-suite rooms, ideal for visitors to the West Country, business people and families alike, and come at competitive rates. Open daily from 11am, lunch from 12-2.00pm and our dinner service runs from 5.30pm. Sunday food hours are 12-3 and 5.30-7.30pm. Our chefs serve up some fabulous food. Hearty pub classics, an exciting range of specials, plus pizza and lighter dishes; all food cooked fresh using locally sourced ingredients. Our Sunday roasts are also not to be missed! Local real ales are always on tap along with crisp lagers, craft beers and local ciders. We have a wonderful wine list and our popular new “Gin List” heads up our selection of premium spirits. We also offer a great range of soft drinks, coffee, tea and cake! This is a popular spot for walkers and naturally, well-behaved dogs are welcome.
tagline: A warm welcome, great food & drink and a cracking pub atmosphere

title: Blakehay Theatre
subtitle: Leading the way in this zeitgeist for Weston-super-Mare the Blakehay Theatre create Theatre for the whole community, bringing national popular shows and treading subject matters onto the stage. A creative hub for artists and performers in the local area and a cultural home for fans of the arts.
bodyContent: The theatre’s uniquely diverse program of locally produced and touring work is curated especially for you. We are striving to create an inclusive creative community to make the most of a beautiful venue by using all of its spaces for artistic endorsers, and we are delighted you want to be a part of it. With an intimate 200 seat main house, 100 seat Studio Theatre and a warm and welcoming theatre bar, the Blakehay Theatre is able to present a variety of shows and events in these spaces. With community classes taking place in our beautiful studios, there is something for everyone at the Blakehay Theatre. We may be little, but we have big ideas! The vision is to build a ‘big-city’ creative culture into the heart of the Victorian seaside resort of Weston-super-Mare. We need continued public support to help sustain and grow this vision through ticket sales, personal donations, sponsorship and help spreading the word! We are constantly working and adapting our programme each season to bring new and exclusive works to Weston-super-Mare, but we can’t do that without your support, so please spread the word and support our little theatre with big ideas!
tagline: Leading the way in this zeitgeist for Weston-super-Mare the Blakehay Theatre

title: Brean Down Circular
subtitle: Brean Down is a promontory of the Mendips Hills extending 1.5 miles out into the Bristol Channel at the eastern end of Bridgwater Bay with views over to the two small islands of Steep Holm and Flat Holm.
bodyContent: The walk takes you around the Down where people have lived, worked and fought since the Bronze Age. Archaeological highlights include the remains on an ancient Roman-Celtic temple and a Victorian fort. Brean Down is also rich in wildlife and is a Site of Special Scientific Interest for both its geological significance and the presence of nationally rare plants including the white rock-rose. For more Info click here
tagline: Brean Down is a promontory of the Mendips Hills.

title: ⭐Shepton Mallet Prison
subtitle: Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’; Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom...
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’, Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom. Shepton Mallet Prison is a recently decommissioned (2013) Georgian jail where visitors can walk in the footsteps of our social history and hear officers shine a light on what life was like for both the incarcerated and those who guarded them through the ages. Before its closure, it was a category C lifer prison holding 189 prisoners. Opened in 1646, it was expanded in 1790, with further building work undertaken in the 1820s and 1830s, including the installation of a treadwheel for those sentenced to hard labour. In 1930, the inmate numbers fell and the prison was closed. During the Second World War, the prison was reopened and used as a military prison. It was initially used by the British Army and later by American forces, who constructed a new execution block for condemned prisoners. It was also used for the storage of important historical documents, including the Domesday Book. It returned to civilian use in 1966. Shepton Mallet prison is also known for its tales of paranormal activity. One of the most popular stories is that of the White Lady. She is frequently seen or sensed in various locations, especially A Wing. Staff and prisoners would often complain of an icy wind moving through the wing, the sweet smell of perfume and shadowy figures. She supposedly dates from the late 1700s, when she spent some time in the prison. During a lovers' tiff which escalated, she murdered her betrothed. Once found guilty and sentenced to death, she was housed in Shepton Mallet Prison. On the evening before her execution, she asked for her wedding dress to be brought to the prison, which they allowed. She wore it to bed that night, but in the morning the officers found that she had died during the night. No cause of death was ever found, so we are left to presume that she died of a broken heart. Perhaps this is why she still haunts the prison? In the early 1950s, the Kray Twins were also held here after deserting the British Army. Today, the prison is open as a tourist attraction offering Guided Tours, Self-Guided Tours, Escape Rooms, Night Behind Bars and Ghost Hunting Behind Bars. This is an immersive experience without gizmos or gimmicks – the jail is very much as it was when the last prisoners left in 2013. In 2025, Shepton Mallet Prison received the prestigious Trip Advisor Travellers’ Choice, for the 7th time running, placing it among the top 10% of attractions worldwide.

title: The Castle at Taunton
subtitle: The Castle Hotel is in the centre of Taunton the old County town for Somerset. It is the gateway to the Black Downs and Exmoor National Park, West Somerset Railway, being 5 minute drive from the main line train station from London Paddington, whilst being 30 minutes from the M5 Junction 25 and close many amenities.
bodyContent: The Castle at Taunton is one of the UK’s most historic & prestigious 4 Star Hotels, having been at the forefront of British cuisine for 40 years. We also operate Brazz, which since 1998 has provided the blueprint for British Brasseries across the country The Castle Hotel is a unique family-owned hotel set in a historic building in the heart of Taunton in Somerset. A simple ethos lies at the heart of the hotel – to offer the warmest of welcomes, give the utmost personal attention and exemplary service to each & every guest. The Castle Hotel is a one-off, not a link in a chain. The Castle’s reputation for fine food and wine, comfort, and attentive service has been built by three generations of the Chapman Family, with a passion for promoting the highest standards in every aspect of the hotel. Taunton lies at the heart of the region, making The Castle the ideal base from which to explore the history, magic and wonder of the West Country. Each of The Castle’s 44 bedrooms are individually decorated, offering its own personality and comfort away from home. Whether you’re looking for healthy or hearty, you’ll find it all at the award-winning restaurant, Brazz. Featuring a wide-ranging menu, you’ll find favourites such as Brazz Fishcakes – which have been present since day one – as well as Quantock Lamb, Brixham Crab and much more. The Castle’s legendary afternoon teas are served Wednesday to Sunday from 2:30pm - 4:00pm. Freshly baked scones with West Country clotted cream and strawberry jam, elegant finger sandwiches, pastries and cakes along with a fine selection of loose-leaf tea, make this a very special occasion… especially if you add a bottle of champagne.
tagline: A unique family-owned hotel set in a historic building in Taunton, the county town of Somerset

title: Glastonbury Tor, National Trust
subtitle: Glastonbury Tor is a well-loved Somerset landmark associated with myths and legends, but it is also a place where children can run about and have fun. Fields at the foot of the Tor are good for games or you could play at the top in the ruined tower.
bodyContent: Prominent hill overlooking the Isle of Avalon, Glastonbury and Somerset. This iconic and evocative landmark offers magnificent views of the Somerset Levels , Dorset, Wiltshire and Wales. Steeped in history and legend, excavations at the top of the Tor have revealed the plans of two superimposed churches of St Michael, of which only a 15th-century tower remains. Glastonbury Tor also has a grisly past. Abbot Richard Whiting was executed here in 1549 on the orders of Thomas Cromwell, the first Earl of Essex. Glastonbury Tor is known as being one of the most spiritual sites in the country. Its pagan beliefs are still very much celebrated. It’s a beautiful place to walk, unwind and relax.
tagline: Glastonbury Tor is a well-loved Somerset landmark associated with myths and legends.

title: Watchet, Washford along the Old Mineral Line
subtitle: The Watchet to Washford walk along the Old Mineral Line is ideal for keen walkers and families. There is loads to see and do in beautiful Watchet.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. The Watchet to Washford walk along the Old Mineral Line is ideal for keen walkers and families. This is a moderate to difficult walk in places, with steps, steep climbs and some uneven surfaces, although it is stile free. There is loads to see and do in beautiful Watchet, including taking a trip from the town’s picturesque station on the West Somerset Railway. Museums include the fascinating Market House Museum with its tales of kings, queens, murderous knights and pirates and the Boat Museum which houses an intriguing collection of local flat bottomed boats. The town is also packed with independent shops and art galleries including Contains Art, a gallery and studios in converted shipping containers on the quayside. For more information click here .
tagline: This is a moderate to difficult walk in places.

Farm View has one large double bedroom and one twin room with bunks, The Elms has two double bedrooms and the Stables has one double bedroom and one with twin beds. All three apartments have sofa beds in the sitting room. There is an outdoor swimming pool, trampoline, climbing frame and extensive relaxing gardens. Well behaved dogs are welcome too! A peaceful retreat between Exmoor, the Quantock Hills and the Somerset coast . Ideal for families.
