title: Talent Gallery
subtitle: Talent Gallery is a beautifully curated and well stocked Gallery in the heart of Wellington. Nina king, owner and resident artist, has her open studio there. Nina runs workshops and loves inspiring people to get creative. The space is full of beautiful art and handcrafted gift ideas, that suit all budgets.
bodyContent: Nina King took over Talent Gallery in June 2024, and it is going from strength to strength. Her vision for the Talent Gallery is to promote Art by our great local artists and artisans, to provide a space for them to exhibit their work and to make that work accessible and available, reaching out to welcome the whole community, for all to enjoy. The gallery supports around 30 local regular and guest artists/artisans with art exhibitions changing every 6 weeks. The gallery is beautifully curated and well-stocked. Customer service is very important to us, and we love making every customer feel welcome. The gallery has a seating area where customers are welcome to sit to view the art and enjoy the atmosphere. The gallery is family and dog friendly, welcoming people to come and browse without feeling pressured to buy. Nina is running successful ‘learn how to paint in Acrylics’ workshops and has plans to expand her workshops into other areas – watch this space! As a successful artist, Nina also exhibits her own work there, and you will find a selection of her new originals, framed & unframed Giclee prints. She also offers commissions. Occasionally Nina branches out into clay and other handmade gifts. She has an open studio within the gallery, where you are welcome to browse and maybe even watch her painting! Nina loves living and working in Wellington, Somerset and she feels happy knowing that the gallery is part of a growing art scene in the area.

title: BrewTwo
subtitle: BrewTwo: Where Somerset Soul Meets Artisanal Flare Nestled in the heart of The Cleve in Wellington, BrewTwo isn't just a café—it’s a destination. Founded by the visionary duo Shopna Nicholls and Josh Baker, this cozy-yet-vibrant bistro captures the essence of Somerset living, blending rustic charm with a sophisticated culinary edge.
bodyContent: BrewTwo: Your Charming Community Hub in Wellington Indulge Your Senses, Support Local, and Give Back BrewTwo has brought a burst of charm to The Cleve in Wellington. As co-founders, Shopna and Josh have poured our hearts into creating a truly special spot where you can kick back, relax, and soak in breathtaking views of the Somerset countryside. Step into BrewTwo and be enchanted by our homely decor, designed to make you feel instantly at ease. But it’s not just about the ambiance – prepare your taste buds for a treat! From freshly brewed coffee that will awaken your senses to a delectable array of afternoon teas and an irresistible selection of cakes, every craving is catered for. A Culinary Delight Awaits Looking for something more substantial? Dive into our mouthwatering brunch, lunch, and evening meals, or unwind with a fantastic choice of alcoholic drinks. We pride ourselves on using local suppliers, ensuring the freshest ingredients while contributing to the vitality of the West Country’s economy. At BrewTwo, we are deeply committed to our community and its wellbeing. That’s why we proudly support local businesses. And our commitment extends to our furry friends too! We are proud to support the St Giles Animal Rescue Centre charity, helping to give animals in need a second chance. Your Perfect Event Destination and Entertainment Hub Beyond a fantastic dining experience, BrewTwo is your go-to for memorable gatherings. We offer a private room, perfect for everything from intimate family celebrations to productive meetings, conferences, and launch parties. If you’re dreaming of hosting an unforgettable event, the entire venue is available for private hire – the possibilities are endless! But the excitement doesn’t stop there. title: Shed-Ache
subtitle: Shed-ache is a lively and imaginative dance theatre show designed for younger audiences and their families. Blending humour, movement and storytelling, it creates a playful world full of surprises and adventure.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Shed-ache is a seriously silly dance theatre show that transports younger audiences and their grown-ups into a world somewhere between reality and make-believe. At the heart of the story are two friends (three if you count the shed), who find themselves on a playful adventure filled with unexpected moments and imaginative twists. As they navigate everything from downpours and lava floors to socks falling from the sky, the performance uses movement and humour to bring the story to life. Along the way, the show explores themes of friendship, imagination and the importance of embracing experiences, whatever the weather. Created as a family-friendly production, Shed-ache combines dance and theatre in a bright, energetic style designed to engage audiences. With a focus on fun and creativity, it offers an uplifting and interactive experience with plenty of opportunities for laughter. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: A playful dance theatre show full of imagination, laughter and family-friendly fun.

title: Wellington Town Crier Tour
subtitle: Novel history tours of Wellington town centre.
bodyContent: Wellington Museum in conjunction with Andrew Norris, the Town Crier are organising history tours of the centre of Wellington. The first one is on Sunday 30 August 2026 at 2.30 pm starting at the museum. Each walk lasts 1 – 1/5 hours and will stop and feature many places of historical interest. Walks are limited to 15 people per tour. Cost is £5 per person and must be booked in person at the museum, which is at The Squirrel. 28 Fore Street, Wellington and open Monday – Friday 10 am – 4 pm and Saturday 10 am – 1pm. Come along and learn about the history and happenings in Wellington a splendid time is guaranteed for all!

title: The Drifters
subtitle: The Drifters return to Taunton with a live concert featuring many of their best-loved hits. One of the most successful vocal groups in popular music history, they continue to perform the songs that have made them international favourites.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } The Drifters are back on tour performing a selection of their most popular songs, including Saturday Night at the Movies, You're More Than A Number, Come on Over to My Place, Under the Boardwalk and Kissin' In The Back Row. Over their long career, The Drifters have been inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, performed for the President of the United States and been recognised by Rolling Stone as among the greatest artists of all time. Under the guidance of Tina Treadwell, daughter of the group's original founders George and Faye Treadwell, the group continues to tour internationally, bringing their music to audiences across the UK. Tickets Available on their Website
tagline: The legendary Drifters perform their classic hits live in Taunton.

title: Remembering Lauren
subtitle: A special evening to remember Lauren Jackson, a much-loved friend and colleague. The event will feature live music from Nigel Reader and The Bird Dogs and include a presentation to Mind in Somerset.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Earlier this year, Lauren Jackson sadly passed away at the age of 17. A much-loved friend and colleague, Lauren was cherished by staff, customers, family and friends, and was a shining light in the lives of those who knew her. This special evening has been organised to remember Lauren's life and celebrate the impact she had on so many people. Following Lauren's passing, Patrick, landlord of The Winchester Arms, undertook a sponsored slim, losing 2 stone 2 pounds and raising more than £2,600 for Mind in Somerset. During the evening, a cheque will be presented to Mind in Somerset for the money raised so far. Guests are invited to come together in remembrance of a remarkable young woman while enjoying live music from Nigel Reader and The Bird Dogs. May Lauren rest in peace.
tagline: A special evening of remembrance, fundraising and live music in memory of Lauren Jackson.

title: Taunton WinterFest 2026
subtitle: Celebrate the start of the festive season at Taunton WinterFest 2026. Taking place in the heart of Taunton town centre, the event will feature market stalls, live entertainment, family attractions and the much-anticipated annual Christmas Lights Switch-On.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Taunton WinterFest returns to the town centre for a full day of festive entertainment, seasonal shopping and family fun. Visitors can explore a range of market stalls, enjoy live entertainment throughout the day and soak up the festive atmosphere across North Street and East Street. The event will culminate with the annual Christmas Lights Switch-On, helping to kick off the Christmas season in Taunton. Additional fairground rides are often available from the Saturday before the event, offering even more festive fun for visitors of all ages. Further details and announcements will be released closer to the event.
tagline: A festive day of markets, entertainment and Taunton's Christmas Lights Switch-On.

title: Pam Ayres – Doggedly Onward, A Life In Poems
subtitle: Much-loved poet, broadcaster and writer Pam Ayres comes to Taunton Brewhouse to celebrate Doggedly Onward – A Life In Poems, reflecting on more than five decades of poetry, storytelling and observations on everyday life.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Pam Ayres has spent a lifetime providing hilarious and profound insights into the delights and tribulations of everyday life. She visits Taunton to talk about her latest book, Doggedly Onward – A Life In Poems, which brings together her work from the 1970s through to the 2020s. The book traces the course of Pam's life and career, showcasing poetry that has made audiences laugh, reflect and occasionally shed a tear. One of Britain's best-loved poets and entertainers, her work continues to resonate with readers and audiences across generations. Pam's recent television appearances include The Cotswolds, This Morning, Alan Titchmarsh, Countdown and Would I Lie To You? Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: Pam Ayres celebrates a lifetime of poetry, laughter and storytelling.

title: Laura Lexx: Yo-Yo
subtitle: Award-winning comedian Laura Lexx brings her brand-new stand-up show Yo-Yo to Taunton Brewhouse. Following the success of her critically acclaimed show Slinky, Laura returns with a hilarious and heartfelt exploration of relationships, self-belief and the realities of everyday life.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } In a ten-year marriage, eventually your partner sees everything: every bad idea, every silly decision and every unfiltered thought. Somehow, they still say they love you. The real twist, according to Laura Lexx, is learning to believe them and perhaps learning to love yourself too. Fresh from the success of her critically acclaimed show Slinky, Laura Lexx returns with her latest show, Yo-Yo. A multi-award-winning comedian, Laura has appeared on Mock The Week, Live at the Apollo, Hypothetical, Pointless Celebrities and Roast Battle, and has earned widespread acclaim for her sharp wit, relatable storytelling and engaging stage presence. Her accolades include Best Show at the Women in Comedy Festival 2024, alongside multiple awards for best compere and master of ceremonies. Yo-Yo promises another evening of insightful, intelligent and laugh-out-loud comedy. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: Award-winning comedian Laura Lexx returns with her new stand-up show Yo-Yo.

title: Dunkeswell Aerodrome
subtitle: Located on the Blackdown hills in Devon, Dunkeswell the highest licenced aerodrome in the UK started life as a WW2 Naval Base and is now a vibrant and busy hub for the general aviation community.
bodyContent: Dunkeswell Aerodrome is situated in the heart of the Blackdown Hills, approximately 6 miles North of Honiton. Once a small quiet parish village, Dunkeswell is now a busy and vibrant Aero hub for one of the largest General Aviation communities in South West England. Initially established as an American Naval base during the peak of WW2, it now supports a network of aviation businesses and commercial developments. ​ We are situated at 839 feet above Sea Level, making us the highest licenced airfield in the United Kingdom. ​ We are open to visitors throughout the year and the Aviator Cafe with terrace is the ideal place to watch the activity at the aerodrome. ​ For more information a heritage museum is located at Dunkeswell. www.southwestairfields.co.uk

title: ACE Arts
subtitle: Located in the beautiful historical Old Town Hall building in the centre of the lovely old market town of Somerton, ACE holds an annual programme of free exhibitions. The retail space allows visitors to purchase items from exhibitors and other mainly local artists.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. Set up in 2016 with the renovation of the stunning Old Town Hall building in the centre of Somerton, ACE Arts was set up as a charity with the principle aim of providing art and creative activity to inspire, empower and enable people to develop and grow. ACE stands for Art, Care and Education to encompass the three areas of our organisation and support our ethos that everyone can benefit from creative inspiration in their lives. We encourage all sectors of the community to take part in good quality arts activity through a varied range of talks, practical workshops and outreach programmes. We have an annual programme of exhibitions, many of which are by local artists and which is designed to be at the centre of everything we do as a charity. Our accessible gallery space allows all works to be showcased in a beautifully designed area of the building. Each exhibition is launched with a private viewing and is usually followed by an artist’s talk where people can meet the artist and learn more about their work. Alongside the gallery area is the ‘making space’ which enables us to offer an exciting range of workshops such as artist-led drawing sessions. Regular sessions such as the art & craft and artists bookmaking groups are also held in the space with weekly life drawing classes held across the room in the more private Parish Rooms. Coffee mornings are held to coincide with the Somerton monthly market and other meetings include a newly established book club and ‘create and connect’, a monthly held session where anyone can come along with their own projects and interact with others as they work. On the ground floor of the building is our retail space where visitors can purchase a huge variety of items from exhibitors past and present together with many other local and new upcoming artists. Income from the shop and the various workshops, group meetings and regular sessions allows us to undertake our outreach programme which is a key part of the ACE ethos. Outreach work we’ve already undertaken includes creative sessions to those in residential care homes in the area, some of which were intergenerational projects with local schoolchildren. All of which focuses on the health and wellbeing of the local community, allowing all to benefit from lives enhanced by art. This summer funding from Somerset Skills and Learning enabled us to hold a summer school with free courses available to all on numerous different creative art based subjects. The series of sessions was very well attended, with a great deal of very positive feedback. The success of this means we would look to be able to offer more such projects in the future together with our extending our existing programme, subject to being able to access suitable funding.

title: Ham Hill Cider
subtitle: We produce award winning ciders here at North Down Farm, crafted from apples produced in some of Somerset’s finest orchards. We are proud to carry out every step in making cider from pruning through pressing and fermentation to bottling and delivering the final product. Come and join us to experience the true taste of Somerset.
bodyContent: At Ham Hill Cider, our aim is to create ciders that are rich in flavour and refreshingly appley. We believe we’ve cracked it. We press only the finest apples, that are grown within 5 miles of Ham Hill, and fully ripened by the late summer sun. We take the juice and carefully craft it into a range of premium ciders, to satisfy the tastes of those in search of something special. It is characteristically Somerset in style, with rich flavours, soft tannins and a hint of apple sharpness, which makes for an easy drinking refreshing cider that appeals to the contemporary taste, while remaining true to our heritage. Tree, we have the privilege of tending some of the finest orchards in Somerset. We prune and plant trees during the winter months, wait for mother nature to do her work over spring and summer and then pick the apples in the autumn. Juice, we use over 25 apple varieties, including, Dabinett, Sweet Coppin, Chisel Jersey, Yarlington Mill and Kingston Black, pressing each variety at their peak of ripeness for maximum flavour. Magic, we allow only the naturally occurring wild yeast to work on our ciders, which means relying on the magic of nature to do its work. With fermentation underway we wait for the first cuckoo of spring to announce the cider has matured is ready for drinking! Cider, the best part of the process is that long anticipated first taste of the new cider and the realisation that the all the hard work was worth it. Ciderworks, to enjoy our ciders at their best join us on a Friday night at the Ciderworks taproom. Our full range of ciders are on tap, and you can take a look around next door where we make them, we provide seasonal home cooked food every week with regular specials of whatever the farm can provide. We also have regular live music nights. Follow us on social media for an up to date programme of events. We are four sons of Somerset with a passion for the press and we welcome you to Ham Hill Cider.
tagline: We produce award winning ciders here at North Down Farm

title: Dough Taunton
subtitle: A small artisan bakery specialising in sourdough and pastries.
bodyContent: Dough is a family run business, we focus on sourcing the best quality organic flour and ingredients the South West has to offer. We're so excited to share our little venture with you and hope you love it. ‘Dough’ offers you a variety of delicious pastries including croissants, cinnamon buns, pain au chocolat and the popular Cruffin, alongside a selection of breads and bakes. Dave is the owner and baker behind Dough and looks forward to welcoming you and tempting you in with his makes. The business started in January 2020 with a few cakes and then branched into breads after the first lockdown but Dave has been a baker for around 6 years. ‘Dough’ provides a number of local businesses with their breads and baked goods including Gaia Garden Delicatessen & Artisan Takeaway, The Little Wine Shop & Social, The Bank, The Mnago Tree and Hestercombe Gardens. title: The Railway Inn
subtitle: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you. Treat yourself to a delicious meal in our restaurant, have a bar snack in our cosy bar, or simply enjoy a pint of Thatchers Somerset Cider.
bodyContent: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you. Treat yourself to a delicious meal in our restaurant, have a bar snack in our cosy bar, or simply enjoy a pint of Thatchers Somerset Cider . The food we proudly serve features regional and seasonal ingredients from local producers, with a strong emphasis on great quality, great taste and sensible prices. Our drinks menu is carefully chosen, with of course the full range of ciders from Thatchers; beers, wines and soft drinks. Our team of enthusiastic front of house staff love to share their knowledge and appetite for products with guests, and are proud to go that extra mile in making visits a memorable one. The Railway Inn has been at the hub of Sandford village for over 140 years. As a reminder of its long tradition, the original signals from the old Sandford railway line take pride of place outside, together with two authentic oak vats. The Railway Inn Cider House and Kitchen is decorated with artefacts and pictures reflecting the cidermaking heritage of Thatchers. Keen to represent local craftsmanship at its best, the bar and restaurant has been given extra special interest with hand carvings in English oak describing the story of the cidermaking year. A short walk along the road and you’ll come to the Thatchers Cider Shop . Here the shelves are packed with our ciders, alongside produce such as local cheeses and chutneys, and gifts including books and clothing. Our draught ciders are available straight from the barrel so you can try before you buy. Please call the Railway Inn on 01934 611518, or book online at www.therailwayinn.com
tagline: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you.

title: Blakehay Theatre Re-Opening
subtitle: The Blakehay Theatre, in Weston-super-Mare, is delighted to announce that they are re-opening in January 2022.
bodyContent: Having closed in March 2020 due to the pandemic, and after receiving a Culture Recovery Fund Grant in October 2020, the theatre staff were able to create Blakehay@Home, and stage ‘Comedy at the Quarry’ in June 2021. However, the majority of this fund was to make alterations to the theatre and in May 2021, the contractors moved into the theatre. During 2021 the contractors have been busy installing a new ventilation system and altering the backstage dressing rooms. At the same time the theatre has undergone a complete electrical re-wire making the theatre future-proof and helping with the theatre’s carbon footprint. Work on the theatre is now in the last stages of completion and will re-open to the public in January 2022 with the first performance performed by Weston Operatic Society juniors, OPPITTS, with their aptly named show ‘Opening Up’ with songs from all your favourite shows from stage and screen on Saturday 29 th and Sunday 30 th January, tickets on sale now. The studios will be re-opening in week commencing Monday 10 th January with the return of our Community Classes, including a few new classes for 2022. Check out the theatre website for more information. “We are so happy to be opening the theatre bringing live performances back. It has been a tough couple of years, not just for us but for the whole industry. The pandemic has impacted heavily on theatre and we hope that 2022 will be our busiest year yet. We have an amazing variety of shows and we are confident that there is something for everyone. We can’t wait to welcome people back into this beautiful building, there really is nothing like sitting in a theatre and watching live performance.” – Sally Heath, Theatre Manager. As an important venue in the heart of Weston-super-Mare the Blakehay Theatre will be welcoming back local groups to perform on the stage as well as professional productions that were postponed from 2020. “The small but beautiful Blakehay Theatre is the town’s own theatre, owned by the people of our town through the town council. It is wonderful to see it reopening after nearly 2 years and a refurbishment and I’m definitely going to take the opportunity to see a show in early 2022.” Malcolm Nicholson, Town Clerk The Blakehay Theatre is an approved venue to be able to use the industry-wide ‘See it Safely’ mark, so you can feel confident and safe knowing that our venue is COVID-secure and will be following the latest government guidance. If you would like to see the work that has been done at the theatre, there will be an open day on Saturday 22 nd January 2022 from 10am to 4pm . Everyone is welcome to pop in and have a look around the theatre as well as buy tickets to our upcoming shows and events. For further information and to book your tickets, please visit the theatre’s website www.blakehaytheatre.co.uk
tagline: The Blakehay Theatre, in Weston-super-Mare, is delighted to announce that they are re-opening

title: Hit the Streets of Clevedon for a healthy walk
subtitle: Walking groups are helping people across North Somerset stretch their legs, make new friends and feel healthier. Organised walks usually last about an hour but a new group has launched in Clevedon to offer residents a slightly more vigorous, 90-minute route. Life joined them to take in the sights around the town…
bodyContent: How to get there Start at map ref: ST 408710 Car: Parking is available at the former Morrisons supermarket, off Great Western Road - Route information Distance: just over 3 miles Difficulty: easy – a fairly flat route around the town Duration: allow up to 90 minutes Map: OS Explorer 153 Walking groups are helping people across North Somerset stretch their legs, make new friends and feel healthier. Organised walks usually last about an hour but a new group has launched in Clevedon to offer residents a slightly more vigorous, 90-minute route. Life joined them to take in the sights around the town… Start the walk in Queen’s Square, then turn left onto Old Church Road. Turn right onto Queen’s Road and continue uphill towards the crossroads at the end. Cross the road and turn left into Sunnyside Road. At the next crossroads turn right, which is still Sunnyside Road. From here you can go through a gate into Sunhill Park. Follow the path to your right, through the trees, and then head towards Sunhill House. This is now Clevedon Community Centre after being bought by the people of the town in 1949. Go around the side of the building and exit through the car park onto Princes Road. Turn right onto this road, cross over, and then at the junction turn left into Linden Road, then right into Herbert Road. Go through a wooden gate into Herbert Gardens, which was donated to the people of Clevedon by the Elton family in 1865. Follow the path and you will pass a ruined stone structure, which formed part of Wycliffe Girls School. Click HERE for full details and FREE PDF copy

title: Goodfellows
subtitle: Smart restaurant and cafe with fish-centric, Modern Mediterranean dishes made from local produce.
bodyContent: Adam and Martine Fellows opened Goodfellows in September 2004, quickly becoming one of the most popular restaurants in the area. Adam spent 17 years perfecting his style while working in many of the best restaurants across England, France and Belgium. He was Head Chef for seven years at the Michelin starred Charlton House Hotel. For the last 15 years Adam has delighted customers with his modern European dishes featuring fish, meat and vegetarian dishes which are light but intense with flavour. The fish comes mainly from day boats off the coast of Devon and Cornwall and is cooked inventively, enhancing the natural flavours of the fish but never over-complicating them. Goodfellows has two AA Red Rosettes and is included in the The Good Food Guide and Trencherman Guide

title: Sharpham Park
subtitle: Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels near Glastonbury.
bodyContent: Our organic farm and mill Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels near Glastonbury . It’s the home of Mulberry founder Roger Saul who moved from the world of fashion to food in 2004 when he launched the Sharpham Park brand from his organic farm. At Sharpham Park we grow organic spelt and stone grind it in the traditional way to preserve the delicious, nutty taste of the ancient grain. Today, we turned the milled spelt into flour, cereals and grains however history records show spelt has been grown for approximately 4,000 years in the area since the Bronze and Iron ages. The farm is also sustainably managed – the spelt fields have 4 metre margins and the hedgerows are cut every other year meaning wildlife such as wild deer, hare, bees and dormice are allowed to shelter and forage for food all year round. The ancient grain Spelt is an ancient grain which as has gained popularity in recent times because it’s an excellent source of dietary fibre and contains protein as well as some vitamins and minerals. It’s both easy to digest and leaves you feeling fuller for longer as well as being a good source of slow release energy; so much so the Roman Army called it their “marching grain”. Within working with Bowel Cancer UK Eating a high fibre diet is important in the fight against Bowel Cancer and we have teamed up with Bowel Cancer UK to spread this message. More than 40 top chefs have donated spelt recipes to the campaign and you can find these Great British Spelt Recipes on our website. Sharpham Pantry restaurant at Kilver Court Designer Village You can enjoy a range of spelt dishes in the Sharpham Pantry restaurant including our spelt flat breads and spelt bread and butter pudding. You can find the full range of our delicious spelt products in the Great House at Kilver Court Designer Village in Shepton Mallet. Come and browse our selection of cereals including flakes, muesli and porridge as well as our grains and four different types of flour made to meet all of your baking needs.
tagline: Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels.

title: Somerset Rural Life Museum
subtitle: Visitors to Somerset Rural Life Museum can explore rural life from the 1800s onwards and discover more about the county’s heritage including its landscape, food and farming, working life and rural crafts.
bodyContent: Visitors to Somerset Rural Life Museum can explore rural life from the 1800s onwards and discover more about the county’s heritage including its landscape, food and farming, working life and rural crafts. The museum tells the story of Somerset’s rich rural and social history. Visitors can enjoy the five Farmhouse Galleries which explore the themes of ‘Creating’, ‘Learning’, ‘Believing’, ‘Celebrating’ and ‘Remembering.’ In the large Farmyard Gallery the major themes are ‘Working Village’ and ‘Working the Land’. The magnificent 14th-century Abbey Barn remains the centrepiece of the site, providing a unique and remarkable setting for exhibitions and events. Outside spaces, including the Farmyard and the Orchard, contain sculpture and family trails that interpret the history of the site and its buildings. The Grain Store Café is open all year round at this family-friendly destination, offering high-quality locally-sourced food and drink. A programme of seasonal events take place throughout the year.
tagline: Visitors to Somerset Rural Life Museum can explore rural life from the 1800s onwards.

title: Fondo Lounge
subtitle: Our all-day food menus have something for everyone for eat-in or takeaway!
bodyContent: Lounges was founded in 2002 by a trio of long standing friends, Dave Reid, Alex Reilley and Jake Bishop. Having spent years in the restaurant and bar trade – not to mention just as many propping up the bars in Bristol (all of course in the name of research) – they decided it was time they did their own thing . The motivation was simple and very selfish; they wanted somewhere to drink themselves. FOOD Everyone is welcome in a Lounge, so we look after every taste from fresh, zingy salads to massive burgers with all the trimmings. We spend a lot of time working on exciting new dishes but we’ll always be somewhere you can go for classic British food like a cracking bacon butty too. We’re proud that our gluten free and vegan menus are not second best; we take pride in making sure they are packed with plenty of interesting, satisfying dishes just like our other menus. Last, but not least, we know that if mum and dad are going to enjoy themselves, then the kids need to be happy. Our proper kids’ menu features healthy, indulgent and fun dishes too.

title: Stowey Sutton
subtitle: Stowey is a small village within the Chew Valley in Somerset, England. It lies south of Chew Valley Lake and north of the Mendip Hills, approximately 10 miles south of Bristol on the A368 road Weston-Super-Mare to Bath.
bodyContent: Stowey is a small village within the Chew Valley in Somerset, England. It lies south of Chew Valley Lake and north of the Mendip Hills , approximately 10 miles south of Bristol on the A368 road Weston-Super-Mare to Bath . Stowey and its neighbouring and larger village, Bishop Sutton, form the civil parish of Stowey Sutton. It is an area rich with flora and fauna whilst developing with the needs of its community. The aim of Stowey Sutton Parish Council is to provide facilities that are required by its local community and to help people make the most of where they live by connecting with their neighbours. The community has been lacking in open social areas recently and the Councils desire is to create those facilities, build on interest, maintain desire, and deliver suitable facilities to be used by all without prejudice. Stowey Sutton Parish Council welcomes the views of all parishioners and residents in its decision-making process. Any interested parishioner is encouraged to attend our regular monthly meeting to raise any issue they feel relevant or participate in any volunteer groups or projects. Stowey Sutton Parish Council has a number of projects underway to achieve these aspirations. Currently being installed is a new play area for children on Bishop Sutton Recreation Ground, a zipwire aimed at its teenage population, and adult gym equipment for those seeking the opportunity to get fit in their own time. A pathway will be created around the perimeter of the recreation ground for walkers, runners, scooters, pushchairs or cycling. And then we have the Community Library, we are aiming for a late summer launch. 2018 is proving to be an extremely busy year for Stowey Sutton Parish Council. Everyone is enjoying the project work and are keen to involve as many volunteers as possible and maybe even encourage another possible councillor or two to join us on this journey. Should you be interested in one of our councillor vacancies available by co-option, please contact clerk@stoweysuttonpc.org .

title: Sharpham Park
subtitle: Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels near Glastonbury.
bodyContent: Our organic farm and mill Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels near Glastonbury . It’s the home of Mulberry founder Roger Saul who moved from the world of fashion to food in 2004 when he launched the Sharpham Park brand from his organic farm. At Sharpham Park we grow organic spelt and stone grind it in the traditional way to preserve the delicious, nutty taste of the ancient grain. Today, we turned the milled spelt into flour, cereals and grains however history records show spelt has been grown for approximately 4,000 years in the area since the Bronze and Iron ages. The farm is also sustainably managed – the spelt fields have 4 metre margins and the hedgerows are cut every other year meaning wildlife such as wild deer, hare, bees and dormice are allowed to shelter and forage for food all year round. The ancient grain Spelt is an ancient grain which as has gained popularity in recent times because it’s an excellent source of dietary fibre and contains protein as well as some vitamins and minerals. It’s both easy to digest and leaves you feeling fuller for longer as well as being a good source of slow release energy; so much so the Roman Army called it their “marching grain”. Within working with Bowel Cancer UK Eating a high fibre diet is important in the fight against Bowel Cancer and we have teamed up with Bowel Cancer UK to spread this message. More than 40 top chefs have donated spelt recipes to the campaign and you can find these Great British Spelt Recipes on our website. Sharpham Pantry restaurant at Kilver Court Designer Village You can enjoy a range of spelt dishes in the Sharpham Pantry restaurant including our spelt flat breads and spelt bread and butter pudding. You can find the full range of our delicious spelt products in the Great House at Kilver Court Designer Village in Shepton Mallet. Come and browse our selection of cereals including flakes, muesli and porridge as well as our grains and four different types of flour made to meet all of your baking needs.
tagline: Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels.

title: Minehead Storywalks
subtitle: Storywalks are simple digital trails, which are accessible through the browser in smart phones and tablets. Just click on the web link, all info is then downloaded and away you go. The walks are free and at the end is a geocache log for you to sign.
bodyContent: The innovative and award winning storywalks are simple, family friendly and free. Each tale is unique, and each trail and narrative are carefully crafted, you follow them like a bread crumb trail. Each new chapter directs you to the next, and when in location the text will reveal the story unfurl. In Minehead we have created 6 trails covering the towns Hidden Histories and Secret Stories. Pop into the Minehead Information Centre to find out more.

title: The Railway Inn
subtitle: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you. Treat yourself to a delicious meal in our restaurant, have a bar snack in our cosy bar, or simply enjoy a pint of Thatchers Somerset Cider.
bodyContent: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you. Treat yourself to a delicious meal in our restaurant, have a bar snack in our cosy bar, or simply enjoy a pint of Thatchers Somerset Cider . The food we proudly serve features regional and seasonal ingredients from local producers, with a strong emphasis on great quality, great taste and sensible prices. Our drinks menu is carefully chosen, with of course the full range of ciders from Thatchers; beers, wines and soft drinks. Our team of enthusiastic front of house staff love to share their knowledge and appetite for products with guests, and are proud to go that extra mile in making visits a memorable one. The Railway Inn has been at the hub of Sandford village for over 140 years. As a reminder of its long tradition, the original signals from the old Sandford railway line take pride of place outside, together with two authentic oak vats. The Railway Inn Cider House and Kitchen is decorated with artefacts and pictures reflecting the cidermaking heritage of Thatchers. Keen to represent local craftsmanship at its best, the bar and restaurant has been given extra special interest with hand carvings in English oak describing the story of the cidermaking year. A short walk along the road and you’ll come to the Thatchers Cider Shop . Here the shelves are packed with our ciders, alongside produce such as local cheeses and chutneys, and gifts including books and clothing. Our draught ciders are available straight from the barrel so you can try before you buy. Please call the Railway Inn on 01934 611518, or book online at www.therailwayinn.com
tagline: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you.

title: DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House
subtitle: Great motorway links M5 junction 20 & 21 Bristol International Airport only 12 minutes away Bristol City Centre only 25 minutes away. With local access to Cheddar Gorge and Mendip AONB only 45 minutes away.
bodyContent: Welcome to DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House, the South West’s finest four-star boutique hotel and spa. An enchanting venue set within rolling English countryside, Cadbury House is the ideal backdrop for your special occasion whether a wedding, private party, business event, spa break or dining experience. With truly breath-taking views across North Somerset and the Bristol Channel, Cadbury House effortlessly combines old and new, with the traditional country house and the elegant boutique-style hotel. There is also an onsite Marco Pierre White Steakhouse Bar & Grill, an award-winning health club and a renowned spa. The hotel offers 132 luxury bedrooms including suites, on-site parking and excellent transport access meaning guests can enjoy the facilities for both business and pleasure. Please note from May 1 st , 2022 overnight parking will be chargeable at £5.00 per vehicle. Corporate customers are also well catered for with 12 meeting rooms, multiple breakout areas, and a dedicated conference team on hand. Whether you are hosting a small business meeting to a multi-day conference, DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House does not disappoint as a destination location for business needs.
tagline: The South West’s finest four-star boutique hotel and spa.

title: The Playhouse in Weston super Mare
subtitle: The Playhouse Theatre is available for hire for both community and professional shows and as a venue for conferences, meetings and corporate events. In addition to the main auditorium the theatres facilities include a licensed bar, meeting and rehearsal spaces and full disabled access.
bodyContent: Located in the centre of Weston-Super-Mare the Playhouse is a friendly and welcoming 664-seat theatre which offers a lively and diverse programme of events to meet the entertainment, creative and educational requirements of its local and surrounding community. The Playhouse’s high quality programme of professional and community events includes around 300 performances per year including music, drama, comedy, dance, musicals, film, children’s shows, pantomime and more recently West End Productions. The Playhouse Theatre is available for hire for both community and professional shows and as a venue for conferences, meetings and corporate events. In addition to the main auditorium the theatres facilities include a licensed bar, meeting and rehearsal spaces and full disabled access. Our dedicated and professional staff are used to working with all visiting companies and hirers to ensure a successful event while our welcoming and caring front of house team ensure patrons an enjoyable entertainment experience. The Playhouse Theatre is managed by Parkwood Theatres working in partnership with North Somerset Council.

title: Lakeside Holiday Park
subtitle: An ideal place to enjoy a family holiday or short break, heated pool, entertainment, private fishing.
bodyContent: Lakeside Holiday Park in the favourite Somerset resort of Burnham-on-Sea , is an ideal place to enjoy a family holiday or short break, and always offers real value for money. • Private fishing • Drinks terrace & beer garden • Children's play area • Free Wi-Fi hotspot • Big screen Freeview TV • Bar & Takeaway throughout 2021 • Top of the range caravans include, double-glazing, bed linen, DVD player, freezer, plus crockery and cutlery upgrade It's the perfect base to explore the area or simply relax by the pool or tree-lined lake. Burnham's High Street and famous seven-mile long sandy beach are just a short, level walk away with West Country favourites such as Weston-Super-Mare , Wells , Bristol, Bath , and Cheddar (to name but a few) all within easy reach by car. There's something for everyone to enjoy and all so accessible from Lakeside! The park offers a wide choice of great, self-catering static caravans from the leading manufacturers. All holiday homes are 12ft wide and sleep up to 8 people - some are that little bit extra special and have double-glazing and gas central heating to make your stay even more enjoyable. There is something to suit everyone's holiday home demands! Whether you're catching fish in our private lake - Wild, Mirror, Common Carp, Roach, Rudd, Tench, Bream, Pike and Perch are all present - or not, Lakeside delivers an intoxicatingly relaxing setting! *Please visit www.lakesideholidays.co.uk for further information regarding availability of on-Park facilities and other conditions. Central Booking Office on 01278 792222 is open 7 days a week (except Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year’s Eve and New Year’s Day.)

title: Rock Inn
subtitle: 3 Flavours already has a duo of thriving neighbourhood eateries in Barnet and Banbury and ‘3 Flavours Kitchen’ is the first to launch in the Southwest, with many more planned to roll-out in the near future. Chef Chanaka Fernando’s vision for 3 Flavours Kitchen is to provide an exceptional dining experience that combines culinary excellence with the charm of Waterrow, near Taunton.
bodyContent: Steaks are a standout feature on the menu with options such as the Rib-Eye Steak (250g) priced at £26.50, Sirloin Steak (250g) at £25.00, and Rump Steak (250g) at £21.00. Diners can enhance their steak experience with a variety of sauces, including peppercorn, mushroom, béarnaise, garlic butter, and chimichurri for an additional £2.00 each, or upgrade to a luxurious truffle red wine sauce for £3.00. Grill & Burger highlights include the Grilled Chicken Burger at £14.50 and the 3 Flavours Signature Beef Burger at £15.00, both served with caramelised onions, truffle mayo, rocket, ketchup, relish, and fries. Seafood lovers can indulge in the Miso Grilled Salmon at £23.50, served with a Japanese salad and sesame. Vegetarian options feature the Grilled Cauliflower Steak (v) at £15.50, paired with roasted pepper sauce, basil, and olive salsa, and the Grilled Vegetable Burger (V) at £11.00, featuring caramelised onion, mushroom, grilled courgettes, hash browns, rocket, and spicy mayo. Curries are a cornerstone of the new menu, offering a range of aromatic dishes served with steamed rice and crispy shallots. Notable dishes include the Monkfish & Tiger Prawn curry at £22.00, Aromatic Chicken Green Curry at £16.50, and the Ceylon Lamb at £17.50.
tagline: 3 Flavours Kitchen at The Rock Inn in Waterrow, near Taunton is the latest culinary concept

title: Glastonbury Abbey
subtitle: Glastonbury Abbey, Glastonbury, Somerset is connected with legend to a degree that is unparalleled by any other abbey in England. Since Medieval times it has held legendary status as the earliest Christian foundation in Britain linked to Joseph of Arimathea and the burial place of King Arthur.
bodyContent: Glastonbury Abbey, Glastonbury, Somerset is an internationally renowned site attracting visitors from around the world for its history, heritage, myths and legends as well as for its spiritual enrichment and there has been a church on the site for at least 1500 years with evidence of even earlier occupation. Glastonbury was the richest monastery in England at the end of the Saxon period and was second only to Westminster at the close of the middle ages. Its Abbot lived in considerable splendour and wielded tremendous power with the main surviving example of this power and wealth to be found in the Abbot’s Kitchen, one of only three surviving medieval examples in the world. It’s history is intertwined with English traditions; one of its Abbots – St Dunstan, wrote the Coronation words last used for the coronation of our present Queen Elizabeth II and William Blake’s popular “Jerusalem” is said to be written about the story that a young Jesus, accompanied by Joseph of Arimathea, visited Glastonbury . The Holy Thorn which grows at Glastonbury Abbey has become part of the legend of Joseph of Arimathea. According to the story when Joseph arrived in Britain he landed on the island of Avalon and climbed up Wearyall Hill, exhausted he thrust his staff into the ground and rested. By morning his staff had taken root and it grew into the miraculous thorn tree which flowers every Easter and Christmas. In 1191 the monks told the world they had found the bodies of King Arthur and his Queen found on the south side of the Lady Chapel. On 19th April 1278 their remains were removed in the presence of King Edward 1 and Queen Eleanor to a black marble tomb within the abbey itself. The tomb survived until the dissolution of the abbey in 1539. In 1536, during the 27 th year of the reign of Henry VIII, there were over 800 monasteries, nunneries and friaries in Britain. By 1541 there were none and the last abbot of Glastonbury , Richard Whiting was hung, drawn and quartered on Glastonbury Tor ; a brutal end for a pious man. Today it is a tranquil setting in which visitors can discover the stories behind Glastonbury Abbey with tours from costumed Living History presenters in the grounds; these tours are free but should be booked in advance for groups. A packed events calendar brings theatre, concerts, exhibitions and workshops to the abbey grounds every year and the abbey’s spectacular Night at the Abbey which last year won a national award. School and university groups can enjoy tailor-made itineraries and there are specific activities for families too. An accredited museum showcases items from the abbey’s history and gives more information about the chronology of events, archaeological finds and gives an insight into monastic life. There are 36 acres of parkland to explore with a dedicated wildlife area as well as new plans to recreate a Medieval Kitchen Garden. Groups are welcomed with a pre-booked meet and greet service available too and a special rate; driver and tour guide go free. A full access statement is on the abbey’s website – www.glastonburyabbey.com – along with maps in 14 different languages. Find us on Facebook /GlastonburyAbbeySomerset, follow us on Twitter @Glastonburyabbe or give us a call on 01458 832267. We look forward to meeting you
tagline: Glastonbury Abbey is connected with legend to a degree that is unparalleled by any other abbey

title: Walk Minehead to Brean
subtitle: Explore some of Somerset’s superb coast with a walk along part or all of the new 58-mile route that is the latest addition to the National Coast Path.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. From glorious beaches to amazing wildlife, historical delights to geological marvels, the Somerset stretch of the England Coast Path offers walkers of all levels - from holidaymakers and families to serious walking enthusiasts - the chance to explore, relax and enjoy some of Britain's most unusual and beautiful coastal scenery. Starting from the genteel Victorian resort of Minehead and walking east towards the natural promontory of Brean Down, you will pass a medieval village , alabaster rocks, an ancient harbour, a stunning waterfall , limestone pavements, saltmarshes, sand dunes and a lighthouse on legs. For more info click here
tagline: Explore some of Somerset’s superb coast with a walk along part or all of the new 58-mile route.

title: The Beach Hotel
subtitle: The award winning Beach Hotel overlooks Minehead Seafront and the iconic West Somerset Steam Railway. New England décor greets you inside, allowing for a relaxing drink in our bar and snug areas.
bodyContent: The Beach Hotel in Minehead overlooks Minehead Seafront and the iconic West Somerset Steam Railway . New England décor greets you inside, allowing for a relaxing drink in our bar and snug areas. Eat in our award winning Galley restaurant, locally sourced food providing a menu for all tastes. Our onsite facilities include a fully equipped gym and exercise classes. We have two meeting rooms for weddings, parties and conferences. Most of our bedrooms look over the sea or the West Somerset Railway and all have en suite facilities. We strive to be sustainable as much as possible, therefore we supply fresh milk in your rooms for your tea and coffee along with delicious homemade shortbread biscuits.

I am a big Hallmark movie fan, bring on the sloppy afternoon Christmas flick, where the actors swap throughout all of them, honestly its my favourite part of the season​ 5. title: The George Harrison Project
subtitle: Enjoy the ultimate live music tribute to George Harrison, performing his best-loved hits from The Beatles, his solo career, and The Traveling Wilbury’s. This hit-packed show includes well-loved songs such as “My Sweet Lord”, “Here Comes the Sun”, “Something”, and “Got My Mind Set on You”.
bodyContent: Not to be missed! Here comes the perfect tribute to a Beatles legend! Enjoy the ultimate live music tribute to George Harrison, performing his best-loved hits from The Beatles, his solo career, and The Traveling Wilburys. After the Liverpudlian four-piece called time on Beatlemania, George Harrison enjoyed a successful solo career, releasing 12 studio albums, including Living In The Material World, Cloud Nine, Brainwashed and the classic triple album All Things Must Pass. He also formed the supergroup The Traveling Wilburys with Bob Dylan, Jeff Lynne, Roy Orbison and Tom Petty. Visiting Taunton Brewhouse as part of their 2026 tour, these talented musicians authentically recreate some of George Harrison’s best-known tracks, earning rave reviews. The hit-packed show includes well-loved songs such as “My Sweet Lord”, “Here Comes The Sun”, “Something”, “While My Guitar Gently Weeps”, “Got My Mind Set On You”, and many more! Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre

title: Wellington Town Trails
subtitle: Discover Wellington on foot with three free trails that reveal the town’s history, architecture, green spaces and natural treasures.
bodyContent: Discover Wellington on Foot with Three Town Trails Wellington is a town with plenty of stories to tell, and three specially designed trails from Wellington Town Council offer an enjoyable way for residents and visitors to discover them. The Wellington Town Trail takes walkers around some of the town’s most interesting landmarks, encouraging them to look more closely at familiar buildings and uncover stories along the way. A particularly family-friendly Children’s Scavenger Hunt turns the route into an engaging fact-finding mission, with questions based on locations including Wellington Museum, St John’s Church, the Old Police Station, The Iron Duke, Wellington House and Wellington Park. For those who enjoy nature, the Wellington Park Tree Trail explores some of the notable trees in the town’s historic park. The Grade II listed Edwardian park was created in 1903 to commemorate the coronation of King Edward VII, on land donated by Fox Brothers, and the trail reveals the history and significance of some of its most interesting specimens. Among the highlights are a Wellingtonia planted in 2022 as part of the Queen’s Green Canopy, an English oak planted for the coronation of King George V in 1911, and the impressive Western Red Cedar known locally as “The Big Tree”. Together with the third trail, they provide an excellent excuse to slow down, explore Wellington on foot and see the town from a fresh perspective — whether you are discovering it for the first time or have lived here all your life. Our Dog Walking Guide has been tested and approved by the dogs of Wellington Town Council! We work closely with the community to ensure responsible dog ownership and this guide usefully clarifies permittable areas in and around the town. Further interest and involvement in the local community in terms of how we weave our lives into our environment, can be accessed here through Transition Town Wellington .

title: Medieval history with steam nostalgia!
subtitle: Get the train to old county town of Taunton and start your journey off with a nights stay in the Castle Hotel. Then drive down to Bishop's Lydeard, the home of the longest heritage railway in the UK. Let your adventure into Medieval history begin with some 20th century Nostalgia thrown in!

title: Adrenalin Weekender (intermediate) two night
subtitle: If you are at work and needing to break out for the weekend and burn some energy, then our Adrenaline Weekender tour in and around the stunning Mendip Hills for those with intermediate experience of outdoor activities is just the package for you and your friends.

title: Three Day Family Fun in and around Minehead
subtitle: Minehead has been a famous family destination for decades, reflecting a rural community on the fringes of Exmoor in West Somerset with a long sandy beach framed by a picturesque harbour and the iconic North Hill behind. Where better then to start your Minehead family fun with a Day Pass to Butlins resort, found at the end of the promenade and brimming with fun! There are rides, the Splash Waterworld, play areas, activities and the entertainment in Skyline pavilion plus so much more.

title: Coco Blue Boutique
subtitle: Coco Blue Boutique is an independent boutique featuring design-led clothing, footwear and accessory brands from Europe and beyond. We are known for sourcing niche labels which are little found in the UK - our buying takes us to Milan, Paris, London, Berlin and Copenhagen, in order to create a curated collection of easy to wear, quality and stylish pieces.
bodyContent: In 2006 Sarah and Kellie opened the doors of Coco Blue at the Riverside, Taunton. As sisters and young mums (with five children between us!) we decided to concentrate on everyday style with a luxe edge. They choose European labels crafted from only the finest fabrics, which are beautifully cut, and can be worn season after season. They believe in slow-fashion and supporting companies whose years of knowledge and experience allows them to produce beautiful, artisan pieces. They add to our portfolio consistently and one of the best parts of our jobs is finding labels that they truly believe in. They love nothing more than catching the early flight to Paris, never quite knowing what we will be bringing home! They hope to give every customer a true ‘Coco Blue’ experience - offering genuine and personal style advice to help you feel and look amazing. We are passionate about recreating this online, so please do introduce yourself and allow us to get to know you.
tagline: Boutique situated in Taunton's Independent Quarter.

title: TEALS
subtitle: TEALS is a brand new eco farm store offering locals - as well as holiday makers - a surprising and very special destination to stop off at. It comprises a colourful food market, bakery, bottle shop and gift store and is set next to a spacious apple orchard.
bodyContent: Stop for lunch, a coffee break and to stretch the legs, or to stock up on fresh and tasty groceries. Remaining loyal to local and celebrating the region’s best producers, TEALS is packed with sustainably sourced products from fantastic local suppliers. Discover fresh meats from nearby hills and locally churned cheeses, delicately flavoured gelato and locally ground coffee. A bakery and bottle store sell wine and local cider, while the healthy kitchen serves up tasty and nutritious plates from across the region. There’s also a nature-inspired kids play area and a gift store. With a strong sustainability ethos and powered by renewable energy, TEALS is an agricultural build on a greenfield site. It uses reclaimed timber, minimises waste and trees were planted to help offset the build - it is also pending B Corp status. It’s the mission of local co-founders Ash and Nick Sinfield to make a positive contribution to the region, connecting communities to producers, as well as travellers to the area. Situated halfway between London and Cornwall - at the North/South Cadbury junction - TEALS is the ideal stop off for those travelling between the two regions, as well as the local community. With eight electric car charging points, TEALS is the first low plastic, fuel-free services on the A303. Bringing life, vibrancy and a welcoming atmosphere, as well as original experiences, TEALS promises to enrich each journey with a powerful sense of local.
tagline: TEALS is a brand new eco farm store for locals - as well as holiday makers

title: Lasseter's
subtitle: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion. It serves locally sourced dishes created by a team of professional chefs.
bodyContent: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion. It serves locally sourced dishes created by a team of professional chefs. The restaurant focuses on bringing high-quality dining and great-value food to Weston, and is quickly gaining a reputation for excellent food, atmosphere and welcoming service. The restaurant boasts stunning views of Weston-super-Mare’s bay, as well as exciting menus that are based around fresh ingredients. It serves lunch and dinner from Wednesday to Saturday – including special set lunch menus and early-bird pre-theatre offers – and a carvery on Sundays from noon. Lasseter’s also serves an extensive range of cocktails, spirits and wines, with over 100 drinks to choose from. The wine list has been hand-selected by the restaurant manager, with a variety of different types and styles for all tastes. There is something for everyone at Lasseter’s. You can relax in the bar or on the terrace – with a snack if, you fancy – or enjoy a meal in our glorious restaurant overlooking the seafront.
tagline: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion.

title: Blakehay Theatre
subtitle: Leading the way in this zeitgeist for Weston-super-Mare the Blakehay Theatre create Theatre for the whole community, bringing national popular shows and treading subject matters onto the stage. A creative hub for artists and performers in the local area and a cultural home for fans of the arts.
bodyContent: The theatre’s uniquely diverse program of locally produced and touring work is curated especially for you. We are striving to create an inclusive creative community to make the most of a beautiful venue by using all of its spaces for artistic endorsers, and we are delighted you want to be a part of it. With an intimate 200 seat main house, 100 seat Studio Theatre and a warm and welcoming theatre bar, the Blakehay Theatre is able to present a variety of shows and events in these spaces. With community classes taking place in our beautiful studios, there is something for everyone at the Blakehay Theatre. We may be little, but we have big ideas! The vision is to build a ‘big-city’ creative culture into the heart of the Victorian seaside resort of Weston-super-Mare. We need continued public support to help sustain and grow this vision through ticket sales, personal donations, sponsorship and help spreading the word! We are constantly working and adapting our programme each season to bring new and exclusive works to Weston-super-Mare, but we can’t do that without your support, so please spread the word and support our little theatre with big ideas!
tagline: Leading the way in this zeitgeist for Weston-super-Mare the Blakehay Theatre

title: Clevedon Court, National Trust
subtitle: Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is a remarkable survival from the medieval period.
bodyContent: Clevedon Court in Clevedon, Somerset, National Trust property is an outstanding 14th-century manor house and 18th-century terraced garden Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is a remarkable survival from the medieval period. The house was purchased by Abraham Elton in 1709 and it is still the much-loved family home of his descendants today. Explore the striking display of Eltonware pottery and a fascinating collection of Nailsea glass.
tagline: Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is remarkable.

Enjoy the cosy living room, garden views, and warm hospitality from hosts Sarah and Nick.

title: Southwest Tailored Tours (Wells)
subtitle: Why not get the most out of your visit to Bath and Somerset with a professional guide. Every tour is individually tailored to suite your interests, fit in with your schedule and specific requirements.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. Why not get the most out of your visit to Bath and Somerset with a professional guide. Every tour is individually tailored to suite your interests, fit in with your schedule and specific requirements. Visit the Cathedrals and churches of the South West to learn about saints and sinners, bishops, builders and bodies, as well as admiring the fabric of these beautiful buildings. Tour the great landscape gardens of the region and learn about their creators. See the influence of the Arts and Craft movement in gardens, houses, churches in the area. Walking tours are an excellent way to get to know a city. Every town has its stories and a guided tour will fill the streets with life.

title: Sweets Tea Rooms
subtitle: Country cafe tea room near Wedmore & Glastonbury & Street, Somerset
bodyContent: A wonderfully deceptive yard leads you to one of Somerset's best kept secrets. Generous traditional food from pies to the best cakes & cream teas with a very warm welcome. Proper Somerset fayre that you won't find for miles around. Using quality local suppliers this is a little hideaway not to be missed. We are a regular cycling stop cafe and approved by the British Horse Society. In the Winter alongside the cosy cafe there is a woodburner in the cabin area. Perfect for dogs, walkers and cyclists. This is also the home of the Peat & Science Museum, a lifetime family collection of working the levels including WW1 bomber parts! title: The Chalice Well
subtitle: Historical well with legends in Glastonbury, Somerset.Chalice Well at the foot of Glastonbury Tor.
bodyContent: Chalice Well is one of Britain's most ancient wells, nestling in the Vale of Avalon between the famous Glastonbury Tor and Chalice Hill. Surrounded by beautiful gardens and orchards it is a living sanctuary in which the visitor can experience the quiet healing of this sacred place. Over three acres of peace. For over two thousand years this has been a place where people have gathered to drink the waters and find solace, peace and inspiration. At present we work with the theme of 'Many Paths, One Source' to welcome all people of goodwill to the gardens throughout the year. We also mark 'the wheel of the year' at regular intervals with events of celebration, silence and meditation, and conversation. This includes an evening programme of music, poetry and performance throughout the summer months in our candlelit gardens.
tagline: Historical well with legends in Glastonbury, Somerset.Chalice Well at the foot of Glastonbury Tor.

title: The King Alfred
subtitle: At the King Alfred you will find wonderful freshly prepared pub food, a fine selection of wines and ales and a warm welcome from your hosts.
bodyContent: The King Alfred also offers a selection of well-appointed guest rooms so you can relax and stay with us as well. King Alfred was one of England’s most famous and respected Kings who had close links to this area of Somerset. We are delighted to have named the pub in his memory and we have lots of historic memorabilia on the walls for our customers to view. You can be guaranteed a warm welcome from Paul and the team and we hope you will come and visit us soon!
tagline: At the King Alfred you will find wonderful freshly prepared pub food

title: Shoscombe
subtitle: Shoscombe parish lies close to the south eastern boundary of Peasedown St John marked out by the bypass that encircles its southern edge.
bodyContent: Shoscombe parish lies close to the south eastern boundary of Peasedown St John marked out by the bypass that encircles its southern edge. Shoscombe Parish is made up of 8 small hamlets set in this peaceful, rural part of Somerset, and yet only 7 miles from the World Heritage city of Bath . The hamlets are Shoscombe village, Shoscombe Vale, Paglinch, Shoscombe Halt, Single Hill, Stony Littleton, White Hill and Double Hill The population is less than 500 The community values this rural landscape in which we live, and it is our determination to protect it for what it offers, by way of its diverse, and sometimes quite rare examples of wildlife, - for us, and for the visitors who come here.

title: Godminster Cheese
subtitle: Here at Godminster, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe. Our shop is open seven days a week and we have cheese available to sample every day.
bodyContent: Here at Godminster, Somerset, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe. Our shop is open seven days a week and we have cheese available to sample every day. There is free parking outside, so come and taste for yourself why Godminster has so many loyal friends around the world. We also offer fruit-infused vodka spirits, and over 18s are welcome to try those too. If you’re looking for a lovely foodie gift or a delicious souvenir of your trip to Somerset, come and take your pick from our range. Godminster’s Vintage Organic Cheddar is a deliciously soft and creamy cheddar matured for up to 12 months, at which point we select the best cheese to be made into one of our award-winning truckles. This sumptuous cheese is encased in the iconic burgundy wax to emphasise its pedigree and truly special status. The cheese is full bodied with a long, nutty, savoury bite. We also offer an Oak-Smoked Vintage Organic Cheddar, which sees the same top quality cheddar smoked over sustainably sourced oak chippings. The cheddar has a rich depth of flavour and the smokiness is evenly balanced with the acidity of the cheddar. Godminster Farm is set on the outskirts of the town of Bruton, Somerset, whose historic pedigree is recorded in the Doomsday Book of 1086. The Farm was registered as organic in 1999 and now boasts orchards with cider apples, peaches, nectarines and grapes, whilst keenly observing Soil Association and Government regulations relating to animal husbandry and the environmentally varied approach to business. The farm boasts a herb garden that enhances the natural remedies used to treat cows on the farm, 15 ponds supporting bio-diversity, and reeds which filter ground water. 25,000 broadleaf trees have been planted at the Farm since owner Richard Hollingbery took over, fostering diverse habitats and encouraging increases in the wildlife population. The cows at Godminster Farm, Somerset enjoy a simple and wholesome life. Richard sees them as the foundations for a truly holistic approach to his business, with the Farm’s milk turned into Godminster Vintage Organic Cheddar. Our mantra is "Nature repays those who treat her kindly," and that ethos runs across the business. Can’t make it to Bruton this time? Visit our website www.godminster.com let’s be friends on social media – we’re on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and Pinterest.
tagline: Here at Godminster, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe.

subtitle: Woodcombe Lodge, Minehead, Self catering Cottages and lodges in Somerset, on the edge of Exmoor National Park near Minehead seafront and shops, 1.5 miles. Wheelchair friendly, disabled access self catering cottages on Exmoor. Dog friendly cottages in Somerset/Devon border
bodyContent: Woodcombe Lodges & Cottages are to be found down a short country lane on the outskirts of the seaside town of Minehead . Set in 3 acre gardens on a quiet country lane only 1+ mile from Minehead & its sandy beach. All face south so the verandas enjoy full sun during the day. All accommodation is 4-star rated, the beaches, seafront, restaurants and shops of Minehead are just a 5 minute drive or 20 minute walk away. We are a dog friendly location and a stunning base for walking, country escapes and family holidays. We are also fully accessible with Holly, Laburnum and Cherry Lodges all wheelchair friendly spacious and well equipped, two with accessible shower wet rooms. We have a games room including table tennis, pool and table football which is also an ideal space for a family gathering or special party. Outside there is plenty of space for children to play with swings whilst parents can enjoy our putting green. Electricity included in the rate from May to the end of September only. ​​​

title: Walk Minehead to Porlock Weir
subtitle: The South West Coast Path is England’s longest waymarked footpath running for 630 miles from Minehead. This first section is 8.9 miles and takes you to Porlock Weir.
bodyContent: Leave the pavements of Minehead behind as you set off onto the first section of the 630-mile trail, through woodland, along steep cliff tops, farm tracks and up and down beautiful wooded combes with bracken, gorse and bubbling streams. Find out more information: https://www.southwestcoastpath.org.uk/walksdb/136/#

title: The Yarn Market Hotel
subtitle: Ideally located in the centre of the medieval village of Dunster. The hotel is two and half hours via the A39 from the M5 - but is ten minutes away from the West Somerset Railway England's longest heritage railway. With Minehead 20 minutes away there are all the major facilities you need.
bodyContent: The Yarn Market Hotel in Dunster is ideally located in the centre of Dunster, one of the most perfectly preserved medieval villages in England, and the gateway to Exmoor National Park. The magnificent Dunster Castle is at the end of the street and the West Somerset Railway runs close by. There are many themed breaks on offer throughout the year, and the area is perfect for those who enjoy outdoor activities or just a relaxing break. For walkers the hotel has excellent facilities including a boot and drying room, and maps are readily available combined with local knowledge to help you with your walks. Most of the bedrooms have either a view over the village or the surrounding countryside. Pets are most welcome at the hotel in the dog-friendly rooms. The restaurant opens daily for dinner, reservations are advisable.
tagline: Our Hotel is situated in the beautiful Village of Dunster, within the Exmoor National Park.

title: Dunster Circular
subtitle: This walk takes you from the shingle beach at Dunster up to the magnificent medieval village with its yarn market and topped off with a castle.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. This walk takes you from the shingle beach at Dunster up to the magnificent medieval village with its yarn market and topped off with a castle. Originally “Dunn’s Torre”, a craggy fortification overlooking the Bristol Channel, the settlement was given by William the Conqueror gave to the powerful de Mohun family to build a castle to protect the coast. In 1375 the feudal barony was purchased by the Luttrell family who owned the Castle until 1976 when it was gifted to the National Trust. Having explored the streets and shops, the walk takes you past the heritage railway station back to the beach along the riverside. Click here for more information
tagline: This walk takes you from the shingle beach at Dunster up to the magnificent medieval village.

title: Lasseter's
subtitle: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion. It serves locally sourced dishes created by a team of professional chefs.
bodyContent: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion. It serves locally sourced dishes created by a team of professional chefs. The restaurant focuses on bringing high-quality dining and great-value food to Weston, and is quickly gaining a reputation for excellent food, atmosphere and welcoming service. The restaurant boasts stunning views of Weston-super-Mare’s bay, as well as exciting menus that are based around fresh ingredients. It serves lunch and dinner from Wednesday to Saturday – including special set lunch menus and early-bird pre-theatre offers – and a carvery on Sundays from noon. Lasseter’s also serves an extensive range of cocktails, spirits and wines, with over 100 drinks to choose from. The wine list has been hand-selected by the restaurant manager, with a variety of different types and styles for all tastes. There is something for everyone at Lasseter’s. You can relax in the bar or on the terrace – with a snack if, you fancy – or enjoy a meal in our glorious restaurant overlooking the seafront.
tagline: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion.

title: Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Mendip Activity Centre is the ultimate outdoor adventure playground in Somerset. They’ve been delivering adventurous outdoor activities for nearly 40 years, growing from humble beginnings to the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West!
bodyContent: It’s Time for Adventure with Mendip Activity Centre! Nestled in 250 acres of ancient woodland in the Mendip Hills National Landscape, Mendip Activity Centre is the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West. Just 20 minutes from Weston-super-Mare and Cheddar and open year-round, Mendip have been delivering Adventure, Learning and Training for individuals, families, schools, and groups since 1987. Activities available include: · Air Rifle · Tobogganing · Archery · Skiing · Snowboarding · Frisbee Golf · Kayaking · Nerf & Gel Battles · Caving · Paddle Boarding · Rock Climbing · Axe Throwing · ArcheryActive · Abseiling · Canoeing Come for the day or stay longer. In summer, pitch your tent at the award-winning Mendip Basecamp (link to https://mendipbasecamp.com/), a family adventure campsite awarded second at the Visit England Awards 2025. Pitch where you like, check out when it suits, camp fires encouraged, dogs welcome and endless adventure is on offer! Adventure for Everyone Mendip is more than just activities. It’s a place to switch off from screens, reconnect with nature, and each other. Whether you're learning something new, developing an existing skill or simply having fun outside, you’ll leave with muddy boots and big smiles. We believe in adventure for everyone. Many of our activities are adaptable for additional needs, and our friendly team will work with you to make it happen Refuel at the Alpine Lounge Overlooking the Ski Slope, the Alpine Lounge café serves pizzas, paninis, coffee and cake with stunning views- perfect for après-adventure refreshments
