title: Dunster Castle
subtitle: Fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years, remodelled 100 years ago. Fine 17thC staircase and plaster ceilings. Terrace garden of rare shrubs.
bodyContent: During the winter months, the castle, watermill, and grounds are open at weekends and closed during the week. The Watermill Tearoom, Stables Shop and Parkland are open daily from 10am until 4pm. The car park is also open daily from 10am until 5pm. From 5 April 2025, the whole site is open daily. A fortress that became a family home for the Luttrells, who lived at Dunster for 600 years, the castle was extensively remodelled in the 1870s to create a Victorian country house. The castle boasts breath-taking views over Exmoor, Somerset, and the Bristol Channel as well as holding fine interior features such as a fine 17 th century carved staircase, ornate plaster ceilings, and rare leather wall hangings. Discover how Dunster Castle was used in its heyday and how the family hosted grand occasions from society balls to polo matches with the brilliant ‘Chapters’ guide as well as ‘Castle Explorers, available for children. You can then enjoy a leisurely stroll through beautiful terraced gardens with a collection of palms, sub-tropical plants, and the Dunster Lemon tree. Sited on the River Avill, Dunster Castle is also home to a working watermill that sits within the river gardens. Visit the mill to see the waterwheels in action and even purchase some of the freshly-milled flour. Refreshments are available in the newly-refurbished Watermill Tearoom and also outside the castle in the Tenants’ Hall Café. Accessibility Overview here. Facilities in addition to those listed below: Baby changing facilities Children's trails Courtesy vehicle Stair Climber Trampers available to book
tagline: Dramatically sited on a wooded hill and the fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years.

title: Watchet Market House Museum
subtitle: Watchet Market House Museum houses a fine collection of local artefacts, fossils and marine paintings. The town’s rich maritime history features in many of the exhibits. With visitor numbers averaging 30,000 per season, this small Museum is a ‘not to miss’ attraction.
bodyContent: Located next to the harbour, where the Esplanade meets Market Street, Watchet Market House Museum occupies the ground floor of the town’s former Market House. We celebrated our 40th birthday in 2019. A special exhibition celebrates West Somerset’s Victorian industrial heritage when the West Somerset Mineral Railway carried iron ore from the Brendon Hills to Watchet for shipment to the steel making furnaces of South Wales. The Jurassic coast of West Somerset is highlighted with a splendid external window display describing it’s formation, with impressive fossils inside including an Ichthyosaur and a huge ammonite. A ‘Watchet Chronology’, is on display with a pictorial timeline by local artists telling the story of the town’s rich and varied past. These colourful displays will be of great interest to both young and old, as will the many photographs which will bring back many memories. Watchet’s rich maritime history is an important part of the museum and features in many of the exhibits on show with the ‘Yankee Jack’ statue and the ‘Ancient Mariner’ taking pride of place on the Esplanade.
tagline: Watchet Market House Museum houses a fine collection of local artefacts

title: Bath & West Showground
subtitle: Nestled in the heart of the West Country, the Bath & West Showground is the perfect place to entertain the whole family. Thirty Minutes from the city of Wells and 10 minutes from the main line train from London to Castle Carey. You are also 45 minutes from Frome and another train station and further strong amenities. The Show Ground doesn't have a hotel, however ample space for camping and parking of large amounts of resource applications.
bodyContent: Although best known for the annual Royal Bath & West Show, one of the largest multi-day agricultural shows in the country, the Bath & West Showground plays host to a wide range of public events, exhibitions, conferences together with world class sports, recording artists and record-breaking music festivals throughout the year. From crafting to camping, markets to music festivals or collectors’ fairs to comedy nights, there really is an experience to entertain everyone at the Bath & West Showground. The Showground has ample car parking, as well as an onsite bar & restaurant, allowing you to refuel on delicious coffee & cake, or enjoy a tasty locally sourced lunch, before you continue with the rest of your day. Visit our website to see What’s On at the Bath & West Showground. Are you already a regular visitor to the Showground? Or you live locally? Why not become a Member at the Bath & West. You’ll receive FREE entry to the Royal Bath & West Show, along with discount to other events held on the Bath & West Showground. Click HERE for more information. Please note: Bar & Restaurant opening times vary for each event. Please check before attending
tagline: The Bath & West Show Ground is the perfect place to entertain the whole family.

title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
subtitle: An outdoor production of A Midsummer Night’s Dream brings Shakespeare’s magical comedy to life with a playful and inventive twist. Full of humour and imagination, it offers a joyful theatre experience for all ages.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } This outdoor production of A Midsummer Night’s Dream invites audiences into an imaginative and light-hearted take on Shakespeare’s much-loved comedy. Presented by Four Forty Theatre, the show follows runaway lovers, magical creatures and a group of determined actors who find themselves in over their heads. With quick character changes, playful invention and a sense of silliness throughout, the performance reimagines the classic story in a lively and accessible way. Blending humour with creativity, it brings a fresh and engaging approach to one of Shakespeare’s most well-known plays. Designed to appeal to both long-time fans and those new to Shakespeare, the production is filled with warmth, laughter and unexpected moments. title: Bookshop by the Blackdowns
subtitle: Bookshop by the Blackdowns is an independent, family-run bookshop in the centre of Wellington.
bodyContent: Nestled at the foot of the beautiful Blackdown Hills on the borders of Somerset and Devon, we are easy to find, just off Junction 26 of the M5 motorway. We aim to serve our local community and celebrate the wonderful county of Somerset. We are surrounded by an eclectic mix of other small shops and, so, are a perfect stopping off point if you are travelling to the West Country. ​ We stock a carefully curated range of adult and children’s fiction and non-fiction, with an emphasis on the natural world, as well as unusual, beautiful cards and gifts often with a book theme.

title: Rhys James: Chop Logic
subtitle: Comedian Rhys James brings his latest stand-up show, Chop Logic, to Taunton Brewhouse. Known for his sharp observations and intelligent comedy, James delivers an evening of big ideas, overthinking and fast-paced humour.
bodyContent: Rhys has made a discovery that could fix everything. It’s been staring him in the face the whole time, in a mirror held behind his head. If he can ignore his own problems for long enough, he might just be able to solve yours. A fast, forensic show of big ideas and gag-dense overthinking from one of the nation’s sharpest stand-ups. Star of TLC’s Mock The Week and BBC Radio 4’s Rhysearch, also seen furrowing his brow on QI, Live At The Apollo and his viral U&Dave lecture, ‘I Stalk Strangers Online’. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: A sharp and fast-paced stand-up show from comedian Rhys James.

title: Art with Abandon: Messy Play for Grown Ups
subtitle: Rediscover the joy of play and creativity in this relaxed, adults-only workshop led by Art Psychotherapist Stacey Kiely. Designed to help participants let go of perfectionism, the session provides a supportive space to experiment, create and enjoy the process without judgement.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Adults are invited to rediscover the joy of play at Art with Abandon: Messy Play for Grown Ups , a creative wellbeing workshop led by experienced Art Psychotherapist Stacey Kiely. This unique session offers a rare opportunity to explore creativity in a supportive, judgement-free environment. No artistic ability is required, just an hour to play, unwind and reconnect with yourself through colour, creativity and freedom. Part of the Museum of Somerset's summer season of PLAY, the workshop encourages participants to switch off their inner critic, get messy and enjoy the process of creating. Tickets Available on their Website
tagline: A creative wellbeing workshop encouraging adults to play, create and let go of perfectionism.

bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Sheppy's Christmas Craft Fair returns for a festive weekend at Sheppy's House of Cider. Taking place across the House of Cider site, the event will feature a wide range of craft stalls showcasing handmade gifts, crafts and seasonal products from local makers and artisans. Visitors can browse the stalls while enjoying food and drink from the House of Cider Café and additional outdoor refreshment vendors. subtitle: Step back into the golden age of disco and funk with an evening dedicated to the unforgettable sounds of the 1970s and early 1980s. title: Cosy Cuddle Farm
subtitle: A private animal experience in the Somerset countryside where every booking is exclusively yours, giving you and your guests uninterrupted time with our friendly animals in a peaceful, relaxed setting.
bodyContent: Welcome to Cosy Cuddle Farm We are a private animal experience in the Somerset countryside. Every booking is exclusively yours, giving you and your guests uninterrupted time with our friendly animals in a peaceful, relaxed setting just off the M5. There are no crowds, no queues and no rushing from one activity to the next. Bring the family together, celebrate a birthday, host a hen party or reward your team with a unique corporate experience. Enjoy a peaceful, distraction-free experience in the beautiful Somerset countryside to relax, connect and unwind. We can also come to you for care home visits. With miniature pigs, rabbits, guinea pigs, ducklings and kid goats available for your events - weddings or birthday parties included. Our Story After spending 25 years as a primary school teacher, I wanted to create a haven where people could slow down, connect with animals, and enjoy time together, away from the pressures of everyday life. Watching children -and adults- relax and smile around animals inspired me to create Cosy Cuddle Farm. My hope is that every visitor leaves happier, calmer and with memories they will treasure. Finish your visit with a treat Why not make your visit even more special by adding one of our delicious Cream Teas? Children can have an ice cream if they prefer. We can't wait to welcome you Whether it's your first visit or you're returning to see your favourite furry faces, you'll always receive a warm welcome at Cosy Cuddle Farm. Come and experience the joy, relaxation, and unforgettable memories that only spending time with animals can bring.

subtitle: Great motorway links M5 junction 20 & 21 Bristol International Airport only 12 minutes away Bristol City Centre only 25 minutes away. With local access to Cheddar Gorge and Mendip AONB only 45 minutes away.
bodyContent: Welcome to DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House, the South West’s finest four-star boutique hotel and spa. An enchanting venue set within rolling English countryside, Cadbury House is the ideal backdrop for your special occasion whether a wedding, private party, business event, spa break or dining experience. With truly breath-taking views across North Somerset and the Bristol Channel, Cadbury House effortlessly combines old and new, with the traditional country house and the elegant boutique-style hotel. There is also an onsite Marco Pierre White Steakhouse Bar & Grill, an award-winning health club and a renowned spa. The hotel offers 132 luxury bedrooms including suites, on-site parking and excellent transport access meaning guests can enjoy the facilities for both business and pleasure. Please note from May 1 st , 2022 overnight parking will be chargeable at £5.00 per vehicle. Corporate customers are also well catered for with 12 meeting rooms, multiple breakout areas, and a dedicated conference team on hand. Whether you are hosting a small business meeting to a multi-day conference, DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House does not disappoint as a destination location for business needs.
tagline: The South West’s finest four-star boutique hotel and spa.

title: The Playhouse in Weston super Mare
subtitle: The Playhouse Theatre is available for hire for both community and professional shows and as a venue for conferences, meetings and corporate events. In addition to the main auditorium the theatres facilities include a licensed bar, meeting and rehearsal spaces and full disabled access.
bodyContent: Located in the centre of Weston-Super-Mare the Playhouse is a friendly and welcoming 664-seat theatre which offers a lively and diverse programme of events to meet the entertainment, creative and educational requirements of its local and surrounding community. The Playhouse’s high quality programme of professional and community events includes around 300 performances per year including music, drama, comedy, dance, musicals, film, children’s shows, pantomime and more recently West End Productions. The Playhouse Theatre is available for hire for both community and professional shows and as a venue for conferences, meetings and corporate events. In addition to the main auditorium the theatres facilities include a licensed bar, meeting and rehearsal spaces and full disabled access. Our dedicated and professional staff are used to working with all visiting companies and hirers to ensure a successful event while our welcoming and caring front of house team ensure patrons an enjoyable entertainment experience. The Playhouse Theatre is managed by Parkwood Theatres working in partnership with North Somerset Council.

title: Ensemble
subtitle: This is a beautiful family owned and run business.
bodyContent: Ensemble is a family owned and run restaurant in the heart of Wells with an enviable view of the Cathedral from our tables. We have been in Sadler Street for over five years and the extended family has a long history of hospitality in the area going back to the 1960s. We serve an eclectic range of food, wines and beers with the emphasis being on quality, local suppliers, whom we support as much as possible.

title: Hide on the Hill
subtitle: We currently offer our two beautiful bed & breakfast rooms for you to enjoy and the chance to relax away from the bustle - located on the margins of the Avalon marshes near Glastonbury in Somerset.
bodyContent: The Orchard room to the north provides a vista to the Mendip Hills. It has a luxurious king size Hypnos hideaway bed with luxury cotton sheets. (17m 2 ) The Garden room faces south with views down to the levels and is decorated to enhance the luminosity of the ​Somerset sky into the room. It is a large twin room that can accommodate a child up to 5 years for additional charges. (23m 2 ) Facilities Both rooms are brand new and have large en-suite bathrooms with big showers, towels and soaps. Each room has free internet access and we have decides not to provide televisions as many guests said they ​already had good 4G signals on their network preferring to use their own devices. Facilities include a tray to make tea and coffee replenished each day, a hairdryer is available, toiletries in the en-suite to be left for the next guests . Your Stay CHECK-IN is from 4pm on the day of arrival. It really helps if you give us an approximate time to make your welcome great. You will be greeted in the conservatory with a welcoming drink and chat about how to chill after your drive. Please note that any balance on the stay must be settled after you have settled in. BREAKFAST is served between 8am and 9.30am in the dining room, but should you require an early breakfast please let us know. Later breakfasts will be in the form of a convenient breakfast in a bag (no beans obviously!). You can relax in the dining room with the fantastic views up until 12am for the long stay guests. Our continental and full English breakfast are standard and you will be able to upgrade, for an additional charge, to a selection of special breakfasts like kedgeree, smoked salmon, chilly rice , pancakes and Goan curry on fried coconut bread, all of which have to be booked in advance. ​We strive to be organic as possible with named local produce and our own garden produce. Our excellent bread is from a local artisan baker, meat from a small Gloucester Old Spot pig farm, and jams and organic trout from a aquaponics. Depending upon the weather you can have a continental breakfast tray outside on the terrace or in one of the garden retreats. CHECK-OUT is by 11am and some guests are requested to settle any additional charges along with the keys after breakfast. We would appreciate your feedback and suggestions. PARKING is close to the house and free Fully complaint fire and smoke detectors are present for your additional safety which means you can only smoke in the designated area outside the building. ENERGY USE Hide on The Hill uses sustainable energy including a pellet boiler, Powerdiverter, loads of insulation and solar panels which help to reduce the impact of the travellers carbon footprint. Laundry is washed during daylight hours to utilise the suns energy and for longer staying guests sheets are changed after 3 days. Towels are removed and replaced if left in the basket but otherwise left for further use. Heating is on every morning and evening and is controlled by thermostats. Additional hypo allergenic bed linen can be provided if requested. THE GARDEN has many quiet spots for lazing in the sun on deckchairs or siting by the caravan to read and make yourself a cup of tea. There is a living willow spiral and firepit with a basket of free wood to use in the early evening. AMBIENCE at our hilltop hide will become obvious on your first walk around the gardens and we believe that you'll value the peace and quiet so we decided to not have televisions in the rooms. We would request that music is moderated by 10pm please . Many guests use their tablets for streaming which is fine but please turn down the volume thereafter. PETS are, at present,not able to be part of your stay but those with registered guide dogs will be considered if we know from you how to best manage the arrangement. WALKERS AND CYCLISTS are most welcome with a range of facilities to help including a drying room, outside boot area to change walking gear, a small jet wash for muddy bikes, a bike wall to repair bikes and a lockup for your bike

title: White Stuff Wells
subtitle: Hello, make yourself at home! We create places where people feel welcome whether they are in our shops, online or flicking through one of our books. Our shops are more than homely hangouts. We love our customers to pop in for a cuppa and bring their pets for a bowl of water and a treat. In fact kids, friends, everyone is welcome!
bodyContent: We want to make a meaningful difference by connecting people, enhancing communities and creating our beautiful products in a way that benefits those around us. To achieve this, we focus on four key areas: our community, our people, our supply chain and our environment. By actively engaging our customers, teams, suppliers and communities we make sure that we are all creating responsibly. e're a sociable, talented and energetic bunch here at White Stuff, proud to be part of such a great business, and passionate about our customers. We work hard to put people at the heart of our business, building and sustaining a sense of community and shared success, where everyone feels like they're part of something special. Each day we learn and grow together in a place that truly values creativity, sociability, responsibility and determination. Whether we're talking to our customers face-to-face, or engaging via email, online content or social media campaigns, our conversations connect on a human level, inspiring our customers with exciting visuals, social experiences or relevant content. Unlike a 'theme' our seasonal conversations tell a story and actively encourage our customers to take part and join in to enrich and personalise the story. Our conversations show our customers that we share the same interests and values and help us to maintain a meaningful relationship. Fused with our distinctive, funny and sometimes just unconventional personality our conversations engage and inspire our customers wherever they may be.

title: Wells Cathedral High Parts Tours
subtitle: Climb the spiral staircase to walk in the footsteps of Wells Cathedral masons with new behind-the-scenes tours of Wells Cathedral’s High Parts; one of the most memorable things to do in Wells!
bodyContent: Climb the spiral staircase to walk in the footsteps of Wells Cathedral masons with new behind-the-scenes tours of Wells Cathedral’s High Parts; one of the most memorable things to do in Wells ! - Discover hidden spaces, galleries and chambers, including behind the Wells clock - See one of only two surviving tracing floors in the country where masons drew templates on the floor - Walk along the singing gallery and learn about trumpet holes! - Explore the south transept roof space - And marvel at the nave from a very different perspective! (Note that the tour route does not take in the top of the tower). High Parts Tours take place regularly throughout the week; bookings can be made via the Cathedral's website up to 24 hours prior to the tour taking place. Want to make a last minute booking? Call us on 01749 672773 or ask at the Welcome desk on the day of your visit. The tour length is 1.5 hours. Tour and tea packages are also available. Who can book: The maximum number in any upper levels tour is 12 and no children under the age of 10 years are permitted on the tour. Children between the ages of 10 and 16 years must be accompanied by one adult for every two children, unless they are part of an organised youth group when at least two adults must be in attendance. Any visitors with a fear of heights or confined spaces and/in poor health should consider carefully their suitability for the tour. There are up to 250 steps, uneven floors, low ceilings and the narrowest point is just 60cm (2ft.) wide. The tour route does not include access to the top of the tower. Other Terms and Conditions of Booking do apply (see website for details). Where to meet your Guide: At the Donation Desk in the entrance of the Cathedral 15 minutes before your Tour begins. You will unfortunately not be able to join the Tour if you miss the start time. If you purchase a Tour and tea package, your Guide will indicate where to take your refreshments at the end of the Tour. www.wellscathedral.org.uk/visit/tours
tagline: Climb the spiral staircase to walk in the footsteps of Wells Cathedral masons.

title: Ring O'Bells
subtitle: Free house local pub in Somerset between Street & Glastonbury.
bodyContent: The Ring O’Bells is an 18th Century “free house” pub in the Somerset village of Ashcott near Street and Glastonbury, which for the last 29 years has been run by a family partnership. A unique pub with unique food, all prepared by us in our own kitchens. Local meat from a local butcher. Somerset produce at its best. Daily Specials blackboard including freshly made desserts. Home-made fudge with your coffee to finish! We are a genuine Free House and it is our policy to feature beers from small independent breweries, many from the West Country but occasionally also more “exotic” visitors! The range of beers varies constantly but our list of forthcoming beers features usually at least one beer from one of the local micro breweries. CAMRA Good Beer Guide 2016 CAMRA Good Pub Food Guide 2016, (star-rated, and entered in this guide for the nineteenth consecutive year). AA Pubs and Inns Guide 2016 The Good Pub Guide 2016
tagline: Free house local pub in Somerset between Street & Glastonbury.

title: Honeysuckle Farm Cottages
subtitle: 3 Luxury Sustainable Cottages for your holiday break in Glastonbury
bodyContent: Get away from it all in the fascinating town of Glastonbury. Situated on the ‘light side’ of Glastonbury Tor, Honeysuckle Farm Cottages forms a wonderful sun-trap, perfectly balancing the peace and tranquility of a rural get away, with the vibrancy of Glastonbury’s unique town centre. We have 3 luxury, self-sustainable, self-catering cottages which sleep between 4 and 8 people each. Our ethos is to provide a really enjoyable, environmentally responsible and practical self-catering holiday destination. Once here, you won’t need your vehicle – there’s so much to see and do all within walking or cycling distance – we even provide the bicycles! Steeped in history, with excellent facilities, friendly people, beautiful surroundings and some amazing local attractions you’re sure to have a fantastically inspiring time.

title: Glastonbury Abbey
subtitle: Glastonbury Abbey, Glastonbury, Somerset is connected with legend to a degree that is unparalleled by any other abbey in England. Since Medieval times it has held legendary status as the earliest Christian foundation in Britain linked to Joseph of Arimathea and the burial place of King Arthur.
bodyContent: Glastonbury Abbey, Glastonbury, Somerset is an internationally renowned site attracting visitors from around the world for its history, heritage, myths and legends as well as for its spiritual enrichment and there has been a church on the site for at least 1500 years with evidence of even earlier occupation. Glastonbury was the richest monastery in England at the end of the Saxon period and was second only to Westminster at the close of the middle ages. Its Abbot lived in considerable splendour and wielded tremendous power with the main surviving example of this power and wealth to be found in the Abbot’s Kitchen, one of only three surviving medieval examples in the world. It’s history is intertwined with English traditions; one of its Abbots – St Dunstan, wrote the Coronation words last used for the coronation of our present Queen Elizabeth II and William Blake’s popular “Jerusalem” is said to be written about the story that a young Jesus, accompanied by Joseph of Arimathea, visited Glastonbury . The Holy Thorn which grows at Glastonbury Abbey has become part of the legend of Joseph of Arimathea. According to the story when Joseph arrived in Britain he landed on the island of Avalon and climbed up Wearyall Hill, exhausted he thrust his staff into the ground and rested. By morning his staff had taken root and it grew into the miraculous thorn tree which flowers every Easter and Christmas. In 1191 the monks told the world they had found the bodies of King Arthur and his Queen found on the south side of the Lady Chapel. On 19th April 1278 their remains were removed in the presence of King Edward 1 and Queen Eleanor to a black marble tomb within the abbey itself. The tomb survived until the dissolution of the abbey in 1539. In 1536, during the 27 th year of the reign of Henry VIII, there were over 800 monasteries, nunneries and friaries in Britain. By 1541 there were none and the last abbot of Glastonbury , Richard Whiting was hung, drawn and quartered on Glastonbury Tor ; a brutal end for a pious man. Today it is a tranquil setting in which visitors can discover the stories behind Glastonbury Abbey with tours from costumed Living History presenters in the grounds; these tours are free but should be booked in advance for groups. A packed events calendar brings theatre, concerts, exhibitions and workshops to the abbey grounds every year and the abbey’s spectacular Night at the Abbey which last year won a national award. School and university groups can enjoy tailor-made itineraries and there are specific activities for families too. An accredited museum showcases items from the abbey’s history and gives more information about the chronology of events, archaeological finds and gives an insight into monastic life. There are 36 acres of parkland to explore with a dedicated wildlife area as well as new plans to recreate a Medieval Kitchen Garden. Groups are welcomed with a pre-booked meet and greet service available too and a special rate; driver and tour guide go free. A full access statement is on the abbey’s website – www.glastonburyabbey.com – along with maps in 14 different languages. Find us on Facebook /GlastonburyAbbeySomerset, follow us on Twitter @Glastonburyabbe or give us a call on 01458 832267. We look forward to meeting you
tagline: Glastonbury Abbey is connected with legend to a degree that is unparalleled by any other abbey

bodyContent: Grape& Grain brasserie is a small family run restaurant serving seasonal food to suit everyone’s taste. By day we serve a selection of delicious lunches from baguettes and burgers to Aqua pazza and cassoulet. As the night draws in the lamps and candles bring a romantic and cosy feel giving the perfect setting for an evening of eclectic Wine, Beer and delicious food. title: Dunkerton and Tunley
subtitle: Situated on the northern slope of the valley of the Cam Brook, Dunkerton has been in existence for a thousand years or more.
bodyContent: Situated on the northern slope of the valley of the Cam Brook, Dunkerton has been in existence for a thousand years or more. It is mentioned in Domesday Book; its name derives from the Anglo-Saxon words Dun/Carn/Ton, signifying “the town of the cairn on the hill”, and this is a reference to a stone structure which long ago stood on Duncorne Hill about a mile towards the city of Bath. Nowadays the Parish of Dunkerton and Tunley has a population of a little over 400, living in about 220 households; these are mainly situated in the two principal settlements of Tunley and the village of Dunkerton itself, although there are other groups of houses in such locations as Withyditch and along the old Roman Fosse Way. It was once a thriving industrial community – there were several coalmines, and both the Somersetshire Coal Canal and the southern branch of the Bristol and North Somerset Railway passed through the parish. However, local industry withered away with the closure of the pits and the railway in the mid-twentieth century, and there is now little local employment, although the farming tradition continues, with several farms based in the parish. Neither Dunkerton nor Tunley has much of a village “core”. Dunkerton has a pleasant little church, dating from the 13th century, but no school, shop or public house, while Tunley has one excellent pub. There are three public halls, Dunkerton Parish Hall, Tunley Recreation Centre and the old Schoolroom at Withyditch. In addition, Dunkerton has a fine cricket ground and Tunley a well-patronised football pitch. The parish has the benefit of being set in very attractive and largely unspoiled countryside, as well as being on the Limestone Link public footpath and having some interesting archaeological, scientific and literary associations.

title: Middlewick Holiday Cottages
subtitle: Self catering cottages in Glastonbury. Perfect short break in Somerset with indoor pool.
bodyContent: A secluded holiday resort just minutes from Glastonbury town centre, with stunning views of Glastonbury Tor and the Mendip Hills. Set on 16 peaceful acres, The Middlewick offers self-catering accommodation in 10 cottages converted from original 17th-century farm buildings, 3 log cabins and 3 glamping pods. Our properties range from 1 to 5 bedrooms, offering plenty of choice for couples, families, friends and groups looking for country getaway. Many are dog friendly. We have a Café , Farm Shop and Spa on site – all of which are open to day visitors as well as guests staying with us. Our site, including our indoor heated pool and steam room, is powered by renewable energy, and Spa treatments take place in our cosy Shepherd’s Huts. Surrounded by apple orchards, this is a real escape to the Somerset countryside – with plenty of space to roam in the beauty of nature. Visitors can walk to Glastonbury Tor easily in under 30 minutes. There’s so much to explore nearby, with Glastonbury Tor, Chalice Well and Gardens, Glastonbury Abbey and Clark’s Village on our doorstep. Glastonbury is a unique market town bustling with unusual shops and alternative events. The Avalon Marshes Nature Reserve, Cathedral City of Wells and Cheddar Gorge are within easy driving distance from The Middlewick. Somerset is known for its food, music and outstanding natural beauty – and this is the ideal base from which to explore the best of the county.

title: Mendip Basecamp
subtitle: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure campsite in the Mendip Hills...
bodyContent: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure camp in the Mendip Hills National Landscape - just minutes from the M5 and Weston-super-Mare. Surrounded by ancient woodland you can pitch where you like, park right by your tent and enjoy evenings around the campfire. Well-behaved dogs are welcome! With no check-out time, you can leave whenever you are ready. Mendip Basecamp is camping how it should be: rural, laid-back and relaxed but with essential luxuries. Usually reserved for schools and private groups, in 2020, Mendip opened Basecamp up to families for the very first time- and hasn’t looked back since. Public bookings are available throughout the summer holidays and summer weekends. Bring your own tent or campervan, book bell tents, glamphouses or stay in Mendip Lodge (with free breakfast). Facilities include hot showers, clean flushing toilets, a camp shop, a country Lodge with a cider garden (and live music), an onsite activity centre, USB charging and WIFI. Free activities throughout the summer include live music, orienteering, circus skills, treasure hunts, free climbing tower and nature craft. The campsite is less than a 5-minute woodland walk from Mendip Activity Centre, home to over 20 different adventurous, outdoor activities including rock climbing, kayaking, archery, frisbee golf and air rifle. New for 2026, Mendip Basecamp is launching Mendip Mini Fests - six family-friendly festivals running throughout the summer holiday weekends. Great entertainment, headline bands, local talent competition, and more! Included at no extra cost, exclusively for campsite guests.
tagline: Mendip Basecamp was delighted to be awarded the Gold campsite at the 2023-2024

title: ⭐Shepton Mallet Prison
subtitle: Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’; Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom...
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’, Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom. Shepton Mallet Prison is a recently decommissioned (2013) Georgian jail where visitors can walk in the footsteps of our social history and hear officers shine a light on what life was like for both the incarcerated and those who guarded them through the ages. Before its closure, it was a category C lifer prison holding 189 prisoners. Opened in 1646, it was expanded in 1790, with further building work undertaken in the 1820s and 1830s, including the installation of a treadwheel for those sentenced to hard labour. In 1930, the inmate numbers fell and the prison was closed. During the Second World War, the prison was reopened and used as a military prison. It was initially used by the British Army and later by American forces, who constructed a new execution block for condemned prisoners. It was also used for the storage of important historical documents, including the Domesday Book. It returned to civilian use in 1966. Shepton Mallet prison is also known for its tales of paranormal activity. One of the most popular stories is that of the White Lady. She is frequently seen or sensed in various locations, especially A Wing. Staff and prisoners would often complain of an icy wind moving through the wing, the sweet smell of perfume and shadowy figures. She supposedly dates from the late 1700s, when she spent some time in the prison. During a lovers' tiff which escalated, she murdered her betrothed. Once found guilty and sentenced to death, she was housed in Shepton Mallet Prison. On the evening before her execution, she asked for her wedding dress to be brought to the prison, which they allowed. She wore it to bed that night, but in the morning the officers found that she had died during the night. No cause of death was ever found, so we are left to presume that she died of a broken heart. Perhaps this is why she still haunts the prison? In the early 1950s, the Kray Twins were also held here after deserting the British Army. Today, the prison is open as a tourist attraction offering Guided Tours, Self-Guided Tours, Escape Rooms, Night Behind Bars and Ghost Hunting Behind Bars. This is an immersive experience without gizmos or gimmicks – the jail is very much as it was when the last prisoners left in 2013. In 2025, Shepton Mallet Prison received the prestigious Trip Advisor Travellers’ Choice, for the 7th time running, placing it among the top 10% of attractions worldwide.

title: Watchet Boat Museum
subtitle: Discover the fascinating history of the flatner the origins of which date back to before the Viking invasion. The story is celebrated through photographs, full size displays and local fishing paraphernalia. There is a collection of scale models on the upper deck, and activities for children to enjoy.
bodyContent: We are located opposite the West Somerset Railway station, adjacent to the Harbour Road car park, and accessed through Watchet Visitor Centre. The building was designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel and built in 1862 as a goods shed for the terminus of the Bristol and Exeter Railway. Its lofty roof creates an ideal space for displaying fully rigged boats. Interactive exhibits for children (and parents and grandparents!)) include dress-up and play in the play boat, a working ships wheel with engine room telegraph, and children’s trails and activity sheets. Learn how to catch salmon and fish for eels, see rope being made, learn how to tie knots and make an eye splice, and us old boys will teach Grandad to splice a mainbrace. Learn the lingo: What is a putcher? A grapple? How can you ride a mudhorse, and what is rayballing? The museum is run by volunteers from the Friends of the Flatner Association. It is our aim for you to have a good day and leave with new knowledge and experiences.
tagline: Discover the fascinating history of the flatner

title: The Yarn Market Hotel
subtitle: Ideally located in the centre of the medieval village of Dunster. The hotel is two and half hours via the A39 from the M5 - but is ten minutes away from the West Somerset Railway England's longest heritage railway. With Minehead 20 minutes away there are all the major facilities you need.
bodyContent: The Yarn Market Hotel in Dunster is ideally located in the centre of Dunster, one of the most perfectly preserved medieval villages in England, and the gateway to Exmoor National Park. The magnificent Dunster Castle is at the end of the street and the West Somerset Railway runs close by. There are many themed breaks on offer throughout the year, and the area is perfect for those who enjoy outdoor activities or just a relaxing break. For walkers the hotel has excellent facilities including a boot and drying room, and maps are readily available combined with local knowledge to help you with your walks. Most of the bedrooms have either a view over the village or the surrounding countryside. Pets are most welcome at the hotel in the dog-friendly rooms. The restaurant opens daily for dinner, reservations are advisable.
tagline: Our Hotel is situated in the beautiful Village of Dunster, within the Exmoor National Park.

title: Chandni Chowk
subtitle: Chandni Chowk specialises in very high quality textiles, hand made in India by wonderfully skilled crafts people to a very high quality.
bodyContent: Chandni Chowk specialises in very high quality textiles, hand made in India by wonderfully skilled crafts people to a very high quality. We are an ethical company producing fashion, accessories and home furnishings collections. We follow no set seasons, our collections simply grow and change as and when inspiration dictates! To compliment both of these departments we have a range of Hand Woven Kilim Rugs, Hand Made Jewellery and Greetings Cards. Established by Rosalind Price and Paul Garrod in 1978 Chandni Chowk acquired its name from an early customer who said we reminded her of the ancient ‘Chandni Chowk’ market in Delhi. The name is Hindi and translates approximately as “shiny/silver/bright/moon - place/area”. At the time, the company was based on a table in the famous Barnstaple Pannier Market; it later progressed into the upstairs of the wonderful Heavens Above restaurant and then to the site of the first permanent Chandni Chowk store in Barnstaple. Today the company is still based firmly in the south west with our HQ housing the design facility, administration and central warehouse in deepest beautiful Devon. We now have five branches and a well-established on-line shopping website.

We also host various live events including theme nights, live bands, and open mic nights. Furthermore, we also offer overnight accommodation with our Bed & Breakfast services and local cottage rentals. So for more details about our menus, events, or overnight stays, feel free to get in touch. We look forward to hearing from you.

bodyContent: Welcome to our Creative Café & Shop, a unique space where imagination meets relaxation! Our space is for everyone – adults young and old, as well as children! Whether you’re a lifelong LEGO® fan or just discovering the joy of building, you can unwind in our cosy and inviting atmosphere while creating amazing sets. If we’re not fully booked with builders, you’re also welcome to drop in for a coffee and some locally made cake, snacks and sausage rolls.​ Choose from our extensive LEGO® set selection and build as much as you like within your chosen time. Enjoy tasty drinks and snacks as you let your imagination run wild, designing and constructing together. It’s the perfect way to relax, create, and make unforgettable memories.​ "It's not just a kids' thing – it's for all ages!" ​​​

title: The Beambridge Inn at Wellington
subtitle: The Beambridge Inn is a place of warmth, wholesome food, generous hospitality and a room to stay for your onward journey if needed.
bodyContent: We have eight tastefully appointed en-suite bedrooms which are furbished to a high standard and offer comfort and relaxation, whether you visit for business or leisure. Whatever the reason for your visit, we are easy to find, off the A38, 3 miles from both J26 & J27 of the M5. Free WIFI available across the inn and rooms are supplied with tea and coffee making facilities and large flat screen TV’s. Set in the parish of Sampford Arundel, 1.5 miles south of Wellington town there has been a public house at the Beambridge since 1832. Originally a traditional coaching inn, the business and building has grown extensively over the last 200 years, masking its origins and age. The area, “Beambridge” holds a claim to fame in railway history as a place for the shortest serving railway station which was built a few yards from the pub and opened on the 1st May 1843 for exactly one year, whilst the Whiteball tunnel was built a mile or so up the line when the South West line was extended to Exeter.

title: Wifi Wars
subtitle: From classic TV game shows and word puzzles to retro video games and first person shooters, Wifi Wars has something for everyone. bodyContent: From classic TV game shows to zen-like word puzzles, from retro video games to modern first person shooters, WiFi Wars has something for everyone in its truly original whistlestop tour of all the ways you can have fun, in public. The entire audience competes, both as teams and as individuals, on games, quizzes and more that are magically beamed into their smartphones and tablets using WiFi Wars ’ Guinness World Record-Breaking tech, developed in residency at London’s prestigious Royal Institution. Hosted by comedian Steve McNeil (team captain on the hit TV show “Dara O’Briain’s Go 8 Bit”), WiFi Wars is the Award-Winning must-see show that’s like nothing you’ve seen before. As teams and players thrive and fail, each show’s unique narrative emerges hilariously in real time, with freshly-minted heroes becoming local legends in every place they visit. title: Blues Music with The Travelling Riverside Blues Show
subtitle: Take a musical journey through the Mississippi Delta with The Travelling Riverside Blues Show, featuring acclaimed guitarist Remi Harris and vocalist Roger Keenan. Combining live blues music with storytelling, the performance celebrates the roots and traditions of the blues.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Join two exceptional musicians for an evening exploring the sounds, stories and history of the Mississippi Delta. The Travelling Riverside Blues Show brings together traditional acoustic guitar and soulful vocals to celebrate the musicians who laid the foundations of modern blues music. The performance features renowned jazz and blues guitarist Remi Harris, whose influences include Django Reinhardt, Peter Green, Wes Montgomery and Robert Johnson. His career has taken him from local busking performances to appearances at Buckingham Palace, the Montreal Jazz Festival and the BBC Proms at the Royal Albert Hall. Joining him is Roger Keenan, a seasoned vocalist whose lifelong passion for blues music spans both the American Delta tradition and the British Blues Boom of the 1960s and beyond. Together, they combine music and storytelling to bring the people, places and emotions behind the blues vividly to life. Tickets Available Online
tagline: A live blues concert celebrating the music and stories of the Mississippi Delta.

The line-up includes: Bob Gallie – Originally from South Wales, Bob has enjoyed a varied musical career that included performing as vocalist with Brian Tatler's band Radio Moscow. After time away from music, he returned to his roots as a singer-songwriter and now performs regularly at festivals and venues across the region. Lee Rahn – A South West singer-songwriter and graduate of London's ICMP Music College, Lee is known for his folk influences, distinctive vocals and thoughtful songwriting. Darren Hodge – An acclaimed guitarist recognised for both technical ability and musical expression. His career has included performances at Glastonbury Festival, the London Acoustic Guitar Show and the Wroclaw Guitar Festival in Poland. Grouvecat – Led by Mark, Grouvecat blends years of performance experience with engaging songwriting and live musicianship developed through touring across the UK and Europe. Tickets Available Online

title: The Duck and Brush
subtitle: Discover the joy of painting at Wellington’s first Pottery and Wooden Duck Painting Studio.
bodyContent: Pottery Painting Pottery painting is a relaxing, hands-on creative experience where you transform everyday ceramics into something completely personal. No experience is needed - just bring your imagination, pick up a brush, and enjoy creating something you’ve that you’ll treasure long after the paint has dried. Wooden Duck Painting Wooden duck painting is a truly unique and playful creative experience, where each hand-carved duck becomes your own little character. Whether you keep it simple with soft colours or go bold with patterns and personality, no two ducks are ever the same. It’s relaxed, fun, and perfect for all ages—no experience needed, just imagination. 🦆🎨 Parties & Work Events From children’s birthday parties to milestone celebrations, hen parties, and relaxed corporate get-togethers, our studio offers a creative experience that brings people together in a fun and meaningful way. Guests can unwind, chat, and get hands-on with pottery or wooden duck painting, creating something personal while making memories along the way. What’s On (Events) Exciting events are on the way—so watch this space! We’ll soon be hosting relaxed sip and create evenings, calming mindfulness sessions, and therapeutic creative workshops designed to help you switch off and Unwind. Whether you’re looking for a fun night out or a moment of calm, our upcoming events will bring creativity, connection, and a little joy to your week. 🎨✨ Paint at Home Enjoy painting from the comfort of home with our take-home kits—perfect for a cosy night in, a family activity, or a special occasion with a creative twist. Each kit includes everything you need to relax, unwind, and create something truly personal at your own pace. We also bring the experience to you with mobile events, ideal for care homes, schools, nurseries, community groups, corporate teams, and private gatherings—making creativity accessible, social, and enjoyable wherever you are. 🎨🦆 Online Shop Our online shop is coming soon—bringing a little creativity straight to your door. You’ll be able to browse a range of paint-at-home gift boxes, thoughtful creative gifts, and beautifully designed cards, perfect for any occasion. Whether you’re treating yourself or someone else, there’ll be something special to choose from. Gift vouchers also available, 🎁🎨

title: MakeBeth
subtitle: A playful and interactive retelling of Shakespeare's Macbeth, designed especially for families and young audiences. Combining crafts, puppetry, music and audience participation, MakeBeth transforms the Scottish play into an imaginative cardboard adventure.

Featuring live music, puppetry and plenty of opportunities to get involved, the production turns one of Shakespeare's most famous tragedies into an engaging and creative theatrical experience. Audiences are invited to help bring the story to life by making witches, becoming the moving trees of Birnam Wood and even assisting Lady Macbeth with that infamous "damned spot". Using Cardboard Adventures' trademark sustainable cardboard designs, the show encourages imagination and participation throughout. Created by Cardboard Adventures and Shakespeare's Globe in partnership with Chichester Festival Theatre and Leeds Playhouse, MakeBeth offers an exciting introduction to Shakespeare through crafts, storytelling and play. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre

title: Festivals & Events in Brean and Berrow
Festivals & Events in Brean and Berrow
Three Day Family Fun Itinerary
subtitle: Explore the Unexplored! There’s always fun and adventure to be had at Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions... Hidden away beneath the Mendip Hills is a spectacular underground network of breath-taking caverns! Wookey Hole is the UK’s largest show caves system, home to the infamous Witch of Wookey Hole and our new Chamber 20 with rare rock formations. With these world famous caves PLUS over 20 magnificent attractions, Wookey Hole is a great day out for all the family.

title: Coastal walks, Street Art and other amazing discoveries around Weston-super-Mare
subtitle: Fresh air and discoveries without the hassle of driving and parking? Then this is the two day experience for you. We start in Weston-super-Mare at the town’s newly refurbished museum just back from the seafront in Burlington Street. With free entry, this is the ideal base from which to learn about the town and surrounding area that will give great context for your two day discovery. With 50,000 objects there is no shortage of diversity!

title: Hats by Janine
subtitle: With a passion for hats, Janine has 30 years experience in helping women look fabulous At Hats by Janine you can expect a warm and friendly service when choosing just the right accessories for your special event.
bodyContent: 'Hats by Janine' is a boutique in Taunton, Somerset, specialising in ladies occasion hats. There is a fabulous selection in store and online for events such as weddings, race days, garden parties and mother of the bride. If you are looking for something extra special to make your hat unique Hats by Janine offers a bespoking service adding beautiful trimmings, feathers, flowers & fabrics available in an array of colours to your chosen hat. Whether it's a modest suggestion to compliment your outfit or a bold & daring design to make a statement Hats by Janine can help you create your perfect hat. For that finishing touch we also stock beautiful LUNAR shoes with matching evening bags, gorgeous jewellery, handbags and accessories. Hats by Janine always welcome a call, or visit into the shop to see the collection. There is a lovely fitting room if you'd like to bring your occasion outfit to match it with the perfect accessories.
tagline: With a passion for hats, Janine has 30 years experience in helping women look fabulous

title: Loafers

bodyContent: Come and visit us for a great selection of breakfast rolls, daily roasts, burgers , panini and wraps plus various cold fillings served from our salad bar. Contact us for info on our excellent office lunches or call us to book in an order for collection from the shop.

title: Godminster Cheese
subtitle: Here at Godminster, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe. Our shop is open seven days a week and we have cheese available to sample every day.
bodyContent: Godminster, near Bruton, crafts award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe, plus an Oak-Smoked variety, both matured in iconic burgundy wax. Sample daily at our shop, open seven days a week with free parking. Over 18s can also try our fruit-infused vodkas. Set on an organic farm rich in biodiversity, Godminster makes for a perfect foodie gift or Somerset souvenir. Visit us or find Godminster online and on social media.

title: Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Mendip Activity Centre is the ultimate outdoor adventure playground in Somerset. They’ve been delivering adventurous outdoor activities for nearly 40 years, growing from humble beginnings to the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West!
bodyContent: It’s Time for Adventure with Mendip Activity Centre! Nestled in 250 acres of ancient woodland in the Mendip Hills National Landscape, Mendip Activity Centre is the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West. Just 20 minutes from Weston-super-Mare and Cheddar and open year-round, Mendip have been delivering Adventure, Learning and Training for individuals, families, schools, and groups since 1987. Activities available include: · Air Rifle · Tobogganing · Archery · Skiing · Snowboarding · Frisbee Golf · Kayaking · Nerf & Gel Battles · Caving · Paddle Boarding · Rock Climbing · Axe Throwing · ArcheryActive · Abseiling · Canoeing Come for the day or stay longer. In summer, pitch your tent at the award-winning Mendip Basecamp (link to https://mendipbasecamp.com/), a family adventure campsite awarded second at the Visit England Awards 2025. Pitch where you like, check out when it suits, camp fires encouraged, dogs welcome and endless adventure is on offer! Adventure for Everyone Mendip is more than just activities. It’s a place to switch off from screens, reconnect with nature, and each other. Whether you're learning something new, developing an existing skill or simply having fun outside, you’ll leave with muddy boots and big smiles. We believe in adventure for everyone. Many of our activities are adaptable for additional needs, and our friendly team will work with you to make it happen Refuel at the Alpine Lounge Overlooking the Ski Slope, the Alpine Lounge café serves pizzas, paninis, coffee and cake with stunning views- perfect for après-adventure refreshments

title: The Fountain Inn
subtitle: We are a Restaurant/Bar with an exciting menu which features freshly prepared dishes with interesting flavour combinations.
bodyContent: We pride ourselves on using locally-sourced ingredients of the highest quality. Our team are passionate about the consistency and quality of the service and food. We have a warm inviting atmosphere with a quirky, eclectic interior which adds to the overall dining experience. You can find us located in the conservation area of Wells adjacent to the world renowned Wells Cathedral and a short walk from Vicars' Close, which is the oldest residential street (mid-14th century) in Europe. CHILDREN We are delighted to welcome well behaved children to The Fountain Inn. We have a children’s menu and we provide high chairs available on request. We do insist that children are seated with adults and supervised at all times and that any noise or disruption is kept to a minimum. DOGS/PETS Sorry, we do not allow dogs/pets except Guide dogs and Assistance Dogs. FOOD ALLERGIES & INTOLERANCE'S If you have any food allergies or intolerance's, please make a member of our Team aware as not all ingredients are listed on the Menu. *Note of Warning - We cook in an environment that uses most allergens on a regular basis. Whilst we endeavour to do our best, there can be no guarantee of an allergen free product. If you have a serious allergy, we request you bring your correct medication with you when dining. PRE-ORDERS, DEPOSITS AND SERVICE CHARGES We require a pre-order for covers of 10 or more and a deposit of £5.00 per head for covers of five or more. A service charge of 10% will apply for tables of 10 covers or more. FACILITIES Our Restaurant/Pub is a listed building and therefore we are limited with the provision of customer facilities such as a disabled washroom and baby changing room. We do apologise for this inconvenience. CAR PARKING (Subject to Availability) We have made provision for our customers to park in the car park opposite when dining with us and we have a Free Parking Permit facility. Please ask a member of staff for your Parking Permit upon arrival. It is the customers responsibility to request a permit and clearly display this in the vehicle. The car park is pay & display and managed by Car Parking Management (CPM) UK an independent company. Customers can park between 12pm - 4pm and 6pm - 10.30pm. Parking without a valid permit may lead to a parking penalty. Penalty charges received MUST be queried with CPM directly and NOT the Fountain Inn. We are not responsible for any parking fines received. Please request a Permit when we are open for business to avoid any disappointment!

title: Ebborways Farm B&B
subtitle: Ebborways Farm is not just a bed and breakfast; it’s a camping site and one of the main camping sites for Priddy Folk Festival. We also hold rallies and are a wedding reception venue.
bodyContent: Ebborways Farm Bed and Breakfast is situated in a small village called Priddy, on top of the Mendip Hills near Wells in Somerset. We are in an area of outstanding natural beauty, and therefore it is a very popular area for walkers, cavers and horse riders alike. If you are looking for a romantic break or a holiday set in stunning scenery or if you wish to explore this beautiful county of Somerset, and all it has to offer, either by car, foot, bike or horse. At Ebborways Farm Bed and Breakfast we will do everything possible to ensure a memorable stay. The farm is perfectly positioned for sightseeing places such as Cheddar Gorge and Caves (5 miles), Wookey Hole Caves and Wookey Hole Paper Mill (2.7 Miles), Wells Cathedral (4 miles), Burrington Combe (5 miles), Bristol, Bath, Longleat and many other places of interest are also within easy reach. Annual attractions include Priddy Folk Fair in July, Priddy Funday & Craft Fair in September and also in November the Illuminated Carnival Season.

title: Wells & Mendip Museum
subtitle: We aim to give you a stimulating and enjoyable experience, and our volunteers will provide you with a warm welcome. Find us in the Cathedral Close, in the former home of the Cathedral Chancellors.
bodyContent: Our museum tells the stories of Wells and the Mendip Hills. Our displays include a Jurassic sea dragon, and unique archaeology collections from the Mendip caves, featuring the bones of ancient animals who roamed here thousands of years ago. Find out about the incredible array of rocks and minerals to be found on the Mendip Hills, and how people have explored its caves. We have a wonderful collection of embroidery samplers, and tell the story of the early Cathedral stonemasons through a collection of sculpture and statues on loan from the cathedral. Our temporary exhibitions feature the work of local and well-known artists. We also have a library and are home to the Wells City Archives (both open to researchers by appointment). The museum shop stocks an array of attractive gifts, cards and books.
tagline: We aim to give you a stimulating and enjoyable experience

title: Kingsdon Inn
subtitle: The Kingsdon Inn is a beautiful 300 year old thatched pub, located in the small village Kingsdon in Somerset.
bodyContent: The pub used to be a Cider House many years ago, no doubt serving the locals with its own cider brew. Today the pub is hosted by Adam and Cinzia who have a wealth of experience in some of the UK's most respected hotels and restaurants. They have made food a key part of the Kingsdon's appeal. Making use of seasonal, local and often organic produce.​ The Kingsdon Inn has been known for years as the secret stop (for lunch or dinner) for travellers heading up and down the A303, as we are located just off the A303 roundabout at Podimore. (Shhh, we're not supposed to tell anyone.)
tagline: The Kingsdon Inn is a beautiful 300 year old thatched pub

title: Farleigh Hungerford
subtitle: Historic village dominated by the ruined castle.
bodyContent: Historic village dominated by the ruined castle. The castle is in the care of English Heritage and admission is charged. A walk around will reveal hundreds of years of gory goings on topped off with a visit to the crypt. Explore the rest of the village with a Village Trail available from Frome Tourist Information. Over the river Stowford Manor Farm offers cream teas in summer along with a range of workshops from glass working to stonemasonry. In July each year thousands flock here to the Village Pump Festival for four days of the best folk and world music in an idyllic setting on the river banks.

title: Ian Waite & Vincent Simone… The Ballroom Boys - ACT TWO!
subtitle: Strictly stars waltz into 2022 with UK and Ireland Tour…
bodyContent: Strictly Come Dancing double act, Ian Waite and Vincent Simone, continue their 5 star rated tour ACT TWO in 2022. The tour follows on from Waite and Simone’s first 5 star offering as a dancing duo back in 2019, with more old-school variety - glamour, dance, comedy and song! ACT TWO, which began touring in Autumn 2021, picks up again in April 2022 after a short break to continue wowing audiences. Vincent will introduce his new leading lady, Despina Violari, a world class Argentine Tango and Salsa specialist, while Ian’s leading lady, the phenomenal Faye Huddleston of Burn the Floor and Rip It Up fame, returns along with West End vocalist Amelia Adams. Ian says of the new show “Myself and Vince joined up for the 2019 tour because we wanted to do something completely different to all the other Strictly tours. We never imagined that it would be so popular, the audiences loved it, which is amazing! So we thought, why not do it again?” Vincent adds, “I’m so happy to be performing with Ian again. We have loved getting back on the road and entertaining audiences. And I’m sure they have missed me a lot!! We are really overwhelmed with all the support we saw for the first leg of Act Two in the autumn.” Having both been professional dancers for the hit BBC show for a number of years, with their partners including Zoe Ball, Penny Lancaster, Rachel Stevens, and Louisa Lytton, Ian and Vincent continued to be involved with the show in different roles - Ian was a regular on It Takes Two for ten years with his ‘Waite’s Warm-Up’ section until announcing in May 2021 that he would be stepping away from the show and Vincent regularly choreographs the Argentine Tango routines that are seen on the main programme. The fabulous Strictly Come Dancing stars promise another wonderful evening, with beautiful costumes, gorgeous lighting and world-class routines. If you enjoyed The Ballroom Boys, then make sure you don’t miss the hilarious dancing duo when they bring you…ACT TWO! For the latest up to date information about the new dates head to www.theballroomboys.com Tickets can be booked directly through the theatres or at www.theballroomboys.com There are also a limited number of VIP Meet and Greet tickets available at each venue.

title: Wookey Hole Caves & Attractions
subtitle: Wookey Hole Caves is a magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for all ages. It’s an experience millions of years in the making with plenty to do inside and out. Enjoy vintage penny arcades, museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, and of course the famous, beautiful caves.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Wookey Hole Caves and attractions lies In the heart of Somerset. A magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for the young and young at heart. When you visit Wookey Hole, you’ll enjoy an experience millions of years in the making. There is plenty to do inside and out, from vintage penny arcades to museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, to name but a few of the attractions. Not forgetting the breathtakingly beautiful caves, for which Wookey Hole is renowned. Your visit will take you through 8 chambers. Each with a unique beauty and story. You’ll also pass our cheese tunnel, home to the delicious Wookey Hole cheese. The cheese is not the only resident of the caves. Over the years, Wookey Hole has been home to giant hyenas, bears, Neanderthals, and many local people. It has even been a site of pagan and Roman worship. You’ll find Wookey Hole holds a surprise around every corner. You might even get to meet our most famous resident, the Witch of Wookey Hole. We have found she most likes to visit during school holidays! The world-famous Wookey Hole Circus School performs at Wookey Hole at weekends and in School Holidays. Every year over 250,000 people visit Wookey Hole and take-home cherished memories of a great day out. Whether it is your first time or your fiftieth, there is always something new to discover. We can’t wait to welcome you.
tagline: At Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions, Somerset, there’s always fun and adventure to be had.

title: West Somerset Railway
subtitle: West Somerset Railway, Somerset, is a heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton. It is the longest independent railway in Britain, (20 miles).
bodyContent: West Somerset Railway, Somerset is the longest Heritage line in the United Kingdom. Time Table can be seen HERE for 2024 The line is situated in Somerset, four miles outside the County town of Taunton , starting at Bishops Lydeard and finishing at Minehead . The line meanders through the Quantock Hills , an area of outstanding natural beauty and along the Bristol Channel Coast. We have 10 stations along the line each having something different to offer. There are various historic sites that may be of interest to visitors to the area, for example Crowcombe Heathfield station was the location for the filming of the Beatles’ “A Hard Days Night” and scenes from “The Land Girls” were also shot here. The historic town of Watchet dates back to Saxon times, and boasts narrow streets, local shops, museums and lots of places to eat and drink. Washford is a great place to alight, just a short walk from the station we have Cleeve Abbey and the Torre Cider Farm, which are both well worth a visit. Fancy something a little different then why not visit Dunster Castle which is nestled in the medieval village of Dunster ? Dunster also has a working Watermill , the Old Yarn Market building and the Dolls Museum or continue on to Minehead home of our final station. Minehead is situated at the foot of North Hill where the beach is literally right across the road, we have cafes, shops and plenty of arcades along the seafront, making this a go to location. The West Somerset Railway also have combined tickets on selected dates throughout the year. These include, Cream Tea and Cheese and cider specials and linked trips with Hestercombe Gardens and Dunster Castle. We organise Steam Galas in the Spring and Autumn, and we are host to a Diesel Gala too. In the latter part of the year we have our popular Christmas services, we have Santa services running out of Minehead and Bishops Lydeard from the end of November until Christmas Eve, we also have our Sherry and Mince pie specials for you to enjoy.
tagline: Heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton.

title: Wookey Hole Hotel
subtitle: Wookey Hole Hotel is 20 minutes from the oldest medieval city in the UK Wells and sixty minutes from the City of Bath so well positioned for all local locations.
bodyContent: Come and stay at the Wookey Hole Hotel for great value family breaks all year round. Ideally placed in the heart of Somerset, the Wookey Hole Hotel can boast comfortable accommodation in picturesque surroundings. Receive access when you book directly! The Wookey Hole Hotel, located on the southern edge of the rolling Mendip Hills , lies in the Sleepy village of Wookey Hole, with easy access to the historic city of Wells and its stunning Cathedral. The Mendip Hills have been recognised as an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and offer stunning landscapes of sweeping slopes and limestone gorges, with endless walking trails and sightseeing spots. Traverse the Mendips and the hills fall away to the breath-taking lakes of the Chew Valley, just a short drive from Wookey Hole. Also close by are Cheddar Gorge and the ancient town of Glastonbury , with Bath, Bristol and the beaches of Burnham-on-Sea and Weston-Super-Mare slightly further afield. The Hotel includes free and secure car and coach parking, modern bedrooms with free wifi plus a stylish Bar and Bistro. The perfect place for a family break or special occasion - we look forward to welcoming you! And of course, discounted tickets to Wookey Hole Caves and attractions!
tagline: Come and stay at The West Country’s newest hotel. Great value family breaks all year round.

bodyContent: We are a family run guesthouse and we will always endeavour to make you feel welcome. Whether you’re in Wellington for a one night stop or for a week on business, The Blue Mantle is the perfect spot to call home. Enjoy comfy beds (all made by Relyon), tea and coffee, and a hot shower. We have a total of 8 rooms available all with either an ensuite or their own private bathroom. Fresh towels and clean linen are prepared for your stay. The guesthouse has excellent wifi connection throughout at no extra cost. Breakfast is an optional extra for those staying. A simple but well prepared menu is available, and the guesthouse is happy to cater for specific dietary requirements wherever possible. Organic and quality local produce have helped make the breakfast receive numerous excellent reviews. Unfortunately pets are not accepted.

title: The Bowie Experience
subtitle: The Bowie Experience brings a live tribute celebrating the music of David Bowie. Covering his long and eclectic career, the show combines fan favourites with deeper cuts in a high-energy performance.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } The Bowie Experience delivers a live tribute to David Bowie, celebrating one of music’s most influential artists through a performance that spans his long and varied career. title: The Bon Jovi Experience
subtitle: The Bon Jovi Experience returns for 2026 with a high-energy tribute celebrating the band’s classic hits. Delivering powerful performances and an authentic rock atmosphere, it recreates the spirit of stadium rock.
bodyContent: Following on from the 30 th Anniversary Tour, which saw their meteoric rise and selling out theatres, The Bon Jovi Experience is back for 2026! Get ready to rock your way through an unforgettable journey with the only show to be endorsed by Jon Bon Jovi himself! Immerse yourself in a phenomnal celebration of Bon Jovi’s timeless classics as our talented performers recreate the magic that defined an era, delivered with an electrifying energy that will have you on your feet from the first song. Every note, chord and powerful vocal will transport you back to the heyday of stadium rock, leaving you craving for more. Tony, the founding member and MD of The Bon Jovi Experience said: “Bon Jovi’s music brings back memories for people and everyone can remember the first time they heard ‘Livin’ On a Prayer.’ We have a fantastic catalogue of songs and such variety as well for every rock fan!” The Bon Jovi Experience features smash-hits such as ‘Livin’ On a Prayer’, ‘Always’, ‘It’s My Life’, ‘You Give Love a Bad Name’, ‘Bad Medicine’ and many more. Whether you’re a lifelong Bon Jovi devotee or a new fan seeking an unforgettable night out, this show promises an experience like no other. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: A high-energy Bon Jovi tribute packed with classic hits and stadium rock anthems.

title: Fox Mill Shop
subtitle: Step into the Fox Mill Shop to discover garments and accessories crafted with exceptional skill and care.
bodyContent: Housed in The Counting House, the shop blends historical character with a calm, considered environment, inviting visitors to explore at leisure and experience the legacy of one of Britain’s most esteemed cloth makers. Inside, racks of soft-shouldered jackets, flannel trousers, woollen knitwear, hand-finished accessories, and homeware showcase Fox Brothers’ commitment to precision, provenance, and refined style. Alongside wardrobe essentials, visitors will encounter limited runs, archival reissues, and exclusive pieces, each reflecting the individuality and distinction that have defined the brand for generations. Seasonal collections sit alongside timeless staples, providing inspiration for those who value craftsmanship and thoughtful design. The Cloth Room offers a rare opportunity to purchase vintage bolts of Fox cloth, providing a direct connection to the company’s cloth-making tradition. Every piece demonstrates the skill, expertise, and care that have shaped Fox Brothers since its founding in Somerset, a county long synonymous with sartorial craft and carefully made garments. More than a shop, the Fox Mill Shop offers an immersive journey into Somerset tailoring and classic design. Visitors can explore the textures, patterns, and rich colours of flannel, worsted, and woollen cloth, while appreciating the meticulous attention behind each creation. Whether seeking bespoke-inspired style, classic wardrobe staples, or a deeper understanding of British cloth heritage, the Fox Mill Shop delivers a considered and enriching experience where tradition, craftsmanship, and refined design come together.

title: Holly Bush Park
subtitle: Seasonal and touring pitches, plenty of room for campers and open all year round
bodyContent: Welcome to Holly Bush Park Leah, Matthew and family extend a very warm welcome to Holly Bush Park, a small and friendly campsite set in the heart of the glorious Blackdown Hills in Somerset just a few minutes from the Devon border. We have both seasonal and touring pitches, plenty of room for campers and we are open all year round which is great for the hardier caravanners and motorhomers (and campers of course) amongst you! There are miles and miles of beautiful walks and cycling routes in this quiet, unspoilt area of Somerset. It's only a half hour or so drive to either South Devon or North Devon, so a trip to the Jurassic coastline of Dorset (Lyme Regis, Charmouth, Sidmouth) or the rugged Exmoor coastline is a must. Facilities include (and there are no hidden extras!) electric hook-ups (10 amp), wi-fi, hot showers, laundry room, campers washing up area and a chemical toilet disposal. We also stock calor gas. A fully-stocked Community Shop & Post Office is a 10min drive away. We have recently extended into a 7 acre adjacent field which offers an unspoilt environment - an ideal area for walking your dog, or a nice relaxing space for unwinding after your journey. This lower field section of Holly Bush Park has 25 new pitches and a 3 acre dog walking area and a wild meadow, etc. A short walk away is the lovely Holman Clavel Inn, a traditional country pub where a warm welcome awaits visitors. The pub serves really good food (except Tuesdays - chef's day off!) and also has live music on the last Friday of each month. The pub is famous for its "Tricky" cider (aptly named!) and has a fascinating history dating back to the 15th century as well as a resident ghost!!!! Their takeaway food van visits Holly Bush regularly, during July and August.
