title: Somerset Levels & Moors
subtitle: The Internationally important Somerset Levels and Moors stretch from the clay-based coastal plains across peat-based Avalon Marshes to the feet of the Mendip and Blackdown Hills.
bodyContent: SOMERSET LEVELS At the heart of Somerset and giving the County its name, are the internationally important Levels and Moors. Among the lowest, flattest areas in the UK, they were once covered by sea apart from the curious mumps and mounds that rose above them as islands. Somerset is therefore ‘the land of the summer people’ as the rich grazing pastures of the Levels were only accessible in the drier months. To reach the grasslands from the ‘islands’, prehistoric people built raised wooden tracks, of which there is still evidence today. The most famous is the ‘Neolithic’ period' Sweet Track at Shapwick. The Romans tried managing the Levels but did not have as much success as the monks of Glastonbury. Dutch engineers eventually drained them in the 17th century but thankfully not until after King Alfred had used the marshes to escape the Vikings or English history might have taken a different turn. Still farmed and used for growing willow, the wetlands attract huge numbers of wading birds including the reintroduced Common Crane. The Polden Ridge cuts across them as do a handful of rivers and numerous smaller waterways. Sudden and unexpected viewpoints rise mysteriously having once formed islands in a flooded plain. The result is a unique patchwork landscape steeped in history and brimming with rare wildlife. As well as supporting a huge array of plant and bird species, the Somerset Levels and Moors are dotted with quaint villages which bear witness to the fact they have been exploited by people since the earliest times. The Avalon Marshes is home to the world’s oldest known wooden trackway and ancient lake villages. The second largest haul of Roman coins ever found was discovered here. In the middle ages the monks from nearby monasteries drained much of the land to farm it. This is where King Alfred the Great lived and the legends of King Arthur still resonate. Today the area is mostly grassland and arable with willow grown commercially. It is a magnet for nature lovers and those with creative and artistic talents who have workshops and galleries here. With its fabulously rich wildlife it enjoys special protection and supports a number of reserves. It has the largest lowland population of breeding wading birds and is a great place to hear bittern, see starling murmurations and watch otters. Often overlooked, the Somerset Levels and Moors offer the chance to relax and unwind; to see rare species of plant, bird and animals under a wide expanse of sky surrounded by tranquil waterscapes. Off the beaten track it is well served by footpaths and cycle routes as well as outlets for local crafts and produce.

title: The Wheelhouse
subtitle: The Wheelhouse forms part of Gawbridge Mill with the river Parrett flowing under the building, dating back to the 18th Century and reputably built with the Ham stones from the derelict Muchelney Abbey
bodyContent: The Wheelhouse forms part of Gawbridge Mill with the river Parrett flowing under the building, dating back to the 18th Century and reputably built with the Ham stones from the derelict Muchelney Abbey. Gawbridge Mill was fully working until the 1960's.Some of the old workings are still in place Water Wheel, gearing, grinding stones, winches & winding wheels. Now the much loved home of Lynda and Tony Holliss a very warm welcome awaits you at The Wheelhouse B&B with Tony's quirky sense of humour & Lynda's expertise in the kitchen. You can step into "the Good Life", we have our own chickens, pigs, large vegetable plot and stables and produce 50% of our own electricity. We also make all our own bread, cakes, jams & marmalades. Situated near Martock, The Wheelhouse B&B is a perfect base to fish the river (providing you have a licence), canoe on the Parrett, walk, horse trek, cycle or bird watch in the wonderful Somerset Levels all within 2 miles or just sit on the Sun terrace or garden with a good book. Excellent local pubs selling real ales, local ciders and wonderful homemade meals. We welcome well behaved dogs.

title: Mendip Basecamp
subtitle: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure campsite in the Mendip Hills...
bodyContent: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure camp in the Mendip Hills National Landscape - just minutes from the M5 and Weston-super-Mare. Surrounded by ancient woodland you can pitch where you like, park right by your tent and enjoy evenings around the campfire. Well-behaved dogs are welcome! With no check-out time, you can leave whenever you are ready. Mendip Basecamp is camping how it should be: rural, laid-back and relaxed but with essential luxuries. Usually reserved for schools and private groups, in 2020, Mendip opened Basecamp up to families for the very first time- and hasn’t looked back since. Public bookings are available throughout the summer holidays and summer weekends. Bring your own tent or campervan, book bell tents, glamphouses or stay in Mendip Lodge (with free breakfast). Facilities include hot showers, clean flushing toilets, a camp shop, a country Lodge with a cider garden (and live music), an onsite activity centre, USB charging and WIFI. Free activities throughout the summer include live music, orienteering, circus skills, treasure hunts, free climbing tower and nature craft. The campsite is less than a 5-minute woodland walk from Mendip Activity Centre, home to over 20 different adventurous, outdoor activities including rock climbing, kayaking, archery, frisbee golf and air rifle. New for 2026, Mendip Basecamp is launching Mendip Mini Fests - six family-friendly festivals running throughout the summer holiday weekends. Great entertainment, headline bands, local talent competition, and more! Included at no extra cost, exclusively for campsite guests.
tagline: Mendip Basecamp was delighted to be awarded the Gold campsite at the 2023-2024

title: The Red Lion Babcary
subtitle: Our award-winning, 17th century thatched pub and restaurant is set in the heart of this idyllic Somerset village, open every day of the year.
bodyContent: Oozing charm with traditional flagstone floors, exposed beams, open fires, cosy nooks and crannies and pretty garden. We offer everything from great local ales, inspiring à la carte menu, hearty Sunday lunch and outdoor wood-fired pizzas to individually planned weddings for up to 120 people. We are conveniently situated in a rural and peaceful location, just a few minutes north of Podimore roundabout on the A303 in Somerset, off the A37. Accessible down a winding country lane, you will stumble across us, past the village Church, open fields and a handful of stone cottages. We are very much a locals’ pub, welcoming familiar faces into our rural watering hole to sit, chat, eat and drink in these beautiful surroundings. Equally we love to see new faces who might be visiting this beautiful county – looking for their own ‘escape to the country’. The Red Lion is an ideal stopover point for lunch or an overnight stay on the way to Devon and Cornwall or back to London and the home counties.

title: Midsomer Norton
subtitle: Stroll through the cosy town centre and stop at one of the many charming cafés. History buffs will be fascinated with the local area: nursery rhymes including Jack and Jill, Little Jack Horner and Ring o’ Roses are all thought to have originated around Midsomer Norton.
bodyContent: What to do in Midsomer Norton Welcome to one of the best-preserved coal mining towns in England: home to iconic nursery rhymes and inspiration for the name of long-running television series Midsomer Murders thanks to its quintessentially British moniker. Midsomer Norton has existed since the Iron Age, but the settlement boomed in the 1700s when the town’s coal mine opened - and you’ll see traces of its industrial past even today, most strikingly with the volcano-like figure of the mine’s spoil heap on the western edge of town. Discover more about the town’s history at the Midsomer Norton Museum, housed in the former market hall, where a range of exciting exhibits show what life’s been like in north-east Somerset for the past 200 years. The railway routes that used to service the mining town are now lush greenways - stretching all the way to Frome and beyond, ideal for walking or cycling and taking in the serene Somerset setting. In true Somerset spirit, the Midsomer Norton Farmers’ Market is hosted on each first Saturday of the month on the high street - perfect for getting your hands on local meat, fish, fruits, vegetables and cheeses. Enjoy your purchases with a picnic on The Hollies, a green space surrounded by shops right in the middle of the high street. For family fun, stop at the Somerset and Dorset Railway , a heritage trust line run by volunteers that’s being lovingly restored. Look around the old station site and take a ride on the reinvigorated engines down the one-mile track into the countryside.

Our famous Carvery is available on Tuesdays, Thursdays and of course Sundays offering a choice of freshly cooked joints of meat accompanied by a selection of garden vegetables, Roasted Potatoes and all the trimmings. Afternoon Tea Appetites are indulged with an afternoon tea for two or four, which pleases palates with a selection of sandwiches and a pot of tea for each person. The sweet edge is provided in the form of homemade scones with dollops of clotted cream and jam, plus a slice of traditional English Victoria Sponge. Guests also have the option to include a glass of Prosecco for a fizzy twist.
tagline: Open to both residents and non-residents this proves to be a very popular eatery to all.

subtitle: This apartment is located in Weston-super-Mare.
bodyContent: The Grand Pier and Weston-Super-Mare Golf Club are worth checking out if an activity is on the agenda, while those wishing to experience the area's natural beauty can explore Cheddar Gorge and Mendip Hills. Brean Leisure Park and Animal Farm Adventure Park are also worth visiting.

title: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm
subtitle: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is a conservation charity and the largest zoo in Somerset with over 100 species of animals. The multi award winning Zoo is open 7 days a week and aims to make Noah's Ark a place of joy, wonder, adventure and refreshment that supports the well-being of all visitors, staff and volunteers. Through education and fun, they aim to inspire and motivate this generation and the next to consider sustainable lifestyles and care for our planet.
bodyContent: Amazing Animals The home of the big Zoo animals! Visit Noah’s Ark and come face to face with a cheeky mob of meerkats, be awed by African elephants and dazzled by the zebra herd! Experience the majestic beauty and see the skies come alive during the daily birds of prey displays! The Wings of Wonder display showcases the owls, hawks, falcons and eagles in an unforgettably mesmerizing spectacle. Indoor and Outdoor Adventures Play and adventure never stops with our 10 play areas across the 100-acre site. Enjoy the huge indoor play barns including under 5’s soft play and a giant rainbow slide. The Zoo also has accessible play equipment including nest swings and a wheelchair accessible roundabout. Fancy an a-maze-ing adventure? Navigate through Britain’s longest hedge maze. The British wildlife themed maze has 3.4km of paths and wooden nest tower at the center. Keep the whole family smiling and active all day, whatever the weather! Accessibility Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is proud to be an accessible attraction. Facilities include multiple accessible toilets, Changing Places facility, accessible play equipment, hearing loops and more. Please visit the website before your visit for up-to-date information and to view the Access guide. Prices Buy online and save! Noah’s Ark recommends that all tickets, including those for free essential carers and under 2’s are purchased online prior to your arrival. Prices are seasonal, please check the website for up-to-date ticket prices. Food and Drink With a range of delicious hot and cold food and drink options available in our Food Barn and convenient snack kiosks across the Zoo, there is something for everyone! Alternatively, visitors are very welcome to bring their own lunch and enjoy it in one of our many picnic spots. Mini Experiences Noah’s Ark offers incredible up-close mini experiences with Meerkats, Capybara, Andean Bears and Giant Tortoise. You will enjoy 20 minutes behind the scenes with the keeper, learn some interesting facts and get involved with their feeding and enrichment programme. Pre-book your experience online to ensure availability. Minimum age and terms and conditions apply. Animal Experiences Find out what it’s like to be a keeper for the day with our one-to-one keeper experiences before the zoo opens. Experiences include: African Elephants, Junior Keeper Experience, and Giraffe and Rhino experience.
tagline: You’ll be amazed at the variety of nature you’ll see with over 100 species of animals

title: Southfield Farm Caravan Park
subtitle: Quiet friendly Caravan Park with owner occupied static caravans and seasonal touring caravans on a farm adjacent to sandy beach in Brean, Somerset
bodyContent: At Southfield Farm Caravan Park you can enjoy happy holidays on a farm beside the sea. This quiet family park provides pitches for owner occupied static caravans and seasonal touring caravans on a pleasant open site with distant views of the Mendip Hills and only five minutes’ walk from a safe sandy beach. Brean is a favourite place for holidays with everything you need within walking distance. There are plenty of attractions to visit in Somerset as well as wonderful food and wildlife. Static Park open end March to end October, Seasonal Park opens mid May to end September. The Pavilion area hosts 48 luxury pitches for 12' and 13' static caravans, we often have statics for sale please visit: Pavilion Brean Statics for sale. If you are looking for a seasonal pitch (mid May to end September) why not call us? Prices vary but an all inclusive package of grass pitch, electric and winter storage is £1,380

title: The Castle at Taunton
subtitle: The Castle Hotel is in the centre of Taunton the old County town for Somerset. It is the gateway to the Black Downs and Exmoor National Park, West Somerset Railway, being 5 minute drive from the main line train station from London Paddington, whilst being 30 minutes from the M5 Junction 25 and close many amenities.
bodyContent: The Castle at Taunton is one of the UK’s most historic & prestigious 4 Star Hotels, having been at the forefront of British cuisine for 40 years. We also operate Brazz, which since 1998 has provided the blueprint for British Brasseries across the country The Castle Hotel is a unique family-owned hotel set in a historic building in the heart of Taunton in Somerset. A simple ethos lies at the heart of the hotel – to offer the warmest of welcomes, give the utmost personal attention and exemplary service to each & every guest. The Castle Hotel is a one-off, not a link in a chain. The Castle’s reputation for fine food and wine, comfort, and attentive service has been built by three generations of the Chapman Family, with a passion for promoting the highest standards in every aspect of the hotel. Taunton lies at the heart of the region, making The Castle the ideal base from which to explore the history, magic and wonder of the West Country. Each of The Castle’s 44 bedrooms are individually decorated, offering its own personality and comfort away from home. Whether you’re looking for healthy or hearty, you’ll find it all at the award-winning restaurant, Brazz. Featuring a wide-ranging menu, you’ll find favourites such as Brazz Fishcakes – which have been present since day one – as well as Quantock Lamb, Brixham Crab and much more. The Castle’s legendary afternoon teas are served Wednesday to Sunday from 2:30pm - 4:00pm. Freshly baked scones with West Country clotted cream and strawberry jam, elegant finger sandwiches, pastries and cakes along with a fine selection of loose-leaf tea, make this a very special occasion… especially if you add a bottle of champagne.
tagline: A unique family-owned hotel set in a historic building in Taunton, the county town of Somerset

title: The Iron Duke
subtitle: Popular JD Wetherspoon pub in the centre of Wellington.
bodyContent: The Iron Duke Arthur Wellesley, first Duke of Wellington, who took his title from the town, is commemorated on the Blackdown Hills obelisk, overlooking the town. The Wellington Monument was erected to celebrate his Battle of Waterloo victory, its foundation stone being laid in 1817, on land owned by the ‘Iron Duke’. Its completion was not until 1892. Best remembered as the general who defeated Napoleon, the duke twice held office as prime minister.

title: Wellington Travelodge
subtitle: There’s lots to keep the kids entertained in this Somerset location.
bodyContent: Our Wellington Somerset hotel has been extensively refurbished, with all areas of the hotel fully modernised. Experience a great night’s sleep in our new design rooms, featuring contemporary décor and our signature king size Travelodge Dreamer® bed. Rooms are complete with blackout curtains, bedside USB charging points, a spacious desk, complimentary tea and coffee making facilities, and hand, hair & body wash in the refurbished ensuite. Check-in & check-out Standard check-in time: from 3pm. Standard check-out time: until 12pm (noon). Early check-in and late check-out available as extras. Hotel staffed 24/7. Food & drink Breakfast Our Breakfast To Go includes breakfast favourites cornflakes, a pain au chocolat and an oaty flapjack snack to keep you powered until lunch. Snacks & soft drinks available by the reception 24/7. NEW Choose Your Room Great news! Selected stays at this hotel now come with the option to choose your room using our interactive floorplan. Whether that’s rooms close together with family or friends, a specific view or you prefer the top or ground floor – it’s time to choose your room. It’s first come, first served – so don’t hang about! To choose your room, visit the "Manage booking" section of our website. Charges apply. Facilities In every Travelodge room, you’ll find complimentary hair and body wash, as well as coffee and tea making facilities. Our Wellington Somerset hotel has cots and hair dryers available on request (subject to availability). Pet-friendly rooms available Don't leave your best friend behind! Our hotels welcome pets with open arms, ensuring a comfortable stay for both you and your pet companion. Holidays are for the whole family, after all. WiFi Stay connected while you're with us thanks to our hotel-wide WiFi. With our Premium WiFi by Virgin Media, whether you want to catch up on social media, browse the news or send those important emails, you can do it all.

title: Roy Orbison & The Traveling Wilburys Experience
subtitle: The UK’s number 1 tribute to the legendary Traveling Wilburys, featuring 5 tributes in one show and covering all of your favourite artists, including Roy Orbison, Bob Dylan, Tom Petty, George Harrison, and ELO’s Jeff Lynne.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } A first time visit for this much loved show. Come and enjoy a fantastic evening of entertainment jam-packed with non-stop hits, big-screen action, expert narrative and lots of fun. You will be taken on a journey through several decades of pop as we celebrate the music of Jeff Lynne’s ELO , Roy Orbison , Bob Dylan , Tom Petty & The Heartbreakers and The Beatles’ George Harrison . Also the collective genius that was The Traveling Wilburys. Although the Wilburys never toured, here you have the chance to experience what it might have been like to see them live, as we explore their many collaborative hits. Now in its 11 th year of successful touring, this popular show is an up-tempo feel-good celebration of classics such as “Pretty Woman”, “Mr Blue Sky”, “Please Please Me”, “End of The Line”, “Handle with Care”, “Free Falling”, “Blowin in the Wind”, “Tweeter and the Monkey Man”, “Heading for the Light”, “Only the Lonely” and many more. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: A feel-good tribute celebrating Roy Orbison, the Traveling Wilburys and classic pop hits.

title: White Hart Hotel
subtitle: Food critic William Sitwell’s re-launched restaurant, bar and hotel in Wiveliscombe.
bodyContent: It’s been one of the most talked about hospitality launches of the year. When restaurant critic William Sitwell launched his own establishment all eyes were on the MasterChef judge and Telegraph critic. Six months ago he took over The White Hart, an ancient inn that stands proud on the town square of Wiveliscombe, the gateway of Exmoor, some 20 minutes from Taunton. With a restaurant serving Italian food and occasional special events, visiting chefs and collaborations, a great wine list, white tablecloths, linen napkins and uniformed service the White Hart proved an instant hit. There’s Sitwell’s Lunch club, Wednesday to Saturday, offering three courses and a glass of wine for just £35, delectable bar snacks, an à la carte menu of dishes from zucchini fritti to chicken Milanese, great pastas, fish from Brixham market and a focus on local venison. Many of the dishes are cooked over charcoal and embers and, as one recent wrote The White Hart delivers simply: ‘Good food, cheerful service, great atmosphere and it’s not pretentious. What more do you want?

title: Taunton Town FC Lion Trail 2026
subtitle: Join the Lion Trail around Taunton town centre this summer and discover 48 colourful lion displays inspired by football nations from around the world. Designed for families and children, the trail combines exploration, observation and the chance to win prizes.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Explore Taunton this summer with the Taunton Town FC Lion Trail, a free family-friendly trail featuring 48 colourful lion displays in shop windows across the town centre. Each lion represents a different football nation, challenging visitors to identify the countries and complete the trail sheet as they make their way around town. Completed entries must be submitted by 14 August 2026 for a chance to win prizes, including a Taunton Town FC 2026/27 home shirt. Pick up a trail sheet from the Taunton Visitor Centre and start your lion-hunting adventure around the town! Map can be found online at 80348_Taunton-Town-Football-Club-Ltd_Lion-Trail-Map-Leaflets-V2-Not-Printed-FOR-WEB.pdf

title: And Finally…Phil Collins
subtitle: And Finally… Phil Collins celebrates the music of Phil Collins and Genesis in a live tribute show featuring a nine-piece band, classic hits and the distinctive sound that made Collins one of the world's most successful artists.
bodyContent: Chris O’Connell brings the unmistakable charisma, voice, and style of Phil Collins to the stage in this award-winning, five-star tribute show. Celebrating one of the most successful artists of all time, the production pays homage to the man who fronted Genesis before launching a phenomenal solo career that has sold over 150 million albums worldwide. Audiences are treated to a high-energy performance packed with Collins’ greatest hits, including classics such as “In The Air Tonight,” “Another Day in Paradise,” and “Sussudio”. With a tasteful nod to his Genesis years, the show offers something for every fan. The production features a world-class 9-piece band, two full drum kits delivering that trademark Collins sound, and the exceptional And Finally Horns, bringing authenticity and power to every performance. More than just a concert, this is the definitive Phil Collins experience - heartfelt, electrifying, and unforgettable. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: A live tribute celebrating the music of Phil Collins and Genesis.

Headlining the event are The Masonics, celebrated for their energetic blend of 1960s garage punk, rhythm and beat. They are joined by a diverse line-up including Quick Romance, Monaux, Rosbif Attack, Nervous Twitch, Delicious Patricia and The Burntwick Smugglers, offering everything from surf instrumentals and psychedelic pop to new wave and rock and roll. title: Alfie Moore: Acopalypse Now
subtitle: Former police officer turned comedian Alfie Moore brings his latest stand-up show, Acopalypse Now, to Taunton Brewhouse. Combining comedy, current affairs and stories from a policing career, the show takes a humorous look at some of today's biggest challenges.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } The Four Horsemen of rising crime, global warming, AI and culture wars are apparently galloping towards us, but former police officer and acclaimed comedian Alfie Moore believes laughter may be the best antidote. In his latest tour show, Acopalypse Now, he explores the challenges of modern life with wit, sharp observations and stories drawn from his years in policing. Having encountered more than his fair share of egotistical dictators and difficult characters during his career, Alfie shares the lessons he's learned about defusing tension, handling chaos and navigating an increasingly unpredictable world. Known for combining comedy with real-life experience, Alfie delivers an evening that is both thought-provoking and entertaining. As one reviewer described him:“Offbeat, revealing and very funny.” Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: Stand-up comedian Alfie Moore tackles modern life with wit, insight and humour.

title: The Bishop's Palace
subtitle: The Bishop’s Palace and Gardens in Wells has been home to the Bishops of Bath and Wells for over 800 years and this stunning medieval palace is now open for all to enjoy. It’s a great family day out in Somerset with a full programme of year-round events, free guided walks, open-air music and theatre, garden workshops and more and a slice of cake with afternoon tea at the ever-popular Bishop’s Table café is always welcome!
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Visit Highlights: There are 14 acres of outstanding RHS Partner gardens to explore (including the beautiful well pools from which the city takes its name), Dragon’s Lair play area, guided tours, children’s trails and workshops and a café with the best views in Wells! Multi media tours of the Palace building are also included with admission with the choice of an adult version or one tailored for a more family audience including quizzes, treasure hunts and talking Bishops from years gone by! Visitors are guided around the Palace buildings through five narrative themes using stories, music, imagery, quizzes and talking Bishops bringing stories of their tenure and legacy at the Palace to life in an interactive and engaging way. A year-round programme of themed family events is also included with admission including a Civil War Weekend; Archery, Vikings and more! Other events are ticketed separately including summer outdoor theatre; the Palace’s Garden Fair and History Live. The Bishop’s Palace dates from the early-thirteenth century when Bishop Jocelin Trotman received a crown licence to build a residence and deer park on land to the south of the Cathedral of St Andrew. Although home to the Bishop and other families, visitors can walk in the footsteps of past bishops through a number of rooms within the Palace. Visitors are also welcome to look around the Bishop’s private Chapel and explore the ruined Great Hall. The moat has been home to mute swans since the 1800s. The tradition of swans on the moat at The Bishop’s Palace in Wells is thought to go back to the 1850’s when it is likely that a Bishop’s daughter first taught the swans to ring a bell at the Gatehouse for food. We now have two swan bells – one just beneath the window on the left of the Gatehouse, the other to the right – both with a rope hanging down for the swans to pull. The Palace Gardens are open daily from 10am until 4pm in winter and 9.30am - 5.30pm in summer although there may be restricted access due to events and activities taking place (check the website for details). There are toilets on site. Guided tours are also included with Admission – check available times at the Ticket Office on arrival. Families: There’s so much for families to do at The Bishop’s Palace, whatever the weather. Little ones love to explore the gardens, trying to spot the swans and their cygnets; there are waterfalls and springs to see, trees to climb and places to hide. Children also love to explore the magical discovery area that is the Dragon’s Lair in a far corner of the Gardens! And throughout the school holidays, there are always plenty of events to keep families busy including crafting, outdoor gardening, family trails, storytelling and more. Refreshments: The Bishop’s Table café is open daily serving delicious, locally-sourced homemade food and some of the best coffee and cake you'll find in Wells. It’s the perfect place to meet friends for breakfast, lunch and afternoon teas or Sunday Lunches are now being served! Accessibility: From the main entrance of the Palace to the Palace building, around the gardens and to the café's dining area, there is level access. We have one lift to all floors of the Palace building. The outer gardens are accessible via a bridge which is 810mm wide. There are fully accessible toilets with level access within the Stableyard area and the Palace building. There are three spaces available on site for accessible parking, however, it is necessary to book these at least 48 hours before arrival via info@bishopspalace.org.uk or call 01749 988111.
tagline: The Bishop's Palace and Gardens, Wells, Somerset is a great family day out in Somerset.

title: Cheddar
subtitle: On the edge of the Somerset Levels, Cheddar’s elevation soars 500 feet to the top of Cheddar Gorge. Home to the country’s highest inland cliffs, Cheddar boasts one of Great Britain's most impressive landmarks alongside world-famous produce.
bodyContent: Things to do in Cheddar, Somerset - Visitors to the village of Cheddar and Cheddar Gorge have been astounded by Cheddar’s magnificent limestone Gorge for centuries. Cheddar Gorge can be viewed from the public road running through the ravine or by footpaths along the top of the cliffs where you can drink in spectacular 360° views of the Mendip Hills . Formed over one million years ago during the last ice age, Cheddar Gorge and Cheddar Caves are available to explore and are home to prehistoric findings including Britain’s oldest complete skeleton, the Cheddar Man. Unsurprisingly, Somerset’s impressive gorge boasts three impressive titles: a Site of Special Scientific Interest, a Special Area of Conservation, and an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. However, it’s not just the iconic landscape that puts Cheddar on the map: Cheddar cheese is world famous and the traditional method of cheese making can still be seen at the Cheddar Gorge Cheese Company . Before you leave, stop at the gift shop to pick up authentic Cheddar cheese - matured in Cheddar’s Gough's Cave itself. Head down to the Lower Gorge and village for gentle riverside walks, quaint tearooms, and a variety of restaurants and cafés. Cheddar village boasts ancient architecture including the remains of a saxon palace, old market cross and Minster Church as well as charming gift shops, toy museum and crazy golf course. Nearby Cheddar reservoir is a fantastic place to spot wildlife or take a gentle bike ride. If you’re looking for a longer cycle route, take The Strawberry Line’s 10-mile path from Cheddar to Yatton. The former railway line opened in 1869 and was essential for transporting famous Cheddar strawberries, as well as passengers - making it the ideal way to take in stunning Somerset landscapes.

subtitle: Explore some of Somerset’s superb coast with a walk along part or all of the new 58-mile route that is the latest addition to the National Coast Path.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. From glorious beaches to amazing wildlife, historical delights to geological marvels, the Somerset stretch of the England Coast Path offers walkers of all levels - from holidaymakers and families to serious walking enthusiasts - the chance to explore, relax and enjoy some of Britain's most unusual and beautiful coastal scenery. Starting from the genteel Victorian resort of Minehead and walking east towards the natural promontory of Brean Down, you will pass a medieval village , alabaster rocks, an ancient harbour, a stunning waterfall , limestone pavements, saltmarshes, sand dunes and a lighthouse on legs. For more info click here
tagline: Explore some of Somerset’s superb coast with a walk along part or all of the new 58-mile route.

title: The Helicopter Museum
subtitle: The Helicopter Museum is the largest dedicated Helicopter Collection in the World with over 100 helicopters on display in an all weather undercover hangar. Exhibits include two of the Queen's Royal Flight helicopters, the current world speed record holder G-LYNX, a Vietnam Veteran Huey and a Russian Hind Gun Ship.
bodyContent: In addition to over 100 helicopters, the Helicopter Museum includes other breathtaking attractions like its WWII Pilots’ Block, Weston Aviation Exhibition and Blood Hound Missile. This all contributes to a fun day-out for all the family with plenty of opportunity to learn about these marvellous machines and their huge impact on Somerset’s history. The museum hosts various special events throughout the year. These include various car shows, hair-rasing Halloween hilarity and festive Christmas events. The most popular of these special events are the World At War Weekend and Balloons, Birds & Bubbles . At these events, the museum is completely transformed to provide visitors the opportunity to enjoy authentic military vehicles or hold a live owl! Those who haven’t had their fill of aviation history can also attend one of the museum’s open cockpit days. Here visitors can climb into the pilot’s seat of a genuine helicopter and be taken through the controls by an experienced volunteer, many of whom have spent their careers flying such aircraft. Those who really want to feel the thrill of soaring high up in the clouds can even book their seat on one of the many helicopter experience flights the museum offers throughout the year. After all that excitement, visitors can refuel in the museum’s new café which was opened as part of a new visitor service building in July 2020. It offers drinks, snacks and tasty lunches. A particular highlight is the pilots’ all-day breakfast that is big enough to satisfy even the hungriest aviation superfan!
tagline: The Helicopter Museum is the largest dedicated Helicopter Collection in the World

Our Mission is to enrich, educate and entertain our community by providing superior theatre and arts experiences. Our regular programme of events, shows and talks; produced by professional and community companies is ever expanding, attracting a diverse audience from across the county and beyond. Take a look at our What’s On . Our strong links across the community means the arts centre offers a great deal of activities to cater for all tastes including: crafts, visual arts, youth theatres and wellbeing groups. Take a look at our Activities Page. The Gallery space in the Cafe plays host to artists both professional and amateur alike and we are very proud of the work that is presented on our walls. 2021 will see our Theatre and studio space beautifully refurbished and with further capital development plans in the pipeline everyone at the Princess is excited.

title: Westhill Farm Caravan Park
subtitle: Small campsite near Burnham on Sea and Brean in Somerset. Static caravans.
bodyContent: Westhill Farm Caravan Park is almost eighty acres of tranquility on the banks of the river Brue. This static, touring caravan and tenting holiday park is set amongst willow trees, landscaped grounds and farmland in a quiet, peaceful area of the Somerset countryside. We currently have 46 privately owned static caravans, 10 seasonal touring pitches, a commercial and 5CL touring site for all to enjoy. Our touring site caters for long or short stays and one night stop overs. Small laundry on site and owners are resident in the farmhouse. We welcome children and pets. Excellent fishing available on our section of the River Brue. Just a few minutes drive from Burnham on Sea & Brean.
tagline: Small campsite near Burnham on Sea and Brean in Somerset.

title: The Ashbrittle Yew
subtitle: The ancient yew tree has an astonishing diameter of almost 40 feet and in 2002 it was selected as one of the 50 Great British Trees to celebrate the Golden Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II.
bodyContent: Trees are an integral part of our natural surroundings and in addition to offering shade and shelter from the sun and rain, they also provide homes for many species of birds and animals. Sadly however with the recent demand for new housing in Somerset, mature trees and woodlands are being felled by the acre, seemingly with little care or concern for the wildlife contained within, nor for the natural environment that has evolved over time and which is being destroyed forever - all we are told in the name of progress. With this in mind during the course of the summer months we took it upon ourselves to discover some of the ancient trees and woodlands that are located within Somerset - and there are many. One trip took us to the small hilltop village of Ashbrittle which is near Wellington, situated about 10 miles south west of Taunton close to the border with Devon, where in the churchyard of St John the Baptist is situated one of the oldest trees, not just in Somerset but in the whole of England. While the church dates from the latter half of the 13th century the yew tree in the church yard is thought to be 3,000 years old and predates Stonehenge - something which is unimaginable. Yew trees are commonly found in churchyards in this country and many are reckoned to be over 1,000 years old, but the one at Ashbrittle is quite an exceptional specimen. Another fact that makes the Ashbrittle Yew so special is that it has its own signpost directing visitors to the churchyard, where it stands to the left of the entrance porch. There are various theories as to why yews are found in churchyards including the fact that they were grown to provide a source of wood to make longbows from, while others suggest that their poisonous berries would help top repel livestock. The Ashbrittle Yew, consisting of a central trunk that is hollow around which there are six ancient solid trunks make it a spectacular sight, standing as it does on a slightly raised mound which is thought by some to be a burial ground from the Bronze Age. The ancient yew has an astonishing diameter of almost 40 feet and in 2002 it was selected as one of the 50 Great British Trees to celebrate the Golden Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II. Alongside the Ashbrittle Yew is an ornate metal plaque which reads : The Ashbrittle Yew, Taxus Baccata, Reputed To Be Over 3000 Years Old. This tree was mature when Stonehenge was in use. Predating the church, its origin is obscure, but may have been intended to mark a holy place or remains from a nearby battle. Generations of local people have cherished this tree, one of the oldest living things in Britain. Please respect its antiquity and do not climb or walk inside the branches. The sign also contains several lines from the poem "Yew Trees" by William Wordsworth that was written in 1813. Outside the church porch is a wooden bench, which features a carving of the Ashbrittle Yew, which is in need of restoration before it starts to fall to pieces. Some say that the Ashbrittle Yew is dying while other experts claim that it is just going through a period of regeneration after which it will continue to thrive. Whatever the case, if you haven’t been to see the oldest tree in Somerset put it onto your hit list and go an enjoy the peace and tranquillity of this lovely rural part of the county. by Richard Walsh

title: Fox Mill Shop
subtitle: Step into the Fox Mill Shop to discover garments and accessories crafted with exceptional skill and care.
bodyContent: Housed in The Counting House, the shop blends historical character with a calm, considered environment, inviting visitors to explore at leisure and experience the legacy of one of Britain’s most esteemed cloth makers. Inside, racks of soft-shouldered jackets, flannel trousers, woollen knitwear, hand-finished accessories, and homeware showcase Fox Brothers’ commitment to precision, provenance, and refined style. Alongside wardrobe essentials, visitors will encounter limited runs, archival reissues, and exclusive pieces, each reflecting the individuality and distinction that have defined the brand for generations. Seasonal collections sit alongside timeless staples, providing inspiration for those who value craftsmanship and thoughtful design. The Cloth Room offers a rare opportunity to purchase vintage bolts of Fox cloth, providing a direct connection to the company’s cloth-making tradition. Every piece demonstrates the skill, expertise, and care that have shaped Fox Brothers since its founding in Somerset, a county long synonymous with sartorial craft and carefully made garments. More than a shop, the Fox Mill Shop offers an immersive journey into Somerset tailoring and classic design. Visitors can explore the textures, patterns, and rich colours of flannel, worsted, and woollen cloth, while appreciating the meticulous attention behind each creation. Whether seeking bespoke-inspired style, classic wardrobe staples, or a deeper understanding of British cloth heritage, the Fox Mill Shop delivers a considered and enriching experience where tradition, craftsmanship, and refined design come together.

title: Flickers Tent - Tone Valley View Glamping
subtitle: Off-grid stargazing belle tent on an adult only site, with wood burning fire and stargazing roof you will feel really connected with nature. Private bathroom with shower and kitchenette. Outside there is your own wood burning hot tub and fire pit. The view is truly spectacular across the Tone Valley.
bodyContent: The tent is a lotus 5m Stargazer bell tent with Outbacker wood burners. It is truly beautiful, and they make the most of the spectacular views and stars at night. The tent is off grid, and we have a small solar system with batteries that provides power. It has a double bed. All linens and towels are provided. We even include extra blankets and an electric blanket. It is about 12 meters away from one of our other units but there are separated with a privacy fence. It has a fire pit and a wood burning hot tub. The hot tub will need to be lit and heated by you during your stay. In summer, it takes 1.5–2 hours to heat from cold (less if it’s already warm). We can pre-light it and bring it to temperature before your arrival for a £30 charge. A bin of wood is provided with every stay, and additional bags are available for £7 each. We can also offer packages for special occasions, contact us for details. In addition to this you get your own stable! The horses have moved out and a new bathroom and Kitchenette (Fridge with ice box, Sink, Twin hot plate, Toaster and Kettle) have been installed. The stable is insulated and have mains electric heating and electric hot water. The tent is a short walk from the stables, so we have a stone path connecting them.

title: Brazier Coffee Roasters
subtitle: Brazier Coffee Roasters is nestled in a historic red-brick building at the Tonedale Mill Site. The flagship café is open 7 days a week, and is situated next to their roasting plant, where they roast coffee for their wholesale customers (open to the public Monday-Friday).
bodyContent: “Our coffee story began on a hot afternoon in the dusty centre of Australia, where Claire’s from. Drinking fabulous coffee in the outback, we talked of how there was nothing similar in our corner of England, and decided to do something about it. After much tasting, talking and training with some of the best roasters in Australia, we bought our own Giesen roaster, and set up in the Somerset county side in 2015. Ten years later, and we’re now based at the heart of the Fox’s Tonedale Mill site in Wellington, with our roastery and on-site cafe breathing new life into this historic site. We’re passionate about sourcing, roasting and sharing exceptional coffees. From Seed to Cup. Tom & Claire Brazier

title: Frankie – The Concert
subtitle: Frankie – The Concert celebrates the music of Frankie Valli and The Four Seasons, bringing their best-known hits to the stage in a live tribute production featuring a nine-piece band.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Frankie – The Concert hits all of the high notes, telling the story behind the music of one of the biggest pop acts in the world, Frankie Valli and The Four Seasons – the original Jersey Boys! The uncanny Stephen James as Frankie Valli, leads an impressive cast, featuring a world-class nine piece band with a fabulous brass section. This show has it all! Fun, tears, laughter, harmonies and of course those wonderful hits such as ‘Can’t Take My Eyes Off You’, Walk Like a Man‘ ,’Sherry’, Big Girls Don’t Cry‘ ,’Oh, What a Night’ and so many more! Change your sad rags into glad rags and take a trip down memory lane with this critically acclaimed, award-winning production. A powerhouse of a show – definitely not to be missed! “Closest you can get without seeing the real thing” – The Telegraph “Best show we have ever seen” – Four Seasons Memorabilia “Wow” – Robby Robinson (Frankie Valli’s Musical Director) Please be aware this is a tribute concert. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre

title: Love Conquers All - Blackdowns Early Music Projects
subtitle: Music for voices and instruments by Claudio Monteverdi, Sigismondo d'India and Marc-Antoine Charpentier, inspired by the words of sixteenth-century poet Battista Guarini and the mythical world of Arcadia.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Music in this concert takes its text from the words of poet Battista Guarini, court wordsmith to Duke Alfonso II in Ferrara during the latter part of the sixteenth century. Guarini used the ancient mythical stories of Arcadia, home to shepherds and shepherdesses whose lives were influenced by gods and goddesses, as his inspiration. When Diana becomes displeased with the Arcadian mortals, she demands the sacrifice of a maiden descended from the gods. It is a convoluted story, so don't worry about following every twist and turn, simply enjoy the glorious music by Claudio Monteverdi, Sigismondo d'India and Marc-Antoine Charpentier that brings the tale to life. Tickets on sale in person at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: Music inspired by the myths, gods and shepherds of Arcadia.

title: The Snow Queen
subtitle: Ballet Theatre UK presents a retelling of Hans Christian Andersen's classic fairy tale The Snow Queen. Featuring international dancers, costumes and stage sets, the production brings this much-loved story to life through ballet.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Join Ballet Theatre UK for a ballet adaptation of The Snow Queen, following the story of Gerda and her search for her friend Kay, who has fallen under the spell of the mysterious Snow Queen. As Gerda travels across the frozen north, she encounters a cast of colourful characters including gypsies, enchanted reindeer and a mysterious Lapland woman. Her journey eventually leads her to the Snow Queen's Palace of Ice, where only her love for Kay can break the curse of eternal winter. Performed by Ballet Theatre UK's company of international dancers, the production combines choreography, costumes and staging with a specially selected score to create a festive family performance. title: Pandaemonium at Hestercombe
subtitle: Celebrate the 25th anniversary of Pandaemonium with a special screening at Hestercombe House. Shot largely in Somerset, the film tells the story of poets Samuel Taylor Coleridge and William Wordsworth and showcases many of the landscapes that inspired their work.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } To mark the 25th anniversary of Pandaemonium, Screen Somerset and the Hestercombe Gardens Trust are hosting two special screenings of the acclaimed film at Hestercombe House. Starring John Hannah as William Wordsworth and Linus Roache as Samuel Taylor Coleridge, Pandaemonium is a passionate story of poetry, love and rivalry. Filmed largely in Somerset, it showcases the landscapes of the Quantock Hills and Exmoor that inspired some of the poets' most celebrated works, including The Rime of the Ancient Mariner and Kubla Khan. A key scene was filmed at Hestercombe's Pear Pond, making the venue a fitting location for this anniversary event. The screenings will take place in Hestercombe House's historic wood-panelled dining room, the first time the space has been used in this way. The evening screening is expected to be introduced, subject to availability, by the film's director and Somerset resident, Julien Temple. Visitors will also have the opportunity to explore Hestercombe House and Gardens as part of their ticket.
tagline: A relaxed day with music, storytelling and family-friendly fun.

title: Taunton Country Market
subtitle: Taunton Country Market is a cooperatively run shop, selling a range of locally made produce. We supply fresh local food, plants and crafts, lovingly handmade by our members.
bodyContent: Available products include baked goods and preserves, fruit and vegetables, plants and flowers, a range of handmade craft and much more available in shop and made to order. The Shop: Taunton Country Market is found in Bath Place in Taunton. This busy, historic thoroughfare is home to a diverse and special collection of shops – our shop is a co-operative, built up as a team of local artisans, gardeners, florists, apple pressers, bee keepers, bakers, jam and chutney makers. The shop houses all sorts of goods made by local independent producers to supply local people with homegrown and homemade quality produce. Our market in Taunton is part of the National Country Markets Ltd which incorporates over 450 various markets around England, Wales and the Channel Islands. Home made: A wide selection of fresh, local handmade produce is available throughout the week. Chutneys, jams, marmalades and honey are regular shelf inhabitants, as well as a deli supplying local cheeses, meat and eggs. A varying range of sweet and savoury treats are a favourite, from cakes and biscuits to savoury quiches, and scones. If you have any allergy requirements, our team of bakers are happy to take orders to suit your dietary needs – please contact the shop or pop in to talk to one of our many lovely bakers who will do their best to cater for your tummy. Special Occasions: We are also in the company of bakers and sugar crafters who can help to make a celebration cake for any special occasion and qualifed florists who can cater for your weddings, funerals and special occasions – please pop in or contact the shop with enquiries. Home grown: An assortment of local home grown produce is available. Fresh, seasonal fruit and vegetables, beautiful posies of flowers, plants of various kinds. Craft: The Craft Department is home to a diverse collection of local artisans making all sorts of unique decorative objects alongside more functional and practical everyday items, all produced (by hand) with loving care. Many of our makers are available to custom meet your requirements – colour, size and quantity are examples of regular requests for custom orders.
tagline: Supplying fresh local food, plants and crafts, lovingly handmade by our members.

title: ⭐Shepton Mallet Prison
subtitle: Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’; Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom...
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’, Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom. Shepton Mallet Prison is a recently decommissioned (2013) Georgian jail where visitors can walk in the footsteps of our social history and hear officers shine a light on what life was like for both the incarcerated and those who guarded them through the ages. Before its closure, it was a category C lifer prison holding 189 prisoners. Opened in 1646, it was expanded in 1790, with further building work undertaken in the 1820s and 1830s, including the installation of a treadwheel for those sentenced to hard labour. In 1930, the inmate numbers fell and the prison was closed. During the Second World War, the prison was reopened and used as a military prison. It was initially used by the British Army and later by American forces, who constructed a new execution block for condemned prisoners. It was also used for the storage of important historical documents, including the Domesday Book. It returned to civilian use in 1966. Shepton Mallet prison is also known for its tales of paranormal activity. One of the most popular stories is that of the White Lady. She is frequently seen or sensed in various locations, especially A Wing. Staff and prisoners would often complain of an icy wind moving through the wing, the sweet smell of perfume and shadowy figures. She supposedly dates from the late 1700s, when she spent some time in the prison. During a lovers' tiff which escalated, she murdered her betrothed. Once found guilty and sentenced to death, she was housed in Shepton Mallet Prison. On the evening before her execution, she asked for her wedding dress to be brought to the prison, which they allowed. She wore it to bed that night, but in the morning the officers found that she had died during the night. No cause of death was ever found, so we are left to presume that she died of a broken heart. Perhaps this is why she still haunts the prison? In the early 1950s, the Kray Twins were also held here after deserting the British Army. Today, the prison is open as a tourist attraction offering Guided Tours, Self-Guided Tours, Escape Rooms, Night Behind Bars and Ghost Hunting Behind Bars. This is an immersive experience without gizmos or gimmicks – the jail is very much as it was when the last prisoners left in 2013. In 2025, Shepton Mallet Prison received the prestigious Trip Advisor Travellers’ Choice, for the 7th time running, placing it among the top 10% of attractions worldwide.

title: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm
subtitle: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is a conservation charity and the largest zoo in Somerset with over 100 species of animals. The multi award winning Zoo is open 7 days a week and aims to make Noah's Ark a place of joy, wonder, adventure and refreshment that supports the well-being of all visitors, staff and volunteers. Through education and fun, they aim to inspire and motivate this generation and the next to consider sustainable lifestyles and care for our planet.
bodyContent: Amazing Animals The home of the big Zoo animals! Visit Noah’s Ark and come face to face with a cheeky mob of meerkats, be awed by African elephants and dazzled by the zebra herd! Experience the majestic beauty and see the skies come alive during the daily birds of prey displays! The Wings of Wonder display showcases the owls, hawks, falcons and eagles in an unforgettably mesmerizing spectacle. Indoor and Outdoor Adventures Play and adventure never stops with our 10 play areas across the 100-acre site. Enjoy the huge indoor play barns including under 5’s soft play and a giant rainbow slide. The Zoo also has accessible play equipment including nest swings and a wheelchair accessible roundabout. Fancy an a-maze-ing adventure? Navigate through Britain’s longest hedge maze. The British wildlife themed maze has 3.4km of paths and wooden nest tower at the center. Keep the whole family smiling and active all day, whatever the weather! Accessibility Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is proud to be an accessible attraction. Facilities include multiple accessible toilets, Changing Places facility, accessible play equipment, hearing loops and more. Please visit the website before your visit for up-to-date information and to view the Access guide. Prices Buy online and save! Noah’s Ark recommends that all tickets, including those for free essential carers and under 2’s are purchased online prior to your arrival. Prices are seasonal, please check the website for up-to-date ticket prices. Food and Drink With a range of delicious hot and cold food and drink options available in our Food Barn and convenient snack kiosks across the Zoo, there is something for everyone! Alternatively, visitors are very welcome to bring their own lunch and enjoy it in one of our many picnic spots. Mini Experiences Noah’s Ark offers incredible up-close mini experiences with Meerkats, Capybara, Andean Bears and Giant Tortoise. You will enjoy 20 minutes behind the scenes with the keeper, learn some interesting facts and get involved with their feeding and enrichment programme. Pre-book your experience online to ensure availability. Minimum age and terms and conditions apply. Animal Experiences Find out what it’s like to be a keeper for the day with our one-to-one keeper experiences before the zoo opens. Experiences include: African Elephants, Junior Keeper Experience, and Giraffe and Rhino experience.
tagline: You’ll be amazed at the variety of nature you’ll see with over 100 species of animals

title: Glastonbury Wedding and Events Venue
subtitle: An old pre Norman village church lovingly restored to its former glory offering a special place for couples to get married , to celebrate an anniversary , or to just have a party . comes with a large car park , glamping site and accommodation with kitchen, toilets and fully stocked licensed bar .
bodyContent: The old village church was closed back in 1998 owing to lack of attendance ,and with strong family ties was purchased by ourselves back in 2002 , The surrounding farmland and farm has been in our family for six generations so we did not want the church to fall into disrepair , and after a period of time we thought with the right planning we could get a civil license and have marriages and events there once more. After 37 months we finally got all the licenses that we required , then after a major building and renovation work we were ready to open up to the public again after a 16 year absence . With weddings and events coming from near and afar , it was decided to offer accommodation , so planning was sought for some glamping pods , these have been installed during the covid lockdowns and are now ready for the summer of 2021. Guests can now enjoy themselves even more with a relaxing stay without the need to drive , whether it is a wedding , anniversary or party a whole weekend with friends can be a enjoyable occasion without the rush and stress . The glamping pods are all ensuite with double bed ,showers, toilets , kitchenette , fridge freezers, microwave and TV . There is also a three bedroom cottage that can sleep six so more friends and family can stay on site.

title: The Red Lion West Pennard
subtitle: Barrie brings over 15 years experience in the hospitality industry, including at some of Somerset’s best quality pubs and hotels, as well as popular venues in London.
bodyContent: Along with his hobby of interior design, Barrie has brought fresh ideas to the newly named The Lion, and hopes to keep developing the pub’s look into the future to attract both locals, and those from afar who want a traditional British stay in the heart of Somerset. Steeped in history, The Lion dates back about 500 years, and was built when King Charles I was on the British throne and even before the famous Gunpowder Plot of 1605. Originally constructed as a house, for centuries the quirky building has been welcoming visitors as a traditional British pub. With its low ceilings, exposed beams and homely inglenook fireplaces, it has all the charm of what you expect from a historic pub and restaurant. Listed as one of the Britain’s most important buildings, this is a slice of history set right in the heart of the Somerset countryside in a popular English village. The characterful and homely rooms offer a comfortable stay for those wanting to holiday or spend a night or two in this stunning part of the UK.
tagline: Barrie brings over 15 years experience in the hospitality industry

title: Camerton
subtitle: Camerton is home to about 600 people living in 258 dwellings spread over a large geographical area (2 miles by 2 miles).
bodyContent: Camerton is home to about 600 people living in 258 dwellings spread over a large geographical area (2 miles by 2 miles). It lies in the heart of the Cam Valley with the SNCI Cam Brook running through. With its geographical location in the east/west running Cam Valley, steep sided hills run to the north and south from the valley plain. The Cam Brook flows through Camerton. Key Views and Landmarks Camerton Batch Local Nature Reserve, an award winning feature of the parish managed by local volunteers. New Pit Batch Ancient monuments – Iron Age Fort, Anglo Saxon Burial Ground and a Roman settlement. The church the oldest part of which dates back to the 15th century Camerton Court - This magnificent house was designed by G.S Repton who gave it the classical Greek revival style, built by John Jarrett, the local estate and coal mine owner. The Limestone Link National Footpath runs east/west through the parish centre SNCI Cam Brook The Powder House Community Hall and associated playing field. In the past Camerton has accommodated a canal and railway both used to transport coal with the result that many of the older more traditional houses are former miners’ cottages. Positive Features and Special Qualities A mainly green and open parish with many beautiful vistas Children’s Play Area Extensive network of public rights of way Coal mining and railway heritage legacy – e.g. as well as the Local Nature Reserve and the New Pit Batch mentioned above the old coal mining tramway known as the Drammyway, the remains of the Somerset Coal Canal, the Old Miners canteen and the Camerton Branch Line. Interesting historical figures. These include Reverend John Skinner who was one of the most renowned rectors of St Peter’s Church Camerton. Reverend John Skinner was a learned antiquarian, an artist, poet, scholar and a dutiful country priest. He is best known for his journals; he kept a diary of the harsh everyday life in Camerton. Also William Smith who was known as ‘Strata’ Smith as he made the connection between fossils and the layer of rocks in which they were embedded. It is believed that during the time he was working in the Cam valley on surveying of the canal he devised his principles of the science of Geology. He published the first Geological map of England and Wales in 1815 and is known as the ‘Father of Stratigraphy’ and ‘Father of English Geology’. Information on Reverend Skinner, William Smith and Camerton Court courtesy of Julieann Biggs

title: West Somerset Railway
subtitle: West Somerset Railway, Somerset, is a heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton. It is the longest independent railway in Britain, (20 miles).
bodyContent: West Somerset Railway, Somerset is the longest Heritage line in the United Kingdom. Time Table can be seen HERE for 2024 The line is situated in Somerset, four miles outside the County town of Taunton , starting at Bishops Lydeard and finishing at Minehead . The line meanders through the Quantock Hills , an area of outstanding natural beauty and along the Bristol Channel Coast. We have 10 stations along the line each having something different to offer. There are various historic sites that may be of interest to visitors to the area, for example Crowcombe Heathfield station was the location for the filming of the Beatles’ “A Hard Days Night” and scenes from “The Land Girls” were also shot here. The historic town of Watchet dates back to Saxon times, and boasts narrow streets, local shops, museums and lots of places to eat and drink. Washford is a great place to alight, just a short walk from the station we have Cleeve Abbey and the Torre Cider Farm, which are both well worth a visit. Fancy something a little different then why not visit Dunster Castle which is nestled in the medieval village of Dunster ? Dunster also has a working Watermill , the Old Yarn Market building and the Dolls Museum or continue on to Minehead home of our final station. Minehead is situated at the foot of North Hill where the beach is literally right across the road, we have cafes, shops and plenty of arcades along the seafront, making this a go to location. The West Somerset Railway also have combined tickets on selected dates throughout the year. These include, Cream Tea and Cheese and cider specials and linked trips with Hestercombe Gardens and Dunster Castle. We organise Steam Galas in the Spring and Autumn, and we are host to a Diesel Gala too. In the latter part of the year we have our popular Christmas services, we have Santa services running out of Minehead and Bishops Lydeard from the end of November until Christmas Eve, we also have our Sherry and Mince pie specials for you to enjoy.
tagline: Heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton.

title: Weston Museum
subtitle: There is something for everyone here at Weston Museum. We want to open the museum to as many people as possible, so we’re constantly putting on events for all ages and interests. Head to the museum website to find out what is coming up soon.
bodyContent: “Once you know your history you understand more of who you are, you learn from the past and find ways to predict the future and even help create a better one.” Housed in a beautiful and distinctive historic building. We tell the story of the town and the surrounding area from prehistoric times to the present day. The museum is dedicated to being a social and educational hub for the people of Weston and its visitors. You can come to learn, relax or just have fun! The North Somerset Council museum collection contains around 50,000 individual objects. The newly refurbished museum also allows our guests to grab lunch at the cosy Clara’s Café, hire a space for a meeting or even a party in the courtyard. Museum’s do not have to be dull and dusty, in fact, Weston Museum encourages a hands-on approach to history. We also work closely with local schools and community groups to help support the Weston of today and grow the Weston of tomorrow. Our diverse volunteering programme also gives you the chance to get involved. Diversity is key! Our William Mable Gallery allows us, for the first time, to host exhibitions suitable for the world stage. We’ve already been able to display items from the Imperial War Museum and The British Museum. The content of this gallery changes throughout the year, so there is always something new at Weston Museum. Weston Museum is working towards being as accessible as possible. There is a lift for wheelchair users and those who cannot manage stairs to access the main upper floor galleries. Due to the nature of Clara’s Cottage being built in 1865, this part of the museum is unfortunately not completely accessible to wheelchair users due to narrow corridors and a staircase. Weston Museum’s free admission means that the museum is truly for everyone and is quickly becoming a popular destination among tourists as one of Weston's top attractions. Facilities Wheelchair Friendly, Café, Gift Shop, Baby Change Facilities, Accessible Lift, Parking Nearby, Disabled Toilet Available, Toilets Available
tagline: There is something for everyone here at Weston Museum.

title: The Old Vicarage Hotel and Restaurant, Bridgwater, Somerset
subtitle: This unique and quirky hotel is a 10 minute drive from the main line station at Bridgwater or 24 minutes from M5 Junction 24 - so is close to all connecting services and local amenities and supermarkets.
bodyContent: “Looking for somewhere really special to stay, look no further you have found it”, “I don’t think I have ever been made to feel so welcome”, are just some of our recent 5-star reviews. This historic hotel has been lovingly renovated with bedrooms individually designed for complete relaxation and comfort. If you want to be spoilt, relax and eat delicious food visit Candy, Peter and their friendly, professional team whose mission to give every guest (and their dogs) the warmest of welcomes and most memorable stay. The Old Vicarage is tucked away in peaceful surroundings overlooking St Mary’s Church, the only building in Bridgwater older than it, yet is only 10 minutes from the M5. The hotel is full of historic importance dating back to 1327; it is said that Isambard Kingdom Brunel designed the town bridge in the 17th century Oak Room and Judge Jeffery’s stayed, one of the bedrooms even has its own wig cabinet. Each of the 18 en-suite bedrooms are individually designed and kept spotlessly clean with the most comfortable beds and views over the gardens or church. The south facing gardens are glorious, perfect for weddings and enjoying in the sunshine. On cooler evenings there is a cosy bar and snug with comfy sofas for enjoying a drink or two in front of the fire, an oak panelled restaurant and a brand new undercover patio with a pizza oven. A short drive and you can be alone on the Quantock Hills walking in Coleridge’s footsteps, bird watching on the Somerset Levels or hunting for fossils on the Jurassic Coast at Kilve. For the more energetic kayaking, coasteering, mountain biking, pony trekking are all on hand or if shopping is your thing Bristol, Bath, Taunton, Glastonbury and Wells are not far away. Book today for your perfect holiday.
tagline: “Looking for somewhere really special to stay, look no further you have found it”

title: Wellington Monument
subtitle: This monument to Wellington’s victory at Waterloo in 1815 is situated overlooking the town of Wellington in Somerset.
bodyContent: The monument is visible from many miles around and surrounded by idyllic parkland on rolling hills, and the grand walk up to it is a delight. Reaching 175 feet, the design of the monument (by Thomas Lee) was inspired by an Egyptian obelisk, but built in the shape of the type of bayonet used by Wellington’s armies. First proposed in the year of victory, it wasn’t completed until 1854, as the initial funds raised proved far short of what was required. The monument also called for 24 cannons captured from the French at Waterloo to be installed around the base but this never happened. Some were initially shipped for display but remained in the port of Exeter, where all but one were eventually used as bollards. The replacements were found to be from Scotland and had never had the mud of a Belgian field on their wheels. Eventually, four others were placed at the monument but were removed during the Second World War for scrap metal, although they were never used as scrap and were eventually buried at Watchet . It wasn’t until 1984 that the one remaining Exeter cannon was finally placed in position. Wellington Monument is now fully repaired. Following the £3.1 million restoration project, Wellington Monument is now in an even better condition than when it was first completed, and visitors are now able to climb to the top once more. Tours of the monument will resume on 3rd April 2026.

title: The Pop-Up Shop
subtitle: Wellington's Pop-Up Shop is a novel store that changes its 'owner' every one, two or four weeks.
bodyContent: The Pop-Up Shop first opened in autumn of 2019 and has been one of the Town Council's biggest successes welcoming many passionate traders and non-profit groups over the years. title: Raffle's Lodge - Tone valley view glamping
subtitle: Raffles Lodge is a truly relaxing and beautiful stay awaits you. We are an adults only site.
bodyContent: Raffle’s lodge has full LED lights and sockets so you can charge phones. We are off grid so power is provided by our solar panels and batteries nearby. Therefore we can not run hairdryers or kettles in the unit.....however you do get a Stables with your booking. It has been converted in to your own bathroom and kitchen unit with full running hot water and mains electric. The hot tub will need to be lit and heated by you during your stay. In summer, it takes 1.5–2 hours to heat from cold (less if it’s already warm), and in winter, it takes 3–4 hours due to the cooler temperatures. We can pre-light it and bring it to temperature before your arrival for a £30 charge. A bin of wood is provided with every stay, and additional bags are available for £7 each. We can also offer packages for special occasions like birthdays and anniversary. Message for details. Your stable! The horses have moved out and a new bathroom (Shower, Toilet, Sink, Towel rad) and Kitchenette (Fridge with ice box, Sink, Twin hot plate, Toaster and Kettle) have been installed. Each is dedicated to a pod, so no sharing needed. They have been insulated and have mains electric heating and electric hot water. The lodge is a short walk from the stables, so we have a stone path connecting them and we give you a lantern. There is also a carpark area with parking for one car per tent.

title: Pipes Unveiled
subtitle: Organist Ed Jenkins presents Pipes Unveiled, a lunchtime recital featuring a selection of well-known organ works. The programme includes music by Bach, Haydn, Mendelssohn, Messiaen, Whitlock and Widor, offering an introduction to the range and character of the organ repertoire.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Join organist Ed Jenkins for Pipes Unveiled, a lunchtime recital featuring a selection of renowned works from the organ repertoire. The programme includes some of the instrument’s most recognisable music, from Bach’s iconic Toccata and Fugue in D minor to Widor’s exhilarating Toccata from Symphony No. 5. Audiences will also hear music by Haydn, Mendelssohn, Messiaen and Whitlock, offering a varied programme that showcases the many colours and capabilities of the organ. From moments of quiet lyricism to music of great power and grandeur, the recital highlights why these works continue to captivate audiences. A retiring collection will support 4Louis Baby Loss Charity and St John’s Church.
tagline: A recital of celebrated organ works performed by organist Ed Jenkins.

bodyContent: “ Chin Music ” has two meanings. One is idle talk. The other is a brushback throw in baseball or cricket to intimidate the batter. Both describe Rich Hall’s comedy. Ever. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
