title: Chandni Chowk
subtitle: Chandni Chowk specialises in very high quality textiles, hand made in India by wonderfully skilled crafts people to a very high quality.
bodyContent: Chandni Chowk specialises in very high quality textiles, hand made in India by wonderfully skilled crafts people to a very high quality. We are an ethical company producing fashion, accessories and home furnishings collections. We follow no set seasons, our collections simply grow and change as and when inspiration dictates! To compliment both of these departments we have a range of Hand Woven Kilim Rugs, Hand Made Jewellery and Greetings Cards. Established by Rosalind Price and Paul Garrod in 1978 Chandni Chowk acquired its name from an early customer who said we reminded her of the ancient ‘Chandni Chowk’ market in Delhi. The name is Hindi and translates approximately as “shiny/silver/bright/moon - place/area”. At the time, the company was based on a table in the famous Barnstaple Pannier Market; it later progressed into the upstairs of the wonderful Heavens Above restaurant and then to the site of the first permanent Chandni Chowk store in Barnstaple. Today the company is still based firmly in the south west with our HQ housing the design facility, administration and central warehouse in deepest beautiful Devon. We now have five branches and a well-established on-line shopping website.

title: A Christmas Carol – A Radio Play Live on Stage
subtitle: Charles Dickens' festive classic comes to life in a radio-play-live-on-stage production featuring Colin Baker and Sophie Aldred. Set in a radio studio with live sound effects, the performance retells the story of Ebenezer Scrooge and his journey of redemption.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Presented by the Crime And Comedy Theatre Company, this new adaptation of A Christmas Carol reimagines Charles Dickens' beloved festive tale as a radio-play-live-on-stage. The production stars Colin Baker and Sophie Aldred, with a specially recorded appearance by Tom Baker as Jacob Marley. On Christmas Eve, Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by the ghost of his former business partner, Jacob Marley, and warned that three spirits will soon appear. Through encounters with the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Yet To Come, Scrooge is confronted with the consequences of his actions and given the opportunity to change his future. Set within a radio studio, the actors perform as though making a live broadcast, with sound effects created in front of the audience to bring Victorian London to life. This special production marks the 180th anniversary of Dickens' timeless story of charity, forgiveness and redemption. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: A live radio-play adaptation of Dickens' festive classic, A Christmas Carol.

title: Sheppy's Harvest Hoedown Barn Dance
subtitle: Celebrate the end of summer with an evening of live music, dancing, cider and food at Sheppy's Cider Farm. Held in the farm's cowsheds, the Harvest Hoedown Barn Dance promises a lively night of country-inspired entertainment and classic Somerset hospitality.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } If waiting for the annual Sheppy's Wassail feels too long, the Harvest Hoedown Barn Dance offers the perfect excuse to dust off your dancing boots and enjoy an evening of music, cider and fun. Hosted in the cowsheds at Sheppy's Cider Farm, the event brings together live entertainment, great food and a welcoming atmosphere. Live music will be provided by Fresh Aire, performing from 8:00pm to 11:00pm. Guests can enjoy a hearty beef burger included in the ticket price, with vegan and gluten-free options available. A fully stocked bar will also be serving Sheppy's cider throughout the evening. With real barn-dance vibes, fresh country air and plenty of opportunities to dance, the evening promises to be a memorable celebration of the harvest season. This is a strictly adults-only event.
tagline: A barn dance featuring live music, cider, food and country-style entertainment.

title: La Belle Boudoir
subtitle: La Belle Boudoir is a place that allows you to browse through exquisite lingerie under the expert care and guidance of Carmela.
bodyContent: Carmela's philosophy is that all women deserve to feel beautiful, and she is ready to share it with you. She was first interested in lingerie when she discovered the importance, comfort and even the joy of a beautifully fitting bra. It wasn’t long before she trained professionally in bra fitting. subtitle: With over 15 years experience we aim to provide an old fashioned & friendly level of service, while using the latest techniques and advanced equipment. From battery replacements and pressure testing, to strap replacements, and watch sales, we try to cover all your timepiece requirements.
bodyContent: Watch Repairs - we do many watch repairs on-site including glass, crown, movement and battery replacements, some of which can be done on the same day. Battery Replacements - we use the best batteries on the market. For our Watch battery replacements we use Renata, it has developed its 0% mercury battery line in close cooperation with the Swiss Watch Industry. subtitle: Discover and explore the South-West from a Luxury B&B in Podimore, Somerset. Ideal for weekend breaks for couples and families alike.
bodyContent: Church Farm Barn is a stunning barn conversion in Podimore, Somerset, overlooking the historic 14th-century village church of St Peter. Blending original character with modern comforts, this luxury B&B offers two beautiful en-suite rooms with seating areas and quality furnishings, perfect for relaxing weekend breaks for couples and families. Ideally placed for exploring the South-West, Church Farm Barn is a great base for visiting National Trust properties and gardens at Montacute, Lytes Cary and Barrington, plus Tintinhull, the Fleet Air Arm Museum and Haynes Motor Museum. Nearby villages include Sherborne, Somerton, Castle Cary and Ilchester. Just a mile from Podimore roundabout, it also suits business guests seeking a peaceful stay.
tagline: Discover and explore the South-West from a Luxury B&B in Podimore, Somerset.

title: The Helicopter Museum
subtitle: The Helicopter Museum is the largest dedicated Helicopter Collection in the World with over 100 helicopters on display in an all weather undercover hangar. Exhibits include two of the Queen's Royal Flight helicopters, the current world speed record holder G-LYNX, a Vietnam Veteran Huey and a Russian Hind Gun Ship.
bodyContent: In addition to over 100 helicopters, the Helicopter Museum includes other breathtaking attractions like its WWII Pilots’ Block, Weston Aviation Exhibition and Blood Hound Missile. This all contributes to a fun day-out for all the family with plenty of opportunity to learn about these marvellous machines and their huge impact on Somerset’s history. The museum hosts various special events throughout the year. These include various car shows, hair-rasing Halloween hilarity and festive Christmas events. The most popular of these special events are the World At War Weekend and Balloons, Birds & Bubbles . At these events, the museum is completely transformed to provide visitors the opportunity to enjoy authentic military vehicles or hold a live owl! Those who haven’t had their fill of aviation history can also attend one of the museum’s open cockpit days. Here visitors can climb into the pilot’s seat of a genuine helicopter and be taken through the controls by an experienced volunteer, many of whom have spent their careers flying such aircraft. Those who really want to feel the thrill of soaring high up in the clouds can even book their seat on one of the many helicopter experience flights the museum offers throughout the year. After all that excitement, visitors can refuel in the museum’s new café which was opened as part of a new visitor service building in July 2020. It offers drinks, snacks and tasty lunches. A particular highlight is the pilots’ all-day breakfast that is big enough to satisfy even the hungriest aviation superfan!
tagline: The Helicopter Museum is the largest dedicated Helicopter Collection in the World

title: Worth House
subtitle: Located in the beautiful Somerset countryside, close to the medieval city of Wells, Worth House dates back 400 years.
bodyContent: Worth House, a 16th-century former farmhouse near Wells, offers stunning Mendip Hills and farmland views. Ideally placed for Wookey Hole Caves, Glastonbury and Cheddar Gorge, with country pubs nearby including The Pheasant. Enjoy the cosy living room, garden views, and warm hospitality from hosts Sarah and Nick.

title: The Mendip Inn
subtitle: The Mendip Inn is an exciting country pub and coaching rooms concept at the foot of the Mendip Hills, near Glastonbury, owned and run by hospitality entrepreneur, Matthew Lowe.
bodyContent: Styled by the talented team behind Jamie Oliver’s Fifteen restaurant, The Mendip Inn takes the concept of a great British Pub and adds an exciting, contemporary style of its own, to the food and design, without losing that sense of welcome you receive at the very best pubs. First class service is at the heart of all that we do. The Mendip Inn offers a fantastic, modern and fresh à la carte menu, seven days a week. We have a weekly specials menu, highlighting local, seasonal produce, cooked to express the flavours of the ingredients, with a twist on exceptional pub recipes. Wednesday is Steak Night, Friday is Fresh Fish Friday, with fresh market fish specials each week, and Sundays are, of course, for fabulous traditional roasts.
tagline: The Mendip Inn is an exciting country pub and coaching rooms

title: Ring O'Bells
subtitle: Free house local pub in Somerset between Street & Glastonbury.
bodyContent: The Ring O’Bells is an 18th Century “free house” pub in the Somerset village of Ashcott near Street and Glastonbury, which for the last 29 years has been run by a family partnership. A unique pub with unique food, all prepared by us in our own kitchens. Local meat from a local butcher. Somerset produce at its best. Daily Specials blackboard including freshly made desserts. Home-made fudge with your coffee to finish! We are a genuine Free House and it is our policy to feature beers from small independent breweries, many from the West Country but occasionally also more “exotic” visitors! The range of beers varies constantly but our list of forthcoming beers features usually at least one beer from one of the local micro breweries. CAMRA Good Beer Guide 2016 CAMRA Good Pub Food Guide 2016, (star-rated, and entered in this guide for the nineteenth consecutive year). AA Pubs and Inns Guide 2016 The Good Pub Guide 2016

title: Farmborough
subtitle: Farmborough is a small village and civil parish, 6 miles (9.7 km) south west of Bath in the unitary authority of Bath & North East Somerset, England. The Farmborough ward is represented by one councillor on the Bath & North East Somerset council.
bodyContent: Farmborough is a small village and civil parish, 6 miles (9.7 km) south west of Bath in the unitary authority of Bath & North East Somerset, England. The Farmborough ward is represented by one councillor on the Bath & North East Somerset council. Farmborough Parish Council has responsibility for local issues, including setting an annual precept to cover operating costs and producing annual accounts for public scrutiny. The Parish Council evaluates local planning applications and works with the local police, district council officers, and other groups on matters of crime, security and traffic. The Parish Council's role, through local groups, also includes the maintenance and repair of parish facilities, such as the Village Hall, the Recreation Ground and Pavilion and children's playgrounds, as well as consulting with the district council on the maintenance, repair and improvement of highways, drainage, footpaths, public transport and street cleaning.

bodyContent: We extend a warm, friendly welcome to all our guests. Saxonia is a thriving guest house with nine en-suite rooms that have been successfully run for the last 20 years. Our aim is simple - to give you the best accommodation at the most reasonable price you ever had.

title: The Grand Pier - Weston Super Mare
subtitle: Opening 4th July 2020 The Grand Pier is open every day, except Christmas Day, so come hail, rain or shine, you’ll always get a warm welcome. Whatever the weather is doing outside, it’s still fun, fun, fun on the inside.
bodyContent: The Grand Pier, Weston super Mare, Somerset is the ideal destination for non-stop indoor family theme park fun. This North Somerset pier, with its state-of-the-art Pavilion is a truly iconic destination for: family days out, events, concerts, weddings, and corporate events. With rides, attractions and the latest arcade games a visit to the Pier is the perfect treat for kids of all ages. On weekends, and during the North Somerset school holidays, unlimited rides wristbands are available for adults and children - see here for details - don’t miss out as they add exceptional value to your fun day out. Come and discover everything the Grand Pier, Somerset has to offer, including: · The very latest amusements - including giant screen Space Invaders · Thrilling rides including: Sidewinder, Freefall and Robocoaster · An amazing two level 300 meter indoor Go-Kart track · Seaside favourites, including: dodgems, house of horrors and helter skelter · A three level soft play area with dedicated adult seating area · A choice of places to eat and drink - we even serve your favourite Costa coffee! With hundreds of amusements and games to play, a range of thrilling rides, and a choice of attractions for all ages everyone gets to have fun in the amazing Pavilion - it really is one big house of fun!!! When you’re ready for a bite to eat you’re spoilt for choice from traditional fish and chips to afternoon tea, and of course ice cream too! There’s even a pub for you to enjoy a relaxing drink as you take in the spectacular views. As a unique location our function rooms are always in demand, and we love creating the perfect setting for weddings and family celebrations. For businesses our dedicated events team is on hand for corporate events, ranging from team meetings and training sessions to large scale conferences.The fun continues into the night with a wide range of events from concerts to whodunnits. To make sure you don’t miss out visit and book your tickets online today. For even more value, annual Grand Pier Membership is just £12 for Individual Membership or £25 for a Family Pass (up to 4 people) and gives you unlimited free access onto the Pier, exclusive “Treats” and a range of discounts too. There’s a whole year of fun waiting for you and your family to discover on the Grand Pier. With a fascinating history in an amazing location the Pier is a popular destination for school and group visits, and we are pleased to offer talks and tours for your group. To find out how we can make your group visit extra special please contact our Events Team on: 01934 646 155 or email: events@grandpier.co.uk.
tagline: The Grand Pier, is the ideal destination for non-stop indoor family theme park fun.

subtitle: Self catering accommodation with tennis court near Burnham on Sea, Somerset
bodyContent: Welcome to Jonswood Lodge, our bespoke luxury holiday lodge with tennis court, gym and games room, sleeping 6 in 3 bedrooms. With the legendary beauty of the Somerset Levels on the doorstep and the gorgeous sandy beaches of Burnham-on-Sea and Brean only a few miles away our newly built and very stylish lodge makes an ideal holiday base. Boasting its own tennis court and fitness room, it sits in the hamlet of Watchfield, within easy reach of the area's famous attractions including the caves and cliffs at Cheddar Gorge , underground rivers and pools at Wookey Hole , Clarks Shopping Village at Street , Glastonbury Tor and the lovely Cathedral and Bishop's Palace at Wells , whilst the elegant city of Bath is a little further afield. Do call to enquire, we can accommodate most requests.

title: Shepherd's Rest - Tone Valley View Glamping
subtitle: Shepherd’s Rest romantic retreat for two in a peaceful, adults-only glamping site. Enjoy a king-sized bed, underfloor heating, a mini kitchen, and an ensuite bathroom. Outside, relax in the log-burning hot tub, fire pit, BBQ, or bistro dining set. Embrace wellness with the tranquil surroundings and rejuvenating hot tub experience.
bodyContent: Shepherd’s Rest is located at Tone Valley View Glamping, an adults-only site in Somerset with three private units. The setting is truly stunning, offering breathtaking views and starry skies at night. The shepherd's hut features underfloor heating, a king-sized bed, a log burner, and an ensuite bathroom. The kitchen includes an espresso machine, fridge with ice box, sink, microwave, twin hot plate, air fryer, toaster, and kettle—please note, there’s no oven. All linens and towels are provided. Outside, enjoy a private, enclosed area with a firepit, BBQ, dining table, and sun loungers. The centrepiece is our log-burning hot tub with Bubbles, which you can light and heat during your stay. The hot tub will need to be lit and heated by you during your stay. In summer, it takes 1.5–2 hours to heat from cold (less if it’s already warm), and in winter, it takes 3–4 hours due to the cooler temperatures. We can pre-light it and bring it to temperature before your arrival for a £30 charge. A bin of wood is provided with every stay, and additional bags are available for £7 each. We can also offer packages for special occasions, please contact us for details. For wellness, relax in the hot tub, or visit a nearby local sauna business for an extra dose of relaxation. We can also arrange spa packages delivered right to your unit, making it the perfect place to unwind.

title: Wellington Local History and Museum Society
subtitle: The society’s main purpose is the running of Wellington Museum
bodyContent: This fascinating museum is housed on the ground floor of the historic Squirrel Hotel (1673 – 1973) in the centre of the town. It displays items relating to the history of Wellington, its people and the surrounding villages. The museum was completely refurbished in the winter of 2025/6 and now also has new digital interactive displays as well as other hands on exhibits that will appeal to all ages. There is also a children’s quiz to do while touring the museum. The museum has an extensive range of gifts and publishes books and documents on local history. It organises public events to further local knowledge of history for members and non members. The museum organises guided tours for schools and other organisations and also goes out to visit these. Registered Charity No: 801321

title: Dermot O'Leary's – Toto the Ninja Cat
subtitle: Based on Dermot O'Leary's bestselling children's book, Toto the Ninja Cat brings a family adventure to the stage with puppetry, music and plenty of fun. Follow Toto and her brother Silver as they set out on a daring mission through the streets of London.
bodyContent: A Little Angel Theatre, Mercury Theatre, Colchester and Mayflower Southampton co-production. Meet Toto. She might look like an ordinary cat, but she’s no ordinary feline. Almost completely blind, Toto has incredible ninja skills, a big heart, and a nose for adventure. By day, she naps like any other pet… but by night, she’s out on daring missions with her cheeky brother, Silver. In their very first adventure, a deadly King Cobra has escaped onto the streets of London, and it’s up to Toto to use every ounce of her courage and cunning to save the day. Based on Dermot O’Leary’s best-selling children’s book, illustrated by Nick East, this purr-fectly thrilling tale is filled with original music, laugh-out-loud fun, and extraordinary puppetry, promising fun for the whole family. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: A family adventure featuring Toto the Ninja Cat, music, puppetry and fun.

title: The Dave Hankin Big Band
subtitle: The Dave Hankin Big Band returns to the Tacchi-Morris Arts Centre with a programme of classic big band music, featuring songs associated with artists including Count Basie, Duke Ellington, Frank Sinatra and Glenn Miller.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Following a number of successful appearances, The Dave Hankin Big Band returns with a new show celebrating the sounds of the big band era and beyond. The programme includes music associated with artists such as Count Basie, Frank Sinatra, Duke Ellington, Nelson Riddle, Buddy Rich, Glenn Miller and Maynard Ferguson. Recognised as one of the South West's leading big bands, the ensemble brings together experienced musicians performing a varied repertoire of jazz, swing and popular favourites. The concert also features vocal performances from session singer Bern Stewart, whose career has included work with the BBC and other major broadcasters. Whether you're a long-time fan of big band music or discovering the genre for the first time, the performance offers an afternoon of well-known melodies and live musicianship. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: A live big band concert featuring jazz, swing and popular classics.

title: ⭐East Lambrook Manor Gardens
subtitle: The quintessential English cottage garden created by the celebrated 20th-century plantswoman and gardening writer Margery Fish and made famous through her many books. It is a unique garden of great beauty and charm with noted collections of snowdrops, hellebores and geraniums and an excellent specialist plant nursery and tea room.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The garden may have changed ownership but the quintessential English cottage garden created by the celebrated 20th-century plantswoman and gardening writer Margery Fish is still open. The garden was made famous through her many books, and it retains a unique beauty and charm, with noted collections of snowdrops, hellebores and geraniums and an excellent specialist plant nursery, and Tea Room. East Lambrook Manor Gardens in South Somerset is a hidden gem, yet it is easily accessible from the A303 at South Petherton, near Yeovil. The home from 1938 to 1969 of the doyenne of cottage gardening Margery Fish, it was here that she developed her own unselfconscious style, combining plants in a relaxed and informal manner to create a garden of great beauty and charm that has encouraged generations of budding gardeners. Open Tuesday to Saturday 10 am to 5 pm, the internationally famous garden was given Grade-1 status by English Heritage in 1992 and is recognised as the premier example of the English cottage garden style. Winding paths between abundantly planted beds and borders, often edged with the local hamstone, typify the garden which is divided into different areas such as the Terrace Garden, Silver Garden, the newly restored Green Garden and The Ditch. The latter, along with the Woodland Garden, contain most of the garden’s extensive collection of snowdrops and hellebores. The 17 th century Malthouse is home to the Tea Rooms serving coffee, tea, cakes and cold drinks. The Margery Fish Plant Nursery specialises in cottage garden plants and interesting perennials. Accessibility: Limited disabled access due to some narrow paths and steps. Dogs on leads permitted. Disabled toilets.

title: Thorney Lakes and Caravan Park
subtitle: A caravan and camping park with full facilities and coarse fishing available.
bodyContent: A caravan and camping park with full facilities and coarse fishing available. One mile form the historic village of Muchelney, our scenic park is perfect for touring the Somerset level and Moors , one of the most unchanged and distinctive landscape of lowland Britain. There are many interesting walks on the wetlands which are rich in flora, fauna and birdlife. Fishing lakes established in 1993, the setting attracts a host of wildlife and is regualry visited by otters, badgers, rabbits, deer and 70 species of birdlife including kingfishers. Just a short level walk from the caravan path the two miles of nature trails are a perfect for a short stroll or to enjoy a chat with the local fisher folk.
tagline: A caravan and camping park with full facilities and coarse fishing available.

title: Weston Museum in Weston super Mare
subtitle: Weston Musuem in Weston super Mare has something for everyone. We want to open the museum to as many people as possible, so we’re constantly putting on events for all ages and interests. Head to the museum website to find out what is coming up soon.
bodyContent: “Once you know your history you understand more of who you are, you learn from the past and find ways to predict the future and even help create a better one.” Housed in a beautiful and distinctive historic building. We tell the story of the town and the surrounding area from prehistoric times to the present day. The museum is dedicated to being a social and educational hub for the people of Weston and its visitors. You can come to learn, relax or just have fun! The North Somerset Council museum collection contains around 50,000 individual objects. The newly refurbished museum also allows our guests to grab lunch at the cosy Clara’s Café, hire a space for a meeting or even a party in the courtyard. Museum’s do not have to be dull and dusty, in fact, Weston Museum encourages a hands-on approach to history. We also work closely with local schools and community groups to help support the Weston of today and grow the Weston of tomorrow. Our diverse volunteering programme also gives you the chance to get involved. Diversity is key! Our William Mable Gallery allows us, for the first time, to host exhibitions suitable for the world stage. We’ve already been able to display items from the Imperial War Museum and The British Museum. The content of this gallery changes throughout the year, so there is always something new at Weston Museum. Weston Museum is working towards being as accessible as possible. There is a lift for wheelchair users and those who cannot manage stairs to access the main upper floor galleries. Due to the nature of Clara’s Cottage being built in 1865, this part of the museum is unfortunately not completely accessible to wheelchair users due to narrow corridors and a staircase. Weston Museum’s free admission means that the museum is truly for everyone and is quickly becoming a popular destination among tourists as one of Weston's top attractions. Facilities Wheelchair Friendly, Café, Gift Shop, Baby Change Facilities, Accessible Lift, Parking Nearby, Disabled Toilet Available, Toilets Available
tagline: There is something for everyone here at Weston Museum.

title: Thorner’s Farm Shop
subtitle: Thorner’s began with the simple idea of providing quality butchery meat, sourced in Somerset whenever possible. This is still one of our core values and now, in addition to fresh meat, we are proud to offer an award winning range of pies, quiches, savouries, ready meals, desserts & cakes.
bodyContent: Where did it all begin? Born and bred in Somerset Mr Jon Thorner opened one of the regions very first farm shops in 1979, as an extension of the family farm and abattoir. The core of the business was built upon using locally sourced and high welfare meat with a strong focus on fair pricing for suppliers. A passion for success The meat industry has changed dramatically since 1979 and it was important for Thorner’s to diversify. So in 2005 the first Thorner’s pie was baked! As the kitchen gained confidence, the number of awards grew and they knew they had something special to offer. The range has grown significantly now offering a range of pies, quiches, savouries, ready meals, desserts and cakes – and did you know each pie is still hand crimped and individually filled. Award winning The quality of our ingredients, the authentic homemade appearance and flavour of our kitchen range has delivered us multiple awards across the food industry including Great Taste, British Pie Awards, Taste of the West and Smithfield Awards, and our staff and the business have also been recognised regionally and within the industry at Somerset Business and Mendip Business Awards.

title: Cameley and Temple Cloud
subtitle: Cameley dates back to Anglo Saxon times when it was part of the ‘Hundred of Chewton’. It is recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086 as ‘Camelie’ and it lies on the Cam Brook. The name means ‘the curved river meadows’ from the Celtic word of ‘cam’ and the old English ‘leah’.
bodyContent: Cameley dates back to Anglo Saxon times when it was part of the ‘Hundred of Chewton’. It is recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086 as ‘Camelie’ and it lies on the Cam Brook. The name means ‘the curved river meadows’ from the Celtic word of ‘ cam’ and the old English ‘ leah’ . After the Norman Conquest, the Bishop of Coutances held the manor but about 1150 the manor was given to Bath Abbey by the d’Alneto family who came from Normandy after the Conquest. Later the manor was held by another French Norman family the de Marisco family who are better known for their connection with the island of Lundy. In a grant of 1201, King John passed control to the Knights Templar but during the 13th and early 14th centuries the manor was again under the control of the de Marisco family. It was in the early 14th century that the area of the parish previously called ‘Cloude’ started to be referred to as Temple Cloud, indicating almost certainly that the Knights Templar owned or occupied land within the parish. Ownership of the manor passed through the hands of the religious houses of Bath Abbey and Glastonbury Abbey in the late Middle Ages. The church at Cameley dates back to the 13th century. It is dedicated to St James and may well have been built on the site of an earlier one. The tower was constructed a little later. The church is now looked after by the Churches Conservation Trust and is widely regarded for its wall paintings and its 15th and 17th century pews and pulpit. The Victorians did nothing in the church so it remains much as it was 200 years ago. When the religious houses were dissolved by Henry VIII, the manor was passed with others to Richard Watkin Vaughan, a courtier who passed it to his son Polydore on his death. Polydore sold the manor in 1561 to John and Mary Hippisley and the Hippisley family owned the manor of Cameley and the village of Temple Cloud until they sold it house by house and farm by farm along with the land at an auction in July 1919. Temple Cloud developed because it was on the road from Bristol to the south and the population gradually moved from the area around St James Church to be near the road - a process that was accelerated when the turnpike roads were developed. Cottages were built along the road, many of which remain today. In about 1916 some residents petitioned for a church to be built in Temple Cloud to avoid them having to make the long walk to St James in Cameley and the Hippisley’s agreed. St Barnabas Church was constructed in the style of the Arts and Crafts Movement from Temple stone and was built using local labour in the mid 1920s. Temple Cloud expanded with the usual trades and shops to serve the community including three or four public houses. At the height of its activity, it was said that Temple Cloud had everything except a railway station. Temple Cloud had quarries where Pennant sandstone was to be found. This hard stone was used for pavements and kerbs among other things. There was also a brick works and a saw mill but farming was the main activity within the parish. The parish of Cameley is well positioned for commuting to work or for leisure activities. The main road, the A37 means that Bristol and Shepton Mallet are each about 10 miles away with Bath and Wells much the same distance. There is a regular bus service to Bristol and Wells and the nearest railway stations are Bristol Temple Meads, Keynsham and Bath Spa . Recent Development Over the years a small number of developments have been built within the parish which has included homes at Goldney Way and further development at Paulmont Rise and more recently a larger development at Meadway. Building work is also due to be completed at two sites on Temple Inn Lane – one at Brandown Close and the other adjoining the main road where the Temple Inn pub has recently been redeveloped to contain a number of letting rooms and several houses. Facilities Today, Temple Cloud is home to Cameley CEVC Primary School which is rated by OFSTED as 'good'. There is also Cameley Surgery which is partnered with Harptree Surgery, and many other thriving local businesses including a Post Office contained within the petrol station shop. Temple Cloud Garage and Cameley Primary School kindly both host public access defibrillators provided by the Parish Council. There are many vibrant community groups and activities within the village and surrounding area which includes: Temple Cloud in Bloom, Temple Cloud WI, St Johns Ambulance and many more. The parish is supplied with an informative Parish Magazine - Clutton & Temple Cloud News, copies of which are available at the local petrol station shop and to which residents can subscribe for a small fee. The Parish Magazine publishes local news, local events, adverts, details of the mobile library and contains a directory at the back. In 2017 the Parish Council undertook an exciting project to expand the Playground on Cameley Playing Field which now provides a wide range of equipment for all ages and abilities. Parish Council Aims Temple Cloud with Cameley Parish Council aims to represent the local community, deliver services to meet local needs, and improve the quality of life and community wellbeing. The Parish Council provides and maintains a variety of important and visible services. These include: street sweeping through the employment of two village operatives, grass cutting on the Village Green and Playing Fields, monitoring public rights of way and highways. The Parish Council also own and maintain Cameley Playing Fields and owns and manages Temple Cloud Village Hall. In addition, the Parish Council scrutinises all planning applications and provides a voice for the local community on various issues and consultations and also works with the Local Authority (B&NES Council) to ensure local services are delivered and the Parish is well maintained. The Parish of Cameley is a civil parish in Bath and North East Somerset Council area, which is made up of the larger village of Temple Cloud and the smaller village of Cameley. At full membership, the Parish Council has nine Parish Councillors and currently employs two Village Operatives and one Parish Clerk. Parish Council Meetings and Current Projects The Parish Council hold a Parish Council Meeting on the second Wednesday of the month which starts at 7.00pm at Temple Cloud Village Hall. Members of the public are always welcome to attend these meetings and a public participation session is held at the start of the meeting where residents are invited to speak to their Councillors or raise issues of concern. From time to time vacancies arise and the Parish Council advertise such vacancies on the two Parish Council noticeboards - one situated on the corner of Temple Inn Lane at the junction with the main road and the second by the bus stop on the Village Green. Temple Cloud with Cameley Parish Council are currently undertaking a project to rejuvenate the Village Hall and carpark and currently have a consultation and competition open. You can find out more on the Parish Council website. The Parish Council has a website – www.templecloud.org.uk and a Facebook Page. For enquiries please contact the Parish Clerk, Jenny Howell at: info@templecloud.org.uk . This piece was drafted as a collaboration between Temple Cloud with Cameley Parish Council and local residents with an interest in local history, The Parish Council thanks all contributors.

title: Buddy Holly – No Buddy Does It Better
subtitle: Buddy Holly – No Buddy Does It Better celebrates the music and story of Buddy Holly and The Crickets in a live rock ‘n’ roll tribute show. Featuring classic hits and a full band performance, it recreates the energy of a defining era in music.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Buddy Holly – No Buddy Does It Better is a live tribute show celebrating the music of Buddy Holly and The Crickets. Led by Danny Gill, the performance recreates the look and sound of one of rock ‘n’ roll’s most influential artists, backed by a full live band. Audiences can enjoy a selection of well-known hits including “Peggy Sue”, “That’ll Be the Day”, “Raining in My Heart” and “Oh Boy”. The show follows Buddy Holly’s story through his career, bringing his music and legacy back to life on stage. The performance culminates with the Winter Dance Party, featuring songs associated with both The Big Bopper and Ritchie Valens, creating a celebration of an important chapter in rock ‘n’ roll history. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre

title: Art Exhibition
subtitle: Artists in oil, acrylic and Ink
bodyContent: Come and view our exciting new exhibition! Ends 13th August. We also have a range of artisans in the gallery selling ceramics, wood, Jewellery, glass and more. All made locally. Nina King Artist and owner - Nina is a landscape artist and she is based in Wellington, Somerset. Her collection at the Talent Gallery features acrylic paintings inspired by nature and the local area. You'll find a range of options available from cards and prints to framed original paintings. Annie Musgrove - Annie Musgrove lives on the Somerset-Devon border working mostly in oil, adding layers to build up a depth to her work in which she captures the elemental nature of the rural landscape around her. Annie’s work captures the vigour and wonder of nature that surrounds us. Julie Ruth Bramley - Julie Ruth Bramley is an artist living in Chard, Somerset. Her oil on canvas paintings of flowers are inspired by the flowers that she grows in her own garden. Jane Savin - Jane lives on the edge of Exmoor National Park. Her art is vibrant, bold and colourful using a combination of different mediums and surfaces and is about colour, shape and movement with a little bit of intensity thrown in from time to time! Jane often uses repurposed surfaces and frames for her artwork which adds to the vintage feel of her paintings. title: Gordon Hendricks as Elvis – The King's Voice
subtitle: Award-winning Elvis tribute artist Gordon Hendricks brings The King's Voice to the Tacchi-Morris Arts Centre. Celebrating the music and legacy of Elvis Presley, the show recreates iconic performances from the 1968 Comeback Special through to the Vegas years.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Gordon Hendricks is one of the UK's most recognised Elvis tribute artists, having won numerous titles including the Ultimate Elvis Tribute Artiste Champion at Graceland and the European Elvis Champion. He is also known for winning Stars In Their Eyes and has performed around the world. The King's Voice takes audiences on a journey through Elvis Presley's career, from the famous 1968 Comeback Special to the legendary Las Vegas performances. Featuring classic songs, iconic costumes and the energy of a live concert, the show celebrates the music and style of one of the most influential performers in popular music history. Endorsed by Elvis Presley Enterprises, the production has earned a reputation for capturing the sound and spirit of Elvis on stage. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: An award-winning tribute celebrating the music and legacy of Elvis Presley.

title: LISZT in Taunton: Julian Trevelyan – International Prize-Winning Pianist
subtitle: Award-winning pianist Julian Trevelyan performs a programme of works by Liszt and Rachmaninov, alongside piano transcriptions inspired by the music of Schubert. A former BBC Young Musician finalist, Trevelyan is recognised as one of the UK's leading young classical pianists.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Julian Trevelyan, one of the UK's most accomplished young pianists, brings his internationally acclaimed artistry to Taunton for a recital featuring virtuoso piano works by Liszt and Rachmaninov, alongside piano transcriptions inspired by the compositions of Schubert. A former chorister of St Alban's Cathedral, Julian was a finalist in the 2014 BBC Young Musician Competition. At just sixteen years old he was awarded second prize at the prestigious Concours Long-Thibaud-Crespin, with no first prize being awarded. He has since received further international recognition as a prize winner in the Concours Géza Anda and as a finalist in the 2024 Leeds International Piano Competition.
tagline: Acclaimed pianist Julian Trevelyan performs music by Liszt, Rachmaninov and Schubert.

title: ⭐The Grand Pier - Weston Super Mare
subtitle: The Grand Pier is open every day, except Christmas Day, so come hail, rain or shine, you’ll always get a warm welcome. Whatever the weather is doing outside, it’s still fun, fun, fun on the inside.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The Grand Pier, Weston super Mare, Somerset is the ideal destination for non-stop indoor family theme park fun. This North Somerset pier, with its state-of-the-art Pavilion is a truly iconic destination for family days out, events, concerts, weddings, and corporate events. With rides, attractions and the latest arcade games a visit to the Pier is the perfect treat for kids of all ages. On weekends, bank holidays and North Somerset school holidays, Unlimited Ride Wristbands are available for both adults and children, explore here . Don't miss out on this fantastic deal for your fun-filled day! Come and discover everything the Grand Pier, Somerset has to offer, including: · The very latest amusements - including giant screen Space Invaders · Thrilling rides including: Sidewinder, Freefall and Robocoaster · An amazing two level 300 meter indoor Go-Kart track · Seaside favourites, including: dodgems, house of horrors and helter skelter · A three-level, dinosaur themed soft play area with dedicated adult seating · A choice of places to eat and drink - we even serve your favourite Costa coffee! With hundreds of amusements and games to play, a range of thrilling rides, and a choice of attractions for all ages everyone gets to have fun in the amazing Pavilion - it really is one big house of fun!!! When you’re ready for a bite to eat you’re spoilt for choice from traditional fish and chips to afternoon tea, and of course ice cream too! There’s even a pub for you to enjoy a relaxing drink as you take in the spectacular views. As a unique location our function rooms are always in demand, and we love creating the perfect setting for weddings and family celebrations. For businesses our dedicated events team is on hand for corporate events, ranging from team meetings and training sessions to large scale conferences.The fun continues into the night with a wide range of events from concerts to whodunnits. To make sure you don’t miss out visit and book your tickets online today.

title: East Cottage
subtitle: This gorgeous holiday cottage, which dates back to the 17th century, has an abundance of period features and traditional English country charm.
bodyContent: This gorgeous holiday cottage, which dates back to the 17th century, has an abundance of period features and traditional English country charm. This is tastefully combined with the provision of all the modern conveniences that you would expect to find in a 5 star cottage. The standard of the accommodation at East Cottage reflects our very high expectations of quality, cleanliness, attention to detail and service. Our charming holiday cottage is set in a beautiful rural location; lots of fresh air, farmland and farm animals with great walks and country pubs on the doorstep – always a good combination for keeping children, and parents (!) amused. The cottage itself has many lovely attributes. On the ground floor is the beamed living/dining-room with open inglenook fireplace, exposed stone walls and stone mullion windows, as well as TV, DVD and IPod dock; well-equipped kitchen with fridge, freezer, gas hob, electric oven and microwave; and utility room with washing-machine and dishwasher. A beautiful stone spiral staircase leads up to the first floor to the 2 large double bedrooms and bathroom with WC, washbasin, bath and separate shower cubicle. Again, beams, mullion windows and charming features in abundance! The cottage sleeps 4 (plus cot) in two bedrooms comprising 1 with king size double bed, and the other which can either be made up as a super king size double, or with 2 twin single beds. The cottage is therefore ideal for both families with children, or for couples trying to escape them! Children of all ages are welcome at East Cottage. A travel cot is provided, as well as stair-gates and high chair. We provide a baby-changing mat and baby bath, and there is also a toy box and a selection of games, jigsaws, books and DVDs. The cottage has gas central heating and free Wi-Fi. Towels are provided, as well as tea towels, toiletries, quality bed linen and an initial supply of logs for cosy nights in by the fire. We also provide basics such as tea, coffee, milk, sugar and cake! There are 2 parking spaces for the exclusive use of guests staying at East Cottage in the courtyard to the right of the cottage. Behind the courtyard, a small flight of steps leads to the private, secluded and gated garden. The well-established walled garden includes lawned areas, herbaceous borders and a south-facing patio, ideal for ‘al fresco’ dining. We also provide a barbeque and a supply of charcoal. The cottage is about 100 yards walking distance of the village shop, which sells local produce,and 300 yards to the wonderful village pub. The cottage is available for hire for a minimum of 2 nights. However in July & August it is let for whole weeks only, Saturday to Saturday. Please email or phone direct for tariff and seasonal offers. We look forward to welcoming you soon!
tagline: The standard of the accommodation at East Cottage reflects our very high expectations

title: Flavours of the Mediterranean
subtitle: Flavours restaurant is a celebration of the rich, diverse, and vibrant cuisine that the Mediterranean region has to offer.
bodyContent: Indulge your senses in a culinary journey. At Flavours, we invite you to savour the enchanting delights of the Mediterranean, right here in Wellington. Our restaurant is a celebration of the rich, diverse, and vibrant cuisine that the Mediterranean region has to offer. Our Story Your host and Head Chef Herman, comes from Turkey and has created a haven for food enthusiasts seeking an authentic taste of the Mediterranean. Our journey begins with a simple yet profound idea – to bring the warmth and richness of Mediterranean cuisine to your table. Our passionate chefs have roamed the shores of Greece, Italy, Spain, Turkey, and beyond to bring you a menu that’s as diverse as the Mediterranean itself. A Feast for the Senses Our menu is a reflection of the region’s bountiful produce, aromatic spices, and centuries-old cooking traditions. From the smoky allure of grilled kebabs to the vibrant flavours of sun-kissed tomatoes, olives, and olive oil, every bite is a journey through this ancient and cherished culinary heritage. Wine and Spirits Complement your meal with an extensive selection of Mediterranean wines and spirits. We take pride in curating a wine list that perfectly harmonizes with our dishes, enhancing your dining experience. Warm Ambiance Our restaurant’s warm and welcoming ambiance is reminiscent of Mediterranean hospitality. Whether you’re dining with family, friends, or that special someone, our cosy and inviting space will make you feel right at home. Take a Culinary Journey with Us Flavours of the Mediterranean is not just a restaurant; it’s a voyage through the Mediterranean’s enticing and diverse culinary landscape. Join us for an unforgettable experience filled with the Flavours of the Mediterranean. Book your table today and let your taste buds embark on a journey they won’t soon forget. We look forward to sharing our love for Mediterranean cuisine with you.

title: Taunton Flower Show 2026
subtitle: Experience a festival atmosphere at the oldest flower show in the country, set in the heart of Taunton.
bodyContent: Taunton Flower Show is an annual two-day family show held on the first Friday and Saturday of August each year, attracting around 16,000 visitors over the two days. Established in 1831, Taunton Flower Show is the longest running Flower Show in the UK, and second oldest in the World. Set in the lovely surrounds of Vivary Park, the Show is a feast for all the family. Our fantastic competition marquee shows off the talents of our community and the floral marquee and designer gardens demonstrate national horticultural excellence. You will also find music, arena entertainment, local and national traders and fun for all the family. Save by purchasing your tickets in advance and enjoy a brilliant day out! Assistance dogs only allowed into the showground. Tickets on sale at Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: A vibrant festival surrounded by flowers

title: Remembrance Sunday in Wellington
subtitle: The Remembrance Sunday service is held in Wellington Park at 3.15pm.
bodyContent: The Remembrance Sunday service is held in Wellington Park, led by the Royal British Legion Wellington Branch, and takes place from 3:15 in Wellington Park. The parade marches to the park from Wellington School - they step off for this at 2:55. They then march back to the school following the conclusion of the service. Please note that rolling road closures will be in effect whilst the parade marches and those affected are very much thanked for their patience.

title: An Audience with Jules Hudson
subtitle: Join television presenter Jules Hudson for an evening of conversation, stories and reflections from a career spanning three decades in broadcasting. Best known for Escape to the Country, Jules shares insights from television, countryside life and Britain's heritage.
bodyContent: 2026 marks thirty years in television for Jules Hudson, and there’s a lot to talk about. Best known as the longest-serving presenter on the BBC’s multi-award-winning Escape to the Country, Jules has also been a Countryfile regular for over a decade, a field archaeologist, a Naval Reserve officer, a furniture maker, and now an author. His autobiography, Wild at Heart: My Journey to a Country Life, publishes this year, making this the perfect moment to see him live on stage. Jules grew up meeting people from every walk of life in his mother’s B&B, and that warmth has always defined his broadcasting style. In conversation he ranges across television, archaeology, military history, country living, craft, and Britain’s landscape and heritage, all delivered with the good humour that’s made him a household name. His credits include Escape to the Country, Countryfile, Dig 1940, Dive WW2 and How We Won the War (BBC), On The Farm (Channel 5) and Defenders of the Sky (History Channel). Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre

title: Talent Gallery
subtitle: Talent Gallery is a beautifully curated and well stocked Gallery in the heart of Wellington. Nina king, owner and resident artist, has her open studio there. Nina runs workshops and loves inspiring people to get creative. The space is full of beautiful art and handcrafted gift ideas, that suit all budgets.
bodyContent: Nina King took over Talent Gallery in June 2024, and it is going from strength to strength. Her vision for the Talent Gallery is to promote Art by our great local artists and artisans, to provide a space for them to exhibit their work and to make that work accessible and available, reaching out to welcome the whole community, for all to enjoy. The gallery supports around 30 local regular and guest artists/artisans with art exhibitions changing every 6 weeks. The gallery is beautifully curated and well-stocked. Customer service is very important to us, and we love making every customer feel welcome. The gallery has a seating area where customers are welcome to sit to view the art and enjoy the atmosphere. The gallery is family and dog friendly, welcoming people to come and browse without feeling pressured to buy. Nina is running successful ‘learn how to paint in Acrylics’ workshops and has plans to expand her workshops into other areas – watch this space! As a successful artist, Nina also exhibits her own work there, and you will find a selection of her new originals, framed & unframed Giclee prints. She also offers commissions. Occasionally Nina branches out into clay and other handmade gifts. She has an open studio within the gallery, where you are welcome to browse and maybe even watch her painting! Nina loves living and working in Wellington, Somerset and she feels happy knowing that the gallery is part of a growing art scene in the area.

title: The Sixties Roadshow
subtitle: Take a trip back to the swinging sixties with The Sixties Roadshow, a live music show celebrating some of the most iconic British and American artists of the decade. Featuring classic hits and a talented live band, the show recreates the sound and spirit of a memorable era of music.

title: John Bishop Live in Taunton
subtitle: One of the UK's best-known comedians, John Bishop, returns to the stage for a special open-air performance at the Cooper Associates County Ground. Joining him for the evening will be fellow comedians Justin Moorhouse and Sally-Anne Hayward.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Comedy fans are in for a rare treat as John Bishop returns to the stage for one night only at the Cooper Associates County Ground. Part of the Stuff on the Stage Festival, the event marks Bishop's first headlining UK performance since 2025. Known for his storytelling, quick wit and observational humour, Bishop has become one of the UK's most popular stand-up comedians, performing sell-out arena tours across the country. Joining John Bishop on the night will be comedians Justin Moorhouse and Sally-Anne Hayward, making this a packed evening of live comedy under the stars. Tickets available on their website

title: Mickey Market

Whether you’re looking to find a prized item or simply enjoy a day out, the event offers something for everyone. Visitors can explore a marketplace filled with traders, discover collectibles and merchandise, and enjoy a shared experience with others who have a passion for Disney. title: 5 Mistakes That Changed History
subtitle: 5 Mistakes That Changed History is a live show blending comedy, storytelling and history. Exploring how small and large mistakes shaped the world, it delivers an entertaining and insightful experience.
bodyContent: 5 Mistakes That Changed History is a hilarious historical storytelling show performed by historian and comedian, Paul Coulter, about five people and how their mistakes (big and small!) changed the world. Blending history, storytelling and comedy the show has been a smash-hit, sell-out success on the comedy festival circuit, selling out both Edinburgh Festival Fringe and Adelaide Fringe Festival three years in a row in 2023, 2024 and 2025. Suitable for history lovers of all ages the show was named by British Comedy Guide as one of the ‘Best Reviewed Edinburgh Fringe Shows’ and was chosen as one of the ‘Picks of the Fringe’. Paul is the author of the bestseller ’10 Mistakes That Changed History’ published by Penguin Random House in 2025. Paul has appeared on air talking about History’s greatest mistakes on BBC World News, BBC Radio 2, BBC Radio 5, BBC Radio London and Times Radio. If you love history, don’t let your mistake be missing out on this show! Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre

title: Andy Ford: Alright My Luvver?!
subtitle: West Country comedian Andy Ford returns with Alright My Luvver?!, a comedy show packed with laughter, storytelling and the humour that has made him a popular entertainer across the South West.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Andy Ford brings his latest comedy show, Alright My Luvver?!, to the Tacchi-Morris Arts Centre. Drawing on more than five decades of experience as a performer, the much-loved comedian delivers an evening of comedy, stories and observations in his distinctive style. Best known across the South West for his stage work and pantomime appearances, Andy has entertained audiences throughout his career as a singer, comedian and performer. His television appearances include ITV's Big Big Talent Show, which led to an invitation to perform at the Royal Variety Show. Described as uplifting and full of humour, this live show offers an opportunity to see one of the region's most familiar entertainers on stage. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: An evening of comedy and laughter with West Country entertainer Andy Ford.

title: Olive and Rosy
subtitle: Olive and Rosy tucked away down on North Street is home to a collection of carefully curated food and fashion inspired by the tastes, slower pace and aesthetics of Italy. Stefano and Rachael have been bringing a little of the Italian experience to Wellington since December 2016.
bodyContent: Often described as a ‘hidden gem’, many visitors are surprised by how much there is to discover behind those small windows. With two floors to explore, you are encouraged to slow down, take your time, have a browse through their recipe and style books or try some samples of fresh produce before you buy should you wish. Downstairs the little Italian store offers you authentic food and wines - a small but mighty collection of delicious produce, from Stefano's best loved staples to new and exclusive finds. Everything is chosen with attention to its taste, quality and product story. The deli has become particularly popular for its range of olive oils, pastries, speciality cheeses and accompaniments plus sharing platters made to order. Olive and Rosy are regulars at Wellington’s markets and outdoor events, when fresh focaccia and pizza is also available. If you are planning a weekend visit to the park, why not call in on the way and pick up some picnic treats? The clothing boutique upstairs replicates the same careful consideration of story and quality, with a collection of garments ranging through sustainable, natural, upcycled or pre-loved boutique brands. Think loved linens, restored cashmere, vintage inspired prints and that classic Italian flair! Olive and Rosy also sell your pre-owned clothing for you and help to otherwise rehome no-longer-worn pieces through hosting regular Clothes Swap events within the town.

title: Bridgwater Guy Fawkes Carnival
subtitle: Experience one of Somerset's most famous traditions as Bridgwater Guy Fawkes Carnival returns with its spectacular illuminated procession. Featuring elaborate carnival carts, performers, music and entertainment, the event attracts thousands of visitors each year.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Bridgwater Guy Fawkes Carnival is the UK's oldest carnival and one of Europe's largest illuminated carnival processions. Each year, carnival clubs spend months creating spectacular illuminated entries featuring thousands of lights, costumes, music and special effects. The procession transforms Bridgwater's streets into a moving display of creativity and entertainment, with around 100 entries taking part. Visitors can enjoy a full day of activity in the town before the evening procession gets underway. The celebrations begin with a fireworks display on Friday evening, followed by the main carnival procession on Saturday. The event traditionally concludes with the famous Squibbing display in Bridgwater High Street. See their website for more information
tagline: A spectacular illuminated carnival procession through the streets of Bridgwater.

title: Shakspeare Glass & Arts
subtitle: Visit Shakspeare Glass for one of a kind handblown glass pieces from master glassblower Will Shakspeare, and a gallery with unique pieces from a selection of other British makers. Enjoy a slice of cake and a coffee while you’re here, with the best views in Langport!
bodyContent: Overlooking the River Parrett, Shakspeare Glass & Arts is home to one of the finest master glassblowers in the country. Will Shakspeare creates individual pieces of handblown glass drawn from his influences of the Somerset countryside and coast. Browse the Gallery and shop for unique heirloom pieces and gifts, including works from other selected makers. A range of Will’s bespoke glass lighting, including chandeliers, pendant and wall lights are on display throughout the workshop and Gallery and are also available to order online . The coffee shop offers a variety of cakes and coffee and teas, and the perfect views across the river. It’s the ideal place to meet with friends and sit on the decking on a bright day, and during certain times, you can watch Will as he goes about his craft, blowing glass at the furnace. Will has been creating and making his own inimitable glassware for more than 30 and is one of the country’s most collected makers. He also offers occasional demonstration evenings and one-to-one glassblower workshops which are advertised through the website and on the Shakspeare Glass social media channels.
tagline: Visit Shakspeare Glass for one of a kind handblown glass pieces

title: Lesser Litter
subtitle: We are Kate and Pete, and are proud to be part of the Taunton & Somerset community. We want to give the people of Taunton a positive option for shopping ethically, organically and packaging free.
bodyContent: We see Lesser Litter as part of the solution to the huge environmental issues we, as a community and as a planet, face. We believe in reusing packaging, circular supply and supporting sustainable organic farming practices. Shopping ethically should be accessible for everyone. We firmly believe this should be more economical, both for the individual and for the environment. We sell a range of groceries - we mostly sell organic and pride ourselves on competing with the major supermarkets and brands on price. Where we can, we offer British and local options. Currently everything in store is vegan, except for the sustainably and responsibly sourced honey, beeswax wraps and sunscreen.
tagline: Offering a positive option for shopping ethically, organically and packaging free.

title: Chew Stoke
subtitle: CHEW STOKE has a population of around a 1000 and lies at the foot of the Mendip Hills – designated an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.
bodyContent: CHEW STOKE has a population of around a 1000 and lies at the foot of the Mendip Hills – designated an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The village sits at the northern end of Chew Valley Lake, 9 miles south of Bristol, 11 miles north of wells and 12 miles west of Bath . Listed in the Domesday Book as Chiwestoche the suggestion is it may have had some military connection at the time – the name “Stoke” comes from the old English stoc meaning a stockade. This lengthy history is reflected in the number of heritage listed buildings throughout the Chew Valley. The long established Stoke Inn and the welcoming restaurant the Chew Kitchen sit close to the village centre. There are two lakeside restaurants, The Salt and Malt (specialising in fish and chips) and Woodford Lodge. The community includes a primary school, a medical centre and GP’s surgery, the multi-use Church Hall, and boasts a number of flourishing clubs and societies. Bed and breakfast accommodation is catered for by Orchard House and the Stoke Inn . The buildings at Fairseat Farm , once a working dairy, have been converted to office and workshop use – spaces which include a hairdressing salon, a joinery, an artist’s studio, an osteopath practice, a flower design shop, and a TV and video business. A century old national cycling route – the Bristol to Padstow West Country Way – is still popular with cyclists and runs through the village The village’s substantial claim to history, is its double century association with the BILBIE FAMILY – clock makers and bell founders, who lived and worked in Chew Stoke from the late 17th to late 19th century. The family cast 1350 bells for churches all over the west country and the south west. The oldest surviving bell, cast in 1698, is still working in the village church of St Andrew. CHEW STOKE CHURCH HALL is situated on the corner of Church Lane. It is used for church events, and by a number of village organisations – including the Parish Council, the WI, Chew Stoke Film Club, the Dramatic Society, Scissors Exercise Class, the Hall Singers and Chew Valley Choral Society. Insured and licensed for 100 people, the hall is available for hire by individuals, clubs and societies; and is an ideal venue for public meetings, private events, suppers, parties and wedding receptions. Every month it plays host to the Majestic , the village Neighbourhood Cinema, supported by the British Film Institute and the National Lottery. For more church hall details, facilities and booking arrangements, visit www.chewstokechurchhall.org.uk For village information, news, events, activities and celebrations, visit chewstoke.org.uk

title: Circus of Horrors: The Witch
subtitle: The Circus of Horrors is back with its latest incarnation ‘THE WITCH’ – A sensational new phantasmagoria which encompasses amazing and bizarre circus acts with an original rock score, and a sinister story of Witchcraft - the darkest of magic - and includes the legendary Witch trials and even a burning at the stake.
bodyContent: When the Circus of Horrors began 26 years ago at Glastonbury 1995 many people thought it wouldn’t last 26 weeks let alone 26 years. But with its ability to reinvent itself time and time again it has taken the extreme to the mainstream and become a household name after reaching the finals of Britain’s Got Talent and performing in London’s West End. Whether a Rock fan or theatre gore The Circus of Horrors has something for everyone. Imagine a brilliant rock show combined with amazing, bizarre & dare devil Circus acts, a stellar light show and all performed with a forked tongue firmly in each cheek. If Quentin Tarantino had directed Cirque Du Soleil you would be half-way there. Celebrity Quotes: 'It was phenomenal, one of those shows that if you missed you would say Gosh I wish I could have seen that'. title: Brazier Coffee Roasters
subtitle: Brazier Coffee Roasters is nestled in a historic red-brick building at the Tonedale Mill Site. The flagship café is open 7 days a week, and is situated next to their roasting plant, where they roast coffee for their wholesale customers (open to the public Monday-Friday).
bodyContent: “Our coffee story began on a hot afternoon in the dusty centre of Australia, where Claire’s from. Drinking fabulous coffee in the outback, we talked of how there was nothing similar in our corner of England, and decided to do something about it. After much tasting, talking and training with some of the best roasters in Australia, we bought our own Giesen roaster, and set up in the Somerset county side in 2015. Ten years later, and we’re now based at the heart of the Fox’s Tonedale Mill site in Wellington, with our roastery and on-site cafe breathing new life into this historic site. We’re passionate about sourcing, roasting and sharing exceptional coffees. From Seed to Cup. Tom & Claire Brazier

Now in its 20th year, the show continues to entertain audiences with its combination of recognisable songs, colourful costumes and energetic performances from the cast. A brand-new production for 2025 adds a fresh element while staying true to the original spirit of the music. title: West Somerset Railway Forties Event 2026
subtitle: Expect a spectacular weekend bursting with the sights, sounds, and spirit of the 1940s!
bodyContent: Expect a spectacular weekend bursting with the sights, sounds, and spirit of the 1940s! From the moment you arrive, you’ll be swept into a world of swinging music, vintage charm, and wartime nostalgia. Enjoy a dazzling line-up of live musical performances, meet wonderfully costumed characters, and discover a host of exciting events taking place at stations all along the line. Each stop offers its own unique slice of 1940s magic - so be sure to explore them all! Travel couldn’t be easier - your adventure is completely flexible with our rover tickets, letting you hop on and off trains throughout the day. Even better, Annual Passes are valid during this fantastic weekend, as it’s a standard fare event. For the best value, we recommend purchasing rover tickets in advance to receive a discount on your tickets. On-the-day prices are £38 per adult and £19 per child. Prefer a shorter journey? Intermediate station tickets and simple return fares are also available to purchase on the day, either at the booking office or onboard the train. And as the sun sets, the celebrations continue! Our ever-popular Saturday night platform dance returns to Minehead station - promising an evening of toe-tapping tunes, lively dancing, and vintage glamour under the stars. With multiple musical acts bringing the era to life, it’s the perfect way to end your day in true 1940s style. (Please note: a separate ticket is required for the dance.) Don your finest vintage attire, bring your dancing shoes, and get ready for a weekend that truly captures the magic of the 1940s! We have the option of a discounted two day ticket to visit for both days of the event! To purchase a ticket for two days, please select 'Book Now' on the Saturday date below. This will take you to a screen which will allow you to select the second day only, therefore you need to add the Sunday to your booking. Once selected, you will see a box that says 'return to basket'. Select this and you will see both days added. Please make sure you have the two correct days selected before heading to the check out.
tagline: Expect a spectacular weekend bursting with the sights, sounds, and spirit of the 1940s!

title: Arrival – The Hits of ABBA
subtitle: Arrival – The Hits of ABBA returns with a brand-new production celebrating the music of one of pop’s most iconic bands. Featuring classic songs and an immersive performance style, the show offers a lively and engaging experience.
bodyContent: 50 years since ABBA’s iconic ‘Arrival’ album first lit up the charts, the multi-award-winning show that shares the same name, Arrival – The Hits of ABBA, is back with a brand-new production! This year, the show is more immersive than ever. Alongside even more songs from the landmark ‘Arrival’ album and the addition of interactive video projection, you can sing along to the lyrics on screen at the top of your lungs and become part of the performance! With sensational vocals, expert musicianship, dazzling costumes, and breathtaking visuals, Arrival – The Hits of ABBA takes you on an unforgettable journey through the timeless music that changed pop history. From the Eurovision-winning ‘Waterloo’ to infectious disco anthems like ‘Gimme! Gimme! Gimme!’, ‘Mamma Mia’, ‘Voulez-Vous’, and ‘Fernando’, every song will have you dancing in the aisles and singing along with pure joy and nostalgia! Whether you’ve been a fan since day one or are discovering their magic for the first time, this is the ultimate celebration of a legendary band and the ‘Arrival’ album that helped define an era. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: An immersive ABBA tribute packed with classic hits, visuals and singalong moments.

title: Pilgrimage of Hope
subtitle: A young violinist’s “Pilgrimage of Hope” sees him perform in churches across the UK and Europe, using music to raise funds and spread a message of faith and hope.
bodyContent: a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; } Anthony Knight, a young violinist studying at the Royal College of Music, has undertaken a “Pilgrimage of Hope”, performing in churches across the UK and Europe to raise money for charity. His journey began in 2022, when he chose to use his musical talent to support fundraising efforts, initially focusing on the Ukraine appeal. Starting with performances in Somerset, he visited dozens of churches and raised significant funds, later expanding his project internationally. His travels have taken him to multiple countries, performing in a wide range of church settings while continuing to support charitable causes. Alongside the performances, Knight encourages audiences to reflect and engage with the music in a meaningful way, using his recitals to promote a message of hope and unity. His work has been widely recognised, and he continues to perform as part of an ongoing journey combining music, faith and charitable fundraising. Donations in aid of UNICEF
tagline: A young violinist shares his journey using music to raise funds and inspire hope.

title: Westfield
subtitle: The parish of Westfield surrounds an ancient Roman Road, the Fosseway. Although Westfield was not named in the Domesday Book it finally got its full identity when it was named as a Civil Parish in 2011. Positioned between the towns of Midsomer Norton and Radstock, Westfield is emerging as a true community with a character all of its own.
bodyContent: The parish of Westfield surrounds an ancient Roman Road, the Fosseway. Although Westfield was not named in the Domesday Book it finally got its full identity when it was named as a Civil Parish in 2011. Positioned between the towns of Midsomer Norton and Radstock, Westfield is emerging as a true community with a character all of its own. By the early nineteenth century Westfield still consisted mostly of rural land and coal mining works, with little residential development. Westfield’s unique street scene emerged with the building of large numbers of terraced miners' cottages along the Fosse Way in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries and the area developed into a more populous neighbourhood in its own right. Modern housing estates were developed on land on both sides of the Fosse Way from the 1970’s onwards. Industrial coal mining was established in 1763 and for two centuries was the major employer in the area. There were three mines in Westfield, two at Norton Hill and one in Wellsway. In the early nineteenth century, whilst Westfield was still very rural, a large three storey building was built immediately adjacent to the main Fosse Way. This property still exists and is now a listed building. Many rumours have grown up about the purpose of the building – was it a private house of maybe an Isolation Hospital for Bath patients? It was called Westfield House. Through the late nineteenth century and twentieth century the population of Westfield grew very quickly. Work was varied from coal mining, canal work, railway and haulage work, shoemaking and printing. All these industries have long gone but, despite this, Westfield is still very much a thriving parish. Currently there is a large industrial estate which is constantly growing and developing, providing local employment. Things to do: Heritage walks Westfield has three heritage walks of different levels, from an easy stroll to slightly rougher terrain, designed to open up and show off the beautiful parish. Along the way walkers will be able to read up on boards dedicated to the history of where they are standing. The trails take in, among other things, a former pit path, two Second World War pill boxes and old engine house and pit pony stables, thought to be the only such stables left in the country and two churches. Recreation grounds Westfield Parish Council is responsible for two recreation grounds that were donated to the parish by miners’ trusts back in the time of coal mining for the recreation of miners and their families. Norton Hill Recreation Ground on the Fosseway has a football pitch for hire, with changing facilities, a tennis court, boules pitch, permanent table tennis table and basketball hoop, as well as a children’s play area. Westhill Recreation Ground, Westhill Road, has a football pitch for hire, with changing facilities at Westhill Club, a BMX track and children’s play area. There is ample free parking at both sites. Bowls There are two bowls clubs in Westfield – NorWest Bowls at Norton Hill Recreation Ground, 01761 410861, https://sites.google.com/site/norwestbowlingclub/home . Norwest has a lane for casual use if you call ahead, and Prattens on Charlton Lane, contact 01761 412705, Barry Dando, Chairman https://prattensbowlsclub.com/ . title: Treasure Island
subtitle: Treasure Island is a festive adventure filled with music, laughter and storytelling. Following a young hero’s journey at sea, the production brings a classic tale to life with energy and imagination.
bodyContent: Will you risk everything for gold? Or is some treasure worth more than money? Jim Hawkins is growing up in the salt-aired historic harbour town of Watchet on the coast of West Somerset, but wants more from life than one day becoming the owner of the family B&B. The arrival of a mysterious sailor and the treasure map he brings with him turns Jim’s ordinary world upside down. Home comforts are soon a distant memory as Jim is aboard a ship bound for who knows where in search of stolen gold, sailing alongside a crew of colourful rogues, brave adventurers, and one utterly unforgettable, silver-tongued pirate: Long John Silver. Digging for buried treasure brings many things to the surface and Jim must face a question that no map can answer. Bursting with rousing folk music, crashing waves, daring adventures, and a great deal of laughter, this is a story about loyalty, courage, and the most important journey of all – growing up and working out what really matters. Tickets on sale at the Taunton Visitor Centre
tagline: A festive adventure filled with pirates, music and a high-energy retelling of a classic tale.
