title: Murder Mystery Events 2026
subtitle: Calling all amateur sleuths!!
bodyContent: Full Stop - Murder! - 26th September 2026 It's 1929. The next train might be delayed - there’s a dead body in the Waiting Room! Travel writer, Miles Suppertrak has written his final chapter but which of his travelling companions is cutting short his career? Is publisher Mac Millan pressed for a deadline? Is fiancée Bree Fenn-Cownter hiding something in her dust jacket? Or is secretary, Celia Wholesupp looking for something between the covers? Duration: 3 hours Location: Departs from Bishops Lydeard, travels to Minehead and returns. Booking: Advanced booking is essential, as spaces are limited. Accessibility: We are unable to accommodate mobility scooters and wheelchairs on these services. If you have any accessibility requirements, please give us a call on 01643 704996. Dogs: Please note that no dogs are permitted on this service, with the exception of assistance dogs. Please advise us of this in advance when making your booking. Calling all amateur sleuths!! Do you see yourself as Miss Marple, Hercule Poirot or Sherlock Holmes? Well, the West Somerset Railway's Murder Mystery season is a must for all you amateur crime fighters! As you go peacefully about your train journey, the actors will be staging a murderous tale for you to solve. Apart from the dastardly doings, your steam train ride will also include fish and chips, plus a drink served at your seat on the outward journey. There will also be Styles ice cream served as you travel back to Bishops Lydeard. The entertainment begins on the platform (Bishops Lydeard) promptly at 19:00. Boarding is from 18:45. Passengers should arrive in good time to find their seats and leave the train again for the first scene on the platform. The dress code is 'smart casual' and we encourage you to enter the spirit of the event by dressing in appropriate period costume if you desire! Please be aware due to the nature of the stock, we are unable to accommodate mobility scooters and wheelchairs on these specials. If you have any accessible requirements, please do give us a call on 01643 704996. These evenings are not suitable for children. Please note that no dogs are permitted on this service, with the exception of assistance dogs. Please advise us of this in advance when making your booking. The food options for the Murder Mystery Specials are: Standard Fish and Chips Jumbo Sausage and Chips Chicken and Chips (gluten free option) Vegetarian Burger and Chips Halloumi fries and Chips (gluten free option) Palm Oil is used for all frying. The drinks options for the Murder Mystery Specials are: WSR Quantock Steamer Ale, an amber beer served in a 440ml can with an 3.8% ABV Thatcher’s Gold Cider 440ml Can 4.8% ABV Carlsberg Lager Pint Can 3.4% ABV Red Wine Hidden Road Merlot 187ml 11% Vol Rose Wine Hidden Road White Zinfandel 187ml 10.5% White Wine Pinot Grigio 187ml 11% Pink Gin & tonic can 250ml 5% Vol Orange Juice Apple Juice Bottle of Water Upon booking your tickets, these options will appear in a tick box format. Please select one menu option and one drink option for each person travelling. Please note that the times are approximate and may change. If this is the case, we will contact you by email.
tagline: Calling all amateur sleuths!!

title: Ham Hill Cider
subtitle: We produce award winning ciders here at North Down Farm, crafted from apples produced in some of Somerset’s finest orchards. We are proud to carry out every step in making cider from pruning through pressing and fermentation to bottling and delivering the final product. Come and join us to experience the true taste of Somerset.
bodyContent: At Ham Hill Cider, our aim is to create ciders that are rich in flavour and refreshingly appley. We believe we’ve cracked it. We press only the finest apples, that are grown within 5 miles of Ham Hill, and fully ripened by the late summer sun. We take the juice and carefully craft it into a range of premium ciders, to satisfy the tastes of those in search of something special. It is characteristically Somerset in style, with rich flavours, soft tannins and a hint of apple sharpness, which makes for an easy drinking refreshing cider that appeals to the contemporary taste, while remaining true to our heritage. Tree, we have the privilege of tending some of the finest orchards in Somerset. We prune and plant trees during the winter months, wait for mother nature to do her work over spring and summer and then pick the apples in the autumn. Juice, we use over 25 apple varieties, including, Dabinett, Sweet Coppin, Chisel Jersey, Yarlington Mill and Kingston Black, pressing each variety at their peak of ripeness for maximum flavour. Magic, we allow only the naturally occurring wild yeast to work on our ciders, which means relying on the magic of nature to do its work. With fermentation underway we wait for the first cuckoo of spring to announce the cider has matured is ready for drinking! Cider, the best part of the process is that long anticipated first taste of the new cider and the realisation that the all the hard work was worth it. Ciderworks, to enjoy our ciders at their best join us on a Friday night at the Ciderworks taproom. Our full range of ciders are on tap, and you can take a look around next door where we make them, we provide seasonal home cooked food every week with regular specials of whatever the farm can provide. We also have regular live music nights. Follow us on social media for an up to date programme of events. We are four sons of Somerset with a passion for the press and we welcome you to Ham Hill Cider.
tagline: We produce award winning ciders here at North Down Farm

title: Radstock
subtitle: Radstock is renowned as one of the best preserved former coal-mining towns in England which is the basis of its conservation status. Much more can be learnt with a visit to Radstock Museum which houses a range of exhibits, giving visitors the opportunity to immerse themselves in the town’s industrial and social history.
bodyContent: Nestled on the edge of the Mendips , Radstock has access to spectacular routes for both walking and cycling with quiet country lanes and beautiful countryside. It is home to the Radstock Museum where a wide range of exhibits give an insight into much of Radstock’s varied history and geology.and close to Writhlington School, notable for its orchid collection which has won numerous awards and houses the largest collection of orchids outside of Kew Gardens. There's so much more to discover about Radstock.

title: The Royal Hotel Weston
subtitle: The Royal Hotel is a charismatic and elegant Georgian Building, is ideally located on the Seafront. Standing in its own extensive lawns, which extend to the Promenade, the Royal enjoys beautiful sea views, and is also in close proximity to our Town Centre and accessible by public transport.
bodyContent: The Royal Hotel is a charismatic and elegant Georgian Building, is ideally located on the Seafront. Standing in its own extensive lawns, which extend to the Promenade, the Royal enjoys beautiful sea views, and is also in close proximity to our Town Centre and accessible by public transport. The 44 attractive and comfortable rooms here at The Royal, feature ensuite bathrooms, Freeview TV, Tea & Coffee making facilities, Dressing Table/Desk, Direct-dial telephone, Hairdryer, Trouser press and complimentary toiletries. Wi-Fi is complimentary throughout the hotel. Newspapers and early morning wake up calls are available on request. Due to our fantastic location, all bedrooms boast lovely views of either Weston Seafront, The picturesque Italian Gardens, or the bustling Town Square. We provide a wide range of accommodation, choose from the following options….Doubles, Singles, Twins, Four Posters, Family Rooms that sleep 4-6, and our impeccable, brand new range of Royal Luxury Doubles! Disabled access is plentiful throughout the ground floor facilities, including the Bar & Restaurant. There is a lift to both floors, as well as disabled friendly bedrooms featuring a specialised wet-room. Please contact us to discuss any special requirements you may need. Our comfortable and traditional Feathers Bar is open daily for Drinks, Real Ales, Snacks, Afternoon Tea and Coffees. Enjoy a game of pool, or relax into a comfy sofa with a paper and a glass of wine. Friday night is party night in Feathers with a range of regular entertainment to kick off the weekend! Our Award Winning Restaurant epitomises the elegant regency style for which Weston was formally renowned. In these captivating surroundings you can enjoy dishes carefully selected for our appealing menu which has been designed to tempt and excite all tastes. Open for Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner every day, with our famous Carvery available Tuesdays, Thursdays – and of course, Sundays. This charming Georgian Hotel is renowned as Weston’s premier wedding venue, due to our first class reputation built on the outstanding reviews from the many bride and grooms whose weddings we have planned and hosted. Our Ballroom boasts idyllic sea views across Weston Bay and our extensive lawn with its sweeping bay windows makes it the perfect setting for a romantic Wedding. We hold a Civil Wedding & Civil Partnership licence, enabling you to simplify your arrangements by holding all aspects of your special day in one venue. For more information why not take a look at our Wedding Brochure online, or download our brand new & exclusive Wedding App for smart phones and tablets. For any questions, or to book a viewing, please contact our Wedding & Events team at the hotel. Hair Salon Pin-ups Hair Salon promises a ‘different vibe’ to other hairdressers and Owner Kaysha says it will definitely be a cut above the rest! Customers can expect a relaxed, comfortable experience, extremely reasonable prices and a friendly service with a bubbly atmosphere. Kaysha and her team offer preferential rates to Royal Hotel residents and Hotel bridal parties. For appointments and further information please contact Pin-ups Hair Salon Reception on 01934 624788 or 07794565280. Beauty Room Exciting new Beauty Salon Opening 2018! Beauty Within will offer a complete range of treatments, skincare and beauty therapies. More details coming soon! FREE WIFI & PARKING FOR RESIDENTS

title: Santas Grotto
subtitle: Meet the great man himself at The Grand Pier this Christmas!
bodyContent: Join us on a magical adventure to Santa’s Grotto where you can meet the great man himself and some of his trusty elves! As you step through the twinkling entrance with your mixed group of other girls and boys eagerly awaiting to meet Santa Claus, you’ll find yourself in the one and only Santa’s Toy Shop. Oh, how marvellous it is! You’ll see toys of all shapes and sizes and those little rascal elves, all hard at work, getting everything ready for Santa’s big night! The elves will be super eager to guide you through the festive trail, leading you all the way to Santa’s very own Grotto to hear all about your wishes and dreams for Christmas day! Santa will warmly welcome each of you, offering a precious photo to cherish forever, as well as a wonderful moment of story time, and rest assured, he has a special gift for everyone. Oh, but be on the lookout! Santa’s playful naughty elf might make an appearance during your visit, adding a touch of excitement to the experience! Before Santa sets off on his Christmas Eve journey around the world, don’t miss the chance to hop into his sleigh, parked nearby during your visit! (Please note: The Santa’s Grotto experience lasts for approx. 10 minutes. Each ticket provides admission for 1x child and 1x adult. Tickets are non-refundable and non-transferable)

title: Kingsmead Centre Camping
subtitle: A small family run campsite set in the Blackdown Hills on the Devon/Somerset Border. We have a range of pitches, static caravans and glamping plus two fishing lakes. Open all year round.
bodyContent: At Kingsmead we strive to offer a truly unique, and peaceful camping experience, which reflects the special qualities of Devon and Somerset. As a result, we offer a range of accommodation from a simple grass pitch to a luxuriously furnished, hand crafted yurt, where you can come and stay for a couple of nights or a long summer break. However you choose to stay, you are always guaranteed a warm welcome. Onsite you will find two well equipped facilities blocks with toilets, showers, washing up room, laundry and even a small shop selling ice creams, snacks and camping gear. To top off the experience, fishing on our two lakes is included in the price. A peaceful atmosphere is further maintained by our no music policy, ensuring everyone can immerse themselves in nature and relax. We are passionate about ensuring our visitors feel at home by providing a welcoming experience, which sees the same faces return year after year to stay with us.

title: Autumn Steam Weekend
subtitle: Join us as the much-loved Autumn Steam Weekend returns to mark a special milestone — 50 years of the WSR in preservation.
bodyContent: Join us as the much-loved Autumn Steam Weekend returns to mark a special milestone — 50 years of the WSR in preservation. We’re delighted to welcome an exciting lineup of visiting and home fleet locomotives, making this a must-see event for steam enthusiasts and families alike. Across all three days, an intensive timetable will keep the action moving, giving you plenty of opportunities to explore our beautifully preserved stations, ride behind iconic engines, and take in the stunning autumn scenery along England’s longest heritage railway. From the rolling Quantock Hills to the Somerset coast, trains will be running from early morning into the evening. The whole railway comes alive for the weekend, with museums, heritage displays, and model railways open throughout — perfect for visitors of all ages. And with steam engines against a backdrop of autumn colour, don’t forget your camera! Ticket information: Advance ticket sales close at 10am the day before travel to allow time for preparations. After this point, tickets will need to be purchased on the day at one of our booking offices.
tagline: Join us as the much-loved Autumn Steam Weekend returns to mark a special milestone

title: Yeovil Railway Centre
subtitle: Originally formed in 1994 to preserve the original turntable, the Centre has grown to offer Steam and Diesel days, special events, Shop and Café, and welcomes the occasional main line steam engine. Please check days we open and what’s happening.
bodyContent: The Southern Railway turntable installed in 1947 has been overhauled and visitors can watch the spectacle of large steam engines being turned and serviced. A Peckett steam engine ‘Pectin’ is currently operational and provides the power for public rides on the demonstration line of around 1/3 rd mile. Visitors ride in a historic brake van or in a coach. During these events, both Miniature and Model Railways are normally available together with light refreshments and the Shop. Demonstration of the turntable is often given. There are several Industrial diesels on site, one of which is used on our Diesel Days. Special events (including Model Railways, Tractors, Halloween and Characters) operate on a regular basis and of course our ever-popular Santa Specials are run in December – pre-booking essential to avoid disappointment. We offer pre-booked Driver Experience -see website. Our Shop has ‘Thomas’ and other children’s gifts for sale as well as a large selection of books (new and second hand) and lots of other railway related items. The Shop opens every Sunday (except Christmas and New Year) from 10am to 12 noon and longer during most events. A historic 1864 built Transfer Shed acts as home to our Visitor Centre and Café, Museum area and Signalling exhibiton. Can be hired for meetings etc. The Charity is run by a friendly group of volunteers who endeavour to make our visitors as welcome as possible. Please remember to check our website of Facebook for when we are open and what’s happening!
tagline: Yeovil Railway Centre was formed in 1994 to preserve the original Southern Railway turntable.

title: Buckland Farm Camping
subtitle: Buckland Farm Camping is situated at the foot of the beautiful Blackdown Hills, with views to the hills from the site. It is a peaceful meadow campsite, the main source of noise being from an occasional working tractor.
bodyContent: Choose a standard or fenced pitch (all suitable for tent, campervan/motorhome or caravan), or leave the tent behind and hire one of our furnished bell tents. Please note that as we are an off grid site, we do not have electric hook-ups, although there is a freezer and ample USB charging points for phones and gadgets. Our spacious pitches are mown into the long grass, which gives a feeling of privacy, as well as encouraging the birds and butterflies our guests enjoy watching and hearing. Our glamping bell tents are furnished with a double bed, two single futons, two bedside tables, a storage chest and some soft furnishings, and thick rugs underfoot. Outside, each has a picnic table and firepit for your personal use. The pitches for these tents are extra large. We ask guests to bring your own bedding and cooking gear. We have six composting loos (so no loo queues), three hot showers, washing up sinks, a bell tent lounge with books games and local information. There is a solar powered room with a freezer (with ice blocks to swap) and charging points for phones and small gadgets. Firepits and firewood are also available. We welcome dogs (and other pets!). Our popular fenced pitches give dogs (and therefore owners) a chance to relax. Dogs also have an off-lead paddock, and lots of local walks to enjoy. Guests enjoy the peaceful nature of Buckland Farm Camping – we hope you will enjoy it too, and would love to welcome you here.

title: The Royal Hotel Weston
subtitle: The Royal Hotel is a charismatic and elegant Georgian Building, is ideally located on the Seafront. Standing in its own extensive lawns, which extend to the Promenade, the Royal enjoys beautiful sea views, and is also in close proximity to our Town Centre and accessible by public transport.
bodyContent: The Royal Hotel is a charismatic and elegant Georgian Building, is ideally located on the Seafront. Standing in its own extensive lawns, which extend to the Promenade, the Royal enjoys beautiful sea views, and is also in close proximity to our Town Centre and accessible by public transport. The 44 attractive and comfortable rooms here at The Royal, feature ensuite bathrooms, Freeview TV, Tea & Coffee making facilities, Dressing Table/Desk, Direct-dial telephone, Hairdryer, Trouser press and complimentary toiletries. Wi-Fi is complimentary throughout the hotel. Newspapers and early morning wake up calls are available on request. Due to our fantastic location, all bedrooms boast lovely views of either Weston Seafront, The picturesque Italian Gardens, or the bustling Town Square. We provide a wide range of accommodation, choose from the following options….Doubles, Singles, Twins, Four Posters, Family Rooms that sleep 4-6, and our impeccable, brand new range of Royal Luxury Doubles! Disabled access is plentiful throughout the ground floor facilities, including the Bar & Restaurant. There is a lift to both floors, as well as disabled friendly bedrooms featuring a specialised wet-room. Please contact us to discuss any special requirements you may need. Our comfortable and traditional Feathers Bar is open daily for Drinks, Real Ales, Snacks, Afternoon Tea and Coffees. Enjoy a game of pool, or relax into a comfy sofa with a paper and a glass of wine. Friday night is party night in Feathers with a range of regular entertainment to kick off the weekend! Our Award Winning Restaurant epitomises the elegant regency style for which Weston was formally renowned. In these captivating surroundings you can enjoy dishes carefully selected for our appealing menu which has been designed to tempt and excite all tastes. Open for Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner every day, with our famous Carvery available Tuesdays, Thursdays – and of course, Sundays. This charming Georgian Hotel is renowned as Weston’s premier wedding venue, due to our first class reputation built on the outstanding reviews from the many bride and grooms whose weddings we have planned and hosted. Our Ballroom boasts idyllic sea views across Weston Bay and our extensive lawn with its sweeping bay windows makes it the perfect setting for a romantic Wedding. We hold a Civil Wedding & Civil Partnership licence, enabling you to simplify your arrangements by holding all aspects of your special day in one venue. For more information why not take a look at our Wedding Brochure online, or download our brand new & exclusive Wedding App for smart phones and tablets. For any questions, or to book a viewing, please contact our Wedding & Events team at the hotel. Customers can expect a relaxed, comfortable experience, extremely reasonable prices and a friendly service with a bubbly atmosphere. Kaysha and her team offer preferential rates to Royal Hotel residents and Hotel bridal parties. For appointments and further information please contact Pin-ups Hair Salon Reception on 01934 624788 or 07794565280. Beauty Room Exciting new Beauty Salon Opening 2018! Beauty Within will offer a complete range of treatments, skincare and beauty therapies. More details coming soon! FREE WIFI & PARKING FOR RESIDENTS

title: Middlewick Holiday Cottages
subtitle: Self catering cottages in Glastonbury. Perfect short break in Somerset with indoor pool.
bodyContent: A secluded holiday resort just minutes from Glastonbury town centre, with stunning views of Glastonbury Tor and the Mendip Hills. Set on 16 peaceful acres, The Middlewick offers self-catering accommodation in 10 cottages converted from original 17th-century farm buildings, 3 log cabins and 3 glamping pods. Our properties range from 1 to 5 bedrooms, offering plenty of choice for couples, families, friends and groups looking for country getaway. Many are dog friendly. We have a Café , Farm Shop and Spa on site – all of which are open to day visitors as well as guests staying with us. Our site, including our indoor heated pool and steam room, is powered by renewable energy, and Spa treatments take place in our cosy Shepherd’s Huts. Surrounded by apple orchards, this is a real escape to the Somerset countryside – with plenty of space to roam in the beauty of nature. Visitors can walk to Glastonbury Tor easily in under 30 minutes. There’s so much to explore nearby, with Glastonbury Tor, Chalice Well and Gardens, Glastonbury Abbey and Clark’s Village on our doorstep. Glastonbury is a unique market town bustling with unusual shops and alternative events. The Avalon Marshes Nature Reserve, Cathedral City of Wells and Cheddar Gorge are within easy driving distance from The Middlewick. Somerset is known for its food, music and outstanding natural beauty – and this is the ideal base from which to explore the best of the county.

title: Santas Grotto
subtitle: Meet the great man himself at The Grand Pier this Christmas!
bodyContent: Join us on a magical adventure to Santa’s Grotto where you can meet the great man himself and some of his trusty elves! As you step through the twinkling entrance with your mixed group of other girls and boys eagerly awaiting to meet Santa Claus, you’ll find yourself in the one and only Santa’s Toy Shop. Oh, how marvellous it is! You’ll see toys of all shapes and sizes and those little rascal elves, all hard at work, getting everything ready for Santa’s big night! The elves will be super eager to guide you through the festive trail, leading you all the way to Santa’s very own Grotto to hear all about your wishes and dreams for Christmas day! Santa will warmly welcome each of you, offering a precious photo to cherish forever, as well as a wonderful moment of story time, and rest assured, he has a special gift for everyone. Oh, but be on the lookout! Santa’s playful naughty elf might make an appearance during your visit, adding a touch of excitement to the experience! Before Santa sets off on his Christmas Eve journey around the world, don’t miss the chance to hop into his sleigh, parked nearby during your visit! (Please note: The Santa’s Grotto experience lasts for approx. 10 minutes. Each ticket provides admission for 1x child and 1x adult. Tickets are non-refundable and non-transferable)

title: The Old Pigsty
subtitle: Set in a tranquil location in Churchstanton in the Blackdown Hills, close to the Somerset Devon border and yet only six miles from Wellington and Taunton. The Old Pigsty has had many satisfied visitors commenting on their holiday experiences and the quiet, picturesque location.
bodyContent: The Old Pigsty offers most attractive studio style accommodation, therefore, is ideal for couples. Tastefully furnished, well equipped and with the benefit of its own terrace; it makes an ideal base for touring and relaxation. There are excellent walks and cycle routes nearby. The barn is located in the owners' pretty rear garden via seven small steps which lead to the entrance. There is ample space for parking with off-road parking nearby. The accommodation is on one floor with original beams and a ceramic tiled floor and comprises of a lounge/dining room and well-equipped kitchen. There is a double bed and French doors opening onto the patio area. Inside the shower room there is a double size shower cubicle, toilet and hand basin. The property benefits from central heating with constant hot water. All fuel, electricity, bed linen and towels are included. Water is supplied from the owners' freshwater spring. The courtyard garden and patio area has its own furniture and is perfect for relaxing in the evening sun. The property is not suitable for children over the age of 6 months or for more than 2 adults.

title: Taunton Sinfonietta’s -  English Connections Concert
subtitle: The magic and beauty of Taunton’s Orchestra in this early Autumn Concert.
bodyContent: The concert promises an evening of rich musical storytelling rooted in England’s enduring musical heritage, in a a celebration of english musical identity The Taunton Sinfonietta has long been known for its thoughtful programming and its ability to bring classical music to life for local audiences. With English Connections , the ensemble invites listeners on a journey through works that reflect the landscapes, traditions, and emotional depth of English composers. From pastoral serenity to stirring grandeur, English classical music has a distinct voice—one shaped by countryside vistas, literary influence, and a deep sense of place. This concert embraces that identity, offering a programme that feels both reflective and uplifting, and thoroughly connected to the cultural fabric of the region. TICKETS AVAILABLE AT THE TAUNTON VISITOR CENTRE

title: Double-Gate Farm
subtitle: Georgian farmhouse B&B accommodation with self catering converted barns in a peaceful location in Somerset, near Glastonbury & Wells.
bodyContent: Welcome to Double-Gate Farm, our Georgian farmhouse situated on the banks of the River Sheppey. Our farm offers views of the Mendip Hills and the surrounding countryside. Whether you're looking for a romantic getaway, a family vacation, or a group retreat, we have a variety of accommodations to choose from. Our converted barn is perfect for couples, families, and groups, while our accessible Riverside rooms and facilities cater to everyone's requirements. Our seasonal Tea Room is open from March to December and offers a range of delicious breakfasts, light lunches, home-baked cakes, and our speciality, Afternoon Tea. How about renting our BBQ Hut for a fun and sociable evening of cooking with your loved ones? Our Games Room is the perfect place to unwind after a long day of exploring. With a full-size snooker table, table-tennis, and lots of board games and local information, you'll never run out of things to do. At Double-Gate Farm, we pride ourselves on providing a peaceful and relaxing environment that allows you to unwind and enjoy nature. You can fish from your patio, watch the wildlife, or simply sit back and read. We welcome everyone, including cycling groups, walkers, and countryside lovers. Our location is perfect for exploring Somerset's hidden gems. With easy access to Glastonbury, Wells, and Cheddar, you'll be able to experience all that this beautiful region has to offer. We're also dog-friendly, so you don't have to leave your furry friend behind. Two of our Riverside rooms are pet-friendly, so please call us to check availability when booking with your dog. Finally, our farm is next door to a renowned gastropub that serves food and local brews. It's just a short walk away, so you don't have to worry about transportation. Come and experience the beauty of Double-Gate Farm for yourself.
tagline: Georgian farmhouse B&B accommodation with self catering converted barns

title: Priest's House, National Trust
subtitle: Late medieval house with large Gothic hall windows, originally residence of priests serving the parish church opposite.
bodyContent: The Priest's House, Somerset National Trust This medieval hall-house was built in 1308 for the parish priest of the church opposite, and has been little altered since the early 17th century. Interesting features include the Gothic doorway, magnificent double-height tracery windows and a massive 15th-century stone fireplace.

title: Tintinhull, National Trust
subtitle: A place of floral beauty, tranquillity and innovation - a gardener's garden paradise.
bodyContent: The garden, complete with working kitchen garden and orchard, lies in the charming village of Tintinhull, Somerset. Glittering pools, secluded lawns, colourful borders and clipped hedges provide the perfect spot to relax and unwind away from the hustle and bustle. The 17th century house is a National Trust holiday cottage sleeping up to eight people. Surrounded by the mellow colours of old brick and Ham stone, Tintinhull garden is the creation of two twentieth century gardeners: the first was an untrained amateur whose name is often still unrecognised, and the second is one of the UK’s most distinguished garden writers and designers. The garden was created around a 17 th century, Grade I listed house; garden and house are intertwined, with the house visible from every part of the garden and the garden layout planned with an eye to those looking out from house. The strong design of the garden was the work of Phyllis Reiss, who bought Tintinhull with her husband in 1933 and left it to the National Trust after her death in 1961. She was a shy woman, born into a disappearing world of leisured prosperity; influenced by gardens such as Hidcote and travels throughout France and Italy, she was part of a circle of gardeners that included the renowned Vita Sackville-West, then creating her own garden at Sissinghurst. Reiss took a ‘painterly’ approach to her garden, aiming for impact and emotional effect. She took ideas from famed garden designer Gertrude Jekyll, but simplified the herbaceous planting and planned imaginative and bold colour schemes. The garden is deceptively disciplined, with a strict formal framework offset with much looser floriferous planting; Reiss also included architectural plants for year-round interest. Twenty years after Reiss’s death, Penelope Hobhouse took on the tenancy at Tintinhull with her husband Professor Malins. It was while living at Tintinhull that Hobhouse developed her ideas on colour and became an internationally renowned garden designer and writer; many of her books reference her work at Tintinhull, where she used pots to dramatic effect and maintained Reiss’s experimental spirit. Reiss intended her ‘happy’ garden to be a place of peace and tranquillity, especially so after the creation of the Pool Garden in memory of her nephew, who was killed in the Second World War. After more than 50 years in National Trust ownership, Tintinhull is a garden with dramatic impact, but also a haven of quiet calm. If you need to call Tintinhull please ring 01458 224471, but be aware that the line connects to Lytes Cary Manor. Access Mobility drop off point outside main courtyard, car park approx 200m Mobility toilet available Braille guide Building - Level entrance. One wheelchair to borrow Grounds accessible with care, but paths are uneven and can be difficult to navigate. Arboretum and orchard not accessible

title: Lytes Cary Manor, National Trust
subtitle: Intimate manor house with Arts and Crafts-style garden
bodyContent: Lytes Cary Manor is an intimate medieval manor house with a beautiful Arts and Crafts garden where you can imagine living. Originally the family home of Henry Lyte, where he translated the unique Niewe Herball book on herbal remedies, Lytes Cary was then lovingly restored in the 20th century by Sir Walter Jenner. The garden rooms contain a magical collection of topiary and herbaceous borders, while tranquil walks on the estate take you along the River Cary. To complete your visit, take a stroll among our community allotments and discover their creative and colourful designs. The garden that you see today at Lytes Cary Manor is very different to the garden that would have originally existed when the Lyte family were in residence. In the beginning The garden would have once been a very practical, working space. Henry Lyte, who lived in the house in the 1550s, was a keen herbalist and gardener. His son Thomas wrote that he grew apples, pears, plums, grapes, cherries, walnuts and peaches. Sadly, much of the original garden was lost after the Lytes family sold the estate in 1755. The following years saw a series of owners and tenants occupying the Manor, and the garden disappeared as the land was farmed right up to the house. Twentieth century changes When the Jenner family took up residence in 1907, Sir Walter and Lady Flora created a new garden. The design was Arts and Craft inspired and featured mostly rectangular ‘rooms’ separated by yew hedges and stone walls, each reflecting a different mood or purpose. After Sir Walter passed the house and estate to the National Trust, it was again let to tenants. In 1955, Jeremy Chittenden and his wife, Biddy, took the lease. Both worked tirelessly over the next 45 years to transform the gardens into those we now know.

title: Barrington Court, National Trust
subtitle: Barrington Court, located in the stunning south Somerset countryside, is a charming Tudor manor house complimented beautifully with Gertrude Jekyll-inspired gardens, apple orchards and a working kitchen garden.
bodyContent: Barrington Court Somerset National Trust - Discover the haunting echoes of the past at Barrington Court, a Tudor manor house free from collections and furniture. Explore using your imagination and your senses to discover a house full of memories, where light fills the rooms and you feel you can almost touch the past. The property was saved from ruin and restored by the Lyle family in 1920s, when the Court House resembled a barn rather than the proud manor house that it is. Close your eyes and you’ll almost be able to hear the sounds and see the sights of the glamorous parties held in the great hall during Barrington’s heyday. On the first floor listen out for the voices resonating from the past, of the young evacuees who called Barrington home during the Second World War. Stroll through the Gertrude Jekyll inspired gardens, which with their focus on plant varieties and colours are a delight for all the senses. Be spurred on in your own garden or allotment by the stone-walled kitchen garden that produces a variety of delicious fruit and vegetables. Don’t just take our word for it, why not stop off in the Strode House Restaurant to taste these home-grown delights. Barrington Court predominantly featured in BBC’s highly acclaimed recent production of Hilary Mantel’s Wolf Hall.

title: Montacute House, National Trust
subtitle: Montacute House is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design
bodyContent: Montacute House, Somerset is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design. With its towering walls of glass, glow of ham stone and its surrounding gardens, it is a place of beauty and wonder. Sir Edward Phelips was the visionary force and money behind this masterpiece, which was completed in 1601. Built by skilled craftsman using local ham stone under the instruction of William Arnold, master mason, the house was a statement of wealth, ambition and showmanship. Come face to face with the past in the Long Gallery; measuring over 52 metres, it is the longest of its kind in England. The Gallery houses over 60 Tudor and Elizabethan portraits on loan from the National Portrait Gallery. Beautiful gardens surround Montacute, constantly changing, filling the house with scent in summer and providing an atmospheric backdrop for a winter walk. Whether you just want to let the children run and explore, or be inspired by the collections housed within the walls of Montacute, you will leave with lasting memories and a desire to soon return. You may even recognise some of the sights, as Montacute House featured in the BBC’s highly acclaimed production of Hilary Mantel’s Wolf Hall. Within 20 minutes’ drive you will find four fascinating smaller properties, each with a unique character, history and story to tell. Their combined age of 2,300 years spans from the medieval period to the early 19th century. Explore Stoke Priory, a fine collection of medieval farm buildings; Treasurer's House, with its great hall and unusual wall painting; Stembridge Tower Mill, the last remaining thatched windmill in England; and the Priest’s House, a medieval home of great character not to be missed. While you’re in the area, why not also visit Lytes Cary Manor and Tintinhull Garden (see the National Trust website for more details).
tagline: Montacute House in Somerset is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design

title: The Best of Take That Performed by Rule The World
subtitle: As Take That celebrate 30 years dominating the charts, Sweeney Entertainments presents Rule The World, an exciting high-energy production dedicated to the UK’s number one Boy Band!
bodyContent: This spectacular tribute comes complete with a five-piece line up and supporting dancers, magnificent lighting, fast costume changes and exceptional live vocals. The result is an incredibly accurate portrayal of a Take That concert. Rule The World have featured on ITV’s Daybreak as well as appearing alongside the real Take That on The Graham Norton Show. They are the only Take That tribute to have ever been praised by Gary Barlow himself, who described them as “Brilliant!” Sweeney Entertainments, co-founded by Julie and Peter Sweeney, has been providing a wide repertoire of top-quality touring shows for theatre and corporate events for over fifteen years both in the UK and internationally and now boasts a repertoire of fourteen touring productions. Julie Sweeney said: “Rule The World is an exciting new addition for Sweeney Entertainments! These extremely talented performers bring to you the very best tribute to Take That. The boys’ superb vocals harmonise beautifully to recreate the very best hits of Take That from the 90’s to the current day!” This unmissable show features all the biggest Take That hits including Never Forget, Greatest Day, Back For Good, Relight My Fire, Everything Changes, Shine, Pray and many more.

title: Muchelney Abbey
subtitle: Muchelney Abbey, which lies two miles south of Langport, was once a landmark in the Somerset Levels and still has much to offer its visitors – history lovers in particular will enjoy this fascinating site but there is also plenty for families to do.
bodyContent: Muchelney Abbey, which lies two miles south of Langport , was once a landmark in the Somerset Levels and still has much to offer its visitors – history lovers in particular will enjoy this fascinating site but there is also plenty for families to do. It was once a wealthy Benedictine house and the second oldest religious foundation in Somerset, but as part of the dissolution the abbey’s principal buildings were demolished by Henry VIII in 1538. Visitors can still see the clearly laid out foundations of the abbey, parts of the richly decorated cloister walk and thatched monks’ lavatory- the only one of its kind in Britain. The 16th-century abbots’ house remains intact with its magnificent rooms, and site finds are on display illustrating monastic life. With plenty of rooms to explore, this is an ideal day out whatever the weather and on sunny days, children have plenty of room to play in the grounds. Don't Miss: The Tudor house with lovely intact rooms and beautiful architecture A walk along the richly decorated cloister The only complete thatched monks' lavatory in England Our family interactive story bag 'Daniel and The Great Flood'

subtitle: One of the nations best loved Strictly Come Dancing professionals is coming out of retirement to star in ‘Come What May’, one of the UK’s most exciting theatre productions touring across the UK in Spring 2022
bodyContent: Come What May - The Ultimate Tribute to Moulin Rouge and other hit movie musicals including Rocketman, The Greatest Showman, A Star is Born, Burlesque and more; today announces full casting. The show, which stars Strictly Come Dancing professional Robin Windsor, heads out on a major national theatre tour starting January 2022 and plays across the UK at venues including Dartford Orchard Theatre, Wolverhampton Grand, Grand Theatre Swansea and Theatre Royal Windsor. Joining Robin Windsor are - Charlotte Gallagher, David Wyatt, Ollie Augustin, Óscar Fonseca, Chloe Gatward, Emma Jane, Georgia McEnaney, Hannah Morcos, Stuart Rouse and Reece Woodier. Travel back in time as the children of the revolution take you into the sexy and glamorous underworld of Paris at the Moulin Rouge. Journey into the flamboyant world of Elton John, delve into the imagination of the original showman P.T Barnum and finally head to the bright lights of Los Angeles before exploring the glamour of Sunset Boulevard’s Burlesque Lounge. This musical extravaganza is packed with timeless classics from the movie Moulin Rouge including Come What May, Your Song, Diamonds Are A Girls Best Friend, Roxanne and Lady Marmalade as well as featuring hits from other iconic movie musicals including Come Alive, Saturday Night’s Alright, Shallow and Show Me How You Burlesque. This ‘Spectacular, Spectacular’ all-singing, all-dancing show is an unforgettable combination of dreams, adventure and above all – love! The show is currently on a major national tour with Britain’s Got Talent winner Jai McDowall, which started in September 2021 and played across the UK including Mercury Theatre Colchester, Mayflower Theatre Southampton, New Theatre Royal Lincoln and Buxton Opera House where it will take a break before continuing in January with Robin.

title: Fleet Air Arm Museum
subtitle: The all-weather attraction is the perfect place for all the family. With immersive experiences like the Search and Rescue Sea King Helicopter walk through and a walkthrough of the iconic Concorde 002.
bodyContent: This year make sure to set your sights on the Fleet Air Arm Museum in Ilchester and see where time flies. This must-see attraction has four large exhibition halls each containing dozens of incredible aircraft which tell the rich history of naval aviation. Grab your wingman and step inside the first British Concorde, experience the thrills of a working flight deck, and get up close to a wide range of rare and historical aircraft.

title: Glastonbury Wedding and Events Venue
subtitle: An old pre Norman village church lovingly restored to its former glory offering a special place for couples to get married , to celebrate an anniversary , or to just have a party . comes with a large car park , glamping site and accommodation with kitchen, toilets and fully stocked licensed bar .
bodyContent: The old village church was closed back in 1998 owing to lack of attendance ,and with strong family ties was purchased by ourselves back in 2002 , The surrounding farmland and farm has been in our family for six generations so we did not want the church to fall into disrepair , and after a period of time we thought with the right planning we could get a civil license and have marriages and events there once more. After 37 months we finally got all the licenses that we required , then after a major building and renovation work we were ready to open up to the public again after a 16 year absence . With weddings and events coming from near and afar , it was decided to offer accommodation , so planning was sought for some glamping pods , these have been installed during the covid lockdowns and are now ready for the summer of 2021. Guests can now enjoy themselves even more with a relaxing stay without the need to drive , whether it is a wedding , anniversary or party a whole weekend with friends can be a enjoyable occasion without the rush and stress . The glamping pods are all ensuite with double bed ,showers, toilets , kitchenette , fridge freezers, microwave and TV . There is also a three bedroom cottage that can sleep six so more friends and family can stay on site.

title: Matilda - The Musical - jr
subtitle: Wellington Arts Association Events present Matilda - The Musical - JR.
bodyContent: Inspired by the twisted genius of Roald Dahl, Matilda is a little girl with astonishing wit, intelligence and psychokinetic powers. She's unloved by her cruel parents but impresses her schoolteacher Miss Honey. During her first term at school, the two forge a bond as Miss Honey begins to recognize and appreciate Matilda's extraordinary personality. Matilda's school life isn't completely smooth sailing, however – the school's mean headmistress, Miss Trunchbull, hates children and just loves to punish those who don't abide by her rules. But Matilda has courage and cleverness in equal amounts, and could be the school pupils' saving grace! Matilda is a joyous girl power romp. Children and adults alike will be thrilled and delighted by the story of the special little girl with an extraordinary imagination.

title: Shrek - The Musical
subtitle: Wellington Arts Association Events - Shrek The Musical at the Wellesley, Wellington.
bodyContent: "Once upon a time, there was a little ogre named Shrek…" And thus begins the tale of an unlikely hero who finds himself on a life-changing journey alongside a wisecracking Donkey and a feisty princess who resists her rescue. Throw in a short tempered bad guy, a cookie with an attitude, and over a dozen other fairy tale misfits, and you've got the kind of mess that calls for a real hero. Luckily, there's one on hand...and his name is Shrek. Everyone's favorite ogre is back in the hilarious stage spectacle based on the Oscar-winning smash hit film. Shrek The Musical is a Tony Award-winning fairy tale adventure Shrek brings all the beloved characters you know from the film to life on stage, and proves there's more to the story than meets the ears.

title: Celebrate the Best of the West at the Taste of Somerset Event!
subtitle: Get ready to embark on a culinary journey through Somerset at the highly anticipated Taste of Somerset event on Saturday, June 15th at Brean Leisure Park
bodyContent: Celebrate the Best of the West at the Taste of Somerset Event! Date: Saturday, June 15th, 2024 Location: Brean Leisure Park, at the front of the Tavern and Entrance to the Theme Park (TA8 2QY) Time: 10:30 AM - 4:00 PM Admission: Free Brean, Somerset – Get ready to embark on a culinary journey through Somerset at the highly anticipated Taste of Somerset event! On Saturday, June 15th, Brean Leisure Park will transform into a food lover's paradise, showcasing some of the best food and drink producers the county has to offer. This free-to-attend, family-friendly event promises a day filled with delectable delights and fun for all ages. From the rich, refreshing flavours of Rich's Cider Farm to the freshly baked goods from Winnies Bakery, the vibrant tastes of Salsa Stories, and the savory treats of Somerset Charcuterie, there is something to tantalize every palate. Operations Manager, Darren Cavill, expressed his enthusiasm for the event, saying, “We are thrilled to bring our celebration of amazing food and drink from Somerset to Brean, and we are proud to support local artisan producers. We very much look forward to welcoming the community and visitors to the area to showcase the best the west has to offer!” The Taste of Somerset event is committed to being accessible to all. The venue is equipped to accommodate families and individuals with disabilities, ensuring everyone can enjoy the diverse flavours of the region. Join us at Brean Leisure Park for a day dedicated to celebrating local food and drink. Sample and savour the best that the South West has to offer and support our talented local producers.

title: Summer Music Festival, Brean, Saturday 3rd August midday to 7pm
subtitle: ‘Summer Music Festival’, to be held on the ‘Market Field’ at Warren Farm Holiday Park.
bodyContent: Summer Music Festival, Brean, Saturday 3rd August midday to 7pm Brean’s historic Grade 2 listed Church St Bridget’s was last year threatened with possible closure. A group of concerned Brean villagers (both churchgoers and not) formed the “Friends of St Bridget’s” to fundraise to ensure closure did not happen, assisted by several local businesses. After successful music concerts inside the church last year, this year’s events include a ‘Summer Music Festival’, to be held on the ‘Market Field’ at Warren Farm Holiday Park. Three live acts will perform including: Beat Route Jam performing their immaculate “Sounds of the 60’s - Before and After” concert, Teresa Alexander performing an incredible eclectic range of chart hits from the 60s to present day, and also SIX MACHINE who celebrate world famous artists including Bruno Mars, Adele, Elton John, The Bee Gees, Guns 'n' Roses and The Killers to name but a few. Alister Wilmott is a multi-talented entertainer who will host the afternoon to ensure continuity of fabulous entertainment. A bar with will be open, plus food and soft drinks from vendors on site. Tickets are £10 Adults (18 years and over), £5 Children and Free entry for young children (Under 1.2m height). Ticket numbers are restricted to 500 in total and are available in advance from Pat Holland on 07988 601378, or on the gate from 11.30am onwards. Tickets are also available at face value with no additional admin fee from https://www.eventbrite.com/e/brean-music-festival-2024-tickets-929753215897?aff=oddtdtcreator scan here

title: National Trust Easter Trails at Brean Down
subtitle: Search for shells, wildlife and landmarks at Brean Down – you’ll be rewarded with a chocolate egg at the end.
bodyContent: Explore Brean Down this Easter Bank Holiday weekend as you follow our trail along the beach and up the down. Search for shells, wildlife and landmarks – you’ll be rewarded with a chocolate egg at the end. Have a go at Easter crafts in the café too. Free admission, £3 per trail, includes an Easter trail sheet and a chocolate egg, or a vegan ‘Free-From’ chocolate egg, both made using cocoa from Rainforest Alliance Certified farms. Car-parking charges for non-members apply.

title: The Fleetwood Mac Songbook
subtitle: Earning rave reviews wherever they play and ranked in the ‘Top 20 Tribute Artists & Bands in the World’ by Champions UK plc Entertainment Agency, six piece tribute band ‘The Fleetwood Mac Songbook’ are bringing their non-stop, hit packed show to The Princess on Friday September 22nd
bodyContent: The band perform a spell binding recreation of the stellar ‘songbook’ of ‘Fleetwood Mac’, drawing from over six decades of songs. Their set of course includes soft rock anthems from the ‘Rumours’ and ‘Tango In The Night’ albums but they don’t forget founding member, Blues guitar legend Peter Green, and dedicate a portion of the show to a selection of his work. Every detail is immaculate to ensure that the unmistakable ‘Mac’ sound is recreated faithfully – the exceptional three part harmonies are a standout as well as the band’s guitarist using the famous Lindsey Buckingham Rick Turner model of guitar that gives the songs that final polish. You will be assured of a night to remember in the company of these fine musicians for an unforgettable evening suitable for all ages. Tickets are £18 and can be purchased online or call the Box Office on 01278 784464

title: Absolute Bowie A lovingly crafted Bowie show" – NME
subtitle: Winners of the ‘Best Bowie Tribute’ and ‘Best Band’ in the UK at the Agents Association of Great Britain Awards July 2018. “Britain’s top Bowie tribute” – The Times “Great fun” – The Times “Unmissable” – Mail on Sunday
bodyContent: Now in their 12th year of touring, the UKs ‘Best Tribute Band’ and ‘Best Bowie’ act, would like to come and meet you and they might just blow your mind… With an electrifying performance from our main Starman, and theatrical mid-set costume ch-ch-ch-anges, Absolute Bowie will take you on a musical journey through the greatest hits of David Bowie with their huge stage show. “A lovingly crafted Bowie show” says NME, and “an unmissable tribute act” hails the Mail on Sunday, the band will leave you wanting more from the most genuine David Bowie tribute out there. Is it any wonder when you are too cool to fool. David Bowie’s evolving image has mesmerised fans since the early 70’s and for the first time ever Absolute Bowie will take audiences on a trip that presents all his best-loved personas in all their glory. Performed by a world class five-piece band, this unique concert features two long sets and more costume changes than any other show. A true extravaganza of the wonder that is Bowie’s work. The band have listened to fans and evolved the show’s setlist to really give an all-killer performance and no Bowie fan is left out. All of the Starman’s greatest hits are performed plus the band perform tracks from the albums David Bowie, Ziggy Stardust & The Spiders From Mars, Heroes, Aladdin Sane, Hunky Dory, Let’s Dance and Young Americans through to the hits of later albums.

title: Monthly Wednesday Matinees
subtitle: The Princess Theatre & Arts Centre is excited to launch its monthly Wednesday matinees. We will screen well-loved classic films at the venue on the first Wednesday of every month at 2pm from February.
bodyContent: Tickets, priced £5, are available to buy on the website. The Princess is also introducing £10 tickets to include the film and lunch. You will be able to choose from Hellend’s Kitchen Small Main Menu Meals and your choice of hot drink. Starting with Breakfast and Tiffany’s on Wednesday February 2 nd at 2pm, Casablanca on Wednesday 2 nd March and Some Like It Hot on Wednesday 6 th April. To book seats for Breakfast at Tiffany’s, visit https://www.theprincesstheatre.co.uk/events/film-breakfast-at-tiffanys/ To book seats for Casablanca, visit https://www.theprincesstheatre.co.uk/events/film-casablanca/ To book seats for Some Like It Hot, visit https://www.theprincesstheatre.co.uk/events/film-some-like-it-hot/ Film and Lunch booking only available up to 48 hours prior to the showing. Table bookings will be made for 12pm on the day of the matinee. The Princess is also delighted to announce this season’s National Theatre screenings; from London’s West End Tom Stoppard’s Olivier Award-winning play Leopoldstadt, screening on Saturday February 5 th at 7pm. At the beginning of the 20th century, Leopoldstadt was the old, crowded Jewish quarter of Vienna, Austria. But Hermann Merz, a factory owner and baptised Jew now married to Catholic Gretl, has moved up in the world. We follow his family’s story across half a century, passing through the convulsions of war, revolution, impoverishment, annexation by Nazi Germany and the Holocaust. A company of 40 actors represent each generation of the family in this epic, but intimate play.

title: National Trust offering new volunteering roles at Brean Down
subtitle: The National Trust team in the Somerset countryside are looking for volunteers to fill a diverse range of roles.
bodyContent: The National Trust team in the Somerset countryside are looking for volunteers to fill a diverse range of roles. From Brean Down to the Holnicote Estate in Exmoor National Park, the conservation charity looks after many much-loved beauty spots across the county, and they are looking for extra pairs of hands to care for them and welcome visitors. On 22, 23 & 24 February, there will be a pop-up shop in Wellington town centre for anyone who is interested in leading tours at Wellington Monument. Members of the public can drop in anytime between 10am and 4pm to find out more about volunteering at the tallest three-sided obelisk in the world. On 1 & 2 March, volunteer recruitment days are being held in the Music Hall at Fyne Court. From gardening to events, visitors can drop in and learn how they can get involved at the 90-acre estate on the Quantock Hills near Taunton. Other volunteering roles across Somerset include butterfly surveying on the Mendip Hills, bookshop assistants at Brean Down and helping in the tree nursery on the Holnicote Estate. Jess Midgley, Volunteering & Community Manager for the National Trust in Somerset, says: “Our places across the Somerset countryside offer some brilliant opportunities for volunteering from assisting our rangers with their nature conservation projects to welcoming visitors to our events. “It’s also a great way of learning different skills and making new friends. Come along to one of our volunteer recruitment days or get in touch with us to find out more.” To see all the National Trust volunteering opportunities in Somerset, you can search online at https://myvolunteering.nationaltrust.org.uk/opportunity-search or contact the team by emailing somerset.countryside@nationaltrust.org.uk

title: Summer Music Festival, Brean, Saturday 3rd August midday to 7pm
subtitle: Summer Music Festival’, to be held on the ‘Market Field’ at Warren Farm Holiday Park.
bodyContent: Summer Music Festival, Brean, Saturday 3rd August midday to 7pm Brean’s historic Grade 2 listed Church St Bridget’s was last year threatened with possible closure. A group of concerned Brean villagers (both churchgoers and not) formed the “Friends of St Bridget’s” to fundraise to ensure closure did not happen, assisted by several local businesses. After successful music concerts inside the church last year, this year’s events include a ‘Summer Music Festival’, to be held on the ‘Market Field’ at Warren Farm Holiday Park. Three live acts will perform including: Beat Route Jam performing their immaculate “Sounds of the 60’s - Before and After” concert, Theresa Alexander performing an incredible eclectic range of chart hits from the 60s to present day, with the third act yet to be announced. Additionally a DJ will ensure continuity of music throughout the event. A bar with will be open, plus food and soft drinks from vendors on site. Tickets are £10 Adults (18 years and over), £5 Children and Free entry for young children (Under 1.2m height). Ticket numbers are restricted to 500 in total and are available in advance from the Friends via 07733 031564 (Richard) or 07988 601378 (Pat), or on the gate from 11.30am onwards.

title: Brean Country Club introduces Somerset's first and only public padel tennis courts
subtitle: Located at Brean Country Club in Brean, the two outdoor courts are set to revolutionise the sports scene in the region.
bodyContent: Padel tennis, a popular racquet sport that combines elements of tennis and squash, is taking the country by storm, and Brean Country Club is proud to bring this exciting sport to the community. With the opening of these two public outdoor courts, residents and visitors alike will have the opportunity to enjoy padel tennis without travelling to the nearest courts in Bristol. In addition to the courts, Brean Country Club offers racket and ball hire for those looking to try out this thrilling sport. Whether you're a seasoned player or a beginner, we welcome players of all skill levels to come and experience the excitement of padel tennis. Coaching will also be available. To make your visit even more convenient, Brean Country Club provides free car parking for all guests. Additionally, the club offers changing rooms and shower facilities to ensure that players can freshen up after a game and also enjoy a drink or bite to eat at The View Kitchen & Bar , located at Brean Country Club. "We are delighted to introduce Somerset's only public padel tennis courts at Brean Country Club," said Sarah House. "We believe that padel tennis is a fantastic sport that offers fun and fitness for people of all ages and abilities. We can't wait to welcome players to and provide them with a top-notch experience on and off the court." Don't miss the opportunity to be among the first to experience padel tennis at Brean Country Club and discover the thrill of this exciting sport in a welcoming and inclusive environment. If you are new to padel and would like to learn more, we have a quick guide here . The Padel courts will be open daily and bookings can be made online for a 1hr session via our website . For more information about Brean Country Club and its padel tennis facilities, and to book your padel session, please visit www.breancountryclub.com

title: Free Guided Walks in Brean
subtitle: Everyone is welcome to join the free guided walks, every Thursday during October, which start from Warren Farm Holiday Centre in Brean
bodyContent: There are weekly guided walks taking place in Brean throughout October (2024). Everyone is welcome to join the free guided walks, every Thursday during October, which start from Warren Farm Holiday Centre in Brean. A spokesperson said: “Our guide, Amanda Baldwin, is an experienced hiker, photographer and bird spotter. Her passion for rambling and the great outdoors is infectious, and she can't wait to share that enjoyment with you! “The guided walks are open to everyone; you don’t have to be staying at Warren Farm. Please wear suitable footwear and clothing. Please ensure you bring a bottle of water and don’t forget your camera!” There is a morning and an afternoon walk every Thursday during October. The morning destinations vary as follows: Thursday 3rd October at 10am: Guided ramble to Brean Down Thursday 10th October at 10am: Guided ramble to Uphill Cafe Thursday 17th October at 10am: Guided ramble to Berrow Shipwreck Thursday 24th October at 10am: Guided ramble to Uphill Cafe Thursday 31st October at 10am: Guided ramble to Berrow Shipwreck The afternoon walks are around the Farm Walk at Warren Farm, which is a shorter, flat route, approximately two miles. Every Thursday at 2.30pm: Guided ramble around the Farm Walk There is no need to pre-book. Please meet outside the Warren Farm Shop 10 minutes prior to departure. Dogs are welcome, but must be kept on leads on Brean Down for their own safety. title: Festive Christmas Concert in Brean
subtitle: A festive Christmas Concert will take place on Friday 13th December 2024, at Saint Bridget’s Church in Brean.
bodyContent: A festive Christmas Concert will take place on Friday 13 th December 2024, at Saint Bridget’s Church in Brean. The upcoming concert will feature well-known pianist Richard Lennox, supported by local singers Francesca Bowkett, Owen James and Lynda James. Francesca Bowkett, Mezzo-Soprano, said: “Richard Lennox is set to return with a Christmas Concert at Saint Bridget’s Church in Brean. “Come and enjoy some well-known Christmas songs and carols. The concert will feature religious and secular music, and the audience will be encouraged to sing or hum along with us!” Special festive lighting will be provided by Tom Johnson of TJ Lighting (based in Weston-super-Mare). Tickets are £10 per person, including refreshments. They are on sale now from Burnham Post Office or Burnham Tourist Office. It is advisable to purchase tickets prior to the concert as seating is limited. Richard Lennox is a professional pianist and organist. He has played at many prestigious venues including The Royal Albert Hall, Wells Cathedral and Bristol Cathedral. Francesca Bowkett has sung leading roles in opera, operatics and choral concerts around the county and further afield. She is well-known for her Prom concerts including 15 years as Finale Soloist at the Bristol Beacon. The Christmas Concert takes place on Friday 13 th December 2024 at 7.30pm, at Saint Bridget’s Church in Brean.

title: Exciting developments at UNITY Holiday Parks, Brean Sands
subtitle: UNITY Holiday Parks is revolutionising the UK holiday experience with a multi-million-pound investment into new entertainment venues, world-class shows, exciting restaurants, and thrilling activities.
bodyContent: UNITY Holiday Parks is revolutionising the UK holiday experience with a multi-million-pound investment into new entertainment venues, world-class shows, exciting restaurants, and thrilling activities. The ‘Comes Alive in 25’ campaign is set to redefine the traditional seaside getaway, breathing new life into British family holidays and positioning UNITY as the UK’s No1 destination for holiday makers and owners. Bringing Back the Magic of the British Seaside For generations, the Great British Holiday was the pinnacle of family fun, and UNITY is bringing that cherished experience back in a bigger and better way than ever before. With state-of-the-art entertainment complexes, live performances, and a dynamic lineup of activities, UNITY Holiday Parks is recreating the magic of the golden age of British seaside breaks, all while adding a modern touch. A Multi-Million-Pound Investment for Unforgettable Holidays UNITY is not just updating its parks, it’s completely transforming them. The substantial investment is creating brand-new entertainment venues featuring spectacular live shows, interactive family experiences, and high-energy performances. Guests can expect a holiday atmosphere like no other, where every night feels like a celebration. title: TV, Film and Literature around Brean and Berrow
subtitle: Brean and Berrow have become stars in their own right. This coast offers the perfect escape for film fans, and lovers of unspoilt scenery alike.
bodyContent: Brean Brean is a prime location for filming with seven miles of golden sands set against the imposing backdrop of Brean Down, rising 300ft from the beach. Productions include: The Crow Girl (2025) A tense six-part psychological thriller starring Dougray Scott and Eve Myles. The beach features in episode five. Pic: The Crow Girl 2024 © Buccaneer/Paramount+ Photographer Joss Barratt​ Shed and Buried - Classic Cars (2024) In episode one the beach car park is used to test drive their restored beach buggy and they even consider a dip in the sea! The Killing Kind (2023) is a gripping six-part thriller. Most was filmed in and around Bristol, but the scenes of the star, Ingrid (Emma Appleton), walking on the beach are at Brean. Sanditon (2017) This period drama is based on Jane Austen's unfinished novel about Sanditon, the “finest seaside resort on the South Coast.” The horse-drawn bathing huts, beach scenes and dunes are at Brean, but the swimming took place in Weston-super-Mare’s Marine Lake. Fulll Fire Arms (2011) used the Fort at Brean Down as a set in this production, the first feature film by British artist Emily Wardill. Bonekickers (2008) is an eight-part archaeological drama featuring Brean Down in episode two. Elizabeth: The Golden Age (2007) is an award-winning film starring Cate Blanchett as Queen Elizabeth I, who addresses the troops from horseback on the beach (standing in for Tilbury in Essex). Dracula (2006) stars Marc Warren as Count Dracula. The shipwreck scene was filmed at Brean with the cliffs in the background. The Doombolt Chase (1978) is a six-part children’s TV series that features the Fort and Brean Down in the last episode. To do Climb to the top of Brean Down (steep) and walk to the end for stunning views. Explore the remains of the Palmerston Fort and look out for rare flora and fauna. Trampers are available to hire. Stroll along one of the longest stretches of sandy beach in Europe. Enjoy coffee and cake upstairs in the National Trust café for beautiful views over the beach. Berrow Beach Berrow Beach stood in for Jersey in Another Mother’s Son (2015), a film based on the true story of Louisa Gould set during World War II. The Crimson Field (2014) was a World War I TV series. Berrow Beach was used as the French field hospital and for a game of football - this scene shows Hinkley Point Power Station in the distance, which wasn’t built until 1957! Aquila (1997) was a BAFTA-nominated children’s TV show that ran for two series with thirteen episodes and is said to have used Berrow Beach as a location. French and Saunders (1996) series five, episode one, is a spoof of Baywatch, which the BBC reported as being filmed on Berrow Beach. To do This stretch of coast has the second highest tidal range in the world, topped only by Canada’s Bay of Fundy. When the tide goes out at Berrow, the skeletal remains of the Nornen, a shipwreck from 1897, rise from the sand. Head to the Sundowner Beach Bar Café, tucked in the dunes, for food, drinks and views or get a takeaway to enjoy on the beach. They also have live music at weekends during the summer. Grateful thanks to Nell Barrington for researching and writing this piece

title: Talent Gallery celebrates its one-year anniversary
subtitle: Talent Gallery, a welcoming and vibrant hub for local art and creativity, is proud to be celebrating its first anniversary.
bodyContent: Talent Gallery, a welcoming and vibrant hub for local art and creativity, is proud to be celebrating its first anniversary. Over the past year, the gallery has become a cornerstone of the community, providing a platform for talented artists and makers to showcase their work and connect with art enthusiasts. In 2024, the former Talent Gallery was due to shut down, however local artist and resident Nina King had a bold vision to transform the space and create something of her own, always with the people of Wellington at the forefront of the space. She re-opened the gallery in June 2024 with a new mission and fresh purpose. “It's been an incredible first year, and I'm so proud of the community we've built at Talent Gallery.” says Nina, Gallery Owner and Artist. “My vision for Talent Gallery was to create a space where local artists feel supported and where everyone can discover the joy of art. Reaching this milestone is a testament to the talent within our community and the wonderful support we've received.” Driven by a passion for supporting local creatives, Talent Gallery offers a diverse range of artwork and handcrafted items. As an artist herself, the gallery owner understands the challenges artists face and has created a welcoming environment for both creators and collectors. You’ll often find Nina painting a new local landscape from her studio space in the gallery, allowing visitors a unique glimpse into the artistic process. “What a gem of find. A really charming gallery, light spacious and deceptively full of local artists work. And a wonderfully warm welcome from Nina.” Says Mark Perks on a Google review. In its first year, Talent Gallery has also successfully launched art workshops, providing enriching experiences for everyone to explore their own creativity. “Nina runs excellent landscape art classes. I learned so much about techniques with acrylics, that I would never have imagined existed. A fun time was had with other beginners - Nina started with basic principles and very gently eased us on to more sophisticated techniques.” Says Richard Chivers on a Google review. Looking ahead, Talent Gallery remains committed to its mission of celebrating local talent. The gallery regularly rotates its exhibitions, ensuring there is always something new and exciting to discover. “We're excited for what the next year holds and look forward to continuing to serve our vibrant artistic community.” says Nina King. Talent Gallery also wishes to remind our community that supporting local creatives, with even the smallest purchases like cards and prints, makes a significant difference in sustaining the local arts scene, especially during challenging times. Visit Talent Gallery at 11 Fore Street, Wellington, Somerset, TA21 8AA and discover the latest collection of local talent. Talent Gallery website

title: Junction 26 and A38 Chelston Link Road to reopen ahead of schedule
subtitle: Junction 26 and A38 Chelston Link Road will reopen on Sunday 7 September.
bodyContent: A £5.7 million Somerset Council scheme to replace a deteriorating 51-year-old concrete road is progressing well with Junction 26 and the A38 Chelston Link Road now planned to reopen ahead of schedule. All slip roads at Junction 26, the roundabout and the A38 link road from the motorway to the Chelston roundabout are set to reopen overnight on Saturday 6 September to Sunday 7 September. The early reopening has been made possible by a combination of overnight and extended working and use of innovative techniques. The project team prioritised work which would enable the road to reopen as soon as possible. Works will continue during September but will be completed after the closure has been lifted. Cllr Richard Wilkins , Somerset Council’s Lead Member for Transport and Waste Services, said: “We pledged to do everything in our power to keep disruption to a minimum and it is fantastic news that the A38 and motorway junction will reopen well ahead of schedule. “We appreciate this has been a hugely challenging project to deliver and we are very grateful to local communities, businesses and the travelling public for their patience. “Thanks also to our project team and contractors Heidelberg Materials for their hard work. I am proud of their efforts to deliver these long overdue improvements much earlier than planned. “It means the government funding we worked so hard to secure has been put to good use and we can all benefit from a smoother, quieter road surface with improved drainage for years to come.” Jonathan Hill, National Highways Route Manager, said: “It’s good to see Somerset Council and their teams deliver this significant road improvement scheme ahead of schedule. “As the Chelston Link Road scheme necessitated the closure of the Junction 26 slip roads, we’ve worked closely with the council over the last few years during planning for these works to ensure the impact on our roads and our road users was minimised as far as possible. We’re grateful to drivers for their patience during the programme of work.” The refurbishment of Junction 26 of the M5 along with the A38 Chelston link road, which were built in 1974, was entirely funded by Government grants. For the A38 link road, the council’s contractor Heidelberg Materials used an innovative technique known as rubblization to break up the existing concrete road surface using heavy machinery. Instead of removing 7,300 tonnes of concrete from site, the materials were retained and recycled as sub-base for the new road. This modern recycling method, often used on airport runways, saved 200 tonnes in carbon and around 1,130 lorry movements, compared to traditional road construction methods. This was achieved by removing the need to export waste material and quarry and import new stone – better for the environment, but also enabling work to be completed faster. Rubblization could not be used on the J26 roundabout due to the height of the overhead bridges, so for this section an entire excavation of more than one metre in depth was required in order to build the new surface. Other programme optimisations included the use of asphalt kerbs in this scheme instead of traditional methods which take longer to install. The project included works to create a whole new drainage system which will reduce the risk of flooding and will also be easier to access for future maintenance. The window and timescale for the work was agreed with National Highways and dictated by forthcoming M5 works, alongside the need to allow National Highways to access its gritting depot off the Chelston Link Road during winter. To minimise disruption to road users, partner organisations National Grid and National Highways took advantage of the closures to carry essential improvement works which would have otherwise required traffic management.
