title: Somerset’s Coastal Challenge celebrates another successful year
subtitle: The walk began in glorious sunshine at County Gate, near the Devon border, and concluded eight days later at Brean Down, at the edge of the Mendip Hills.
bodyContent: The second annual 80 Miles in Eight Days Challenge Walk has once again proved a resounding success, with 23 enthusiastic walkers covering a collective 500 miles along Somerset’s stunning coastline. Walking on the South West Coast Path and the King Charles III England Coast Path, the event show-cased the region’s diverse landscapes—from moorlands and farmland to sweeping beaches and estuaries. Richard Taylor and Richard Pinnington are two of the walkers who completed the full eight-day challenge, walking the entire Somerset coast. “Well done to the Richards. Completing this walk in the timescale is not easy,” said Isobel Pring, speaking on behalf of the Somerset Trail Partnership for the King Charles III England Coast Path. “The first two days are packed with steep climbs, and the final ascent up the steps to the top of Brean Down demands a last burst of energy.” Organised by the Somerset Trail Partnership in collaboration with Exmoor National Park, the walk also met its fundraising goal of £700 for The Outdoor Guide Foundation’s Waterproofs and Wellies Campaign. “Thanks to the generosity of our supporters, we’ll be able to provide two sets of waterproofs and wellies—ten pairs each—for two coastal primary schools in Somerset,” said Isobel. The walk began in glorious sunshine at County Gate, near the Devon border, and concluded eight days later at Brean Down, at the edge of the Mendip Hills. Participants praised the event’s scenic beauty and camaraderie, with feedback including: “Such a great walk and beautiful scenery,” and “I really enjoyed my four days of walking—good company and perfect weather.” “This stretch of coast is a joy to walk,” said Isobel. “It offers everything from gentle, flat paths to the dramatic hills and combes of Exmoor. We were lucky to have a fantastic group of walkers and great weather this year.” Looking ahead, 2026 marks the tenth anniversary of the opening of the King Charles III England Coast Path between Minehead to Brean Down, and the Trail Partnership aims to run the 80 Miles in Eight Days Challenge Walk for a third time. Plans are also underway to introduce a series of circular walks throughout the year, and the Partnership is actively seeking coastal partners to help host and sponsor these events. Provisional dates for 2026 are; September 12 – 19 - Walking Brean to County Gate *September 19 – 26 - Walking County Gate to Brean *September 26 – October 3 - Walking Brean to County Gate October 3 – 10 - Walking County Gate to Brean There will be more walks celebrating the 10 th anniversary of the KCIIIECP from Minehead to Brean Down. For more information about walking on Somerset’s coast visit www.somersetcoastfestival.co.uk . Challenge Walk finishers: Richard Taylor and Richard Pinnington celebrate on the top of Brean Down (Photo credit: Isobel Pring).

title: Innovative new nature reserve project begins in Wellington, improving river health and supporting sustainable development across Somerset
subtitle: Work has begun on a new 27-hectare nature initiative on the edge of Wellington.
bodyContent: Work has begun on a new 27-hectare nature initiative on the edge of Wellington, marking a major step forward for local nature recovery and long-term habitat protection, while also easing planning delays for much-needed homes and infrastructure across the region. The project brings together two linked sites. The Trinity Nature Reserve will form the final piece of the Wellington Green Corridor: a long-planned ‘green wedge’ designed to protect open space, improve water quality and connect important wildlife sites for decades to come. The nearby Eastcombe Fields Nature Area adds further habitat areas and strengthens the overall environmental benefits for the local landscape. Together, the sites include grassland, woodland, hedgerows, lakes and wetlands, all designed sensitively around existing local ecological networks to improve habitat connectivity for protected species. It is part of a recently approved Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) scheme which guarantees long-term management and protection of these habitats. The project is being led by local landowners KS Coles in partnership with Greenshank Environmental, whose technical expertise has been central to designing a scheme that delivers both ecological and development benefits. The intention is for the site to be designated as a Local Nature Reserve in future. Kim Connor Streich, CCO of Greenshank Environmental, said: “This is a genuine long-term boost for Wellington. The Coles family have created something special here – space for wildlife, space for nature recovery and a real asset for the local area. What I love about this project is its legacy: these habitats will be protected for decades, giving future generations cleaner rivers, more wildlife and a stronger connection to the natural landscape around them.” The sites are also helping to unblock stalled housing and infrastructure projects by tackling the issue of nutrient neutrality. This is one of the first UK nutrient-mitigation schemes to use an innovative drainage-ditch system to mitigate phosphorus pollution. Because these measures improve the local river environment, other developers can now buy BNG units or nutrient-mitigation credits from the Wellington schemes to offset their own projects. This is vital for unlocking housing sites that cannot proceed until they meet important environmental requirements. More information here . Image(s) Damien Bouyou for Greenshank Environmental

title: Nether Stowey
subtitle: The village of Nether Stowey is an ideal base for exploring the Quantock Hills – England’s first Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty – as its famous former resident Samuel Taylor Coleridge discovered more than 200 years ago.
bodyContent: The poet, who completed most of his best work while living in Nether Stowey , was on a walking tour of Somerset when he met Thomas Poole, another important resident whose legacy is everywhere in the village and who became a lifelong friend. For a while, William Wordsworth rented a mansion nearby and the two poets walked miles together across the hills and along the route to Lynmouth now known as Coleridge Way. As if the National Trust owned Coleridge Cottage were not enough, Nether Stowey is packed with other gems including a ruined Norman castle, a Victorian town clock and lock up, cobbled pavement, a stream running down the side of the street and a clutch of ancient cottages. Today Nether Stowey is divided in two by the A39 but it does mean there is less traffic in the centre. Across the road from the main village is the imposing Stowey Court with a stone gazebo built into its outer wall and St Mary’s Church with its substantial memorial to Thomas Poole. Stowey Estate belonged to Lord Audley in 1343 but fell into ruin for several hundred years before being completed. A hoard of silverware was found nearby thought to date from the Civil War. Also on this side of the village is Cricketer Farm Shop and cafe.

title: TRADITIONAL FARM SHOP FAIR
subtitle: Our family run business offers a traditional farm shop serving a wide range local meat, dairy and veg plus plenty of seasonal and speciality produce.
bodyContent: TRADITIONAL FARM SHOP FAIR Our family run business offers a traditional farm shop serving a wide range local meat, dairy and veg plus plenty of seasonal and speciality produce. Well stocked butchery, delicatessen and dairy counters bring you all that's best in local West Country produce - our daily deliveries of free-range eggs are a local favourite. There's always a something unique and tasty to be found in our baked goods - cakes, biscuits and pastries. Outside the shop you'll find an seasonal garden products, logs and other fuels. BUTCHER At our butchery you'll find a selection of home produced meats, including mince, hams, sausages, and of course cuts of meat to meet your desires or requirements! Wherever possible, we look to use eco-friendly packaging for all our meat - because it's the right thing to do. At the moment, you can buy 3 packs of meat for £10 , and this includes all of our barbeque packs. Pop in to speak to our butcher or call before you visit to make sure we have exactly what you're looking for. DELICATESSEN We offer a wide and diverse selection of fresh fruit and veg, grown and sourced by us, for you. You can also find: Home cooked ham Home made sasuage rolls Quiches Pasties Pies
tagline: Our family run business offers a traditional farm shop serving a wide range local produce

title: Portishead Summer Show
subtitle: The Portishead Summer Show (formerly Portishead Flower Show) is a two day family show that combines a traditional flower show with activities that promote local country life, nature and the environment. In addition there is an array of family entertainment, live music, food, drink, children’s activities and a dog show.
bodyContent: The Portishead Summer Show (formerly Portishead Flower Show) is a two day family show that combines a traditional flower show with activities that promote local country life, nature and the environment. In addition there is an array of family entertainment, live music, food, drink, children’s activities and a dog show. For the flower show part of the event, the classes range from flowers, fruit and vegetables to art, photography and cookery. Download 2020 Schedule (PDF) The entertainment for that year included: The Marionettes with 1940s swing, The Quack Pack, singer, Louise Victoria, Punch and Judy shows, Ridgeside Little Nippers and Ridgeside Falconry. The were also adults and children’s sports events. The Show Field is located on the corner of Clapton Lane and Clevedon Road opposite Gordano School. The post code is BS20 7RA. Gordano School Academy kindly permit us to use their field for parking the weekend of the Show without charge.
tagline: The Portishead Summer Show (formerly Portishead Flower Show) is a two day family show

title: The Black Horse
subtitle: The kicker, as it is affectionately known, is a welcoming 14th Century inn steeped in charm and character, set in the tranquil countryside of Clapton-in-Gordano.
bodyContent: The kicker, as it is affectionately known, is a welcoming 14th Century inn steeped in charm and character, set in the tranquil countryside of Clapton-in-Gordano. The locals are extremely friendly as are the members of staff, who offer a cheery smile and plenty of conversation. Horses tethered up outside and tractors in the car park are the 'norm' at this delightful country pub. The home cooked food and filled baguettes served Monday to Saturday lunchtime 12-2:30pm are highly recommended and if you're not driving, the real ales and cider are definitely worth sampling. All of these can be enjoyed in the lovely beer garden, or on the patios and terraces surrounding the pub. A visit to the Black Horse is like being transported to a different world in. Sitting in the heart of the Gordano Valley, it's somewhere you can watch the world go by. There are plenty of glorious country walks that can be enjoyed from the Kicker and the Gordano Valley cycle route is close by. Keep an eye on the website for details of live music and other events or join them on Facebook.
tagline: The kicker, as it is affectionately known, is a welcoming 14th Century inn

title: Gotha Villa
subtitle: Gotha Villa is a characterful Victorian property in Portishead. Its enviable location means that it enjoys dramatic views of the Severn Estuary, whilst being within easy walking distance of a popular pub (serving good food) and the shops in the High Street.
bodyContent: Gotha Villa is a characterful Victorian property in Portishead. Its enviable location means that it enjoys dramatic views of the Severn Estuary, whilst being within easy walking distance of a popular pub (serving good food) and the shops in the High Street. Accommodation There is an ensuite double bedroom available to guests. The house has a lovely position over the Severn Estuary looking out at the remote Denny Island, to the Welsh hills beyond and the lake grounds and fields below. The bedroom overlooks the Victorian walled gardens. The room has a TV . There is also internet access. Off-street parking is available To enquire further or to book, please contact us . (We cannot take pets as we already have our own friendly Golden Retriever).

title: One Craft Gallery
subtitle: One Craft Gallery is a well-established co-operative owned and run by the craft gallery members. The gallery showcases members work and offers a wide range of creative and decorative pieces.
bodyContent: One Craft Gallery is a well-established co-operative owned and run by the craft gallery members. The gallery showcases members work and offers a wide range of creative and decorative pieces. The high-quality work displays ceramics, jewellery, knitwear, millinery, glass, painting, print making and woodturning. All gallery members are available to discuss commissions. On a regular basis, carefully identified guest exhibitors will supplement the wide range of products with their work. One Craft Gallery is ideally positioned in a grade 2 listed billing in the market square in the heart of Shepton Mallet in Somerset.

title: The Glastonbury Town House
subtitle: Paula welcomes you to her comfortable 4 Star Edwardian Bed & Breakfast close to Glastonbury Town Centre, Glastonbury Tor, Chalice Well Gardens , Rural Life Museum and other local attractions.
bodyContent: We offer a quality bed and breakfast service in the heart of Glastonbury , from where exploring Glastonbury Abbey, Glastonbury Tor and the Glastonbury Thorn is a matter of a short stroll. The Bed and Breakfast offers group bookings. 2 twin rooms and a king room offer up to 6 people accommodation. Paula offers packed lunches, afternoon tea and evening meals at an extra cost for group bookings. Liaise with Paula direct to book group bookings. The Townhouse is only a few minutes’ walk from the hustle of Glastonbury‘s busy town centre full of unusual shops, churches, historic buildings and varied cafes and bars. The house has far reaching views of Glastonbury town and the Mendip Hills beyond. The Townhouse offer secure facilities for cyclists and is Proximity to Millfield school. The Glastonbury Townhouse is 1 miles from Street and the Clarkes Outlet Village and 3 miles from the various nature reserves on the Somerset levels. We are 28 miles South of Bristol and Bath, 20 miles from Bristol International airport and within easy reach of Stonehenge , Yeovilton Airbase and other historic places of interest. The Glastonbury Townhouse can be used as a base for exploring the Isles of Avalon, Somerset Peat Levels, Exmoor (Lorna Doone country), the North Somerset Coast and large parts of the county of Dorset . Our visitors tell us that our proximity to Bristol Airport , Bath , the bath and west showgound, Shepton Mallet, Frome, Wells, Street, Yeovil is a key part of their decision to make their stay with us in Glastonbury . Of course we also have guests who visit specifically for the Glastonbury Festival, Glastonbury Extravaganza and the famous Glastonbury Carnival, we are on the route, watch from the comfort of your room! We are also open for Christmas and New Year bookings.

title: Living Homes
subtitle: Somerset’s Premier Furniture & Electrical Store
bodyContent: An independent, family-owned, retailer of upholstery, furniture, beds, flooring and electrical goods, based in multiple High Street locations in the town of Street, including the historic Board School. Description: Celebrating 50 years of trading in 2020, Living Homes has been operating from their landmark premises on Street High Street for almost 45 years. Specialising in the sale of upholstery, furniture, beds, flooring and electrical goods, Living Homes has built up an enviable reputation within the local community for quality, service and value. Expanding within the town over the years, Living Homes now occupies a number of different locations on the High Street, including the old Board School building. We pride ourselves on having created a relaxed, low-pressure environment, so please feel free to come and take a look around. Free customer parking is available at the rear of our Furniture Centre, from which all showrooms can easily be reached on foot.

title: Ask Italian
subtitle: FROM OUR KITCHEN TO YOUR HOME
bodyContent: The ASK Italian chain of restaurants produces a good range of Italian dishes including pizza, pasta and salads. The informal dining experience appeals to all age groups from lunches to evening meal. We chose just about the most beautiful building we could find for our ASK Italian restaurant in Wells: the Market Hall on Market Place. Of course it can’t compare to the sheer majesty of Wells Cathedral, or the moated Bishop’s Palace, both a few minutes’ stroll from our doors, but the historic architecture of Wells is one of the main reasons the city is such a lovely place to live and so popular with holidaymakers. We bring a little continental culture ourselves, overlooking the river with a view of Bishops castle, we boast a menu crammed with dishes flavoured with ingredients straight from Italy, and a friendly, relaxing atmosphere. Outside the city there are more natural and manmade wonders to explore. We recommend the Mendip Hills and Somerset Levels, Cheddar Gorge and Wookey Hole Caves in particular, but a stop at Wells Visitor Information Service in Wells Museum will allow you to plan a perfect itinerary. It’s just a five-minute walk from our restaurant.

title: Mistral
subtitle: As a spirited, independent teenager, our founder Tracey followed her love of the fashion industry to London.
bodyContent: She earned her stripes in the heartland of the great British highstreet, gaining experience on the buying team of a major retailer, before leaving the capital to start a family. In the mid-90s, still passionate about casual wear, Tracey joined forces with her father John, forming a formidable father-daughter team that combined their business skill and creative flair. As a result, the first Mistral shop opened in Malmesbury. Our Talented Team The Mistral brand has come a long way since we started out with just five staff (including John and Tracey)! Over time, and as a result of our team’s hard work and passion, Mistral has grown. Today you’ll find our stores on high streets across the UK, and a booming wholesale business run across the UK and Europe. We’re going from strength to strength online too – pulling out all the stops to ensure that our lovely customers can get their Mistral fashion fix wherever or whenever they please. John retired in March 2020, but has left the business in excellent hands. The future is looking as bright as Mistral's signature prints. When it comes to our distinctive style, we have our talented in-house creatives to thank. Inspired by the ever-changing landscapes around us, as well as destinations further afield, all of our beautiful print designs start life in our head office. Each one is crafted by our fabulous designers, who can be found cutting lino and happily painting on a daily basis. Our Company Statement We are a community of like-minded, empowered, creative and lively individuals who are brought together by fashion. Our uniquely crafted, quirky DNA and colourful in-house designs inspires confidence, pride and fun by making fashion a feeling to all. Bright and Beautiful At Mistral, our designs are guided by you, our lovely customers. You are totally central to the heart of the clothing we produce, and we will always listen to your loves, wishes, wants and feedback. We have always been passionate about the bright, bold prints that you tell us you love so much, and we’re committed to creating garments which bring a smile to your faces, and help you feel like the glorious individuals that you are. Our culture reflects our fun, family ethos. We care deeply about our staff, and in turn they care for each other and our customers. We try to reflect this commitment to a supportive, kind environment in our social responsibility. We are constantly reviewing and striving to do the very best we can for our customers, our community and the wider environment.

title: Luxe & Twine interiors
subtitle: Luxe & Twine, blending luxury style and rustic elements to create a interior space that is inspirational, comfortable and unique.
bodyContent: We are here to help you realize your dream interior from start to finish. With that in mind, we offer everything you need from wallpaper and fabrics to furniture, lighting, accessories and art, all at affordable prices. ​ In addition to our extensive retail line, we also provide a full interior design service. Our head designer, Jonathan Marshall, is ready to achieve your home's or business' full potential. From concept to finish, we can guide you every step of the way. ​ Jonathan Marshall has 6 years professional experience in interior design. He has completed work on several well known Somerset properties, including the beautiful Swan Hotel in Wells, the Oakhill Brewery Development, and The Shrubbery Hotel in Ilminster. His passion for interior design has brought him all the way from Las Vegas to share his design aesthetic with the British community.

title: The shop at Dunster Castle
subtitle: Explore the atmospheric 17th-century stables and visit the shop for high quality, original gifts and local products. Our shop is brimming with beautiful things, so you are sure to find something to tempt you, whether it's a treat for yourself or a gorgeous gift for a friend.
bodyContent: Explore the atmospheric 17th-century stables and visit the shop for high quality, original gifts and local products. Our shop is brimming with beautiful things, so you are sure to find something to tempt you, whether it's a treat for yourself or a gorgeous gift for a friend. A working watermill Bake the perfect loaf with some organic Dunster Watermill flour. Ground on site there's been a mill here since Domesday. If that doesn’t take your fancy how about some Dunster Watermill porridge or even a bag of muesli, made to our secret recipe. Harry's Cider Made in the heart of Somerset this premium quality cider is made on Harry's farm with 100% cider fruit. Different varieties are pressed, fermented and matured for several months before being blended to give a distinctive and refreshing taste. Find out more by visiting their website here. Handy history guide Get the most from your visit to Dunster Castle and Gardens with our new souvenir guidebook. With beautiful colour photographs, reconstruction drawings, historical images and a tour of the castle, it is a great momento of your day.

title: Bridgwater
subtitle: A rich legacy as a port and commercial centre is joined by Europe’s largest illuminated carnival, which lights up the streets every November.
bodyContent: Historic market town Bridgwater is home to the most illustrious of Somerset’s famous street carnivals A rich legacy as a port and commercial centre is joined by Europe’s largest illuminated carnival, which lights up the streets every November. What to do in Bridgwater A lively town with a rich history, Bridgwater Carnival best symbolises the town’s festive spirit. Residents near and far come together each November to witness the largest illuminated procession in Europe. To get in on the action, check the official Bridgwater Carnival Website for this year’s date, travel advice and accommodation information. Learn about the history of Bridgwater at the Blake Museum, where you’ll discover its past as a port and centre of commerce. The centre of Bridgwater is small enough to explore on foot, so head out to find examples of the fine architecture built during its commercial heydey - check out Cornhill, Castle Street and King Square for some key construction landmarks. Absorb some local culture at the Bridgwater Arts Centre - one of the first in the country - as well as Somerset Brick and Tile Museum, and the Bridgwater and Taunton Canal and Docks. Head to the town centre to find a combination of well-known and independent shops, plus lots of options for dining.

title: Taunton
subtitle: As befits a County Town, Taunton is steeped in history and has much to entertain our visitors, from the superb Somerset Museum in the remnants of the castle to the Cricket Ground and Racecourse. A centre for Arts and Culture, it has shops, cafes, restaurants, riverside walks and a weekly Farmers’ Market. Rooted between the majestic Quantock Hills, Somerset Levels and the woodland-cloaked Blackdowns, Taunton’s lively nature plays host to major sports centre Somerset County Cricket Club. It’s also
bodyContent: Things to do in Taunton Taunton’s ideal location and identity as county town of Somerset makes it perfect for exploring the wider area of Taunton Deane - everywhere from the cattle-grazed meadows of the Somerset Levels to the windswept heights of the Quantock Hills and striking Blackdowns . It also boasts an impressive cultural offering, ranging from museums and ancient monuments like the ancient Taunton Castle to contemporary centres like the Brewhouse Theatre & Arts Centre. Explore the Museum of Somerset , based at the 12th-century Taunton Castle, and follow Somerset’s history from prehistoric times to the present day. Stunning Perpendicular Gothic style architecture can be found soaring 163 feet above Taunton at the historic St Mary Magdalene Church, while Hestercombe Gardens are a paradise for nature lovers with fifty acres of enchanting gardens, stunning terraces, lakes and cascades. Taunton’s town centre is a mecca for shopping, with well-known high street brands and a brilliant selection of eateries and bars, as well as pubs serving locally-sourced food and drink. Take the Taunton Heritage Trail’s self-guided tour around the town’s historical sites to ensure you don’t miss a thing. Featured in the trail you’ll find Bath Place, a picturesque narrow street with 19th-century shop fronts now brimming with independent retailers and cafés. At the top of the high street proudly sits the Victorian-designed Vivary Park, home to the annual Taunton Flower Show, proudly described as the ‘The Chelsea of the West’. Taunton’s world-class sporting scene doesn’t disappoint. Catch a lively cricket match at The Cooper Associates County Ground or visit the Somerset Cricket Museum to explore the game’s fascinating history. Soak up a thrilling atmosphere at the Taunton Races or attend one of the racecourse’s brilliant events throughout the year, ranging from rural shows to concerts and circuses. For a quieter affair, the tranquility of Trull meadows and waterfall make them the perfect spot for a picnic or follow the towpath of the Bridgwater and Taunton Canal for a picturesque cycle ride. Taunton Visitor Centre Now based in the western wing of the landmark Market House, the Taunton Visitor Centre is the place to go to make the most of your time in Taunton. The county town has plenty to offer from individual boutiques to historic architecture, modern dining to traditional tea rooms and unspoilt views to the Blackdown Hills and Quantock Hills (both Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty). Taunton offers a wide mix of activities, attractions and events - we can’t wait to help you plan the perfect trip! Services offered: The Taunton Visitor Centre holds information on many wide and varied things to do within Taunton and the surrounding areas. Now a part of the bustling town centre mix, we welcome over 100,000 visitors and local residents through our doors each year. The Visitor Centre Box Office offers tickets for most local and regional events taking place, including the hugely popular Taunton Flower Show. We are a box office for the Brewhouse Theatre and Tacchi-Morris Arts Centre in Taunton and the Playhouse Theatre in Weston-super-Mare. If you're looking for that special "experience" gift then give the gift of theatre with our Theatre Tokens Gift Cards. The Travel Centre acts as an agent for Bakers Dolphin, Berry’s Coaches, Falcon bus service, Holiday Extras and National Express. As well as the booking service we offer friendly advice for local transport, parking and accommodation to make your trip stress-free. We also offer multiple advertising and marketing opportunities to local businesses, events organisers, charities and more. Souvenirs and Publications: The Visitor Centre shop is bursting with products that will help you take home a taste of Taunton, including locally produced biscuits and preserves, hand-crafted cards and a variety of colourful souvenirs. We also stock a large range of local maps, guides and books to help you truly discover Taunton and the surrounding areas.

title: Ilminster
subtitle: Ilminster takes its name from the River Ile and the Minster church dating from 1450. The town grew up around the church and some of the oldest buildings are close to the churchyard including the grammar school founded in 1549.
bodyContent: In Victorian times the town was an important staging post for travellers with east-west and north-south routes converging there. Market Square has a colonnaded market cross rebuilt in 1813 and is surrounded by handsome buildings. Ilminster is an attractive and peaceful town with a good variety of shops, a theatre and enchanting street names like Strawberry Bank. Must See and Do Indulge in retail therapy at shops like Dyers - a traditional drapers Enjoy the latest art at the Meeting House Arts Centre with coffee and a cake or lunch Find ancient and modern at the 15th century Minster with engraved glass doors added for the Millenium Watch the latest production at the Warehouse Theatre Sample cider and discover how it's made at Perry's Cider Mill in Dowlish Wake Learn something different at Dillington House where an exciting range of courses, concerts and events is on offer Stretch your legs on the Stopline Way - walk details from the Information Centre Local Facilities Accommodation Library Petrol Station Pharmacy Post Office Pubs and eating places Supermarket and range of small shops Road Directions lminster is 10 miles south east of Taunton and the M5 Maps: Multimap Rail: Nearest stations are Taunton and Crewkerne Bus: for routes and timetables got to the https://www.visitsomerset.co.uk/plan-your-visit/travel/

title: Warrens Holiday Village
subtitle: Welcome to Warrens Holiday Village! We offer superb lodge-style self catering and hotel-style accommodation in a tranquil setting in Clevedon, North Somerset, just 5 minutes from Junction 20 of the M5, offering easy access to Bristol City Centre, the South West and the M4 corridor.
bodyContent: Holiday Park Self Catering & Hotel in Somerset Our comfortable chalets accommodate from between 1 and 4 people, all being en-suite, double glazed and central heated throughout, freeview TV and the additional benefit of full catering facilities and a separate sitting room. Please be aware that we supply bed linen only in our self catering chalets. All ensuite rooms have bed linen and towels provided. title: The Princess Theatre and Arts Centre, Burnham on Sea
subtitle: The Princess Theatre and Arts Centre, is the main venue for arts and entertainment in Burnham on Sea and Highbridge welcoming more than 7000 audience members last year.
bodyContent: The Princess Theatre and Arts Centre, is the main venue for arts and entertainment in Burnham on Sea and Highbridge welcoming more than 7000 audience members last year. Our Mission is to enrich, educate and entertain our community by providing superior theatre and arts experiences. Our regular programme of events, shows and talks; produced by professional and community companies is ever expanding, attracting a diverse audience from across the county and beyond. Take a look at our What’s On . Our strong links across the community means the arts centre offers a great deal of activities to cater for all tastes including: crafts, visual arts, youth theatres and wellbeing groups. Take a look at our Activities Page. The Gallery space in the Cafe plays host to artists both professional and amateur alike and we are very proud of the work that is presented on our walls. 2021 will see our Theatre and studio space beautifully refurbished and with further capital development plans in the pipeline everyone at the Princess is excited.

title: Blakehay Theatre Re-Opening
subtitle: The Blakehay Theatre, in Weston-super-Mare, is delighted to announce that they are re-opening in January 2022.
bodyContent: Having closed in March 2020 due to the pandemic, and after receiving a Culture Recovery Fund Grant in October 2020, the theatre staff were able to create Blakehay@Home, and stage ‘Comedy at the Quarry’ in June 2021. However, the majority of this fund was to make alterations to the theatre and in May 2021, the contractors moved into the theatre. During 2021 the contractors have been busy installing a new ventilation system and altering the backstage dressing rooms. At the same time the theatre has undergone a complete electrical re-wire making the theatre future-proof and helping with the theatre’s carbon footprint. Work on the theatre is now in the last stages of completion and will re-open to the public in January 2022 with the first performance performed by Weston Operatic Society juniors, OPPITTS, with their aptly named show ‘Opening Up’ with songs from all your favourite shows from stage and screen on Saturday 29 th and Sunday 30 th January, tickets on sale now. The studios will be re-opening in week commencing Monday 10 th January with the return of our Community Classes, including a few new classes for 2022. Check out the theatre website for more information. “We are so happy to be opening the theatre bringing live performances back. It has been a tough couple of years, not just for us but for the whole industry. The pandemic has impacted heavily on theatre and we hope that 2022 will be our busiest year yet. We have an amazing variety of shows and we are confident that there is something for everyone. We can’t wait to welcome people back into this beautiful building, there really is nothing like sitting in a theatre and watching live performance.” – Sally Heath, Theatre Manager. As an important venue in the heart of Weston-super-Mare the Blakehay Theatre will be welcoming back local groups to perform on the stage as well as professional productions that were postponed from 2020. “The small but beautiful Blakehay Theatre is the town’s own theatre, owned by the people of our town through the town council. It is wonderful to see it reopening after nearly 2 years and a refurbishment and I’m definitely going to take the opportunity to see a show in early 2022.” Malcolm Nicholson, Town Clerk The Blakehay Theatre is an approved venue to be able to use the industry-wide ‘See it Safely’ mark, so you can feel confident and safe knowing that our venue is COVID-secure and will be following the latest government guidance. If you would like to see the work that has been done at the theatre, there will be an open day on Saturday 22 nd January 2022 from 10am to 4pm . Everyone is welcome to pop in and have a look around the theatre as well as buy tickets to our upcoming shows and events. For further information and to book your tickets, please visit the theatre’s website www.blakehaytheatre.co.uk
tagline: The Blakehay Theatre, in Weston-super-Mare, is delighted to announce that they are re-opening

title: Queen of Cups Restaurant and Freehouse
subtitle: Queen of Cups is a restaurant and free house based in Glastonbury that focuses on local and seasonal food and drink combined with Mediterranean flavours. The talented kitchen team is helmed by Chef Proprietor Ayesha Kalaji. We stock local wines, ales and spirits and offer unique takes on cocktails and mocktails. Queen of Cups caters for omnivores, vegetarians, vegans and special diets alike.
bodyContent: Queen of Cups is open for lunch and dinner year round. The menu changes seasonally and all desserts are made in-house. The space features a lovely back garden as well as a suntrap pavement terrace for after-work drinks. We have been named the #1 restaurant in Glastonbury on TripAdvisor, as well as #3 in Somerset. As we occupy what was the famous Hawthorns Hotel, we have kept on their weekly music nights such as Sunday Blues Jam and Tuesday Open Mic (please refer to Facebook or our website for event updates). Not forgetting our incredibly well stocked bar, we are a proud member of CAMRA: the Campaign for Real Ale. Queen of Cups also offers a private dining room that seats up to 12 people, curated by Kim Von Coels of Heart of the Tribe. In the private dining room we offer our popular Queen's Feast sharing menu, as well as create custom menus.
tagline: Queen of Cups is a restaurant and free house based in Glastonbury

title: Mahalia's Kitchen
subtitle: Mahalia's Kitchen, formally known as Mahalia's Whole Food Café, was opened in August 2019 in the quiet village of Street, Somerset, by Mahalia Purchase a Certified Health Coach. Mahalia became a health coach in 2017, after overcoming her health challenges through lifestyles changes. The entrepreneur was born in Guyana, South America, formally knowas British Guiana.
bodyContent: She grew up helping her parents in their restaurant as a little girl, where many life skills were learnt, including her parent's well kept secret recipes. In 2005, Mahalia moved to Street, Somerset and now has a family of her own raising two amazing children. Her love and passion for good, healthy, tasty whole foods, catapulted her to open acafé offering fresh, seasonal whole foods. However after the pandemic struck, her innovation would have enabled her to stay in business. Mahalia embarked on creating an outdoor space with a tropical feel - "Backyard Café". The mouth-watering menu now reflects her vibrant Guyanese Caribbean roots. As an establishment, we are an Outdoor Café and Takeaway Service. One can guarantee to be served tasty, healthy, seasonal wholefoods infused with Guyanese and Caribbean flavours. The needs of everyone is catered for here; - vegetarians, vegans, meat eaters, and those with special gluten, dairy free and other dietary needs. You have special healthy lifestyle diets? Come on down! You are not to be excluded! Most of our ingredients are sourced from local suppliers. Friday is our Curry Club Day offering mouth-watering Guyanese curries! Mahalia's Kitchen offers a Click & Collect and Delivery Services. Plunge into the experience today! You won't regret it! Mouth watering? after reading this? Waste no time in making Mahalia's Kitchen yourfood stop today!

title: Revo Kitchen & Terrace
subtitle: Revo Kitchen & Terrace, is an enticing new restaurant located on Weston-super-Mare’s seafront in what was, until March 2019, the SeaQuarium. It’s hard to imagine anywhere that could offer better views whilst enjoying a meal, a snack or tea and cake in a relaxing environment. With views over the bay, the Grand Pier and over the water to Wales, it’s fast becoming the venue of choice.
bodyContent: And talking of the environment, Revo is highly conscious of its duty to care for our beautiful world. There are paper compostable straws for all drinks, all takeaway packaging is compostable and they aim to use local suppliers for all produce. Cakes and bakes are not bought in, the in-house bakery team come in as early as 3am some mornings to produce traditional and innovative baked goods, created freshly each day with locally sourced ingredients and high-quality produce. The homemade bread is a key ingredient in some of the brunch, lunch and dinner dishes. Weston-super-Mare is blessed with spectacular sunsets and with its panoramic windows, Revo is the perfect venue for a sundowner cocktail or mocktail, they even have fire-pits on the terrace which they’ll be pleased to light for you on request. You can get an idea of some of the delights on offer from their main menu here Revo Kitchen welcomes dogs on their leads, just remember that excessive barking is not so welcome, there’s a “3 barks and you’re out” policy. And if you’re feeling active, there’s an amazing indoor Glo Golf crazy golf course, try your skills in the darkened room with glowing golf holes and a bar in the middle! Normally open from 12 noon daily, it’s a great fun activity suitable for all age groups.
tagline: Revo Kitchen & Terrace, is an enticing new restaurant

title: Blakehay Theatre Re-Opening
subtitle: The Blakehay Theatre, in Weston-super-Mare, is delighted to announce that they are re-opening in January 2022.
bodyContent: Having closed in March 2020 due to the pandemic, and after receiving a Culture Recovery Fund Grant in October 2020, the theatre staff were able to create Blakehay@Home, and stage ‘Comedy at the Quarry’ in June 2021. However, the majority of this fund was to make alterations to the theatre and in May 2021, the contractors moved into the theatre. During 2021 the contractors have been busy installing a new ventilation system and altering the backstage dressing rooms. At the same time the theatre has undergone a complete electrical re-wire making the theatre future-proof and helping with the theatre’s carbon footprint. Work on the theatre is now in the last stages of completion and will re-open to the public in January 2022 with the first performance performed by Weston Operatic Society juniors, OPPITTS, with their aptly named show ‘Opening Up’ with songs from all your favourite shows from stage and screen on Saturday 29 th and Sunday 30 th January, tickets on sale now. The studios will be re-opening in week commencing Monday 10 th January with the return of our Community Classes, including a few new classes for 2022. Check out the theatre website for more information. “We are so happy to be opening the theatre bringing live performances back. It has been a tough couple of years, not just for us but for the whole industry. The pandemic has impacted heavily on theatre and we hope that 2022 will be our busiest year yet. We have an amazing variety of shows and we are confident that there is something for everyone. We can’t wait to welcome people back into this beautiful building, there really is nothing like sitting in a theatre and watching live performance.” – Sally Heath, Theatre Manager. As an important venue in the heart of Weston-super-Mare the Blakehay Theatre will be welcoming back local groups to perform on the stage as well as professional productions that were postponed from 2020. “The small but beautiful Blakehay Theatre is the town’s own theatre, owned by the people of our town through the town council. It is wonderful to see it reopening after nearly 2 years and a refurbishment and I’m definitely going to take the opportunity to see a show in early 2022.” Malcolm Nicholson, Town Clerk The Blakehay Theatre is an approved venue to be able to use the industry-wide ‘See it Safely’ mark, so you can feel confident and safe knowing that our venue is COVID-secure and will be following the latest government guidance. If you would like to see the work that has been done at the theatre, there will be an open day on Saturday 22 nd January 2022 from 10am to 4pm . Everyone is welcome to pop in and have a look around the theatre as well as buy tickets to our upcoming shows and events. For further information and to book your tickets, please visit the theatre’s website www.blakehaytheatre.co.uk
tagline: The Blakehay Theatre, in Weston-super-Mare, is delighted to announce that they are re-opening

title: The Princess Theatre and Arts Centre, Burnham on Sea
subtitle: The Princess Theatre and Arts Centre, is the main venue for arts and entertainment in Burnham on Sea and Highbridge welcoming more than 7000 audience members last year.
bodyContent: The Princess Theatre and Arts Centre, is the main venue for arts and entertainment in Burnham on Sea and Highbridge welcoming more than 7000 audience members last year. Our Mission is to enrich, educate and entertain our community by providing superior theatre and arts experiences. Our regular programme of events, shows and talks; produced by professional and community companies is ever expanding, attracting a diverse audience from across the county and beyond. Take a look at our What’s On . Our strong links across the community means the arts centre offers a great deal of activities to cater for all tastes including: crafts, visual arts, youth theatres and wellbeing groups. Take a look at our Activities Page. The Gallery space in the Cafe plays host to artists both professional and amateur alike and we are very proud of the work that is presented on our walls. 2021 will see our Theatre and studio space beautifully refurbished and with further capital development plans in the pipeline everyone at the Princess is excited.

bodyContent: The Moon and Sixpence is one of the most popular pubs in Clevedon. Situated in a prime seafront position looking out over the Bristol Channel and facing Clevedon's famous Victorian Pier. The Moon & Sixpence is a welcoming, popular bar, restaurant and hotel offers a range of accommodation and entertainment as well as great pub food in comfortable surroundings. title: Warrens Holiday Village

bodyContent: Holiday Park Self Catering & Hotel in Somerset Our comfortable chalets accommodate from between 1 and 4 people, all being en-suite, double glazed and central heated throughout, freeview TV and the additional benefit of full catering facilities and a separate sitting room. Please be aware that we supply bed linen only in our self catering chalets. All ensuite rooms have bed linen and towels provided. title: The shop at Dunster Castle
subtitle: Explore the atmospheric 17th-century stables and visit the shop for high quality, original gifts and local products. Our shop is brimming with beautiful things, so you are sure to find something to tempt you, whether it's a treat for yourself or a gorgeous gift for a friend.
bodyContent: Explore the atmospheric 17th-century stables and visit the shop for high quality, original gifts and local products. Our shop is brimming with beautiful things, so you are sure to find something to tempt you, whether it's a treat for yourself or a gorgeous gift for a friend. A working watermill Bake the perfect loaf with some organic Dunster Watermill flour. Ground on site there's been a mill here since Domesday. If that doesn’t take your fancy how about some Dunster Watermill porridge or even a bag of muesli, made to our secret recipe. Harry's Cider Made in the heart of Somerset this premium quality cider is made on Harry's farm with 100% cider fruit. Different varieties are pressed, fermented and matured for several months before being blended to give a distinctive and refreshing taste. Find out more by visiting their website here. Handy history guide Get the most from your visit to Dunster Castle and Gardens with our new souvenir guidebook. With beautiful colour photographs, reconstruction drawings, historical images and a tour of the castle, it is a great momento of your day.

title: Wraxall Vineyard
subtitle: The Grapes. The View. The Experience. The Memories.
bodyContent: Working in harmony with our surroundings, nurturing the vines and understanding the terroir is at the heart of the Vineyard; and the Vineyard is where great wine begins! Situated on a beautiful south-facing hill just south of the Mendips in Somerset, Wraxall Vineyard is surrounded by verdant countryside and breath-taking views. Blessed with a mild South West climate and rich fertile soils, our location is perfect for growing vines. Yet growing vines and producing wine is a slow process and a real labour of love. Owners David and Lexa took over Wraxall Vineyard as a family venture in 2021. Their aim and vision is to dedicate time and passion into producing truly great wines for all to share, celebrate and enjoy.
tagline: The Grapes. The View. The Experience. The Memories.

title: Alfred Gillett Trust
subtitle: Explore our magnificent collection based on the Clark family and their 200-year-old global shoemaking business. With over 100,000 objects, we are open to the public for research, enquiries, tours, and events. We are building a museum that will inspire the world with the family and community stories behind Clarks shoes, opening by 2025.
bodyContent: With objects and archives spanning six generations of a family firm, we tell the story of the development of Street as a company village, 200 years of shoemaking heritage, the Clark family and their economic, social and political concerns based around their Quaker beliefs, and local history, including our popular collection of fossilised marine reptiles – the ichthyosaurs that swam in these waters under our feet 200 million years ago, found right here in Street. Community and family are rooted at the heart of Clarks history. Iconic material from marketing design, commissioned from the best artists and photographers of the day, can be found alongside examples of shoes from across the globe, collected to energise and inform creative design. Day-to-day records of running a company over two hundred years sit alongside stories of innovation and experimentation with fascinating stories of factory working life. With aspirations to build a museum and to expand the archive we are poised and ready to convert the site to a fully open public offer in time for the 200-year anniversary of the founding of the company in 2025 including a number of galleries, newly landscaped grounds, a café and a shop, welcoming visitors from near and afar. We operate a research and enquiry service by appointment, conduct tours and talks for interested groups, and have an annual programme of events such as outdoor theatre and cinema in the grounds of the Grange.

bodyContent: Tucked behind a high wall up a quiet no-through lane, Maplestone dates from 1650, once part of a workers' cottage row. Great local-produce breakfasts, early options, free fast wi-fi throughout.

title: RISE
subtitle: Built in the early 1800s, RISE is a lovingly restored former church located in the heart of Frome. Within the building there are two venue hire spaces catering for a wide variety of classes and events, a contemporary art gallery, a gift shop, and a cafe and garden to enjoy.
bodyContent: We believe the history and heritage of RISE and the role the building has played in the togetherness of the community is worth preserving. As a family owned and thriving community hub we aim to honour the history and heritage of our magnificent building, supporting community togetherness in everything we do. As a place to be together, RISE offers: VENUE HIRE with two light, airy and beautifully restored rooms, The Old School Room and The Sun Room - perfect for uplifting classes, workshops and events. THE WHITTOX GALLERY, a stunningly beautiful contemporary art gallery exhibiting the finest contemporary and cutting-edge artists and designers. CAFE run by RYE BAKERY, an independent cafe who champion local and organic produce and use traditional baking methods and ancient grains to create artisan bread. With a play space for children, a wicker pod for breastfeeding mums and serving delicious pizzas, the cafe is a popular choice for families. OFFICES & WORK SPACE - currently leased to OpenStoryTellers, a charity which works to enrich and empower the lives of people with learning disabilities and autism.
tagline: Built in the early 1800s, RISE is a lovingly restored former church

title: Yew Tree House
subtitle: We look forward to welcoming guests to Yew Tree House. This area of Somerset is a great place to come away to, for a quiet break, a busy family holiday or a catch up with friends and family living or staying in the area.
bodyContent: Yew Tree House offers a warm welcome near the seven-mile Burnham-Berrow-Brean beach, the King Charles III coast path and Brean resort — ideal for quiet breaks, family holidays or exploring Somerset. Six comfortable rooms (three in the main house, three garden rooms) offer doubles, kings, twins and family options, each with WIFI, heating, TV and tea/coffee facilities. Enjoy private parking, bike storage and a relaxing garden. Award-winning breakfast, using local produce, is included daily. Walk to the beach or Brean, or reach nearby golf courses, cycle routes, Brean Splash pool and evening entertainment. Easily accessed via M5 Junction 22 or the Somerset Coaster bus.
tagline: Bed & Breakfast in Burnham on Sea, Somerset.

title: Stay Wells and Somerset (Grange Cottage)
subtitle: Lovely property in the heart of Somerset, sleeps 10 Bowlish Grange is a beautiful house of Jacobean origins, our large guest cottage (Grange Cottage) is available on a self catering basis. We are close to art and culture, wonderful countryside, pubs and restaurants. Visitors will love the historical setting. The cottage and garden is perfect for families.
bodyContent: Bowlish Grange is a beautiful house of Jacobean origins with a large garden for the little ones to play. We are close to art and culture, wonderful countryside, pubs and restaurants. Visitors will love the historical setting and the location. We are close to Glastonbury, Wells and the Bath and West Showground. The cottage is perfect for couples, families and business groups. We offer four double bedrooms. There are two private bathrooms each with shower and bath facilities. There is a large reception room with lovely parquet flooring, corner sofa and widescreen 4K UHD smart television with on-demand players and additional speakers. There is an impressive kitchen with granite tops and inbuilt appliances which is conveniently positioned between the indoor and outdoor dining areas. The private courtyard also offers a large BBQ and a dining area for up to 10 people. Additionally there is also a spacious decking area which is perfect for evening drinks in the sun. Ultra fast broadband is provided. The cottage is an annex of the main house with its own front door and kitchen. It is entirely self-contained. There will usually be someone around to help you throughout your stay and give you tips on the highlights of the local area including the beautiful Mendip Hills and the historic cities and towns of Bath, Wells and Glastonbury. Bowlish is a short walk from the historic town of Shepton Mallet and very close to Wells.

title: The Curzon Cinema Clevedon
subtitle: The Curzon cinema has been at the centre of life in Clevedon, North Somerset, since 1912.
bodyContent: The Curzon cinema has been at the centre of life in Clevedon, North Somerset, since 1912. One of the country’s oldest, continuously running cinemas: screening everything from blockbusters to classics and arthouse cinema, hosting live comedy and events in a beautiful heritage venue. Opening its doors in 1912, only 5 days after the Titanic disaster, the Curzon is one of the country’s oldest, continuously running cinemas. Enlarged in the 1920s, the neo-classical building houses a 320-seater auditorium, panelled in a rare example of pressed tin; a bar; a 1930s Christie pipe organ and a unique collection of cinema equipment. Alongside our varied film programme, we host live comedy, music and performance and are fully engaged with youth, arts and other community organisations, also running Front Room Cinema which takes the cinema experience out to residential homes. We are supported by a fantastic team of volunteers, who support our Front of House staff, help in the bar, give guided tours and help to maintain our lovely building. Click here you’re interested in finding out about volunteering at the Curzon.
tagline: The Curzon cinema has been at the centre of life in Clevedon, North Somerset, since 1912.

title: The Regal Theatre
subtitle: The Regal Theatre stands in the centre of Minehead, and provides a wide ranging programme of professional and community entertainment that includes drama, film, comedy, dance, music and performance of all kinds
bodyContent: The Regal Theatre stands in the centre of Minehead, and is loved by the people of West Somerset for its wide ranging programme of professional and community entertainment that includes drama, film, comedy, dance, music and performance of all kinds. There are also occasional displays of work carried out by local artists. The theatre bar is open during intervals and before each performance. It is an ideal place to meet friends and enjoy refreshments or to relax on the balcony overlooking the town centre. The MATA Regal Theatre Company Ltd runs the theatre with the help of an army of volunteers all of whom work hard to make you feel welcome and to ensure that you enjoy a splendid night out. .Regal Theatre Gift Vouchers are available from the Box Office BOX OFFICE OPENING HOURS: 9.30am to 12.00pm Monday to Saturday . Please note that most shows are available for booking, online, until 11am on the day of the show. After that, tickets are available via the box-office or at the door.

title: The Northfield
subtitle: The Northfield Hotel is located on the lower slopes of Northhill in nearly 2 acres of landscaped gardens reputed to have been laid out by Gertrude Jekyll.
bodyContent: We have wonderful views from our elevated position from the coast to the Quantocks, Brendon hills and indeed Exmoor itself, walking from the hotel you are on Exmoor in only a few minutes. Our 30 bedrooms are well appointed with en-suite bath or shower, digital TV, tea facilities, complimentary Wi-Fi and bottled water. We have eight categories of bedrooms; from our Classic Singles and Doubles which are very comfortably furnished, to our Superior rooms which are more spacious and benefitting from better views and then our Deluxe being larger still with slippers and sweets included. Our Superior and Deluxe rooms all benefit from new luxury beds and are 5ft, 6ft or twin bedded. Our finest room is our Suite, which is very spacious with stunning views, separate seating area, a roll top bath and separate walk-in shower and super-king sized bed along with dressing gowns, slippers and fresh fruit on arrival. Should you wish to book Dinner, Bed and Breakfast the charge is from £22.50 per person per night.

title: Wells Cathedral
subtitle: Built between 1175 and 1490 Wells Cathedral in Somerset has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals”.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built between 1175 and 1490 Wells Cathedral has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals”. Set in the medieval heart of England’s smallest city, and an easy drive from Bristol, Bath and Cardiff, Wells is the earliest English Cathedral to be built in the Gothic style. The current building is a significant landmark in the South West of England, has an international reputation and is TripAdvisor ranked number one for things to do in Wells and in Somerset. Wells Cathedral has unique features that separate it from other English cathedrals including its iconic West Front and the beautiful ‘scissor arches’ supporting the central tower, as well as one of the largest collections of historic stained glass in the country. The Cathedral also boasts the famous Wells Clock (which is considered to be the second oldest clock mechanism in Great Britain), the fascinating octagonal Chapter House and one of only four chained libraries in the UK. Wells Cathedral welcomes thousands of visitors each year who join in with regular daily services and events or who come simply to enjoy the calm and hospitality of this wonderful and holy place. Stay, if you can, for Evensong with the Cathedral’s world renowned choir (term times); a peaceful and moving end to your day. Tours: Discover hidden spaces and chambers, explore the south transept roof space and marvel at the nave from a very different perspective via the Cathedral's popular and longer High Parts tours which can be pre-booked via the website at www.wellscathedral.org.uk/visit/tours . The Cathedral runs complimentary ground floor tours daily (Monday-Saturday) and tickets include access to an audio tour. Guided tours for group visits can also be pre-booked via the Visits team at visits@wellscathedral.org.uk Families When term breaks up the Cathedral offers creative workshops for children accompanied by their parents or guardians. We also provide free children explorer backpacks which are available free of charge on arrival and which help children to learn about the main highlights and history of the Cathedral. Group Visits: The group rate (+10) for pre booked self guided visits is £10 and £12 to include a highlights tour. Unreserved groups are charged the standard on the door price of £14. For more information, and to book, please email visits@wellscathedral.org.uk Vicars’ Close: Adjoining the Cathedral is Vicars’ Close, believed to be the only complete medieval street left in England. Vicars’ Close was designed to provide accommodation for the Vicars Choral, who sing the daily services, and this is still the case today. This centuries-old tradition is unique and a much valued part of the continuing life of Wells Cathedral. The medieval windows of the houses and the garden archways seem to have survived more or less intact until the early nineteenth century, and even now a few still exist. Make a Day of It A warm welcome awaits you at our Cathedral shop which stocks a wide range of unique mementoes and gifts. The Loft at Wells Cathedral café is also open daily for coffee, delicious home-made lunches and afternoon teas http://www.wellscathedral.org.uk
tagline: Wells Cathedral in Somerset has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals".

title: The Castle at Taunton
subtitle: The Castle Hotel is in the centre of Taunton the old County town for Somerset. It is the gateway to the Black Downs and Exmoor National Park, West Somerset Railway, being 5 minute drive from the main line train station from London Paddington, whilst being 30 minutes from the M5 Junction 25 and close many amenities.
bodyContent: The Castle at Taunton is one of the UK’s most historic & prestigious 4 Star Hotels, having been at the forefront of British cuisine for 40 years. We also operate Brazz, which since 1998 has provided the blueprint for British Brasseries across the country The Castle Hotel is a unique family-owned hotel set in a historic building in the heart of Taunton in Somerset. A simple ethos lies at the heart of the hotel – to offer the warmest of welcomes, give the utmost personal attention and exemplary service to each & every guest. The Castle Hotel is a one-off, not a link in a chain. The Castle’s reputation for fine food and wine, comfort, and attentive service has been built by three generations of the Chapman Family, with a passion for promoting the highest standards in every aspect of the hotel. Taunton lies at the heart of the region, making The Castle the ideal base from which to explore the history, magic and wonder of the West Country. Each of The Castle’s 44 bedrooms are individually decorated, offering its own personality and comfort away from home. Whether you’re looking for healthy or hearty, you’ll find it all at the award-winning restaurant, Brazz. Featuring a wide-ranging menu, you’ll find favourites such as Brazz Fishcakes – which have been present since day one – as well as Quantock Lamb, Brixham Crab and much more. The Castle’s legendary afternoon teas are served Wednesday to Sunday from 2:30pm - 4:00pm. Freshly baked scones with West Country clotted cream and strawberry jam, elegant finger sandwiches, pastries and cakes along with a fine selection of loose-leaf tea, make this a very special occasion… especially if you add a bottle of champagne.
tagline: A unique family-owned hotel set in a historic building in Taunton, the county town of Somerset

title: Wookey Hole Caves & Attractions
subtitle: Wookey Hole Caves is a magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for all ages. It’s an experience millions of years in the making with plenty to do inside and out. Enjoy vintage penny arcades, museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, and of course the famous, beautiful caves.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Wookey Hole Caves and attractions lies In the heart of Somerset. A magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for the young and young at heart. When you visit Wookey Hole, you’ll enjoy an experience millions of years in the making. There is plenty to do inside and out, from vintage penny arcades to museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, to name but a few of the attractions. Not forgetting the breathtakingly beautiful caves, for which Wookey Hole is renowned. Your visit will take you through 8 chambers. Each with a unique beauty and story. You’ll also pass our cheese tunnel, home to the delicious Wookey Hole cheese. The cheese is not the only resident of the caves. Over the years, Wookey Hole has been home to giant hyenas, bears, Neanderthals, and many local people. It has even been a site of pagan and Roman worship. You’ll find Wookey Hole holds a surprise around every corner. You might even get to meet our most famous resident, the Witch of Wookey Hole. We have found she most likes to visit during school holidays! The world-famous Wookey Hole Circus School performs at Wookey Hole at weekends and in School Holidays. Every year over 250,000 people visit Wookey Hole and take-home cherished memories of a great day out. Whether it is your first time or your fiftieth, there is always something new to discover. We can’t wait to welcome you.
tagline: At Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions, Somerset, there’s always fun and adventure to be had.

title: Clevedon Court, National Trust
subtitle: Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is a remarkable survival from the medieval period.
bodyContent: Clevedon Court in Clevedon, Somerset, National Trust property is an outstanding 14th-century manor house and 18th-century terraced garden Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is a remarkable survival from the medieval period. The house was purchased by Abraham Elton in 1709 and it is still the much-loved family home of his descendants today. Explore the striking display of Eltonware pottery and a fascinating collection of Nailsea glass.
tagline: Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is remarkable.

title: Koffmann & Mr. White's
subtitle: The first joint venture between culinary legends, Pierre Koffmann and Marco Pierre White is the brasserie-style eatery Koffmann & Mr. White's.
bodyContent: The first joint venture between culinary legends, Pierre Koffmann and Marco Pierre White is the brasserie-style eatery Koffmann & Mr. White's. The brasserie is located in central Bath just around from Bath Abbey, the Roman Baths and only five minutes walk from Bath Spa train station. Serving a mix of English and French classics for the discerning customer looking for good quality, the restaurant offers French dishes such as Snails à la Bourguignonne and Poulet noir Grand-mère alongside English favourites like Shepherd's Pie and Fish and Chips. Affordable food is served in a relaxed, stylish and unpretentious environment befitting the Georgian surroundings.
tagline: The first joint venture between culinary legends, Pierre Koffmann and Marco Pierre White.

title: The Crown at Wells
subtitle: Located in the very heart of Wells, the 15th century Crown is within easy walking distance of the Cathedral and Bishop’s Palace
bodyContent: Located in the very heart of Wells, the 15th century Crown is within easy walking distance of the Cathedral and Bishop’s Palace, making it a great base from which to explore this wonderful part of Somerset. There is a choice of affordable en-suite rooms, including four poster and family rooms. All are comfortably furnished and have Egyptian cotton sheets and bath sheet towels as standard. There is free Wifi throughout the building. A great selection of imaginative dishes, including tasty vegetarian options, are served in Anton’s Bistrot at The Crown and the Penn Bar throughout the day. All dishes are freshly prepared to order using the finest local produce, wherever possible. Friendly service in relaxed surroundings. Everyone is very welcome.

title: Longleat
subtitle: Explore a world of adventure at Longleat. From a Drive Through Safari expedition, to discovering inside our iconic Elizabethan mansion, there’s plenty to entertain you.
bodyContent: Explore a world of adventure at Longleat. From a Drive Through Safari expedition, to discovering inside our iconic Elizabethan mansion, there’s plenty to entertain you. Travel the globe within this Wiltshire estate – stop off at African Village for a chance to see our new pack of African painted dogs, herd of Grants zebras and leap with lemurs. Say hi to our cheeky monkeys and bring your pack to meet our pack of wolves! Listen out for the Longleat lions’ roars as you explore. Continue your adventure on foot and walk with mischievous meerkats in Jungle Kingdom, feed rainbow lorikeets and watch our playful giant otters. Don’t forget to visit Koala Creek to see England’s only resident koalas, watch our sleepy sloths climb around or check in with our native red squirrels. Hop on board the Boat Safari and explore Half Mile Pond. Home to our family of noisy Californian sea lions, views of Gorilla Colony and Colobus monkeys will make quite a splash. Why not feed the sea lions to add to your unique day out? All aboard Longleat Railway! Enjoy a delightful ride around the lake and keep an eye on the action from our miniature railway. Or discover more about our history by adding a guided house tour to your itinerary. If your little cubs are looking to play, be sure to visit Little Explorer’s Garden and the Adventure Castle for plenty of room to let their imaginations run wild. Why not challenge yourself to our Hedge Maze and see if you can find your way through the winding passages? And no day is complete without a ride on Rockin’ Rhino! Book your tickets for a day out like no other or make your visit extra special with a VIP experience!
tagline: Longleat, nestled within 900 acres of ‘Capability’ Brown landscaped grounds.

title: Fleet Air Arm Museum
subtitle: The all-weather attraction is the perfect place for all the family. With immersive experiences like the Search and Rescue Sea King Helicopter walk through and a walkthrough of the iconic Concorde 002.
bodyContent: This year make sure to set your sights on the Fleet Air Arm Museum in Ilchester and see where time flies. This must-see attraction has four large exhibition halls each containing dozens of incredible aircraft which tell the rich history of naval aviation. Grab your wingman and step inside the first British Concorde, experience the thrills of a working flight deck, and get up close to a wide range of rare and historical aircraft.
tagline: The all-weather attraction is the perfect place for all the family.

title: Dunster Castle
subtitle: Fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years, remodelled 100 years ago. Fine 17thC staircase and plaster ceilings. Terrace garden of rare shrubs.
bodyContent: During the winter months, the castle, watermill, and grounds are open at weekends and closed during the week. The Watermill Tearoom, Stables Shop and Parkland are open daily from 10am until 4pm. The car park is also open daily from 10am until 5pm. From 5 April 2025, the whole site is open daily. A fortress that became a family home for the Luttrells, who lived at Dunster for 600 years, the castle was extensively remodelled in the 1870s to create a Victorian country house. The castle boasts breath-taking views over Exmoor, Somerset, and the Bristol Channel as well as holding fine interior features such as a fine 17 th century carved staircase, ornate plaster ceilings, and rare leather wall hangings. Discover how Dunster Castle was used in its heyday and how the family hosted grand occasions from society balls to polo matches with the brilliant ‘Chapters’ guide as well as ‘Castle Explorers, available for children. You can then enjoy a leisurely stroll through beautiful terraced gardens with a collection of palms, sub-tropical plants, and the Dunster Lemon tree. Sited on the River Avill, Dunster Castle is also home to a working watermill that sits within the river gardens. Visit the mill to see the waterwheels in action and even purchase some of the freshly-milled flour. Refreshments are available in the newly-refurbished Watermill Tearoom and also outside the castle in the Tenants’ Hall Café. Accessibility Overview here. Facilities in addition to those listed below: Baby changing facilities Children's trails Courtesy vehicle Stair Climber Trampers available to book
tagline: Dramatically sited on a wooded hill and the fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years.

title: Ring O'Bells
subtitle: Free house local pub in Somerset between Street & Glastonbury.
bodyContent: The Ring O’Bells is an 18th Century “free house” pub in the Somerset village of Ashcott near Street and Glastonbury, which for the last 29 years has been run by a family partnership. A unique pub with unique food, all prepared by us in our own kitchens. Local meat from a local butcher. Somerset produce at its best. Daily Specials blackboard including freshly made desserts. Home-made fudge with your coffee to finish! We are a genuine Free House and it is our policy to feature beers from small independent breweries, many from the West Country but occasionally also more “exotic” visitors! The range of beers varies constantly but our list of forthcoming beers features usually at least one beer from one of the local micro breweries. title: Flow Bar Frome
subtitle: At the heart of Frome. A place to meet, mixing character, service and independent spirit. Occasional local food offerings and live music.
bodyContent: Flow Bar Frome is in a beautifully renovated Georgian building with contemporary styling, offering two floors of sophisticated bar space on a medieval bridge with views overlooking the river Frome near Bath. Enjoy a seasonal cocktail list using local garnishes and ingredients, local cider, gin and their own Flow Pale Ale, available to drink-in or takeaway. They also collaborate with independent local businesses, providing food offerings such as Tacos and Sharing Platters on certain days. See live and acoustic sets from local DJs and singer/songwriters, as well as specially curated events throughout the year, showcasing the best drinks, food and entertainment that Frome and Somerset have to offer.
tagline: At the heart of Frome. A place to meet, mixing character, service and independent spirit.

title: The Jane Austen Centre
subtitle: The Jane Austen Centre is in the heart of the Georgian city of Bath, between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths. Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The Jane Austen Centre is in the Georgian city of Bath , Somerset , between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths . Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family. Here you will find out more about Jane Austen, her time in Bath and how the city shaped her work. You can also dress up in Regency costume, taste Regency-recipe biscuits, sample perfumes from the era, try your hand at writing with a quill and ink, have your photo taken with their world famous waxwork, try their delightful ‘Tea With Mr Darcy’ in the Regency Tea Room, and browse their bespoke Giftshop.

title: Osip
subtitle: Osip is a Michelin starred farm-to-table restaurant situated in the heart of rural Somerset by award-winning chef Merlin Labron-Johnson.
bodyContent: Osip is a creative concept from acclaimed Chef Merlin Labron Johnson. Located in the heart of rural Somerset just outside the village of Bruton, the restaurant is 15 minutes’ drive from the station at Castle Cary, just one and a half hours from central London’s Paddington Station. The kitchen at Osip, however, begins not in the building but in nearby fields where 85% of the produce used is grown between two farms and an orchard. Biodynamic and dictated by the seasonality of its West Country location, harvesting and foraging are ruled by what nature permits. A low-meat restaurant, Osip’s produce is supplemented by organic meat from a local farm in a hidden valley high in the nearby Quantock Hills. When ordering, the kitchen takes only whole animals and birds and prepares the meat in-house to minimise waste. Osip opens up the conversation beyond the restaurant of how guests experience the energy of its exceptional home. Originally erected 300 years ago, the architectural nuances of the historic building are injected with traditional elements that reflect its history, reimagined for a modern mood. From the entrance lounge and bar to the open kitchen and dining room culminating in a dedicated tea house, design touchpoints and considered colour palettes have been created to unite each in one cohesive flow. Furniture, bespoke art pieces, fabrics and a unifying dark floor encourage visitors to move gradually through the space as they would a gallery.
tagline: Osip is a Michelin starred farm-to-table restaurant situated in the heart of rural Somerset

title: Revo Kitchen & Terrace
subtitle: Revo Kitchen & Terrace, is an enticing new restaurant located on Weston-super-Mare’s seafront in what was, until March 2019, the SeaQuarium. It’s hard to imagine anywhere that could offer better views whilst enjoying a meal, a snack or tea and cake in a relaxing environment. With views over the bay, the Grand Pier and over the water to Wales, it’s fast becoming the venue of choice.
bodyContent: And talking of the environment, Revo is highly conscious of its duty to care for our beautiful world. There are paper compostable straws for all drinks, all takeaway packaging is compostable and they aim to use local suppliers for all produce. Cakes and bakes are not bought in, the in-house bakery team come in as early as 3am some mornings to produce traditional and innovative baked goods, created freshly each day with locally sourced ingredients and high-quality produce. The homemade bread is a key ingredient in some of the brunch, lunch and dinner dishes. Weston-super-Mare is blessed with spectacular sunsets and with its panoramic windows, Revo is the perfect venue for a sundowner cocktail or mocktail, they even have fire-pits on the terrace which they’ll be pleased to light for you on request. You can get an idea of some of the delights on offer from their main menu here Revo Kitchen welcomes dogs on their leads, just remember that excessive barking is not so welcome, there’s a “3 barks and you’re out” policy. And if you’re feeling active, there’s an amazing indoor Glo Golf crazy golf course, try your skills in the darkened room with glowing golf holes and a bar in the middle! Normally open from 12 noon daily, it’s a great fun activity suitable for all age groups.
tagline: Revo Kitchen & Terrace, is an enticing new restaurant
