title: Clarks Village
subtitle: If you haven't experienced the magic of Clarks Village yet, you've been missing out! Nestled amidst the stunning Somerset countryside, our shopping centre offers a serene and breathtaking environment like no other.
bodyContent: Admire the majestic trees, some of which have stood for over a century, and enjoy our abundance of green spaces and landscaped gardens. Take a moment to relax amidst nature, savouring the horticulture, insects, and birds that inhabit our surroundings. We are also proud to be a dog-friendly outlet, where well-behaved four-legged companions are even allowed in most stores. At Clarks Village, we invite you to embark on a retail adventure and explore the remarkable experiences waiting to be discovered in our surrounding area. Come and discover the endless possibilities that await you! Time to shop! With over 75 stores and 90 renowned brands to explore, Clarks Village provides a shopping experience like no other. Enjoy up to 60% off the recommended retail prices every day, allowing you to shop to your heart's content. Take your time; there's no need to rush. As you peruse the stores, make sure to pause and treat yourself to a coffee, or perhaps a refreshing cup of tea—hot, iced, or even bubble tea. And when hunger strikes, indulge in a delightful assortment of snacks, including pasties, of course (because you are in the Westcountry!), cakes, waffles, sandwiches, and so much more. The options are endless. Accessible and Inclusive Clarks Village warmly welcomes all guests. With all stores located on ground level, easy access is provided for those with mobility challenges. Our Guest Services team is dedicated to supporting individuals with hidden disabilities, ensuring a comfortable experience for everyone. For more information, check out our accessibility information page .
tagline: If you haven't experienced the magic of Clarks Village yet, you've been missing out!

title: Sand, sea, caves and elephants! It sounds like an adventure film plot but it is just the start of a wide range of family fun ideas in the county of contrasts, Somerset.
subtitle: Somerset has been a bit of a secret for families, it’s on the way to the south west but with it being half the travel time to some busy resorts, the whole family can have their toes in the sand and sea so much quicker and give you all more holiday memories.
bodyContent: Brean is just minutes off the M5 motorway and has one of the biggest beaches in Europe, a remarkable 7 miles long. It has been an established family holiday destination for decades and has been tipped by the National Press as the hidden discovery for 2024, being only a couple of hours journey from London and the Midlands. With many holiday centres lining the coast, only yards from the beach, families are ensured a traditional beach experience along with entertainment and activities, including the village’s own theme park which is the UK’s biggest that features free admission with over 40 attractions including roller coasters, dodgems, crazy boats and the Terror Castle Ghost Train! Staying at a holiday centre in the village such as Sandy Glade Holiday Park will give you that family entertainment feel after a day at the beach, Brean Theme Park or the nearby Animal Farm Adventure Park. This petting farm is home to more than 250 animals! There are so many exciting places to stay including Holiday Resort Unity , Warren Farm , Diamond Farm , Southfield Farm , or the exquisite B&B at Yew Tree Farm . If you prefer camping then there are lots of options including the above in the village which is overlooked by the imposing Brean Down , a 318’ high extension of the Mendip Hills that extends into the Severn Estuary. A Napoleonic fort at the end is a great discovery and invigorating walk. From the top of Brean Down you can glimpse the famous resort of Weston-super-Mare . You can hire bicycles in the village and take the gentle route into the town and head for the Grand Pier which is packed with rides, attractions and events – you can enjoy lunch here or just along the wide seafront at Revo Kitchen & Terrace which has amazing 360 degree views and its own Revo Glo Golf, a glow in the dark crazy golf course! Whilst in Weston-super-Mare do check out the new attraction, Little Town Adventures which is an immersive children’s play experience. Described as a combination of escape room style activity, theatre and role play, Little Town Adventures is a miniature recreation of the town and includes its own grand pier, town hall, cinema, vets, police station, fire station, supermarket, and café. Charming! The Somerset coast has immense variety all along from Exmoor’s steep cliffs, harbours at Minehead and Watchet , rock formations at Kilve and piers at Burnham-on-Sea , Weston-super-Mare and Clevedon upon which the One Direction video You & I was filmed ten years ago in 2014. Just 15 minutes inland from Clevedon is Noah's Ark Zoo Farm , with over 100 different species, family activities and a host of exciting animal experiences on offer. The work of this charity is to support, protect and care for the natural world, and to inspire people with a love of our planet and with hope for the future. A star attraction is Sutton the African Elephant who has just celebrated his tenth birthday! The world-leading elephant facility covers an area of 20 acres with a wide range of state-of-the-art features including a pool, large heated indoor barn with sand yards and water sprinklers, expansive fields and a large willow plantation - Elephant Eden was designed to provide a natural and spacious environment for elephants to foster their physical and mental well-being. Elephant Eden is home to four African elephants, Shaka, Janu, Uli and Sutton. A common theme along the Somerset coast is how the countryside is always so close and the sense of space and nature being entwined with the holiday experience. The Somerset Levels are a renowned wetland area full of wildlife and a backdrop as you look inland from Brean are the Mendip Hills . The Limestone from which they are comprised is what gives rise to their breath-taking geological features. The village of Cheddar just a few miles inland is famous for its Gorge and Caves , the steep cliffs and vantage points giving panoramic views that capture the variety of this county. The views from the base of the gorge, looking up at Britain’s highest inland limestone cliffs will similarly make the whole family gasp in wonder. Viewing inside the extraordinary subterranean stalactite show caves is a must, plus you will learn many fascinating secrets about our prehistoric ancestors. An immersive multi-sensory visitor experience has been launched this year that uses state of the art lighting, music, animation and colour to tell the story of how the caves were formed and evolved by the power of water. A few miles further east is the exciting Wookey Hole where you will discover caves, legends and adventure as well as the famous witch! A safe route takes families through a number of extraordinary chambers, with added tunnels and walkways. The adventurous can even go deeper with the Wild Wookey experience, an adventure for brave-hearted explorers involving crawling, climbing and abseiling (book in advance via www.wookey.co.uk ). Guided tours are in place throughout the day outside of school holidays. During school holidays, you can walk through the caves at your own pace, with knowledgeable guides on hand to answer questions and share stories and legends from Wookey Hole. It’s easy to spend a whole day experiencing the wide variety of attractions that also include a museum, adventure golf, enchanted valley, Wookey Hole circus, 4D cinema and fun in the mill. As well as the M4 and M5 motorway network, GWR trains give easy access to the Somerset coast, see www.gwr.com . Also Berry’s coaches from London see www.berryscoaches.co.uk Find out more about all of these family holiday ideas via www.visitsomerset.co.uk (pic courtesy Holiday Resort Unity)

title: New Changing Places Toilet at Brean Leisure Park now open
subtitle: The changing places toilet at Brean Leisure Park is accessed by a universal radar key and is available for use daily between Easter and the end of October.
bodyContent: Thanks to Somerset Council working with strategic partners Brean Leisure Park and Muscular Dystrophy UK, using grant funds from the former Department for Levelling Up, Housing & Communities (now known as Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government) It has now been registered and tourists and visitors can locate Changing Places facilities on the following website https://www.changing-places.org/ The changing places toilet at Brean Leisure Park is accessed by a universal radar key and is available for use daily between Easter and the end of October. The room can be found in the outside toilet block next to the ice cream parlour. More information here: https://www.breanjobs.com/post/new-changing-places-toilet-at-brean-leisure-park-now-open

title: UNITY Beach Holiday Parks Comes Alive THIS WEEKEND with the Official Opening This Saturday, 24th May
subtitle: Unity Beach to be officially opened by The One Show's Alex Jones
bodyContent: UNITY Holiday Park is set to revolutionise the UK holiday experience, and it all kicks off this Saturday, 24th May , with the official grand opening of UNITY Beach and a host of exciting new attractions across the park. As part of UNITY’s multi-million-pound ‘Comes Alive in 25’ transformation, the much-anticipated launch marks a new era for British seaside holidays - combining classic family fun with cutting-edge entertainment, dining, and activities. Unity Beach Grand Opening – Saturday 24th May TV favourite and The One Show presenter Alex Jones will officially open UNITY Beach at a ticketed owners-only event earlier in the day, celebrating the next chapter of the park’s evolution. From 5:30pm , all new park facilities will be open to the general public , giving holidaymakers the chance to experience the brand-new entertainment venues, live shows, restaurants, and thrill-filled attractions for the very first time. Bringing Back the Magic of the British Seaside For generations, the Great British Holiday was the pinnacle of family fun, and UNITY is bringing that tradition roaring back to life. With immersive entertainment, family-friendly activities, and all-new venues, UNITY is redefining what a UK seaside escape can be. Multi-Million-Pound Investment for a New Holiday Era This isn’t just a refurbishment, it’s a complete reinvention. The substantial investment has gone into: State-of-the-art entertainment venues Spectacular live shows and high-energy performances Interactive family experiences and soft play centres Innovative, locally sourced dining options Whether you're here for the day or staying the week, every moment promises fun, flavour, and unforgettable memories. Holiday Heaven for All Located at Brean Sands, Somerset , UNITY is designed for both holidaymakers and holiday home owners. From fun rides at Brean Theme Park to splashing around in the water park or relaxing in your private hot tub lodge, there’s something for everyone - pets included! Owners benefit from exclusive events, upgraded facilities, and a vibrant, welcoming community, making their second home truly special. The Great British Holiday is back and it all begins this Saturday. Don’t miss the start of something unforgettable at UNITY Holiday Parks. www.hru.co.uk

title: Brean Seasonal Riverside Walk open until 15th July
subtitle: The Brean Seasonal Riverside Walk provides a walking route on the banks of the River Axe between Brean Down and Brean Cross Sluice.
bodyContent: The signage and information has been recently updated on the Coast Path at the River Axe in Brean where the Seasonal Walk is open from 16th May to 15th July. There is improved directional signage and information boards about the birds that pass here on their migration or overwinter here. The Brean Seasonal Riverside Walk provides a walking route on the banks of the River Axe between Brean Down and Brean Cross Sluice. Each year this sensitive roost site hosts internationally important numbers of Redshank, Oystercatcher, Curlew Whimbrel, Dunlin, Shelduck, Wigeon, and Teal. The birds visit while in passage or to over winter, joining many other waterbirds that live here or seasonally visit the area. To protect the birds when they are visiting, the riverside route is only open between 16th of May and the 15th of July. The rest of the year you can visit the Great Bird Screen of Brean at Brean Cross Sluice where it is possible to see the birds without disturbing them. While here, the birds feed on the extensive areas of mud, sand and saltmarsh at low tide and roost at the water’s edge and on sea defence structures during high tides. If disturbed at this time it can deplete their energy resources leaving them vulnerable and weak. Even when the route is open, there may still be waterbirds in the area and getting close to them, or allowing our dogs to roam on the shore, will disturb the birds. To find out more about the alternative route visit the Brean Seasonal Riverside Walk page.

title: Wellington Choral Society New Season
subtitle: Works by Mozart, Handel and Mendelssohn will be performed in the new season.
bodyContent: After a very successful programme last season when the Wellington Choral Society performed works by Mozart, Handel and Mendelssohn, enjoyed by all audiences, they are now looking forward to the start of their singing season for 2025/26. The first concert will be on Saturday 29 November 2025 at 7.00pm at St John the Baptist Church Wellington when the society will be singing Handel's Messiah Part 1 and Britten's St Nicolas. Both choral works are suited to the festive season. Rehearsals start on Wednesday 3 September 2025. They are a friendly choir and would always love new singers to come and join them. There is no audition and Musical Director Laurence Blyth helps new singers to learn the music. title: Ubley
subtitle: Ubley Parish sits in the Yeo valley at the west end of the Chew Valley. It is bordered to the north and south with ridges of hills, most significantly the Mendips to the south. It sits within the Mendip Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB) and close to Blagdon Lake.
bodyContent: Ubley Parish sits in the Yeo valley at the west end of the Chew Valley. It is bordered to the north and south with ridges of hills, most significantly the Mendips to the south. It sits within the Mendip Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB) and close to Blagdon Lake. Ubley is an attractive village set mostly on the valley floor but rises up on the lower slopes of the Mendip Hills to the south. The surrounding valley landscape is of farmland with small and medium sized fields largely for grazing. Fields are separated by well-kept hedgerows with intermittent mature trees. The whole area is rich in wildlife and is rural and unspoilt in character. There are magnificent views from the slopes of the Mendips across the Parish and as far as South Wales to the west and the hills above Bath to the east. There is quite a lot of greenery throughout the village. There are many mature trees, mostly in gardens and the Churchyard in and around the Conservation Area. The roads are lined by a mixture of hedgerows and walls, the latter of which are of local stone. The slopes of the Mendip scarp are densely wooded with an area known as Ubley Wood. The centre of the village is at The Cross, outside the 13th century St Bartholomew’s Church. This is a conservation area, with charming houses and gardens and a view up to the Mendip Hills. There is also a Primary School and a large village hall with a grass amenity area. The village hall hosts some large events such as the ever-popular beer festival in September which are open to all. The site of the Old Sawmill now hosts an artisan cheese-maker. Ubley has many way-marked paths leading either up to the Mendip Hills or down to the edges of Blagdon and Chew Valley Lakes. From the Mendip Hills above Ubley both lakes can be seen, and on a clear day the view is spread from Cardiff to the hills above Bath. There is an Airbnb property in the village, which has recently been developed from an old Methodist Church. Neighbouring villages have accommodation and public houses and are a good base for fisherman who use both lakes to catch trout. Further information can be found at: · Chew Valley Lake · Fly fishing on the lakes

title: Martock
subtitle: This thriving community is one of the largest parishes in Somerset and has one of the oldest domestic dwellings, the National Trust's Treasurer's House, as well as an impressive 13th parish church with one of the finest carved tie beam roofs in Somerset and an old grammar school founded in 1661.
bodyContent: This thriving community is one of the largest parishes in Somerset and has one of the oldest domestic dwellings, the National Trust's Treasurer's House, as well as an impressive 13th parish church with one of the finest carved tie beam roofs in Somerset and an old grammar school founded in 1661. The Martock Bean used to be a popular plant in the 16th and 17th centuries and old Martockians are known as "Beanies" The Ash village church was constructed between 1840 and 1887 has a simple tower which was added as a war memorial after the First World War - stating the tower was built "in honour of all those who gave their lives for King and Country."

title: 7 Great Walks In and Around Nailsea
subtitle: Nailsea Footpath Group Formed over 40 years ago to encourage people to explore and enjoy the countryside that Nailsea has to offer, Nailsea Footpath Group takes part in a variety of walks of differing distances and difficulty. The walks take place during the weekdays and weekends, and consist of shorter walks in and around Nailsea, as well as longer walks through the Mendips and in Devon.
bodyContent: 7 Great Walks In and Around Nailsea Nailsea Footpath Group Formed over 40 years ago to encourage people to explore and enjoy the countryside that Nailsea has to offer, Nailsea Footpath Group takes part in a variety of walks of differing distances and difficulty. The walks take place during the weekdays and weekends, and consist of shorter walks in and around Nailsea, as well as longer walks through the Mendips and in Devon. New members of all ages are welcome to join, and can take part in up to 2 walks before deciding whether to become a member. For more information, please visit: http://www.nfpg.org.uk/index.htm Moorend Spout Nature Reserve There are few natural sites in North Somerset more beautiful that the Moorend Spout nature reserve. Located to the north of Nailsea, the 6-acre site is the home to a wide range of plants and wildlife, as well as an idyllic, constantly flowing waterfall. Insects such as dragonflies and damselflies can be seen, as can kingfishers and otters. The area lies between the Land Yeo and Jacklands Rhyne and consists of bramble and sedge, a wet woodland and a meadow. It is owned and managed by the Nailsea Environment and Wildlife Trust (NEWT), who aim to restore the wildlife potential and biodiversity of the land. Several features have been introduced to the site in the last decade to make it more accessible to walkers. A series of steps have been installed up to the embankment to Land Yeo in 2017, and a boardwalk was installed in 2010, providing an improved route across the site – particularly during wet weather. NEWT have also installed two ponds, which has become the valuable habitat to all-types of marine life. The Moorend Spout can be accessed from a footpath off Pound Lane, opposite Kingshill School and Greenslade Pre-School. The High Street Having used to be one of the main roads in Nailsea, The High Street has now developed into the heart of the town, providing multiple shops and restaurants. As you walk from one end to the other, you are likely to want to have a quick browse in the range of shops, or stop for a bite at one of the numerous eateries. It’s vibrant atmosphere truly showcases the community spirit of Nailsea and makes a great afternoon stroll. Nowhere Woods Also known as Trendlewood, Nowhere Woods is a small wood situated in the east-end of Nailsea. The wood previously contained several pennant sandstone quarries, but it is now the home to squirrels, birds and other wildlife, making it a popular dog walking route. Ty Sculpture Trail Based in the beautiful woodland of Towerhouse Wood, the Ty Sculpture Trail is a magical trail for the whole family. Secretly dotted around the peaceful wood in Wraxall are 14 wood carvings of animals and animal footprints, including a fox, a hedgehog and a robin. The trail was opened in memory of Ty Partridge, who sadly died from Leukemia in 2010 at the age of 21. Ty and his family lived next to Towerhouse Wood, with their back gate opening on to the 16 acres of Woodland, and Ty spent a lot of his time growing up in the woods, often climbing trees and building dens. However, after Ty had died, his father, Piers, wanted to create something to remember him, and decided an appropriate way to remember Ty was to carve all the animals that lived in the woodland into wood, and create a trail. There is no parking on site, but parking is available at the bottom of Towehouse Lane – which is a 10-minute walk from the main entrance. Backwell Lake Constructed in the 1970s, Backwell Lake is a vital habitat for birds, bats and insects. More than 10 species of birds can be found at the lake, including mute swans and grey herons. Although only a short walk, the footpath circling the lake presents plenty of opportunities to photograph wildlife in their natural environment. A wide range of wild flowers can also be found. The footpath circling the lake is less than a mile, and there is a free car park on-site. However, Backwell Lake can also be accessed by a footpath from the bottom of The Perrings playpark, but bear in mind that this route is considerably hilly. Stockway North Nature Reserve Located in the centre of Nailsea, Stockway North Nature Reserve provides a home for a wide range of birds, plants, amphibians, mammals and more. 180 different species of plants have been recorded here, as well as 30 different species of birds. It has been managed by the Friends of Stockway North Nature Reserve since 1998, and was awarded a Britain in Bloom 2008 Neighbourhood Award of Merit. The group of volunteers have carried out considerable work to the reserve, including creating a large pond and meadow, plantings of native trees and clearing the site of any rubbish and litter. An all-weather path has also been added to the site, making it more accessible for the community. The site is open to the community on Wednesdays from April to August, and the first Saturday of each month.

title: Yeo Valley
subtitle: We’re a family farm and dairy business that’s grown into Britain’s largest organic brand. Somerset is our home, our workplace and the backdrop and inspiration for everything we do. We’ve been farming and making dairy products in Blagdon since 1961. Our business has grown with farms across the Mendips and production sites across Somerset employing over 1,700 people.
bodyContent: We make organic yogurts that are naturally tasty and healthy. At the heart of Yeo Valley Organic is our incredible British Friesian cows who happily graze outside on our organic lush pastures. We farm organically because that’s how to get the best tasting ingredients. This inspires all the incredible products we make from our popular Natural yogurt to our organic fruit compotes and ice cream. We firmly believe that organic is the way forward for our own health, and for the health of wildlife and the planet. It’s about brilliant nutritious dairy, created by nature. We love nothing more than to open up our doors (and farm gates) so that people can come and see it all for themselves. We offer farm tours, cooking demos, garden open days and even a summer music festival. More information
tagline: We’re a family farm and dairy business that’s grown into Britain’s largest organic brand.

title: RNLI Portishead
subtitle: A new state-of-the-art lifeboat station, built by the RNLI, was completed in 2015.
bodyContent: A new state-of-the-art lifeboat station, built by the RNLI, was completed in 2015. The station is close to the exit of Portishead marina, just down from The Royal Inn (see the Where to Eat and Drink ) and as well as the boat house which is home to the Atlantic 85 lifeboat, My Lady Anne, it sports a new ramp and lower slipway to enable launch and recovery of the lifeboat. There is also a delightful RNLI gift shop which is served by volunteers. Training programs operate from the station and a variety of fundraising events can also be found here.

title: The Poacher
subtitle: The Poacher has been a public house since at least the 17th century.
bodyContent: The Poacher has been a public house since at least the 17th century. It was originally two cottages knocked together, the bay windows showing where the front rooms were. Since then it has been used at various times as a courtroom, parish council office and preaching room whilst still operating as a pub. Now a popular High Street Pub in the heart of North Somerset close to the bustling city of Bristol serving great food, with a great selection of drink on offer.
tagline: The Poacher has been a public house since at least the 17th century.

title: ⭐Shepton Mallet Prison
subtitle: Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’; Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom...
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’, Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom. Shepton Mallet Prison is a recently decommissioned (2013) Georgian jail where visitors can walk in the footsteps of our social history and hear officers shine a light on what life was like for both the incarcerated and those who guarded them through the ages. Before its closure, it was a category C lifer prison holding 189 prisoners. Opened in 1646, it was expanded in 1790, with further building work undertaken in the 1820s and 1830s, including the installation of a treadwheel for those sentenced to hard labour. In 1930, the inmate numbers fell and the prison was closed. During the Second World War, the prison was reopened and used as a military prison. It was initially used by the British Army and later by American forces, who constructed a new execution block for condemned prisoners. It was also used for the storage of important historical documents, including the Domesday Book. It returned to civilian use in 1966. Shepton Mallet prison is also known for its tales of paranormal activity. One of the most popular stories is that of the White Lady. She is frequently seen or sensed in various locations, especially A Wing. Staff and prisoners would often complain of an icy wind moving through the wing, the sweet smell of perfume and shadowy figures. She supposedly dates from the late 1700s, when she spent some time in the prison. During a lovers' tiff which escalated, she murdered her betrothed. Once found guilty and sentenced to death, she was housed in Shepton Mallet Prison. On the evening before her execution, she asked for her wedding dress to be brought to the prison, which they allowed. She wore it to bed that night, but in the morning the officers found that she had died during the night. No cause of death was ever found, so we are left to presume that she died of a broken heart. Perhaps this is why she still haunts the prison? In the early 1950s, the Kray Twins were also held here after deserting the British Army. Today, the prison is open as a tourist attraction offering Guided Tours, Self-Guided Tours, Escape Rooms, Night Behind Bars and Ghost Hunting Behind Bars. This is an immersive experience without gizmos or gimmicks – the jail is very much as it was when the last prisoners left in 2013. In 2025, Shepton Mallet Prison received the prestigious Trip Advisor Travellers’ Choice, for the 7th time running, placing it among the top 10% of attractions worldwide.

title: Greenbank Pool
subtitle: Greenbank Pool is an outdoor heated family friendly swimming pool in the heart of Street, Somerset. It is within easy walking distance of both the High Street and Clarks Village.
bodyContent: Greenbank Pool opened in 1937 and is in an art deco style. There are two pools. The smaller one is the children’s pool with a slide for under 8s in the shallow end. There is also a larger pool which is deeper and suitable for competent swimmers. The pools are ringed by low walls containing the paved poolside area. Beyond the low walls is grass which provides a lot of space for picnicking. There is also a wet play area on the site with fountains and jets which is terrific fun for children and the young at heart. The pool also has a small shop on site. In the main building are changing rooms and showers; including a larger sized accessible changing room which is bookable when the pool is open. There are accessible features in the showers and toilets. At the rear of the site is level access for wheelchair users. There is one disabled parking space outside the pool.

title: The Sheppey Inn
subtitle: The Sheppey Inn lies out on the beautiful wilds of the Somerset Levels, surrounded by peat moors, dairy farms and national wildlife reserves.
bodyContent: The pub pulls in people from miles around thanks to the brilliant, eclectic musicians it attracts, its fine selection of local ales and ciders (including all kinds of one-offs and speciality brews), and its fantastic food. Spending the afternoon out here in the countryside, lounging by the river, looking out for voles and kingfishers, isn’t the worst idea in the world, is it? There’s been a pub in Godney servicing the thirsty throats of Levels farmworkers for many centuries. The last owners ran it for 120 years, but on one day in 1976, they ran out of cider and lost the trust of the next two generations of locals. the pub has been renovated, revamped and restored, and now has about six casks of grown-ups’ apple juice on the bar to make sure that the such a thing never happens again. Check out the photos on the right for proof.
tagline: The Sheppey Inn lies out on the beautiful wilds of the Somerset Levels.

bodyContent: The hall hosts a number of professional (and amateur) productions throughout the year which include classical, jazz, folk and rock and pop and cabaret concerts, drama, talks and films. The main recital hall, Eavis Hall, has the capacity for audiences up to 350 and is a flexible and modern performance space. In addition to events in Eavis Hall, it serves as a hub for its significant community outreach, which provides music education (including workshops, concerts and masterclasses) for thousands of primary school children, elderly and disability groups in the South West each year. bodyContent: Elegant collections with a little twist and gorgeous fabrics make dressing exciting again. The Laundry opened its doors in 2008 in Wells, a beautiful city in the heart of Somerset. Theodora fell in love with the city having relocated herself and her family from London in 2004. title: North Petherton
subtitle: Once a large village but now a town, North Petherton has a 15th-century church, St Mary’s, with a handsome Perpendicular-style tower.
bodyContent: The 9th-century Alfred Jewel - now in Oxford’s Ashmolean Museum - was found in the town and Athelney, King Alfred’s hideout on the Levels, is just over ten minutes away, as is Burrow Mump, which was once fortified by the king. North Petherton sits on the edge of the Quantock Hills where the National Trust’s Fyne Court, a country house and nature reserve, is a 15-minute drive away. Head south of town for 15 minutes to visit Hestercombe House, which has 50 acres of gardens with designs by Gertrude Jekyll and Sir Edward Lutyens.

title: Wincanton
subtitle: Two hundred years ago as many as seventeen stage coaches a day would pass through Wincanton. Today approach it from the north along what was once the main London road (the A303 bypasses the town) and it is easy to imagine very little has changed.
bodyContent: Two hundred years ago as many as seventeen stage coaches a day would pass through Wincanton. Today approach it from the north along what was once the main London road (the A303 bypasses the town) and it is easy to imagine very little has changed. The wide street still contains handsome houses and staging inns and the town’s name is still linked with horses Wincanton is officially twinned with Ankh-Morpork - the premier city state in author Terry Pratchett's fantasy Discworld novels - which is represented in the town with its own consulate! Must See and Do Enjoy a day at Wincanton races , frequent meetings throughout the season Visit the Discworld Emporium and obtaon your Discworld passport at the Ankh - Morpork Consulate Get some retail therapy in Wincanton's independent shops Relax with a round of golf at Wincanton golf club Have a happy and healthy time at Wincanton sports centre Local Facilities Library Petrol Station Post Office Pubs and restaurants Sports Centre Supermarket and Shops

title: Cavell House Bed and Breakfast B&B in Clevedon

Beautiful views across to Wales. Paddle steamer trips from the -pier, to Lundy, North Devon, Penarth and Gloucester. An ideal base for walkers and cyclists. title: The Jane Austen Centre
subtitle: The Jane Austen Centre is in the heart of the Georgian city of Bath, between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths. Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The Jane Austen Centre is in the Georgian city of Bath , Somerset , between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths . Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family. Here you will find out more about Jane Austen, her time in Bath and how the city shaped her work. You can also dress up in Regency costume, taste Regency-recipe biscuits, sample perfumes from the era, try your hand at writing with a quill and ink, have your photo taken with their world famous waxwork, try their delightful ‘Tea With Mr Darcy’ in the Regency Tea Room, and browse their bespoke Giftshop.

title: Wells England’s smallest city
subtitle: Revel in the serenity of the Bishop’s Palace with its breathtaking landscaped gardens, then stop for coffee in a nearby artisan café on the medieval high street.
bodyContent: The historic city of Wells is the smallest city in England, lying nestled at the foot of the rolling Mendip Hills. This hidden gem, though compact in size, is home to one of the finest concentrations of medieval buildings in the country. The stunning Wells Cathedral, famed for its astounding 14th century scissor arches, unique Quarter Jack Clock, and breath-taking Jesse Window lies at the heart of the city. Adjacent to the Cathedral is The Bishop’s Palace, medieval home to the Bishops of Bath & Wells for over 800 years and surrounded by 14 acres of beautiful RHS partner gardens in which lie the evocative ancient well pools which give the City its name. The Palace is also famous for its Mute swans which reside on the Moat and are trained to ring a bell on the Gatehouse for food when hungry. Just around the corner from the Cathedral is Vicars Close, the oldest continuously inhabited street in Europe. It is famed for its medieval splendour and unusually tall chimneys and is still inhabited by the Vicars Choral of the Cathedral Choir for whom it was built over 650 years ago. Also to be found near the Cathedral are the medieval buildings of Wells Cathedral School. Founded in 909 it is one of the oldest schools in Europe and the only specialist music school in the country which operates within a normal independent school, benefitting both music students and regular students. Wells and Mendip Museum also sits on Cathedral Green, offering visitors an invaluable source of information on the history of Wells and its surrounding area. Independent markets are held twice weekly in Wells’ elegant Market Place on Wednesdays and Saturdays, with local produce, crafts and gifts and Wells High Street has a wonderful array of independent boutiques and coffee shops alongside national brands. Its narrow streets and eclectic mix of buildings styles reflect the development of the town throughout the ages and the water channels running down either side of the street are a reminder of the gift of water given to the townsfolk by Bishop Beckyngton in 1451. The area surrounding Wells has much to offer too, from the romantic splendours of Glastonbury Tor and the magical ruins of Glastonbury Abbey (only 6 miles from Wells) to the mysteries of the ancient caves at Wookey Hole (1.5 miles away), the sweeping drama of Cheddar Gorge, and the Market Town of Shepton Mallet, home to the Royal Bath & West Show. In addition to the huge range of architectural treats, the City and surrounding area is rich with all sorts of culture, including the sublime musical history of the Cathedral choir, the musical excellence of the Cathedral School and the fabulous new programme at the brand new Cedars Hall concert hall, the annual Festivals of Literature, Food, Contemporary Music & Contemporary Art which take place in October, (the Food Festival being a wonderful reminder of the richness of the area’s food heritage with particular emphasis on local Ciders and Cheddar Cheese!), the Somerset Schools Folk Dancing Festival and the annual Maypole dancing in the Market Place, the outdoor theatre seasons at The Bishop’s Palace and Glastonbury Abbey, the magnificent madness of Glastonbury Festival, and the local ancient Somerset tradition of the January Wassail to secure the cider apple harvest to name but a few!

title: The Pillars Restaurant & Lounge Bar
subtitle: Experience and enjoy the sophisticated atmosphere that Street's newest venue now offers. Set over two floors with a secluded alfresco terrace, the ground floor bar offers an extensive range of wines, Champagnes, beers, as well its own brand of home brewed craft ale. Pillars has been sympathetically refurbished to acknowledge its entertainment history throughout the decades.
bodyContent: Welcome to The Pillars Restaurant and Lounge Bar - an exciting new venue in the heart of Street We're quickly earning a reputation for one of the best venues in town. Set over two floors with a secluded alfresco terrace, our ground floor bar offers an extensive range of wines, Champagnes, beers, ales and ciders as well as our own brand of home brewed craft ale. Experience and enjoy the sophisticated atmosphere that Street's newest venue now offers. The Pillars has been sympathetically refurbished to acknowledge its entertainment history throughout the decades. History of The Site The beginning The building was built in 1920 for two local businessmen, Mr Voaks, a local butcher and Mr Hecks, the forerunner of the local Hecks cider farm. The doors first opened on 15th January, 1921 as "The Playhouse Theatre." The Playhouse had four changing rooms, a 20ft deep stage and a 26ft wide proscenium. The original proscenium arch can still be seen today above what is now the piano deck. The arched ceiling is an original pressed tin design. The transition The Playhouse Theatre gave way to the Playhouse Cinema as technology evolved and the big curtains gave way to the big screen. The age of the cinema The building retained the name "The Playhouse" for 25 years until July 1946, when it was renamed "Maximes Cinema". For over 40 years, the building enjoyed life as a cinema with a variety of owners including Cornell Cinemas until the mid 50's and then Myles Byrne Cinemas. Maximes had one screen and 561 seats. Many local Somerset people will recall watching their first film on the big screen and many we are sure will recall magical and memorable romantic interludes within the many rows! The end of the big screen Maximes cinema played its last film on 15th September 1989. The start of the nightclub After the cinema closed, the seats were removed to create large open spaces. The screen was taken down to create more depth to the building and the next phase of the building's life was born into Maximes Nightclub. Maximes traded as a night club for many years. In 2001, the club embarked on a major refurbishment and was re-born as "Envy". Most residents of Somerset refer to the building now as the 'Envy building'. Envy enjoyed being a popular destination for thousands of party-goers hosting many themed nights and live music presentations. In June 2015, the owner Adam Fynn, announced he was to relocate and set about plans to sell the building and applied for planning permission to develop the site into residential properties. The end of the night club era On 11th December 2016, the then operators of Envy announced that the club would close at the end of the year and on 31st December 2016, Envy Nighclub opened and closed its doors for the very last time. The building sat dormant, empty and cold for nearly four months before going to auction on 27th April 2017. The building failed to sell at auction and the doors at Envy remained closed. A new beginning The building was finally purchased by us in June 2017. The new owner vowed to preserve the historic building and return it to back to its former glory as an entertainment venue for the mid Somerset arena. Throughout the remainder of 2017 and into the first half of 2018, plans were made and relevant planning permissions granted to commence the transformation of the building into the Loft. Throughout the re-development of the site, we have been sympathetic to the buildings unique history as an entertainment venue. We have combined all its past into the future, with food, drink, entertainment and music, all under one roof! We are very proud of the achievements and of the building. We do hope that you enjoy your experience here and look forward to welcoming you back to Pillars again soon. The Management Facilities include: Facilities : Unrivalled Grill Menu Al fresco dining area Regular Live Music & Entertainment Our own craft ales and beers Over 45 wines from around the world Available for private hire Wedding Receptions Unrivalled Cocktail & Gin Bar Market Fresh Daily Food Christmas Parties Christenings Large Dance Floor
tagline: The Pillars Restaurant and Lounge Bar is an exciting venue in the heart of Street.

title: Field 725 Glamping & Camping Venue
subtitle: Nestled within the rolling hills of Somerset, located close to Frome and a stone’s throw from Bruton. Our camping & glamping site, sits peacefully on a hillside next to 100 acres of wild woodland. Beautiful rolling views framed by abundant and biodiverse hedgerows makes for an easy escape back into nature.
bodyContent: At Field 725 we offer various glamping opAons ranging from Safari tents to tradiAonal Tipis, where you can choose either furnished or unfurnished. Saving you the hassle of packing and set up, each of our units comprises of all you will need to enjoy a comfortable stay. Or if you prefer to ‘glamp’ in your own style then you are more than welcome to bring your own tent along. This beauAful locaAon allows you to return to nature where you can chill around a fire, enjoy the 360 starlit views, dine with excellent cuisine and explore the surrounding woodlands. If you have a special occasion or have an idea for a bespoke event then Field 725 is also available for private hire, contact us to see what we can do for you. We have a vast variety of fun and exciAng events taking place throughout the year. From mini acousAc music fesAvals, weddings, anniversary celebraAons or even take part in a living history weekend. Check out our events page to keep up to date and see what’s happening: https://field725.co.uk/explore/events/ As we are situated within the Redwood Rare Breeds Farm you and your family are welcome to take a tour around the farm and refreshments are available too. Besides all this, Field 725 is a perfect base camp for you to visit many local aWracAons such as the vibrant town of Frome, beauAful Bruton, with both Longleat and Cheddar Gorge just 30 minutes away.

title: To The Trees
subtitle: Join Matt, a local nature enthusiast and musician, for a walk around the Glastonbury Countryside, guided by the trees. A unique and inspiring walking Tor that explores some of the intimate nooks and crannies of Avalon, while also orientating visitors towards the town's main attractions.
bodyContent: Join Matt, a local nature enthusiast and musician, for a walking experience around the Glastonbury countryside, guided by the trees. A unique and inspiring walking Tor that explores some of the intimate nooks and crannies of Glastontonbury, while also orientating visitors towards the Town’s main attractions, including the Tor and natural Springs. During the walk, we’ll explore some intimate natural spaces, off the beaten tracks. Matt will share his knowledge of the trees, talk about his relationship with nature, and explain the unique folklore that surrounds the town. We will take time to relax in nature and Matt will share his music and poetry inspired by the Avalon landscape and its trees. This is a relaxing, informative and inspiring walking experience that highlights the beautiful nature of Glastonbury and is accompanied by original music and seasonal poetry dedicated to the trees themselves. Here are some positive words from a recent walker: “We had such a wonderful tour with Matt! He was so informative about the local trees, showing us a great variety. He was also very knowledgeable about the local area and folklore that surrounds it which was fascinating to hear. Lovely touch to listen to some music too - we would highly recommend. It was the highlight of our trip to Glastonbury!”

title: Black Swan Arts
subtitle: Black Swan Arts is a charity and centre for art and crafts in Frome and the wider region. Housed in a listed and locally important building, it has been creating inclusive opportunities for the whole community since 1986.
bodyContent: Black Swan Arts is an established arts centre in the heart of the renowned creative market town of Frome. Our vibrant and varied programme features contemporary and innovative art and craft. We are a popular arts venue for the creative people of Somerset and beyond, providing exhibition, shop, studio and workshop space, and a welcoming place to meet friends in the River House Cafe. Black Swan Arts supports practitioners of contemporary and traditional arts and crafts, at all stages of their careers, acting as a hub for artists and makers to meet, make connections and develop their practice. We bring excellent, thought-provoking and inspirational work to local audiences through our varied programme of exhibitions in the Long Gallery. We also provide opportunities through our studio spaces for early career professionals to develop as small businesses, while our Open exhibitions and Round Tower programme offer the chance for artists at all stages of their career to showcase their work to audiences and make valuable sales.

title: Hollybush lodges
subtitle: Luxury self catering accommodation in the heart of Somerset, we have three traditional wooden lodges within their own tranquil grounds
bodyContent: Fancy escaping to an idyllic countryside retreat in Somerset? Nestled in the heart of the Mendip Hills, an area of outstanding natural beauty, you’ll find Hollybush Lodges. Three beautiful wooden lodges situated on the edge of the small rural village of Leigh on Mendip. Come and enjoy the tranquil setting, countryside views and varied wildlife. Listen to the church bells ring, the vibrant chatter of birds busily nesting in the hedgerows in Spring, maybe even hear the owls hooting their ‘goodnights’ on the evening breeze… All lodges are modern and of a high standard – light and airy with a spacious open plan kitchen / lounge area, are well equipped and sleep 4 people plus a travel cot for 1 baby. Our lodges sit in pleasant lawned grounds. Wooden picnic tables and benches allow you to soak up the great outdoors and eat al fresco in the Somerset sunshine. Step out and enjoy country walks from your doorstep… the village pub, horse riding stables and a beauty room are all within easy walking distance. We are well placed to enjoy many of the West Country’s delights which include the world heritage city of Bath, Bristol with its maritime history, the fantastic music extravaganza and mystical town of Glastonbury, the vibrant city of Wells, award-winning market town of Frome, the Somerset Levels (offering both willow / wetland visitor centres, amazing bird watching and murmurations), the world famous Longleat Safari Park, The Bath and West Showground with it’s varied events and lots more besides.

title: Dunkery Beacon Country House
subtitle: Welcome to Dunkery Beacon Country House near Dunster – a truly unique and special place to stay in the heart of Exmoor National Park.
bodyContent: Dunkery Beacon Hotel near Minehead offers luxury accommodation and provide the perfect place to escape the rigours of day-to-day life and relax and unwind in a truly tranquil, rural location where breath-taking scenery abounds. Dining & Drinks Relaxed, friendly and sophisticated award-winning dining with a seasonally changing menu and a focus on locally-sourced produce. Our extensive wine list is supplied by top London wine merchant Berry Bros. & Rudd and West Country merchant Christopher Piper Wines. Experience Exmoor in all its glory from our idyllic rural location, with spectacular views across the countryside and moor. There’s wild moorland, lush, deep, wooded, river valleys, pretty thatched cottages and acres of woodland. Sit back, relax…and let nature take over!
tagline: Welcome to Dunkery Beacon Country House near Dunster

title: Bistrot Pierre 1994
subtitle: Whether it’s a casual catch up over lunch, a special occasion or relaxed family meal, Bistrot Pierre offers the perfect environment in which to enjoy remarkable dishes, drinks and atmosphere.
bodyContent: Enjoy great value French bistrot cooking and seasonal menus featuring French bistrot classics such as steak-frites, boeuf bourguignon and tarte au citron alongside dishes from France’s many regions as well as vegetarian and vegan dishes. Open seven-days-a-week for lunch and dinner, along with breakfast at the weekend, there is something for everyone. Their NEW Menu Pierre offers three courses and a drink for just £22.95, whilst the extensive all-day menu offers a wide variety of dish options suitable for all tastes. You’ll find plenty of gluten-free dishes as well as a child-friendly menu on offer to help make your experience in the bistrot enjoyable for all. Located on Beach Road, their bistrot has incredible panoramic views across the bay, beach and Grand Pier. Their bistrot seats approximately 180 diners and has a large bar area downstairs, extensive outside terraced areas and a balcony, where their customers are able to enjoy the stunning views whilst they dine. With special events hosted each month (such as the Soiree Gastronomique on the 2nd and 4th Tues of the month) there’s always a reason to celebrate over a great meal and good company. This relaxed and friendly bistrot is the place to go for any occasion.
tagline: Whether it’s a casual catch up over lunch, a special occasion or relaxed family meal

title: Stoddens Farm Holiday Cottages
subtitle: Self catering barn conversions near Burnham On Sea, Somerset.
bodyContent: Stoddens Farm lies on the edge of the countryside, overlooking fields and the ‘Knoll’. 2 x Grade 11 listed Jacobean barn conversions on a former working farm, each sleeping 4. Less than 1.5 miles from the town and beach. Easily reached day trips include Wells, Glastonbury, Cheddar, The Mendips, Quantocks, Bath & Bristol. The cottages are spacious and comfortable, giving that home from home feeling. They have large gardens set out to mainly lawn with patios and patio furniture. No smoking and no pets. Do call to enquire as weekend breaks are available.

title: Cavell House Bed and Breakfast B&B in Clevedon
bodyContent: Make yourself at home 3 minutes walk to the sea, 3 minutes walk to the Pier (best sea fishing in Somerset with fishing off the pier) 3 minutes walk to the shops, 1 minute to the Bank, 5 minutes walk to the pub/Chinese/Indian/English food/antiques/sea front cafes. 10 Min slow stroll along the sea front to the childrens leisure aea passing the sailing club, pub, amusements, fish and chips and ice cream on the way. Beautiful views across to Wales. Paddle steamer trips from the -pier, to Lundy, North Devon, Penarth and Gloucester. An ideal base for walkers and cyclists. Background to Cavell House Originally the Victorian home of Lord and Lady Belgrave, it later became a residential Girls School and Nurse Edith Cavell (the world war one heroine) spent some of her school days here. Prior to George and Daphne Hamnett becoming proprietors in 1996, Cavell House was a childrens home administered by the Assemblies of God Pentecostal Church. Breakfast served in room Box Selection of Cereal, milk, Orange Juice, fruit Muffin, Selection of Nuts, Complemented with Croissant, Fresh Coffee, Tea decafe or caffeinated and fresh fruit. - special requests taken Please let reception know what time you would like breakfast, as a guide between 8am and 10am

title: Dunster Working Watermill, National Trust
subtitle: On site of a mill mentioned in the Domesday Survey of c1086. The present mill dates from 18thC and was restored to working order.
bodyContent: Dunster Working Mill, Somerset, National Trust is a fully restored watermill A restored 18th-century watermill built on the site of a mill mentioned in the Domesday Survey of 1086. The mill is set in peaceful surroundings alongside the River Avill and at the entrance to the Dunster Castle River gardens. The watermill is fully operational. You can often see original milling here and even buy the flour produced.
tagline: A restored 18th-century watermill built on the site of a mill mentioned in the Domesday Survey.

title: Exmoor Coaster
subtitle: With the traditional seaside resort of Minehead at one end, and the traditional fishing village of Lymouth at the other end, the Exmoor Coaster links seaside towns across the dramatic moorland, traversing the insanely steep Porlock Hill as it climbs between coast and moor.
bodyContent: This route is perfect for any walkers who want to hop off and on along the way, taking in the sights. Equally, if you are just looking to stay on board and enjoy the views, you will be wowed by the open top-deck views while journeying on Porlock Hill, the steepest A road in England. Following the steep climb is the beautiful harbour village of Lynmouth. Travel all day for an unlimited amount with our Exmoor Coaster Day Pass! This allows you to enjoy a relaxed scenic round trip, or hop on and off as much as you like. A family ticket allows for 2 adults and any number of children so is the perfect way to save on fuelling and parking your car on a holiday day out! For more information and timetables, please visit: https://www.firstbus.co.uk/adventures-bus/

title: Stay Wells and Somerset - Apartment 1
subtitle: Stylish two bed flat, Wells City Centre, free parking Enjoy a comfortable stay at this stylish centrally-located two bedroom flat. The Guard House is a historic building within a few steps of Wells High Street. The Cathedral, Vicars Close and Bishop's Palace are all very close by, as well as the bustling market in the ancient square. Free parking.
bodyContent: Enjoy a very comfortable stay at this stylish centrally-located two bedroom flat. Brought to you by 'Stay Wells and Somerset', the Guard House is a historic building within a few steps of Wells High Street with a vast array of independent shops, restaurants and cafes. The Cathedral, Vicars Close and Bishop's Palace are all just around the corner as well as a bustling twice weekly market in the ancient market square. This charming two double bedroom luxury flat takes up the entire first floor of the original 18th century Guard House in Guard House Lane and was sympathetically converted just four years ago from an impressive stone building which was originally built to house prisoners of war during the Napoleonic Wars. There is a smart entrance with entry phone system and one set of stairs up to the first floor where the main front door leads to an entrance hall with access to the lounge/kitchen/dining room which is a lovely double aspect room with rooftop views towards the Cathedral. There is engineered oak flooring fitted throughout the flat and a tasteful kitchen fitted with integrated appliances including a Stoves induction hob, oven, dishwasher, washer/dryer and fridge/freezer. There are two bedrooms with kingsize beds, one of which can be converted into a twin and a stylish shower room. There is a generous allocated parking space to the rear. High speed internet, a smart TV, an Alexa music speaker preloaded with the Unlimited Music package are also provided.

title: Museum of Somerset
subtitle: The Museum of Somerset tells the county's story from prehistoric times to the present day using real objects combined with evocative films, sounds and images, and the voices and words of Somerset people past and present.
bodyContent: ENTRY TO THE MUSEUM IS FREE! Visit Taunton Castle Housed in Taunton ’s historic castle, the Museum of Somerset tells the county's fascinating story from prehistoric times to the present day. Within the 12th century castle walls you’ll find contemporary gallery spaces and great family visitor facilities, all situated within the vibrant town centre. Discover 400 million years of history With an amazing nine themed galleries, each with its own distinctive character, there’s something for everyone to discover. Our ‘must see’ exhibits include a 200 million year old Plesiosaur fossil (a type of marine reptile); the impressive Low Ham Roman mosaic; a stunning Bronze Age Gold Torc; the Giant’s Shoes worn by 7ft4 Joseph Sewell; and the Banwell Bear skull of an 80,000 year old Ice Age hunter-killer. The museum also houses The Somerset Military Museum. What's On? There's always something going on for families with activities and family fun days throughout the year. February & October half term Drop in for family fun activities throughout the school holidays Easter Complete our Egg-cellent Easter Trail and take part in themed activities Summer Fun Whatever the weather you'll find something for everyone at our family friendly summer exhibition and events Halloween Explore the Museum on the spookiest night of the year - dress up if you dare! Christmas Visit Santa in his grotto every Saturday in December Entry to the museum is free but donations are welcome. There may be a charge for some activities, events or exhibitions. Café and shop The Courtyard Café offers a selection of home-made Somerset treats, from soups, sandwiches and salads, to pastries and home-made cakes. You can also visit the museum shop which stocks a range of reasonably-priced toys, cards, books and gifts including the ‘Made in Somerset’ range of local food and drink. The Museum of Somerset is part of the South West Heritage Trust, an independent charity committed to protecting and celebrating Somerset and Devon’s rich heritage.

title: The Helicopter Museum
subtitle: The Helicopter Museum is the largest dedicated Helicopter Collection in the World with over 100 helicopters on display in an all weather undercover hangar. Exhibits include two of the Queen's Royal Flight helicopters, the current world speed record holder G-LYNX, a Vietnam Veteran Huey and a Russian Hind Gun Ship.
bodyContent: In addition to over 100 helicopters, the Helicopter Museum includes other breathtaking attractions like its WWII Pilots’ Block, Weston Aviation Exhibition and Blood Hound Missile. This all contributes to a fun day-out for all the family with plenty of opportunity to learn about these marvellous machines and their huge impact on Somerset’s history. The museum hosts various special events throughout the year. These include various car shows, hair-rasing Halloween hilarity and festive Christmas events. The most popular of these special events are the World At War Weekend and Balloons, Birds & Bubbles . At these events, the museum is completely transformed to provide visitors the opportunity to enjoy authentic military vehicles or hold a live owl! Those who haven’t had their fill of aviation history can also attend one of the museum’s open cockpit days. Here visitors can climb into the pilot’s seat of a genuine helicopter and be taken through the controls by an experienced volunteer, many of whom have spent their careers flying such aircraft. Those who really want to feel the thrill of soaring high up in the clouds can even book their seat on one of the many helicopter experience flights the museum offers throughout the year. After all that excitement, visitors can refuel in the museum’s new café which was opened as part of a new visitor service building in July 2020. It offers drinks, snacks and tasty lunches. A particular highlight is the pilots’ all-day breakfast that is big enough to satisfy even the hungriest aviation superfan!
tagline: The Helicopter Museum is the largest dedicated Helicopter Collection in the World

title: ⭐Shepton Mallet Prison
subtitle: Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’; Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom...
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’, Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom. Shepton Mallet Prison is a recently decommissioned (2013) Georgian jail where visitors can walk in the footsteps of our social history and hear officers shine a light on what life was like for both the incarcerated and those who guarded them through the ages. Before its closure, it was a category C lifer prison holding 189 prisoners. Opened in 1646, it was expanded in 1790, with further building work undertaken in the 1820s and 1830s, including the installation of a treadwheel for those sentenced to hard labour. In 1930, the inmate numbers fell and the prison was closed. During the Second World War, the prison was reopened and used as a military prison. It was initially used by the British Army and later by American forces, who constructed a new execution block for condemned prisoners. It was also used for the storage of important historical documents, including the Domesday Book. It returned to civilian use in 1966. Shepton Mallet prison is also known for its tales of paranormal activity. One of the most popular stories is that of the White Lady. She is frequently seen or sensed in various locations, especially A Wing. Staff and prisoners would often complain of an icy wind moving through the wing, the sweet smell of perfume and shadowy figures. She supposedly dates from the late 1700s, when she spent some time in the prison. During a lovers' tiff which escalated, she murdered her betrothed. Once found guilty and sentenced to death, she was housed in Shepton Mallet Prison. On the evening before her execution, she asked for her wedding dress to be brought to the prison, which they allowed. She wore it to bed that night, but in the morning the officers found that she had died during the night. No cause of death was ever found, so we are left to presume that she died of a broken heart. Perhaps this is why she still haunts the prison? In the early 1950s, the Kray Twins were also held here after deserting the British Army. Today, the prison is open as a tourist attraction offering Guided Tours, Self-Guided Tours, Escape Rooms, Night Behind Bars and Ghost Hunting Behind Bars. This is an immersive experience without gizmos or gimmicks – the jail is very much as it was when the last prisoners left in 2013. In 2025, Shepton Mallet Prison received the prestigious Trip Advisor Travellers’ Choice, for the 7th time running, placing it among the top 10% of attractions worldwide.

title: Fyne Court, National Trust
subtitle: Fyne Court is a hidden gem in the heart of the Quantock Hills. Explore a wild garden, reclaimed by nature after once being part of a family estate.
bodyContent: Fyne Court in Somerset National Trust is a hidden gem in the heart of the Quantock Hills. Explore a wild garden, reclaimed by nature after once being part of a family estate. The estate was the home of the Crosse family who lived here until the house was destroyed by fire in 1894. Scientist and poet Andrew Crosse, the ‘Thunder and Lightning Man’ and Fyne Court’s most famous resident, became a recluse after his controversial experiments were made public. Step into the Snug to find out more about Fyne Court’s history. There’s plenty for families to enjoy including den building, climbing on fallen trees, splashing in streams and picnicking on the Courtyard lawn. In summer, see a haze of wildflowers and hear the buzz of bees in the walled garden. The Courtyard Café is open seven days a week all year round and serves hot & cold drinks, light lunches and homemade cakes. Fyne Court is open daily from dawn until dusk (opening times may vary due to weather conditions). There is no charge for entry and parking is free for National Trust members or £5 for non-members. Tramper mobility scooter available – call or email in advance to book. Level access to Courtyard and Café. Accessible route around the garden. Natural play areas for children. To find out more, visit: www.nationaltrust.org.uk/fyne-court or call 01823 451587. For those that wish to stay a little longer, Fyne Court cottage sits above the grounds and sleeps 6. To find out more, visit: https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/holidays/fyne-court-cottage-somerset

title: The Pump Room Restaurant
subtitle: Built in 1795, the Pump Room is one of the most elegant and historical buildings in the country, and still today after more than 300 years people come together to celebrate in this unique venue.

title: The Loft cafe Wells Cathedral
subtitle: The Loft Café at Wells Cathedral boasts views of the magnificent West Front of Wells Cathedral and over the tranquil moat of the Bishop’s Palace. Located on the first floor, it can be reached by a set of stairs or by lift.
bodyContent: The Loft Café at Wells Cathedral boasts views of the magnificent West Front of Wells Cathedral and over the tranquil moat of the Bishop’s Palace. Located on the first floor, it can be reached by a set of stairs or by lift. Our food is freshly prepared and baked by our team on site each day using local Somerset and Fairtrade produce wherever possible. Enjoy a range of morning pastries, warm cheese scones, and light lunch choices, then finish off some tasty homemade cakes and cream teas! Like and follow us on Facebook and Instagram to keep up with the latest deals and news from The Loft! Free hot drinks with our loyalty card! Just 4 stamps to collect on your Loft Loyalty Card and get your 5th hot drink free! Dogs Well behaved dogs are welcome! A water bowl will be available and there are homemade biscuits so that your four-legged-friend can enjoy their visit as much as you! Catering for group visits We can accommodate up to 96 people in our café. If you would like to bring a group for morning coffee, lunch, or afternoon tea, or you have any other enquiries, please contact the catering team on 01749 676 543 or email catering@wellscathedral.org.uk Contact Let us know how we did using our feedback form and be entered into our monthly draw to win a free drink and teatime treat of your choice! If you would like to contact us please email catering@wellscathedral.org.uk or phone us on 01749 676543 . All profits from the café go to supporting the work of the Cathedral.
tagline: The Loft Café at Wells Cathedral boasts views of the magnificent West Front of Wells Cathedral

title: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm
subtitle: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is a conservation charity and the largest zoo in Somerset with over 100 species of animals. The multi award winning Zoo is open 7 days a week and aims to make Noah's Ark a place of joy, wonder, adventure and refreshment that supports the well-being of all visitors, staff and volunteers. Through education and fun, they aim to inspire and motivate this generation and the next to consider sustainable lifestyles and care for our planet.
bodyContent: Amazing Animals The home of the big Zoo animals! Visit Noah’s Ark and come face to face with a cheeky mob of meerkats, be awed by African elephants and dazzled by the zebra herd! Experience the majestic beauty and see the skies come alive during the daily birds of prey displays! The Wings of Wonder display showcases the owls, hawks, falcons and eagles in an unforgettably mesmerizing spectacle. Indoor and Outdoor Adventures Play and adventure never stops with our 10 play areas across the 100-acre site. Enjoy the huge indoor play barns including under 5’s soft play and a giant rainbow slide. The Zoo also has accessible play equipment including nest swings and a wheelchair accessible roundabout. Fancy an a-maze-ing adventure? Navigate through Britain’s longest hedge maze. The British wildlife themed maze has 3.4km of paths and wooden nest tower at the center. Keep the whole family smiling and active all day, whatever the weather! Accessibility Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is proud to be an accessible attraction. Facilities include multiple accessible toilets, Changing Places facility, accessible play equipment, hearing loops and more. Please visit the website before your visit for up-to-date information and to view the Access guide. Prices Buy online and save! Noah’s Ark recommends that all tickets, including those for free essential carers and under 2’s are purchased online prior to your arrival. Prices are seasonal, please check the website for up-to-date ticket prices. Food and Drink With a range of delicious hot and cold food and drink options available in our Food Barn and convenient snack kiosks across the Zoo, there is something for everyone! Alternatively, visitors are very welcome to bring their own lunch and enjoy it in one of our many picnic spots. Mini Experiences Noah’s Ark offers incredible up-close mini experiences with Meerkats, Capybara, Andean Bears and Giant Tortoise. You will enjoy 20 minutes behind the scenes with the keeper, learn some interesting facts and get involved with their feeding and enrichment programme. Pre-book your experience online to ensure availability. Minimum age and terms and conditions apply. Animal Experiences Find out what it’s like to be a keeper for the day with our one-to-one keeper experiences before the zoo opens. Experiences include: African Elephants, Junior Keeper Experience, and Giraffe and Rhino experience.
tagline: You’ll be amazed at the variety of nature you’ll see with over 100 species of animals

title: Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Mendip Activity Centre is the ultimate outdoor adventure playground in Somerset. They’ve been delivering adventurous outdoor activities for nearly 40 years, growing from humble beginnings to the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West!
bodyContent: It’s Time for Adventure with Mendip Activity Centre! Nestled in 250 acres of ancient woodland in the Mendip Hills National Landscape, Mendip Activity Centre is the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West. Just 20 minutes from Weston-super-Mare and Cheddar and open year-round, Mendip have been delivering Adventure, Learning and Training for individuals, families, schools, and groups since 1987. Activities available include: · Air Rifle · Tobogganing · Archery · Skiing · Snowboarding · Frisbee Golf · Kayaking · Nerf & Gel Battles · Caving · Paddle Boarding · Rock Climbing · Axe Throwing · ArcheryActive · Abseiling · Canoeing Come for the day or stay longer. In summer, pitch your tent at the award-winning Mendip Basecamp (link to https://mendipbasecamp.com/), a family adventure campsite awarded second at the Visit England Awards 2025. Pitch where you like, check out when it suits, camp fires encouraged, dogs welcome and endless adventure is on offer! Adventure for Everyone Mendip is more than just activities. It’s a place to switch off from screens, reconnect with nature, and each other. Whether you're learning something new, developing an existing skill or simply having fun outside, you’ll leave with muddy boots and big smiles. We believe in adventure for everyone. Many of our activities are adaptable for additional needs, and our friendly team will work with you to make it happen Refuel at the Alpine Lounge Overlooking the Ski Slope, the Alpine Lounge café serves pizzas, paninis, coffee and cake with stunning views- perfect for après-adventure refreshments

title: Haynes Motor Museum
subtitle: Haynes Motor Museum in Sparkford is a must-visit attraction, home to the UK’s largest collection of cars and motorbikes. Discover pioneering vehicles in The Dawn of Motoring, explore iconic red cars in the Red Room, and experience the thrill of legendary Williams Formula 1 racing cars up close.

title: Dunster Working Watermill, National Trust
subtitle: On site of a mill mentioned in the Domesday Survey of c1086. The present mill dates from 18thC and was restored to working order.
bodyContent: Dunster Working Mill, Somerset, National Trust is a fully restored watermill A restored 18th-century watermill built on the site of a mill mentioned in the Domesday Survey of 1086. The mill is set in peaceful surroundings alongside the River Avill and at the entrance to the Dunster Castle River gardens. The watermill is fully operational. You can often see original milling here and even buy the flour produced.

title: The Sheppey Inn
subtitle: The Sheppey Inn lies out on the beautiful wilds of the Somerset Levels, surrounded by peat moors, dairy farms and national wildlife reserves.
bodyContent: The pub pulls in people from miles around thanks to the brilliant, eclectic musicians it attracts, its fine selection of local ales and ciders (including all kinds of one-offs and speciality brews), and its fantastic food. Spending the afternoon out here in the countryside, lounging by the river, looking out for voles and kingfishers, isn’t the worst idea in the world, is it? There’s been a pub in Godney servicing the thirsty throats of Levels farmworkers for many centuries. The last owners ran it for 120 years, but on one day in 1976, they ran out of cider and lost the trust of the next two generations of locals. the pub has been renovated, revamped and restored, and now has about six casks of grown-ups’ apple juice on the bar to make sure that the such a thing never happens again. Check out the photos on the right for proof.
tagline: The Sheppey Inn lies out on the beautiful wilds of the Somerset Levels.

title: The Strode Theatre
subtitle: Strode Theatre is a part of Strode College in Street, near Glastonbury, in Somerset. It is equipped as both theatre and cinema, incorporating two venues. The main Theatre has 343 seats and a proscenium arch stage. The Studio has 64 seats in a retractable unit and is used for film screenings and for classes and rehearsals.
bodyContent: Strode Theatre is a part of Strode College in Street, near Glastonbury, in Somerset. It is equipped as both theatre and cinema, incorporating two venues. The main Theatre has 343 seats and a proscenium arch stage. The Studio has 64 seats in a retractable unit and is used for film screenings and for classes and rehearsals. We promote a mixed programme of live professional and amateur events on stage (‘Live on Stage’), mainstream and arthouse films as well as live and recorded transmissions of opera, ballet and theatre (‘Live on Screen’). The foyer is home to changing exhibitions of work by local and regional artists. Opened in 1963, funded by the Clarks Foundation, Strode Theatre has been an essential part of the community for more than five decades. We are pleased to offer a warm and welcoming environment for all our visitors, performers and artists. At the heart of the community, we provide spaces for meeting, rehearsing, performing and exhibiting. Opening an hour before a performance our bar gives a friendly place to meet beforehand and a relaxed atmosphere to chat afterwards.
