title: Sharpham Park
subtitle: Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels near Glastonbury.
bodyContent: Our organic farm and mill Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels near Glastonbury . It’s the home of Mulberry founder Roger Saul who moved from the world of fashion to food in 2004 when he launched the Sharpham Park brand from his organic farm. At Sharpham Park we grow organic spelt and stone grind it in the traditional way to preserve the delicious, nutty taste of the ancient grain. Today, we turned the milled spelt into flour, cereals and grains however history records show spelt has been grown for approximately 4,000 years in the area since the Bronze and Iron ages. The farm is also sustainably managed – the spelt fields have 4 metre margins and the hedgerows are cut every other year meaning wildlife such as wild deer, hare, bees and dormice are allowed to shelter and forage for food all year round. The ancient grain Spelt is an ancient grain which as has gained popularity in recent times because it’s an excellent source of dietary fibre and contains protein as well as some vitamins and minerals. It’s both easy to digest and leaves you feeling fuller for longer as well as being a good source of slow release energy; so much so the Roman Army called it their “marching grain”. Within working with Bowel Cancer UK Eating a high fibre diet is important in the fight against Bowel Cancer and we have teamed up with Bowel Cancer UK to spread this message. More than 40 top chefs have donated spelt recipes to the campaign and you can find these Great British Spelt Recipes on our website. Sharpham Pantry restaurant at Kilver Court Designer Village You can enjoy a range of spelt dishes in the Sharpham Pantry restaurant including our spelt flat breads and spelt bread and butter pudding. You can find the full range of our delicious spelt products in the Great House at Kilver Court Designer Village in Shepton Mallet. Come and browse our selection of cereals including flakes, muesli and porridge as well as our grains and four different types of flour made to meet all of your baking needs.
tagline: Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels.

title: Home Made, Home Grown, Hand Crafted!
subtitle: The Country Market is held every Friday morning from 10-11.15am at Christ Church Vestry Hall.
bodyContent: Home Made, Home Grown, Hand Crafted! The Country Market is held every Friday morning from 10-11.15am at Christ Church Vestry Hall. There are a variety of stalls selling plants, crafts, local eggs and cheeses, cooked meat, fish, butter, honey, apple juice, seasonal fruit and veg, preserves and baked goods, including cakes, cookies, savouries and desserts, all made in and around Nailsea. Enjoy a cup of coffee and cake at Nailsea’s Country Market! Orders Country Markets will take orders and are happy to discuss with you what you want – whether it is a large order of cakes or savouries for a special event or just the one item. If you can’t make a market date, each market also has a contact who will take an order and deliver it to your door. Hampers Country Markets also operate a hamper scheme . It works just like Inter Flora and you will be able to order a hamper for delivery anywhere in the country – a perfect present for a new student or elderly relative. New Producers We welcome new producers. Small volume producers are as welcome as those with more to sell. Just pop into your local market and talk to the Market Manager or contact 07939 989805 to become a producer. It costs a nominal amount to join the co-operative and a small commission is taken from anything you sell to cover running costs. All products are sold co-operatively. You do not have your own table as your produce will share table space with other producers in the market. Items you sell must be new and home made, home grown or hand crafted by you. Visit our Facebook page!
tagline: The Country Market is held every Friday morning from 10-11.15am at Christ Church Vestry Hall.

title: Tyntesfield, National Trust
subtitle: At its heart Tyntesfield is a Victorian country house and estate, which serves as a backdrop to the remarkable story of four generations of the Gibbs family. Their tale charts the accumulation of wealth from the guano trade, transformation of a Georgian house to a Victorian Gothic masterpiece and the collection of over 70,000 objects.
bodyContent: At its heart Tyntesfield is a Victorian country house and estate, which serves as a backdrop to the remarkable story of four generations of the Gibbs family. Their tale charts the accumulation of wealth from the guano trade, transformation of a Georgian house to a Victorian Gothic masterpiece and the collection of over 70,000 objects. Their achievements are celebrated through ornate Gothic carvings, flower-filled terraces and an expansive estate amid the Somerset countryside. For young explorers there are three play areas, a woodland adventure play and sculpture trail, and seasonal family trails around the estate. There is also a packed activities programme including open air theatre, food and craft markets and living history. Eating and shopping: Home Farm visitor centre offers year-round homemade dishes using estate-grown ingredients and a shop with plant sales, and a second-hand bookshop. For light bites while exploring, try the Pavilion Café. Dogs: Dogs on short leads are welcome in specified areas of the Tyntesfield estate. There is a map at reception that you can take a picture of.
tagline: At its heart Tyntesfield is a Victorian country house and estate.

title: Fill Good Pantry
subtitle: We Are Fill Good Pantry #dogoodfillgood As two Portishead locals, our mission is to make living sustainably easy regardless of your budget. We want to become a destination for sustainable living and education, by providing opportunities for our customers to join the zero waste movement and benefit our local environment.
bodyContent: We Are Fill Good Pantry #dogoodfillgood As two Portishead locals, our mission is to make living sustainably easy regardless of your budget. We want to become a destination for sustainable living and education, by providing opportunities for our customers to join the zero waste movement and benefit our local environment. As well as our wonderful customers, we also believe strongly in providing an opportunity for local suppliers of great products and good ethics to meet our grocery needs. This promotes sustainability but also the local economy. Our Products We have a full range of products from a variety of local producers that have sustainability tied to their core values. We are always adding new and exciting new ranges to our product list and will keep listening to our customers about what they need to find ways to buy it sustainably. ​ Why Shop Sustainably Environmental issues and consequences of human behaviour, have become more and more well known over the years as the spotlight and awareness spreads. In fact, that raised awareness is a key reason why our shop exists. There is a wealth of information that shows our waste production and lifestyle is fundamentally changing the earth globally but it is also having the same affect locally and devastating our environments. We dont think that change needs to be drastic but can simply start with awareness and small adjustments and at Fill Good Pantry we offer a place to start and learn more.
tagline: We Are Fill Good Pantry

title: DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House
subtitle: Great motorway links M5 junction 20 & 21 Bristol International Airport only 12 minutes away Bristol City Centre only 25 minutes away. With local access to Cheddar Gorge and Mendip AONB only 45 minutes away.
bodyContent: Welcome to DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House, the South West’s finest four-star boutique hotel and spa. An enchanting venue set within rolling English countryside, Cadbury House is the ideal backdrop for your special occasion whether a wedding, private party, business event, spa break or dining experience. With truly breath-taking views across North Somerset and the Bristol Channel, Cadbury House effortlessly combines old and new, with the traditional country house and the elegant boutique-style hotel. There is also an onsite Marco Pierre White Steakhouse Bar & Grill, an award-winning health club and a renowned spa. The hotel offers 132 luxury bedrooms including suites, on-site parking and excellent transport access meaning guests can enjoy the facilities for both business and pleasure. Please note from May 1 st , 2022 overnight parking will be chargeable at £5.00 per vehicle. Corporate customers are also well catered for with 12 meeting rooms, multiple breakout areas, and a dedicated conference team on hand. Whether you are hosting a small business meeting to a multi-day conference, DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House does not disappoint as a destination location for business needs.
tagline: The South West’s finest four-star boutique hotel and spa.

title: Glastonbury Tor, National Trust
subtitle: Glastonbury Tor is a well-loved Somerset landmark associated with myths and legends, but it is also a place where children can run about and have fun. Fields at the foot of the Tor are good for games or you could play at the top in the ruined tower.
bodyContent: Prominent hill overlooking the Isle of Avalon, Glastonbury and Somerset. This iconic and evocative landmark offers magnificent views of the Somerset Levels , Dorset, Wiltshire and Wales. Steeped in history and legend, excavations at the top of the Tor have revealed the plans of two superimposed churches of St Michael, of which only a 15th-century tower remains. Glastonbury Tor also has a grisly past. Abbot Richard Whiting was executed here in 1549 on the orders of Thomas Cromwell, the first Earl of Essex. Glastonbury Tor is known as being one of the most spiritual sites in the country. Its pagan beliefs are still very much celebrated. It’s a beautiful place to walk, unwind and relax.
tagline: Glastonbury Tor is a well-loved Somerset landmark associated with myths and legends.

title: Thorner’s Farm Shop
subtitle: Thorner’s began with the simple idea of providing quality butchery meat, sourced in Somerset whenever possible. This is still one of our core values and now, in addition to fresh meat, we are proud to offer an award winning range of pies, quiches, savouries, ready meals, desserts & cakes.
bodyContent: Where did it all begin? Born and bred in Somerset Mr Jon Thorner opened one of the regions very first farm shops in 1979, as an extension of the family farm and abattoir. The core of the business was built upon using locally sourced and high welfare meat with a strong focus on fair pricing for suppliers. A passion for success The meat industry has changed dramatically since 1979 and it was important for Thorner’s to diversify. So in 2005 the first Thorner’s pie was baked! As the kitchen gained confidence, the number of awards grew and they knew they had something special to offer. The range has grown significantly now offering a range of pies, quiches, savouries, ready meals, desserts and cakes – and did you know each pie is still hand crimped and individually filled. Award winning The quality of our ingredients, the authentic homemade appearance and flavour of our kitchen range has delivered us multiple awards across the food industry including Great Taste, British Pie Awards, Taste of the West and Smithfield Awards, and our staff and the business have also been recognised regionally and within the industry at Somerset Business and Mendip Business Awards.
tagline: Thorner’s began with the simple idea of providing quality butchery meat, sourced in Somerset

title: Goodfellows
subtitle: Smart restaurant and cafe with fish-centric, Modern Mediterranean dishes made from local produce.
bodyContent: Adam and Martine Fellows opened Goodfellows in September 2004, quickly becoming one of the most popular restaurants in the area. Adam spent 17 years perfecting his style while working in many of the best restaurants across England, France and Belgium. He was Head Chef for seven years at the Michelin starred Charlton House Hotel. For the last 15 years Adam has delighted customers with his modern European dishes featuring fish, meat and vegetarian dishes which are light but intense with flavour. The fish comes mainly from day boats off the coast of Devon and Cornwall and is cooked inventively, enhancing the natural flavours of the fish but never over-complicating them. Goodfellows has two AA Red Rosettes and is included in the The Good Food Guide and Trencherman Guide

bodyContent: That’s why Rotisserie chicken is the hero of our menu, alongside tender steaks, stacked burgers and satisfying salads. title: Somerset Antiques & Interiors
subtitle: Welcome to Somerset Antiques and Interiors located in Shepton Mallet, Somerset , Established in 2004.
bodyContent: We have a large extensive showroom and stock a wide range of genuine Antiques, Vintage and Contemporary furniture, including tables, chairs, clocks, soft furniture and many more decorative items. Our Staff offer a friendly and knowledgeable service whereby we will do our utmost to help you find the item you are looking for. We offer a Nationwide and Worldwide delivery service and if you cannot find the item you are looking for we also source and locate specific stock. Our Website contains a selection of our large amount of stock in the shop which is well worth a visit in The Historic Town of Shepton Mallet. Somerset Antiques & Interiors , relocated to Shepton Mallet in June 2011 after six years of successful trading as the Wells Emporium in Priory Road, Wells, Somerset. We now have two extensive floors displaying our large, diverse and constantly changing range of furniture, from antique to contemporary. There really is something to suit every ones taste and budget. We pride ourselves on giving our customers a quality and personal service.

title: Taunton
subtitle: Somerset’s county town lies along the River Tone and proudly displays its history in the Museum of Somerset, which is set in the reconstructed remains of a Norman castle.
bodyContent: Exhibits cover Somerset’s early history, its traditions, artistic inspiration, military might and the Monmouth Rebellion. Taunton itself was once home to a priory and the town profited hugely from the wool trade in Medieval times. The magnificent, 48m-high tower of St Mary Magdalene church, which dominates Hammet Street, is testament to its success. Quirky Vivary Park is a great place for a picnic. Once the site of a medieval fish farm belonging to the old priory, the park has a fountain dedicated to Queen Victoria and views of the hulking red keep of Jellalabad military barracks. Alternatively, the riverside French Weir Park has a cafe and is a great place to hire paddleboards for a scoot downriver.

title: Taunton
subtitle: As befits a County Town, Taunton is steeped in history and has much to entertain our visitors, from the superb Somerset Museum in the remnants of the castle to the Cricket Ground and Racecourse. A centre for Arts and Culture, it has shops, cafes, restaurants, riverside walks and a weekly Farmers’ Market. Rooted between the majestic Quantock Hills, Somerset Levels and the woodland-cloaked Blackdowns, Taunton’s lively nature plays host to major sports centre Somerset County Cricket Club. It’s also
bodyContent: Things to do in Taunton Taunton’s ideal location and identity as county town of Somerset makes it perfect for exploring the wider area of Taunton Deane - everywhere from the cattle-grazed meadows of the Somerset Levels to the windswept heights of the Quantock Hills and striking Blackdowns . It also boasts an impressive cultural offering, ranging from museums and ancient monuments like the ancient Taunton Castle to contemporary centres like the Brewhouse Theatre & Arts Centre. Explore the Museum of Somerset , based at the 12th-century Taunton Castle, and follow Somerset’s history from prehistoric times to the present day. Stunning Perpendicular Gothic style architecture can be found soaring 163 feet above Taunton at the historic St Mary Magdalene Church, while Hestercombe Gardens are a paradise for nature lovers with fifty acres of enchanting gardens, stunning terraces, lakes and cascades. Taunton’s town centre is a mecca for shopping, with well-known high street brands and a brilliant selection of eateries and bars, as well as pubs serving locally-sourced food and drink. Take the Taunton Heritage Trail’s self-guided tour around the town’s historical sites to ensure you don’t miss a thing. Featured in the trail you’ll find Bath Place, a picturesque narrow street with 19th-century shop fronts now brimming with independent retailers and cafés. At the top of the high street proudly sits the Victorian-designed Vivary Park, home to the annual Taunton Flower Show, proudly described as the ‘The Chelsea of the West’. Taunton’s world-class sporting scene doesn’t disappoint. Catch a lively cricket match at The Cooper Associates County Ground or visit the Somerset Cricket Museum to explore the game’s fascinating history. Soak up a thrilling atmosphere at the Taunton Races or attend one of the racecourse’s brilliant events throughout the year, ranging from rural shows to concerts and circuses. For a quieter affair, the tranquility of Trull meadows and waterfall make them the perfect spot for a picnic or follow the towpath of the Bridgwater and Taunton Canal for a picturesque cycle ride. Taunton Visitor Centre Now based in the western wing of the landmark Market House, the Taunton Visitor Centre is the place to go to make the most of your time in Taunton. The county town has plenty to offer from individual boutiques to historic architecture, modern dining to traditional tea rooms and unspoilt views to the Blackdown Hills and Quantock Hills (both Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty). Taunton offers a wide mix of activities, attractions and events - we can’t wait to help you plan the perfect trip! Services offered: The Taunton Visitor Centre holds information on many wide and varied things to do within Taunton and the surrounding areas. Now a part of the bustling town centre mix, we welcome over 100,000 visitors and local residents through our doors each year. The Visitor Centre Box Office offers tickets for most local and regional events taking place, including the hugely popular Taunton Flower Show. We are a box office for the Brewhouse Theatre and Tacchi-Morris Arts Centre in Taunton and the Playhouse Theatre in Weston-super-Mare. If you're looking for that special "experience" gift then give the gift of theatre with our Theatre Tokens Gift Cards. The Travel Centre acts as an agent for Bakers Dolphin, Berry’s Coaches, Falcon bus service, Holiday Extras and National Express. As well as the booking service we offer friendly advice for local transport, parking and accommodation to make your trip stress-free. We also offer multiple advertising and marketing opportunities to local businesses, events organisers, charities and more. Souvenirs and Publications: The Visitor Centre shop is bursting with products that will help you take home a taste of Taunton, including locally produced biscuits and preserves, hand-crafted cards and a variety of colourful souvenirs. We also stock a large range of local maps, guides and books to help you truly discover Taunton and the surrounding areas.

bodyContent: Welcome to Jonswood Lodge, our bespoke luxury holiday lodge with tennis court, gym and games room, sleeping 6 in 3 bedrooms. Boasting its own tennis court and fitness room, it sits in the hamlet of Watchfield, within easy reach of the area's famous attractions including the caves and cliffs at Cheddar Gorge , underground rivers and pools at Wookey Hole , Clarks Shopping Village at Street , Glastonbury Tor and the lovely Cathedral and Bishop's Palace at Wells , whilst the elegant city of Bath is a little further afield. Do call to enquire, we can accommodate most requests.

title: Holmwood Coach House
subtitle: Self-catering, holiday let, in Frome, Somerset, in a restored Victorian coach house, suitable for 1 to 3 people, with undercover car parking and a big garden, within easy strolling distance of the town centre.
bodyContent: Holmwood Coach House is a self-catering, holiday let, in Frome, Somerset. It is an architect designed renovation of a Victorian coach housing, suitable for 1, 2 or 3 people, set in an acre of garden and woodland with tennis court use, and undercover car parking. The historic town centre is easily reached on foot. It is well situated for visits to Bath, Stourhead, Longleat and the Mendip Hills. It has WiFi, a well equipped kitchen, gas central heating, Morso woodburner, internet TV, DVD Blu-ray system, galleried double bedroom, plus a single bedroom with daybed.

title: Still Sisters
subtitle: Our range of Gins are created using locally sourced botanicals from businesses just like ours. Our signature gin contains watercress from organic beds in Longbridge Deverill, our other leading botanicals are roses grown in Chard, Lavender from Warminster and Somerset Cider Apples from Perry’s Orchard.
bodyContent: We are two sisters based in Frome, Somerset producing small batch Gin from our bespoke copper still called Storm. We have great fun exploring and creating our drinks. Our range of Gins are created using locally sourced botanicals from businesses just like ours. Our signature gin contains watercress from organic beds in Longbridge Deverill, our other leading botanicals are roses grown in Chard, Lavender from Warminster and Somerset Cider Apples from Perry’s Orchard. Our Gins are perfect to enjoy with a simple tonic over ice. Our signature Gin using organic watercress enjoys peppery and refreshing undertones. We have explored and sampled a lot of Gins but our watercress, we believe is the best! Visit our beautiful distillery shop, meet one of our gin experts; purchase a bottle of your favourite gin; enjoy a gin & tonic; book one of our gin tasting experiences and learn all about the history of gin, how we make our gin and sample our award-winning gins with a selection of mixers; or visit our gin school and be guided in choosing your botanicals to make your very own gin!
tagline: Our range of Gins are created using locally sourced botanicals

title: Bistrot Pierre 1994
subtitle: Whether it’s a casual catch up over lunch, a special occasion or relaxed family meal, Bistrot Pierre offers the perfect environment in which to enjoy remarkable dishes, drinks and atmosphere.
bodyContent: Enjoy great value French bistrot cooking and seasonal menus featuring French bistrot classics such as steak-frites, boeuf bourguignon and tarte au citron alongside dishes from France’s many regions as well as vegetarian and vegan dishes. Open seven-days-a-week for lunch and dinner, along with breakfast at the weekend, there is something for everyone. Their NEW Menu Pierre offers three courses and a drink for just £22.95, whilst the extensive all-day menu offers a wide variety of dish options suitable for all tastes. You’ll find plenty of gluten-free dishes as well as a child-friendly menu on offer to help make your experience in the bistrot enjoyable for all. Located on Beach Road, their bistrot has incredible panoramic views across the bay, beach and Grand Pier. Their bistrot seats approximately 180 diners and has a large bar area downstairs, extensive outside terraced areas and a balcony, where their customers are able to enjoy the stunning views whilst they dine. With special events hosted each month (such as the Soiree Gastronomique on the 2nd and 4th Tues of the month) there’s always a reason to celebrate over a great meal and good company. This relaxed and friendly bistrot is the place to go for any occasion.
tagline: Whether it’s a casual catch up over lunch, a special occasion or relaxed family meal

title: Woodborough Inn
subtitle: A warm welcome, great food & drink and a cracking pub atmosphere is what makes The Woodborough Inn so special
bodyContent: Sat in the heart of the village of Winscombe and surrounded by the beautiful Mendip hills, The Woodborough Inn is the perfect place to relax and explore the local area which includes the beautiful Cheddar Gorge, the cathedral city of Wells and Glastonbury Tor. The Mendips providing a great space to enjoy the great outdoors. Whether a gentle walk or some extreme mountain biking; The Mendips has it all. Our guest accommodation consists of 7 cosy en-suite rooms, ideal for visitors to the West Country, business people and families alike, and come at competitive rates. Open daily from 11am, lunch from 12-2.00pm and our dinner service runs from 5.30pm. Sunday food hours are 12-3 and 5.30-7.30pm. Our chefs serve up some fabulous food. Hearty pub classics, an exciting range of specials, plus pizza and lighter dishes; all food cooked fresh using locally sourced ingredients. Our Sunday roasts are also not to be missed! Local real ales are always on tap along with crisp lagers, craft beers and local ciders. We have a wonderful wine list and our popular new “Gin List” heads up our selection of premium spirits. We also offer a great range of soft drinks, coffee, tea and cake! This is a popular spot for walkers and naturally, well-behaved dogs are welcome.
tagline: A warm welcome, great food & drink and a cracking pub atmosphere

title: DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House
subtitle: Great motorway links M5 junction 20 & 21 Bristol International Airport only 12 minutes away Bristol City Centre only 25 minutes away. With local access to Cheddar Gorge and Mendip AONB only 45 minutes away.
bodyContent: Welcome to DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House, the South West’s finest four-star boutique hotel and spa. An enchanting venue set within rolling English countryside, Cadbury House is the ideal backdrop for your special occasion whether a wedding, private party, business event, spa break or dining experience. With truly breath-taking views across North Somerset and the Bristol Channel, Cadbury House effortlessly combines old and new, with the traditional country house and the elegant boutique-style hotel. There is also an onsite Marco Pierre White Steakhouse Bar & Grill, an award-winning health club and a renowned spa. The hotel offers 132 luxury bedrooms including suites, on-site parking and excellent transport access meaning guests can enjoy the facilities for both business and pleasure. Please note from May 1 st , 2022 overnight parking will be chargeable at £5.00 per vehicle. Corporate customers are also well catered for with 12 meeting rooms, multiple breakout areas, and a dedicated conference team on hand. Whether you are hosting a small business meeting to a multi-day conference, DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House does not disappoint as a destination location for business needs.
tagline: The South West’s finest four-star boutique hotel and spa.

title: The Playhouse in Weston super Mare
subtitle: The Playhouse Theatre is available for hire for both community and professional shows and as a venue for conferences, meetings and corporate events. In addition to the main auditorium the theatres facilities include a licensed bar, meeting and rehearsal spaces and full disabled access.
bodyContent: Located in the centre of Weston-Super-Mare the Playhouse is a friendly and welcoming 664-seat theatre which offers a lively and diverse programme of events to meet the entertainment, creative and educational requirements of its local and surrounding community. The Playhouse’s high quality programme of professional and community events includes around 300 performances per year including music, drama, comedy, dance, musicals, film, children’s shows, pantomime and more recently West End Productions. The Playhouse Theatre is available for hire for both community and professional shows and as a venue for conferences, meetings and corporate events. In addition to the main auditorium the theatres facilities include a licensed bar, meeting and rehearsal spaces and full disabled access. Our dedicated and professional staff are used to working with all visiting companies and hirers to ensure a successful event while our welcoming and caring front of house team ensure patrons an enjoyable entertainment experience. The Playhouse Theatre is managed by Parkwood Theatres working in partnership with North Somerset Council.

title: Hope Farm Cottages
subtitle: Self catering cottages in a queit setting near Brean. Berrow and weston super mare in Somerset. Short holiday breaks.
bodyContent: Very close to the Somerset coast but surrounded by the beautiful West Country countryside you will find Hope Farm's 4 luxury cottages. The beaches of Brean & Weston Super Mare are minutes drives away and there are a vast array of day trips to surrounding attractions, villages and countryside to keep everyone occupied. Each ground floor self catering cottage is on the edge of a beautiful lawned courtyard with open fields behind. Each has 2 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms and are easily accessible for those that have special requirements. Outside there are picnic tables and deckchairs for those lazy days and Summer evenings. Each cottage has off road, private and security lit parking spaces for 2 vehicles. Hope Farm has a wealth of facilities including a games room, outdoor children's play ground, laundry room and covered storage for bikes or trailers. And if you dont fancy driving there is a bus stop right at the gate to Weston Super Mare, Burnham on Sea , Taunton & Bristol. We can accommodate most requests so do call us to discuss to make your break perfect.
tagline: Self catering cottages in a queit setting near Brean. Berrow and weston super mare in Somerset.

title: Hit the Streets of Clevedon for a healthy walk
subtitle: Walking groups are helping people across North Somerset stretch their legs, make new friends and feel healthier. Organised walks usually last about an hour but a new group has launched in Clevedon to offer residents a slightly more vigorous, 90-minute route. Life joined them to take in the sights around the town…
bodyContent: How to get there Start at map ref: ST 408710 Car: Parking is available at the former Morrisons supermarket, off Great Western Road - Route information Distance: just over 3 miles Difficulty: easy – a fairly flat route around the town Duration: allow up to 90 minutes Map: OS Explorer 153 Walking groups are helping people across North Somerset stretch their legs, make new friends and feel healthier. Organised walks usually last about an hour but a new group has launched in Clevedon to offer residents a slightly more vigorous, 90-minute route. Life joined them to take in the sights around the town… Start the walk in Queen’s Square, then turn left onto Old Church Road. Turn right onto Queen’s Road and continue uphill towards the crossroads at the end. Cross the road and turn left into Sunnyside Road. At the next crossroads turn right, which is still Sunnyside Road. From here you can go through a gate into Sunhill Park. Follow the path to your right, through the trees, and then head towards Sunhill House. This is now Clevedon Community Centre after being bought by the people of the town in 1949. Go around the side of the building and exit through the car park onto Princes Road. Turn right onto this road, cross over, and then at the junction turn left into Linden Road, then right into Herbert Road. Go through a wooden gate into Herbert Gardens, which was donated to the people of Clevedon by the Elton family in 1865. Follow the path and you will pass a ruined stone structure, which formed part of Wycliffe Girls School. Click HERE for full details and FREE PDF copy

title: Sheppy’s House of Cider
subtitle: Sheppy’s House of Cider is nestled between Taunton and Wellington and is the beating heart of Somerset’s oldest family-owned cider-making company. The Apple Bay Restaurant features artisan menus, the farm shop encompasses a butcher’s counter and deli, and the shop itself stocks the entire award-winning range of Sheppy’s premium craft Somerset cider.
bodyContent: Sheppy’s House of Cider Visitor Centre is nestled between Taunton and Wellington, surrounded by their 90 acres of traditional orchards, and is the beating heart of Somerset’s oldest family-owned cidermaking company. It was in 1816 that David Sheppy’s ancestors picked and pressed the first batch of apples on their Somerset farm and the rest, as they say, is history. Two centuries later, the Sheppy family are still championing the same methods to make their cider that were used generations ago, balanced with the very best of modern technology. From apple to bottle, their Master of Cider David Sheppy is involved with every drop of cider that bears the Sheppy's name. Experience, instinct and knowledge are key to all of Sheppy’s award-winning ciders. There is no secret recipe; it's simply about the experience and craftsmanship that has come from 200 years of knowledge and cider making, passed down through six generations of Masters of Cider. In 2016 the business took the next step in the Sheppy’s Cider evolution and opened the doors of the Sheppy’s House of Cider Visitor Centre, where local fans and tourists alike can discover new and award-winning food and drink while they explore the history of Sheppy’s Cider. The Apple Bay Bar & Restaurant features artisan menus serving only the freshest local ingredients, as well as a range of delicious café treats and coffees. The farm shop encompasses a butcher’s counter and deli, stocking a full range of handmade pastries, cakes and bakes alongside local cheese and meat from our in-house butchers. From March 2020 visitors will be able to once again join their weekend tours, where expert guides will offer a peek behind the scenes at one of the oldest cidermakers in the world. The guided tours include a visit to the orchards, the press house, the vat house and the Sheppy’s rural life museum, and culminates with a guided tasting of some of their favourite ciders. Tickets can be booked online via Eventbrite or bought in advance in the farm shop.
tagline: Sheppy’s House of Cider is nestled between Taunton and Wellington

subtitle: Revo Kitchen & Terrace is a new restaurant located on Weston-super-Mare’s seafront. We offer a relaxed environment, a place to enjoy a coffee and cake whilst looking out onto our breath-taking views or where you can come together with friends and tuck into delicious food & cocktails.
bodyContent: Revo Kitchen and Terrace, Weston super Mare - As a lot of our local customers know, our venue used to be the SeaQuarium, which closed in March of 2019. We began building Revo Kitchen in January 2021 and set to work on creating our vision of a relaxed atmosphere for people to enjoy live music, great coffee and impressive food. We are constantly looking to innovate our offerings based on the latest trends and ‘food frenzies’ that explode onto the scene. Our take on brunch is a careful combination of classic and unique dishes, all with a Revo twist. Our lunch & dinner menus are centered around our sourdough pizzas and freshly made burgers. In addition, we have a specials menu which varies depending on the fresh produce that is available. However, it does include some staples such fish and chips, along with our Revo chicken and waffles. We aim to cater to a wide range of dietary requirements, offering a variety of dairy free gluten free and vegan dishes on our menu.
tagline: Revo Kitchen & Terrace is a new restaurant located on Weston-super-Mare’s seafront.

title: The Bishop's Palace
subtitle: The Bishop’s Palace and Gardens in Wells has been home to the Bishops of Bath and Wells for over 800 years and this stunning medieval palace is now open for all to enjoy. It’s a great family day out in Somerset with a full programme of year-round events, free guided walks, open-air music and theatre, garden workshops and more and a slice of cake with afternoon tea at the ever-popular Bishop’s Table café is always welcome!
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Visit Highlights: There are 14 acres of outstanding RHS Partner gardens to explore (including the beautiful well pools from which the city takes its name), Dragon’s Lair play area, guided tours, children’s trails and workshops and a café with the best views in Wells! Multi media tours of the Palace building are also included with admission with the choice of an adult version or one tailored for a more family audience including quizzes, treasure hunts and talking Bishops from years gone by! Visitors are guided around the Palace buildings through five narrative themes using stories, music, imagery, quizzes and talking Bishops bringing stories of their tenure and legacy at the Palace to life in an interactive and engaging way. A year-round programme of themed family events is also included with admission including a Civil War Weekend; Archery, Vikings and more! Other events are ticketed separately including summer outdoor theatre; the Palace’s Garden Fair and History Live. The Bishop’s Palace dates from the early-thirteenth century when Bishop Jocelin Trotman received a crown licence to build a residence and deer park on land to the south of the Cathedral of St Andrew. Although home to the Bishop and other families, visitors can walk in the footsteps of past bishops through a number of rooms within the Palace. Visitors are also welcome to look around the Bishop’s private Chapel and explore the ruined Great Hall. The moat has been home to mute swans since the 1800s. The tradition of swans on the moat at The Bishop’s Palace in Wells is thought to go back to the 1850’s when it is likely that a Bishop’s daughter first taught the swans to ring a bell at the Gatehouse for food. We now have two swan bells – one just beneath the window on the left of the Gatehouse, the other to the right – both with a rope hanging down for the swans to pull. The Palace Gardens are open daily from 10am until 4pm in winter and 9.30am - 5.30pm in summer although there may be restricted access due to events and activities taking place (check the website for details). There are toilets on site. Guided tours are also included with Admission – check available times at the Ticket Office on arrival. Families: There’s so much for families to do at The Bishop’s Palace, whatever the weather. Little ones love to explore the gardens, trying to spot the swans and their cygnets; there are waterfalls and springs to see, trees to climb and places to hide. Children also love to explore the magical discovery area that is the Dragon’s Lair in a far corner of the Gardens! And throughout the school holidays, there are always plenty of events to keep families busy including crafting, outdoor gardening, family trails, storytelling and more. Refreshments: The Bishop’s Table café is open daily serving delicious, locally-sourced homemade food and some of the best coffee and cake you'll find in Wells. It’s the perfect place to meet friends for breakfast, lunch and afternoon teas or Sunday Lunches are now being served! Accessibility: From the main entrance of the Palace to the Palace building, around the gardens and to the café's dining area, there is level access. We have one lift to all floors of the Palace building. The outer gardens are accessible via a bridge which is 810mm wide. There are fully accessible toilets with level access within the Stableyard area and the Palace building. There are three spaces available on site for accessible parking, however, it is necessary to book these at least 48 hours before arrival via info@bishopspalace.org.uk or call 01749 988111.
tagline: The Bishop's Palace and Gardens, Wells, Somerset is a great family day out in Somerset.

Dogs are very welcome in the gardens of The Bishop’s Palace - we do ask that they are kept on a short lead. The only area that dogs are not allowed in is the Dragon’s Lair area in the Arboretum, as this is a safe space for children. Dogs may not enter the Palace buildings unless they are assistance dogs.

title: Tyntesfield, National Trust
subtitle: At its heart Tyntesfield is a Victorian country house and estate, which serves as a backdrop to the remarkable story of four generations of the Gibbs family. Their tale charts the accumulation of wealth from the guano trade, transformation of a Georgian house to a Victorian Gothic masterpiece and the collection of over 70,000 objects.
bodyContent: At its heart Tyntesfield is a Victorian country house and estate, which serves as a backdrop to the remarkable story of four generations of the Gibbs family. Their tale charts the accumulation of wealth from the guano trade, transformation of a Georgian house to a Victorian Gothic masterpiece and the collection of over 70,000 objects. Their achievements are celebrated through ornate Gothic carvings, flower-filled terraces and an expansive estate amid the Somerset countryside. For young explorers there are three play areas, a woodland adventure play and sculpture trail, and seasonal family trails around the estate. There is also a packed activities programme including open air theatre, food and craft markets and living history. Eating and shopping: Home Farm visitor centre offers year-round homemade dishes using estate-grown ingredients and a shop with plant sales, and a second-hand bookshop. For light bites while exploring, try the Pavilion Café. Dogs: Dogs on short leads are welcome in specified areas of the Tyntesfield estate. There is a map at reception that you can take a picture of.
tagline: At its heart Tyntesfield is a Victorian country house and estate.

title: Victoria Art Gallery
subtitle: Opened in 1900, the Victoria Art Gallery boasts an outstanding collection of paintings, sculptures and decorative arts. The gallery is located in the centre of Bath, near the famous Pulteney Bridge. Entry to the permanent exhibitions is free.
bodyContent: Opened in 1900, the Victoria Art Gallery boasts an outstanding collection of paintings, sculptures and decorative arts. The gallery is located in the centre of Bath , near the famous Pulteney Bridge. Entry to the permanent exhibitions is free. You’ll see more than 1,500 artworks, including many by artists who have lived and worked in the Bath area, such as Thomas Gainsborough and Walter Sickert. The work on show spans the 15th century to the present day. In the 18th century Bath was an important centre for portrait painting, and in the 20th century it again became famous thanks to the innovative works being produced by artists at the renowned Bath Academy of Art at Corsham Court. Alongside the permanent collections, the Victoria Art Gallery also hosts an exciting programme of temporary exhibitions and events throughout the year. Please check the Victoria Art Gallery website for the latest information.
tagline: Opened in 1900, the Victoria Art Gallery boasts an outstanding collection.

title: Wells Cathedral
subtitle: Built between 1175 and 1490 Wells Cathedral in Somerset has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals”.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built between 1175 and 1490 Wells Cathedral has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals”. Set in the medieval heart of England’s smallest city, and an easy drive from Bristol, Bath and Cardiff, Wells is the earliest English Cathedral to be built in the Gothic style. The current building is a significant landmark in the South West of England, has an international reputation and is TripAdvisor ranked number one for things to do in Wells and in Somerset. Wells Cathedral has unique features that separate it from other English cathedrals including its iconic West Front and the beautiful ‘scissor arches’ supporting the central tower, as well as one of the largest collections of historic stained glass in the country. The Cathedral also boasts the famous Wells Clock (which is considered to be the second oldest clock mechanism in Great Britain), the fascinating octagonal Chapter House and one of only four chained libraries in the UK. Wells Cathedral welcomes thousands of visitors each year who join in with regular daily services and events or who come simply to enjoy the calm and hospitality of this wonderful and holy place. Stay, if you can, for Evensong with the Cathedral’s world renowned choir (term times); a peaceful and moving end to your day. Tours: Discover hidden spaces and chambers, explore the south transept roof space and marvel at the nave from a very different perspective via the Cathedral's popular and longer High Parts tours which can be pre-booked via the website at www.wellscathedral.org.uk/visit/tours . The Cathedral runs complimentary ground floor tours daily (Monday-Saturday) and tickets include access to an audio tour. Guided tours for group visits can also be pre-booked via the Visits team at visits@wellscathedral.org.uk Families When term breaks up the Cathedral offers creative workshops for children accompanied by their parents or guardians. We also provide free children explorer backpacks which are available free of charge on arrival and which help children to learn about the main highlights and history of the Cathedral. Group Visits: The group rate (+10) for pre booked self guided visits is £10 and £12 to include a highlights tour. Unreserved groups are charged the standard on the door price of £14. For more information, and to book, please email visits@wellscathedral.org.uk Vicars’ Close: Adjoining the Cathedral is Vicars’ Close, believed to be the only complete medieval street left in England. Vicars’ Close was designed to provide accommodation for the Vicars Choral, who sing the daily services, and this is still the case today. This centuries-old tradition is unique and a much valued part of the continuing life of Wells Cathedral. The medieval windows of the houses and the garden archways seem to have survived more or less intact until the early nineteenth century, and even now a few still exist. Make a Day of It A warm welcome awaits you at our Cathedral shop which stocks a wide range of unique mementoes and gifts. The Loft at Wells Cathedral café is also open daily for coffee, delicious home-made lunches and afternoon teas http://www.wellscathedral.org.uk
tagline: Wells Cathedral in Somerset has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals".

title: ChalkUp!
subtitle: Our bouldering wall, established in 2023, was designed to create a fantastic space for visitors to Somerset to explore bouldering. Be it a rainy day out with the kids, relaxing with a coffee while others do the hard climbing, or wanting to develop a newly-found skill in climbing, we have something for everyone.
bodyContent: Situated between Bridwater and Minehead by a rural village, with free parking, ChalkUp! is the ultimate way to spend a day when on holiday with kids without the need to go anywhere near a big city! We welcome anyone to this facility who is interested in giving it a go. This could be to try something new, to keep the kids occupied for the afternoon, for serious boulderers, or for outdoor climbers to be ready for a summer of climbing. No experience necessary; we provide climbing shoes; no need to book a time slot; you can choose to register online in advance or just turn up and register at the desk. No time limit to your climbing session so feel free to take breaks and enjoy a coffee and cake before getting back on the wall. If it’s a sunny day, why not take your coffee to our outdoor picnic area to enjoy the restful views during those must-have rest periods? Bouldering coaching is available on request, just ask our super-helpful staff. We also provide staffed kids’ parties with games and supervision all taken care of and a dedicated kids’ wall for younger children. There is a full fitness facility available free of charge for adult climbers to warm up and warm down. Don’t fancy climbing but want a great workout while on holiday…..we also provide top notch functional fitness classes and use of our wide ranging open gym facilities on a drop in basis. We hope to see you at the wall in the very near future!

title: Blenheim Gardens
subtitle: Minehead premier gardens just off the town centre and a few minutes’ walk from the sea front and the harbour
bodyContent: Blenheim Gardens (maintained and run by Somerset West and Taunton council) is ideally situated in the centre of Minehead and covers nearly 2.5 hectares of parkland. Created in the 1920's it is now a mature, attractive and sheltered haven, popular with residents and visitors. The park provides spring and summer bedding displays, a wide range of trees, shrubs and perennials which thrive in the mild seaside climate. The flower beds and shrub areas are framed by lawns. The park boasts a bandstand for summer weekend concerts/brass bands. There is an 18-hole putting green but currently there is no formal play provision for children. The Gardens contain female, male and disabled toilets maintained and run by Minehead Town Council. There are several access points into the Gardens (from North Road, Blenheim Road and via a footpath from The Avenue) and a public car park with 62 spaces on the eastern boundary accessible from North Road.

title: Glastonbury Tor, National Trust
subtitle: Glastonbury Tor is a well-loved Somerset landmark associated with myths and legends, but it is also a place where children can run about and have fun. Fields at the foot of the Tor are good for games or you could play at the top in the ruined tower.
bodyContent: Prominent hill overlooking the Isle of Avalon, Glastonbury and Somerset. This iconic and evocative landmark offers magnificent views of the Somerset Levels , Dorset, Wiltshire and Wales. Steeped in history and legend, excavations at the top of the Tor have revealed the plans of two superimposed churches of St Michael, of which only a 15th-century tower remains. Glastonbury Tor also has a grisly past. Abbot Richard Whiting was executed here in 1549 on the orders of Thomas Cromwell, the first Earl of Essex. Glastonbury Tor is known as being one of the most spiritual sites in the country. Its pagan beliefs are still very much celebrated. It’s a beautiful place to walk, unwind and relax.
tagline: Glastonbury Tor is a well-loved Somerset landmark associated with myths and legends.

title: The Cheese and Grain
subtitle: The Cheese and Grain is a not-for-profit, member owned social enterprise and also a registered charity. Its main aim is to promote and boost Frome’s social, cultural and economic life.
bodyContent: The Cheese and Grain has an important role in Frome because we can host meetings, large (up to 500 people in the main hall) and small (up to about 30 people in our mezzanine). Every year we hold an annual member's meeting (the Annual General Meeting - the AGM). This is the meeting where the membership elects the Board of Trustees. There's plenty of time at the AGM to meet other members. Want to join now? Contact us and ask to be sent a membership form, or ask at the box office.

title: Club & Spa at DoubleTree by Hilton, Cadbury House
subtitle: Luxury spa hotel in North Somerset near Bristol with gourmet restaurant, DoubleTree by Hilton.
bodyContent: Set in the rolling North Somerset countryside, DoubleTree by Hilton, Cadbury House is one of the region's most popular destination spa hotels. Choose from a range of spa breaks and spa days, with numerous treatment rooms including a couple's suite for shared experiences. The treatment menu covers facials, massages, body wraps, hand and feet treatments, waxing and holistic therapies. Hotel guests also enjoy the 20m swimming pool, sauna, steam room, Jacuzzi and award-winning health club facilities, plus a Marco Pierre White restaurant serving brunch, lunch, dinner and afternoon tea. Recent improvements include an extended relaxation zone, outdoor sauna, hot tub and terrace. Facilities include ladies and men's saunas, an aromatherapy steam room, ladies-only steam room, gym, indoor pool and outdoor sun deck. On-site parking is available, and all major credit cards are accepted.

title: The Pillars Restaurant & Lounge Bar
subtitle: Experience and enjoy the sophisticated atmosphere that Street's newest venue now offers. Set over two floors with a secluded alfresco terrace, the ground floor bar offers an extensive range of wines, Champagnes, beers, as well its own brand of home brewed craft ale. Pillars has been sympathetically refurbished to acknowledge its entertainment history throughout the decades.
bodyContent: Welcome to The Pillars Restaurant and Lounge Bar - an exciting new venue in the heart of Street We're quickly earning a reputation for one of the best venues in town. Set over two floors with a secluded alfresco terrace, our ground floor bar offers an extensive range of wines, Champagnes, beers, ales and ciders as well as our own brand of home brewed craft ale. Experience and enjoy the sophisticated atmosphere that Street's newest venue now offers. The Pillars has been sympathetically refurbished to acknowledge its entertainment history throughout the decades. History of The Site The beginning The building was built in 1920 for two local businessmen, Mr Voaks, a local butcher and Mr Hecks, the forerunner of the local Hecks cider farm. The doors first opened on 15th January, 1921 as "The Playhouse Theatre." The Playhouse had four changing rooms, a 20ft deep stage and a 26ft wide proscenium. The original proscenium arch can still be seen today above what is now the piano deck. The arched ceiling is an original pressed tin design. The transition The Playhouse Theatre gave way to the Playhouse Cinema as technology evolved and the big curtains gave way to the big screen. The age of the cinema The building retained the name "The Playhouse" for 25 years until July 1946, when it was renamed "Maximes Cinema". For over 40 years, the building enjoyed life as a cinema with a variety of owners including Cornell Cinemas until the mid 50's and then Myles Byrne Cinemas. Maximes had one screen and 561 seats. Many local Somerset people will recall watching their first film on the big screen and many we are sure will recall magical and memorable romantic interludes within the many rows! The end of the big screen Maximes cinema played its last film on 15th September 1989. The start of the nightclub After the cinema closed, the seats were removed to create large open spaces. The screen was taken down to create more depth to the building and the next phase of the building's life was born into Maximes Nightclub. Maximes traded as a night club for many years. In 2001, the club embarked on a major refurbishment and was re-born as "Envy". Most residents of Somerset refer to the building now as the 'Envy building'. Envy enjoyed being a popular destination for thousands of party-goers hosting many themed nights and live music presentations. In June 2015, the owner Adam Fynn, announced he was to relocate and set about plans to sell the building and applied for planning permission to develop the site into residential properties. The end of the night club era On 11th December 2016, the then operators of Envy announced that the club would close at the end of the year and on 31st December 2016, Envy Nighclub opened and closed its doors for the very last time. The building sat dormant, empty and cold for nearly four months before going to auction on 27th April 2017. The building failed to sell at auction and the doors at Envy remained closed. A new beginning The building was finally purchased by us in June 2017. The new owner vowed to preserve the historic building and return it to back to its former glory as an entertainment venue for the mid Somerset arena. Throughout the remainder of 2017 and into the first half of 2018, plans were made and relevant planning permissions granted to commence the transformation of the building into the Loft. Throughout the re-development of the site, we have been sympathetic to the buildings unique history as an entertainment venue. We have combined all its past into the future, with food, drink, entertainment and music, all under one roof! We are very proud of the achievements and of the building. We do hope that you enjoy your experience here and look forward to welcoming you back to Pillars again soon. The Management Facilities include: Facilities : Unrivalled Grill Menu Al fresco dining area Regular Live Music & Entertainment Our own craft ales and beers Over 45 wines from around the world Available for private hire Wedding Receptions Unrivalled Cocktail & Gin Bar Market Fresh Daily Food Christmas Parties Christenings Large Dance Floor
tagline: The Pillars Restaurant and Lounge Bar is an exciting venue in the heart of Street.

title: Faust Comes to Life with New Live Soundtrack for the next Wellington Film Festival
subtitle: As part of the Wellington Film Festival 2025, a special screening of F.W. Murnau’s 1926 masterpiece Faust will take place at St John’s Church, Wellington.
bodyContent: A chilling classic of silent cinema will return to the screen with a powerful new sound this Autumn. As part of the Wellington Film Festival 2025 , a special screening of F.W. Murnau’s 1926 masterpiece Faust will take place at St John ’ s Church, Wellington, Somerset on Friday 3rd October 2025 , accompanied by a newly commissioned live soundtrack performed in the church’s evocative setting. This one-night-only event invites audiences to experience Murnau’s iconic vision of temptation and redemption with an original live score, composed and performed by Aidan Steele and Ruby Cox, blending traditional instrumentation such as Chinese folk instruments and guitars with atmospheric synthesiser elements. Devon-based Aidan and Ruby co-wrote the new score whilst studying composition for film at Leeds Conservatoire of Music. Aidan said ”We chose Faust because of its inspiring imagery. You ask yourself how did they create this. Being able to amplify the melodrama really appealed to us. It’s rooted in folk lore so we’ve drawn on traditional folk songs for the harmonies - with a modern approach.” The historic architecture and acoustics of St John’s Church provide a perfect backdrop for this haunting reinterpretation of a silent-era classic and an unforgettable night where cinema, music, and architecture meet. The event is just one highlight in the upcoming Wellington Film Festival , which takes place from October 3rd to 5th 2025, celebrating the power of cinema in unexpected spaces as well as the wonderful Wellesley Cinema, Wellington Arts Centre and Wellington School. The full programme will be announced next month and tickets go on sale August 1st 2025. Follow the festival on Facebook and Instagram to stay up to date with the latest announcements or visit www.wellingtonfilmfestival.org.uk to subscribe to their site newsletter.

title: Southern Sinfonia launches new season and announces residency at Wellington School
subtitle: Southern Sinfonia, the South West’s only professional orchestra, opens its 2025–26 season with a concert at Wellington School’s Great Hall on Friday 14 November at 7pm.
bodyContent: Southern Sinfonia, the South West’s only professional orchestra, opens its 2025–26 season with a concert at Wellington School’s Great Hall on Friday 14 November at 7pm . The concert also marks the first appearance of the orchestra’s new Music Director, John Warner , and the start of a major new partnership between Southern Sinfonia and Wellington School. The programme brings together Mendelssohn’s Hebrides Overture , Mozart’s effervescent Figaro Overture, Haydn’s grand London Symphony (No. 104), and Mozart’s Piano Concerto No. 23. The soloist is Hannah Yap , winner of Taunton Young Musician of the Year , performing with Southern Sinfonia for the first time. The concert launches a new educational residency at Wellington School , through which Southern Sinfonia will offer side-by-side opportunities for young musicians, chamber music and conducting masterclasses, composition workshops, early years projects and more. The residency aims to benefit not only Wellington’s pupils but also students from state schools and across the wider Somerset and Devon communities. Commenting on the residency, John Warner said: “It’s a real privilege to begin my tenure with Southern Sinfonia in Somerset, working with an orchestra I greatly admire and in partnership with a school that is so committed to music. Our aim is to inspire children of all backgrounds to experience orchestral music up-close, and to support the next generation of young musicians in the region.” Gareth Dayus-Jones, Director of Music at Wellington School, added: “We are thrilled to welcome Southern Sinfonia in this educational residency. This partnership will give our pupils - and those from local schools - extraordinary opportunities to learn directly from professional musicians. It is a truly exciting development for music in the area.” Tickets : available from www.southernsinfonia.org.uk www.trybooking.com/uk/FLPM

title: Shoscombe
subtitle: Shoscombe parish lies close to the south eastern boundary of Peasedown St John marked out by the bypass that encircles its southern edge.
bodyContent: Shoscombe parish lies close to the south eastern boundary of Peasedown St John marked out by the bypass that encircles its southern edge. Shoscombe Parish is made up of 8 small hamlets set in this peaceful, rural part of Somerset, and yet only 7 miles from the World Heritage city of Bath . The hamlets are Shoscombe village, Shoscombe Vale, Paglinch, Shoscombe Halt, Single Hill, Stony Littleton, White Hill and Double Hill The population is less than 500 The community values this rural landscape in which we live, and it is our determination to protect it for what it offers, by way of its diverse, and sometimes quite rare examples of wildlife, - for us, and for the visitors who come here.

title: Bruton
subtitle: Bruton is a bit of a one off, even more so than every Somerset town. Miles from anywhere, it’s a tiny and intense place, with shops, houses and chapels crowded close together even though it stands in the middle of tracts of rolling hills, and this gives it a very special character.
bodyContent: Things to do in Bruton, Somerset - In Bruton Arts and crafts flourish here in terraced streets of historic houses, and it’s one of Somerset’s local centres of creativity, punching far above its weight. It’s also a great town for exploring. The name refers to the River Brue, which flowed dramatically fast through this hill country, and often flooded the town. Follow any of the alleys which lead behind the houses, and you’ll see the now tamed and picturesque river winding through a deceptively deep valley in the heart of the town. In medieval times Bruton Abbey was one of the great religious houses of Somerset, and the town owes its success to that. While the skyline of Glastonbury is dominated by the Tor , Bruton has its famous dovecote. Built in the C16, catering for over 200 pigeons, and now managed by the National Trust, it’s visible from everywhere in the town on a neighbouring hilltop, and is the best place from which to view the town. Bruton is surprisingly cosmopolitan because it’s easily reached from London, by rail ( Castle Cary station) and from the A303. As well as all the local artistic ventures, it now boasts the exciting new Hauser and Wirth gallery, ingeniously installed in a restored farm just outside the town, with constantly changing exhibitions. Apart from art, you could say that the main local industry is education. There are three highly regarded boarding schools within the town: Kings School, Sexey’s School, and Bruton School for Girls. These, together with the narrow, closely built streets, give this tiny town a collegiate flavour.

title: Godminster Cheese
subtitle: Here at Godminster, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe. Our shop is open seven days a week and we have cheese available to sample every day.
bodyContent: Here at Godminster, Somerset, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe. Our shop is open seven days a week and we have cheese available to sample every day. There is free parking outside, so come and taste for yourself why Godminster has so many loyal friends around the world. We also offer fruit-infused vodka spirits, and over 18s are welcome to try those too. If you’re looking for a lovely foodie gift or a delicious souvenir of your trip to Somerset, come and take your pick from our range. Godminster’s Vintage Organic Cheddar is a deliciously soft and creamy cheddar matured for up to 12 months, at which point we select the best cheese to be made into one of our award-winning truckles. This sumptuous cheese is encased in the iconic burgundy wax to emphasise its pedigree and truly special status. The cheese is full bodied with a long, nutty, savoury bite. We also offer an Oak-Smoked Vintage Organic Cheddar, which sees the same top quality cheddar smoked over sustainably sourced oak chippings. The cheddar has a rich depth of flavour and the smokiness is evenly balanced with the acidity of the cheddar. Godminster Farm is set on the outskirts of the town of Bruton, Somerset, whose historic pedigree is recorded in the Doomsday Book of 1086. The Farm was registered as organic in 1999 and now boasts orchards with cider apples, peaches, nectarines and grapes, whilst keenly observing Soil Association and Government regulations relating to animal husbandry and the environmentally varied approach to business. The farm boasts a herb garden that enhances the natural remedies used to treat cows on the farm, 15 ponds supporting bio-diversity, and reeds which filter ground water. 25,000 broadleaf trees have been planted at the Farm since owner Richard Hollingbery took over, fostering diverse habitats and encouraging increases in the wildlife population. The cows at Godminster Farm, Somerset enjoy a simple and wholesome life. Richard sees them as the foundations for a truly holistic approach to his business, with the Farm’s milk turned into Godminster Vintage Organic Cheddar. Our mantra is "Nature repays those who treat her kindly," and that ethos runs across the business. Can’t make it to Bruton this time? Visit our website www.godminster.com let’s be friends on social media – we’re on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and Pinterest.
tagline: Here at Godminster, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe.

title: BACKWELL HOUSE HOTEL
subtitle: Backwell House Hotel is a beautiful, luxury Georgian country house in North Somerset with close links to Bristol Airport, trains stations and Bristol City Centre.
bodyContent: Backwell House Hotel is a beautiful, luxury Georgian country house in North Somerset with close links to Bristol Airport, trains stations and Bristol City Centre. We’re nestled within a backdrop of leafy meadow and rolling hills that gives our little touch of Eden a truly tranquil experience. It makes us ideal as a Wedding venue, we can become private for parties or include an entire host of guest speakers for business functions and industry events. We have 9 luxurious, double bedrooms, all classic, boutique stye interiors with their own en-suites and breakfast included, an award winning restaurant, bar and gardens. Backwell House was originally built by a prominent lawyer, Thomas Keedwell around 1813 with an estate of some 120 acres. Since this time it has been the residence of some notable people throughout it’s history. A year after being finished, the house was bought by the Sparrow family, and used as a rental property for different people for many years. In 1861 a family called the Robinson’s took over residency of the house. The six sons were keen cricketers and in 1878, the eldest son, Alfred Robinson, had an invitation to produce a cricket team for a game against West Town. He recruited five more of his cousins and this team became known as the Backwell House XI, made entirely of Robinson family members. The game was played on the August Bank Holiday and for the next 87 years until 1964 was always made up of descendants of the first Robinson family team. One of the most famous matches the team played was in August 1891. The Grace family had a few distinct ties to the Robinson family, one of the members, a notable W.G.Grace, had a few Robinsons as ‘brothers-in-law’. This led to a very famous match being played on the green area in front of Backwell House just beyond the ‘haw-haw’. The house has recently been updated and sympathetically restored to provide a chic interior, worthy of any boutique hotel. Many of the prominent surnames from the history of the house have encapsulated in time by being used in naming of the 9 bedroom suites. With stylish interiors and beautiful countryside surroundings, Backwell House Hotel is confidently the destination-du-jour for weekend getaways, a glass of fizz, family lunches, parties or afternoon teas.
tagline: Backwell House Hotel is a beautiful, luxury Georgian country house in North Somerset

title: The Old Farmhouse

bodyContent: The Old Farmhouse is a stunning Grade II listed former farmhouse, steeped in history, and only a short drive from Bristol. A rustic, family-friendly pub, the Old Farmhouse offers a great experience to all its guests, with a blend of contemporary and traditional ambience and a wide range of delicious homemade food. Our menu has been carefully developed so that every guest is spoilt for choice, with fresh and locally sourced ingredients where possible. And with its beautiful oak beams, stripped timber floor and wood burning stove, grown-up guests can too be sure of a memorable visit, whatever the occasion. We have a dedicated menu for children, as well as a selection of tempting desserts which are hard to resist. We’ve got everything covered from lunch to dinner and on Wednesdays and Sundays, we dish up our mouth-watering carvery with all the trimmings. We are delighted to offer a newly refurbished outside play area for our younger guests to enjoy. Our activity sheets and dedicated children’s menu are also popular favourites with the little ones. title: Sharpham Park
subtitle: Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels near Glastonbury.
bodyContent: Our organic farm and mill Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels near Glastonbury . It’s the home of Mulberry founder Roger Saul who moved from the world of fashion to food in 2004 when he launched the Sharpham Park brand from his organic farm. At Sharpham Park we grow organic spelt and stone grind it in the traditional way to preserve the delicious, nutty taste of the ancient grain. Today, we turned the milled spelt into flour, cereals and grains however history records show spelt has been grown for approximately 4,000 years in the area since the Bronze and Iron ages. The farm is also sustainably managed – the spelt fields have 4 metre margins and the hedgerows are cut every other year meaning wildlife such as wild deer, hare, bees and dormice are allowed to shelter and forage for food all year round. The ancient grain Spelt is an ancient grain which as has gained popularity in recent times because it’s an excellent source of dietary fibre and contains protein as well as some vitamins and minerals. It’s both easy to digest and leaves you feeling fuller for longer as well as being a good source of slow release energy; so much so the Roman Army called it their “marching grain”. Within working with Bowel Cancer UK Eating a high fibre diet is important in the fight against Bowel Cancer and we have teamed up with Bowel Cancer UK to spread this message. More than 40 top chefs have donated spelt recipes to the campaign and you can find these Great British Spelt Recipes on our website. Sharpham Pantry restaurant at Kilver Court Designer Village You can enjoy a range of spelt dishes in the Sharpham Pantry restaurant including our spelt flat breads and spelt bread and butter pudding. You can find the full range of our delicious spelt products in the Great House at Kilver Court Designer Village in Shepton Mallet. Come and browse our selection of cereals including flakes, muesli and porridge as well as our grains and four different types of flour made to meet all of your baking needs.
tagline: Sharpham Park is a 300 acre estate in the heart of the Somerset Levels.

bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. This walk takes you from the shingle beach at Dunster up to the magnificent medieval village with its yarn market and topped off with a castle. Originally “Dunn’s Torre”, a craggy fortification overlooking the Bristol Channel, the settlement was given by William the Conqueror gave to the powerful de Mohun family to build a castle to protect the coast. In 1375 the feudal barony was purchased by the Luttrell family who owned the Castle until 1976 when it was gifted to the National Trust. title: Hit the Streets of Clevedon for a healthy walk
subtitle: Walking groups are helping people across North Somerset stretch their legs, make new friends and feel healthier. Organised walks usually last about an hour but a new group has launched in Clevedon to offer residents a slightly more vigorous, 90-minute route. Life joined them to take in the sights around the town…
bodyContent: How to get there Start at map ref: ST 408710 Car: Parking is available at the former Morrisons supermarket, off Great Western Road - Route information Distance: just over 3 miles Difficulty: easy – a fairly flat route around the town Duration: allow up to 90 minutes Map: OS Explorer 153 Walking groups are helping people across North Somerset stretch their legs, make new friends and feel healthier. Organised walks usually last about an hour but a new group has launched in Clevedon to offer residents a slightly more vigorous, 90-minute route. Life joined them to take in the sights around the town… Start the walk in Queen’s Square, then turn left onto Old Church Road. Turn right onto Queen’s Road and continue uphill towards the crossroads at the end. Cross the road and turn left into Sunnyside Road. At the next crossroads turn right, which is still Sunnyside Road. From here you can go through a gate into Sunhill Park. Follow the path to your right, through the trees, and then head towards Sunhill House. This is now Clevedon Community Centre after being bought by the people of the town in 1949. Go around the side of the building and exit through the car park onto Princes Road. Turn right onto this road, cross over, and then at the junction turn left into Linden Road, then right into Herbert Road. Go through a wooden gate into Herbert Gardens, which was donated to the people of Clevedon by the Elton family in 1865. Follow the path and you will pass a ruined stone structure, which formed part of Wycliffe Girls School. Click HERE for full details and FREE PDF copy

title: Yeovil
subtitle: Known as Ivell in Thomas Hardy’s Wessex, Yeovil is mentioned in the Domesday Book as a thriving market community and is still a country town at heart surrounded by beautiful countryside. An important centre for the leather industry in the 19th century, the town is famous for its glove-making with its football club nick-named the Glovers and for making helicopters. It has numerous shops, a country park, theatre and entertainment centre. Settled in ancient times on a major Roman route through the
bodyContent: Its strategic position on the Fosse Way (now A37) between Dorchester and Ilchester was vital to the Romans, and makes it easy to reach for you. The name just means ‘town on the river’, which goes for most places round here, but no two Somerset towns are alike, and you’ll find that its character is unique. Throughout Saxon and medieval times the town continued to thrive. A market charter from King John, who took a big interest in Somerset, guaranteed its status as the local farming centre. While most Somerset towns surrounded by upland grazing went in for wool, Yeovil developed the speciality of glove making, and the name still survives in the nickname of ‘giant killers’ Yeovil Football Club – the glovers. These days the gloves are off, and you can’t buy a pair made in the town. We can probably fix you up with a helicopter or two, as military equipment is the town’s biggest export, and Leonardo Helicopters the biggest employer. Yeovil is one of these towns which is much bigger than it appears. You can ramble for what seems like miles through the historic centre, built around the noble C14 church of St John the Baptist, passing many fine old buildings, and not passing up many shopping opportunities. There’s a theatre, all sorts of arts and crafts, and the famous football club. If you remember Stephen Potter’s Lifemanship books from the 1950s, they’re based on Yeovil, which Thomas Hardy had previously recreated as Ivell. These days Yeovil only has two railway stations, a comedown from its original four, but it’s on the A37 and A30, a stone’s throw from the A303. title: The Yarn Market Hotel
subtitle: Ideally located in the centre of the medieval village of Dunster. The hotel is two and half hours via the A39 from the M5 - but is ten minutes away from the West Somerset Railway England's longest heritage railway. With Minehead 20 minutes away there are all the major facilities you need.
bodyContent: The Yarn Market Hotel in Dunster is ideally located in the centre of Dunster, one of the most perfectly preserved medieval villages in England, and the gateway to Exmoor National Park. The magnificent Dunster Castle is at the end of the street and the West Somerset Railway runs close by. There are many themed breaks on offer throughout the year, and the area is perfect for those who enjoy outdoor activities or just a relaxing break. For walkers the hotel has excellent facilities including a boot and drying room, and maps are readily available combined with local knowledge to help you with your walks. Most of the bedrooms have either a view over the village or the surrounding countryside. Pets are most welcome at the hotel in the dog-friendly rooms. The restaurant opens daily for dinner, reservations are advisable.

title: The Beachcomber, Brean
subtitle: The Beachcomber is a fantastic pub, restaurant and free entertainment venue in Brean. There is a family restaurant, Cabaret Bar and children's entertainment room.
bodyContent: The Beachcomber is a fantastic pub, restaurant and free entertainment venue in Brean. There is a family restaurant, large beer garden, outdoor play area and two modern entertainment rooms - The Cabaret Bar and The Lounge. The Beachcomber menu includes pub classics, burgers and pizzas. Our legendary Sunday carvery is served all day 12 - 8pm (April - October). The Beachcomber regularly hosts a variety of entertainment including family shows, party bands, tribute and speciality acts, followed by a lively late night disco. Check out the Entertainment Diary on our website www.warrenfarm.co.uk ! The venue is open to the public with free entry and free parking. Free wifi is available to use. Open seasonally (end of March – October) every day from 12 noon ‘til late. See website for winter opening hours.
tagline: The Beachcomber is a fantastic pub, restaurant and free entertainment venue in Brean.
