title: Hope Farm Cottages
subtitle: Self catering cottages in a queit setting near Brean. Berrow and weston super mare in Somerset. Short holiday breaks.
bodyContent: Very close to the Somerset coast but surrounded by the beautiful West Country countryside you will find Hope Farm's 4 luxury cottages. The beaches of Brean & Weston Super Mare are minutes drives away and there are a vast array of day trips to surrounding attractions, villages and countryside to keep everyone occupied. Each ground floor self catering cottage is on the edge of a beautiful lawned courtyard with open fields behind. Each has 2 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms and are easily accessible for those that have special requirements. Outside there are picnic tables and deckchairs for those lazy days and Summer evenings. Each cottage has off road, private and security lit parking spaces for 2 vehicles. Hope Farm has a wealth of facilities including a games room, outdoor children's play ground, laundry room and covered storage for bikes or trailers. And if you dont fancy driving there is a bus stop right at the gate to Weston Super Mare, Burnham on Sea , Taunton & Bristol. We can accommodate most requests so do call us to discuss to make your break perfect.
tagline: Self catering cottages in a queit setting near Brean. Berrow and weston super mare in Somerset.

title: Hardy House
subtitle: Set above Frome, the house is an eight-minute walk along the riverbank to the beautiful artisan centre. The split-level guest annexe has two south-facing double bedrooms and a sitting room with dining/work table, a bathroom and separate loo. Downstairs is a small kitchen. The garden wraps around the house.
bodyContent: Set above Frome, the house is an eight-minute walk along the riverbank to the beautiful artisan centre. The split-level guest annexe has two south-facing double bedrooms and a sitting room with dining/work table, a bathroom and separate loo. Downstairs is a small kitchen. There is a single sofa bed in the sitting room for families whose children don’t wish to share the double bed in the second double bedroom. The garden wraps around the house and there is an area of the terrace/patio which is just for our annexe guests, complete with table and chairs. Dogs can roam the whole garden but it is not suitable for small children as the house is set into the hillside. The property is a short drive from some lovely walks and makes an ideal retreat both for a family trip or a romantic break. The annexe was the original 1940s house and has its own entrance, and we live in the extension that was added on seven years ago. Please note that your space is right next to ours, although there are double doors between the two parts of the house.

title: Friary Drinks
subtitle: Here at Friary, we're passionate about making the best artisan spirits, from our botanical gins to our fruit liqueurs. Whether it's our gins, rums, vodkas, our drinks are great for sharing, as a treat for yourself, or given as gifts for a loved one.
bodyContent: Here at Friary, we're passionate about making the best artisan spirits, from our botanical gins to our fruit liqueurs. Every batch is lovingly created and bottled here in Somerset by my sister Hannah, our mistress distiller. Hannah learnt her trade from our dad Ern who started Friary back in 1995, making-up bottles of his legendary sloe gin and cherry brandy, and taking them to local farmers markets in the boot of his old Ford Granada. After a lifetime working for big-name drinks companies, dad was devoted to using the best ingredients, to make delicious drinks for happy customers. While Friary has grown a little since bottles were rattling around in the back of dad's old car, our commitment to creating outstanding drinks for happy customers remains at the heart of everything we do. Whether it's our gins, rums, vodkas, or even Dad's traditional recipes from those very first markets, our drinks are great for sharing, as a treat for yourself, or given as gifts for a loved one.
tagline: Here at Friary, we're passionate about making the best artisan spirits

title: Choc et al
subtitle: Chocolate shop with delicious thick shakes and hot chocolates.
bodyContent: ‘Choc et al’ is a family run business specialising in handmade chocolates. At our shop in Frome, Somerset, near Bath, wonderful chocolate flavours are created, and also sourced from local chocolatiers. We believe that eating chocolate is an experience to be savoured and would like to take you on a journey of discovery to appreciate the diversity of flavours that can be developed from the amazing cocoa bean. And now you can indulge in a delicious hot chocolate or thick shake as you browse around our shop. We also offer an inhouse ‘Chocolate Workshop/Party’ for groups of all ages where you can learn the art of chocolate crafting and take home your handmade products.

title: The Whittox Gallery
subtitle: A unique art gallery and gift shop, showcasing curated work by contemporary artists and independent makers. Both are located at RISE a lovingly restored church found in the heart of Frome.
bodyContent: The Whittox Gallery is a contemporary art gallery showcasing the finest contemporary professional artists and designers. Located within RISE, a beautifully restored church dating back to the early 1800s. The Gallery is a bright and innovative elevated art space overlooking the Rye Bakery café. The gallery boasts carefully curated work from cutting-edge artists, and for the past five years, has established the gallery's reputation for exhibiting the highest standard of works. Each show is expertly curated in-house by Sarah Robson. Sourcing local and national artists and designers from all different mediums and styles, Sarah’s previous background in the fashion and textile design industry and eye for detail and colour, ensures each collection promises to inspire and excite visitors to the unique gallery setting, while also complimenting the historic and architectural features of the building. Open to the public 5 days a week and all exhibitions are free to attend. Visitors are welcome to explore the gallery and the innovative works of art throughout the year.

title: The Yarn Market Hotel
subtitle: Ideally located in the centre of the medieval village of Dunster. The hotel is two and half hours via the A39 from the M5 - but is ten minutes away from the West Somerset Railway England's longest heritage railway. With Minehead 20 minutes away there are all the major facilities you need.
bodyContent: The Yarn Market Hotel in Dunster is ideally located in the centre of Dunster, one of the most perfectly preserved medieval villages in England, and the gateway to Exmoor National Park. The magnificent Dunster Castle is at the end of the street and the West Somerset Railway runs close by. There are many themed breaks on offer throughout the year, and the area is perfect for those who enjoy outdoor activities or just a relaxing break. For walkers the hotel has excellent facilities including a boot and drying room, and maps are readily available combined with local knowledge to help you with your walks. Most of the bedrooms have either a view over the village or the surrounding countryside. Pets are most welcome at the hotel in the dog-friendly rooms. The restaurant opens daily for dinner, reservations are advisable.
tagline: Our Hotel is situated in the beautiful Village of Dunster, within the Exmoor National Park.

title: The Railway Inn
subtitle: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you. Treat yourself to a delicious meal in our restaurant, have a bar snack in our cosy bar, or simply enjoy a pint of Thatchers Somerset Cider.
bodyContent: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you. Treat yourself to a delicious meal in our restaurant, have a bar snack in our cosy bar, or simply enjoy a pint of Thatchers Somerset Cider . The food we proudly serve features regional and seasonal ingredients from local producers, with a strong emphasis on great quality, great taste and sensible prices. Our drinks menu is carefully chosen, with of course the full range of ciders from Thatchers; beers, wines and soft drinks. Our team of enthusiastic front of house staff love to share their knowledge and appetite for products with guests, and are proud to go that extra mile in making visits a memorable one. The Railway Inn has been at the hub of Sandford village for over 140 years. As a reminder of its long tradition, the original signals from the old Sandford railway line take pride of place outside, together with two authentic oak vats. The Railway Inn Cider House and Kitchen is decorated with artefacts and pictures reflecting the cidermaking heritage of Thatchers. Keen to represent local craftsmanship at its best, the bar and restaurant has been given extra special interest with hand carvings in English oak describing the story of the cidermaking year. A short walk along the road and you’ll come to the Thatchers Cider Shop . Here the shelves are packed with our ciders, alongside produce such as local cheeses and chutneys, and gifts including books and clothing. Our draught ciders are available straight from the barrel so you can try before you buy. Please call the Railway Inn on 01934 611518, or book online at www.therailwayinn.com
tagline: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you.

title: Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Mendip Activity Centre is the ultimate outdoor adventure playground in Somerset. They’ve been delivering adventurous outdoor activities for nearly 40 years, growing from humble beginnings to the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West!
bodyContent: It’s Time for Adventure with Mendip Activity Centre! Nestled in 250 acres of ancient woodland in the Mendip Hills National Landscape, Mendip Activity Centre is the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West. Just 20 minutes from Weston-super-Mare and Cheddar and open year-round, Mendip have been delivering Adventure, Learning and Training for individuals, families, schools, and groups since 1987. Activities available include: · Air Rifle · Tobogganing · Archery · Skiing · Snowboarding · Frisbee Golf · Kayaking · Nerf & Gel Battles · Caving · Paddle Boarding · Rock Climbing · Axe Throwing · ArcheryActive · Abseiling · Canoeing Come for the day or stay longer. In summer, pitch your tent at the award-winning Mendip Basecamp (link to https://mendipbasecamp.com/), a family adventure campsite awarded second at the Visit England Awards 2025. Pitch where you like, check out when it suits, camp fires encouraged, dogs welcome and endless adventure is on offer! Adventure for Everyone Mendip is more than just activities. It’s a place to switch off from screens, reconnect with nature, and each other. Whether you're learning something new, developing an existing skill or simply having fun outside, you’ll leave with muddy boots and big smiles. We believe in adventure for everyone. Many of our activities are adaptable for additional needs, and our friendly team will work with you to make it happen Refuel at the Alpine Lounge Overlooking the Ski Slope, the Alpine Lounge café serves pizzas, paninis, coffee and cake with stunning views- perfect for après-adventure refreshments

title: Monthly Wednesday Matinees
subtitle: The Princess Theatre & Arts Centre is excited to launch its monthly Wednesday matinees. We will screen well-loved classic films at the venue on the first Wednesday of every month at 2pm from February.
bodyContent: Tickets, priced £5, are available to buy on the website. The Princess is also introducing £10 tickets to include the film and lunch. You will be able to choose from Hellend’s Kitchen Small Main Menu Meals and your choice of hot drink. Starting with Breakfast and Tiffany’s on Wednesday February 2 nd at 2pm, Casablanca on Wednesday 2 nd March and Some Like It Hot on Wednesday 6 th April. To book seats for Breakfast at Tiffany’s, visit https://www.theprincesstheatre.co.uk/events/film-breakfast-at-tiffanys/ To book seats for Casablanca, visit https://www.theprincesstheatre.co.uk/events/film-casablanca/ To book seats for Some Like It Hot, visit https://www.theprincesstheatre.co.uk/events/film-some-like-it-hot/ Film and Lunch booking only available up to 48 hours prior to the showing. Table bookings will be made for 12pm on the day of the matinee. The Princess is also delighted to announce this season’s National Theatre screenings; from London’s West End Tom Stoppard’s Olivier Award-winning play Leopoldstadt, screening on Saturday February 5 th at 7pm. At the beginning of the 20th century, Leopoldstadt was the old, crowded Jewish quarter of Vienna, Austria. But Hermann Merz, a factory owner and baptised Jew now married to Catholic Gretl, has moved up in the world. We follow his family’s story across half a century, passing through the convulsions of war, revolution, impoverishment, annexation by Nazi Germany and the Holocaust. A company of 40 actors represent each generation of the family in this epic, but intimate play.

subtitle: Small campsite near Burnham on Sea and Brean in Somerset. Static caravans.
bodyContent: Westhill Farm Caravan Park is almost eighty acres of tranquility on the banks of the river Brue. This static, touring caravan and tenting holiday park is set amongst willow trees, landscaped grounds and farmland in a quiet, peaceful area of the Somerset countryside. We currently have 46 privately owned static caravans, 10 seasonal touring pitches, a commercial and 5CL touring site for all to enjoy. Our touring site caters for long or short stays and one night stop overs. Small laundry on site and owners are resident in the farmhouse. We welcome children and pets. Excellent fishing available on our section of the River Brue. Just a few minutes drive from Burnham on Sea & Brean.

title: Clevedon Court, National Trust
subtitle: Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is a remarkable survival from the medieval period.
bodyContent: Clevedon Court in Clevedon, Somerset, National Trust property is an outstanding 14th-century manor house and 18th-century terraced garden Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is a remarkable survival from the medieval period. The house was purchased by Abraham Elton in 1709 and it is still the much-loved family home of his descendants today. Explore the striking display of Eltonware pottery and a fascinating collection of Nailsea glass.
tagline: Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is remarkable.

title: The Yarn Market Hotel
subtitle: Ideally located in the centre of the medieval village of Dunster. The hotel is two and half hours via the A39 from the M5 - but is ten minutes away from the West Somerset Railway England's longest heritage railway. With Minehead 20 minutes away there are all the major facilities you need.
bodyContent: The Yarn Market Hotel in Dunster is ideally located in the centre of Dunster, one of the most perfectly preserved medieval villages in England, and the gateway to Exmoor National Park. The magnificent Dunster Castle is at the end of the street and the West Somerset Railway runs close by. There are many themed breaks on offer throughout the year, and the area is perfect for those who enjoy outdoor activities or just a relaxing break. For walkers the hotel has excellent facilities including a boot and drying room, and maps are readily available combined with local knowledge to help you with your walks. Most of the bedrooms have either a view over the village or the surrounding countryside. Pets are most welcome at the hotel in the dog-friendly rooms. The restaurant opens daily for dinner, reservations are advisable.
tagline: Our Hotel is situated in the beautiful Village of Dunster, within the Exmoor National Park.

title: Dunster Circular
subtitle: This walk takes you from the shingle beach at Dunster up to the magnificent medieval village with its yarn market and topped off with a castle.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. This walk takes you from the shingle beach at Dunster up to the magnificent medieval village with its yarn market and topped off with a castle. Originally “Dunn’s Torre”, a craggy fortification overlooking the Bristol Channel, the settlement was given by William the Conqueror gave to the powerful de Mohun family to build a castle to protect the coast. In 1375 the feudal barony was purchased by the Luttrell family who owned the Castle until 1976 when it was gifted to the National Trust. Having explored the streets and shops, the walk takes you past the heritage railway station back to the beach along the riverside. Click here for more information
tagline: This walk takes you from the shingle beach at Dunster up to the magnificent medieval village.

title: Thatchers Cider
subtitle: For more than a hundred years, family-run Thatchers Cider has been quietly perfecting the magic that turns apples into cider.
bodyContent: For more than a hundred years, family-run Thatchers Cider has been quietly perfecting the magic that turns apples into cider. Here at Myrtle Farm in Sandford, each generation has passed on cider-making secrets, like encouraging bees to pollinate the apple blossom, or looking after the 150 year old oak vats where the cider matures. We lovingly craft a range of ciders but whichever you choose, they have all been made with the same care and attention, and with the same hands-on experience – we wouldn’t have it any other way. Nestled at the foot of the Mendip Hills , the Thatchers orchards are our pride and joy. With apples such as Dabinett, Somerset Redstreak and Porters Perfection, as well as some newer varieties such as Angela, Lizzie and Prince William, it’s here that the journey starts, inspired by the heritage and values of our company. Our flagship brand Thatchers Gold is a full flavoured, medium dry Somerset cider, with a wonderfully rich, golden colour. Thatchers Vintage is well balanced and mature, with a distinctive depth of character, while Thatchers Haze is a premium cloudy cider that has a crisp, sweet finish. We have recently introduced a new cider to our range, the gloriously pink Rosé, bursting with fruity apple flavours. Our other ciders include Thatchers Katy, Old Rascal and Green Goblin, together with our Stan’s Range of traditional ciders, such as Cheddar Valley, Trad. and Big Apple. Available on line and in our Cider Shop, Finally, holding down the fort at home, we have our award-winning Cider Barn range that’s exclusive to Myrtle Farm.that includes very special ciders such as Thatchers 458, Vilberie and Redstreak. You can buy all our ciders online at www.thatcherscider.co.uk Or visit our Cider Shop at Myrtle Farm. Here the shelves are packed with our ciders, alongside produce such as local cheeses and chutneys, and gifts including books and clothing. Our draught ciders are available straight from the barrel, so you can try before you buy. Why not book onto a tour of Myrtle Farm and see how we make our ciders. Visit www.thatcherscider.co.uk/visitus for more information. To book a tour of Myrtle Farm, please visit www.thatcherscider.co.uk
tagline: For more than a hundred years, family-run Thatchers Cider has been quietly perfecting cider.

title: Wells Cathedral
subtitle: Built between 1175 and 1490 Wells Cathedral in Somerset has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals”.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built between 1175 and 1490 Wells Cathedral has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals”. Set in the medieval heart of England’s smallest city, and an easy drive from Bristol, Bath and Cardiff, Wells is the earliest English Cathedral to be built in the Gothic style. The current building is a significant landmark in the South West of England, has an international reputation and is TripAdvisor ranked number one for things to do in Wells and in Somerset. Wells Cathedral has unique features that separate it from other English cathedrals including its iconic West Front and the beautiful ‘scissor arches’ supporting the central tower, as well as one of the largest collections of historic stained glass in the country. The Cathedral also boasts the famous Wells Clock (which is considered to be the second oldest clock mechanism in Great Britain), the fascinating octagonal Chapter House and one of only four chained libraries in the UK. Wells Cathedral welcomes thousands of visitors each year who join in with regular daily services and events or who come simply to enjoy the calm and hospitality of this wonderful and holy place. Stay, if you can, for Evensong with the Cathedral’s world renowned choir (term times); a peaceful and moving end to your day. Tours: Discover hidden spaces and chambers, explore the south transept roof space and marvel at the nave from a very different perspective via the Cathedral's popular and longer High Parts tours which can be pre-booked via the website at www.wellscathedral.org.uk/visit/tours . The Cathedral runs complimentary ground floor tours daily (Monday-Saturday) and tickets include access to an audio tour. Guided tours for group visits can also be pre-booked via the Visits team at visits@wellscathedral.org.uk Families When term breaks up the Cathedral offers creative workshops for children accompanied by their parents or guardians. We also provide free children explorer backpacks which are available free of charge on arrival and which help children to learn about the main highlights and history of the Cathedral. Group Visits: The group rate (+10) for pre booked self guided visits is £10 and £12 to include a highlights tour. Unreserved groups are charged the standard on the door price of £14. For more information, and to book, please email visits@wellscathedral.org.uk Vicars’ Close: Adjoining the Cathedral is Vicars’ Close, believed to be the only complete medieval street left in England. Vicars’ Close was designed to provide accommodation for the Vicars Choral, who sing the daily services, and this is still the case today. This centuries-old tradition is unique and a much valued part of the continuing life of Wells Cathedral. The medieval windows of the houses and the garden archways seem to have survived more or less intact until the early nineteenth century, and even now a few still exist. Make a Day of It A warm welcome awaits you at our Cathedral shop which stocks a wide range of unique mementoes and gifts. The Loft at Wells Cathedral café is also open daily for coffee, delicious home-made lunches and afternoon teas http://www.wellscathedral.org.uk
tagline: Wells Cathedral in Somerset has been described as “the most poetic of the English Cathedrals".

title: Glastonbury Tor, National Trust
subtitle: Glastonbury Tor is a well-loved Somerset landmark associated with myths and legends, but it is also a place where children can run about and have fun. Fields at the foot of the Tor are good for games or you could play at the top in the ruined tower.
bodyContent: Prominent hill overlooking the Isle of Avalon, Glastonbury and Somerset. This iconic and evocative landmark offers magnificent views of the Somerset Levels , Dorset, Wiltshire and Wales. Steeped in history and legend, excavations at the top of the Tor have revealed the plans of two superimposed churches of St Michael, of which only a 15th-century tower remains. Glastonbury Tor also has a grisly past. Abbot Richard Whiting was executed here in 1549 on the orders of Thomas Cromwell, the first Earl of Essex. Glastonbury Tor is known as being one of the most spiritual sites in the country. Its pagan beliefs are still very much celebrated. It’s a beautiful place to walk, unwind and relax.
tagline: Glastonbury Tor is a well-loved Somerset landmark associated with myths and legends.

title: Wookey Hole Caves & Attractions
subtitle: Wookey Hole Caves is a magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for all ages. It’s an experience millions of years in the making with plenty to do inside and out. Enjoy vintage penny arcades, museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, and of course the famous, beautiful caves.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Wookey Hole Caves and attractions lies In the heart of Somerset. A magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for the young and young at heart. When you visit Wookey Hole, you’ll enjoy an experience millions of years in the making. There is plenty to do inside and out, from vintage penny arcades to museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, to name but a few of the attractions. Not forgetting the breathtakingly beautiful caves, for which Wookey Hole is renowned. Your visit will take you through 8 chambers. Each with a unique beauty and story. You’ll also pass our cheese tunnel, home to the delicious Wookey Hole cheese. The cheese is not the only resident of the caves. Over the years, Wookey Hole has been home to giant hyenas, bears, Neanderthals, and many local people. It has even been a site of pagan and Roman worship. You’ll find Wookey Hole holds a surprise around every corner. You might even get to meet our most famous resident, the Witch of Wookey Hole. We have found she most likes to visit during school holidays! The world-famous Wookey Hole Circus School performs at Wookey Hole at weekends and in School Holidays. Every year over 250,000 people visit Wookey Hole and take-home cherished memories of a great day out. Whether it is your first time or your fiftieth, there is always something new to discover. We can’t wait to welcome you.
tagline: At Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions, Somerset, there’s always fun and adventure to be had.

title: Brothers Drinks
subtitle: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family, who have been making cider in Somerset since 1658.
bodyContent: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family, who have been making cider in Somerset since 1658. We first started selling our Pear Cider at the Glastonbury Festival in 1995 near what was then called the Jazz World Stage. These days it is called The West Holts Stage. Over the years, festival goers kept asking us if it was possible to get our drink when the festival was over and so we decided to market it to pubs and supermarkets. Now you can get it all over the country and at many festivals. We are independent, British and are passionate about what we do. Our free-spirited essence is upheld by approaching things with a unique perspective. Here at Brothers, we take our values and commitment to sustainability very seriously, but it’s something we haven’t really shouted about until now. We have zero to landfill, all our waste is segregated to optimise the opportunity of being recycled or reused. A massive solar panel system is now installed here at the cider mill, where it will directly supply the presses with clean energy and lastly, all our left-over fruit pomace is turned into energy which helps to heat the local swimming pool!

title: The Yarn Market Hotel
subtitle: Ideally located in the centre of the medieval village of Dunster. The hotel is two and half hours via the A39 from the M5 - but is ten minutes away from the West Somerset Railway England's longest heritage railway. With Minehead 20 minutes away there are all the major facilities you need.
bodyContent: The Yarn Market Hotel in Dunster is ideally located in the centre of Dunster, one of the most perfectly preserved medieval villages in England, and the gateway to Exmoor National Park. The magnificent Dunster Castle is at the end of the street and the West Somerset Railway runs close by. There are many themed breaks on offer throughout the year, and the area is perfect for those who enjoy outdoor activities or just a relaxing break. For walkers the hotel has excellent facilities including a boot and drying room, and maps are readily available combined with local knowledge to help you with your walks. Most of the bedrooms have either a view over the village or the surrounding countryside. Pets are most welcome at the hotel in the dog-friendly rooms. The restaurant opens daily for dinner, reservations are advisable.
tagline: Our Hotel is situated in the beautiful Village of Dunster, within the Exmoor National Park.

title: The Chalice Well
subtitle: Historical well with legends in Glastonbury, Somerset.Chalice Well at the foot of Glastonbury Tor.
bodyContent: Chalice Well is one of Britain's most ancient wells, nestling in the Vale of Avalon between the famous Glastonbury Tor and Chalice Hill. Surrounded by beautiful gardens and orchards it is a living sanctuary in which the visitor can experience the quiet healing of this sacred place. Over three acres of peace. For over two thousand years this has been a place where people have gathered to drink the waters and find solace, peace and inspiration. At present we work with the theme of 'Many Paths, One Source' to welcome all people of goodwill to the gardens throughout the year. We also mark 'the wheel of the year' at regular intervals with events of celebration, silence and meditation, and conversation. This includes an evening programme of music, poetry and performance throughout the summer months in our candlelit gardens.
tagline: Historical well with legends in Glastonbury, Somerset.Chalice Well at the foot of Glastonbury Tor.

title: Nunney Castle
subtitle: A small 14thC century moated castle, distinctively French in style.
bodyContent: The striking and picturesque moated castle of Nunney was built in the 1370's by Sir John de la Mere, a local knight who was beginning to enjoy royal favour. Extensively modernised in the late 16th century, the castle was held for the King during the Civil War, but quickly fell to Parliamentarian canon in 1645:not until Christmas Day 1910, however di the gun-damaged portion of the wall finally collapse.
tagline: A small 14thC century moated castle, distinctively French in style.

title: Middlewick Holiday Cottages
subtitle: Self catering cottages in Glastonbury. Perfect short break in Somerset with indoor pool.
bodyContent: A secluded holiday resort just minutes from Glastonbury town centre, with stunning views of Glastonbury Tor and the Mendip Hills. Set on 16 peaceful acres, The Middlewick offers self-catering accommodation in 10 cottages converted from original 17th-century farm buildings, 3 log cabins and 3 glamping pods. Our properties range from 1 to 5 bedrooms, offering plenty of choice for couples, families, friends and groups looking for country getaway. Many are dog friendly. We have a Café , Farm Shop and Spa on site – all of which are open to day visitors as well as guests staying with us. Our site, including our indoor heated pool and steam room, is powered by renewable energy, and Spa treatments take place in our cosy Shepherd’s Huts. Surrounded by apple orchards, this is a real escape to the Somerset countryside – with plenty of space to roam in the beauty of nature. Visitors can walk to Glastonbury Tor easily in under 30 minutes. There’s so much to explore nearby, with Glastonbury Tor, Chalice Well and Gardens, Glastonbury Abbey and Clark’s Village on our doorstep. Glastonbury is a unique market town bustling with unusual shops and alternative events. The Avalon Marshes Nature Reserve, Cathedral City of Wells and Cheddar Gorge are within easy driving distance from The Middlewick. title: Wellington Film Festival
subtitle: Wellington Film Festival returns this autumn with an exciting and eclectic programme set to entertain, engage, and inspire film lovers of all ages.
bodyContent: Wellington Film Festival returns this weekend with an exciting and eclectic programme set to entertain, engage, and inspire film lovers of all ages. Running from 3rd to 5th October, this year’s festival boasts an impressive line-up of screenings, live performances, workshops, and special events across the town. Chair of the Festival Steering Committee Sean Pringle Kosikowsky said: “This year’s programme is packed with unique experiences that bring our community together to celebrate the power of storytelling in all its forms. From classic films to grassroots documentaries, hands-on workshops to engaging talks, Wellington Film Festival has something for everyone.” Festival highlights include a spectacular screening of Murnau’s 1926 silent masterpiece Faust, accompanied by a live score blending guitar, synthesisers, and Chinese folk instruments within the stunning Grade I listed St John’s Church –promising a truly atmospheric experience. Comedy fans can revisit the timeless satire of Monty Python’s Life of Brian, while families can enjoy fantasy classics like Labyrinth and the feel-good musical Mamma Mia. For cinephiles and history buffs alike, a tribute to Buster Keaton will see a collection of his iconic short films screened on his 130th birthday at Brazier’s. A major festival highlight is the Q&A live online from Rome and screened direct into Wellington Arts Centre with Wellington Film Festival Patron and acclaimed actor James Purefoy, followed by a special screening of Fisherman’s Friends, complete with live sea shanties to set the mood. Celebrating nature and environmental storytelling, the festival presents Wilding and Our Town Plants Trees, alongside a special showcase of short films, featuring guest speaker and wildlife filmmaker Lisa Walters. Engaging the community further, the 48 Hour Film Challenge invites young filmmakers to create a short film in just two days, culminating in a gala screening of their efforts. Local creativity also takes the spotlight with Welcome to Wellington – an African Journey, a short documentary exploring the experiences of Wellington’s growing African community. Additional events include a film prosthetics demonstration in Wellington Park, a lively film quiz hosted by BBC Radio Somerset’s Simon Parkin, and a Q&A with Sharon Sheehan, director of the new feature Mary Anning and the Dinosaur Hunters. The festival will take up residency in the towns’ Pop-Up Shop from 29th September, serving as a hub for tickets, promotions, and hands-on activities including children’s mask-making workshops ahead of the Labyrinth screening. For full programme details, tickets, and information on how to participate in the 48 Hour Film Challenge, visit www.wellingtonfilmfestival.org .

title: Dunkerton and Tunley
subtitle: Situated on the northern slope of the valley of the Cam Brook, Dunkerton has been in existence for a thousand years or more.
bodyContent: Situated on the northern slope of the valley of the Cam Brook, Dunkerton has been in existence for a thousand years or more. It is mentioned in Domesday Book; its name derives from the Anglo-Saxon words Dun/Carn/Ton, signifying “the town of the cairn on the hill”, and this is a reference to a stone structure which long ago stood on Duncorne Hill about a mile towards the city of Bath. Nowadays the Parish of Dunkerton and Tunley has a population of a little over 400, living in about 220 households; these are mainly situated in the two principal settlements of Tunley and the village of Dunkerton itself, although there are other groups of houses in such locations as Withyditch and along the old Roman Fosse Way. It was once a thriving industrial community – there were several coalmines, and both the Somersetshire Coal Canal and the southern branch of the Bristol and North Somerset Railway passed through the parish. However, local industry withered away with the closure of the pits and the railway in the mid-twentieth century, and there is now little local employment, although the farming tradition continues, with several farms based in the parish. Neither Dunkerton nor Tunley has much of a village “core”. Dunkerton has a pleasant little church, dating from the 13th century, but no school, shop or public house, while Tunley has one excellent pub. There are three public halls, Dunkerton Parish Hall, Tunley Recreation Centre and the old Schoolroom at Withyditch. In addition, Dunkerton has a fine cricket ground and Tunley a well-patronised football pitch. The parish has the benefit of being set in very attractive and largely unspoiled countryside, as well as being on the Limestone Link public footpath and having some interesting archaeological, scientific and literary associations.

title: Coco Blue Boutique
subtitle: Coco Blue Boutique is an independent boutique featuring design-led clothing, footwear and accessory brands from Europe and beyond. We are known for sourcing niche labels which are little found in the UK - our buying takes us to Milan, Paris, London, Berlin and Copenhagen, in order to create a curated collection of easy to wear, quality and stylish pieces.
bodyContent: In 2006 Sarah and Kellie opened the doors of Coco Blue at the Riverside, Taunton. As sisters and young mums (with five children between us!) we decided to concentrate on everyday style with a luxe edge. They choose European labels crafted from only the finest fabrics, which are beautifully cut, and can be worn season after season. They believe in slow-fashion and supporting companies whose years of knowledge and experience allows them to produce beautiful, artisan pieces. They add to our portfolio consistently and one of the best parts of our jobs is finding labels that they truly believe in. They love nothing more than catching the early flight to Paris, never quite knowing what we will be bringing home! They hope to give every customer a true ‘Coco Blue’ experience - offering genuine and personal style advice to help you feel and look amazing. We are passionate about recreating this online, so please do introduce yourself and allow us to get to know you.
tagline: Boutique situated in Taunton's Independent Quarter.

title: Middlewick Holiday Cottages
subtitle: Self catering cottages in Glastonbury. Perfect short break in Somerset with indoor pool.
bodyContent: A secluded holiday resort just minutes from Glastonbury town centre, with stunning views of Glastonbury Tor and the Mendip Hills. Set on 16 peaceful acres, The Middlewick offers self-catering accommodation in 10 cottages converted from original 17th-century farm buildings, 3 log cabins and 3 glamping pods. Our properties range from 1 to 5 bedrooms, offering plenty of choice for couples, families, friends and groups looking for country getaway. Many are dog friendly. We have a Café , Farm Shop and Spa on site – all of which are open to day visitors as well as guests staying with us. Our site, including our indoor heated pool and steam room, is powered by renewable energy, and Spa treatments take place in our cosy Shepherd’s Huts. Surrounded by apple orchards, this is a real escape to the Somerset countryside – with plenty of space to roam in the beauty of nature. Visitors can walk to Glastonbury Tor easily in under 30 minutes. There’s so much to explore nearby, with Glastonbury Tor, Chalice Well and Gardens, Glastonbury Abbey and Clark’s Village on our doorstep. Glastonbury is a unique market town bustling with unusual shops and alternative events. The Avalon Marshes Nature Reserve, Cathedral City of Wells and Cheddar Gorge are within easy driving distance from The Middlewick. Somerset is known for its food, music and outstanding natural beauty – and this is the ideal base from which to explore the best of the county.

title: Somerset Farmers Market
subtitle: Somerset Farmers’ Markets has been organising farmers’ markets at locations in the county of Somerset for over 20 years!
bodyContent: Somerset Farmers’ Markets has been organising farmers’ markets at locations in the county of Somerset for over 20 years! Markets are held in pretty market squares, vibrant high streets and an indoor market hall. Each market venue provides local communities and visitors with a wide variety of fresh, high quality, locally produced food . In addition, the markets provide a great point for local businesses to make new connections and find suppliers. Find out more about Somerset Farmers' Markets We love Farmers’ Markets! As well as offering great tasting local produce from small, independent businesses, they provide a hub for the community to come together and bring to life High Streets and Market Squares. title: Wells Cathedral High Parts Tours
subtitle: Climb the spiral staircase to walk in the footsteps of Wells Cathedral masons with new behind-the-scenes tours of Wells Cathedral’s High Parts; one of the most memorable things to do in Wells!
bodyContent: Climb the spiral staircase to walk in the footsteps of Wells Cathedral masons with new behind-the-scenes tours of Wells Cathedral’s High Parts; one of the most memorable things to do in Wells ! - Discover hidden spaces, galleries and chambers, including behind the Wells clock - See one of only two surviving tracing floors in the country where masons drew templates on the floor - Walk along the singing gallery and learn about trumpet holes! - Explore the south transept roof space - And marvel at the nave from a very different perspective! (Note that the tour route does not take in the top of the tower). High Parts Tours take place regularly throughout the week; bookings can be made via the Cathedral's website up to 24 hours prior to the tour taking place. Want to make a last minute booking? Call us on 01749 672773 or ask at the Welcome desk on the day of your visit. The tour length is 1.5 hours. Tour and tea packages are also available. Who can book: The maximum number in any upper levels tour is 12 and no children under the age of 10 years are permitted on the tour. Children between the ages of 10 and 16 years must be accompanied by one adult for every two children, unless they are part of an organised youth group when at least two adults must be in attendance. Any visitors with a fear of heights or confined spaces and/in poor health should consider carefully their suitability for the tour. There are up to 250 steps, uneven floors, low ceilings and the narrowest point is just 60cm (2ft.) wide. The tour route does not include access to the top of the tower. Other Terms and Conditions of Booking do apply (see website for details). Where to meet your Guide: At the Donation Desk in the entrance of the Cathedral 15 minutes before your Tour begins. You will unfortunately not be able to join the Tour if you miss the start time. If you purchase a Tour and tea package, your Guide will indicate where to take your refreshments at the end of the Tour. www.wellscathedral.org.uk/visit/tours
tagline: Climb the spiral staircase to walk in the footsteps of Wells Cathedral masons.

title: Somerset Rural Life Museum
subtitle: Visitors to Somerset Rural Life Museum can explore rural life from the 1800s onwards and discover more about the county’s heritage including its landscape, food and farming, working life and rural crafts.
bodyContent: Visitors to Somerset Rural Life Museum can explore rural life from the 1800s onwards and discover more about the county’s heritage including its landscape, food and farming, working life and rural crafts. The museum tells the story of Somerset’s rich rural and social history. Visitors can enjoy the five Farmhouse Galleries which explore the themes of ‘Creating’, ‘Learning’, ‘Believing’, ‘Celebrating’ and ‘Remembering.’ In the large Farmyard Gallery the major themes are ‘Working Village’ and ‘Working the Land’. The magnificent 14th-century Abbey Barn remains the centrepiece of the site, providing a unique and remarkable setting for exhibitions and events. Outside spaces, including the Farmyard and the Orchard, contain sculpture and family trails that interpret the history of the site and its buildings. The Grain Store Café is open all year round at this family-friendly destination, offering high-quality locally-sourced food and drink. A programme of seasonal events take place throughout the year.
tagline: Visitors to Somerset Rural Life Museum can explore rural life from the 1800s onwards.

title: Sweets Tea Rooms
subtitle: Country cafe tea room near Wedmore & Glastonbury & Street, Somerset
bodyContent: A wonderfully deceptive yard leads you to one of Somerset's best kept secrets. Generous traditional food from pies to the best cakes & cream teas with a very warm welcome. Proper Somerset fayre that you won't find for miles around. Using quality local suppliers this is a little hideaway not to be missed. We are a regular cycling stop cafe and approved by the British Horse Society. In the Winter alongside the cosy cafe there is a woodburner in the cabin area. Perfect for dogs, walkers and cyclists. This is also the home of the Peat & Science Museum, a lifetime family collection of working the levels including WW1 bomber parts! title: Godminster Cheese
subtitle: Here at Godminster, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe. Our shop is open seven days a week and we have cheese available to sample every day.
bodyContent: Godminster, near Bruton, crafts award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe, plus an Oak-Smoked variety, both matured in iconic burgundy wax. Sample daily at our shop, open seven days a week with free parking. Over 18s can also try our fruit-infused vodkas. Set on an organic farm rich in biodiversity, Godminster makes for a perfect foodie gift or Somerset souvenir. Visit us or find Godminster online and on social media.
tagline: Here at Godminster, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe.

title: Luce Loves Flowers
subtitle: Rustic & wild country style florist for weddings, funerals and everyday florals.
bodyContent: Rustic & wild country style florist for weddings, funerals and everyday florals. Rustic & wild country style Florist. We are open Tuesday to Saturday for Wedding, Funeral and flower bunches! We also have a range of Houseplants, Gardenalia, Pip Studio, St Eval, Botanicals, Faux Florals, Cornishware, Nutscene Twines and Gardenalia. Come say hello.......we love talking flowers x Make someones day with rustic & wild country style flowers, handtied with love, wrapped in paper and perfectly presented! Beautiful blooms, full of texture and personality that dance joyfully! Hand delivered by Luce Loves flowers. You can find us inside the Victorian Grade 2 listed Crispin Hall, lovingly creating beautiful flowery bunches! Please note we are closed Mondays! Same day delivery is usually available for orders placed by 2pm. Delivery is within an 8 mile radius of Street, including Glastonbury, Wells and surrounding villages. Of course you are always welcome to collect your flowers from Luce Loves Flower shop!
tagline: Rustic & wild country style florist for weddings, funerals and everyday florals.

title: Spindlewood Lodges
subtitle: Spindlewood Lodges is a small park of just 7 log cabins set in 10 acres of pasture, woodland and orchards with stunning views of the surrounding countryside and Glastonbury Tor.
bodyContent: An ideal location for those people who want to experience the peace and quiet the countryside has to offer, with your own outdoor space rather than being right next to your neighbours in a large holiday park. Your short break accommodation is a traditional Scandanavian log cabin. All of our log cabins sleep up to 4 people and are deceptively spacious with 2 bedrooms – one double and one twin. All have a combined modern kitchen/diner with countryside views and you can relax indoors in the spacious lounge with leather sofas or outside on the large south facing covered veranda. We’re surrounded by many different beautiful locations with wonderful wildlife and major attractions. You can read about some of our favourite local attractions and local restaurants across our site. So why not visit us for a short break or weekend to escape everyday life?

title: Honeysuckle Farm Cottages
subtitle: 3 Luxury Sustainable Cottages for your holiday break in Glastonbury
bodyContent: Get away from it all in the fascinating town of Glastonbury. Situated on the ‘light side’ of Glastonbury Tor, Honeysuckle Farm Cottages forms a wonderful sun-trap, perfectly balancing the peace and tranquility of a rural get away, with the vibrancy of Glastonbury’s unique town centre. We have 3 luxury, self-sustainable, self-catering cottages which sleep between 4 and 8 people each. Our ethos is to provide a really enjoyable, environmentally responsible and practical self-catering holiday destination. Once here, you won’t need your vehicle – there’s so much to see and do all within walking or cycling distance – we even provide the bicycles! Steeped in history, with excellent facilities, friendly people, beautiful surroundings and some amazing local attractions you’re sure to have a fantastically inspiring time.

title: Wookey Hole Hotel
subtitle: Wookey Hole Hotel is 20 minutes from the oldest medieval city in the UK Wells and sixty minutes from the City of Bath so well positioned for all local locations.
bodyContent: Come and stay at the Wookey Hole Hotel for great value family breaks all year round. Ideally placed in the heart of Somerset, the Wookey Hole Hotel can boast comfortable accommodation in picturesque surroundings. Receive access when you book directly! The Wookey Hole Hotel, located on the southern edge of the rolling Mendip Hills , lies in the Sleepy village of Wookey Hole, with easy access to the historic city of Wells and its stunning Cathedral. The Mendip Hills have been recognised as an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and offer stunning landscapes of sweeping slopes and limestone gorges, with endless walking trails and sightseeing spots. Traverse the Mendips and the hills fall away to the breath-taking lakes of the Chew Valley, just a short drive from Wookey Hole. Also close by are Cheddar Gorge and the ancient town of Glastonbury , with Bath, Bristol and the beaches of Burnham-on-Sea and Weston-Super-Mare slightly further afield. The Hotel includes free and secure car and coach parking, modern bedrooms with free wifi plus a stylish Bar and Bistro. The perfect place for a family break or special occasion - we look forward to welcoming you! And of course, discounted tickets to Wookey Hole Caves and attractions!
tagline: Come and stay at The West Country’s newest hotel. Great value family breaks all year round.

title: Woodborough Inn
subtitle: A warm welcome, great food & drink and a cracking pub atmosphere is what makes The Woodborough Inn so special
bodyContent: Sat in the heart of the village of Winscombe and surrounded by the beautiful Mendip hills, The Woodborough Inn is the perfect place to relax and explore the local area which includes the beautiful Cheddar Gorge, the cathedral city of Wells and Glastonbury Tor. The Mendips providing a great space to enjoy the great outdoors. Whether a gentle walk or some extreme mountain biking; The Mendips has it all. Our guest accommodation consists of 7 cosy en-suite rooms, ideal for visitors to the West Country, business people and families alike, and come at competitive rates. Open daily from 11am, lunch from 12-2.00pm and our dinner service runs from 5.30pm. Sunday food hours are 12-3 and 5.30-7.30pm. Our chefs serve up some fabulous food. Hearty pub classics, an exciting range of specials, plus pizza and lighter dishes; all food cooked fresh using locally sourced ingredients. Our Sunday roasts are also not to be missed! Local real ales are always on tap along with crisp lagers, craft beers and local ciders. We have a wonderful wine list and our popular new “Gin List” heads up our selection of premium spirits. We also offer a great range of soft drinks, coffee, tea and cake! This is a popular spot for walkers and naturally, well-behaved dogs are welcome.
tagline: A warm welcome, great food & drink and a cracking pub atmosphere

title: Glastonbury Wedding and Events Venue
subtitle: An old pre Norman village church lovingly restored to its former glory offering a special place for couples to get married , to celebrate an anniversary , or to just have a party . comes with a large car park , glamping site and accommodation with kitchen, toilets and fully stocked licensed bar .
bodyContent: The old village church was closed back in 1998 owing to lack of attendance ,and with strong family ties was purchased by ourselves back in 2002 , The surrounding farmland and farm has been in our family for six generations so we did not want the church to fall into disrepair , and after a period of time we thought with the right planning we could get a civil license and have marriages and events there once more. After 37 months we finally got all the licenses that we required , then after a major building and renovation work we were ready to open up to the public again after a 16 year absence . With weddings and events coming from near and afar , it was decided to offer accommodation , so planning was sought for some glamping pods , these have been installed during the covid lockdowns and are now ready for the summer of 2021. Guests can now enjoy themselves even more with a relaxing stay without the need to drive , whether it is a wedding , anniversary or party a whole weekend with friends can be a enjoyable occasion without the rush and stress . The glamping pods are all ensuite with double bed ,showers, toilets , kitchenette , fridge freezers, microwave and TV . There is also a three bedroom cottage that can sleep six so more friends and family can stay on site.

title: The George Hotel in Frome
subtitle: You’ll be spoiled for choice at our pub with hotel rooms in Frome. Not only is it within easy reach of Longleat, Stonehenge and Glastonbury, but you can also explore local jewels like Nunney Castle, the Walled Garden At Mells, Cooper Hall, Catherine Hill, Victoria Park and the artisan market at St Catherine’s.
bodyContent: The George Hotel enjoys a central location in the market town of Frome, surrounded by the stunning Somerset countryside. We’ve got 28 en suite bedrooms and a strong reputation for good home-cooked food (including a gluten-free menu). Our hotel room options include double, double superior and family rooms, along with singles and twins, plus a deluxe room with balcony and four-poster bed. The finer details... Check-in times: 3-10pm. Check-out times: By 11am. No late check-out facility. Accessibility : Please note, none of our rooms are on the ground floor and accessed by stairs, we do not have a lift. Breakfast options: We offer a complimentary continental breakfast and hot breakfast options. Due to Covid-19 restrictions we will not be offering our continental selection as a buffet but will ask for your orders. In-room hospitality : We provide a hospitality tray in each room (kettle, tea, coffee, biscuits), which is refreshed daily. We also provide towels, toiletries, ironing board and iron and a hairdryer. Pet-friendly rooms: We have 4 pet-friendly rooms; 1 Double, 1 Twin, and 2 Singles. Guests travelling with pets must check prior to booking if there is availability. Please do not arrive with unannounced pets as accommodation is not guaranteed. There is a surcharge of £10 per pet, per night. Car parking: Our car park is situated behind The George Hotel. Enter Cork Street at the side of the hotel, then turn right at Westway Cinema, down the ramp. Drive in-between the concrete pillars at the bottom, where you will find our underground parking spaces. The light will turn on as you enter. Please note that spaces are limited, and we are unable to reserve any. There is a 2 metre height restriction and a tight turn to enter the car park so please take care when entering and exiting. PLEASE NOTE – COVID-19: We have reduced the amount of soft furnishings, printed communications, hospitality tray items, laundry and toiletries in our rooms, to ensure minimal risk of exposure. If you require any top ups or additional items, we are happy to supply these upon request.
tagline: You’ll be spoiled for choice at our pub with hotel rooms in Frome

title: Ensemble
subtitle: This is a beautiful family owned and run business.
bodyContent: Ensemble is a family owned and run restaurant in the heart of Wells with an enviable view of the Cathedral from our tables. We have been in Sadler Street for over five years and the extended family has a long history of hospitality in the area going back to the 1960s. We serve an eclectic range of food, wines and beers with the emphasis being on quality, local suppliers, whom we support as much as possible.

title: White Stuff Wells
subtitle: Hello, make yourself at home! We create places where people feel welcome whether they are in our shops, online or flicking through one of our books. Our shops are more than homely hangouts. We love our customers to pop in for a cuppa and bring their pets for a bowl of water and a treat. In fact kids, friends, everyone is welcome!
bodyContent: We want to make a meaningful difference by connecting people, enhancing communities and creating our beautiful products in a way that benefits those around us. To achieve this, we focus on four key areas: our community, our people, our supply chain and our environment. By actively engaging our customers, teams, suppliers and communities we make sure that we are all creating responsibly. e're a sociable, talented and energetic bunch here at White Stuff, proud to be part of such a great business, and passionate about our customers. We work hard to put people at the heart of our business, building and sustaining a sense of community and shared success, where everyone feels like they're part of something special. Each day we learn and grow together in a place that truly values creativity, sociability, responsibility and determination. Whether we're talking to our customers face-to-face, or engaging via email, online content or social media campaigns, our conversations connect on a human level, inspiring our customers with exciting visuals, social experiences or relevant content. Unlike a 'theme' our seasonal conversations tell a story and actively encourage our customers to take part and join in to enrich and personalise the story. Our conversations show our customers that we share the same interests and values and help us to maintain a meaningful relationship. Fused with our distinctive, funny and sometimes just unconventional personality our conversations engage and inspire our customers wherever they may be.

title: Lethal Postmen Vintage
subtitle: True vintage, retro and vintage inspired clothing and accessories from the 1920s to the 1980s at bargain prices.
bodyContent: Come find us in Shepton Mallet, Somerset. To our non-local friends, check out Lethal Postmen’s Etsy page.

title: Clevedon Court, National Trust
subtitle: Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is a remarkable survival from the medieval period.
bodyContent: Clevedon Court in Clevedon, Somerset, National Trust property is an outstanding 14th-century manor house and 18th-century terraced garden Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is a remarkable survival from the medieval period. The house was purchased by Abraham Elton in 1709 and it is still the much-loved family home of his descendants today. Explore the striking display of Eltonware pottery and a fascinating collection of Nailsea glass.
tagline: Home to the lords of the manor of Clevedon for centuries, the core of the house is remarkable.

title: Ilchester
subtitle: Once a major Roman garrison town on the Fosse Way and the county town of Somerset until the 19th century. Ilchester's past is echoed in the Georgian houses and town hall, which contains a fascinating museum. Its 13th century church tower changes from square to octagonal as it rises.
bodyContent: Once a major Roman garrison town on the Fosse Way and the county town of Somerset until the 19th century. Ilchester's past is echoed in the Georgian houses and town hall, which contains a fascinating museum. Its 13th century church tower changes from square to octagonal as it rises. The town prizes its close association with Royal Naval Air Station Yeovilton, the Fleet Air Arm Museum and the Memorial Church of St Bartholomew - home of the Fleet Air Arm Roll of Honour. The 14th century National Trust Lytes Cary Manor and gardens and the hillside village of Kingsdon are all a short drive away.

title: Westhill Farm Caravan Park
subtitle: Small campsite near Burnham on Sea and Brean in Somerset. Static caravans.
bodyContent: Westhill Farm Caravan Park is almost eighty acres of tranquility on the banks of the river Brue. This static, touring caravan and tenting holiday park is set amongst willow trees, landscaped grounds and farmland in a quiet, peaceful area of the Somerset countryside. We currently have 46 privately owned static caravans, 10 seasonal touring pitches, a commercial and 5CL touring site for all to enjoy. Our touring site caters for long or short stays and one night stop overs. Small laundry on site and owners are resident in the farmhouse. We welcome children and pets. Excellent fishing available on our section of the River Brue. Just a few minutes drive from Burnham on Sea & Brean.
tagline: Small campsite near Burnham on Sea and Brean in Somerset.

title: The Bath Arms
subtitle: Established in 1736, The Bath Arms is a traditional yet stylish family-friendly pub. Located on the outskirts of Longleat Estate in the village of Horingsham, it makes a perfect spot for dining, stays or both.
bodyContent: Established in 1736, The Bath Arms is a traditional yet stylish family-friendly pub. Located on the outskirts of Longleat Estate in the village of Horingsham, it makes a perfect spot for dining, stays or both. They serve breakfast, lunch and dinner, seven days a week, with an everchanging menu using locally sourced produce. Their dishes can also be complimented by a selection of real local ales, lagers and wines. It also offers accommodation across sixteen rooms, with simple yet stylish bedrooms set within the pub and converted stable block.

title: Friary Drinks
subtitle: Here at Friary, we're passionate about making the best artisan spirits, from our botanical gins to our fruit liqueurs. Whether it's our gins, rums, vodkas, our drinks are great for sharing, as a treat for yourself, or given as gifts for a loved one.
bodyContent: Here at Friary, we're passionate about making the best artisan spirits, from our botanical gins to our fruit liqueurs. Every batch is lovingly created and bottled here in Somerset by my sister Hannah, our mistress distiller. Hannah learnt her trade from our dad Ern who started Friary back in 1995, making-up bottles of his legendary sloe gin and cherry brandy, and taking them to local farmers markets in the boot of his old Ford Granada. After a lifetime working for big-name drinks companies, dad was devoted to using the best ingredients, to make delicious drinks for happy customers. While Friary has grown a little since bottles were rattling around in the back of dad's old car, our commitment to creating outstanding drinks for happy customers remains at the heart of everything we do. Whether it's our gins, rums, vodkas, or even Dad's traditional recipes from those very first markets, our drinks are great for sharing, as a treat for yourself, or given as gifts for a loved one.
tagline: Here at Friary, we're passionate about making the best artisan spirits

title: RISE
subtitle: Built in the early 1800s, RISE is a lovingly restored former church located in the heart of Frome. Within the building there are two venue hire spaces catering for a wide variety of classes and events, a contemporary art gallery, a gift shop, and a cafe and garden to enjoy.
bodyContent: We believe the history and heritage of RISE and the role the building has played in the togetherness of the community is worth preserving. As a family owned and thriving community hub we aim to honour the history and heritage of our magnificent building, supporting community togetherness in everything we do. As a place to be together, RISE offers: VENUE HIRE with two light, airy and beautifully restored rooms, The Old School Room and The Sun Room - perfect for uplifting classes, workshops and events. THE WHITTOX GALLERY, a stunningly beautiful contemporary art gallery exhibiting the finest contemporary and cutting-edge artists and designers. CAFE run by RYE BAKERY, an independent cafe who champion local and organic produce and use traditional baking methods and ancient grains to create artisan bread. With a play space for children, a wicker pod for breastfeeding mums and serving delicious pizzas, the cafe is a popular choice for families. OFFICES & WORK SPACE - currently leased to OpenStoryTellers, a charity which works to enrich and empower the lives of people with learning disabilities and autism.
tagline: Built in the early 1800s, RISE is a lovingly restored former church

title: Lasseter's
subtitle: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion. It serves locally sourced dishes created by a team of professional chefs.
bodyContent: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion. It serves locally sourced dishes created by a team of professional chefs. The restaurant focuses on bringing high-quality dining and great-value food to Weston, and is quickly gaining a reputation for excellent food, atmosphere and welcoming service. The restaurant boasts stunning views of Weston-super-Mare’s bay, as well as exciting menus that are based around fresh ingredients. It serves lunch and dinner from Wednesday to Saturday – including special set lunch menus and early-bird pre-theatre offers – and a carvery on Sundays from noon. Lasseter’s also serves an extensive range of cocktails, spirits and wines, with over 100 drinks to choose from. The wine list has been hand-selected by the restaurant manager, with a variety of different types and styles for all tastes. There is something for everyone at Lasseter’s. You can relax in the bar or on the terrace – with a snack if, you fancy – or enjoy a meal in our glorious restaurant overlooking the seafront.
tagline: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion.

title: Mendip Basecamp
subtitle: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure campsite in the Mendip Hills...
bodyContent: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure camp in the Mendip Hills National Landscape - just minutes from the M5 and Weston-super-Mare. Surrounded by ancient woodland you can pitch where you like, park right by your tent and enjoy evenings around the campfire. Well-behaved dogs are welcome! With no check-out time, you can leave whenever you are ready. Mendip Basecamp is camping how it should be: rural, laid-back and relaxed but with essential luxuries. Usually reserved for schools and private groups, in 2020, Mendip opened Basecamp up to families for the very first time- and hasn’t looked back since. Public bookings are available throughout the summer holidays and summer weekends. Bring your own tent or campervan, book bell tents, glamphouses or stay in Mendip Lodge (with free breakfast). Facilities include hot showers, clean flushing toilets, a camp shop, a country Lodge with a cider garden (and live music), an onsite activity centre, USB charging and WIFI. Free activities throughout the summer include live music, orienteering, circus skills, treasure hunts, free climbing tower and nature craft. The campsite is less than a 5-minute woodland walk from Mendip Activity Centre, home to over 20 different adventurous, outdoor activities including rock climbing, kayaking, archery, frisbee golf and air rifle. New for 2026, Mendip Basecamp is launching Mendip Mini Fests - six family-friendly festivals running throughout the summer holiday weekends. Great entertainment, headline bands, local talent competition, and more! Included at no extra cost, exclusively for campsite guests.
tagline: Mendip Basecamp was delighted to be awarded the Gold campsite at the 2023-2024

title: Southfield Farm Caravan Park
subtitle: Quiet friendly Caravan Park with owner occupied static caravans and seasonal touring caravans on a farm adjacent to sandy beach in Brean, Somerset
bodyContent: At Southfield Farm Caravan Park you can enjoy happy holidays on a farm beside the sea. This quiet family park provides pitches for owner occupied static caravans and seasonal touring caravans on a pleasant open site with distant views of the Mendip Hills and only five minutes’ walk from a safe sandy beach. Brean is a favourite place for holidays with everything you need within walking distance. There are plenty of attractions to visit in Somerset as well as wonderful food and wildlife. Static Park open end March to end October, Seasonal Park opens mid May to end September. The Pavilion area hosts 48 luxury pitches for 12' and 13' static caravans, we often have statics for sale please visit: Pavilion Brean Statics for sale. If you are looking for a seasonal pitch (mid May to end September) why not call us? Prices vary but an all inclusive package of grass pitch, electric and winter storage is £1,380
tagline: Quiet friendly Caravan Park with owner occupied static caravans and seasonal touring caravans

title: Country View Holiday Park
subtitle: Country View Holiday Park, Sand Bay near Weston Super Mare, Somerset. Touring caravans, motor-homes and tents on a quiet, family orientated site in picturesque surroundings in Somerset.
bodyContent: A warm welcome awaits you at the Country View Holiday Park in Sand Bay next to Weston Super Mare . Come and re-explore the area, there are so many things to see and do for day trips or simply relax on site and enjoy our facilities. Sand Bay beach is only 200 yards. We can accommodate touring caravans, motor-homes and tents on a quiet, family orientated site in picturesque surroundings. The Park is licensed for 190 pitches available for holiday touring purposes and also seasonal pitches. Do call us to enquire regarding rates of seasonal pitches. We also offer a range of static holiday homes for sale, so you could have your own holiday home at Country View in Somerset. Country View boasts a Heated outdoor swimming pool , bar, play area, games room, country meadows and our huge 5 acre dog walk, all complimentary. Superb disabled facilities too, please call with any query.
tagline: Great Holiday Park just yards from the beautiful Sand Bay Beach

title: BRAZZ
subtitle: Taunton's most chic spot to catch up with friends, enjoy a meal with the family or a romantic dinner. Whether you're looking for healthy or hearty, you'll find it at Brazz.
bodyContent: Taunton's most chic spot to catch up with friends, enjoy a meal with the family or a romantic dinner. Whether you're looking for healthy or hearty, you'll find it at Brazz. Start your day off with a delicious Brazz breakfast served with a coffee, Devon roasted to perfection. At lunch, you'll love our salads and grills. They taste out-of-this-world good! All of our food is sourced locally and responsibly and pictures of its provenance adorn our walls. Brazz really comes into its own during the evening. Our plush booths offer the perfect space for larger get-togethers. With great sharing platters and drinks offers, there's no better place to party.

title: Brothers Cider
subtitle: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family, who have been making cider in Somerset since 1658.
bodyContent: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family, who have been making cider in Somerset since 1658. We first started selling our Pear Cider at the Glastonbury Festival in 1995 near what was then called the Jazz World Stage. These days it is called The West Holts Stage. Over the years, festival goers kept asking us if it was possible to get our drink when the festival was over and so we decided to market it to pubs and supermarkets. Now you can get it all over the country and at many festivals. We are independent, British and are passionate about what we do. Our free-spirited essence is upheld by approaching things with a unique perspective. Here at Brothers, we take our values and commitment to sustainability very seriously, but it’s something we haven’t really shouted about until now. We have zero to landfill, all our waste is segregated to optimise the opportunity of being recycled or reused. A massive solar panel system is now installed here at the cider mill, where it will directly supply the presses with clean energy and lastly, all our left-over fruit pomace is turned into energy which helps to heat the local swimming pool!
tagline: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family.

title: Wookey Hole Hotel
subtitle: Wookey Hole Hotel is 20 minutes from the oldest medieval city in the UK Wells and sixty minutes from the City of Bath so well positioned for all local locations.
bodyContent: Come and stay at the Wookey Hole Hotel for great value family breaks all year round. Ideally placed in the heart of Somerset, the Wookey Hole Hotel can boast comfortable accommodation in picturesque surroundings. Receive access when you book directly! The Wookey Hole Hotel, located on the southern edge of the rolling Mendip Hills , lies in the Sleepy village of Wookey Hole, with easy access to the historic city of Wells and its stunning Cathedral. The Mendip Hills have been recognised as an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and offer stunning landscapes of sweeping slopes and limestone gorges, with endless walking trails and sightseeing spots. Traverse the Mendips and the hills fall away to the breath-taking lakes of the Chew Valley, just a short drive from Wookey Hole. Also close by are Cheddar Gorge and the ancient town of Glastonbury , with Bath, Bristol and the beaches of Burnham-on-Sea and Weston-Super-Mare slightly further afield. The Hotel includes free and secure car and coach parking, modern bedrooms with free wifi plus a stylish Bar and Bistro. The perfect place for a family break or special occasion - we look forward to welcoming you! And of course, discounted tickets to Wookey Hole Caves and attractions!
tagline: Come and stay at The West Country’s newest hotel. Great value family breaks all year round.

title: Double-Gate Farm
subtitle: Georgian farmhouse B&B accommodation with self catering converted barns in a peaceful location in Somerset, near Glastonbury & Wells.
bodyContent: Welcome to Double-Gate Farm, our Georgian farmhouse situated on the banks of the River Sheppey. Our farm offers views of the Mendip Hills and the surrounding countryside. Whether you're looking for a romantic getaway, a family vacation, or a group retreat, we have a variety of accommodations to choose from. Our converted barn is perfect for couples, families, and groups, while our accessible Riverside rooms and facilities cater to everyone's requirements. Our seasonal Tea Room is open from March to December and offers a range of delicious breakfasts, light lunches, home-baked cakes, and our speciality, Afternoon Tea. How about renting our BBQ Hut for a fun and sociable evening of cooking with your loved ones? Our Games Room is the perfect place to unwind after a long day of exploring. With a full-size snooker table, table-tennis, and lots of board games and local information, you'll never run out of things to do. At Double-Gate Farm, we pride ourselves on providing a peaceful and relaxing environment that allows you to unwind and enjoy nature. You can fish from your patio, watch the wildlife, or simply sit back and read. We welcome everyone, including cycling groups, walkers, and countryside lovers. Our location is perfect for exploring Somerset's hidden gems. With easy access to Glastonbury, Wells, and Cheddar, you'll be able to experience all that this beautiful region has to offer. We're also dog-friendly, so you don't have to leave your furry friend behind. Two of our Riverside rooms are pet-friendly, so please call us to check availability when booking with your dog. Finally, our farm is next door to a renowned gastropub that serves food and local brews. It's just a short walk away, so you don't have to worry about transportation. Come and experience the beauty of Double-Gate Farm for yourself.
tagline: Georgian farmhouse B&B accommodation with self catering converted barns

title: Bath Theatrical Costume Hire
subtitle: Bath Theatrical Costume Hire, a family business established in 1969 moved from our quirky little shop in Bath to our warehouse in Frome in 2001, housing more than 30,000 costumes. We work with hundreds of companies, casts, actors, and partygoers to ensure they have the best costumes for their event.
bodyContent: Bath Theatrical Costume Hire, from its small beginnings above a hairdresser on the London Road in Bath, is now based in Frome and houses over 30,000 costumes. “When we moved from our overcrowded premises on London Road, we thought we would never fill our new home, even with our two friendly ghosts in tow. Now that too, is crammed with fabulous stuff, some of which is already put together as costumes but much of which is waiting for our touch of magic to bring the characters to life”, said Dinah Auton, the second generation to run the business. Bath Theatrical is like no other business and for those who know it, they are delighted that it is so different. It is perhaps its quirkiness which has helped it ride the economic and professional changes which have flavoured the past 50 years. Through all this Bath Theatrical has managed to add its magic to many a party goer, wedding guest and stage costumes. We service professional and amateurs’ groups, schools, corporate promotions, alternative weddings, events, and a wide array of private hire for parties. Talk to our staff about how we can make your event, production or celebratory occasion that extra special.
tagline: Bath Theatrical Costume Hire, a family business established in 1969

title: Farleigh Hungerford
subtitle: Historic village dominated by the ruined castle.
bodyContent: Historic village dominated by the ruined castle. The castle is in the care of English Heritage and admission is charged. A walk around will reveal hundreds of years of gory goings on topped off with a visit to the crypt. Explore the rest of the village with a Village Trail available from Frome Tourist Information. Over the river Stowford Manor Farm offers cream teas in summer along with a range of workshops from glass working to stonemasonry. In July each year thousands flock here to the Village Pump Festival for four days of the best folk and world music in an idyllic setting on the river banks.
