title: Castle Cary
subtitle: Castle Cary - one of the most attractive of Somerset's market towns. Tucked away in a secluded spot a few miles off the A303, the golden stone of Castle Cary and Ansford exudes a warm glow complemented by its glorious setting in the South Somerset countryside and its friendly inhabitants.
bodyContent: The town has many attractive historic buildings including its 19th century Market House, its 18th century "Roundhouse" or lock-up' and the thatched George Hotel. The main street, stretching down to the old Horse Pond, is full of individual high-quality shops, delicatessens, cafes and restaurants. Tuesday is market day, when fish, bread and organic vegetables are sold on the cobbles in front of the Market House. If you're walking, rambling, or simply looking for a quiet time in the countryside, Cary can provide it. The Leland Trail , the Macmillan Way and Monarch's Way all pass near the town, as does the route to Glastonbury for many festival goers. And the view from the top of Lodge Hill is magnificent. The town is noted for its high quality shops - grocers, outfitters, ironmongers, books, antiques and local produce. There are several inns in the town, wonderful restaurants and tearooms making it perfect destination for a relaxing country break.

title: County Flowers
subtitle: County Flowers of Taunton is not only an independent florist but also a family run business with a team of qualified florists led by Denise Cross a British Master Florist.
bodyContent: We take great pride in working to achieve the highest standards for the benefit of both customers and recipients, using materials that are sourced either locally, nationally or from Holland and lovingly conditioned by hand . We are not only award winning – achieving a silver award 2 years running in The Flower Shop of the Year Awards but have also appeared on the following TV shows: All Over The Shop Come Dine with Me 60 Minute Makeover Local Delivery around Taunton Orders received by 1pm can usually be delivered the same day but this is dependent on the availability of the specific items requested Whilst we offer a local delivery in the Taunton Area we are also able to deliver in the following areas: Bridgwater, Chard, Ilminster, Milverton, North Petherton, Watchet, Wellington, Wiveliscombe and surrounding villages. See details for delivery charges. Weddings When planning your big day, flowers are an important decision to make. You need to feel confident that your florist will create the designs you envisaged for not only your bouquets, buttonholes and corsages but also table centres and all other venue decorating designs. The flowers you choose with the aid of your florist need to reflect your combined personalities and also create the atmosphere you require. Vintage, vibrant, chic or classical the choice is yours. Funerals We all know a funeral is a difficult, stressful, emotional and sensitive time. The capable, qualified and supportive florists at County Flowers are here to help you through this difficult time. We can identify the appropriate tribute whatever that may be. If required we can create a specialist bespoke tribute which reflects the hobbies, passions and life of your loved one. Once your required design(s) are chosen we will liaise with the funeral directors re delivering direct to them leaving you one less thing to worry about Add on Gifts – Balloons, Chocolates, Teddies and Vases We stock a wide range of gifts to add to your Floral Gift –balloons for most occasions, Belgian Chocolates, pink or blue Teddies for babies, traditional coloured teddies for the more mature and a wide selection of vases. Bouquets and Arrangements We are passionate about flowers, plants and all aspects of our trade and delight in creating beautiful bouquets and arrangements that show how stunning are tools of the trade look in their natural beauty. You can rely on County Flowers to produce something suitable whatever the occasion.

title: Immersive Events at Shepton Mallet Prison
subtitle: Established in 2015, Immersive Events or ‘IME’ is an award winning, interactive, immersive events company based in Shepton Mallet Prison.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. Shepton Mallet Prison, Somerset specialise in designing and running events nationwide from Scream Parks & Scare Mazes to Escape Rooms, overnight stays to prison breaks, from corporate training to Hens and Stags. IME has proudly been nominated for a SCAR 2016 – Best Zombie Survival Event for Lockdown and became winner of SCAR 2017 Experience for Lockdown I, Lockdown II and Lockdown Origins. Annual, monthly and weekly a huge variety of events are held at Shepton Mallet Prison. Every year over the Halloween period IME host the sold-out event ‘The Street’. This scare maze is to be endured for a gruelling 25 minutes and is one of a kind. The scare maze is riddled with twists and turns, jump scares and horrors. Due to popular demand, ‘The Street’ at Shepton Mallet Prison, Somerset's Ultimate Scare Maze is re-opening for Christmas; with the addition of Santa's GROTto! Tickets are just £10 and are now on sale. The event will be held on the 21st and 22nd December. Let’s hope you have been good this year! Escape Rooms are held every Saturday at 11:00am, the maximum group size is 18 people and pre-booking is recommended. To escape from a cell in Shepton Mallet you have to complete a sequence of riddles, puzzles and a series of mind-challenging games. Think you can escape from your prison cell? Tickets are just £20pp. New for 2019, IME’s Prison Break event is a much larger scale of an escape room and is heavily interactive. Yourself ‘The Criminal’, is processed by ‘officers’ in reception, giving you the immersed feeling that a convict would have experienced before being led to your cell. To escape not only the cell but escape the prison itself, you will have to answer riddles, solve puzzles and out think the officers. Battle archery is a private pre-book event that requires a minimum of 8 people and costs £25pp for two hours. With bows and foam-tipped safety arrows, this exciting action-packed game offers mission based archery experience. Bespoke packages are also available for this event with the option to add on a cell escape at £35pp (1 hour for each activity). Shepton Mallet Prison, offers a specific type of backdrop and scenery which can’t be accessed in many places. This provides a great opportunity for a truly unique experience for your event or party. Our packages for private parties, stags, hens & birthdays can be custom built to suit your needs. From cocktail making to scare experiences we are sure to put together a package that works for you. We have developed our team building and corporate training days to suit every business, big or small. Team building days aim to motivate your team, increase productivity, collaboration and communication and develop a business with forward thinking employees. Our Team Building days focus on fun and collaborative activities for employees to create and share team memories. We can mix and match any of the activities to create a team building session that is right for you, alternatively you can contact us and we will happily look at customising a package for you.
tagline: Shepton Mallet Prison, Somerset offers specific type of backdrop which can’t be accessed generally

title: Wells & Mendip Museum
subtitle: We aim to give you a stimulating and enjoyable experience, and our volunteers will provide you with a warm welcome. Find us in the Cathedral Close, in the former home of the Cathedral Chancellors.
bodyContent: Our museum tells the stories of Wells and the Mendip Hills. Our displays include a Jurassic sea dragon, and unique archaeology collections from the Mendip caves, featuring the bones of ancient animals who roamed here thousands of years ago. Find out about the incredible array of rocks and minerals to be found on the Mendip Hills, and how people have explored its caves. We have a wonderful collection of embroidery samplers, and tell the story of the early Cathedral stonemasons through a collection of sculpture and statues on loan from the cathedral. Our temporary exhibitions feature the work of local and well-known artists. We also have a library and are home to the Wells City Archives (both open to researchers by appointment). The museum shop stocks an array of attractive gifts, cards and books.
tagline: We aim to give you a stimulating and enjoyable experience

title: The Chalice Well
subtitle: Historical well with legends in Glastonbury, Somerset.Chalice Well at the foot of Glastonbury Tor.
bodyContent: Chalice Well is one of Britain's most ancient wells, nestling in the Vale of Avalon between the famous Glastonbury Tor and Chalice Hill. Surrounded by beautiful gardens and orchards it is a living sanctuary in which the visitor can experience the quiet healing of this sacred place. Over three acres of peace. For over two thousand years this has been a place where people have gathered to drink the waters and find solace, peace and inspiration. At present we work with the theme of 'Many Paths, One Source' to welcome all people of goodwill to the gardens throughout the year. We also mark 'the wheel of the year' at regular intervals with events of celebration, silence and meditation, and conversation. This includes an evening programme of music, poetry and performance throughout the summer months in our candlelit gardens.
tagline: Historical well with legends in Glastonbury, Somerset.Chalice Well at the foot of Glastonbury Tor.

title: Ring O'Bells
subtitle: Free house local pub in Somerset between Street & Glastonbury.
bodyContent: The Ring O’Bells is an 18th Century “free house” pub in the Somerset village of Ashcott near Street and Glastonbury, which for the last 29 years has been run by a family partnership. A unique pub with unique food, all prepared by us in our own kitchens. Local meat from a local butcher. Somerset produce at its best. Daily Specials blackboard including freshly made desserts. Home-made fudge with your coffee to finish! We are a genuine Free House and it is our policy to feature beers from small independent breweries, many from the West Country but occasionally also more “exotic” visitors! The range of beers varies constantly but our list of forthcoming beers features usually at least one beer from one of the local micro breweries. CAMRA Good Beer Guide 2016 CAMRA Good Pub Food Guide 2016, (star-rated, and entered in this guide for the nineteenth consecutive year). AA Pubs and Inns Guide 2016 The Good Pub Guide 2016
tagline: Free house local pub in Somerset between Street & Glastonbury.

title: The George Inn
subtitle: The George Inn is a fantastic village pub in Gurney Slade that welcomes all the family to enjoy our delicious food, our great selection of drinks and great entertainment!
bodyContent: We host a great selection of entertainment from quiz nights, poker nights, bingo nights and more! We’ve even got our own skittle alley… We also have a number of en-suite letting rooms available. For more information or to book, please just give us a call. Children are welcome into the George pub until 9pm. We look forward to seeing you soon.

title: The White Horse
subtitle: At the very heart of Exmoor, nestling by the bridge over the River Exe, you’ll find the Exmoor White Horse Inn.
bodyContent: Festooned in Virginia creeper, this traditional 16th century building with classic period features has been family owned and run for generations. Kick off your boots and unwind beside one of our log fires. Choose from over 200 Malt Whiskys along with our fine selection of local Real Ales, savour our delicious locally sourced produce and at the end of a fantastic evening, retire to a sumptuous room full of charm and character. It’s no more than you would expect from an idyllic Inn, which offers its guests a warm and welcoming atmosphere in a true Westcountry style – a favourite all year round.

title: The Railway Inn
subtitle: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you. Treat yourself to a delicious meal in our restaurant, have a bar snack in our cosy bar, or simply enjoy a pint of Thatchers Somerset Cider.
bodyContent: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you. Treat yourself to a delicious meal in our restaurant, have a bar snack in our cosy bar, or simply enjoy a pint of Thatchers Somerset Cider . The food we proudly serve features regional and seasonal ingredients from local producers, with a strong emphasis on great quality, great taste and sensible prices. Our drinks menu is carefully chosen, with of course the full range of ciders from Thatchers; beers, wines and soft drinks. Our team of enthusiastic front of house staff love to share their knowledge and appetite for products with guests, and are proud to go that extra mile in making visits a memorable one. The Railway Inn has been at the hub of Sandford village for over 140 years. As a reminder of its long tradition, the original signals from the old Sandford railway line take pride of place outside, together with two authentic oak vats. The Railway Inn Cider House and Kitchen is decorated with artefacts and pictures reflecting the cidermaking heritage of Thatchers. Keen to represent local craftsmanship at its best, the bar and restaurant has been given extra special interest with hand carvings in English oak describing the story of the cidermaking year. A short walk along the road and you’ll come to the Thatchers Cider Shop . Here the shelves are packed with our ciders, alongside produce such as local cheeses and chutneys, and gifts including books and clothing. Our draught ciders are available straight from the barrel so you can try before you buy. Please call the Railway Inn on 01934 611518, or book online at www.therailwayinn.com
tagline: At The Railway Inn, Sandford, a warm welcome awaits you.

title: The Fountain Inn
subtitle: We are a Restaurant/Bar with an exciting menu which features freshly prepared dishes with interesting flavour combinations.
bodyContent: We pride ourselves on using locally-sourced ingredients of the highest quality. Our team are passionate about the consistency and quality of the service and food. We have a warm inviting atmosphere with a quirky, eclectic interior which adds to the overall dining experience. You can find us located in the conservation area of Wells adjacent to the world renowned Wells Cathedral and a short walk from Vicars' Close, which is the oldest residential street (mid-14th century) in Europe. CHILDREN We are delighted to welcome well behaved children to The Fountain Inn. We have a children’s menu and we provide high chairs available on request. We do insist that children are seated with adults and supervised at all times and that any noise or disruption is kept to a minimum. DOGS/PETS Sorry, we do not allow dogs/pets except Guide dogs and Assistance Dogs. FOOD ALLERGIES & INTOLERANCE'S If you have any food allergies or intolerance's, please make a member of our Team aware as not all ingredients are listed on the Menu. *Note of Warning - We cook in an environment that uses most allergens on a regular basis. Whilst we endeavour to do our best, there can be no guarantee of an allergen free product. If you have a serious allergy, we request you bring your correct medication with you when dining. PRE-ORDERS, DEPOSITS AND SERVICE CHARGES We require a pre-order for covers of 10 or more and a deposit of £5.00 per head for covers of five or more. A service charge of 10% will apply for tables of 10 covers or more. FACILITIES Our Restaurant/Pub is a listed building and therefore we are limited with the provision of customer facilities such as a disabled washroom and baby changing room. We do apologise for this inconvenience. CAR PARKING (Subject to Availability) We have made provision for our customers to park in the car park opposite when dining with us and we have a Free Parking Permit facility. Please ask a member of staff for your Parking Permit upon arrival. It is the customers responsibility to request a permit and clearly display this in the vehicle. The car park is pay & display and managed by Car Parking Management (CPM) UK an independent company. Customers can park between 12pm - 4pm and 6pm - 10.30pm. Parking without a valid permit may lead to a parking penalty. Penalty charges received MUST be queried with CPM directly and NOT the Fountain Inn. We are not responsible for any parking fines received. Please request a Permit when we are open for business to avoid any disappointment!

title: Dredge & Male
subtitle: We are an independent family run Business, first opened in 1977 we pride ourselves in being an " Aladdin's Cave "
bodyContent: Dredge and male is a family run business serving the community since 1977, the shop was first opened by Tug and Lindy Wilson, they retired in 2006 and the two sons Colin and Alan took over the partnership. In November Colin took sole ownership and continues to run the family business. We pride ourselves in trying to stock ' what you need ' and if we don't have it in stock we will try our hardest to get it for you. Our customer service is personal and we like to be part of the community- supporting the good people of Shepton Mallet as they have supported us for so many years. As an essential shop we have remained open during #Lockdown1 and #Lockdown2. We can deliver locally, but politely ask for a minimum order of £10. Please call 01749 342702 to place your order

title: Dunkery Beacon Country House
subtitle: Welcome to Dunkery Beacon Country House near Dunster – a truly unique and special place to stay in the heart of Exmoor National Park.
bodyContent: Dunkery Beacon Hotel near Minehead offers luxury accommodation and provide the perfect place to escape the rigours of day-to-day life and relax and unwind in a truly tranquil, rural location where breath-taking scenery abounds. Dining & Drinks Relaxed, friendly and sophisticated award-winning dining with a seasonally changing menu and a focus on locally-sourced produce. Our extensive wine list is supplied by top London wine merchant Berry Bros. & Rudd and West Country merchant Christopher Piper Wines. Experience Exmoor in all its glory from our idyllic rural location, with spectacular views across the countryside and moor. There’s wild moorland, lush, deep, wooded, river valleys, pretty thatched cottages and acres of woodland. Sit back, relax…and let nature take over!
tagline: Welcome to Dunkery Beacon Country House near Dunster

bodyContent: Charming Gurney Manor Mill B&B, a converted watermill and barn beside a stream with waterfall, pond and wildlife, in a picturesque village gateway to the Quantock Hills AONB and sea. title: Southfield Farm Caravan Park
subtitle: Quiet friendly Caravan Park with owner occupied static caravans and seasonal touring caravans on a farm adjacent to sandy beach in Brean, Somerset
bodyContent: At Southfield Farm Caravan Park you can enjoy happy holidays on a farm beside the sea. This quiet family park provides pitches for owner occupied static caravans and seasonal touring caravans on a pleasant open site with distant views of the Mendip Hills and only five minutes’ walk from a safe sandy beach. Brean is a favourite place for holidays with everything you need within walking distance. There are plenty of attractions to visit in Somerset as well as wonderful food and wildlife. Static Park open end March to end October, Seasonal Park opens mid May to end September. The Pavilion area hosts 48 luxury pitches for 12' and 13' static caravans, we often have statics for sale please visit: Pavilion Brean Statics for sale. If you are looking for a seasonal pitch (mid May to end September) why not call us? Prices vary but an all inclusive package of grass pitch, electric and winter storage is £1,380

title: Palmer Street Bottle
subtitle: Located in the vibrant St Catherine's quarter, Palmer Street Bottle offers a different kind of eating and drinking experienced cafe.
bodyContent: Located in the vibrant St Catherine's quarter, Palmer Street Bottle offers a different kind of eating and drinking experience. We specialise in Craft Beers, fine ciders, Wines and Spirits showcasing the best in local producers as well as a range of UK based and International makers and brewers. We offer a relaxed space where you can sit and enjoy a drink and something to eat to compliment your chosen beverage. Or if you prefer our bottle shop offers a wide selection of Craft beers, fine ciders, natural wine as well as a refill station where you can select and take home wine or beer of your choice. One of our other great passions is Cheese at Palmer Street Bottle and what would compliment a beautiful craft beer or glass of wine more than a carefully selected artisan organic cheese board either to eat in or takeaway from our deli counter.

title: Silk Mill Studios & Gallery
subtitle: Twenty-two studios and a multifunctional gallery event space
bodyContent: The Silk Mill is situated right in the centre of Frome in one of the best preserved textile mills in the area. The 4 storey listed building had been abandoned for 30 years and was on the ‘Buildings at Risk Register’ before the Moore family began its rescue in 2005. The 22 studios are now occupied by highly talented artists and makers from a wide variety of disciplines from a double bass luthier to glass artists, print makers, painters, dressmakers and jewellers. The Frome Art School (formed in 2022) is based in Silk Mill West and hosts courses and workshops. The top-lit gallery hosts exhibitions, gigs, theatrical productions, private events and markets. For Frome Festival in July an outside stage is erected for events throughout the 10 days. People say that it feels like being in Spain or Italy when they sit on the west facing terrace on a sunny summer’s evening.

title: Still Sisters
subtitle: Our range of Gins are created using locally sourced botanicals from businesses just like ours. Our signature gin contains watercress from organic beds in Longbridge Deverill, our other leading botanicals are roses grown in Chard, Lavender from Warminster and Somerset Cider Apples from Perry’s Orchard.
bodyContent: We are two sisters based in Frome, Somerset producing small batch Gin from our bespoke copper still called Storm. We have great fun exploring and creating our drinks. Our range of Gins are created using locally sourced botanicals from businesses just like ours. Our signature gin contains watercress from organic beds in Longbridge Deverill, our other leading botanicals are roses grown in Chard, Lavender from Warminster and Somerset Cider Apples from Perry’s Orchard. Our Gins are perfect to enjoy with a simple tonic over ice. Our signature Gin using organic watercress enjoys peppery and refreshing undertones. We have explored and sampled a lot of Gins but our watercress, we believe is the best! Visit our beautiful distillery shop, meet one of our gin experts; purchase a bottle of your favourite gin; enjoy a gin & tonic; book one of our gin tasting experiences and learn all about the history of gin, how we make our gin and sample our award-winning gins with a selection of mixers; or visit our gin school and be guided in choosing your botanicals to make your very own gin!
tagline: Our range of Gins are created using locally sourced botanicals

subtitle: Photo|Frome is a new festival dedicated to showcasing and celebrating all levels of photographic endeavours from local, national and international photographers. title: Joe Pasquale: The New Normal. 40 Years Of Cack
bodyContent: About Us Joe Pasquale has been showing off on stage for most of his life and now, after four decades of nonsense, he's dragging out his favourite things for another airing to prove that nothing has ever been really normal. So, is, like me, you have ever asked questions like: can a vegetarian get a job as a Beefeater? If beauty is relative, why are all my relatives ugly? If an Eskimo has a house-warming party, will his igloo melt? Why is it that dead people get to ride in such posh cars? If a nudist split beetroot soup in his lap, would he have a stain on his character? And why don't chicken breasts have nipples? Then this is the show for you! Joe will be supported by comedian Lee Carroll. Tickets: £27 Over60s: £23 Child: £23 Family: £85 Groups: 1 in 10 free

title: Somerset Lavender
subtitle: Buy gorgeous lavender products directly from the people who grow it in the stunning Somerset countryside.
bodyContent: Somerset Lavender in Somerset offers a shopping experience with a difference. Surrounded by the soothing presence of the lavender fields, you can browse our lavender product range in comfort and then relax with tea and cake in our on site café. We stock a wide range of gifts and lavender products made from the lavender grown on our farm. Products range from the lavender essential oil, distilled naturally on the farm using steam, to toiletries and soft furnishings. Our highly sought after honey made by the bees in the lavender field is certainly one to try but do hurry as stocks are limited due to the nature of this product. Lavender plants are also available for purchase. Somerset Lavender in Somerset will be open for six weeks from the 9 th November. A great opportunity to do some relaxed Christmas shopping. Wide range of unique gifts only available on the farm. Cafe will be open too, meet up with friends for a coffee and a chat. Hope to see you soon.

bodyContent: Holmwood Coach House is a self-catering, holiday let, in Frome, Somerset. It is an architect designed renovation of a Victorian coach housing, suitable for 1, 2 or 3 people, set in an acre of garden and woodland with tennis court use, and undercover car parking. title: Midsomer Norton
subtitle: Stroll through the cosy town centre and stop at one of the many charming cafés. History buffs will be fascinated with the local area: nursery rhymes including Jack and Jill, Little Jack Horner and Ring o’ Roses are all thought to have originated around Midsomer Norton.
bodyContent: What to do in Midsomer Norton Welcome to one of the best-preserved coal mining towns in England: home to iconic nursery rhymes and inspiration for the name of long-running television series Midsomer Murders thanks to its quintessentially British moniker. Midsomer Norton has existed since the Iron Age, but the settlement boomed in the 1700s when the town’s coal mine opened - and you’ll see traces of its industrial past even today, most strikingly with the volcano-like figure of the mine’s spoil heap on the western edge of town. Discover more about the town’s history at the Midsomer Norton Museum, housed in the former market hall, where a range of exciting exhibits show what life’s been like in north-east Somerset for the past 200 years. The railway routes that used to service the mining town are now lush greenways - stretching all the way to Frome and beyond, ideal for walking or cycling and taking in the serene Somerset setting. In true Somerset spirit, the Midsomer Norton Farmers’ Market is hosted on each first Saturday of the month on the high street - perfect for getting your hands on local meat, fish, fruits, vegetables and cheeses. Enjoy your purchases with a picnic on The Hollies, a green space surrounded by shops right in the middle of the high street. For family fun, stop at the Somerset and Dorset Railway , a heritage trust line run by volunteers that’s being lovingly restored. Look around the old station site and take a ride on the reinvigorated engines down the one-mile track into the countryside.

title: Somerton
subtitle: As classically Somerset as you can find, Somerton evokes memories of country life at its most quintessential. It’s conveniently walkable: start at the historical heart of Market Square and take in the town’s many landmarks like the rare octagonal-tower Church of St Michael and All Angels.
bodyContent: What to do in Somerton Somerton’s an ancient settlement, mentioned in the Middle Ages as the capital of Wessex - the reason why it lent its name to the county of Somerset. Nowadays it’s a fine example of small-town Somerset life, packed with history and tradition that’s evident from the moment you step foot in Somerton’s old centre point, the aptly-named Cow Square. Begin your tour of Somerton from Cow Square, with its Edwardian water fountain and architecture from the 17th and 18th centuries, by stroll along tree-lined Broad Street to reach the market place. Here, rich stone buildings, paved market space and outdoor café seating bring a continental vibe to the heart of Somerset. You’ll also see the Church of St Michael and All Angels, with its rare octagonal tower and wonderful carved ceiling dating all the way back to 1450. In the centre of the market place you’ll find the wonderful Buttercross, a shelter built in the 1600s to protect butter, cheese and milk from spoiling in the Somerset sun during market days. Drop in to the old town hall to see local works by local artists and craftspeople. The village hosts a range of family events throughout the year, often in an around the town hall. Stop off at one of the cosy tea rooms in the town centre, and venture into the historic side streets to find independent shops selling Somerset souvenirs. Those in search of fresh Somerset air will find walks aplenty on the outskirts of Somerton. One of the best takes you to the viaduct over which runs the railway from London to Taunton , and underneath you’ll find River Cary and the fishing lakes stocked with trout.

title: Walk Minehead to Brean
subtitle: Explore some of Somerset’s superb coast with a walk along part or all of the new 58-mile route that is the latest addition to the National Coast Path.
bodyContent: In the light of COVID-19 please be aware that this event/venue might not be operating as normal so do check before you visit. From glorious beaches to amazing wildlife, historical delights to geological marvels, the Somerset stretch of the England Coast Path offers walkers of all levels - from holidaymakers and families to serious walking enthusiasts - the chance to explore, relax and enjoy some of Britain's most unusual and beautiful coastal scenery. Starting from the genteel Victorian resort of Minehead and walking east towards the natural promontory of Brean Down, you will pass a medieval village , alabaster rocks, an ancient harbour, a stunning waterfall , limestone pavements, saltmarshes, sand dunes and a lighthouse on legs. For more info click here
tagline: Explore some of Somerset’s superb coast with a walk along part or all of the new 58-mile route.

title: The Bishop's Palace
subtitle: The Bishop’s Palace and Gardens in Wells has been home to the Bishops of Bath and Wells for over 800 years and this stunning medieval palace is now open for all to enjoy. It’s a great family day out in Somerset with a full programme of year-round events, free guided walks, open-air music and theatre, garden workshops and more and a slice of cake with afternoon tea at the ever-popular Bishop’s Table café is always welcome!
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Visit Highlights: There are 14 acres of outstanding RHS Partner gardens to explore (including the beautiful well pools from which the city takes its name), Dragon’s Lair play area, guided tours, children’s trails and workshops and a café with the best views in Wells! Multi media tours of the Palace building are also included with admission with the choice of an adult version or one tailored for a more family audience including quizzes, treasure hunts and talking Bishops from years gone by! Visitors are guided around the Palace buildings through five narrative themes using stories, music, imagery, quizzes and talking Bishops bringing stories of their tenure and legacy at the Palace to life in an interactive and engaging way. A year-round programme of themed family events is also included with admission including a Civil War Weekend; Archery, Vikings and more! Other events are ticketed separately including summer outdoor theatre; the Palace’s Garden Fair and History Live. The Bishop’s Palace dates from the early-thirteenth century when Bishop Jocelin Trotman received a crown licence to build a residence and deer park on land to the south of the Cathedral of St Andrew. Although home to the Bishop and other families, visitors can walk in the footsteps of past bishops through a number of rooms within the Palace. Visitors are also welcome to look around the Bishop’s private Chapel and explore the ruined Great Hall. The moat has been home to mute swans since the 1800s. The tradition of swans on the moat at The Bishop’s Palace in Wells is thought to go back to the 1850’s when it is likely that a Bishop’s daughter first taught the swans to ring a bell at the Gatehouse for food. We now have two swan bells – one just beneath the window on the left of the Gatehouse, the other to the right – both with a rope hanging down for the swans to pull. The Palace Gardens are open daily from 10am until 4pm in winter and 9.30am - 5.30pm in summer although there may be restricted access due to events and activities taking place (check the website for details). There are toilets on site. Guided tours are also included with Admission – check available times at the Ticket Office on arrival. Families: There’s so much for families to do at The Bishop’s Palace, whatever the weather. Little ones love to explore the gardens, trying to spot the swans and their cygnets; there are waterfalls and springs to see, trees to climb and places to hide. Children also love to explore the magical discovery area that is the Dragon’s Lair in a far corner of the Gardens! And throughout the school holidays, there are always plenty of events to keep families busy including crafting, outdoor gardening, family trails, storytelling and more. Refreshments: The Bishop’s Table café is open daily serving delicious, locally-sourced homemade food and some of the best coffee and cake you'll find in Wells. It’s the perfect place to meet friends for breakfast, lunch and afternoon teas or Sunday Lunches are now being served! Accessibility: From the main entrance of the Palace to the Palace building, around the gardens and to the café's dining area, there is level access. We have one lift to all floors of the Palace building. The outer gardens are accessible via a bridge which is 810mm wide. There are fully accessible toilets with level access within the Stableyard area and the Palace building. There are three spaces available on site for accessible parking, however, it is necessary to book these at least 48 hours before arrival via info@bishopspalace.org.uk or call 01749 988111.
tagline: The Bishop's Palace and Gardens, Wells, Somerset is a great family day out in Somerset.

title: Glastonbury Abbey
subtitle: Glastonbury Abbey, Glastonbury, Somerset is connected with legend to a degree that is unparalleled by any other abbey in England. Since Medieval times it has held legendary status as the earliest Christian foundation in Britain linked to Joseph of Arimathea and the burial place of King Arthur.
bodyContent: Glastonbury Abbey, Glastonbury, Somerset is an internationally renowned site attracting visitors from around the world for its history, heritage, myths and legends as well as for its spiritual enrichment and there has been a church on the site for at least 1500 years with evidence of even earlier occupation. Glastonbury was the richest monastery in England at the end of the Saxon period and was second only to Westminster at the close of the middle ages. Its Abbot lived in considerable splendour and wielded tremendous power with the main surviving example of this power and wealth to be found in the Abbot’s Kitchen, one of only three surviving medieval examples in the world. It’s history is intertwined with English traditions; one of its Abbots – St Dunstan, wrote the Coronation words last used for the coronation of our present Queen Elizabeth II and William Blake’s popular “Jerusalem” is said to be written about the story that a young Jesus, accompanied by Joseph of Arimathea, visited Glastonbury . The Holy Thorn which grows at Glastonbury Abbey has become part of the legend of Joseph of Arimathea. According to the story when Joseph arrived in Britain he landed on the island of Avalon and climbed up Wearyall Hill, exhausted he thrust his staff into the ground and rested. By morning his staff had taken root and it grew into the miraculous thorn tree which flowers every Easter and Christmas. In 1191 the monks told the world they had found the bodies of King Arthur and his Queen found on the south side of the Lady Chapel. On 19th April 1278 their remains were removed in the presence of King Edward 1 and Queen Eleanor to a black marble tomb within the abbey itself. The tomb survived until the dissolution of the abbey in 1539. In 1536, during the 27 th year of the reign of Henry VIII, there were over 800 monasteries, nunneries and friaries in Britain. By 1541 there were none and the last abbot of Glastonbury , Richard Whiting was hung, drawn and quartered on Glastonbury Tor ; a brutal end for a pious man. Today it is a tranquil setting in which visitors can discover the stories behind Glastonbury Abbey with tours from costumed Living History presenters in the grounds; these tours are free but should be booked in advance for groups. A packed events calendar brings theatre, concerts, exhibitions and workshops to the abbey grounds every year and the abbey’s spectacular Night at the Abbey which last year won a national award. School and university groups can enjoy tailor-made itineraries and there are specific activities for families too. An accredited museum showcases items from the abbey’s history and gives more information about the chronology of events, archaeological finds and gives an insight into monastic life. There are 36 acres of parkland to explore with a dedicated wildlife area as well as new plans to recreate a Medieval Kitchen Garden. Groups are welcomed with a pre-booked meet and greet service available too and a special rate; driver and tour guide go free. A full access statement is on the abbey’s website – www.glastonburyabbey.com – along with maps in 14 different languages. Find us on Facebook /GlastonburyAbbeySomerset, follow us on Twitter @Glastonburyabbe or give us a call on 01458 832267. We look forward to meeting you
tagline: Glastonbury Abbey is connected with legend to a degree that is unparalleled by any other abbey

title: Kingsdon Inn
subtitle: The Kingsdon Inn is a beautiful 300 year old thatched pub, located in the small village Kingsdon in Somerset.
bodyContent: The pub used to be a Cider House many years ago, no doubt serving the locals with its own cider brew. Today the pub is hosted by Adam and Cinzia who have a wealth of experience in some of the UK's most respected hotels and restaurants. They have made food a key part of the Kingsdon's appeal. Making use of seasonal, local and often organic produce.​ The Kingsdon Inn has been known for years as the secret stop (for lunch or dinner) for travellers heading up and down the A303, as we are located just off the A303 roundabout at Podimore. (Shhh, we're not supposed to tell anyone.)
tagline: The Kingsdon Inn is a beautiful 300 year old thatched pub

title: Ring O'Bells
subtitle: Free house local pub in Somerset between Street & Glastonbury.
bodyContent: The Ring O’Bells is an 18th Century “free house” pub in the Somerset village of Ashcott near Street and Glastonbury, which for the last 29 years has been run by a family partnership. A unique pub with unique food, all prepared by us in our own kitchens. Local meat from a local butcher. Somerset produce at its best. Daily Specials blackboard including freshly made desserts. Home-made fudge with your coffee to finish! We are a genuine Free House and it is our policy to feature beers from small independent breweries, many from the West Country but occasionally also more “exotic” visitors! The range of beers varies constantly but our list of forthcoming beers features usually at least one beer from one of the local micro breweries. CAMRA Good Beer Guide 2016 CAMRA Good Pub Food Guide 2016, (star-rated, and entered in this guide for the nineteenth consecutive year). AA Pubs and Inns Guide 2016 The Good Pub Guide 2016
tagline: Free house local pub in Somerset between Street & Glastonbury.

title: The Old Post Office – Central Frome
subtitle: Situated in Frome in the Somerset region, The Victorian Post House - Central Frome is a 5-star property boasting free WiFi.
bodyContent: You’re sure to put your stamp of approval on this former post office, ideally located just a few minutes’ walk from the heart of Frome. The property has the striking and quirky appeal of a boutique hotel, with lots of homely touches that make the Old Post House a welcoming home to return to after visiting the lions of Longleat, or indulging in retail therapy in the historic City of Bath. Families, couples and friends will be left with a wealth of lasting memories after a rewarding stay at the Victorian Post House. The Old Post Office’s corner-street position echoes its past as a community hub, and today it still feels like you’re in the prime location for a Frome adventure. Enter the house through the lovingly restored shop front and door, to find a welcoming open plan living area: comfortable sofas, a dining area and modern kitchen are all easily accessible to your family and friends. Light floods in through the wall of post house windows, and the space will quickly feel like home. Relax into the fluffy cushions with a good film on Netflix or CatchUp TV, while the little ones (or big kids!) amuse themselves with the board games, toys and books provided in house.

title: Littlewell Farm Self Catering and B&B
subtitle: Littlewell Farm family run B & B and self catering in the heart of the Somerset countryside close to Cathedral city of Wells.
bodyContent: Newly converted stable sleeping 4 and a one bedroom chalet sleeping 2 alongside a charming 18th century farmhouse with B&B just 1 mile south of Wells . Beautiful Southwest facing gardens. Spectacular view of the Mendip Hills. Lots of parking. Free wifi. B&B has 4 rooms, a single, double and twin and includes locally produced cooked breakfast. There is also a self-catering option. No pets. A great base to visit Glastonbury, Wookey Hole, Cheddar, Clarks Outlet village, Longleat, Bath & Bristol Please see below for pricing information

title: Lasseter's
subtitle: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion. It serves locally sourced dishes created by a team of professional chefs.
bodyContent: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion. It serves locally sourced dishes created by a team of professional chefs. The restaurant focuses on bringing high-quality dining and great-value food to Weston, and is quickly gaining a reputation for excellent food, atmosphere and welcoming service. The restaurant boasts stunning views of Weston-super-Mare’s bay, as well as exciting menus that are based around fresh ingredients. It serves lunch and dinner from Wednesday to Saturday – including special set lunch menus and early-bird pre-theatre offers – and a carvery on Sundays from noon. Lasseter’s also serves an extensive range of cocktails, spirits and wines, with over 100 drinks to choose from. The wine list has been hand-selected by the restaurant manager, with a variety of different types and styles for all tastes. There is something for everyone at Lasseter’s. You can relax in the bar or on the terrace – with a snack if, you fancy – or enjoy a meal in our glorious restaurant overlooking the seafront.
tagline: Lasseter’s is based in the southern wing of the Winter Gardens Pavilion.

title: Blakehay Theatre Re-Opening
subtitle: The Blakehay Theatre, in Weston-super-Mare, is delighted to announce that they are re-opening in January 2022.
bodyContent: Having closed in March 2020 due to the pandemic, and after receiving a Culture Recovery Fund Grant in October 2020, the theatre staff were able to create Blakehay@Home, and stage ‘Comedy at the Quarry’ in June 2021. However, the majority of this fund was to make alterations to the theatre and in May 2021, the contractors moved into the theatre. During 2021 the contractors have been busy installing a new ventilation system and altering the backstage dressing rooms. At the same time the theatre has undergone a complete electrical re-wire making the theatre future-proof and helping with the theatre’s carbon footprint. Work on the theatre is now in the last stages of completion and will re-open to the public in January 2022 with the first performance performed by Weston Operatic Society juniors, OPPITTS, with their aptly named show ‘Opening Up’ with songs from all your favourite shows from stage and screen on Saturday 29 th and Sunday 30 th January, tickets on sale now. The studios will be re-opening in week commencing Monday 10 th January with the return of our Community Classes, including a few new classes for 2022. Check out the theatre website for more information. “We are so happy to be opening the theatre bringing live performances back. It has been a tough couple of years, not just for us but for the whole industry. The pandemic has impacted heavily on theatre and we hope that 2022 will be our busiest year yet. We have an amazing variety of shows and we are confident that there is something for everyone. We can’t wait to welcome people back into this beautiful building, there really is nothing like sitting in a theatre and watching live performance.” – Sally Heath, Theatre Manager. As an important venue in the heart of Weston-super-Mare the Blakehay Theatre will be welcoming back local groups to perform on the stage as well as professional productions that were postponed from 2020. “The small but beautiful Blakehay Theatre is the town’s own theatre, owned by the people of our town through the town council. It is wonderful to see it reopening after nearly 2 years and a refurbishment and I’m definitely going to take the opportunity to see a show in early 2022.” Malcolm Nicholson, Town Clerk The Blakehay Theatre is an approved venue to be able to use the industry-wide ‘See it Safely’ mark, so you can feel confident and safe knowing that our venue is COVID-secure and will be following the latest government guidance. If you would like to see the work that has been done at the theatre, there will be an open day on Saturday 22 nd January 2022 from 10am to 4pm . Everyone is welcome to pop in and have a look around the theatre as well as buy tickets to our upcoming shows and events. For further information and to book your tickets, please visit the theatre’s website www.blakehaytheatre.co.uk
tagline: The Blakehay Theatre, in Weston-super-Mare, is delighted to announce that they are re-opening

title: Ecohustler - eco shop and nature inspired art gallery
subtitle: Ecohustler is an online ecologically proactive media company that has been running since 2009. We run projects and campaigns in the office and also find, review and sell cool eco brands. People are welcome to come and find out more. We have a fantastic art exhibition on at the moment with lots of great local artists.
bodyContent: Ecohustler is an independent online magazine with a global reach of millions. Our mission is to bring people unexpected, entertaining, ecological content with a focus on connecting with nature and each other, so that we can all become a part of the solution to environmental breakdown. We want to connect with a massive global audience in innovative ways, disrupting the mainstream narrative. We will contribute to the significant numbers of people shifting to a more ecological worldview and provide information, links and tools to empower them to live more in harmony with nature. At Ecohustler, we passionately believe that it is possible and practical to purposely shift to an exciting new world in which human needs are better met without driving the Sixth Mass Extinction. Environmentalism doesn’t have to be doom and gloom and guilt ridden messages about what we shouldn’t do. Our version of green is way more fun than that. We see a more equitable future in which people work less and spend more time with their friends and families in communities being creative. Ultimately, we feel that people won’t change because we tell them to. People will change because we offer a brighter future… and throw better parties. Underpinning everything we do is a deep love of nature and of the animals, plants and other organisms that we share this amazing planet with. There is no more important work right now then restoring ecological systems and we are the people to do it. Thank you for being a part of the journey.

title: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm
subtitle: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is a conservation charity and the largest zoo in Somerset with over 100 species of animals. The multi award winning Zoo is open 7 days a week and aims to make Noah's Ark a place of joy, wonder, adventure and refreshment that supports the well-being of all visitors, staff and volunteers. Through education and fun, they aim to inspire and motivate this generation and the next to consider sustainable lifestyles and care for our planet.
bodyContent: Amazing Animals The home of the big Zoo animals! Visit Noah’s Ark and come face to face with a cheeky mob of meerkats, be awed by African elephants and dazzled by the zebra herd! Experience the majestic beauty and see the skies come alive during the daily birds of prey displays! The Wings of Wonder display showcases the owls, hawks, falcons and eagles in an unforgettably mesmerizing spectacle. Indoor and Outdoor Adventures Play and adventure never stops with our 10 play areas across the 100-acre site. Enjoy the huge indoor play barns including under 5’s soft play and a giant rainbow slide. The Zoo also has accessible play equipment including nest swings and a wheelchair accessible roundabout. Fancy an a-maze-ing adventure? Navigate through Britain’s longest hedge maze. The British wildlife themed maze has 3.4km of paths and wooden nest tower at the center. Keep the whole family smiling and active all day, whatever the weather! Accessibility Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is proud to be an accessible attraction. Facilities include multiple accessible toilets, Changing Places facility, accessible play equipment, hearing loops and more. Please visit the website before your visit for up-to-date information and to view the Access guide. Prices Buy online and save! Noah’s Ark recommends that all tickets, including those for free essential carers and under 2’s are purchased online prior to your arrival. Prices are seasonal, please check the website for up-to-date ticket prices. Food and Drink With a range of delicious hot and cold food and drink options available in our Food Barn and convenient snack kiosks across the Zoo, there is something for everyone! Alternatively, visitors are very welcome to bring their own lunch and enjoy it in one of our many picnic spots. Mini Experiences Noah’s Ark offers incredible up-close mini experiences with Meerkats, Capybara, Andean Bears and Giant Tortoise. You will enjoy 20 minutes behind the scenes with the keeper, learn some interesting facts and get involved with their feeding and enrichment programme. Pre-book your experience online to ensure availability. Minimum age and terms and conditions apply. Animal Experiences Find out what it’s like to be a keeper for the day with our one-to-one keeper experiences before the zoo opens. Experiences include: African Elephants, Junior Keeper Experience, and Giraffe and Rhino experience.
tagline: You’ll be amazed at the variety of nature you’ll see with over 100 species of animals

title: New House Farm (West Country Parks)
subtitle: New House Farm in Walrow is located within a 5-minute drive of the coastal resort of Burnham-on-Sea with miles of golden sandy beaches, shops and amusement activities to enjoy. All facilities are located on the ground floor and each cottage consists of a multi-purpose living room/breakfast area/kitchen, 1-2 bedrooms and a family bathroom;
bodyContent: Located on the fringes of the Somerset Levels , New House Farm is home to 26 l uxury timber holiday lodges and is the ideal holiday park for visitors who want to explore the great outdoors and enjoy country walks whilst experiencing easy access to the entire South West . The seaside town of Burnham-on-Sea is just a short drive from the park, with miles of golden sandy beaches, shops and amusement activities to enjoy. All facilities are located on the ground floor and each cottage consists of a multi-purpose living room/breakfast area/kitchen, 1-2 bedrooms and a family bathroom; Our selection of self-catering holiday cottages offers options to suit parties of 2-4. Kingfisher Cottage sleeps two, boasting a four-poster bedroom with en-suite. Woodpecker Cottage sleeps 3 (one double and one single). Kestrel Cottage sleeps four (one double and one twin). Each cottage is fully equipped with all the necessities that you will need to enjoy your stay with us including gas central heating, digital TV, electric cooker, microwave, cooking utensils, towels, bed linen, hairdryer and an iron and ironing board. Guests also have access to private parking, a shared laundry with coin operated washer/dryers and a shared grass courtyard with outdoor seating area – the perfect place to relax with a glass of wine.
tagline: New House Farm in Walrow is located within a 5-minute drive of the coastal resort of Burnham-on-Sea

title: RHL Beach Race
subtitle: The Weston Beach Race is one of the most eagerly-anticipated events in the town's annual calendar and has to be seen to be believed.
bodyContent: The Weston Beach Race is one of the most eagerly-anticipated events in the town's annual calendar and has to be seen to be believed. Watch the thrills and drama unfold over two days of high-octane motorsport action as the daredevil riders take on the challenging six-mile course in what has been described as the maddest, baddest and biggest event in the UK off-road calendar. The beach is transformed into a giant race track for motorsport's equivalent of the London Marathon where brave amateur and professional riders battle it out for glory in front of the excited crowds. There are junior races, quad racing, side car races in addition to the much-heralded main event. The drama is guaranteed from the moment the riders rev up for the 2km straight start along the beach before turning to tackle an array of man-made sand dunes, tight corners and challenges on what is recognised as the toughest sand track anywhere in the world. The RHL Activities event, which is also known as the Enduro, is so spectacular it was shortlisted in the final three alongside the Tour of Britain for the honour of being the sporting event of the year. Opening Times RHL Beach Race22 Sept 2023 - 24 Sept 2023 Saturday 09:00 - 16:00 Sunday 10:00 - 16:00
tagline: The Weston Beach Race is one of the most eagerly-anticipated events

title: Cheddar
subtitle: On the edge of the Somerset Levels, Cheddar’s elevation soars 500 feet to the top of Cheddar Gorge. Home to the country’s highest inland cliffs, Cheddar boasts one of Great Britain's most impressive landmarks alongside world-famous produce.
bodyContent: Things to do in Cheddar, Somerset - Visitors to the village of Cheddar and Cheddar Gorge have been astounded by Cheddar’s magnificent limestone Gorge for centuries. Cheddar Gorge can be viewed from the public road running through the ravine or by footpaths along the top of the cliffs where you can drink in spectacular 360° views of the Mendip Hills . Formed over one million years ago during the last ice age, Cheddar Gorge and Cheddar Caves are available to explore and are home to prehistoric findings including Britain’s oldest complete skeleton, the Cheddar Man. Unsurprisingly, Somerset’s impressive gorge boasts three impressive titles: a Site of Special Scientific Interest, a Special Area of Conservation, and an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. However, it’s not just the iconic landscape that puts Cheddar on the map: Cheddar cheese is world famous and the traditional method of cheese making can still be seen at the Cheddar Gorge Cheese Company . Before you leave, stop at the gift shop to pick up authentic Cheddar cheese - matured in Cheddar’s Gough's Cave itself. Head down to the Lower Gorge and village for gentle riverside walks, quaint tearooms, and a variety of restaurants and cafés. Cheddar village boasts ancient architecture including the remains of a saxon palace, old market cross and Minster Church as well as charming gift shops, toy museum and crazy golf course. Nearby Cheddar reservoir is a fantastic place to spot wildlife or take a gentle bike ride. If you’re looking for a longer cycle route, take The Strawberry Line’s 10-mile path from Cheddar to Yatton. The former railway line opened in 1869 and was essential for transporting famous Cheddar strawberries, as well as passengers - making it the ideal way to take in stunning Somerset landscapes.

title: Yeovil
subtitle: Known as Ivell in Thomas Hardy’s Wessex, Yeovil is mentioned in the Domesday Book as a thriving market community and is still a country town at heart surrounded by beautiful countryside. An important centre for the leather industry in the 19th century, the town is famous for its glove-making with its football club nick-named the Glovers and for making helicopters. It has numerous shops, a country park, theatre and entertainment centre. Settled in ancient times on a major Roman route through the
bodyContent: Its strategic position on the Fosse Way (now A37) between Dorchester and Ilchester was vital to the Romans, and makes it easy to reach for you. The name just means ‘town on the river’, which goes for most places round here, but no two Somerset towns are alike, and you’ll find that its character is unique. Throughout Saxon and medieval times the town continued to thrive. A market charter from King John, who took a big interest in Somerset, guaranteed its status as the local farming centre. While most Somerset towns surrounded by upland grazing went in for wool, Yeovil developed the speciality of glove making, and the name still survives in the nickname of ‘giant killers’ Yeovil Football Club – the glovers. These days the gloves are off, and you can’t buy a pair made in the town. We can probably fix you up with a helicopter or two, as military equipment is the town’s biggest export, and Leonardo Helicopters the biggest employer. Yeovil is one of these towns which is much bigger than it appears. You can ramble for what seems like miles through the historic centre, built around the noble C14 church of St John the Baptist, passing many fine old buildings, and not passing up many shopping opportunities. There’s a theatre, all sorts of arts and crafts, and the famous football club. If you remember Stephen Potter’s Lifemanship books from the 1950s, they’re based on Yeovil, which Thomas Hardy had previously recreated as Ivell. These days Yeovil only has two railway stations, a comedown from its original four, but it’s on the A37 and A30, a stone’s throw from the A303. Easily accessible for visitors with disabilities, low counter, hearing loop. A pay and display car park is situated at the rear of the building. title: West Somerset Railway
subtitle: West Somerset Railway, Somerset, is a heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton. It is the longest independent railway in Britain, (20 miles).
bodyContent: West Somerset Railway, Somerset is the longest Heritage line in the United Kingdom. Time Table can be seen HERE for 2024 The line is situated in Somerset, four miles outside the County town of Taunton , starting at Bishops Lydeard and finishing at Minehead . The line meanders through the Quantock Hills , an area of outstanding natural beauty and along the Bristol Channel Coast. We have 10 stations along the line each having something different to offer. There are various historic sites that may be of interest to visitors to the area, for example Crowcombe Heathfield station was the location for the filming of the Beatles’ “A Hard Days Night” and scenes from “The Land Girls” were also shot here. The historic town of Watchet dates back to Saxon times, and boasts narrow streets, local shops, museums and lots of places to eat and drink. Washford is a great place to alight, just a short walk from the station we have Cleeve Abbey and the Torre Cider Farm, which are both well worth a visit. Fancy something a little different then why not visit Dunster Castle which is nestled in the medieval village of Dunster ? Dunster also has a working Watermill , the Old Yarn Market building and the Dolls Museum or continue on to Minehead home of our final station. Minehead is situated at the foot of North Hill where the beach is literally right across the road, we have cafes, shops and plenty of arcades along the seafront, making this a go to location. The West Somerset Railway also have combined tickets on selected dates throughout the year. These include, Cream Tea and Cheese and cider specials and linked trips with Hestercombe Gardens and Dunster Castle. We organise Steam Galas in the Spring and Autumn, and we are host to a Diesel Gala too. In the latter part of the year we have our popular Christmas services, we have Santa services running out of Minehead and Bishops Lydeard from the end of November until Christmas Eve, we also have our Sherry and Mince pie specials for you to enjoy.
tagline: Heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton.

title: Phil Bowditch Finest Fresh Fish
subtitle: Established by Phil Bowditch and his wife Christine in 1979, Phil Bowditch Fish Shop have made their name supplying the freshest, Brixham fish to the people of Taunton.
bodyContent: Son Harry Bowditch has stepped in and, to uphold the shop’s reputation for quality, he sets his alarm for a 4am trip to Brixham to buy straight off of the boats.
tagline: Supplying the freshest, Brixham fish to the people of Taunton.

title: Inspired
subtitle: We are a family-run workshop. We have a wide range of activities for children and adults to give everyone the opportunity to experiment with different crafts and materials.
bodyContent: We are a family-run workshop which offers a relaxed and friendly environment for all ages to get imaginative.We have a wide range of activities for children and adults to give everyone the opportunity to experiment with different crafts and materials. Feel free to visit anytime and select projects to try or why not take advantage of some of our workshops and parties. If you're looking for a party that brings out your inner creative, this is the venue. With a wide range of projects to choose from your party will be filled with unique and memorable treasures. Our children's parties are 2 hours long, 1.5 hours of crafting, the remainder for the food and the all important cake. We customise each party to suit the birthday child's request. Our hen parties are a lovely exprience for the bride to be and her friends; with activities such as creating paper flower crowns or making your own bunting for the wedding. In addition to this we have a large range of workshops available for all different crafts, abilities and age groups!
tagline: We are a family-run workshop where you can experiment with different crafts and materials.

title: Granny Smiths
subtitle: Greengrocers in Taunton, selling locally sourced produce.
bodyContent: We are a high quality greengrocers and have been established for 40years. We sell fresh produce sourced locally and from the wholesale market. Our approachable and helpful staff are always on hand to help you. So if you are looking to eat healthier and support your local community come along and take a look!
tagline: Greengrocers in Taunton, selling locally sourced produce.

title: Glastonbury Farmers’ Market
subtitle: While Glastonbury is widely known for its musical festival it was also the host of the first Somerset Farmers’ Markets in 1999!
bodyContent: While Glastonbury is widely known for its musical festival it was also the host of the first Somerset Farmers’ Markets in 1999! With stalls located around Market Cross, visitors are in the perfect position to not only explore the market but also many of Glastonbury’s unique range of shops and cafes and even walk to the top of Glastonbury Tor. Goods regularly on offer at this market: Fruit and vegetables Preserves and chutneys Cheese Pies
tagline: While Glastonbury is widely known for its musical festival

title: The Red Lion Babcary
subtitle: Our award-winning, 17th century thatched pub and restaurant is set in the heart of this idyllic Somerset village, open every day of the year.
bodyContent: Oozing charm with traditional flagstone floors, exposed beams, open fires, cosy nooks and crannies and pretty garden. We offer everything from great local ales, inspiring à la carte menu, hearty Sunday lunch and outdoor wood-fired pizzas to individually planned weddings for up to 120 people. We are conveniently situated in a rural and peaceful location, just a few minutes north of Podimore roundabout on the A303 in Somerset, off the A37. Accessible down a winding country lane, you will stumble across us, past the village Church, open fields and a handful of stone cottages. We are very much a locals’ pub, welcoming familiar faces into our rural watering hole to sit, chat, eat and drink in these beautiful surroundings. Equally we love to see new faces who might be visiting this beautiful county – looking for their own ‘escape to the country’. The Red Lion is an ideal stopover point for lunch or an overnight stay on the way to Devon and Cornwall or back to London and the home counties.
tagline: Our award-winning, 17th century thatched pub and restaurant

title: The King Alfred
subtitle: At the King Alfred you will find wonderful freshly prepared pub food, a fine selection of wines and ales and a warm welcome from your hosts.
bodyContent: The King Alfred also offers a selection of well-appointed guest rooms so you can relax and stay with us as well. King Alfred was one of England’s most famous and respected Kings who had close links to this area of Somerset. We are delighted to have named the pub in his memory and we have lots of historic memorabilia on the walls for our customers to view. You can be guaranteed a warm welcome from Paul and the team and we hope you will come and visit us soon!
tagline: At the King Alfred you will find wonderful freshly prepared pub food

title: The Georgian Manor - Central Frome
subtitle: A striking boutique-style apartment within a grand Georgian manor house, this homestay has the feel of a luxury country hotel, but with the freedom of your own private bolthole in town.
bodyContent: The Georgian Manor in Frome is perfectly situated to give you the best of both worlds: it’s located just a pleasant ten minute walk from the vibrant town centre of Frome, and a short drive from scenic Somerset rambles and inspiring cultural attractions. The ideal decadent retreat for a cultural break or romantic getaway. The space The apartment is a glorious mix of old and new styles, decorated throughout with distinctive statement artwork and ornaments, while retaining the grand magnificence of the eighteenth century building. The original window shutters, cast iron radiators and ornate plasterwork echo the history of the property, while touches of modern luxury such as chandeliers, ornate mirrors and a roll top bath lend an air of opulent decadence. Enter the Georgian Manor through the grand entrance hall, or direct from your private parking area to the rear. The apartment is laid out on one level with a spacious open plan living area, which is bathed in natural light thanks to the double-aspect floor to ceiling sash windows and balcony doors. A particular highlight of the Georgian Manor is the ornate wrought iron balcony, accessed through the patio doors beyond the seating area. The balcony overlooks the communal garden area, and is the perfect place to savour a croissant and coffee for breakfast, or a Somerset sunset at dusk. A compact and well-equipped kitchen to your right boasts an integrated breakfast bar, cooker and washing machine. Chat to your friends or partner relaxing on the leather sofas while you rustle up a Frome feast of local produce. Beyond the kitchen area you will find a classically decorated bathroom, complete with Grecian-style floor tiles and a sumptuous roll top bath. And then finally, the bedroom awaits at the front of the house. After a restorative night’s sleep on the kingsize bed, in Egyptian cotton sheets on a luxurious Vispring mattress , you will wake to a room bathed in glorious sunshine from the grand sash windows. A stay at the Georgian Manor leaves you feeling relaxed and pampered by boutique-style luxury in a homely setting. Guest access The Georgian Manor is accessible via a few stone steps from ground level at the front door. The entire property is on one level, and is wheelchair accessible and suitable for guests with limited mobility. Accompanying guests are welcome to book The Luxury Georgian Apartment, which is located in the same building, which has an entrance just a few steps from that of the Georgian Manor. Other things to note Notes on our cleaning procedures For your comfort and peace of mind we are spending an extra hour at each property prior to arrival, to ensure all touch surfaces are disinfected in line with government recommendations (see here). All sheets and towels are laundered thoroughly at high temperatures with quality non-biological laundry soap.

title: Worth House
subtitle: Located in the beautiful Somerset countryside, close to the medieval city of Wells, Worth House dates back 400 years.
bodyContent: Worth House, a 16th-century former farmhouse near Wells, offers stunning Mendip Hills and farmland views. Ideally placed for Wookey Hole Caves, Glastonbury and Cheddar Gorge, with country pubs nearby including The Pheasant. Enjoy the cosy living room, garden views, and warm hospitality from hosts Sarah and Nick.

title: ‘Tiffany’s Restaurant at The Grand Pier’
subtitle: Make your visit to the seaside truly unforgettable by indulging in the breathtaking panoramic views from Weston-super-Mare’s most picturesque restaurant, Tiffany's.
bodyContent: Situated at the farthest point out to sea, Tiffany’s Restaurant is a charming, Edwardian-style restaurant that boasts breath-taking panoramic views of the bay. From traditional Fish & Chips to a delightful Afternoon Tea for two, the Tiffany’s menu offers a wide selection to satisfy everyone’s cravings.

title: The Playhouse in Weston super Mare
subtitle: The Playhouse Theatre is available for hire for both community and professional shows and as a venue for conferences, meetings and corporate events. In addition to the main auditorium the theatres facilities include a licensed bar, meeting and rehearsal spaces and full disabled access.
bodyContent: Located in the centre of Weston-Super-Mare the Playhouse is a friendly and welcoming 664-seat theatre which offers a lively and diverse programme of events to meet the entertainment, creative and educational requirements of its local and surrounding community. The Playhouse’s high quality programme of professional and community events includes around 300 performances per year including music, drama, comedy, dance, musicals, film, children’s shows, pantomime and more recently West End Productions. The Playhouse Theatre is available for hire for both community and professional shows and as a venue for conferences, meetings and corporate events. In addition to the main auditorium the theatres facilities include a licensed bar, meeting and rehearsal spaces and full disabled access. Our dedicated and professional staff are used to working with all visiting companies and hirers to ensure a successful event while our welcoming and caring front of house team ensure patrons an enjoyable entertainment experience. The Playhouse Theatre is managed by Parkwood Theatres working in partnership with North Somerset Council.

title: DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House
subtitle: Great motorway links M5 junction 20 & 21 Bristol International Airport only 12 minutes away Bristol City Centre only 25 minutes away. With local access to Cheddar Gorge and Mendip AONB only 45 minutes away.
bodyContent: Welcome to DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House, the South West’s finest four-star boutique hotel and spa. An enchanting venue set within rolling English countryside, Cadbury House is the ideal backdrop for your special occasion whether a wedding, private party, business event, spa break or dining experience. With truly breath-taking views across North Somerset and the Bristol Channel, Cadbury House effortlessly combines old and new, with the traditional country house and the elegant boutique-style hotel. There is also an onsite Marco Pierre White Steakhouse Bar & Grill, an award-winning health club and a renowned spa. The hotel offers 132 luxury bedrooms including suites, on-site parking and excellent transport access meaning guests can enjoy the facilities for both business and pleasure. Please note from May 1 st , 2022 overnight parking will be chargeable at £5.00 per vehicle. Corporate customers are also well catered for with 12 meeting rooms, multiple breakout areas, and a dedicated conference team on hand. Whether you are hosting a small business meeting to a multi-day conference, DoubleTree by Hilton Cadbury House does not disappoint as a destination location for business needs.
tagline: The South West’s finest four-star boutique hotel and spa.

title: The Globe Inn
subtitle: This gorgeous pub is set in the cathedral city of Wells.
bodyContent: Set in the cathedral city of Wells, just south of the mendip hills, The Globe Inn is a traditional 300+ year old family run pub. Known for its craft ales, homemade food and cosy atmosphere, The Globe Inn is the perfect place to stop off for lunch, an evening meal or to host your own party in our spacious function room. All ingredients are locally sourced from George's Garden and RD Johns. Our Ales are also from local business' like Cheddar Ales. So if you are in wells or close by, why not come in and visit our friendly team.

title: New House Farm (West Country Parks)
subtitle: New House Farm in Walrow is located within a 5-minute drive of the coastal resort of Burnham-on-Sea with miles of golden sandy beaches, shops and amusement activities to enjoy. All facilities are located on the ground floor and each cottage consists of a multi-purpose living room/breakfast area/kitchen, 1-2 bedrooms and a family bathroom;
bodyContent: Located on the fringes of the Somerset Levels , New House Farm is home to 26 l uxury timber holiday lodges and is the ideal holiday park for visitors who want to explore the great outdoors and enjoy country walks whilst experiencing easy access to the entire South West . The seaside town of Burnham-on-Sea is just a short drive from the park, with miles of golden sandy beaches, shops and amusement activities to enjoy. All facilities are located on the ground floor and each cottage consists of a multi-purpose living room/breakfast area/kitchen, 1-2 bedrooms and a family bathroom; Our selection of self-catering holiday cottages offers options to suit parties of 2-4. Kingfisher Cottage sleeps two, boasting a four-poster bedroom with en-suite. Woodpecker Cottage sleeps 3 (one double and one single). Kestrel Cottage sleeps four (one double and one twin). Each cottage is fully equipped with all the necessities that you will need to enjoy your stay with us including gas central heating, digital TV, electric cooker, microwave, cooking utensils, towels, bed linen, hairdryer and an iron and ironing board. Guests also have access to private parking, a shared laundry with coin operated washer/dryers and a shared grass courtyard with outdoor seating area – the perfect place to relax with a glass of wine.
tagline: New House Farm in Walrow is located within a 5-minute drive of the coastal resort of Burnham-on-Sea

title: Frome Boulder Rooms
subtitle: Bouldering is a discipline of climbing that needs no ropes, harnesses or even anyone else to climb with. This makes it very beginner friendly as there’s no need for any equipment and you can make your session as social as you like!
bodyContent: Opening September 2021, Frome's purpose-built bouldering centre was imagined from the team’s love of climbing and the outdoor lifestyle. After years of travelling, climbing and working all over the place, we decided to combine our passions and know-how into a new active community space in Frome. With a dedicated kids wall, training areas, and over 150 problems to try, we welcome climbers at any level, from beginners to experts, young and old. We have climbing suitable for all ages and abilities, and a range of clubs and courses for those who would like to take part in an instructed session. Our onsite café serves hot and cold drinks, cakes and snacks for those energy slumps mid-climb!
