title: Westons, Golden Jubilee Restaurant
subtitle: Our award winning Golden Jubilee Restaurant in Weston Super Mare, Somerset epitomises the elegant Regency style for which Weston was formally renowned. Open to both residents and non-residents this proves to be a very popular eatery to all.
bodyContent: Our award winning Golden Jubilee Restaurant epitomises the elegant Regency style for which Weston was formally renowned. Open to both residents and non-residents this proves to be a very popular eatery to all. Breakfast We are proud to be presented with the Enjoy England’s Breakfast Award, which we have achieved year after year. Only about 8% of guest accommodation have received this award, recognizing hotels and B&Bs that offer a quality and varied choice of breakfast and high level of service and hospitality. We offer breakfast fit for a king, with our continental buffet-style banquet, followed by either a traditional cooked to order Full English Breakfast, steak and eggs, omelettes or choose from our lighter options such as filled bagels and fish dishes. With unlimited tea and coffee readily available this will most definitely be the best start to your day. Lunch & Dinner In these captivating surroundings you can enjoy dishes carefully selected for our appealing À la Carte menu which has been designed by our Head Chef to tempt and excite all tastes. With our menu changing with the season you are guaranteed that our kitchen only use the best local ingredients allowing our dishes to be full of flavour and goodness! Our cuisine is classic British with a twist of French infusion, offering a variety of fresh fish & meat dishes, steaks and grills along with vegetarian and vegan options. Our famous Carvery is available on Tuesdays, Thursdays and of course Sundays offering a choice of freshly cooked joints of meat accompanied by a selection of garden vegetables, Roasted Potatoes and all the trimmings. Afternoon Tea Appetites are indulged with an afternoon tea for two or four, which pleases palates with a selection of sandwiches and a pot of tea for each person. The sweet edge is provided in the form of homemade scones with dollops of clotted cream and jam, plus a slice of traditional English Victoria Sponge. Guests also have the option to include a glass of Prosecco for a fizzy twist.
tagline: Open to both residents and non-residents this proves to be a very popular eatery to all.

title: The Helicopter Museum
subtitle: The Helicopter Museum is the largest dedicated Helicopter Collection in the World with over 100 helicopters on display in an all weather undercover hangar. Exhibits include two of the Queen's Royal Flight helicopters, the current world speed record holder G-LYNX, a Vietnam Veteran Huey and a Russian Hind Gun Ship.
bodyContent: In addition to over 100 helicopters, the Helicopter Museum includes other breathtaking attractions like its WWII Pilots’ Block, Weston Aviation Exhibition and Blood Hound Missile. This all contributes to a fun day-out for all the family with plenty of opportunity to learn about these marvellous machines and their huge impact on Somerset’s history. The museum hosts various special events throughout the year. These include various car shows, hair-rasing Halloween hilarity and festive Christmas events. The most popular of these special events are the World At War Weekend and Balloons, Birds & Bubbles . At these events, the museum is completely transformed to provide visitors the opportunity to enjoy authentic military vehicles or hold a live owl! Those who haven’t had their fill of aviation history can also attend one of the museum’s open cockpit days. Here visitors can climb into the pilot’s seat of a genuine helicopter and be taken through the controls by an experienced volunteer, many of whom have spent their careers flying such aircraft. Those who really want to feel the thrill of soaring high up in the clouds can even book their seat on one of the many helicopter experience flights the museum offers throughout the year. After all that excitement, visitors can refuel in the museum’s new café which was opened as part of a new visitor service building in July 2020. It offers drinks, snacks and tasty lunches. A particular highlight is the pilots’ all-day breakfast that is big enough to satisfy even the hungriest aviation superfan!
tagline: The Helicopter Museum is the largest dedicated Helicopter Collection in the World

title: Sandy Glade Holiday Park
subtitle: Sandy Glade Holiday Park in Burnham-on-Sea in Somerset boasts plenty of facilities & open, green space for the kids to run free.
bodyContent: Sandy Glade: Sandy Glade Holiday Park in Burnham-on-Sea in Somerset boasts plenty of open, green space for the kids to run free, a fantastic indoor pool with water jets and fountains and an adventure playground so they can let off steam while you relax. In the evenings take a trip to our clubhouse for fun and games and a great entertainment line up. A hop, skip and a jump across the road and its through the dunes onto a long expanse of golden beach where you can feel the sand between your toes and enjoy a 99 ice cream for that perfect UK seaside holiday experience. Just a short drive from the park are the bright lights of the fun fair at Brean Leisure Park, whizz yourself dizzy on the Waltzers, send your tummy tumbling on the Roller Coaster or bump and bash on the Dodgems. Sandy Meadows : Accessed via a quiet lane is Sandy Meadows lodge park, a stunning development of 40 lodges with countryside views. Here you have the peace and tranquillity of a small site yet are only a couple of minutes from sister park Sandy Glade, where you can enjoy all of the park facilities including indoor pool and clubroom. The lodges offer a top of the range holiday experience where you can spread out and enjoy the luxury of extra space, sit out on your private veranda and watch the world go by, or unwind in your very own hot tub.The park is in a fantastic location, just over the road from the beach and within easy reach of some famous beauty spots such as Brean Downs, Cheddar Gorge and Wells, with its historic cathedral. ​​​​​
tagline: Sandy Glade Holiday Park in Burnham-on-Sea in Somerset boasts plenty of facilities & open.

title: Camerton
subtitle: Camerton is home to about 600 people living in 258 dwellings spread over a large geographical area (2 miles by 2 miles).
bodyContent: Camerton is home to about 600 people living in 258 dwellings spread over a large geographical area (2 miles by 2 miles). It lies in the heart of the Cam Valley with the SNCI Cam Brook running through. With its geographical location in the east/west running Cam Valley, steep sided hills run to the north and south from the valley plain. The Cam Brook flows through Camerton. Key Views and Landmarks Camerton Batch Local Nature Reserve, an award winning feature of the parish managed by local volunteers. New Pit Batch Ancient monuments – Iron Age Fort, Anglo Saxon Burial Ground and a Roman settlement. The church the oldest part of which dates back to the 15th century Camerton Court - This magnificent house was designed by G.S Repton who gave it the classical Greek revival style, built by John Jarrett, the local estate and coal mine owner. The Limestone Link National Footpath runs east/west through the parish centre SNCI Cam Brook The Powder House Community Hall and associated playing field. In the past Camerton has accommodated a canal and railway both used to transport coal with the result that many of the older more traditional houses are former miners’ cottages. Positive Features and Special Qualities A mainly green and open parish with many beautiful vistas Children’s Play Area Extensive network of public rights of way Coal mining and railway heritage legacy – e.g. as well as the Local Nature Reserve and the New Pit Batch mentioned above the old coal mining tramway known as the Drammyway, the remains of the Somerset Coal Canal, the Old Miners canteen and the Camerton Branch Line. Interesting historical figures. These include Reverend John Skinner who was one of the most renowned rectors of St Peter’s Church Camerton. Reverend John Skinner was a learned antiquarian, an artist, poet, scholar and a dutiful country priest. He is best known for his journals; he kept a diary of the harsh everyday life in Camerton. Also William Smith who was known as ‘Strata’ Smith as he made the connection between fossils and the layer of rocks in which they were embedded. It is believed that during the time he was working in the Cam valley on surveying of the canal he devised his principles of the science of Geology. He published the first Geological map of England and Wales in 1815 and is known as the ‘Father of Stratigraphy’ and ‘Father of English Geology’. Information on Reverend Skinner, William Smith and Camerton Court courtesy of Julieann Biggs

title: Ilminster
subtitle: Ilminster takes its name from the River Ile and the Minster church dating from 1450. The town grew up around the church and some of the oldest buildings are close to the churchyard including the grammar school founded in 1549.
bodyContent: In Victorian times the town was an important staging post for travellers with east-west and north-south routes converging there. Market Square has a colonnaded market cross rebuilt in 1813 and is surrounded by handsome buildings. Ilminster is an attractive and peaceful town with a good variety of shops, a theatre and enchanting street names like Strawberry Bank. Must See and Do Indulge in retail therapy at shops like Dyers - a traditional drapers Enjoy the latest art at the Meeting House Arts Centre with coffee and a cake or lunch Find ancient and modern at the 15th century Minster with engraved glass doors added for the Millenium Watch the latest production at the Warehouse Theatre Sample cider and discover how it's made at Perry's Cider Mill in Dowlish Wake Learn something different at Dillington House where an exciting range of courses, concerts and events is on offer Stretch your legs on the Stopline Way - walk details from the Information Centre Local Facilities Accommodation Library Petrol Station Pharmacy Post Office Pubs and eating places Supermarket and range of small shops Road Directions lminster is 10 miles south east of Taunton and the M5 Maps: Multimap Rail: Nearest stations are Taunton and Crewkerne Bus: for routes and timetables got to the https://www.visitsomerset.co.uk/plan-your-visit/travel/

title: Taunton Country Market
subtitle: Taunton Country Market is a cooperatively run shop, selling a range of locally made produce. We supply fresh local food, plants and crafts, lovingly handmade by our members.
bodyContent: Available products include baked goods and preserves, fruit and vegetables, plants and flowers, a range of handmade craft and much more available in shop and made to order. The Shop: Taunton Country Market is found in Bath Place in Taunton. This busy, historic thoroughfare is home to a diverse and special collection of shops – our shop is a co-operative, built up as a team of local artisans, gardeners, florists, apple pressers, bee keepers, bakers, jam and chutney makers. The shop houses all sorts of goods made by local independent producers to supply local people with homegrown and homemade quality produce. Our market in Taunton is part of the National Country Markets Ltd which incorporates over 450 various markets around England, Wales and the Channel Islands. Home made: A wide selection of fresh, local handmade produce is available throughout the week. Chutneys, jams, marmalades and honey are regular shelf inhabitants, as well as a deli supplying local cheeses, meat and eggs. A varying range of sweet and savoury treats are a favourite, from cakes and biscuits to savoury quiches, and scones. If you have any allergy requirements, our team of bakers are happy to take orders to suit your dietary needs – please contact the shop or pop in to talk to one of our many lovely bakers who will do their best to cater for your tummy. Special Occasions: We are also in the company of bakers and sugar crafters who can help to make a celebration cake for any special occasion and qualifed florists who can cater for your weddings, funerals and special occasions – please pop in or contact the shop with enquiries. Home grown: An assortment of local home grown produce is available. Fresh, seasonal fruit and vegetables, beautiful posies of flowers, plants of various kinds. Craft: The Craft Department is home to a diverse collection of local artisans making all sorts of unique decorative objects alongside more functional and practical everyday items, all produced (by hand) with loving care. Many of our makers are available to custom meet your requirements – colour, size and quantity are examples of regular requests for custom orders.
tagline: Supplying fresh local food, plants and crafts, lovingly handmade by our members.

title: Izzi Stockton
subtitle: With over 18 years experience as a Bridal Dressmaker, Izzi understands how to help you achieve the perfect look for your big day.
bodyContent: Bridal Gowns Izzi Stockton Bridal in Taunton stocks a great range of beautiful bridal dresses from top UK Designers, Veromia’s Sonsie collecton, Callista Bride and Tiffany’s Jessica Grace Bridal, with prices starting from £300! We have bridal gowns from sizes 10-30 and specialise in gowns for Plus Size Brides. All dresses are altered and fitted in house so that they fit you perfectly, and we can be store your gown until you are ready to collect up to the day before your wedding. With a wide range of Bridesmaids dresses, Junior Bridesmaids and Flower Girls available, you can be sure to find the right dresses for your wedding. Appointments are recommended but not always necessary. Prom Promise Izzi keeps a record of every Prom dress sold ensuring that no two identical dresses go to the same Prom. With dresses from Tiffany’s Illusion collection, Mascara, Goya London, Gino Cerruti and Angel Forever, we have a wide range of colours, styles and sizes to suit you. A great range of accessories is available to help you complete your look.

title: Hats by Janine
subtitle: With a passion for hats, Janine has 30 years experience in helping women look fabulous At Hats by Janine you can expect a warm and friendly service when choosing just the right accessories for your special event.
bodyContent: 'Hats by Janine' is a boutique in Taunton, Somerset, specialising in ladies occasion hats. There is a fabulous selection in store and online for events such as weddings, race days, garden parties and mother of the bride. If you are looking for something extra special to make your hat unique Hats by Janine offers a bespoking service adding beautiful trimmings, feathers, flowers & fabrics available in an array of colours to your chosen hat. Whether it's a modest suggestion to compliment your outfit or a bold & daring design to make a statement Hats by Janine can help you create your perfect hat. For that finishing touch we also stock beautiful LUNAR shoes with matching evening bags, gorgeous jewellery, handbags and accessories. Hats by Janine always welcome a call, or visit into the shop to see the collection. There is a lovely fitting room if you'd like to bring your occasion outfit to match it with the perfect accessories.
tagline: With a passion for hats, Janine has 30 years experience in helping women look fabulous

title: The King Alfred

bodyContent: The King Alfred also offers a selection of well-appointed guest rooms so you can relax and stay with us as well. title: Brothers Cider
subtitle: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family, who have been making cider in Somerset since 1658.
bodyContent: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family, who have been making cider in Somerset since 1658. We first started selling our Pear Cider at the Glastonbury Festival in 1995 near what was then called the Jazz World Stage. These days it is called The West Holts Stage. Over the years, festival goers kept asking us if it was possible to get our drink when the festival was over and so we decided to market it to pubs and supermarkets. Now you can get it all over the country and at many festivals. We are independent, British and are passionate about what we do. Our free-spirited essence is upheld by approaching things with a unique perspective. Here at Brothers, we take our values and commitment to sustainability very seriously, but it’s something we haven’t really shouted about until now. We have zero to landfill, all our waste is segregated to optimise the opportunity of being recycled or reused. A massive solar panel system is now installed here at the cider mill, where it will directly supply the presses with clean energy and lastly, all our left-over fruit pomace is turned into energy which helps to heat the local swimming pool!
tagline: Brothers Drinks Co was established in 1992 by four brothers from the Showering family.

title: Hide on the Hill
subtitle: We currently offer our two beautiful bed & breakfast rooms for you to enjoy and the chance to relax away from the bustle - located on the margins of the Avalon marshes near Glastonbury in Somerset.
bodyContent: The Orchard room to the north provides a vista to the Mendip Hills. It has a luxurious king size Hypnos hideaway bed with luxury cotton sheets. (17m 2 ) The Garden room faces south with views down to the levels and is decorated to enhance the luminosity of the ​Somerset sky into the room. It is a large twin room that can accommodate a child up to 5 years for additional charges. (23m 2 ) Facilities Both rooms are brand new and have large en-suite bathrooms with big showers, towels and soaps. Each room has free internet access and we have decides not to provide televisions as many guests said they ​already had good 4G signals on their network preferring to use their own devices. Facilities include a tray to make tea and coffee replenished each day, a hairdryer is available, toiletries in the en-suite to be left for the next guests . Your Stay CHECK-IN is from 4pm on the day of arrival. It really helps if you give us an approximate time to make your welcome great. You will be greeted in the conservatory with a welcoming drink and chat about how to chill after your drive. Please note that any balance on the stay must be settled after you have settled in. BREAKFAST is served between 8am and 9.30am in the dining room, but should you require an early breakfast please let us know. Later breakfasts will be in the form of a convenient breakfast in a bag (no beans obviously!). You can relax in the dining room with the fantastic views up until 12am for the long stay guests. Our continental and full English breakfast are standard and you will be able to upgrade, for an additional charge, to a selection of special breakfasts like kedgeree, smoked salmon, chilly rice , pancakes and Goan curry on fried coconut bread, all of which have to be booked in advance. ​We strive to be organic as possible with named local produce and our own garden produce. Our excellent bread is from a local artisan baker, meat from a small Gloucester Old Spot pig farm, and jams and organic trout from a aquaponics. Depending upon the weather you can have a continental breakfast tray outside on the terrace or in one of the garden retreats. CHECK-OUT is by 11am and some guests are requested to settle any additional charges along with the keys after breakfast. We would appreciate your feedback and suggestions. PARKING is close to the house and free Fully complaint fire and smoke detectors are present for your additional safety which means you can only smoke in the designated area outside the building. ENERGY USE Hide on The Hill uses sustainable energy including a pellet boiler, Powerdiverter, loads of insulation and solar panels which help to reduce the impact of the travellers carbon footprint. Laundry is washed during daylight hours to utilise the suns energy and for longer staying guests sheets are changed after 3 days. Towels are removed and replaced if left in the basket but otherwise left for further use. Heating is on every morning and evening and is controlled by thermostats. Additional hypo allergenic bed linen can be provided if requested. THE GARDEN has many quiet spots for lazing in the sun on deckchairs or siting by the caravan to read and make yourself a cup of tea. There is a living willow spiral and firepit with a basket of free wood to use in the early evening. AMBIENCE at our hilltop hide will become obvious on your first walk around the gardens and we believe that you'll value the peace and quiet so we decided to not have televisions in the rooms. We would request that music is moderated by 10pm please . Many guests use their tablets for streaming which is fine but please turn down the volume thereafter. PETS are, at present,not able to be part of your stay but those with registered guide dogs will be considered if we know from you how to best manage the arrangement. WALKERS AND CYCLISTS are most welcome with a range of facilities to help including a drying room, outside boot area to change walking gear, a small jet wash for muddy bikes, a bike wall to repair bikes and a lockup for your bike

title: Westons, Golden Jubilee Restaurant
subtitle: Our award winning Golden Jubilee Restaurant in Weston Super Mare, Somerset epitomises the elegant Regency style for which Weston was formally renowned. Open to both residents and non-residents this proves to be a very popular eatery to all.
bodyContent: Our award winning Golden Jubilee Restaurant epitomises the elegant Regency style for which Weston was formally renowned. Open to both residents and non-residents this proves to be a very popular eatery to all. Breakfast We are proud to be presented with the Enjoy England’s Breakfast Award, which we have achieved year after year. Only about 8% of guest accommodation have received this award, recognizing hotels and B&Bs that offer a quality and varied choice of breakfast and high level of service and hospitality. We offer breakfast fit for a king, with our continental buffet-style banquet, followed by either a traditional cooked to order Full English Breakfast, steak and eggs, omelettes or choose from our lighter options such as filled bagels and fish dishes. With unlimited tea and coffee readily available this will most definitely be the best start to your day. Lunch & Dinner In these captivating surroundings you can enjoy dishes carefully selected for our appealing À la Carte menu which has been designed by our Head Chef to tempt and excite all tastes. With our menu changing with the season you are guaranteed that our kitchen only use the best local ingredients allowing our dishes to be full of flavour and goodness! Our cuisine is classic British with a twist of French infusion, offering a variety of fresh fish & meat dishes, steaks and grills along with vegetarian and vegan options. Our famous Carvery is available on Tuesdays, Thursdays and of course Sundays offering a choice of freshly cooked joints of meat accompanied by a selection of garden vegetables, Roasted Potatoes and all the trimmings. Afternoon Tea Appetites are indulged with an afternoon tea for two or four, which pleases palates with a selection of sandwiches and a pot of tea for each person. The sweet edge is provided in the form of homemade scones with dollops of clotted cream and jam, plus a slice of traditional English Victoria Sponge. Guests also have the option to include a glass of Prosecco for a fizzy twist.
tagline: Open to both residents and non-residents this proves to be a very popular eatery to all.

title: Mendip Activity Centre
subtitle: Mendip Activity Centre is the ultimate outdoor adventure playground in Somerset. They’ve been delivering adventurous outdoor activities for nearly 40 years, growing from humble beginnings to the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West!
bodyContent: It’s Time for Adventure with Mendip Activity Centre! Nestled in 250 acres of ancient woodland in the Mendip Hills National Landscape, Mendip Activity Centre is the largest outdoor activity provider in the South West. Just 20 minutes from Weston-super-Mare and Cheddar and open year-round, Mendip have been delivering Adventure, Learning and Training for individuals, families, schools, and groups since 1987. Activities available include: · Air Rifle · Tobogganing · Archery · Skiing · Snowboarding · Frisbee Golf · Kayaking · Nerf & Gel Battles · Caving · Paddle Boarding · Rock Climbing · Axe Throwing · ArcheryActive · Abseiling · Canoeing Come for the day or stay longer. In summer, pitch your tent at the award-winning Mendip Basecamp (link to https://mendipbasecamp.com/), a family adventure campsite awarded second at the Visit England Awards 2025. Pitch where you like, check out when it suits, camp fires encouraged, dogs welcome and endless adventure is on offer! Adventure for Everyone Mendip is more than just activities. It’s a place to switch off from screens, reconnect with nature, and each other. Whether you're learning something new, developing an existing skill or simply having fun outside, you’ll leave with muddy boots and big smiles. We believe in adventure for everyone. Many of our activities are adaptable for additional needs, and our friendly team will work with you to make it happen Refuel at the Alpine Lounge Overlooking the Ski Slope, the Alpine Lounge café serves pizzas, paninis, coffee and cake with stunning views- perfect for après-adventure refreshments

title: Sandy Glade Holiday Park
subtitle: Sandy Glade Holiday Park in Burnham-on-Sea in Somerset boasts plenty of facilities & open, green space for the kids to run free.
bodyContent: Sandy Glade: Sandy Glade Holiday Park in Burnham-on-Sea in Somerset boasts plenty of open, green space for the kids to run free, a fantastic indoor pool with water jets and fountains and an adventure playground so they can let off steam while you relax. In the evenings take a trip to our clubhouse for fun and games and a great entertainment line up. A hop, skip and a jump across the road and its through the dunes onto a long expanse of golden beach where you can feel the sand between your toes and enjoy a 99 ice cream for that perfect UK seaside holiday experience. Just a short drive from the park are the bright lights of the fun fair at Brean Leisure Park, whizz yourself dizzy on the Waltzers, send your tummy tumbling on the Roller Coaster or bump and bash on the Dodgems. Sandy Meadows : Accessed via a quiet lane is Sandy Meadows lodge park, a stunning development of 40 lodges with countryside views. Here you have the peace and tranquillity of a small site yet are only a couple of minutes from sister park Sandy Glade, where you can enjoy all of the park facilities including indoor pool and clubroom. The lodges offer a top of the range holiday experience where you can spread out and enjoy the luxury of extra space, sit out on your private veranda and watch the world go by, or unwind in your very own hot tub.The park is in a fantastic location, just over the road from the beach and within easy reach of some famous beauty spots such as Brean Downs, Cheddar Gorge and Wells, with its historic cathedral. ​​​​​

title: Weston Museum in Weston super Mare
subtitle: Weston Musuem in Weston super Mare has something for everyone. We want to open the museum to as many people as possible, so we’re constantly putting on events for all ages and interests. Head to the museum website to find out what is coming up soon.
bodyContent: “Once you know your history you understand more of who you are, you learn from the past and find ways to predict the future and even help create a better one.” Housed in a beautiful and distinctive historic building. We tell the story of the town and the surrounding area from prehistoric times to the present day. The museum is dedicated to being a social and educational hub for the people of Weston and its visitors. You can come to learn, relax or just have fun! The North Somerset Council museum collection contains around 50,000 individual objects. The newly refurbished museum also allows our guests to grab lunch at the cosy Clara’s Café, hire a space for a meeting or even a party in the courtyard. Museum’s do not have to be dull and dusty, in fact, Weston Museum encourages a hands-on approach to history. We also work closely with local schools and community groups to help support the Weston of today and grow the Weston of tomorrow. Our diverse volunteering programme also gives you the chance to get involved. Diversity is key! Our William Mable Gallery allows us, for the first time, to host exhibitions suitable for the world stage. We’ve already been able to display items from the Imperial War Museum and The British Museum. The content of this gallery changes throughout the year, so there is always something new at Weston Museum. Weston Museum is working towards being as accessible as possible. There is a lift for wheelchair users and those who cannot manage stairs to access the main upper floor galleries. Due to the nature of Clara’s Cottage being built in 1865, this part of the museum is unfortunately not completely accessible to wheelchair users due to narrow corridors and a staircase. Weston Museum’s free admission means that the museum is truly for everyone and is quickly becoming a popular destination among tourists as one of Weston's top attractions. Facilities Wheelchair Friendly, Café, Gift Shop, Baby Change Facilities, Accessible Lift, Parking Nearby, Disabled Toilet Available, Toilets Available
tagline: There is something for everyone here at Weston Museum.

title: The Eat Festival Clevedon
subtitle: The award-winning food and drink festivals known for their local produce in the South West is coming to Clevedon! We have teamed up with Eat Festivals to bring a fiesta of food in support of small businesses.
bodyContent: The award-winning food and drink EAT festivals known for their local produce in the South West is returning to Clevedon! Clevedon BID has teamed up with Eat Festivals for a fourth time to bring a fiesta of food and fun in support of small businesses. On 28th October, eat:Clevedon will take over Alexandra Road and Queens Square to connect all areas of Clevedon together, in support of all the businesses and local suppliers who have kept our cupboards filled and the sense of community full of good spirits during the last year. The Clevedon BID have been working closely with the Eat Team to create this celebration, Chair Tom Vaughan said, “We have been looking forward to bringing the Eat Festival to Clevedon again, we at the BID are so pleased we can bring another open air event to the town that supports our local businesses and invites locals to enjoy something special.” Approx 90 food and drink producers are expected to take part in the celebration of locally and regionally resourced products; and local small businesses will be open too for you to browse, purchase and enjoy. Beverley said: “We are really grateful for the support of Clevedon BID and Thatchers Cider with this event in Clevedon. “The town is perfect to showcase micro and small producers from across the region “We are using Alexandra Road and Queens Square for the market – encouraging residents to wander between the two areas and explore the town. The market will be held in the open air and is designed to be well-spaced out in both areas, with some socially distanced entertainment. To make it easy to travel around Clevedon, the Clevedon BID have organised vintage busses to take passengers to and from each market site, as well as around the town to ensure locals can enjoy all the flavours that Eat:Clevedon has to offer. title: Wincanton
subtitle: Two hundred years ago as many as seventeen stage coaches a day would pass through Wincanton. Today approach it from the north along what was once the main London road (the A303 bypasses the town) and it is easy to imagine very little has changed.
bodyContent: Two hundred years ago as many as seventeen stage coaches a day would pass through Wincanton. Today approach it from the north along what was once the main London road (the A303 bypasses the town) and it is easy to imagine very little has changed. The wide street still contains handsome houses and staging inns and the town’s name is still linked with horses Wincanton is officially twinned with Ankh-Morpork - the premier city state in author Terry Pratchett's fantasy Discworld novels - which is represented in the town with its own consulate! Must See and Do Enjoy a day at Wincanton races , frequent meetings throughout the season Visit the Discworld Emporium and obtaon your Discworld passport at the Ankh - Morpork Consulate Get some retail therapy in Wincanton's independent shops Relax with a round of golf at Wincanton golf club Have a happy and healthy time at Wincanton sports centre Local Facilities Library Petrol Station Post Office Pubs and restaurants Sports Centre Supermarket and Shops

title: Farmborough
subtitle: Farmborough is a small village and civil parish, 6 miles (9.7 km) south west of Bath in the unitary authority of Bath & North East Somerset, England. The Farmborough ward is represented by one councillor on the Bath & North East Somerset council.
bodyContent: Farmborough is a small village and civil parish, 6 miles (9.7 km) south west of Bath in the unitary authority of Bath & North East Somerset, England. The Farmborough ward is represented by one councillor on the Bath & North East Somerset council. Farmborough Parish Council has responsibility for local issues, including setting an annual precept to cover operating costs and producing annual accounts for public scrutiny. The Parish Council evaluates local planning applications and works with the local police, district council officers, and other groups on matters of crime, security and traffic. The Parish Council's role, through local groups, also includes the maintenance and repair of parish facilities, such as the Village Hall, the Recreation Ground and Pavilion and children's playgrounds, as well as consulting with the district council on the maintenance, repair and improvement of highways, drainage, footpaths, public transport and street cleaning.

title: Woodcombe Lodges and Cottages
subtitle: Woodcombe Lodge, Minehead, Self catering Cottages and lodges in Somerset, on the edge of Exmoor National Park near Minehead seafront and shops, 1.5 miles. Wheelchair friendly, disabled access self catering cottages on Exmoor. Dog friendly cottages in Somerset/Devon border
bodyContent: Woodcombe Lodges & Cottages are to be found down a short country lane on the outskirts of the seaside town of Minehead . Set in 3 acre gardens on a quiet country lane only 1+ mile from Minehead & its sandy beach. All face south so the verandas enjoy full sun during the day. All accommodation is 4-star rated, the beaches, seafront, restaurants and shops of Minehead are just a 5 minute drive or 20 minute walk away. We are a dog friendly location and a stunning base for walking, country escapes and family holidays. We are also fully accessible with Holly, Laburnum and Cherry Lodges all wheelchair friendly spacious and well equipped, two with accessible shower wet rooms. We have a games room including table tennis, pool and table football which is also an ideal space for a family gathering or special party. Outside there is plenty of space for children to play with swings whilst parents can enjoy our putting green. Electricity included in the rate from May to the end of September only. ​​​
tagline: Self catering cottages and lodges in Somerset on the edge of Exmoor National Park near Minehead

title: Taunton Watch Services Ltd
subtitle: With over 15 years experience we aim to provide an old fashioned & friendly level of service, while using the latest techniques and advanced equipment. From battery replacements and pressure testing, to strap replacements, and watch sales, we try to cover all your timepiece requirements.
bodyContent: Watch Repairs - we do many watch repairs on-site including glass, crown, movement and battery replacements, some of which can be done on the same day. Battery Replacements - we use the best batteries on the market. For our Watch battery replacements we use Renata, it has developed its 0% mercury battery line in close cooperation with the Swiss Watch Industry. Most of the major luxurious Swiss Watch Brands rely on Renata. Watch straps and bracelets - choose from a variety of styles to fit your needs. Whether formal, casual, or sports, you can find the exact watch strap or watch bracelet to suit your timepiece. Pressure testing - on-site pressure testing up to 100 metres.
tagline: We treat every watch with great care and attention.

title: Lesser Litter
subtitle: We are Kate and Pete, and are proud to be part of the Taunton & Somerset community. We want to give the people of Taunton a positive option for shopping ethically, organically and packaging free.
bodyContent: We see Lesser Litter as part of the solution to the huge environmental issues we, as a community and as a planet, face. We believe in reusing packaging, circular supply and supporting sustainable organic farming practices. Shopping ethically should be accessible for everyone. We firmly believe this should be more economical, both for the individual and for the environment. We sell a range of groceries - we mostly sell organic and pride ourselves on competing with the major supermarkets and brands on price. Where we can, we offer British and local options. Currently everything in store is vegan, except for the sustainably and responsibly sourced honey, beeswax wraps and sunscreen.
tagline: Offering a positive option for shopping ethically, organically and packaging free.

title: Jane Armour Trading
subtitle: An independent card and gift shop in the heart of the Riverside shopping area of Taunton.
bodyContent: This charming independent retailer selling a range of a quality and quirky greetings cards, presents and gift wraps.

title: Godminster Cheese
subtitle: Here at Godminster, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe. Our shop is open seven days a week and we have cheese available to sample every day.
bodyContent: Here at Godminster, Somerset, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe. Our shop is open seven days a week and we have cheese available to sample every day. There is free parking outside, so come and taste for yourself why Godminster has so many loyal friends around the world. We also offer fruit-infused vodka spirits, and over 18s are welcome to try those too. If you’re looking for a lovely foodie gift or a delicious souvenir of your trip to Somerset, come and take your pick from our range. Godminster’s Vintage Organic Cheddar is a deliciously soft and creamy cheddar matured for up to 12 months, at which point we select the best cheese to be made into one of our award-winning truckles. This sumptuous cheese is encased in the iconic burgundy wax to emphasise its pedigree and truly special status. The cheese is full bodied with a long, nutty, savoury bite. We also offer an Oak-Smoked Vintage Organic Cheddar, which sees the same top quality cheddar smoked over sustainably sourced oak chippings. The cheddar has a rich depth of flavour and the smokiness is evenly balanced with the acidity of the cheddar. Godminster Farm is set on the outskirts of the town of Bruton, Somerset, whose historic pedigree is recorded in the Doomsday Book of 1086. The Farm was registered as organic in 1999 and now boasts orchards with cider apples, peaches, nectarines and grapes, whilst keenly observing Soil Association and Government regulations relating to animal husbandry and the environmentally varied approach to business. The farm boasts a herb garden that enhances the natural remedies used to treat cows on the farm, 15 ponds supporting bio-diversity, and reeds which filter ground water. 25,000 broadleaf trees have been planted at the Farm since owner Richard Hollingbery took over, fostering diverse habitats and encouraging increases in the wildlife population. The cows at Godminster Farm, Somerset enjoy a simple and wholesome life. Richard sees them as the foundations for a truly holistic approach to his business, with the Farm’s milk turned into Godminster Vintage Organic Cheddar. Our mantra is "Nature repays those who treat her kindly," and that ethos runs across the business. Can’t make it to Bruton this time? Visit our website www.godminster.com let’s be friends on social media – we’re on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and Pinterest.
tagline: Here at Godminster, we create award-winning Vintage Organic Cheddar to a 90-year-old recipe.

title: The Red Lion West Pennard
subtitle: Barrie brings over 15 years experience in the hospitality industry, including at some of Somerset’s best quality pubs and hotels, as well as popular venues in London.
bodyContent: Along with his hobby of interior design, Barrie has brought fresh ideas to the newly named The Lion, and hopes to keep developing the pub’s look into the future to attract both locals, and those from afar who want a traditional British stay in the heart of Somerset. Steeped in history, The Lion dates back about 500 years, and was built when King Charles I was on the British throne and even before the famous Gunpowder Plot of 1605. Originally constructed as a house, for centuries the quirky building has been welcoming visitors as a traditional British pub. With its low ceilings, exposed beams and homely inglenook fireplaces, it has all the charm of what you expect from a historic pub and restaurant. Listed as one of the Britain’s most important buildings, this is a slice of history set right in the heart of the Somerset countryside in a popular English village. The characterful and homely rooms offer a comfortable stay for those wanting to holiday or spend a night or two in this stunning part of the UK.
tagline: Barrie brings over 15 years experience in the hospitality industry

title: The Mendip Inn
subtitle: The Mendip Inn is an exciting country pub and coaching rooms concept at the foot of the Mendip Hills, near Glastonbury, owned and run by hospitality entrepreneur, Matthew Lowe.
bodyContent: Styled by the talented team behind Jamie Oliver’s Fifteen restaurant, The Mendip Inn takes the concept of a great British Pub and adds an exciting, contemporary style of its own, to the food and design, without losing that sense of welcome you receive at the very best pubs. First class service is at the heart of all that we do. The Mendip Inn offers a fantastic, modern and fresh à la carte menu, seven days a week. We have a weekly specials menu, highlighting local, seasonal produce, cooked to express the flavours of the ingredients, with a twist on exceptional pub recipes. Wednesday is Steak Night, Friday is Fresh Fish Friday, with fresh market fish specials each week, and Sundays are, of course, for fabulous traditional roasts.
tagline: The Mendip Inn is an exciting country pub and coaching rooms

title: Ebborways Farm B&B
subtitle: Ebborways Farm is not just a bed and breakfast; it’s a camping site and one of the main camping sites for Priddy Folk Festival. We also hold rallies and are a wedding reception venue.
bodyContent: Ebborways Farm Bed and Breakfast is situated in a small village called Priddy, on top of the Mendip Hills near Wells in Somerset. We are in an area of outstanding natural beauty, and therefore it is a very popular area for walkers, cavers and horse riders alike. If you are looking for a romantic break or a holiday set in stunning scenery or if you wish to explore this beautiful county of Somerset, and all it has to offer, either by car, foot, bike or horse. At Ebborways Farm Bed and Breakfast we will do everything possible to ensure a memorable stay. The farm is perfectly positioned for sightseeing places such as Cheddar Gorge and Caves (5 miles), Wookey Hole Caves and Wookey Hole Paper Mill (2.7 Miles), Wells Cathedral (4 miles), Burrington Combe (5 miles), Bristol, Bath, Longleat and many other places of interest are also within easy reach. Annual attractions include Priddy Folk Fair in July, Priddy Funday & Craft Fair in September and also in November the Illuminated Carnival Season.

title: Stay at Penny's Mill
subtitle: Luxury Bed & Breakfast in Nunney, Somerset
bodyContent: Our lovely 200-year old watermill, set in the charming Somerset village of Nunney, is the ideal centre for a West Country break – close to Bath, Frome, Longleat, Stourhead, The Newt in Somerset, Hauser & Wirth and Babington House. We offer you our hospitality, the freedom of our beautiful house – and the chance to enjoy Rosie’s famous breakfasts! Most of all, we will do our level best to give you a relaxed, informal, comfortable stay in our people-friendly Bed & Breakfast – one of Somerset’s most special places to stay. Each of our three spacious rooms at Penny’s Mill provides comforts such as crisp white cotton bedlinen, down pillows and duvets (with man-made alternatives available), large towels, free wireless broadband & flat screen TVs

title: Lower Stock Farm Bed and Breakfast
subtitle: Our lovely Bed and Breakfast nestles at the foot of the Mendip Hills in picturesque North Somerset, between the villages of Lower Langford and Wrington.
bodyContent: Lower Stock Farm sits amid 250 acres of countryside, 30 minutes from Bristol and Weston-super-Mare, under 6 miles from Bristol Airport. We offer stay-park-fly parking, taxi arrangement, en-suite rooms with TV and hot drinks facilities, an on-site Beauty Salon, and locally-sourced breakfasts catering to dietary needs.
tagline: Our lovely Bed and Breakfast nestles at the foot of the Mendip Hills

title: Mendip Basecamp
subtitle: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure campsite in the Mendip Hills...
bodyContent: Basecamp is an award-winning, off-grid family adventure camp in the Mendip Hills National Landscape - just minutes from the M5 and Weston-super-Mare. Surrounded by ancient woodland you can pitch where you like, park right by your tent and enjoy evenings around the campfire. Well-behaved dogs are welcome! With no check-out time, you can leave whenever you are ready. Mendip Basecamp is camping how it should be: rural, laid-back and relaxed but with essential luxuries. Usually reserved for schools and private groups, in 2020, Mendip opened Basecamp up to families for the very first time- and hasn’t looked back since. Public bookings are available throughout the summer holidays and summer weekends. Bring your own tent or campervan, book bell tents, glamphouses or stay in Mendip Lodge (with free breakfast). Facilities include hot showers, clean flushing toilets, a camp shop, a country Lodge with a cider garden (and live music), an onsite activity centre, USB charging and WIFI. Free activities throughout the summer include live music, orienteering, circus skills, treasure hunts, free climbing tower and nature craft. The campsite is less than a 5-minute woodland walk from Mendip Activity Centre, home to over 20 different adventurous, outdoor activities including rock climbing, kayaking, archery, frisbee golf and air rifle. New for 2026, Mendip Basecamp is launching Mendip Mini Fests - six family-friendly festivals running throughout the summer holiday weekends. Great entertainment, headline bands, local talent competition, and more! Included at no extra cost, exclusively for campsite guests.
tagline: Mendip Basecamp was delighted to be awarded the Gold campsite at the 2023-2024

title: Nunney Castle
subtitle: A small 14thC century moated castle, distinctively French in style.
bodyContent: The striking and picturesque moated castle of Nunney was built in the 1370's by Sir John de la Mere, a local knight who was beginning to enjoy royal favour. Extensively modernised in the late 16th century, the castle was held for the King during the Civil War, but quickly fell to Parliamentarian canon in 1645:not until Christmas Day 1910, however di the gun-damaged portion of the wall finally collapse.
tagline: A small 14thC century moated castle, distinctively French in style.

bodyContent: This walk takes you along the Portishead to Clevedon coastal path as far as Black Nore Lighthouse, it is approximately two miles and is fairly easy going but can be slippery if wet – watch out for roots and rocks. Duration: 1.5 hrs round trip; OS grid ref: ST461 768, walk instructions

title: Warren Farm Holiday Centre
subtitle: Warren Farm Holiday Centre is a family-run holiday park in Brean, near Burnham-on-Sea.
bodyContent: The award-winning park offers touring & camping pitches, static caravan hire and hot tub accommodation. There is everything you need for the perfect family holiday, from the beach and children's activities to restaurants and evening entertainment. Located by stunning Somerset countryside and a large stretch of sandy beach, Warren Farm was crowned the UK’s Holiday Centre of the Year in the AA Awards 2023/24! Touring & Camping Facilities Grass, hardstanding & en-suite super pitches Award-winning washrooms Launderette & dish washing facilities Dog-friendly areas Wi-fi hotspots Holiday Accommodation Modern static caravans by the beach, some with hot tubs Shops & Eateries The Beachcomber restaurant & clubhouse Ice cream parlour Chinese takeaway Fish ‘n’ chips shop Convenience stores Caravan accessories & fishing shop Things To Do Play Barn - Indoor soft play, arcade & bowling Pets Corner - Meet the animals! Outdoor play areas Fishing lake Games field Farm walk Live entertainment Weekly Market (end of May – mid September) Children’s activities (May half term and Summer holidays) Caravan Sales See our caravans for sale at www.breancaravans.com Day Visitors Day visitors are also welcome at Warren Farm and The Beachcomber. With free parking in The Beachcomber car park and free entry to the complex, it makes a great day out for all ages. Please visit our website www.warrenfarm.co.uk for more information. You can find The Beachcomber Entertainment Guide at www.beachcomberbrean.co.uk – everyone welcome!

title: Jo & Nic's Crinkly Cloth Books
subtitle: Nursery Times crinkly cloth newspapers with a range of over 45 titles. Junior Design Awards Gold award winner 2021 for best baby book 0-2 years.
bodyContent: Jo and Nic are the founders of Jo & Nic's crinkly cloth books. Both designers and illustrators are based in the southwest. They have created a sensory cloth book which is suitable for newborns and babies from 3+ months. The books are also great for toddlers and the rhyming text is good for early reading skills. The range of titles includes high contrast images which are great for children with visual impairment. Our range aims to be gender-neutral and include all races and cultural differences. Each book comes packed in its own pack so makes a really unique gift and is light and easy to pop in the post. Personalisation is also available and these are a great way of making tactile memory books which can be shared with everyone. A safe, washable and tactile cloth book is every parent's must-have. We supply our books to most independent gift, toy and bookshops around the UK and now have over 100. At Studio One, I hold illustration workshops for both adults and children. title: Crewkerne
subtitle: The surrounding fields and hills are crossed by public footpaths & bridleways which are enjoyed by local walkers and riders. Bincome Beeches Nature Reserve provides panoramic views of the town and the surrounding countryside.
bodyContent: An historic and attractive stone built country Market Town in the South Somerset Hills, Crewkerne has its origins in Saxon times. The name derives from cruc - a hill, and aern - a house or storehouse. Coins were minted here in the reign of King Ethelred (978-1016). The 15 th Century parish church, St Bartholomew's, overlooking Bincombe Valley, was built with the wealth of the flourishing medieval wool industry. The Town Centre is a Conservation Area with some fine examples of 19 th Century Georgian houses. Today Crewkerne has a range of cafes, pubs and restaurants, supermarkets and small shops,a swimming pool and gym facilities all in the town centre. The surrounding fields and hills are crossed by public footpaths & bridleways which are enjoyed by local walkers and riders. Bincome Beeches Nature Reserve provides panoramic views of the town and the surrounding countryside.

title: Cameley and Temple Cloud
subtitle: Cameley dates back to Anglo Saxon times when it was part of the ‘Hundred of Chewton’. It is recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086 as ‘Camelie’ and it lies on the Cam Brook. The name means ‘the curved river meadows’ from the Celtic word of ‘cam’ and the old English ‘leah’.
bodyContent: Cameley dates back to Anglo Saxon times when it was part of the ‘Hundred of Chewton’. It is recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086 as ‘Camelie’ and it lies on the Cam Brook. The name means ‘the curved river meadows’ from the Celtic word of ‘ cam’ and the old English ‘ leah’ . After the Norman Conquest, the Bishop of Coutances held the manor but about 1150 the manor was given to Bath Abbey by the d’Alneto family who came from Normandy after the Conquest. Later the manor was held by another French Norman family the de Marisco family who are better known for their connection with the island of Lundy. In a grant of 1201, King John passed control to the Knights Templar but during the 13th and early 14th centuries the manor was again under the control of the de Marisco family. It was in the early 14th century that the area of the parish previously called ‘Cloude’ started to be referred to as Temple Cloud, indicating almost certainly that the Knights Templar owned or occupied land within the parish. Ownership of the manor passed through the hands of the religious houses of Bath Abbey and Glastonbury Abbey in the late Middle Ages. The church at Cameley dates back to the 13th century. It is dedicated to St James and may well have been built on the site of an earlier one. The tower was constructed a little later. The church is now looked after by the Churches Conservation Trust and is widely regarded for its wall paintings and its 15th and 17th century pews and pulpit. The Victorians did nothing in the church so it remains much as it was 200 years ago. When the religious houses were dissolved by Henry VIII, the manor was passed with others to Richard Watkin Vaughan, a courtier who passed it to his son Polydore on his death. Polydore sold the manor in 1561 to John and Mary Hippisley and the Hippisley family owned the manor of Cameley and the village of Temple Cloud until they sold it house by house and farm by farm along with the land at an auction in July 1919. Temple Cloud developed because it was on the road from Bristol to the south and the population gradually moved from the area around St James Church to be near the road - a process that was accelerated when the turnpike roads were developed. Cottages were built along the road, many of which remain today. In about 1916 some residents petitioned for a church to be built in Temple Cloud to avoid them having to make the long walk to St James in Cameley and the Hippisley’s agreed. St Barnabas Church was constructed in the style of the Arts and Crafts Movement from Temple stone and was built using local labour in the mid 1920s. Temple Cloud expanded with the usual trades and shops to serve the community including three or four public houses. At the height of its activity, it was said that Temple Cloud had everything except a railway station. Temple Cloud had quarries where Pennant sandstone was to be found. This hard stone was used for pavements and kerbs among other things. There was also a brick works and a saw mill but farming was the main activity within the parish. The parish of Cameley is well positioned for commuting to work or for leisure activities. The main road, the A37 means that Bristol and Shepton Mallet are each about 10 miles away with Bath and Wells much the same distance. There is a regular bus service to Bristol and Wells and the nearest railway stations are Bristol Temple Meads, Keynsham and Bath Spa . Recent Development Over the years a small number of developments have been built within the parish which has included homes at Goldney Way and further development at Paulmont Rise and more recently a larger development at Meadway. Building work is also due to be completed at two sites on Temple Inn Lane – one at Brandown Close and the other adjoining the main road where the Temple Inn pub has recently been redeveloped to contain a number of letting rooms and several houses. Facilities Today, Temple Cloud is home to Cameley CEVC Primary School which is rated by OFSTED as 'good'. There is also Cameley Surgery which is partnered with Harptree Surgery, and many other thriving local businesses including a Post Office contained within the petrol station shop. Temple Cloud Garage and Cameley Primary School kindly both host public access defibrillators provided by the Parish Council. There are many vibrant community groups and activities within the village and surrounding area which includes: Temple Cloud in Bloom, Temple Cloud WI, St Johns Ambulance and many more. The parish is supplied with an informative Parish Magazine - Clutton & Temple Cloud News, copies of which are available at the local petrol station shop and to which residents can subscribe for a small fee. The Parish Magazine publishes local news, local events, adverts, details of the mobile library and contains a directory at the back. In 2017 the Parish Council undertook an exciting project to expand the Playground on Cameley Playing Field which now provides a wide range of equipment for all ages and abilities. Parish Council Aims Temple Cloud with Cameley Parish Council aims to represent the local community, deliver services to meet local needs, and improve the quality of life and community wellbeing. The Parish Council provides and maintains a variety of important and visible services. These include: street sweeping through the employment of two village operatives, grass cutting on the Village Green and Playing Fields, monitoring public rights of way and highways. The Parish Council also own and maintain Cameley Playing Fields and owns and manages Temple Cloud Village Hall. In addition, the Parish Council scrutinises all planning applications and provides a voice for the local community on various issues and consultations and also works with the Local Authority (B&NES Council) to ensure local services are delivered and the Parish is well maintained. The Parish of Cameley is a civil parish in Bath and North East Somerset Council area, which is made up of the larger village of Temple Cloud and the smaller village of Cameley. At full membership, the Parish Council has nine Parish Councillors and currently employs two Village Operatives and one Parish Clerk. Parish Council Meetings and Current Projects The Parish Council hold a Parish Council Meeting on the second Wednesday of the month which starts at 7.00pm at Temple Cloud Village Hall. Members of the public are always welcome to attend these meetings and a public participation session is held at the start of the meeting where residents are invited to speak to their Councillors or raise issues of concern. From time to time vacancies arise and the Parish Council advertise such vacancies on the two Parish Council noticeboards - one situated on the corner of Temple Inn Lane at the junction with the main road and the second by the bus stop on the Village Green. Temple Cloud with Cameley Parish Council are currently undertaking a project to rejuvenate the Village Hall and carpark and currently have a consultation and competition open. You can find out more on the Parish Council website. The Parish Council has a website – www.templecloud.org.uk and a Facebook Page. For enquiries please contact the Parish Clerk, Jenny Howell at: info@templecloud.org.uk . This piece was drafted as a collaboration between Temple Cloud with Cameley Parish Council and local residents with an interest in local history, The Parish Council thanks all contributors.

title: Ring O'Bells
subtitle: Free house local pub in Somerset between Street & Glastonbury.
bodyContent: The Ring O’Bells is an 18th Century “free house” pub in the Somerset village of Ashcott near Street and Glastonbury, which for the last 29 years has been run by a family partnership. A unique pub with unique food, all prepared by us in our own kitchens. Local meat from a local butcher. Somerset produce at its best. Daily Specials blackboard including freshly made desserts. Home-made fudge with your coffee to finish! We are a genuine Free House and it is our policy to feature beers from small independent breweries, many from the West Country but occasionally also more “exotic” visitors! The range of beers varies constantly but our list of forthcoming beers features usually at least one beer from one of the local micro breweries. title: Glastonbury Wedding and Events Venue
subtitle: An old pre Norman village church lovingly restored to its former glory offering a special place for couples to get married , to celebrate an anniversary , or to just have a party . comes with a large car park , glamping site and accommodation with kitchen, toilets and fully stocked licensed bar .
bodyContent: The old village church was closed back in 1998 owing to lack of attendance ,and with strong family ties was purchased by ourselves back in 2002 , The surrounding farmland and farm has been in our family for six generations so we did not want the church to fall into disrepair , and after a period of time we thought with the right planning we could get a civil license and have marriages and events there once more. After 37 months we finally got all the licenses that we required , then after a major building and renovation work we were ready to open up to the public again after a 16 year absence . With weddings and events coming from near and afar , it was decided to offer accommodation , so planning was sought for some glamping pods , these have been installed during the covid lockdowns and are now ready for the summer of 2021. Guests can now enjoy themselves even more with a relaxing stay without the need to drive , whether it is a wedding , anniversary or party a whole weekend with friends can be a enjoyable occasion without the rush and stress . The glamping pods are all ensuite with double bed ,showers, toilets , kitchenette , fridge freezers, microwave and TV . There is also a three bedroom cottage that can sleep six so more friends and family can stay on site.

title: Art Trail, Port Marine
subtitle: Centred around The Marina, extending in to the Port Marine and Village Quarter housing developments, more than twenty outstanding visual artists have contributed to the Portishead Public Art Trail. Their works, which reflect the town’s rich history and heritage, are integrated into the landscape.
bodyContent: A work that looks like used matches, entitled, "When Shall We Three Meet Again?", reflects on the history of the former phosphorous plant in Portishead (PDF), while the "Arc of Angels", in Jubilee Park, shows five female figures which commemorate the masts of Portishead Radio (ask any naval person) that stood above the town, used to control shipping movements across the world. Whilst the service was run from Burnhgam-on-Sea, the business end, the masts which broadcast the signals, had to be located on higher ground here in Portishead. A trail map and more information about the art trail can be found here ,

subtitle: The feature debut from the directing partnership of Gina Gammell and Riley Keough, War Pony has a kinship with the work of Chloé Zhao and Roberto Minervini. It won the Caméra d’Or for best first feature at last year’s Cannes film festival…
bodyContent: “The feature debut from the directing partnership of Gina Gammell and Riley Keough, War Pony has a kinship with the work of Chloé Zhao and Roberto Minervini. It won the Caméra d’Or for best first feature at last year’s Cannes film festival…There’s a desperate, unforgiving beauty to the landscape – shot, with liberal use of pink-hued, magic-hour glow, in generous widescreen, by Colombian cinematographer David Gallego (Embrace of the Serpent, I Am Not a Witch ). And the non-professional cast, drawn from the community in which these interlocking, quasi-mythic tales of manhood in the making are set, is rooted, real and persuasive.” – The Guardian At 23, Bill (Jojo Bapteise Whiting) just wants to make something of himself. Whether it’s siphoning gas, delivering goods or breeding Poodles, he is determined to hustle his way to the “American Dream”. Meanwhile, 12-year-old Matho (LaDainian Crazy Thunder) can’t wait to become a man. Desperate for approval from his young father, a series of impulsive decisions turns Matho’s life upside down and he finds himself unequipped to deal with the harsh realities of the adult world. title: Langport
subtitle: This ancient market town lies at the heart of the Somerset Levels, strategically placed at a crossing point over the River Parrett.
bodyContent: Its central location makes Langport both a thriving hub for the neighbouring villages, and an ideal base to explore, by car, on foot or by bike, the surrounding nearby towns such as Yeovil , Taunton , Bridgwater , Street and Glastonbury , and the flora and fauna of the Somerset Levels , one of England's most unchanged landscapes. Langport boasts a fine range of modern facilities, including a post office, library, pharmacy and medical centre; retail outlets ranging from supermarkets to a wide variety of independent shops and craft workshops, and many good places to eat and drink. There are pleasant walks around the town, with attractive picnic areas beside the river and in the Walter Bagehot Town Garden, overlooking the moors. The Hill, the oldest part of town, provides unrivalled views of the surrounding countryside, as well as an eclectic mix of fine old buildings. River and moor walks A network of mainly level footpaths can take you along beside the River Parrett (part of the River Parrett Trail), through Northmoor or around the town. Most paths are suitable for disabled access, though in severe wet weather some may become unusable. There are seats and picnic tables on Cocklemoor and in the Walter Bagehot Town Garden for you to rest and enjoy the beautiful tranquil views. A footpath map is available in the Langport Information Centre. Historic buildings Langport and its neighbouring parish of Huish Episcopi boast many fine historic buildings. Especially notable are the distinctive Hanging Chapel in the old town wall on The Hill; the two parish churches of All Saints’, Langport, and St Mary’s, Huish Episcopi; and the houses on Bow Street which lean gently backwards, possibly because their fronts had the benefit of the foundation of the Roman causeway. The Hanging Chapel, The Hill The Grade 1 listed Hanging Chapel is the jewel in Langport’s crown. It is a 15th century structure with 12th century origins. Contrary to popular myth, its name comes from its construction over the road, not because anyone was hanged there by the infamous Judge Jeffreys (they weren’t). Over time it has been the town hall, a Sunday School, an armoury, museum, grammar school and, since 1891, a masonic lodge. All Saints’ Church, The Hill All Saints’ Church has dominated the skyline since the 15th century. The Tower’s portcullis emblems pay tribute to Lady Margaret Beaufort (mother of King Henry VII), who, as Lady of the Manor, paid for much of its construction. The famous crowned portcullis used by the Houses of Parliament came from this Beaufort coat of arms. The east window has a fine collection of medieval stained glass, and the west window was installed in memory of Walter Bagehot. A fine collection of unusual stone carved ‘hunky punks’ decorate the outside. The Town Hall, Cheapside Langport Town Council still meets in the Town Hall, which was built in 1733. At various times the building has housed the town’s horse-drawn fire engine, the cells and the county court. It has a fine octagonal clock, originally installed in 1802. In the 19th century Langport had several clockmakers. William Preddy, who worked here in the 1820s-1830s, has over 20 signed clocks that are still in existence. Despite this, the present clock was made in London! Great Bow Wharf , Bow Street River-based trade was vital to Langport’s commercial prosperity until the coming of the railway. This restored warehouse, next to Great Bow Bridge, was once operated by the important trading company, Stuckey & Bagehot. The warehouse is now a multi-purpose community facility, with an attractive and popular riverside café. St Mary’s Church, Huish Episcopi The Norman doorway with its distinctive dogtooth design is the earliest part of the mainly 15 th century building, dating back to the 12 th century. The ornate west tower is said to be one of the finest in Somerset. The stained glass window in the south aisle was designed by Burne-Jones and made in the workshops of William Morris. It is dedicated to James Kelway, founder of the world-famous Kelways Nurseries. Walter Bagehot Langport is the home of the famous Victorian constitutional and financial writer and long-time editor of The Economist , Walter Bagehot (1826-77). He was born in Bank Chambers in Cheapside, lived at Hurds Hill, and is buried in All Saints’ Churchyard on The Hill. The Town Garden has been renamed in his honour, and has a splendid interpretation board celebrating his life and achievements. His family were not only commercially important to Langport through the 19th century Stuckey & Bagehot trading company, but also, with their relatives, the Stuckeys, through the regionally important Stuckey’s Bank (which at one time could boast a banknote circulation second only to the Bank of England itself!), which began in Langport and which eventually, through mergers, became part of the National Westminster Bank. Battle of Langport An important English Civil War battle took place to the east of Langport on 10 th July 1645. The Parliamentarian Army, under the command of Sir Thomas Fairfax, defeated the Royalist troops, led by General Goring. As the Royalists fled westwards over Bow Bridge they set fire to some of the houses in Bow Street, but the locals doused the flames as fast as they arose. Oliver Cromwell himself was present, and wrote a detailed account of this ‘happy victory’ near ‘a very strong place of the enemy’s called Langport’. This triumph at Langport, gained with few casualties, enabled Cromwell to consolidate his position in the South West. DOWNLOAD OUR ONLINE FLYERS BELOW!

title: Thorner’s Farm Shop
subtitle: Thorner’s began with the simple idea of providing quality butchery meat, sourced in Somerset whenever possible. This is still one of our core values and now, in addition to fresh meat, we are proud to offer an award winning range of pies, quiches, savouries, ready meals, desserts & cakes.
bodyContent: Where did it all begin? Born and bred in Somerset Mr Jon Thorner opened one of the regions very first farm shops in 1979, as an extension of the family farm and abattoir. The core of the business was built upon using locally sourced and high welfare meat with a strong focus on fair pricing for suppliers. A passion for success The meat industry has changed dramatically since 1979 and it was important for Thorner’s to diversify. So in 2005 the first Thorner’s pie was baked! As the kitchen gained confidence, the number of awards grew and they knew they had something special to offer. The range has grown significantly now offering a range of pies, quiches, savouries, ready meals, desserts and cakes – and did you know each pie is still hand crimped and individually filled. Award winning The quality of our ingredients, the authentic homemade appearance and flavour of our kitchen range has delivered us multiple awards across the food industry including Great Taste, British Pie Awards, Taste of the West and Smithfield Awards, and our staff and the business have also been recognised regionally and within the industry at Somerset Business and Mendip Business Awards.
tagline: Thorner’s began with the simple idea of providing quality butchery meat, sourced in Somerset

bodyContent: You will receive all the little extra touches such as dressing gowns, slippers, etc., together with a welcoming Brunch Pack on arrival. title: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm
subtitle: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is a conservation charity and the largest zoo in Somerset with over 100 species of animals. The multi award winning Zoo is open 7 days a week and aims to make Noah's Ark a place of joy, wonder, adventure and refreshment that supports the well-being of all visitors, staff and volunteers. Through education and fun, they aim to inspire and motivate this generation and the next to consider sustainable lifestyles and care for our planet.
bodyContent: Amazing Animals The home of the big Zoo animals! Visit Noah’s Ark and come face to face with a cheeky mob of meerkats, be awed by African elephants and dazzled by the zebra herd! Experience the majestic beauty and see the skies come alive during the daily birds of prey displays! The Wings of Wonder display showcases the owls, hawks, falcons and eagles in an unforgettably mesmerizing spectacle. Indoor and Outdoor Adventures Play and adventure never stops with our 10 play areas across the 100-acre site. Enjoy the huge indoor play barns including under 5’s soft play and a giant rainbow slide. The Zoo also has accessible play equipment including nest swings and a wheelchair accessible roundabout. Fancy an a-maze-ing adventure? Navigate through Britain’s longest hedge maze. The British wildlife themed maze has 3.4km of paths and wooden nest tower at the center. Keep the whole family smiling and active all day, whatever the weather! Accessibility Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is proud to be an accessible attraction. Facilities include multiple accessible toilets, Changing Places facility, accessible play equipment, hearing loops and more. Please visit the website before your visit for up-to-date information and to view the Access guide. Prices Buy online and save! Noah’s Ark recommends that all tickets, including those for free essential carers and under 2’s are purchased online prior to your arrival. Prices are seasonal, please check the website for up-to-date ticket prices. Food and Drink With a range of delicious hot and cold food and drink options available in our Food Barn and convenient snack kiosks across the Zoo, there is something for everyone! Alternatively, visitors are very welcome to bring their own lunch and enjoy it in one of our many picnic spots. Mini Experiences Noah’s Ark offers incredible up-close mini experiences with Meerkats, Capybara, Andean Bears and Giant Tortoise. You will enjoy 20 minutes behind the scenes with the keeper, learn some interesting facts and get involved with their feeding and enrichment programme. Pre-book your experience online to ensure availability. Minimum age and terms and conditions apply. Animal Experiences Find out what it’s like to be a keeper for the day with our one-to-one keeper experiences before the zoo opens. Experiences include: African Elephants, Junior Keeper Experience, and Giraffe and Rhino experience.
tagline: You’ll be amazed at the variety of nature you’ll see with over 100 species of animals

title: Kobi & Teal
subtitle: Kobi & Teal was co-founded by designers Nick Fraser and Polly Bell to offer a considered collection of artwork and objects presented alongside their own work. With a mission to bring together a diverse group of small design brands, individual makers, and contemporary artists, Kobi & Teal holds focus on self-production.
bodyContent: The rich and varied range represents our enthusiasm for the individual. With the inclusion of traditional craft and contemporary design or a combination of both, we look to feature thoughtful products that find a balance between the playful and sophistication. Kobi & Teal brings a unique experience for its visitors; offering an exciting product range together with one-off and small batch samples. With a solid background in interior product and textile design, Nick and Polly are privileged to work collaboratively with their designers often making individual pieces specifically for the Kobi & Teal customers. These on-going developments will be accessible to the wider audience through our website along with updates of events and exhibitions. The gallery space offers Kobi & Teal a welcome opportunity to enhance its visual and exploratory content. Each exhibition will introduce a contrasting discipline to the last from artists and designers with a variety of backgrounds and experiences. This distinctive addition to the shop will contribute to the ever-evolving nature of this business, creating a destination for those looking for something new. The vibrant selection of work Kobi & Teal offer will continue to grow, bringing something to everyone who wants to support the independent and help it thrive, not through duty but because it’s the better way to shop. Nick and Polly are committed to making Kobi & Teal a hub of creative talent, supporting and promoting all its designers, makers and artists.
tagline: Kobi & Teal was co-founded by designers Nick Fraser and Polly Bell

title: Monthly Wednesday Matinees
subtitle: The Princess Theatre & Arts Centre is excited to launch its monthly Wednesday matinees. We will screen well-loved classic films at the venue on the first Wednesday of every month at 2pm from February.
bodyContent: Tickets, priced £5, are available to buy on the website. The Princess is also introducing £10 tickets to include the film and lunch. You will be able to choose from Hellend’s Kitchen Small Main Menu Meals and your choice of hot drink. Starting with Breakfast and Tiffany’s on Wednesday February 2 nd at 2pm, Casablanca on Wednesday 2 nd March and Some Like It Hot on Wednesday 6 th April. To book seats for Breakfast at Tiffany’s, visit https://www.theprincesstheatre.co.uk/events/film-breakfast-at-tiffanys/ To book seats for Casablanca, visit https://www.theprincesstheatre.co.uk/events/film-casablanca/ To book seats for Some Like It Hot, visit https://www.theprincesstheatre.co.uk/events/film-some-like-it-hot/ Film and Lunch booking only available up to 48 hours prior to the showing. Table bookings will be made for 12pm on the day of the matinee. The Princess is also delighted to announce this season’s National Theatre screenings; from London’s West End Tom Stoppard’s Olivier Award-winning play Leopoldstadt, screening on Saturday February 5 th at 7pm. At the beginning of the 20th century, Leopoldstadt was the old, crowded Jewish quarter of Vienna, Austria. But Hermann Merz, a factory owner and baptised Jew now married to Catholic Gretl, has moved up in the world. We follow his family’s story across half a century, passing through the convulsions of war, revolution, impoverishment, annexation by Nazi Germany and the Holocaust. A company of 40 actors represent each generation of the family in this epic, but intimate play.
