title: John Fowler Holiday Parks
subtitle: Here at John Fowler Holiday Parks, we want to provide you with the very best family UK break that we can. Established for over 60 years!
bodyContent: Here at John Fowler Holiday Parks, we want to provide you with the very best family UK break that we can. Established for over 60 years, every year thousands of people trust us with their family holidays in the UK and every year we try to make that experience better than ever! We’ve invested millions of pounds to achieve that with new and upgraded lodges , caravans and chalets, new facillities and activities for you to enjoy plus an action packed entertainment programme. We've also added to our line up of themed weekends to bring you some unforgetable experiences. Plus we’ve held prices across many dates and parks so you’ve got more money left in your pocket for that extra little bit of holiday fun! With 11 amazing Holiday Parks in fantastic locations you’ll be amazed at how easy they are to reach. From Devon to Cornwall to Somerset, there’s loads to do and see. So why not book in a flash today and start painting those magical memories...... The choice is yours When you book your holiday or short break with John Fowler Holidays, you can rest assured you are getting a fantastic range of accommodation choices at the very best value price. From caravans to lodges, chalets, bungalows, cottages, houses and apartments. We also have lodges with hot tubs available at two of our sites for that special treat. So whatever you’re looking for, there’s sure to be something to suit you. We want to make your self catering holidays in the UK as relaxing as possible and that means feeling at home from the moment you step through the door. In our 60 plus years, we have learnt that there is nothing as ‘one size fits all’ which is why we have holiday homes that sleep from 2 to14. We grade our accommodation from top of the range platinum for extra luxury through to our value range so that our holidays are affordable for everyone. The grading is indicative of the age and recency of refurbishment of the unit. Sandy Glade Our Sandy Glade Holiday Park in Burnham-on-Sea in Somerset boasts plenty of open, green space for the kids to run free, a fantastic indoor pool with water jets and fountains and an adventure playground so they can let off steam while you relax. In the evenings take a trip to our clubhouse for fun and games and a great entertainment line up. A hop, skip and a jump across the road and its through the dunes onto a long expanse of golden beach where you can feel the sand between your toes and enjoy a 99 ice cream for that perfect UK seaside holiday experience. Just a short drive from the park are the bright lights of the fun fair at Brean Leisure Park, whizz yourself dizzy on the Waltzers, send your tummy tumbling on the Roller Coaster or bump and bash on the Dodgems. Swimming Pool Opening Times High Season: 9am- 1pm and 2pm-6pm Low Season: 9am - 12pm and 1pm-5pm Restaurant Opening Times 9am - late
tagline: Here at John Fowler Holiday Parks, we want to provide you with the very best family UK break.

title: Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny
subtitle: Harrison Ford returns to the role of the legendary hero archaeologist for this highly anticipated final instalment of the iconic franchise
bodyContent: – a big, globe-trotting, rip-roaring cinematic adventure. Starring along with Ford are Phoebe Waller-Bridge (Fleabag), Antonio Banderas (Pain and Glory), John Rhys-Davies (Raiders of the Lost Ark), Shaunette Renée Wilson (Black Panther), Thomas Kretschmann (Das Boot), Toby Jones (Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy), Boyd Holbrook (Logan), Olivier Richters (Black Widow), Ethann Isidore (Mortel), and Mads Mikkelsen (Another Round). Directed by James Mangold (Ford v Ferrari, Logan) and written by Jez Butterworth & John-Henry Butterworth and David Koepp and James Mangold, based on characters created by George Lucas and Philip Kaufman, the film is produced by Kathleen Kennedy, Frank Marshall and Simon Emanuel, with Steven Spielberg and George Lucas serving as executive producers. John Williams, who has scored each Indy adventure since the original Raiders of the Lost Ark in 1981, has once again composed the score. More Films HERE
tagline: Harrison Ford returns to the role of the legendary hero archaeologist

title: Minehead Park Run - Every Saturday 10am
subtitle: A free, fun, and friendly weekly 5k community event. Walk, jog, run, volunteer or spectate – it's up to you!
bodyContent: When is it? Every Saturday at 9:00am. Where is it? The event takes place at The Beach Hotel, The Avenue, Minehead, Somerset, TA24 5AP. See Course page for more details. What does it cost to join in? Nothing - it's free! but please register before you first come along. Only ever register with parkrun once and don't forget to bring a scannable copy of your barcode ( request a reminder ). If you forget it, you won't get a time . How fast do I have to be? We all take part for our own enjoyment. Please come along and join in whatever your pace! Minehead parkrun needs you! It is entirely organised by volunteers - email minehead@parkrun.com to help. We're friendly! Every week we grab a post parkrun coffee in The Beach Hotel - please come and join us!

subtitle: Marksbury Parish encompasses the villages of Marksbury and Stanton Prior and the hamlet of Hunstrete.
bodyContent: Marksbury Parish encompasses the villages of Marksbury and Stanton Prior and the hamlet of Hunstrete. It is located 7 miles south west of Bath . The surrounding countryside is rural and undulating and hence there are expansive views both into and from the Parish. Farming is still a significant influence in the Parish together with a small leisure industry.

title: Merchant Menswear
subtitle: We have been quietly going about business since 2016. The store was born out of a genuine passion for urban menswear and premium retailing with a mission to offer thoughtfully edited brands with a strong emphasis on quality fabrics and provenance.
bodyContent: We are interested in product and design more than the label be it Japanese selvedge denim or handmade British footwear. We offer contemporary and heritage brands that have a story to tell and do not shout but offer understated style for the fashion connoisseur. As an independent retailer we strive to offer things that you will not see on the high street and we hope you will pay our store a visit and share in our passion.

title: Worth House
subtitle: Located in the beautiful Somerset countryside, close to the medieval city of Wells, Worth House dates back 400 years.
bodyContent: Worth House, a 16th-century former farmhouse near Wells, offers stunning Mendip Hills and farmland views. Ideally placed for Wookey Hole Caves, Glastonbury and Cheddar Gorge, with country pubs nearby including The Pheasant. Enjoy the cosy living room, garden views, and warm hospitality from hosts Sarah and Nick.

title: SHARE:Frome
subtitle: Like a normal library, you can sign up as a member and borrow items for as long as you need. We have a large variety of items, such as power tools, kitchen appliances, gardening tools and sporting equipment. We help to save you money and space, while reducing waste and emissions.
bodyContent: Did you know that the average drill is used for only 13 minutes in its entire lifetime? Do you want to start saving waste and reducing your footprint by borrowing instead of buying? Simply join as a one of our 4 membership types (Standard, Subscriber, Low Income and Student) which suit a range of incomes. This can be done in store, or online at sharefrome.org/membership. And then start borrowing! We charge a small fee for each item and based on the length of borrow. We have just under a thousand items, in 10 categories, which are Arts and Crafts, Baby and Children, Events, DIY, Gardening tools, Household and Garden, Kitchen Equipment, Leisure and Camping, Music, Media and Audio/Visual and Sports and Games. Planning a camping trip in the summer? You can also reserve items in advance to guarantee you will have access to the things you need. Having a clear out and want to donate your working appliances to the SHARE catalogue? Want to volunteer a few hours a week to help with the running of SHARE or repairing items? Find our wish list of items, volunteer application and more ways to donate here: sharefrome.org/donate Although SHARE:Frome is currently closed for the current lockdown, I have put our new opening hours for once we re-open, hopefully in March. These hours will change by late spring/early summer, however, as we are in the process of hiring more staff to be able to open more frequently.
tagline: SHARE:Frome is a Library of Things.

title: Lungi Babas
subtitle: Food is energy - We are a Frome based business on a mission to provide nourishing food at affordable prices, using ingredients that are as seasonal, locally sourced and environmentally friendly as we can. Yum!
bodyContent: Food is energy - We are a Frome based business on a mission to provide nourishing food at affordable prices, using ingredients that are as seasonal, locally sourced and environmentally friendly as we can. Yum! Life is too short to eat food that isn’t tasty and satisfying. Our food includes all six tastes of nature at every meal so that the major food groups and nutrients are represented and you feel satisfied. We mix home cooked food made from scratch with stories and community focused events. Our products and services include popup events, cooking workshops, bespoke events catering and our regular South Indian inspired Thali plate and street food lunches. Health & Safety Your health and safety continue to be our priority. Our hygiene rating continues to be 5, the highest. Any employee who feels unwell will stay at home. We follow all government COVID19 guidelines to keep you and our workers safe. Please do wear a mask if you can to pick up your food from us, and remember to stay 2m away from other customers if you have to queue. If you need any other support while staying at home, please let us know. We will try to help you or to direct you to someone who can. Lets all try and support one another. Now more than ever, Lungi Babas is committed to providing freshly-cooked, nutritious food to Frome and the wider community! Let us help you eat healthy and fresh food to nourish your bodies and your immune system.
tagline: We are a Frome based business on a mission to provide nourishing food at affordable prices

title: The Place To Stay
subtitle: "Our Mission Is To Give Our Guests A Highly Comfortable, Relaxing and Unforgettable Stay, Making Them Want To Rush Back When They Leave!"
bodyContent: We are Joss and Sam Green-Armtyge, and as a mother and son team, in 2013 we took over ‘The Place To Stay’ at Knoll Hill Farm on the edge of the small Somerset village of Trudoxhill on the edge of the Mendip Hills. The ex-farm, its buildings and its adjoining acres were in a sorry state, but we felt the old early 20 th Century Farmhouse had loads of character and the adjacent barns had much potential. We developed a vision to provide really superior bed and breakfast accommodation based on what we would want ourselves - and with Trudoxhill being a 'stones throw' from Longleat and Longleat Safari Park, and being close to so many other lovely places such as Stourhead Gardens, Bath, Wells, Cheddar Gorge Caves and Wookey Hole, we felt The 'Place To Stay' would make a popular touring base. Two years later, an extensive refurbishment of the rooms in the old farmhouse and renovation and conversion of the old barns into smart and distinctive living accommodation, and ‘The Place To Be’ was moulded into a beautiful, boutique Guest House with 9 very stylish and individual rooms. Landscaping of the gardens followed and space was created for a collection of rare breed birds to be given a home and our lovely mare, Lucy and her companion pony, Rosie were treated to a new stable block with green pastures to graze in. Our friendly house dog, Dylan and pony Rosie are often available for children to spend time with.

title: The Helicopter Museum
subtitle: The Helicopter Museum is the largest dedicated Helicopter Collection in the World with over 100 helicopters on display in an all weather undercover hangar. Exhibits include two of the Queen's Royal Flight helicopters, the current world speed record holder G-LYNX, a Vietnam Veteran Huey and a Russian Hind Gun Ship.
bodyContent: In addition to over 100 helicopters, the Helicopter Museum includes other breathtaking attractions like its WWII Pilots’ Block, Weston Aviation Exhibition and Blood Hound Missile. This all contributes to a fun day-out for all the family with plenty of opportunity to learn about these marvellous machines and their huge impact on Somerset’s history. The museum hosts various special events throughout the year. These include various car shows, hair-rasing Halloween hilarity and festive Christmas events. The most popular of these special events are the World At War Weekend and Balloons, Birds & Bubbles . At these events, the museum is completely transformed to provide visitors the opportunity to enjoy authentic military vehicles or hold a live owl! Those who haven’t had their fill of aviation history can also attend one of the museum’s open cockpit days. Here visitors can climb into the pilot’s seat of a genuine helicopter and be taken through the controls by an experienced volunteer, many of whom have spent their careers flying such aircraft. Those who really want to feel the thrill of soaring high up in the clouds can even book their seat on one of the many helicopter experience flights the museum offers throughout the year. After all that excitement, visitors can refuel in the museum’s new café which was opened as part of a new visitor service building in July 2020. It offers drinks, snacks and tasty lunches. A particular highlight is the pilots’ all-day breakfast that is big enough to satisfy even the hungriest aviation superfan!
tagline: The Helicopter Museum is the largest dedicated Helicopter Collection in the World

title: Saxonia Guest House
subtitle: Saxonia Guest House combines the personal, friendly service you would expect from a bed and breakfast with facilities you would find in an hotel.
bodyContent: We extend a warm, friendly welcome to all our guests. Saxonia is a thriving guest house with nine en-suite rooms that have been successfully run for the last 20 years. Our aim is simple - to give you the best accommodation at the most reasonable price you ever had.

title: Settlers Stores
subtitle: Everyone’s a settler from somewhere - tweed clothing to travel the world.
bodyContent: Cultural fusion is in our DNA and we celebrate colour, diversity and historical influences from around the world in our tweed clothing collection that is lined in Dutch wax cotton batik. A Kashmiri pheran is the original inspiration for our tweed robe, the Battuta, while our fitted tweed women’s waistcoat incorporates elements of Prussian military styling and leather biker jackets; our tweed tunics nod to Mary Quant and the spirit of the 60’s and our trouser suits channel a seventies vibe in tweeds, velvets or corduroy.
tagline: Everyone’s a settler from somewhere - tweed clothing to travel the world.

title: Lake Grounds, Esplanade and Lake Road
subtitle: The seafront Lake Grounds is referred to as the jewel in Portishead’s crown.
bodyContent: This relatively unspoilt area, surrounded by trees and bushes, is where families enjoy picnics and you will see cricket being played at weekends. This is also home to the town’s bowls club and tennis club. Football coaches and running clubs utilise the green open space, while others keen to keep fit use the promenade gym equipment. A boating lake operates throughout the warmer months of the year and you will find a variety of play equipment to keep younger visitors happy. The Lakeside Café is situated alongside the lake and play parks, while the Lido Café, run by volunteers, is at the opposite end of the seafront, adjacent to the open air pool. Portishead residents have successfully fought to keep parking free of charge at the Lake Grounds.

title: John Fowler Holiday Parks
subtitle: Here at John Fowler Holiday Parks, we want to provide you with the very best family UK break that we can. Established for over 60 years!
bodyContent: Here at John Fowler Holiday Parks, we want to provide you with the very best family UK break that we can. We’ve invested millions of pounds to achieve that with new and upgraded lodges , caravans and chalets, new facillities and activities for you to enjoy plus an action packed entertainment programme. title: Clevedon Market Every Thursday – (Clevedons Historic Charter Market)
subtitle: Clevedon’s Charter Market is located in the heart of town in Queen’s Square and operates every Thursday throughout the year.
bodyContent: It has a fabulous history…It was granted charter status in 1346 by King Edward lll and still holds that status today. This means that it has a zone of protection around it of six and three quarter miles and no other market is allowed to set up on a Thursday within that area. It would take an act of parliament to shut it down. Over the years as permanent retail shops appeared, the market disappeared, but then in 2003 was revived and today goes from strength to strength. We have around 20 regular stalls and several casuals stalls. Most weeks you will find a wonderful selection of food ranging from Fresh Fruit and Veg, Fish, Amazing Cheese and an award winning Bread and Cakes. There are Jewellery stalls, Clothing, Smoking Sundries. Plants. Craft stalls plus much much more Monday: closed Tuesday: closed Wednesday: closed Thursday: 09:00 – 16:00 (Some stalls open from 0630) Friday: closed Saturday: closed Sunday: closed
tagline: Clevedon’s Charter Market is located in the heart of town in Queen’s Square

title: Avalon - The Birth of a Legend
subtitle: A Waterfront Production by Fred Owen
bodyContent: AVALON – The Birth of a Legend The final battle of Camlann is over and Arthur lies dying of his mortal wounds at the Abbey of Glastonbury. The civil war has been costly and nobody’s really sure who has won. The family are gathering like carrion, though each with their own agenda. Into the maelstrom stumbles Amergin; a travelling bard and his sister Rhiannon. Outside, the civil war is over, but inside the walls of the abbey it’s just beginning. Will the illicit lovers Guinevere and Bedywyr succeed in turning Arthur into a Christian martyr to ease the pain caused by their part in his downfall, or will his sister Morgan succeeds in claiming him for the old gods? Of course, she has many a trick up her sleeve, but there are also a few surprises that even she hadn’t bargained for.

title: Chew Stoke
subtitle: CHEW STOKE has a population of around a 1000 and lies at the foot of the Mendip Hills – designated an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.
bodyContent: CHEW STOKE has a population of around a 1000 and lies at the foot of the Mendip Hills – designated an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The village sits at the northern end of Chew Valley Lake, 9 miles south of Bristol, 11 miles north of wells and 12 miles west of Bath . Listed in the Domesday Book as Chiwestoche the suggestion is it may have had some military connection at the time – the name “Stoke” comes from the old English stoc meaning a stockade. This lengthy history is reflected in the number of heritage listed buildings throughout the Chew Valley. The long established Stoke Inn and the welcoming restaurant the Chew Kitchen sit close to the village centre. There are two lakeside restaurants, The Salt and Malt (specialising in fish and chips) and Woodford Lodge. The community includes a primary school, a medical centre and GP’s surgery, the multi-use Church Hall, and boasts a number of flourishing clubs and societies. Bed and breakfast accommodation is catered for by Orchard House and the Stoke Inn . The buildings at Fairseat Farm , once a working dairy, have been converted to office and workshop use – spaces which include a hairdressing salon, a joinery, an artist’s studio, an osteopath practice, a flower design shop, and a TV and video business. A century old national cycling route – the Bristol to Padstow West Country Way – is still popular with cyclists and runs through the village The village’s substantial claim to history, is its double century association with the BILBIE FAMILY – clock makers and bell founders, who lived and worked in Chew Stoke from the late 17th to late 19th century. The family cast 1350 bells for churches all over the west country and the south west. The oldest surviving bell, cast in 1698, is still working in the village church of St Andrew. CHEW STOKE CHURCH HALL is situated on the corner of Church Lane. It is used for church events, and by a number of village organisations – including the Parish Council, the WI, Chew Stoke Film Club, the Dramatic Society, Scissors Exercise Class, the Hall Singers and Chew Valley Choral Society. Insured and licensed for 100 people, the hall is available for hire by individuals, clubs and societies; and is an ideal venue for public meetings, private events, suppers, parties and wedding receptions. Every month it plays host to the Majestic , the village Neighbourhood Cinema, supported by the British Film Institute and the National Lottery. For more church hall details, facilities and booking arrangements, visit www.chewstokechurchhall.org.uk For village information, news, events, activities and celebrations, visit chewstoke.org.uk

title: Weston Museum in Weston super Mare
subtitle: Weston Musuem in Weston super Mare has something for everyone. We want to open the museum to as many people as possible, so we’re constantly putting on events for all ages and interests. Head to the museum website to find out what is coming up soon.
bodyContent: “Once you know your history you understand more of who you are, you learn from the past and find ways to predict the future and even help create a better one.” Housed in a beautiful and distinctive historic building. We tell the story of the town and the surrounding area from prehistoric times to the present day. The museum is dedicated to being a social and educational hub for the people of Weston and its visitors. You can come to learn, relax or just have fun! The North Somerset Council museum collection contains around 50,000 individual objects. The newly refurbished museum also allows our guests to grab lunch at the cosy Clara’s Café, hire a space for a meeting or even a party in the courtyard. Museum’s do not have to be dull and dusty, in fact, Weston Museum encourages a hands-on approach to history. We also work closely with local schools and community groups to help support the Weston of today and grow the Weston of tomorrow. Our diverse volunteering programme also gives you the chance to get involved. Diversity is key! Our William Mable Gallery allows us, for the first time, to host exhibitions suitable for the world stage. We’ve already been able to display items from the Imperial War Museum and The British Museum. The content of this gallery changes throughout the year, so there is always something new at Weston Museum. Weston Museum is working towards being as accessible as possible. There is a lift for wheelchair users and those who cannot manage stairs to access the main upper floor galleries. Due to the nature of Clara’s Cottage being built in 1865, this part of the museum is unfortunately not completely accessible to wheelchair users due to narrow corridors and a staircase. Weston Museum’s free admission means that the museum is truly for everyone and is quickly becoming a popular destination among tourists as one of Weston's top attractions. Facilities Wheelchair Friendly, Café, Gift Shop, Baby Change Facilities, Accessible Lift, Parking Nearby, Disabled Toilet Available, Toilets Available
tagline: There is something for everyone here at Weston Museum.

title: Kobi & Teal
subtitle: Kobi & Teal was co-founded by designers Nick Fraser and Polly Bell to offer a considered collection of artwork and objects presented alongside their own work. With a mission to bring together a diverse group of small design brands, individual makers, and contemporary artists, Kobi & Teal holds focus on self-production.
bodyContent: The rich and varied range represents our enthusiasm for the individual. With the inclusion of traditional craft and contemporary design or a combination of both, we look to feature thoughtful products that find a balance between the playful and sophistication. Kobi & Teal brings a unique experience for its visitors; offering an exciting product range together with one-off and small batch samples. With a solid background in interior product and textile design, Nick and Polly are privileged to work collaboratively with their designers often making individual pieces specifically for the Kobi & Teal customers. These on-going developments will be accessible to the wider audience through our website along with updates of events and exhibitions. The gallery space offers Kobi & Teal a welcome opportunity to enhance its visual and exploratory content. Each exhibition will introduce a contrasting discipline to the last from artists and designers with a variety of backgrounds and experiences. This distinctive addition to the shop will contribute to the ever-evolving nature of this business, creating a destination for those looking for something new. The vibrant selection of work Kobi & Teal offer will continue to grow, bringing something to everyone who wants to support the independent and help it thrive, not through duty but because it’s the better way to shop. title: East Cottage
subtitle: This gorgeous holiday cottage, which dates back to the 17th century, has an abundance of period features and traditional English country charm.
bodyContent: This gorgeous holiday cottage, which dates back to the 17th century, has an abundance of period features and traditional English country charm. This is tastefully combined with the provision of all the modern conveniences that you would expect to find in a 5 star cottage. The standard of the accommodation at East Cottage reflects our very high expectations of quality, cleanliness, attention to detail and service. Our charming holiday cottage is set in a beautiful rural location; lots of fresh air, farmland and farm animals with great walks and country pubs on the doorstep – always a good combination for keeping children, and parents (!) amused. The cottage itself has many lovely attributes. On the ground floor is the beamed living/dining-room with open inglenook fireplace, exposed stone walls and stone mullion windows, as well as TV, DVD and IPod dock; well-equipped kitchen with fridge, freezer, gas hob, electric oven and microwave; and utility room with washing-machine and dishwasher. A beautiful stone spiral staircase leads up to the first floor to the 2 large double bedrooms and bathroom with WC, washbasin, bath and separate shower cubicle. Again, beams, mullion windows and charming features in abundance! The cottage sleeps 4 (plus cot) in two bedrooms comprising 1 with king size double bed, and the other which can either be made up as a super king size double, or with 2 twin single beds. The cottage is therefore ideal for both families with children, or for couples trying to escape them! Children of all ages are welcome at East Cottage. A travel cot is provided, as well as stair-gates and high chair. We provide a baby-changing mat and baby bath, and there is also a toy box and a selection of games, jigsaws, books and DVDs. The cottage has gas central heating and free Wi-Fi. Towels are provided, as well as tea towels, toiletries, quality bed linen and an initial supply of logs for cosy nights in by the fire. We also provide basics such as tea, coffee, milk, sugar and cake! There are 2 parking spaces for the exclusive use of guests staying at East Cottage in the courtyard to the right of the cottage. Behind the courtyard, a small flight of steps leads to the private, secluded and gated garden. The well-established walled garden includes lawned areas, herbaceous borders and a south-facing patio, ideal for ‘al fresco’ dining. We also provide a barbeque and a supply of charcoal. The cottage is about 100 yards walking distance of the village shop, which sells local produce,and 300 yards to the wonderful village pub. The cottage is available for hire for a minimum of 2 nights. However in July & August it is let for whole weeks only, Saturday to Saturday. Please email or phone direct for tariff and seasonal offers. We look forward to welcoming you soon!
tagline: The standard of the accommodation at East Cottage reflects our very high expectations

title: Flow Bar Frome
subtitle: At the heart of Frome. A place to meet, mixing character, service and independent spirit. Occasional local food offerings and live music.
bodyContent: Flow Bar Frome is in a beautifully renovated Georgian building with contemporary styling, offering two floors of sophisticated bar space on a medieval bridge with views overlooking the river Frome near Bath. Enjoy a seasonal cocktail list using local garnishes and ingredients, local cider, gin and their own Flow Pale Ale, available to drink-in or takeaway. They also collaborate with independent local businesses, providing food offerings such as Tacos and Sharing Platters on certain days. See live and acoustic sets from local DJs and singer/songwriters, as well as specially curated events throughout the year, showcasing the best drinks, food and entertainment that Frome and Somerset have to offer.

title: The Malthouse
subtitle: Fall in love with The Malthouse, a romantic Grade II listed building with modern levels of space and comfort, perfectly located for family holidays in Somerset. 7 bedrooms, 4 bathrooms, modern kitchen, with open fire, two large living areas, reliable wi-fi and idyllic views over the garden and private parking.
bodyContent: As soon as you walk through the heavy oak door into the original cart-way, you feel this warm friendly space, from the cart-way you will see the stylish handmade kitchen and dining room, complete with working stone fireplace. The huge pine dining table is just asking to host up to 14 people for an extended family meal or several breakfast sittings, cooked up in the well-equipped kitchen. A utility room in the basement has a washing machine, tumble drier and extra tall fridge plus a useful storage area for extra food. The two lounges are comfortable and thoughtfully furnished. One has an inglenook fireplace, very welcoming on those colder days, deep sofa, workspace and cosy lighting. The other is the garden room where you can enjoy far-reaching views of the idyllic countryside. Elegantly proportioned and plenty of room for family games, relaxation and 50inch smart TV. The 7 bedrooms are large and comfortable with crisp Egyptian cotton linen and fluffy towels. One king bedroom on the ground floor with its own bathroom, 1st and second floor a further 6 bedrooms and 3 bathrooms. Decorated with style and comfort in mind. There's a big open courtyard and large, long, well-managed garden. Guests enjoy alfresco dining and barbecues. A range of outdoor games including table tennis are provided for screen-free fun, well behaved dogs welcome. Private parking. On your doorstep Bath, Bristol, Longleat all easily reached, as well as many local walks and National Trust gardens.

title: Holy Trinity Church
subtitle: Unique Collection of 9 Burne-Jones Stained Glass windows in one place.
bodyContent: The nine windows were designed by the Pre-Raphaelite artist Edward Burne-Jones, they span the entirety of his careers in stained glass (1866-1896) and were manufactured in the famous William Morris workshops between 1880 and 1903. These windows with the strongly rendered figures, beautifully designed foliate backgrounds and tich colours are outstanding in their quality, and together they form what is perhaps the most impressive collection of Burne-Jones/Morris and Co stained glass in the south west.
tagline: Unique Collection of 9 Burne-Jones Stained Glass windows in one place.

subtitle: The Grand Pier is open every day, except Christmas Day, so come hail, rain or shine, you’ll always get a warm welcome. Whatever the weather is doing outside, it’s still fun, fun, fun on the inside.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The Grand Pier, Weston super Mare, Somerset is the ideal destination for non-stop indoor family theme park fun. This North Somerset pier, with its state-of-the-art Pavilion is a truly iconic destination for family days out, events, concerts, weddings, and corporate events. With rides, attractions and the latest arcade games a visit to the Pier is the perfect treat for kids of all ages. On weekends, bank holidays and North Somerset school holidays, Unlimited Ride Wristbands are available for both adults and children, explore here . Don't miss out on this fantastic deal for your fun-filled day! Come and discover everything the Grand Pier, Somerset has to offer, including: · The very latest amusements - including giant screen Space Invaders · Thrilling rides including: Sidewinder, Freefall and Robocoaster · An amazing two level 300 meter indoor Go-Kart track · Seaside favourites, including: dodgems, house of horrors and helter skelter · A three-level, dinosaur themed soft play area with dedicated adult seating · A choice of places to eat and drink - we even serve your favourite Costa coffee! With hundreds of amusements and games to play, a range of thrilling rides, and a choice of attractions for all ages everyone gets to have fun in the amazing Pavilion - it really is one big house of fun!!! When you’re ready for a bite to eat you’re spoilt for choice from traditional fish and chips to afternoon tea, and of course ice cream too! There’s even a pub for you to enjoy a relaxing drink as you take in the spectacular views. As a unique location our function rooms are always in demand, and we love creating the perfect setting for weddings and family celebrations. For businesses our dedicated events team is on hand for corporate events, ranging from team meetings and training sessions to large scale conferences.The fun continues into the night with a wide range of events from concerts to whodunnits. To make sure you don’t miss out visit and book your tickets online today.
tagline: The Grand Pier, is the ideal destination for non-stop indoor family theme park fun.

title: The Royal Hotel Weston
subtitle: The Royal Hotel is a charismatic and elegant Georgian Building, is ideally located on the Seafront. Standing in its own extensive lawns, which extend to the Promenade, the Royal enjoys beautiful sea views, and is also in close proximity to our Town Centre and accessible by public transport.
bodyContent: The Royal Hotel is a charismatic and elegant Georgian Building, is ideally located on the Seafront. Standing in its own extensive lawns, which extend to the Promenade, the Royal enjoys beautiful sea views, and is also in close proximity to our Town Centre and accessible by public transport. The 44 attractive and comfortable rooms here at The Royal, feature ensuite bathrooms, Freeview TV, Tea & Coffee making facilities, Dressing Table/Desk, Direct-dial telephone, Hairdryer, Trouser press and complimentary toiletries. Wi-Fi is complimentary throughout the hotel. Newspapers and early morning wake up calls are available on request. Due to our fantastic location, all bedrooms boast lovely views of either Weston Seafront, The picturesque Italian Gardens, or the bustling Town Square. We provide a wide range of accommodation, choose from the following options….Doubles, Singles, Twins, Four Posters, Family Rooms that sleep 4-6, and our impeccable, brand new range of Royal Luxury Doubles! Disabled access is plentiful throughout the ground floor facilities, including the Bar & Restaurant. There is a lift to both floors, as well as disabled friendly bedrooms featuring a specialised wet-room. Please contact us to discuss any special requirements you may need. Our comfortable and traditional Feathers Bar is open daily for Drinks, Real Ales, Snacks, Afternoon Tea and Coffees. Enjoy a game of pool, or relax into a comfy sofa with a paper and a glass of wine. Friday night is party night in Feathers with a range of regular entertainment to kick off the weekend! Our Award Winning Restaurant epitomises the elegant regency style for which Weston was formally renowned. In these captivating surroundings you can enjoy dishes carefully selected for our appealing menu which has been designed to tempt and excite all tastes. Open for Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner every day, with our famous Carvery available Tuesdays, Thursdays – and of course, Sundays. This charming Georgian Hotel is renowned as Weston’s premier wedding venue, due to our first class reputation built on the outstanding reviews from the many bride and grooms whose weddings we have planned and hosted. Our Ballroom boasts idyllic sea views across Weston Bay and our extensive lawn with its sweeping bay windows makes it the perfect setting for a romantic Wedding. We hold a Civil Wedding & Civil Partnership licence, enabling you to simplify your arrangements by holding all aspects of your special day in one venue. For more information why not take a look at our Wedding Brochure online, or download our brand new & exclusive Wedding App for smart phones and tablets. For any questions, or to book a viewing, please contact our Wedding & Events team at the hotel. Hair Salon Pin-ups Hair Salon promises a ‘different vibe’ to other hairdressers and Owner Kaysha says it will definitely be a cut above the rest! Customers can expect a relaxed, comfortable experience, extremely reasonable prices and a friendly service with a bubbly atmosphere. Kaysha and her team offer preferential rates to Royal Hotel residents and Hotel bridal parties. For appointments and further information please contact Pin-ups Hair Salon Reception on 01934 624788 or 07794565280. Beauty Room Exciting new Beauty Salon Opening 2018! Beauty Within will offer a complete range of treatments, skincare and beauty therapies. More details coming soon! FREE WIFI & PARKING FOR RESIDENTS
tagline: The Royal Hotel is a charismatic and elegant Georgian Building, is ideally located on the Seafront.

title: Westfield
subtitle: The parish of Westfield surrounds an ancient Roman Road, the Fosseway. Although Westfield was not named in the Domesday Book it finally got its full identity when it was named as a Civil Parish in 2011. Positioned between the towns of Midsomer Norton and Radstock, Westfield is emerging as a true community with a character all of its own.
bodyContent: The parish of Westfield surrounds an ancient Roman Road, the Fosseway. Although Westfield was not named in the Domesday Book it finally got its full identity when it was named as a Civil Parish in 2011. Positioned between the towns of Midsomer Norton and Radstock, Westfield is emerging as a true community with a character all of its own. By the early nineteenth century Westfield still consisted mostly of rural land and coal mining works, with little residential development. Westfield’s unique street scene emerged with the building of large numbers of terraced miners' cottages along the Fosse Way in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries and the area developed into a more populous neighbourhood in its own right. Modern housing estates were developed on land on both sides of the Fosse Way from the 1970’s onwards. Industrial coal mining was established in 1763 and for two centuries was the major employer in the area. There were three mines in Westfield, two at Norton Hill and one in Wellsway. In the early nineteenth century, whilst Westfield was still very rural, a large three storey building was built immediately adjacent to the main Fosse Way. This property still exists and is now a listed building. Many rumours have grown up about the purpose of the building – was it a private house of maybe an Isolation Hospital for Bath patients? It was called Westfield House. Through the late nineteenth century and twentieth century the population of Westfield grew very quickly. Work was varied from coal mining, canal work, railway and haulage work, shoemaking and printing. All these industries have long gone but, despite this, Westfield is still very much a thriving parish. Currently there is a large industrial estate which is constantly growing and developing, providing local employment. Things to do: Heritage walks Westfield has three heritage walks of different levels, from an easy stroll to slightly rougher terrain, designed to open up and show off the beautiful parish. Along the way walkers will be able to read up on boards dedicated to the history of where they are standing. The trails take in, among other things, a former pit path, two Second World War pill boxes and old engine house and pit pony stables, thought to be the only such stables left in the country and two churches. Recreation grounds Westfield Parish Council is responsible for two recreation grounds that were donated to the parish by miners’ trusts back in the time of coal mining for the recreation of miners and their families. Norton Hill Recreation Ground on the Fosseway has a football pitch for hire, with changing facilities, a tennis court, boules pitch, permanent table tennis table and basketball hoop, as well as a children’s play area. Westhill Recreation Ground, Westhill Road, has a football pitch for hire, with changing facilities at Westhill Club, a BMX track and children’s play area. There is ample free parking at both sites. Bowls There are two bowls clubs in Westfield – NorWest Bowls at Norton Hill Recreation Ground, 01761 410861, https://sites.google.com/site/norwestbowlingclub/home . Norwest has a lane for casual use if you call ahead, and Prattens on Charlton Lane, contact 01761 412705, Barry Dando, Chairman https://prattensbowlsclub.com/ . Facilities: 3 Churches Pharmacy Primary School Special School 3 Cafes Co-op Supermarket Large Industrial Estate Allotments Contact: 01761 410669 Westfieldparishcouncil.co.uk council@westfieldparishcouncil.co.uk Twitter - @westfield_pc Facebook – Westfield Parish Council

title: Doris Hatt Exhibition in Queen’s Square
subtitle: Wander through Queen’s Square and see what would have been empty windows, filled with the artwork of the late, great, Clevedon local, Doris Hatt.
bodyContent: The windows of Feast, the walls of The Baptist Church and the east side of the square will each exhibit some of Doris Hatt’s lively style of painting Doris developed in the early 1930s. Despite the lack of establishment recognition she contributed to numerous exhibitions, both solo and with others, over the next 40 years at various venues, including Clevedon Art Club, Clifton Arts Club and the RWA Bristol. Doris grew up in Bath but moved to Clevedon’s Swiss Valley in 1922 and lived there for the rest of her life. Amongst her achievements, and the one in which she took most pride, was designing a house in the International Modernist style to be her new home. It was called Littlemead and it still stands. Doris and her partner, Margery Mack Smith, a school teacher and weaver, made Littlemead a meeting place for lively discussions about science, the arts and politics. You can learn more about Doris Hatt from a small book, ‘Doris Hatt: Revolutionary Artist.’ Copies are available (£7.99) from Clevedon Community Bookshop and Books on the Hill. Clevedon BID would like to thank: the picture owners for permission to reproduce them, ThatCopyShop for the design, print and install and Clevedon Baptist Church and Feast for display space. This scheme was made possible by the generous support of Wessex Investors. It has been funded by the Welcome Back Fund financed by the European Regional Development Fund as part of the European Structural and Investment Funds Growth Programme 2014-2020.
tagline: Wander through Queen’s Square and see what would have been empty windows

title: Polkadot Gallery
subtitle: Polkadot Gallery is a jewellery shop situated in Taunton's Independent Quarter.
bodyContent: Established by photographer Charles Parsons and Julia Heppell in 2001, Polkadot Gallery started life as Polkadot Art Gallery and was based in Exeter’s South Street. It quickly became apparent that jewellery, a lifelong passion of Julia’s, was such a strong medium it warranted a dedicated gallery and so in 2003 began Polkadot Precious, based at 12 Martins Lane, Exeter. We’re still enjoying our spot along the cobbles, a stones throw away from the Cathedral today, although we’re now known as Polkadot Gallery. The Exeter gallery was and continues to be such a success that Julia opened a second store in Riverside Place, Taunton, close to the beautiful River Tone, in 2007. Both galleries employ staff from jewellery making and art backgrounds, who are passionate about the work they sell and knowledgeable about both quality and design. 2016 has seen us launch a new online store, allowing us sell our diverse and distinct collection worldwide. Julia travels to Munich, Basle and Amsterdam to source fresh and interesting jewellery and to Copenhagen for Arne Jacobsen watches. Polkadot Gallery is also proud to encourage and exhibit the best of emerging and established designers Devon, Cornwall and Somerset have to offer. This eclectic mix of local and international makers gives our customers an unrivalled choice of contemporary jewellery.
tagline: Local and international jewellery.

title: Postscript
subtitle: Small but amazing independent stationery, arts and crafts, design and print shop in the heart of Frome. A small company with big appeal. An Aladdin's Cave of product, featuring brands like Lamy, Moleskine, Leuchtturm, Rhodia and many more.
bodyContent: Postscript was created in 2015 by Garry and Rachel who's team of creatives love design and all things art, craft and stationery. With an emphasis on sustainable and ethical product, Postscript verges on being a gift shop with plenty of diverse products to suit all ages, abilities and needs! Lacking creative ideas? Rachel's background in art and teaching makes her the perfect personal shopper - whether face to face, over the phone or via a Whatsapp video call! Bridie is Postscript's talented lead designer, and alongside Garry, who specialises in business and marketing, they offer design and print services for individuals, creatives and small and large businesses. From weddings to brand and packaging design, or business cards, or just simple quality printing, Postscript has something to offer everyone. Postscript has a high volume laser colour printer and a full colour wide format printer on site, and can print from A6 to A0 and beyond! They also outsource print commissions locally, where possible and always deliver the best value service in the business. "Postscript is not just our business, it is our way of life!" say Garry and Rachel. "We have a large and talented family, many of who have been and are still involved in the business. Our staff are our extended family and even Otis, our dog, is part of what we do!". Postscript have recently launched a website to offer most of their products and services to a larger audience.
tagline: Small but amazing independent stationery

title: Radstock
subtitle: Radstock is renowned as one of the best preserved former coal-mining towns in England which is the basis of its conservation status. Much more can be learnt with a visit to Radstock Museum which houses a range of exhibits, giving visitors the opportunity to immerse themselves in the town’s industrial and social history.
bodyContent: Nestled on the edge of the Mendips , Radstock has access to spectacular routes for both walking and cycling with quiet country lanes and beautiful countryside. It is home to the Radstock Museum where a wide range of exhibits give an insight into much of Radstock’s varied history and geology.and close to Writhlington School, notable for its orchid collection which has won numerous awards and houses the largest collection of orchids outside of Kew Gardens. There's so much more to discover about Radstock.

title: Wells Touring Park, Self catering lodges & cottages
subtitle: Fabulous self catering cottages & lodges near Wells, Somerset.
bodyContent: Wells is one of the most popular holiday destinations in the UK, so why not enjoy a romantic break, or even a last minute getaway to one of our cottages or lodges? We have 4 small holiday cottages and one luxury lodge. They all sleep two adults (doubles) and are self-catering accommodation. With an open plan living space, the delightful little cottages with be perfect for your cosy breaks away. You can always remain connected during your stay with Club Wi-Fi throughout the touring park. Rent one of our exclusive Lodges for your perfect luxurious holiday or short romantic break. These are all brand new and fully fitted. Wells Touring Park has its very own dog shower for your use after winter walks for guests staying in the cottages where dogs are allowed. We are perfectly placed for Cheddar , Wookey, Weston Super Mare , Glastonbury and Clarks outlet village or just come and relax in our peaceful location. See website for further information/photos or just call us to enquire.

title: Somerset Lavender
subtitle: Buy gorgeous lavender products directly from the people who grow it in the stunning Somerset countryside.
bodyContent: Somerset Lavender in Somerset offers a shopping experience with a difference. Surrounded by the soothing presence of the lavender fields, you can browse our lavender product range in comfort and then relax with tea and cake in our on site café. We stock a wide range of gifts and lavender products made from the lavender grown on our farm. Products range from the lavender essential oil, distilled naturally on the farm using steam, to toiletries and soft furnishings. Our highly sought after honey made by the bees in the lavender field is certainly one to try but do hurry as stocks are limited due to the nature of this product. Lavender plants are also available for purchase. Somerset Lavender in Somerset will be open for six weeks from the 9 th November. A great opportunity to do some relaxed Christmas shopping. Wide range of unique gifts only available on the farm. Cafe will be open too, meet up with friends for a coffee and a chat. Hope to see you soon.
tagline: Buy gorgeous lavender products directly from the people who grow it in the stunning countryside.

title: The Royal Hotel Weston
subtitle: The Royal Hotel is a charismatic and elegant Georgian Building, is ideally located on the Seafront. Standing in its own extensive lawns, which extend to the Promenade, the Royal enjoys beautiful sea views, and is also in close proximity to our Town Centre and accessible by public transport.
bodyContent: The Royal Hotel is a charismatic and elegant Georgian Building, is ideally located on the Seafront. Standing in its own extensive lawns, which extend to the Promenade, the Royal enjoys beautiful sea views, and is also in close proximity to our Town Centre and accessible by public transport. The 44 attractive and comfortable rooms here at The Royal, feature ensuite bathrooms, Freeview TV, Tea & Coffee making facilities, Dressing Table/Desk, Direct-dial telephone, Hairdryer, Trouser press and complimentary toiletries. Wi-Fi is complimentary throughout the hotel. Newspapers and early morning wake up calls are available on request. Due to our fantastic location, all bedrooms boast lovely views of either Weston Seafront, The picturesque Italian Gardens, or the bustling Town Square. We provide a wide range of accommodation, choose from the following options….Doubles, Singles, Twins, Four Posters, Family Rooms that sleep 4-6, and our impeccable, brand new range of Royal Luxury Doubles! Disabled access is plentiful throughout the ground floor facilities, including the Bar & Restaurant. There is a lift to both floors, as well as disabled friendly bedrooms featuring a specialised wet-room. Please contact us to discuss any special requirements you may need. Our comfortable and traditional Feathers Bar is open daily for Drinks, Real Ales, Snacks, Afternoon Tea and Coffees. Enjoy a game of pool, or relax into a comfy sofa with a paper and a glass of wine. Friday night is party night in Feathers with a range of regular entertainment to kick off the weekend! Our Award Winning Restaurant epitomises the elegant regency style for which Weston was formally renowned. In these captivating surroundings you can enjoy dishes carefully selected for our appealing menu which has been designed to tempt and excite all tastes. Open for Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner every day, with our famous Carvery available Tuesdays, Thursdays – and of course, Sundays. This charming Georgian Hotel is renowned as Weston’s premier wedding venue, due to our first class reputation built on the outstanding reviews from the many bride and grooms whose weddings we have planned and hosted. Our Ballroom boasts idyllic sea views across Weston Bay and our extensive lawn with its sweeping bay windows makes it the perfect setting for a romantic Wedding. We hold a Civil Wedding & Civil Partnership licence, enabling you to simplify your arrangements by holding all aspects of your special day in one venue. For more information why not take a look at our Wedding Brochure online, or download our brand new & exclusive Wedding App for smart phones and tablets. For any questions, or to book a viewing, please contact our Wedding & Events team at the hotel. Hair Salon Pin-ups Hair Salon promises a ‘different vibe’ to other hairdressers and Owner Kaysha says it will definitely be a cut above the rest! Customers can expect a relaxed, comfortable experience, extremely reasonable prices and a friendly service with a bubbly atmosphere. Kaysha and her team offer preferential rates to Royal Hotel residents and Hotel bridal parties. For appointments and further information please contact Pin-ups Hair Salon Reception on 01934 624788 or 07794565280. Beauty Room Exciting new Beauty Salon Opening 2018! Beauty Within will offer a complete range of treatments, skincare and beauty therapies. More details coming soon! FREE WIFI & PARKING FOR RESIDENTS
tagline: The Royal Hotel is a charismatic and elegant Georgian Building, is ideally located on the Seafront.

title: Nativity The Musical
subtitle: In association with The MATA Regal Theatre Co. Ltd, the award-winning team that brought ‘Chitty Chitty Bang Bang’ and ‘Grease’ to the Regal stage are proud to present the first MATA Winter Show – Nativity: The Musical.
bodyContent: Feel-good, funny and full of joy, this cracker of a musical was adapted for the stage by Debbie Isitt, the creator of the much-loved films. Every child in every school has one Christmas wish, to star in a Nativity, and at St Bernadette’s School they’re attempting to mount a musical version! Only trouble is teacher Mr Maddens has promised that a Hollywood producer is coming to see the show to turn it into a film. Join him, his teaching assistant the loveable Mr Poppy, hilarious children and a whole lot of sparkle and shine as they struggle to make everyone’s Christmas wish come true. Featuring all of your favourite sing-a-long hits from the movies including Sparkle and Shine, Nazareth, One Night One Moment, She’s the Brightest Star and a whole host of new songs, this musical really ‘ is a heartfelt hit ’ (The Times). Book now and join us for some MAYHEM in Bethlehem!

title: André Rieu White Christmas
subtitle: Join André Rieu and his Johann Strauss Orchestra for their brand-new Christmas Concert. An unforgettable festive treat for the whole family!
bodyContent: For many, Christmas is the most wonderful time of the year. This year it will come early with André Rieu’s cinema special White Christmas — a celebration you will never forget. From the first jingled bell, you will be immersed in the incomparable Christmas atmosphere of André’s winter wonderland. Marvel at the magnificently decorated Christmas palace, complete with snow, two ice rinks, gorgeous winter scenes, romantic lighting, red carpet, countless lights, 150 beautiful chandeliers and more than 50 Venetian candelabras. Savour the spirit of the season while singing and dancing in the aisles to timeless Christmas carols, romantic waltzes and beautiful songs from all over the world — Jingle Bells, Ave Maria, Oh Holy Night, Hallelujah, Sleigh Ride and many more! Cinema audiences will also enjoy exclusive backstage access, as cinema host Charlotte Hawkins speaks with André about creating his musical winter wonderland. It’s a perfect early Christmas present for André fans! Join André Rieu and his Johann Strauss Orchestra for their brand new Christmas concert. An unforgettable festive treat for the whole family! Get your tickets now for André Rieu’s White Christmas!

title: Middlewick Holiday Cottages
subtitle: Self catering cottages in Glastonbury. Perfect short break in Somerset with indoor pool.
bodyContent: A secluded holiday resort just minutes from Glastonbury town centre, with stunning views of Glastonbury Tor and the Mendip Hills. Set on 16 peaceful acres, The Middlewick offers self-catering accommodation in 10 cottages converted from original 17th-century farm buildings, 3 log cabins and 3 glamping pods. Our properties range from 1 to 5 bedrooms, offering plenty of choice for couples, families, friends and groups looking for country getaway. Many are dog friendly. We have a Café , Farm Shop and Spa on site – all of which are open to day visitors as well as guests staying with us. Our site, including our indoor heated pool and steam room, is powered by renewable energy, and Spa treatments take place in our cosy Shepherd’s Huts. Surrounded by apple orchards, this is a real escape to the Somerset countryside – with plenty of space to roam in the beauty of nature. Visitors can walk to Glastonbury Tor easily in under 30 minutes. There’s so much to explore nearby, with Glastonbury Tor, Chalice Well and Gardens, Glastonbury Abbey and Clark’s Village on our doorstep. Glastonbury is a unique market town bustling with unusual shops and alternative events. The Avalon Marshes Nature Reserve, Cathedral City of Wells and Cheddar Gorge are within easy driving distance from The Middlewick. Somerset is known for its food, music and outstanding natural beauty – and this is the ideal base from which to explore the best of the county.

title: Double-Gate Farm
subtitle: Georgian farmhouse B&B accommodation with self catering converted barns in a peaceful location in Somerset, near Glastonbury & Wells.
bodyContent: Welcome to Double-Gate Farm, our Georgian farmhouse situated on the banks of the River Sheppey. Our farm offers views of the Mendip Hills and the surrounding countryside. Whether you're looking for a romantic getaway, a family vacation, or a group retreat, we have a variety of accommodations to choose from. Our converted barn is perfect for couples, families, and groups, while our accessible Riverside rooms and facilities cater to everyone's requirements. Our seasonal Tea Room is open from March to December and offers a range of delicious breakfasts, light lunches, home-baked cakes, and our speciality, Afternoon Tea. How about renting our BBQ Hut for a fun and sociable evening of cooking with your loved ones? Our Games Room is the perfect place to unwind after a long day of exploring. With a full-size snooker table, table-tennis, and lots of board games and local information, you'll never run out of things to do. At Double-Gate Farm, we pride ourselves on providing a peaceful and relaxing environment that allows you to unwind and enjoy nature. You can fish from your patio, watch the wildlife, or simply sit back and read. We welcome everyone, including cycling groups, walkers, and countryside lovers. Our location is perfect for exploring Somerset's hidden gems. With easy access to Glastonbury, Wells, and Cheddar, you'll be able to experience all that this beautiful region has to offer. We're also dog-friendly, so you don't have to leave your furry friend behind. Two of our Riverside rooms are pet-friendly, so please call us to check availability when booking with your dog. Finally, our farm is next door to a renowned gastropub that serves food and local brews. It's just a short walk away, so you don't have to worry about transportation. Come and experience the beauty of Double-Gate Farm for yourself.
tagline: Georgian farmhouse B&B accommodation with self catering converted barns

title: The Nutcracker
subtitle: LIVE from The Royal Opera House on Sunday, 17th December at 2:00pm The Royal Ballet brings you THE NUTCRACKER.
bodyContent: Discover the enchantment of ballet with this sparkling festive treat for the whole family. Join Clara at a delightful Christmas Eve party that becomes a magical adventure once everyone else is tucked up in bed. Marvel at the brilliance of Tchaikovsky’s score, as Clara and her enchanted Nutcracker fight the Mouse King and visit the Sugar Plum Fairy in the glittering Kingdom of Sweets. Peter Wright’s much-loved production for The Royal Ballet, with gorgeous period designs by Julia Trevelyan Oman, keeps true to the spirit of this festive ballet classic, combining the thrill of the fairy tale with spectacular dancing. Running time: 170 minutes, including one interval.

title: The Snow Queen
subtitle: Minehead Panto People presents ‘THE SNOW QUEEN’. Hans Christian Andersen’s classic tale has been adapted for Pantomime and runs for the following dates. Saturday 30th December 2:30 & 7:30. Sunday 31st December 2:30. Monday 1st January 2:30, Thursday 4th January 7:30, Friday 5th January 7:30, Saturday 6th January 2:30 & 7.30
bodyContent: Show dates are as follows (Please note there are some matinees in addition to the evening shows): 30 December Saturday – 2.30 and 7.30 31 December Sunday – 2.30 1 January Monday – 2.30 4 January Thursday – 7.30 5 January Friday – 7.30 6 January Saturday – 2.30 and 7.30 Minehead Panto People present ‘The Snow Queen’ by Emma Houldershaw and Samantha Cartwright. Adapted from Hans Christian Andersen’s classic tale this is an entirely original version of The Snow Queen which has been adapted for Pantomime. The land of Norderdell is under the spell of the Snow Queen. When her brother Kai is stricken by a slither of the Queen’s evil mirror, Greta embarks on a journey to rescue him, and on her quest she is helped by various oddball characters, Batty Bridget the Dame, the Easter Bunny, Jingle and Jangle, the Tooth Fairy and the Sandman. The Snow Queen gives her the chance of saving Kai if she will procure for her the magical Dark Oracle Orb, which is safeguarded by the weird Witches. Jack Frost is also under the Snow Queen’s spell and falls for Greta.

title: The Great Escaper (cert 12A)
subtitle: Starring Michael Caine and Glenda Jackson in her last film.
bodyContent: Starring Michael Caine and Glenda Jackson in her last film, The Great Escaper is based on a true story that made national news about pensioner Bernard Jordan who in 2014 absconded from his care home in Hove to join fellow war veterans on a beach in Normandy for an event commemorating the 70th anniversary of the D-Day landings. After the local police were notified the care home received a call that evening to say that Bernard Jordan had been found safe and well in France. title: RHL Beach Race
subtitle: The Weston Beach Race is one of the most eagerly-anticipated events in the town's annual calendar and has to be seen to be believed.
bodyContent: The Weston Beach Race is one of the most eagerly-anticipated events in the town's annual calendar and has to be seen to be believed. Watch the thrills and drama unfold over two days of high-octane motorsport action as the daredevil riders take on the challenging six-mile course in what has been described as the maddest, baddest and biggest event in the UK off-road calendar. The beach is transformed into a giant race track for motorsport's equivalent of the London Marathon where brave amateur and professional riders battle it out for glory in front of the excited crowds. There are junior races, quad racing, side car races in addition to the much-heralded main event. The drama is guaranteed from the moment the riders rev up for the 2km straight start along the beach before turning to tackle an array of man-made sand dunes, tight corners and challenges on what is recognised as the toughest sand track anywhere in the world. The RHL Activities event, which is also known as the Enduro, is so spectacular it was shortlisted in the final three alongside the Tour of Britain for the honour of being the sporting event of the year. Opening Times RHL Beach Race22 Sept 2023 - 24 Sept 2023 Saturday 09:00 - 16:00 Sunday 10:00 - 16:00
tagline: The Weston Beach Race is one of the most eagerly-anticipated events

title: The Old Oak (Cert 15)
subtitle: Veteran British director Ken Loach’s compassionate, forthright and hopeful film is about a young Syrian woman who joins forces with a pub landlord to unite two traumatised communities in the North East of England.
bodyContent: The Old Oak is a struggling pub in what was previously a thriving mining community, and tensions start to rise in the town when Syrian refugees are placed in the empty houses in the community. Ken Loach, who is 87-years-old, says this will be his last film so don’t miss it! Trailer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fwb0c5zqsyM Guardian review: https://www.theguardian.com/film/2023/sep/30/the-old-oak-review-compassionate-refugee-drama-from-ken-loach

title: Joe Pasquale: The New Normal. 40 Years Of Cack
bodyContent: About Us Joe Pasquale has been showing off on stage for most of his life and now, after four decades of nonsense, he's dragging out his favourite things for another airing to prove that nothing has ever been really normal. So, is, like me, you have ever asked questions like: can a vegetarian get a job as a Beefeater? If beauty is relative, why are all my relatives ugly? If an Eskimo has a house-warming party, will his igloo melt? Why is it that dead people get to ride in such posh cars? If a nudist split beetroot soup in his lap, would he have a stain on his character? And why don't chicken breasts have nipples? Then this is the show for you! Joe will be supported by comedian Lee Carroll. Tickets: £27 Over60s: £23 Child: £23 Family: £85 Groups: 1 in 10 free

title: An Evening of Heartwarming Tales
subtitle: Hosted in our Bar area, by Alexandra Simson, of Story-Well, a unique well-being and training service founded in 2011.
bodyContent: Once there was a well full of ancient stories. For generations storytellers would visit the well, sharing its stories with others. People of all ages, backgrounds and professions were inspired by the stories they heard. They began to awaken to themselves and with each other, to nature and the world around them. Life transformed and the magic that was always then, now and forever came into being… “Alex is an AMAZING storyteller of the very best kind; her voice is liquid, buttery and deep, while her stories are adapted from traditional ancient tales that she gathered from all over the world. A sound-well event leaves you immersed in the story for days after; it’s a fascinating experience of creative listening and inner growth.” (Cynthia J Hurn, co-author with Dr. Bernie S. Siegel, ‘Love, Animals and Miracles.) Join Alex for an evening of Heartwarming Tales this January.

title: Making Plans For Hugo
subtitle: An absurd comedy about a new Father (Nigel) who takes his Son (Hugo) on a journey to see the world and step out of childhood
bodyContent: An absurd comedy about a new Father (Nigel) who takes his Son (Hugo) on a journey to see the world and step out of childhood Inspired by Surrealism, Dada, and the absurd, this story is held together by flights of fancy and love between a father and his newly found bin baby son Hugo. Nigel wants Hugo to grow up to be better than him but is he really doing it for his son? A road trip around the world ensues to see all its possibilities. The Mona Lisa will talk to them, Conger Eels will attack them and Black Holes will eat them! Bonnet Dog is Joe Brooks & Will Jones. Both are actors & theatre makers based in Weston-super-Mare. Frequent makers of strange things in From The Mud Cabaret. Both have a love for the odder side of comedy.

title: Rusalka
subtitle: Dvorák RUSALKA The Royal Opera ENCORE LIVE BROADCAST from The Royal Opera House
bodyContent: A poetic, contemporary new staging of Dvo?ák’s lyric fairytale opera reveals our uneasy relationship with the natural world and humanity’s attempts to own and tame it. Rusalka, a water spirit, lives with her family in the pure waters of the forest lake. When she falls in love with a prince, she sacrifices her voice and leaves her home in the hope of finding true love in a new world – a world that does not love her back. Filmed live at the Royal Opera House in 2022, Semyon Bychkov conducts an all-star cast featuring Asmik Grigorian as Rusalka, with David Butt Philip, Emma Bell, Sarah Connolly, Matthew Rose, Ross Ramgobin, Hongni Wu, Vuvu Mpofu, Gabriel? Kupšyt?, Anne Marie Stanley, Josef Jeongmeen Ahn. Sung in Czech with English subtitles Running time: 225 minutes, including one interval.

title: Dairy Festival
subtitle: Weston’s Dairy Festival was originally born in the 1960s, and was a regular feature of the town’s summer programme of events and drew thousands of people to the seafront. Thanks to some enterprising dairy fanatics and the support of local businesses, the festival is back and we hope it will be bigger and better than ever with a combination of live entertainment and an array of stalls featuring local produce.
bodyContent: Puxton Park are pleased to bring to you the Dairy Festival, a celebration of livestock, agriculture and local producers of food and crafts from all over the South West. Since the re-launch, the event has been brought up to date promoting farming & healthy living. The Dairy Festival has now become one of the largest and most popular events in North Somerset drawing crowds from all over the South West from both the farming and non-farming communities. The event is all about educating its visitors on modern day farming and rural living in a fun, family-oriented way. On show will be • Sheep shearing • Cow milking • Calf parade • Petting zoo • Vintage Tractors and machinery • Craft Fair with all sorts of hand-made items, cheeses, pies and cakes There will also be a cafe bar inside the tent. Visit the website to see the full schedule: https://www.dairyfestival.co.uk/
tagline: Weston’s Dairy Festival was originally born in the 1960s, and was a regular feature

title: Manon
subtitle: Macmillan MANON The Royal Ballet LIVE from The Royal Opera House
bodyContent: Torn between her desire of a life of splendour and riches and her devotion to her true love Des Grieux, the feckless and capricious Manon pays the ultimate price. This adaptation of Abbé Prévost’s novel embodies Kenneth MacMillan at his best, his acute insight into human psychology and his mastery of narrative choreography finding full expression in the impassioned duets of the central couple. Choreography: Kenneth MacMillan. Music: Jules Frédéric Massenet Running time 195 minutes, including two intervals.

title: Jersey Beats
subtitle: A sensational show celebrating the wonderful music of Frankie Valli & The Four Seasons!
bodyContent: This is music with a broad appeal including ‘Sherry’ ‘Beggin’, ‘Grease’ and ‘My Eyes Adored you’ PLUS more music from the era – so no worries about individual taste or pleasing a big group. It’s the show night out not to be missed – wowing crowds in Blackpool since 2014, and now touring the country – OH WHAT A NITE! is a different style of tribute show to any other that you will have seen or heard of before. Matt Andrew leads our vocal quartet as our tribute to Frankie Valli – telling the story of the band and how they formed the group which took them to the dizzy heights of television appearances, fame and fortune… all performed alongside an amazing trio of vocal talent – Johnny, Michael and Toby who take the roles of Nick Massey, Bob Guadio and Tommy Devito. Comedy host Leye D Johns can’t be kept away from the stage for too long either, bringing a light hearted flavour to proceedings and ensuring the crowd leave with a big smile on their face. Our Viva showgirls complete the cast line-up – bringing the moves of the 60s and 70s to the stage as well as backing vocals, and solo numbers of their own bringing the era back to life! The show also has a way of bringing current hits to life too, with that same Doo Wop style – again making OH WHAT A NITE! different to any tribute show you’ll ever see!
