subtitle: Whether you fancy exploring or taking in the views of the county’s many charming villages and towns, you’ll find more with easier local travel. Even for commuters, whether it's our Yeovil services you require, or one of our Taunton or Bridgwater bus routes, we're here to help make your journey hassle-free.
bodyContent: As well as our core network, we also have one of our Adventures By Bus tours operating in the area; the stunning open-top Exmoor Coaster which journeys through Exmoor National Park, from Doniford to Lynmouth. For more information about this route, and our other Adventures By Bus, including timetables and prices, please visit our Adventures By Bus website. From online tickets to timetables and route maps, we have a vast amount of resources to help you get around as easily as possible. We operate services running regularly throughout Somerset and the surrounding area, meaning there is always a bus ready to take you where you need to go. Above, you can find information regarding our bus services including timetables, prices and you can even use our journey planner to ensure a smooth ride. Here at The Buses of Somerset, we care about giving you the best possible journey, giving you a better bus service on every journey. Enjoy The Buses of Somerset.

title: Dunster Castle
subtitle: Fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years, remodelled 100 years ago. Fine 17thC staircase and plaster ceilings. Terrace garden of rare shrubs.
bodyContent: During the winter months, the castle, watermill, and grounds are open at weekends and closed during the week. The Watermill Tearoom, Stables Shop and Parkland are open daily from 10am until 4pm. The car park is also open daily from 10am until 5pm. From 5 April 2025, the whole site is open daily. A fortress that became a family home for the Luttrells, who lived at Dunster for 600 years, the castle was extensively remodelled in the 1870s to create a Victorian country house. The castle boasts breath-taking views over Exmoor, Somerset, and the Bristol Channel as well as holding fine interior features such as a fine 17 th century carved staircase, ornate plaster ceilings, and rare leather wall hangings. Discover how Dunster Castle was used in its heyday and how the family hosted grand occasions from society balls to polo matches with the brilliant ‘Chapters’ guide as well as ‘Castle Explorers, available for children. You can then enjoy a leisurely stroll through beautiful terraced gardens with a collection of palms, sub-tropical plants, and the Dunster Lemon tree. Sited on the River Avill, Dunster Castle is also home to a working watermill that sits within the river gardens. Visit the mill to see the waterwheels in action and even purchase some of the freshly-milled flour. Refreshments are available in the newly-refurbished Watermill Tearoom and also outside the castle in the Tenants’ Hall Café. Accessibility Overview here. Facilities in addition to those listed below: Baby changing facilities Children's trails Courtesy vehicle Stair Climber Trampers available to book
tagline: Dramatically sited on a wooded hill and the fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years.

title: Charlton House, Montigo Resorts Somerset
subtitle: Discover an oasis of calm at Montigo Resorts, Somerset. With luxurious, individually designed rooms, a spa inspired by Asian traditions, and farm-to-table dining, Charlton House offers an unparalleled rural escape. Experience relaxation, rejuvenation, and the best of Somerset’s local flavours.
bodyContent: Somersets, Montigo Resorts - Charlton House, Shepton Mallet - is nestled in the heart of Somerset’s picturesque countryside, Montigo Resorts, Somerset at Charlton House offers the perfect escape. This historic estate features 28 uniquely designed rooms, each with its own character and charm, combining contemporary comforts with the building’s rich heritage. Whether you’re seeking a cosy hideaway or a spacious suite for a longer stay, there’s a room to suit every taste. The resort’s spa is a serene sanctuary where Asian wellness meets the healing power of nature. Boasting state-of-the-art thermal facilities, hydrotherapy pools, and specialist therapies like Balinese and Thai massages, you’re assured a deeply relaxing experience. For dining, Montigo Resorts showcases the best of Somerset’s seasonal produce; from the colourful cocktails, seasoned meats, and fresh, locally sourced seafood, cooked to perfection, at Tiigo, our kitchen garden pop up promises an authentic pan-Asian experience in a laid-back setting, while the Charlton House restaurant offers a more refined affair and Bob’s Bistro ensures you can grab a bite in the bar or lounge at any time. title: The Yarn Market Hotel
subtitle: Ideally located in the centre of the medieval village of Dunster. The hotel is two and half hours via the A39 from the M5 - but is ten minutes away from the West Somerset Railway England's longest heritage railway. With Minehead 20 minutes away there are all the major facilities you need.
bodyContent: The Yarn Market Hotel in Dunster is ideally located in the centre of Dunster, one of the most perfectly preserved medieval villages in England, and the gateway to Exmoor National Park. The magnificent Dunster Castle is at the end of the street and the West Somerset Railway runs close by. There are many themed breaks on offer throughout the year, and the area is perfect for those who enjoy outdoor activities or just a relaxing break. For walkers the hotel has excellent facilities including a boot and drying room, and maps are readily available combined with local knowledge to help you with your walks. Most of the bedrooms have either a view over the village or the surrounding countryside. Pets are most welcome at the hotel in the dog-friendly rooms. The restaurant opens daily for dinner, reservations are advisable.
tagline: Our Hotel is situated in the beautiful Village of Dunster, within the Exmoor National Park.

title: Cheddar Gorge & Caves
subtitle: Cheddar Gorge & Caves boasts extraordinary subterranean show caves, awe-inspiring cliffs and holds many fascinating secrets about our prehistoric ancestors.
bodyContent: Our Day Ticket gives access to six great attractions: Gough’s Cave: Prepare to be amazed by our stunning show cave featuring spectacular stalagmite and stalactite formations created over 500,000 years ago! See cheddar cheese maturing in the caves, view the site where Cheddar Man’s 10,000-year-old skeleton was discovered and learn about the extraordinary DNA discovery. A free audio guide is available in six languages, and there is also a special version for children. Cox’s Cave featuring Yeo’s Journey: The Power of Water. This spectacular immersive multimedia experience tells the captivating story of how our iconic caves were formed and evolved through the ‘Power of Water’. The story is brought to life using state-of-the-art animation, sound, lighting and colour. Beyond the View: Take a seat in front of our state of the art 270-degree screen. Discover historic tales, enjoy breathtaking aerial panoramic views, and learn about the special wildlife and plants that call the gorge home. Museum of Pre-History: Discover amazing artefacts unearthed in the Cheddar area that help tell the story of how people lived thousands of years ago. Jacob’s Ladder & The Lookout Tower: Venture up the 274 steps to the top of the gorge with rest stops along the route to admire the view. Marvel at the panoramic views and mosaic of landscapes across the Mendips and Somerset Levels. Cliff­ -Top Walk: Hike the 3-mile loop around the gorge. Look out for the wildlife and enjoy the stunning scenery. If you don’t have time to do the full circuit, you can go for a shorter walk up to the Pulpit Rock look out point, and head back down the ladder. Gough’s Café Sit back, relax, and take in the beauty of the gorge at Gough’s Cafe, close to the entrance of Gough's Cave. Enjoy a thirst-quenching chilled drink, warm yourself up with a hot beverage or choose from a selection of alcoholic drinks. Serving light lunches, delicious snacks, cream teas and delicious cake, to include vegetarian and vegan options. Enjoy the spectacular views from the comfort of our air-conditioned cafe or relax on the large patio where dogs are welcome. We even have a welcome bowl of water for our doggy friends. Our small play area for under 2-year-olds will keep the little ones entertained too! Accessibility Cheddar Gorge & Caves provides accessible toilets, free parking for blue badge holders and free admission for carers accompanied by a full paying visitor. The audio tour of Gough's cave is printed in braille. Assistance Dogs are permitted, and the museum is wheelchair accessible with lift. Those with severely restricted mobility or who are wheelchair dependent will find areas of Cheddar Gorge & Caves inaccessible. If you have any questions prior to your visit, please email Guest Services on info@cheddargorge.co.uk or call 01934 742343. Dog-Friendly Dogs are welcome in all attractions and water bowls are provided in the cave entrances, shop and café patio. Family and Children Cheddar Gorge & Cave is family friendly. We have baby changing facilities, buggy parking and are breast-feeding friendly. Gough’s café has a small play area for under two year olds, water refills and highchairs are available. Entry is free for children under the age of 5 years. Groups Cheddar Gorge & Caves has special group rates, coach parking and drop off points for group tours. We offer discounted exclusive group sessions for Rocksport adventure activities – adventure caving, rock climbing and freefall. Special Events We have a fantastic programme of events throughout the year to keep the whole family entertained, including the school holidays. Visit our What’s On page for more details. Thirst for adventure or a puzzle-solving mind? Rocksport: Imagine climbing the gorge rockface in the shadow of the 450ft cliffs, caving deep underground or taking part in our exhilarating Blackcat freefall in Gough’s Cave. Suitable for all abilities. Sessions available for adults and children aged 8 years and over. Escape Rooms : Up for a challenge? Our two Cheddar-themed rooms, Caved In and The Vault will test your brain power as you race against the clock to try to escape. Double the fun with our Ultimate Escape combo ticket at a discounted rate. Suitable for 12 years and over in groups of up to six people. Nature, wildlife, history, adventure - experience the wonder on an all-season day out in Somerset. For more information on how to plan your day at Cheddar Gorge & Caves and to book please visit www.cheddargorge.co.uk
tagline: Explore Britain’s biggest gorge, from the stunning stalactite caverns to the dramatic cliffs.

title: Tudor Adventure at Montacute House
subtitle: Montacute House is a masterpiece of Elizabethan Renaissance architecture and design. With its towering walls of glass, glow of ham stone and its surrounding gardens, it is a place of beauty and wonder.
bodyContent: Sir Edward Phelips was the visionary force and money behind this masterpiece, which was completed in 1601. Built by skilled craftsman using local ham stone under the instruction of William Arnold, master mason, the house was a statement of wealth, ambition and showmanship. Come face to face with the past in the Long Gallery; measuring over 52 metres, it is the longest of its kind in England. The Gallery houses over 60 Tudor and Elizabethan portraits on loan from the National Portrait Gallery. Beautiful gardens surround Montacute, constantly changing, filling the house with scent in summer and providing an atmospheric backdrop for a winter walk. Whether you just want to let the children run and explore, or be inspired by the collections housed within the walls of Montacute, you will leave with lasting memories and a desire to soon return. You may even recognise some of the sights, as Montacute House featured in the BBC’s highly acclaimed production of Hilary Mantel’s Wolf Hall. Within 20 minutes’ drive you will find four fascinating smaller properties, each with a unique character, history and story to tell. Their combined age of 2,300 years spans from the medieval period to the early 19th century. Explore Stoke Priory, a fine collection of medieval farm buildings; Treasurer's House, with its great hall and unusual wall painting; Stembridge Tower Mill, the last remaining thatched windmill in England; and the Priest’s House, a medieval home of great character not to be missed. While you’re in the area, why not also visit Lytes Cary Manor and Tintinhull Garden (see the National Trust website for more details).

title: Glastonbury
subtitle: Discover shops selling everything from vintage clothes to healing crystals. Stop to visit the mystical Chalice Well en route to the remarkable Glastonbury Tor.
bodyContent: Add to this St. Patrick, St. Brigit, St. David, St. Margaret, and the illustrious Dunstan – ‘catching the Devil by the nose’; the Landscape Zodiac, Chalice Well, the White Spring, ‘the holyest erthe in Englande’, William Blake’s Jerusalem, IESUS MARIA, and mysterious, ancient journeys from the ‘Holy Land’… It’s hard to deny Glastonbury is unique. Of course – for many – Glastonbury’s special significance is amplified by the mid-summer ‘Glastonbury Festival’; its Biblical scale tented city appearing – out of nowhere – as a literal Brigadoon; where time bends and a whole month’s worth of fantasy is packed into a few days… until the festival goers return to the ‘real’ world for another year. As if all this were not enough, there’s the Abbey’s mysterious founding in the Wattle Church, Glastonbury’s connection with Joseph of Arimathea, the Holy Thorn, and – of course – the Holy Grail Quite rightly, for all these reasons, Glastonbury is known worldwide; and its unique cultural and spiritual heritage has even attracted the attention of the EU’s Enterprise and Industry Directorate General, as they seek to develop and promote a new pan-European spiritual and cultural tourism route, a modern-day pilgrim’s way, based on the legend of the Holy Grail, which crosses Bulgaria, Crete, Greece, Malta, Spain, and France, before arriving on our shores; culminating at the ultimate focus for all the strands of the Grail’s story: Glastonbury. In the words of the Holy Grail project team leader Professor Paul Fidgeon: “Glastonbury is the Mega-Node!” At the height of the Abbey’s fame, mediaeval Glastonbury was second only to Rome. Glastonbury was actually known as “the Second Rome”; Roma Secunda. Glastonbury was recognised as a spiritual centre of worldwide importance and significance in the past. Today, Glastonbury still flourishes as a unique visitor destination… Who knows? Perhaps the quest for the Grail ends here after all? “May Glastonbury Flourish!”

title: The Castle at Taunton
subtitle: The Castle Hotel is in the centre of Taunton the old County town for Somerset. It is the gateway to the Black Downs and Exmoor National Park, West Somerset Railway, being 5 minute drive from the main line train station from London Paddington, whilst being 30 minutes from the M5 Junction 25 and close many amenities.
bodyContent: The Castle at Taunton is one of the UK’s most historic & prestigious 4 Star Hotels, having been at the forefront of British cuisine for 40 years. We also operate Brazz, which since 1998 has provided the blueprint for British Brasseries across the country The Castle Hotel is a unique family-owned hotel set in a historic building in the heart of Taunton in Somerset. A simple ethos lies at the heart of the hotel – to offer the warmest of welcomes, give the utmost personal attention and exemplary service to each & every guest. The Castle Hotel is a one-off, not a link in a chain. The Castle’s reputation for fine food and wine, comfort, and attentive service has been built by three generations of the Chapman Family, with a passion for promoting the highest standards in every aspect of the hotel. Taunton lies at the heart of the region, making The Castle the ideal base from which to explore the history, magic and wonder of the West Country. Each of The Castle’s 44 bedrooms are individually decorated, offering its own personality and comfort away from home. Whether you’re looking for healthy or hearty, you’ll find it all at the award-winning restaurant, Brazz. Featuring a wide-ranging menu, you’ll find favourites such as Brazz Fishcakes – which have been present since day one – as well as Quantock Lamb, Brixham Crab and much more. The Castle’s legendary afternoon teas are served Wednesday to Sunday from 2:30pm - 4:00pm. Freshly baked scones with West Country clotted cream and strawberry jam, elegant finger sandwiches, pastries and cakes along with a fine selection of loose-leaf tea, make this a very special occasion… especially if you add a bottle of champagne.
tagline: A unique family-owned hotel set in a historic building in Taunton, the county town of Somerset

title: Dunster Castle
subtitle: Fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years, remodelled 100 years ago. Fine 17thC staircase and plaster ceilings. Terrace garden of rare shrubs.
bodyContent: During the winter months, the castle, watermill, and grounds are open at weekends and closed during the week. The Watermill Tearoom, Stables Shop and Parkland are open daily from 10am until 4pm. The car park is also open daily from 10am until 5pm. From 5 April 2025, the whole site is open daily. A fortress that became a family home for the Luttrells, who lived at Dunster for 600 years, the castle was extensively remodelled in the 1870s to create a Victorian country house. The castle boasts breath-taking views over Exmoor, Somerset, and the Bristol Channel as well as holding fine interior features such as a fine 17 th century carved staircase, ornate plaster ceilings, and rare leather wall hangings. Discover how Dunster Castle was used in its heyday and how the family hosted grand occasions from society balls to polo matches with the brilliant ‘Chapters’ guide as well as ‘Castle Explorers, available for children. You can then enjoy a leisurely stroll through beautiful terraced gardens with a collection of palms, sub-tropical plants, and the Dunster Lemon tree. Sited on the River Avill, Dunster Castle is also home to a working watermill that sits within the river gardens. Visit the mill to see the waterwheels in action and even purchase some of the freshly-milled flour. Refreshments are available in the newly-refurbished Watermill Tearoom and also outside the castle in the Tenants’ Hall Café. Accessibility Overview here. Facilities in addition to those listed below: Baby changing facilities Children's trails Courtesy vehicle Stair Climber Trampers available to book

title: The Jane Austen Centre
subtitle: The Jane Austen Centre is in the heart of the Georgian city of Bath, between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths. Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The Jane Austen Centre is in the Georgian city of Bath , Somerset , between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths . Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family. Here you will find out more about Jane Austen, her time in Bath and how the city shaped her work. You can also dress up in Regency costume, taste Regency-recipe biscuits, sample perfumes from the era, try your hand at writing with a quill and ink, have your photo taken with their world famous waxwork, try their delightful ‘Tea With Mr Darcy’ in the Regency Tea Room, and browse their bespoke Giftshop.

title: Wookey Hole Hotel
subtitle: Wookey Hole Hotel is 20 minutes from the oldest medieval city in the UK Wells and sixty minutes from the City of Bath so well positioned for all local locations.
bodyContent: Come and stay at the Wookey Hole Hotel for great value family breaks all year round. Ideally placed in the heart of Somerset, the Wookey Hole Hotel can boast comfortable accommodation in picturesque surroundings. Receive access when you book directly! The Wookey Hole Hotel, located on the southern edge of the rolling Mendip Hills , lies in the Sleepy village of Wookey Hole, with easy access to the historic city of Wells and its stunning Cathedral. The Mendip Hills have been recognised as an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and offer stunning landscapes of sweeping slopes and limestone gorges, with endless walking trails and sightseeing spots. Traverse the Mendips and the hills fall away to the breath-taking lakes of the Chew Valley, just a short drive from Wookey Hole. Also close by are Cheddar Gorge and the ancient town of Glastonbury , with Bath, Bristol and the beaches of Burnham-on-Sea and Weston-Super-Mare slightly further afield. The Hotel includes free and secure car and coach parking, modern bedrooms with free wifi plus a stylish Bar and Bistro. The perfect place for a family break or special occasion - we look forward to welcoming you! And of course, discounted tickets to Wookey Hole Caves and attractions!

title: Burnham, Berrow, Brean
subtitle: The character of the coast changes completely around the mouth of the Parrett with the rocky cliffs and shingle giving way to sand flats that run all the way to the promontory that is Brean Down. Sand naturally attracts holiday makers especially those keen to wield a bucket and spade which is one of the reasons for the popularity of the resorts and parks here. The three Bs - Burnham, Berrow and Brean - are famed for their miles of sand, ideal for walking, running, riding, angling, kite-flying an
bodyContent: As well attracting families looking for a fun-packed break, the beaches of Burnham, Berrow and Brean are also ideal for those wanting to get away from it all because there is room for all. There are dog walkers, wildlife watchers, horse riders, sand sailors, wind surfers and sand artists who all find what they’re seeking on these flat, open beaches with one of the world’s highest tidal ranges. Views across the Channel take in the islands of Steep Holm and Flat Holm and are particularly stunning at sunset. The tidal range and soft mud flats at low water do mean that visitors need to be cautious and avoid walking towards the sea at certain times. There is plenty of information about the dangers as well as beach wardens and rescue services. Burnham’s beaches have something for everyone with some focused on family and others appealing to those who want to watch boats or birds. Further along the strip is Berrow which has a section protected as a Site of Special Scientific Interest because of its rare sand dune habitat. Part of this area is managed by Sedgemoor District Council as a Local Nature Reserve. Vehicles are allowed to park on the sand and there are refreshments available in the summer. The beaches at Burnham and Berrow have been given Seaside Awards by Keep Britain Tidy. At the end of the strip is the headland Brean Down which offers fabulous 360 degree views over the sea on one side, across the Somerset Levels on the other and taking in some of the County’s best known features such as Glastonbury Tor and the Mendip Hills . A bonus some days is an elevated view of the work of sand artists who cannot resist the massive canvas.

title: The Plume of feathers
subtitle: Plume of Feathers is above all, a traditional English country pub. Serving the local community for over 200 years as a place to relax, enjoy company and exchange news and information.
bodyContent: A Traditional Country Pub Plume of Feathers is above all, a traditional English country pub. Serving the local community for over 200 years as a place to relax, enjoy company and exchange news and information. We have a hand picked selection of fine ales from the local Buttcombe brewery and always have one guest ale, and a traditional cider. A wide selection of wines are available by the glass or bottle, and our top shelf includes quality single malt whiskeys and other fine spirits. Families Welcome We welcome families and accompanied children. A stream runs past outside, and there is a shallow ford one hundred metres away. We have a beer garden at the rear of the pub . We have a variety of very traditional pub games including shove ha'penny, table skittles, darts and a pool table. Please think carefully before challenging the "Old Boys" to cribbage for 50p a corner. Board games and playing cards are available on request. The Food We use only fresh ingredients in all our meals. We use local produce and suppliers wherever possible for our meat, fish and vegetables. We have a dining room that seats twenty, and additional tables are available in our bar area. English weather permitting, food may also be served in our beer garden. Our chef shops on a daily basis, sourcing the freshest and best produce available, and only then deciding the best way to cook it. For this reason it is impossible to maintain an accurate menu of exactly what is on the blackboard today. title: Burrington Beginners Climbing Climb Adventure
subtitle: Climbing in beautiful and tranquil Burrington Combe in Somerset. The Combe cuts a swathe through the peaceful Mendip Hills - but some of the routes here are anything but tranquil! This crag offers some perfect beginners and children's climbing - on easily accessible rock. This is a modular session - which means you can pick a session from 2 hours up to the full weekend. Pricing is shown below - and is according to the length.
bodyContent: This session will see you exploring the range of faces on offer at the Combe. There are many crags here and a range of climbing possibilities - as well as some other interesting locations close by. We shall be rotating climbing - as none of us will be able to climb solidly all day - and you will need to belay for a climbing partner during the day. There will also be time for lunch, and time for a tea break here and there - in one of Cheddar Gorge's well known coffee hang outs! For more Info Click here

title: Cycling
subtitle: The area around Weston-super-Mare offers cyclists of all abilities some fantastic opportunities. There’s the challenging climbs of the Mendip Hills but also large areas of flat riding along the levels which mean you don’t need to have the latest carbon fibre bike and all the flashy lycra gear to get out there and enjoy the countryside.
bodyContent: Cycling If you don’t have a bike or haven’t brought it with you on holiday, you can hire a bike, a tandem or even a side-by-side tandem, in Weston from http://www.in2gear.biz/ Here below are a few rides for you to enjoy, or alternatively you can spread out your Ordnance Survey map or tap into Google Maps to create a ride of your own. The Brean Down Way This ride starts slap bang in the middle of Weston and takes you right out to one of Somerset’s finest viewpoints, through nature reserves and under the shadow of the Uphill cliffs. It then climaxes with a spectacular ride along the rocky headland that is Brean Down to reach Palmerston Fort at the very tip of the peninsula. The eight-mile outward ride is varied in both landscape and terrain, starting out as a flat promenade heading south from Weston’s Grand Pier. It then takes you to the pretty village of Uphill, with its cliff-top church, and out through the Walborough and Bleadon nature reserves before arriving at Brean Down. There you can follow the Old Military Road along to the old fort taking in awesome views past the islands of Flat Holm and Steep Holm and across to Wales or looking back to Weston. You can also stop off for some refreshments and reward yourself at one of the cafes along the route. More HERE

title: Stunning views from Sand Point
subtitle: Sand Point is an extension of the Mendip Hills and walkers trekking across the peninsular will be rewarded with wonderful views across the Bristol Channel.
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: about 4 miles Difficulty: medium to hard: narrow, rugged paths, a couple of wooden stiles. Wear suitable footwear Duration: allow 2-2.5 hours at a leisurely pace Map: OS 153 Explorer Sand Point is an extension of the Mendip Hills and walkers trekking across the peninsular will be rewarded with wonderful views across the Bristol Channel. Head onto the beach from the Sand Road car park. The sand dunes are man-made sea defences, installed in 1983/4 after a major storm in 1981. More than 600,000 tonnes of sand was dredged up from the Severn Estuary to raise the beach by about three metres. Fencing was also installed to help stabilise the dunes and encourage vegetation. Head north on the beach, towards Sand Point. The sand becomes grassy and it can get a bit muddy so you might want to step up onto firmer ground, next to the trees. You will come to a wall, the remains of concrete forts which were used as a line of defence during World War 2 by local troops and the Home Guard. Walk alongside the wall and at the end there are a couple of steps leading to a path and the National Trust car park. For more info and a PDF please click HERE

title: Exploring the tidal trail around Uphill
subtitle: Take a tour through salt-marshes and open grasslands just south of Uphill to see some award-wining nature reserves.
bodyContent: The walk starts in Uphill boat yard, a tranquil spot alongside Uphill quarry. Wharf Side Tea Room is now open if you need some refreshments before you head off. Continue past the preserved lime kiln, which was built between 1780 and 1850 to provide lime, through the kissing gate into Uphill Nature Reserve. The reserve has recently been awarded another Green Flag. Uphill Quarry was used from the 1800s to 1940s and in 1826 three caves were discovered that had been used by Neanderthal people during the Ice Age. Tools and bones were discovered, including those from a woolly mammoth and cave lion. Follow the path through the reserve, past the 19th century explosives store, which was used for blasting the quarry stone. Dogs need to be kept under close control as cattle graze in the fields. Go through the wooden gate and follow the path up the hill. Look behind you for wide-ranging views of Brean Down, Uphill, and across the Severn estuary. title: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm
subtitle: Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is a conservation charity and the largest zoo in Somerset with over 100 species of animals. The multi award winning Zoo is open 7 days a week and aims to make Noah's Ark a place of joy, wonder, adventure and refreshment that supports the well-being of all visitors, staff and volunteers. Through education and fun, they aim to inspire and motivate this generation and the next to consider sustainable lifestyles and care for our planet.
bodyContent: Amazing Animals The home of the big Zoo animals! Visit Noah’s Ark and come face to face with a cheeky mob of meerkats, be awed by African elephants and dazzled by the zebra herd! Experience the majestic beauty and see the skies come alive during the daily birds of prey displays! The Wings of Wonder display showcases the owls, hawks, falcons and eagles in an unforgettably mesmerizing spectacle. Indoor and Outdoor Adventures Play and adventure never stops with our 10 play areas across the 100-acre site. Enjoy the huge indoor play barns including under 5’s soft play and a giant rainbow slide. The Zoo also has accessible play equipment including nest swings and a wheelchair accessible roundabout. Fancy an a-maze-ing adventure? Navigate through Britain’s longest hedge maze. The British wildlife themed maze has 3.4km of paths and wooden nest tower at the center. Keep the whole family smiling and active all day, whatever the weather! Accessibility Noah’s Ark Zoo Farm is proud to be an accessible attraction. Facilities include multiple accessible toilets, Changing Places facility, accessible play equipment, hearing loops and more. Please visit the website before your visit for up-to-date information and to view the Access guide. Prices Buy online and save! Noah’s Ark recommends that all tickets, including those for free essential carers and under 2’s are purchased online prior to your arrival. Prices are seasonal, please check the website for up-to-date ticket prices. Food and Drink With a range of delicious hot and cold food and drink options available in our Food Barn and convenient snack kiosks across the Zoo, there is something for everyone! Alternatively, visitors are very welcome to bring their own lunch and enjoy it in one of our many picnic spots. Mini Experiences Noah’s Ark offers incredible up-close mini experiences with Meerkats, Capybara, Andean Bears and Giant Tortoise. You will enjoy 20 minutes behind the scenes with the keeper, learn some interesting facts and get involved with their feeding and enrichment programme. Pre-book your experience online to ensure availability. Minimum age and terms and conditions apply. Animal Experiences Find out what it’s like to be a keeper for the day with our one-to-one keeper experiences before the zoo opens. Experiences include: African Elephants, Junior Keeper Experience, and Giraffe and Rhino experience.
tagline: You’ll be amazed at the variety of nature you’ll see with over 100 species of animals

title: Rock Inn
subtitle: 3 Flavours already has a duo of thriving neighbourhood eateries in Barnet and Banbury and ‘3 Flavours Kitchen’ is the first to launch in the Southwest, with many more planned to roll-out in the near future. Chef Chanaka Fernando’s vision for 3 Flavours Kitchen is to provide an exceptional dining experience that combines culinary excellence with the charm of Waterrow, near Taunton.
bodyContent: Steaks are a standout feature on the menu with options such as the Rib-Eye Steak (250g) priced at £26.50, Sirloin Steak (250g) at £25.00, and Rump Steak (250g) at £21.00. Diners can enhance their steak experience with a variety of sauces, including peppercorn, mushroom, béarnaise, garlic butter, and chimichurri for an additional £2.00 each, or upgrade to a luxurious truffle red wine sauce for £3.00. Grill & Burger highlights include the Grilled Chicken Burger at £14.50 and the 3 Flavours Signature Beef Burger at £15.00, both served with caramelised onions, truffle mayo, rocket, ketchup, relish, and fries. Seafood lovers can indulge in the Miso Grilled Salmon at £23.50, served with a Japanese salad and sesame. Vegetarian options feature the Grilled Cauliflower Steak (v) at £15.50, paired with roasted pepper sauce, basil, and olive salsa, and the Grilled Vegetable Burger (V) at £11.00, featuring caramelised onion, mushroom, grilled courgettes, hash browns, rocket, and spicy mayo. Curries are a cornerstone of the new menu, offering a range of aromatic dishes served with steamed rice and crispy shallots. Notable dishes include the Monkfish & Tiger Prawn curry at £22.00, Aromatic Chicken Green Curry at £16.50, and the Ceylon Lamb at £17.50.
tagline: 3 Flavours Kitchen at The Rock Inn in Waterrow, near Taunton is the latest culinary concept

title: The Old Vicarage Hotel and Restaurant, Bridgwater, Somerset
subtitle: This unique and quirky hotel is a 10 minute drive from the main line station at Bridgwater or 24 minutes from M5 Junction 24 - so is close to all connecting services and local amenities and supermarkets.
bodyContent: “Looking for somewhere really special to stay, look no further you have found it”, “I don’t think I have ever been made to feel so welcome”, are just some of our recent 5-star reviews. This historic hotel has been lovingly renovated with bedrooms individually designed for complete relaxation and comfort. If you want to be spoilt, relax and eat delicious food visit Candy, Peter and their friendly, professional team whose mission to give every guest (and their dogs) the warmest of welcomes and most memorable stay. The Old Vicarage is tucked away in peaceful surroundings overlooking St Mary’s Church, the only building in Bridgwater older than it, yet is only 10 minutes from the M5. The hotel is full of historic importance dating back to 1327; it is said that Isambard Kingdom Brunel designed the town bridge in the 17th century Oak Room and Judge Jeffery’s stayed, one of the bedrooms even has its own wig cabinet. Each of the 18 en-suite bedrooms are individually designed and kept spotlessly clean with the most comfortable beds and views over the gardens or church. The south facing gardens are glorious, perfect for weddings and enjoying in the sunshine. On cooler evenings there is a cosy bar and snug with comfy sofas for enjoying a drink or two in front of the fire, an oak panelled restaurant and a brand new undercover patio with a pizza oven. A short drive and you can be alone on the Quantock Hills walking in Coleridge’s footsteps, bird watching on the Somerset Levels or hunting for fossils on the Jurassic Coast at Kilve. For the more energetic kayaking, coasteering, mountain biking, pony trekking are all on hand or if shopping is your thing Bristol, Bath, Taunton, Glastonbury and Wells are not far away. Book today for your perfect holiday.
tagline: “Looking for somewhere really special to stay, look no further you have found it”

title: Wookey Hole Caves & Attractions
subtitle: Wookey Hole Caves is a magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for all ages. It’s an experience millions of years in the making with plenty to do inside and out. Enjoy vintage penny arcades, museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, and of course the famous, beautiful caves.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Wookey Hole Caves and attractions lies In the heart of Somerset. A magical place of caves, legends, and adventure for the young and young at heart. When you visit Wookey Hole, you’ll enjoy an experience millions of years in the making. There is plenty to do inside and out, from vintage penny arcades to museums, adventure golf, and soft play zones, to name but a few of the attractions. Not forgetting the breathtakingly beautiful caves, for which Wookey Hole is renowned. Your visit will take you through 8 chambers. Each with a unique beauty and story. You’ll also pass our cheese tunnel, home to the delicious Wookey Hole cheese. The cheese is not the only resident of the caves. Over the years, Wookey Hole has been home to giant hyenas, bears, Neanderthals, and many local people. It has even been a site of pagan and Roman worship. You’ll find Wookey Hole holds a surprise around every corner. You might even get to meet our most famous resident, the Witch of Wookey Hole. We have found she most likes to visit during school holidays! The world-famous Wookey Hole Circus School performs at Wookey Hole at weekends and in School Holidays. Every year over 250,000 people visit Wookey Hole and take-home cherished memories of a great day out. Whether it is your first time or your fiftieth, there is always something new to discover. We can’t wait to welcome you.
tagline: At Wookey Hole Caves and Attractions, Somerset, there’s always fun and adventure to be had.

title: ⭐Shepton Mallet Prison
subtitle: Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’; Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom...
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Built in 1610 following on Act introduced by King James I, which stated that all counties had to have their own ‘House of Correction’, Shepton Mallet was the oldest working prison in the United Kingdom. Shepton Mallet Prison is a recently decommissioned (2013) Georgian jail where visitors can walk in the footsteps of our social history and hear officers shine a light on what life was like for both the incarcerated and those who guarded them through the ages. Before its closure, it was a category C lifer prison holding 189 prisoners. Opened in 1646, it was expanded in 1790, with further building work undertaken in the 1820s and 1830s, including the installation of a treadwheel for those sentenced to hard labour. In 1930, the inmate numbers fell and the prison was closed. During the Second World War, the prison was reopened and used as a military prison. It was initially used by the British Army and later by American forces, who constructed a new execution block for condemned prisoners. It was also used for the storage of important historical documents, including the Domesday Book. It returned to civilian use in 1966. Shepton Mallet prison is also known for its tales of paranormal activity. One of the most popular stories is that of the White Lady. She is frequently seen or sensed in various locations, especially A Wing. Staff and prisoners would often complain of an icy wind moving through the wing, the sweet smell of perfume and shadowy figures. She supposedly dates from the late 1700s, when she spent some time in the prison. During a lovers' tiff which escalated, she murdered her betrothed. Once found guilty and sentenced to death, she was housed in Shepton Mallet Prison. On the evening before her execution, she asked for her wedding dress to be brought to the prison, which they allowed. She wore it to bed that night, but in the morning the officers found that she had died during the night. No cause of death was ever found, so we are left to presume that she died of a broken heart. Perhaps this is why she still haunts the prison? In the early 1950s, the Kray Twins were also held here after deserting the British Army. Today, the prison is open as a tourist attraction offering Guided Tours, Self-Guided Tours, Escape Rooms, Night Behind Bars and Ghost Hunting Behind Bars. This is an immersive experience without gizmos or gimmicks – the jail is very much as it was when the last prisoners left in 2013. In 2025, Shepton Mallet Prison received the prestigious Trip Advisor Travellers’ Choice, for the 7th time running, placing it among the top 10% of attractions worldwide.

title: Oakham Treasures
subtitle: Oakham Treasures is one of the largest privately owned museums of retail and farming history in the UK. Opened to the public for the very first time since July 2008, it has already become an award winning major attraction, and guarantees to give you an amazing and uplifting trip down memory lane.
bodyContent: Whether you are 8 or 80, you'll be fascinated by this vast and unique collection of memorabilia from the last century. There really is something for everybody, from the thousands of items in the historic stores, to the impressive display of vintage tractors and farm equipment. Collections include Grocery Store The grocery store is the largest of the shops on display at Oakham Treasures. Stocked from floor to ceiling behind the original shop counters and weighing scales, there is a vast array of not only real live grocery contents, but their packaging, merchandising and advertising signs as well! The store provides a fascinating view of the vast number of grocery brands in existence throughout the 20th century. Famous names such as OXO, Coca Cola, Colman's, Heinz and Huntley and Palmers have all changed little in appearance, whereas others, such as Birds Egg Substitute, Smiths Crisps and Black Boy Coffee are all long gone! As you browse through shelf upon shelf of stock, you'll be amazed at just how many old products you recognise from your past. Do you remember doing the laundry with Rinso, Fairy Snow, Drive, Clozone, Fab or even Omo? It's all here in this vast treasure trove of grocery items, just waiting to be rediscovered by you on your nostalgic trip down memory lane! Sweet Shop Remember that wonderful aroma when you dived into the corner sweet shop with your hard earned pocket money? Being spoilt for choice between rows and rows of brightly coloured jars behind the counter? Then you'll love the sweet shop at Oakham Treasures, whatever your taste! From Polar Mints to Murray Mints, Brown Bros India Rock to Zubes, Fruit Gums to Fry's Chocolate and Blue Bird Liquorice Rolls to Cadbury's Sixpenny Cake Chocolate, this sweet tooth haven has it all! There are rows and rows of chocolates, still in their original packaging, all presented in a beautiful and traditional sweet counter. There's even a Nestlé and After Eight Mints salesman's display case, traditionally used by the sales representative when travelling round the independent retailers. There's also an especially impressive display of locally manufactured Fry's memorabilia, showing the breadth of chocolate bars produced together with the original merchandising including the still famous 'Five Boys' advertising campaign on metal signs. And more ....

title: Stunning views from Sand Point
subtitle: Sand Point is an extension of the Mendip Hills and walkers trekking across the peninsular will be rewarded with wonderful views across the Bristol Channel.
bodyContent: Walk information Distance: about 4 miles Difficulty: medium to hard: narrow, rugged paths, a couple of wooden stiles. Wear suitable footwear Duration: allow 2-2.5 hours at a leisurely pace Map: OS 153 Explorer Sand Point is an extension of the Mendip Hills and walkers trekking across the peninsular will be rewarded with wonderful views across the Bristol Channel. Head onto the beach from the Sand Road car park. The sand dunes are man-made sea defences, installed in 1983/4 after a major storm in 1981. More than 600,000 tonnes of sand was dredged up from the Severn Estuary to raise the beach by about three metres. Fencing was also installed to help stabilise the dunes and encourage vegetation. Head north on the beach, towards Sand Point. The sand becomes grassy and it can get a bit muddy so you might want to step up onto firmer ground, next to the trees. You will come to a wall, the remains of concrete forts which were used as a line of defence during World War 2 by local troops and the Home Guard. Walk alongside the wall and at the end there are a couple of steps leading to a path and the National Trust car park. For more info and a PDF please click HERE

title: Exploring the tidal trail around Uphill
subtitle: Take a tour through salt-marshes and open grasslands just south of Uphill to see some award-wining nature reserves.
bodyContent: The walk starts in Uphill boat yard, a tranquil spot alongside Uphill quarry. Wharf Side Tea Room is now open if you need some refreshments before you head off. Continue past the preserved lime kiln, which was built between 1780 and 1850 to provide lime, through the kissing gate into Uphill Nature Reserve. The reserve has recently been awarded another Green Flag. Uphill Quarry was used from the 1800s to 1940s and in 1826 three caves were discovered that had been used by Neanderthal people during the Ice Age. Tools and bones were discovered, including those from a woolly mammoth and cave lion. Follow the path through the reserve, past the 19th century explosives store, which was used for blasting the quarry stone. Dogs need to be kept under close control as cattle graze in the fields. Go through the wooden gate and follow the path up the hill. Look behind you for wide-ranging views of Brean Down, Uphill, and across the Severn estuary. title: Dunster Castle
subtitle: Fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years, remodelled 100 years ago. Fine 17thC staircase and plaster ceilings. Terrace garden of rare shrubs.
bodyContent: During the winter months, the castle, watermill, and grounds are open at weekends and closed during the week. The Watermill Tearoom, Stables Shop and Parkland are open daily from 10am until 4pm. The car park is also open daily from 10am until 5pm. From 5 April 2025, the whole site is open daily. A fortress that became a family home for the Luttrells, who lived at Dunster for 600 years, the castle was extensively remodelled in the 1870s to create a Victorian country house. The castle boasts breath-taking views over Exmoor, Somerset, and the Bristol Channel as well as holding fine interior features such as a fine 17 th century carved staircase, ornate plaster ceilings, and rare leather wall hangings. Discover how Dunster Castle was used in its heyday and how the family hosted grand occasions from society balls to polo matches with the brilliant ‘Chapters’ guide as well as ‘Castle Explorers, available for children. You can then enjoy a leisurely stroll through beautiful terraced gardens with a collection of palms, sub-tropical plants, and the Dunster Lemon tree. Sited on the River Avill, Dunster Castle is also home to a working watermill that sits within the river gardens. Visit the mill to see the waterwheels in action and even purchase some of the freshly-milled flour. Refreshments are available in the newly-refurbished Watermill Tearoom and also outside the castle in the Tenants’ Hall Café. Accessibility Overview here. Facilities in addition to those listed below: Baby changing facilities Children's trails Courtesy vehicle Stair Climber Trampers available to book
tagline: Dramatically sited on a wooded hill and the fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years.

title: The Castle at Taunton
subtitle: The Castle Hotel is in the centre of Taunton the old County town for Somerset. It is the gateway to the Black Downs and Exmoor National Park, West Somerset Railway, being 5 minute drive from the main line train station from London Paddington, whilst being 30 minutes from the M5 Junction 25 and close many amenities.
bodyContent: The Castle at Taunton is one of the UK’s most historic & prestigious 4 Star Hotels, having been at the forefront of British cuisine for 40 years. We also operate Brazz, which since 1998 has provided the blueprint for British Brasseries across the country The Castle Hotel is a unique family-owned hotel set in a historic building in the heart of Taunton in Somerset. A simple ethos lies at the heart of the hotel – to offer the warmest of welcomes, give the utmost personal attention and exemplary service to each & every guest. The Castle Hotel is a one-off, not a link in a chain. The Castle’s reputation for fine food and wine, comfort, and attentive service has been built by three generations of the Chapman Family, with a passion for promoting the highest standards in every aspect of the hotel. Taunton lies at the heart of the region, making The Castle the ideal base from which to explore the history, magic and wonder of the West Country. Each of The Castle’s 44 bedrooms are individually decorated, offering its own personality and comfort away from home. Whether you’re looking for healthy or hearty, you’ll find it all at the award-winning restaurant, Brazz. Featuring a wide-ranging menu, you’ll find favourites such as Brazz Fishcakes – which have been present since day one – as well as Quantock Lamb, Brixham Crab and much more. The Castle’s legendary afternoon teas are served Wednesday to Sunday from 2:30pm - 4:00pm. Freshly baked scones with West Country clotted cream and strawberry jam, elegant finger sandwiches, pastries and cakes along with a fine selection of loose-leaf tea, make this a very special occasion… especially if you add a bottle of champagne.
tagline: A unique family-owned hotel set in a historic building in Taunton, the county town of Somerset

title: The Jane Austen Centre
subtitle: The Jane Austen Centre is in the heart of the Georgian city of Bath, between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths. Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family.
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available The Jane Austen Centre is in the Georgian city of Bath , Somerset , between the architectural attractions of Queen Square and the Circus, and just a short stroll from Bath Abbey, the Assembly Rooms and the Roman Baths . Come and meet their costumed ‘character’ guides, and enjoy being shown Bath’s fascinating history and its associations with Jane Austen and her family. Here you will find out more about Jane Austen, her time in Bath and how the city shaped her work. You can also dress up in Regency costume, taste Regency-recipe biscuits, sample perfumes from the era, try your hand at writing with a quill and ink, have your photo taken with their world famous waxwork, try their delightful ‘Tea With Mr Darcy’ in the Regency Tea Room, and browse their bespoke Giftshop.

title: Glastonbury
subtitle: Discover shops selling everything from vintage clothes to healing crystals. Stop to visit the mystical Chalice Well en route to the remarkable Glastonbury Tor.
bodyContent: Add to this St. Patrick, St. Brigit, St. David, St. Margaret, and the illustrious Dunstan – ‘catching the Devil by the nose’; the Landscape Zodiac, Chalice Well, the White Spring, ‘the holyest erthe in Englande’, William Blake’s Jerusalem, IESUS MARIA, and mysterious, ancient journeys from the ‘Holy Land’… It’s hard to deny Glastonbury is unique. Of course – for many – Glastonbury’s special significance is amplified by the mid-summer ‘Glastonbury Festival’; its Biblical scale tented city appearing – out of nowhere – as a literal Brigadoon; where time bends and a whole month’s worth of fantasy is packed into a few days… until the festival goers return to the ‘real’ world for another year. As if all this were not enough, there’s the Abbey’s mysterious founding in the Wattle Church, Glastonbury’s connection with Joseph of Arimathea, the Holy Thorn, and – of course – the Holy Grail Quite rightly, for all these reasons, Glastonbury is known worldwide; and its unique cultural and spiritual heritage has even attracted the attention of the EU’s Enterprise and Industry Directorate General, as they seek to develop and promote a new pan-European spiritual and cultural tourism route, a modern-day pilgrim’s way, based on the legend of the Holy Grail, which crosses Bulgaria, Crete, Greece, Malta, Spain, and France, before arriving on our shores; culminating at the ultimate focus for all the strands of the Grail’s story: Glastonbury. In the words of the Holy Grail project team leader Professor Paul Fidgeon: “Glastonbury is the Mega-Node!” At the height of the Abbey’s fame, mediaeval Glastonbury was second only to Rome. Glastonbury was actually known as “the Second Rome”; Roma Secunda. Glastonbury was recognised as a spiritual centre of worldwide importance and significance in the past. Today, Glastonbury still flourishes as a unique visitor destination… Who knows? Perhaps the quest for the Grail ends here after all? “May Glastonbury Flourish!”

title: Bath Theatrical Costume Hire
subtitle: Bath Theatrical Costume Hire, a family business established in 1969 moved from our quirky little shop in Bath to our warehouse in Frome in 2001, housing more than 30,000 costumes. We work with hundreds of companies, casts, actors, and partygoers to ensure they have the best costumes for their event.
bodyContent: Bath Theatrical Costume Hire, from its small beginnings above a hairdresser on the London Road in Bath, is now based in Frome and houses over 30,000 costumes. “When we moved from our overcrowded premises on London Road, we thought we would never fill our new home, even with our two friendly ghosts in tow. Now that too, is crammed with fabulous stuff, some of which is already put together as costumes but much of which is waiting for our touch of magic to bring the characters to life”, said Dinah Auton, the second generation to run the business. Bath Theatrical is like no other business and for those who know it, they are delighted that it is so different. It is perhaps its quirkiness which has helped it ride the economic and professional changes which have flavoured the past 50 years. Through all this Bath Theatrical has managed to add its magic to many a party goer, wedding guest and stage costumes. We service professional and amateurs’ groups, schools, corporate promotions, alternative weddings, events, and a wide array of private hire for parties. Talk to our staff about how we can make your event, production or celebratory occasion that extra special.
tagline: Bath Theatrical Costume Hire, a family business established in 1969

title: West Somerset Railway
subtitle: West Somerset Railway, Somerset, is a heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton. It is the longest independent railway in Britain, (20 miles).
bodyContent: West Somerset Railway, Somerset is the longest Heritage line in the United Kingdom. Time Table can be seen HERE for 2024 The line is situated in Somerset, four miles outside the County town of Taunton , starting at Bishops Lydeard and finishing at Minehead . The line meanders through the Quantock Hills , an area of outstanding natural beauty and along the Bristol Channel Coast. We have 10 stations along the line each having something different to offer. There are various historic sites that may be of interest to visitors to the area, for example Crowcombe Heathfield station was the location for the filming of the Beatles’ “A Hard Days Night” and scenes from “The Land Girls” were also shot here. The historic town of Watchet dates back to Saxon times, and boasts narrow streets, local shops, museums and lots of places to eat and drink. Washford is a great place to alight, just a short walk from the station we have Cleeve Abbey and the Torre Cider Farm, which are both well worth a visit. Fancy something a little different then why not visit Dunster Castle which is nestled in the medieval village of Dunster ? Dunster also has a working Watermill , the Old Yarn Market building and the Dolls Museum or continue on to Minehead home of our final station. Minehead is situated at the foot of North Hill where the beach is literally right across the road, we have cafes, shops and plenty of arcades along the seafront, making this a go to location. The West Somerset Railway also have combined tickets on selected dates throughout the year. These include, Cream Tea and Cheese and cider specials and linked trips with Hestercombe Gardens and Dunster Castle. We organise Steam Galas in the Spring and Autumn, and we are host to a Diesel Gala too. In the latter part of the year we have our popular Christmas services, we have Santa services running out of Minehead and Bishops Lydeard from the end of November until Christmas Eve, we also have our Sherry and Mince pie specials for you to enjoy.
tagline: Heritage steam railway operating between Minehead and Bishop's Lydeard, near Taunton.

title: New Manor Farm Shop and Cafe
subtitle: The Farm Shop has been open since 2002 starting life as one of the smaller farm buildings in the Farm Courtyard.
bodyContent: The Farm Shop and cafe The Farm Shop has been open since 2002 starting life as one of the smaller farm buildings in the Farm Courtyard. We are an outlet for fully traceable meat, mainly reared here on the farm. Our own Angus & Hereford Beef, Lamb and Gloucestershire Old Spots and Large White Pork, plus local free range Chicken, and a good variety of seasonal game such as Venison, Duck, Pheasant, Partridge, Guinea Fowl and Rabbit. Add to this a great selection of our own recipe sausages, made on the premises, and choices of hams and bacon, alongside local free range eggs, and our own organic eggs from the Farm itself. Our chilled cabinets are well stocked with our home produced milk, and the delicatessen is home to a large range of British and continental cheeses, some of which are local, plus fabulous olives and continental cured meats. The Tearooms The tea rooms are open 7 days a week and we are looking forward to welcoming you all back! Centered around our traditional Farm Court Yard you will find the Stable Tea Rooms, adjacent to our Farm Shop. The Tea Rooms are open everyday from 9:30 in the morning, closing at 5:30 during the week, and at 5:00 at the weekends. Breakfasts, lunches and teas are available everyday, with a large and varied homemade menu which changes daily. A great opportunity for visitors to try our home produced meat and produce.

title: King John's Hunting Lodge, National Trust
subtitle: This early Tudor timber-framed wool merchant's house (circa 1500) provides a fascinating insight into local history.
bodyContent: King John's Hunting Lodge, Somerset, National Trust - This early Tudor timber-framed wool merchant's house (circa 1500) provides a fascinating insight into local history. Its strong medieval character is enhanced by the appearance of arcaded stalls opening onto the street on the ground floor (recreated by the National Trust during the building's restoration). Please note: King John's Hunting lodge is run as a local history museum by Axbridge and District Museum Trust. There is a small entrance charge of £2.50 per person for all adults. Free to all National Trust members.

title: The Bishop's Palace
subtitle: The Bishop’s Palace and Gardens in Wells has been home to the Bishops of Bath and Wells for over 800 years and this stunning medieval palace is now open for all to enjoy. It’s a great family day out in Somerset with a full programme of year-round events, free guided walks, open-air music and theatre, garden workshops and more and a slice of cake with afternoon tea at the ever-popular Bishop’s Table café is always welcome!
bodyContent: ⭐ Reward Card Discount Available Visit Highlights: There are 14 acres of outstanding RHS Partner gardens to explore (including the beautiful well pools from which the city takes its name), Dragon’s Lair play area, guided tours, children’s trails and workshops and a café with the best views in Wells! Multi media tours of the Palace building are also included with admission with the choice of an adult version or one tailored for a more family audience including quizzes, treasure hunts and talking Bishops from years gone by! Visitors are guided around the Palace buildings through five narrative themes using stories, music, imagery, quizzes and talking Bishops bringing stories of their tenure and legacy at the Palace to life in an interactive and engaging way. A year-round programme of themed family events is also included with admission including a Civil War Weekend; Archery, Vikings and more! Other events are ticketed separately including summer outdoor theatre; the Palace’s Garden Fair and History Live. The Bishop’s Palace dates from the early-thirteenth century when Bishop Jocelin Trotman received a crown licence to build a residence and deer park on land to the south of the Cathedral of St Andrew. Although home to the Bishop and other families, visitors can walk in the footsteps of past bishops through a number of rooms within the Palace. Visitors are also welcome to look around the Bishop’s private Chapel and explore the ruined Great Hall. The moat has been home to mute swans since the 1800s. The tradition of swans on the moat at The Bishop’s Palace in Wells is thought to go back to the 1850’s when it is likely that a Bishop’s daughter first taught the swans to ring a bell at the Gatehouse for food. We now have two swan bells – one just beneath the window on the left of the Gatehouse, the other to the right – both with a rope hanging down for the swans to pull. The Palace Gardens are open daily from 10am until 4pm in winter and 9.30am - 5.30pm in summer although there may be restricted access due to events and activities taking place (check the website for details). There are toilets on site. Guided tours are also included with Admission – check available times at the Ticket Office on arrival. Families: There’s so much for families to do at The Bishop’s Palace, whatever the weather. Little ones love to explore the gardens, trying to spot the swans and their cygnets; there are waterfalls and springs to see, trees to climb and places to hide. Children also love to explore the magical discovery area that is the Dragon’s Lair in a far corner of the Gardens! And throughout the school holidays, there are always plenty of events to keep families busy including crafting, outdoor gardening, family trails, storytelling and more. Refreshments: The Bishop’s Table café is open daily serving delicious, locally-sourced homemade food and some of the best coffee and cake you'll find in Wells. It’s the perfect place to meet friends for breakfast, lunch and afternoon teas or Sunday Lunches are now being served! Accessibility: From the main entrance of the Palace to the Palace building, around the gardens and to the café's dining area, there is level access. We have one lift to all floors of the Palace building. The outer gardens are accessible via a bridge which is 810mm wide. There are fully accessible toilets with level access within the Stableyard area and the Palace building. There are three spaces available on site for accessible parking, however, it is necessary to book these at least 48 hours before arrival via info@bishopspalace.org.uk or call 01749 988111.
tagline: The Bishop's Palace and Gardens, Wells, Somerset is a great family day out in Somerset.

bodyContent: We're all about community. And we're all about getting people outdoors on the beautiful Strawberry Line. We think that cycling is for everyone and our range of traditional and adaptive bikes to rent reflects that, and so do our brilliant staff - we offer people with learning disabilities meaningful employment and training. We have a café on site We can also offer bike rentals for short break or holiday periods.

title: Cheddar Gorge & Caves
subtitle: Cheddar Gorge & Caves boasts extraordinary subterranean show caves, awe-inspiring cliffs and holds many fascinating secrets about our prehistoric ancestors.
bodyContent: Our Day Ticket gives access to six great attractions: Gough’s Cave: Prepare to be amazed by our stunning show cave featuring spectacular stalagmite and stalactite formations created over 500,000 years ago! See cheddar cheese maturing in the caves, view the site where Cheddar Man’s 10,000-year-old skeleton was discovered and learn about the extraordinary DNA discovery. A free audio guide is available in six languages, and there is also a special version for children. Cox’s Cave featuring Yeo’s Journey: The Power of Water. This spectacular immersive multimedia experience tells the captivating story of how our iconic caves were formed and evolved through the ‘Power of Water’. The story is brought to life using state-of-the-art animation, sound, lighting and colour. Beyond the View: Take a seat in front of our state of the art 270-degree screen. Discover historic tales, enjoy breathtaking aerial panoramic views, and learn about the special wildlife and plants that call the gorge home. Museum of Pre-History: Discover amazing artefacts unearthed in the Cheddar area that help tell the story of how people lived thousands of years ago. Jacob’s Ladder & The Lookout Tower: Venture up the 274 steps to the top of the gorge with rest stops along the route to admire the view. Marvel at the panoramic views and mosaic of landscapes across the Mendips and Somerset Levels. Cliff­ -Top Walk: Hike the 3-mile loop around the gorge. Look out for the wildlife and enjoy the stunning scenery. If you don’t have time to do the full circuit, you can go for a shorter walk up to the Pulpit Rock look out point, and head back down the ladder. Gough’s Café Sit back, relax, and take in the beauty of the gorge at Gough’s Cafe, close to the entrance of Gough's Cave. Enjoy a thirst-quenching chilled drink, warm yourself up with a hot beverage or choose from a selection of alcoholic drinks. Serving light lunches, delicious snacks, cream teas and delicious cake, to include vegetarian and vegan options. Enjoy the spectacular views from the comfort of our air-conditioned cafe or relax on the large patio where dogs are welcome. We even have a welcome bowl of water for our doggy friends. Our small play area for under 2-year-olds will keep the little ones entertained too! Accessibility Cheddar Gorge & Caves provides accessible toilets, free parking for blue badge holders and free admission for carers accompanied by a full paying visitor. The audio tour of Gough's cave is printed in braille. Assistance Dogs are permitted, and the museum is wheelchair accessible with lift. Those with severely restricted mobility or who are wheelchair dependent will find areas of Cheddar Gorge & Caves inaccessible. If you have any questions prior to your visit, please email Guest Services on info@cheddargorge.co.uk or call 01934 742343. Dog-Friendly Dogs are welcome in all attractions and water bowls are provided in the cave entrances, shop and café patio. Family and Children Cheddar Gorge & Cave is family friendly. We have baby changing facilities, buggy parking and are breast-feeding friendly. Gough’s café has a small play area for under two year olds, water refills and highchairs are available. Entry is free for children under the age of 5 years. Groups Cheddar Gorge & Caves has special group rates, coach parking and drop off points for group tours. We offer discounted exclusive group sessions for Rocksport adventure activities – adventure caving, rock climbing and freefall. Special Events We have a fantastic programme of events throughout the year to keep the whole family entertained, including the school holidays. Visit our What’s On page for more details. Thirst for adventure or a puzzle-solving mind? Rocksport: Imagine climbing the gorge rockface in the shadow of the 450ft cliffs, caving deep underground or taking part in our exhilarating Blackcat freefall in Gough’s Cave. Suitable for all abilities. Sessions available for adults and children aged 8 years and over. Escape Rooms : Up for a challenge? Our two Cheddar-themed rooms, Caved In and The Vault will test your brain power as you race against the clock to try to escape. Double the fun with our Ultimate Escape combo ticket at a discounted rate. Suitable for 12 years and over in groups of up to six people. Nature, wildlife, history, adventure - experience the wonder on an all-season day out in Somerset. For more information on how to plan your day at Cheddar Gorge & Caves and to book please visit www.cheddargorge.co.uk
tagline: Explore Britain’s biggest gorge, from the stunning stalactite caverns to the dramatic cliffs.

title: Burrington Beginners Climbing Climb Adventure
subtitle: Climbing in beautiful and tranquil Burrington Combe in Somerset. The Combe cuts a swathe through the peaceful Mendip Hills - but some of the routes here are anything but tranquil! This crag offers some perfect beginners and children's climbing - on easily accessible rock. This is a modular session - which means you can pick a session from 2 hours up to the full weekend. Pricing is shown below - and is according to the length.
bodyContent: This session will see you exploring the range of faces on offer at the Combe. There are many crags here and a range of climbing possibilities - as well as some other interesting locations close by. We shall be rotating climbing - as none of us will be able to climb solidly all day - and you will need to belay for a climbing partner during the day. There will also be time for lunch, and time for a tea break here and there - in one of Cheddar Gorge's well known coffee hang outs! For more Info Click here

title: Blenheim Gardens
subtitle: Minehead premier gardens just off the town centre and a few minutes’ walk from the sea front and the harbour
bodyContent: Blenheim Gardens (maintained and run by Somerset West and Taunton council) is ideally situated in the centre of Minehead and covers nearly 2.5 hectares of parkland. Created in the 1920's it is now a mature, attractive and sheltered haven, popular with residents and visitors. The park provides spring and summer bedding displays, a wide range of trees, shrubs and perennials which thrive in the mild seaside climate. The flower beds and shrub areas are framed by lawns. The park boasts a bandstand for summer weekend concerts/brass bands. There is an 18-hole putting green but currently there is no formal play provision for children. The Gardens contain female, male and disabled toilets maintained and run by Minehead Town Council. There are several access points into the Gardens (from North Road, Blenheim Road and via a footpath from The Avenue) and a public car park with 62 spaces on the eastern boundary accessible from North Road.

New England décor greets you inside, allowing for a relaxing drink in our bar and snug areas. Eat in our award winning Galley restaurant, locally sourced food providing a menu for all tastes. Our onsite facilities include a fully equipped gym and exercise classes. We have two meeting rooms for weddings, parties and conferences. Most of our bedrooms look over the sea or the West Somerset Railway and all have en suite facilities. We strive to be sustainable as much as possible, therefore we supply fresh milk in your rooms for your tea and coffee along with delicious homemade shortbread biscuits.

title: Dunster Castle
subtitle: Fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years, remodelled 100 years ago. Fine 17thC staircase and plaster ceilings. Terrace garden of rare shrubs.
bodyContent: During the winter months, the castle, watermill, and grounds are open at weekends and closed during the week. The Watermill Tearoom, Stables Shop and Parkland are open daily from 10am until 4pm. The car park is also open daily from 10am until 5pm. From 5 April 2025, the whole site is open daily. A fortress that became a family home for the Luttrells, who lived at Dunster for 600 years, the castle was extensively remodelled in the 1870s to create a Victorian country house. The castle boasts breath-taking views over Exmoor, Somerset, and the Bristol Channel as well as holding fine interior features such as a fine 17 th century carved staircase, ornate plaster ceilings, and rare leather wall hangings. Discover how Dunster Castle was used in its heyday and how the family hosted grand occasions from society balls to polo matches with the brilliant ‘Chapters’ guide as well as ‘Castle Explorers, available for children. You can then enjoy a leisurely stroll through beautiful terraced gardens with a collection of palms, sub-tropical plants, and the Dunster Lemon tree. Sited on the River Avill, Dunster Castle is also home to a working watermill that sits within the river gardens. Visit the mill to see the waterwheels in action and even purchase some of the freshly-milled flour. Refreshments are available in the newly-refurbished Watermill Tearoom and also outside the castle in the Tenants’ Hall Café. Accessibility Overview here. Facilities in addition to those listed below: Baby changing facilities Children's trails Courtesy vehicle Stair Climber Trampers available to book
tagline: Dramatically sited on a wooded hill and the fortified home of the Luttrells for 600 years.

title: Sandford Station Railway Heritage Centre
subtitle: Located at Sandford, five miles from Yatton Station along The Strawberry Line, seven miles from Weston-super-Mare and seventeen miles from Bristol
bodyContent: View this historic station restored to its former glory. Step inside the vintage carriage, complete with compartments and guards van. Browse the authentic railway artefacts. Restored 1940’s Sentinel shunting engine. The Gauge One Model Railway is run frequently, but not every open day and not all day. There may well be up-to-date information on the Facebook page.
